§ 154.01 ADOPTION OF NATIONAL PROPERTY MAINTENANCE CODE.
   Pursuant to KRS 83A.060(5), the 2012 International Property Maintenance
Code, and subsequent amendments and future editions thereto, as published by
the International Code Council, be and is hereby adopted as the Property
Maintenance Code of the City of Independence, Kenton County, Kentucky for
regulating and governing the conditions and maintenance of all property,
buildings and structures, by providing the standards for supplied utilities and
facilities and other physical things and conditions essential to ensure that
structures are safe, sanitary and fit for occupation and use; and the
condemnation of buildings and structures unfit for human occupancy and use, and
the demolition of such existing structures as herein provided; providing for
the issuance of permits and collection of fees therefor; and each and all of
the regulations, provisions, penalties, conditions and terms of said Property
Maintenance Code on file in the City of Independence are hereby referred to
adopted, and made a part hereof, as if fully set out in this section, with the
additions, insertions, deletions and changes, prescribed in Section III of the
ordinance codified herein.
(Ord. 2015-O-21, passed 9-14-15)

Independence, KY City Council Meeting Minutes
Contains meeting minutes current from January 13, 1998 through March 19, 2025
1998 Minutes
January 13, 1998
City Of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard, and the Pledge of Allegiance
was done. The Mayor explained the meeting was being held at the Kenton County
Extension Center due to the on-going renovations at the Courthouse.
At Roll Call, all council members were in attendance.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
1- The minutes from the December 8 meeting were approved without change, by
motion of Mr. Weber, seconded by Mr. Holten, with all ayes. The minutes from
the December 9th meeting were approved with amendments by motion of Mr. Weber,
seconded by Mr. Holten, with all ayes.
NEW BUSINESS
2- The Mayor asked if anyone wished to add to the agenda. Additions to New
Business were Community Access on Cable (Mrs. Henson) and Discussion regarding
Personnel Policy changes (Mayor Gabbard). Items added under Old Business were
Mr. Kolb’s Development Plan (Mrs. Henson), and the Planning Session (Mayor
Gabbard).
BUDGET CHANGES PRIOR TO AMENDMENT
3- Mr. Scott asked council to review a list of budget line item changes which
will be addressed in an amended budget ordinance later. He provided a handout
with known changes, and these were explained to council as needed.
4- Mr. Scott informed council about the $ 60,000 from the 1996-97 budget which
was spent for Shaw Park site preparation during the 1997-98 fiscal year.
Council would have to decide whether this money would be removed from the 1997-
98 budget under General Fund or from the existing Park Budget. After some
discussion, council asserted it was their intent this money be spent from the
prior year budget, and that the money should come from the General Fund instead
of the current Park Budget.
5- Mayor Gabbard explained to council that the line item for Fowler Creek
expenses was overspent or will be shortly. The Mayor will check this item out
and bring this topic back for discussion at the January 27 meeting.
CABLE BOARD COMMUNITY ACCESS
6- Mrs. Henson wished to inform council, the Mayor and the public that the
Telecommunications Board will have a Community Program Advisory Committee. She
asks that anyone interested in applying to be on this committee notify her.
This committee would have various duties and report to the Cable Board.
AMENDING THE PERSONNEL POLICY
7- Mayor Gabbard suggested the Personnel Committee review and change several
current policies. One change would be to allow 2 weeks of vacation for new
staff vs. the existing 1 week. A second change would be to allow for a 90 day
probation period for new staff. The Mayor asked the committee to review these
ideas and possibly bring a document to the January 27th meeting for a first
reading.
8- Mrs. Henson commented the committee had stopped meeting after the summer,
and that she recommended an outside service be brought in to complete the
revisions to the policy, at a cost of $ 3000-6000. Mr. Holten said he was not
anxious to spend more money in this direction, and discussion followed
regarding the expense for the service and for legal review. Mr. Scott was asked
to work with the Personnel Committee, and Mr. Jed Deters said his office had
offered to do this work for a minimal fee. It was established that Mrs. Henson
has been the chairperson for this committee.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
9- The Mayor opened up this section of the meeting. Mr. Robert Exeler addressed
council regarding water service on Fowler Creek. He provided a document to the
Mayor and asked if the City would look into providing water for this area.
Discussion ensued as to grant money available to fund this project plus a need
to get the remainder of the city tied into water service. The Mayor and City
Administrator will look into this.
OLD BUSINESS
POSSIBLE CHANGE TO 3RD CLASS CITY
10- Mr. Scott gave out information to council regarding the benefits of
becoming a 3rd Class City. He explained the benefits of moving to a 4th class
city also, but said that with city population, we should consider the 3rd class
status.
   He believes the fire department is not required to be a part of a 3rd class
city, only fire service. The process to become a 3rd class city would begin
with council adopting a resolution to petition the General Assembly, and ask
local legislators to sponsor a bill. Data would need to be provided to all
these parties, but the procedure is generally a smooth one.
11- Mrs. Steffen added that there were a few other benefits to becoming a 3rd
class city, which she shared with council. The Mayor spoke about recognition
which comes with 3rd class status. Council discussed this and had concerns
about down-sides to this change. It was determined that council would probably
be willing to draft such a resolution, but only after Mr. Scott could provide
legal, written confirmation regarding the fire department, and explaining the
pros and cons of such a move.
SEWERING HOMES ON MADISON
12- Dan Briggs, Cardinal Engineering, spoke to council about sewering homes
between the Swindler Funeral Home and the Independence Christian Church. Old
figures he had from April, 1996, stated costs estimated at $ 15,000 for one
home. He has surveyed a route, and said cost would run $ 30,000-38,000
depending on the direction the pipes are run. It might be easier and more cost
effective to run in a southerly direction. These costs do not include legal or
engineering fees of probably an additional 15%.
13- Discussion followed regarding cost and other concerns. Mr. Exeler spoke on
this, and Mr. Briggs said if the city could work with the church, costs could
be cut by as much as $ 6000.
14- Mrs. Henson raised the possibility of sending a letter to the residents
involved, stating approximate costs for the project. Mr. Weber stated this
should only be as a proposed project in the letter, and council agreed. Council
would then wait to see what resident’s reactions were before committing to the
project. Mr. Jed Deters had concerns regarding other “pockets” of the community
who are also without water and cautioned not over-extending until the City can
find out how it is doing with the Fowler Creek assessments.
15- It was suggested that Dan Briggs do 2 work-ups: the Madison area and the Mc
Cullum area, and bring this information back to council.
ARCHITECTURAL FEES
16- Mr. Scott said the price charged for the service the City received in
architectural rendering was reasonable and in-line with what we received in
work. He recommended the city pay the bill. Mrs. Weber asked that the city quit
hiring architects for projects until we actually plan to act on something.
APPOINTMENT TO PLANNING/ZONING COMMITTEE
17- Mr. Russ England is the current representative to this committee. The Mayor
told council he had decided to re-appoint Mr. England since he himself had not
been approved by council. Discussion followed as to 2 other candidates who had
applied to the Mayor and whether he had met with them or considered them. There
were questions about Mr. England’s attendance and other concerns regarding his
service to the city while on the committee. Questions were raised as to the
Mayor appointing Mr. England when the Mayor originally had requested this
position for himself, and concerns about Mr. England’s ties to builders.
Discussion continued, with council finally taking a vote.
18- Motion was made by Mrs. Gabbard, seconded by Mrs. Steffen, to approve Mr.
England to the position on the Planning and Zoning Committee. Vote was taken by
roll call, with 2 yes votes, and 4 no votes coming from Mrs. Weber, Mr. Weber,
Mr. Holten and ,Mrs. Henson. Mrs. Henson added that her no vote was given
because the 2 other candidates had not been interviewed. The motion failed.
19- The Mayor commented that he will now allow the decision to fill Mr.
England’s spot to be made by NKAP board, since neither he nor Mr. England were
approved. The Mayor was asked if he would consider holding off on this decision
and interview the 2 candidates, Mr. Exeler and Mr. Feldhaus. Mrs. Henson
volunteered to check as to procedure so Mr. Feldhaus and Mr. Exeler could still
apply.
FOLLOW-UP
20- Mr. Al Bowling spoke about the junk autos on Wayman. He said letters needed
to go out about this, and it could be taken to court. He is currently working
with Mr. Wong of NKAP, and Mr. Dave Kean. The Mayor was concerned about the
lack of follow-through by NKAP and again voiced concern the City might have to
take over the zoning work. Mr. Scott said there is a way that cities can group
together to contract with a firm to do this work, and he would like to bring
information to council on this. Cardinal Engineering had also expressed
interest in doing the zoning work.
21- Discussion ensued as to the amount of money paid for zoning services; in
particular, Mr. Wong’s fees. The city would remain in contract with NKAP but
would not have to remain in contract with them for zoning, and the money
currently spent to pay Mr. Wong could be applied toward another zoning
administrator.
22- Mr. Bowling spoke about Cherokee Bowl and his meeting a week ago with one
of the owners, Mr. Scott, a real estate agent , and 2 other parties. The
meeting was to discuss city concerns and review possible options. Mr. Bowling
said the building is definitely structurally sound, so no condemnation can
occur based on that. Mr. Bowling and Mr. Scott will continue to look into ways
to deal with this problem site.
23- Mrs. Henson brought up a concern regarding a 1996 notice about a pool
without a fence. This has gone unresolved for 18 months or more. Mr. Bowling
said he would speak with Mr. Wong about this again.
KOLB DEVELOPMENT PLANS
24- Mrs. Henson had asked this item to be on the agenda since she was not aware
that a meeting had been set up to deal with it. Now that she is aware a
committee is meeting on this January 15th, it does not need to be discussed at
this time. Item is withdrawn.
PLANNING SESSION
25- The Mayor spoke about dates and times for an upcoming Planning Meeting. A
Friday session would run 6-10 p.m., with a Saturday session running from 9:00
a.m. to 5:00 p.m.. After some discussion, the dates of January 30-31 were
decided upon, and the City Clerk was asked to look into possible sites. The
Mayor and City Administrator asked that council provide, within a week,
information as to topics they wish to discuss. Council members also mentioned
this was an open meeting and residents could attend if they chose.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
Police Department
26- Chief Porter informed council of a recent DARE graduation service held at
Kenton Elementary. There were over 120 students in attendance, along with
family members.  The room was overflowing with people, and the group
enthusiastically supported the DARE program. Chief Porter commented that this
was a good experience, and was pleased with the attendance at the event, as
well as the enthusiasm it generated.
Building Inspector
27- Mr. Bowling reported that he had arranged for Rumpke to use his numbers in
the future as guideline for their billing. Cherokee Auto Parts is set to be
inspected on January 14th by Mr. Bowling, Mr. Wong and a representative from
the Fire District.
Engineering Report
28- Dan Briggs referred to the items on “follow-up” and said the raw sewage
problem in the Beechgrove area had probably been resolved. Regarding the
potholes on Berrywood, this is a dedicated city street, and work will begin on
this soon. Regarding lighting at the Beechgrove Clubhouse, the Mayor is waiting
for a letter from the Homeowners Association rep, Sandy Brewer. Lighting was
requested near the clubhouse area.
29- Rickey Lane residents had complained about sewer smells due to a forced
main discharge. Mr. Briggs explained this could be alleviated in part with
chemical injection costing $ 3200 for equipment and $ 60 per month for
chemicals. The Mayor will review the budget for money to do this work.
30- Holten Drive’s report has been received and Thelen recommends total
replacement. Dan Briggs is reviewing options, including white-topping and grant
or other funds to assist with costs.
31- Sewer monitors are in place, but will be pulled for approximately 3 months
to go to areas where problems are suspected. Reports are being given to EPA.
32- Mr. Exeler asked what could be done about “blackwater” on Fowler Creek near
the pumping station. Mr. Briggs will check into this.
City Attorney
33- Mr. Jed Deters had nothing to report and there were no ordinances to be
read.
City Administrator
34- Mr. Scott spoke about talks he had with Cinergy regarding street lights. He
would like to propose that in future when plats are done, a letter should go to
the builder about our ordinance with a request for the $ 50.00 fee and 5
copies. Once these are received, the city would then release, instead of
putting Cinergy in the middle.
35- There was a concern that some street light backs were being blacked out at
the request of residents, due to the light shining into their homes. There is a
question as to who should pay for this. Mr. Scott suggests the residents should
call the city and we can inform Cinergy to do this work, if we approve.
36- “Blighted property” such as the Cherokee Bowl site can be better addressed
once we achieve 3rd Class City status. The city may have options of its own
that are not now available.
37- Mr. Scott informed council he had attended a Budget Seminar.
   He wanted to follow the plan for budget preparation he learned about. From
this information, he had plans to meet with department heads (and was currently
doing so) to begin work on the 1998-99 budget. He wishes to have the budget
read and accepted in July, 1998.
38- Regarding committees, Mr. Scott said he encourages the committees to
present information at council meetings so it can be acted upon. Most concerns
should be ironed out prior to submitting the ideas to council so the council
meetings will not spend undue time on these topics.
39- Mr. Weber asked about a light at Rice and Klette Roads that has been out
for some time, as well as a light on the hill on Rice Road. This will be
checked out by Mr. Scott.
40- The Mayor spoke about a letter to UHLP/Cinergy and Owen Electric regarding
charges for the proper amount of lights. Mr. Scott was asked to follow up on
this to ascertain correct information for billing.
41- A question arose about lighting at subdivision entrances. Mrs. Weber asked
how we get these lit properly. The Mayor said Arlinghaus proposed 3 lights on
Hartland Blvd., but no entrance lights. Discussion ensued about whether the
city should adopt an ordinance regarding entrance lighting, plus cost to the
city. Mr. Deters was asked to begin work on an ordinance, and Mr. Scott will
review the existing street light ordinance to see how it may address this
concern.
Mayor’s Report
42- Mayor Gabbard said he and Mr. Scott attended a recent NKAP meeting that
dealt with Drees’ request for re-zoning of property. He and Mr. Scott spoke
against this, and the motion was defeated by an 8-7 vote. The Mayor also stated
an Executive Session was needed this evening.
43- Mr. Holten, who is on a Northern Kentucky Chamber of Commerce committee,
asked the Mayor to hold a meeting with Taylor Mill regarding business within
the city limits, preferably in March or April. The Mayor responded that
Independence is not in the Chamber and he would have to think about this and
wished to look over any material related to this proposed meeting.
44- Motion was made by Mrs. Weber, seconded by Mr. Weber, to adjourn to
Executive Session, with all ayes.
45- Motion was made to return to regular session by Mr. Holten, seconded by
Mrs. Henson, with all ayes. A motion was then made to adjourn the regular
meeting by Mrs. Henson, seconded by Mr. Weber, with all ayes, The meeting was
officially adjourned.
                  _________________________
                  Isaac Gabbard, Mayor
___________________________________
Linda L. Baker, City Clerk
January 27, 1998
City Of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard, followed by the Pledge of
Allegiance, and an invocation by Reverend William Risher of the New Banklick
Baptist Church.
ROLL CALL
Roll call was taken, with all council members being present.
The Mayor welcomed council and the audience members. He explained this was the
first meeting held in the newly renovated room of the Courthouse. He thanked
Kenton County Fiscal Court for their work and the expense in renovating the
area, and commented that the City had provided funds toward the sound system.
The Mayor asked for the minutes of January 13 to be approved or if there were
any changes. Council members commented they did not want to deal with this, and
Mr. Holten requested the agenda be changed to deal with the fact that no legal
counsel was present. This needed to be the first order of business.
CITY ATTORNEY - CONCERNS
1- Motion was made by Mr. Holten, seconded by Mr. Weber, to address this issue
before other business. Discussion ensued as to whether legal representation at
the meeting was necessary. Roll call vote was 4 ayes, with 2 no votes (Gabbard
and Steffen). Motion passed.
2- Mr. Holten said an ordinance had been prepared to re-appoint the Deters,
Benzinger, and Lavelle firm as City counsel. He presented this to council and
city staff. Mr. Holten motioned, seconded by Mrs. Weber, that the ordinance be
read. The Mayor asked for time to review the document before proceeding. He
then asked for comments.
3- A long argument ensued over the merits of Mr. Deters vs. Mr. Wichmann, and
the experience of both attorneys. The Mayor commented on Judge Summe’s ruling
of January 15th stating which led to the City having no legal counsel. Council
members argued with the Mayor at length on this issue, and there were several
comments from residents, also. Discussion ended, with a vote being called to
read the ordinance: vote of 4 ayes and 2 no votes (Gabbard and Steffen). Motion
passed.
4- The ordinance was read by the City Clerk, after which a motion was made to
approve the first reading (Holten/K Weber). Vote was 4-2, and passed.
5- Mr. Jed Deters advised an emergency ordinance would be needed before
resumption of counsel duties. Discussion followed as to the effect on the city
of acting without counsel, and possible retention of Mr. Deters for a short-
term period ranging, from 2 to 6 weeks, to carry on city business. Motion was
made by Mr. Holten, seconded by Mr. Weber, to adjourn the meeting, due to lack
of counsel. Discussion followed.
6- The Mayor read, for the record, the appointment document regarding Mr. Frank
Wichmann as City Attorney. (see addendum). Discussion ensued about Mr. Deters
representing the City in the past, having done so well, and council’s concerns
regarding why Mr. Deters was let go by the Mayor.
7- There was discussion about whether Mr. Deters had acted in conflict with the
City interests, being a property owner in the City. This led to argument over
the ruling by Judge Summe as to whether it did or did not affirm the Mayor.
Some council members stated they did not wish to adjourn.
8- A resident, Mr. Wilson, commented on his struggles with the City regarding
an on-going problem with parking his truck in the driveway. He remarked that
the power struggle caused people to suffer, and that council and the Mayor
needed to be for the people.
9- Discussion ensued regarding Mr. Wilson’s problem and ordinances which had
been introduced to deal with it. No ordinance had been completed and approved
to date on this. The Mayor spoke out about Mr. Wichmann being the original
author of several documents this city has used. The gross receipts tax
ordinance and the ordinance prohibiting the removal of non-elected city
officers was drafted from his models for another city.
10- The Mayor spoke about Mr. Kolb’s business before council on the agenda and
that a time-line requirement meant it would need to be addressed quickly. Mr.
Napier, a resident, said council seemed unwilling to hire Mr. Wichmann for an
interim period, and could a compromise with the Mayor be reached. Council
members and the Mayor responded with arguments for their choices.
11- After more discussion, a vote was called to adjourn the meeting based on
Mr. Holten’s earlier motion. The motion was modified to no adjournment, but the
meeting would continue on only to hear concerns but not vote on issues. Roll
call vote was a 3 - 3 tie. The Mayor broke the tie and the meeting continued
with agenda items to be addressed.
12- Mrs. Henson motioned that Mr. Wichmann be appointed the city counsel for an
interim period of 2 -4 weeks. Motion was seconded by Mrs. Gabbard. Discussion
ensued with questions being addressed to Mr. Wichmann. Mr. Jed Deters commented
that Mr. Wichmann would be in a conflict of interest due to the suit, and Mr.
Wichmann responded that the Deters’ firm would then be in the same conflict.
Mrs. Henson withdrew her motion.
13- Mr. Holten motioned that impeachment proceedings be started against the
Mayor. Due to lack of a second, the motion died.
14- Citizen comments continued about setting aside personal problems to get on
with City business. Several spoke of being embarrassed by these and past
proceedings. The Mayor was challenged by one citizen to get on with the meeting
and appoint an attorney.
15- Mr. Napier, who attended due to a zoning problem, asked for assistance. Mr.
Scott referred him to the Board of Adjustments and advised Mr. Napier to meet
with him the following morning on this issue.
16- Tempers flared and shouting ensued, with comments about council members
having personal agendas against the Mayor. Mrs. Henson, in particular, spoke
out that this was not so for herself. Mrs. Weber agreed.
17- Mr. Bill Wilson spoke again about his problem with parking his truck.
Council and the Mayor addressed his concerns, and Mrs. Steffen asked if this
could be dealt with immediately by a vote. Response was no, since no attorney
to advise.
CRAIG KOLB - DEVELOPMENT OF PROPERTY
18- Mr. Scott updated council on the committee meeting of January 15th
regarding the development of property at Taylor Mill and Cox Road. Deed
restrictions were agreed to, and read to council by Mr. Scott at this time.
Basically, it seemed an agreement had been reached that Mr. Kolb should be
granted his zone change.
19- Mr. Kolb showed his revised site plan based on changes of the January 15
meeting. New plans include a 200 foot buffer zone and office buildings. He is
getting recommendations from other sources re how to handle curb cuts.
20- Discussion ensued re the problem of curb cuts, with Mr. Kolb asking the
city to allow a deviation from 600’ to 275’ minimum. Discussion continued about
how to over-ride the Area Planning decision for no zone change. Mr. Wichmann
offered an opinion wherein Mr. Kolb could have the city override the NKAP
decision by using their transcript of that meeting and voting on zone changes.
21- The Mayor said the city would look into this and speak with Mr. Kolb. Also,
he spoke about a possible Public Hearing. Mr. Kolb was under the impression
that the December 9th council meeting was indeed a public hearing, and this was
clarified for him. Motion was made by Mrs. Steffen, seconded by Mrs. Gabbard,
to overturn the NKAP decision regarding the zoning of this property, with the
understanding a public hearing would be held to address the issue. Discussion
followed.
22- Comments were made about council being told not to attend the January 15th
committee meeting. A resident, Mr. Napier, commented on the city taking action
for Mr. Kolb’s project when other people’s concerns were not being dealt with.
Council was not prepared to vote on the re-zoning based on Mr. Wichmann’s
advice. The motion was withdrawn.
23- A resident asked that Mr. Kolb verify in writing what he will do with the
property. Mrs. Weber commented this any document re property development should
be a legal document, including the deed restriction information. Council agreed
a public hearing date should be set to deal with the re-zoning concern.
TRAILER PARKING
24- Mrs. Steffen asked if she could present her ordinance to deal with parking
of trailers and trucks via conditional use permits. She motioned that a first
reading be done, which was seconded by Mrs. Henson, who commented she had
presented similar regulations which had been voted down.
25- Discussion ensued with Mr. Wilson commenting on his experience, and council
commenting on the existing ordinance. As the form provided to council was not
in ordinance format, the motion Ms. Steffen made was withdrawn.
26- After considerable comment and discussion, Mrs. Henson suggested 3 council
members volunteer to form a committee with others to address this concern of
truck parking. She volunteered to chair the committee, and Mrs. Steffen and
Mrs. Weber agreed to serve.
27- Mr. Wilson asked if the city could back off this issue with him for a
while, Mrs. Weber spoke with Mr. Bowling who said he would not follow through
on this until the committee had met to discuss solutions. It was suggested that
Mr. Wilson check with Mr. Bowling as to how he would be notified.
AMENDED BUDGET 1997-98
28- The Mayor asked council to review the amended budget document provided to
them and asked the City Clerk to explain changes made. Information was provided
by the clerk, and Mrs. Weber asked if the corrections had been reviewed by Mr.
Frank Keller. As they had not, 1st reading was delayed. The Mayor reminded
council that some bills could not be paid or work continued until more money
had been appropriated as noted in the amended budget.
MR. KOLB
29- Mr. Kolb stated that during the meeting he had noted that the 90 days he
had to act within would end as of February 4th. He asked for clarification as
to how to proceed. He was asked to get the transcript of the meeting at NKAP at
which his proposed zone change had been turned down. The public hearing would
be set for the 4th, with a special council meeting after it at which council
could vote on whether to re-zone or not.
3RD CLASS CITY STATUS
30- Mr. Scott did not have any legal document which answered council’s
questions about moving to 3rd class city status. Since these were unavailable
yet, this item will be re-visited at a later meeting.
KY ACTION RESOLUTION
31- Mr. Scott provided a document to council regarding a resolution to support
the KY ACTION alliance, whose goal is to give communities more power to deal
with tobacco use by children. Mrs. Gabbard motioned council adopt the
resolution, but with no second, the motion died. Mr. Scott urged council and
residents to contact state legislators if they support the issue.
RESOLUTION RE SB 66
32- Mr. Scott explained this resolution would provide grant money for community
improvement projects, with qualifications. He read aloud the resolution. Motion
was made by Mrs. Gabbard, seconded by Mrs. Steffen to adopt the resolution.
Vote was 2 ayes, 1 no (Mrs. Henson) and 3 “not voting” (K Weber, R Weber, S
Holten). Motion passed.
PLANNING SESSION
33- Discussion was opened about the Planning Session, but was stymied by
concerns regarding lack of legal counsel. Mrs. Henson motioned council instruct
the Mayor to begin a search for legal counsel. This was seconded by Mrs. Weber,
with all 6 voting aye. Motion passed.
ADJOURNMENT
34- Motion was made by Mrs. Henson, seconded by Mrs. Weber, to adjourn the
meeting. Vote was all ayes, and the meeting officially adjourned.
                _______________________________
               Isaac Gabbard, Mayor
_____________________________
Linda L. Baker, City Clerk
FEBRUARY 2, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
1.   Mayor Gabbard called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. The meeting was
attended by council members Ken Weber, Scott Holten, Anita Steffen & Barbara
Gabbard
2.   Mayor Gabbard stated this meeting had been called for the purpose of
discussion and taking possible action on legal services contracts for the city
and discussion of the Kenton Circuit Court Action #97-CI-00594. The Mayor
opened the floor for discussion.
3.   Mr. Weber asked the Mayor if he was aware of the alternate proposal that
he had spoke to the City Administrator about. He replied that he had spoke to
Mr. Scott regarding the city attorney situation. Charles Deters stated that the
city had agreed to pay $4,000 per month for legal services and does not wish to
see the city pay more than that. He said that a motion has been filed before
the judge to ask for payment for the time spent on ordinances and litigation
which is more than the $4,000. He would like payment up until the day of the
judgement by Judge Summe on January 22, 1997. He feels that hiring Frank
Wichmann is a conflict of interest because Mr. Wichmann is involved as a party
in the lawsuit against the city. He questioned how the city could hire someone
that is suing the city. Mr. Deters’ would like to settle the lawsuit, but will
not do so without payment of services for the last several months, otherwise he
will take it to the Court of Appeals.
4.   Mr. Deters proposed as settlement for council: (1) pay the Deters firm the
usual $4,000 per month fee from April 1, 1997 up to the date of judgement (1-
22-97); (2) dismiss the lawsuit, which would settle the conflict of interest
for Mr. Wichmann, then; (3) council will agree to hire Frank Wichmann through
June 30, 1998 to handle both the legislative and executive sessions. Mr. Deters
suggested contracting with Mr. Wichmann for $3,500 per month with $500.00 per
month retainer being set aside for council to receive services from Jed Deters
on possible legislative concerns. Mr. Deters mentioned that council still has
reservations because of Mr. Wichmann’s allegiance to the Mayor and not council.
5.   Mayor Gabbard stated that while he does not agree with everything in Mr.
Deters proposal, that it is a start and worth considering. He stated that there
is a shortfall in the budgeted legal fees.
6.   Mr. Weber thinks the proposal is a workable solution for everyone in a no-
win situation. Mr. Wichmann suggested seeing if two attorneys is workable then
it is just a matter of settling on money and fees. Mr. Weber responded that the
majority of council is opposed to having two attorneys and reiterated that he
thinks the proposal outlined by Mr. Deters is a just and fair offer. Mr. Deters
stated that council does not think that dividing the city legal work is a
workable solution and will only complicate the situation further. Mr. Wichmann
stated that he did not agree.
7.   Mr. Wichmann does not agree with the part of the proposal where the Deters
firm is paid 100% for their services for the past several months and does not
include payment for his services, as he has attended all the council meetings,
prepared documents and conferred with the Mayor. He feels he should be paid as
well. Mr. Holten reminded Mr. Wichmann that he asked him at previous meetings
if he was willing to work non-gratis as council did not provide funding in the
budget to pay for his services. Mr. Wichman stated that he did not agree to
work non-gratis. Mr. Deters stated that council agreed that the Deters firm
would be doing all the city work. Mr. Holten stated that he will back Mr.
Wichmann’s services in this proposal now, but will not pay for previous
services. Mrs. Gabbard asked what the plans for legal services was after June
30, 1998. Mr. Weber stated that council will address that issue at a later
date.
8.   Mayor Gabbard stated that he feels council has made a reasonable offer but
would need two considerations to accept this offer: (1) Frank Wichmann should
be contracted to work through December 31, 1998 which would be the end of the
current administration’s term; and (2) money for Mr. Wichmann’s previous work,
as the judge said there was no valid contract for either attorney. The Mayor
said he needed time to take this proposal under consideration and requested the
proposal be put in writing. He would like to discuss this issue again at the
next special meeting on Wednesday, February 4, 1998.
9.   Mr. Deters asked if this would be just discussion or if a decision would
be made, as this proposal needs to be done in the form of formal documents,
contracts, etc. The Mayor responded that he needs the proposal in writing and
needs time to consider it. Mr. Deters stated that he would fax a written
proposal to the city office tomorrow morning. He also stated that all parties
to the lawsuit would need to participate in the sign-off of the agreement. Mr.
Deters presented the Mayor with a copy of the motion they filed with Judge
Summe in answer to her judgement on Case #97-CI-00594.
10.   There was a short discussion regarding legal representation for the city
at the special meeting on Wednesday (2-4-98) to discuss and take possible
action regarding the zone change request for the property at Cox & Taylor Mill
Rds owned by Mr. Craig Kolb.
11.   Ken Weber made a motion to adjourn. Scott Holten seconded the motion.
Meeting adjourned at 7:30 p.m.

February 9, 1998
City of Independence, KY
Special Council Meeting
Minutes
CALL TO ORDER
The Mayor called the meeting to order at 7:40 p.m. The special meeting was
called to address two issues: Legal services contracts, and Kenton Circuit
Court Action # 97-CI-00594. Discussion had begun on these issues at a prior
special meeting of February 2, 1998. The meeting was originally set for the
Courthouse, but was moved at the last minute to the City Building due to
problems getting into the Courthouse building.
ROLL CALL
Roll call was taken, with all members being present.
DISCUSSION
The Mayor opened the floor to council members to discuss the issues on the
agenda. After considerable discussion, these are the basic points of the
meeting:
Mr. Deters offered and read an ordinance outlining payment to his firm (see
attached document). He also provided a detailed list of services provided to
the City over the past 10 months. Mr. Wichmann did not have such a list
prepared, but stated he had provided to the Mayor a statement for services
rendered which outlined what he had done. He offered to provide such a list
again if necessary.
Mrs. Steffen offered information on City Attorney salaries as a comparison for
council to review. Discussion centered on why the Deter’s firm was paid so much
originally, and a concern that future attorney fees could be lower, now the
city has a City Administrator.
The Mayor was asked several times if he had instigated a search for a neutral
attorney, to which he responded he had not done so yet. When asked if he had
plans to begin this search, he responded he had no plans to begin a search at
this time.
No compromise was reached, due to concerns that hiring Mr. Wichmann would put
him in conflict with the City due to the ouster suit he is handling for Mayor
Gabbard.
A point of impasse appeared to be reached, and Mrs. Henson motioned for an
adjournment, seconded by Mr. Holten, with all ayes. Meeting was officially
adjourned.

February 10, 1998
City of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order at 7:00 by Mayor Gabbard. The pledge of
allegiance was followed by an invocation offered by Reverend Greg Fightmaster
of the Beechgrove Baptist Church.
ROLL CALL
Roll call was answered by 5 council members, with Mrs. Gabbard being the only
absent councilperson.
APPROVAL OF MINUTES
Motion was made to approve the minutes of January 13, 1998, as amended (K
Weber/R Weber), and passed with all ayes. Motion was made to approve the
January 27 minutes, as amended (R Weber/K Weber) with 4 ayes and 1 abstention
by Mrs. Henson. Motion was made to approved the February 2nd minutes without
amendment (K Weber/Holten), passing with 3 ayes, and 2 abstentions. Mrs. Weber
and Mrs. Henson abstained due to being absent from that special meeting.
NEW BUSINESS
Mrs. Pegg - Easter Egg Hunt/Independence Lions Club
1-Mrs. Leann Pegg addressed council regarding funding requested for the Easter
Egg Hunt planned for April 4th at Kenton Elementary. She said the Easter Bunny
would be there, that there would be pictures taken with the bunny, for a fee,
and that each child would hopefully receive a gift (her letter of intent is
attached). Discussion ensued as to cost of film, and keeping advertisement of
the event within the city. A vote was called (Henson/Steffen) to approve $600
for Easter Egg Hunt expenditures. Money would come from the line item in the
Recreation budget for events. Vote was all ayes, motion passed, and the Mayor
thanked Mrs. Pegg. (The fee to be charged, if any, was up to the City).
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
2- The Mayor asked that anyone wishing to address council please sign in at the
table on the sheet provided. Mrs. Donna Yeager signed up as she wished to
speak.
3- Mrs. Yeager informed council of recent changes she had made to the budget
lines for the recreation budget. She and Mr. Gary Scott explained that with
less line items, more flexibility was built into how money could be spent
without having to re-address council for budget amendments. Mr. Scott spoke
about his proposal that future budgets be more streamlined, still allowing the
control council needs. Mrs. Henson asked if a monthly report could be provided
3 Cont. - regarding activity, and Mrs. Yeager said this could be done.
Currently a monthly report would not be necessary but would with increased
activity in the spring.
4- It was decided that these changes would be incorporated into the amended
budget figures and presented to council later so all changes could be made in
one amendment. Mrs. Yeager could go ahead and solicit bids since hopefully the
budget amendment would precede her March 16 date for bids to be back.
Privileges of the floor ended as no other person wished to speak.
OLD BUSINESS
City Attorney
5- Mrs. Weber spoke of the February 9th special council meeting where no
agreement could be reached regarding city counsel. She had a proposed ordinance
she wished everyone to consider, and re-capped the events of the February 9th
meeting saying the Mayor would not look for a third party attorney. Mrs. Weber
stated that Lawson Walker, current attorney for Villa Hills, had agreed to act
for the City of Independence (see ordinance copy attached).
6- Motion was made to read the Ordinance (Holten/Henson). Mrs. Weber read the
ordinance. Motion was made to accept the reading (R Weber/Henson). Before the
vote, Mr. Holten asked the Mayor if he could live with this decision. The Mayor
responded he was bothered because a compromise could have been reached through
further negotiation, and that the suit is not resolved by this action. Also, he
was bothered by the comment that Mr. Wichmann would be in violation or conflict
due to the ouster suit, since he had planned to release Mr. Wichmann from that
suit if hired by the City. The Mayor wished to proceed with negotiations.
7- Mr. Holten questioned if the Mayor was concerned about the interim, and
while the Mayor allowed that he was, he still wished to make more effort before
closing this situation.
8- Mrs. Henson asked to re-cap the events of February 9th saying litigation was
pending, and due to irreconcilable differences, including the ouster suit, no
decision was reached on a city attorney. She commented about research she had
done and that the she was not willing to pay city money for back services of
Mr. Wichmann amounting to approximately $ 25,000, since the services were
primarily to the Mayor. She explained that council could not direct the Mayor
to act, since council’s authority extended only to matters of budget and
legislation. If the Mayor chooses not to do what council requests, council
cannot act on this. She asked that a vote be called on the motion.
9- The Mayor commented that we had had 2 meetings on this already, and that
there had been problems, but he commented that Judge Summe’s ruling said
neither attorney should be paid, and there were no guarantees what the court
might decide. The Mayor asked that this be worked out.
10- Mrs. Henson commented she would like cable coverage for future special
meetings since Mr. Wichmann and the Mayor had both stated on February 9 that
they would not compromise on certain issues. The Mayor said cable could
certainly be invited, and continued to ask for adult negotiation and
compromise.
11- Mrs. Weber commented that the ordinance now before council would allow for
a temporary solution so the City could function again. If the Mayor did not
wish this to occur, she would like to hear from him.
12- Mr. Scott spoke about a proposal, discussed at the City Building, which
would allow for Mr. Deters and Mr. Wichmann to iron out their claims to
reimbursement and present their compromise to council within a few weeks. He
asked that the emergency ordinance be held until it was determined this
alternate plan could not work.
13- Comments were made about the immediate need for attorney services, and it
was decided a vote would be taken on this issue. Roll call vote had 4 ayes, a 1
abstention by Mrs. Steffen. Motion passed, 1st reading was accepted.
14- Discussion ensued about the appropriateness of doing a second reading, even
though this was an emergency ordinance. Motion was made to do a 2nd reading (R
Weber/K Weber) with all ayes. The Ordinance, 1998-0-01, was re-read by Mrs.
Weber. Motion was made to accept the 2nd reading (Henson/K Weber), passing with
all aye votes. The document was given to the City Clerk for inclusion in their
next packet and for presentation later to the Mayor. Mrs. Henson thanked the
Weber’s for their assistance.
AMENDED BUDGET
15- Mr. Scott requested this be discussed at the next meeting when revised
documents would be available.
SEWERING HOMES ON MADISON
16- There was nothing new to report regarding this situation, so it will come
back as Old Business.
CITY CLASS STATUS
17- Mr. Scott updated council regarding 3rd and 4th class city status. He still
has not received formal information to present to council, but will address
this soon.
PERSONNEL COMMITTEE
18- Mrs. Henson commented that due to other pressing city concerns, neither the
Personnel nor the Parking Committee had met. She hoped to have meetings within
the next 2 weeks. Mrs. Henson felt not having interim counsel for the city had
an impact on the above-stated pressing city concerns.
PLANNING SESSION
19- The Mayor asked council if they wished to wait on this until we had an
attorney. It was decided, after some discussion, that a meeting be called to
deal with the outstanding issue of Mr. Deters and Mr. Wichmann. No date could
be set at the meeting, but the Mayor said he would contact council members and
others himself to see how many could attend a meeting held on February 17th.
POLICE DEPT. REPORT
20- Chief Porter said there would be a Block Watch Meeting on Saturday,

subdivision residents. On Friday, February 20th, 2 officers, Gill and Paul,
will graduate. Past services were normally at 10:00 a.m., but the Chief will
provide information on the time to council.
BUILDING INSPECTOR REPORT
21- Mr. Bowling said he had several concerns to bring to council. He began with
a request for a refund of sewer tap fee for a resident at Richardson/Turkeyfoot
Roads. The refund was requested because the owner opted to tie into the
Sanitation District line over the City line since it was less expensive to
complete and easier to tie into. Mr. Bowling provided a sketch to council to
review.
22- The Mayor said he had a problem with setting a precedent in allowing people
to tie into the Sanitation District when City lines are available. Discussion
ensued as to the “flow” of this line, with Mr. Briggs being asked to do a grade
shoot to help determine if there was a hardship to the resident/developer. Mr.
Briggs agreed with the Mayor and Mr. Scott regarding setting an unfortunate
precedent, and that verification would be needed that there was a problem in
tapping in to the City line.
23- Mr. Bowling was concerned about the Independence Town Center area. There
are 3 zones in that area, some requiring underground utilities and some not.
There was discussion concerning brick wrap of buildings in this area, and
Mr.Bowling asked for direction on how to proceed with the developers.
24- Mr. Holten and others spoke about the intent of the wording in the
ordinance in that it was to encompass the entire city. (ordinance referred to
has been copied and sent to council: 1996-0-21) Mr. Steve Feldhaus commented
that the ordinance was set for residential, not commercial property.
25- The Mayor commented about the original ordinance in 1994 under which
conditions were set for the entire zone. Later, in 1996, an underground utility
ordinance may have amended this. Mr. Bowling said he would have an engineer at
the next meeting, and that he had already faxed and called the developer to
make them aware of his concerns.
26- Mr. Bowling and Mr. Bruce Wong, of NKAP, had inspected the Cherokee Auto
Parts site, and recently revisited it. Mr. Bowling commented there had been 80%
removal of cars, and more removal will follow.
27- The Mayor asked if any progress had been made in dealing with Mr. Goodman,
of Wayman Drive. No action seems to have been taken by Mr. Goodman to comply,
and both Mr. Wong and Mr. Bowling said the matter probably needed to be taken
to court. Mr. Scott spoke about the Board for Code Enforcement he was working
on, and how this could be handled in future.
28- Mr. Holten said this Board was a do-able project and steps should be taken
to get it moving. He commented it could be one of the first works of Lawson
Walker to look into this project. Mrs. Henson concurred the Board is a good
idea, and she had brought back information from a KLC convention regarding it.
Mr. Scott explained that Ethics Board members could be used for this, by
expanding their scope, so new personnel would not have to be looked for.
29- Mrs. Henson asked if non-residents could be citation officers, and Mr.
Scott says he believes so, but will check, but it would seem sensible they be
outside the city.
30- Mr. Bowling returned to the topic of the Independence Town Center and said
he would notify the engineer that underground utilities applied to all the
zones, and told council to be prepared for developers to attend the next

issued, but Mr. Bowling said he would wish to speak with Lawson Walker before
doing something of that nature. Discussion ended with notification to
developers being a better option as a first step than a stop-order.
31. Mr. Wong provided a written and oral update on zoning services, with
information on how busy the city had been in this regard. He talked about

32. Mr. Briggs has been updating Mr. Scott weekly at staff meetings. He brought

CITY ADMINISTRATOR
33- Mr. Scott said the Personnel Committee issue had already been addressed, so

ADJOURNMENT

February 17, 1998
City of Independence
Special Council Meeting
Minutes
Mayor Gabbard called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the Courthouse. He
explained the purpose of the meeting was to discuss and take possible action on
Legal Services Contracts, and the Kenton Circuit Court Action # 97-CI-00594.
No other topics would be up for discussion.
Roll call was answered by all 6 council members.
The Mayor began by saying he had a proposal to place before council. No one was
present representing the Deters firm, nor was Mr. Wichmann present. The Mayor
explained his position as follows:
   - hire Mr. Frank Wichmann through December 31, 1998, and set a reasonable
fee for this service
   - any conflict of interest seen by council in Mr. Wichmann’s representation
of the Mayor in the ouster suit would be nullified by Mr. Wichmann being
released from that role and the Mayor hiring another attorney.
   - Council had appeared unwilling to pay Mr. Wichmann for his past services,
and the Mayor agreed to pay him $ 0.00 for the past 10 months.
   - the Mayor expressed a willingness to pay Mr. Charles Deters for past
services, but only to a point of $ 28,800, which was a compromise from the $
38,000 figure proposed originally by Mr. Deters.
The Mayor asked for comment on his proposal. Comment included concerns over
hiring Mr. Wichmann beyond the end of this fiscal year; concerns over the Mayor
being so adamant about hiring Mr. Wichmann, and Mr. Wichmann being busy working
for other cities.
After some discussion, it was decided that the Mayor should put his proposal in
writing, present it to both attorneys in question, and give them a “reasonable
time frame” in which to respond. The Mayor agreed to provide this information
by fax on Wednesday, February 18.
Question arose as to the other issue of concern, what would be done in the
interim while this is being negotiated? Council referred to the emergency
ordinance of February 10, hiring Lawson Walker on a month-to-month basis, and
asked the Mayor about his plans regarding this. The Mayor said he had not
decided yet how to proceed with the ordinance, since he had been working on a
compromise on the other issue. He said he would review the ordinance, but if he
could not sign it he would like to propose a week- to-week arrangement,
possibly hiring Mr. Wichmann.
Discussion continued about the two separate issues regarding legal counsel: the
need for an interim attorney to handle daily city needs, and the long-term
question of settling the Deters/Wichmann issue.
Motion was made to adjourn the meeting (K Weber/S Holten), with all ayes. The
meeting was officially adjourned at about 7:40 p.m.

                  Isaac Gabbard, Mayor

February 24, 1998
City of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
CALL TO ORDER
The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard at approximately 7:05 p.m., at
the courthouse, with Pledge of Allegiance and an invocation by Reverend Greg
Fightmaster of the Beechgrove Baptist Church.
ROLL CALL OF MEMBERS
All 6 council members were present and answered at roll call.
WELCOME
The Mayor welcomed those in attendance, and introduced Officers Gill and Paul
who are recent graduates from police training at Eastern Kentucky University.
The Mayor also asked that anyone planning to speak should sign in on the sheet
provided, and no other person would be allowed to speak if not signed up. Mr.
Charles Deters was the only person requesting to speak.
CITY ATTORNEY
1- Approval of the Minutes was delayed due to a motion (Holten/Henson) to
discuss the Mayor’s veto of the Ordinance 1998-0-01 hiring Lawson Walker as
interim attorney for the city. Motion passed with all ayes.
2- The Mayor opened the floor to Mr. Holten who asked where the City went from
here, due to the veto. The Mayor responded he had made proposals that had gone
unanswered, and that while he had spoken to Mr. Deters re his proposal, Mr.
Deters had not responded in writing with his counterproposal.
3- Discussion ensued as to why the Mayor refused to hire Mr. Walker as interim
attorney, with Mrs. Henson reading aloud the Mayor’s letter regarding why he
vetoed Ordinance 1998-0-01. Comments were made about over-riding the veto, but
the Mayor cautioned that both sides needed to agree for the ordinance to be
valid.
4- Mr. Holten commented he felt the city would be in jeopardy if it remains
unrepresented by legal counsel, and that business could not be conducted.
5- Comment moved to there being two issues to be settled: one being the interim
counsel and the other being the settling of the pending suit involving Judge
Summe’s ruling. The Mayor asked for council to provide something in the way of
innovative counter-proposals. Meanwhile, Mr. Deters had written up his counter-
proposal and handed it to the Mayor.
6- Mrs. Henson commented we were very close to settling and asked the Mayor to
reconsider his veto. Mrs. Weber asked the attorneys in question for their
input. The Mayor read aloud the proposal written by Mr. Deters and explained
Mr. Wichmann’s proposal. Mr. Wichmann stated that council needed to know he had
conceded on most issues, and had nothing left to concede. When asked if he had
yet removed himself from the ouster suit, Mr. Wichmann replied he had not, but
has been searching for someone to take this over. He assured Mrs. Henson and
all of council that the time frame for this transition would be minimal.
7- Vote was called to over-ride the Mayor’s veto of Ordinance 1998-0-01 (R
Weber/Henson) with 4 aye votes, and 2 no votes (Gabbard/Steffen). Motion needed
a 5 vote majority to pass, so it failed with only 4 aye votes. Veto was not
over-ridden.
8- Mr. Weber asked Mrs. Steffen to explain why her vote was so cast, and the
Mayor intervened saying no explanation was required.
9- Discussion ensued about Judge Summe’s decision and the Mayor’s
interpretation of it, with Mrs. Weber commenting that the Mayor is holding this
office illegally.
10- Mr. Deters spoke about his proposal to the Mayor, and requested payment of
$ 35000 (down from the original figure) since he had performed all the duties
asked of him by the city. The Mayor responded that Judge Summe’s ruling stated
the city owed no money to Mr. Deters from March 10, 1997, and that he could
wait to see what the court decided if Mr. Deters would not accept a compromise.
He commented that this could be resolved in one evening, hopefully this
evening.
11- The Mayor talked about council possibly appropriating money to pay Mr.
Wichmann but that he would not agree to hiring a new attorney until this was
settled. Discussion ensued as to paying Mr. Deters $ 35,000 as requested if he
would withdraw from the law suit, and a motion was made to this effect (Henson/
R Weber). Motion was later withdrawn.
12- The Mayor stated he would be unwilling to agree to this since it includes
no provision for Mr. Wichmann. Discussion ensued as to hiring Mr. Wichmann
through the remainder of the fiscal year, with Mr. Wichmann saying he wanted a
contract that went through December 31, 1998. The Mayor commented that city
staff had worked well with Mr. Wichmann and council could question department
heads about their work relationship with Mr. Wichmann and/or what he had
handled for them. No one on council had any questions for department heads who
were present.
13- Comments were made about lowering the attorney fees in the 1998-99 fiscal
year to bring them more in line with other cities, and since the work involved
has changed. Mrs. Henson said the Mayor had shot down 4 proposals, but he
responded that it was a large compromise to consider paying Mr. Deters $
35,000.
14- Mr. Holten commented he was disgusted with the Mayor’s pettiness and
bickering. Mrs. Gabbard commented that Mr. Holten had been an embarrassment to
the council for a long time. Motion was made to recess (R Weber/K Weber). Roll
call vote had 4 no’s and 2 ayes, so the motion failed. No recess was taken.
15- Mrs. Henson questioned the City Clerk about pending legal concerns or
litigation that required legal counsel. Mrs. Henson wanted to show that the
lack of legal counsel had put the city in a position of jeopardy. The clerk
responded that there were some law suits pending, and some other legal issues
needing attention at this time. The Mayor commented that some of these legal
concerns could be handled by the insurance company involved.
16- Mrs. Steffen asked if the city could pay Mr. Deters $33,000 and hire Mr.
Wichmann through the end of July or August. Mr. Deters said this would be okay,
while Mr. Wichmann said he had given up money for previous services and felt he
should get $ 4000 per month compensation. Mrs. Weber suggested an offer of
$5000 for Mr. Wichmann to walk away now. Mr. Wichmann, in response to a
question from Mrs. Henson, stated he was here to make money. This was clarified
as certainly being a provider of a service for a fee, and there being nothing
wrong in that. Mr. Wichmann maintained he, too, thought he had a valid contract
with the city, and that he had provided services to city staff and at least 2
council members. He claimed his position was identical to that of Mr. Deters.
17- Comments were made by several council members about not being able to trust
Mr. Wichmann’s due to his relationship with the Mayor. Motion was made to pay
Mr. Deters $ 35,000 to withdraw from the law suit and to hire Mr. Wichmann
through December 31 at $ 2000 per month, with no hourly fees (Henson/Steffen).
18- Discussion followed regarding retainer fees and litigation compensation as
an additional cost. Mr. Wichmann was questioned as to retainer fees paid to him
by Taylor Mill. Vote was called with 4 members voting yes to the contract (Mrs.
Gabbard’s “yes” being contingent upon Mr. Wichmann being agreeable to the
contract), and 2 no votes (K Weber/Holten). Motion passed.
19- The Mayor asked for a recess of 10 minutes. Motion was made (Henson/
Gabbard) and was tied at 3 yes/3 no votes.(Weber/Weber/Holten) The Mayor broke
the tie, and recess was taken.
20- Motion was made (Henson/Holten) to return to session, with all ayes.
21- The Mayor commented on his talk with Mr. Wichmann during the recess. He
needed information on where the city stood on litigation, since this
information had not been provided to him by Mr. Deters upon request. Mr. Deters
responded that when he has been paid, the information will be provided or
returned to the city. The Mayor asked that information regarding pending
litigation be provided in writing before Mr. Wichmann has to decide to accept.
Mr. Wichmann and Mr. Deters conferred briefly.
22- Mr. Deters said there was really no pending litigation beyond foreclosures.
The Mayor argued that there is a suit pending (Baker) and then Mr. Deters
commented on one filed previously (Hoppenjans/Maines). Mr. Deters clarified
that everything else was basically cleared up: consolidation of County,
easements, etc. He said he knew of no other current suits.
23- The Mayor commented on bond work, if needed, being done by someone other
than Mr. Wichmann, and that money would need to be set aside for this
specialist. Mrs. Weber commented this would be acceptable, if Mr. Gary Scott is
a part of this.
24- Discussion ensued when the Mayor asked council to say on the record that
they were not opposed to getting another attorney for bond work, and several
council members refused to do this. Motion was made to adjourn (Holten/Henson).
Vote to adjourn was 2 ayes, 4 no votes, (Gabbard/Steffen/Weber/Weber) and
therefore failed. Mrs. Weber asked to hear from Mr. Whitacre since he was here
to provide a report.
25- Mrs. Henson asked Mr. Wichmann if he was satisfied with the information
provided by Mr. Deters on current litigation. Mr. Wichmann said he was, and
would seriously consider accepting if the monthly fee could be increased to $
2200 through December 31. The Mayor commented on being close to a decision.
26- Discussion took a turn into budgetary needs when Mr. Scott commented that
due to inability to pass an amended budget, Mr. Bowling, Building Inspector,
had been temporarily laid off.. He explained about the line item for Mr.
Bowling’s salary being overspent even though a corresponding line for income
generated by Mr. Bowling was there to offset expenses. Mr. Scott commented on
the nature of the line item budget requiring this sort of amendment as opposed
to a more flexible, departmental budget.
27- Comments were made about lack of trust being a reason for the line item
budget. Council had concerns about allowing this freedom to the current Mayor.
Discussion moved back to the issue of the vote on hiring Mr. Wichmann at $ 2200
per month. Motion was made (Henson/Gabbard) to hire Mr. Wichmann through
December 31, 1998 at a monthly fee of $ 2200, with no additional fees to be
paid.
28- Discussion followed about this being put in written form, and vote was
called. Roll call vote was a 3-3 tie, with the Mayor voting yes to break the
tie. Motion passed. Mrs. Henson asked Mr. Wichmann to draw up a contract by
Monday, March 2, and that it would be understood he was not working for the
city until he had a signed contract.
29- Mrs. Henson motioned to adjourn at this point, but the motion died for lack
of a second.
30- Mr. Dave Whitacre, Cardinal Engineering, reported to council on sewer
issues, storm water regulations which will ultimately effect the city, and
other cities’ plans to deal with this. He spoke about flow monitoring going on,
and now occurring in the Beechgrove area. Monitoring showed 4 in-flow problems
at previous sites.
31- Mr. Whitacre commented on concerns regarding new subdivisions abuse of flag
lots, and that in some cases these hinder emergency vehicles. He informed
council they may need to create an ordinance to deal with this concern, and
outlined some options for how to minimize problems.
32- A question/answer period followed regarding sewer work remaining, and
payments for sewer work. Talk continued about the possible need in future to
bond for sewer funding. The Mayor suggested any bonding might be for a new City
Building, The Mayor commented that the city only owes on Fowler Creek, and that
there would probably be a need to bond on this in the coming years.
33- Questions followed about people not being hooked up to the sewer system,
and the City process for following through with these residents. Mr. Holten
commented that the City has an ordinance regarding fines for not hooking up to
the sewer system. He warned that residents needed to comply or face penalties
for not doing so, Also, questions were raised as to street repairs and the
bidding process for street repair work. Comment was made by Mr. Whitacre about
upcoming major repair of Holton Drive., and concerns regarding a traffic light
there.
34- Motion was made to adjourn the meeting (Holten/K Weber), and passed with
all ayes. Meeting was officially adjourned.

March 9, 1998
City of Independence
Special Council Meeting
The meeting was called to order by the Mayor at approximately 7:10 p.m. He
explained the purpose of the meeting was to discuss settlement of the legal
counsel issue, and that no other business would be discussed.
Roll Call was answered by all council members except Mrs. Weber, who arrived at
about 7:35 p.m.
1- The Mayor opened the floor for discussion or to hear a motion to approve
Municipal Order 1998-MO-01 hiring Mr. Wichmann as City Attorney. Mrs. Henson
had some questions which she addressed to Mr. Wichmann, including why the dates
and other particulars of an employee contract were not included in the
documents presented tonight. Mr. Wichmann explained he was contracting with the
city vs. being hired as an employee, and that much of what Mrs. Henson
requested was included in the documents.
2- Mr. Weber said there was no allowance for a dismissal or clause to remove
Mr. Wichmann. After some discussion on these issues, the Mayor asked if a
separate contract could be provided to council later in the week. Mr. Wichmann
told Mrs. Henson he could have it by the March 10th regular council meeting.
Regarding the “clause for dismissal” issue, Mr. Wichmann assured council that
if he failed to do his job properly, he could be discharged for breach of
contract at any time if the Mayor and council agreed to this.
3- Mrs. Henson commented on specific phrasing of the document, in particular
the page regarding Mr. Deters’ release of claims, wherein it was stated
“doubtful, disputed and denied by the persons hereby released”.
4- Discussion began about the payment term for Mr. Wichmann and concerns that
Mr. Bridges, who would take over for Mr. Wichmann in the lawsuit involving
Mayor Gabbard., might make a motion which would delay the suit coming to an
end. Mr. Wichmann stated that a continuance would probably not be granted to
Mr. Bridges, assuming he did ask for one. Mrs. Henson was reluctant to approve
the Municipal Order until she had a guarantee.
5- The Mayor suggested a 5 minute recess might be helpful, and motion was made
to do so (Gabbard/Holten). Vote was a 3-3 tie, with the Mayor breaking the tie
by voting for the recess.
6- Motion was made to return to session (Holten/Henson) with all ayes.
7- The Mayor said that after some discussion during the recess, it seemed
possible to agree that any action of Mr. Bridges should be limited to a
voluntary action as opposed to a possible health issue which could cause a
delay in changeover. This was agreed to after minimal discussion.
8- Mrs. Henson returned to the phrasing issue. It was decided to add wording
saying that Mrs. Henson, Mr. and Mrs. Weber and Mr. Holten take exception to
this because they agree Mr. Deters has/had a valid claim. Mr. Deters provided
changed wording to the Clerk for inclusion in the document.
9- Motion was made to approve Municipal Order 1998-MO-01 (Holten/Henson), with
4 ayes and 2 no votes (B. Weber/K. Weber), and comments by Mrs. Henson and Mr.
Holten that their aye votes were for the document with the appropriate changes
made to it.
10- It was agreed that corrected copies of the documents would go to all
council members as soon as possible. After a brief discussion, it was decided
that signing the documents could follow after adjournment of the meeting and
did not have to take place during the meeting. Due to this, a motion was made
to adjourn (Holten/Henson) with all ayes.
The meeting was officially adjourned.
Notation: Documents were duly signed as required, and Mr. Deters was paid via
check the amount stated in the settlement agreement. This took place
immediately after the meeting was adjourned.

March 24, 1998
City of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard, followed by the Pledge of
Allegiance. Roll call was answered by all council members.
1- The Mayor welcomed everyone present to the meeting and asked if anyone who
planned to speak would please sign in. Only representatives from Bristow
Meadows Stage II development (Kiser/Leesman) signed.
2- Modifications were made to the existing agenda: addition of Project Prom and
Behringer Crawford Museum requests for funds were added to New Business. The
Resolution for TKR/Intermedia, Sewering of 4-5 Homes on Madison, and Planning
Session were added to Old Business, with Bristow Meadows being moved to the end
of the agenda. The Mayor also advised council he would ask for an Executive
Session.
3-Motion was made to approve the minutes of the March 9th meeting (KWeber/
Henson). This was approved with all ayes. Motion was made to approve the
minutes of the March 10th meeting, as amended (RWeber/Holten). Mr. Weber had
asked for a comment to be added to item # 12.
4- Bids for Park Maintenance Work - Gary Scott said he had spoken with Donna
Yeager regarding deferring this item until the April 14th meeting, since there
was no critical need for immediate action. Council agreed, and this was
postponed.
5- Behringer Crawford Museum - Mrs. Henson commented on information in the
council packet regarding a request for a donation. Discussion followed as to
spending the money outside the city and on a service funded by county tax
dollars. Motion was made (Henson/Steffen) to approve $ 500 be donated to
Behringer Crawford Museum. Roll call vote was 3-3, with the Mayor choosing to
“pass” and not break the tie. (“No” votes: B Weber, K Weber, S Holten). Motion
was made to contribute $ 100 to this purpose ( R Weber/Steffen) with 5-1 vote
to pass (no vote: Holten). Motion passed.
6- Project Prom/Simon Kenton -Mrs. Weber spoke to council about the “lock-in”
activity at Simon Kenton on prom night, open to students and their guests. This
event helps to provide students with a safe, drug/alcohol free environment to
party after prom.
Mrs. Henson said she could not participate in discussion on this issue as she
felt it was a conflict of interest. Mrs. Weber asked Mr. Wichmann if he felt
her own discussion of this was a conflict since she works at Simon Kenton, but
Mr. Wichmann said it would not be. Mrs. Weber offered to remove herself from
this issue if council saw it as a conflict.
Chief Porter commented on the safety aspect of this event, with the Mayor
agreeing. Motion was made to allocate $ 600 to Project Prom (RWeber/Gabbard).
Vote was 5 yes votes, with Mrs. Henson abstaining. Motion passed.
7- Privileges of the Floor - Since no one had signed in to speak during this
session, council moved on to Old Business items.
8- Personnel Committee - Gary Scott sent a letter out last week looking for
dates for the committee to meet. It seemed impossible to get all members
together, so a meeting might be set which could include the largest number of
members.
9- Parking Ordinance Committee - Mrs. Henson said this group met March 23rd and
have a proposal (given to council at this meeting) which she asked council
members and other parties review. She asked for feedback by April 1.
10- House Bill 509- A copy of the bill had been provided to council via
packets. Council members Steffen and Henson commented on concerns they had
about this bill (which makes fleeing an officer a felony instead of a
misdemeanor). Chief Porter said the language in HB 509 did make the current law
more “defensible”, but he commented that council should “vote their conscience”
on this. Motion was made to accept a resolution supporting House Bill 509
(Henson/R Weber). Vote was 1 yes - 5 no votes (no votes: Weber/Weber/Holten/
Gabbard/Steffen). Motion failed.
11- Sewers for 4-5 Homes on Madison - The Mayor commented that he had several
calls from residents concerning this issue. Cardinal Engineering had provided
information at previous meetings which determined costs to be $ 30,000-$38,000
for this work. It was determined that property owners in question were aware
there would be an assessment for the sewer service, and that easements were not
a problem except for the property of Mrs. Williams, whose family would need to
be contacted since she is in a nursing home. Discussion ensued about how to pay
for this project, and other “pockets” of un-sewered homes within the city. It
was decided that there were too many difficulties involved to combine projects.
Comments followed about the need for easements “up front” before projects begin
and Mrs. Weber asked if the homeowners in question on Madison could tell what
they would be willing to pay to get this service. Motion was made (Holten/
RWeber) to authorize the Mayor to investigate costs for sewering the 5
properties on Madison in question. Vote was unanimous ayes: motion passed.
12- Planning Session - The Mayor asked which of the two dates given to council
would be best for holding the planning session. After some discussion, it was
settled that the planning session would be held May 29 (6-10 p.m.)and 30 (9-
5 p.m.). Mr. Scott and Mrs. Baker will work on location, food, etc. and report
back to council.
13- TKR/Intermedia Resolution - Motion was made to approve the initial
resolution regarding TKR/Intermedia (Henson/Holten). This will be Resolution
1998-R-03. Vote passed with all ayes. Motion was made to rescind the 1998-0-02
Resolution regarding TKR/Intermedia (Henson/R Weber). This passed with all
ayes.
14- Police Department Report - Chief Porter told council that Lt. Shawn Butler
had recently applied for and been accepted by the Criminal Justice Executive
Development Force for 8 weeks of training over a 2 year period. Only 20
officers in the state will attend, so this is an honor for the City and for Lt.
Butler to be accepted. This training is held in Richmond, Kentucky.
15- Engineer’s Report - Dave Whitacre of Cardinal Engineering reported to
council on:
   - flow monitors in Hunter’s Green area
   - Holten Drive estimates which will be coming to council soon
   - potholes on Carrie Way being addressed
   - a walk-through set for Plantation Heights, with comment that the Michels
contract needs follow-up in regard to paying retainange money
   - air tests and subdivision inspections are on-going
16- Questions followed about bids for street repair, with Mr. Whitacre saying
these would be needed by April 10th, 1998.
17- City Administrator’s Report - Mr. Scott said he and Chief Porter had
recently attended a meeting regarding Code Enforcement Boards. This concept is
in use in other cities, and is supported by our Building Inspector, Mr.
Bowling. Mr. Scott provided information to council and asked them to review it.
Mr. Holten asked about the Budget Training session Mr. Scott attended, and was
told that 4 people from the city had gone to this, and we had some ideas about
revenue sources and other ideas which we would share with council.
18- Mayor’s Report - The Mayor commented his report was handed out this
evening, and he suggested that a motion be made to go into Executive Session to
discuss possible litigation against the City. Motion was made to go into
Executive Session (KWeber/RWeber), and passed with all ayes.
19- Motion was made to return to regular session (Holten/Henson) with all ayes.
Mr. Leesman and Mr. Kiser addressed council regarding Bristow Meadows/Stage II.
After some discussion and amendments to the proposed ordinance regarding this
project, motion was made (Henson/KWeber) to do the 1st reading of the
ordinance, with all ayes.
Mr. Wichmann read the ordinance, as amended this evening by council, and a
motion followed to accept the 1st reading (Holten/KWeber) with all ayes.
20- Motion was made to adjourn the meeting (Holten/Henson) with all ayes.
