April 14, 1998
City of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
1- The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard at 6:05 p.m., followed by
the Pledge of Allegiance and an invocation by Fr. Berscheide, St. Cecilia
Church.  Roll Call was taken, with four council members in attendance and 2
absent (Mrs. Henson, Mrs. Steffen). The Mayor commented on it having been 3
weeks since the last council meeting, and that Mr. Leesman and Mr. Kaiser be
moved up on the agenda to speak to council.
2- Prior to hearing about Bristow Meadows, a motion was made and seconded to
accept the minutes from the March 24th meeting (Holten/Gabbard). This passed
with all ayes.
3- Bristow Meadows - An update was provided to council on work done at this
site. A motion was made to go ahead with the 2nd reading of the ordinance
regarding Bristow Meadows (1998-0-03) (K Weber/Holten). This motion was
followed by all aye votes. However, prior to reading the ordinance for the 2nd
time, Mr. Bowling stated the builders needed a letter from the city for the
Planning Commission stating the city would allow building at less than the 150’
distance from the road. Discussion followed, with Mr. Wichmann, City Attorney,
asking that he be allowed to meet with Mr. Leesman to discuss this, as he was
confused on this issue. It was agreed this item would be returned to once the
discussion was completed satisfactorily.
4- Park Maintenance Bids - Mr. Gary Scott spoke to council regarding bids
received for work on park and city property mowing, etc. Rowe Group had the
lowest bid, and Mr. Scott had checked out their references. He suggested
council go with the Rowe Group for the work, commenting though on past, quality
work done by Malco. The Mayor also commented on Malco’s past work, its good
quality and Barry Mallott’s willingness to help out. He suggested the city
continue to use Malco, even if the bid were higher. Mrs. Donna Yeager of the
Independence Park Committee commented she liked Malco and appreciated how work
was sometimes “volunteer” rather than charged for. After some discussion,
motion was made (Holten/RWeber) to accept Rowe Group’s bid for the park work.
Roll call vote had 3 ayes and1 no vote (Gabbard). Mrs. Gabbard commented on the
dependability of Malco in the past and that she was pleased with their work.
Motion passed.
5- Mr. Scott brought up a second set of bids, these received on April 6th,
regarding paving and other work at Shaw Park. The lowest bidder was Michels &
Son, with next lowest being from Westside. Mr. Scott asked if council felt they
could vote to award this contract now. Motion was made (Holten/RWeber) to award
this work to Michels and Son. Roll call vote was all ayes, motion passed.
6- Bristow Meadows - Mr. Wichmann returned to this issue after discussion with
Mr. Leesman. He stated that the decision at this point lies with Mr. Bowling,
Zoning Administrator, and not council. The original plan presented for review
was revised to move the intersection farther from Bristow Road, and the builder
made this change, with Planning approving it. For Planning to have concerns
about language regarding the intersection at this date was a moot point, since
Mr. Bowling could approve or disapprove. Mr. Wichmann said he felt council
could proceed with a 2nd reading on the ordinance regarding Bristow Meadows.
7- Questions were raised about whether the current language of the ordinance
addressed prior concerns regarding street lights and signs (fire lane/no
parking). Mr. Wichmann said the fire lane/parking issue was not currently in
the language, but could be added. However, parking is dealt with in the
ordinance (Section B-Page 2), and he spoke about the Fire Department’s ability
to require signs for fire lanes. Mr. Wichmann added language to the ordinance
document to address concerns of Mr. Weber and Mr. Leesman. Motion was made
(Holten/KWeber) to do the 2nd reading of this ordinance. Roll call vote was
answered with 3 ayes and 1 no (R Weber), with Mr. Weber stating she had had
concerns about this development being too close to Bristow Road from the
beginning.
Motion passed,
8- Mr. Wichmann read Ordinance 1998-0-03 regarding Bristow Meadows for its 2nd
reading. Motion was made (Holten/K Weber) to accept the 2nd reading. Motion
passed with 3 ayes, 1 no (R Weber).
9- Health Insurance - Mr. Scott explained that the City had been faced with a
possible 45% increase in costs for health insurance if we kept with the current
plan. After some shopping around, the city has chosen a new plan which is
basically identical to the existing plan but requires each member to determine
a “primary care provider”. Mr. Scott said the new coverage would begin May
15th, 1998, with only an 11% increase in cost. Health care costs had no
increases for the past two years.
10- Sewers for Homes on Madison - Mayor Gabbard commented that he and Gary
Scott had met with residents in the area between Carrie Way and the Christian
Church. There is currently one “bootleg” hookup with the resident paying a
sewer bill plus cost of tapping in. Mr. Holten asked the Mayor to check if the
resident was paying toward a sewer assessment (CBD - Central Business
District). The Mayor continued that only 2 homes no required sewers, and talk
ensued about prohibitive expenses. Mr. Dan Briggs, Cardinal Engineering, said
residents could purchase grinder pumps and run lines to the nearest manhole
with an expense (by plumber) of approximately $6500, with the resident paying
for any maintenance. The Mayor said the Christian Church had given these
residents permission to tap in to their manhole.
11- Concerns were raised about the grinders vs. tying in to the sewer line, as
well as procuring easements from residents (Miss Williams in particular). Mr.
Holten suggested the city put 2 options before the residents in question and
let them decide which option to take. The Mayor questioned why a plumber’s cost
could be $6500 when Cardinal’s estimates for work were double this amount. Mr.
Briggs commented on engineer fees, controlled fill costs and providing an 8”
line vs. a 4” line. It was decided that Mr.Briggs, Mr. Scott and others meet
regarding securing easements and getting work done. Mr. Holten asked it work
could be completed by summers’ end, but Mr. Briggs said this would depend on
the residents.
12- Mayor Gabbard asked about the 12 unit apartment building at Richardson. As
this is part of Mr. Bowling’s report, it will be addressed later in the
meeting.
13- Planning Session - Mr. Scott said he is working on this agenda. The Mayor
asked for input from council by next week. Dates are set for May 29th and 20th,
at Beechgrove Clubhouse. Times are 6-10 p.m. Friday, 9-5 p.m. Saturday. Agendas
will be forthcoming.
14- Personnel Committee Update - Mr. Scott said the committee met a few weeks
ago and made some headway. Four members were present for the meeting. Next
meeting date is set for April 20th with a June date for the “finished product”.
15- Mr. Holten asked about the Parking Ordinance. Mr. Wichmann said it was not
on this agenda since changes had been made to the ordinance language and he had
not had an opportunity to meet with Mrs. Henson to review them. This could be
an agenda item for the April 28th meeting.
16- Police Department - Chief Porter commented that Lt. Butler is currently in
Richmond for the first of his training events. Questions were addressed to
Chief Porter about recent vandalism (re a letter from a resident on Flintlock).
Chief Porter responded s to how the department had already responded and on
plans to deal with this in future. He said these were isolated events involving
the same people. The Mayor said he will be meeting or talking with residents on
Flintlock to address this issue.
17- Cardinal Engineering - Dan Briggs spoke about the Northern Kentucky
Land Development Commission hearing, and asked if Mr. Scott wanted him to
attend this. Mr. Scott said yes. Also, Mr. Briggs spoke about storm water
concerns at Production  Drive,  showing a map of 4 plats with no easements for
pipes. Work on storm sewers there would require easements or cost-sharing.
18- Mr. Weber asked about restoration of Plantation Heights, and voiced
concerns about the grass re-seeding. Mrs. Weber asked about a culvert placement
and ruts that are keeping one resident from mowing. Mr. Briggs said he would
look into these concerns.
19- Apartments Fronting on Richardson - This issue had been brought up earlier
and was now re-addressed. The concern is an on-going problem with a property
owner who wishes to hook into Sanitation Department lines vs. City lines to
save the cost of piping over 300’. Mr. Bowling provided a map of this area,
showing the possible routes of pipes. Concerns arose over allowing residents to
tie into Sanitation lines vs. City lines, and whether the resident could pay
Debt Reduction fees if tapped in to Sanitation’s lines. The Mayor stated that
if it is feasible to tie into a city line, residents should do so.
20- Mr. Holten said the question was whether the owner would be willing to
compensate the city if allowed to tie into Sanitation lines. Mr. Wichmann said
that to tap in to city lines required a building permit. After some discussion,
it was decided that Mr. Wichmann would look into city ordinances regarding
sewer lines and discuss his findings with the Mayor. Mr. Bowling stated this
was his only issue for his report.
21- Mr. Holten asked whether the city is waiting on mandates regarding Storm
Water Systems or proceeding on it. Mr. Wichmann spoke about changes in recent
legislation on Storm Water issues and that he has not received most recent
language changes. Discussion followed regarding obtaining this legislation
information. Also, there were concerns about whether the city will be mandated
on how to act. The Mayor spoke about information he and Mr. Scott gathered
down-state: that cities in the Sanitation District has no choice, but
Independence and Alexandria would have to “contract” with Sanitation for sewage
in order to get their assistance with storm drains. It was decided that this
issue needed to be on the agenda for the Planning Session, and that no
committee meeting should be held prior to obtaining legislative updates on this
issue.
22- Dan Briggs spoke about an effective date of March 1, 1999 with an 8 yr-
9 month period for compliance. Discussion followed about effective dates, EPA
rules and other concerns. It was decided that Mr. Wichmann research this issue
and get back to council as soon as possible (certainly prior to the Planning
Session dates of May 29-30).
23- City Administrator - Gary Scott said he had asked Mr. Wichmann to prepare
an ordinance document relating to the Code Enforcement Board. This was provided
to council this p.m. The Mayor asked if council wanted to review it now and do
a first reading. It was decided this was also a good item for the Planning
Session and that there were too many questions for a reading to take place at
this time. Mr. Scott asked that council contact him regarding questions or
concerns so these could be addressed prior to the Planning Session, or at least
known so they could be addressed at that time.
24- Mr. Wichmann commented that the model for this ordinance (from Bellevue and
Dayton) was considerably longer than his version since he did not wish to
repeat statutory language. He explained that if statutes were revised, such
language in ordinances could be a problem. Mr. Scott said original statutes
required 5 people on this panel, but now only 3 were required. Mr. Wichmann
said he preferred to have 5-7 people on this panel to provide for more
flexibility, but he did allow it would make the task more difficult to get that
many people to serve.
25- With business completed, motion was made to adjourn (K Weber/Holten),
followed by all ayes. Meeting was officially adjourned.

April 28, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
1.   Mayor Gabbard called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Roll call was answered by Council Members Rebecca Weber, Jaimie
Henson, Ken Weber, Anita Steffen and Barbara Gabbard. Council Member, Scott
Holten arrived at 7:09 p.m., after roll call was taken. Also in attendance was
the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Frank Wichmann.
2.   Ken Weber made a motion to approve the minutes of the April 14, 1998
Council Meeting as amended. Barbara Gabbard seconded the motion. Motion carried
with five ayes and one abstain vote cast by Mrs. Henson.
3.   Mayor Gabbard introduced Ms. C.G.Eubel as the new city employee hired as
the Finance Director. Council welcomed her; Mr. Holten stated that he was
looking forward to her advise.
4.   Jeff Klump, a representative of National Contructors appeared before
council to discuss the first floor brick wrap requirement for the apartments
(Brentwood of Independence & Townhomes at Lake Independence) being constructed
behind the Independence Towne Center. Mr. Klump stated that the first building
in the Brentwood development is nearly completed and hopes to have tenants
occupy the building by June 1, 1998. The first building has been vinyl sided on
the first floor. He stated that the drawing was approved by NKAPC and city
council. The contractors were not aware of the brick wrap requirement until a
couple of weeks ago when the city building inspector stopped by the development
and informed the superintendent of this building stipulation. In order to
comply with the brick wrap, the foundations would need to be re-designed at a
substantial cost to the developer. Mayor Gabbard informed Mr. Klump that the
property owner agreed to this requirement in 1994 when granted the zone change
to develop this land. Mrs. Gabbard stated that while she did not want to add to
their costs she feels that they should comply with the 1994 ordinance. Mrs.
Henson stated that while she does not agree with the brick wrap requirement the
ordinance is very clear, and that it is not the city’s fault that the
qualifying factors put on the zone change was overlooked by the developers. Mr.
Holten commented that the 1994 ordinance supercedes the building plans. Mr.
Weber asked Mr. Klump if a ledger attached to the foundation will have a
negative effect on the construction as opposed to a concrete footer. Mr. Klump
stated that it shouldn’t, but that he would have to consult with a structural
engineer. Mr. Klump commented that attaching a ledger would be the least
expensive route to take in order to comply with the brick wrap requirement.
Mrs. Weber told Mr. Klump that she felt the city could not make exceptions for
some builders/developers and not others.
5.   Mayor Gabbard asked Mr. Klump who was going to take the responsibility for
the 5-acre retention pond being built. Mr. Klump said he would need to ask the
developer.
6.   Scott Holten made a motion to recess into executive session for the
purpose of discussing possible litigation. The motion was seconded by Jaimie
Henson. The city attorney, Frank Wichmann, commented that he didn’t know if
this subject warranted an executive session. Mr. Holten strongly felt this
could be a possible lawsuit in the future. Motion carried with all ayes.
Executive session commenced at 7:30 p.m.
7.   At 7:44 p.m. Barbara Gabbard made a motion to return to regular session,
seconded by Rebecca Weber. Motion carried with all ayes.
8.   Mayor Gabbard stated that no action was taken in executive session. He
stated the consensus of council was that the brick wrap had to be added as
required by the zoning change ordinance for this property as was agreed to by
the owners. Mr. Klump stated that he would relay that information to the
parties involved and was unsure if the owner would consider this a dead issue
and comply or consult his attorney about further action. Mr. Klump asked for a
copy of the zoning ordinance which council talked about that was passed on that
development. Mr. Wichmann stated that the stipulations on that development were
not part of the regular zoning ordinance. He explained that when an application
is made for a zoning map amendment, it is required that a development plan be
submitted. At the time when the zone and/or annexation change is granted,
restrictions can be attached.
9.   Donna Yeager, Chairman of the Independence Recreation Committee, reported
that the city had received a $25,000 donation toward the construction of the
amphitheater in the Shaw Road Park. Ms. Yeager informed council that parking
lot construction bids had been received for both the Hartland Park and the Shaw
Road Park. The low bid for the Hartland parking lot exceeded the amount
budgeted for this project, so she requested council transfer approximately
$12,000 from the Shaw Park construction line item in the budget to the Hartland
Park construction line item. That would leave enough in the Shaw Park
construction line item to cover the low bid for the Shaw Park parking lot. Gary
Scott, City Administrator, explained that the construction cost for the
Hartland parking lot was underestimated.
10.   Mr. Weber made a motion to transfer money from Shaw Park construction to
Hartland Park construction as needed to accept the low bids. The motion was
seconded by Jaimie Henson. Mayor Gabbard stated that had to be done as part of
the amended budget. Ms. Yeager asked if council would vote on awarding the bid.
The Mayor stated that a second reading of the amended budget ordinance would
need to take place before awarding the bid. There was a brief discussion on
splitting the contract so the bid could be awarded and the contractor could
begin work. Mr. Wichmann stated that the contract could be awarded but that a
contract could not be signed until the funds were appropriated in the budget.
Mr. Weber withdrew his motion and Mrs. Henson withdrew her second.
11.   Jaimie Henson made a motion to accept the low bid ($48,748.00) by
Schumacher Dugan for construction of the Hartland Park parking lot and grading
for the play ground, contingent upon reference checks by the City
Administrator. Scott Holten seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with
all ayes. Motion carried.
12.   Under new business, Gary Scott informed council of the need to set new
sewer rates and maintenance charges for the General and Fowler Creek Sewer in-
house billing. Currently the Sanitation District is collecting these fees for
the city. The plan is to begin the billing in July. Ordinance No. 5-2-80 will
need to be amended before starting the new billing system as the ordinance now
states that the Sanitation District is to do the billing for the city.. One of
the penalties discussed for non-payment of sewer fees would be to have water
service turned off. Mrs. Wichmann advised that, by statute, the city has the
authority to do this but written notice would have to be sent to the Northern
Kentucky Water Service District. Currently penalty and interest is based on
water usage. Mr. Wichmann stated that the ordinance in effect now provides for
a 10% penalty of the amount due. Mr. Wichmann advised that the rate and fees
charged should be a sufficient amount to pay off the Fowler Creek Sewer bond
when it comes due. Mrs. Henson asked the city engineer to come up with some
city wide numbers to aide council in setting a rate. Scott Holten suggested
moving along with the agenda as the rate would not be set until more
information is obtained.
13.   Mayor Gabbard informed council that Craig Kolb’s second development plan
for the corner of Taylor Mill Rd. and Cox Rd. has been rejected by NKAP&Z. The
city has ninety days from April 2, 1998 to make a decision regarding this
matter; the deadline being July 2, 1998. The Mayor stated that council could
reject the plan, override it or hold a public hearing. He stated that he feels
there are issues that would need to be resolved before overriding the
recommendation by NKAP. Mr. Wichmann advised council that they would have to
come up with their own factual decision based on the same evidence that was
used by the NKAP staff. Mr. Holten stated that he knows of no change since last
submitted by Mr. Kolb and the city has received two recommendations from the
planning commission. Mr. Wichmann suggested obtaining a transcript of the
public hearing held by the planning commission on this zone change and to
contact Mr. Kolb requesting he put into writing the stipulations he will adhere
to if granted the zone change by council.
14.   Jaimie Henson made a motion to accept the NKAPC staff recommendation for
disapproval of the Kolb zone change. Anita Steffen seconded the motion. Roll
call vote was answered with two yes votes and four no votes cast by Mr. Holten,
Mr. Weber, Mrs. Weber and Mrs. Gabbard. Mrs. Gabbard clarified her vote by
stating that while she does not like to see more development in the city, she
felt the surrounding residents were more responsive to Mr. Kolb’s latest
development plan.
15.   Scott Holten made a motion to direct the city administrator to contact
Mr. Kolb and request he put in writing the development stipulations he will
adhere to; and, purchase a copy of the transcript of the April 2, 1998 NKAP
meeting. Ken Weber seconded the motion. No roll call; motion carried with all
ayes.
16.   Mrs. Henson announced that May 11th Police Memorial Week will be observed
with May 15th being Police Memorial Day. She suggested everyone fly their flags
at half mast in memory of all the dedicated officers who have fallen in the
line of duty.
17.   Under old business, Mrs. Henson reported that she had not received any
feedback before tonight on the latest changes proposed for Section 9.23 of the
zoning ordinance. Mrs. Weber stated that she felt the issue of going before the
Board of Adjustments to appeal the size of a vehicle would need to be looked
into by the city attorney. Mr. Wichmann stated that the Board of Adjustments
has specific functions which include granting variances, approving conditional
uses and acting as appeals for the zoning administrator. The Board cannot
change a zoning ordinance or a decision of the Zoning Administrator. The city
attorney advised that a new zoning ordinance will not allow for a Board of
Adjustment hearing. Mr. Holten commented that this proposed text amendment has
been “kicked around” for months and he does not see a lot of support from
council to make any significant change.
18.   Mr. Holten made a motion to leave Section 9.23 of the zoning ordinance as
is. Ken Weber seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with two yes
votes by Mr. Holten and Mr. Weber and four no votes by the remaining council
members. Motion defeated.
19.   Council scheduled a Parking Ordinance Committee meeting for May 7th at 2:
00 p.m. at the City Administration Building to continue reviewing Section 9.23
of the zoning ordinance.
20.   Police Officer, Brian Butler reported that the department has received a
federal grant that would provide for the hiring of four additional police
officers. Three have already been hired and they are in the process of hiring a
fourth. Ken Weber asked if the federal funds provided for the cost of cruiser
and uniforms. Officer Butler advised that the grant was only for salaries and
benefits.
21.   Dave Whitacre, City Engineer, reported up-dates on several projects that
his firm is supervising. He stated the restoration work of Phase II (Plantation
Heights) of the Fowler Creek sewer project has not been completed mainly due to
the wet condition of the ground with eight inches of rain that has fallen this
month. He assured council that he is keeping track of the complaints. Also the
contractor (Edgewood Excavating) for Phase IV had asked the city for an
extension of time for restoration work and is now submitting his additional
costs to the city. Mr. Whitacre stated that he does not feel these costs are
justified. He also reported that one of the flow monitors is being repaired.
The Beechgrove area is having a tree root problem along with a significant
amount of storm water influx. When weather permits they will conduct smoke
testing in these lines to pinpoint the problem areas. He informed council that
the mapping is incorrect; manholes did not show up and some are covered over.
22.   Mrs. Weber asked Mr. Whitacre about the sidewalks in the Battleridge
subdivision and he said they meet standards but would have another look. She
also reported that surveyor stakes were placed on Don Williams’s property at
the corner of Skyway Drive and PawPaw. Mr. Whitacre will check on this matter
and get back to council.
23.   Mr. Whitacre reported that the “wish list” for street repairs amounts to
approximately $528,000. There are several areas deteriorating and a lot of
crack sealing needed. Mayor Gabbard commented the budget would have to be cut
considerably to spend that kind of money. Mr. Whitacre asked council to give
him a set amount for road repairs and he would work from that. They are in the
process of up-dating the street repair listing that was done a few years ago
wherein the streets were rated on a scale of 1-5 based on the condition of the
road. Mr. Scott and Mrs. Weber asked to have this list when completed.
24.   Mr. Whitacre stated that a radius repair was done at the corner of Pearl
and Independence Station Road. This corner houses a gas valve which a school
bus was running over every time it turned the corner.
25.   Mrs. Weber asked about the sewer backup in a house in the Beechgrove area
last week. Mr. Scott said they are aware of it and are working with the
resident to resolve the matter. Mrs. Weber introduced Mr. McHargue who lives on
Sassafras Drive. He has not had his property restored to its original condition
yet and now has an overgrowth of weeds along with debris that he is unable to
maintain. She stated that he is willing to wait to get this area restored but
does not want to be forgotten and asked if a weed whacker could be brought in
to cut down some of this overgrowth. Mayor Gabbard said that he would send
someone over to Mr. McHargue’s property this week to clean up the area.
26.   Mayor Gabbard read the letter he wrote to the state in October 1997
regarding the state installing a traffic light and turn lane at Industrial Road
and Holten Drive. He also read the state’s April 1998 response which addressed
only the traffic light. The state said a turn lane was needed or a traffic
light would be of no value. Mr. Weber commented that perhaps the state did not
have money in their budget for this project and the city should request they
budget funds for this. The Mayor said he will pursue the issue and follow up
with another letter
27.   Gary Scott reported the Personnel Committee is still up-dating the policy
manual. Mrs. Weber asked to be removed from the committee as they continue to
meet mid-day when she is at work. Mr. Scott said her input was valuable and
asked if she could she meet at 4:00 p.m. So a Personnel Committee meeting was
scheduled for May 7th at 4:00 p.m. at the City Administration Building. Mr.
Scott reported that he is working on an agenda for the Planning Session to be
held the end of May and welcomed topics for the agenda from council members no
later than Friday, May 1st. Mrs. Steffen stated she had submitted a list and
asked if she needed to re-submit it. He reminded council of the Budget meeting
set for May 19th at the Kenton County Extension Center.
28.   Mr. Scott stated the need to amend the current budget to provide the
transfer of funds for the recreation department as previously discussed at this
meeting and to include a few minor changes. The amendments are:
∙   Auditor Contract - increase from      $6,600 to $10,600
∙   Add new line item - Zoning Administrator Contract   $2,600
∙   Street Signs & Erection - increase from       $8,000 to $20,000
∙   Sewer Fund - Billing Service - increase from    $3,000 to $5,000
∙   Police - Cleaning/Restroom Supplies - increase from    $500 to $700
∙   Recreation - Transfer of $12,000 from Shaw Park Construction to Hartland
Park Construction
1.   Also, Mr. Scott advised council that he has sent written notification to
NKAPZ advising that the city will no longer be utilizing their services for
zoning administration. He stated that the Building Inspector, Al Bowling, would
temporarily take over enforcement of the zoning. Mr. Holten asked the city
attorney how he felt about the city doing the zoning administration in-house.
Mr. Wichmann commented that he preferred in-house zoning mainly because NKAPZ
does not make any decisions and that it would help to prevent prosecution of
zoning violators as it would be monitored more closely. Mr. Scott offered to
schedule a meeting of council members and some representatives of local cities
who have in-house zoning administrators. Mr. Holten replied that he would like
that. Mayor Gabbard said he arrived at the $2,600 amount by calculating $200/
week for 13 weeks (the end of the current fiscal year) of zoning administration
for Mr. Bowling.
2.   Mr. Scott also reported that he plans to back-bill the developers for all
the street signs the city has installed in the new subdivisions. He is hoping
to recover 95% of that expense.
3.   Jaimie Henson made a motion to have a first reading to amend the budget
ordinance. The motion was seconded by Barbara Gabbard. Motion carried with all
ayes. Mr. Wichmann read the amended budget ordinance.
4.   Scott Holten made a motion to accept the first reading; seconded by
Barbara Gabbard. No roll call, motion carried with all ayes.
5.   Mr. Holten commented that he feels the city needs to keep better track of
the Fowler Creek expenses; perhaps the line items need to be more specific. A
discussion ensued regarding the legality of moving monies from the Fowler Creek
fund into the General fund. The city attorney advised that the financing
documents may not allow this and he needed to look at the documents in order to
proceed as there may be provisions restricting the manner in which this is
done. He will check the documents before the second reading of the amended
budget.
6.   Frank Wichmann, City Attorney, did not have a formal report for council.
He commented that is busy familiarizing himself with the city’s sewer and other
important documents. He will be ready by the Planning Session at the end of
May.
7.   Ken Weber made a motion to adjourn. Motion seconded by Anita Steffen.
Motion carried with all ayes. Meeting adjourned at 10:14.p.m.

May 12, 1998
City of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
1. The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard at 7:08 p.m., followed by
the Pledge of Allegiance and an invocation by Reverend Shelton of Grace Baptist
Church.
2. ROLL CALL was answered by four council members; Mrs. Gabbard, Mrs. Henson,
Mr. Holten, and Mrs. Steffen. Absent were Mr. and Mrs. Weber. Mrs. Henson
commented that the Webers were attending a school function and would arrive
late. They did arrive, at approximately 7:40 p.m.
3. The Mayor welcomed everyone to the meeting and explained that the sound
system was not operating for the meeting since we could not get in to turn it
on. He hoped we could all be heard, and encouraged people to speak up for the
audience and the videotaping.
4. Motion was made to Approve the Minutes from the April 28th meeting after
some amendments to them (Holten/Gabbard). Votes were all ayes, and motion
passed.
5. The Mayor reminded the audience members that anyone wishing to address
council should sign in. As no one had done so, and no one requested to speak,
the Privileges of the Floor section of the agenda was passed over.
6. Mrs. Steffen commented she would like to add to the agenda and discuss a
problem of a homeowner in the area of Wedgewood and Clubhouse Drives. The
problem is one of water overflow, especially in times of storms. Mrs. Steffen
provided information to council and others regarding the nature and location of
the problem. Mr. Scott had been made aware of this concern, as well as Mr.
Briggs of Cardinal Engineering. Mr. Briggs stated that he will re-visit the
area and check out the problem, reporting back to council at the May 26th
meeting.
7. Mr. Holten asked if there could be discussion under Old Business around the
issue of the park funding under the budget ordinance. Mayor Gabbard explained
that once the Ordinance was approved by the second reading, the contractors
could begin the work Mrs. Yeager had told them about. As the 2nd reading of
this ordinance is on the agenda for this meeting, business moved on to the next
item.
8. A request had been made by Mrs. Yeager and city staff that an ordinance be
created to address park rental fees and setting a fee for shelter users to
offset expenses for restroom cleaning. Mr. Wichmann said he had not brought
this paperwork with him to do this reading. After some discussion about the
urgency of getting this reading done, it was decided that Mr. Wichmann try to
draft an ordinance for reading later in the meeting.
9. The purpose of the ordinance would be to set out that a $ 40 fee would be
charged at the time of rental application, with $ 25 being returned to the
renter if the site is left in satisfactory condition. The remaining $ 15 would
be kept by the City to offset the cost of extra restroom cleaning.
10. The Mayor asked if there were any other changes to the agenda, and there
were none. He reminded council of the Special Meeting upcoming on May 19th at
7:00 p.m. at the Kenton County Extension Center.
11. The next item discussed was Sewering of Homes on Madison Pike. Mr. Scott
commented that he and Mr. Briggs had met with Mrs. Stephens regarding her
options, and Mr. Scott had later met with Mrs. Stephens brother-in-law, a
builder, to clarify this. The other family, the Williams’ home, will go through
the church property, and Mr. Scott said he is trying to set up a meeting or
have a conversation with this resident, but they keep missing each other. Mr.
Holten questioned what financial assistance would be offered. Mr. Scott said he
is working on getting the easements.
12. To allow Mr. Wichmann time to draft the Park Rental Fee ordinance, council
moved on to department reports. Chief Porter reported that the Police
Department building was recently visited by OSHA inspectors with some serious
and some not so serious concerns stemming from this inspection. A report will
follow, after which the department has 30 days to correct violations. Chief
Porter spoke about searching for temporary housing for the police department
and that there were several options at this time. Mrs. Steffen asked if there
were fines for the deficiencies, and it was reported there were none since this
is a voluntary compliance, otherwise there could be large fines.
13. Also reported was that Cops MORE received approval and 2 new officers had
been hired; Greg Hallau of Cincinnati, and Mike Thatcher of Bowling Green.
14. Engineer’s report was provided in written form by Dan Briggs of Cardinal
Engineering. He explained he wished to provide an up-to-date written report to
council that they can get hopefully right before council meetings. He commented
on work stopped at Plantation Heights due to wet ground, NCC4 being completed
with inspection and release upcoming. He said Quast Paving contracts were
mostly completed and that sewer monitoring was on-going. He had provided an
updated street evaluation list and a memo to the Mayor and Mr. Scott regarding
street lighting.
15. Mr. Briggs asked Mr. Wichmann if Battleridge Phase 4 would be under the
ordinance requiring street lighting. Mr. Wichmann said that the existing
ordinance covered this. Discussion moved to sidewalks with Mr. Wichmann
commenting that older homes were not under the requirement to put in sidewalks,
but the City could choose to put them in and pay for them or assess the
property owner.
16. Mrs. Henson asked for clarification on the street evaluation list and why
some ratings had not changed. Mr. Briggs commented the number remained the same
if only part of the work on the street was completed. Questions then followed
as to the sense of doing partial work. Mr. Briggs explained the idea was to use
budgeted money to keep roads from deteriorating and that some work was simply
preventive maintenance vs. total road replacement.
17. Mr. Bowling, Building Inspector, reported to council on sidewalk concerns
in the city, in particular in Courthouse Estates. He noted that there were
places where the owner refused to install sidewalks and that one area was
asphalted instead of concrete. Discussion followed as to how to get the
developers and builders to be responsible for sidewalk installation in future,
and whether some of these exceptions were prior to the sidewalk ordinance going
into effect.
18. Mrs. Henson asked if there was an ordinance regarding sidewalk cleaning
since it appeared a resident had been told there was one. She commented that
city staff should check their facts before giving information to residents.
19. Discussion returned to sidewalk installation, with the Mayor asking Mr.
Wichmann if our zoning ordinances could address this. Mr. Wichmann said there
is no reason why they could not be addressed via zoning ordinances.
20. Mr. Bowling commented on an ordinance from 1982 that allowed the city to
cut grass at unkempt properties that were declared a nuisance. This ordinance
had been lost from the city files, and recovered by Mr. Bowling through
research. He had given it to Mr. Wichmann to review before applying it to
existing situations. Mrs. Henson commented on a large tree limb down on the
property adjacent to the Police Department, with Mr. Bowling saying he would
contact the owners of the property and ask them to dispose of the tree limb.
21. Gary Scott, City Administrator, reported to council on recent meetings of
the Personnel Committee and Building Committee. No upcoming meetings are
planned for the Personnel Committee, but Mr. Scott will try to set a date with
Building Committee members to meet soon. He said an architect had been brought
in, at no expense, to view several proposed sites and comment. Mr. Holten
volunteered to provide information to the Building Committee on work done in
the past.
22. Regarding the May 29-30 Planning Session, Mr. Scott was concerned that
quite a few council members had expressed concerns they might not be able to
attend. After some discussion, a new tentative meeting date was set for June
19-20th. Mr. Scott had an agenda prepared at this time, and will wait to hear
from council members to see if the June dates will work.
23. Returning to the Park Fee ordinance, a motion was made to do a 1st reading
(Henson/Holten), with all ayes. Mr. Wichmann read this as an Emergency
Ordinance, becoming effective after the 1st reading and publication. After the
reading, he explained a 2nd reading would still be done on May 26th, as this is
his personal preference. Discussion followed as to charging fees to use the
park, and clarifying the purpose of the $ 15 fee that would not be refunded.
Motion was made to accept the 1st reading (Holten/Henson), later restated and
re-seconded to “enact the 1st emergency reading”. Roll call vote was all ayes,
and the motion passed.
24. Motion was made to do a 2nd reading of Ordinance 1998-0-04 regarding the
Amended Budget for 1997-98 (K Weber/Henson) with all ayes. Mr. Wichmann read
the ordinance for the 2nd time. Mr. Holten asked about the transfer money from
the Fowler Creek Sewer Fund and asked Mr. Wichmann about his recommendations
for transfer of such funds. Mr. Wichmann clarified that no funds should move
from a Special Fund to the General Fund unless all bond conditions had been
satisfied. Based on his recommendation, the transfer of funds originally on the
budget document were negated.
25. Motion was made to accept the 2nd reading of Ordinance 1998-0-04 (Holten/
K Weber) with roll call response of all ayes. Motion passed.
26. With all business being completed, motion was made (Henson/K Weber) to
adjourn, followed by all aye votes. The meeting was officially adjourned.

May 26, 1998
City of Independence, Ky.
Council Meeting
Minutes
1- The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard, followed by the Pledge of
Allegiance and an invocation by Reverend Shelton of Grace Baptist Church. Roll
call was answered by 5 council members, with Mrs. Steffen being the only absent
member. She had explained earlier she would be late since she had a school
function to attend. Mrs. Steffen arrived at approximately 8:00 p.m.
2- The Mayor welcomed those present to the meeting and explained the agenda
focused primarily on the proposed budget for 1998-99.
3- Motion was made to accept the minutes of the May 12th meeting, as amended
(Holten/Henson), with all ayes. Motion was made to accept the minutes of the
May 19th Special budget meeting without amendment (Holten/Henson), followed by
all ayes.
4- The Mayor recognized Mrs. Nancy Ballinger, who asked to speak as a resident
of the city regarding the proposed civic/senior center item which had been
removed from the budget at the May 19th meeting. She strongly supports this
concept, and answered council’s questions about what the Senior Services would
assist with in regard to the center and about center activities. She asked
council to form a committee to study the questions of liability and such
relating to a center.
5- The Mayor recognized Mrs. Donna Yeager of the Independence Park Committee
who spoke, as she did at the May 19th meeting, regarding floating a bond for a
community center. She explained that she and city staff were working on a
Federal grant which would require matching funds to build a community building.
Discussion then ensued regarding the possibilities of fund-raising via
residents and corporations, and Mr. Weber’s concern that council make a
commitment to match the grant funds now. Mr. Weber referred to the April 30th
statement showing money available in General Fund C.D.’s that could be
appropriated later, if necessary , to match Federal funds. He commented on the
$ 777,000+ balance on CD’s in the General Fund and how this money had been
sitting there doing nothing since he had been on council previously.
6- Discussion moved to what the city might have in the way of surplus funds
after this fiscal year, and how that information would be helpful in
determining if matching funds could be found from this. The Mayor stated he
would not know surplus figures until after June 30th.
7- Mrs. Henson asked about the recent resignation of Ms. Uebel, who was leaving
her post as city finance/bookkeeper. Mr. Scott explained the opportunity which
had opened up for Ms. Uebel, which she felt she needed to pursue. Comment was
also added that interviewing had taken place with one candidate to fill this
position, who was qualified and also knowledgeable of the Frey computer system.
8- Motion was made to do the second reading of the Park Fee Ordinance 1998-0-05
(Holten/Henson), with all ayes. Mr. Wichmann read the document. Motion was made
to accept the reading (K Weber/Henson), passing with a roll call vote of 5
ayes, 0 nays.
9- The Mayor read aloud his budget message, which had been provided to council
and which is maintained in city permanent files. Mrs. Henson commented there
did not seem to be the $ 453,000 additional revenue compared to the 1997-98
budget, as noted in the Mayor’s budget address. Questions were raised about the
balanced budget not addressing 4-5 concerns mentioned in the budget message.
The Mayor explained his part was to provide the budget to council, and it was
for them to revise it as they wished. The Mayor stated Mr. Scott had asked
council on May 19th to provide him with questions about the budget so he could
be prepared to answer them, and that no council members had provided questions.
Mrs. Henson commented she had held her questions until such time as citizens
could hear and see what was being done.
10- The Mayor asked if council wished to recess so that budget presentation
materials could be set up. Motion was made to recess for 5 minutes (Holten/
R Weber) with all ayes. Motion was made to return to session (Holten/R Weber)
with all ayes. Mr. Scott fielded questions regarding revenue and transfers of
funds. Questions then were directed to Chief Ed Porter of the Police Department
about Universal Hiring, Cops More and Cops Fast. Questions were raised as to
where the idea of the 5% salary increase had come from and why not 3.5% or 2.5%
compared to other cities. Comments followed from council about benefits to city
employees and changes in personnel policy which will increase benefits and/or
pay.
11- Questions and comments followed about leasing vs. purchase of police
vehicles, average mileage, and Explorer’s being cheaper to purchase than Crown
Vic’s. Other questions arose about capital outlay for the police department and
growth vs. spending. Chief Porter commented on keeping training costs down and
pursuing grants as ways of searching for additional revenue to offset costs.
Discussion moved to the Seizure/Forfeiture line (130) and concerns about seized
money or weapons. Both Chief Porter and attorney Frank Wichmann responded to
councils’ concerns, and Mrs. Henson commented she is still working on getting
information to council regarding Seizure laws.
12- Mrs. Henson asked how revenue could increase, departments be cut and the
information on the budget not seem to fit. Mr. Wichmann suggested that council
get information regarding expected surpluses, since this would help them in
making their decisions about the proposed budget. The Mayor and Mr. Scott
agreed to provide a more workable budget at the next council meeting. After
some discussion, Mrs. Henson commented that without the surplus figures and
asset information she felt she could not continue to discuss the budget and
motioned to adjourn. Mr. Scott said he would have information for council by
the next regular meeting regarding expected surpluses. Mrs. Henson’s motion to
adjourn was seconded (R Weber) and followed with all ayes. The meeting was
officially adjourned.

Linda L. Baker, City Clerk
June 9, 1998
City of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
1- The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard at approximately 7:10 p.m.,
followed by the Pledge of Allegiance. There was no invocation given since
Reverend Toole was absent.
2- Roll call of council members was taken, with 4 being present and 2 being
absent (R Weber, K Weber). The Mayor welcomed everyone to the meeting,
apologizing for the delay in starting and for the lack of videotaping (cable’s
equipment was not working).
3- Business moved to the approval of the minutes from the May 26th meeting,
with a motion being made (Holten/Henson) to accept the minutes as amended. This
passed with all ayes.
4- Mr. Holten asked if Mr. Wichmann would be attending the meeting, as he was
not present at this time. Mr. Scott explained Mr. Wichmann was on his way and
would be arriving shortly.
5- The Mayor reviewed the sign-in sheet for people who wished to speak to
council. He recognized Mr. Butler, who was attending to speak on the Daniels
Map Amendment, along with Mr. Clayton. Mr. Butler showed to council a property
map and explained the current borders of the property at Harris Pike and Route
17/Madison Pike. He is asking for a zone change from Residential to
Neighborhood/Commercial. The Planning Commission had approved the zone change
at a prior meeting. Mrs. Henson commented she had received a copy of this
letter regarding the approval, while the Mayor commented he had not received
it.
6- Discussion centered around the unreliability of information on the route and
final plan for the “new” Madison Pike. Council and the Mayor had concerns that
they could not rely on existing information about where the proposed road would
go, and therefore were unwilling to commit to plans for any development at that
crucial intersection. Mr. Butler stated he would be willing to provide
documentation on the road plan from KDOT, and bring this to council. The Mayor
said this information should be provided to the city on or before the Thursday/
Friday that council packets go out, so this information could be included for
council to review prior to the meeting. The Mayor commented that one of the
conditions for this project’s acceptance by the city would be that sewer tie-in
is to the east side, meaning the Fowler Creek sewer project.
7- Discussion then concerned the number and nature of the structures to be
developed. The original plan had called for 2 structures (a convenience-type
store with gasoline service), and a “later development plan” called for a
possibility of a bank, dentist/doctor offices, etc in two other structures.
There were concerns about the outer appearance of these structures (the Dairy
Mart) and Mr. Butler maintained they would conform to whatever is needed. He
commented there would be no “fast food” buildings.
8- Mr. Dan Briggs, Cardinal Engineering, commented about sewer system concerns
and asked for some assurance about the capacity of this development. There were
concerns about traffic problems, but Mr. Butler said this intersection would be
fully signalized and there would be speed reductions for that area.
9-Concerns moved to curb cuts, especially a cut onto Harris Pike. Mr. Butler
asked council to reserve their opinions on this until more information was
available on Harris Pike plans. The Mayor commented on city regulations
requiring curb cuts no closer than 600 ft. Both curb cuts, at Harris and at
Madison, would be in violation of existing city zoning regulations.
10- The Mayor suggested that Mr. Butler and Mr. Clayton reschedule to meet with
council again, and bring documentation regarding proposed layout for “new”
Madison Pike and Harris Pike. Regarding the question of timing, it was
determined that there were 90 days to respond to this issue from the May 7th
date. Mr. Butler was asked by Mr.Holten if he would be willing to abide by the
developmental controls the city might wish to impose, and he said he would be
willing to work on this. He commented the plan had already taken into account
de-acceleration lanes, screening, landscaping, etc. Mr. Butler said he would be
able to work with Mr. Gary Scott, City Administrator, on any developmental
controls.
11- Ms. Donna Yeager, of the Independence Recreation Committee, addressed
council regarding rain delays on summer work at parks. Her concern was that
work might not be completed under the current fiscal year budget, and would
money be carried over to the next budget if contracts could not be fulfilled by
June 30, 1998. The Mayor said that any existing contracts would be paid, once
completed, from the current budget, or council could make provision for amount
of monies owed for these projects in the next budget for 1998-99.
12- The Mayor added an item to the agenda by calling council’s attention to a
request from Ms. Zona King of the Independence Historical Group. This group
will be holding a special meeting on Saturday, June 13th at 10:00 a.m. at the
Independence/KC Library, at which speakers will be recalling memories of the
city. The Mayor encouraged all council members to attend, if possible.
13- Mr. Klump, of Brentwood Construction, had contacted the city office and
asked to be moved to the June 23rd agenda, so his business was deleted from
this evening’s agenda.
14- Regarding the Resolution for the Park Trail System at Shaw Park, Mr.
Wichmann stated he did not have the resolution document ready at this time for
a reading. It was clarified to council that this resolution is not regarding
money or matching funds; it is simply a requirement of the grant application
made months ago that the city state its support of this project by resolution
format. This will be carried over to the next meeting.
15- Regarding the Kolb development of property at Taylor Mill and Cherokee, the
Mayor commented at this time about a letter to council from Mr. Wichmann, and
then read to council and the audience from an agreement coming from a meeting
earlier in the day, June 9th, attended by the Mayor, City Administrator, Mr.
Wichmann and Mr. Kolb.
The Mayor referred to page 3 regarding restrictions agreed to on the
development plan. He commented on a 200’ buffer zone/green space being agreed
to, but that a forced main was not in the agreement. The forced main should be
a gravity feed instead. The Mayor noted that entrances from Cox and Taylor Mill
violated the 600 ft. curb cut regulations of the city and had concerns that no
easement was held on property across the street on Mills Road. The Mayor said
his major concern was the 1st curb cut off Taylor Mill, since he sees this as a
safety concern. He also referred to minutes from a December 1997 meeting and
questioned the “underground storm water system”. Mr. Kolb said he could clarify
that later.
16- The Mayor also referred to the traffic engineer’s report (page 5) and had
concerns that the state would not agree to “signalize” this entrance at Cox and
Taylor Mill. If not, that would be a major problem. The Mayor opened the floor
to discussion among council members. Mr. Holten said he felt the city owed it
to Mr. Kolb to make a decision tonight. Mrs. Gabbard commented she had concerns
also about the entrances off Taylor Mill. Mr. Wichmann responded to a concern
of Mrs. Henson’s about the obtaining of the easement on the property at Mills
Road and said that Mr. Kolb was committed at the earlier meeting on June 9 to
obtaining that easement since without it, the development could not proceed.
Mr. Kolb agreed to developmental controls the city requested but held firm that
the entrances were critical to the success of the development since many of the
businesses required “quick in/ quick out” access.
17- After some clarification from Mr. Wichmann as to council’s duty in this
process, the topic moved to providing sewer access to residents on Jimae, which
Mr. Kolb agreed would occur whether via a pump station operation or gravity
feed. He did comment he needed easements from 2 property owners (Ogden and
Clayton) for the gravity feed, or he had the option of crossing the street to
tie in. Either way this would serve Jimae residents and Mr. Holten clarified
this meant those residents would be paying into the Fowler Creek debt
reduction.
18- Mr. Holten made a motion to override Planning and Zoning’s decision
regarding the zone change. The Mayor explained the motion would need to be
modified. After another attempt to make a motion, the Mayor asked if council
would consider a 5 minute recess to discuss the motion language. Motion was
made to recess for 5 minutes (Henson/Gabbard), with all ayes.
19- Motion was made to return to session (Holten/Steffen) with all ayes. Mr.
Holten said he would make a motion (to override the Planning and Zoning
decision) using the language prepared by Mr. Wichmann and he read it verbatim
from the offered statement.
Motion was seconded by Mrs. Henson, followed by a 2-2 vote (yes=Henson, Holten;
no=Steffen, Gabbard). The Mayor explained that a vote to override Planning and
Zoning required 4 “yes” votes, and this was not a situation where he could
break the tie vote. The motion failed.
20- The Mayor asked for departmental reports, beginning with Chief Porter of
the Police Department. Chief Porter said the 4th and final officer hired under
grant this year will start on June 25th. The officer is Ms. Tanya Paul. He
commented on the annual reports given out to council at the last meeting,
saying more were available if needed. Feedback was given as to this annual
report.
21- The Mayor commented that the Police Department will be moving to temporary
headquarters on the second floor of the Independence/Kenton Co. Courthouse. He
said an arrangement had been worked out with county regarding costs. No rent
would be charged, but any extra expenses incurred by the county on gas/electric
bills, for instance, would be payable by the city. Chief Porter said the move
could be completed by July 1. Council had varying comments about moving of
equipment.
22- Mrs. Henson asked that there be consideration for an outside phone at the
new site and comments were made about signs to note the change of location.
Chief Porter said the department could remain as long as 2 years in that
location before outgrowing it.
23- Mrs. Steffen brought up the concerns about violence in the schools, and
discussion followed as to how to address these concerns, with Chief Porter
urging a program of education at school sites (as is done at St. Cecilia) along
with on-site visitation at random times to provide a presence on school
property.
24- Mr. Al Bowling, Building Inspector/Zoning Administrator, addressed council
and told them May 1998 was the busiest recorded month for building permits in
the city’s history, but he expects June 1998 may even exceed those figures. He
commented he has been issuing zoning permits since June 1, 1998. He provided an
additional handout to council on zoning violations that had not been ready for
the packet materials.
25- Mr. Dan Briggs, of Cardinal Engineering, addressed council and provided a
written report. He commented that a meeting is set for either June 11 or 12
with A. O. Smith representatives regarding discharge at that site. He was
questioned about the time frame on the sewering of the few homes on Madison
adjacent to the Christian Church. Mr. Briggs stated an easement is still needed
from Ms. Williams. Mr. Holten asked Mr. Wichmann if he would work to get this
easement granted. Mr. Briggs commented that a manhole was needed and a proposal
for this would be given to the Mayor for approval, as it could cost $ 10,000.
Mr. Briggs said actual work might take 10 days, but the time frame for
completion depended on authorization from the city for the manhole.
26- Mr. Briggs commented on monitoring of sewers and said he needed
authorization or direction from the city as to how to proceed with areas
outside of easements. Mr. Wichmann will meet with Mr. Briggs to resolve this
issue. Mrs. Steffen asked about the water problems at Wedgewood/Clubhouse
Drive, and Mr. Briggs said he had visited this site in dry weather and not seen
any obvious problems. He needs to revisit it during a time of rain to see what
problems occur. Mr. Briggs commented on information he wished to give to
council at the Planning Session regarding potholes and street repair work. He
also stated the city needs to be prepared to spend $ 150,000 on sewer repair in
the next fiscal year. Discussion followed as to sewer repair and identification
of problem areas. Mr. Briggs referred to a system adopted by Taylor Mill and
Florence involving a Sanitary Sewer Commission. The Mayor said the Storm Sewer
Committee needed to be resurrected to work on this issue.
27- Discussion moved to Schumacher-Dugan and why work was taking so long. Mr.
Briggs commented that the rainfall had made the ground too wet to support the
equipment needed to complete this work, and that they could argue the delay was
unavoidable.
28- The council moved on to discuss the 1998-99 Proposed Budget. The Mayor
commented he had Ms. Linda Chapman of Rankin and Rankin present to answer
questions if needed. Mr. Holten asked Ms. Chapman about reserves of money and
she explained the city operated on an accrual basis vs. cash. She commented the
city should, as a rule of thumb, maintain sufficient money in reserve to
operate for a 3-4 month period.
29- The Mayor asked Ms. Chapman about a comment made about a balanced budget,
and that the City had never had one. He explained he had presented a balanced
budget for the next fiscal year, and if adopted, this would be the first
balanced budget for the city. She said the 1998-99 budget, as proposed now, was
a balanced budget and clarified that she had been referring to previous year’s
budgets when saying they were not balanced.
She commented that the city budget is “balanced” when the General Fund revenues
and General Fund expenses figures match.
30- Gary Scott explained how the figures for the June 30th balances were
arrived at, and explained these balances were shown as the “carried forward”
balances estimates for the 1998-99 proposed budget Schedule A. It was clarified
that May 30th actual balances would not be available from Mr. Keller until the
June 23rd meeting. Council members Holten and Henson commented on the budget
meetings being held separate from the council meetings due to time constraints
at regular meetings. Motion was made (Holten/Henson) to schedule a special
meeting to discuss the proposed budget. A roll call vote was taken with 3 ayes
and 1 no (Gabbard). Motion carried. Meeting dates were discussed as either June
15 or 16.
31- The Mayor commented he would be unable to attend the Planning Session set
for June 19-20th. Gary Scott said he would review the budget with council from
the first line item through the last, but he preferred that council review the
budget and return with questions on specific line items with which they have a
problem. This would save time, as all line items are not in contention.
32- Discussion followed as to whether it was necessary for Ms. Chapman to
attend budget meetings and whether discussion on the budget should be continued
more tonight.
The Mayor clarified for Ms. Henson his statement in the budget address that he
was comparing proposed 1998-99 revenue figures with figures from the 1997-98
budget as initially adopted in October of 1997. In that particular instance,
the Mayor was not comparing revenue to the amended 1997-98 budget revenue.
33- Motion was made to go into executive session to discuss possible land
acquisition and a litigation concern (Gabbard/Steffen). Motion carried with 3
ayes (Mrs. Henson abstained from voting). Mrs. Henson stated it was not her
intent when saying she wished council to address budget in special meetings to
mean she did not wish to continue to work on the budget at this meeting.
34- Motion was made to return to regular session, with no action being taken
from the executive session (Henson/Gabbard), with all ayes. Motion followed to
adjourn the regular session (Henson/Holten) with all ayes.

                  Isaac Gabbard, Mayor

June 23, 1998
City of Independence
Council Meeting
Minutes
1- The meeting was called to order by Mayor Gabbard at approximately 7:00 p.m.,
followed by the Pledge of Allegiance and an invocation by Reverend Toole of the
Hickory Grove Baptist Church.
2- Roll call was taken, with all council members present except Mrs. Henson who
had notified us she would be unable to attend due to a family emergency.
Acceptance of the minutes from the June 9 meeting were tabled after a motion
(Holten/R Weber) requesting review of the audio tape in regards to item # 29.
The tape will be reviewed to see if what is noted in the minutes reflects what
was said.
3- The Mayor recognized Mr. Rodney Cain, Judge Executive for Kenton County. He
was present at the meeting to provide information to council and residents
about a proposed jail site in the city, in the area of Webster Road. Mr. George
Neack, Deputy Judge Executive, was also in attendance to assist with providing
information and answering questions.
4- A sign-in log was kept of residents wishing to address or ask questions of
Mr. Cain and Mr. Neack (see attached). A brief synopsis of the 2 hour
discussion session includes the following information: a) the search has been
going on for over 8 years, b) there have been numerous sites considered, with
many being found unsuitable, c) there are lawsuits pending which encourage the
county to resolve the jail issue reasonably soon, d) the most residents
concerns were centered around 3 concepts: safety, property values, and concern
that the jail should be located in an industrialized area instead of a
residential area. Maps were provided to show the proposed jail site in relation
to a proposed dam and water retention area. Mr. Cain and Mr. Neack encouraged
residents to attend Kenton County Fiscal Court meetings which are held 4 times
a month, 2 in the morning and 2 in the evening. Residents will be able to speak
at these open meetings and hear what is going on. Mr. Cain also encouraged
residents to contact their state representatives and senators and tell them
they need to ensure a new state prison be built to house state prisoners.
5- A motion was made to recess after discussion of the proposed jail site was
completed (K Weber/Holten). This passed with all ayes. Motion was made to
return to session (Holten/R Weber), passing with all ayes.
6- Before discussion began on the Park Trails Resolution, Mr. Weber had
concerns that the city not overlook the need to address the Daniels Map
Amendment regarding property at Harris Pike and Madison. This had been set for
this meeting’s agenda, and moved by the developers to the July 14th meeting. It
was noted that they wished to provide the city with “expert testimony”
regarding the road plans for the new route 17. This could not be done prior to
the July 14th meeting. Mr. Weber was concerned that the 90 days to possibly
override the NKAPC decision (to approve the zoning change) began on May 7 and
that if this were not placed on an agenda soon, it might get lost and not dealt
with.
This would mean the city would not be able to override NKAPC’s decision if they
chose to. With information the these developers would return on July 14th,
council was satisfied.
7- Motion was made (Holten/K Weber) to read the Park Trails Resolution. Mr.
Wichmann read the resolution (1998-R-04) for council. This was followed by a
brief discussion with questions addressed to Donna Yeager as to the city
matching the funds for these trails, etc. Motion was made (Holten/R Weber) to
accept the resolution reading,and passed with all ayes.
8- Mr. Holten suggested that rather than discuss the proposed budget, we move
on to departmental reports. Chief Porter commented the move to the Courthouse
facility will be completed by July 6th and operational at that time. He added
that he had extras of the Police Department’s Annual Report and left a few
copies for people to take. Mr. Bowling commented that May 1998 had been our
busiest month ever in building permits, but June will surpass it. He was asked
if he is finding sufficient time to deal with zoning duties and how that was
going, and commented it was busy and he had talked to the Mayor about the need
for time. He said he was dealing more with zoning concerns called in by
residents that in actually going out and finding violations on his own. He will
provide a written report in early July.
9- Dave Whitacre of Cardinal Engineering spoke about sewer lines in the Boxwood
area of Beechgrove having roots in the laterals and that residents would be
notified of this so they could take action themselves. He reported on the
meeting recently with staff at A. O. Smith, and said the company was willing to
be pro-active in dealing with problems and monitoring of sediment. He talked
about recent “marking” of property at both Shaw and Hartland parks, but little
had been done beyond some rough grading at Shaw due to consistent rains and wet
ground. Mrs. Steffen asked for an update on the rain-related water problems at
Wedgewood, and Mr. Whitacre said no line blockages were found there. Mrs. Weber
commented on a call she had gotten regarding residents on Stephens Road who
wanted sewers and were still waiting on Cardinal for feedback regarding their
options. Dan said they would review the old estimates and get back in touch
with the residents.
10- The Mayor added to the agenda by informing council that a new sewer
ordinance needs to be written to address the city taking over billing of
maintenance fees, etc. He discussed setting a fixed rate for residential and
business sites, that the ordinance should state the city would take over the
billing from Sanitation, and that the city needs to define in this document
what areas are to tie into Fowler Creek and what areas tie into other lines. An
example of an existing concern is the proposed development at Harris and
Madison. Discussion ensued about allowing commercial development in these
areas, and whether the city could require residents/commercial users to incur
an additional expense to tie in where the city wants them to (especially if
this assists in retiring the Fowler Creek debt). Mr. Wichmann assured council
the city could require users to incur additional expense. Comments were made
about the size and scope of this venture and a need to act quickly. After some
discussion, it was decided that Cardinal, city staff and Mr. Wichmann had
different duties to carry out to get the preparation of the ordinance, and then
it could be brought before council for vote. Motion was made (Holten/R Weber)
that essentially asked the city staff, Cardinal Engineering and the city
attorney to work together to create a comprehensive sewer ordinance and that
this be ready in approximately 60 days. Motion passed with all ayes.
11- Mrs. Weber asked Mr. Scott to look into getting a read-out from the Water
District vs. using a flat fee for maintenance charges. He said he will look
into this. Mrs. Weber had concerns this might penalize some residents.
12- It was clarified, also, that the city would be taking over the maintenance
fee billing from Sanitation on all residents, not just those in the Fowler
Creek section.
13-    Mrs. Gabbard commented that she had been asked by a resident if the city
had considered buying the property the proposed jail would be on and avoiding
the jail being placed there. A resident spoke to council saying that during the
break, Mr. Cain had commented to him that the city could purchase that land,
pre-empting the jail coming in. This created anger on the part of some council
members because it implied that county executives had been less than open with
council and it confused the issue of whether the city had any say over the jail
coming in or not. After some discussion, it was decided that council members
would contact Mr. Cain on their own to voice their feelings, and also to
clarify the issue of buying the property as a park. There was comment from Mrs.
Steffen about privatization of the jail and what this might mean. After a brief
discussion on this topic, a motion was made to adjourn (Holten/R Weber), and
passed with all aye votes. The meeting was officially adjourned.

                  Isaac Gabbard, Mayor
