Linda L. Baker, City Clerk
July 14, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
1.   Mayor Gabbard called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Rebecca Weber, Jaimie Henson, Ken Weber, Anita
Steffen and Barbara Gabbard answered roll call. Council Member, Scott Holten
was ill and not able to attend the meeting. Also in attendance were the City
Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Frank Wichmann.
2.   The Mayor asked the council members if they had any additions to the
agenda. Mrs. Weber wanted to discuss installing additional streetlights in the
Beechgrove area and street repairs in Beechgrove. Mrs. Henson commented that
discussion regarding Section 9.23 of the Zoning Ordinances is being postponed
until an August meeting. Mayor Gabbard stated that there would be a short
Executive Session at the end of this meeting.
PRIVILEDGES OF THE FLOOR
3.   Susie Morehead, a resident of the Harvest Hills subdivision (located
outside of the city limits) submitted a petition to council voicing opposition
to the new Kenton County jail site on Webster Road. She asked if council had
taken a vote on this matter. The Mayor advised her that a vote had not been
taken, it would do little good, as the county has the right of eminent domain.
He also stated that council has not made an official statement in regard to
their position on the proposed jail site on Webster Road.
4.   Rebecca Weber to table approval of the minutes of the June 9th and June
23rd meetings made a motion. Jaimie Henson seconded the motion. Motion carried
with all ayes.
5.   Under new business, Mrs. Weber stated that she had spoken to a
representative of the Beechgove Homeowners Association who said that they were
promised streetlights for safety reasons and want to know when they will get
the lights. Mayor Gabbard stated he did not recall speaking to anyone from the
Association regarding lights, but that the current budget that the city is
operating under does not include a line item for the installation of
streetlights. The proposed 98/99 budget does include money for streetlights.
Mrs. Weber also submitted to the Mayor an invoice for approximately $600 for
pothole and grading work that was done by the Association for which they would
like reimbursement from the city. Mrs. Weber reported that a slab of concrete
covering a storm sewer on Arbor Court is large enough for an adult to get
under. She asked Mr. Briggs of Cardinal Engineering if he was aware of this
situation. Mr. Briggs replied that he is not aware of a storm sewer matter like
the one she is describing. Mrs. Weber feels the city should look into this
problem. The City Administrator, Gary Scott, will talk to a representative from
the Homeowner’s Association about these problems so they can be resolved.
6.   Under old business was the Daniel’s map amendment for property located at
the corner of Harris Pike and Madison Pike. Mr. Gene Daniels along with his
attorney, Martin Butler, engineer for the proposed project, Dwight Clayton, and
George Hoffman from the Kentucky Highway Transportation Cabinet made a
presentation to the Mayor and council regarding their plans for development of
the site for which they would like a zone change.
7.   Mr. Butler presented some general information about the property - it is a
five-acre parcel at the corner of Harris Pike and Madison Pike currently owned
by Mr. Joseph Knapp. It is currently zoned single family (R-1C) and they are
asking for a change to neighborhood commercial (NC). The Northern Kentucky Area
Planning & Zoning staff recommendation was to disapprove the change because it
was not a part of the Comprehensive Plan. But the Kenton County & Municipal
Planning & Zoning Commission voted (12-1) to approve the zone changes to
neighborhood commercial.
8.   Mr. George Hoffman from the Transportation Cabinet updated council in
regard to the placement of the new construction of Highway Route 17. He
indicated that construction is set to begin next spring. He stated that
seventy-five percent of the property has been either purchased or the owner has
been contacted. The plans for the section from Pelly Road to Nicholson are
currently being designed with plans to turn in the acquisition plans in the
summer of 1999. He informed council that they are in the final stages of the
St. Rt.17 development and no alternative route plans are under consideration at
this time.
9.   There was a lengthy exchange of questions and answers between council and
Mr. Butler and Mr. Hoffman. Issues discussed included sidewalks for the school
children to travel, future widening of St.Rt.536, and the type of development
planned (Dairy Mart w/gas pumps, bank, and pharmacy, dry cleaners and office
space).
10.   Mrs. Steffen stated that she was cautious to vote for the map amendment
since the state cannot give an exact final plan for the placement of the new
state route. Mrs. Henson stated she did not feel the need to put another retail
development similar to the one on the adjacent corner. Mrs. Weber stated that
she had spoken with Mr. Daniels earlier regarding this project and said that
tonight’s discussion did not persuade her to vote in favor of this map
amendment. She stated that she is in favor of providing conveniences for the
residents but felt that five gas stations within a two-mile area were too much.
11.   Mr. Butler read a letter from the property owner, Mr. Knapp (who was also
present at the meeting) wherein he states that he feels his property would be
perfect for commercial development due to the current commercial growth in that
area. Mr. Butler advised council that Mr. Knapp should have the opportunity to
sell his property. He also commented that the Comprehensive Plan did not take
into consideration of St.Rt.17 rerouting plan. He asked council to focus on
K.R.S.100.213 and whether current use is appropriate and proposed use is
appropriate.
12.   Mrs. Weber asked Mr. Butler how they proposed accessing the Fowler Creek
sewer line. Mr. Butler replied that Mr. Daniels’ would be willing to work with
the city engineer for the best way to do that, which would benefit both the
city and some surrounding residents. Mr. Daniels commented that there has not
been one person to speak against this zone change. Mrs. Weber and Mrs. Henson
stated that some residents that are in opposition have approached them. Mrs.
Weber told Mr. Daniels that she is not against all commercial development and
advised him to bring his proposal back to council in a couple of years when a
more definite road plan is in place. Mrs. Henson noted that the final
Comprehensive Plan was passed in December of 1996 and she feels quite sure that
the Planning & Zoning staff was aware of the rerouting of St.Rt.17. Mr. Butler
disagreed and said the road plans were changed more recently, after 1996.
13.   After Mr. Butler completed the group’s presentation, Rebecca Weber made a
motion to override the recommendation of the Kenton County & Municipal Planning
& Zoning Commission to approve the map amendment proposed in proceedings
numbered 1349R. The basis of this motion is as follows:
1.     A factual determination from the Kenton County & Municipal Planning &
Zoning Commission record of those proceedings that the facts described in the
staff report are true and correct.
2.     The following conclusions from the facts described in the staff report:
A.     The proposed map amendment is not in agreement with the adopted
comprehensive plan.
B.     The existing zoning classification of the property involved in the
proposal is appropriate; and the proposed zoning classification is
inappropriate.
C.     There have been no major changes of an economic, physical or social
nature within the area involved which were not anticipated in the adopted
comprehensive plan, and which have substantially altered the basic character of
the area.
D.     There is no compelling need for the proposed zoning map amendment.
Jaimie Henson seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with five ayes.
Motion carried with a 5-0 vote.
14.   Mr. Daniels commented that he has never seen a council prepare a motion
in advance to deny a zone change. Mrs. Weber stated that two motions had been
prepared; for and against the change.
15.   The City Administrator advised council that he would like authorization
to hold a silent auction of all fixtures and unwanted items left in the Police
Station at 5290 Madison Pike since the police department has moved to the
second floor of the Kenton County Courthouse. He also suggested having the
building razed possibly by the Independence Fire District.
16.   Mrs. Weber made a motion to dispose of all equipment and fixtures left in
the old police station and to have the building destroyed. Jaimie Henson
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 5-0.
17.   Lt.. Shawn Butler reported that the police department has made the
transition from the station at 5290 Madison Pike to the new location on the
second floor of the Kenton County Courthouse. He reported they are looking into
an intercom system and signs for their new quarters. He stated that the
D.A.R.E. grant in the amount of $27,000 had been renewed. Also a new grant has
been awarded to the police department in the amount of $22,000 to fund overtime
for Community Crime Prevention. Currently there are six active block watch
programs and this new grant will help to fund that endeavor. Sgt. Ed Bailey is
the administrator of this grant.
18.   Al Bowling reported to council that he is working with Mr. Gary Haynes
who is interested in purchasing a lot on the north side of Marshall Road &
Decoursey which presently does not meet the city’s building set-back
requirements. The current zoning (RRE) was approved in 1980 before this
property was annexed into the city. The size of the lot is a little over an
acre and Mr. Haynes would like to purchase it if the city will give him relief
on the setback requirement so that he can build a house. Mr. Bowling suggested
asking the No. Ky. Area Planning & Zoning staff to make a recommendation on
this. Mayor Gabbard suggested talking to Mr. Wichmann first to discuss the
legal research and get his recommendation. Mr. Wichmann commented that he
thinks if the same person owns two non-conforming lots then it is treated as
one lot.
19.   Mr. Bowling presented council with photos of the Brentwood of
Independence apartment buildings behind the Independence Towne Center. He
pointed out that in the photos the front of the buildings are first floor brick
wrapped, but the rear of the buildings show only the lower level is brick
wrapped. This is particularly noticeable on the side of the buildings. Mr.
Bowling has met with the developers to discuss this and he suggested council
accept the buildings as is. There was a brief discussion surrounding this type
of building condition for future development in the city. Mr. Wichmann stated
that with Brentwood the brick wrap was part of the condition of the zone
change, which the city cannot go back and change. Mr. Bowling advised that in
the future the city should stipulate a percentage figure for brick material.
20.   Rebecca Weber made a motion to take a short break, seconded by Ken Weber.
Motion carried with all ayes.
21.   At 9:25 p.m. Jaimie Henson made a motion to reconvene the regular
meeting, seconded by Rebecca Weber. Motion carried with all ayes.
22.   Dan Briggs, Cardinal Engineering, presented council with a written report
with updates on various sewer and road projects. He reported that Bob Exeler of
the Independence Christian Church has informed him that the church board is now
hesitant about granting a sewer easement to a private individual. He told Mr.
Exeler all decisions regarding sewering that area of Madison Pike was up to the
city. He reminded council that Cardinal Engineering has submitted a couple of
cost estimates for sewers along this section of Madison Pike and are waiting
for authorization to prepare plans and bid documents for the construction.
23.   Mr. Briggs advised council that initial work had begun on Hartland Park
and Shaw Park. The Hartland Park drainage is basically complete but the grading
is unfinished due to a third contractor building concrete park bench pads in
the grading area.
24.   Mr. Briggs also reported that HP Contracting is requesting retainage
money to be released as they feel the work they did on Plantation Heights Phase
II section of the Fowler Creek sewer project is complete. HP’s attorney has
written the city regarding this retainage. Mr. Briggs will give all pertinent
information to Mr. Wichmann. Mr. Wichmann advised council that he would review
this information and send a response letter to HP’s attorney.
25.   Under old business, discussion ensued on the proposed 1998/99 Budget.
Since a new budget was not passed by July 1st, Mr. Wichmann advised that the
city would operate under the previous fiscal year budget by reverting back to
the original dollar amounts. This is specifically addressed for cities, under
the K.R.S. Mrs. Weber and Mrs. Henson said that if this was the case then why
couldn’t the city install streetlights in the Beechgrove area. Mayor Gabbard
replied there was no line item designating money for street light installation.
The streetlighting line item is for the expense of electricity utilities. Mrs.
Henson asked if the current proposed budget had included the carryover amounts
from the 1997/98 fiscal year for the recreation department. Mayor Gabbard said
those figures would not be available until the Financial Report is completed
around the end of July.
26.   Mrs. Henson said a revenue line item would need to be added to the
proposed budget to include revenue received from the auction of the police
station fixtures and equipment. This should be revenue under the general
government department budget, not the police department budget.
27.   Mr. Scott suggested that council address any questions regarding the
proposed budget to him before the next council meeting so that the budget
process can move forward as quickly as possible.
28.   Mrs. Henson stated she was not ready to have a first reading of the
proposed budget, as she would like to look over the recent changes and try to
find more money for the Recreation Department. Mr. Weber commented that the
hold up for him is the road budget. He does not feel $200,000 is an adequate
amount for road repairs especially since the city established the five-year
road improvement program three years ago. Repairs to Holten Drive need to be
addressed; whether to assess the business owners or completely be funded by the
city. Mayor Gabbard commented that the city had spent 1M plus in the last
couple of years for road repairs and that in order to present a balanced budget
the street repairs line item would have to be cut. Mr. Weber commented that
while he feels the city needs to adhere to a three-month reserve, perhaps
council should consider spending down some of the reserve in order to fund
capital expenses such as Holten Drive and a Municipal Building fund. Mr. Weber
stated that he feels the projected revenue is going to increase considering
payroll tax from the two new schools and new commercial development at the
Independence Towne Center.
29.   Mr. Scott suggested that this fall and winter the city start a cycle of
putting out bid specs in February/March for capital expenses.
30.   Mrs. Henson and Mrs. Weber agreed that it is hard to be prepared to do a
first reading of the budget considering they are handed a new budget at every
meeting. Mrs. Weber noted that one of her concerns with the proposed budget is
the salary increases and the fact that some employees are receiving higher
increases than others. She would like to see a breakdown of each employee’s
salary. Mrs. Weber stated that if council is not happy with the next budget
presented to them that perhaps they might form a committee of council members
to draft a budget proposal. Mayor Gabbard stated he thought that was a good
idea. He also advised council to direct all their concerns regarding the
proposed budget to the City Administrator.
31.   At 10:05 p.m. Rebecca Weber made a motion to enter into an executive
session to discuss possible litigation. Ken Weber seconded the motion. Motion
carried with all ayes.
32.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to go back to the regular session, seconded by
Mrs. Weber. Motion carried with all ayes.
33.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to adjourn, seconded by Mr. Weber. Motion
carried with all ayes.

August 11, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
1.   Mrs. Weber called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Rebecca Weber, Jaimie Henson, Ken Weber, Anita
Steffen, Barbara Gabbard and Scott Holten answered roll call. Also in
attendance were the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Frank
Wichmann.
2.   Mr. Scott made a motion to have the council member with the highest votes
(Rebecca Weber) to preside over tonight’s meeting, as Mayor Gabbard has
resigned. Mrs. Steffen seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
3.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the resignation of Mayor Isaac Gabbard.
Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with five yes votes
and one no vote from Mrs. Gabbard.
4.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to accept the council minutes of the June 9,
1998 meeting. Mr. Holten seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
5.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the council minutes of the June 23,
1998 meeting. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Mrs. Henson abstained from voting
as she was absent that meeting. Motion carried with five yes votes and one
abstain.
6.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to accept the council minutes of the July 14,
1998 meeting, as amended. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Mr. Holten abstained
from voting as he was absent that meeting. Motion carried with five yes votes
and one abstain.
7.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the council minutes of the August 3,
1998 special council meeting. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Mrs. Henson
abstained from voting as she was absent that meeting. Motion carried with five
yes votes and one abstain.
8.   Mrs. Weber opened the floor to audience comments before proceeding with
the meeting. A resident petitioned the council members to pass the proposed
text amendments to the zoning ordinance Section 9.23 which pertains to the
parking and storage of large vehicles. He stated that he felt the law should be
more lenient to allow residents to keep their recreational vehicles, etc. on
their property. He submitted a petition to Mrs. Henson with signatures from
others who share his view.
9.   Since the resident brought this subject up, Mrs. Weber suggested moving
this topic up from Old Business to discuss it. Mrs. Henson informed those in
attendance that the purpose of the text amendment was an attempt to protect the
densely populated areas (subdivisions) of the city while allowing the larger
property owners the right to store larger vehicles. The proposed changes to
this ordinance were given to council for review and a lengthy discussion
ensued. Mrs. Weber stated that some of the council members felt the ordinance
should remain as is, but were willing to look at possible changes that would be
less restrictive on property owners of one-half acres plus. Mrs. Henson feels
Independence is unique in the fact that the city has several densely populated
areas as well as many rural sections. Mrs. Gabbard commented that she was still
uneasy about making these text changes and thinks it might complicate matters.
Some of the discussion centered on the parking of commercial tractor-trailers
and whether they were owner/operator for a home business or employee take home
vehicles. Mrs. Henson felt the proposed changes would allow school bus drivers
to take the bus home overnight. But it was pointed out that most school busses
exceed the proposed twenty-four foot restriction in the proposed amendment. Mr.
Weber stated that he feels council has tried to work on this but agrees with
Mr. Holten and does not want to make changes to Section 9.23 of the zoning
ordinance. He stated that most zoning ordinances are to protect the citizens
from unkempt property, which is a determent to the city in general. Mrs. Henson
stated that when she first took these proposed changes to the Planning and
Zoning Commission last summer, they agreed our parking ordinance was too
restrictive and would be willing to approve a more lenient ordinance. She feels
it could be enforced by the city zoning administrator.
10.   Mrs. Steffen made a motion to make application to the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning & Zoning for review and recommendation of text amendments to
Section 9.23 of the zoning ordinance as submitted. Mr. Holten seconded the
motion. Motion carried five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Holten.
11.   Under new business, council discussed filling the vacant seat of the
Mayor. Mr. Holten handed out the resume of a resident who has submitted an
application for the interim mayor. Mrs. Weber commented that applications for
interim mayor would be accepted until August 15, 1998. Mr. Holten stressed the
urgency of filling the position as soon as possible. Mrs. Weber reminded the
council members that while the city administrator can sign checks and take care
of the daily business, that only the mayor can sign certain contracts, etc.
12.   The City Attorney, Frank Wichmann, advised council that it would be
safest to fill the mayor position thirty days from Mayor Gabbard’s actual
resignation which was July 31, 1998 and not the KRS effective date which was
August 11, 1998. He stated there is a gray area between the actual resignation
date and the effective date and felt it would be the safe thing to do to name a
interim mayor by August 30, 1998. He also reminded council that in order to
call a special meeting a majority of the council members would need to sign a
request to hold the meeting. Mr. Holten drafted the document by hand and it was
signed by five council members (Mrs. Gabbard did not sign it) and given to the
City Administrator.
13.   Mr. Holten made a motion to hold a special council meeting on August 18,
1998 at 8:00 p.m. to interview candidates at fifteen-minute intervals and
possibly select the interim mayor. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll call
was answered with all ayes. Motion carried.
14.   Mr. Gary Scott, City Administrator, read the proposed Resolution
authorizing the city to file for a 1998 Kentucky Community Development Block
Grant. Mr. Scott explained that while the grant is for funds up to $1,000,000,
the city is asking for approximately $200,000. Mrs. Gabbard asked Mr. Scott
what the source would be for the city share of this matching grant. Mr. Scott
was not sure of that yet, but would look into that if the application is
granted. This resolution is just making application for the grant. He explained
that this resolution is council just giving the authority to go forward in
seeking this grant.
15.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to approve Resolution 1998-R-05 authorizing the
filing of a 1998 Kentucky Community Development Block Grant Application. Mr.
Holten seconded the motion. Roll was answered with all ayes. Motion passed.
16.   Mr. Holten made a motion to adopt the proposed property tax rate of $.160
per $100.00 of assessed value for the 1998 calendar year. Mr. Weber seconded
the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried.
17.   Mr. Weber made a motion to read the proposed ordinance setting the
residential trash collection fee for the 1998 calendar year. Mr. Holten
seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
18.   There was a brief discussion regarding the cost increase for trash pick-
up. Mr. Scott explained that due to EPA regulations and mandates the solid
waste cost continues to rise and this increase is passed on to the city. Some
council members commented they have received complaints from residents
regarding Rumpke’s service. They agreed to look more closely at Rumpke’s
contract for this service at the time of yearly renewal.
19.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the first reading of the proposed
ordinance setting the trash collection fee of $84.60 for the 1998 calendar
year. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Motion passed with five yes votes and one
no vote from Mrs. Steffen.
20.   The next item on the agenda was the proposed 1998/99 fiscal year budget.
Discussion ensued on employee pay raises. At an informal meeting with the city
administrator on August 5, 1998, some of the council members agreed to a 4%
across the board pay increase and to go to a paid time off schedule. The
additional time off would be written into the personnel policy, which is
currently being updated. Mr. Holten felt this would be a good compromise as
money is not a sole motivator. Mr. Weber agreed, commenting that the employees
he spoke with were receptive to additional time off with pay. Mrs. Gabbard
stated that she did not feel the loss of employee moral would be worth the
small 1-% savings to the city budget. Mrs. Steffen commented she feared the
city police department would lose officers with so many other local departments
hiring. Mr. Weber stated that he believed Independence is in the top 50% of the
cities regarding salary structure. He wants to keep and attract qualified
people, but with other line items being cut in the budget this year, he does
not feel the city can afford to give a better raise this year. Chief Porter
handed-out information regarding figures from other police departments in the
greater Cincinnati area. Mr. Holten remarked that they are larger communities
with larger budgets than Independence. Mr. Holten also feels the city provides
a good employee benefit package. Mrs. Weber stated it is difficult to explain
large employee pay raises when money is badly needed for street repairs.
21.   Mrs. Henson commented that the budget was showing additional revenue but
not showing where it was being expended. She recommended the $19,000+ overage
in revenue be put into the Hartland Park to put the park in usable condition.
Mr. Holten suggested it be used for the city’s share of the $20,000 matching
grant the city recently received for park trails. Council agreed to this.
22.   Discussion resumed once again on the pay raises. Mrs. Henson stated the
difference between 4% and 5% increase was only $7,000 overall and she did not
feel this was an outrageous amount. Mrs. Weber stated that the 4% she agreed to
was up from the original 3% that she wanted to give.
23.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to reflect a 5% pay increase for all twenty-
seven city employees in the proposed 1998/99 budget only. Mrs. Gabbard seconded
the motion. Roll call vote was answered with four yes votes and two no votes
cast by Mr. Weber and Mrs. Weber. Motion carried.
24.   Mr. Scott said he would have the changes discussed at this meeting
implemented and asked council to be prepared to have a first reading of the
proposed 1998/99 budget at the special meeting on August 18, 1998.
25.   Mr. Scott reported to council that the new pay plan currently being
prepared, will include merit raises. He hopes to have the entire personnel
policy ready for council to adopt by the end of this year. He will get a copy
of the current policy to the city attorney for review. Mr. Wichmann will also
need to review the revised policy before adoption by council. After some
discussion it was decided to hold a Personnel Policy Committee meeting at 6:00
p.m. on August 18, 1998 at the city building.
26.   Chief Porter reported that the police department has been awarded a
Community Crime Prevention grant. This grant has a lot of flexibility and he
has already increased bike patrol in several areas of the city.
27.   Al Bowling, Building Inspector, reported that he has been approached
regarding a lot on Mills Road which does not meet the city’s current building
requirements but did meet the county’s at the time of annexation. City sewers
are not available for this lot (size is 1.079 acres) so discussion centered on
the use of a septic tank. Mr. Wichmann advised council that if all requirements
are met, the owner could build on this lot without meeting the city building
requirements.
28.   Mr. Bowling also reported that the Shaw Estates Subdivision is close to
recording a final plat. The zoning commission is requesting a letter of support
regarding a retention/detention pond planned on the site. This particular pond
adjoins another lot. Similar ponds have also been designed in the Liberty
Orchard and Reveres Crossing subdivisions. Council asked Dan Briggs of the
Cardinal Engineering who is required to maintain these retention ponds. Mr.
Briggs replied that he is not aware of any edict that makes the city
responsible for the ponds. Mr. Finnell, one of the developers of Shaw Estates,
stated that a homeowner’s association is being formed for this subdivision and
it will maintain the pond. Mr. Wichmann stated that Area Planning & Zoning is
requiring a letter of support for the pond because interpretation of the zoning
is up to the zoning administrator (in this case, Al Bowling) and may be
different from the interpretation of their zoning staff.
29.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to direct the city attorney to draft a letter
to the Area Planning & Zoning Commission regarding this retention pond and to
bring back to council for review. Ken Weber seconded the motion. No roll call;
motion carried with all ayes.
30.   Mr. Scott advised council that he met with a Mr. Meyer who wants to run
city sewer lines to three existing houses near Oby Drive and Madison Pike plus
he wants to build another house, so he would like to sewer a total of four
houses. Mr. Meyer is willing to pay the cost of this himself. Mr. Scott stated
that it is 340 feet from the right of way main line to the rear tap in for
these four houses. A discussion ensued between council and Dan Briggs of
Cardinal Engineering regarding the sewering of several “pocket areas” in the
city. Mr. Briggs stated that he was just waiting for direction from council to
design these sewer tie-in sections. Mrs. Weber stated that the city would need
to treat all “pocket areas” equally, as there are a lot of them. She stated
that one area that has been left dangling is the area of Madison Pike near the
Independence Christian Church. Mr. Briggs stated that he supplied the city with
a cost estimate to sewer this area but was never directed to design that
section of sewer lines. Mr. Weber feels the city should secure the easements
and tie in as many homes in the area as possible. Mr. Bob Exeler, who is a
member of the church board, commented that the church would like compensation
for any sewer easement given to the city for restoration work plus additional
recompense. Mr. Briggs stated that another access would be off Carrie Way,
which would be better served than crossing the church property. He also felt
the design should serve as many homes as possible. Council briefly discussed
making these assessment projects. Mr. Wichmann explained that if council chose
to assess the property owners for the sewer improvement project, there would be
a series of ordinances, public hearing, etc. and this could take about two-
three months to complete. He also stated that if easements are not obtained
freely it could take longer.
31.   Mr. Holten made a motion to direct the city engineer’s office to prepare
reports as required by statute for an assessment project to sewer the “pocket
area” on Madison Pike near Carrie Way. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried.
32.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to direct the city engineer’s office to prepare
reports as required by statue for an assessment project to sewer the “pocket
area”on Jimae Court and another “pocket area” on Madison Pike near Oby Drive.
Mr. Holten seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried.
33.   Mr. Briggs advised council that a walk through on Phase I in Plantation
Heights has passed inspection and a final release has been given. The 10%
retainage is due and payable to Michels.
34.   Discussion arose regarding the possibility of updating the McMillan Drive
and Fowler Creek sewer pump stations with new impellers in order for the
stations to work more efficiently and be more cost effective. Mr. Briggs
estimated the cost to be approximately $40,000. Mr. Weber asked the city
administrator to research the city finances to see where the money could be
found to fund this expense. He suggested the Fowler Creek maintenance fees
could be used to pay for the new impellers. The possibility of a grant may be
available to “gravity feed” the Fowler Creek pump station. The city
administrator and the city engineer will look into this.
35.   Mr. Holten made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mr. Weber. The motion
carried with all ayes. The meeting adjourned at 10:40 p.m.
   ______________________________________

August 18, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
1.   Mrs. Weber called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. She explained that the
purpose of the meeting was to discuss and take possible action on electing an
interim mayor to fill the unexpired term of Isaac Gabbard who resigned on July
31, 1998. Also on the agenda was a possible second reading of the 1998 property
tax rate, possible second reading of the 1998 trash assessment rate and
discussion and possible first reading of the 1998/99 budget.
2.   Council members Rebecca Weber, Jaimie Henson, Ken Weber, Anita Steffen,
Barbara Gabbard and Scott Holten answered roll call. Also in attendance was the
City Administrator, Gary Scott.
3.   Mr. Holten stated that he wanted to go on record as objecting to legal
counsel’s absence. Mrs. Gabbard commented that she understood that Mr. Wichmann
would be here near the end of the meeting before council made any decisions.
Mrs. Henson stated that she understood Mr. Wichmann to say he would send a
representative from his office for the first part of the meeting. There was a
brief discussion regarding Mr. Wichmann’s absence, with council deciding to
proceed as Mr. Wichmann had stated that he could be here by 8:30 –9:00 p.m.
4.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to move into executive session to discuss
personnel matters. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
5.   At 8:20 p.m., Mrs. Henson made a motion to return to the regular meeting.
Mr. Holten seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
6.   Mr. Holten thanked the candidates that applied for the interim mayor
position. Those applying were Donna Yeager, Jim Kudera, Robert Scherder and
Marion Schadler.
7.   Mr. Holten made a motion to appoint Jim Kudera as interim mayor. Mrs.
Henson seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one
no vote by Mrs. Gabbard.
8.   Mr. Holten made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance setting the 1998 property tax rate at $1.60 per $1, 000 of assessed
value. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Scott
read the ordinance.
9.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the second reading of Ordinance No.
1998-0-06 setting the 1998 property tax rate. Roll call was answered with all
ayes. Motion carried.
10.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to have a second reading (the summary version)
on the proposed ordinance setting the trash collection assessment for 1998. Mr.
Holten seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
11.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept Ordinance No. 1998-0-07 setting the
trash collection assessment at $84.60 for the 1998 calendar year. Mr. Weber
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried.
12.   Next on the agenda was discussion of the 1998/99 proposed budget.
Discussion centered on the proposed employee 5-% salary increase. Mrs. Henson
stated the revised figures in the police department salaries were higher than
agreed on at the last meeting. Chief Porter explained that some of the officers
were due for their 6-% raise they are given when they come off of probation and
some have had increases since July 1. Mrs. Henson stated she does not feel an
employee that was not employed as of July 1, 1998 is entitled to the 5-% raise
nor should they receive a 5-% raise on top of the 6-% raise. Chief Porter
stated that this was the only way to keep pace with inflation and to increase
the starting pay. Mrs. Henson and Mr. Holten disagreed and felt that the pay
plan is addressed in the personnel policy and has no effect on the budgetary
raises.
13.   Mrs. Steffen, Mrs. Weber and Mrs. Henson expressed reservations at having
a first reading of the budget until the salary adjustments are made. Mr. Holten
stated that he felt the budget is a working document and is not “written in
stone.” Mrs. Henson stated, for the record, that she would not vote for a
second reading if these salary figures were not amended by the next meeting.
She also requested a list of employee salaries as of July 1, 1998. Mrs. Weber
asked the clerk to reflect Mrs. Henson’s request for employee salary
information in the official minutes of this meeting.
14.   Mr. Holten made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed 1998/99
budget. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
15.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the first reading of the proposed
1998/99 budget. Mr. Weber seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all
ayes. Motion carried.
16.   Mr. Weber made a motion to adjourn at 9:10 p.m., seconded by Mrs. Henson.
Motion carried with all ayes.

August 25, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening Statements
1.   Mayor Kudera called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Rev. Fightmaster of Beechgrove Baptist Church gave the invocation.
Council Members Rebecca Weber, Jaimie Henson, Ken Weber, Anita Steffen, Barbara
Gabbard and Scott Holten answered roll call. Also in attendance were the City
Administrator, Gary Scott and the City attorney, Frank Wichmann.
2.   Mayor Kudera addressed council regarding his interim position as mayor by
stating that it was an honor to serve the City of Independence. He detailed
what he hopes to accomplish over the next four months and assured the members
of council that he will keep them apprised of city business.
3.   Mr. Holten welcomed Mayor Kudera and publicly thanked the other interim
mayor candidates for taking the time to apply for the position. The candidates
included Donna Yeager, Robert Scherder and Marion Schadler. Mrs. Steffen asked
that council and mayor send a letter to the candidates thanking them.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
4.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to adopt the minutes of the August 11, 1998
council meeting, as amended. Scott Holten seconded the motion. Roll call vote
was answered with all ayes.
5.   Mr. Holten made a motion to adopt the minutes of the August 18, 1998
Special Council meeting, as amended. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll call
was answered with all ayes.
Privileges of the Floor
6.   A representative from Intermedia Cable made a presentation to council
about the new digital and internet services the company will be providing.
Intermedia acquired TKR Cable on April 30, 1998. The new services will be added
by August 31, 1998 and will include a single line digital system, 200 channel
options with 130 being digital, high speed internet access, and more pay-per-
view channels. Intermedia will invest $24M in the re-building of the cable
system and it should be completed in January 1999 for the Independence area.
7.   Barbara Hellman addressed council regarding the proposed new jail site on
Webster Road. She read a statement from citizens opposed to the site and
requested support from the council and mayor. Several members of council stated
they have individually attended Kenton County Fiscal Court meetings and have
voiced their positions regarding the jail site. Mrs. Henson asked Ms. Hellman
if she had taken the statement and shared her concerns to the Fiscal Court. Ms.
Hellman replied that she had. Mrs. Steffen expressed her concern that the
Fiscal Court may allow the jail to be operated as a private facility. Mrs.Weber
stated that council does care about this issue and the fiscal court has assured
her they are still looking for alternative sites and the Webster Road site is
not a done deal. Mrs. Gabbard said she thinks the majority of the citizens are
against the Webster Road site and she is also concerned about the privatization
of the facility. Mayor Kudera commented that he shared Ms. Hellman’s concern
but stated no one wants the jail located in his or her community and felt the
county government was struggling with this issue. He encouraged Ms. Hellman and
other concerned citizens to work on presenting solutions to the fiscal court
not just oppositions.
End Privileges of the Floor
8.   Mrs. Gabbard questioned Mayor Kudera regarding two items in the minutes of
an administrative staff meeting that was inserted in the council packets. She
asked about severing contact with ex-Mayor Gabbard and other candidates and
requiring mayoral/council candidates to fill out a public records request form
when asking for public records. On severing contact with the ex-mayor, Mayor
Kudera replied that he wanted assurance the city office was not turned into a
campaign forum for any council/mayoral candidate. He also assured Mrs. Gabbard
that the staff meeting minutes would be adjusted to reflect that all persons
requesting public records must fill out a public records request form.
Executive Session
9.   At 8:00 p.m. Mrs. Henson made a motion to go into an executive session for
the purpose of discussing the appointment of office personnel. Mr. Holten
seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
10.   At 8:35 p.m. Mr. Holten made a motion to return to regular session of the
meeting. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
City Clerk Appointment
11.   Mr. Weber made a motion to promote Pat Taney to the non-elected office of
City Clerk of Independence to become effective immediately. Mrs. Weber seconded
the motion. Roll call vote was answered with all ayes. Motion carried.
Committee Meetings Scheduled
12.   After some discussion, council scheduled the following committee
meetings: Personnel Policy Committee will hold a meeting on September 1, 1998
at 6:00 p.m. at the city building; and the Building Committee will conduct a
meeting on September 1, 1998 at 8:00 p.m. at the city building.
Proposed 1998-99 Budget
13.   Mrs. Henson began by pointing out she found some mathematical errors
while reviewing the budget. She also noted a few line items were changed since
the first reading of the budget at the last meeting. Mr. Wichmann advised that
if the line items were changed a new first reading would need to be read. Mrs.
Henson reviewed the proposed changes with council, noting the corrections.
Aside from the mathematical corrections on Schedule A, the changes included:
line 52-Northern Ky. Area Development $0 to $3,500; line 88-Police Specialist
from $73,000 to $89,000; line 89-Police Officers from $325,000 to $300,000 and,
line 152-Hartland Park playground equipment $13,442 to $19,442. Mrs. Gabbard
asked if these changes still presented a balanced budget. Mrs. Henson replied
yes. Mrs. Henson and Mrs. Weber expressed the importance of renewing the city’s
affiliation with the Northern Kentucky Area Development District as they offer
many services. Mrs. Henson stated they have been very helpful on several
occasions even though the city has not been a member for the last two years.
After further discussion with the city attorney on how to proceed with a second
reading, it was decided to have a second reading on the budget read at the last
meeting and then proceed with a first reading on an ordinance to amend the
budget.
14.   Mr. Holten made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance 1998-O-08
adopting the budget for the 1998-99 fiscal year. Mrs. Henson seconded the
motion. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Wichmann read Ordinance No. 1998-O-
08.
15.   Mr. Holten made a motion to adopt Ordinance 1998-O-08 approving the 1998-
99 fiscal year budget. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll call was answered
with four yes votes and two no votes by Mr. Weber and Mrs. Weber. Motion
carried 4-2.
16.   After Mr. Wichmann drafted a proposed ordinance to amend the 1998-99
budget ordinance to include the latest revisions, Mr. Holten made a motion to
have a first reading of the amended 1998-99 budget ordinance. Mr. Weber
seconded the motion. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Wichmann
read the proposed budget amendment.
17.   A brief discussion ensued wherein Mr. Holten tried to persuade the other
council members to vote in favor of this budget amendment so that it could be
passed as an emergency ordinance (an emergency ordinance requires a unanimous
vote). Mrs. Weber stated she could not in all conscience vote in favor of the
budget, as she does not agree with cutting services the city provides to
residents in order to give 5 percent salary raises to employees. She stated
when she sees an increase in revenues then she could see increasing employee
salaries. She said she has voiced this concern for months and could not give
her approval of this budget.
18.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the first reading of the proposed
ordinance amending the 1998-99 budget. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll
call vote yielded four yes votes and two no votes from Mrs. Weber and Mr.
Weber. Motion carried and the first reading passed. Mr. Wichmann advised a
second reading would be required to pass this ordinance.
Building Inspector, Al Bowling
19.   Mr. Bowling reported to council that the Board of Adjustments had a
hearing regarding a proposed day care/nursery school facility on Thomas Drive
wherein the builder, Carl Johnson, was requesting a conditional use permit to
complete the construction. Originally this new construction was for a single
family residential home. The Board of Adjustments granted the conditional use
permit subject to conditions such as ingress and egress, etc. before final
permits will be issued.
Cardinal Engineering
20.   Mr. Whitacre, City Engineer, informed council that a pump came loose at
the McMillan Drive pump station, it twisted and came out of it’s housing and
broke an impeller and rotor. The pump station is now in need of emergency
repairs and he anticipates that it may take 10-12 weeks to get the parts
needed, as they are special order. Mr. Whitacre gave council several costs
estimates, from a minimum $5,000 to return the pump station to it’s current
position to $120,000 to do a major overhaul of the station. Mr. Whitacre’s
advise as the best option was to upgrade in order to increase the flow
(currently the pump is near capacity) and serve all development in those
drainage areas. He stated this is an emergency because if the remaining pump
goes down the city will have major problems. As is, the pump is operating on
borrowed time. He stated the upgrade will cost $51,800 and will take a few
weeks to get the pump. He also reported the Fowler Creek station needs new
impellers, estimated at $8,000 to keep up with the Marshall Road pump station.
A brief discussion ensued regarding how to fund these emergency expenses;
probably from the sewer maintenance fees collected and the sewer fund’s capital
outlay.
21.   Mr. Whitacre also reported that his office working on cost estimates that
council requested to provide sewers to a few “pocket areas” of the city and a
street repairs/maintenance list.
22.   Mrs. Steffen asked Mr. Whitacre to inspect a water drainage problem on
Clubhouse Drive near house number 1066 (Mrs. Steins). This problem affects
about 5-6 homes. Apparently two pipes are going into a drop box, the pipes are
too small and water is gushing. Mr.Whitacre has looked at this some time ago
but agreed to take another look to see if the pipes are adequate and see what
the city may need to do. He said he would write up a proposal and cost
estimate.
City Administrator
23.   Mr. Scott reported he has the draft for the Senior/Community Center grant
available at the city office for anyone who wishes to look at it. The grant
application is due in Frankfort by August 31, 1998. The city should be
receiving the $20,000 Trail Grant money awarded by the state sometime in
September.
24.   Mrs. Weber asked how the streetlighting plans for the Beechgrove area
were coming along. Mr. Scott replied that Dan Briggs of Cardinal Engineering
was in the process of putting together a plan.
Chief of Police, Ed Porter
25.   Chief Porter reported that Patrol Officer Matt Mullins will graduate on
September 4, 1998 and will proceed into the FPO program. Mrs. Henson asked
Chief Porter to bring new officers, PO Mullins and PO Tonya Jumonville to a
council meeting for introductions. Mrs. Henson also asked the status of having
the old city/police building demolished. Mr. Scott stated the building has been
stripped of all fixtures and the electricity will soon be taken out. Mrs.
Henson asked the building inspector if the building had been officially
condemned and expressed some concern that the Kenton County Fiscal Court could
basically “hold us captive” now in charging rent for the second floor of the
courthouse which the Police Department now occupies. Mr. Bowling replied that
the building had not been officially condemned but he felt it was not wise to
return to it. Chief Porter also reported that a auction had been set for
Saturday, September 12, 1998 to auction off abandoned vehicles and the remains
(file cabinets, desks, air conditioner unit, etc.) of the building. The public
sale will be held on the parking lot of the city/police building and at Kenton
County Motors where the vehicles are stored. Mrs. Henson also asked Chief Porte
to post signs at the old building to direct people to the police department on
the second floor of the courthouse.
City Administrator
26.   Mr. Scott reported to council that he is looking into sewering some
additional “pocket areas” of the city, mainly the southern and central
sections. The areas include Roselawn Dr., Peach Dr., Apple Dr. and Cherry
Drive. He stated these areas were left out of the main sewer project as it was
too expensive, but due to so many complaints coming from this area he feels the
city needs to look at this again. He has asked the city engineer’s office to
start this process while he investigates the possibility of obtaining federal
grant money to fund this project. Mrs. Weber stated she had discussed this
subject with the governor and he too is looking into this federal program. Mrs.
Weber agreed that this needs to be re-addressed with the hopes of providing
this area with sewers.
Adjournment
27.   At 9:30 p.m. Mrs. Henson made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mrs.
Weber. Motion carried with all ayes.

                  James Kudera, Mayor

Patricia H.Taney, City Clerk
September 8, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kudera called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance and the invocation. Council Members Rebecca Weber, Jaimie Henson,
Ken Weber, Anita Steffen, Barbara Gabbard and Scott Holten answered roll call.
Mrs. Steffen was absent due to duties with the U.S. Naval Reserves. Also in
attendance were the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Frank
Wichmann.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
2.   Mr. Weber made a motion to accept the council minutes of August 25, 1998,
as amended. Jaimie Henson seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all
ayes. Motion carried.
Privileges of the Floor
3.   Mrs. Glenna Chapman, a resident on Carrie Way addressed council regarding
raw sewage that is running onto her property along the Independence Christian
Church on Madison Pike and originating from the Hargrove property at 5233
Madison Pike. She stated she and her husband have spoken to representatives
from the E.P.A. and the church and the city building inspector, Al Bowling
regarding the situation. When the church extended their parking lot the
drainage pipes were never connected. Mr. Bowling stated that the building plans
that were submitted to the city showed the pipes were to be connected to the
sewer line. Mrs. Chapman expressed concern that this could become a health
hazard. She feels she is getting the “run around” and asked council to have
something done. Mayor Kudera assured Mrs. Chapman the city was aware of the
situation and is having the city engineers work on a solution to the problem.
4.   A discussion ensued regarding the sewering of several homes in this area.
It is one of the “pocket areas” that the city engineer is presently working on
designs and cost estimates. Mr. Holten asked how quickly construction could
begin once cost estimates are submitted to council. Mr. Wichmann advised
council that if this project was to be an assessment project that it would take
several months and he outlined the procedures of such a project as required by
K.R.S. He figured by the time the public hearing was held, easements, obtained,
etc., that it would be next spring before construction could be started. Mr.
Scott, City Administrator assured Mrs. Chapman that he along with Mayor Kudera
and Dan Briggs of Cardinal Engineering would look at the problem tomorrow.
End Privileges of the Floor
Chief of Police, Ed Porter
5.   Police Chief, Ed Porter, introduced the newest member of the police force,
Matthew Mullins to council. He has been employed by the city for three months
and just graduated from the academy and will enter the FTO program.
Ordinance No. 1998-0-09 (amending 1998-99 Budget)
6.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to have the second reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend Ordinance No. 1998-0-08 (1998/99 Budget). Mr. Holten
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried. Mr.
Wichmann read proposed Ordinance 1998-0-09 amending Ordinance 1998-0-08.
7.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept Ordinance No. 1998-0-09 amending
Ordinance 1998-0-08 as read. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mrs. Weber and Mr. Weber.
Motion carried 4-2.
Annexation Issue – 35 Pelly Road – Wayne Ferguson Property
8.   Mr. Wayne Ferguson, 35 Pelly Road, spoke to council regarding property he
owns on Pelly Road. He stated he owns two contiguous lots on Pelly Road and he
is considering selling the vacant lot but was inquiring about the possibility
of having the city annex it so that it could be tied into city sewer which he
feels will make it more marketable. Mr. Bowling, Building Inspector reported
that both lots back up to the Liberty Orchard subdivision and is six feet from
the main sewer line. Mr. Ferguson asked several questions relating to the
possible annexation, as he wasn’t sure if he wanted to be annexed or not
depending on the conditions that would be imposed by the city. Dan Briggs
explained the debt reduction assessment that all users of the Fowler Creek
Sewer System pay into. Mr. Ferguson stated he is also considering requesting a
zone change for this vacant lot in order to sub-divide into 2-3 lots. Mr.
Wichmann advised zone change and annexation could be done at the same time but
that the zone change would have to have approval from the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning & Zoning Commission. Mayor Kudera suggested the city engineer,
building inspector and city administrator inspect the property with Mr.
Ferguson so some answers could be obtained in order to proceed with the
annexation process, if Mr. Ferguson so chooses.
Deferred Compensation for Kentucky Public Employees
9.   Mr. Donald Mossman, representative for the Kentucky Deferred Compensation
program made a presentation to council outlining the benefits for the city
employees. He stated the city was under no obligation to match employee
contributions by offering this program and that all administration fees would
be deducted from the individual employee accounts. He stated that all
contributions go in tax-free and grow tax-free. It would be taxed as ordinary
income when it is withdrawn. There are two plans available and is vested the
first day. Mr. Scott advised council the only expense for he the city would be
a nominal fee charged by the city’s payroll service company (Paycor). Also this
program has no affect on Social Security or C.E.R.S. (retirement program). Mr.
Mossman asked for the city approval by passing a Resolution adopting this
program.
Resolution 1998-R-06
10.   Mr. Holten made a motion to read the resolution in support of offering
city employees enrollment in the state deferred compensation program. Motion
seconded by Mr. Weber. No roll call. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Wichmann
read the resolution.
11.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept Resolution No. 1998-R-06 approving the
deferred compensation program for city employees. Mr. Weber seconded the
motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
Cardinal Engineering
12.   Mr. Briggs advised council that the current ordinance that regulates the
type of streetlights the city will permit to be installed on city maintained
streets preclude the use of high-pressure sodium lights. During recent
discussions with Owen Electric regarding the installation of new streetlights
on Beechgrove Drive, he was informed this utility company only uses high-
pressure sodium lights. Mr. Briggs stated they use this type of light, as it is
more economical to service and operate. He stated the city’s only other option
would be to purchase, install and maintain their own light system in Owen
County’s service region. He asked council to look into amending the present
ordinance (1997-0-22) to allow the high-pressure sodium lights when no other
type is available. Mr. Wichmann stated he would prepare an ordinance amendment
for council to review at the next meeting.
13.   Mr. Briggs informed council that the development section of the
Independence Towne Center known as Lakeside of Independence is possibly being
converted from townhomes for sale to rental units. This may change the status
of the streets from private to public wherein the developer would be asking the
city to accept for maintenance. If the streets were dedicated as public streets
they would have to be upgraded to public street standards. Mrs. Weber suggested
adopting an ordinance that would address the need to make all private roads
built to public use standards. Mr. Wichmann advised that the existing zoning
ordinance has included compliance regulations which are standard provisions in
all zoning ordinances. Mrs. Weber would like to see this reviewed before more
of this type of building changes occur. Mr. Briggs said he would also like to
see an ordinance that would protect the city from sub-standard building. Again,
Mr. Wichmann stated he felt the city has some existing protection now, as most
zoning ordinances state that the conditions must be brought up to standard in
order for the city to take over maintenance. He also advised council the city
has the authority to repair a deteriorated street with multiple owners then
assess the residents of that street for the expense. Mayor Kudera stated they
would review the ordinances the city currently have in place and then see what,
if any, ordinances need amendments or drafting.
14.   Mr. Briggs updated council on the status of the McMillan Drive pump
station, which is undergoing emergency repairs. The pumps have arrived and are
awaiting installation. He reported the labor to rebuild the station will be
approximately $45,000.00. The station will be shut down and a by-pass installed
while the new pump station is being erected. Mayor Kudera advised council that
he has instructed that the dismantling of the pump station be documented to see
if it was originally constructed per specifications. If it was not, the city
will investigate the possibility of recovering some of the expenses of
rebuilding a new station.
Police Department
15.   Ed Porter, Chief of Police, reminded council of the police auction to be
held on Saturday, September 12, 1998 at 10:00 a.m. The auction will begin at
Kenton County motors where approximately 50 vehicles will be auctioned then
move to the old city/police building to dispose of the contents of the
building. Preview of items to be auctioned will begin at 8:00 a.m. Saturday
morning.
16.   Chief Porter also reported a Child/Special Persons I.D. Program would be
held on September 22, 1998 at the Wildwood Place Apartments at 3910 Wynnbrook
Drive between the hours of 6:00 and 8:00 p.m. It is being expanded to include
special persons to see the kind of response it gets.
City Administrator
17.   Mr. Scott reported that he is currently setting up two interviews with
candidates for the part-time Zoning Administrator position. He hopes to have
the position filled by October 1, 1998 and would like to take a pro-active
approach to enforcing the zoning laws.
18.   Mr. Scott also reported he has met with representatives from the
businesses on Production Drive regarding storm drainage problems. Mr. Scott
will have the city engineering firm look into the water run-off problems. He
stated there might be a need for a retention basin. He will begin to look into
the drainage problems on the west side of the city. Mrs. Weber asked if this
was a recently developed problem. Mr. Briggs replied it has been over three
years; since the large expansion on Holten Drive.
Production Dr./Holten Dr. Study
19.   Mrs. Weber made a motion to authorize Cardinal Engineering to do a study
on the storm drainage problems in the Production Drive & Holten Drive in the
Industrial Park area and report back to council. Mrs. Henson seconded the
motion. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
City Attorney Report
20.   Mr. Wichmann reported that he is spending time on several litigation
matters for the city. A motion to dismiss has been filed in the lawsuit wherein
several Northern Kentucky cities have been named regarding the flooding of the
Banklick Creek area. The hearing is in approximately two weeks. He stated most
cities do not have any torte insurance to cover this kind of liability. He
advised that Captain Bill Howard’s termination has been appealed. Also, Mr.
Gene Daniel’s suit against the city for denying a zone change has a hearing
scheduled for September 28, 1998. He is also working on a few smaller lawsuits.
Mayor’s Report
21.   Mayor Kudera advised a new police officer has been hired and will begin
on September 21, 1998. He is already certified and will go directly into the
FTO program. Also, in the Clerk’s Office, Kathy Stenger will move up to the
Assistant Clerk position and that Cheryl Vornberger will move into the Deputy
Clerk position.
22.   Mayor Kudera reported that the city’s October edition of the newsletter
would provide one-half page of space to all candidates running in the general
election for position of mayor or council member.  He stated that all
candidates have been asked to submit a profile. He has had positive reactions
to this gesture.
Second Annual Christmas Walk
23.   Mrs. Henson announced the Second Annual Christmas Walk has been scheduled
for December 9, 1998. Anyone wishing to help with the plans or make inquiries
can call herself or Donna Yeager.
Adjournment
Mr. Holten made a motion to adjourn at 9:03 p.m.; seconded by Mr. Weber. Motion
carried with all ayes. Meeting adjourned.
______________________________________
                  James Kudera, Mayor

September 22, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kudera called the meeting to order at 7:05 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance and the invocation. Council Members Rebecca Weber, Jaimie Henson,
Ken Weber, Barbara Gabbard and Scott Holten answered roll call. Mrs. Steffen
was absent due to duties with the U.S. Naval Reserves. Also in attendance were
the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Frank Wichmann.
2.   Police Chief Porter introduced one of the new police officers: Patrol
Officer Tonya Jumonville. P.O. Jumonville came to Independence from the Park
Hills Police Department. Chief Porter reported that her hire date was effective
June 25, 1998 and that she has completed the FTO Program and is actively
patrolling the streets.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
3.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to accept the council minutes of September 8,
1998, as amended. Mr. Holten seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
Privileges of the Floor
4.   Mayor Kudera cautioned the audience that the privilege of the floor was
not to be used to make political statements and he would interrupt anyone who
abused this time to address council.
5.   Mrs. Kathi Hargrove, a resident of 5233 Madison Pike, addressed council
regarding her sewage drainage problem at that address. Mrs. Hargrove stated she
and her husband bought the house in 1996 unaware that it was not tied into city
sewers. In 1997 she discovered she has no sewage system as she found that raw
sewage was running on the property and the neighboring Independence Christian
Church property as well. She told council that this problem existed for many
years before she purchased the property and she has been trying to get some
help with correcting this but has not been able to get a straight answer from
anyone. Since July of 1997, she has been seeking assistance from the former
city mayor, the city building inspector, Al Bowling, the E.P.A. and the Board
of Health. In 1997 the Board of Health recommended using a gravity flow pump as
they would not allow a septic system as the property is not large enough to
support one.
6.   On behalf of the city, Mayor Kudera apologized for any injustice she has
experienced and also the delay in getting some answers to repair the sewer
drainage problem in her area. The mayor turned the floor over to Dave Whitacre,
the city engineer, who presented some options to correct the matter.
7.   Mr. Whitacre presented some options (with cost estimates) which include:
1)   Install a septic tank and leach field         $ 8,000 - $12,000
2)   A city sewer tie-in involving 4-5 neighboring properties – easements would
need to be obtained which may be a problem                  $45,400
3)   Grinder pumps which require maintenance and have a 5-10 year life
span                  $31,500
4)   Install a city sewer tie-in 22 feet deep under the funeral home parking
lot with all neighboring properties being able to gravity in         $39,250
8.   Mr. Whitacre stated that only four houses would reap any benefit from this
sewer project as the other homes in this area already have sewers. Mayor Kudera
commented that he didn’t think council would be able to reach a decision
tonight as each option would have to be examined further and suggested forming
a sub-committee to come up with a solution. Mr. Weber suggested the sewer
committee hold a special meeting to address and review the options and bring a
recommendation back to council. Mr. Whitacre advised that it would take several
months if the city decides to take on this project before anyone could tap in.
Mr. Weber commented that he hoped the residents would be willing to wait if the
city could assure them it is being worked on. He stated he would rather see a
permanent solution to this problem instead of a temporary fix.
9.   Mr. Holten asked if the homes that are already connected to city sewers by
private laterals were legal and if they were paying maintenance fees and debt
reduction fees. Mr. Wichmann stated they would be considered legal if easements
had been obtained. Mr. Scott stated he believes those tapped into sewers in
that area are currently paying maintenance and debt reduction fees. Mrs. Glenna
Chapman of 10 Carrie Way stated that her father-in-law installed and owned the
private sewer system that many of the surrounding homes on Madison Pike and
Carrie Way tapping into and those homes did not pay a tap-in fee. In 1980-81
ownership of the sewer plant was turned over to the city along with $10,000.
10.   Mayor Kudera suggested setting a committee meeting to start the process
of solving this situation. Mr. Holten suggested scheduling a meeting of the
Sewer Committee for September 30, 1998 at 8:00 p.m. at the city administration
building. Mr. Holten stated that while individual costs can not be determined
yet, it could run between $6,300 and $15,000 per property to sewer this “pocket
area.”
11.   Mr. Holten asked the city engineer if preliminary reports had been
compiled for the sewering of the other “pocket areas” as discussed at the
previous council meeting. Mr. Whitacre stated they were still working on the
cost figures. Mrs. Henson suggested the sewer committee discuss those areas,
too.

has been completed and will be submitted for approval at the same time as the

Clubhouse Dr./Wedgewood Dr. Drainage Study
14.   Mr. Whitacre reported the McMillan Drive pump station re-construction
should begin by next week. He also stated proposals are being prepared for work
on Clubhouse/Wedgewood Drives and storm water runoff on Production Drive. He
said the detention basins for the storm water runoff of Production Drive are
not holding water and he will need to research this to see why. It may take up

16.   A discussion ensued as Mr. Holten stated his objection to allocating
funds to study storm water drainage problems in one area of the city and not
others. He stated the city might become inundated with requests for storm water
studies. Mr. Scott commented that he was including a drainage survey in the
October edition of the city newsletter. The survey has been used elsewhere and
should generate a lot of responses. When completed surveys are returned to the
city office he will meet with the city engineer to develop a plan to address
the problem areas. Mr. Scott recommended going ahead with the Clubhouse/
Wedgewood Drives study and then address the other areas at a later date. Mrs.
Weber stated council has been hearing about these drainage problems for years
and they are not going away. She commented that council needs to start
somewhere and the survey sounds like a good idea. Mr. Scott stated the survey
would give the city an inventory of problem areas. Mr. Holten expressed
reservations that the city may be appearing to shoulder the liability for
correcting these problems. Mr. Whitacre stated he would address the problems
private versus city, which would be public assessment projects, where there are
current easements and where there are no easements. Mr. Weber suggested some of
the engineer costs could be recouped if an assessment project is done. Mr.
Holten would like to see council set guidelines as to how involved the city
will become in these projects.
17.   Mrs. Weber amended her motion to allocate $1,000 to Cardinal Engineering
to work up a proposal to solve the storm water drainage problem at Clubhouse/

address these problems; any implementation to solve the problems and passage of

answered by all ayes. Motion carried.
