October 13, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kudera called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance The invocation was given by Reverend Randy McCafferty of the
Independence Christian Church.
2.   Before roll call was taken, Council Member Scott Holten presented former
Mayor Marion Schadler with the plaque that had been affixed to the old city
building at 5290 Madison Pike when it was dedicated in 1979. Mr. Holten thanked
Mr. Schadler for his many years of dedicated service to the city. Mr. Schadler
accepted the plaque and commented that up until 1979 city records were kept in
a private home until the property on Madison Pike was acquired and converted
into city offices. Mayor Kudera stated it was an honor to grant Mr. Schadler
the dedication plaque in appreciation for his public service to the city.
3.   Council Members Ken Weber, Anita Steffen, Rebecca Weber, Scott Holten,
Barbara Gabbard and Jaimie Henson answered roll call. Also in attendance were
the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Frank Wichmann.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
4.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the council minutes of September 22,
1998, as amended. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with
all ayes.
Halloween Trick-or-Treat Hours
5.   Mrs. Gabbard asked if council was going to set Halloween trick-or-treating
hours as she has been getting some phone calls regarding this. Mayor Kudera and
Mr. Scott stated that the time for trick-or-treating this year would be between
the hours of 6:00 and 8:00 p.m. on Saturday, October 31, 1998. There was a
brief discussion about the setting of Halloween hours every year. Some council
members felt the hours should be conjunctive with other cities.
6.   Mr. Holten made a motion to direct the city attorney to prepare an
ordinance setting the annual Halloween hours in conjunctive to other cities.
Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
Introduction of New Finance Director
7.   Mr. Scott introduced Mrs. Amy K. Guenther as the city’s new Finance
Director. She comes to the city from Von Lehman & Company CPA firm. He stated
Mrs. Guenther is a Certified Public Accountant and will be an asset to the city
in this new position. Council members welcomed Mrs. Guenther. Mrs. Guenther
informed council of her credentials and advised them she is setting the city’s
finances up on the computer which will provide more accurate and timely
financial reports.
Audit Report for 1997/98 Fiscal Year
8.   Linda Chapman from Rankin, Rankin & Company CPA firm made a presentation
to council on the audit of the 1997/98 fiscal year financial statements.
Council members asked Ms. Chapman some general questions regarding the audit.
Mrs. Chapman pointed out a few recommendations for areas that need improvement.
One being to get the city finances computerized which the city is in the
process of doing with the hiring of Mrs. Guenther, the new Finance Director.
She stated this would provide a more accurate set of numbers on the monthly
financial statements and give a more realistic view of where the city stands
financially. She also noted the city needs to keep better records of assets.
Mrs. Chapman also commented the city is getting the best certificate of deposit
interest rates she has seen.
Discussion of Bonding of the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt
9.   Mr. Joe Nance, an investment banker with Ross, Sinclaire & Associates,
Inc. appeared before council to provide an update on where the city stands
regarding the re-financing of the Fowler Creek Sewer Project debt from a short-
term loan into a long-term loan. He informed council that a payment was due in
December, which amounted to $343,794.00 ($175,000 principal and $168,794
interest). The current anticipation note has a $5.8 million balloon payment due
the year 2003 for the entire debt. He stated the anticipation note was
originally meant to be a short-term loan until the construction of the sewer
project was completed. He also emphasized that since current interest rates are
very attractive – at a record low – it would be a wise time for the city to
bond this debt. He explained that in order to calculate the total dollars
needed to bond this debt several considerations were taken into account. They
include the current sewer debt reduction and maintenance fees being collected,
and the projection over the next 4-5 years of current, planned and speculated
residential developments and fund balances available. Mr. Nance assured council
that the numbers being presented are good projection figures. He stated there
would be fees involved to finance a bond (fiscal agent fee, bond counsel fee,
bank fee, bond rating fee, etc.) and the bonds would be bid out which his
company would handle. The grand total of bonds to bid out is $6,060,000.00.
Mrs. Henson asked if bonding this debt would extend the time of the term of the
loan. He replied that it would but that the city would be locking in a historic
lower interest rate. Currently the average rate is 4.39% for 25 years (and
4.59% when you factor in the other fees involved) making a $402,000 per year
payment which will be considerably lower from the amount the city is now
paying. He commented that if the city delayed this matter for a year or so the
interest rates may go up – with odds that the rate could go down a bit more –
but eventually the rates will start to climb again. Mr. Nance also pointed out
that assuming the city continues to grow every year council could review this
and lower the quarterly assessment fee charged to the users or leave as is to
build up a cash reserve to pay off the bond. He advised that by bonding the
debt now they would not be tying the hands of future seated councils to lower
the fees. Mr. Nance stated these bonds could be paid off after 12 years with no
penalty for early payoff.
10.   A lengthy discussion ensued regarding the pros and cons of bonding this
debt. Mr. Holten expressed concern that the debt reduction fees would be set up
into another fund and not used to retire the debt. Mr. Nance stated it would be
set up, to be adopted by ordinance, to include convenants wherein restricted
funds could not be used for other purposes. Mayor Kudera summarized by stated
this was a good time to bond this debt with the low interest rate locked in for
twenty-five years and asked for a motion to authorize Ross, Sinclaire and
Associates, Inc. to proceed with the bonding of this debt. Mrs. Gabbard
interjected by suggesting council hold a few public meetings to get citizen
input since they are the ones to pay for it. Mayor Kudera explained that by
procrastinating the city is taking the risk of the interest rate rising. Mrs.
Henson stated she feels the council members have been entrusted by the citizens
to make these decisions. Mrs. Weber commented this is the best news she has
heard in the five years since this sewer project began when she wasn’t sure if
the city could pay for it and liked the option that future councils would be
able to lower the debt reduction fee if feasible. Mrs. Gabbard commented she
was given the prepared ordinance at this meeting with no opportunity to review
it. Again, she expressed the desire to have open meetings for the citizens to
comment. Mr. Holten stated that we live in a representative government and
every matter cannot be delayed in order to hold public meetings before deciding
important matters.
11.   Mrs. Weber made a motion to authorize Ross, Sinclaire & Associates to
proceed with the bonding procedures as presented and prepare an ordinance
pertaining thereto. Mr. Holten seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered
with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mrs. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1.
Extending Sewer Lines to “Pocket Areas”
12.   Mr. Gary Scott reported the Sewer Committee met as scheduled and
discussed the three options outlined by Cardinal Engineering to sewer several
homes in the Madison Pike/Carrie Way area. The preliminary selection chosen by
the committee was option #2 as it would best serve this area. It would involve
installing a sewer line 22 feet down for a gravity flow system across Carrie
Way. The estimated cost for this option is $39,900. Mr. Scott asked for
council’s approval to have the city engineer’s office complete a comprehensive
study to proceed with the process. Mr. Holten commented the city would finance
the project and assess five property owners as all five will benefit. Mrs.
Chapman, a resident on Carrie Way asked council what would be done with the
manhole on her property. Mayor Kudera responded that the manhole was a separate
issue that would have to be addressed at another time. Mr. Briggs commented the
manhole and the existing ground is not stable enough to support a sewer line
without extensive excavation. Mayor Kudera stated the area is not compacted and
Option #2 is the least intrusive and least expensive and the city will proceed
with it. Mrs. Gabbard asked if the funeral home has given their permission to
cross through their lot. Mr. Holten replied that he spoke with Mr. Ed Currin
and although he has not signed easements yet he most likely will be agreeable.
13.   Mr. Holten made a motion to authorize the city engineers to prepare a
comprehensive report as required by Kentucky statute for a sewer assessment
project for the five homes in the Madison Pike/Carrie Way area, which is listed
as Option #4 in the September 22, 1998 council meeting minutes; and request the
city attorney to obtain the necessary easements by the Spring of 1999. Mrs.
Henson seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with all ayes (6-0).
Motion carried.
14.   Mayor Kudera stated an attempt would be made to get this process underway
by the first regularly scheduled meeting in November (11-10-98) or possibly
scheduling a special meeting.
Sanitation District – Discussion of Transfer of Sewer Lines
15.   Mayor Kudera stated that Mr. Jeff Eger and other representatives from the
Sanitation District were in attendance to discuss the possible agreement of a
merger of the city’s sanitary sewer lines. Council members voiced their
concerns and asked several questions about the proposed agreement. Mrs. Henson
wanted to know if the city could continue to extend lines to residents. Mr.
Eger stated the city could build at city expense and assess the resident users
for the projects, that there is no language in the proposed agreement that
would exclude this. He stated that in the past five years the District has not
turned down any extensions. The District would have no objection to any project
funded 100% by the city. Mr. Eger explained that the District has to go through
the same procedures that any city would to build new lines in communities.
There was discussion regarding the $203,220 repairs needed in the city
recommended in the 1992 GRW study. Mrs. Henson questioned why the city would
have to reimburse the District 100% of this cost when the statutes state 50%.
Mr. Eger replied the 50% reimbursement amount was extended to those cities that
opted into the District before the deadline. And Mr. Eger stated the District
would honor that study, which does not reflect repairs made to date. Mr. Eger
also discussed with council the process by which interested residents can
petition for sewer lines in their neighborhood. Once again, Mr. Eger stated the
process is the same the city would have to use as this is mandated by K.R.S.
Mrs. Gabbard asked what advantage there would be for the city to transfer the
sewer lines to the District as she feels the city would be giving up control.
Mr. Eger stated the city would no longer have the expense of maintaining the
sewer lines, which can be costly. Discussion also centered on the rates and how
the money could be used. Mayor Kudera reminded council the city recently
incurred approximately $100,000 in repairs on two pump stations (Fowler Creek
and McMillan Drive) and it is unknown what the Beechgrove area may cost the
city in the future. He stated the city does not have the resources and manpower
the District has. Mr. Eger stated the Sanitation District would increase their
tap-in (“capacity connection fee”) fee to $1800 effective August 1999.
16.   Another discussion ensued on the storm water management issue. The Phase
II Clean Water Act will require a report be submitted by the year 2001 on storm
water management. The state is currently developing a storm water management
plan. Mr. Weber asked Mr. Eger what cost would be incurred and how to assess
that cost. Mr. Eger replied it was too premature to discuss this issue but it
should be a nominal fee in relation to the service provided. He also stated
that the three county judge-executives would have to approve the plan.
17.   Mr. Eger restated that by merging with the Sanitation District the big
savings for the city would be the cost of maintaining the sewer lines. Mr.
Holten agreed the city is not prepared to take on the responsibility and needs
to pursue the merger issue. Mrs. Gabbard agreed for the need to revisit the
merger issue but does not see the need to do it now. Mayor Kudera stated the
option was available through December 31, 1998 and council would be holding
short meetings, one in November and one in December. Mrs. Henson commented she
felt it was irresponsible to dump this decision on the next seated council and
is prepared to take some action. Mrs. Weber remarked that the proposed
agreement is very different from the one proposed a few years ago. A few years
ago she was concerned the sewer project would not be completed if merged with
the District. Also the matter of the storm water management is something the
city will not be able to handle. She feels this agreement is a better plan.
First Reading of Proposed Ordinance to Transfer Sewer Lines to Sanitation
District No.1

1.

Resolution No. 1998-R-07 (Supporting H.R. 4171)

enforce laws to improve the safety of those persons providing assistance at
roadside accident scenes. The laws would require motorists approaching a
roadside emergency to decrease the speed of their vehicle to 10 mph less than
the posted speed limit and move to the traffic lane for their direction of
travel which is furthest from the road side emergency scene.

Privileges of the Floor

October 20, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kudera called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. by stating that the
purpose of this special meeting was to discuss and take possible action on two
issues. He stated the first order of business on the agenda was the matter of
bonding the Fowler Creek Sewer Project debt. Secondly, there would be
discussion with the possible second reading of an ordinance to transfer the
city’s sanitary sewer system to the Sanitation District No. 1.
2.   Barbara Gabbard, Anita Steffen, Ken Weber, Jaimie Henson, Scott Holten and
Rebecca Weber answered roll call. Also in attendance was Gary Scott, City
Administrator and Linda Schaeffer, City Attorney filling in for Frank Wichmann.
Bonding of the Fowler Creek Sewer Project Debt
3.   Bond Counsel attorney, Dirk Bedarff, of Peck, Shaffer & Williams addressed
council regarding the bid process for bonds. Mr. Bedarff told council that by
bonding the current bank note it would be financed on a permanent basis. He
advised that the city would need to advertise for bids for the purchase of the
bonds (in compliance with KRS Chapter 58) then the bonds would be awarded to
the best bidders. Mrs. Steffen asked what the interest rate would be and Mr.
Bedarff advised the interest rate would be set when the bonds are sold. He also
stated the proposed ordinance estimates an interest rate of 4-½% with a cap of
5-½%. Mrs. Gabbard asked why it would be bonded for 25 years. Mr. Bedarff
stated this allows the city to be at the upper limit. Mayor Kudera reminded
council that at the last meeting they were informed the city had the option for
an early pay off after only twelve years penalty free. Mayor Kudera also
recalled they were advised at the last meeting that the future council will
have the discretion to reduce the $70 quarterly debt reduction payment
currently being paid by the sewer project users or to keep it the same. Mr.
Scott stated the debt will be there whether or not council chooses to bond it
and it may take longer than 25 years if the number of users does not increase
significantly. Mrs. Henson added that the original ordinance was open-ended in
regard to the number of years it would be paid off. She also commented the city
could be debt free sooner if council planned wisely.
Motion for 1st Reading of Bonding Ordinance for Fowler Creek Sewer Project Debt
4.   Mr. Holten made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed ordinance
authorizing the issuance of $6,060,000,000 in bonds for financing of the Fowler
Creek Sewer System Project debt. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion and requested
the ordinance be read in summary form. Motion carried with all ayes. City
Attorney, Linda Schaeffer read the proposed ordinance.
5.   Mayor Kudera opened the floor for discussion. Mrs. Gabbard questioned
mayor/council why this matter was being acted on so quickly. Mrs. Gabbard also
stated she felt the city should hold public meetings so residents could voice
their opinions regarding the bonding of this debt. Several council members
responded. Mrs. Weber commented that she felt this debt should have been bonded
long before now and that council is doing what is best for the city. Mr. Weber
also felt this was a wise move for council to bond this debt, but suggested the
possibility of notifying all affected homeowners by letter explaining what the
purpose of the ordinance was and why council has made this decision. Mayor
Kudera responded to Mr. Weber’s suggestion by advising the longer the city
waited the higher the risk of the interest rates rising. Mrs. Henson stated
some citizens are being misinformed regarding this issue and wanted to stress
that the debt reduction fee the users of this sewer system are being charged is
not going to increase with the bonding of this debt. She also expressed concern
that the city will not be able to make future payments with the current
financing; especially the 5.5M balloon payment that will be due in the year
2003. Mr. Weber stated that as city officials they are being fiscally
responsible and expressed the need to move forward with this.
6.   Mayor Kudera asked the clerk to call the roll on the motion. Roll call was
answered with four yes votes from Mr. Holten, Mrs. Henson, Mrs. Weber and Mr.
Weber; one no vote from Mrs. Gabbard and one abstain from Mrs. Steffen. Motion
carried 4-1-1.
Resolution 1998-R-08 (Authorizing Advertisement for Bond Bids)
7.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to read Resolution 1998-R-08 authorizing the
advertisement for bids for the purchase of a principal amount of $6,060,000 of
General Obligation Improvement Bonds. Mrs. Weber seconded the motion. Motion
carried with all ayes. Ms. Schaeffer read the resolution.
8.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to adopt Resolution 1998-R-08; seconded by Mrs.
Weber. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mrs.
Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
Transfer of the City Sanitary Sewer System to the Sanitation District No. 1
9.   Mr. Holten made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
Ordinance No. 1998-0-10 to transfer the city’s operational sanitary sewer
system over to Sanitation District No. 1. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion.
Motion carried with all ayes. Ms. Schaeffer read the ordinance.
10.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to accept the second reading of Ordinance No.
1998-0-10. Mrs. Weber seconded the motion.
11.   Mayor Kudera opened the floor for any discussion. Mrs. Steffen commented
that while she sees both the pros and cons regarding the transfer of the sewer
lines to the Sanitation District she is concerned the city might loose some
control. She added that she wants to do what is best for the city. Mrs. Steffen
also discussed some other concerns but Mayor Kudera assured her those concerns
were covered in the ordinance. Mr. Weber stated he feels the Sanitation
District will not extend sewer lines in areas just for the sake of extending
the lines, as they will not be able to afford that without recovering the cost
from users. Mrs. Henson stated she feels the proposed agreement with the
Sanitation District will allow city input regarding any future construction of
sewer lines. Mrs. Weber remarked that joining the Sanitation District at this
time was in the best interest of the city. She stated that she was against
joining the District a few years ago when the city was in the process of
constructing the Fowler Creek Sewer Project improvements as that agreement had
too many restrictions and no guarantee that the District would complete the
project the city had set forth. She continued that she felt the city would have
more freedom with the proposed agreement and would be empowered to extend sewer
lines to other areas if so inclined. Mrs. Weber also maintained that when the
GRW study debt ($203,220.00) was paid off the city could use the debt reduction
fees to other advantages. Mrs. Gabbard interjected that she still didn’t see
what the rush was to transfer the city’s control of the sewer system over to
the Sanitation District and again asked that the city hold a couple of public
hearings for citizen input.
12.   Mayor Kudera closed the floor for discussion and asked the clerk to call
the roll. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by
Mrs. Gabbard. Motion carried with a 5-1 vote in favor.
13.   At 7:35 p.m. Mr. Holten made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mr. Weber.
Motion carried with all ayes. Meeting adjourned.

James Kudera, Mayor

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
November 10, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kudera called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation.
2.   Council Members Ken Weber, Anita Steffen, Rebecca Weber, Scott Holten,
Barbara Gabbard and Jaimie Henson answered roll call. Also in attendance was
the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Frank Wichmann.
3.   Mr. Scott read a letter from former Mayor Marion Schadler wherein he
thanked Mayor Kudera and Council for presenting him with the plaque that had
been mounted on the old city building as it is scheduled for demolition. In his
letter he stated the plaque would be displayed in his Oxley Museum located at
5234 Madison Pike as a reminder of the history of Independence. Mayor Kudera
requested a copy of the letter from Mr. Schadler be attached to the official
minutes of this meeting.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
4.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the council minutes of October 10, 1998
as amended. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Motion passed with all ayes; no
roll call.
5.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to accept the council minutes of the special
meeting of October 20, 1998, as amended. Mr. Holten seconded the motion. Motion
passed with all ayes; no roll call.
Motion (and discussion) to Bond the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt
6.   Mr. Holten made a motion to have a second reading on the proposed
ordinance authorizing the issuance of $6,060,000.00 in bonds for the Fowler
Creek Sewer Project debt. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mrs. Gabbard. Motion
carried 5-1. Mr. Wichmann read the proposed ordinance.
7.   Mayor Kudera opened the floor for discussion relating to the bond issue.
Mrs. Gabbard stated she felt the timing for this was wrong for doing this sort
of major project with a new mayor and council taking office in a couple of
months. She also suggested the city should hold public hearings for citizen
input. Mr. Holten replied he felt the timing is right especially with the
interest rates at an all-time low. He also commented this sewer project has
been on going, from the onset of the planning until the present with the
completion of construction., for approximately nine years, and did not
understand how Mrs. Gabbard could defend her comment that council is rushing
into the bonding of this debt. Mrs. Henson added the city only has enough
financial resources to meet this year’s payment for the present loan for this
debt. Mrs. Gabbard stated the city might have the money for next year’s
payment. Mrs. Henson stated that based on the assessment rates now being
collected the city will not have the money for the next year’s payment. Mrs.
Steffen remarked that while she somewhat agrees with Mrs. Gabbard, she feels
this decision to bond the debt will give the city some flexibility and feels
the need to proceed.
8.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to accept the second reading of Ordinance No.
1998-O-11 authorizing the bonding of the Fowler Creek Sewer Project debt. Mr.
Weber seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one
no vote cast by Mrs. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor for the adoption of
Ordinance No. 1998-O-11.
Discussion on Proposed Amendment of Street Lighting Ordinance
9.   New information regarding the types of lights available for installation
in subdivisions has surfaced and discussion as to whether or not to proceed
with the second reading of the proposed amendment to this ordinance ensued.
Originally, Owen Electric could only install sodium vapor (yellow) lights,
which are prohibited in our current ordinance. Mr. Dan Briggs of Cardinal
Engineering stated that Owen Electric has recently applied for a tariff sheet,
which would allow them to install mercury vapor (white) lights as the city
ordinance mandates. Mr. Wichmann recommended not doing anything on the proposed
amended ordinance, in essence tabling the second reading. Mrs. Henson felt if
the proposed ordinance passed then Owen Electric would install the yellow
sodium vapor lights instead of the white mercury vapor the city prefers. Mr.
Wichmann stated he was not aware of a time limit between first and second
readings of a proposed ordinance.
10.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend the current streetlight Ordinance No. 1997-O-22. Mr. Holten
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried; Mr.
Wichmann read the proposed ordinance.
11.   Mrs. Henson made a motion to accept the second reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend the current street light Ordinance No. 1997-O-22 as read.
Mr. Holten seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with six not votes.
Motion defeated 6-0.
12.   Mrs. Weber commented that she hoped this issue of providing street lights
would not die and stressed the need for council to address this in the future
as many neighborhoods are requesting this service. Mrs. Weber expressed concern
for subdivisions that are having problems with vandalism and asked the police
chief if this type of activity decreases during the winter months. He replied
that generally it does decrease during the cold months with the increase being
in the summer when school is out. Mr. Briggs will keep in contact with Owen
Electric regarding the availability of the mercury vapor (white) lights.
Other Street Lighting Up-dates
13.   Under old business, Mrs. Henson wanted to inform everyone that the street
lights for the Falcon Ridge Subdivision has not been forgotten, rather the
Bristow Road re-construction project has delayed the installation for the time
being. Mrs. Weber asked for an update on the lighting of the main road of the
Hartland Subdivision. Mr. Briggs reported a lighting plan has been submitted
and approved and should be installed soon. He also added that a transformer
would be installed for future use, if necessary. He stated the lights will not
be placed down the center of the boulevard but on the park side and the lights
will be bright enough to illuminate the entire boulevard. Mrs. Weber asked
about “Slow – Children at Play” signs being placed in the new subdivisions. Mr.
Scott replied the signs had been ordered.
Hartland Park “Tot Lot” Bids
14.   Under new business, Mr. Scott stated the city had received three bids for
the construction of a “tot lot” in the Hartland Park. Bids were received from
Jennings, Gametime and Little Tikes Commercial Play Systems. Mrs. Donna Yeager,
IRC (Independence Recreation Commission) Chairperson, presented council with a
report of the evaluation/comparison of each bid received. Mr. Scott went on to
say that the consensus of the IRC was that the best bid was the one submitted
by Little Tikes. It was the highest bid at $19,107.00 (the lowest being
$16,726.00) but included a drainage system. Mr. Scott reported the City of
Dayton gave a good recommendation for Little Tikes. Mr. Holten asked Mrs.
Yeager if she felt the Little Tikes bid was 15% better than the other two bids
submitted as 15% is a substantial difference. She replied that it was because
it met all required specifications and then some. Mr. Steve Feldhaus, council
member-elect, commented the drainage system included in the Little Tikes bid is
in-ground which will drain the water away and is the reason for the price
difference. Mrs. Henson asked what age group this play equipment was designed
for. Mr. Yeager stated it is for the 5-12 years of age range. Mrs. Henson asked
about equipment for the 0-5 age group. Mrs. Yeager commented additional money
would need to be budgeted in order to purchase more playground equipment. There
was a short discussion on the use of chopped tires versus wood chips for the
surface. Mr. Feldhaus stated that fire retardant wood chips are available and
felt this would be preferable over chopped tires which are not fire-retardant.
Mrs. Henson requested “No Smoking” signs be placed in the city parks. Mr.
Holten suggested this might not be a good idea since the state of Kentucky’s
main commodity is tobacco. Mayor Kudera and Mr. Holten thanked Mrs. Yeager for
all the volunteer work she had done on behalf of the city parks. Mrs. Henson
asked when the “tot lot” would be installed. Mrs. Yeager stated the bid
required the equipment to be in place no later than April 30, 1999.
15.   Mrs. Weber asked if the city has insurance coverage for individuals who
do volunteer work for the city. Mr. Scott replied he would check on that with
the city’s insurance agent. Mayor Kudera added he has recently engaged with
Schiff, Kreidler-Shell to handle the city’s insurance needs; a much-needed
change. He went on to say the city was under insured with the old policies. He
stated the new insurance package and carrier went into effect on October 26,
1998 with more extensive and comprehensive coverage. Mr. Scott will check into
coverage regarding large volunteer groups.
Sewering of Carrie Way/Madison Pike “Pocket Areas” – Comprehensive Report
16.   Mr. Briggs of Cardinal Engineering submitted to council a comprehensive
report to sewer the “pocket area” of Carrie Way and Madison Pike. Mr. Briggs
reviewed the report with council wherein five proposals are included and
designed for an assessment project. This sewer improvement would be the
construction of a gravity system between 5233 Madison Pike and 5235 Madison
Pike. Parcels affected include 5233, 5235, 5241, 5243, 5245 Madison Pike and 10
Carrie Way. The only property that currently has sewer service in this project
is 5245 Madison Pike; current owner – Swindler Funeral Homes, Inc. Mrs. Henson
asked Mr. Briggs if he looked at the possibility of going around the funeral
home’s parking lot. Mr. Briggs replied that would add further costs to the
project. Mrs. Gabbard asked if Mr. Currin of the funeral home had given an
easement or was interested in giving an easement to the city. Mr. Briggs
replied no easements had been obtained yet. Mr. Currin who was in the audience
commented he just recently learned of this project and that he is willing to be
a good neighbor but is concerned about being assessed for this project when he
is already tapped in to sewers. Mr. Briggs commented the funeral home is tapped
into a private system not a public one. Mr. Holten stated he would agree to
eliminate the option that includes the funeral home as long as Mr. Currin is
going to take full responsibility for his lateral line. Discussion ensued
regarding the time frame to get this project started. The city attorney advised
that a copy of the comprehensive report would need to be sent to all affected
homeowners and a public hearing would need to be held. Mr. Wichmann also stated
that he would need a day or so to review the report and then speak with the
mayor about setting a date for a public hearing.
17.   Mayor Kudera asked Mrs. Chapman if this plan settled the matter for her.
Mrs. Chapman, 10 Carrie Way, asked what was going to e done about Independence
Christian Church contaminating her lake. Mayor Kudera stated that was a
separate issue. Mrs. Chapman also stated she doesn’t understand why none of the
proposed plans for this section of sewer improvements isn’t utilizing the
manhole on her property. She went on to say that she would speak with her
attorney about suing the city if her manhole isn’t used. Mrs. Henson asked why
she would sue the city if her manhole is not used but sue if the manhole is
used. She stated the city installed this manhole several years ago and feels
the manhole should be removed if it is not going to be used. Mrs. Chapman
stated she grows tobacco and is unable to earn a fair price because of the
condition of the ground around the manhole. Mrs. Chapman requested the council
members to look at her land. Mrs. Henson, Mrs. Steffen and Mr. Scott stated
they would set up a time to inspect the field. Mr. Briggs advised council the
problem is not with Mrs. Chapman’s manhole but with the surrounding land.
Miscellaneous Up-Dates
18.   Mayor Kudera asked Chief Porter about the vandalism problem on the west
side of town. Chief Porter replied a Block Watch Program has been set up in the
Hunters Green Subdivision.
19.   Mrs. Henson informed the police chief she has received reports that
police officers are congregating in area parking lots for what appears to e the
purpose of talking. She stated the budget was increased to include more
officers so that an officer could be in each section of the city on each shift
and wondered why they would congregate. Chief Porter stated the officers are
encouraged to share information so this is within the realm of their duties so
long as it is not excessive. Mrs. Henson also noted that it appears Kenton
County Police are still providing a lot of backup to the city. Police. Chief
Porter responded that often the county police would respond if they are in the
vicinity and find the call interesting.
20.   Mrs. Steffen informed council the OKI Board of Trustees is presently
taking nominations for next year. The city representative needs to be an
elected official. She noted that she would leave copies of the nomination form
at the city office for the newly elected council members.
21.   Mrs. Henson stated the CPCAC is seeking nominations for next year, also.
She stated the city representative does not have to be an elected official; an
be, but not necessary. Mrs. Weber stated that twice she applied for a seat on
the CPC board and never received a response.
Closing Remarks
22.   In closing, Mayor Kudera acknowledged some matters that council had been
working on had been deferred due to more pressing issues taking precedence and
he stated those matters could be placed on the next agenda. He stated the
Personnel Committee should be ready by the December meeting with the updated
manual. He reported the health coverage for the employees is being reviewed for
possible improvement.
23.   Ms. Weber wanted council to be ware of the two co-op students working in
city offices. Tricia Green is a senior at Simon Kenton High School and is
working in the clerk’s office and Jamie Cooper, also of Simon Kenton High
School is working in the police department.
24.   Mrs. Henson announced the Second Annual Downtown Christmas Walk and Tour
would take place on Wednesday evening, December 9, 1998 from 6:00 p.m. until 9:
00 p.m. The walk will open at the Independence Christian Church with the
lighting of the community Christmas tree. Santa Claus, refreshments, door
prizes, horse carriage rides and historic homes will be decorated and open for
viewing. Mrs. Henson encouraged participation and/or attendance.
25.   Mr. Scott informed council he was proceeding with the ISTEA grant
application. In the application he is requesting grant money to help finance
the installment and replacement of sidewalks on Madison Pike beginning at
Summit View Schools to the Independence Towne Center area. This would provide
for continuous walkways closing all present gaps. The grant is due by December
4, 1998 and will be available at the city office for review.
26.   Mr. Scott also commented that he expected to hear something regarding the
Senior/Community Center grant the city applied for no later than the first part
of December.
Cancellation of the November 24 and December 22, 1998 Regular Meetings
27.   Mayor Kudera reminded council that historically the second meetings in
the months of November and December are cancelled due to the Thanksgiving and
Christmas holidays. Council discussed this briefly.
28.   Mr. Holten made a motion to cancel the November 24, 1998 and December 22,
1998 regular council meetings due to the holidays during those weeks with the
stipulation that a special meeting could be held if necessary. Mrs. Weber
seconded the motion. Motion passed with all ayes; no roll called.
Adjournment
29.   At 8:20 p.m. Mr. Weber made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mrs. Henson.
Motion carried with all ayes.

December 8, 1998
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Council Member, Rebecca Weber called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m.
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Ken Weber, Anita Steffen,
Rebecca Weber, Scott Holten, Barbara Gabbard and Jaimie Henson answered roll
call. Also in attendance were the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City
Attorney, Lawson Walker. Mayor Jim Kudera was absent due to outpatient surgery
performed earlier in the day. Mrs. Weber presided over the meeting.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
2.   Mr. Holten made a motion to accept the council minutes of November 10,
1998 as submitted. Mrs. Henson seconded the motion. Motion passed with all
ayes; no roll call.
Second Annual Christmas Walk
3.   Mrs. Henson reminded council of the Second Annual Downtown Christmas Walk
and Tour on Wednesday evening December 9, 1998 between the hours of 6:00 and 9:
00 p.m. The festivities will commence with the lighting of the community
Christmas tree at the Independence Christian Church and the community is
invited to decorate the tree. The Walk and Tour will take place on Madison Pike
between the Independence Christian Church and St. Cecilia Church. Other
activities include carriage rides, tours through the Oxley Museum, visits with
Santa and choirs performing at two locations.
New City Attorney
4.   Mrs. Weber introduced Mr. H. Lawson Walker as the new city attorney.
Finance Reports and Checks Issued List
5.   Mrs. Gabbard questioned the payment made to Estes Engineering which was
listed on the Check Reconciliation Report submitted in the council packets. Mr.
Scott explained the payment was made for outstanding invoices from 1995 in
exchange for city records that Estes Engineering was in possession of. Mr.
Scott stated this payment was for full settlement.
Old Business
6.   It was the consensus of council to forego a first reading on the proposed
ordinance relating to the design and construction of improvements in
developments as the majority of the council members terms would end on December
31, 1998. They felt it would be best for the incoming mayor and council members
to address that proposed ordinance.
Personnel Policy Update
7.   Mr. Scott reported the personnel policy update was being submitted to
council for adoption by resolution. He stated the policy had been sent to the
Municipal Law Center, the Department of Local Government, Northern Kentucky
Area Development District and former city attorney, Frank Wichmann for review.
The changes were made as advised by the professionals. Mr. Weber commented she
had not been given ample time to review the new policy and did not feel ready
to take action on this. Mrs. Gabbard concurred and stated she also had not read
the policy yet. Mr. Weber made comments regarding several sections of the
policy that he disagreed with namely probationary status, performance
evaluations, notice of retirement bonus and the involuntary separation section.
Mr. Holten commented he had questions regarding the Retirement & Reception
section. Mrs. Gabbard stated she felt the grievance procedure section and the
“at-will employees” term were contradictions. A lengthy discussion ensued
regarding these sections of the proposed policy. City Attorney, Mr. Walker
stated he had not read the proposed policy as it was just given to him, but he
advised the council members of the legal aspects on the sections that were
brought up for discussion.
8.   Mrs. Weber commented that updating the personnel policy has been an on-
going project for the last few years and feels it is still not ready for
approval. She would like Mr. Walker to review it and then let the new mayor and
council approve it. Mrs. Henson commented it has taken two years to draw up
this policy and encouraged council to pass it by resolution.
9.   Mr. Walker explained to council the difference between an ordinance and a
resolution and that city policy can be passed by either one. He stated that
ordinances as defined are permanent by nature but that a resolution would be
just as effective. He stated the personnel policy does not need to be adopted
by ordinance and in fact is more economically practical to pass it by
resolution, as a resolution does not require publication. Mr. Holten stated he
felt all members of council would never be able to agree on every section of
the personnel policy and the policy presented to council was far superior to
the present policy.
Motion to Adopt Resolution Number 1998-R-09 (Personnel Policies)
10.   Mr. Holten made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 1998-R-09 updating the
personnel policy. Motion seconded by Mrs. Henson. Roll call vote was answered
with four yes vote and two no votes by Mr. Weber & Mrs. Weber. Motion carried
4-2.
Motion to Adopt Resolution Number 1998-R-10 (City owned Property)
11.   Thomas Rumpke, attorney for Deters, Benzinger & LaVelle law firm,
addressed council requesting the adoption of a resolution that would authorize
the mayor to sign a Release and Waiver of Restrictions for lots 20 & 21 of the
New Frontier Subdivision which is currently owned by the City of Independence.
In 1964 the developer of the subdivision placed a number of restrictions of
record for lots 1 – 21. He explained that in 1976 Swindler Funeral Home
acquired original lots number one and two in order to expand their parking lot.
He went on to say this use was in violation of the subdivision restrictions and
in order to expand the parking lot had to obtain a signed release and waiver of
the restrictions from all the record owners of the remaining lots. At the time
lots 20 & 21 were owned by Union Savings & Loan Association. Mr. Rumpke stated
that Swindler Funeral Home just recently discovered that there is no
recognizable or notarized signature from a representative of that bank on the
release. As the city is the current owner of the lots in question, Swindler is
requesting the city to sign a release and waiver. Mrs. Henson made a motion,
seconded by Mr. Holten to adopt Resolution Number 1998-R-10 authorizing Mayor
Kudera to sign the Release and Waiver of Restrictions for the city owned lots
20 & 21 of the New Frontier Subdivision. No roll call, motion carried with all
ayes.
Chapman Property on Carrie Way
12.   Mrs. Steffen reported she had met with the Chapman’s and inspected their
property on Carrie Way. She stated the ground was so wet they were not able to
get their tobacco out. Mr. Scott and Mr. Briggs commented they too had
inspected the property and said they could not see any evidence where tobacco
had been planted in many years. Mr. Holten stated the Chapman’s have two
problems – 1) Sanitary - which the city is trying to rectify and, 2) excess
storm water running onto their property from the Independence Christian Church,
in which the city should not intervene.
Closing Comments
13.   Mrs. Henson thanked everyone for the last two years she has sat on
council. Mrs. Weber thanked Mayor Kudera for the last several months he spent
as the interim mayor. She stated she appreciated his energy and dedication for
all he was able to accomplish. She also wished good luck to the incoming mayor,
Tom Kriege and new council members.
Adjournment
14.   At 7:50 p.m. Mrs. Henson made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mr.
Holten. Motion carried with all ayes.

1999 Minutes
January 12, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Reverend Charles Steger of Hickory Grove Baptist Church gave the
invocation. Mayor Kriege welcomed everyone and introduced the five new council
members. Council members Jim Ellison, Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps Greg Steffen,
Donna Yeager and Steve Feldhaus answered roll call. Also in attendance were the
City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Lawson Walker.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of December 8,
1998 as submitted. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Motion passed with all
ayes; no roll call.
Request for Sewer Services at Oby Drive & Madison Pike by Mr. Nordman Meier
3.   Mr. Nordman Meier of 11448 Madison Pike addressed council with a request
to have sewer lines extended to two houses he owns at the corner of Madison
Pike and Oby Drive and a third house which he plans to build there. He stated
two easements would need to be obtained which he would like the city to do. He
feels the neighbors would be agreeable to signing easements to cross their
property. After a brief discussion, the city attorney reminded council the city
had recently turned over ownership of the city sewer lines to the Sanitation
District. Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Meier to take his request to the Sanitation
District with the assurance that the city would assist in the process if
needed.
Privileges of the Floor
4.   Mr. Russell Connors of 10950 Taylor Mill Road addressed council regarding
the highly publicized and anticipated Y2K computer crash in the year 2000. He
stated he believes there will be disruptions with the loss of electrical power,
telecommunications and banking services. He would like to see the city make
preparations, suggested employing contingency plans, and offered to be a part
of a group that develops a plan. Mayor Kriege thanked Mr. Connors and advised
him that local government officials have begun to look at the issue and he will
contact him in the near future. The mayor assured him the city would be
investigating some preliminary strategies.
Dr. Dennis Sies, N.K.U. Director of Master in Public Admin. Program
5.   Dr. Sies submitted to council a proposal in which his department would
conduct a services/satisfaction survey for the city. The MPA Program at N.K.U.
would design, administer and evaluate the survey for the city for the sum of
$2,000. The cost of mailing the survey and return postage would be additional.
His proposal suggested mailing the survey with the city newsletter in February.
He stated the survey process would begin immediately and end in May with a
final report to council. Dr. Sies stated that his department has conducted this
type of survey with Grant County and the cities of Fort Thomas and Edgewood.
There was a brief discussion that included what purpose the survey would serve
and how to fund this unbudgeted expense. Dr. Sies commented that the result of
this type of survey is generally used as a planning tool to improve services to
the community.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to proceed with the services/satisfaction
survey to be conducted by the MPA Department of N.K.U. Mrs. Yeager seconded the
motion. Roll call was answered with six yes votes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Northern Kentucky Area Development District Proposals
7.   Mr. Brian Dehner from the NKADD addressed council with a proposal to
perform several risk management projects for the city. The projects include: 1)
the development of a web site, 2) the development of employee job descriptions,
3) the development of an employee performance review and improvement process,
4) the development of an employee benefit and pay plan, 5) the analysis of
compliance of wage and hour laws, and 6) strategic planning. He stated the
total cost for all six projects is $9,000 and he assured council the NKADD
would be flexible with the city regarding payment for these services. Mr. Scott
commented the money for the codification of ordinances would not be spent out
of this year’s budget and suggested using those funds for the proposed
projects. Mr. Dehner stated he would lead the projects with assistance from
three other people in his division. Discussion centered on finding the funds to
back these projects in the budget. Mayor Kriege stated an amended budget would
be presented to council sometime in February.
8.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to enter into a contract with the Northern
Kentucky Area Development District for the proposal and bid as submitted for a
total of $9,000. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all
ayes. Mrs. Gabbard clarified her vote by stating she voted yes on the condition
that the budget would be amended to include this expense. Motion carried 6-0 in
favor.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
Police Department – Ed Porter
9.   Chief Porter reported the Records Management program which links with
other community records at the local police departments went into effect
January 1, 1999 and is totally operational. He also reported his department has
been re-working the operational policies and procedures in order to acquire
state accreditation. He stated they would begin the application process, which
should be complete by July 1999. Mr. Feldhaus asked if receiving the state
certification would lower the city’s liability insurance rate. Chief Porter
felt that it should. Mr. Scott stated he would check with the city’s insurance
carrier to confirm this. In closing, Chief Porter commented the Neighborhood
Block Watch Program, with four current programs, is going well despite the bad
weather.
Building Inspector – Al Bowling
10.   Mr. Bowling suggested to council the need for a zoning text amendment
regarding the R-RE zones. He stated the Board of Adjustments would like to see
this change to avoid unnecessary hearings. The R-RE zone in Independence is
mainly in the Mills Road/Hill-n-Dale Drive areas, which affects many homes.
Mayor Kriege stated that while he has no objection to this request he suggested
Mr. Bowling look at other cities’ restrictions for the R-RE zone and then bring
the text amendment request back to council when he can supply more information.
City Administrator – Gary R. Scott

Contract With H. Lawson Walker As The City Attorney
18.   Mayor Kriege submitted to council two options for contracting with H.
Lawson Walker to provide legal counsel for the city. Under “Plan A” Mr. Walker
would attend all council meetings and perform routine city business for $1,200/
month. “Plan B” would provide for everything except litigation and
administrative hearings for $2,500/month. Council members questioned Mr. Walker
regarding both “Plans”. Mr. Walker commented that he believes the hiring of the
city attorney is an executive power of the mayor and that both “Plans” permit
the city to terminate the legal representation agreement on thirty days notice.
19.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to contract with Mr. Walker as the city
attorney under the “Plan A” proposal. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mrs. Gabbard.
Public Hearings For AT&T Cellular Tower At 5388 Madison Pike

February 11, 1999 at 9:00 a.m. Mr. Feldhaus voiced opposition that the KCMPZ
Commission was holding a public hearing at a time (9:00 a.m.) when most of the
public is unable to attend. He asked the city attorney if he could draft a
resolution to document formal opposition with the Commission. After a brief
discussion, Mr. Walker drafted a resolution petitioning the Commission to
change the time and date of the public hearing regarding the cell tower to be
constructed at the Highland Cemetery on Madison Pike, which he read. Mr.
Feldhaus made a motion to accept Resolution No. 1999-R-01 as read. Mr. Steffen
seconded the motion. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.

00-9:00 p.m. on Friday and 9:00 a.m. – 2:00 p.m. on Saturday.

January 26, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Council members Jim Ellison, Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps Greg
Steffen, Donna Yeager and Steve Feldhaus answered roll call. Also in attendance
were the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney, Lawson Walker.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of January 12,
1999 as submitted. Mrs. Gabbard stated she wanted the minutes to reflect the
reason she voted no on the motion to contract with Lawson Walker as City
Attorney. Mayor Kriege requested the clerk listen to the tape and re-submit the
minutes at the next meeting. The motion died for lack of a second.
Appointment of Kevin Barbian as Zoning Administrator
3.   Mr. Scott introduced Kevin Barbian as the new city’s zoning administrator.
Mr. Barbian is currently a part-time employee of the City of Fort Thomas in the
zoning department and will continue to work for Fort Thomas in addition to
contracting on a part-time basis for Independence. He will begin work for the
city on February 10, 1999 when Al Bowling, Building Inspector, returns from
vacation. Mr. Scott mentioned that Mr. Barbian would take the building
inspection certification exam in March.
Gene Daniels Zone Change Request of the Jos. Knapp Property at 11011 Madison
Pike
4.   Mr. Gene Daniels presented to council his proposal to develop property on
the southeast corner of Madison Pike and Harris Pike, which is currently owned
by Joseph Knapp. He stated the property is approximately 5.5 acres and he would
like council to consider changing the zone from R1-C to NC (neighborhood
commercial). The entire development would consist of a Dairy Mart (with
gasoline pumps) and possibly a drug store, dry cleaners and offices. Mr.
Daniels advised he would develop the property in stages as the land has a lake
and steep hill that would be filled in when the state highway department
reconstructs Madison Pike. The new road will cut through the middle of this
property. Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission approved the
zone change request as they felt no one would erect a residential structure
that would be encased by a highway. The Northern Kentucky Area Planning &
Zoning staff recommendation was to deny the zone change, as it was not part of
the 5-year Comprehensive Plan. A brief discussion ensued regarding the fact
this is the second time Mr. Daniels has brought this request before council.
The previous council denied his request and Mr. Daniels has filed a lawsuit
appealing the city’s adverse decision. Mr. Daniels is requesting the newly
seated council and mayor reverse the previous council’s decision. Since this is
a pending lawsuit, council decided to discuss this issue further in executive
session later on in the meeting.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Administrator – Gary R. Scott
5.   Mr. Scott reported the Annual Planning Session is scheduled for Friday and
Saturday January 29 and 30, 1999. The session will be held Friday from 5:00
p.m. until 9:00 p.m. and on Saturday from 9:00 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. He advised
the attempt of the Planning Session is to put together long range and short
range plans for the city. He also stated that in February he would be working
on forming a Strategic Planning Group that would develop an integral plan for
the city.
6.   In response to questions asked at the last meeting regarding a building
feasibility study contracted a few years ago, Mr. Scott reported that in
researching this matter he learned that bids were accepted and the bid was
awarded to R. Ehmet Hayes & Associates to do a feasibility study. He stated
that for unknown reasons, a contract was never entered into with Hayes &
Associates to actually perform the feasibility study. Mr. Scott advised council
that the city has contracted with GBBN Architects to perform a building
feasibility study, which will include design plans, site plans, building costs,
etc. He stated he would keep council apprised of the progress of the study.
7.   Mr. Scott reported the potholes throughout the city are being repaired as
quickly as possible. Two streets, Holton Drive and Fleming Drive are immediate
problems and Willow Drive is in need of major repairs.
8.   Budget – Mr. Scott advised that an amended budget for the current fiscal
year will be presented to council in February and that discussions/meetings
will soon begin to work on next year’s budget.
Police Department – Ed Porter
9.   Chief Porter reported that Officer Phil Dunford has completed D.A.R.E.
training and will be filling that position in the department. Currently the
D.A.R.E. program services six hundred fourth and fifth graders in four schools
in Independence each week. This program is funded by a grant and is a very
positive program for the department.
Dave Whitacre – Cardinal Engineering
10.   Mr. Whitacre advised council that as soon as he is provided with proposed
funding for the 1999/2000 budget he would begin establishing priority projects
for the coming year. He stated he has a “wish list” of projects that need to be
performed amounting to $450,000. A discussion ensued regarding how to bid out
the road work projects when a final fund amount won’t be determined for a few
months until the budget process is well under way. The Public Works Committee
can begin work on a priority list of street repairs as soon as the committee is
established. Mr. Whitacre stated they would continue to update the 5-year
street plan listing in order to bring the roads up to a decent condition and
continue maintenance on the roads currently in good shape. He reported the
streets are prioritized according to need and that most were very serviceable
going into this winter. He advised council that street repair bids should be
out as soon as possible as the contractors have not scheduled work for the 1999
spring/summer yet. He stated he would need a more accurate dollar amount to be
budgeted for street repairs before bids requested. Council decided to discuss
the street repair matter in more detail at the Planning Session this weekend.
11.   Mr. Whitacre also informed council that most developers did not have
final plats prior to the establishment of the streetlighting ordinance, which
required developers to install streetlights in the new subdivisions.
12.   Mr. Whitacre indicated storm water floods are a problem in the Industrial
Park area of the city. He feels the detention basins were developed according
to regulations but there are still problems with flooding as the storm sewers
are undersized and the detention areas are too small. The future needs are to
be determined.
13.   Mrs. Yeager asked Mr. Whitacre for the status of the Chapman property in
regard to the needed sewers in that area. Mr. Whitacre reviewed the options to
provide sewer to this “pocket area” to the new council members. He advised it
would take approximately $45,000 to do this sewer project. He stated the last
council considered the options but had made no decision. The topic of providing
sewers to “pocket areas” resulted in a brief discussion. Mr. Walker reminded
council that all sewer lines, easements, etc. had been turned over to the
Sanitation District. But it was the consensus of council to assist the
residents in areas of the city that desire sewer service. Some council members
stated the city had assured certain areas would be sewered at a later date and
would like to see the city fulfill this promise. Mr. Whitacre agreed to put
together a package to address those areas – stating that cost estimates could
run between $8,00-$12,000 per lot and as high as $21,000 per lot. He will
provide a summary of those cost estimates.
Appointment of Anita Steffen to the Board of Adjustments
14.   Mayor Kriege recommended the appointment of Anita Steffen to the Board of
Adjustments. Mr. Feldhaus voiced an objection as Mrs. Steffen is the spouse of
a current council member and he felt the city should take applications to fill
this position. He suggested tabling this appointment until the next meeting.
15.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to table the appointment of the vacant
position on the Board of Adjustments. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Motion
defeated with two yes votes and four no votes.
16.   A brief discussion ensued concerning any infraction this appointment may
cause. Mr. Walker recommended Mr. Steffen abstain from voting on this matter
before council. Other than that, he did not feel this appointment should
present an ethical conflict of interest.
17.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to appoint Anita Steffen to the Board of
Adjustments as recommended by Mayor Kriege. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with three yes votes, two no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus and
Mr. Ellison, and one abstain vote cast by Mr. Steffen. Motion carried 3-2-1.
Old Business
18.   Mr. Walker informed council that the request the city made to the Kenton
County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission to re-schedule the public hearing
for the AT&T cell tower was denied as it is their policy to hold these meetings
in the a.m. because this is not a zone change.
Resolution 1999-R-02 Requesting KCMP&Z to Reschedule Public Hearing
19.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have the city attorney read Resolution No.
1999-R-02 petitioning the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning to
reschedule all public hearings to evening hours when the public is able to
attend. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. No roll call; motion carried with all
ayes.
Mayor’s Report – Tom Kriege
20.   Mayor Kriege referred council to a letter received from a Mr. Trenkamp
regarding the TANK bus routes in Independence. Mr. Trenkamp’s grandchildren go
to school in Latonia and ride the bus from Latonia to Independence on school
days. As there is limited TANK bus service in Independence his grandchildren
have to walk several blocks to their home on Sylvan Drive. Mr. Trenkamp was
concerned over the limited bus service and also the condition of sidewalks on
Madison Pike, where there are sidewalks. There was a brief discussion wherein
it was noted TANK, in the past, has maintained additional ridership is
necessary in order for them to increase bus service in this area. Council
directed Mr. Scott to call TANK and investigate options for increased bus
service and then reply to Mr. Trenkamp.
21.   Mayor Kriege reminded council the Annual Planning Session would be held
this weekend: Friday 5-9 p.m. and Saturday 9 a.m. until 5:00 p.m. The planning
session is open to the public and encouraged citizens to attend.
Executive Session
22.   At 8:25 p.m. Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to enter into executive session
for the purpose of discussing litigation matters according to K.R.S. 61.810 and
also take a brief recess to give the cable company time to pack up their
equipment. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
23.   At 9:15 p.m. Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to close the executive session
and return to the regular meeting; seconded by Mr. Steffen. Motion carried with
all ayes
Closing Comments
24.   Mayor Kriege commented that the city attorney would be contacting Mr.
Daniels’ attorney regarding the pending lawsuit to appeal the zone change
request denied by council.
Adjournment
25.   At 9:20 p.m. Mr. Dupps made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mrs. Yeager.
Motion carried with all ayes. Meeting adjourned

CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Reverend Greg Fightmaster of Beechgrove Baptist Church gave the

Steffen and Donna Yeager answered roll call. Mr. Feldhaus was absent. Also in
attendance were the City Administrator, Gary Scott and the City Attorney,
Lawson Walker.
Adoption of Council Meeting Minutes
2.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to accept the council minutes of the January
12, 1999 regular meeting as submitted. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Motion
carried with all ayes; no roll call.
3.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to accept the council minutes of the January 26,
1999 regular meeting as submitted. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Motion
carried with all ayes; no roll call.
Privileges of the Floor
4.   Ms. Beth Savchick of 33 Peach Drive, Independence, Kentucky addressed
council requesting sanitary sewers. She asked council to form a committee to
conduct a feasibility (that would include cost estimates) study to extend sewer
lines to the Peach Drive area. She stated many residents in the area would like
public sewer service. There was a brief discussion with Dan Briggs of the city
engineer’s office regarding previous researches into sewering that section of
town. Mr. Briggs will send council previous data on sewering this section of
the city.
Gene Daniels Zone Change Request for the Jos. Knapp Property at 11011 Madison
Pike
5.   Mr. Tim Theissen introduced himself as the attorney for Mr. Gene Daniels.
He reminded council that Mr. Daniels was currently in litigation with the city;
appealing the zone change denial made by the previous council members. Mr.
Theissen urged council to reconsider the matter at the next council meeting by
allowing Mr. Daniels to make a new presentation regarding his zone change
request. Mr. Walker, City Attorney reported that he had been conferring with
Mr. Theissen regarding this matter. He advised council of their options. He
stated that if requested by the city, Judge Summe has the power to remand the
decision back to city council by way of issuing an Agreed Order. Secondly, he
advised that if council chose to reconsider the zone change but decided to
uphold the denial by the previous council members, then the lawsuit would
resume. And thirdly, he counseled that if council chose to vote tonight, with
the majority voting in favor of the change, then Mr. Daniels would dismiss the
lawsuit.
6.   Mrs. Gabbard suggested Mr. Theissen’s possible conflict of interest in
this matter as he holds the position of Chairman of the Kenton County Municipal
Planning & Zoning Commission. Mrs. Gabbard recalled the KCMPZ Commission had
voted in favor of Mr. Daniels zone change request. Mr. Theissen responded the
attorney of record was Marty Butler, his law firm associate, and he was filling
in for Mr. Butler tonight as he was unable to attend. He also explained that
when this matter was brought before the KCMPZ Commission he removed himself
from the proceeding.
7.   Mr. Theissen urged council to place the lawsuit in abeyance for a couple
of months while they take a fresh look the facts to be presented to them at a
future council meeting. Mr. Ellison stated that he felt the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning staff performed well in making their decision to deny Mr. Daniels
request and that KCMPZ Commission ruled in error when approving the zone
change. He felt the lawsuit should proceed. Mrs. Gabbard commented she had seen
no changes that would persuade her to vote in favor of this zone change. A
brief discussion ensued regarding the planned construction of the re-routing of
State Route 17 (Madison Pike) and its effect on Mr. Daniels development plan
for the property.
8.   Once again Mr. Theissen urged council to reconsider by stating Mr. Daniels
was very flexible regarding the exact development plans and would work with
council on what was and was not appropriate structures to put in this proposed
neighborhood commercial plan. He assured council Mr. Daniels would address
council’s concerns.
9.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to reconsider Mr. Daniels zone change request for
the property located at 11011 Madison Pike (corner of Shaw Road and Madison
Pike). Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call vote produced five no votes;
motion defeated 5-0.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Administrator – Gary R. Scott
10.   Mr. Scott reported he is compiling a list of interested persons to form a
Strategic Planning Group. He expects to begin meetings in March with this
group. Mayor Kriege requested volunteers from council to participate on this
planning group. Council members Donna Yeager and Eric Dupps stated they were
interested in taking part in this group.
11.   Mr. Scott reported the city engineers are surveying the condition of the
streets for future repairs. He stated he planned to bid out the repair work in
the next few weeks in order to get contracted with the asphalt companies before
they get busy. This also should ensure a competitive bid price. Council members
expressed a desire to expedite this project as some of the roads are in dire
need of repairs.
12.   Mr. Scott also reported that work is continuing on the Municipal Building
feasibility study. He commented that a possible site had been inspected today
and that the feasibility study will also suggest what parameters are needed.
13.   Regarding the plans for a Code Enforcement Board, Mr. Scott reported he
spoke with the Board of Ethics with regard to undertaking code enforcement
responsibilities and noted the group was interested in assuming those duties.
Mr. Scott has asked the city attorney to review the model ordinance and other
related material for a Code Enforcement Board and will keep council updated on
the progress of this matter.
14.   Mr. Scott advised council he has spoken with a representative of AT&T
regarding the proposed cell tower they would like to construct in Independence.
He stated he would be meeting with them before the next council meeting to

Police Department – Ed Porter
15.   Chief Porter presented council with a schedule of up-coming Neighborhood
Block Watch meetings. He noted comments on the schedule regarding the Child and
Special Needs Person Photo I.D. Program to be held in March and April.
Dan Briggs – Cardinal Engineering
16.   Mr. Briggs gave a report regarding future road repairs. He stated he
could begin to advertise for bids for the repairs when he is advised of an
amount that will be allotted from the budget to fund the repairs. He stated
that many of the city streets were built after WWII and are approaching fifty
years old and some of these streets will need total reconstruction within five
to seven years. He stated the current revenue tax dollars does not meet the
needs to replace the existing streets and suggested looking at ways to generate
funds or consider assessment projects to make the needed replacements. Mr.
Briggs stated that Holten Drive alone would cost between $460,000 and $600,000
to replace the street. Mr. Briggs also apprised council of the need to resolve
the problem involving the deteriorating condition of Crowe Road.
17.   There was a brief discussion regarding the enforcement of street light
installation in the new subdivisions as mandated by city ordinance. Mr. Briggs
advised council that several subdivision developers have not complied with this
ordinance. Mr. Walker suggested sending a letter to the developers regarding
this and see what kind of response the city receives. Mr. Scott will draft a
letter to the developers.
City Clerk Report
18.   Pat Taney, City Clerk reported the office has begun the process of
codification of ordinances for the last few years. The process will take a few
months and this cost will be budgeted in the 1999/00 fiscal year.
19.   Mrs. Taney also reported she has contacted this area’s Regional
Administrator at the Department for Libraries and Archives regarding the
disposal and retention of city documents. She stated funds will need to be
budgeted for 1999/00 for the permanent storage of city records and anticipates
this project to be completed by the end of summer.
Appointment of Council Committees
20.   Council members agreed to the following committee appointments:
Public Safety – Eric Dupps, Barbara Gabbard, Greg Steffen

be an official council committee but some of the council members (Mrs. Yeager &
Mrs. Gabbard) would represent city council on that committee which is comprised

New Business
22.   There was a brief discussion exploring acquisition of the land at the

patrons of public bus service.
1998/99 Budget Amendment
23.   Mr. Scott reminded council of his suggestion at the last meeting to adopt
a departmental budget instead of the current line item budget. He stated that a
departmental budget would give the department heads more flexibility in
managing the funds for their office. With that in mind, he instructed the
Finance Director to combine the line items and prepare an amendment to the
current budget to form a departmental budget, which he presented to council.
Mr. Scott stated he would continue to write next year’s budget by line item but
that it would be adopted as a departmental budget.
24.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to read Ordinance 1999-O-01 amending the 1998/
99 budget from a line item to departmental budget. Mr. Dupps seconded the
motion. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes. The city attorney read the
ordinance.
Mayor’s Report – Tom Kriege
25.   Mayor Kriege reported he had received a letter from the State Highway
Department regarding a traffic study they conducted at Madison Pike (Route 17)
and Declaration Drive in from of the new Independence Towne Center. Mayor
Kriege advised that the traffic study was requested by former Mayor Kudera
because of the increased traffic in that area due to recent development. He
stated the State Highway Department has declined a traffic signal at that
intersection, as the traffic count numbers did not justify a light at this
time. Mr. Ellison suggested the city conduct its own traffic study and
requested the Police Chief to position the Smart Radar unit in the area for a
few days.
Adjournment
