three ayes and one abstain (3-1).
Donation to Independence Lions Club Annual Easter Egg Hunt
3.   A letter from Ms. Leann Pegg, Chairman of the Independence Lions Easter
Egg Hunt, was presented to council requesting a donation to help defray the
costs associated with this yearly event. The egg hunt will be held on the
grounds of the Kenton Elementary School on March 28, 1999 at 4:00 p.m. The
city’s donation helps purchase prizes, plastic eggs, candy and camera film for
pictures with the Easter Bunny.
4.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to donate $600 to the Independence Lions Club to
be used for the annual Easter Egg Hunt. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll
call vote was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 4-0.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Mr. Ernest C. Friedrich, 1 Faye Drive, Taylor Mill, Kentucky addressed
council regarding a proposed zone change request for the ten acres of property
located at the corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road. He presented council
with a map that outlined his plans for the development of the property. He
stated the development would be constructed in two phases. Mr. Friedrich
explained the first phase would include a food mart with gasoline pumps and the
second phase of construction would allow for a drug store or some type of
clothing store or dry cleaners. He commented that the intersection needed
clearing as the visibility for vehicles was very bad and he felt that by
clearing the land and developing it that it would greatly improve the safety of
the intersection. Council members expressed concern that a development at the
corner would increase the congestion not alleviate it. There was discussion
regarding the installation of a traffic light, but comments were made on how
difficult it is to get support from the state highway department to install a
light on a state maintained road. Also some council members commented that
another food store and drug store was not necessary in that area, as there is
an IGA and Cherokee Drug Store on the adjacent corner. Mr. Friedrich thanked
council for hearing his presentation and asked them to consider his proposal
for a zone change.
1998/99 Budget Amendment – Ordinance No. 1999-O-01
6.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
amendment to budget Ordinance No. 1998-O-09. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion.
Motion carried with all ayes; no roll call (4-0). City Attorney, Lawson Walker
read the proposed ordinance.
7.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to adopt Ordinance 1999-O-01 as read. Mrs.
Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with four ayes and no nays.
Motion passed 4-0.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Administrator – Gary Scott
8.   Presently AT&T have been given approval from the Planning Commission to
erect a cellular tower on Independence Cemetery property. Council has objected
to this plan and has asked AT&T to reconsider and find another site, possibly
at the Shaw Park. Mr. Scott reported that he would be meeting a representative
from AT&T to inspect possible alternative sites for the construction of the
tower. Mr. Walker interjected that because of the encounter with city
disapproval this matter has now returned before the Public Services Commission
and action is pending. He advised council that if the Public Services
Commission decides to go ahead with the cemetery location, it would go there,
short of the city filing a lawsuit. He also informed council there is very
little case law on this type of judgement and that a federal statute would
supercede a state law. He commented there was plenty of reason to challenge
this decision and conveyed that AT&T representatives indicated a preference for
the cemetery location over the Shaw Park site. The consensus was to discuss
this possible lawsuit in more detail in executive session.
9.   Mr. Scott updated council regarding the formation of a Strategic Planning
Committee. He advised several names have been submitted to serve on the
committee and that he will notify the interested persons the first of March. He
commented that if the group is too large he will divide into smaller groups and
the Northern Ky. Area Development District may provide a facilitator.
10.   Mr. Scott advised council the budget process has begun for the 1999/2000
fiscal year. He stated that after the department heads submit their budget
numbers he will review with Mayor Kriege and then it will be presented to the
Budget & Finance Committee for review and recommendation before being presented
to council for adoption around May or June.
11.   As of today, twenty-two of the twenty-six employee benefit surveys were
completed and returned. The Northern Ky. Area Development District will compile
the results of the survey and make a report to council.
12.   Mr. Scott stated the Public Works Committee met and discussed ways of
providing the needed services to the community and will incorporate this into
the budget process.
Police Department – Ed Porter
13.   Chief Porter submitted a Block Watch meeting schedule to council as
requested. He also directed council to contact Sergeant Ed Bailey regarding any
community public relations type of functions where a police officer is desired.
He stated Sgt. Bailey would take an active interest and make the necessary
arrangements for this type of community involvement.
14.   Chief Porter also informed council his department is in the process of
conducting a traffic count near the Independence Towne Center. Council
requested the city conduct its own count to submit to the State Highway
Department as the state has denied installing a traffic light on Madison Pike
near the shopping center. Chief Porter commented the state did not supply the
city with their traffic count numbers, therefore he will not be able to make a
comparison.
Building Inspector – Alan Bowling
15.   Mr. Bowling reported he had received a request for information on the
procedures for placing cell equipment on an existing tower across from Nie’s
Drug store on Madison Pike. He advised him to submit a plan and then he would
advise him on the process involved.
16.   Mr. Bowling also addressed council regarding a property owner on
Turkeyfoot Road who paid two sewer tap-in fees. One to the Sanitation District
and one to the City. This occurred several months ago when he constructed a
multi-dwelling building. The property owner has sent the city a written request
asking the city to refund the tap-in fees ($2,100.00) paid to the city. After a
short discussion council requested Mr. Bowling to supply council with a map
showing the placement of the sewer lines.
17.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to table the decision to refund the tap-in fee
of $2,100.00 until the next meeting. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Motion
carried with all ayes.
18.   There was a brief discussion wherein Mr. Ellison asked who was
responsible for setting building bonds. He suggested the city adopt an
ordinance wherein they would have the sole authority in setting the bond
amounts as the city has been bound in the past by building bonds that were
inadequate. Mr. Walker advised that the authority of the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning & Zoning Commission set all subdivision regulation bonds and that the
city had the authority for bonds relating to zoning matters.
19.   Mr. Ellison also asked Mr. Bowling to find out what builder left five
propane cylinders on a street in the Battleridge Subdivision. He felt this was
a safety violation. Mr. Bowling promised to investigate the matter.
20.   Mr. Feldhaus also asked Mr. Bowling to make inquiry as to when the
sidewalks will be installed along Shaw Road and Madison Pike in the
Independence Towne Center area.
Zoning Administrator – Kevin Barbian
21.   The city’s new Zoning Administrator, Kevin Barbian advised council that
he began work last week and that he is still getting oriented. Mr. Bowling has
been helpful familiarizing him with the city. Mr. Barbian stated he would
submit a zoning report to council next month.
City Engineer – Dave Whitacre
22.   Mr. Whitacre reported the bids for the first phase of street repairs for
concrete work are due March 8, 1999. He also stated the specs for the bids for
the blacktop repairs would be ready in two weeks. He explained that April and
May are too wet to do the blacktop repairs and the weather would need to be
warmer in order for the blacktop to adhere.
23.   Mr. Whitacre informed council his office is working on the small drainage
issues and compiling a long-range street maintenance construction schedule.
NEW BUSINESS
Code Enforcement Board
24.   Mr. Scott addressed council regarding the formation of a Code Enforcement
Board. He spoke with the Board of Ethics about also serving on the enforcement
board. One member of the Ethics Board for personal reasons did not want to
serve on the enforcement board but wanted to remain on the Board of Ethics. A
discussion ensued regarding the options available and what course to take. If
council chose to go from a five-member to four-member board Mr. Walker advised
the current ethics ordinance would have to be amended. Also Mr. Walker stated
another ordinance would need to be adopted in order to have a duel board. Mr.
Scott stated he felt there should be two separate boards or one board to serve
both needs. The consensus of council was that it would simplify matters to have
a duel board and directed Mr. Scott to speak to the Ethics Board member that is
unable to serve on a duel board and look for a replacement for that position.
25.   Mr. Ellison stated he felt the Code Enforcement Board and the Ethics
Board members should be compensated for the meetings they attend, as the city’s
Board of Adjustments members receive a $30/meeting stipend. He felt this was
only fair. There was a brief discussion relating to this and council decided to
compensate each member $30 for every board meeting they attend. Mr. Walker will
draft a Code Enforcement Board ordinance to be presented at the next meeting.
Proposal to Change Day and Number of Monthly Council Meetings
26.   Mr. Feldhaus suggested changing from two regular meetings per month to
one. He stated that with Mayor Kriege’s establishment of active council
committees that a lot of the city matters could be deliberated in committee
before coming before council if action is necessary. He also commented that
special meetings could be called if important matters needed to be acted on
before the next regular scheduled meeting. In addition, he felt that with
Kenton County Fiscal Court moving all its regular meetings to the Independence
courthouse they may want to schedule all their meetings on Tuesday evenings;
not just the first and third Tuesday of each month. Mr. Feldhaus proposed
meeting on the first Monday of each month. There was a brief discussion
regarding Mr. Feldhaus’ proposal with the attending council members in
agreement. Mr. Walker will draft an ordinance to be presented at the next
council meeting.
Mayor Kriege’s Report
27.   Mayor Kriege reminded residents to complete the citizen survey that was
inserted in the newsletter and return to the city office by March 8, 1999. He
stated the results of the survey would help city officials in planning current
and future needs for the community.
AT&T Cellular Tower at the Independence Cemetery
28.   Mr. Tom Honebrink, General Manager of the Independence Cemetery spoke to
council regarding the proposed cellular tower on the cemetery grounds. He
attended tonight’s meeting as he thought there would be residents that opposed
the tower also in attendance and wanted to reassure city officials and
residents, especially the residents in the nearby Hartland Subdivision that the
tower would be 575 feet from the nearest neighbor in that subdivision. He
stated that while the cemetery board was interested in the opportunity to
generate revenue from the leasing of the property to AT&T, they wanted to
remain a good neighbor and did not want everyone to think the cemetery board
was trying to pull something over on the city. He stressed they are willing to
cooperate with the city in this matter. He stated they would not need the area
of the cemetery where the cell tower is proposed for at least one hundred years
and by then the tower will be defunct. Mr. Ellison advised the cell towers are
designed to break into two and most damage would be done to the cellular
equipment, a panel building that immediately surrounds the base of the tower.
He stated that council too is willing to be a good neighbor but feels the
cemetery board should pursue other options.
Executive Session
29.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to enter into executive session to deliberate
pending litigation and possible property acquisition according to KRS 61.810(b
& c). Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes.
Return to Regular Session
30.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to end the executive session and return to the
regular session of the meeting. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Motion carried
with all ayes.
Adjournment
31.   At 9:10 p.m. Mr. Steffen made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mr.
Ellison. Motion carried. Meeting adjourned.

CITY OF INDEPENDENCE

Privileges of the Floor
3.   Mr. Daniel Schuh informed council that he was considering development of
property located on Taylor Mill Road south of Rickey Lane that is currently
zoned R-1C. The development plan would require a change to an R-1D zone. Mr.
Schuh stated he did not want to pursue a zone change if the council’s overall
position was to reject a change in that area. He stated he did not want to go
through the time and expense of requesting a zone change that the majority of
council was not in favor or making. Mr. Feldhaus informed Mr. Schuh that this
matter would need to go before the city’s Planning & Zoning Committee for

recommendation to council and if council decided to give initial approval of
the zone change the city would make application for him to the Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission. The Planning & Zoning Committee decided to

carried with all ayes.

restriction of storm water flow. He also commented that if this ditch were

be setting precedence for future similar requests.

Code Enforcement Board Ordinance – Second Reading
5.   The city attorney reminded council that at the last meeting a second
reading was made on the proposed ordinance to establish a code enforcement
board but because there were changes made to a section of the ordinance then it
becomes a first reading again. Mr. Walker advised that a legislative body does
not have the power to approve the removal of a person from the board but stated
council could pass the ordinance with that stipulation. He doesn’t feel it is
necessary, as the mayor would need to provide a reason for removing one from
the board. Mr. Walker stated that each version of the ordinance has had a first
reading and council could have a second reading tonight on either version.
6.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to have a second reading on the March 9, 1999
(first reading) version on establishing a code enforcement board. Mrs. Yeager
seconded motion. Motion carried with four ayes and one nay vote cast by Mr.
Steffen. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
7.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to adopt Ordinance 1999-O-02 establishing a Code
Enforcement Board. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Mr. Steffen initiated a
discussion wherein he stated that after much consideration he feels
apprehensive having a dual board perform duties of both the Ethics and Code
enforcement. He stated he feels it would be more beneficial to appoint people
to the code enforcement board that have a more aggressive temperament to
actively pursue these types of matters. Mrs. Gabbard commented she feels the
code enforcement board is badly needed but is also having second thoughts on
merging the two boards. Mr. Scott remarked how difficult it can be finding
volunteers to hold positions on city boards and committees and by having a dual
board it allowed the city to utilize people already interested and willing to
serve the city in this capacity. He suggested the ordinance could be amended in
the future if the dual board did not work out. Mayor Kriege commented he does
not anticipate a problem combining the two boards nor does he see a conflict.
Mr. Scott also advised the zoning administrator would still be enforcing the
violations but the board would hear peoples concerns if they want to contest
the violation. Roll call vote was answered with three yes votes and two no
votes cast by Mr. Steffen and Mrs. Gabbard. Motion carried.

APRIL 27, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara
Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance
were Gary Scott, City Administrator and H. Lawson Walker, City Attorney.
Approval of Council Minutes
2.   After amendments were made to the council meeting minutes of April 13,
1999, Mr. Ellison made a motion to adopt the minutes; seconded by Mr. Dupps.
Motion carried 5-1 with Mr. Feldhaus abstaining because he did not attend that
meeting.
Presentation of the Citizen Survey Results by Dr. Michael Thomson of N.K.U.
3.   Michael Thomson, Ph.D. with the Department of Public Administration
presented the results of the recent citizen survey, which had been inserted in
the February city newsletter. He stated 502 surveys out of the 4110 mailed were
returned. This is a 12% return rate that is a little less than other cities
where the survey has been conducted. But he added those cities have a higher
geographic density. He also advised there is roughly a 5% error rate. He stated
this was a good baseline survey and advised conducting another survey between
3-5 years from now. Some facts of the representation of households in the
survey include: 43% are over 50 years of age, 66% have college experience, 63%
have an income over $45,000, 60% have children and 78% voted in the last city
election.
4.   Dr. Thomson advised that 92-97% of those responding were satisfied with
services being provided by the city with no demographic group “less happy.”
Street maintenance rated lowest. He commented that the parks, city facilities,
and personnel with an average 90% rating projected a very positive image.
According to the survey citizens are staying abreast of city information by way
of the city newsletter (75%), the Kenton County Recorder (61%) and the Kentucky
Post (49%) being the top three. The survey also concluded that 49% have
internet access in their homes, mainly the 30-50 years of age group, and that
38% plan to have access in the future. The survey data also revealed that 77%
of those responding wanted the property tax rate to stay the same, but if the
tax rate was increased, 47% wanted the increase to be used for street
maintenance. If services had to be cut in order to keep the current tax rate,
60% of those responding felt recreation expenses should be trimmed.
5.   Dr. Thomson stated that 40% of survey participants made open comments,
which is a very high percentage and indicates a very motivated group. Most
comments were directed toward public infrastructure. In conclusion, Dr. Thomson
stated that overall citizens are satisfied with city services. He commented
that the Census 2000 data will not be available until the year 2002 and
suggested the city may want to conduct the second citizen survey after the
census data is available – possibly in 2003.
6.   Mayor Kriege thanked Dr. Thomson for compiling the survey data and making
the presentation. He also advised council that he and the city staff would
review the survey in more detail with regard to looking at needed improvements
in city services.
Recess
7.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to take a short recess; seconded by Mr. Dupps.
Motion carried with all ayes.
8.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to return to regular session; seconded by Mr.
Ellison. Motion carried with all ayes.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
9.   Ms. Nancy Ballinger, who co-ordinates the Meals-on-Wheels program in
Independence addressed council regarding the need to provide services to the
senior citizens. She informed council of the huge cuts in funding to the
present program that services the senior citizens. Ms. Ballinger appealed to
council to consider allocating funds to continue providing meals to recipients
of the Meals-on-Wheels program. She stated recipients are short and long term
and the annual cost of providing one meal per day is $1,400. She added that the
meal is only a part of the service provided by this program; that sometimes the
person delivering the meal is the only human contact that senior may have
during the day. Also with medical prescriptions so costly sometimes a senior
will have to cut their grocery budget in order to pay for their medicine needs.
Ms. Ballinger stated that currently the City of Covington and the City of
Bellevue have provided funds for this program and remarked that cities need to
take ownership of their senior citizens. In closing Mrs. Ballinger encouraged
council to consider her request, as the Meals-on-Wheels program is a valuable
program which allows the seniors to remain in their own home where they are
happiest.
10.   Council requested Ms. Ballinger provide a more defined financial request
and other pertinent data for the next regular council meeting to be held May 3,
1999. She stated she would provide that information and will request the
Executive Director of the Northern Kentucky Senior Services to address council
at that meeting.

MAY 3, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara
Gabbard, Gregory Steffen, and Eric Dupps answered roll call. Also in attendance

Presentation of Certificate of Accreditation to the Police Department
2.   Mr. Mike Bischoff former Police Chief for the City of Fort Thomas
presented the Certificate of Accreditation to Chief Ed Porter. Mr. Bischoff
acted as the assessment team leader for the police department during the
lengthy application process. He explained the accreditation procedures to the
audience and how much of the work involves the development of policy and
procedures, which cover high liability issues. Mr. Bischoff commented that the
department’s hard work and dedication toward attaining this endorsement proves
to the citizens that they want to be the best. Chief Porter accepted the
certification on behalf of all the members of the Police Department as he
explained it has been a group effort. All members of the police department were
introduced to council and the audience.
Adoption of Council Minutes
3.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of the April 27,
1999 meeting, as submitted. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Motion carried
with all ayes.
Privileges of the Floor
4.   Betty Woods, member of the Independence Recreation Committee, submitted to
council the committee’s recommendations for names for the parks in Hartland
Subdivision and Shaw Road. She stated individual’s names were submitted for the
park at Shaw Road but the committee preferred not to name the park after an
individual but instead proposed “Memorial Park”. Mrs. Woods explained the
committee suggested a memorial wall, plaque, or other type of dedication for
individuals. The name suggested by the committee for the Hartland Subdivision
park was “Hartland City Park”.
5.   Mrs. Woods also reminded council and wanted to make new residents aware of
the Memorial Tree Program at the city parks. For $300-$325 a tree will be
planted with a 6x8 memorial plaque in remembrance of a loved one.

“Hartland City Park.” Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. The motion was answered
with five ayes and one nay vote cast by Mr. Steffen. Motion carried 5-1.
7.   Nancy Ballinger and Ellen Cook of the Senior Services of Northern Kentucky
addressed council requesting the city allocate funds to provide meals via the
Meals-on-Wheels Program to needy senior residents in Independence. Ms. Cook
stated the program has been affected by the recent cuts in state funding with
Kenton County alone dropping 6,378 meals to residents. Ms. Cook reported that
in March 1999 fifteen Independence seniors were receiving meals (with more on a
waiting list) but that number has declined to six being currently served. Ms.
Cook also stressed that any funds the city would allocate for the meals on
wheels program would be used for Independence residents. She explained the city
would be billed monthly for the meals. Ms. Cook also advised it cost $1,400 per
year per individual for the meal service. Mayor Kriege asked the Budget &
Finance Committee to discuss the possibility of appropriating some funds for
this program at the May 5, 1999 meeting.
Department Reports
City Administrator – Gary R. Scott
8.   Mr. Scott reported the request for proposals for banking services had been
received from six banks. Finance Director, Amy Guenther, reviewed the summary
of proposals with council. She explained the proposal packet requested certain
services the city required. She stated the city is currently receiving on-line
banking services with Fifth Third Bank in order to reconcile the monthly bank
statements in a more timely manner. She stated the priority for the city was to
maximize net investment income. Ms. Guenther stated she and Mr. Scott met with
the Budget & Finance Committee to review the proposals and concluded that Fifth
Third Bank offered all the services the city desired. Fifth Third Bank was able
to offer an investment rate much higher because they do a “daily sweep” and
recommended liquid asset management for the city’s investments by possibly
using U.S.Government securities. Mr. Padgett of Fifth Third Bank, who was in
the audience, advised they would work with the Finance Committee to set
guidelines for security investments which would be actively managed accounts,
reviewed on a daily basis. He stressed these types of investments are actually
owned by the city and are not certificate of deposits. Mr. Padgett also assured
council the U.S. Government securities comply with all KRS regulations.
Award of Banking Services Proposal to Fifth Third Bank

city’s banking services; seconded by Mr. Feldhaus. Roll call was answered by

Proposed Resolution to Adopt a new Employee Pay Plan
12.   Mr. Scott submitted a proposed resolution to the council members wherein
the city would be adopting personnel pay scales as part of the personnel
policies. He explained the Northern Ky. Area Development District conducted a
market study to see how the city compares with other local cities. The Budget &
Finance Committee reviewed the pay plan with no opposition noted. He explained
that by adopting this resolution it would become part of the Personnel Policy
adopted in December 1998 and would become effective with the 1999/2000 fiscal
year budget. Mr. Scott advised the spread sheet would change over time as the

MAY 18, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. He explained the
purpose of this special meeting was to discuss the proposed 1999/2000 budget he
has submitted to council for adoption. Council members, Jim Ellison, Eric
Dupps, Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Barbara Gabbard, and Gregory Steffen
answered roll call. Mayor Kriege introduced Mr. Paul Alley who was substituting
for the city attorney, H. Lawson Walker. Also present were Gary Scott, City
Administrator and Amy Guenther the city’s Finance Director.
Mayor Kriege’s Budget Address and Proposed Budget for F/Y 1999/2000
2.   In his Budget Address to council, Mayor Kriege highlighted the present and
future needs of the city. Mayor Kriege presented two proposed budgets – Version
A and Version B – and indicated that he was endorsing Version A which included
the addition of three police officers to the Police Department, $400,000 for
road repairs, and the addition of a Public Works Department with two employees.
Mayor Kriege commented that the growing population is the reason for the need
for more police officers and a Public Works Department. He also addressed the
need for additional office space and will begin actively searching for a site
to build a new city facility with the hopes of breaking ground in the fall of
the year 2001.
Discussion of the Proposed F/Y 1999/2000 Budget
3.   As a member of the Finance and Budget Committee, Mr. Feldhaus began the
discussion by explaining the primary difference between the two proposals was
the addition of three police officers and the amount funded for street repairs.
Both proposals include an overall 5% increase in employee salaries. Mr.
Feldhaus stated the recent citizen survey revealed the residents were unhappy
with the condition of the streets and he would like to see more funds allocated
for street maintenance and repairs. He indicated that one new officer would be
hired to replace the patrol officer that was assigned DARE duties. Chief Porter
stated that Version A would fund three new officers: one lieutenant, one
sergeant, and one patrol officer. Mr. Feldhaus questioned the need for another
lieutenant and sergeant.
4.   Mrs. Gabbard commented that the need for three officers or only one just
boils down to a matter of opinion. She said that she feels three addition
police officers are needed considering the continuing growth. She also stated
there is not a problem with money for the city to handle three additional
officers. Mr. Feldhaus stated he feels Version A is a “want” budget not a need
budget. He would like to see more funds directed to the road fund.
5.   Mr. Dupps commented that recent development plans call for an additional
1200 homes on the Taylor Mill Road side of the city indicating phenomenal
growth. Mrs. Yeager stated those homes won’t be constructed in the coming year.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus pointed out that with the addition of three more officers
would also mean leasing three more cruisers. Currently the police department’s
home fleet program is at twenty-three cars. Mr. Ellison provided history on the
program by stating that when the home fleet program was established there were
only eight cars and the officers lived in the city. Now some officers do not
live in the city but the city allows participation in the program. Mr. Feldhaus
stated that in the past employee salaries were low and the take home fleet
program was an incentive to keep the officers on the department. Chief Porter
advised that Version A of the proposed budget include the cost for three
additional cruisers. Mr. Feldhaus responded that he was not against the home
fleet program.
7.   Chief Porter stated that officer response time is valuable and they would
be able to gain time with additional officers. Mr. Feldhaus stated that adding
another officer would make twenty-one officers – well over 1.5/1000 population.
Chief Porter responded that the national average is 2.5/1000 population. Mr.
Ellison stated the Kenton County Police and Sheriff Departments also cover the
Independence area. Mrs. Gabbard remarked the county police are busy all the
time.
8.   At this point in the meeting, Mr. Scott encouraged council to address all
concerns with the budget tonight before a first reading of the ordinance
because any line items changed afterwards would be cause for a new first
reading.
9.   Mr. Ellison maintained his position by stating he felt the city only
needed to add a patrol officer to replace the officer now handling the DARE
duties. He stated he is in favor of providing a DARE officer for the school
programs. He voiced his opposition to adding more lieutenants and sergeants to
increase the police office staff thereby adding a level of bureaucracy that in
his opinion the city doesn’t need. Mr. Ellison stated he felt more officers
should be patrolling the streets. He also expressed the need to establish the
Public Works Department in the coming year by supplying that department with
needed equipment.
10.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Steffen what his thoughts were regarding the
proposed budget. Mr. Steffen questioned the uniform allowance line item under
the administration department’s budget. The Mayor indicated this was discussed
at the Planning Session in February and would provide for a more professional
appearance in the city clerk’s department. A discussion ensued regarding
uniforms for the public works employees. Mr. Scott stated they would possibly
order city t-shirts and/or photo identification for public works employees. Mr.
Steffen also asked about the auto lease under the administration budget and the
Mayor explained that was for the city administrator’s vehicle.
11.   Mr. Steffen also expressed reservations regarding the allocation of
$15,000 for the Meals on Wheels program. He stated that he felt the city was
getting into the business of social service, which may be hard to bow out of in
the future. Mr. Feldhaus commented that the cuts in federal and state funding
were forcing the city to provide this service. Mayor Kriege assured Mr. Steffen
this line item would be re-evaluated each year but felt that as along as the
city could afford to allocate some funds that we should do it. Mr. Ellison and
Mrs. Yeager also voiced support for this contribution. Mr. Ellison commented
that the seniors need this service and he doesn’t see this as a permanent
arrangement for the meals program but more as a stopgap measure while they seek
other sources of revenue. Mrs. Yeager concurred and added the meal is only part
of the service; this is a good way to watch over our seniors. Mr. Steffen
stated he felt other services were just as worthy of city funding and
reiterated his concern of this becoming a permanent fixture in the budget.
12.   Mr. Steffen asked the Mayor why $75,000 was allocated in the building
fund for a building. Mayor Kriege responded he had no set plans for that line
item. Mr. Ellison asked what the difference was between the line items of city
attorney contract and attorney fees. Mr. Scott explained the contract was for
the monthly retainer fee and the attorney fees were for miscellaneous charges
for lawsuit work not covered under the retainer contract.
13.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mrs. Guenther how much money was in the city’s reserve
fund. Mrs. Guenther stated there was 1.3M in the general fund reserve with a
total 2.81M for all city funds. A discussion ensued regarding recommended
guidelines for reserves. Mrs. Guenther informed council the state
recommendation is three to six months of operating expenses that should be kept
in reserve, which would be approximately $67,000 per month for the city. Mr.
Feldhaus felt that with such a large reserve more money should be allocated to
the road budget for the street maintenance/repairs. Mrs. Guenther felt the
reason for the large reserve was that in the past the revenue was not projected
in accordance with the rapid growth of the city. She also stated the revenues
in the proposed budget have been conservatively projected.
14.   Mayor Kriege advised that thirty-five percent of the budgeted figures in
Version A has been taken out of the reserve funds. He stated the city shouldn’t
hold onto the large reserve when facing issues such as a new building facility,
needed storm sewer improvements, etc. Mr. Steffen suggested pulling more money
from the reserves to fund the needed street repairs. Mr. Feldhaus commented he
is uncomfortable sitting on 1.3M in reserves when it should be spent on public
services or the council should consider lowering the property tax rate. Mayor
Kriege voiced reluctance in lowering the reserve too drastically during his
first year in office. He advised the budget could be amended later in the
fiscal year when the expenses and revenues were reviewed.
15.   At this point, a portion of reserve funds was redirected to increase
several expenditure line items. The line items included: Special Events from
$10,000 to $15,000 (to cover the full cost of the July 4th fireworks
celebration), Road repairs from $400,000 to $500,000, Police training from
$14,000 to $20,000 and the total operational expenses for the parks from
$30,000 to $40,000.
First Reading of the Proposed Budget for F/Y 1999-2000
16.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of Version B of the
proposed budget for f/y 1999/2000; seconded by Mrs. Yeager. Roll call vote was
answered with three yes votes and three no votes cast by Mr. Dupps, Mrs.
Gabbard, and Mr. Steffen. Mayor Kriege broke the 3/3 tie by voting no. Motion
defeated 4-3.
17.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion have a first reading of Version A of the
proposed budget for the f/y 1999-2000. Mr. Dupps made a motion to second the
motion but suggested adding another $100,000 to the road repairs line item.
Under the attorney’s advice, Mrs. Gabbard withdrew her motion.
18.   Mr. Ellison resumed the discussion regarding the addition of three police
officers in Version A of the proposed budget by saying the increase of three
patrolmen was more preferable than additional administrative staff. Chief
Porter responded that in the past there have been problems due to lack of
supervision and the goal is to increase patrol and supervision. He stated that
currently the department is not even close to that and is trying to expand that
building block. Again, the number of calls each officer responds to was
discussed and Chief Porter stated that calls consist of only one-third of an
officer’s duties with the other two-thirds being proactive patrolling and
administration work. He stated that currently an officer is posted eight hours
a day at Simon Kenton High School. Mr. Ellison commented that the Kenton County
School Board and the Kenton County Police Department need to share that expense
and responsibility. He felt the citizens shouldn’t be penalized by taking a
patrol officer off the street and placed as a guard at the school. Council
agreed that with only two weeks of school left an officer could remain at the
school but the school board would have to make other safeguarding arrangements
in the future.
19.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a first reading of Version A of the
proposed 1999/2000 Budget Ordinance as amended. Mrs. Gabbard seconded the
motion. Roll call vote was answered with three yes votes and three no votes
cast by Mr. Ellison, Mr. Feldhaus, and Mrs. Yeager. Mayor Kriege broke the tie
vote by casting a yes vote. Motion carried 4-3.
20.   City Attorney, Mr. Alley requested a short recess before reading the
ordinance so that he could confer with Ms. Guenther on the correct totals.
21.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a short recess; seconded by Mr.
Steffen. Motion carried with all ayes.
22.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to resume the meeting; seconded by Mr. Yeager.
Motion carried with all ayes.
23.   Mr. Alley read the revised Version A of the proposed 1999/2000 Budget
ordinance.
Adjournment
24.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mrs. Gabbard. Motion
carried and the meeting adjourned at 9:27 p.m.
____________________________________
Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
JUNE 7, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara
Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance
were Gary Scott, City Administrator and Paul Alley, City Attorney sitting in
for H. Lawson Walker.
Approval of Council Minutes
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to approve the council minutes of the May 3,
1999 regular meeting as submitted. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Motion
carried 6-0 with all ayes.
3.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to approve the council minutes of the special
budget meeting held on May 18, 1999 as submitted. Mrs. Yeager seconded the
motion. Motion carried 6-0 with all ayes.
Eric Deters – 5K Memorial Race
4.   Mr. Eric Deters addressed council regarding a 5K Memorial Race he is
planning in memory of his deceased wife who was an avid runner. He stated the
event is scheduled for September 11, 1999 at 7:00 p.m. He informed council that
he sees this as a major fundraiser for several organizations he has been
affiliated with all profits going to charity. It will be a festival like
atmosphere with music and food available. Mr. Deters stated the race will be
professionally run, but the exact route of the race is not yet determined. He
mentioned he would like to build a permanent stage at his cost by way of
corporate sponsors or other contributors. Mrs. Yeager stated the city is in the
process of getting donations to build an amphitheater. Mr. Deters stated he
would be happy to collaborate with the city in that endeavor. He stated he
would like to make this 5K Memorial Race an annual event for the city. He asked
for the city’s support, as he would like to use Memorial Park. Mrs. Yeager
stated the Independence Recreation Commission would work with him on the
details of the event. Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Deters that Mr. Scott and Police
Chief Porter would help him obtain the needed permits and arrange the policing
needs for this event.
Discussion of Proposed Development on Senour Road by Fischer Homes
5.   Several representatives for Fischer Homes made a formal presentation for
the proposed Valley Park Development on Senour Road. Attorney, Elizabeth
Horowitz, started out by saying that Fischer Homes was requesting the city to
grant a zone change from R1-C to R1-C/RCD overlay. The R1-C/RCD overlay would
permit 50-foot lots. She stated that a section of the development is in
Covington but it would be treated as one parcel. Ms. Horowitz advised council
that this zone change was approved by a 10-1 vote in favor of the development
as it meets all the elements of the comprehensive plan. Ms. Horowitz said that
the overlay zone would provide variation in the density to the greatest extent
possible. She also cautioned council that the described development plan is to
be voted on as presented.
6.   Mr. Jim Gorman, Vice President and General Manager for Fischer Development
Company, stated that the property on Senour Road was purchased with the clear
understanding of the 80-foot lot requirements but felt the RCD overlay zone
could provide for more recreation and open space. He also stated that the homes
to be built in this development are smaller than Fischer usually builds.
7.   Another representative advised council that he prepared the land design on
this project. He described the current land as a mixture of mature trees,
pasture, a creek with both major wooded areas and open meadow areas for a total
of 103.18 acres. He stated that with the proposed development there would be
ten fewer homes. This would enable leaving twenty percent open space which is
required for the overlay zone. Three parks will be developed in the open space
for a total 24 acres of recreational space. He stated a homeowners’ association
will maintain the lake and parks. The parks will provide both active (soccer
and baseball fields) and passive (nature setting) recreation. In closing, he
stated that the overlay makes for a strong community and will be an asset to
the city. If developed at the current zone of R1-C the subdivision will have a
very generic look, whereas the overlay creates a nice variety.
8.   Next to speak was Mr. Ray Erpenbeck, the engineer on the project. He
explained to council that currently there are no public sewers in this area of
the city. He advised that the Sanitation District has a few sewer pumps in the
area and the land is serviceable for sewers. In regard to storm water run-off,
he stated that the storm sewers would be built to the current subdivision
regulations. He stated this type of cluster development would generate less
storm water run-off. Mr. Erpenbeck also advised council that a traffic study
had been conducted and he provided council with a copy of that report. He
indicated that the reconstruction of Rt. 17 will change the traffic pattern
somewhat and will help alleviate the traffic problem in the area.
9.   Mr. Henry Fischer addressed council by stating that he is currently
developing the Liberty Orchard subdivision in the Madison Pike area and he had
received some nice comments from the council regarding that subdivision. He
stated that the primary market he is going to serve is the homeowner in the
$100-$140,000 price range. He stated he is willing to make some additional
commitments relative to the houses such as side garage entries on the Senour
Road houses in order to provide more road appeal. He also stated he would have
50 and 70-foot setbacks on Senour Road to maintain a more rural environment.
Mr. Fischer stated that the smaller lots are aimed at the young professionals
and empty nesters. He stated that he met with the council’s Planning & Zoning
Committee on two separate occasions wherein the e issues raised were storm
water retention and traffic. He stated that he is also willing to commit to
putting on the south side of the development playground equipment more central
to the development. He stated that all garages would be two-car garages, which
will provide for four off-street parking spaces. He stated he is willing to
construct 28-foot wide loops to help with the traffic flow. He advised that if
the land is developed at the current zone of R1-C that many trees would be
removed. He also reminded council that the Kenton County Municipal Planning &
Zoning Commission is obligated to approve the development plan when it meets
all requirements.
10.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Fischer if he was going to develop the rear
section of the subdivision. Mr. Fischer stated that it was a high probability
but that he could not guarantee that he would. Mr. Fischer stated the homes on
the larger lots would be similar to the homes built in the Liberty Orchard
subdivision.
11.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to table any action on the requested zone
change for the property on Senour Road in order to gather more information. Mr.
Steffen seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 6-0.
Motion for a Brief Recess
12.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to take a short recess; seconded by Mrs.
Gabbard. Motion carried with all ayes.
13.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to reconvene the meeting; seconded by Mrs.
Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
PRIVELEGES OF THE FLOOR

approximately 400 feet south of Rickey Lane. Mr. Cox stated this development

Discussion of re-naming Hartland Park
15.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to reconsider the naming of Hartland Park and
Memorial Park. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. A discussion ensued wherein Mrs.
Gabbard stated she has had more time to think about the name of Hartland Park
and doesn’t feel the city should advertise the name of a subdivision. Mayor

the park. Mr. Feldhaus stated the Independence Recreation Committee recommended

consensus was to ask the Recreation Committee to make a new recommendation for

Motion to Repeal old Personnel Policies

6-0
Proposed Budget for 1999/2000
20.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to have the second reading of proposed
ordinance adopting a budget for the 1999/2000 fiscal year. Mr. Dupps seconded
the motion. A lengthy discussion followed the motion.
21.   The discussion centered on Option A of the proposed budget that provides
for the addition of three new officers in the police department. Mr. Feldhaus
stated that at the current staffing of twenty officers that provides for a 1.6
officers per1000 population ratio and Option B will raise that ratio to 1.7/
1000. He compared that to the Department of Justice survey average of 2.5/1000
with the average for major cities like New York, Los Angeles, etc. being 2.3/
1000. He also cited the bookings are comparable with other smaller departments.
Mr. Feldhaus also stated that the city currently has a take home fleet of
twenty cruisers and that larger departments carry an average of 57 cruisers/100
officers. He stated that on the local level the number of sworn officers is 11/
10,000 giving a 1.1 ratio which the city of Independence is above that average
at 1.6. He reminded council that at the January planning session Chief Porter
indicated that each officer handles three calls per shift. He stated that a
good indication of the need for more officers would be an excessive amount of
overtime dollars being paid out. Mr. Feldhaus stated that when the overtime
hours increase then you need to look at the addition of more officers. He
stated that currently only $8,100 has been paid out in overtime. He stated that
he feels to be fiscally sound that three officers are not necessary now. He
also went on to say that the current population is estimated at around 12,000
but that during the day the population drops between 6,000 – 8,000. In closing,
Mr. Feldhaus stated that he feels that Option B overall is a good budget with
5% employee salary increases and adding one police officer to replace the
D.A.R.E. officer. He asked council to reconsider Option B as the chose for next
year’s budget.
22.   Mr. Ellison commented that from the mileage report he received from the
police department it reveals that most cruisers travel less than fifty miles on
each shift. He believes this is a low rate especially when they are being used
to travel to and from work.
23.   Mrs. Gabbard commented that she thought all these concerns had been
cleared up at the last meeting, but appreciated receiving the additional
information.
24.   Mr. Scott advised council that it was best to settle the budget tonight
but that a special meeting could be scheduled for June 22, 1999. Mr. Feldhaus
commented that the budget could still get passed by July 1, 1999. But to
inflate the police department when the numbers don’t justify the increases is
an injustice to the taxpayers.
25.   Officer Shawn Butler, who was sitting in for Chief Porter, commented that
what the community wants and council wants dictates what police services are
performed. There is a wide variety of services that need to be funded
26.   Mr. Feldhaus stated that previous councils have increased the police
department substantially since 1995 – from 13 officers with a budget of
$680,000 to the current 20 officers with a budget of $1.3M in 1998/99. He
stated that there might be a need to increase the department, but not this
much, as indications do not support the increase of three officers.
27.   At this time, Mayor Kriege asked for a roll call vote on the above stated
motion for a second reading of the proposed budget for 1999/2000. Roll call was
answered with three no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus, Mrs. Yeager and Mr. Ellison
and three yes votes cast by Mrs. Gabbard, Mr. Dupps and Mr. Steffen with Mayor
Kriege voting yes to break the tie. Motion carried 4-3. The city attorney, Mr.
Alley, read the proposed ordinance.
Motion to Adopt Budget Ordinance No. 1999-O-05
28.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to adopt the 1999/2000 Budget Ordinance No.
1999-O-05 as read. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered
with three no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus, Mrs. Yeager and Mr. Ellison and three
yes votes cast by Mrs. Gabbard, Mr. Steffen and Mr. Dupps with Mayor Kriege
voting yes to break the tie. Motion carried 4-3 in favor.
29.   Mr. Dupps commented that he agrees with Mr. Feldhaus that the police
department is doing a good job but cited the increased growth in population and
the need for the budget to reflect the needs of the future.
Motion to read proposed Ordinance to Amend the 1998/99 Budget
30.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend the 1998/99 budget; seconded by Mr. Steffen. Roll call was
answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0. Mr. Alley read the proposed
ordinance. Mr. Scott advised council that although the expenditures increased,
the revenues exceeded what was estimated keeping up with the expenses.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS

Police Department – Lt. Shawn Butler

Cardinal Engineering – Dave Whitacre
35.   Mr. Whitacre reported the asphalt street repairs are nearly complete in
the Beechgrove area. They have also taken care of the pothole repairs. He
indicated the need to schedule a meeting to discuss storm sewers in the
Beechgrove area. Many of the pipes in the city are literally falling apart. He

come in too high as he feels the design may cost over $10,000. The Mayor asked
about landscaping around the Park and Ride lot. Mr. Whitacre stated he was not
handling the landscaping of the lot.
36.   There was a brief discussion regarding storm sewers. Mr. Whitacre
expressed the need for the city to establish criteria and set policy in
handling extensions and easements. Mr. Scott stated this would be something the
Public Works Committee could explore. There was also a brief discussion
regarding the pond behind some homes on Gunstock Court in the Hunters Green
Subdivision. The pond is in the common area that is deeded to the subdivision’s
homeowners’ association and is causing a land erosion problem for the nearby
homes. The city attorney was asked to research the city’s liability if the city
filled in the pond.
City Attorney – Paul Alley (sitting in for H. Lawson Walker)
37.   Mr. Alley stated there were two resolutions before council for adoption.
The first one was regarding the job descriptions for the public works employees
and the second was the adoption of an employee pay plan. There was a brief
discussion regarding the wording of the titles for the public works employees
(to non-gender) and whether or not the lead worker would be classified as an
exempt or non-exempt employee. Mr. Scott assured council both public works
positions would be laborer jobs, as a management position was not needed at
this time.
Resolution No. 1999-R-04 Adopting Public Works Employees Job Descriptions
38.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to read Resolution No. 1999-R-04; seconded by
Mr. Feldhaus. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Walker read the proposed
resolution.
39.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 1999-R-04; seconded by

Resolution No. 1999-R-03 Adopting a Pay Plan for the City Employees
40.   Mrs. Feldhaus made a motion to read Resolution No. 1999-R-03; seconded by

resolution.
41.   There was a brief discussion regarding the wording of the proposed pay
plan for the city employees. Mr. Feldhaus suggested the structure should be
across the board for all employees and asked that the wording for the police
department employees be the same as the rest of the city employees.
42.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 1999-R-03 adopting a
pay plan for the city employees as amended. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion.
Roll call vote was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0.
New Business

L Highway jail site to be sent to the Kenton County Fiscal Court. Mr. Dupps
made a motion to read the proposed resolution to support the building of the
new Kenton County jail on the 3-L Highway site. Mr. Feldhaus seconded the

44.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 1999-R-05 supporting
the 3-L Highway site for the new Kenton County jail. Mr. Steffen seconded the
motion. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr.
Ellison and Mrs. Gabbard. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.

June 22, 1999
City of Independence
Special Council Meeting
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara Gabbard, Eric
Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance was the city
administrator, Gary R. Scott and city attorney, Paul Alley sitting in for H.
Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege opened the meeting by stating this special meeting had been
called to discuss three items; an annexation request by Mr. Wayne Ferguson who
resides at 35 Pelly Road, discussion and possible action on the proposed
amended 1998/99 budget, and the discussion and possible action on the proposed
development by Fischer Homes on Senour Road.
Discussion of possible annexation of 35 Pelly Road – owner Wayne Ferguson
3.   Mr. Ferguson stated he would like to tie into the sewer system prompting
his request to be annexed into the city limits. He stated a neighbor is buying
a portion of the lot and does not wish to hook into the sewer line but that he
plans to tie his home into the sewer line. Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Ferguson if
he was under any time restraints to proceed. He stated he had been, but was
given the okay to proceed by the city administrator. Mr. Dupps stated that Mr.
Ferguson met with the city’s Planning and Zoning Committee to discuss his
request. Mayor Kriege stated an ordinance would be prepared by the next regular
council meeting. Mr. Ellison suggested having an emergency reading of the
ordinance at the next meeting as this sewer tie in is in progress.
Proposed Ordinance to Amend the 1998/99 Budget Ordinance
4.   The next item on the agenda was the amendment of the 1998/99-budget
ordinance to reflect the current and projected revenue and expenditures through
June 1999.
5.   Mr. Feldhaus questioned Police Chief Porter about funds that may have been
expended for the formation of a SWAT team. Chief Porter confirmed that some
funds had gone for the expense of tactical equipment and training for a SWAT
program. Mr. Ellison asked the Chief if the city was in the process of forming
a SWAT team. Chief Porter stated that training has been provided and was paid
for through existing resources. Chief Porter offered to speak to council
regarding the SWAT program at the next regular meeting.
6.   Mr. Dupps questioned Amy Guenther, Finance Director, regarding the lack of
revenue received for the D.A.R.E Program as it was originally budgeted for
$24,000.00, but the amended budget shows $0.00 received. Ms. Guenther stated
that some funds should be received in June but was unsure what that amount
would be so she left it at zero.
7.   Mrs. Yeager expressed concern regarding her recent discovery of the
formation of a SWAT program. Mr. Steffen stated the Public Safety Committee was
just recently informed of the program. Mr. Ellison asked the Police Chief if
any equipment had been purchased. Chief Porter replied that holsters, etc. had
been purchased. Mr. Ellison stated he feels expected to adopt this amended
budget that has expenditures for a program that were not known about by this
council. Mr. Scott discussed the appropriation of forfeitures and seized monies
and explained those funds had to be used for non-budgeted police items. Mr.
Feldhaus questioned Mayor Kriege and Mr. Scott as to their knowledge of this
SWAT program. Mayor Kriege stated he was not aware of training but was somewhat
aware of the SWAT program. Mr. Feldhaus stated that in all the meetings council
has had, especially during the discussions regarding the adoption of the 1999/
2000 budget, no mention was ever made of expenses for a SWAT program. Mayor
Kriege attempted to assure council that the SWAT program was not a secret but
that the topic just never came up. Chief Porter commented that public
advertisement of the city’s inability to handle extreme incidents is not
something that should be broadcast over public access television. He also
advised that the City of Covington would no longer provide any SWAT support due
to a recent occurrence with another local city. He stated that he saw a void
and discussed the SWAT program with the Mayor and the City Administrator. He
maintained that existing funds were used for the recent SWAT expenses. Mr.
Feldhaus reminded Chief Porter and council that the city just funded three
additional officers for the police department and stated he feels they will be
pulled to cover officers absent due to training time for a SWAT unit. He stated
he feels this was trying to be hidden from council. Mrs. Gabbard commented that
there was nothing wrong with the Police Chief using existing money in his
budget for these expenses. Mr. Ellison commented that the formation of a SWAT
unit goes against what local cities and the county is trying to do by
consolidating a lot of public services in order to save the tax payer’s money.
Chief Porter asserted that a SWAT program would be a benefit to the police
department and all citizens.
8.   Mayor Kriege directed Chief Porter to bring back a full report that
includes all funds expended on SWAT related items to council by the next
regular council meeting on July 12, 1999.
9.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to table the second reading of the amended 1998/
99 budget ordinance until the next regularly scheduled council meeting of July
12, 1999 when council received Chief Porter’s report requested by Mayor Kriege.
Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered by three yes votes
and four no votes cast by Mr. Dupps, Mrs. Gabbard, Mr. Steffen with Mayor
Kriege breaking the tie.
10.   Mr. Scott and Mr. Alley advised council that the amended budget needed to
be adopted by July 1, 1999. There was a brief discussion to schedule a special
meeting.
11.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to schedule a special council meeting on June
29, 1999 to review Chief Porter’s report on SWAT expenditures as it relates to
the amended budget. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call vote was
answered with all ayes. Motion carried.
12.   Council concurred that the ordinance relating to Mr. Ferguson’s
annexation into the city would be added to the agenda of the special meeting on
June 29, 1999.
Proposed Development by Fischer Homes on Senour Road
13.   Representatives from Fischer Homes addressed council regarding their
request for a zone change on Senour Road from R1-C to R1-C/RCD. They provided a
summary chart that showed what could be developed using the existing R1-C zone
as compared to the proposed R1-C/RCD. They invited questions and asked they be
allowed to respond to all citizen comments.
14.   Mrs. Yeager expressed her concern with the three parks planned for the
proposed development being maintained by a homeowners’ association. She
requested a provision be included that if the homeowners’ association would go
defunct that the parks be deeded to the city. Fischer representatives pointed
out that two of the three planned parks would be within the city limits of
Independence but the other one would be in the City of Covington. While they
expressed confidence that the homeowners’ association would not become defunct
they agreed to work with the city attorney to make that a provision in the
homeowners’ association deed. Mr. Dupps suggested swapping land with the City
of Covington and Mr. Alley advised that it was possible if Covington would
agree to that. Mrs. Gabbard requested those proposals be in writing.
15.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Fischer what the cost would be to install a pump
station on the north side of the development. Mr. Fischer estimated that the
pump station, force main, etc. would cost $60-65,000.00
16.   Mrs. Gabbard questioned an overlay being considered a zone change. Ms.
Horowitz, legal counsel for Fischer Homes, explained the RCD zone had been
enacted to allow restrictions and that it is a special process that doesn’t
apply to an ordinary zone change.
17.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mayor Kriege how he feels about the proposed zone
change. Mayor Kriege stated that the land would be developed either way;
existing or proposed. While he feels the development will be a strain on the
area he stated preference to the proposed R1—C/RCD as it allows more green
space and frontage than the existing zone.
18.   Mrs. Gabbard asked if the state highway department has plans to widen
Senour Road. Fischer representatives stated they were not aware of any
immediate plans by the state.
19.   At this point, Mayor Kriege requested citizen input. Jay Scharold of
Senour Road commented that the state has had plans for the last thirty years to
widen Senour Road but the budget has never allotted funds – but the project is
in the works.
20.   Mr. Mark Ellison, 37 Carrie Way stated that he is a thirteen year
resident of the city. He reminded council that some of them made campaign
promises last fall that they would control the growth of the city. He stated
the city is not able to handle this growth and the traffic jams on Route 17
confirm this. He feels there should be no more development until the state and
county roads catch up. He commented that the new schools were just built to
help alleviate the overcrowding and they are close to capacity already.
21.   Mr. William Miller of Oliver Road commented that this development would
only add to the overflowing of the Banklick Creek when more trees are
destroyed.
22.   Fischer representatives reminded council that state highway funds are
committed to improve Route 17. They did not feel their development would worsen
the overflowing of the Banklick Creek as the plans call for retention ponds.
They also reported that the Water District is currently working on a project to
install water lines and they will be under construction by next summer. Mr.
Miller requested council confirm that statement with the Water District. Mr.
Feldhaus commented that even if they did confirm it that nothing is written in
stone.
23.   Mr. Ellison advised the residents that council would be voting on one of
the proposals; either the existing R1-C zone or the proposed R1-C/RCD zone. He
stated that Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission has
recommended approval of the zone change. But because the land in question is
currently zoned R1-C it would just be an administrative formality for Fischer
Homes to re-submit the development using the existing zone wherein they can
construct 308 homes.
24.   Discussion centered on the overcrowding at the local schools and that the
Planning Commission does not take the schools into consideration when making
their recommendations on development projects. A comment was made that the
Senour Road development would place children in the Taylor Mill Elementary
school. Mr. Feldhaus cited the current enrollment at some of the local
elementary schools and each school’s capacity enrollment. Ms. Horowitz advised
that KCMP&Z do not take schools into consideration because they have no
authority to do so.
25.   Mr. Ellison also pointed out that the residents are currently being asked
to conserve water because of the lack of adequate water facilities in the area
and the fact that the water district has not kept up with the rapid development
in this part of Kenton County.
26.   Mrs. Gabbard stated that she agrees but that she feels the city doesn’t
have much choice as the property is already zoned residential. Mr. Fischer
advised council he has the legal right to subdivide the property and that they
are asking for approval of a development plan that they feel is far superior to
the existing R1-C zone. Ms. Horowitz commented that the current zoning of R1-
C allows for at least 300 homes, but Fischer Homes, by way of an overlay to the
current zoning, wanted to supply more amenities and variety with the proposed
development.
Motion on Fischer Homes proposed development on Senour Road
27.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to deny the proposed zone change on Senour
Road from R1-C to R1-C/RCD by Fischer Homes for the following reasons:
1.   As elected officials, the city is responsible for the public safety of its
residents. The city conducted its own traffic count at the Route 16/Senour Road
intersection, which indicated a high volume of traffic. Also there is a blind
spot when making a left turn from Senour Road onto Route 16.
2.   Overcrowding at the local schools. It is the responsibility of the city
officials to take into consideration the schools. Presently local schools are
at near capacity and if the overcrowding continues there is a possibility that
students would be bussed out of the community.
3.   Water – the current shortage is cause for a public safety issue. New water
transmission lines need to be installed before more development.
4.   The developer has not been required by the state highway department to
signal the Route 16/Senour Road intersection.
Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Mayor Kriege asked if there was any further
discussion. Mr. Steffen expressed concern that if the current water condition
in the city is inadequate that it could cause low water pressure and pose a
safety problem to fight fires. Mr. Dupps expressed hesitance as he agreed with
other council members concerns but is aware the land can be developed at the
current zoning. Once again, Mr. Feldhaus stressed council’s responsibility for
the public safety of its citizens. Mrs. Gabbard again pointed out that the land
could be developed at the current zone without council approval. Mr. Alley
advised council that it would be merely an administrative function for Fischer
Homes to develop the land under the current zone. Mr. Dupps stated that while
he has many of the same concerns of council and the fact it can be developed at
the current zone he feels the overlay proposal provides recreational areas and
other amenities. He is concerned that what the city ends up with may not look
as good or function as well as the overlay. Mr. Alley once again advised
council that provisions could be worked out in regard to the recreational
facilities being turned over to the city if the homeowners association would
become defunct. Mrs. Yeager stated she agreed with Mr. Dupps and had mixed
emotions on this development. Mayor Kriege stated he concurred with Mrs. Yeager
and Mr. Dupps.
28.   Mayor Kriege called for a roll call vote on the above stated motion by
Mr. Feldhaus and second by Mr. Steffen. Roll call was answered with three yes
votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus, Mr. Steffen and Mr. Ellison and four no votes cast
by Mr. Dupps, Mrs. Yeager, Mrs. Gabbard with Mayor Kriege breaking the tie.
Motion defeated 4-3.
Motion to have a short recess
29.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to take a short recess; seconded by Mr. Dupps.
Motion carried with all ayes.
30.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to resume the meeting; seconded by Mr. Dupps.
Motion carried with all ayes.
Motion to accept R1-C/RCD overlay zone change request by Fischer Homes for
Senour Rd.
31.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to accept the zone change from R1-C to R1-C/RCD
requested by Fischer Homes for the planned Senour Road development with the
following eight conditions for development:
1.   All streets in the development must be 28 feet wide
2.   Development must include retention ponds for water run-off.
3.   Installation of a turn lane on Senour Road onto Route 16 and a turn lane
on Route 16 at the intersection of Senour Road.
4.   First floor brick wrap on all homes.
5.   Two-car attached garages.
6.   Doublewide driveways.
7.   Sidewalks constructed on both sides of the streets built to ADA
specifications.
8.   Provisions made to deed over the parks to the city if the homeowners’
association would become defunct; including the park on the Covington side.
Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. A brief discussion ensued wherein Mr. Fischer
stated he would not agree to three of the conditions listed in the motion. The
three conditions he would not agree to are: first floor brick wrap on all
homes, 28-foot wide streets throughout the development, and the installation of
turn lanes. Mr. Fischer went on to say that while some homes will have a
portion of brick, the brick-wrap condition doesn’t fit the target market this
development is planned for and that the turn lanes are not his responsibility.
Mr. Ellison stated that if the state highway department overruled the city on
that condition then the city would be agreeable to that. Mr. Fischer did agree
to construct 28-foot wide streets on specific sections of the roadway but not
throughout the subdivision. Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Fischer if he was committing
to build all the homes in this subdivision. Mr. Fischer stated that it was a
high probability but would not make that commitment.
32.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Ellison if he were willing to amend his motion to
the conditions that Mr. Fischer would agree to. Mr. Ellison said he would not
amend his motion. Mayor Kriege asked for the vote to be called. Roll call on
the above motion was answered with four yes votes cast by Mr. Ellison, Mrs.
Yeager, Mr. Dupps and Mrs. Gabbard and two no votes cast by Mr. Steffen and Mr.
Feldhaus. Motion carried 4-2.
Motion to Adjourn
33.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mrs. Yeager. Motion
carried with all ayes. Meeting adjourned at 8:40 p.m.
                     ____________________________________
                     Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor
