Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
JUNE 29, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. He began by announcing the following agenda items: proposed
ordinance for the annexation of the Ferguson property at 35 Pelly Road;
proposed ordinance approving a zone change from R1-C to R1-C/RCD with the eight
conditions for the planned development on Senour Road by Fischer Homes; and,
discussion of the amended budget ordinance for fiscal year 1998/99 with a
briefing on a police SWAT program. Mayor Kriege advised all discussions and
actions would be limited to the items on the agenda.
2.   Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara Gabbard and Mr. Dupps
answered roll call. Council Member Gregory Steffen was absent. Also in
attendance was City Administrator, Gary R. Scott and Paul Alley, City Attorney
sitting in for H. Lawson Walker.
First Reading on the Annexation Ordinance of 35 Pelly Road
3.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading (in summary) of the
proposed ordinance to annex the Ferguson property located at 35 Pelly Road. Mr.
Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. City
Attorney, Paul Alley read the proposed ordinance.
Discussion/Action regarding the proposed development on Senour Road by Fischer
Homes
4.   Mayor Kriege informed council that two ordinances were before them for
review and possible adoption regarding the proposed development by Fischer
Homes on Senour Road.
Motion for a Brief Recess
5.   Mr. Ellison made a motion for a short recess to give council time to read
the proposed ordinances. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Motion carried with all
ayes.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to resume the council meeting; seconded by Mr.
Dupps. Motion carried with all ayes.
7.   Mayor Kriege began the discussion by stating that the council members,
with the exception of Mr. Feldhaus and Mr. Steffen, met with a representative
of Fischer Homes this past week to preview their proposal.
8.   Mr. Ellison commented that he has met several times and talked at great
length with Fischer representatives. He stated he feels the counteroffer is a
watered down version of the eight conditions council imposed when approving the
zone change requested by Fischer Homes for this property. He went on to say he
is not comfortable with the location of this development and with Mills Road
Park in close proximity to Senour Road there is no longer an incentive to
accept this proposal.
9.   Mr. Feldhaus stated that he expressed at the last special council meeting
that he was opposed to both the old and new proposals due to the small (55-
foot) lot sizes. He expressed concern with the development of a park on the
south side of Senour Road with only seven houses and with 291 houses across the
street he felt there was a safety issue involved with children who would be
crossing that road to use the park. He believes the only reason a park is being
planned for that side of Senour Road is because Fischer Homes is avoiding the
cost of a sewer pump station. Mr. Feldhaus appealed to the other council
members to deny both proposals. He went on to say that to approve this type of
cluster, trailer-park style development, when the city is not landlocked, is
ridiculous.
10.   Mrs. Gabbard questioned the city attorney regarding the difference
between the two proposed ordinances for this development. Mr. Alley advised
that the first ordinance version included the eight conditions outlined in Mr.
Ellison’s motion at the last council meeting on June 22, 1999 wherein the zone
change requested by Fischer Homes would be approved if the conditions were met.
He stated the second ordinance version incorporated the letter of commitment by
Mr. Fischer and some other provisions.
11.   Mayor Kriege commented that all conditions by Mr. Ellison and committed
conditions by Mr. Fischer were laid out at the last council meeting and
incorporated into the two proposed ordinances before them tonight.
Motion to Deny the Proposed Zone Change by Fischer Homes
12.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to turn down the Fischer Homes proposal by
reverting back to the current zone of R1-C. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion.
13.   Mayor Kriege asked if there was any further discussion. Mr. Alley
restated the one proposed ordinance outlined the eight conditions imposed by
council if they chose to grant the proposed zone change.
14.   Mr. Trauth, attorney for Fischer Homes, reminded council that Mr. Fischer
agreed to five of those conditions and certain elements of the other three
conditions. He also stated they superimposed some additional conditions.
15.   Mrs. Gabbard questioned the city attorney regarding guidelines in turning
down this zone change. Mr. Alley stated council needed to state their findings.
16.   Mr. Dupps cautioned the other council members in turning down this zone
change request as Mr. Fischer is offering amenities that are not required. Mr.
Ellison replied that he feels the amenities do not outweigh the drawbacks and
the city needs to look to the future. He stated he agreed with Mr. Feldhaus
that a cluster development is not necessary with an abundance of land in the
city.
17.   Mr. Feldhaus commented that Fischer Homes has proposed this cluster
development because it is more cost effective for them. Once again he voiced
his reasons for his opposition to this development, those being; concern for
the safety of children crossing Senour Road to use the proposed park, small lot
size of 55 feet, and apprehension that Mr. Fischer will not be developing this
subdivision but parceling it out to other developers.
18.   Mayor Kriege stated the Planning Commission has recommend the city
approve this plan and does not feel they would have done so if the plan was
substandard. Mr. Ellison commented that it is just a recommendation and if the
city agrees with that type of development then it is okay with them.
19.   Mrs. Gabbard agreed that Mr. Feldhaus and Mr. Ellison had some valid
points. She questioned the Fischer representatives regarding the brick-wrap
condition. Mr. Gorman of Fischer Homes stated that Mr. Fischer would not commit
to brick-wrap and stated that vinyl can be done nicely and maintenance free. He
did state that in all likelihood some homes would have partial brick. And
regarding Mr. Fischer developing the entire subdivision, he stated he would be
the builder depending on which plan was approved by council.
20.   At this time Mayor Kriege asked for a roll call vote on the above stated
motion. Roll call vote was answered with three yes votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus,
Mr. Ellison and Mrs. Yeager and two no votes cast by Mr. Dupps and Mrs.
Gabbard. Motion carried to turn down the Fischer Homes proposal by reverting
back to the current zone of R1-C.
Motion for a Brief Recess
21.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to take a brief recess; seconded by Mr. Dupps.
Motion carried with all ayes.
22.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to resume the meeting; seconded by Mrs. Gabbard.
Motion carried with all ayes.
Discussion on Amended Budget Ordinance No. 1999-O-06 (with Police SWAT
briefing)
23.   Mayor Kriege informed council that Chief Ed Porter was present to provide
a briefing on the SWAT program per their request at the last council meeting.
24.   Chief Porter gave a presentation on the SWAT program he has formed. He
began by stating he personally has twenty-one years of tactical unit experience
with ten of those years being with a tactical/SWAT unit. He showed a ten-minute
film depicting a swat situation wherein the law enforcement response was poor
and he commented that this situation made law enforcement officials recognize
the need for special tactical units. Chief Porter explained that in the last
three and one-half years since he has been chief, the city has been
experiencing an increase in drug trafficking, domestic violence and barricade/
suicide cases. He stated that during the last twelve months the police
department has experienced three high-risk situations.
25.   Chief Porter stated that currently the City of Covington and the Kentucky
State Police departments have tactical units and the City of Crescent Springs
has a composite unit. He explained that response time would be poor and that he
did not think the use of those units was a viable option for the City of
Independence. He informed council that he feels it would be wrong not to
respond to the need for a tactical unit. He stated that currently six
Independence officers and two Elsmere officers have received SWAT training. He
reported that expenses to date include $1,666.00 for uniforms and $3,913.00 for
other related equipment. Also, state surplus supplies have been received at no
cost to the city. He explained that some of the costs have been partially
offset through forfeiture funds collected.
26.   In closing, Chief Porter stated that he took an oath to lookout for the
citizens’ safety and feels the cost of a single incident could outweigh the
cost of funding the SWAT unit.
27.   Mr. Dupps asked if the SWAT team would be an ad hoc unit to be used as
needed. Chief Porter said they would but would come together for training, etc.
Mr. Feldhaus asked the Chief if he had spoken with Chief Bosse of Covington and
Chief Porter replied that he had. Officer Nichols interjected that other cities
contract with Covington to provide SWAT services as needed. Mr. Feldhaus asked
what other cities paid to contract with Covington. Officer Nichols stated that
it varied and could be as high as $10,000. Mr. Feldhaus stated that he felt
Independence should look into contracting with Covington because the city has
already spent over $5,000 for this program. Mrs. Gabbard questioned how the
city could put a price on what it costs to save a life.
28.   A lengthy discussion ensued regarding the cost of the SWAT program and
the feasibility of contracting with another local agency for this type of
tactical service as the need arises. Mayor Kriege informed council that when
Chief Porter initially discussed this program with him he felt it was an
important endeavor and gave his support. He stated that with the addition of so
many new households this is a public safety program the police department needs
to develop with backup help from the other agencies. Mr. Scott asked Chief
Porter what the annual maintenance cost would be for this program. Chief Porter
stated that much of the equipment purchased can have dual purposes and
estimated an additional $2,000-$3000 to complete the purchase of tactical
equipment. After that, there will be minimal maintenance, mainly four hours of
training per month per officer. Mrs. Yeager questioned whether there was a
mutual aid agreement with the City of Elsmere. Mr. Ellison asked Chief Porter
if the Northern Kentucky Police Chiefs Association had discussed a SWAT
program. Chief Porter stated that would be inappropriate. Mr. Ellison stated he
felt a Northern Kentucky unit should be formed before forming another
individual unit. Mr. Feldhaus suggested contracting with the City of
Covington’s SWAT team for a couple of years to get an idea of what the costs
will be and whether or not it would be practical to form our own unit. Once
again, Chief Porter stated that in the last year there have been six possible
incidents where a SWAT team could have been used.
29.   Mr. Dupps questioned Chief Porter about the four hours of training needed
each month. Chief Porter clarified that the four hours of training would be in
addition to the in-service requirement.
30.   Mrs. Gabbard restated that the money spent for this program was from
budgeted funds and she did not see a problem with that. Mr. Feldhaus reminded
council that the police department budget for the 99/00 fiscal year increased
from $1.3M to $1.5M. Mr. Ellison stated that during the Planning Session held
in January the SWAT program was never mentioned. He stated the program should
have been a long-term plan for the city.
31.   Mayor Kriege stated that when he spoke with Chief Porter regarding this
program last winter he told him he would support it as long as it was within
the realms of his budget. He stated that discussion of the SWAT unit was not
intentionally hidden from council and apologized for failing to discuss this
with council. Mr. Feldhaus stated he believed Mayor Kriege did not consciously
withhold this information. Mayor Kriege stated the Chief felt the formation of
this program fell under his realm.
32.   Mayor Kriege suggested having finance/budget meetings prior to the
regular council meetings. He also suggested forming a Tactical Unit Committee
and asked Mr. Dupps, Mrs. Yeager and Mr. Feldhaus to serve on this committee.
He stated he would like to get this resolved and suggested working with the
City of Elsmere to see what resources they could provide. Mr. Feldhaus stated
he would like to see what other options are available. Mr. Ellison agreed the
city should try to tap other resources. He also commented the city would be
remiss to overlook the skills of Chief Porter.
33.   Mayor Kriege instructed council of the need to amend the 98/99 budget and
pressed for a conclusion toward this disagreement.
Motion for a Second Reading of Ordinance No. 1999-O-06 to Amend the 1998/99
Budget
34.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance No. 1999-O-
06 to amend the 1998/99 Budget. Mrs. Gabbard second the motion. Roll call vote
was answered with all ayes. Paul Alley read the proposed ordinance.
35.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 1999-O-06; seconded by
Mrs. Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
36.   After a brief discussion wherein Amy Guenther, Finance Director, pointed
out that the $15,000 revenue and expense items for the Community Crime
Prevention grant was inadvertently omitted from the first and second readings
of the amended budget ordinance it was decided to have an emergency reading of
the ordinance.
37.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to have an emergency reading of the proposed
Ordinance No. 1999-O-06 to amend the 1998/99 budget in order to include the
revenue and expense line of $15,000 for the Community Crime Prevention grant.
Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried and Mr. Alley read proposed Ordinance No. 1999-O-06.
38.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 1999-O-06 as read;
seconded by Mrs. Gabbard. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried.
Adjournment
39.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mrs. Yeager. Motion
carried with all ayes. Meeting adjourned at 9:03 p.m.

Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

JULY 12, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Rev. Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave the
invocation. Council members Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara Gabbard, and
Eric Dupps answered roll call. Council members Gregory Steffen and Steve
Feldhaus were absent. Mr. Feldhaus and Mr. Steffen were out of town. Also in
attendance were Gary Scott, City Administrator and H. Lawson Walker, City
Attorney.
2.   Mayor Kriege recognized and welcomed two groups in the audience, the first
being Boy Scout Troop 779 from St. Pius in Edgewood who have members that
reside in Independence. The boy scouts were observing the meeting to earn their
citizenship merit badge. The second group was from Northern Kentucky
University. Professor Bill Dorsey’s Local Government Management class was
observing the meeting as a class assignment.
Approval of Council Minutes
3.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to adopt the minutes of the June 7, 1999 council
meeting as amended. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Motion carried with all
ayes.
4.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to adopt the minutes of the June 22, 1999 special
council meeting as submitted. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Motion carried
with all ayes.
5.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to adopt the minutes of the June 29, 1999
special council meeting as submitted. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Motion
carried with all ayes.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
6.   There was a large group of residents in the audience to speak in
opposition of the planned development of the land at the corner of Cox and
Taylor Mill Roads by James Berling on behalf of the Scheben Group. Mayor Kriege
stated that the city was aware the Kenton County & Municipal Planning & Zoning
Commission had approved the zone change and informed the residents that Mr.
Berling has not approached the city regarding this matter. Mayor Kriege went on
to say that the city will have sixty days to respond before the rezoning
actually takes effect and the city will review the issue and make a decision by
the regular council meeting in August (8-2-99).
7.   City Attorney, Lawson Walker, advised the residents that the city would,
by law, be unable to override the Planning Commission’s decision unless, as an
appellate body reviewing their recommendation, was able to find something wrong
– a fact that would cause the decision to be overturned. Mr. Walker reiterated
that the city is given a sixty-day interval to review the recommendation by the
Planning Commission.
8.   Spokespeople for the Jimae Avenue area that voiced opposition to the
planned development of ninety-eight condominiums by Berling included: Ron
Flack, John Little, Eric Thomas, William Ruzinok, Donald Barnett, Pat Yeager
and Doug Davidson. The residents major concerns were the increase in the
traffic at that intersection which is already a problem, unsafe ingress and
egress points, fear that their property values will decrease, an overall change
of the community’s environment, and being surrounded by more multi-family
buildings in a single family residential area. Mr. Ruzinok was concerned that
members on the Planning Commission do not live in Independence yet are able to
dictate what can be built in another community. A comment was made that Mr.
Berling has informally met with some of the Jimae area residents regarding the
possibility of tapping into sewer lines that will be available (for a fee) if
the development is constructed. Mr. Barnett stated that while he is not against
progress he felt ninety-eight units was too much and expressed concern that the
development would become low-income housing.
9.   The discussion turned to the increasing problem with vandalism and theft
in the Jimae Avenue area. Residents stated that paychecks have been stolen from
mailboxes, new trashcans have been stolen, and homes have been broken into.
Chief Porter attempted to address their concerns and encouraged their aiding
the police department in deterring the crime in the area. Mr. Dupps and Mr.
Ellison encouraged the residents to form a Neighborhood Watch Program. Chief
Porter stated that Sgt. Bailey would be glad to meet with them to form this
program.
10.   In closing, Mayor Kriege advised the residents that this re-zoning issue
would probably be on the August 2, 1999 council meeting and encouraged them to
attend that meeting.
Second Reading of Ordinance No. 1999-O-07 Annexing 35 Pelly Road
11.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance No. 1999-O-

Pelly Road. Mrs. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call vote 4-0 in favor;

AUGUST 2, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara Gabbard, Eric
Dupps, Steve Feldhaus and Greg Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance
were Gary Scott, City Administrator and H. Lawson Walker, City Attorney.
Presentation of Proclamation
2.   Mayor Kriege presented a Proclamation from the city to John Crawford for
his Eagle Scout Achievement. John Crawford was not able to attend the meeting.
Adoption of Council Minutes
3.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to accept the minutes of the July 12, 1999 council
meeting as amended. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Motion carried with 5 ayes
and 1 abstain by Mr. Feldhaus.
Scheben Group – Zone Change for Property at Cox and Taylor Mill Roads
4.   Mr. Feldhaus presented a portion of the taped meeting of July 1, 1999 of
the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission regarding the request
for a zone change at the Taylor Mill & Cox Road property by the Scheben Group.
Privileges of the Floor
5.   Gail Wallace of 6396 Jimae Court spoke about her feelings on the zone
change request by the Scheben Group. She stated that her property adjoins this
property and she is not happy about having an apartment complex built in her
back yard and she also felt there was a danger now, at the corner of Cox Road
and Taylor Mill Rd because of a rise in the road going west before you get to
Jimae. She felt an increase in traffic would create more accidents even if they
do install a turn lane.
6.   William Ruzinok stated the petition that was turned in has a lot of
complaints about water pressure on Jimae and he feels that is another reason
the city does not need 96 units built on this land. Mr. Feldhaus advised Mr.
Ruzinok that any water problems in that area needs to be reported to Taylor
Mill Utilities.
7.   John Little at 6413 Jimae stated he prefers single-family homes as opposed
to an apartment complex.
8.   Don Barnett stated he fears that this apartment complex will turn into low
income housing, increased traffic will be a problem and water and sewage run
off will be a problem. He stated that after viewing the tape of the Kenton
County Municipal Planning and Zoning meeting he feels they are ignoring the
comprehensive plan and he feels that is a good reason for the city not to
approve the zone change.
9.   Mr. Feldhaus wanted council to be aware that if they vote to change the
zoning to R-2 it does not mean that only condominiums will be built. Once the
zone is changed there will be nothing to restrict the developer from putting in
apartments if they want to.
10.   Mayor Kriege stated that he feels Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission is not following the comprehensive plan with regard to density.
Mayor Kriege entertained a motion to present council with a resolution to
approve or reject the zone change.
11.   City Attorney, Mr. Walker advised council that they must follow KRS,
chapter 100 laws and what occurred at the planning commission public hearing
meeting. Mrs. Gabbard asked the city attorney if council decides to reject the
zone change, would council have to give a reason for the rejection. Mr. Walker
advised Mrs. Gabbard that council would need to find a reason to reject the
zone change. Mr. Walker said he tends to agree with Northern Kentucky Municipal
Planning & Zoning attorney, Mr. Schneider that the legal issue is a single
family residence with approximately 5 units per acre, and a multi-family zone
at 10 units per acre and the planning commission staff condition was to impose
the condition to go to 7 units per acre to match the comprehensive plan. Mr.
Walker stated that they removed that condition from the staff’s recommendation
and went to 10. Mr. Walker felt there was room for this council to conclude
what it wants to conclude if that is their desire.
12.   Kevin Barbian, Zoning Administrator advised Mayor and council that this
zone change request has not been to the planning and zoning sub-committee. He
stated he was under the impression that no decisions would be made until after
that meeting. Mayor Kriege advised Kevin Barbian that council has to act within
45 days and the next council meeting is not until September 13th. He stated the
concerned residents in the audience were told that action would be taken at
this meeting
13.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to draft a resolution rejecting the zone
change at the corner of Taylor Mill and Cox Road for the following reasons: the
zone change is not compatible with the comprehensive plan, overcrowding of
schools, increase of traffic when the density is increased, inadequate water
pressure, infrastructure, and the curb cut is not adequate. Mr. Dupps seconded
the motion. Mayor Kriege asked the city attorney if the city could apply for a
zone change to make it a certain zone. Mr. Walker advised the city could go
through the same process as a planner would to get a zone change. Roll call was
answered with all ayes.
14.   Mayor Kriege asked if anyone from the audience had anything else to
discuss. A resident did ask if the meeting on Wednesday to discuss the Mills
Road development was still scheduled. Mr. Scott stated it was and it will take
place at the Kenton County Court House due to an interest from the public.
Motion to Recess
15.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to take a five-minute recess. Mr. Feldhaus
seconded the motion. The motion was carried with all ayes.
16.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion for the meeting to return to session. Mr.
Ellison seconded the motion. The motion was passed with all ayes.
OLD BUSINESS
Renaming the Park in Hartland Subdivision
17.   Mayor Kriege stated they have the issue of renaming the park at Hartland
Subdivision. He stated this recommendation came from the Independence
Recreation Committee. Mr. Ellison made a motion to rename the park to
Independence Park. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Mr. Steffen stated that
Independence Park was a bland name. Mr. Feldhaus asked if he had any
suggestions. Mr. Steffen suggested the name of Marshall Hopperton Park. Ms.
Yeager stated they are going to take care of that at Memorial Park. They are
planning on having memorials for the policemen and fire department and also for
people that have donated their time to the developing of the parks and also war
memorials. Mayor Kriege added that he liked that idea better because it gave
the city an opportunity to recognize the people that have died. He felt that
memorials were better than naming parks after people. Roll call was answered
with 5 yeas and 1 nay cast by Mr. Steffen.
NEW BUSINESS

18.   Mayor Kriege stated the next item of business is a first reading of a
proposed Ordinance for setting the 1999 tax rate for the City of Independence.
Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have the ordinance read. Mr. Ellison seconded the

First Reading of Ordinance to set Trash Assessment
19.   Mayor Kriege stated the next item of new business pertains to a first
reading of a proposed ordinance setting the 1999 trash assessment rate. Mr.
Scott advised council that this rate is based on the contract we have with
Rumpke and it was not debatable unless council chooses to break the contract.
Mr. Feldhaus asked if this was the third year of a five-year contract. Mr.
Scott noted it was.
20.    Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have the ordinance read. Mr. Steffen
seconded the motion. The motion was carried with all ayes. City Attorney,
Mr.Walker read the ordinance in summary. Mr. Ellison asked if there was a cut
off of 4 units per dwelling and after that are the residents on their own for
having their trash picked up. Mr. Walker stated that the contract reads “each
unit of any building which is used for residential purposes no matter how many
units there are.” Mr. Ellison stated that there used to be a maximum of 4 units
and after that you would have to go to a dumpster service which was more
costly. Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Scott to look into this matter for the next
council meeting.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Administrator-Gary Scott
21.   Mr. Scott stated that the Finance Committee has reviewed and recommended
the Investment Policy enclosed in council packets. It, in essence, establishes
an investment policy for the city according to the KRS 66.480. We will not
invest in Mortgaged Backed and Derivative Securities and it gives the maturity
parameters, allows the finance committee to meet once a year to review, allows
the Mayor and City Administrator to oversee the investment of funds, no more an
5% of the portfolio may be invested in any single issuer except the U.S.
Government and its agencies or repurchase agreements Collateralized by U.S.
Government Securities, and the city use qualified investment agents under KRS
91A.060 and 66.480. The finance committee along with Amy Guenther and members
of Fifth Third Bank has reviewed these guidelines. He also stated this policy
has been reviewed by Mr. Walker.
22.    Ms. Yeager made a motion to adopt the Investment Policy and Guidelines.
Mrs. Gabbard seconded the motion. The motion was passed with all ayes.
23.   Mr. Scott stated the next item on the agenda was Resolution 1999-R-06. He
stated this was “boiler plate” language that comes right out of the manual for
applications for Community Development Block Grants. The city is reapplying
this year for funding for the Independence Senior Center. Last year the city
was not selected to receive funds for this.
24.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to read and accept Resolution 1999-R-06. Mr.
Ellison seconded the motion. The motion was passed with all ayes. City
Attorney, Walker read the Resolution in summary.
Building/Zoning Administrator-Kevin Barbian
25.   Mr. Barbian advised mayor and council that 71 new building permits had
been issued for the month of July probably due to the increase in sewer tap in
fees being increased to $1,800.00 by the Sanitation District.
26.   Mr. Barbian gave an update on trucks being parked on vacant lots around
the city. He stated that he had received a letter from Cherokee IGA, not
Cherokee Bowl at the present time, giving him approval to tow any vehicles off
of their lot. Mr. Feldhaus asked if there were laws regarding hazardous
materials being stored on these trucks that are being parked in the city. If
these trucks do not have a plaqer showing what they are carrying this could be
a hazard for the residents in the area. Chief Porter stated that we are dealing
with federal regulations as far as trucks being parked on private property. Mr.
Feldhaus asked Mr. Walker if the city could draft an ordinance to prohibit this
type of action. Mr. Walker stated you couldn’t interfere with a trucks right to
come in and out of the city. Mr. Walker advised is it hard to regulate private
property. Chief Porter stated the problem is the trucks are parking on the
Cherokee Bowl side of the parking lot. He stated that the zoning ordinance
stated we have the right to tow without the permission of the property owner.
Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Barbian to also get a letter to the owner of the trim
shop at the corner of Taylor Mill and Cox Road regarding tractors being parked
there.
27.   Mr. Barbian reported he is also in the process of revoking the building
permit at 4011 Thomas Drive since no activity has taken place for 6 months and
will also be asking the Board of Adjustment, to revoke the conditional use
permit for a day care at the same address.
28.   Mr. Feldhaus stated he received info in his packet about the deviation at
Lakefield Subdivision regarding the asphalt and a moisture density test. Mr.
Scott advised Mr. Feldhaus that they are looking into that. He stated that even
though it was outside of what they liked, it was still in the parameters and it
was okay.
29.   Mayor Kriege asked about the site distance at Battle Ridge Subdivision on
Bristow Road. Mr. Feldhaus asked if they were in the process of correcting the
problem. Mr. Scott said they were not. Mr. Feldhaus asked if the city was going
to stop the building permits in Battle Ridge. Mr. Scott stated that the state
was asked to do some corrections there and the state turned down the request to
make any changes. Mr. Scott stated there is a sight distance problem on Bristow
Road by Biz Cain’s farm. Mr. Scott asked Mr. Walker if the city could stop any
building permits if it is approved under the planning and zoning commission and
it is within the zone, because of the site distance problem. Mr. Walker stated
that it would be in the jurisdiction of the state and not the city because
Bristow Road is a state road. Mr. Feldhaus stated the access point would be
under the direction of the developer. Mr. Scott stated that the planning
commission is aware of this problem. Mr. Feldhaus asked if the city was going
to permit continued building with this problem. Mayor Kriege stated the city
should follow up with the planning commission on this violation and stop the
building permits until the city can get some action.

ten days before repairs are totally complete and those repairs could cost an
additional $20,000.00.
35.   Discussion was about an old pond behind Gunstock. Mr. Briggs suggested a
drainage study be done to see if the pond is needed. Ms. Yeager asked Dan
Briggs to give the city a price on this so something can be done. Mr. Feldhaus
asked Mr. Briggs to bring back to the next council meeting a price on digging
out the pond and a price on eliminating the pond. Mr. Scott stated that whether
or not it was designed as a retention basin it has become one over the years
and it will eventually affect the resident homes down stream and we have enough
drainage problems there without creating a new one. Mr. Briggs advised council
and mayor that repair costs to the pond would be determined as based on whether
or not the pond was actually needed.
36.   Mr. Briggs reported that Clubhouse Drive has had 18 tons of asphalt added
to the street where it was needed. He stated asphalt was more cost effective
because Clubhouse is on a 2 to 3 year rebuild cycle. He stated that he met with
a mud jacking company and they are going to pump some concrete under Falcon
Ridge Drive because after 4 years the panels are starting to break which is not
good in such a short period of time.

38.   Mr. Briggs stated the sidewalks from Simon Kenton to Summit View Schools

could help out due to it being such a big project.

SEPTEMBER 13, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara
Gabbard, Eric Dupps and Greg Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance
were Gary Scott, City Administrator and H. Lawson Walker, City Attorney.
Approval of Council Minutes
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of the regular
meeting of August 2, 1999 as submitted. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. No
roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Motion to Reject Zone Change Application by Clint Fornash
3.   Mayor Kriege informed the audience that Mr. Fornash has withdrawn his
request to re-zone his property on Mills Road. Mr. Walker informed council that
this withdrawal of the zone change application is before them and recommends
they make a formal acceptance.
4.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to reject zone change application number Z-99-
07-10-1424R based on the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission’s
recommendation to deny the change. Mrs. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call
vote was unanimous. Motion carried 6-0.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Mr. Ehmet Hayes, 870 Bristow Road, spoke in defense of the RCD Overlay
Zone, which the city has made application to the Kenton County Municipal
Planning & Zoning Commission for a text amendment to the Zoning Ordinance to
add provisions to discontinue its use. Mr. Hayes stated that he is a
professional architect and mainly designs commercial building. He stated that
the RCD Overlay Zone, when used properly, is a good plan and perhaps the
original intents could be incorporated in the Comprehensive Plan when it is
updated next year. He went on to say that the overlay reserves greenspace and
landscape features that are being destroyed otherwise. He feels that a
vehicular problem is occurring because it is becoming necessary to get in a car
to go to parks and other green space areas. He stated there was a lot of
comments at the Area Planning Commission meeting and again, reiterated the
overlay zone is a great tool when used properly. Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Hayes
if he would be willing to serve on a committee to help formulate the
Comprehensive Plan for the next update in the year 2001. Mr. Hayes agreed to
serve on a planning committee.
6.   Mr. Wayne Bridges, 732 Scott Avenue, Covington, Kentucky, stated that he
was present at this meeting to speak on the Fornash property zone change issue
but since that matter has been withdrawn he stated he would like to comment on
the RCD Overlay Zone issue. He spoke in opposition to this type of zone because
the city is developing public parks for the resident’s use and objects to
subdivision developers designating unbuildable hillsides as parks. He also
commented that most Homeowner Association’s don’t work, with Beechgrove being
the only exception.
7.   Mayor Kriege stated that he concurred with council and feels the city
should begin planning these types of developments for the future.
8.   Mr. Jeffrey J. Jarboe, 10174 Marshall Road, submitted to council a three
page written document outlining the reasons to deny the zone change request by
Clint and Loraine Fornash et al. Some of the reasons included: public safety
due to increased traffic, water run-off flooding, infrastructure inadequacies,
and the overcrowding of local schools.
9.   Mr. Dupps commented that he agrees with Mr. Hayes regarding the RCD
overlay. He would like to see as much greenspace reserved as possible but would
like it to be a benefit to the city. He went on to say that the infrastructure
was not in place for the proposed locations that have recently been chosen for
these types of developments.
10.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Jarboe if he would volunteer to sit on the
Comprehensive Plan update committee that the Mayor would like to assemble. Mr.
Jarboe replied that he would. Mayor Kriege asked those interested in serving on
this committee to leave their name with the City Clerk.
11.   Mrs. Gabbard stated that the current city parks are centrally located and
accessible to all residents and encouraged involvement
First Reading of Proposed Ordinance to discontinue the RCD Overlay Zone & Flag
Lots
12.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to provide provisions to discontinue the RCD overlay zone and to
prohibit flag lots. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. The City Attorney, Mr.
Walker read the ordinance.
Second Reading of Ordinance No. 1999-O-08 Setting the 1999 Tax Rate
13.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance No. 1999-O-
08 setting the 1999 real estate and personal property tax rate. Mr. Steffen
seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes. The City Attorney, Mr.
Walker read the ordinance.
14.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 1999-O-08 as read;
seconded by Mrs. Yeager. Roll call vote was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 6-0 in favor.
Second Reading of Ordinance No. 1999-O-09 Setting the 1999 Trash Assessment
Rate
15.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to assess the trash rate for 1999; seconded by Mr. Ellison. A
discussion ensued regarding the residential unit charge for duplex and multi-
family dwellings. The City Clerk commented that the individual unit rate is
multiplied by two, three or four depending on the number of units present at
the location address and that the larger apartment buildings generally contract
privately for dumpster service at the location. Mr. Ellison was concerned that
multi-family buildings housing over four units would be using the city trash
service at a lesser cost that a dumpster. Mayor Kriege advised that the city is
in the third year of a five-year contract with Rumpke for the trash collection
and that he would need to review the contract to see how it relates to multi-
family units. Mr. Feldhaus also commented that the cost last year for each
residential unit was $84.60 and the 1999 rate will be $86.88, up by $2.28 over
last year. He also advised that the assessment is a pass-through cost to the
residents.
16.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to accept Ordinance No. 1999-O-09; seconded by
Mr. Steffen. Roll call vote was answered with five yes votes and one no vote
cast by Mr. Ellison. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance to Adopt a Supplement to the Code of Ordinances
17.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to have a first reading on the proposed
ordinance to adopt the supplement to the Code of Ordinances of the city;
seconded by Mrs. Yeager. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
18.   There was a brief discussion regarding this ordinance. Mr. Lawson stated
he did not draft this ordinance but that the Burlington Publishing Company
supplied it to the city as a service along with the codification supplement.
Mr. Feldhaus also asked the City Clerk to look into purchasing the codification
on compact discs. The City Attorney, Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Discussion of a Proposed Ordinance to Amend Ordinance No. 1995-O-05
Establishing Building/Zoning Fee Schedule for the City
19.   Mayor Kriege introduced a discussion regarding the amendment of Ordinance
No. 1995-O-05 that would increase the new construction building fee rate for
single and multi-family dwellings from .09 cents per square foot to .20 cents
per square foot. Some council members voiced concern that the commercial
construction should also be charged the increased fee and not just target the
single and multi-family dwellings. Mr. Dupps suggested sending this matter to
the Planning & Zoning Committee for review and recommendation to council at a
later date.
20.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to table the amendment of Ordinance No. 1995-O-
05; seconded by Mrs. Gabbard. Motion carried with all ayes.
Discussion of a Proposed Dangerous Animal Ordinance
21.   Mayor Kriege submitted a draft ordinance to council, which he asked the
city attorney to prepare that would prohibit vicious dogs and provide for their
registration. Mr. Feldhaus asked what prompted this ordinance to be drafted.
Police Chief Porter replied there was an incident on Sugar Camp Drive wherein
the mother of the owner of the dog was viciously attacked and the dog was
killed. Mr. Walker, City Attorney, informed council that he learned the City of
Maysville had an ordinance of this type that was considered very good and
requested a copy to use as a guideline. He stated he feels the ordinance is a
good one to begin working with as he feels the ordinance is all encompassing.
He stated the ordinance sets forth conditions to permit such animals to be
within the city and does not outright ban them. He advised that an ordinance
that would ban vicious animals would be subject to challenge. He stated that
the ordinance submitted to them could be enacted in partially or in its
entirety. There was a brief discussion and the consensus of council was to have
the proposed ordinance reviewed by the Public Safety Committee and brought back
to the next meeting with a recommendation(s).
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Administrator – Gary R. Scott
22.   Mr. Scott reported the Public Works Department put out bids for a dump
truck and that the dealership that submitted the lowest bid would not be able
to deliver the vehicle for six to eight weeks. The next bid came in at
$43.465.00 and the vehicle is available now. Since the department is currently
renting a pickup truck for one of the workers he stated he feels it would be
more feasible to take the next lowest bid because of the availability. He
requested council declare the $43,465.00 bid as the best bid. Mr. Feldhaus
agreed and stated that waiting six to eight weeks or more would be courting
with the bad weather months.
23.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the bid from Middletown Ford for a
dump truck at the cost of $43,465.00 as the lowest and best bid. Mr. Steffen
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0.
24.   Mr. Scott also reported he would gather a staff committee to develop a
Park Plan for the city. He stated that with the rapid growth of the city he
would like to realize a solid plan so that a fiscal fund can be devoted to
capital improvements of the parks. Mrs. Yeager stated that the Independence
Recreation Committee already develops plans for the parks and asked what role
the IRC would play in this. Mr. Scott replied the staff committee would plan
development steps with budgeted funds in an orderly manner and then would
present the scheme to the IRC. There was a brief discussion regarding the lack
of adequate parking spaces at the Independence Park as this area is used by the
Independence Soccer League as a practice facility and there is not enough
spaces for parking. Mayor Kriege asked the Park Plan Committee to look at that
matter to determine a possible solution.

spending much of her time becoming familiar with the city.

Cardinal Engineering – Dave Whitacre
32.   Mr. Whitacre stated that due to the recent drought he has some concerns
with regard to the streets. He informed council that when the ground becomes
this dry and hard it begins to pull away from the roads. When the fast and hard
rains come the water will run under the road and in between the cracks and
cause erosion and slabs to settle. He stated there is no preventive measure the
city can take; just hope the first rains of the season are slow and steady
until the ground is fully saturated and the gaps are closed.
33.   There was a brief discussion regarding liability when a manhole cover

with this condition in the Independence Pointe Subdivision.

Discussion on the SWAT Committee
45.   Mr. Feldhaus suggested to Mayor Kriege that an update on the SWAT
Committee be reported to council. Mayor Kriege advised that Chief Porter and
Chief Green from the City of Elsmere were going to review an equitable
agreement between the two cities with plans to eventually expand to Kenton
County and the City of Erlanger. Mr. Feldhaus stated that when he agreed to be
a member of the SWAT Committee he thought it was to review the feasibility of
forming a SWAT team. He now feels the decision was already made. Mayor Kriege
disagreed and stated that as long as he stayed within the budget council
provided him that there shouldn’t be a problem. Mr. Feldhaus argued that not
once during the Budget meetings or the Public Safety Committee meetings was the
formation of a SWAT team ever mentioned. He went on to say that he felt that
the City of Covington’s SWAT team could provide this type of tactical services
when the need arises.
46.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to discontinue the SWAT team. The motion died
for lack of a second.
47.   Mrs. Gabbard commented that she disagrees with Mr. Feldhaus and that as
long as the expenses for the SWAT team come from the allotted budget that she
has no problem with that.
48.   Mayor Kriege informed council that he has spoken with the City
Administrator of Erlanger who expressed an interest in joining the SWAT team.
He also stated he has been told that Kenton County is interested too. He said
the city needs to present them with an option and is in the process of setting
this up with Chief Green. Mayor Kriege disputed Mr. Feldhaus’ statements by
maintaining he feels he has allowed the council members to be a part of the
executive decisions and makes every effort to keep them informed. Mayor Kriege
closed the discussion.

CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. He began by announcing the following agenda items for this special
meeting of council:
a)   Discussion and possible action regarding the proposed development at the
corner of Taylor Mill and Cox Roads by the Scheben Company.
b)   Discussion and possible second reading of the proposed Ordinance providing
for the addition of provisions to discontinue the RCD Overlay Zone and to
prohibit flag lots.
2.   Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps,
and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. City Administrator, Gary R. Scott, and
City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker was also present.
Proposed Ordinance to Discontinue the RCD Overlay Zone & Prohibit Flag Lots
3.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance that would provide for the addition of provisions to discontinue the
RCD Overlay Zone and to prohibit flag lots in the city. Mr. Steffen seconded
the motion. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Walker read Ordinance No. 1999-O-
11.
4.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 1999-O-11 as read. Mr.
Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried.
Discussion of Planned Development by the Scheben Group at corner of Cox &
Taylor Mill Roads
5.   City Attorney, Mr. Walker, began by explaining that at the last regular
meeting council had moved to re-consider the zone change request for the
property at the corner of Cox and Taylor Mill Roads. He advised that the
decision to re-consider did not rescind the previous motion at the August 2,
1999 meeting wherein council rejected the zone change request. Mr. Walker
informed the audience that council could hear their comments regarding this
proposed zone change but that council had to make their decision based on
Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission’s recommendation. He went
on to say that this meeting was not a public hearing on the matter. Mr. Walker
also stated that he was aware there have been meetings between the developer
and some residents of the Jimae Court area. At this time he offered the floor
to Mr. Jerry Dusing, the attorney representing the Scheben Group.
6.   Mr. Dusing reiterated Mr. Walker’s advise to council that this meeting was
not a public hearing and that council had to make their decision based on the
recommendation before them from the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning
Commission. Mr. Dusing stated that the developer was willing to agree to the
following conditions: 1) they would change the access road from Cox Road to
Taylor Mill Road, 2) they would extend the sewer line free of charge to the
Jimae Court residents, but that does not include the tap-in fee charged by the
Sanitation District or the cost of the lateral line, and 3) they would
guarantee no more than ten percent ownership by a single person to assure this
development would not become low income housing in the future.
7.   Mr. Dusing commented that representatives of the Scheben Group had met
with the adjoining residents before they moved forward with the development
plan and had not received any unfavorable comments. He stated many of the
issues concerning the residents were not discussed at the public hearing held
by the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission.
8.   Mr. Berling, with the Scheben Group, told council that the condition to
change the egress from Cox Road to Taylor Mill Road would be subject to
approval from the Kentucky Department of Transportation on the encroachment
permits. He also clarified that the main sewer line would be extended free of
charge but that the property owner would be responsible for the cost of the
lateral line along with the tap-in fee charged by the Sanitation District.
9.   Mayor Kriege asked council if they were prepared to take action tonight on
this issue. Again, Mr. Walker explained to council that their decision to
approve or deny this zone change request needed to be based on the
recommendation of the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission. He
advised there is sufficient facts to decide either way. He stated that the
staff recommendation from Northern Kentucky Area Planning and Zoning was for
approval of the development with certain conditions; one of those conditions
being to lower the density to comply with the Comprehensive Plan. When the
development plan was submitted to KCMP&Z Commission for recommendation they
removed the density requirement. Mr. Walker advised council the NKAP&Z staff
has given them a reason to deny this zone change request. There was a brief
discussion regarding whether the motion made at the KCMP&Z Commission meeting
was in error regarding the number of units per acre. Mr. Walker advised council
they would need to go into an executive session to discuss this matter in more
detail. Mr. Feldhaus suggested they could possibly reach an agreement with the
developer to lower the number of units per acre. Mr. Walker advised that
council was not writing a zone but acting on the Planning & Zoning Commission’s
recommendation.
10.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Dusing how the condition of no more than ten-
percent ownership by an individual would guarantee this development would not
become low-income housing in the future. Mr. Dusing replied they felt this
would be a practical and effective guarantee because low-income housing
requires single ownership. Mr. Walker added that council could request that
condition be made a restrictive covenant.
Motion to Deny the Zone Change Request for Property Located at Cox & Taylor
Mills Rds.
11.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to reject the Kenton County Municipal Planning
& Zoning Commission’s recommendation on matter Z-99-06-07-1413R by finding that
the recommendations and Staff Report of the Kenton County Municipal Planning
Commission are sufficient to make its decision solely on the record before the
Planning Commission and disregarding any statements made in any meeting of the
City Council. The Council finds that the supporting information in the NKAPCP
Staff recommendation determined that the land use element of the 1996 area wide
Comprehensive Plan identifies the subject site for residential development at
4.1 to 7.0 dwelling units per acre and that the requested R-2 zone allows for a
maximum of ten dwelling units per acre and further notes that the Staff
recommended a condition be imposed upon the zone change that density not exceed
7.0 dwelling units per net acre to be consistent with the 1996 area wide
Comprehensive Plan. Since the recommendation from the Planning Commission
removed this condition and therefore if Council were to approve the zone change
as before it, development up to ten dwelling units per acre would occur and
Council finds such density not to be consistent with the area wide
Comprehensive Plan and therefore rejects the recommendation. Mr. Dupps seconded
the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Adjournment
12.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to adjourn seconded by Mr. Feldhaus. Motion
carried with all ayes. Meeting adjourned at 7:30 p.m.

Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

PRESENTATION OF THE “INDEPENDENCE TOMORROW” STRATEGIC PLAN
6.   Mayor Kriege submitted to the council members the completed strategic plan
for the city and introduced Mr. Bob Dodson, a member of the committee, to give
an overview of the document.
7.   Mr. Dodson stated the Strategic Plan is the compilation of several months
of work, from January through September of 1999. He stated that Mayor Kriege
had enlisted people from business owners to private citizens to be members of
this committee. The first order of business for the committee was to compose a
mission statement. Then the committee branched off into several sub-committees
that included Administration/Public Works, Community Development, Human
Services, and Public Safety. Each sub-committee highlighted the city’s
strengths and weaknesses for that category and recommended long and short-term
goals and objectives for the plan.
8.   Mr. Dodson emphasized that the Strategic Plan document is a work in
progress and that the committee would meet quarterly or annually to review its
progress. He stressed the recommendations in the Plan came from the citizens of
the community and is asking for council’s support.
9.   Mr. Dupps commented that the committee consisted of dedicated individuals
who put a lot of work into the development of this document. He reminded
everyone that the development of a Strategic Plan was discussed at the city’s
annual Planning Session, which was held in January of this year. Mr. Dupps
suggested adopting the Plan by Resolution at the November council meeting.
10.   Mayor Kriege stated that many objectives in the Strategic Plan have been
accomplished or in some stage of advancement.
11.   Mr. Feldhaus thanked the city staff, committee members, council members,
and facilitators for working on this Plan and stated that it provides an
excellent guideline to use as a planning tool. As an added comment he stated
that he doesn’t think the city will be able to increase representation on the
Planning & Zoning Commission but would like all interested citizens to have
input into the Comprehensive Plan update.
12.   Mrs. Yeager added that she was impressed with the committee and will be
glad to support the Strategic Plan. Mrs. Gabbard also thanked everyone involved
in the development of this plan.
13.   Mayor Kriege thanked the committee members and commented that it will be
helpful for the future planning needs of the city. He asked council to review
the document before the November meeting.

NOVEMBER 1, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Jim Ellison, Eric Dupps, Donna Yeager, Greg
Steffen, and Steve Feldhaus answered roll call. Council Member Barbara Gabbard
was absent due to illness. Also in attendance were Gary Scott, City
Administrator and H. Lawson Walker, City Attorney.
Approval of Council Minutes
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of the regular
meeting of October 4, 1999 as amended. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. No roll
call; motion carried with all ayes.
Discussion and Action Regarding the Proposed Kenton County Jail Site in Elsmere
3.   Mr. Feldhaus requested Mayor Kriege permit Beth Wulfeck to address council
regarding the Kenton County Fiscal Court’s decision to build the new jail in
Elsmere. Ms. Wulfeck was signed in to speak during the privileges of the floor
but Mayor Kriege allowed her to speak before council began the scheduled agenda
business.
4.   Ms. Wulfeck began by stating she has been working with Mr. Feldhaus and
other Independence residents regarding the Fiscal Court’s decision to build the
new jail in Elsmere. She stated a petition drive has been started in the
Beechgrove area and that a rally is scheduled for Saturday, November 6, 1999
from three until five o’clock at Turkeyfoot Acres. She informed council there
is overwhelming support in the fight against the proposed jail site. She stated
that Bob Carran, Elsmere’s city attorney would like Independence to discuss
this issue tonight. Ms. Wulfeck presented a letter from Mayor Diane Whalen,
City of Florence, to the Fiscal Court, expressing their city’s concern about
the location chosen for the new jail. She stated that Florence’s City
Administrator, Jeff Koenig stated Florence would not take any action for thirty
days. Ms. Wulfeck also passed out copies of the resolution passed by the City
of Erlanger wherein they expressed support for the 3-L Highway site as the best
location for the new jail. In closing Ms. Wulfeck requested city council to
join in the lawsuit that the City of Elsmere has filed.
5.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to instruct the city attorney to join in the
legal action with the City of Elsmere against the proposed jail site chosen by
the Kenton County Fiscal Court. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. A brief
discussion ensued regarding the necessity to discuss this matter in executive
session. Mr. Walker advised that he had not read the contents of the lawsuit
filed by the City of Elsmere and would therefore be unable to contribute to
this discussion. He stated that he does not know what the basis of the lawsuit
is. Mr. Dupps reminded council that they had recently passed a resolution in
support of the 3-L Highway site.
6.   With a motion and a second on the floor, roll call was answered with three
yes votes and two no votes cast by Mrs. Yeager and Mr. Steffen. Motion to join
in the lawsuit with the City of Elsmere carried 3-2 in favor.
Discussion Regarding the Increase in the Building & Zoning Permit Fees
7.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor for public comments regarding the proposed
increase in the building and zoning permit fees.
8.   Don Wiedeman, Executive Vice President of the Northern Kentucky Home
Builders Association addressed council with his agency’s concerns. He
distributed a list of reasons why the current building permit fee (.09cents/
sq.ft.) is in line with other area cities and counties along with a comparative
analysis of fees charged by other local cities and counties. He expressed
concern that the increased fees would be added to the cost of a home thereby
making it difficult to produce affordable housing. He also stated the Kentucky
Building Code maintains the fees charged should not exceed the cost of the
service performed and his agency feels the fees would produce revenue far in
excess of the expenses. He requested the council re-examine the proposed fees.
9.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Scott what factors were used to determine the
proposed fees. Mr. Scott advised the city now has more employees doing what one
person used to do. Mayor Kriege commented the Planning & Zoning Committee,
prior to being presented to council, approved these increases.
10.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to increase the building and zoning permit fees. Mr. Feldhaus
seconded the motion.
11.   Discussion continued when Mr. Feldhaus asked Mr. Wiedeman if the increase
in the zoning permit fee from $30.00 to $50.00 and the building permit fee from
.09 cents to .20 cents per square foot were the only issues the Home Builders
Association had opposition to. Mr. Wiedeman stated it was. Mr. Feldhaus noted
two other local cities have the same fees that Independence is proposing. Mr.
Feldhaus asked Mr. Scott how the building inspector is paid. Mr. Scott replied
that Mr. Barbian receives one-half of the revenue collected for building
permits. He reiterated that two people are now doing what one person was doing,
more staff time is involved, and this was taken into the computation of the
proposed rates. Mr. Walker advised the city is not entitled to make a profit
off regulations and does not feel that applying the overhead costs to the
expenses is outside the range. He advised the proposed fees are legally
sustainable as the city can charge indirect expenses, not just the building
inspector’s fee.
12.   Don Laake and Ted Arlinghaus, representatives of Arlinghaus Builders
addressed council. Mr. Laake felt it was unfair to make a comparison to the
City of Fort Thomas as they have little building going on. Mr. Arlinghaus
commented that other cities build for half the cost being proposed by
Independence.
13.   Larry Sprague, a representative from Henry Fischer Homes questioned
whether the city knows the actual cost and stated the public should be able to
see the data that was used to determine the proposed increase. He commented
that the City of Fort Thomas has a sophisticated building/engineering
department that includes in-house mapping data. Mr. Sprague feels the city
should show the services provided to justify the increase of fees as these fees
are passed onto the new homebuyer.
14.   Mr. Scott advised council that the current ordinance regulating the
building/zoning fees is approximately 4-5 year old. Mr. Dupps suggested working
with the Home Builders Association to come to an equitable agreement on the
proposed fees. Mr. Feldhaus concurred and withdrew his second to the motion to
have a second reading of the proposed ordinance. Mr. Steffen declined to
withdraw his motion. The motion died for lack of a second.
15.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to send the proposed ordinance increasing the
building/zoning permit fees back to the committee for review and possible
amendments. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. No roll called; motion carried with
four ayes and one nay cast by Mr. Steffen. Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
16.   Mr. Steffen suggested the city perform an assessment of actual costs.
Mayor Kriege stated a committee meeting will be scheduled and members of the
Home Builders Association will be notified.
Second Reading of Proposed Ordinance No. 1999-O-14 Lakefield Subd. Map
Amendment
17.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to enact a map amendment changing an approximate 38.4-acre section in
the Lakefield Subdivision off Taylor Mill Road from R-1C to R-1D. Mr. Ellison
seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance in summary.
18.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 1999-O-14 as read;
seconded by Mr. Dupps. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 5-
0 in favor.
Presentation of the 1998/99 Audit by Rankin & Rankin
19.   Mr. Jim Sparrow, from Rankin, Rankin & Company, reviewed the audit
performed by his company for the city. He stated that the cash had decreased
due to the payoff of the bond anticipation note but that the city had a solid
year as the revenues had increased in the areas of real estate and payroll
taxes. Council members had no questions of Mr. Sparrow.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
20.   Mr. Bob Dodson of Hunters Green Drive stated he lives on a cul de sac
where the other residents park their cars overnight on their front lawns. He
wanted to know if this was a violation of zoning regulations and asked council
to look into the matter. Mayor Kriege replied the Zoning Administrator would
investigate the situation.
21.   Steve Curley informed council that he is a builder and is currently
building homes in the Battleridge Subdivision. He stated that no building
permits are being issued in this subdivision due to the fact that the developer
has not installed streetlights yet. He informed council that all paper work has
been completed for the street lights and they are waiting for Owen Electric to
install the light equipment. Since the developer has complied with the street
lighting ordinance he requested council’s permission to begin new construction
while awaiting Owen Electric’s installation. Mayor Kriege explained the reason
behind the city’s ban on building permits in the Battleridge Subdivision. Mr.
Barbian added that some sections of the subdivision were platted before the
ordinance requiring the developer to install streetlights was adopted. Mr.
Feldhaus stated that Mr. Barbian should check with Owen Electric regarding the
streetlight installation plans and if he feels confident then he could resume
issuing permits. Council concurred.
Proposed Map Amendment by Keeney Development for Manor Hill Subdivision on
Marshall Road
22.   Before hearing public comments regarding the proposed development of the
Manor Hill Subdivision on Marshall Road, Mr. Walker explained to those in
attendance that this council meeting was not a public hearing. He advised this
matter was before the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission and
that the City of Independence was now in a legal position to act on the
recommendation of the Planning Commission. Mr. Walker advised the audience to
limit their remarks to what occurred at the Planning Commission’s public
hearing that was held on October 7, 1999 and stated that council not take new
findings into consideration when making their decision on this matter.
23.   Mr. Jerry Dusing, attorney for Keeney Development stated he would address
any topics of concern to council. He stated they are requesting the property be
re-zoned from R-1B to R-1C (PUD) in order to have a mix of houses and take
advantage of the natural features of the land. He went on to say this is one of
the finest developments he has seen and that it is very inclusive by addressing
concerns of storm water management, density, and traffic while maximizing
greenspace. He stated the development plan is in conformity with the
Comprehensive Plan and added that the storm water retention plan far exceeds
what is mandated for this type of project.
24.   Mr. Feldhaus questioned what capacity the additional 25% equated to. Mr.
Dusing replied the extra 25% allows the retention pond to hold a 100-year storm
where the minimum retention design is for a 50-year storm.
25.   Allan Sebastian, 10532 Marshall Road, expressed concern for public safety
for the planned park, which is located in a secluded area. He wanted to know if
a fence would be installed to keep park visitors off his property. He also
wanted to know who would be responsible to maintain the pond. Mr. Sabastian’s
other concern was that the curve in Marshall Road be straightened. Mr. Dusing
replied there were no plans for a security fence and that the sport fields
would be owned and maintained by a homeowners association.
26.   Mr. Dusing commented that the storm water issue is a big concern with
many of the residents downstream. He stated that is why the developers went to
the 125% when designing the storm water management system, which also would be
maintained by the homeowners’ association.
27.   Mr. Dusing stated that 31% of the 89 acres is greenspace that includes
streams, hillsides, retention ponds, and park areas. Discussion turned to lot
sizes, as some residents would like to see two homes per acre. Mr. Walker
stated the basis for the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning
recommendation was for a density of 2.3 dwelling units per net acre. Mr.
Ellison commented that only a portion of the development was within the city
limits with the rest being located in unincorporated Kenton County. Mr. Ellison
went on to say that the section planned in the city limits calls for 1.3 units
per acre.
28.   Jim Knarr, 10157 Marshall Road, commented that the topography changes for
every new development. He stated he is not against development and thinks the
one planned is wonderful but the houses should be placed on larger lots. He
also cited the flooding problems currently in the Marshall Road area with fears
of the problem worsening with all the new developments in that vicinity of
Taylor Mill Road.
29.   Mr. Walker explained council’s perspective to Mr. Knarr by stating the
density is controlled by the Comprehensive Plan not the city council members.
He added that if the council doesn’t follow the Plan then the city would be on
shaky legal ground. Mr. Ellison stated that by requesting a PUD overlay that
the density could be changed. Mr. Dusing commented that the developer exceeded
the stringent requirements, as the density of approximately 1.5 units per acre
is better than the current zone requirement. He stated that the density is a
guideline that takes in factors such as roads, sewers, schools, etc.
30.   Mr. Joe Jarboe, 10174 Marshall Road, distributed a written proposal of
reasons to deny this zone change request by the Keeney’s. His chief concerns
included lots that have less than one-half acre of land, which does not meet
the Comprehensive Plan and public safety issues (roads, sidewalks, and sewers).
He stated he has a petition of over four hundred names of people against this
development. Mr. Jarboe also was concerned about the sewer pump station on
Marshall Road, which is at capacity. Mr. Dusing responded to Mr. Jarboe’s
concerns.
31.   Linda Schoborg, 10822 Marshall Road stated that her biggest concern was
the PUD overlay which allows the developer to be creative and fears that 4.9
units per acre could become a reality. She stated that she heard a rumor that
the county section of this development will be annexed into the city limits.
She also expressed concerns about who would enforce the building regulations.
Mr. Lawson advised that the market controls the building regulations and that
prices are controlled by the square footage of the house. He added that neither
the Planning Commission nor the city can regulate the price of a house and that
generally speaking bigger is better. Mr. Lawson added that the Homeowners’
Association would regulate deed restrictions. Mr. Ellison commented that the
developer enforces the subdivision regulations. Mr. Lawson stated that it would
take either a court order or an agreement of all parties involved to remove a
deed restriction. Mr. Steffen reported that the Planning & Zoning Committee has
discussed doing away with the PUD overlay zone.
32.   In closing, Ms. Schoborg asked council to stick with the one half acre
lot requirement.
33.   Mr. Dusing stated that Ms. Schoborg’s father sold the land to the
Keeney’s with the knowledge that it was to be developed. He also added that
after streets are taken out that there would be two units per net acre.
34.   At this point, Mayor Kriege asked council what, if any action they wanted
to take. Mr. Walker advised that their decision had to be based on the
recommendation of the Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission. He
stated that since the KCMPZ recommendation was made on October 7, 1999 council
has until January 5, 2000 to make a decision. He stated that council can take
no action by then and it would automatically pass or that the city could state
their findings and turn down the request by the Keeney’s.
35.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to approve the recommendation by the Kenton
County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission for the Keeney Manor Hill
Development request for a map amendment to Area “B” (that lies within the city
limits) from R-1B to R-1C (PUD) overlay for property along Marshall Road. Mrs.
Yeager seconded the motion.
36.   A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Feldhaus stated that he did not see how
the city could legally deny this map amendment request. He explained that even
if the council didn’t take action within ninety days of the Planning
Commission’s recommendation that their decision would go into effect anyway. He
added that it especially hard to turn this project down when the developer has
planned a density lower than what is required. Mr. Feldhaus made brief mention
of the Fiscal Court’s recent discussions about charging cities an impact fee
for the flooding that is occurring. He stated this zoning matter goes before
the Fiscal Court at their November 16th meeting and he suggested waiting to see
what action the Court takes regarding this. Mr. Steffen agreed and suggested
the decision on this matter be taken at the council’s December 6th meeting.
37.   Roll call was taken on the motion to approve the map amendment for the
Keeney Manor Hill Development on Marshall Road with two yes votes and three no
votes cast by Mr. Dupps, Mr. Steffen, and Mr. Feldhaus. Motion failed. Mr.
Walker advised the motion to approve has failed as four votes are needed to
turn this down.
Motion to take a Brief Recess
38.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to take a brief recess; seconded by Mr. Dupps.
Motion carried with all ayes.
39.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to return to regular session; seconded by Mr.
Feldhaus. Motion carried with all ayes.
Request for Site Plan Revision to Bristow Meadows by Long & Kiser
40.   Tom Kiser of Long and Kiser Development addressed council with a request
to amend the original site plan for Bristow Meadows. The original plan called
for seven duplex units and the revised site plan calls for the addition of four
more lots. The addition is considered a major change. Mr. Barbian stated
approval for this change was the recommendation of the Kenton County Municipal
Planning & Zoning Commission at their September 2, 1999 meeting.
41.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to approve the revised site plan for Bristow
Meadows based on the facts and findings of Kenton County Municipal Planning &
Zoning Commission’s recommendation. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call
vote was answered with four yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Steffen.
Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
Proposal to Adopt by Resolution a Strategic Plan for the City
42.   Dan Wormald, speaking on behalf of the “Independence Tomorrow” Strategic
Planning Committee, reminded council of the goals and expectations that were
presented at the last meeting and urged council to adopt the Strategic Plan.
Mr. Ellison shared his feelings and concerns with the document as submitted to
council. He stated that some of the ideas suggested were good but that many of
the details were redundant. He stated he felt that the Plan needed some
revisions before being adopted by Council.
43.   Mayor Kriege stated that he feels the Strategic Plan is a work in
progress and the committee members will continue to be involved in the
implementation of the Plan. Mr. Wormald also commented that the committee
members were just average citizens with thoughts and ideas they wanted to
present to council. He stated the purpose was to present positive suggestions
for the progress of the city and that there was no intent for negativism. Mr.
Wormald added that the committee looks forward to making any revisions based on
council’s input.
44.   Mr. Dupps stated that while many ideas are not original the intent was to
place focus on and set time lines to try to accomplish these goals. Mr. Ellison
replied that the goals should include ways to succeed and suggested that the
Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission be asked to assist in the long-range
plans. He stated that APA planners could also be of assistance in a strategic
plan for the city. Mr. Dupps agreed with Mayor Kriege in that the Strategic
Plan is a living document that should be revised as needed. Mr. Ellison stated
that he felt the submitted Plan needed revision before being adopted by
council. Mayor Kriege asked that council submit any revisions to Mr. Scott
before the next council meeting so that the Plan can be presented for adoption.
Discussion of Proposing a Public Referendum Imposing A Tax Levy on Parks &
Recreation
45.   Mr. Steffen stated that he has been perusing the Kentucky Revised
Statutes to find a way to increase funding for the city’s parks. He submitted
to council a resolution he is proposing that would allow a public referendum
for taxes to be levied on parks and recreation. The referendum would need to be
placed on the general election ballot in November 2000. He stated the proposed
tax, if passed, could generate $250,000 per year which could be used for the
acquisition of land and the operation of the parks. Mr. Steffen also added that
a Park Board would need to be established if the referendum passes. Mrs. Yeager
stated she is not prepared to vote on this matter, as she would like to discuss
this with the Independence Recreation Committee and Mr. Scott.
