DECEMBER 6, 1999
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison,
Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in
attendance were Gary Scott, City Administrator and H. Lawson Walker, City
Attorney.
2.   Mayor Kriege introduced Lt. Shawn Butler and announced that he recently
graduated from Advanced Leadership Training. Mayor Kriege congratulated Lt.
Butler and presented him with an engraved pewter cup.
3.   Mr. Dupps requested an executive session at the end of the regular meeting
to discuss the Kenton County jail site lawsuit.
Approval of Council Minutes
4.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of the regular
meeting of November 1, 1999 as amended. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. No
roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
OLD BUSINESS
Proposed Map Amendment by Keeney Development for Manor Hill Subdivision on
Marshall Road
5.   Mayor Kriege stated that at the previous council meeting the council heard
the debate regarding the proposed map amendment by the Keeney Development
Company for property on Marshall Road. He asked council if they needed to
discuss this matter further. Mr. Feldhaus commented that Kenton County Fiscal
Court has only had a first reading regarding this map amendment wherein they
gave initial approval to the change. Mrs. Gabbard asked if the developer would
be asking for annexation of “Area A” into the city limits. Mr. Dusing stated
that hadn’t been decided. Mr. Feldhaus stated that “Area A” had the smaller lot
sizes. Mrs. Gabbard wondered what control the city would have over the county
section of this development. Mayor Kriege stated that the council is only
taking action on the section that is within the city limits. Mr. Walker advised
that part of Kenton County Area Planning Commission’s recommendation for
approval of the development was that both the city and the county must support
the zone change.
6.   Mrs. Gabbard again questioned Mr. Dusing why the Keeney’s have not asked
for annexation for “Area A” of this development. Mr. Dusing stated it wasn’t
necessary as the site plan is within the Comprehensive Plan. Mr. Feldhaus
commented that the lot sizes do not meet the R-1B zone; the density is smaller
with smaller lot size.
7.   Mrs. Gabbard expressed concern regarding the 1994 ordinance requiring
annexation to any property outside the city that wished to tap into the city
sewer system and how the city will recover sufficient debt reduction fees to
retire this debt. She stated she doesn’t see how the city will benefit. Mr.
Feldhaus stated that since the Sanitation District now owns the city sewer
system there is no requirement to be annexed into the city for sewer services.
He also stated that the Fowler Creek Sewer Project was planned for the existing
city area, not property outside the city limits. Mrs. Gabbard asked if the 1994
ordinance had been repealed. Mr. Ellison commented that if the city no longer
owns the sewer system then the ordinance automatically becomes null and void.
Mr. Walker advised that the Sanitation District now lease the sewer lines to
the city.
8.   Mr. Dusing stated there was never any intention by the developer to
request annexation into the city but that it could be arranged if that would
become a requirement for the approval of this map amendment. Mrs. Gabbard
stated she would like to see that promise in a written contract.
9.   Mr. Steffen stated that his biggest concern was that the request for a PUD
was just a RCD in disguise.
Motion to hold a Public Hearing on the Manor Hill Development Map Amendment
Request
10.   Further discussion resulted in Mr. Steffen making a motion to have a
full-scale public hearing on the Manor Hill Development, seconded by Mrs.
Gabbard. Mr. Feldhaus stated he didn’t see the point in having a public hearing
as the Kenton County Fiscal Court and the Kenton County Municipal Planning &
Zoning Commission held public hearings. Mrs. Yeager stated she did not feel any
new information would be revealed at another public hearing. Mr. Feldhaus
stated the audience was free to ask any questions at this meeting. Mayor Kriege
called for a vote. Roll call vote yielded two yes votes and four no votes cast
by Mrs. Yeager, Mr. Feldhaus, Mr. Dupps, and Mr. Ellison. Motion to have a
public hearing on the Manor Hill Development defeated 4-2 against.
11.   Mr. Steffen went on to read the definition of a PUD zone which allows
commercial development along with residential. Mr. Feldhaus stated the
developer has agreed not to institute other portions of a PUD zone. Mr. Steffen
stated that he felt this was clear attempt by the developer to get around the
existing zoning ordinance. He stated this site plan calls for strictly
residential with no mix of development. Mr. Ellison stated an RCD overlay has a
reduced lot size and with PUD you cannot make the lots smaller than the
restriction. Mr. Walker advised that while a PUD zone allows a greater mix, the
ordinance does not require the development to have more than single family
residences. He went on to say that if the use were changed the developer would
have to come back to the city for approval.
12.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Dusing if he would like to respond. Mr. Dusing
stated that a PUD zone does not require a mix of development but rather allows
a mix. He stated the developer feels this property is not an appropriate site
for commercial structures and by using the PUD zone it will allow for better
use of the greenspace, water management, etc. At this time Mr. Dusing submitted
a hand-written agreement wherein Keeney Development would request annexation
into the city as a condition of the zone change approval.
13.   Mrs. Gabbard commented that the planned development looked beautiful but
would like to see some of the homes in the rear area cut from the plan. Mr.
Dusing stated that in order to plan the management of the storm water that
there needed to be a mixture of lot sizes to make this site plan work.
14.   Mr. Steffen expressed concern with having the property open to R-1C
zoning and stated that if it met the R-1B zone with nineteen less lots he
wouldn’t have a problem with the site plan.
15.   At this time the floor was opened for comments from the audience. Mr.
Walker instructed the council to disregard anything said here and reminded them
that they just voted not to hold a public hearing on this matter.
16.   Mr. Jim Knarr, 10157 Marshall Road, stated that he lives downstream of
the planned development site. He stated there is a real issue with flooding in
the area. He would like to see the current R-1B zone go unchanged to keep the
neighborhood the way it is.
17.   Mr. Jeff Jarboe, 5468 Madison Pike, stated that he would like the city to
obtain a permit from the Corp of Engineers approving the construction of the
planned detention ponds for this development. He told council that their
constituents want them to vote against this map amendment.
18.   There was a brief discussion about Mr. Jarboe’s suggestion and Mr. Dusing
stated that the detention ponds would require approval from the Corp of
Engineers.
19.   Mr. Feldhaus expressed concern with the current flooding in the area even
with the planned detention ponds. He wondered if the city would be creating
another Banklick Creek watershed and if this would constitute a reason to
reject the project. He also stated that even though the Kenton County Fiscal
Court gave initial approval to the development he would like to wait to see if
they give final approval before making his decision.
20.   Mr. Ellison stated the Banklick Creek flooding problem has been going on
for over thirty years and doesn’t feel the city is responsible. He also
commented that the city is only deciding on the fifty-three acres of this
development that is within the city limits. He stated that under the current
zone one hundred six houses could be built and the Keeney’s site plan calls for
seventy-three houses.
21.   Mrs. Yeager commented this was a hard decision and Mrs. Gabbard
concurred. Mrs. Gabbard added that the council is here to watch guard the whole
city and feels the development will create problems for the current residents.
22.   Mr. Walker advised council that in order to turn down this map amendment
they would have to make factual findings from the public hearings held by the
Fiscal Court and Kenton County Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission that
would prove the recommendation is not in accordance with the Comprehensive
Plan. Council would also have to state why the recommended zone change is
inappropriate for the area. Mr. Walker also advised that if council does
nothing by January 5, 2000, then the zone change would be automatic on that
date. He reminded council their next regular council meeting is scheduled for
January 3, 2000 and it will take two readings of an ordinance if they plan to
turn down this zone change.
23.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to take a brief recess; seconded by Mr.
Feldhaus. After briefly discussing the reason for the brief recess with Mr.
Walker Mrs. Gabbard withdrew her motion to recess and Mr. Feldhaus withdrew his
second. Mr. Walker also advised this matter could not be discussed in a closed
executive session, as it does not meet the conditions required by K.R.S.
24.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to have a first reading of a proposed ordinance
(1999-O-15) to approve the recommendation by the Kenton County Municipal
Planning & Zoning Commission to rezone area “B” of the Keeney property on
Marshall Road from R-1C to R-1C (PUD) overlay in conformance with the
Comprehensive Plan. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call vote was
answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Steffen. Motion passed
with 5-1 in favor.
Motion to take a Brief Recess
25.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to take a brief recess; seconded by Mr. Dupps.
Motion carried with all ayes.
26.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to resume regular session; seconded by Mrs.
Gabbard. Motion carried with all ayes.
Discussion of Proposed Ordinance to Amend the Building/Zoning Permit Fees
27.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to table the discussion and possible first
reading of the proposed ordinance to amend the building/zoning permit fees and
send back to the committee as no representatives from the Home Builders
Association was present at the last committee meeting. Mr. Ellison seconded the
motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mayor Kriege stated that he promised Mr.
Wiedeman at the last council meeting that the committee would work the Home
Builders Association to arrive at a fair increase in fees. Mr. Ellison
suggested the committee meet at the offices of the Home Builders Association as
they have reference materials there that could be helpful. Mayor Kriege
suggested scheduling a meeting for next week. Roll call vote was answered with
five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Steffen. Motion carried 5-1 in
favor.
Discussion of a Proposed Resolution for a Referendum Imposing a Tax Levy for
Parks & Recreation
28.   Mr. Steffen addressed council about a resolution he is proposing that
would place a referendum on the November 2000 general election ballot that
would impose a tax levy to raise funds for the development and operation of the
city parks. He stated that last month he submitted this resolution for
council’s review and the tax rate was .05 cents on each $100 of taxable
property but has revised that to .03 cents per $100 valuation which would
amount to $30.00 per year on a house valued at $100,000. He stated a Park Board
would be appointed by the council to manage the budget and operation of the
parks. He said this tax would generate $150,000 per year for the operation of
the city parks and urged the council to pass this resolution. Mrs. Yeager was
concerned what role the Independence Recreation Committee members would have
with the establishment of a Park Board. She stated she would like to see the
current IRC members be a part of the Park Board.
29.   Mr. Feldhaus stated he had a problem asking for a tax levy when the city
is sitting on a $1M surplus and some areas of the current budget have some
“fat”. Mrs. Gabbard commented that some areas of the budget are over. Mr. Scott
advised council that some line items in the current budget are over but that
the department totals have not gone over what was budgeted. Mrs. Gabbard and
Mrs. Feldhaus agreed that they need to take a look at the budget. Mr. Ellison
stated that the parks have steadily improved over the last few years without
overburdening the city budget. He stated that he thinks it is premature at this
time to be asking for a tax levy for the parks and instead the city should be
looking at cost saving measures.
30.   Mr. Steffen stated that if the tax referendum passed in November 2000,
then this council would have the opportunity to appoint the members to the
first Park Board before the end of their terms. Mr. Steffen stated the IRC
members voted 9-2 in support of this referendum. He felt the current IRC
members could serve on the new Park Board.
31.   Mr. Dupps stated he liked the idea of having designated funds just for
the parks and felt this would free up additional funds for other city projects
like sidewalks.
32.   Mr. Walker advised that what is enacted by referendum could only be
rescinded by referendum. So that the .03 cents per $100 valuation could only be
increased/decreased by referendum.
33.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to read the proposed resolution proposing a
public referendum for property tax to be levied on parks and recreation and to
be placed on the November 2000 general election ballot. Mrs. Gabbard seconded
the motion. Roll call was answered with a 4-2 vote against; no votes cast by
Mr. Feldhaus, Mrs. Yeager, Mr. Dupps, and Mr. Ellison. Motion defeated.
NEW BUSINESS
Resolution Approving Transfer of Fire Station to the Kenton County Fiscal Court
34.   Mr. Walker submitted to council correspondence from Kenton County
Attorney, Garry Edmondson wherein the Fiscal Court is requesting the city pass
a resolution granting the Mayor the power to sign the Bill of Sale along with a
quitclaim deed for the sale of the Fire Station located at 5278 Madison Pike.
The Fiscal Court is purchasing the building from the Independence Fire
District. He explained they are requesting the city be involved in the transfer
of this property by way of signing a quitclaim deed for the purpose of
clarifying the record title and to give back any arguable interest the city may
have in the property. He stated that at one time the property was subject to a
lease to the city, which was assigned to the Fire District.
35.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to read the proposed resolution authorizing Mayor
Kriege to execute any and all documents necessary to complete the sale and
transfer of property located at 5278 Madison Pike from the Independence Fire
District/City of Independence to the Kenton County Fiscal Court. Mr. Ellison
seconded the motion. Mr. Walker read Resolution No. 1999-R-10.
36.   In a brief discussion Mr. Feldhaus expressed some concern over how the
county plans to utilize the building. He stated that at one time there was talk
about expanding their garage operations on that site. He was concerned that
this would no be an appropriate place for that type of operation in light of
the city’s plans to revitalize the downtown area. Mr. Ellison thought the city
gave up any interest in the property many years ago.
37.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to adopt Resolution No.1999-R-10; seconded by
Mr. Ellison. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by
Mr. Feldhaus. Motion carried 5-1.
Discussion of Amendments to the Personnel Policy
38.   A proposed resolution was submitted to council with the revisions of the
current personnel policy as recommended by the Personnel Policy Committee.
There was discussion of retirement benefits and unused sick time. Employees
currently accrue 1.5 hours of sick leave every pay period and council discussed
removing that accrued time benefit as the city carries short and long-term
disability insurance policy. Mr. Steffen questioned when the city approved a
new Recreation Department under the organizational chart. Mr. Steffen also felt
the police officers should receive their service weapon upon retirement and
would like to see that benefit remain in the policy. Council also discussed
removing or decreasing the longevity pay currently paid to the employees the
first pay period in December. Mr. Walker stated this might be grandfathered in
as it is being paid as wages.
39.   Mayor Kriege asked the Personnel Committee to take council’s suggestions
back for review and advised council to be prepared to take action on this
resolution at the next council meeting in January 2000.
40.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to table any further discussion or action on
the revisions of the Personnel Policy. Mrs. Gabbard seconded the motion. No
roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
First Reading of Proposed Ordinance to Amend Ordinance 1993-O-2 Relating to
Mayor/Council Compensation
41.   Mr. Steffen submitted to council a proposed ordinance to amend Ordinance
1993-O-2 relating to the compensation of the city’s elected officers. He stated
the proposed ordinance would add a new subsection that would state beginning on
March 1, 2004 the compensation of all elected city officials would be adjusted
by the amount of change in the consumer price index of the preceding year as
calculated by the Department of Local Government. He felt by adding this
subsection it would be unnecessary to revise this ordinance every few years. He
stated the proposed ordinance would also increase the Mayor’s salary from
$5,000 to $6,000 per year beginning with the next Mayor’s term on January 1,
2003 and increase the salary of council members from $1,000 to $3,000 effective
January 1, 2001.
42.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to have a first reading of a proposed ordinance
to amend Ordinance 1993-O-2 relating to the compensation of the elected city
officials. Mrs. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with
four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus and Mr. Ellison. Motion
carried 4-2 in favor.
Discussion Relating to Imposing a Bank Franchise & Local Deposit Tax
43.   Mr. Steffen reported that he had submitted the proposed ordinance that
would impose a bank franchise and local deposit tax but suggested discussion of
this matter be delayed as he is waiting on further information regarding this
type of tax. There was a brief discussion wherein Mr. Walker advised council
that fewer cities are getting any income from this tax as each bank’s main
branch is credited for the deposits, therefore many of the local cities have
lost revenue as headquarters move to a larger city. Mr. Steffen stated he may
bring this back in the future.
NEW BUSINESS
Discussion Regarding the Upgrading of City Classification from 5th Class to 3rd
Class
44.   Council Member, Mr. Steffen introduced a resolution that would upgrade
the city’s classification from fifth class to third class. He stated that he
feels there are many benefits to be had by upgrading to third class. He
reported that most fifth class cities have a population of 1,000 to 3,000.and
with our current population approaching 15,000 we would meet the third class
classification. He stated that even though many of the powers of a third class
city would not be of interest to Independence, just the recognition that comes
with the upgrade would aide Independence in becoming one of the important
cities in Northern Kentucky.
45.   Mrs. Gabbard stated that she feels this reclassification is long overdue.
Mr. Feldhaus stated he doesn’t see the benefit of moving up to third class city
and expressed concern that it could cost the city. Mr. Ellison requested the
city attorney research this matter. Mr. Walker stated that it is clear the city
is eligible and advised the main requirements for a third class city is that
the city must provide police and fire services. Mayor Kriege suggested the city
attorney review the possibility of upgrading the city to third class and table
further discussion until the next regular meeting. Mr. Steffen stated he would
withdraw the resolution until then.
Miscellaneous Matters of Discussion
46.   Mr. Ellison stated that the Schoborg and Lipscomb properties on Madison
Pike are having trouble getting their property lines between county and city
affirmed. Mr. Scott stated that he is currently working with Mike Schwartz of
Northern Kentucky Area Planning & Zoning to get this matter resolved.

town. Mr. Scott stated they continue to work on this as they are reported.

are being rude and would like to see the city institute a “citizen contact
card” to provide the residents with a way to voice their complaints. Mr. Scott
stated he would look into getting these cards.

Proposal for Text Amendment relating to Roller Rinks
16.   Mr. Tom Breidenstein, legal counsel for Dale Roland, addressed council
regarding the text amendment the city has made application for with regard to
roller rinks. He urged council to approve Kenton County & Municipal Planning &
Zoning Commission’s favorable recommendation for this amendment, as it is
consistent with other land uses of this type. Mayor Kriege opened the
discussion for council comments. Mr. Feldhaus stated that NKAP&Z’s staff
recommendation was to deny this zoning text amendment and cited the main reason
was because roller rinks are more conducive to commercial development areas.
Mr. Feldhaus agreed with the staff recommendation and felt that approval of
this amendment would place commercial activity in residential zones. He stated
Mr. Roland should look into placing this type of structure in a neighborhood
commercial area. Mr. Steffen stated the Planning & Zoning Committee applied for
this text amendment because Independence has no where to place this and the
committee felt it was a worthwhile endeavor. He stated that even with the text
amendment, final approval would have to come from the Board of Adjustments. He
commented that golf courses, country clubs, and swimming pools are currently
allowed as a conditional use in residential areas. Mr. Breidenstein stated that
the Board of Adjustments would have the power to impose conditions, such as
hours of operation, etc. Mrs. Gabbard expressed concerns of evening traffic and
security lights for surrounding residential homes and also considered this type
of development more suitable for a commercial area. Mr. Roland read a prepared
statement urging the approval of this text amendment. Mr. Feldhaus stated he
has a big problem with the effect this will have on residential areas.
17.   Motion was made by Mr. Steffen and seconded by Mrs. Yeager to have a
first reading of the proposed ordinance to approve the zoning text amendment
relating to the inclusion of roller rinks in residential areas. Roll call vote
was answered with three yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus and Mr.
Ellison. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Second Reading of Proposed Ordinance to Amend Ordinance 1993-O-2 Relating to
Mayor/Council Compensation
18.   Motion was made by Mr. Steffen and seconded by Mrs. Gabbard to have a
second reading of proposed Ordinance No. 2000-O-02 relating to Mayor and
Council Members compensation. Roll call vote was answered with three yes votes
and two no votes cast by Mr. Ellison and Mr. Feldhaus. Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance.
19.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 2000-O-02 seconded by
Mrs. Gabbard. A brief discussion ensued. Mrs. Yeager stated that she didn’t
feel a raise in compensation was necessary but did like the addition of the
subsection that would provide for an automatic annual adjustment based on the
amount of change in the consumer price index. Mr. Steffen stated the city has
grown tremendously and felt an increase in compensation may entice more
candidates to run for office. Mayor Kriege commented that the Mayor’s stipend
was not a factor when he filed to run for the office and feels that most people
do not take that into consideration when filing for office. Mr. Feldhaus stated
he feels the current compensation is adequate. He also stated that he thinks
the majority of candidates that ran in the last election didn’t even know what
the salary was, with thirteen candidates filing for six council positions and
six candidates for the office of Mayor. Mr. Ellison commented that he doesn’t
feel elected offices are money driven. Mayor Kriege explained that this raise
in compensation would be given to the winners of the next council and mayor
elections and not the officials currently holding the positions. There was a
brief discussion of adjusting the amounts being proposed (from $5,000 to $6,000
for the mayor and from $1,000 to $3,000 for each council member). Mr. Walker
explained that if the adjustments were made, then the reading of the ordinance
would become a new first reading, not a second reading. Roll call vote was
answered with three yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus and Mr.
Ellison. Motion carried 3-2.
Discussion Regarding the Upgrading of City Classification from 5th Class to 3rd
Class
20.   Mr. Walker presented to council the research he compiled with regard to
upgrading from fifth class to third class. He stated that the biggest change
for Independence would be the electoral process as third class cities are
required to hold a primary election with a filing deadline in January if
thirteen or more run for council or three or more run for the office of mayor.
Also the city would have the option to adopt the civil service regulations. He
stated the city is already in compliance with a Police Department requirement
and he believes the courts would sanction the Independence Fire District to
continue providing fire protection.
21.   Mr. Steffen pointed out that the last election would have been better if
the city had a primary election to eliminate some of the six people running for
the office of mayor. Mr. Feldhaus stated the primary election was abolished
several years ago due in part to the January filing date. Mr. Steffen commented
that Erlanger and Covington have primary elections and never seem to lack for
candidates.
22.   Mr. Ellison stated that as a third class city Independence would be
required to establish an Alcohol Beverage Board. He also felt the city should
consider a gradual change in class and not jumping from fifth to third.
23.   Mrs. Gabbard stated she felt that increasing the city’s class to third
would raise the status of Independence and gives the city more options. Mr.
Ellison stated he doesn’t see where Independence would gain more benefits or
powers and that social status is unimportant.
24.   Mr. Steffen stated that the current population of Independence warrants
the upgrade to third class. He also stated that he doesn’t see the primary
election as a bad thing. Mr. Feldhaus maintained that the city isn’t loosing
anything by remaining a fifth class city and has heard no compelling reason to
change the status. Mr. Steffen and Mrs. Gabbard insisted there were no
disadvantages to increasing the city’s class.
25.   Mr. Walker advised council there was a time restraint in making this
decision as the resolution would need to be decided no later than March in
order to petition the current legislative session for the change in class. Mr.
Steffen requested further discussion and possible action on the proposed
resolution be continued at the next regular meeting of council.
Mayor’s Report – Thomas M. Kriege
26.   Mayor Kriege announced the annual Planning Session of Council is
scheduled for January 28 and 29 at the Holiday Inn in Fort Mitchell. After a
brief discussion it was decided to re-schedule for February 10, 11, & 12, 2000
as Mr. Steffen is unable to attend weekend sessions. The extra day would
include a Thursday evening so Mr. Steffen could participate in that session.
27.   Mayor Kriege announced he received a letter from employees of the police
department expressing misgivings regarding council’s plans to delete some of
the current benefits while revising the Personnel Policy. He advised council
that he will make himself available at different roll calls in order to listen
to their concerns in person.
City Administrator – Gary R. Scott

position be pulled from another account. Mrs. Gabbard questioned whether a job
description had been created. Mayor Kriege added that the job description
should be included in the personnel policy and the pay plan.

FEBRUARY 7, 2000
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison,
Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in
attendance was Gary Scott, City Administrator and City Attorney, H. Lawson
Walker.
Presentation of Plaque to Preston Tillett
2.   Mayor Kriege presented H. Preston Tillett with a plaque as a token of the
city’s appreciation of the twenty-five years of service Mr. Tillett contributed
by holding office as a city council member and Board of Adjustments member. The
council members joined Mayor Kriege in thanking Mr. Tillett for his dedication
to the city.
Report on the AT&T cell tower
3.   Mayor Kriege introduced Peggy Murphy, legal counsel for the city in the
lawsuit filed against AT&T to prevent them from erecting a cell tower in the
Independence Cemetery. Ms. Murphy reported that after many claims were filed in
court and many months of hearings that Kenton County Circuit Judge Bartlett
ruled in favor of the City of Independence which has precluded AT&T from
placing the cell tower in the cemetery. She stated that Judge Bartlett has
agreed to grant a permanent injunction. She also advised council that AT&T has
thirty days from February 2, 2000 to file an appeal.
Approval of Council Minutes
4.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of the regular
meeting of January 3, 2000 as amended. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with five ayes and one abstain cast by Mr. Dupps. Motion
carried 5-1.
Request from Independence Lions Club for Donation for the Annual Easter Egg
Hunt
5.   Ms. Karen Nitschke, Secretary for the Independence Lions Club requested
council to provide funds to sponsor the annual Easter Egg Hunt. She stated that
last year the city donated $600.00 for the hunt but because of the increase in
attendance at this event was requesting an increase in the amount allocated.
She stated that last year they ran short of prizes and would like to increase
the number of eggs.
6.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to donate $700.00 to the Independence Lions Club
annual Easter Egg Hunt; seconded by Mr. Ellison. Roll call was answered with
all ayes. Motion carried 6-0.
Text Amendment for Roller Rinks – Second Reading of Ordinance No. 2000-O-03
7.   Mrs. Gabbard began the discussion by asking Mr. Walker if it was necessary
to do a text amendment for roller rinks and questioned the Board of Adjustments
role with the zoning of this type. Mr. Walker stated that the Board of
Adjustments can only grant variances and conditional uses. Mr. Feldhaus
interjected that the other alternative would be to re-zone the property in
questions to meet an existing zone that already permits roller rinks. He voiced
his objection to this text amendment as he feels it will open all residential
areas to this type of structure. Mrs. Gabbard concurred and stated this was
also her concern.
8.   Mayor Kriege yielded the floor to Mr. Mark Smith, 747 Stephens Road, who
spoke in objection to this proposed text amendment. He stated that while he was
not against roller rinks, he was against placing them in residential areas. Mr.
Smith also sees this text amendment being challenged by other businesses. He
submitted a petition with forty-nine signatures against this text amendment.
9.   Mr. Dale Roland, who is requesting this text amendment, stated that he
views a roller rink as recreational rather than commercial and noted the city’s
two largest commercial properties are not accepting of a roller rink. He stated
the city’s Board of Adjustment would still have control, as the proposed text
amendment would require a conditional use permit.
10.   Motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Steffen to have a second reading of
the proposed ordinance to add roller rinks as a conditional use in residential
zones. Roll call yielded a 3-3-tie vote. Mr. Ellison stated that it was his
understanding that the mayor could not vote on zoning related matters. Mr.
Walker advised the mayor could break the tie vote for a second reading but
could not vote to adopt the ordinance. Mayor Kriege voted yes to break the tie.
Motion to have a second reading carried with a 4-3 vote.
11.   A lengthy discussion ensued. Mr. Feldhaus, Mr. Ellison and Mrs. Gabbard
spoke against the text amendment, both separately and collectively, for the
following reasons:
§   Jeopardizes residential areas and this amendment would be open to all
residential zones
§   Felt Mr. Roland could have requested a zone change for the property under
consideration
§   Felt Mr. Roland preferred residential property as it is less expensive than
commercial property
§   Commercially operated business more intrusive in a residential zone
§   KCP&Z staff recommended against this amendment
12.   Mr. Steffen, Mr. Dupps, and Mrs. Yeager spoke in favor of the text
amendment. They cited the following reasons for adoption:
§   As with all conditional uses, this would still have to go before the Board
of Adjustments and had faith the Board would exercise care with this type of
development
§   There are more residential than commercial locations in the city and many
undeveloped residential properties could be possible good locations.
§   Feels roller rinks are more recreational use than commercial.
§   Feels more control over a residential property with a conditional use than
having a zone change where any type of commercial business would be able to use
the land, which may pose potential problems.
§   Feels a conditional use could set the hours of operation, type of signage,
lighting, etc.
§   Feels it would be nice for the local children to have local recreational
facilities.
13.   Mayor Kriege stated that Independence is unique in that it has so much
residential property available. Mr. Roland commented that roller rinks are
neither commercial nor industrial. He advised the nine-acre site under
consideration is on Independence Road near the Bristow Road intersection; a
sparsely populated area. He stated the building would be designed to look like
a riding stable to conform to the environment. Mr. Roland held that the KC&MP&Z
Commission’s recommendation was based on the Comprehensive Plan.
14.   Mr. Mark Smith commented that permitting this type of conditional use in
a residential area would preclude notifying the surrounding neighbors as is
needed for a zone change. Consequently adjoining property owners would not be
aware this type of development was being considered in order to voice their
objections.
15.   Motion by Mr. Steffen and second by Mr. Dupps to adopt the proposed
ordinance to add roller rinks as a conditional use in residential zones. Before
roll call vote was taken, Mr. Walker advised that he believes the Mayor is able
to vote on a zoning matter but that it takes four members of a body to override
– if there is a tie vote then it passes. Roll call vote was answered with three
yes votes by Mr. Steffen, Mr. Dupps, and Mrs. Yeager; and three no votes cast
by Mrs. Gabbard, Mr. Feldhaus, and Mr. Ellison. Mr. Walker stated that because
the vote is tied that it is looked at as though council did not override Kenton
County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission’s recommendation to adopt. Mr.
Feldhaus questioned the city’s Planning and Zoning Committee’s authority to
make application for this text amendment without the majority of council
approving this. There was a brief discussion regarding how this is addressed in
the Kentucky Revised Statutes Section 100.
16.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to take a brief recess to research KRS Section
100; seconded by Mr. Feldhaus. Motion carried with all ayes.
17.   Upon motion by Mr. Feldhaus and second by Mrs. Gabbard the meeting
resumed.
18.   Mr. Walker stated he stood by his recommendation, as he has no reason to
believe the application was defective because the city’s Planning & Zoning
Committee did not seek the approval of the full council before applying for the
amendment. Mr. Feldhaus disagreed with Mr. Walker’s conclusion. Mr. Scott
stated that he has signed other applications during the past two years he has
served as City Administrator. Mr. Feldhaus requested Mr. Walker research the
legality of this matter.

CITY OF INDEPENDENCE

1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison,
Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in
attendance was Gary Scott, City Administrator and City Attorney, H. Lawson
Walker.
Approval of Council Minutes
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept the council minutes of the regular
meeting of February 7, 2000 as amended. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. No
roll call; motion carried 6-0.
Text Amendment for Roller Rinks – Discussion/Second Reading - Ordinance
No.2000-O-03
3.   Mayor Kriege announced that the matter concerning the text amendment to
permit roller rinks in residential zones was again before council due to the
confusion at the last meeting about the mayor’s ability to vote on zoning
issues. He stated that Mr. Dale Roland was in attendance tonight and asked him
if he had any new information that would cause council to reconsider the
matter.
4.   Mr. Tom Breidenstein, legal counsel for Mr. Roland, spoke on Mr. Roland’s
behalf. He stated that during the last few weeks, after much consideration and
a closer look at the statues, he is requesting council to take another vote on
the proposed text amendment ordinance so that Mayor Kriege can cast a vote.
5.   Council member, Mr. Dupps asked Mr. Walker to comment on Mr.
Breidenstein’s statement. Mr. Walker stated, that in his opinion, when the
majority vote of the legislative body (council) results in a tie vote, that the
Mayor then acts in a legislative capacity in order to break the tie vote. He
stated that since the previous vote resulted in a tie, the vote was perceived
as not being passed, so it can be voted on again. He went on to say there is no
prior appellate level court decision on this particular matter. Mr. Walker also
commented that the legal community is divided in the interpretation of this
statute.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus adhered to his contention that the mayor is not a member of
the legislative body and that it takes four members of the legislative body to
constitute a majority. Mr. Walker reiterated that the courts have not ruled on
this matter.
7.   Mayor Kriege commented that the statute is vague and the question of a
mayor’s right to vote on certain matters comes before many city councils. He
asked council how they wanted to proceed. Mr. Steffen stated that he felt it
necessary to vote again because of the confusion.
8.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 2000-O-03 as read at the
February 7, 2000 regular council meeting. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll
call vote was answered with three yes votes and three no votes cast by Mr.
Feldhaus, Mr. Ellison, and Mrs. Gabbard. Mayor Kriege cast the deciding yes
vote. Motion carried 4-3 in favor.
9.   Mr. Ellison commented, and Mrs. Gabbard concurred, that all residential
zones would now be open to all types of recreational business – roller rinks,
bowling alleys, etc.

ordinance just for the grant.

DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Administrator – Gary R. Scott
9.   Mr. Scott reported he is beginning work on gathering the necessary data to
start the annexation process for four parcels of land, most of which is
surrounded by incorporated areas of the city. He explained this annexation
would clean up the city’s boundary lines. He suggested and council agreed to
have Cardinal Engineering research the legal descriptions of the property to be
annexed. He stated that by starting this process now it would enable the city
to have this issue placed on the November general election ballot.
10.   Mr. Walker advised that since these parcels are multi-dimensional, there
should be a majority of council expressing interest in proceeding with the
annexation process before authorizing the city engineer to gather the needed
information. During a brief discussion, Mr. Steffen acknowledged that the
property owners have not requested annexation nor have they been informed of
the city’s interest to annex. Mr. Feldhaus suggested sending a letter to the
property owners to advise them of the city’s plan to annex. Mr. Walker advised
council that after the city adopts an ordinance stating the intent to annex the
land then the property owners would have sixty days to protest. Mr. Steffen
stated that due to the annexation process there are time constraints to
consider in order for this matter to be placed on the November ballot. Mr.
Feldhaus voiced his objection to annexing the property. Mr. Steffen stated he
would agree to dispense with annexing the three small tracts but feels the city
should proceed with annexation of the larger tract as it is completely in the
city’s service area.
11.   Mr. Dupps asked what expenses would be involved if council decides to
proceed with the annexation process. Mr. Walker replied there would be
engineer’s fees and publication costs. He stated a first reading could not take
place tonight as the city engineer will need to provide him with the legal
descriptions of the properties to be annexed. Council discussed holding a
special meeting prior to the next regular meeting in order to complete a first
and second reading of a proposed ordinance in keeping with the deadline to get
this matter on the November ballot.
12.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to proceed with the annexation process by
notifying the property owners of the smaller tracts of land via certified
letter and advertising the larger tract in the newspaper. Mrs. Gabbard seconded
the motion. Roll call vote was answered with four yes votes and two no votes
cast by Mr. Ellison and Mr. Feldhaus. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.
Concrete Street Repairs for 2000 – Award of the Contract
13.   Mr. Scott reported the city accepted bids for concrete street repairs and
received two proposals. The two bids submitted were JPS Construction Inc. for
$116,950.00 and Buchanan Construction Company, Inc. for $133,562.50. Mr. Scott
stated that it was estimated the concrete would run $42.00/sq.yd. but that the
bids came in at $35.00/sq.yd. and $39.25/sq.yd. This is twenty percent lower
than expected. Some council members inquired what streets were included in this
project. Mr. Smith, Public Works Foreman, stated that sections of Oby Drive,
Jamestown, Hunters Green, Clubhouse Drive, Wooddale, and Wedgewood Drive were
some of the streets that would be repaired in this project.
14.   Mr. Feldhaus suggested that partial improvements be made to Holten Drive
with the twenty-percent difference that was saved. Mr. Scott stated they would
look into that possibility.
15.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to award the concrete street repairs bid to JPS
Construction Inc in the amount of $116,950.00. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion.
Roll call was answered with six yes votes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Cardinal Engineering – Dave Whitacre

APRIL 27, 2000
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Council Members Jim
Ellison, Donna Yeager, Barbara Gabbard, Gregory Steffen, and Steve Feldhaus
answered roll call. Mr. Dupps called earlier in the day to say he would attend
but would arrive late. (Mr. Dupps arrived at 7:45 p.m.) Also in attendance were
Gary Scott, City Administrator, City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and Finance
Director, Amy Guenther.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated the purpose of the special meeting was to discuss and
possibly take action on amending both the current budget and the proposed
budget for the 2000/01 fiscal year.
First Reading of the Proposed Ordinance to Amend the 99/00 Budget
3.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of a proposed ordinance
relating to the amendment of the 1999/00 annual budget that would increase
receipts of the General Fund by $270,000.00 to include revenues from the
Department of Local Government for the construction of a Senior Center. Mr.
Ellison seconded the motion. Motion carried 5-0 (Mr. Dupps absent).
4.   During a brief discussion, Mayor Kriege stated that he would like to hold
off making this amendment to the current budget as he would like to amend the
full budget in June and does not wish to have the expense of advertising an
amended budget twice. He advised the city has received the first invoice from
the architect firm that is designing the Center. Mr. Scott stated we might need
to have the ordinance adopted in order to begin paying bills. Mayor Kriege
stated he would speak with the Grant Administrator, Bryan Kirby, tomorrow to
inquire whether the city could wait until June to pass the amended budget. Mr.
Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Mayor Kriege’s Presentation of the Proposed 2000/01 Fiscal Year Budget
5.   Mayor Kriege presented the proposed 2000/01 budget for council’s review
and discussion. He stated that this past year many new programs and services
were instituted and next year’s budget would need to provide funding to
maintain those additions to the budget. In his address, Mayor Kriege stated
that next year’s budget was a challenge, as difficult decisions had to be made
to ensure services for future years. He stressed that the city staff worked
well to develop and create a conservative budget and while the proposed budget
has been reduced as much as possible he pronounced the need to hire a grant
writer to access capital and operating funds. He also advised the city has been
notified of a 31% premium increase of the employee’s health insurance but that
he is working with the city’s health insurance agent as they shop for a good
medical program with a lower rate. He also stated the proposed budget includes
the city’s share ($8,000) for the emergency sirens recently installed in Kenton
County. Mayor Kriege stated the proposed budget would increase the Recreation
Director from a part-time position to full-time.
6.   In closing, Mayor Kriege advised the proposed 2000/01 budget includes
pulling $169,000.00 from reserve funds, making this the second year the city
has needed to dip into the reserve funds in order to provide the necessary
services while maintaining operating expenses. Mayor Kriege stated that in his
opinion the city is in a budget crisis and proposed imposing an insurance
premium tax at a rate of 5%. He advised that Independence is one of the few
cities that do not currently impose the insurance premium tax with the average
rate being 8%. He expressed the need for Independence to begin long-range
budget plans instead of the current year-to-year plan. He expressed concern
that if the city continues with the current practice of using reserve funds for
each year’s budget that the reserves would be depleted within 3-5 years. At
this time, Mayor Kriege opened the floor for general discussion of the proposed
budge for 2000/01.
7.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed 2000/01
budget; seconded by Mrs. Yeager. Discussion ensued.
8.   Mr. Walker asked if the budget would be passed by line item or summary.
Mr. Feldhaus stated it would be adopted by summary.
9.   Mrs. Gabbard commented that she thought it was too soon to have a first
reading of the budget as there may be suggested changes after there is more
time for review.
10.   There was a brief discussion about the property tax rate for the year
2000. Mrs. Guenther, Finance Director, stated the preliminary figures indicate
the tax rate will be .1570 for compensating plus four and .151 without plus
four.
11.   Mrs. Gabbard questioned the high attorney fees the city supported this
year. Mr. Walker stated he has discussed the matter of his fees with Mayor
Kriege and he feels confident they can agree on a retainer fee that would be
more inclusive than the current monthly retainer. Mr. Walker also reminded
council the city was involved in several lawsuits this past year that resulted
in additional attorney fees, i.e. the City vs. AT&T. He added that he feels his
firm is becoming more efficient as they become more familiar with the city.
12.   Mr. Feldhaus asked Mrs. Guenther if there could possibly be a $170,000
carry-over. Mrs. Guenther stated she did not foresee that large of a carry-
over. Mrs. Guenther stated the amendments for the current budget will be
presented in June and does not anticipate the figures changing from what has
been projected.
13.   Mrs. Yeager commented the city would be receiving $200,000 from the State
for use in the parks. Mr. Scott suggested this donation from the state not be
added to the budget until the funds are actually received, as we do not know
when the state will bestow this allocation.
14.   There was a brief discussion surrounding the use of the Fowler Creek
Sewer funds. Mrs. Guenther questioned if the city was able to pay any sewer
expenses from the debt reduction fees collected. Mr. Walker advised that in his
opinion, as long as the city was not indebted to a third party, the city could
use this revenue to pay any expenses as long as sufficient money is retained to
make the bond payments. Mr. Feldhaus expressed concern that ordinances were
adopted that established how the fees would be spent. Mr. Walker advised that
the budget ordinance would override any prior ordinances adopted. Mr. Ellison
also commented that the purpose of the previous ordinances no longer existed,
as the city no longer collects sewer tap-in fees.
15.   Discussion turned to employee wages and the current pay scale. Mr. Scott
stated he would like to see employees receiving at least the minimum pay for
their position on the pay scale. Lt. Shawn Butler stated there was not enough
funding to get everyone into the pay range that was adopted last year. Mrs.
Yeager stated she thought everyone was required to be paid at least the minimum
of the scale. Mr. Feldhaus commented that he feels there is no method in place
to get employees up from the minimum to the top of the scale. Lt. Butler stated
they are still attempting to get some employees in the scale that was set for
their job position. He stated one of the sergeants, with six years experience,
is still being paid $2,000 less than the minimum in the pay scale.
16.   Mr. Feldhaus suggested that by withdrawing from the Cable Board the city
would be able to collect the entire 5% franchise fee and felt this additional
revenue could solve the budget problem to fund the personnel expenses. Mrs.
Gabbard asked what benefit the city would have by remaining a member of the
Cable Board. Mr. Feldhaus stated the Cable Board currently tapes the council
meetings free of charge; if the city was not a member the charge to tape the
meetings would run $30-$40/hour.
17.   Mr. Steffen commented that the city shouldn’t balance the budget on the
backs of the people who make the least amount of money and felt the city should
add the needed revenue for personnel expenses even if it was necessary to dip
into the reserve fund to do so.
18.   Lt. Butler stated the police department has made the necessary cuts but
he feels they can live with them. A brief discussion ensued on the take home
fleet of cruisers. Lt. Butler advised they would be losing five leased vehicles
at the end of the year. The company will not renew the lease nor will they sell
the vehicles to the city. He also stated that several of the remaining vehicles
are 7-10 years old. Council discussed the cost of maintaining home fleet cars
versus pool cars. Lt. Butler stated he is confident that home fleet vehicles
can be on the road seven years. He shared his concern of the imminent loss of
the leased vehicles compounded with the remaining aged fleet. He stated he
would be researching possible solutions to this matter.
19.   Mr. Steffen asked Lt. Butler if they would be funding a school resource
officer. Lt. Butler stated they are currently looking for grants that would
cover the full cost of a resource officer, and meanwhile will continue the
current program in the schools. He advised the DARE grant has expired and they
are examining other options and programs.
Adjournment
20.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mr. Ellison. Motion
carried with all ayes. The meeting adjourned at 7:58 p.m.

Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk

Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with the Pledge

Approval of the Minutes of April 3, 2000 Meeting

favor
Privileges of the Floor
3.   Mr. Tom Brinker, 1192 Constitution Drive, spoke to council regarding the
maintenance of Flagstone Drive. He explained that Flagstone Drive runs off of
Cody Road and is the entrance to Independence Pointe Subdivision that was
developed by Finke Homes. Mr. Brinker stated that development of the
subdivision is complete and Finke Homes has indicated they will no longer
provide landscaping and lawn maintenance on Flagstone Drive. Mr. Brinker stated
the residents are currently maintaining the area but are requesting the city
take over the maintenance. Mayor Kriege stated this matter would have to be
treated as a zoning violation, as the property is not owned by the city. Mayor
Kriege asked Melissa Bradford, Zoning Administrator, to notify Finke Homes of
non-compliance. Mr. Brinker stated the residents were under the impression that
the property in question became under city ownership when the developer left
town. Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Brinker that the city’s only recourse is to
request that Finke Homes comply to the zoning ordinance.
4.   Neil Stiegelmeyer introduced himself to Mayor Kriege and Council as the
President of the Deters Company. He stated he was the former Superintendent of
the Kenton County Board of Education. Mr. Stiegelmeyer said the Deters Company,
as owners of the Independence Towne Center, are desirous to have a positive
working relationship with the city.
Proposed Resolution No. 2000-R-08 – Authorizing CDBG Monthly Expenses for
Senior Center
5.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to read Resolution No. 2000-R-08 authorizing

motion. There was a brief discussion regarding the significance of council
authorizing the payment of all invoices related to the construction of the
Senior Center. Mr. Walker advised there is no legal significance as long as the
funds are budgeted. Mr. Scott informed council that the grant administrator for
this project, Bryan Kirby, has directed the city to accept this procedure in
keeping with auditing standards. Motion carried with all ayes.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to accept Resolution No. 2000-R-08 as read;

Discussion of the Proposed Budget for the 2000/01 Fiscal Year
7.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have the first reading of the proposed 2000/
01 Budget; seconded by Mr. Ellison.
8.   Before a vote was taken, council discussed several line items. Mr. Steffen
asked if the Police Department’s personnel line item included the additional
funds needed to bring each officer up to the minimum wage for each position.
Mrs. Guenther stated that it had.
9.   Mrs. Gabbard expressed concern regarding the figure estimated for the
employee health benefits. She stated she would prefer to hold off on a first
reading of the ordinance until the health insurance cost is confirmed. Mr.
Feldhaus stated that if the health insurance rate comes in lower than budgeted
then there would be a surplus. Mayor Kriege explained that the amount in the
proposed budget was for the renewal of the current policy, which had a thirty-
one percent increase. He stated he has instructed our insurance agent to look
for a policy with lower rates, so the budgeted amount will not be exceeded.
10.   Mrs. Gabbard also brought up the matter of attorney fees. She feels the
fees will run higher than the $50,000 budgeted for next year. Mr. Walker stated
he is working with Mayor Kriege to devise a more inclusive retainer contract
and reminded council that the high cost of recent legal expenses were due to
the unusual amount of lawsuits.
11.   Mrs. Gabbard asked about the Cable Board issue and expressed concern that
Independence does not have a resident representative on the Board. Mrs. Yeager
stated that many cities do not have a representative on the Board. Mr. Walker
advised council that if the city decides to terminate association with the
Cable Board that there would be a process by which to do that.
12.   Mr. Steffen asked about the budgeted amount of $275,000 for the Building
Fund. Mrs. Guenther explained this would fund the purchase of land and a
building for the Public Works Department for the storage of vehicles, supplies,
and equipment. Mayor Kriege stated the Building Fund would have no impact on
the General Fund.
13.   Mrs. Gabbard commented that the proposed budget does not address expenses
that will be associated with housing for the Police Department. Mrs. Guenther
stated that some of the expense has been worked into this budget. Mayor Kriege
assured council that proposed facilities for the Police Department would be
presented to council for approval.
14.   Mr. Steffen voiced his objection to the loan proceeds line item under the
Building Fund Revenues since the city would not build this year. Mr. Steffen
made a motion to remove the loan proceeds line item; seconded by Mrs. Gabbard.
A discussion ensued regarding the city’s need to provide future housing
facilities for Public Works, Police Department, and Administration. Mayor
Kriege urged council to afford him some flexibility as the Public Works
Department has no place to store equipment and is limited to renting space
($425/month) in the old Fire Department building on Madison Pike. He commented
that the dump truck purchased this year is sitting outside and feels this
vehicle will depreciate faster being exposed to the elements. Council discussed
prioritizing all the department’s facility needs. Roll call vote on Mr.
Steffen’s motion to remove the loan proceeds line item of $80,000 from the
proposed budget yielded three ayes and two no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus and
Mrs. Yeager. Motion carried 3-2.
15.   Mr. Steffen asked how the budgeted amount for the Senior Center Building
was determined. Mayor Kriege stated that standard construction costs were used
to estimate that expense.
16.   Again Mrs. Gabbard stated she would like to wait on the budget until the
final cost comes in on the medical insurance premiums. Mayor Kriege reiterated
that the budgeted amount is based on the thirty-one percent increase with our
current policy and that the cost may go lower if we switch to another company,
but that the cost will not increase.
17.   At this time a roll call vote was taken to have a first reading of the
proposed budget for 2000/01 with three yes votes and two no votes cast by Mrs.
Gabbard and Mr. Steffen. Motion carried 3-2 in favor. Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance.

JUNE 5, 2000
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Rev. Randy McCafferty of Independence Christian Church gave the
invocation. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara
Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance
were Gary Scott, City Administrator and City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker.
Approval of the Minutes of the April 27, 2000 Special Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to approve the minutes of the April 27, 2000
special meeting. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes;
6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the May 1, 2000 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to approve the minutes of the May 1, 2000
council meeting as amended; seconded by Mrs. Yeager. Motion carried with five
ayes and one abstain cast by Mr. Dupps.
Proposed Ordinance to Annex Certain Unincorporated Territories in the Fowler
Creek Road Area
4.   Mayor Kriege turned the floor over to Council Member, Greg Steffen by
asking him to give the audience in attendance a description of the area the
city is proposing to annex and the reason behind the annexation.
5.   Mr. Steffen explained his reason for proposing the annexation was to clean
up the current boundary lines. He went on to describe in detail the areas of
Fowler Creek Road and Pelly Road that would be involved in the annexation. He
also explained that the proposed ordinance would only begin the process of
annexation and the residents would then take the next step to either oppose or
approve the city’s plan.
6.   Mr. Dupps commented he has received phone calls from residents in the
Harvest Hill Subdivision and wanted to point out that that subdivision is not
included in this annexation.
7.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor for discussion. Mr. Feldhaus stated that he
is opposed to this annexation. Mr. Ellison also voiced his objection to the
annexation. Mrs. Gabbard stated that she was originally in favor of the
annexation plan in an effort to explore the interest of the residents in the
area. Mrs. Yeager concurred with Mrs. Gabbard.
8.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor to the public in attendance for comments but
asked that a couple of representatives be appointed to speak for the group. Mr.
Lloyd Brueckner, 135 Pelly Road stated he was against being annexed into the
city. Mr. G.E. Zimmerer, 120 Pelly Road, advised council that five years ago
the city attempted annexation of this area and the residents submitted a
petition with ninety names in opposition to the plan.
9.   Mr. Walker, City Attorney explained that if the proposed ordinance is
passed tonight, then the residents would have sixty days to submit a petition
in opposition. He advised that if more than fifty percent of the property
owners to be annexed opposed the plan then the city could have the issue placed
on the general election ballot in November. Mr. Walker reiterated that the
proposed ordinance would have to pass a second reading tonight in order to
begin the annexation process.
10.   Mr. Zimmerer stated he would proceed with a petition to protect the land
owners interest.
11.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to have a second reading on the ordinance
proposing annexation of certain unincorporated territories that lie inside the
present city limits. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered
with three yes votes and three no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus, Mrs. Yeager, and
Mr. Ellison. Mayor Kriege cast the deciding vote of no. The motion was defeated
4-3 against a second reading of the ordinance proposing annexation.
Privileges of the Floor
12.   Mr. Jimmy Barton, 30 Locust Lane, addressed council regarding the
condition of the street directly in front of his property. He stated that an
asphalt overlay put down last year but stopped short of the end of the street.
The area that was not surfaced is now deteriorating and requested that this
section of Locust Lane be inspected for repairs. Mr. Barton also inquired about
getting water lines run to Locust Lane. He stated there are water lines all
around Locust Lane but that the residents on the street do not have access to
water lines. Mayor Kriege stated the city would work with the engineers at the
Northern Kentucky Water District to check into the cost and feasibility of
running water lines to the residents on Locust Lane. Mr. Ellison and Mr.
Feldhaus advised Mr. Barton that the Water District would assess the property
owners for this type of project.
13.   Ms. Geneva Wade, 640 Willow Drive, addressed council concerning the
shoddy condition her property was left in after the construction of the Fowler
Creek sewer line. She also voiced her objection to the $280.00 debt reduction
assessment for the vacant lot she owns which she now feels has been destroyed.
Mayor Kriege stated that Mr. Scott and Mr. Smith, of the city’s Public Works
Department, would meet with her tomorrow morning at 10:00 a.m. to inspect her
property.
14.   A resident from the Independence Pointe Subdivision advised council that
Finke Builders are not maintaining the hillside on Flagstone Drive. He stated
that some of the residents worked together to mow the area before the Memorial
Day weekend as Finke has indicated to them that he has no plans to continue
maintenance of the area. This resident also stated that Finke wants to retain
ownership of this property for possible future development. Mr. Scott stated
that he hand delivered a zoning violation notice to Finke Builders regarding
this matter and afterward received a call from a Finke representative who
agreed to continue the maintenance of the area. Mr. Ellison suggested
withholding building permits in other Finke subdivisions in the city if this
problem persists. Mr. Feldhaus asked who was responsible for the sidewalks on
Flagstone Drive. Mr. Walker stated that Finke is responsible. Mr. Dupps
expressed concern that the maintenance of entryways, retention ponds, etc. is
becoming a common problem when a developer leaves town and expects the city to
care for this land that is still owned by the developer. Mayor Kriege stated
that he does not want the residents maintaining the area to become the
permanent solution to the matter.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a Supplement to the Code of Ordinances – 1st
Reading
15.   Mrs. Gabbard stated she would like to delay the first reading of this
ordinance until she has had ample time to review the supplement. There was a
brief discussion regarding the changes to the codification. Mr. Walker
clarified the intent of this ordinance; being that it was the addition of the
1999 ordinances to the current codification.
16.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to adopt the 1999 supplement to the Code of Ordinances. Mr. Ellison
seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with three yes votes and three
no votes cast by Mrs. Gabbard, Mr. Dupps, and Mr. Steffen. Mayor Kriege voted
yes to break the tie. Motion carried 4-3 in favor. Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Appointing an Alcoholic Beverage Administrator
17.   Mr. Steffen stated he requested the city attorney to draft the proposed
ordinance as the city will be reclassified to a third class city effective in
July and as a third class city will be required to appoint an alcoholic
beverage control administrator. He suggested this be a duty of the city
administrator. Mr. Feldhaus suggested appointing an existing ABC State officer.
Mrs. Yeager and Mr. Ellison expressed concern at adding another level of
bureaucracy. After a brief discussion, it was decided to have the city attorney
research this matter further.
Proposed Ordinance – Amendment of Election Procedures
18.   Mr. Walker, City Attorney introduced an ordinance that would require
primary elections for the nomination of candidates to a city office regardless
of the number of candidates running for each office. He explained that primary
elections are a requirement of a third class city. Mr. Walker suggested that in
order to avoid any confusion that council might want to delay adopting this
ordinance until the current election cycle is over. Mr. Steffen agreed that the
first reading should be delayed until August. Mr. Feldhaus questioned the
necessity of enacting this type of ordinance because in recent years the city
abolished primary elections in order to entice more candidates to run for
office. He stated that having a primary election requires candidates to file in
February and many people are not thinking that far in advance of a November
general election. Mr. Steffen commented that ‘write-in’ candidates could file
ten days prior to Election Day. To answer Mr. Feldhaus’ question, Mr. Walker
stated that as a third-class city, Independence must hold primary elections. He
went on to advise council that the third-class status does not take effect
until July 15, 2000 and that the city is still operating under the fifth-class
status for this year’s election.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Zoning/Building Permit Fees
19.   Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian, advised council this proposed
ordinance is being reintroduced with the revisions recommended by the Planning
& Zoning Committee. He stated that the Homebuilders Association has accepted
the proposed fee increase to be fair and equitable. Mayor Kriege stated that
since changes were made to the proposed ordinance from the original first
reading last September that a reading of this ordinance would become a first
reading again. Mr. Barbian pointed out a few other modifications in the
ordinance and a brief discussion followed.
20.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend the schedule of fees for zoning and building permits. Mr.
Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one
no vote cast by Mr. Feldhaus. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Text Amendment to Zoning Ordinance Regarding Sign
Regulations
21.   Mr. Walker suggested combining the two proposed ordinances submitted to
council regarding the text amendments to the zoning ordinance revising Section
14.6 and Section 14.7 classifying types of signs.
22.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to have a first reading of a proposed ordinance
to adopt a text amendment to the zoning ordinance revising Section 14.6 and

Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 99/2000 Budget Ordinance No. 1999-O-05
23.   Mayor Kriege presented an ordinance that would amend the current fiscal
year’s budget. He advised this could be read as an emergency since the next
regular meeting is in July. Or if council chooses, a special meeting could be
scheduled this month to transact a second reading. A brief discussion ensued.
Mr. Steffen stated he did not feel this constituted an emergency because a
special meeting could be scheduled this month to have a second reading of the
ordinance. Mr. Feldhaus stated that council might not be able to comprise a
quorum as many people go on vacation during the month of June.

proposed ordinance to amend the 99/00 budget. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion.

25.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to enact Ordinance Number 2000-O-07 amending
the Fiscal Year 99/00 Budget Ordinance Number 1999-O-05, to be read in summary.
Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call vote was unanimous – 6-0 in favor.

Proposed Ordinance – Second Reading Adopting Budget Ordinance No. 2000-O-08
26.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to adopt a budget for fiscal year 2000/01. Mrs. Yeager seconded the
motion. Discussion followed.
27.   Mrs. Gabbard asked where the $7,000 was derived to increase the police
department’s salary minimums. Mrs. Guenther stated that it had to be taken from
the reserve account. Mr. Dupps asked how the bank deposit tax revenue was
calculated. Mrs. Guenther stated that this figure is an estimate, which she
feels is conservative since this will be the first year that the city collects
this tax.
28.   Mrs. Gabbard questioned the miscellaneous expenditure for the transfer of
$40,000 to the Senior Center. Mrs. Guenther stated this was for six months of
operating expenses; $20,000 for interest on the loan and $20,000 for a grant
writer. Mrs. Gabbard voiced her concern at hiring another employee and
suggested the next city administrator that is hired should write the grants.
She also pointed out that the Special Events line item has increased
significantly. She stated that she foresees the city will need to cut expenses
or services or raise property taxes to cover the additional expenses.
29.   Mr. Feldhaus stated that just because the expense was being budgeted
doesn’t mean it will necessarily be spent; just available if needed. Mrs.
Gabbard also questioned the loan proceeds line item of $330,000. Mrs. Guenther
replied that it is estimated it will cost $600,000 to built the Senior Center
and the city will need to secure a construction loan to fund that expense. Mrs.
Gabbard stated she did not see the need to budget expenses that may not be
needed until April or May. Mr. Feldhaus stated that the budgeted funds would
not be moved until there are expended.
30.   At this time a roll call vote was taken on the motion to have a second
reading on proposed Ordinance Number 2000-O-08. Roll call was answered with
four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mrs. Gabbard and Mr. Steffen. Motion
carried 4-2 in favor and Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Motion to adopt Budget Ordinance No. 2000-O-08
31.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to adopt Ordinance Number 2000-O-08
establishing a budget for the fiscal year 2000/01. Mrs. Yeager seconded the
motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Steffen stated the city is spending too
much money and that taxes will need to be increased if expenses continue to
climb. Mr. Feldhaus voiced objection to Mr. Steffen’s statement and reminded
him of the various tax proposals he has introduced to council the last several
months. Mr. Steffen replied that all tax levies introduced by him would have
required to be placed on the November general election ballot for the residents
to vote on with the exception of the bank tax which the county was collecting
because of the city’s failure to take action to collect this money.
32.   Mayor Kriege asserted that the he worked along with the staff and feels
they were able to trim this budget of all excess. He stated that the revenue
figures appear deficient because it was conservatively estimated and the
increase in expenditures is a result of growing pains. Mrs. Gabbard again
stressed the need to cut services or raise taxes. Mr. Feldhaus suggested that
if the projected revenue comes up short then the budget could be revised to
address the situation. Mayor Kriege stated that his greatest concern was the
practice of pulling funds from the reserve account in order to balance the
budget. He advised that each department have been asked to develop a five-year
plan to project the operation costs of that department. He expressed a serious
need to look at future budgets, not just the current one.
33.   At this point, Mayor Kriege requested the vote to be taken on the motion/
second already on the floor to adopt Ordinance No. 2000-O-08 establishing a
budget for fiscal year 2000/01. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and
two no votes cast by Mrs. Gabbard and Mr. Steffen. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Administrator – Gary. R. Scott
34.   Mr. Scott stated that four bids were received for the maintenance of the
lawn and ballfields. He stated that he has reviewed them and recommended
contracting with Malco who currently provides this service to the city. Mr.
Scott stated that Malco’s bid was overall one of the low bids and commented
that their previous service was reliable, often going over and above what is
required. Mrs. Gabbard remarked that Malco has provided the city with several
years of service.
Award of the Lawn and Ballfield Maintenance Contract
35.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to award the contract for the lawn and
ballfield maintenance to Malco Services as the best bid. Mr. Ellison seconded
the motion. Roll call was answered with six yes votes; motion carried 6-0 in
favor.
Motion for a Brief Recess
36.   Upon motion by Mr. Feldhaus and second by Mr. Steffen the meeting was
interrupted for a brief recess. Motion carried with all ayes.
37.   Upon motion by Mr. Feldhaus and second by Mr. Dupps the meeting
reconvened. Motion carried with all ayes.
Employee Job Description

by ordinance and if council chooses to adopt the revisions by resolution then

creation of a job position should be adopted by ordinance but that the job

month’s meeting. Mr. Dupps suggested any changes be submitted to the Personnel

Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance

council meeting as amended, seconded by Mr. Dupps. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
