Proposed Ordinance - Appointment of an Alcoholic Beverage Administrator – 1st
Reading
12.   Next on the agenda was the proposed ordinance to appoint an Alcoholic
Beverage Administrator. City Attorney, Mr. Walker explained this ordinance
would create the position, which is required for cities of the third class. He
stated that during his research he learned that the county ABC officer cannot
hold both a city and county position but that the city could enter into an
interlocal agreement to procure that county official to fill the position for
the city. He also advised that another city officer could be appointed. Mr.
Feldhaus suggested the city approach the county to see if they were interested
in signing an interlocal agreement for this position’s services. Mr. Walker
informed council that by statute the Mayor has the authority to make the
appointment for this position. Mayor Kriege stated he was agreeable to an
interlocal agreement with the county.
13.   After the brief discussion to re-word Section I of the proposed ordinance
Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed ordinance
providing for a city alcoholic beverage administrator in compliance with KRS
241.160. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with six yes
votes. Motion carried and Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Repealing Job Descriptions for Certain Non-Elected City
Officers – 1st Reading
14.   City Attorney, Mr. Walker explained the purpose of the proposed ordinance
was to repeal the various employee job descriptions that had been originally
adopted by ordinance so that they could be re-adopted by resolution. He went on
to say that in the past as employee positions were created the job description
was adopted by ordinance. He advised that in the future only the creation of a
position be adopted by ordinance and that the job description be adopted by
resolution.
15.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to repeal the job descriptions for certain non-elected city offices.
Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Steffen voiced
some concern regarding the job descriptions for the contracted positions of
treasurer, building inspector and city attorney. Mr. Walker advised these could
be deleted. Mr. Steffen also suggested repealing Section 35.40 that pertains to
a Volunteer Fire Department which the city no longer operate. Council concurred
on the suggested revisions to the proposed ordinance. Roll call vote was
answered with six yes votes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Employee Job Descriptions for Non-Elected City
Officers – 1st Reading
16.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to adopt the employee job descriptions for non-elected city officers.
Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Mr. Walker defined the term ‘city officer’ as
the City Administrator, City Clerk, Police Chief and Zoning Administrator as
these positions hold a certain amount of authority. Roll call vote was answered
with six yes votes; motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Resolution No. 2000-R-11 – Amendment to the Personnel Policy
17.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to read Resolution No. 2000-R-11 to amend the

MAYOR’S REPORT – Thomas M. Kriege
35.   Mayor Kriege announced that he is promoting Lt. Shawn Butler to
permanently fill the vacant position of Police Chief. He stated that it is time
to provide the department with some stability. Mrs. Gabbard stated that Lt.
Butler, as Acting-Chief, has all the authority of the Police Chief and that
since there is pending litigation with former Chief Ed Porter she wondered
where that would leave Lt. Butler if Ed Porter were reinstated. City Attorney,
Mr. Walker explained that in a typical case when a former employee petition the
court for reinstatement and the employee wins the lawsuit, they generally are
awarded money not restored to their former position. He stated there are very
few case law instances where a court ordered reinstatement of the position with
an employer. Mr. Walker advised that the city’s insurance company attorney will
be at the August hearing regarding the lawsuit filed by Mr. Porter
36.   Mayor Kriege felt that appointing Shawn Butler as Police Chief was the
right thing to do for the city. Mr. Steffen stated that council is not required
to approve the Chief of Police position. Mr. Ellison agreed that it was the
Mayor’s job to make this appointment. Mr. Walker stated that if council wanted
to waive their approval of this appointment then they could do that. Mayor
Kriege stated that council’s approval would be a good opportunity to show
support for Lt. Butler. Mr. Dupps agreed with Mr. Ellison that the Mayor has
the authority to hire the Police Chief without council approval.
37.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to approve Executive Order 2000-EO-07
appointing Shawn Butler to the position of Chief of Police. Mr. Ellison
seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with four yes votes by Mr.
Feldhaus, Mr. Ellison, Mrs. Yeager and Mr. Dupps, one no vote cast by Mrs.
Gabbard and one abstain by Mr. Steffen. Mrs. Gabbard clarified her vote by
stating that the appointment of Police Chief is an executive decision and does
not require council approval. Motion carried 4-1-1.

AUGUST 28, 2000
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Rev. Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Jim Ellison, Eric Dupps, Donna Yeager, Barbara Gabbard, Gregory
Steffen and Steve Feldhaus answered roll call. Also in attendance was attorney
Mr. William Gullett from Brown, Todd and Heyburn who was sitting in for H.
Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
§   Proposed 2000 Tax Rate for Real and Personal Property
§   Appointment of City Administrator
§   Proposed 2000 Trash Assessment Rate
§   Proposed Ordinance to Amend Ordinance No. 1999-O-14 regarding the Lakefield
Subd.
§   Contracting with NKAPC for the city’s Zoning Administration
§   Bristow Meadows Development
§   Pay Play
Proposed 2000 Tax Rate for Real and Personal Property –1st Reading of the
Ordinance
3.   Mayor Kriege presented the proposed ordinance imposing the tax rates for
both real and personal property for the year 2000. He stated the proposal was
the compensating rate plus four percent. The four-percent increase would only
be applicable on real estate property.
4.   Upon review of the proposed ordinance, Mr. Feldhaus asked how much revenue
was budgeted for the 2000/01 fiscal year. He also asked the Mayor how the extra
revenue would be spent. Mayor Kriege stated there were no definite allocations
at this time but expressed a desire to plan the construction of sidewalks. Mr.
Feldhaus expressed concern that the proposed tax rate would generate more
revenue than was budgeted. Mr. Ellison commented that the budgeted amount was
just an estimate of the revenue, not the exact number.
5.   Mrs. Gabbard expressed concern of the term “personal property” in the
proposed ordinance. She felt the residents might fear that their personal
property would also be subject to taxation. Mr. Gullett explained that the term
“personal” is used because it is all-inclusive and is widely accepted in this
type of document. Mayor Kriege explained the only personal property that is
taxed by the city is for commercial inventory and not for residential personal
items.
6.   Mr. Dupps asked Mayor Kriege when the public hearing would be held to take
citizen comments regarding this rate. Mr. Steffen made a motion to hold a
public hearing, seconded by Mrs. Gabbard. Mayor Kriege advised the public
hearing has been scheduled for 6:30 p.m. on September 11, 2000, one-half hour
before the regularly scheduled council meeting. Mr. Steffen and Mrs. Gabbard
withdrew their motion and second.
7.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed ordinance
imposing the real and personal property tax rate for 2000. Mrs. Yeager seconded
the motion. There was a brief discussion regarding Section III that establishes
the penalty and interest rates for delinquent tax payments. It was decided to
set the penalty rate at fifteen percent and the interest rate at six percent
per annum. Roll call was taken and answered with all ayes. Motion carried. Mr.
Gullett read the proposed ordinance.
Appointment of City Administrator
8.   Mayor Kriege read a prepared statement wherein he reported on the search
to fill the position of City Administrator. The statement is attached to these
minutes as a part of the official record.
9.   Ex-Mayor Jim Kudera, 80 McMillan Drive, concurred with Mayor Kriege’s
remarks. Moreover, Mr. Kudera reprimanded the council members for their failure
to support Mayor Kriege and scolded them for prolonging petty squabbles. Mr.
Kudera stated he was ashamed and embarrassed by council’s behavior and informed
them that it was time to serve the residents they represent in this city.
10.   Mrs. Gabbard, Mr. Feldhaus and Mr. Ellison wished to make rebuttals to
Mr. Kudera’s personal charges. Mrs. Gabbard was upset that Mayor Kriege did not
permit the council members to dispute Mr. Kudera’s attacks before he stormed
out of the council chambers. She commented this was a good opportunity for the
citizens to see Mr. Kudera, who is a candidate for a council seat in the
general election this year.
11.   There was a brief exchange of comments regarding the City Administrator
position. Mrs. Gabbard stated she would not endorse a personal friend of the
Mayor’s for the position and expressed concern for his lack of communication.
Mayor Kriege stated the committee he formed interviewed four candidates out of
sixty applicants for the job. Mr. Dupps was part of that committee and sat in
on the interviews. He stated that he had reported this information to council
and no one asked if they were to be involved in the interview process. Mayor
Kriege stated they would continue daily operations with the existing staff in
the absence of a City Administrator. He also advised that he is personally
putting in long hours on city matters as well as his full time job. In closing,
Mayor Kriege reiterated that he stands by the procedure that was used to
conduct the search for a City Administrator.
12.   Mr. Dupps confirmed Mayor Kriege’s position that the candidates
interviewed for the position were very qualified possessing the municipal
experience and education required. He stated that as a third class city there
are commercial and business interests that need to be addressed. Mr. Dupps also
commented the city’s rapid growth demands the position of a full time
administrator.
13.   Mr. Feldhaus frowned on the television cameras present for this special
meeting and suggested that others were also guilty of political nonsense. He
also objected to Mayor Kriege’s refusal to allow rebuttals to Mr. Kudera’s
accusations. In addition, Mr. Feldhaus cited the following reasons why he would
not support Mayor Kriege’s candidate: objected to the proposed three-year
contract, as the conditions of the contract were not discussed with council;
the candidate had no experience in the State of Kentucky; did not review the
resumes of the other candidates vying for the position, and did not meet the
candidate. He commented that in the past council had the opportunity to meet
with the top three or four candidates and review their resumes. Mrs. Gabbard
also had objections to a three-year contract.
14.   Mayor Kriege stated that in all good conscious he could not bring in a
City Administrator at this time. Mrs. Gabbard reminded Mayor Kriege of his
obligation to fill the position. There was a brief exchange of comments
regarding the benefits that could be provided to a city administrator.
15.   In closing, Mr. Steffen wanted to explain that the legal fees that Mr.
Kudera made reference to were not due to political issues, but were in large
part due to lawsuits with AT&T, who wanted to erect a cell tower in the local
cemetery and lawsuits with developers that were denied zone requests. He stated
that this money for legal representation was well spent and in the best
interest of the citizens.
Proposed 2000 Trash Assessment Rate –1st Reading of the Ordinance
16.   Mr. Feldhaus asked if the proposed rate of $89.40 was a “pass through”
rate. Pat Taney, City Clerk advised that it was. She also stated this is an
increase of $2.52 from last year and that the increase is minimal because the
city is in the fourth year of a five-year contract with Rumpke.
17.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to impose a trash assessment rate of $89.40 for the year 2000. Mr.
Steffen seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried and Mr. Gullett read the proposed ordinance.
Discussion of Lakefield Subdivision Plans for Park Area
18.   Nita Brake reported to council that they have recently learned that the
green space donated to the city by Drees in the Lakefield Subdivision includes
part ownership of a lake. She stated the green space is to be developed as a
park and is divided by a street with the lake on one side of the road. She
reported that ownership of the lake is shared with several other properties on
which homes have been built. She advised council that they were unaware that
the land Drees was donating contained a lake and she expressed concern that the
lake could be a liability for the city. Ms. Brake reported she is working with
a Drees representative and feels certain they will agree to take back the lake
area to develop as lakefront lots. She has also requested that Drees develop
the park according to ADA regulations, which they have taken under
consideration but not committed to. Mr. Steffen stated that he remembers seeing
the lake and though it would be nice but had not considered the liability
issue. He made a motion to turn this matter over to the Planning and Zoning
Committee to meet with Drees to work out an agreement for the development of
the park area. Mrs. Yeager advised council that the city attorney’s office was
currently in discussions with Drees about this. Mr. Steffen withdrew his
motion. Mr. Gullett stated that the attorney’s office needs direction from
council as to what they do and do not want with regard to the lake area and the
development of the park. In the original ordinance (Ordinance No. 1999-O-14)
that granted the map amendment the green space was to be developed as a park
and then deeded over to the city for future ownership and maintenance. In
closing, Ms. Brake stated she would like to see the park area of 1.83 acres be
ADA accessible, include four or five parking spaces and not have pea gravel in
the play area. They will continue negotiations with Drees.
Contract Zoning Administration with the Northern Ky. Area Planning Commission
19.   Mayor Kriege presented council with a proposed contract with the Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission for the city’s zoning administration. He
introduced Russell Cloyd who answered questions for council. Mr. Feldhaus asked
how much time would be spent in Independence. Mr. Cloyd stated the work load
would dictate the amount of time spend in the city but that they would be able
to provide forty hours per week if that is what Independence wants. Mrs.
Gabbard asked if there would be follow up on zoning violation complaints. Mr.
Cloyd stated they would be hiring two additional staff members to handle the
workload. He stated that the Planning Commission has recently obtained a new
software program that will aid in tracking the zoning violations for follow-up
after the initial contact. Mayor Kriege stated the Planning Commission would
provide council with a monthly report.
20.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into a
contract with Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission for the city’s zoning
administration. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Mrs. Gabbard asked if legal
counsel had reviewed this contract. Mayor Kriege stated the proposed contract
is nearly identical to the contract with other cities in Northern Kentucky. Mr.
Steffen asked Mayor Kriege if he had given up on hiring a city employee to fill
the position of Zoning Administrator. Mayor Kriege stated he received few
responses to the advertisement for the position. He suggested trying the
services of NKAPC as an immediate solution, then re-evaluating the arrangement
in six months. He added that NKAPC would handle the Board of Adjustment and
Code Enforcement Board meetings. Mrs. Gabbard commented that she feels the city
needs a full time employee to handle zoning issues and would like to see the
search to fill this position continued. Mr. Feldhaus agreed but stated that the
city needs zoning assistance now while continuing the search. Mr. Ellison
concurred. There was a brief discussion to change the job description for the
Zoning Administrator to include more benefits. Roll call vote was answered with
six yes votes, with Mrs. Gabbard and Mr. Steffen clarifying their vote by
stating they wanted the city to continue the search for a city employee to fill
the position of Zoning Administrator. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Discussion of Bristow Meadows Development
21.   Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian reported that the drainage calculations
for the Stage II development of Bristow Meadows should be submitted by the next
regular council meeting. The recommendations will be made by then so that
council can vote on the matter. He assured council that he would not issue a
Certificate of Occupancy until this is resolved. Mr. Scott Holten, 853 Bristow
Road, expressed concern for the culvert pipe running under Bristow Road and
asked if the developer (Long & Kiser) would be permitted to continue
construction while this is being decided. Mr. Barbian stated he did not feel it
was necessary to issue a “stop work” order. Mr. Feldhaus commented that two
buildings are under construction. Mr. Barbian advised the developer is
currently hanging drywall but assured council that he would not issue a
Certificate of Occupancy before this matter is resolved.
Adjournment
22.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to adjourn; seconded by Mr. Dupps. Motion
carried 6-0 and the meeting adjourned at 8:25 p.m.

SEPTEMBER 11, 2000
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege was out of town on business. Council Member, Donna Yeager
presided at the meeting and called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Rev. Randy McCafferty of Independence Christian Church
gave the invocation. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison,
Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in
attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker.
2.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to amend the agenda by moving the approval of
the Special Council Meeting minutes below the Mayor’s Report and adding council
comments after that. Mrs. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call vote was
answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Dupps. Motion carried
5-1 in favor.
Approval of the Minutes of the August 7, 2000 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to approve the minutes of the August 7, 2000
council meeting; seconded by Mr. Dupps. Roll call was answered with all ayes.
Motion carried 6-0.
UPDATE ON SENIOR CENTER PROJECT
4.   Mark Gribler, architect for Moody/Nolan Ltd., reported to council
regarding the recent bids received by the city for the construction of a new
Senior Center building at Memorial Park. He reported that the sealed bids were
received and publicly opened on Wednesday, August 30, 2000. He stated that
eight proposals were received with the three lowest bids from Hemmer Industries
($1,082,000.), Century Construction ($1,156,000.) and Mark Spaulding
Construction ($1,180,859.). Following the bid opening, the low bidder Hemmer
Industries discovered a $113,000 mathematical error in the computation and
subsequently withdrew their bid. Mr. Gribler stated that the preliminary cost
estimate for the project was approximately $694,000 and the bids were
considerably higher than that estimate. Therefore, he recommended the city
reject all bids received and the project should be rebid and emphasized that
the design would not be affected. He also suggested that the funding for the
project be reviewed, possibly to include the construction of the amphitheater.
He felt that making use of the utility companies and subcontractors while they
are on the site would be beneficial for both projects.
5.   Mr. Ellison asked if the prevailing wage law affected the project. Mr.
Gribler replied yes. Mr. Gribler added that compliance issues are a substantial
burden.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to reject all bids received for the
construction of the Senior Center and rebid the project. Mr. Dupps seconded the
motion. Roll call vote was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
7.   Brenda Chasteen, 1281 Victory Lane addressed council about two issues.
First, she reminded council about the ongoing struggle to get Finke Homes to
comply with their verbal agreement to maintain the area surrounding the
entrance to the Independence Pointe Subdivision. She stated that this entrance
area was well maintained during the construction of the subdivision but now
that Finke Homes has finished building they are inconsistent with the mowing.
She stated that several homeowners have taken on the task of keeping the area
mowed. Mr. Tom Brinker, 1192 Constitution Drive concurred that Finke Homes had
made a verbal agreement with Gary Scott, (former City Administrator) months ago
to mow every two weeks. Mr. Brinker stated that now Finke is saying they will
mow every thirty days but that they only do it when prompted. Mr. Brinker and
Ms. Chasteen asked council to mediate this matter between the property owners
of Independence Pointe Subdivision and Finke Homes.
8.   Mr. Dupps asked Kevin Barbian the status of this zoning violation. Mr.
Barbian stated he left a message with Finke and was assured that the area would
be mowed. Mr. Feldhaus asked if the zoning ordinance specified a height for
grass and weeds. Mr. Barbian stated that there are no specifics cited in the
ordinance. Mr. Dupps suggested researching the zoning ordinance to make
possible amendments by adding height limit for unsightly grass/weeds. Mr.
Feldhaus explained the process the city has to take when citing a zoning
violation. Mr. Ellison suggested withholding building permits in other Finke
subdivisions until they come into compliance with this zoning violation at
Independence Pointe. Mr. Walker cautioned against this. Mr. Ellison then
suggested the city mow the area and file a lien on the property. Mr. Feldhaus
suggested filing a suit against Finke Homes for violation of deed restrictions.
Mr. Walker advised they could file a public nuisance action backed up with
restriction violation but cautioned that it is a slow process. Mr. Walker
suggested that the city take aggressive action to enforce the zoning ordinance.
Mr. Brinker wanted to see the city hold the builders responsible for their
actions and suggested a written agreement with Finke Homes be obtained. Mrs.
Yeager asked Mr. Barbian to actively pursue this zoning violation until Finke
Homes comes into compliance.
9.   The other matter Brenda Chasteen presented to council was the storm sewer
that is causing erosion on her property (1281 Victory Lane). She stated she had
spoken to Mayor Kriege and Gary Scott regarding this issue. This erosion is
also occurring on her neighbor’s property. Jeff Smith, Public Works crew leader
stated that the city will begin work on that next week. The work has been
contracted out to Lucas Sanitation.
10.   Betty Eichelberger, 6258 Taylor Mill Road spoke to council regarding the
barking dogs in her neighborhood. She has a neighbor that has several dogs that
bark all night long. She reported that she has called the police on several
occasions and the dog warden has cited the dog owner. She asked council for a
solution to this matter. Police Chief, Shawn Butler suggested taking the dog
owner to district court and offered to meet with Ms. Eichelberger to discuss
this matter.
Discussion of the Proposed 2000 Tax Rate for Real & Personal Property
11.   Mr. Feldhaus stated that prior to this meeting a Public Hearing was held
to discuss adopting a real property tax rate of .158 per $100.00 of assessed
value. He stated that rate was the compensating rate plus four percent. He
expressed reservations about adopting this rate as the compensating rate of
.152 would generate $60,000 additional revenue and did not feel the city needed
to take the four- percent.
12.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to read a new ordinance to adopt the
compensating rate of .152/$100.00 assessed value; seconded by Mr. Ellison. Mr.
Dupps expressed concern that the city would not be able to meet the budgeted
expenditures, especially for the park and police facilities. He was also
concerned that this lower rate will cause the city to once again pull from the
reserve fund just to meet the budgeted expenses. Mrs. Gabbard stated that she
felt the city needed to tighten the expenditures and suggested reviewing the
budget. Mrs. Yeager reminded council that the city police department is
occupying rental space in the courthouse because the city is unable to provide
this department with it’s own facility. Mr. Dupps suggested adopting a rate mid
way between .152 to .158. Mr. Steffen suggested adopting the compensating rate
plus two percent. Mr. Feldhaus stated that that could increase a property
owner’s tax if the property was reassessed by PVA this year. Mr. Walker advised
that a first reading was taken on the .158/$100 rate at the last meeting and a
new rate would require two readings or could be enacted by emergency. Roll call
vote resulted in a tie; three yes votes by Mr. Feldhaus, Mr. Ellison and Mrs.
Gabbard and three no votes cast by Mr. Dupps, Mr. Steffen and Mrs. Yeager.
13.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to adopt the compensating rate plus two percent
for a rate of .155/$100 of assessed value for the 2000 real estate taxes. Mr.
Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call vote resulted in a tie; those voting in
favor were Mr. Steffen, Mr. Dupps and Mrs. Yeager and those opposed were Mr.
Feldhaus, Mrs. Gabbard and Mr. Ellison.
14.   A brief discussion followed. Council discussed three different tax rates
and the revenue that would be generated from each rate. Mrs. Gabbard commented
that she was opposed to raising the tax rate but acknowledged that a rate of
.155/$100 would be a good compromise, as it would generate enough revenue to
fund the needed projects. She reiterated that she felt the city could still
find ways to cut some expenses, too.
15.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to reconsider adopting the .155/$100 real
property tax rate for 2000. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call vote was
answered with four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus and Mr.
Ellison. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.
16.   Amy Guenther, Finance Director, advised council that if the real property
rate was changed from the originally proposed .158/$100 then the personal
property rate would also have to be changed. Council discussed this briefly and
arrived at a rate of .181/$100 for personal property taxes.
Adopting the Real and Personal Property Tax Rates for 2000 – Ordinance No.
2000-O-15
17.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a first reading of proposed Ordinance No.
2000-O-15 adopting a real property tax rate of .155/$100 of assessed value and
.181/$100 of assessed value for personal property for the year 2000. Mr.
Steffen seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and two
no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus and Mr. Ellison. Motion carried 4-2 in favor and
Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
18.   Mr. Walker advised council that in order to forgo a second reading of
this ordinance they would need to declare an emergency exists to enact this
immediately. Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to declare Ordinance No. 2000-O-15 an
emergency; seconded by Mr. Dupps. Roll call was answered with five yes votes
and one no vote cast by Mr. Steffen. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
19.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to enact by emergency Ordinance No. 2000-O-15
adopting the real property tax rate for 2000 at .155/$100 and the personal
property tax rate for 2000 at .181/$100. Mrs. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll
call vote was answered with four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr.
Feldhaus and Mr. Ellison. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance No. 2000-O-16 – Adopting 2000 Trash Assessment Rate

Proposed Ordinance to Prohibit Weekday Parking on Alvin Drive between 7 AM and
3 PM
27.   Police Chief, Shawn Butler addressed council regarding the proposed
ordinance to prohibit parking on Alvin Drive between the hours of 7 a.m. and 3
p.m. during the weekdays. He reported that Alvin Drive is a very narrow street
and the overflow parking from nearby Simon Kenton High School has become a
hazard as it would be nearly impossible for emergency vehicles to access the
nine homes on the street. Currently the vehicles parking there during school
hours are parked legally. He stated that they have requested the school to ask
students not to park on Alvin Drive but the students are not complying. Mr.
Ellison asked if a parking limit of two hours would solve the problem. Chief
Butler replied that he doesn’t have the manpower that would be needed to time
the parking, mark the street with chalk, etc. Mr. Feldhaus stated he would
prefer to set a time limit rather than prohibit parking altogether. Mr. Ellison
stated that he felt the residents should be able to park on the street. Chief
Butler informed council that the police department has been working with the
residents on Alvin Drive to arrive at a solution that would favor the
residents. He stated he has spoken to the majority of the residents on the
street and they were not opposed to the ban on parking during the designated
hours.
28.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading in summary of the
proposed ordinance to prohibit parking on Alvin Drive between the hours of 7
a.m. and 3 p.m. Monday through Friday. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor. Mr. Walker read
the proposed ordinance.
29.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to declare that an emergency exists on Alvin
Drive because public safety is a concern and to waive the second reading of the
ordinance at the next regularly scheduled council meeting. Mr. Feldhaus
seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered with all ayes. Motion carried
6-0 in favor.
30.   Mr. Steffen moved and Mr. Feldhaus seconded to enact by emergency
Ordinance No. 2000-O-17 that would prohibit parking on Alvin Drive, between the
hours of 7 a.m. and 3 p.m. Monday through Friday. Roll call vote was answered
with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
New Business – Proposed Amendment to Ordinance No. 2000-O-08
31.   Council Member, Jim Ellison introduced a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2000-O-08 that adopted the current fiscal year budget. He
stated that would like the budget, which was adopted in summary to be changed
to show line item expenditures. He stated that he feels there will be more
accountability using a line item budget.
32.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend budget Ordinance No. 2000-O-08; seconded by Mrs. Gabbard. A
brief discussion ensued. Mr. Dupps stated he was unclear as to why this change
was needed. Mr. Ellison stated that with a line item budget in place that funds
could not be spent prior to council approval. Finance Director, Amy Guenther
advised that she spoke to the Department of Local Government and they advised
that the budget ordinance should not be too detailed as to halt the daily
operations of the city. She advised that it would be difficult to adhere to a
line item budget, as there are currently five line items that have exceeded the
budgeted amount. Ms. Guenther also cautioned that the ordinance might have to
be amended on a monthly basis if council decides to make this change in the
budget. She recommended staying with a summary budget and offered to provide
council with a more detailed financial report each month. Mr. Walker advised
that if council chooses to adopt the budget by line item then the daily
government operations could be restricted. He also reminded council that every
time a line item is changed throughout the year, then the ordinance has to be
amended, causing two readings and publication that would become quite costly.
Mr. Ellison reiterated that there needs to be more accountability and with the
City Administrator position vacant that council needs to be aware of all
spending. At this time roll call vote was taken and answered with three yes
votes cast by Mr. Ellison, Mr. Feldhaus and Mrs. Gabbard; and three no votes
cast by Mr. Dupps, Mr. Steffen and Mrs. Yeager. The motion resulted in a tie
vote 3-3. Mr. Walker explained that since there is no way to break the tie vote
the motion is declared lost.
Recess

Proposed Ordinance to Adopt a Text Amendment to Abolish R-1E zones and

to adopt a text amendment to the zoning ordinance that would abolish R-1E zones
and establish day cares in the NSC zone. Motion seconded by Mr. Feldhaus. Roll
call was answered with six yes votes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Discussion and Adoption of the Special Council Meeting Minutes of August 28,
2000

2000 Special Council meeting minutes. He asked Mr. Walker’s advice and wondered

CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison, Barbara
Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in attendance
was attorney, Jeff E. Smith, who was sitting in for City Attorney, H. Lawson
Walker who was unable to attend this meeting.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 11, 2000 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve the minutes of the September 11, 2000
council meeting, as amended. Mr. Feldhaus seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Addition to the Agenda
3.   Mrs. Gabbard requested to be added to the agenda under old business, as
she said that she had a statement that she would like to read aloud.
Presentation of 1999/2000 Audit by Linda Chapman of Rankin, Rankin & Co.
4.   Linda Chapman of Rankin, Rankin & Company reviewed the audit report with
council. She stated the records are in good shape and that no irregularities
were found. Ms. Chapman stated that the city’s total assets are 10M with a
twenty-one percent increase from the investments. She reported the total
revenue received increased by $460,000 from last year but that expenses were
high due to refinancing of the sewer debt fund account. She also noted that
there are timing issues that occur at the end of the fiscal year such as
encumbrances and prepays. So that while it appears the city was ahead in
anticipated revenue, other foreseen expenses were carried over.
5.   Mr. Feldhaus referred to page twenty-one regarding internal controls. Ms.
Chapman stated that it is recommended the city prepare a fixed asset register
and continue to maintain that register throughout the years by adding and
deleting major effects. She stated that this is a necessary and useful tool for
insurance purposes. She advised taking a good inventory of all city owned
assets and establishing a fixed dollar amount for each item in order to
maintain internal control. Ms. Chapman informed council that by July 2003 this
internal control plan will be required to meet GASB standards and that is why
she suggests we begin this process now. She stated that the list of fixed
assets should also include city streets, bridges, etc.

NEW BUSINESS
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2000/01 Fiscal Year Budget – First Reading
9.   Mrs. Amy Guenther, Finance Director, submitted a proposed ordinance to
amend the current budget. She stated there have been some changes in the
projected revenue and expenditures that made it necessary to amend the budget
at this time. Mr. Feldhaus suggested waiting until May 2001 to make this
amendment. Mrs. Guenther advised that these changes were too significant to
carry most of the fiscal year. Linda Chapman, Auditor for Rankin, Rankin and
Company, commented that most cities wait until May but to comply with K.R.S.,
funds have to be budgeted before you can expend them. Mrs. Guenther stated that
to receive the state funds for the amphitheater for Memorial Park the budget
has to be amended to reflect that revenue. Mr. Feldhaus commented that it seems
like a waste of funds to publish an amended budget ordinance more than once
during the year.
10.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend budget Ordinance No. 2000-O-08. Mrs. Yeager seconded the
motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Steffen suggested this would be a good
time to change the format of the budget to a ‘line item’ budget instead of the
current summary format. Mrs. Gabbard and Mr. Ellison agreed with this
suggestion. Mr. Ellison felt a line item budget would assist them in tracking
all expenditures making it easier to follow. Mrs. Gabbard stated that in light
of the fact that the city was currently without a City Administrator that it
would be best to convert to a ‘line item’ budget. Mr. Dupps disagreed by
stating that he did not see how a ‘line item’ budget was going to change the
process by which city business was conducted. Mr. Feldhaus asked Mrs. Guenther
how the budget would be prepared. Mrs. Guenther assured council that although
the budget is adopted using a summary format she will to provide a ‘line item’
detail report each month for their review. Mr. Feldhaus questioned the
publication expense of a ‘line item’ budget. Mr. Jeff Smith (attorney) advised
that the publication costs could be extremely expensive if the ‘line items’
were changed several times during the fiscal year. Mrs. Yeager commented that
she preferred to adopt the amended budget by summary. Mr. Steffen made a motion
to amend Mr. Feldhaus’s motion to include ‘the incorporation of a ‘line item’
budget.’ Mrs. Gabbard seconded Mr. Steffen’s motion. At this time, Mrs. Yeager
withdrew her second to Mr. Feldhaus’s motion for a first reading of the
proposed ordinance to amend the budget. Mr. Feldhaus stated he would like to
have time to review the ‘line item’ report that Mrs. Guenther provided. After
some thought Mr. Feldhaus placed his original motion on the floor to have a
first reading (in summary) of the proposed ordinance to amend the 2000/01
budget as presented. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Motion carried with all
ayes and Mr. Smith read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance to Establish Primary Elections – 1st Reading

effective no later than the 2002 city election. He urged council to support
this establishment of a primary election, which is a requirement of third class
cities

NOVEMBER 6, 2000
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty from the Independence Christian Church
gave the invocation. Council Members Steve Feldhaus, Donna Yeager, Jim Ellison,
Barbara Gabbard, Eric Dupps, and Gregory Steffen answered roll call. Also in
attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker.
Proclamation Presented to Eagle Scout, Trevor Moser
2.   Mayor Kriege presented a proclamation to Independence resident, Trevor
Moser for his achievement on attaining the rank of Eagle Scout.
Approval of the Minutes of the October 2, 2000 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to approve the minutes of the October 2, 2000
council meeting, as amended. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
Bob Exeler – Water Lines on Fowler Creek Road
4.   Mr. Bob Exeler of 5296 Fowler Creek Road presented council with a petition
signed by eighteen residents of Fowler Creek Road requesting that public water
lines be installed in that area. Mr. Exeler stated that he has been researching
the possibility of obtaining a grant from the state to help defray the cost of
installing water lines. He stated he has been in contact with Richard Harrison
of the Northern Kentucky Water District and Sally P. Davis who is Governor
Patton’s Northern Kentucky liaison and reported that both offered their
support. Mayor Kriege stated he spoke to Mr. Harrison who encouraged him to
apply for this CBDG grant, as it will take time to obtain it. Mrs. Yeager asked
if the grant was for the entire cost or if the city would need to match the
grant amount. Mayor Kriege replied that it would be a matching grant. Mr.
Exeler voiced objections to the city’s recent discussions to install sidewalks
and construct an amphitheater when there are so many areas of the city that do
not have access to public water lines. Mrs. Yeager advised Mr. Exeler that the
funds for the amphitheater were obtained by private donations and allocated
state dollars from the Governor’s budget.
5.   Mr. Exeler requested the city make application for a grant to install the
water lines in the Fowler Creek Road area. Mrs. Gabbard voiced reluctance to
vote on this matter when the city does not know what the matching cost of the
grant would be for the city. Mr. Feldhaus pointed that the estimated
construction cost was $274,000. Mayor Kriege stated that the Water District
would provide the design for no charge. There was a brief discussion about the
cost to the residents and how this project would be assessed to each property
owner. Mr. Exeler stated that the more pocket areas serviced the more
economical the project would be for each owner. He informed council that the
Water District is only able to apply for a limited number of grants so he urged
council to apply for this grant for the residents. Mayor Kriege asked that
council consider making a commitment to move forward with the necessary
paperwork by applying for the grant. He advised that if the grant is awarded to
the city, that it would then need further approval from council to offer the
matching funds. He advised that Mr. Harrison would assist with the grant
application process.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus made a motion to proceed with the necessary paperwork to
apply for a grant to construct water lines in the Fowler Creek Road area. Mr.
Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried
6-0 in favor.
Charles Deters – Courthouse Restaurant at the Independence Towne Center
7.   Mr. Deters addressed council on behalf of Nathan Deters who was unable to
attend the meeting. Mr. Deters presented to council a proposed change of
location from the original site plan of the Independence Towne Center for the
Courthouse Restaurant. He explained this would be a sit-down type of
restaurant. Mr. Deters told council that too much parking space was allocated
on the original site plan for the Towne Center and that the proposed new
location for the restaurant is on a parcel that was initially designated for
parking.
8.   Mr. Russell Cloyd of the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission
advised council that this proposed change is back before council to decide
whether this is a minor or major change to the original site plan. A lengthy
discussion ensued regarding criteria used to decide what constitutes a minor or
major change. Mr. Cloyd stated that NKAPC could approve this site change if
council considers this a minor change.
9.   Mr. Feldhaus commented that he feels this change in location would be a
major change to the site plan. He added that he would consider changes in
landscaping, parking spaces, etc to be minor changes, but not moving from one
location to another.
10.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Cloyd for his expert opinion. Mr. Cloyd stated,
that although the proposed restaurant is smaller than the sum of the two
outlots on the original site plan, the consensus opinion of the Planning
Commission staff is that this is a major change, as no building was planned for
the new site. Mr. Cloyd went on to say that they felt that council should make
the final determination.
11.   Mrs. Gabbard voiced concerns that the restaurant would require additional
lighting that would intrude upon the surrounding residents in that area. Mr.
Deters stated that this structure would not require additional lighting. He
advised that deflectors have recently been installed on the lights at the BP
Station.
12.   Mr. Feldhaus reiterated that a new building being constructed on a site
where one was not planned constitutes a major change and suggested this request
go through the review process. Mr. Deters stated this process would require the
entire site plan to be amended which would entail a public hearing. He stated
that this would delay the project for three months and they were anxious to get
started before winter sets in.
13.   Mr. Walker stated that he has never been to a council meeting where
council was to decided a major/minor change. Mr. Cloyd commented that due to
the newness of the contract with the city and being unfamiliar with council,
they felt it was best to bring this proposal to the city. Mr. Deters
interjected that this requires an interpretation of the zoning ordinance.
14.   Mr. Ellison stated that since the lot has not been paved there should not
be a problem with water runoff and the Towne Center has ample parking. Mr.
Deters stated there is no better water retention in the county as the overflow
drains into the lake.
15.   Mr. Deters stated the Towne Center has and continues to bring many new
conveniences to the city residents and it is only a third of the way completed.
He urged council to show cooperation so that they can move forward with this
project without a three-month delay.
16.   Mr. Steffen stated this be submitted as a major change. Mrs. Gabbard
expressed concern that the city would be setting precedent if this site
location were ruled as a minor change. Mr. Walker commented that every
development stands on its own merits and that nothing will prevent another
person from asking council to do the same. He advised that the Rich McAllister
and Mr. Cloyd of the Planning Commission, as the contracted Zoning
Administrator for the city, is seeking guidance in this matter, just as an
employee of this city would do.
17.   Mayor Kriege asked council if they would prefer to leave this decision to
the Planning Commission. Mrs. Yeager replied she did not want to see Mr.
Deters’ project delayed for three months. Mr. Cloyd stated that the city’s
zoning ordinance is vague and that he could argue for and against this request.
But he advised they would research the matter further and handle
administratively if that is what council desires.
18.   Mr. Feldhaus requested a special meeting be scheduled to decide this
matter after the Planning Commission has done their research. Mr. Ellison
suggested they research K.R.S. and city ordinance criteria. Council concurred
and a special council meeting was scheduled for Wednesday, November 8, 2000 at
5:00 p.m.
Ray Kerl – Independence Soccer Club
19.   Mr. Kerl, 3933 Thomas Drive, introduced himself to council as the
President of the Independence Soccer Club. He addressed council regarding two
complaints he had regarding the city parks. Mr. Kerl stated that the shelter
building restrooms at Staggs Park are always locked. He asked why this building
was not open so that the public could use the restroom facilities. He stated
that other cities give keys to the Police Department so the shelters can be
open. Nita Brake, Recreation Director, stated the shelter building is locked
because of the vandalism when left open. Police Chief, Shawn Butler, stated he
is trying to work out a schedule with the patrol officers so that the restrooms
can be opened more often.
20.   Mr. Kerl stated the other matter he wanted to speak about concerned the
soccer goals. He informed council that the Independence Recreation Committee
requires the Soccer Club to dismantle and remove the soccer goals by November
5. Mr. Kerl objected to this practice as it is an undue burden on the Soccer
Club and he sees no logical reason to remove the goals for the winter months.
He stated that the county and other cities do no require removal of the goals
during the off season. Nita Brake, Recreation Director, responded to Mr. Kerl’s
grievance by informing council that the Soccer Club agreed to remove the goals
at the July 7th I.R.C. meeting. She stated that this was a compromise with the
residents in the Hartland Subdivision. Ms. Carolyn Fields, 5278 Millcreek
Circle, whose property abuts the Independence Park in Hartland Subdivision,
stated the park is not a soccer field where games are played, just a practice
area for the teams. Mayor Kriege agreed that the park in Hartland was a unique
situation and felt it was necessary to work with the residents. Rita King, 6523
Sugar Camp Drive, stated that until recently the goals were left up year round
at Staggs Parks and she does not see why they have to be removed.
21.   In closing, Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Kerl that the city would make every
attempt to keep the Staggs Park Shelter restrooms open for public use, but
stated the city would not leave them open twenty-four hours a day to be
subjected to vandals. Mr. Ellison stated that council should uphold the
Independence Recreation Committee’s recommendations. In addition, Mr. Dupps
advised Mr. Kerl to plead his case at a future Recreation Committee meeting.
Tom Brinker – Independence Pointe Subdivision front Entrance
22.   Mr. Brinker, 1192 Constitution Drive, presented a review of the year’s
activity regarding the matter of Finke Homes’ repeated non-compliance in
maintaining the land at the entrance of the Independence Pointe Subdivision on
Flagstone Drive off Cody Road. He stated that Finke was in violation 70% of the
time and was not issued a fine once. He stated that he was hopeful that the new
contracted Zoning Administrator would assess fines next year. There was a brief
discussion on how the matter would be handled next year. Mr. Steffen suggested
citing Finke to the Code Enforcement Board. Mayor Kriege stated he had
discussed this matter with the Home Builders Association and was advised the
city could file a grievance with the association against Finke Homes.
Ike Gabbard
23.   Mr. Gabbard, 5140 Madison Pike, address council regarding property on
Richardson Road that is an eyesore. He did not have an address but was advised
to obtain one and Mr. McAllister, Zoning Administrator, would follow up on this
violation.

Falcon Ridge Development – Request for City to Assume Maintenance of Storm
Water Retention
29.   Bob Schroder, Falcon Ridge Development, came before council to request
the city assume ownership of the retention system that was constructed by them
in the Falcon Ridge Subdivision.
30.   Council Member, Jim Ellison announced that he would remove himself from
the discussion of this matter as his participation could be construed as a
conflict of interest.
31.   Mr. Schroder explained to council that shortly after the subdivision
began development, several residents complained of the storm water runoff from
the subdivision. He stated that because of these complaints they purchased a
small parcel of adjoining land and obtained an easement for storm water
drainage and retention and installed a storm water system within the land and
easement. The system consists of two ponds, underground pipes and a drainage
easement, which has been inspected and approved by the Planning Commission. Mr.
Schroder stated that he felt it would be appropriate for the city to accept
this land and easement as it benefits several residents.
32.   Mayor Kriege expressed concerns, that with limited Public Works staff and
resources, that the city would have difficulty maintaining this system. Mr.
Feldhaus stated the city does not own and maintain any retention system in the
various subdivisions in the city. Mrs. Gabbard stated that she does not see why
the city would want to take ownership of this type of property. Mr. Schroder
stated the city should maintain this as a public service to the residents. Mr.
Feldhaus inquired as to whether the retention system was in the subdivision and
the condition of the system. Mr. Schroder informed council that the retention
area was not in the subdivision, but just outside the development and he
reported the system to be in good condition as the Planning Commission approved
it.
33.   There was a brief discussion surrounding the probability that the Kenton
County Sanitation District would assume maintenance of all storm water systems
within the next couple of years. At that point, the District will take over all
public easements, but it is uncertain if private property systems will be
addressed. Council advised Mr. Schroder to approach the Sanitation District
sometime in the future about taking over maintenance of this retention area.
Resolution No. 2000-R-17 – Approving the Payment of Monthly Expenses for the
Senior Center
34.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to read Resolution No. 2000-R-17 approving the
monthly CBDG fund expenses for the Senior Center. Mr. Ellison seconded the

5.   Mayor Kriege introduced a resolution for council’s consideration that
would show support for a regional skate park facility. He advised this effort
has been initiated by the Kenton County Mayors’ Group who have been researching
the development a skate park that would serve the entire area.
6.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to read Resolution No. 2000-R-18 supporting the
development of a regional skate park facility. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion.
A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Feldhaus voiced concern that if the city adopted
this resolution and the county chose a location within the city that did not
meet council’s approval, that it may leave the city with little recourse. Mayor
Kriege stated that by adopting this resolution the city would be supporting the
development of a skate park, not the design or location of the park. Mr.
Feldhaus stated that he felt it was premature to support this type facility as
it may have adverse affects. Mrs. Gabbard concurred with Mr. Feldhaus. Mr.
Steffen stated that if the skate park is located within an existing county park
then the city will not have any voice in the matter. Mayor Kriege stated the
possible locations include both public and private property. Mrs. Gabbard
stated she is in favor of exploring a regional skate park facility but is not
ready to offer her support at this time. Mr. Dupps stated if a skate park was
located in Independence that it would have to be located in an industrial area
as that is the only area zoned for such a development. Mayor Kriege advised
this type facility has been researched for the past year. He urged council to
show support of this effort. Mrs. Yeager reminded Mayor Kriege that a motion
was on the floor and asked that the vote be taken. Roll call vote was answered
with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Feldhaus. Motion carried 5-
1 and Mr. Walker read the proposed Resolution.
7.   Mr. Steffen made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 2000-R-18 supporting the
development of a regional skate park facility; seconded by Mr. Dupps. Roll call
was answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Feldhaus. Motion
carried 5-1 in favor.

DECEMBER 7, 2000
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Jim Ellison, Donna Yeager, Barbara Gabbard, Gregory Steffen and
Steve Feldhaus answered roll call. Eric Dupps was absent due to a conflict in
his schedule. Also in attendance was City Attorney. H. Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
§   Senior Center – Construction Bids
§   Justice Lane – Regarding Maintenance of the Street
§   Clover Ridge Subdivision – Stage II Development Plan
§   Administration/Police Facility – Preliminary Concept Design
Senior Center – Discussion Regarding the Project
3.   Mayor Kriege introduced Michael Robson of Moody/Nolan Architects. Mr.
Robson presented council with a bid summary and recommendation for the award of
the construction of the Senior Center. Mr. Robson stated that sealed bids were
received and opened on November 29, 2000 and of the eight bids received, the
three lowest bids were received from Mark Spaulding Construction ($827,300),
Hemmer Industries ($858,000) and Millay Construction ($859,100). Mr. Robson
informed council that the preliminary cost estimate for the project was
approximately $694,000.00. He stated that because the bids received were higher
than that estimate Moody/Nolan is recommending the city choose one of three
options available. He stated the first option (Option A) was to award the
contract to the low bidder (Mark Spaulding) at the proposed bid of $827,300.00,
as they believe that it is a fair price for this building. The second option
(Option B) suggested taking time to review the funding options and building
requirements then reconvene to decide whether to award the contract to the low
bidder. Mr. Robson advised the bid specifications allow the city forty-five
days following the day of the bid opening to give the successful bidder a
“notice of award.” This would give council until January 13, 2001 to award the
bid. Mr. Robson stated that the third option (Option C) would involve reviewing
the building plan and possibly reducing the square footage by at least 500
square feet. He stated this would reduce the overall cost of the project and
eliminate the need for a sprinkler system, in addition to removing any items
from the project, which could aid in cost reduction. Then the project could be
re-bid.
4.   Mr. Robson recommended that the city choose Option A thereby awarding to
the low bidder (Mark Spaulding Construction). Mr. Robson indicated that Option
B would allow the city more time while deciding the best course to take. Mr.
Robson also indicated that Mrs. Yeager and Mrs. Brake were looking into
additional funding to subsidize the difference in the estimated cost.
5.   Mayor Kriege stated that upon review of the three options he felt that
Option C would have an adverse effect as this is the second time bids have been
taken for this project. Mr. Robson interjected that the general contractors’
interest begins to wane for a second and third bid process. Mr. Robson stated
that cost estimates are difficult to predict early in a project due to the
changing market and that at this time they have a greater understanding of what
the market bears.
6.   Mr. Feldhaus asked if 500 square feet was eliminated what would be the
cost savings. Mayor Kriege advised that Bryan Kirby, grant administrator for
this project, has stated that the CBDG grant has restrictions that prohibit
downsizing of the building after the bids have been received in order to reach
the preliminary cost estimate of $694,000. Mr. Feldhaus asked if the grant had
restrictions on the size of the building and suggested reducing the size of the
building to offset the cost. Mr.Robson stated that the grant funds emphasized
the type of facility built, not the size of the facility. Mrs. Gabbard asked if
the city would loose the grant funds if the building size were reduced. Mr.
Robson replied no and went on to say that in order to arrive at the estimated
construction cost the building may need to be reduced by more than 500 square
feet. He informed council that reducing the size of the building was discussed
before the second bid process, and the consensus was to stay with the proposed
size, but to look at other features of the building to reduce the cost. He
stated that by reducing the building 500 square feet it would then become
unnecessary to install a sprinkler system thereby saving $23,000.
7.   A lengthy discussion ensued concerning ways to get the construction cost
closer to the budgeted amount. Mr. Ellison suggested reducing the square
footage to shave off $100,000. Mayor Kriege introduced the low bidder, Mark
Spaulding, and asked him if he could provide some insight. Mr. Spaulding stated
that he did not think it would be possible to get the cost down to $694,000
with the current design. Mayor Kriege stated that redesigning the building
would incur additional architect fees. Mrs. Yeager stated she was told the city
would not have to pay for redesign fees only for the re-bidding.
8.   Mr. Ellison expressed concern that the re-bidding could have been avoided
if they were told at the onset to keep the building under a certain size. Mrs.
Gabbard stated that while she likes the concept and favors a Senior Center, she
felt the entire project needed to be re-examined as the city only has a
budgeted amount to spend. Mayor Kriege stated that he did not think that 6500
square feet was too great and if the size of the building was reduced then the
city may be looking at expanding it in less than ten years. Mr. Robson
interjected that a sprinkler system is not required for buildings less than
6000 square feet and if the building was reduced in size now and an addition
was added at a later date the installation would be very disruptive to the
entire building.
9.   Mayor Kriege recommended that council choose Option B that would give the
city time to look at other options, seek additional funding and then reconvene
to make a decision later. Mrs. Yeager stated that the Senior Center Board of
Directors is seeking contributions and asked council to trust the Board would
obtain the additional funding and proceed with the project by choosing Option
A. Mrs. Gabbard stated the city has to be able to pay for this building. Mr.
Ellison stated that he favored choosing Option B or C.
10.   Mr. Spaulding assured council that he would help any way he could but
advised that the subcontractors may not be able to uphold their estimates on
this project if council takes the full forty-five days to award the bid. Mr.
Steffen commented that he felt the building should be built as designed in
order to address the future needs of the city.
11.   Mayor Kriege remarked on how much he appreciates the effort, passion and
dedication Mrs. Yeager has invested in the realization of a Senior Center, but
stated that he does not feel the city can commit to awarding this bid until we
have an understanding of all available resources. Mr. Feldhaus stated that he
felt the newly elected council members that take office in January should be
making this decision and voiced his opposition to awarding the contract. He
stated the new city officials will be the ones that will see this project
through to completion and they should look at the finances to see if additional
funds are available to cover the overrun.
12.   Mr. Ellison also expressed concern that the city could not afford the
proposed building. He stated the city has other needs to address and suggested
downsizing the Senior Center in order to proceed, then adding on to the
building as the city’s needs grow. He stated that he supported Mayor Kriege’s
recommendation that council choose Option B. Mrs. Gabbard concurred by stating
Option B would give the city time to look at the whole picture.
13.   Mr. Steffen stated he felt it was better to settle this matter now than
to delay the project until the new officials take office. Mr. Robson informed
council that by choosing Option B it would leave open Option C and/or Option A
as alternatives, if necessary.
14.   Mrs. Gabbard made a motion to accept the architect’s Option B
recommendation regarding the bids received for the Senior Center. Mr. Ellison
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and one no vote
cast by Mr. Feldhaus. Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
Justice Lane – Discussion Regarding Street Maintenance
15.   City Attorney, Lawson Walker addressed council about the maintenance of
Justice Lane. He provided some history about Ordinance No. 1-11-87 that
accepted Justice Lane as a city street for maintenance purposes as it presently
exists. Mr. Walker explained the ordinance was drafted for the sole purpose of
assisting a property owner in order to obtain a loan to build a house on the
street. He stated some of the residents of Justice Lane are requesting the city
maintain the street according to the ordinance. Mr. Walker informed council
that in researching this matter they have discovered the street was never
platted in order to be dedicated as a city street. He advised that Kentucky
statutes are very specific regarding procedures necessary to take ownership of
a street. He stated that since the city does not own the land it would be
necessary for the owner to donate the land or be willing to sell it to the
city. Mr. Walker offered two options to council. The first option would be to
have the city engineer survey the area that needs to be dedicated and get a
realtor appraisal, then offer to buy the land from the owner, if the owner
refuses, then exercise the city’s power of condemnation to acquire the land.
The second option would be for the city to prove there has been five years of
continuous use as an open street, which would probably end in a lawsuit. Mr.
Steffen commented the owner would probably argue it was permissive use.
16.   There was a brief discussion regarding ingress and egress for the
residents on Justice Lane. Mr. Walker stated he knows of only one owner that
has access limitations. Mrs. Gabbard stated all property owners have the one
access. It was also discussed as to whether or not the street is actually owned
by the resident that claims it. Mr. Ellison stated the resident has in his
possession survey blueprints that shows he owns the land. In that case, Mr.
Walker advised it would be necessary for the city engineer to get permission to
go onto private property to survey the area and if permission is not granted it
would be necessary to obtain a court order to go onto the property. Mr. Ellison
suggested asking Jed Deters to borrow the surveyor blueprints from the property
owner before going onto the land.
17.   Mrs. Yeager asked why the city was getting involved in this matter as she
felt this was a civil dispute between the property owners on Justice Lane. Mr.
Walker stated the property owners bought the land to develop knowing there was
only a private drive to access the land. Mayor Kriege stated there are property
owners concerns that the city needs to address. Mr. Walker suggested there are
potential claims against the city that would need to be discussed further in an
executive session.
Clover Ridge Subdivision – Stage II Development Plan
18.   Mr. Walker re-introduced the Stage II Development Plan for the Senour
Road subdivision known as Clover Ridge. He advised council that the Planning
Commission does not act when the plan is in compliance; they just announce the
plan as approved.
19.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to accept the recommendation of the Planning
Commission and approve the Stage II Development plan for the Clover Ridge
Subdivision. Mrs. Yeager seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with three
yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Steffen and Mr. Feldhaus. Motion carried
3-2 in favor.
Administration/Police Facility – Discussion of Preliminary Concept Design
20.   Mayor Kriege introduce Mark Gribler an architect whom he asked to submit
a proposal for a facility(s) for the Police and Administration Departments. Mr.
Gribler informed council that he had been working on the Senior Center project
as an employee of Moody/Nolan Ltd. but has recently parted company with the
firm. He assured council that he will continue to be available to assist with
the Senior Center project regardless of his relationship with Moody/Nolan Ltd.
21.   Mr. Gribler stated that his proposal for Police and Administration
facilities would involve a more prudent, systematic approach that would fulfill
the needs of the city. He stated he would perform an assessment study that
would take into consideration the city’s growth and he recommended a
construction firm be engaged to obtain cost estimates. He also suggested that
financing options be investigated. Mr. Gribler stated that when looking into
the facility review and assessment, proposals will include the following
options: two separate buildings (one for police and one for administration), a
new police building and/or the remodeling of the current administration
building.
22.   Mayor Kriege commented that the Senior Center did not have a schematic
plan, which he feels would have been advantageous. Mr. Gribler stated the
entire process might take up to twenty-four months.
23.   Mr. Feldhaus commented that he felt since the city has received the
Renaissance designation that the city offices should remain in the downtown
area and the city should look at existing buildings. He stated that he did not
think the city needed to build a multi-million-dollar building. Mr. Gribler
stated information would be compiled to see what is feasible. He assured Mr.
Feldhaus that considerations would be taken in regard to the Renaissance
Program and he would assist the city in attaining the silver status. Mrs.
Gabbard agreed that the city should look at all options and build what is
practical. Mayor Kriege commented that it would be helpful to have a
construction company assist before going forward. Mr. Ellison concurred with
Mr. Feldhaus that the city should look at existing properties in the downtown
area.
24.   Mayor Kriege urged council to move forward with this feasibility study as
presented by Mr. Gribler for a fee of $39,000. Mr. Feldhaus suggested the newly
elected council members taking office in January should look at the budget and
make this decision. Mrs. Gabbard stated she like the ideals presented by Mr.
Gribler but concurred with Mr. Feldhaus in that the new council should make
this decision. Mr. Ellison agreed and added the new council members may have
ideas they would like to present. Again, Mayor Kriege urged council’s approval
so that the process would not be delayed another month. Mr. Feldhaus stated he
did not want to start the process for a project the city may not be able to
afford.
25.   Mrs. Yeager made a motion to authorize Mayor Kriege to accept the
proposal submitted by Mr. Gribler to do a schematic design for a Police/
Administration building(s) for $39,000. Mr. Steffen seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with two yes votes and three no votes cast by Mr. Feldhaus,
Mr. Ellison and Mrs. Gabbard. Motion was defeated 3-2.
Adjournment
26.   Upon motion by Mr. Feldhaus and second by Mr. Ellison the meeting was
adjourned. Motion passed unanimously and the meeting adjourned at 9:40 p.m.

                        Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

CITY OF INDEPENDENCE

3.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve the minutes of the December 4, 2000

PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Kenton County Sheriff, Chuck Korzenborn, addressed council regarding
“Operation Grinch” which was a project of the Sheriff’s Department to clear up
outstanding warrants. He stated that with the help of the Independence Police
Department they were able to clear up 1900 warrants. Sheriff Korzenborn stated
that this was a highly confidential project kept secret until the last minute.
When he telephoned Chief Butler to request the assistance of Independence
police personnel, Chief Butler immediately gave a positive response. Sheriff
Korzenborn stated that his department will be glad to offer assistance to the
city any time and thanked the Independence Police Department for all their help
in making “Operation Grinch” such a success.
Holten Drive – Kent Howard, CEO Balluff Inc.
6.   Mayor Kriege stated that he and Jeff Smith have met with several
representatives of the businesses located on Holten Drive regarding some of the
concerns they have on city services. Mayor Kriege introduced Mr. Kent Howard,
President and CEO of Balluff Inc who addressed council regarding these
concerns.
7.   Mr. Howard advised the other businesses on Holten Drive include A.O.
Smith, Camco, The Discovery Channel and Appleton Papers. He stated that Mayor
Kriege and Jeff Smith have been helpful by listening to their concerns in an
effort to arrive at some solutions. Mr. Howard stated that two of the major
concerns is the condition of the street, which is in need of major repairs/
upgrades, and the addition of a traffic light and turn lane at the Holten/
Industrial Road intersection. He went on to say that the street was not
designed to support the heavy traffic of the trucks that now travel this road
on a daily basis. Another concern was the difficulty in existing Holten Drive,
as there is not a traffic light to regulate the flow. He stated that there is
sometimes a fifteen or twenty minute wait to get out onto Industrial Road. He
stated the businesses have tried staggered quitting times to alleviate this
problem to no avail. Mr. Howard stated he is aware Industrial Road is a state-
maintained street but would like the city’s assistance in requesting a traffic
light from the state for this intersection.
8.   Mr. Howard informed council that Balluff is looking into a possible
addition to their building but is also looking at the possibility of a location
with more accessibility.
9.   Mayor Kriege informed council that he has met twice with this business
group to start a dialogue. They are working on short term solutions while
addressing viable long-term solutions. He stated other issues that have been
discussed include services from the Fire/EMS Department, Police Department and
Public Works Department. Mayor Kriege stated he will continue to work toward
resolving their concerns and advised council these businesses would like a
commitment from council to move forward.
10.   Mr. Kudera asked if a cost has been estimated for the road repairs. Mayor
Kriege stated that the preliminary estimate for short-term road repairs is
$85,000 and long term repairs would run between $500,000 to $1,000,000.
11.   Mr. Ellison expressed concern that the Appleton Papers warehouse was
making a major contribution to the wear and tear of the road but not making a
significant contribution to the tax base. He indicated it would be appropriate
for that business to commit financial assistance for the major road repairs
that are needed. Mr. Ellison suggested that Mayor Kriege speak with
representatives of Appleton Papers regarding a possible road repairs
assessment. Mr. Howard commented that the business owners have not ruled out
possible contributions to get this street repaired. Mr. Gabbard agreed that the
city needed to work with the business owners to obtain financial assistance to
solve this matter.
12.   There was a brief discussion regarding a possible turn lane and traffic
signal at that intersection. Mayor Kriege stated that permits would need to be
obtained from the state for a turn lane. Mr. Dupps stated that historically the
city has not been successful getting traffic signals on state roads that run
through the city. He asked Chief Butler to obtain the necessary traffic data so
that he city will have a stronger case when making the request. Mayor Kriege
instructed Chief Butler to record the busiest times of the workday. Mr.
Moriconi asked if the proposal for repairs was for 1000 feet. Mr. Howard stated
the proposal was for repairs of the entire street but indicated that the back
half of the street was in better condition than the front half.
13.   Mayor Kriege advised council the city needs to plan to include the cost
of these repairs in the next fiscal year (2001-2002) budget.
OLD BUSINESS
Senior Center – Moody/Nolan Architects – Michael Robson and Mark Spaulding
14.   Mayor Kriege introduced Michael Robson and Mark Spaulding from Moody/
Nolan Architects. Mayor Kriege gave a brief update to council of the Building
Committee meeting held at 5:00 p.m. before this meeting. He stated the
committee discussed financing the Senior Center for ten years and obtaining a
one-year construction loan.
15.   Mr. Robson reviewed the Senior Center project proposal that was presented
to the outgoing council at the December 7, 2000 special council meeting. He
advised the project was originally budgeted at $694,000 and that the lowest bid
received from the first Notice of Bids was well over $1,000,000. Since the bids
received were over the estimated budget, he stated that it was decided to put
the bid out a second time wherein the contractor could bid a base price for
construction of the building and bid separately on the optional features (deck,
canopies, roofing, kitchen equipment, lighting). Mr. Robson stated the low bid
received and opened on November 29, 2001 was for $827,300 from Mark Spaulding
Construction. He stated that the opinion of Moody/Nolan Architects is that this
is a fair market price for the building.
16.   Mr. Robson presented three options to council:
§   Option A – Award the bid to Mark Spaulding Construction as the low bid for
$827,300. He advised the bid specifications allowed the city forty-five days
following the bid opening to give the successful bidder a “notice of award.” He
stated that forty-five day deadline is January 13, 2001.
§   Option B – Take time to review the funding options and building
requirements then reconvene to make a decision about awarding the bid. He
stated the outgoing council at the December special meeting chose this Option.
Since that time additional funding has been obtained; Kenton Council Fiscal
Court has committed $200,000 to the project.
§   Option C – Review the building plan and possibly reduce the square footage
by at least 500 square feet and eliminate items from the project which would
aid in the cost reduction. Then the project could be re-bid.
Mr. Robson advised council that the deadline for awarding the bid is
approaching this Friday. He recommended awarding the low bid to Mark Spaulding
Construction for the base amount of $827,300 and include Alternate No. 1 for
the construction of the deck for $53,268 for a total of $880,568.00.
17.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to award the bid for the construction of the
Senior Center to Mark Spaulding Construction for $827,300 plus the additional
cost of $53,268 for the deck. Mr. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call vote
was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
18.   Mayor Kriege informed Mr. Spaulding he necessary documents would be
completed by Friday.
