Executive Order – Appointing Chris Moriconi as Vice Mayor
51.   Mayor Kriege introduced an Executive Order to appoint Council Member,
Chris Moriconi as Vice-Mayor, which he asked Mr. Walker to read.
52.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve Executive Order No. 2001-EO-01
appointing Chris Moriconi as Vice Mayor. Mr. Bushong seconded the motion. A
brief discussion ensued.
53.   Mr. Gabbard expressed his objection to this Executive Order. He stated he
spoke with Bill Thielen, legal counsel with the Kentucky League of Cities, who
advised that many powers of the mayor could not be delegated to a council
member. Mr. Gabbard also stated there have been several Attorney General
Opinions on this matter. Mr. Kudera expressed his approval of designating a
Vice-Mayor in case of an emergency. Mr. Ellison stated that he thinks Mr.
Gabbard’s objection is with the term ‘vice-mayor’ and not the appointment. Mr.
Gabbard stated that the mayor could not delegate authority to a council member
because council members are not subordinate to the mayor. He stated the
Executive Order should be more specific in the duties to be carried out by a
vice-mayor. Mayor Kriege stated that he might not always be available to
perform ceremonial events, etc. In closing, Mayor Kriege stated the Executive
Order specifically states the vice-mayor appointment only “delegates those
duties, power and responsibilities as permitted by the statutory provisions”.
54.   At this time, roll call vote was taken. Roll call was answered with three
yes votes and one abstain by Mr. Moriconi and one pass vote cast by Mr. Gabbard
for reasons stated. Mayor Kriege voted yes. Motion carried 4-1-1 in favor.

JANUARY 22, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. Jim Bushong,
Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered
roll call. Also in attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion of approving an Executive Order to appoint Mark Wendling as City
Administrator. He asked for a motion and second then he would open the floor
for discussion. Mr. Gabbard requested that he be given the opportunity to ask
Mr. Wendling some questions since he missed the special meeting of council on
January 13, 2001, at which time the candidates were interviewed. Mayor Kriege
stated that it would be necessary to enter an executive session.
Executive Session
3.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to enter executive session in accordance with
K.R.S. 61.810 (f). Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with
three yes votes and three no votes cast by Mr. Kudera, Mr. Moriconi and Mr.
Bushong. Mayor Kriege broke the tie with a yes vote. Motion carried 4-3 in
favor.
4.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Ellison the council went back
to the regular session. Motion carried with all ayes.
Review of Proposed Contract for City Administrator
5.   Mr. Gabbard requested a moment to review the changes made to the final
copy of the proposed contract with Mr. Wendling.
6.   Mr. Ellison referred to page two, section three regarding suspension and
asked if past employees had been afforded a hearing. Mayor Kriege stated that
wording has been deleted in the revised copy of the contact attached to the
Executive Order.
7.   Mr. Gabbard referred to section four regarding termination and severance
pay that afforded the city administrator four months’ salary and health
insurance upon termination for reasons other than just cause. He stated that he
believes the Kentucky Constitution and Attorney General Opinions would render
this an illegal provision. Mayor Kriege stated that would be reviewed and if
found to be in violation, the section would be renegotiated. Mr. Walker advised
the section of the Constitution that Mr. Gabbard referred to prohibit the
payment for lack of services. He went on to say that he understands the intent
of that but he does not believe there has ever been a case involving severance
pay. He mentioned several local cities and agencies that provide 4-6 months
severance pay in their administrator’s contract, if terminated for lack of
cause. Mr. Walker stated there is no consideration for the severance at the end
of the term.
8.   Mr. Bushong asked what council’s role was with regard to the appointment
of the City Administrator. He wondered if it was council’s job to dissect the
contract. Mr. Walker stated that the city is operating under K.R.S 83A wherein
the mayor has the authority to nominate this candidate, while the statute
requires the council’s approval of the hiring. He stated that his experience
with other cities, agencies and governments recognized council’s input into the
terms of the contract, as it is part of the budget, and they certainly have the
right to make inquires, but it is not council’s job to negotiate the contract.
9.   Mr. Gabbard concurred that council should have the right to make inquiries
of the contract as well as the citizens. Mr. Walker confirmed that Mr.
Bushong’s understanding was accurate in that council’s role was to approve or
disapprove the hiring and the contract is for the mayor to negotiate. Mr.
Bushong stated that he was not disagreeing with the right to ask questions but
that he just wanted to know if the contract negotiation was their function. Mr.
Ellison stated that he did not want to vote on an issue where he did not
understand the contract and wanted the opportunity to ask questions.
10.   Mr. Ellison questioned the term “exclusive use” under section ten
relating to the use of a city car and asked that the wording be changed to
“official city business”. Mayor Kriege stated the section reads “in accordance
with city policy” which should be adequate. He stated the vehicles could not be
used for personal vacations, etc. Mr. Gabbard asked if a policy has been
established on city vehicles. The City Clerk responded that the Personnel
Policy has a very brief reference to city vehicles under section five (11)
regarding travel wherein it states “use of privately owned vehicles is
discouraged city vehicles should be used whenever possible.” Mayor Kriege
stated this probably needs to be reviewed as the last city administrator had no
guidelines regarding the use of the city vehicle and suggested the Personnel
Committee look into amending this section of the Personnel Policy.
11.   Mr. Gabbard suggested that before hiring Mr. Wendling two things need to
be accomplished. First, the probationary clause of the Personnel Policy which
requires all employees, regardless of position, to pass a six month
probationary period, needs to be amended if it is going to be waived for Mr.
Wending. Secondly, he felt it would be necessary to amend the budget ordinance
to reflect the adjustment of the administrator’s salary.
12.   Mr. Moriconi commented that the six-month probationary clause might apply
automatically since it is not specifically addressed in the contract.
13.   Mayor Kriege stated a first reading of the Pay Plan Ordinance was
conducted at the January 8, 2001 council meeting. Mr. Gabbard stated that is
the Pay and Classification Plan and does not set forth the money in the budget.
Mayor Kriege stated the money is in the budget to accommodate the proposed
salary for Mr. Wendling. Mr. Ellison stated that as long as the city has not
exceeded the total amount set aside for salaries in the budget then we are
within the law. Mayor Kriege stated the city administrator salary expenditures
are currently at 41% of the budgeted amount. Mr. Kudera stated that it could
not be approved if this was the start of the fiscal year because it would be
$58,000 versus $51,000 and would exceed the budgeted amount. Mr. Gabbard
asserted that it was his belief these changes had to be made first.
14.   Mr. Walker advised that the city has not adopted an itemized budget. He
stated there is no legal budget for the city that lists the administrator’s
salary. He went on to say the $51,000 city administrator salary is not a legal
number, as it has never been published. He stated the legal ordinance lists the
summary totals for each department and that amount is lumped into the
administration summary. He went on to explain why budgets are adopted in this
manner; specifically so that city’s would not have to pay costly legal
publishing expenses. Mr. Walker also stated that if budgets were adopted in a
line item format, the city would be amending the budget month in and month out.
Budget amendments would jam up the council agendas as well as expending city
funds to publish each amendment. He stated a legal budget only is required to
state the proposed income and expenses; it does not have to be broken down into
individual line items. Mr. Walker stated the current dollar amount in the
budget shows the estimated expense to run the entire administration department
and that no individual employee’s salary is singled out in the legal budget
ordinance adopted by the city.
15.   Mr. Gabbard questioned section thirteen that pertains to the use of a
cell telephone provided by the city. He suggested there be a cap on the use for
personal calls. Mayor Kriege advised that section thirteen states “in
accordance with city policy” and cell phone use is addressed in the Personnel
Policy by stating that the phone may be used for non-business calls but the
employee must reimburse the city for those calls.
16.   Mr. Gabbard brought up the use of a city vehicle and wanted to know if
the city had a policy to use as a guideline. Mayor Kriege stated the city has
not adopted a policy but would be a good idea to look into this. Mr. Walker
stated that police and fire is exempt but that civilian employees that have an
assigned city vehicle are required to pay a personal use tax. Mr. Kudera stated
he thinks the cap is set by the IRS. Mr. Gabbard also objected to the phrase
“exclusive use” and requested this section be reworded.
17.   Mr. Dupps requested that section nine include “of the Mayor” at the end
of the paragraph. Mayor Kriege concurred.
18.   Mr. Gabbard questioned section eight regarding hours of work and the use
of compensatory time off. He stated that the CAO, as an exempt employee, does
not get comp time according to the Labor Cabinet. Shawn Butler, Chief of
Police, interjected that the Police Chief’s Association had speakers from both
the State and Federal Department of Labor address their organization at the
December meeting. He advised there have been changes to this that permit the
employer to allow comp time.
19.   Mr. Gabbard had several questions on page four of the proposed contract
regarding professional development, general expenses and civic club membership.
He expressed concern that these sections were too broad in nature and suggested
a limitation be set for these expenses. Mayor Kriege advised that continued
professional training was considered standard expenses for a city to keep staff
well trained. Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Kudera concurred. Mayor Kriege went on to
say that these expenses were budgeted for the previous city administrator as
well as other staff members.
20.   Mr. Ellison asked for an explanation of Section eighteen regarding civic
club memberships. Mayor Kriege stated these would be for local organizations
such as the Chamber of Commerce. Mr. Ellison stated that is covered in section
fifteen and asked that section eighteen be deleted as it sounds as if the city
is buying into a membership to a golf course. Mayor Kriege advised it would be
taken into consideration.
21.   Mayor Kriege permitted several audience members to make comments. One
comment questioned the length of the proposed contract for the city
administrator. Mayor Kriege assured everyone that a contract has become a
necessary tool as an incentive for employment in a political climate where job
security is unpredictable because of changing elected administrations. Mr.
Walker advised that under the terms of the proposed contract the administrator
could still be terminated for cause in which case he would not receive the
severance benefits.
Executive Order No. 2001-EO-02 Appointing Mark T. Wendling as City
Administrator
22.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve Executive Order No. 2001-EO-02
appointing Mark T. Wendling as City Administrator. Mr. Moriconi seconded the
motion. Mr. Walker read the Executive Order.
23.   A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Ellison stated that he thought a hiring
was done by ordinance. Mr. Walker stated that he has seen it done both ways; by
ordinance or executive order. He advised that the Mayor has the authority to
make an appointment, but in accordance with state statute, the appointment has
to be approved by the council. Mr. Gabbard argued that the Mayor does not have
the authority to hire the city administrator under an Executive Order but that
the hiring should be by Municipal Order, as it requires council’s approval. Mr.
Walker disagreed, as it would still require that the Mayor make the appointment
by an Executive Order because the hiring/firing of employees is an executive
duty of the mayor.
24.   Mr. Ellison called for the question to the motion. Roll call on the
motion and second to approve Executive Order No. 2001-EO-02 yielded five yes
votes and one abstain cast by Mr. Gabbard. Mr. Gabbard clarified his vote by
stating he felt the hiring of the city administrator should be done by
Municipal Order not by an Executive Order. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
Municipal Order No. 2001-MO-02 Appointing Mark T. Wendling as City
Administrator
25.   After a brief discussion, Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve Municipal
Order No. 2001-MO-02 appointing Mark T. Wendling as City Administrator. Mr.
Ellison seconded the motion. Mr. Walker read the Municipal Order. Roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Adjournment
26.   Upon motion by Mr. Gabbard and second by Mr. Kudera the meeting was
adjourned at 8:15 p.m. Motion carried with all ayes.

Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
FEBRUARY 5, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES

1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty from the Independence Christian Church
gave the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Kudera, and
Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Council Member Jim Ellison was unable to
attend due to his obligation at work and Council Member, Ike Gabbard was out of
town on vacation. Also in attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege presented a plaque of recognition to Don Bridges, who
recently resigned as a member of the Board of Adjustments. Mayor Kriege thanked
Mr. Bridges for his many years of service on this Board.
Approval of the Minutes of the January 8, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to accept the minutes of the regular Council
Meeting of January 8, 2001 as presented. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 4-0 in favor.

Meeting of January 22, 2001 as submitted. Mr. Bushong seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 4-0 in favor.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
Donation for Easter Egg Hunt
6.   Ms. Karen Nitschke, Secretary of the Independence Lions Club, addressed
council about the annual Easter Egg Hunt. She stated the hunt would be held on
April 8 at Memorial Park. She also stated the event attracted over two hundred
children last year. She informed council the city donated $700.00 last year and
asked them to consider increasing the donation to $1,000, as they ran short of
prizes last year.
7.   Mr. Dupps asked if other organizations were asked to contribute to this

contributing this year. She stated the Lions may be able to contribute $100 and
the Leos may hold a raffle as a service project to help raise funds to defray
the cost.
8.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to donate $850 to the annual Easter Egg Hunt
seconded by Mr. Kudera. Roll call was answered with four yes votes. Motion
carried 4-0 in favor.
Discussion of the Independence Towne Center (Specifically the Madison Pike Turn
Lane)
9.   Mr. Charles Deters addressed council regarding the construction of a turn
lane on Madison Pike, a condition imposed when the Planning Commission approved
the Towne Center’s site plan. He informed council that this condition was based
on the results of a traffic impact analysis study that was made several years
ago. The study recommended a turn lane be constructed to alleviate traffic in
the area. He stated that according to Section I (c) of Ordinance No.1996-O-18
“the roadway improvement as recommended by Pflum, Klausmeier & Gehrum
Consultants dated August 14, 1996 be constructed prior to, or simultaneous
with, the construction of either the proposed commercial development or the
proposed residential development which is a part of this review, whichever is
developed first.”
10.   Mr. Deters stated the he and the Planning Commission have differing
opinions of the interpretation of this ordinance, most specifically with “prior
to, or simultaneously with, the construction of either the proposed commercial
development or the proposed residential development…. whichever is developed
first.” Mr. Deters stated that this difference of opinion has recently
escalated as the Planning Commission is refusing to approve zoning permits for
further development until the roadway improvements are made. Mr. Deters stated
that he feels the Planning Commission is being arbitrary with no objective
criteria on which to base their decision. He questioned the Planning
Commission’s decision to require the construction of the road improvements when
the development is only 35% complete. Mr. Deters went on to say that a current
traffic impact study was to be completed by now and this new data could result
in opposing recommendations for that stretch of roadway. Mr. Deters stated that
when the city did not require immediate development of the turn lane he assumed
the city’s position was that the roadway improvements should be made when the
commercial construction was complete. In closing, Mr. Deters stated that he has
come before council to ask that they provide an interpretation of Section 1(c)
of Ordinance No. 1996-O-18.
11.   Mayor Kriege asked Scott Hiles, Planning Engineer with Northern Kentucky
Area Planning Commission to respond to Mr. Deters statements. Mr. Hiles
concurred that the Planning Commission staff and Mr. Deters disagree on the
interpretation of some of the wording in the ordinance. He feels that Mr.
Deters is interpreting the word “developed” as “finished” and the intention of
the Planning Commission was that the road improvements be constructed “prior to
or simultaneously with the development.” Mr. Hiles went on to say that the
Planning Commission’s standpoint is that the condition is not being met,
therefore they denied Fifth Third Bank’s request for zoning/building permits.
He stated the Planning Commission anticipated the roadway would be improved
before Kroger’s opened for business. Mr. Hiles stated the NKAP Commission staff
decided that it was time to require the Independence Towne Center to comply
with the roadway improvement condition by requesting a bond for the final road
development before additional permits would be issued. Mr. Deters stated that
two years ago he posted a $125,000 bond for this intersection.
12.   A lengthy discussion ensued. Mr. Deters emphasized the importance of a
new traffic study as the reconstruction of Route 17 will completely bypass the
Towne Center making the original study meaningless. He states this is another
reason he is reluctant to begin the road improvements until the study is
completed. Mr. Hiles stated their decision was based on the 1996 study and that
traffic in the area has increased considerably since then.
13.   Mr. Walker, City Attorney considered the opposing statements from Mr.
Deters and Mr. Hiles and advised that it was his opinion that Mr. Deters appeal
should be presented to the city’s Board of Adjustment for a ruling on the
interpretation of Ordinance No. 1996-O-18. He advised that council could not
interpret it’s own legislation. He went on to say that council could bypass the
Board of Adjustment and rule on this, but he advised against doing this, as it
is not proper procedure. Mr. Walker stated that if the Board of Adjustment
denies Mr. Deters’ appeal that it may come back to council for a ruling anyway.
14.   Mr. Kudera commented that it was apparent there is an arbitrary conflict
between this developer and the Planning Commission and suggested the matter be
resolved so that development can move forward. He expressed concern that Mr.
Deters has a significant amount of money tied up in the Towne Center and the
need to get answers to the questions asked tonight.
15.   Mr. Moriconi wondered what percent of the development needed to be
complete in order to comply with the word “simultaneous.” He asked Mr. Hiles
what prompted the Planning Commission to enforce the road improvement at this
time. Mr. Hiles responded that the Planning Commission was promised the
condition would be met in 1999 and it was not. He stated they are not trying to
be obstinate, just trying to look out for public safety and they feel the time
has come to enforce this condition.
16.   Mayor Kriege commented that he feels the language used in the ordinance
is “wide-open” and pointed out that, the wording in the ordinance was taken
from the Planning Commission’s recommendation on approving the site plan for
the Towne Center. He felt it was going to be difficult to interpret the word
“simultaneous.” Mayor Kriege stated that he felt the Planning Commission is
acting in good faith but expressed concern that this dispute is holding up
development at the Towne Center.
17.   Council Member, Mr. Bushong concurred and added that holding up zoning/
building permits is penalizing the city and is counterproductive. Mr. Deters
stated it took three months to get an approval for the Courthouse Restaurant.
18.   Mr. Walker advised that it was in everyone’s best interest to arrive at a
solution, in an effort to circumvent lengthy delays caused by an appeal to the
Board of Adjustment and the possibility of this matter ending up in Circuit
Court. He stated that if there are other relevant factors, they should be
considered and then Mr. Deters should commit to a dead line to making the road
improvements.
19.   Mr. Deters reiterated that he felt it was necessary to wait for the
results of the new traffic analysis study and expressed concern on predicting
the final positioning of Route 17 after the reconstruction is complete. In
addition, he advised it would cost a third of a million dollars to relocate
utility lines, an expense he did not want to incur needlessly. He stated that
the relocation of Route 17 was going to have a tremendous impact to the city of
Independence. He also informed council that he had applied to the state for a
traffic light at the corner of Declaration Drive and Roue 17 and was denied. In
closing, Mr. Deters expressed his concern that future development at the Towne
Center would be prohibited by the Planning Commission unless the road
improvements are made immediately.
20.   Mayor Kriege stated that he is willing to sit down with Mr. Deters and
the Planning Commission representatives in an effort to get a time frame for
this matter to be resolved. He indicated he would inquire on the status of the
recent traffic study conducted. It was decided that Mr. Walker would schedule a
meeting with all parties involved.
OLD BUSINESS

FEBRUARY 5, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty from the Independence Christian Church
gave the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Kudera, and

PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
Donation for Easter Egg Hunt
6.   Ms. Karen Nitschke, Secretary of the Independence Lions Club, addressed
council about the annual Easter Egg Hunt. She stated the hunt would be held on
April 8 at Memorial Park. She also stated the event attracted over two hundred
children last year. She informed council the city donated $700.00 last year and
asked them to consider increasing the donation to $1,000, as they ran short of
prizes last year.
7.   Mr. Dupps asked if other organizations were asked to contribute to this

the cost.
8.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to donate $850 to the annual Easter Egg Hunt
seconded by Mr. Kudera. Roll call was answered with four yes votes. Motion
carried 4-0 in favor.
Discussion of the Independence Towne Center (Specifically the Madison Pike Turn
Lane)
9.   Mr. Charles Deters addressed council regarding the construction of a turn
lane on Madison Pike, a condition imposed when the Planning Commission approved
the Towne Center’s site plan. He informed council that this condition was based
on the results of a traffic impact analysis study that was made several years
ago. The study recommended a turn lane be constructed to alleviate traffic in
the area. He stated that according to Section I (c) of Ordinance No.1996-O-18
“the roadway improvement as recommended by Pflum, Klausmeier & Gehrum
Consultants dated August 14, 1996 be constructed prior to, or simultaneous
with, the construction of either the proposed commercial development or the
proposed residential development which is a part of this review, whichever is
developed first.”
10.   Mr. Deters stated the he and the Planning Commission have differing
opinions of the interpretation of this ordinance, most specifically with “prior
to, or simultaneously with, the construction of either the proposed commercial
development or the proposed residential development…. whichever is developed
first.” Mr. Deters stated that this difference of opinion has recently
escalated as the Planning Commission is refusing to approve zoning permits for
further development until the roadway improvements are made. Mr. Deters stated
that he feels the Planning Commission is being arbitrary with no objective
criteria on which to base their decision. He questioned the Planning
Commission’s decision to require the construction of the road improvements when
the development is only 35% complete. Mr. Deters went on to say that a current
traffic impact study was to be completed by now and this new data could result
in opposing recommendations for that stretch of roadway. Mr. Deters stated that
when the city did not require immediate development of the turn lane he assumed
the city’s position was that the roadway improvements should be made when the
commercial construction was complete. In closing, Mr. Deters stated that he has
come before council to ask that they provide an interpretation of Section 1(c)
of Ordinance No. 1996-O-18.
11.   Mayor Kriege asked Scott Hiles, Planning Engineer with Northern Kentucky
Area Planning Commission to respond to Mr. Deters statements. Mr. Hiles
concurred that the Planning Commission staff and Mr. Deters disagree on the
interpretation of some of the wording in the ordinance. He feels that Mr.
Deters is interpreting the word “developed” as “finished” and the intention of
the Planning Commission was that the road improvements be constructed “prior to
or simultaneously with the development.” Mr. Hiles went on to say that the
Planning Commission’s standpoint is that the condition is not being met,
therefore they denied Fifth Third Bank’s request for zoning/building permits.
He stated the Planning Commission anticipated the roadway would be improved
before Kroger’s opened for business. Mr. Hiles stated the NKAP Commission staff
decided that it was time to require the Independence Towne Center to comply
with the roadway improvement condition by requesting a bond for the final road
development before additional permits would be issued. Mr. Deters stated that
two years ago he posted a $125,000 bond for this intersection.
12.   A lengthy discussion ensued. Mr. Deters emphasized the importance of a
new traffic study as the reconstruction of Route 17 will completely bypass the
Towne Center making the original study meaningless. He states this is another
reason he is reluctant to begin the road improvements until the study is
completed. Mr. Hiles stated their decision was based on the 1996 study and that
traffic in the area has increased considerably since then.
13.   Mr. Walker, City Attorney considered the opposing statements from Mr.
Deters and Mr. Hiles and advised that it was his opinion that Mr. Deters appeal
should be presented to the city’s Board of Adjustment for a ruling on the
interpretation of Ordinance No. 1996-O-18. He advised that council could not
interpret it’s own legislation. He went on to say that council could bypass the
Board of Adjustment and rule on this, but he advised against doing this, as it
is not proper procedure. Mr. Walker stated that if the Board of Adjustment
denies Mr. Deters’ appeal that it may come back to council for a ruling anyway.
14.   Mr. Kudera commented that it was apparent there is an arbitrary conflict
between this developer and the Planning Commission and suggested the matter be
resolved so that development can move forward. He expressed concern that Mr.
Deters has a significant amount of money tied up in the Towne Center and the
need to get answers to the questions asked tonight.
15.   Mr. Moriconi wondered what percent of the development needed to be
complete in order to comply with the word “simultaneous.” He asked Mr. Hiles
what prompted the Planning Commission to enforce the road improvement at this
time. Mr. Hiles responded that the Planning Commission was promised the
condition would be met in 1999 and it was not. He stated they are not trying to
be obstinate, just trying to look out for public safety and they feel the time
has come to enforce this condition.
16.   Mayor Kriege commented that he feels the language used in the ordinance
is “wide-open” and pointed out that, the wording in the ordinance was taken
from the Planning Commission’s recommendation on approving the site plan for
the Towne Center. He felt it was going to be difficult to interpret the word
“simultaneous.” Mayor Kriege stated that he felt the Planning Commission is
acting in good faith but expressed concern that this dispute is holding up
development at the Towne Center.
17.   Council Member, Mr. Bushong concurred and added that holding up zoning/
building permits is penalizing the city and is counterproductive. Mr. Deters
stated it took three months to get an approval for the Courthouse Restaurant.
18.   Mr. Walker advised that it was in everyone’s best interest to arrive at a
solution, in an effort to circumvent lengthy delays caused by an appeal to the
Board of Adjustment and the possibility of this matter ending up in Circuit
Court. He stated that if there are other relevant factors, they should be
considered and then Mr. Deters should commit to a dead line to making the road
improvements.
19.   Mr. Deters reiterated that he felt it was necessary to wait for the
results of the new traffic analysis study and expressed concern on predicting
the final positioning of Route 17 after the reconstruction is complete. In
addition, he advised it would cost a third of a million dollars to relocate
utility lines, an expense he did not want to incur needlessly. He stated that
the relocation of Route 17 was going to have a tremendous impact to the city of
Independence. He also informed council that he had applied to the state for a
traffic light at the corner of Declaration Drive and Roue 17 and was denied. In
closing, Mr. Deters expressed his concern that future development at the Towne
Center would be prohibited by the Planning Commission unless the road
improvements are made immediately.
20.   Mayor Kriege stated that he is willing to sit down with Mr. Deters and
the Planning Commission representatives in an effort to get a time frame for
this matter to be resolved. He indicated he would inquire on the status of the
recent traffic study conducted. It was decided that Mr. Walker would schedule a
meeting with all parties involved.

CITY OF INDEPENDENCE

Allegiance. Reverend Kent Allender from Nicholson Christian Church gave the
invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard,
Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance was City
Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.

2.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to accept the minutes of the regular Council
Meeting of February 5, 2001 as submitted. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion.
Roll call was answered with four ayes. Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard chose to
pass, as they were both absent from that meeting. Motion carried 4-0 in favor.
Oath of Office – New Patrol Officer, Bryan Wells
3.   Mayor Kriege administered the Oath of Office to Bryan Wells. Mayor Kriege
stated Mr. Wells would begin work with the city on March 8, 2001 as a patrol
officer in the Police Department.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
Doug Sloan, 795 Cox Road
4.   Mr. Sloan addressed council about the recent zoning violation notice he
has received regarding the vehicles he has parked on his property. He stated he
has been working with Mr. McAllister to meet compliance requirements and
currently has moved the cars to the rear of his property, but according to Mr.
McAllister is still in violation. Mr. Sloan voiced his objection to other
properties throughout the city that have similar violations that have gone
unnoticed by the city. Mr. Sloan also criticized the lack of dog control
enforcement. He reported there are many dogs running at large in his
neighborhood and was concerned about the safety of his child and others.
5.   Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Sloan the council would not be able to solve his
concerns at this meeting but asked that he meet with the City Administrator and
Mr. McAllister to work on a solution. He stated that it sounds as if progress
is being made on his zoning compliance and advised Mr. Sloan to provide the
city with addresses of other properties that are in violation of the zoning
laws so that the owners can be notified.
Bill Miller, 4394 Oliver Road
6.   Mr. Miller addressed council regarding the mention in today’s Kentucky
Post that council would be proposing an increase in taxes. He reminded council
that some of them had voiced opposition to a tax increase at the Candidates
Forum last fall when they were running for office. He stated he would like to
see the city implement a reduction in expenses before resorting to a tax
increase. He expressed concern for the many senior citizens on fixed incomes,
for which a tax increase would be a hardship.
7.   Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Miller that the discussion regarding tax
increases was removed from tonight’s agenda as he would rather hold a couple of
public hearings in April for the sole purpose of discussing this issue. He
stated that residents would be encouraged to present council their thoughts and
suggestions regarding the revenue and expense concerns that are currently
facing the city. He also advised Mr. Miller that the City of Independence has
one of the lowest property tax rates in Northern Kentucky. Mr. Miller stated
that he felt it should not be necessary to raise property tax rates with
twenty-two subdivisions currently under construction.
8.   Mr. Gabbard stated he would not vote for the insurance premium tax, as he
believes the city needs to cut expenses first. He stated if it was necessary to
raise taxes that it should be in a small way, if needed, and only after the
city has tightened its belt.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-01 Enacting a Personnel and Pay Classification Plan
9.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance No. 2001-O-
01 enacting an employee pay and classification plan for the city. Mr. Kudera
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with six ayes; motion carried 6-
0 in favor.

Project Prom Donation – Simon Kenton High School
12.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Ellison, a donation of
$500.00 was approved to Simon Kenton High School’s Project Prom. Roll call was
answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Proposed Resolution to Bond the Senior Center
13.   Mayor Kriege presented a resolution that would approve a bond for the
financing of the Senior Center. Mr. Gabbard asked what the amount of the bond
was and requested the amount be included in the resolution. Mayor Kriege stated
it was between $400,000 and $500,000 and would be bonded for a ten-year period.
He advised council of the need to begin the bond process for this project as
construction would begin next week. He advised council the city would not
borrow more than the necessary amount. Mayor Kriege reminded council the CBDG
grant was $270,000 and that the Kenton County Fiscal Court contributed $200,000
for a total of $470,000. He went on to say with the total cost of the
construction awarded for $887,000 that would leave about $410,000 to bond.
14.   Mr. Gabbard reiterated that he felt the exact amount of the bond should
be included in the resolution adopted by council. Mr. Bushong concurred that
council should know the exact amount of this bond. He also asked if there was a
possibility to get the state legislature to release the $200,000 donation for
the amphitheater for transfer of those funds to the Senior Center project.
Mayor Kriege replied that with only four days left in the General Session that
it seemed unlikely.
15.   Mrs. Guenther, Finance Director, advised council that a ten-year loan
would be obtained from the Kentucky League of Cities at an interest rate of
4.18% for approximately $500,000. She advised the city has paid architect fees
which were not payable with the CBDG grant funds. Mayor Kriege stated the
architect fees were paid from budgeted money in the Building Fund. Mrs.
Guenther stated the average annual payment for the bond would be $63,000 as
each year the payment will decrease. Mayor Kriege advised council that the
Danville Bond Pool through the Kentucky League of Cities, by far, had the
lowest interest rate at 4.18% compared to area banks offering a 6% rate.
16.   Mr. Ellison asked when the first bond payment would be due. Mayor Kriege
replied the first payment would be due in June 2001. Mr. Ellison also asked if
the money taken from the Building Fund to pay the architect fees would be
reimbursed to the Building Fund. Mayor Kriege stated that it would not, as that
would just be more money that would have to be borrowed.
17.   Mr. Moriconi stated that he did not want to hold up the project while
waiting on an exact bond amount for the resolution. Mrs. Guenther assured
council the city would not find a lower interest rate than the 4.18%; a
variable rate the city can lock into at any time without a penalty. Mr. Bushong
stated the city should not write an interest rate in the resolution as it is
something we have no control over.
18.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to enter into a contract with the Kentucky
League of Cities to bond the Senior Center for approximately $450,000 at a rate
not to exceed 4.5% for a period of ten years. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion.
Roll call was answered with six yeas. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Application for a Zoning Text Amendment with Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission
19.   Upon recommendation of the Planning & Zoning Committee, Mr. Barbian,
Building Inspector, introduced a proposed zoning text amendment that would
change the wording of the section of the zoning ordinance pertaining to
accessory structures. He stated a recent permit request for an accessory
structure to be placed in a front yard has prompted this amendment as the
current zoning ordinance permits structures in the front yards. Mr. Barbian
reported that the Planning & Zoning Committee feels that allowing accessory
structures in the front yard is aesthetically objectionable. He went on to say
that the committee has met with Mike Schwartz of the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning & Zoning Commission to discuss this re-wording. Mr. Barbian stated
that this text amendment would prohibit accessory structures, such as swimming
pools and storage sheds from being located in front yards. The proposed re-
wording was submitted to council for their approval.
20.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to submit the proposed zoning text amendment
regarding accessory structures to the Northern Kentucky Area Planning & Zoning
Commission for approval. Mr. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with six ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Facility(s) Feasibility Study
21.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to approve that Matrix Architects conduct a
facility(s) feasibility study for $27,000. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. A
brief discussion ensued. Mayor Kriege advised this proposal would include
programming and facility assessment along with the schematics, budget and
schedule. In addition, Dugan & Meyers Construction Co. will provide the
construction, budget and schedule analysis for the project.
22.   Mr. Bushong commented that it was his understanding that a feasibility
study was conducted a few years ago by GBBN Architects and wondered what the
outcome of that study was. Mr. Kudera stated no conclusion came of that study.
Mr. Ellison commented that he felt this allocation of funds would be better
spent elsewhere. Mayor Kriege stated the funds would come from the Building
Fund, not the General Fund. He reminded council there was favorable agreement
to go ahead with a facility(s) review at the Annual Planning Session. Mr.
Ellison stated he has changed his mind.
23.   Roll call on Mr. Gabbard’s motion and Mr. Moriconi’s second was answered
with four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Ellison and Mr. Dupps. Motion
carried 4-2 in favor to contract with Matrix Architects for a facilities
feasibility study for $27,000.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS

24.   Mr. McAllister distributed his monthly zoning violation report to council

26.   Mr. Moriconi asked what is required of an owner of a vacant house other
than keeping the grass cut. Mr. McAllister replied that it is necessary for the
house to be secure so that a safety concern does not exist.
27.   Mr. Gabbard asked what was being done regarding the condition of
disrepair of the Williams’ property across from the City Administration
Building. Mr. Barbian stated the owner of the property has been in a nursing
home for the last several years. He has been working with the social worker at
the nursing home in an effort to get the needed maintenance on the house. Mr.
Gabbard stated the owner had a relative that was handling her affairs. Mr.
Barbian replied the owner’s relative has advised the city he will no longer
assist in this matter.
Building Inspector – Kevin Barbian
28.   Mr. Barbian reported that building permit applications has increased, in

a habit with developers and suggested enacting an ordinance so that the city
would be better able to follow these name changes.

APRIL 2, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty from Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike
Gabbard, Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance
was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the March 5, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to accept the minutes of the regular Council
Meeting of March 5, 2001 as presented. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
3.   Bill Ahearn, 2032 Mapletree Drive addressed council regarding a zoning
violation at 11513 Madison Pike which abuts his property. He stated this vacant
lot has become a parking area for tractor-trailers. Mr. Ahearn stated that last
fall he spoke to the Zoning Administrator, Rich McAllister about the condition
of this property. Mayor Kriege stated the city would check on the status of
this complaint.
OLD BUSINESS
Bonding of the Senior Center
4.   City Administrator, Mark Wendling, stated he has been in contact with
Nancy Wylie of the Kentucky League of Cities regarding participation in the
Danville Kentucky Municipal League Pooled Lease Financing Program for the
construction of the new Senior Citizens Center. Mayor Kriege advised the city
would collaborate with bond counsel and reintroduce this matter at next month’s
meeting.
Flag Memorial
5.   Mayor Kriege introduced Mr. Greg Bridges. Mr. Bridges presented a proposal
for a flag memorial, which he would like to erect in memory of his father,
Wayne Bridges, who recently passed away. He stated he would assume the cost of
construction, with the exception of the flag and flagpole. He suggested the
flag memorial be temporarily installed at the present city building, but in the
event the city building is re-located, asked that the flag memorial also be
relocated. Mr. Bridges distributed a drawing plan of the proposed flag memorial
for the council members to review. Mr. Wendling stated that approximate costs
that the city would incur would be a twenty-foot pole ($165.), 4x6 flag ($42.),
installation of an electric line from the city building to the flag memorial
($1,000.) and the cost of a light to shine on the flag at night.
6.   A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Moriconi asked what the time frame was for
the construction. Mr. Bridges stated sixty days. Mayor Kriege stated that he
would like to see the flag memorial construction in time to plan a Memorial Day
ceremony. Mayor Kriege agreed that the flag memorial should be moved if the
city building would move. Mr. Wendling suggested the relocation of the flag
memorial could be added as an alternate bid if the city constructs a new
facility. Mr. Ellison suggested this flag memorial be construction on the
vacant lot across from the courthouse or at the new Senior Building in Memorial
Park, and then it would not be necessary to relocate it in the future. Mayor
Kriege stated he thought a flag memorial would be a nice feature in the
downtown area since the city building currently does not have a flag. Mr.
Ellison stated that he felt it would be more appropriate to have a flag
memorial at Memorial Park. Mr. Dupps concurred with Mr. Ellison and suggested
the construction of a flag memorial at the Park would be a better option. Mayor
Kriege stated he felt this would delay the project. Mr. Kudera was concerned
that electricity would not be available for the flagpole at Memorial Park until
the construction of the Senior Center was complete. Ms. Brake advised conduits
are already in place in the parking lot area of the park.
7.   Mr. Gabbard asked Mr. Bridges what he would like to do. Mr. Gabbard stated
that he feels the city is beholden to Wayne Bridges, who served as city
attorney for seventeen years and added that he does not object to placing the
flag memorial at Memorial Park. He suggested Mr. Bridges look at the park area
for a possible location. Mr. Bridges agreed to do that. In keeping with the
Renaissance Program, Mr. Moriconi stated he thought it would be nice for the
flag memorial to be located in the downtown area.
8.   Mr. Bridges stated that he felt Mr. Ellison had a valid point, as Memorial
Park will attract more people. Mr. Bushong stated other cities have constructed
flag memorials that included memorial bricks. He asked Mr. Bridges if he wanted
this flag memorial to be an exclusive memorial to his father. Mr. Bridges
stated that since he is providing the funding that he would like it to be
exclusive. He stated that it would cost $3,000 to $5,000 to construct a 24”
tall bronze plaque memorial to his father. Mayor Kriege suggested other sites
be considered and then council can make a determination at a future meeting.
Resolution No. 2001-R-01 – Renaissance Kentucky Direct Appropriation Proposal
Application
9.   Mayor Kriege presented a resolution to council that would support the
application for Direct Appropriation Grant Funds for $5,000 to purchase
computer equipment, a digital camera, educational training, tours and reference
materials for the Renaissance Committee. Mr. Walker read Resolution No. 2001-R-
01.
10.   Upon motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Kudera Resolution No. 2001-R-
01 was approved. Roll all was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in
favor.
Resolution No. 2001-R-02 – Approving Payment of Monthly CDBG Expenses for the
Senior Center
11.   Mayor Kriege presented a resolution to draw down CDBG funds for
$15,660.00 for Invoice #1 from Mark Spaulding Construction Company. Mr. Walker
read Resolution No. 2001-R-02.
12.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Moriconi Resolution No.
2001-R-02 was approved. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-
0 in favor.
NEW BUSINESS
13.   Mr. Gabbard asked that a more up to date general ledger report be
provided to council. Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Gabbard that because the council
meetings often fall within the first week of the month it is impossible for the
Finance Director to close out the books before the meeting.

APRIL 16, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Jim Bushong,
Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered
roll call. Also in attendance was City Attorney, Jeffrey S. Smith and City
Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   Bonding and other related matters of the Senior Center
∙   The proposed budget for fiscal year 2001/02
Discussion of Senior Center Bonding and Related Documents
3.   Mayor Kriege stated that council was provided with several documents
relating to the bonding of the Senior Center and advised, that while he is not
ready to take action on this matter, he opened the floor for the council
members to ask questions regarding the documents. He stated he was aware of the
incorrect bond amount and advised that would be corrected.
4.   Mr. Gabbard stated that he had many of questions. Some of his concerns
included specific wording in several Sections of the Purchase Agreement under
Exhibits D, E, G and I. He stated he would also like to know the fees the city
would incur for the bond counsel. Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Gabbard to submit
his list of questions in writing before the next regular council meeting (5-7-
01) so that the bond counselor (William Skees) could prepare written answers.
He also advised that Mr. Skees would attend the May meeting to answer
additional questions council may have. Mr. Gabbard also suggested that variable
interest rate language is needed in the document. City Attorney, Jeffrey S.
Smith concurred with Mayor Kriege that any questions should be submitted to Mr.
Skees in writing prior to the meeting so that Mr. Skees has time to prepare a
response. Mr. Gabbard agreed to have his questions written down.
Mayor’s Budget Address and Proposal for F/Y 2001-02
5.   Mayor Kriege presented council with the annual proposed budget and budget
message for fiscal year 2001-02 (July 1, 2001 through June 30, 2002). The Mayor
reviewed the highlights of the General Fund Revenues and Expenditures for the
coming year.
6.   He stated the estimated revenues are $3,141,550, based on the assumption
that council will adopt a compensating plus 4% property tax rate ordinance and
projecting the city will collect an additional 5% in payroll/gross receipts
taxes. He stated that preliminary calculations show estimated revenue of
$901,000 if the compensating rate is adopted or $930,000 if the compensating
rate plus 4% is adopted. He requested council keep that in mind as they move
forward through the budget process. He stated an anticipated loss of $113,000
in police revenues is due to the conclusion of the Universal Hiring Program and
DARE grants.
7.   Mayor Kriege advised that the general fund expenditures are estimated at
$3,315,341.00. He stated this figure is a slight decrease from the current
(2000-01) budget. He stated he is requesting no additions in personnel for the
coming year. He stated that health insurance quotes that were originally
forecast for twenty-one percent could be held at only a four percent increase
with slight adjustments to the current plan. He went on to say that the staff
continues to look at additional plan options and estimates. He stated that
previously discussed expenses’ regarding a municipal building has been deferred
to the 2002-03 fiscal year budget. Staff has requested two computers and a
computer form printer for the tax bills.
8.   Regarding the police section of the proposed budget, Mayor Kriege stated
the same cost containment applies regarding the health insurance expenses. He
advised no additional personnel is being requested for this department. Mayor
Kriege stated it has been recommended to eliminate the horse patrol program. He
reported the most significant expense would be for ten new cruisers to replace
four aging vehicles and six vehicles that have leases that will expire at the
end of this calendar year. With the newer vehicles, it is expected that
maintenance expenses will decrease.
9.   Mayor Kriege advised the Public Works Department would incur a very small
overall increase from the current year’s budget, as no additional personnel,
facility or major equipment purchase will be realized.
10.   Mayor Kriege stated the miscellaneous expenditures would include
transfers from the General Fund to the Municipal Road Aid Fund to cover road
repairs. In addition, there will be a General Fund Transfer to the Senior
Center Fund to cover the building and loan costs.
11.   Mayor Kriege stated the Recreation budget shows a drastic reduction in
capital outlay from $170,188 to $24,100 with operational expenses showing a
slight increase.
12.   He reported the General Fund Estimated Fund Balance at 2001-02 year end
is $1,364,084.00, which is much better than anticipated, as shown in the
projections due to some unexpected receipt of revenues coming in, and some
recent scaling-down.
13.   Mayor Kriege reported the anticipated revenues and expenditures for the
various funds, which include Municipal Road Aid, Sewer, Building, Senior Center
and the Fowler Creek Sewer. He stated he is recommending a total expenditure of
$750,135 in the Road Fund, which will be accomplished with a general fund
transfer of $312,603.00. He stated he will continue to be aggressive with the
upkeep of the roads. He reported that no transfer of monies was expected from
the Sewer Fund into the Fowler Creek Debt with an anticipated year-end balance
of $1,016,925.00.
14.   Regarding the Building Fund, Mayor Kriege advised that the revenues are
estimated at $208,000 with $371,191 in expenses. He stated this would include
$253,000 for the construction of the amphitheatre in Memorial Park, which is
partially funded by the State of Kentucky ($200,000). He stated a budget of
$118,191 is included but not anticipated to be spent and may be used in the
development of plans for a future Municipal Building. The Senior Center Fund
revenues are estimated at $523,500 and expenditures at $623,500. He stated a
10% contingency for construction of the Senior Center has been included.
15.   Lastly, the Fowler Creek Sewer Fund revenues are estimated at $322,000
with expenses estimated at $405,400.00. He explained that the expenditure is
for paying off the bonding of the sewer project.
16.   In closing, Mayor Kriege stated that he presented this proposed budget to
council for their consideration with trust that they would find it to be both
reasonable and workable. He stated a proposed ordinance has been included in
the packet for a first reading, but that it was not necessary to do at this
time, but was included as an option if council chose to proceed with the
adoption of the budget as presented. He opened the floor for questions from
council.
Discussion of the Proposed Budget for Fiscal Year 2001-02
17.   Mr. Gabbard stated he would prefer to delay the first reading of the
ordinance until the May 7th council meeting. He had questions regarding the
revenue, principal payment of the bond and the GRW Study expenses from the
Fowler Creek Sewer Fund. Finance Director, Amy Guenther advised the GRW Study
expense was paid out of the General Sewer Fund not the Fowler Creek Fund. She
stated that last year money was transferred from the general sewer into the
Fowler Creek Fund as the revenue was low at the time, but that the excess funds
can be transferred back. Ms. Guenther also advised the tap-in fee revenues were
conservatively estimated, but came in higher.
18.   Mr. Bushong asked how the ten percent contingency was determined for the
Senior Center Fund. Mayor Kriege replied it was ten percent of the construction
costs ($880,000) and that this contingency will be used for additional costs
due to engineering change orders. He stated that change orders will be
presented to council for approval.
19.   Mr. Gabbard asked how the funds were saved in this budget. Mayor Kriege
stated that if you look at the amended budget there are several areas that came
in lower than expected while there was a considerable increase in the payroll/
gross receipts tax revenue. The delay of the expenditure of a municipal
building has also controlled costs. Additionally, Ms. Guenther stated the city
has realized more interest income and there was savings on personnel while the
city was without a city administrator for several months. Mayor Kriege stated
there is a better depiction now than two months ago, but advised there is no
fat in this proposed budget and the city still maintains a $170,000 deficit. He
stated that many major expenditures, such as facilities for police/
administration and public works have been postponed and that the police
department is losing thousands of dollars in grant money. He stated that he
trusts the commercial growth revenue will continue to help offset these losses.
20.   Mr. Gabbard expressed concern over the city attorney contract fees. He
stated that he felt the city should contract to pay no more than $50,000-
$60,000 per year and that the contract should include all services. City
Attorney, Mr. Smith responded by stating one cannot predict the amount of
services or time that lawsuits will take. He stated that litigation takes an
inordinate amount of work and time and the court system cannot be controlled.
Mr. Kudera concurred with Mr. Gabbard that the city has spent an extraordinary
amount of money in legal fees. In addition, he went on to say that he believes
some of the frivolous expenses are the responsibility of some of the council.
Mr. Kudera stated that council could not fault the attorney’s for billing the
city for services they have provided. Mayor Kriege stated the attorney expenses
decreased from $104,000 to $77,000 last year. Mr. Gabbard reiterated that
paying $75,000 to $100,000 per year was excessive and he felt this was an area
of the budget that could be controlled. Mr. Dupps stated that he felt the city
received very good legal counsel on the AT&T cell tower matter and that the
money was well spent. Mr. Gabbard stated he felt there are good attorney’s that
are qualified that will work with the city for a lower fee. Mr. Dupps commented
there are a lot of qualified attorneys but not that many that are good. Mr.
Smith interjected that Frost, Brown Todd is on a $4,000 per month retainer fee,
so that any costs incurred over that is for representation that goes beyond
what is considered routine. Mr. Gabbard stood firm that he felt this was an
area where the city could save $15,000-$25,000 per year.
21.   Mayor Kriege commented that he felt Mr. Walker and Mr. Smith have
provided the city with good legal representation, however if the majority of
council wanted to solicit a law firm that would provide services for $60,000
per year or less, then he would consider their request.
22.   Mr. Kudera commended Mayor Kriege for presenting a very strict budget,
however expressed concern that it was a not a budget that was representative of
a growing city. He expressed concern that the city has a police department
without permanent housing, and a public works department without a way to
operate. He stated that the property taxes represent only 28% of the city’s
revenue, tangible 7%, payroll/gross receipts tax 43% and the other revenues in
various small numbers. He noted that the 2000 census indicates the city has
increased in population by 43.5 %. Mr. Kudera also reported the property tax
rate has decrease 93% over the last 12 years from .2909/$100 of assessed value
in 1988 to .155/$100 in 2000. He stated that this council needs to take a hard
look at the numbers and regardless of whether or not “no new taxes” was a
campaign promise it is foolish to say the city should not be spending more. He
commented that a business would not stay in business very long if it did not
have projections for revenue increases. He stated this city has not had the
backbone and fortitude to meet what it should; the city has not even taken the
compensating plus four percent tax rate in the last few years. Mr. Kudera went
on to say that the home values in the city have increased largely because the
city has made investments in the community, which does not come free. He stated
the city cannot provide services for free, and fears the city cannot afford a
Senior Center or a Police Department. He expressed concern that the police
department is already stretched to capacity as the city continues to operate as
it was ten years ago.
23.   Mayor Kriege commented that the citizens in Independence do not move out
of this city because of the low tax rate. Mr. Kudera concurred that
Independence has one of the lowest property tax rates in Northern Kentucky. A
member of the audience stated that the Kenton County Property Valuation
Assessor’s office has mailed re-assessment notices to many of the Independence
residents that will be effective this year and he asked how much revenue this
would generate for the city. Mayor Kriege informed the audience that the
compensating rate goes down when the property values increase. Ms. Guenther
stated it should be about $60,000.00.
24.   Mr. Moriconi asked when was the last year that the property tax rate was
increased. Mr. Kudera replied that from 1997 the rate went from .1539 to .160
in 1998. Mr. Gabbard stated that rate may have been calculated incorrectly. Mr.
Kudera expressed concern that the city is standing still and seems content to
remain status quo despite the population boom. He reiterated the city does not
have adequate police facilities or public work facilities, and that road funds
have been held back for the last two years and by doing this have made the
numbers look good. Mr. Kudera stated that he is not advocating a tax rate but
rather taking a stand on facing the issues at hand and urged the council to
face the facts.
25.   Mayor Kriege stated he presented a very stagnant budget; no additional
personnel or capital outlay expenses. He stated the city has many needs. The
Public Works department does not have a facility. The police department
currently rents space on the second floor of the Kenton County Courthouse but
the county has asked the city to find another facility, as the county needs to
reclaim the space. He stated that the preliminary projections looks somewhat
optimistic, but it is not a rosy picture as the city will loose $200,000 in
grant revenues and the city will have to find a way to replace that money
somehow. Mayor Kriege stated the city may be able to get through one more year
without additional revenue.
26.   Mr. Gabbard stated that one of the duties of this elected body is to
decide on how the taxpayer’s money will be spent. He agreed that the Mayor has
presented a reasonable budget, with the exception of a couple of items. He
commented that from 1998 through last year the budget has increased over a
million dollars. He knows there were extra police officers added and other
things but he feels the city has lost many things, most notably the sewer
system that was relinquished to the Sanitation District. He stated that the
sewer lines were used as collateral for the original construction loan and that
turning them over to the Sanitation District cost the city much needed revenue.
He reported the city currently receives from the Sanitation District $300 for
each new sewer tap in and will continue to collect that revenue until 2008, at
which time this revenue will cease. In addition, he expressed concern that the
city would be encumbered with paying off a $10M debt for sewer lines that
belong to the Sanitation District. A lengthy debate ensued regarding the Fowler
Creek Sewer System.
27.   Mr. Kudera stated that if the city continues to dwell on the past it
would hinder any chance of building on the future. Mr. Gabbard stated that it
is of major importance to keep the taxes down. Mayor Kriege reminded Mr.
Gabbard that during his term as mayor, it was noted in the council minutes that
he suggested adopting the insurance premium tax in his budget message to the
council. Mr. Gabbard stated he does not recall proposing that tax.
28.   Mr. Kudera urged council to seriously consider the insurance premium tax
as a way to generate additional revenue for the city. He expressed concern that
the city may be faced with the loss of police personnel if we only provide four
percent annual increases and then take away a portion of that increase by
approving a higher payroll tax deduction. Mayor Kriege concurred and shared his
concern in finding a solution to the impending deficit. He encouraged council
to put forth possible solutions. Mr. Gabbard stated that one of the options
discussed at the annual Planning Session was the road tax and wondered the
status of that idea. Mayor Kriege stated it is up to a council member to
introduce that legislation before the body.
29.   Mr. Moriconi favorably acknowledged Mayor Kriege’s efforts in presenting
a budget that was noticeably trimmed.
30.   At this time, a discussion ensued about the property tax rate. Mayor
Kriege explained that the rate adopted each year by council is limited by state
statute. He went on to explain that the additional revenue generated by the
increased housing boom is not keeping pace with the increase in population. Mr.
Kudera added that the city has not been able to increase services. Mr. Gabbard
stated that personnel have increased over the last few years. Mr. Kudera
replied that the reserves have been dwindling because of these added expenses.
Chief Butler explained his staffing needs; the police officer per capita, in
order to provide adequate public safety services to the growing population.
31.   Mrs. Barb Gabbard, a member of the audience shared her thoughts on the
matter of increasing taxes. She expressed concern that the city can only
develop so fast and only at a rate that the residents can afford to pay.
32.   Once again, Mr. Kudera espoused the need to support some type of revenue
enhancement. He stated the city could not continue to suspend the city’s needs
indefinitely. Mr. Kudera expressed concern that once the city started to play
“catch up” that it would take years to do so.
33.   Mr. Ellison advised council that in 1990 the “reserve fund” was going to
the bank to obtain a loan. He stated that he did not feel it was necessary to
increases taxes just yet and the city did not need to move at an increased
pace. Mr. Ellison recounted the growth of Independence over the last decade. He
stated the city was relieved of the expense of the fire department when they
became a Fire District thereby becoming its’ own taxing authority. In addition,
he stated there has been many services consolidated between the city and county
and that has resulted in cost-savings for the city. He acknowledged the city
has had its hands full with major expenses such as street repairs/improvements,
increased police personnel and paying off the sewer debt for a sewer system the
city was forced to build. He also recognized that Mayor Kriege has proposed a
‘barebones’ budget and that the city is growing by leaps and bounds. But Mr.
Ellison was still not convinced of the need to increase taxes.
34.   Mr. Kudera replied that he would make no apologies and could not, in good
conscience, agree to provide less city services in order to hold tax increases
at bay.
Brief Recess
35.   At 8:37 p.m., upon motion by Mr. Gabbard and second by Mr. Moriconi a
brief recess was called. Motion carried with all ayes.
36.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Gabbard, the regular meeting
resumed. Motion carried with all ayes.
Discussion of Proposed Budget for the 2001-02 Fiscal Year
37.   Mr. Gabbard suggested putting an additional $10,000-$15,000 in the budget
for city engineer expenses. He stated that he feels it would be well spent to
have the city engineers oversee the new streets in the subdivisions so that
they are built to regulations. He stated he feels the street maintenance
expenses have increased because the new streets are deteriorating since the
engineers ceased regular inspections.
38.   Mr. Gabbard also suggested doing a complete overhaul on a few of the
older cruisers in the police fleet, thereby saving the cost of complete
replacement. Chief Butler advised that a complete overhaul would cost as much
as $15,000. He stated that for another $5,000 the city could purchase a new
vehicle and as a result be able to finance the purchase. Unlike a complete
overhaul which would have to be paid in full at the time of service.
39.   Mr. Gabbard questioned the need for seasonal employees for the Public
Works Department. Mr. Smith stated the additional labor was needed for summer
street repairs.
40.   Mr. Gabbard questioned the $50,000 allocation for storm sewers. He
suggested cutting that amount by $10,000 and putting it into the engineer fees
for streets. A brief discussion ensued regarding new street inspections. Mr.
Ellison stated that the Independence Pointe Subdivision has had problems this
year. He also advised that the Northern Kentucky Area Planning & Zoning
Commission does not have enough inspectors to perform these inspections for the
concrete streets.
41.   Mr. Moriconi asked about the rent paid for the police department. Chief
Butler stated the city pays less than $1,000 per month for 1600 square feet of
space. He also commented that the county did not charge rent for the first two
years the department occupied the space.
42.   Mr. Ellison commented that the budget presented shows all departments
have made cutbacks, most notably the Public Works and Parks.
Mayor’s Closing Remarks
43.   In closing, Mayor Kriege advised the budget should be adopted by June. He
stated he would plan public hearings to discuss projections for future years.
Meanwhile, he asked council to stay focused on the budget presented. He
commented that budget concerns were presented at the Annual Planning Session
and applauded Mrs. Guenther for doing a great job compiling past years
financial data. He stated this would be very helpful to council as they strive
to make the right decisions for the city.
Adjournment
44.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Ellison, the meeting was
closed. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting adjourned at 9:07 p.m.
_______________________________________
Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

MAY 7, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:01 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty from Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike
Gabbard, Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance
was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
OLD BUSINESS
Bond Counselor, Bill Skees Regarding the Bonding of the Senior Center Building
2.   Mayor Kriege introduced Mr. Bill Skees a bond attorney with Frost Brown
Todd who would discuss and answer any questions regarding the proposed
resolutions and related documents for the bonding of the Senior Center
building. Mr. Skees gave a presentation and overview of the bonding process. He
stated that various options were discussed with Mayor Kriege regarding
obtaining a bond with a bank versus the bonding pools of Mayfield or Danville
offered through the Kentucky League of Cities (KLC). Mr. Skees advised that the
Danville pool is the most inexpensive in today’s market. He stated that to
become a part of the program it would be necessary for the city to enter into
an interlocal agreement with KLC. He stated that KLC would charge a .25%
administrative fee. He stated that the interest rate will vary but at this
time, the rate is currently very low at 4.18%. He stated that a major bank must
provide backing, so PNC Bank will provide this service. He advised council that
his role is to ensure that KLC properly executes this bonding.
3.   Mr. Dupps asked what other cities have entered the KLC bonding pools. Mr.
Skees replied that among others, the cities of Elizabethtown, Florence, Hazard,
Glasgow and Bowling Green have used this bond pool. He went on to say that the
City of Danville has repaid the up front costs, so that no dollars will be
taken out of our initial cost and that the cost of issuance will be very low.
He advised that as part of the financing it will be necessary to deed part over
but, that it will come back to the city when it is paid off.
4.   Mr. Bushong expressed some concern at deeding city property over. Mr.
Skees assured Mr. Bushong that this is a common procedure. Mr. Gabbard stated
that nowhere in the documents does it state that the bond will be for ten years
nor that the interest rate will start at 4.18%. Mr. Skees advised that the
amortization schedule will not be prepared until a day or two before the
closing as the interest rate will be set that week. He advised council they
could impose condition parameters for the Mayor. Mr. Bushong questioned who
would maintain the lease for the Senior Center. Mr. Skees advised the lease
agreement would be with the city, as the city would indemnify the Senior Center
building.
Resolution No. 2001-R-03 – Authorizing Interlocal Agreement with KLC Funding
Trust Program for the Senior Center
5.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to read, in summary, Resolution No. 2001-R-03
authorizing the Mayor to enter into an interlocal agreement with the Kentucky
League of Cities Funding Trust Program for the Senior Center. Mr. Kudera
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-
0 in favor and Mr. Walker read the resolution.
Resolution No. 2001-R-04 – Authorizing Participation in the Kentucky Municipal
League Pooled Lease Program for the Bonding of the Senior Center
6.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to read Resolution No. 2001-R-04 authorizing the
Mayor execute the necessary documents to participate in the Kentucky Municipal
League Pooled Lease Program for the Senior Center for a length not to exceed
ten years with an interest rate for no more than 4.5%. Mr. Ellison seconded the
motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor and
Mr. Walker read the resolution.
Approval of the Minutes of the April 2, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
7.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to accept the minutes of the regular Council
Meeting of April 2, 2001 as presented. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call
was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Approval of the Minutes of the April 16, 2001 Special Council Meeting
