PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
10.   Mr. Tom Brinker, 1192 Constitution Drive addressed council regarding the
vacant land at the entrance to the Independence Pointe Subdivision owned by
Finke Development Company. He gave a brief history of the efforts made over the
past year to compel Mr. Finke to comply with the city’s zoning ordinance
regarding the lawn maintenance of property owners. He stated he has begun to
lose faith in the system as he feels the city has not enforced the zoning laws
by not citing Mr. Finke for non-compliance. City Administrator, Mr. Wendling
advised council that the grass had been cut this past weekend but suggested
that council may want to amend the present zoning code to add a specific grass
height because the current code does not define what height is considered to be
too high. Mr. Wendling assured Mr. Brinker that he is looking into this matter
further and asked for his continued patience.
11.   Mr. Gabbard suggested an ordinance that includes penalties be drafted to
remedy this type of blight problem. Mr. Wendling stated he is researching such
an ordinance. Mr. Walker advised that care be taken when defining what is a
nuisance and where it is to be applied. He also advised when changing a zoning
code that it would first be necessary to get approval from the Kenton County
and Municipal Planning and Zoning Commission before council approval. He stated
that amending the zoning code is the best place for long-term enforcement but
that taking it to the Planning and Zoning Commission will add more time to the
process. Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Brinker that the city would continue to
pursue this matter with Mr. Finke until a text amendment is made. In closing,
Mr. Brinker advised that he has filed a complaint against Finke Development
Company with the Better Business Bureau and the Home Builders Association.
12.   Dan Piersall, 522 Upton Drive, Mike Nolan, 548 Upton Drive, Peggy
Bradley, 5414 Cody Road and Linda McHargue, 5408 Cody Road addressed council
regarding their desire to have water lines run to their homes.
13.   Mr. Piersall stated that Upton Drive adjoins the new Troopers Crossing
Subdivision that is being developed by Berling. He stated that he and some of
the other residents have approached the developer about extending the
subdivision’s water lines to the residents on Upton Drive and the few houses on
Cody Road in that area. He stated they have also spoken to Mr. Richard Harrison
at the Northern Kentucky Water District and was advised that preliminary
estimates reveal it would be about $12,000 per house to extend water lines.
Mayor Kriege advised it might be possible to obtain a grant through the state
but the residents would need to be in agreement to petition for one. Mr.
Piersall also complained of the dust in the construction area and the effect it
is having on the resident’s cisterns. He asked for the city’s assistance in
requiring the contractors to water down the dust.
14.   Mr. Ellison stated that he has looked at the area and senses the
residents would just like to have water lines complete the loop from the cul de
sac to Upton Drive.
15.   Mr. Nolan advised council that he has lived in Independence for thirty
years and has never had to have his cistern cleaned until this year, due to the
construction dust from Troopers Crossing. He stated he is also concerned
because there are fewer water haulers to purchase water from and the prices
have increased from $20 to $25 per load. He stated he would like council to
encourage the developers to run water lines to the homes on Upton Drive and
Cody Road. He feels the residents will not be successful without the city’s
assistance.
16.   Peggy Bradley, 5414 Cody Road, stated she has lived on Cody Road, paid
city taxes for the past twenty-three years, and still has no public water or
sewer lines or cable television services. She stated the long time residents
are not being recognized while all the builders are providing services to new
residents.
17.   Mayor Kriege advised that the city would try to work with Northern
Kentucky Water District and Berling Development Company and explore options.
18.   Mr. Gabbard suggested enlisting the help of Sally Davis in Frankfort to
get state assistance for a grant. Mr. Kudera advised that a few months ago the
residents on Fowler Creek Road proceeded with the grant process only to have
several residents back out because they would not commit to part of the
financial burden for the water lines. He went on to say that the residents
would have to be willing to bear some of the expense. Mr. Nolan stated that it
was his understanding that the city required Berling to install water lines in
other subdivisions. Mayor Kriege stated that was county areas and reiterated
that the city will need to look at all options but that the residents would
probably have to pay a portion of the cost.
19.   Mr. Bushong advised that the Water District and Sanitation District
require 75% participation to install service in an area and that the engineer
study fee is $150 per home, which has to be paid in advance.
20.   Linda McHargue, 5408 Cody Road, voiced her concern that the city
continues to raise taxes but not services.
21.   Mayor Kriege requested that Mike Nolan be the liaison with the city for
the residents.
Miscellaneous Comments
22.   Mr. Gabbard addressed Mr. Kudera regarding comments he made at the April
16, 2001 special council meeting. Specifically when Mr. Kudera attributed
costly legal fees were due to excessive calls to the city attorney by some of
the council members. Mr. Gabbard stated that he spoke to Mr. Walker regarding
this charge and was told that council members phone calls were part of his
retainer fee.
23.   Mr. Gabbard also clarified that the Fowler Creek sewer pipes were used
for collateral for the construction loan of that project. He referred to
Ordinance 1998-O-11 Section 7 regarding this. Mr. Kudera stated that he did not
dispute the matter.
Proposed Ordinance – Zoning Text Amendment regarding Accessory Buildings – 1st
Reading
24.   Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian explained the proposed ordinance to
council. He stated this would eliminate accessory structures from being located
in front yards.
25.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Ellison, a first reading of
the proposed ordinance was achieved. Motion carried with all ayes. Motion
carried 6-0 in favor and Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance in summary.
Resolution No. 2001-R-05 – Approving Payment of CDBG Monthly Expenses for the

26.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Ellison, there was a reading
of Resolution No. 2001-R-05 approving payment of monthly expenses totaling
$59,903.00 for construction of the Senior Center. Roll call was unanimous;
motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Walker read the resolution.
Proposed Ordinance – Setting the Speed Limit for Streets within the City in
Accordance with KRS
27.   Mr. Walker explained this ordinance was being proposed as a result of an
Order by Judge Sheehan in the Kenton County District Court. He stated that the
Order rules that individual city ordinances regarding speed limits that were
not based upon engineering and traffic investigations are void. Mr. Walker
stated that the simplest solution, without the expense of an engineering study,
is to enact a 20 mph speed limit, which is acceptable, and then enact the fine
schedule that exists under K.R.S. 189.390. Chief of Police, Shawn Butler
advised that most cities had not revised their city ordinance in accordance
with K.R.S. 189.390. Mr. Walker stated the proposed ordinance would amend the
city’s current traffic ordinance that was adopted in 1983.
28.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance; seconded by Mr. Kudera. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 6-0 in favor and Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Creating Citation Officers – 1st Reading
29.   Mr. Walker explained the purpose of this proposed ordinance is to
establish the positions and appoint citation officers in accordance with K.R.S.
He stated this would provide a more efficient and time responsive enforcement
of the codes.
30.   Mr. Gabbard expressed concern in adopting this type ordinance. He stated
this has not been discussed and felt this needs more review. Mr. Dupps stated
this issue was first introduced with the previous council and it was felt that
this ordinance would provide the city additional reinforcement. Mr. Bushong
asked what types of violations would be cited. Mr. Walker replied this
ordinance provides procedures for citations issued according to state statute
to the Code Enforcement Board and would include zoning code and nuisance
sections such as barking dogs, high grass, etc. Mr. Moriconi stated he felt
this would be good as the city receives many of these kinds of complaints.
31.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed ordinance
to create citation officer positions. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor and Mr. Walker
read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Budget for 2001/02 Fiscal Year – 1st Reading
32.   Mayor Kriege reintroduced the proposed budget for the 2001/02 fiscal year
for council’s discussion and possible action. Mr. Gabbard asked where the
$5,000 liability insurance deductible to settle the Porter vs. City of
Independence lawsuit would be taken. Mayor Kriege advised that money would come
out of the current budget, not next year’s budget.
33.   Mr. Gabbard stated that he thought the pay increases for employees was
going to be 4.5% but it appears that Public Works employees are figured at 5%.
Mrs. Guenther, Finance Director, advised that when the pay increases were
discussed at the Annual Planning Session that the consumer price index (cpi)
was 2.9% but that has risen and is now 3.8%, which is why the wages were
increased. Mr. Gabbard asked how the pay raises were determined. Mayor Kriege
replied the salaries are based on employee performance reviews.
34.   Mr. Dupps commended Mayor Kriege for presenting a prudent budget. Mayor
Kriege stated that during the last few months the revenues have come in higher
than projected due in part to the commercial development.
35.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a first reading, in summary, of the
proposed budget for the 2001/02 fiscal year; seconded by Mr. Bushong. Roll call
was answered by five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion
carried 5-1 in favor and Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
DEPARTMENT REPORTS
City Engineer – Dave Whitacre, Cardinal Engineering
36.   Mr. Whitacre reported that four bids were received by the city for the
Holten Drive Repairs Project. The bid was divided into two options; one for the
concrete widening and one for asphalt repairs and overlay to the remainder of
the street. He stated the project was bid in this manner so that the city would
have the option to complete he entire project or partially, as budget
constraints dictate. He reported that the four bids were received from JPS
Construction, Michels Concrete Construction, Quast Paving & Sealing and Barrett
Paving. He stated that overall JPS Construction is the low bid, but that
Michels was the low bidder on the asphalt option. Mr. Whitacre advised that he
has worked with both companies and reported that both are very good.
37.   Mayor Kriege commented that JPS Construction did work for the city last
year. Mr. Whitacre confirmed that they did some concrete work last year and
there was a problem with the concrete provided by the concrete supplier. It was
not the fault of JPS, but the replacement of the street still falls under
warranty.
38.   Mayor Kriege stated the current budget couldn’t afford to include Option
2 at this time. He asked Mr. Whitacre if the contractor would hold the bid
amount until July. Mr. Walker advised the city couldn’t appropriate more than
is in the current budget. Mr. Bushong asked if the bad spots on Holten Drive
would also be included in this project. Mr. Whitacre stated the existing

(Option 2) until July.

accessibility sidewalk ramps for a grade change. He stated they will do the
best they can to make ramps work on steep streets but doubts it will be
possible to meet code. City Attorney, Mr. Walker advised that the ADA
requirement is not retroactive, but if the city is making repairs to a street
then it is required to meet the ADA code and, of course, all newly constructed
streets have to comply with ADA.

JUNE 4, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty from Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike
Gabbard, Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance
was City Attorney, Jeffrey S. Smith (sitting in for H. Lawson Walker) and City
Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the May 7, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to accept the minutes of the regular council
meeting of May 7, 2001, as amended. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call
was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Amendment to the Minutes of the May 1, 2001 Special Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Gabbard requested the minutes of the special council meeting on May 1,
2001 be amended to reflect the City Attorney’s request that the terms of the
settlement of the Porter versus the City lawsuit, as discussed in executive
session, be kept confidential. Mayor Kriege stated that if council agreed, this
could be included in the minutes, but he added that he felt it was irrelevant,
as the final agreement did not stipulate confidentiality. Mr. Ellison asked Mr.
Gabbard if he wanted that documented in the open session of the minutes. Mr.
Gabbard stated that he did.
4.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to amend the minutes of the Special Council
Meeting of May 1, 2001 to include Lawson Walker’s admonition concerning
confidentiality of the Porter versus the City lawsuit settlement. Mr. Ellison
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with six yes votes. Motion carried
6-0 in favor.

Road, who stated they did not wish to speak at this time, but reserved the

hillside had become before it was mowed last Wednesday. He stated that Finke

Company and will continue to work with him in order to get this land mowed on a
more regular basis.

Ordinance No. 2001-O-03 Setting the Speed Limit at 20 mph on City Streets in
Accordance with K.R.S.
11.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance No. 2001-
O-03 to set the speed limit at 20 miles per hour, in accordance with K.R.S. on
all city maintained streets within the city. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion.
Mr. Smith, City Attorney, read the proposed ordinance. A brief discussion
ensued wherein Mr. Gabbard stated that he has received calls from residents
asking that the speed limit be set at 25 mph. Mr. Ellison stated that he felt
that most people drive at 25 mph even though the limited is posted at 20 and
that if the limit is 25 mph then they will drive 30 or 35 mph. He thought it
was best to keep the limit at 20 mph. Roll call was answered with all ayes.
Motion carried 6-0 in favor.

Ordinance No. 2001-O-05 Adopting a Budget for the 2001-02 Fiscal Year
13.   A motion was made by Mr. Kudera and a seconded by Mr. Dupps to have a
second reading of proposed Ordinance No. 2001-O-05 adopting a budget for the
2001-02 fiscal year. Mr. Smith read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Kriege opened
the floor for discussion of the proposed budget.
14.   Mr. Gabbard stated he felt it was necessary to look at the amendments to
the current budget before discussing the proposed budget and pointed to the
police salary line item that reflected a $100,000 increase in the proposed
amended budget. Mr. Ellison asked what the percentage rate was for the
retirement contribution. Mr. Wendling stated that it varied depending on
whether it was a hazardous or non-hazardous employee. He advised that the non-
hazardous rate was about seven percent and the hazardous rate was approximately
seventeen percent.
15.   Mr. Gabbard asked how the final salary increase figures were calculated.
Mr. Wendling stated that the final raise amounts are not complete but that a
five percent was figured for the budget by using the current Consumer Price
Index rate with a merit increase of one to two percent. Mr. Gabbard wanted to
know what factors determine an employee’s merit percent increase. Mr. Wendling
replied than throughout the year there may have been significant times where
the employee took on additional responsibilities, etc. Mr. Gabbard asked if
most employees would be on the plus side of a five percent increase. Mr.
Wendling replied that it depended on the situation and that some would be
higher.
16.   At this time, roll call was taken and answered with four yes votes and
two no votes by Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 4-2 in favor. Mr.
Gabbard stated that he voted against the proposed budget do to the following
four reasons:
§   He objected to the $12,500 payment to Porter and the attorney’s fees for
representation in the Ed Porter vs. The City of Independence lawsuit. He
disputed the Mayor’s right to dismiss Mr. Porter and the settlement amount.
§   He objected to the $2,400 spent on the Christmas Dinner and that the dinner
was held at a facility outside the city limits.
§   He objected to the amount of money paid to the City Attorney for legal
counsel. He stated that other comparable cities (Erlanger, Fort Thomas,
Florence) pay much lower fees.
§   He objected to the $16,000 paid to former City Administrator, Gary Scott as
severance pay. He stated that he feels this was an illegal payment and that the
Opinion of the Attorney General (OAG 78.206) supports his belief.
17.   Mayor Kriege refuted Mr. Gabbard’s assertions. He stated he would not
debate the details of the settlement, but advised Mr. Gabbard that the
disbursement would be paid by the insurance company and disbursed over a
twenty-year period making the value of the settlement markedly depreciating. In
addition, he informed Mr. Gabbard that the Christmas Dinner was the Annual
Appreciation Dinner held each year for volunteers and employees and that it was
held outside the city as there is no facility in Independence large enough to
accommodate the assemblage.
Approval of Map Amendment for Donald Newsom Property on Stephens Road
18.   Mr. Ellison reported that Mr. Newsom made application to the Planning
Commission to approve a map amendment to plat the existing residential
building, and approximately one acre of land, from the remaining property
totaling approximately 124 acres. In addition, Mr. Newsom requested a waiver of
sidewalks along Stephens Road and no public improvements. Mr. Ellison advised
that Kenton County and Municipal Planning and Zoning Commission recommended the
map amendment for approval with the condition that a sidewalk be provided along
the portion of Stephens Road fronting the proposed lot. Mr. Ellison reminded
council the city has ninety days to act on NKMP&Z Commission’s recommendation.
19.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to support the Kenton County and Municipal
Planning & Zoning Commission’s recommendation to approve the map amendment
subject to the condition that a sidewalk be installed. Mr. Gabbard seconded the
motion. Roll call vote was unanimous and the motion carried.
Grand Communities, Ltd (Fischer Development) Request for a Zone Change East of
Fowler Creek Road
20.   Mayor Kriege stated that Grand Communities has requested a zone change
for property east of Fowler Creek Road and stated that representatives were
present to address this matter. The Mayor cautioned the council and audience
that a public hearing has already been held on this zone change and that
council needs to make a decision based on the findings of the Kenton County and
Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission’s recommendation. Mayor Kriege advised
council the city has until August 3, 2001 to act on the Commission’s
recommendation leaving time for the city to hold its’ own public hearing if
council so desires.
21.   Mr. Steve Feldman, Ms. Elizabeth Horowitz and Mr. Don McDonough were in
attendance to represent Grand Communities, Ltd. (Fischer Homes). Mr. Feldman
explained that Fischer Homes is requesting that a seventy-seven acre tract on
the east side of Fowler Creek Road be re-zoned from R-1C to an R-1D cluster
development. He stated their proposed development would preserve the hillsides,
lake and ravine on the property along with the construction of 120-150 single-
family homes with a price range of $200,000 to $250,000. He stated the zone
change request has been given approval of the Kenton County and Municipal
Planning & Zoning Commission.
22.   Mr. McDonough added that the homes will be 2000 to 3200 square feet in
size and will include more features and customization than the Clover Ridge
Subdivision.
23.   Ms. Horowitz advised that five acres of the seventy-seven acres would
remain under private ownership. She stated the current zone of R-1C would
permit two hundred homes, but with the R-1D zone they are requesting, the
maximum number of homes would be 150-155. She stated the R-1D zone would also
provide a variety of lot sizes with the smallest lot size being seventy foot,
having a mixture of housing styles and a more attractive streetscape. Ms.
Horowitz advised that the adjoining properties are in the process of
development so there will be multiple ingress/egress.
24.   Mr. Ellison asked if the Planning Commission recommended turn lanes on
Fowler Creek Road. Mrs. Horowitz stated that would be a recommendation of the
Subdivision Review and that they need a zone change before a preliminary plat
is submitted for review.
25.   Mr. Gabbard asked how the steep areas of the land would be developed. Ms.
Horowitz stated that by granting the zone change they could build the same
number of houses, but in smaller spaces, thereby keeping the hillsides as
undeveloped green space. Mayor Kriege asked about water runoff. Ms. Horowitz
stated that until a preliminary plat is designed, that will not be known. Mr.
Dupps questioned the elevation of the lake on the property. Mr. Feldman
answered there will be a retention basin. Mr. Gabbard wondered if the lake
would be used for retention. Mr. Dupps was concerned about water retention to
secure the Banklick Creek area. Mrs. Horowitz advised they couldn’t increase
storm water run off, in any case, to what it would be in its natural state. Mr.
Ellison expressed concern that the property was physically restrictive for
development. Mr. Moriconi asked if the main road would be widen to handle the
increase traffic. Ms. Horowitz stated that would be part of a preliminary plat
when it is designed.
26.   At this time, Mr. Gabbard stated that pursuant to KRS 100.211 he was
making a motion to override the recommendation of the Kenton County and
Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission to approve the proposed map amendment to
the Independence Zoning Ordinance to change an approximate seventy-seven acre
area located along the east side of Fowler Creek Road, between Senour Road and
Cox Road, approximately 3,000 feet south of Senour Road, from R-1A and R-1C to
R–1D. He stated the basis to override the Planning Commission’s recommendation
is: the proposed development associated with the map amendment will severely
diminish the privacy of the area, the character of the natural environment of
the subject property will be destroyed, the proposed development will not serve
to preserve the green space of the subject property and the existing roadway
and infrastructure cannot accommodate the traffic to be generated by the
proposed development. In addition, the above stated reasons demonstrate the
existing zoning classification for the property is appropriate and the proposed
zoning classification is inappropriate; there have been no major changes of an
economic, physical, or social nature within the area which were not anticipated
in the adopted comprehensive plan and which have substantially altered the
basic character of the area; and there is no compelling reason for the proposed
zoning map amendment. He stated the reasons for rejection of the Planning
Commission’s recommendation stems solely from the public hearing conducted by
the Planning Commission on this matter on May 3, 2001 at 6:15 p.m. and
contained within the Findings of Fact and Statement of Recommendation by the
Planning Commission. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. There being no further
discussion, roll call was taken and answered with four yes votes and two no
votes cast by Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Bushong. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.
Recess

requested. Motion carried with all ayes.

reconvened. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance to Amend the 2000/01 Budget – 1st Reading
29.   Mayor Kriege advised council the current budget would need amending to
reflect the increases in revenue and expenditures. Mr. Jeff Smith, City

July that it would be necessary to schedule a special meeting or proceed under
an emergency reading tonight. Mr. Gabbard stated that he believed it did not
meet the standard for an emergency reading. Mr. Smith advised that the statute
allows council to discern the criteria that constitutes an emergency.
30.   Mayor Kriege referred council to the memo from Mr. Wendling explaining

expenditures increased due to additional attorney fees, insurance settlement,

not be reflected on the audit.

Discussion of Enforcement Methods of Zoning Regulations
32.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to make a text amendment to the zoning ordinance providing the zoning
administrator discretionary powers to determine a civil or criminal action.
33.   City Attorney, Mr. Smith stated that a proposed ordinance has not been
drafted yet. He referred Mayor Kriege and council to the letter in the council
packets addressed to Rich McAllister and Mark Wendling from Dianne Kuhnell of
Frost, Brown, Todd regarding code enforcement methods used by the Zoning
Administrator. Ms. Kuhnell advised that according to the Kentucky League of
Cities the city could enforce its zoning regulations by civil or criminal
proceedings allowing the Zoning Administrator to use his/her discretion in each
case. However, Mr. Smith advised the city Code Enforcement Board could only
preside over civil proceedings.
34.   Mr. Smith stated that based on Ms. Kuhnell’s findings, it has been
determined that several sections of the current zoning ordinance may need a
text amendment to include the phrase “…determine at his discretion the
necessary civil or criminal action...”. Mr. Ellison stated that he feels the
Planning & Zoning Committee should review this information to determine if this
is necessary. Mayor Kriege agreed this matter should be sent to the committee
for review with Mr. McAllister.
35.   Following this discussion, Mr. Bushong withdrew his motion. Mr. Ellison
made a motion that the Planning & Zoning Committee review a possible text
amendment to the zoning ordinance and make a recommendation to the council. Mr.
Gabbard seconded the motion. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 1-11-82 Re: Nuisance/Control of
Grass & Weeds
36.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance amending two out-dated ordinances (Ordinance No. 1-11-82 and
Ordinance No. 2-5-80) regarding the nuisance and control of weeds and grass.
Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. No roll call; motion carried unanimously. Mr.
Smith, City Attorney, read the proposed ordinance.
37.   A brief discussion ensued regarding Section I of the proposed ordinance
wherein “…overgrown grass is considered to be in excess of eight (8) inches in
length for purposes of this ordinance…” Mayor Kriege asked if eight inches was
reasonable. Mr. Dupps stated that he is aware of only one other city that
states a grass length in their ordinance. Mr. Gabbard stated that during a
rainy period that grass can grow several inches in a week’s time. Council
amended Section I to include that the notice could be hand-delivered and/or
mailed to the last know address of the property owner. Also discussed was
Section III and applying a fine of $100. Consensus was to make the fine $100
per day. Mr. Kudera stated that a fine or penalty is supposed to “hurt.”
38.   After the changes were made to the proposed ordinance, Mr. Gabbard made a
motion to approve the amendments as discussed and reviewed. Mr. Moriconi
seconded the motion. No roll call; motion carried unanimously. Mr. Smith read
the proposed ordinance with amendments.
39.   Mr. Kudera suggested the second reading of this ordinance be added to the
agenda of the Special Council Meeting later this month so that enforcement can
begin.

JUNE 25, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. Council Members
Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call.
Council Members, Jim Ellison and Ike Gabbard were absent. Also in attendance
was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was to
discuss and take action on the second readings of a proposed ordinance to amend
the 2000/01 fiscal year budget and a proposed ordinance regarding the nuisance
control of overgrown grass and weeds on non-agricultural properties.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-06 – Regarding Control of Grass/Weeds on Non Agricultural
Properties – 2nd Reading
3.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Dupps Ordinance No. 2001-O-06
was read by City Attorney, Lawson Walker. Mayor Kriege commented that he felt
the adoption of this ordinance would ease the enforcement of the current
problems in the city regarding property lawn maintenance. Mr. Dupps pointed out
two property locations – the entrance to the Independence Pointe Subdivision
owned by Finke Homes and the property at the corner of Briarwood and Richardson
Road – that have been consistently in violation with overgrown grass and weeds.
Mayor Kriege advised the city has been monitoring these properties and will
continue to do so. At this time, roll call was taken and answered with four yes
votes. Motion carried 4-0 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-07 – Amending the 2000/01 Budget – 2nd Reading
4.   Mayor Kriege stated that it is necessary to amend the current budget in
order to be in compliance with financial audit regulations.
5.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to amend the 2000/01 fiscal year budget, seconded by Mr. Moriconi.
City Attorney, Lawson Walker read the proposed ordinance. There was a brief
discussion wherein Finance Director, Amy Guenther reported that the proposed
revenues for the year came in higher than estimated. She also reported that
some expenses were higher due to the settlement of the Porter lawsuit,
expiration of grants and expenses related to the Senior Center.
6.   Roll call on Mr. Bushong’s motion and Mr. Moriconi’s second yielded four
yes votes. Motion carried 4-0 in favor of adopting the amended budget
ordinance.
Adjournment
7.   Upon motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Kudera, the meeting was
adjourned. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 7:11 p.m.

JULY 2, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant from Grace Community Church gave the
invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard,
Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance was City
Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the June 4, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to accept the minutes of the regular council
meeting of June 4, 2001, as amended. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Roll call
was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Approval of the Minutes of the June 25, 2001 Special Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to accept the minutes of the special council
meeting of June 25 as submitted. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Roll call
vote was answered with four yes votes with Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard
abstaining. Motion carried 4-0 in favor.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
4.   Richard Maines, 5254 Courtney Court, addressed council regarding the
citywide trash pick-up by Rumpke. He expressed displeasure with the service
provided by the company and wanted to know if the city had always contracted
with Rumpke. Councilman Ellison replied that Rumpke has contracted with the
city since 1990. Mayor Kriege informed Mr. Maines that the contract with Rumpke
would expire next year, at which time the city will seek bids. Mr. Maines
expressed a desire to contract with another company and increase the number of
days per week that trash is picked up.
5.   Geneva Wade, 640 Willow Drive, addressed council regarding the on-going
problems with her property since the Fowler Creek Sewer lines were installed.
She stated that this is not the first time she has addressed council regarding
the condition of her land and was upset that the city has not responded to this
matter. She depicted the rear area of her property as a marshland and has been
told there are natural springs in the area, yet this area was not constantly
wet before the sewer lines were installed. In addition, she complained about
paying the debt reduction assessment on a ‘fixed income’ for something she does
not use. She stated that the 43% population increase should have eased this
burden on the other residents. She requested council give her some answers to
this matter.
6.   Mitchell Wade, 640 Willow Drive, confirmed there was no water in the area
before the trees were cleared to install the sewer lines. He stated that he
felt if a natural spring was severed then the city should repair the damage.
Mr. Gabbard asked if the Wades had notified the city in writing back in 1996-97
when this occurred because the city would have had recourse with the excavation
contractor under the one year guarantee. He stated that it would be difficult
now to look to the contractor to make repairs. Mayor Kriege suggested reviewing
the council minutes from that time to discover any discussions about the
matter. Mr. Ellison suggested sending the city engineer over to inspect the
property and bring a recommendation back to council. Mayor Kriege asked Ms.
Wade to meet with city representatives to make an inspection of her property.
OLD BUSINESS
Zone Change Request by Grand Communities Ltd. – East Side/Fowler Creek Rd.
(Sycamore Creek Subd.)
7.   Mayor Kriege stated that representatives from Grand Communities Ltd.
(Fischer Development Company) were present and requested that council permit
them to make a second presentation regarding the zone change they are seeking
for 77 acres on the east side of Fowler Creek Road and ask that they reconsider
the matter.
8.   Mr. Jim Gorman, President of Fischer Development Company explained to
council that Grand Communities is seeking a zone change from R-1A and R-1C to
R-1D for this tract of land along the Fowler Creek Road. He stated that Grand
Communities feels this development will be unique, as no more than one-third of
the lots will have a width of seventy feet with the remaining lots a minimum
width of eighty feet. He stated that the design of the subdivision would be
livable with ample open space throughout. Mr. Gorman proposed six conditions in
addition to the conditions imposed by the Kenton County and Municipal Planning
& Zoning Commission. The conditions are:
§   The density of the site would not exceed a maximum density of 2.5 dwelling
units per net acre.
§   No more than one-third of the total lots will have the minimum R-1D lot
width of seventy feet with the remaining lots having a minimum width of eighty
feet.
§   Turn lanes on Fowler Creek Road will be added for traffic into the
subdivision in accordance with the Kentucky Department of Highways.
§   The houses to be constructed will meet the specifications of the Founders
Series of Homes offered by Fischer Homes. If Grand Communities, Ltd. sells some
of the lots, or the entire property to one or more other builders, it will be a
requirement to build homes substantially equivalent to the Founders Series of
Homes. The houses will have a first story brick wrap, except for isolated areas
not directly supported by a concrete foundation. An example of such an isolated
area would be cantilevered walls, bay windows, etc.
§   A homeowners association will be formed to maintain the common open space.
§   No building lot shall be accessed directly from Fowler Creek Road.
9.   He also presented a letter from Raymond Erpenbeck Engineers addressing the
regulatory requirements and current state of improvements for storm water
runoff control. He stated that Scott Hiles of the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission concurs with the assessment recommendations. He went on to
say that this development has been geared to protect and enhance the natural
features of the land with high quality homes and that the zone change will
preserve more land as open green space with a varied streetscape that will be
unique to Independence. He urged council to reconsider their previous decision
to deny this zone change request made at last month’s council meeting.
10.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor for questions from the council. Mr. Bushong
asked what is different in this presentation than from last month. Mr. Gorman
stated that the development plan is unchanged; just that further explanation of
the plan and the addition of building conditions that were not included in the
original presentation to council.
11.   Ms. Elizabeth Horowitz added that they also have provided more
information on the storm water runoff plan and the turn lane on Fowler Creek
Road. Grand Communities also wanted to assure council that the housing will be
the Founders Series type of structure and that subsequent builders would be
required to follow suit.
12.   Mr. Ellison expressed concern over the traffic study conducted in the
area and wondered if the study was based on speed and sight distance. Mr.
Gorman indicated the speed study was given to the Kentucky Department of
Highway.
13.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to reconsider the zone change request being made
by Grand Communities, Ltd. based on the conditional information provided,
density plan and the assurance that all homes in the development will be
required to adhere to the Founders Series of Homes style. Mr. Dupps seconded
the motion. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by
Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
14.   Further discussion ensued. Mr. Ellison expressed concern regarding the
width of the subdivision streets and asked if the streets would be twenty-five
feet wide. Ms. Horowitz stated that could be done. Mayor Kriege was concerned
that condition number four, wherein subsequent lot owners would be required to
meet the specifications of the Founders Series of Homes, would be difficult to
enforce. City Attorney, Lawson Walker advised that a covenant could be placed
on the plat, which would be the only way to ensure this condition is met. Ms.
Horowitz agreed to put a covenant on the plat. There being no further
discussion, Mayor Kriege asked council how they wanted to proceed.
15.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve the zone change request for a
seventy-seven acre tract of land east of Fowler Creek Road, contingent on all
conditions imposed by the KCMP&Z Commission along with the additional
conditions presented by Grand Communities, Ltd and the attachment of the NKAPC
traffic study. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with
five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in
favor. Mr. Lawson Walker advised that this map amendment would require an
ordinance, which will be prepared and presented at the next council meeting for
a first reading.
Miscellaneous Updates
16.   Mr. Gabbard asked for an update on providing water lines in the Cody
Road/Upton Drive area per the residents’ request at the May council meeting.
Mr. Wendling replied that he spoke with Sally Davis in Frankfort regarding a
possible grant and met with Mr. Nolan, Mr. Scheben and a representative of the
Northern Kentucky Water District to discuss this matter. He stated that he
found the residents do not qualify for a Community Block Development Grant. Mr.
Wendling reported he is waiting to hear from Mr. Berling and his response to
extend the water lines from his development to the residents on Cody Road and
Upton Drive, but suspects he will want to be compensated.
17.   Mr. Gabbard also inquired on the status of obtaining a copy of the Porter
vs. the City settlement agreement. Mr. Walker stated it has been four weeks and
he is still waiting for the documents to be signed by all parties involved and
a fully executed copy returned to him.
LSI Industries – Request for Map Amendment
18.   Mr. Frank Dornbach, Manager at the LSI Industries corporate office in
Blue Ash, Ohio addressed council regarding the request the company has to
rezone 4.3 acres of their property on the east side of Turkeyfoot Road from
residential (R-1B) to IP (an industrial park zone). He stated that the building
on the site currently houses 163 employees. He stated that when they recently
applied for a permit to improve the building’s parking lot, it was discovered
that the area was incorrectly zoned residential. He stated that LSI is aware of
resident complaints regarding storm water control and sound levels, which they
feel they have made every effort to correct. He advised that LSI has incurred
expenses to conduct sound studies by an environmental engineer, contacted
soundproof consultants and purchased material to re-deflect sound to the
residential areas. After doing that, the sound level was retested to be sure it
was in compliance. Mr. Dornbach stated that in addition, last spring the storm
water runoff and drainage system was designed. He stated the facility was
purchased with the full knowledge that the entire property was zoned industrial
and they have gone to great expense recently to improve this property.
19.   At this time, Mayor Kriege cautioned council and everyone in attendance
that this was not a public hearing and that all discussion would need to adhere
to the information that was disclosed at the Kenton County & Municipal Planning
& Zoning Commission hearing on June 7, 2001. He also advised council that their
decision regarding this matter would have to be based on the facts from that
meeting and the recommendations made by the Planning Commission.
20.   Mr. Gabbard asked if there were reports from the consultants that
performed the improvements. Mr. Dornbach stated they have the reports and
advised the environmental engineer was unable to attend this meeting. He stated
that studies were conducted at different times of day to pinpoint the
improvement needs. Mr. Gabbard asked if the wooded area would be removed to
relocate the parking area. Mr. Dornbach stated the woods would remain as a
greenbelt barrier as recommended by the KC&MP&Z Commission. He stated the plan
is to relocate the parking lot to the rear of the property and add on to the
front of the building. Mr. Dupps asked if the zone change request was made in
order to install the parking lot. Mr. Dornbach stated there were two reasons
for the zone change request, the first being that the property needs to be the
appropriate zone and the second was to construct the parking lot.
21.   Mr. Dornbach added that he feels this proposed plan would adequately
control the current water runoff situation. There was a brief discussion with
Mr. Kudera and Mr. Ellison relating to the solution that would best correct the
drainage problem. Mr. Ellison felt that putting drain tiles into the nearby
creek were not the best solution and that a retention pond should be
constructed. Mr. Dornbach stated that the drain plan was submitted and approved
by the Planning Commission. He stated that when the new parking lot is built
they would be able to design a better retention area by converting the pond to
counteract the drainage.
22.   Mr. Jeff Neal, 3422 Bottomwood Drive, Erlanger, Ky. addressed council to
voice opposition to LSI’s zone change request. He stated that he could point
out information that could have changed the KC&MP&Z Commission’s decision.
Mayor Kriege cautioned Mr. Neal that he could not introduce any information
that was not heard at the Planning Commission’s public hearing. Mr. Neal
informed council that the LSI facility is surrounded by residential properties
with three hundred homes in the area. He expressed doubt regarding the sound
studies and the credentials of the professionals who conducted the studies. Mr.
Neal brought blueprints and photos to share with council, but Mayor Kriege
advised him that if these were not submitted at the KC&MP&Z Commission’s
meeting then council could not consider them. Mr. Neal stated that he was not
allowed to speak at the meeting. Mr. Walker explained council’s situation to
Mr. Neal and advised him that the city cannot help that the Planning Commission
would not hear his debate over this matter. Mr. Walker went on to inform Mr.
Neal that he can challenge LSI’s expert’s opinion, but that council cannot hear
information that did not transpire at the public meeting held by the Planning
Commission. Mayor Kriege would not permit review of the photos Mr. Neal
presented as the public hearing was a month ago and the photos were taken
yesterday. The photos showed water damage to his property due to the runoff
water from the LSI property. He stated that he feels the addition of a parking
lot will increase the water drainage problem.
23.   Mr. Neal’s other complaint was the sound level from the LSI facility,
which he claims awakens his children at night. Councilman Gabbard stated that
this manufacturing plant has been at this location for the past 30-50 years.
Mr. Neal stated that the facility now has three shifts of workers and they are
constantly expanding operations. Mr. Gabbard reasoned that since the plant has
maintained this location for such a long period of time that it would be unfair
to chastise them for growth especially since they provide an economic base for
the community. Mr. Neal felt that there has to be a limit and suggested that
LSI move to another section of the Industrial Park, as there are other
locations available.
24.   Mr. Neal maintained that if council approves this zone change the result
would be a water runoff problem to surrounding properties. He asked if LSI or
the city was willing to provide written confirmation they would correct any
situation that should arise.
25.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to table discussion and action of this zone
change until the Planning & Zoning Committee could review and make a
recommendation to council at the next council meeting. Mr. Ellison seconded the
motion. Further discussion ensued.
26.   Mr. Dornbach expressed his frustration that council would consider
tabling this request. He reiterated that all plans submitted to the Planning
Commission have been reviewed and approved. He also suggested that since the
city has a ‘noise ordinance’ they should be cited and fined if they are in
violation of this law, which he does not feel they are as their records
indicate they are within the law. He went on to say the Independence facility
is not equipped to handle additional workload without the needed expansion,
thereby sending extra business to the Blue Ash plant.
27.   Mr. Gabbard advised that the council would like to make a decision that
would be beneficial to everyone. Mr. Dupps commented that the summary of the
evidence and testimony presented by the opponents and proponents states the
summary is “believed to be accurate but has not been reviewed or approved by
the Commission.” Mayor Kriege stated that is a summary sheet of the KC&MP&Z
Commission’s public hearing. Mr. Barbian stated he believes it has been
approved or it wouldn’t be before the council. Mr. Gabbard stated there is
probably now available a better summary or transcript.
28.   Mr. Moriconi stated that he would prefer not to table this matter as he
doesn’t think there will be any changes in the next few weeks, and he didn’t
want to see it delayed for another month. Mr. Kudera agreed. He commented that
he sees this is frustrating for the business and while he sympathizes with the
residents he is not in favor of tabling this matter.
29.   At this time a roll call vote was taken and answered with four no votes
cast by Mr. Kudera, Mr. Moriconi, Mr. Bushong and Mr. Dupps and two yes votes
cast by Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard. The motion to table this rezoning matter
was defeated 4-2 in favor.
30.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve the zone change requested by LSI
Industries for an approximate 4.3 acre area located along the east side of
Turkeyfoot Road from R-1B to IP based on the KC&MP&Z Commission’s
recommendations. Mr. Bushong seconded the motion. Roll call vote was answered
with 4 yes votes and 2 no votes cast by Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard. Mr.
Gabbard commented that he felt the city’s Planning & Zoning Committee should
review this matter before approving the request. Motion carried 4-2 in favor of
the zone change.
Resolution No. 2001-R-07 – Approving Payment of CDBG Monthly Expenses for the
Senior Center
31.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Bushong, there was a reading
of Resolution No. 2001-R-07 approving the payment of monthly expenses totaling

carried 6-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance –Pay Plan & Classification – 1st Reading
32.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance adopting a pay plan and classification. Mr. Kudera seconded the
motion. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance by
title and summary.
Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
33.   Mr. Wendling reported that the four bids received for the construction of
the Memorial Park Amphitheatre ranged from $284,000 to $487,000. He advised the
total funding allocated for this project is $286,000 and was received from the
Kentucky Department of Local Government ($200,000), R.C. Durr ($75,000),
Cinergy ($5,000) and interest income ($6,000). Mr. Wendling stated that to date
the city has spent $30,000 in architect and engineering fees leaving a balance
of $256,000 for the construction. He advised that since the lowest bid exceeds
the amphitheatre account balance by $28,000 he recommended that council reject
all bids, review the project then re-bid. Mayor Kriege commented that the bids
were higher than anticipated and the lowest bid at $28,000 more than budgeted
could climb even higher if change orders emerge during the construction. Mr.
Moriconi stated that he would like to see the achievement of this project, as
it will be a unique attraction for the city. He stated he would like to see the
project modified so that the city can proceed. Mr. Wendling stated he would
work with the architect to this end and felt confident that modifications could
be accomplished without compromising the overall design. Mr. Bushong questioned
whether deleting one of the restrooms would be cost effective. Mr. Wendling
stated it would only save about $1,000. Mayor Kriege asked if the project was
bid at prevailing wage. Mr. Wendling replied that the bids did not include
prevailing wage. Mr. Walker stated that legally the city couldn’t accept these
bids if they are not prevailing wage.
34.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to reject all four bids received for the
construction of the Memorial Park Amphitheatre and to review the project in
order to keep the construction cost under the budgeted amount of $256,000. Mr.
Gabbard seconded the motion. Mr. Moriconi asked if this project had to be
completed by a certain date. Mr. Wendling replied that the city has until 2002
to construction the amphitheatre. Mr. Dupps asked what the architects’ time
frame was. Mr. Wendling replied that they would like to rebid within one month.
Mayor Kriege advised that new bids would probably be presented to council at
the September meeting. Mr. Dupps asked if the restrooms could be added later.
Mr. Wendling stated that alternate bids could be included in the bid packet so
that portions could be rejected in order to meet budget. There being no further
discussion, roll call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0 in
favor of rejecting all bids.

Discussion of Contract with Building Inspector for Zoning & Other Related
Services
57.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to approve the proposed contract, with the
deletion of section 2 (c), with Mr. Kevin Barbian for building inspection and
other related services. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. A brief discussion
ensued. Mr. Gabbard stated he did not feel the city should compensate Mr.
Barbian to attend council and committee meetings. Mr. Moriconi asked if council
really wanted to eliminate Mr. Barbian’s needed presence at the meetings. Mr.
Kudera asked who would determine if Mr. Barbian’s presence would be needed. Mr.
Wendling stated that he or the mayor would make that decision. Mr. Ellison felt
that all zoning related matters should be directed to Mr. McAllister of the
NKAPC. Mr. Barbian stated that it is easier to assist Mr. McAllister in many
matters as he is in the city office every day. Mr. Gabbard stated that over the
course of one year the city would be paying an additional $2,000 to $3,000 for
Mr. Barbian’s services. Mayor Kriege advised council that if they did not agree
to compensate Mr. Barbian $20/hour to assist in zoning related matters that
there will be a void in services that he is now providing for free. Mr. Gabbard
stated that if there is enough work for an in-house zoning administrator then
the city should hire a full time employee for this job.
58.   Roll call was taken at this time and was answered with three yes votes
and three no votes cast by Mr. Kudera, Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Bushong. Mayor
Kriege broke the tie by casting a no vote. The motion was defeated 4-3.
59.   Mr. Kudera commented that he felt the council was being pennywise and
pound-foolish by not wanting to pay for necessary services. Mayor Kriege
suggested that the agenda format be amended so that the contracted personnel
could report at the beginning of the meetings and leave afterward. Mr. Dupps
suggested that section 2 (c) be amended to compensate Mr. Barbian $20.00 per
hour for performing zoning-related matters and delete the same compensation for
attendance at meetings.
60.   Upon motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Kudera, section two (c) of the
proposed contract with Kevin Barbian would be amended to delete compensation
for attendance at council/committee meetings while keeping the wordage to
compensate him at the rate of $20.00 per hour for performing zoning-related
matters. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and two no votes cast by
Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.
Adjournment
61.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Gabbard the meeting was
adjourned. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting closed at 10:10 p.m.

AUGUST 6, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:03 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard,
Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance was City
Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the July 2, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to accept the minutes of the regular council
meeting of July 2, 2001, as submitted. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Presentation of Proclamations
3.   Mayor Kriege announced that the city was prepared to present proclamations
to Hometown Pizza and Century 21 Garner Properties to acknowledge the recent
improvements made to their buildings in the downtown area. Since a
representative was not yet present from each company, the mayor moved on with
the agenda.
Senior Center Board of Directors
4.   Mayor Kriege introduced Phil Turner and Kurt Keeney, members of the Senior
Center Board of Directors and advised council they would give an update of the
activities of the Board.
5.   Mr. Turner addressed council regarding the Capital Campaign Fund Drive
that has been launched in an effort to raise $100,000. These funds will be used
to furnish the kitchen area of the Senior Center with commercial grade
appliances and equipment, as well as tables and chairs. Mr. Turner stated that
to date they have received $16,500 in donations. He stated that they will
accept donations on a three year commitment. In addition to the Capital
Campaign Fund Drive, he stated the Board of Directors is commencing a
membership campaign. Mr. Turner stated that membership dues is $12.00 per
person per year. He stated that while membership is encouraged, no one will be
turned away and that sponsorships will be available. He stated that this would
provide annual support for the facility and encouraged the council members to
obtain membership. He informed council that the Board is also seeking corporate
donations who will be recognized at different levels based on the amount of
funding contributed by the corporation.
6.   Mr. Kurt Keeney informed council that all local business that have been
approached to donate to the Center have provided positive response and shows
there is a lot of support for this Center in the business community. He stated
that Donna Yeager is the chairman of the membership campaign.
7.   Mr. Kudera asked if the entire $100,000 would be used for kitchen
equipment. Mr. Turner stated that after the kitchen is equipped the remaining
funds would be used to purchase other furniture, office equipment, etc. Mr.
Moriconi stated he felt it was important that the residents understand that all
citizens will operate this facility as a Senior and Community Center for use.
Mr. Turner stated that for funding purposes the facility is now being referred
to as a Senior Center, but that future activities will encompass a multi-
generational community.
8.   In closing, Mr. Turner voiced appreciation for Mr. Wendling’s support and
guidance to the Board of Directors.
Discussion of the Defunct Hunters’ Green Homeowners Association and the Common
Grounds
9.   Ms. Tammy Dorgan, 3917 Gunstock Court, addressed council regarding the
lake behind her property that is the ‘common green space area’ originally owned
and maintained by the Hunters’ Green Homeowners Association that went defunct
many years ago.
10.   Ms. Dorgan stated that when she purchased her house a few years ago that
the lake was very picturesque and was an attraction that encouraged her to
purchase this particular home. But over the years she stated the depth of the
water has decreased and the little remaining water has become stagnant causing
both a health and safety concern. Ms. Dorgan stated she has contacted both the
Health Department and the E.P.A. to assist in resolving this matter, only to
have both agencies tell her to go to the city for help. She stated that she was
here, along with some other neighbors, to ask council to make the necessary
repairs to restore the lake to its’ original condition. She distributed photos
of the lake area for council to review.
11.   Mayor Kriege expressed his appreciation to Ms. Dorgan and the others in
attendance regarding this matter for taking the time to present their concern
to council. He stated that he would have the City Engineer and City
Administrator to investigate the matter.
12.   Mr. Wendling, City Administrator, referred council to a letter from the
city engineer in their council packets. He stated that the engineer’s
inspection revealed that the pond is on private property (owned by the former
Hunters Green Subdivision Homeowners Association) and that the water level of
he pond appears to have been about eight feet higher than the current level.
The engineer also reports that a dam on the north side of he pond has broken
and there is a large notch eroded in the dam. The report also reveals that a
vertical pipe extends about eight feet above the water level that used to be
the outlet for the water from the pond. Mr. Wendling advised that the engineer
believes that the majority of the decrease in water depth is a result of the
dam eroding away. It is also believed that the construction of the Apple Valley
Drive apartments caused some sedimentation in the pond, which also increased
the amount of storm water into the pond thus resulting in the dam eroding at a
faster pace.
13.   Mr. Wendling informed council that the developer (from Houston, Texas) of
the Hunters Green Subdivision is no longer in business. He stated that in his
discussions with the city attorney, he learned that the only way to revive the
Homeowners’ Association would be by court order. He expressed his concern for
the city’s liability if council would decide to go onto this private property
to make repairs. He cautioned council to be certain what, if any, action they
wanted to take regarding this situation. In closing, he stated that the
maintenance of this ‘common area’ in this subdivision seems to recur on a
regular basis and that he recommended council to bring closure to the matter.
14.   Mayor Kriege asked the City Engineer, Dave Whitacre, for his input. Mr.
Whitacre gave a brief overview of his inspection of the pond area, which lies
in a common area listed as Common Area H at the rear of lots 140 through 145
and part of lot 146 (3913 thru 3917 Gunstock Court) in the Hunters Green
Subdivision. He stated that when the homeowners association went defunct there
was no one in charge of maintenance and the areas gradually became a marsh area
with debris.
15.   Mr. Whitacre suggested two options that could be put in place to maintain
the area. The first option would be to breech the dam completely which would
provide some storm water detention and the second option would be to repair the
dam and install an overflow pipe. He informed council that these repairs would
probably be in the area of $10,000. Engineering design would be an extra
expense. He also mentioned that the pond could revert into a weedy open field
Mr. Whitacre advised council that no easements exist for the city and that the
city has no investment or right to be on the property.
16.   Ms. Dorgan stated she would hate to see the pond filled in but if that is
the only option they would approve it. She expressed concern that no one is
responsible for this land and that that is the bigger problem.
17.   Mayor Kriege stated that the bigger issue for the city is stepping onto
property that is privately owned. City Attorney, Lawson Walker advised that
this is not in the city’s jurisdiction, especially regarding the health
concerns, which is clearly the responsibility of the Health Department. He went
on to say that he has advised the city that they will be liable if they take
over maintenance of the property and has advised against it. Mayor Kriege
suggested fixing the dam on the pond and then conveying the property over to
the abutting property owners. Mr. Walker advised that the city couldn’t convey
land it doesn’t own. Mayor Kriege suggested condemning the land. Mr. Walker
advised that condemnation would be an option, but a costly option for the city.
He stated he would have to research the property title in order to further
advise on that. Mr. Gabbard stated that in 1995-96 the city attorney at that
time researched this matter and suggested searching city records for the
findings of that research. Mr. Ellison suggested another alternative; allowing
the city attorney to provide legal advise to the residents in the subdivision
in order to revive the homeowners association. Mr. Walker stated that the
residents could not be forced to join the homeowners association unless this
was a provision of the covenant documents. He stated he is not an expert, but
there is probably very little leverage to force this.
18.   Ms. Dorgan said that she might consider a homeowners association but
agreed that others can’t be forced to join. She also was concerned how a
homeowners association would recover common area land that had been taken over
by adjoining property owners to extend their yard.
19.   Mrs. Dorgan appealed to council to breech the dam. She stated that she
feared she would not be able to sell her house with the abutting pond that has
become an eyesore and safety hazard.
20.   Mr. Kudera voiced his concern for the property owners dilemma and
suggested that the abutting residents share the $10,000 estimate (by the city
engineer) to make the necessary repairs to the pond. He stated that at roughly
$1,880 per resident, this would be a reasonable amount in order to maintain
their property values. Mr. Kudera went on to say that he could not consent to
the city taking on this maintenance and liability. He stated that the property
owners should make the necessary repairs and then take over the property since
there is no one to contest this action. He stated that the city would be
establishing a precedent if they agreed to go onto this private property to
make the repairs, thus making the city liable. He stated this would not be fair
to the rest of the city.
21.   Ms. Dorgan stated that she just assumed the property behind her was
public property and knows now that was a wrong assumption. Mr. Ellison
commented that this subdivision was developed before it was annexed into the
city. Mayor Kriege commented that he would like to help but that the liability
is a major issue for the city to consider.
22.   Mr. Bushong commented that the Beechgrove Homeowners Association spends
about $81,000 per year for the upkeep of the Beechgrove lakes. He stated that
he fears Ms. Dorgan will not get resident support to revive the homeowners
association, but suggested she check plats, etc. to see what area is ‘common’
before moving forward with the idea. Mr. Bushong went on to say that he is very
concerned with this situation but shares equal concern regarding the liability
for the city. He stated he would be in favor of helping in some way. Discussion
centered on suggestions to fill in the lake without hindering the residents
downstream with storm water runoff.
23.   Mr. Gabbard stated his awareness of the serious situation with this pond,
but that in terms of the city’s liabilities and amount of funds for the needed
repairs, felt the city was not in a position to assist the residents. He also
suggested the city would be setting a precedent, especially in light of the
current developments in the city that have planned homeowners associations to
maintain the common area in the subdivision. He feared that if those
associations also go defunct, they too, would look to the city to maintain the
common areas.
24.   Mr. Walker stated there area laws to solve this situation, one of which
is called ‘adverse possession’. But he stated that these type of legal
processes are very expensive and time consuming with the value of the land
added to their property much less than the cost of the legal proceedings to
acquire it. He stated that another big concern with condemnation by the city
would be the flow of the water after the pond is repaired. The city would then
be liable to any damage to the property owners downstream. He stated the flow
of water would need to be studied and evaluated by the city engineer prior to
any repairs.
25.   Mr. Ellison voiced empathy for the resident’s dilemma, but expressed
reservations with using tax dollars to make repairs on private property.
26.   Mr. Ken Ziegler, 3911 Gunstock Court, addressed council. He stated the
pond is not holding water. He also shared the same concerns of Ms. Dorgan
regarding the health and safety issues.
27.   Mr. Kudera stated that he was inclined to make a motion to split the
$10,000 repair estimate with the residents in order to begin the process of
correcting this problem, as this is an issue that is been ongoing for some
time. He reiterated his feeling that the residents would need to help fund this
repairs in order to maintain their own property values. He stated that he feels
this would be a fair compromise with the residents while keeping the city free
of liability.
28.   Mr. Walker stated that the city may be able to seek liability indemnity
from these residents but can’t insulate liability from third parties and
advised the city could be left ‘holding the bag’ if these repairs are done
under the backing of the city. He restated that this pond is on private
property.
29.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to offer the Hunters Green Subdivision residents
$5,000.000 to be used to research a solution to making repairs to the pond
adjoining some of the properties on Gunstock Court. Mr. Dupps seconded the
motion. Discussion on the motion ensued. Mr. Gabbard asked if this $5,000 would
be used for engineering fees. Mr. Kudera stated that was not part of the
motion. Mr. Gabbard asked if contributing these funds would hold the city
liable. Mr. Walker affirmed that this could bring potential liability to the
city.
30.   Mr. Whitacre suggested tabling a decision on this matter for a month so
that he can prepare cost estimates and report back at the September council
meeting. Mr. Gabbard stated that he would agree to that but that the city
doesn’t have funds to appropriate to private property. Mr. Kudera requested
that his motion be brought to a vote to see what the consensus of council was.
Mr. Moriconi stated he would like more engineering information before voting to
allocate $5,000 to this venture. Mr. Gabbard questioned where the city would
take money for this in this year’s budget. Mr. Wendling again cautioned council
that they will be setting a precedent by allocating money for maintenance on
private property and that other groups will expect the same consideration. Mr.
Dupps suggested that recent repairs made on Holten Drive were similar in being
that the property was private. Mayor Kriege remarked that repairs made to
Holten Drive was not private property but a public right of way.
31.   At this time roll call was taken on Mr. Kudera’s motion and Mr. Dupps
second to contribute $5,000 toward finding a solution to the pond behind
Gunstock Court. Roll call was answered with five no votes and one yes vote cast
by Mr. Dupps. Motion failed 5-1 opposing.
32.   Mayor Kriege asked council if there was support to table this matter
until the September meeting, as suggested by the City Engineer, when Mr.
Whitacre will return to council with his recommendations.
33.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Bushong the matter was
tabled for a month until the city engineer returns to council with his
recommendations. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving LSI Industries Map Amendment for Zone Change –
1st Reading
34.   Upon motion by Mr. Gabbard and second by Mr. Moriconi there was a first
reading of the proposed ordinance to rezone 4.3 acres along the east side of
Turkeyfoot Road between Industrial road and Bottomwood Drive from R-1B to IP.
No roll call; motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance.
35.   There was a brief discussion on the wording in this ordinance. Mr.
Ellison stated that the wording was a little suggestive that Bottomwood Drive
was rezoned. Mr. Walker stated that the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission supplied this definition for the ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving Fischer Homes (Sycamore Creek Subd) Map
Amendment for Zone Change – 1st Reading
36.   Upon motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Bushong there was a first
reading of the proposed ordinance rezoning an approximate seventy-seven acre
tract located along the east side of Fowler Creek Road between Senour Road and
Cox Road from R-1A and R-1C to R-1D. Motion carried with all ayes and Mr.
Walker read the proposed ordinance.
37.   A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Gabbard raised concerns about a timeline
for the installation of the turn lane on Fowler Creek Road. He wondered if the
Kentucky Highway Standards mandated a completion date for this condition of the
development. Mr. Walker stated that it does not state specifically when the
turn lane is to be installed. Mr. Gabbard stated that he felt the city needed
to address this detail of the development and suggested the turn lane be
completed by the time the first house is constructed. Mr. Walker advised that
this condition could be specified in the ordinance and made the revision.
38.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to amend the first reading of the proposed
ordinance for this rezoning to include this provision. Mr. Bushong seconded the
motion. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes and Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance. Ms. Elizabeth Horowitz, legal counsel for Grand Communities
Ltd. (Fischer Homes) requested that the wording of the ordinance be revised to
state that the turn lane be installed before the Certificate of Occupancy is
issued on the first house constructed. Mr. Gabbard hesitated to consider that
as he felt several other houses could be built even though the first house had
not sold. Ms. Horowitz argued that additional traffic would not be generated if
there were no occupants in the newly constructed houses. Mr. Gabbard stated the
city needed to have a definitive time for the turn lane. Mr. Dupps stated that
the issuance of a Certificate of Occupancy is a definite time frame. Mr.
Moriconi concurred. Mr. Gabbard agreed to amend his motion to state the turn
lane shall be completely constructed and operational prior to the issuance of
the Certificate of Occupancy for the first house constructed. Roll call was
answered with six yes votes in favor. Motion carried and Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance with the amendment.
Award Bid for Phase II of the Holten Drive Repair Project
39.   City Engineer, Dave Whitacre reported that the low bidder of the Holten
Drive Repair Project was JPS Construction at a total cost of $134,820.00, which
was proposed in May. He stated that JPS has agreed to extend the bid price
beyond the ninety-day term for Phase II, which was bid at $79,042.50. He
advised the other bidders of the Phase II were Michels Paving, Quast Paving &
Sealing and Barrett Paving. He stated Michels Paving submitted the lowest bid
for Phase II at $76,795.00, but that the overall lowest bid for the entire
project was by JPS Construction. Mr. Whitacre stated that it was difficult to
make a recommendation to award this bid due to the uncertainty of the amount of
asphalt that will be needed. He stated that for bid purposes it was estimated
that 350 yards of concrete work would be required but that this amount could
change. Mr. Dupps asked if he was satisfied with the work performed on Phase I
by JPS Construction. Mr. Whitacre stated that the work was satisfactory,
although he fire hydrant has not been relocated yet as they are waiting for a
wet tap. Mr. Bushong questioned the contingency bid items. Mr. Whitacre
explained that the unit price bidding is based on the estimate of 610 tons,
which is the only fair way to bid this type project. He stated that if you hold
a “not to exceed price” then the contractors up their bid price by twenty
percent or put down thinner layers of asphalt.
40.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to award the Phase II bid of the Holten Drive
Repair Project to Michels Paving and authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into this
contract. Mr. Bushong seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all
ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
OTHER OLD BUSINESS

Mayor Kriege stated this will be reviewed and a written response will be

hydrants in the Troopers Crossing development off of Cody Road. He stated that

Mayor Kriege advised the city would look into this matter and report back.

regarding her water drainage problem on her property (640 Willow Drive). Mr.

Approval of a Master Lease-Purchase Agreement with Fifth Third Bank for Ten
Cruisers
45.   Mr. Wendling informed council that the police department has acquired the
ten vehicles that will replace some of the aging and leased vehicles. He stated
that the city has saved $7,000 by purchasing the vehicles now instead of
waiting until the spring. Chief Butler reminded council that the purchase of
these ten vehicles was included in the current budget. He added that Fifth
Third Bank requires the execution of a Lease-Purchase Agreement to complete the
necessary paperwork for the financing at a rate of 4.5% interest. Mr. Gabbard
asked how much was financed and for how long. Chief Butler advised that the ten
vehicles were purchased with the city making an annual payment of $72,000 for
three years.
46.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into a master
lease-purchase agreement with Fifth Third Bank to finance the purchase of the
ten vehicles for the police department. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance Amending Ordinance 1994-O-18A Regarding the Fowler Creek
Sewer Debt Reduction – 1st Reading
47.   Mr. Kudera made a motion made a motion to have a first reading of the
proposed ordinance to amend Ordinance 1994-O-18A regarding the collection of
the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt Reduction assessment. Mr. Moriconi seconded the
motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Gabbard stated that he had between 3-
5 callers that voiced concern regarding the payment being made to the city on
an annual basis instead of the quarterly payment to the Sanitation District.
Mr. Bushong stated he also had a few calls. Mr. Wendling explained the city
would continue to work with residents that have difficulty paying a lump sum
payment. He advised council that billing this assessment quarterly would be
costly for the city in terms of updating computer software, postage and staff
labor. Mr. Ellison expressed his concern that payment of the $280 annual
assessment at the end of the year would be cumbersome for some residents. Mrs.
Taney, City Clerk assured council that the city would assist individual
residents who request additional time to make this payment, as has been
provided in the past with other water and sewer assessments. No roll call;
motion carried with all ayes and Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Setting the Trash Assessment Rate for 2001 at $91.16 per
Unit – 1st Reading
48.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Gabbard there was a first
reading of the proposed ordinance setting the trash assessment rate at $91.16
per mobile home and residential unit for the year 2001. No roll call; motion
carried with all ayes. Mayor Kriege stated the proposed rate is up roughly
$2.00 over last year’s rate. He also advised council that the city is in the
last year of a five-year contract with Rumpke. He stated this contract would
need to be re-bid before it expires the end of April 2002. Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance by title only.
Resolution No. 2001-R-09 – Entering an Interlocal Agreement with the Northern

49.   Mayor Kriege presented to council a proposed resolution that would
authorize him to sign an agreement for improvements by and between the city and
the Northern Kentucky Water District for the reconstruction of Beechgrove
