street project.
50.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to read Resolution No. 2001-R-09 that would
authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into an agreement with the Water District for

roll called; motion carried with all ayes and Mr. Walker read the resolution.
51.   Mr. Ellison requested the repairs be completed before the cold weather
arrives.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2001/02 Budget Ordinance – 1st Reading
52.   Mr. Wendling presented to council an ordinance that would amend the
current budget Ordinance No. 2001-O-05. He explained that the city has
experienced some expenses early in this fiscal year, which were expected to be
paid out of the 2000/01 budget. Many expenses and projects were estimated to be
paid and/or completed in June. He cited the Senior Center construction and
lights in the park as two projects that were not completed in June. He also
stated that the budget needs to be amended to include the $50,000 T-21 grant
the city has received to construct sidewalks along a section of Madison Pike,
from Hartland Subdivision to Walnut Hall Drive. Mayor Kriege advised that most
of these changes are basically a re-appropriation of funds from last year’s
budget to this year’s budget.
53.   Mr. Gabbard questioned why the change orders for the construction of the
Senior Center have been so high. He felt these things should have been in the
original bid. Mr. Wendling stated that changes have been architectural in
nature and not construction changes. He stated that contractor submitted the
bid according to specs. He stated there have been several code issues that were
missed by the architect. Mr. Gabbard suggested the architect pay for the change
orders if there were flaws with the design. He stated he understand the city
has to build to code but that these expensive change orders are hard on the
city budget. Mayor Kriege stated that it would be desirable to have a capital
project without change orders, but to expect that would be unrealistic. He
stated that architects couldn’t guarantee that every item will not be
overlooked.
54.   Mr. Ellison asked if the city had money in the budget to match the
$50,000 grant funds received for the sidewalks. Mr. Wendling stated the city
only had to match $20,000. Mayor Kriege advised the city could pay the cost of
‘in kind’ services, such as engineering fees, etc. for the balance. Mr. Bushong
asked when the sidewalks would be installed. Mr. Wendling stated the city would
soon begin the process to request the funds, have the bid specs drafted then
advertise for bids.
55.   Mr. Ellison asked if additional change orders for the Senior Center were
expected. Mayor Kriege and Mr. Wendling replied that they hoped not.
56.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Ellison to have a first
reading of the proposed ordinance to amend the 2001/02 budget. Roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 in favor and Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance.
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT – Mark T. Wendling
57.   Award of Bid for Asphalt Overlays on Beechgrove Drive and Roselawn Drive
- Mr. Wendling referred council to the Calendar of Events he submitted in his
written report. He reported that bids have been received for the 2001/02 street
reconstruction and overlay projects. Mr. Whitacre presented a tabulation sheet
of the bids received for the asphalt maintenance and the concrete
reconstruction projects. He stated the that two bids were received for the
asphalt overlays on Beechgrove Drive and Roselawn Drive; Paul Michels & Sons in
the amount of $70,646.00 and Barrett Paving in the amount of $72,488.60. Mr.
Wendling advised council that Beechgrove Drive badly needs the repairs and
recommended awarding the bid for the asphalt repairs so that the contractor
could move quickly on this project.
58.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into a
contract with Paul Michels & Sons for the asphalt overlay repairs on Beechgrove
Drive and Roselawn Drive in the amount of $70,646.00. Mr. Ellison seconded the
motion. Mr. Ellison asked Mr. Whitacre if he thought the blacktop fiberglass
was beneficial on overlay projects. Mr. Whitacre stated that the material keeps
water from getting into the joints and that sometimes he recommends this
material be used, but eventually the material will develop small cracks,
generally within a year or two. Mr. Ellison asked if he thought it would be
worthwhile to spend an additional $12,000 to install the material on Beechgrove
Drive. Mr. Whitacre stated that would be difficult to determine, as it might
help, but felt it may not be worth the added expense on this particular street
with only a single overly. Mr. Whitacre added that he did not feel the material
would benefit Roselawn Drive. At this time roll call was taken and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 in favor of awarding the asphalt repairs to
Paul Michels & Sons in the amount of $70,646.00
59.   Mr. Wendling recommended that council delay awarding the concrete repairs
for Adahi Drive and Rickey Lane until the second reading of the amended 2001/
02-budget ordinance when the funds will be available. Mayor Kriege stated that
a special council meeting may be scheduled later this month and asked the clerk
to poll the council for a date that would be available for the council members.
Mr. Gabbard stated that he would be unavailable beyond next week.
60.   Update on Feasibility Study for Municipal Buildings – Mr. Wendling
reported that the scope of the project has changed due to cost concerns at the
proposed construction sites. He stated that Matrix Architects has been asked to
extend the scope, which will require the city to contribute another $2,500
toward the investment in this project. He recommended that council support this
additional expense and advised the funds could be expended from the Building
Fund. Mayor Kriege advised the completed feasibility study should be ready to
present to the Building Committee later this month with a presentation to the
entire council at the September meeting.
61.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to approve a change order approving an
additional $2,500 in expenses to complete the feasibility study for municipal
buildings. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with four
yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried
4-2 in favor.
62.   Police Department Command Restructure – Mr. Wendling asked Chief Butler
to address council regarding his proposal for a command restructure of the
police department. Chief Butler advised that he had spoken individually with
each council member.
63.   Geneva Wade Property, 640 Willow Drive – Mayor Kriege asked for an update
on the inspection of Mrs. Wade’s property. Mr. Wendling stated that he, along
with Mr. Whitacre and Mr. Smith of the Public Works Department inspected the
property on August 1, 2001, as well as reviewed videotapes taken on the
property before construction. Mr. Wendling stated there is some questions on
the condition of the rear property before construction began. He stated that
Ms. Wade also claims that the repeated overlays of the street have raised the
pavement above the level of her driveway, which has added to the drainage
problems. Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Whitacre what course of action he recommended.
Mr. Whitacre stated that he would bring a full report to the September meeting
that will include construction plans, etc. Mr. Wendling stated the report would
also include inspection of the street that may have been raised.
64.   Mr. Art Ziegler, 636 Willow Drive stated that he is a neighbor of Ms.
Wades’ for the past 1-1/2 years. He reiterated Ms. Wade’s claim that the city
engineer inspected the property last year and advised that a natural spring had
been hit. He stated that his property also has a ten-foot by twenty-foot swampy
area that is a breeding ground for mosquitoes and a health and safety concern
for his small children. He stated he has a videotape of the drainage problem
during a rainstorm. He suggested the city finding a solution to diverting the
water. Mayor Kriege stated the city would look at last year documents to see if
there is a report of a natural spring being hit. Ms. Wade stated she was not
aware of springs in the area before the sewer pipes were installed. Mr. Gabbard
commented that there are natural springs all over the city. Mr. Wendling stated
that the pre-construction video reveals the area on Ms. Wade’s property was
overgrown. Ms. Wade disputed Mr. Wendling’s assertion and stated he must have
looked at the wrong property. Mayor Kriege suggested presenting a viewing of
the video at the September meeting. He advised Ms. Wade that the city may not
give her the answer she is looking for but that the city will provide her with
a definite response in an effort to settle this matter. Mr. Ziegler stated that
they just wanted the city to return the property to it’s original condition and
get the water diverted. He stated that easements were provided to the city so
the city should fix this area. Mayor Kriege advised the city would fix it only
if it has been determined that the city is responsible for the problem. He
advised Mr. Ziegler that the city would not make repairs on private property
unless the city council deems the city is responsible. Mr. Ziegler asked if the
council would view his videotape that was filmed showing the water runoff
during a rainstorm. Mayor Kriege stated the city would view that tape along
with the pre-construction video at next month’s meeting.

AUGUST 21, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the special meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the
Independence Fire District Station #1. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps,
Jim Ellison, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Council Member
Ike Gabbard were absent. Also in attendance was City Administrator, Mark T.
Wendling and City Attorney, Jeffrey S. Smith sitting in for H. Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was to
discuss and take action on the following agenda items:
§   Proposed ordinance approving the LSI Industries map amendment
§   Proposed ordinance approving Fischer Homes (Sycamore Creek Subd.) map
amendment
§   Proposed ordinance setting the trash assessment rate for 2001
§   Proposed ordinance amending Ordinance No. 1994-O-18A regarding the
collection of the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt Reduction assessment
§   Proposed ordinance amending the 2001/02 budget ordinance
§   Proposed ordinance setting the real estate and personal property tax rates
for 2001
§   Proposed ordinance creating the position of Assistant Police Chief
§   Proposed ordinance adopting a Pay Plan and Classification for employees
§   Award the bid for concrete street repairs
§   An executive session
§   Building Inspector’s contract with the city
Ordinance No. 2001-O-08 – Approving a Map Amendment for LSI Industries on
Turkeyfoot Road – 2nd Reading
3.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Bushong there was a second
reading of the proposed ordinance to approve the map amendment for an
approximate area of 4.3 acres along the east side of Turkeyfoot Road changing
the zone from R-1B to IP. Mr. Smith read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Kriege
questioned “Attachment A” which was not attached to the ordinance. The City
Clerk advised that the attachment contained the description of the parcel that
the zone change affected which had not been received by the city yet. Mayor
Kriege advised council they could delay approving this map amendment until the
parcel description is received if they were hesitant to do so without it. Roll
call was answered with four yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Ellison.
Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-09 – Approving Sycamore Creek Subdivision Map Amendment –
2nd Reading
4.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Moriconi there was a second
reading of a proposed ordinance to approve the map amendment changing an
approximate seventy-seven acre area along the east side of Fowler Creek Road
from R-1A and R-1C to R-1D for the development of a subdivision named Sycamore
Creek by Grand Communities, Ltd. (Fischer Homes). There was a brief discussion.
Mr. Ellison questioned the change from R-1A and R-1C. He thought this was an
error. Ms. Elizabeth Horowitz, who was attending the meeting to represent the
interests of Grand Communities, assured Mr. Ellison that the current zone of
the seventy-seven acres was both R-1A and R-1C. Roll call was answered with
five yes votes. Motion carried 5-0 in favor of the map amendment.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-10 – Setting the Trash Assessment Rate for 2001
5.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Dupps for a second reading of
the proposed ordinance to adopt the trash assessment rate for 2001 at $91.16
per residential unit and mobile home. Mr. Moriconi asked what the assessed rate
was for last year. The City Clerk advised that last year’s rate was $89.40 per
unit; an increase of $1.76. Mr. Smith read Ordinance No. 2001-O-10. Roll call
was answered with five yes votes. Motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-11 – Amending Ordinance No. 1994-O-18A Regarding the
Fowler Creek Sewer Debt Reduction Assessment
6.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Moriconi for a second reading
of Ordinance No. 2001-O-11 amending Ordinance No. 1994-O-18A relating to the
collection of the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt Reduction Assessment. During a brief
discussion, Mr. Ellison expressed concern to collecting this assessment on an
annual basis and felt this may be a hardship for some residents to pay the $280
assessment in a lump sum at the end of the year. Mayor Kriege responded that
this change in billing was carefully considered after looking at the lack of
available resources, in limited staff and funds that the city would incur to
continue to bill this on a quarterly basis as the Sanitation District had done
for the city in past years. He stated the city does not currently bill any
charges on a quarterly basis and this would present a burden to the current
staff and add expenses that are not budgeted. He stated that this assessment
could be added to the property owner’s escrow account, which probably fifty
percent or more homeowners maintain. He assured council that amending this
ordinance to adopt an annual billing is not meant to assail the users of this
system. The City Clerk advised that residents who needed special payment
arrangements would be accommodated. Mr. Smith read the proposed ordinance. Roll
call was answered with four yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Ellison.
Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-12 – Amending the 2001//02 Budget
7.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Bushong for a second reading
of the proposed ordinance to amend the 2001/02 Budget. A brief discussion
ensued. Mr. Bushong questioned the increase of $100,000 for the Senior Center
Fund. Mr. Wendling explained the additional funds would cover four items;
$59,000 for change orders in the construction of the Senior building, $15,000
for landscaping that was not included in the budget or bid, transfer of the
remaining construction costs that were anticipated to come out of last year’s
budget, and an extra $26,000 for further change orders or unexpected expenses.
Mr. Bushong asked when the construction of the building would be complete. Mr.
Wendling advised that the building is expected to be finished at the end of
September and that the Senior Board of Directors is planning a Grand Opening
for late October or early November. Mr. Smith read the proposed ordinance. Roll
call was answered with five yes votes. Motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Setting the Real Estate & Personal Property Tax Rates for
2001 – 1st Reading
8.   Mayor Kriege presented a proposed ordinance that would set the tax rates
for 2001 for real estate and personal property. Mr. Ellison questioned the
legality of having a first reading of the proposed ordinance prior to the
publication of a legal notice in the paper regarding the proposed rates. The
City Clerk advised that the legal notice has been sent to the Kentucky Post and
that it will run for two consecutive weeks prior to the public hearing on the
rate as required by the Kentucky Revised Statutes. She stated that the
publication, according to K.R.S., must be prior to adoption of the rate, which
would be on the second reading of the ordinance. Finance Director, Amy
Guenther, read the section of the K.R.S. that pertains to this requirement.
City Attorney, Mr. Smith concurred that the public hearing is required before
the adoption or passage of the ordinance. Mr. Ellison stated that he felt the
public hearing of the rate should occur prior to the first reading of the
ordinance. The City Clerk informed council that historically the public hearing
for the proposed tax rates has been held prior to the second reading of the
ordinance.
9.   Mrs. Guenther presented council with an analysis of the computation of the
proposed tax rates for 2001. She advised the proposed rate for real estate
property is .147 for $100 of assessed value and that the proposed rate for
personal property is .205 for $100 of assesses value. She stated that both
rates are compensating plus four percent. Mrs. Guenther informed council that
last year’s real estate rate was .155 of $100 assessed value and the personal
property rate was .181 of $100 assessed value. Mr. Moriconi commented that the
real estate rate has decreased. Mrs. Guenther stated that the Northern Kentucky
Area Development District figured the rates and she confirmed the calculations.
Mayor Kriege advised the increase in the property values have caused the tax
rate to decrease.
10.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to have a first reading on the proposed tax
rates ordinance; seconded by Mr. Moriconi. No roll call; all ayes. Mr. Smith
read the proposed ordinance. There was a brief discussion regarding the
deadline of November 1 to receive the two percent discount. The City Clerk
advised that due to unforeseen circumstances, the printer would not be able to
ship the tax form mailers that have been ordered until September 28. This will
delay the printing and mailing of the bills to the property owners. Council
discussed this and opted to extend the two percent discount period until
November 16, 2001.
11.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Bushong for the first
reading of the proposed ordinance to set the property tax rates amended Section
III to provide a two percent discount if paid by November 16, 2001. Motion
carried all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Creating Position of Assistant Police Chief – 1st Reading
12.   There was a motion by Mr. Moriconi and second by Mr. Dupps for a first
reading of the proposed ordinance to create the position of Assistant Police
Chief. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Ellison asked if the police budget had
funds to cover this position. Chief Butler stated that funds would be adjusted
within the budget and that additional funds would not be requested to create
this position. Mr. Moriconi stated that he felt the creation of this position
would provide the city with a good backup plan. Mr. Ellison concurred that this
would ensure that someone would always be at the helm when the Chief was not
available. Mr. Dupps agreed this position was needed because currently two
lieutenants are in charge when the Chief is away. Motion carried with all ayes
and Mr. Smith read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Pay Plan & Classification – 1st Reading
13.   There was a motion by Mr. Kudera and a second by Mr. Bushong for a first
reading of a proposed ordinance to adopt an employee pay plan and
classification. No discussion. Motion carried with all ayes and Mr. Smith read
the proposed ordinance.
Award of Bid for Concrete Street Repairs
14.   Mayor Kriege presented council with the bid tabulation for the concrete
street reconstruction project for three streets: Adahi Drive, Rickey Lane and
Roselawn Drive. He stated that two bids were received, one from JPS
Construction and one from Michels, with JPS’s bid being the lowest.
15.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into a
contract with JPS Construction, as the best and lowest bidder, for a total of
$361,534.60 for the concrete street repairs on Adahi Drive, Rickey Lane and
Roselawn Drive. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with five
yes votes. Motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Executive Session
16.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Moriconi council entered
into an executive session for the propose of discussing pending litigation and
the contract with the building inspector in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c)
and K.R.S. 61.810 (g) respectively. Motion carried with all ayes.
17.   Upon motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Moriconi council resumed the
regular meeting. Motion carried with all ayes.
Contract with Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian
18.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to authorize Mayor Kriege to negotiate a new
contract with current Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian and to terminate the
current contract. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Adjournment
19.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Moriconi the meeting was
adjourned at 7:56 p.m.

Presentation of the Facilities Feasibility Study by Matrix Architects

accommodations for the police and administration departments. Mayor Kriege

schematic site plan and building plan. She stated they inspected and evaluated
five possible sites for placement of a municipal building that would house all
administration and police offices. Ms. Keeny advised they are submitting two
distinct building plans to conform to the sites presented. Ms. Keeny reported
that the entire process involved cooperation from the city staff, whom assisted
with programming and presenting possible sites, and commended them for their
sense of thoroughness and vision. She stated the city staff was also fiscally
responsible, as the initial size of the building was 36,000 square feet and was
reduced by 10,000 square feet to make it more affordable.
8.   Ms. Keeny stated the following five sites were considered:
§   Sterling Staggs Park at the site of ball field #1
§   Memorial Park at the Route 17/Madison Pike area (Memorial Park #1)
§   Memorial Park at the site of the playground and shelter building (Memorial
Park #2)
§   Madison Pike near Pelly Road and Patriot Way
§   Madison Pike at the current site of the Administration Building (5247
Madison Pike)
She stated that the site of the current Administration Building was eliminated
early on as it was determined that there is not adequate property at that site.
She stated that this site would require the purchase of additional land. Ms.
Keeny stated that it was also determined that access from the curve on Madison
Pike at that location would be difficult to maneuver. There would be an
additional problem of relocating the offices temporarily, which would be an
added cost to the project, and the temporarily offices would have to meet code.
She stated that further analysis is provided in the report.
9.   Ms. Keeny reported that the Memorial Park/Route 17 site would have
immediate access off of Madison Pike but that due to the natural lay of the
land it would require extensive site work to make it buildable. She stated that
the terrain, which is a deep hole, would be a great disadvantage and that even
with extensive site work the roof of the building would not be much higher than
street level. This site will only accommodate the split-level floor plan.
10.   Ms. Keeny reported that the Pelly Road/Patriot Way site would require
funds to purchase the land and was a little compact. She cited that the
advantage to this site is that it would allow generous parking space but that
it was located in a residential area. She stated this site would accommodate
the split-level building plan and that it was near the Route 17 new lateral
connector road.
11.   Ms. Keeny stated that the Sterling Staggs Park site is currently
dedicated as a ball field and the disadvantage of this site would be the
elimination of this field and the need to reconfigure the playground area. She
stated that the advantages to this site is that the building would face the
incoming traffic into town, which would make for a nice presence, and a
separate entry for the building could be off of Sylvan Drive.
12.   Ms. Keeny stated that their recommended site for a municipal building
would be the Memorial Park Site No. 2, near the new Senior Center building. She
stated this site could accommodate a split-level building design and provide
additional parking for the entire area. She stated that public parking is
presently established in this area so an extension of the current parking lot
could be developed. She stated that this area already has other public
developments. Ms. Keeny stated that the disadvantage to this site would be that
a building would encroach on the existing playground and shelter areas. She
stated that Matrix Architects is proposing the city design a master plan for
Memorial Park that would address the facility needs for the entire park.
13.   In closing her presentation, Ms. Keeny advised council that the cost
estimates to construct a building was developed for each site ranging from
$3,500,000 to $4,000,000. She stated that the most expensive site was Memorial
Park at Route 17 (site #1) and the least expensive site was Staggs Park. She
stated that all analysis is provided in the feasibility report.
14.   Mr. Faulkner stated that they have recommended the Memorial Park site #2
because the split-level floor plan works best for this area and because this is
an ideal site. He stated that the park could become the central focus of a
municipal center, as this will provide the opportunity to develop more features
for the park. Mr. Faulkner stated that the play equipment and shelter at
Memorial Park could be taken apart in sections and relocated to other areas in
the park. He stated that the site of the current city building is the most
dangerous site as it sets on a perilous stretch of Route 17
15.   Mr. Dupps expressed concern with the number of stairwells and restrooms
in the building plans. Ms. Keeny stated that building code dictates the number
of stairwells and restrooms required in a building and that only the number
required by code was designed in the building plans; no more, no less. Mr.
Faulkner added that the square footage and the number of occupants determine
the actual number of fixtures. He stated that the central stairway is a feature
that allows easy access when elevators are in use or nonfunctional due to
maintenance, etc. Ms. Keeny advised that the lobby area size was reduced from
the original plan, but was able to keep it large enough to provide adequate
gathering space for visitors. Mr. Faulkner stated that the lobby should be a
collector’s area before and after council meetings. He stated that overall the
rooms and corridors were reduced by thirty percent from the original plan.
16.   Mr. Charles Deters, who was in the audience, asked if the building has
been designed with future growth in mind. Ms. Keeny stated that a certain
amount of growth has been programmed into the current design as storage areas
can be converted to offices later if needed. Mr. Faulkner stated that most
sites would have to be reviewed to adjust the position of the building to
accommodate future add-ons, but advised that it would be a span of 10-15 years
before an addition would be needed.
17.   Mr. Ellison commented that he felt it was a nice proposal but that he
would need more time to review the study and determine what the city could
afford.
18.   A member of the audience announced that the residents in the area of
Memorial Park do not want this building to be constructed in the park. She
stated that the park is a nice area and suggested the city locate a building
somewhere else in the city. Ms. Keeny responded that provisions could be made
for the relocation of the football field with the possibility of regrading to
improve the field.
19.   Mr. Faulkner advised that a master plan for the park would make Memorial
Park more livable and useable for all residents. He stated that while most
parks in general are devoted to one use that multiuse parks are more
successful. He stated that with the firehouse, Senior Center and a planned
amphitheatre the area will take on a campus type atmosphere. He advised the
current drainage problem near the football field would be corrected with the
regrading of the field. He stated there is no attempt to displace or exclude
this sport but rather to enhance the park overall. He stated that only a small
section of the twenty-six acre park is being utilized and that currently there
are no other access points to the rest of the acreage. He stated that a master
plan for the park could design those linkages with facilities that could be
used by children and adults of all ages. He stated this park area has a lot of
terrain and natural ideas to focus on, which warrants looking at the entire
park.
20.   Mayor Kriege assured the audience and council that the proposed master
plan study for Memorial Park would include a public forum for citizen input.
21.   Father Paul Berschied of St. Cecilia Church stated that he supported the
idea of consolidating city services under one campus area. He stated that the
other acres of the park need to be developed and also supported a master plan
study. He commented that the present configuration of the park doesn’t allow
access to adjoining streets. He stated that he also liked the idea of the
police station being located where our children play.
22.   Mr. Deters reminded council that a condition of his deeding this land to
the city was that a city building would be constructed there as well as the
development of a city park. He stated that this was part of the whole concept
for the Towne Center as ten percent of the land was donated to the Fire
District and City for a fire station, city building and park. He stated that
the current entrance to the park is inadequate and feels that the total picture
for this plot of land has not been evaluated.
23.   Mr. Moriconi asked what properties border the park. Mr. Deters replied
that part of the park adjoins Russ England’s property. He stated the park area
has a long tail with 1000 feet or so that is wooded which would be well suited
for trails and shelters. He stated there is plenty of room in this park for the
children and expressed concern that only the edge of the park has been
developed.
24.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Faulkner what the next step would be. Mr. Faulkner
stated that he felt it was critical to develop a master plan for the park,
especially considering that plans are underway for the construction of an
amphitheatre. He stated that he felt it was important to develop a road map for
the park to analyze linkages to access the park. He assured council they would
conduct a public forum as he felt it was the best way to incorporate ideas from
the residents. He stated that the end result of the master plan study would be
an adequate site plan for the park with a phasing in schedule.
25.   Mayor Kriege commented that he feels the city needs to provide adequate
office space for the city employees, in particular the police department who is
currently renting space in the county courthouse. He stated that while the
parks are needs, the departments that provide services to the citizens are in
need of office space and he feels this is just as important and vital need.
Mayor Kriege stated that he thinks the design of a master plan for Memorial
park makes good sense. Mr. Kudera asked for the status of the amphitheater.
Mayor Kriege advised that Mr. Deters has obtained a new set of drawings for the
amphitheater and that it is too late this year to proceed so the plan is to
obtain construction bids in the spring. He stated the city has until June/July
of 2002 to complete the project. Mr. Kudera agreed that Memorial Park would
benefit from a master plan. He asked how long it would take to design the
master plan. Mr. Faulkner stated it would take about six weeks to design a mid-
level plan. Mayor Kriege advised he just received the park master plan proposal
and would provide council with copies for the special meeting on Thursday.
26.   Mr. Moriconi stated that the city needs to move forward with office
space, especially for the police department. He stated that he would not vote
to disfigure the park or destroy the play area for the children. He stated that
he feels the park could be taken to the next level that would include
restrooms, more shelters and water fountains. He would like to see the park
improved upon.
27.   Mayor Kriege stated he does not want to see the city go to the expense of
purchasing land, as it will add considerable cost to the project. He went on to
assure the citizens in attendance that opposed the building site in the park
that the city would hold a public forum to give them the opportunity to voice
their ideas.
28.   Mr. Ellison commented that the Memorial Park site number two only shows a
small part of the park. He stated that with the construction of an amphitheater
there would be a need for more parking, which will result in more water runoff.
He stated that a possible entrance for the park could be on the backside of the
park – Peach Drive. Mr. Faulkner stated that a buffer needs to be installed
between the property owners in the Forest Run Subdivision and the play area of
the park. He stated that this is a community park, not a neighborhood park, and
is the largest park the city owns.
29.   Mr. Faulkner announced that the plans are just preliminary schematics and
encouraged the residents to attend the public forum to be held at a later date.
Mayor Kriege stated the Memorial Park master plan proposal would be added to
the agenda for the special meeting on Thursday, September 13, 2001 in an effort
to move forward.
Recess
30.   Upon motion by Mr. Moriconi and second by Mr. Kudera a brief recess was
taken. Motion carried with all ayes.
31.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Kudera the meeting resumed.
Motion carried with all ayes.
Privileges of the Floor
32.   Mitchell Wade, 640 Willow Drive addressed council regarding a letter he
received from the city regarding the ongoing problem he has had with drainage
in the rear of his yard which he alleges was the result of the installation of
the Fowler Creek sewer lines. Mr. Wade referred to the before and after videos
that were taken of his property which he stated was the basis of the city’s
position that the property was returned to it’s original condition after the
construction.
33.   Mr. Art Ziegler, 636 Willow Drive, reminded council that at the last city
council meeting he and Mr. Wade were promised that there would be a television
and vcr available at this meeting so that the before and after videos could be
viewed. He stated that he feels these videos prove that the properties were not
restored to the original condition. He stated the area is swampy and requires a
weedeater and knee hi boots to cut the overgrowth. He stated that he did not
receive a letter from the city and had to learn of the city’s decision from Mr.
Wade even though he has been communicating with Mr. Wendling. He requested the
city reconsider their decision and take the time to sit down and review these
videos as promised.
34.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Whitacre to respond to Mr. Wade and Mr. Ziegler.
Mr. Whitacre stated that he has reviewed this matter in several ways. He has
spoken with the company that installed this section of the sewer project, has
inspected the property, and reviewed all written records and correspondence and
has come to the conclusion that there was no indication that additional work
was necessary at these properties. He stated that the assumption is that the
matter was resolved. He stated that the pre-construction video was taken in a
year that was not a wet season, but the video shows a ditch, which indicates
there was an existing erosion problem or drainage problem. He stated that the
city improved upon the original condition as the ditch was not restored. Mr.
Whitacre stated that since no further requests for restoration was made at that
time (1996-1997) then the restoration was adequate. He stated that Jeff Cox of
Lucas Sanitation conveys that street drainage problems were documented, as the
street has no storm sewers or catch basins. But this is on the street side and
not the rear of the property.
35.   Mr. Whitacre went on to explain the possibility of encountering a natural
spring. He advised the water would follow the pipe bedding until it goes
downhill and a water line will follow the grade of the land and then surface
anywhere. Mr. Whitacre advised council that in order to make a good decision
they should view the videotapes. Mayor Kriege stated that it sounds like there
is not much good information to go on. Mr. Whitacre stated that nothing has
been done over the last several years as the previous administrations felt that
no further restoration was needed.
36.   Mr. Kudera and Mr. Ellison agreed that in an effort to move forward and
settle this matter that council should view the videos. Mayor Kriege stated
this matter would be added to the agenda and the videos would be viewed at the
special meeting on Thursday, September 13, 2001.
37.   Tammy Dorgan, 3917 Gunstock Court, returned to council to resume her
appeal to the city to assist the residents of the Hunters Green Subdivision
with the detention pond behind her property that has become an eyesore and a
safety concern for the neighborhood.
38.   Mr. Whitacre presented council with a written report and detailed cost
estimate in the amount of $14,033 to install an overflow structure that would
control the level of water in the pond. He stated that it appears that the
existing outlet had too small of a pipe which would result in the pond
overflowing the dam frequently. He advised that this continual overflow has
eroded the dam and resulted in the current condition. Mr. Whitacre stated that
the pond would continue to decrease each year as the dam overflows and the pond
will fill in from sediment and vegetation. He advised council that the proposed
overflow structure is a less expensive and a more realistic approach to solving
this problem. He stated additional costs for this project would be about $2,500
for engineering and surveying and $2,000 to bid this project out and provide
construction inspection.
39.   Mr. Dupps commented the project would then be approaching $20,000. Mr.
Wendling advised council the city could not go onto the detention pond
property, owned by the defunct Hunters Green Homeowners’ Association, without
incurring legal fees, etc.
40.   Mr. Kudera commented that he understood the council decided at last
month’s meeting to decline involvement with this situation. Mayor Kriege stated
that Mr. Whitacre was asked to provide cost estimates for the residents.
41.   Mike Whitacre, Tammy Dorgan’s father, commented that he understands the
legal ramifications the city is faced with, but thought when the city annexed
the subdivision that it assumed all responsibility for the area and not just
added the tax base assets. He suggested that the next time a developer wants to
deed green space to the city that the city should decline the offer.
42.   Mr. Bob Dodson, 3921 Trappers Court, commented that when the Apple Valley
Apartments were constructed the additional runoff from the development
deteriorated the pond. Mr. Ellison stated that the apartment complex has a
retention pond but is unsure if it is operational or even maintained.
43.   Mr. Kudera commented that the city does not have the funds to correct
this pond. Mr. Ellison stated that the city has offered assistance by way of
attorney and engineering advise on what needs to be done to correct the
situation. Mr. Kudera advised the property owners near this pond should work
together to remedy the situation so that their properties do not decrease in
value. He stated it would be worth the investment to maintain their properties.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-13 – Creating the Position of Assistant Chief of Police –

44.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed

49.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Dupps there was a first

foot parcel of property located adjacent to the physical terminus of Scherry
Avenue as an unmaintained and unimproved public right of way. Motion carried

City Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
50.   Senior Center Update – Mr. Wendling reported the project is scheduled to
be complete by the end of September and that the grading should occur this
week. He reported the Senior Board of Directors has raised approximately
$50,000, which is half way to their goal of $100,000, which they hope to
achieve by the end of the month. The Board is currently focusing on programming
and staffing needs. Mr. Wendling stated that the Kenton County Fiscal Court has
appointed Elizabeth Patterson and Brandon Voelker as the county representatives
on the Board.
51.   Street Repairs Update – Mr. Wendling reported the Holton Drive and
Beechgrove repairs are scheduled to begin next week as well as concrete
replacement for Rickey Lane and Adahi.
52.   Industrial Road Improvements – Mr. Wendling reported that he attended a
meeting regarding proposed improvements to Industrial Road. The meeting had
representatives from the Department of Transportation, Tri-Ed, the Northern
Kentucky Industrial Park and various companies. He stated that the Northern
Kentucky Industrial Park presented their findings of a corridor study and is
recommending that improvements be included in the state’s six-year plan.
Suggested improvements would include widening the entire road to three lanes. A
letter from the city has been sent indicating support for the project.
53.   Cody Road Fire Hydrants – Mr. Wendling reported that he has learned that
the developer (Berling Construction) of Trooper’s Crossing voluntarily agreed
to install the water main outside his development limits but was under no
obligation to install the six fire hydrants. He stated that the cost to install
the hydrants would be approximately $6,000 for materials and that the Water
District would provide the labor and equipment necessary once a payment is
received for the materials. He also reported that the Water District is
contributing up to $20,000 towards the total water line extension along Cody
Road and Independence Station Road through refunds per it’s filed PSC tariff.
Mr. Ellison suggested the city send letters to the nearby residents to inquire
if they have interest in assisting in the cost to install the hydrants.
54.   Police Department Golf Outing – Chief Butler reported the golf outing
fundraiser was successful in raising approximately $2,500 and he credited Sgt.
Tony Lucas with making this event a success.
55.   Police Department – Chief Butler reported that Lt. Dave Nichols has been
accepted into the FBI Academy. He stated that Lt. Nichols is one of twelve in
the state to receive this recognition. He stated that this ten-week program is
specially designed for police officers.
56.   Lakefield Park – Mr. Wendling reported that the park in Lakefield
Subdivision is currently under construction by Drees with the installation of
play equipment and sidewalks. At this time he is unsure when the Drees Company
will be deeding the land over to the city.

SEPTEMBER 13, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the special meeting to order at 6:50 p.m. at the
Kenton County Courthouse in Independence, Ky. Father Paul Berschied of St.
Cecilia Catholic Church gave the invocation Council Members Eric Dupps, Jim
Ellison, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Council Members Jim
Bushong and Ike Gabbard were absent. Mayor Kriege declared that a quorum was
present. Also in attendance was City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling and City
Attorney, Jeffrey S. Smith sitting in for H. Lawson Walker.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was to
discuss and take action on the following agenda items:
§   Discussion and possible action regarding a master plan for Memorial Park
including how it relates to the recent feasibility study for Police and
Administration facilities and a possible site selection for a facility.
§   Discussion and possible action regarding the proposed ordinance setting the
tax rates for 2001.
§   Discussion and possible action relating to Willow Drive properties.
Master Plan for Memorial Park/Feasibility Study for Police/Admin Facilities &
Site Selection
3.   Mayor Kriege advised that Matrix Architects presented a proposal to design
a master plan for Memorial Park at the September 10, 2001 regular council
meeting. Mr. Wendling stated that Matrix would do a brief overview of the park
as it currently exists and propose potential uses for the site with additional
emphasis on site preparation, future site elements and potential phasing
opportunities. He stated that the master plan project would include holding
public meetings to present and receive public input and preliminary
construction cost estimates. Additionally, he stated that the study would take
four to six weeks to complete.
4.   Mayor Kriege stated that a master plan would be a good tool to analyze
utilization of the park with a concept that could be phased in over time. In
addition, he commented that he believed the proposal of a master plan for
Memorial Park would legitimize the recent recommendation to locate a new
administration/police building on the site.
5.   Mayor Kriege recognized the number of citizens in the audience that were
in attendance to address council regarding the plans for Memorial Park. He
advised that he would first give the council members an opportunity to address
the master plan proposal and then give them the opportunity to speak.
6.   Mr. Moriconi commented that he is glad to get input from those in the
audience tonight. He stated that he is aware of the rumors circulating that the
football field would be eliminated from the park. He stated that he would like
to hear points of view from both sides and hopefully answer questions that
could arrest any unfounded rumors. Mr. Moriconi stated that he felt that the
entire acreage of the park should be utilized and that currently only a small
section of the land is being made use of by the residents.
7.   Mr. Kudera commented that it was important for the residents to understand
that council is obligated to serve the community at large. He stated that he
found the number of calls he received this week concerning petitions and flyers
circulating with untold truths to be very troubling. He expressed his
frustration with unforthcoming dissident citizens that won’t personally
confront this council but instead choose to circulate incorrect material. He
reiterated that his position is to serve the entire city, and that decisions
regarding Memorial Park must be for the good of the whole city.
8.   Mr. Ellison commented that he wants to support the city and with some
foresight felt that Memorial Park can be restructured to include Mr. Deters’
original intention for this parcel of land, which was to plot a section for a
new city building. He went on to say that there are twenty-six acres of land in
this park and it is cheaper for the taxpayers to build there than to purchase
land to build elsewhere. Mr. Ellison tried to reassure those in attendance that
no decision would be made tonight regarding a site for the city building but
that council would just decide on whether or not to proceed with a master plan
for the park. He stated that other sites are being reviewed, but explained that
the Staggs Park would have to be eliminated as that land was purchased with
federal dollars that would prohibit a building being located there. He stated
that the architect consultants have recommended the Memorial Park site number
two as the best location for a new city building, but that he is willing to
listen to residents’ comments before making a decision. In closing, Mr. Ellison
stressed that for the last ten years there has been a dire need for a new
building to house the city’s employees, especially the police department, and
that council’s responsibility is to look at the best interest of the city and
all its’ citizens.
9.   Mr. Dupps expressed concern that the city may be putting the cart before
the horse. He questioned conducting a master plan project before deciding on a
site for the city building. Mayor Kriege stated that he would like to see
council commit to a site selection tonight as he feels it is time to move
forward with plans for a city building. But Mr. Dupps stated he wanted to be
sure the city moved in the right direction.
10.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve and authorize Mayor Kriege to enter
into a contract with Matrix Architects to design a master plan for Memorial
Park as presented in the proposal for the amount of $10,200. Mr. Ellison
seconded the motion. Further discussion ensued. Mr. Kudera strongly expressed
his commitment to move forward with the creation of a new city center. He
initiated his support for this project as he felt the city needed to move
forward. Mr. Dupps stated that he would like to have more time to discuss this
matter and was concerned that the Building and Recreation Committee had not had
an opportunity to review the proposal. Mayor Kriege stated this was discussed
with the architect and that the committee will review the master plan before it
is presented at a regular council meeting. Mr. Dupps asked if Matrix has
designed other park plans. Mr. Wendling stated that they have done other park
designs and assured Mr. Dupps that he is satisfied that this firm is capable of
this project. Mr. Dupps commented that he feels there are some positive things
in their proposal, such as the phasing of the development. Mr. Wendling stated
that he feels a master plan is necessary for the park in order to make it the
best it can be as it is located in the heart of town and will probably be the
city’s largest park. Mr. Ellison stated that he agrees the park needs a master
plan and felt it should be tied in with the plans for a city building. Mr.
Kudera stated that he does not want to submerge the opposition to this project,
but merely wishes the opponents of this proposed project to come forward to
present their views directly to council. Mr. Dupps asked how the city would pay
for this expense. Mayor Kriege stated the cost for the master plan would be
taken from the Building Fund. Mr. Moriconi commented that he would like to see,
at minimum, water fountains and restrooms in this park and hoped that this
project would accomplish that.
11.   At this time, Mayor Kriege opened the floor for comments from the
audience regarding this matter.
PRIVILIDGES OF THE FLOOR
12.   Father Paul Berschied, St. Cecilia Church, 5313 Madison Pike, addressed
council in support of approving the master plan study for Memorial Park. He
stated twenty-six acres of existing land is not accessible and feels there is a
need for other entrances into the park. He stated that he feels that the
$10,200 will be well spent to design a plan that would explore more uses and
obtain more recreational facilities for the city. Father stated that he would
also like to see better sanitation facilities and better spacing of the
recreational equipment. He stated he would like to see the park more accessible
to a greater number of people and felt certain that it would benefit St.
Cecilia School for educational purposes. In closing, Father Berschied stated
that it would be prudent to correctly position the building site and is in
favor of the study to look at the best use of the proposed city building site,
regardless of whether or not the building is located there. He commented that
without a park plan that things would be developed in a mishmash manner.
13.   Perry Wing, 10734 Cypresswood, told council that he was interested in
obtaining some clarity and answers to the recent rumors circulating about the
proposed plans for Memorial Park. He also offered to volunteer to be part of
the planning process of the park. Mr. Wing expressed concern regarding the
increased traffic that would be generated from locating a city building near
the Delaware Crossing/Route 17 intersection. He stated that he felt this area
is currently inadequate to handle the traffic flow as well as other sections of
Route 17 especially during peak times such as morning and lunchtime. He stated
he would like to see a turn lane installed in the Independence Square for
safety and to prevent further injuries. Mr. Wing also felt that the additional
traffic would jeopardize the safety of the seniors visiting the Senior Center
nearby when it opens for business later this year.
14.   Mr. Wing also expressed displeasure with the architect’s placement of the
access road to the proposed city building as presented at Monday’s council
meeting. He stated that it appears that the road would be at his backyard and
doesn’t feel the site is appropriate. He stated that while he understands the
city needs a building he feels the council needs to stay focused on the safety
issue and should keep the businesses separate from the residential part of
town. Mr. Wing hoped that if the city does choose the architects’ recommended
site for the city building that the necessary setback would be maintained.
Mayor Kriege assured Mr. Wing the city would maintain an adequate setback but
could not commit to constructing a wall as a barrier. Mr. Wing also requested
the city provide non-glaring lights as a courtesy to the nearby properties.
15.   Rita King, 6523 Sugar Camp Drive, asked Mayor Kriege and council if a
merger of the Kenton County Police Department and the Independence Police
department has ever been considered. She stated that the police department
expends two-thirds of the city’s budget. Mayor Kriege stated that it was not
uncommon for the police and fire departments to consume a large portion of the
budget. In addition, he responded that Independence is the fastest growing city
in the area and he would not consider dissolving the city police department.
Ms. King stated she felt the city could use the funds for a city building if
the county and police services were merged. Chief Butler responded that the
citizens of Independence would not get the same level of service if the two
departments merged. He also commented that Kenton County is currently looking
for a new building, as their current building on Route 17 near Nicholson will
be taken by the re-routing of Route 17.
16.   Ms. King expressed concern as to why a park plan wasn’t prepared before
installing the shelter and play equipment and questioned the cost that will be
associated with relocating these structures. Mayor Kriege stated those issues
will be addressed in the master plan. Mr. Wendling advised that the architect
has stated that relocation of the current structures will be a nominal expense.
Ms. King asked why the city is not considering the Pelly Road/Madison Pike
location as the site for a new city building. Mr. Wendling stated that the
purchase of the land would add about $600,000 to the cost of the project. Ms.
King also suggests the city purchase land adjacent to the park. Mr. Wendling
advised the land did not have good access.
17.   Ms. King also voiced her concern for citizens’ safety when cruisers
enter/exit the proposed Memorial Park site for a city building when responding
to calls. Mr. Wendling stated that currently Memorial Park is a major safety
issue during the week during peewee football practice and that the entire
safety issue will be addressed with the design of a master plan for the park
area.
18.   Maura Snyder, 5129 Dana Harvey, addressed council in support of the need
for adequate office space for the police department. She stated that their
current rented space is substandard with no space for storage. She stated that
the residents should get acquainted with the police officers. She stated the
city building may be inconvenient for the residents nearby but she feels the
presence of the police officers would help deter drug loitering in the park.
Ms. Snyder stated that if the land was given to the city to construct a city
building and park then the city should not spend an additional $600,000 to
purchase more land and suggested the city move forward with plan.
19.   Cheryl Depolt, 10761 Autumnridge Drive, was concerned with the type of
city building to be constructed, and wondered if it would resemble one like the
City of Taylor Mill or the City of Florence. She also was concerned with the
safety issue and additional traffic at the intersection of Delaware Crossing
and Route 17. She stated that the noise factor should be considered, when
adding a police station near the fire station. Mayor Kriege stated this is the
kind of input needed for the master plan.
20.   Ms. Depolt stated that she moved here from Massachusetts where the taxes
were much higher, but in exchange the community in which she lived enjoyed
beautiful parks and schools and people were happy because they had a beautiful
city. She stated that one of the reasons she bought the property in the Forest
Run Subdivision was because the park was located there, and she urged council
to spend the money to do the site preparation needed to put the city building
on the Memorial Park site number one. She stated that this extra expense to the
city would be worth it to her and that she would be willing to pay more taxes.
Mayor Kriege responded that the majority of the residents do not feel like she
does and prefer the property tax rates to remain low. Mr. Wendling encouraged
Ms. Depolt to review the master plan for the park when it is completed before
rejecting the possibility. Ms. Depolt requested the council to go door to door
in the Forest Run Subdivision and talk to the residents so they can hear that
they want a park, not a parking lot.
21.   Michael McFallen, 10730 Cypresswood Drive, informed council that his main
concern with regard to locating the city building in Memorial Park is the
safety issue. He stated that the park is already busy, non-stop, and feared
that additional traffic created by a city building will increase the safety
concern. He stated that he felt the council’s decision has already been made
and is set on this site. He stated that he is impressed by the city’s police
department and understand that a building is needed but stressed that the area
needed to remain safe for children. Mr. McFallen inquired if a jail would be in
the police building. Chief Butler assured Mr. McFallen that the police
department is not in the business of storing prisoners and that no holding cell
would be constructed in the building. He stated the police department would
continue to transport prisoners to the county jail. In closing, Mr. McFallen
stated that he feels he will loose his privacy, and with the availability of so
much land in Independence, urged council to look at other options.
22.   Wilma Wright, 1819 Forest Run Drive, briefly stated that she agrees with
her neighbors in the subdivision and they do not want a city building in the
park.
23.   Richard Noah, 1843 Forest Run Drive, stated that he has great admiration
for the police department. He commented that he uses Memorial Park on a regular
basis and feels confident that all traffic and safety concerns will be
addressed in the master plan. He stated that he would be willing to pay
additional taxes for the city’s needs but that he would prefer a tax increase
be avoided. Mr. Noah commented that the current layout of the park is very
unsafe and feels that drivers won’t speed in front of a police station. He
stated that he understands that the adjoining property owners are looking out
for their own interests but feels the city will do a good job in constructing a
building in an attractive manner. In closing, he stated that he would like to
see council move forward with the master plan for the park.
24.   Donna Miller, 4394 Oliver Road, stated that her main concern was how the
city proposed paying for a new city building. Mayor Kriege stated that funds
for a building has been projected in the city’s five-year plan. Mrs. Miller
commented that she has been striving for years to see the police department get
acceptable facilities and she is sorry if it is in someone’s backyard, but it
is time for a new building. She reiterated that her main concern is how the
city will fund the building. Mayor Kriege stated that no final decisions have
been made regarding the funding.
END PRIVILEDGES OF THE FLOOR
25.   Mr. Kudera agreed that safety is a concern in the area and informed
everyone that the state highway department is addressing this matter at the
intersection of Route 17 and Delaware Crossing.
26.   Mr. Dupps commented that he would like to see the Building and Recreation
Committee review the master plan proposal before a presentation is made to
council.
27.   Mr. Ellison also agreed that safety is a major concern and has been for
the last ten years or so. He stated that when Governor Brereton Jones was in
office the city was promised that Route 17 would be reconstructed, which is
finally in progress. Mr. Moriconi commented that a traffic light is proposed
for the intersection of Walnut Hall/Route 17/Delaware Crossing. Chief Butler
stated that the city does not control speed and traffic lights on state
highways, but does lobby for these changes and is often denied, but he stated
that turn lanes in the area have been promised by the state. Chief Butler
stated the he will continue to request these road improvements.
28.   At this time roll call was taken on Mr. Kudera’s motion and Mr. Ellison’s
second to authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into a contract with Matrix
Architects to design a master plan for Memorial Park. Roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 4-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Setting the Property Tax Rates for 2001 – Second Reading
29.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to set the tax rates for real and personal property for 2001. Mr.
Dupps seconded the motion. City Attorney, Jeffrey S. Smith read the proposed
ordinance which would set the real estate tax rate at .147/$100 and .205/$100
for personal property. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 4-
0 in favor.
Recess
30.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Dupps a brief recess was
taken. Motion carried with all ayes.
31.   Upon motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Ellison the meeting resumed.
Motion carried with all ayes.
Discussion of Willow Drive Properties
32.    Mr. Art Ziegler and Mr. Mitchell Wade, 636 Willow Drive and 640 Willow
Drive respectively, returned to council to continue the discussion about the
drainage problem at the rear of their property that they contend was brought
about from the construction of the Fowler Creek Sewer lines installed years
ago. Mayor Kriege consented to a public viewing of the preconstruction video
tape recorded by Cardinal Engineer, in addition to viewing the residents’ video
tape as the drainage problem exists currently.
33.   After viewing the tapes, a lengthy discussion ensued. Mr. Ziegler asked
council for assistance with solving this drainage problem on their property.
Mr. Wade said this lack of drainage has caused his basement to leak, which he
stated was not a problem before the sewer lines were installed. He stated the
lay of the land was altered and he feels the video shows where the land was cut
down.
34.   Mayor Kriege asked City Engineer, Dave Whitacre to respond to the videos.
Mr. Whitacre stated that he feels that comparing the two videos is like
comparing apples to oranges. He stated that the preconstruction video was
recorded several feet up hill, in contrast to the residents’ video, which was
recorded up close. He stated that to really know how the area drains that there
needs to be a stretch of dry weather. Mr. Whitacre stated that this
construction was done over a two-month period in the fall of 1996 and that the
contractor installing the lines restored the property the best as he could for
that time of year. He stated it was difficult to get grass to grow at that time
of year. He stated he has attempted to speak with the construction company that
performed this job but that some of the people are no longer there. Mr.
Whitacre advised council that several city representatives have inspected this
property over the last few years and made the determination that the city had
no further liability. He admitted that this water has nowhere to drain but
doesn’t know that it is any different now than before the installation of the
lines. He read notations from the punch list that was documented for this
project, which did not reveal that a problem existed. He also advised that
during a site visit by GRS it was determined that additional work was not
required.
35.   Mr. Dupps asked what it would cost to solve this drainage problem. Mr.
Whitacre stated that 4”– 6” perforated pipe would run $1.00/foot but he advised
the biggest problem will be getting the heavy equipment to the area without
destroying the property.
36.   Mr. Whitacre posed the question of whether or not the city was still
liable for this drainage problem since the sewer lines were turned over to the
Sanitation District a few years ago. Mr. Ellison thinks that the District owns
along the easement and that the right of ways belongs to the city. Mr. Kudera
stated that he believes the city is not liable for any of the construction area
per the Agreement with the Sanitation District. Mr. Ellison stated he believes
that a hydrologist is on staff at the Sanitation District and the city should
request that the hydrologist inspect this property. City Attorney, Jeffrey S.
Smith advised that his office should review the Agreement with the Sanitation
District to understand what the agreement entails. Mr. Moriconi agreed that the
Sanitation District should be called in to inspect this property. Mr. Wade
stated he has spoken with the District and they have promised to send someone
out. He stated that something has to be done to correct this condition, as he
cannot tolerate it much longer and that he had hoped he would be able to reach
an agreement with the city. Mr. Kudera stated that he felt the videos did not
give a raw view of where the problem is and he didn’t see evidence when he made
a site visit. Mayor Kriege commented that there are so many unknowns that are
hindering a solution.
37.   Mr. Dupps suggested the city work with the Sanitation District for Mr.
Wade. Mayor Kriege stated that Mr. Wendling could facilitate this process but
wanted Mr. Wade and Mr. Ziegler to understand that the city was not promising
to solve this problem but will agree to provide assistance with the Sanitation
District. Mr. Moriconi concurred and stated that he felt it would be worth the
efforts to coordinate this matter and see what assistance the Sanitation
District can provide. Mr. Ellison stated he would like the Sanitation District
to provide the city with a copy of the report after the inspection is complete.
Mayor Kriege advised that in the meantime, legal counsel for the city would
review the Agreement with the Sanitation District when they took over
maintenance of the sewer lines.
38.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to request the city staff to facilitate with
the Sanitation District an inspection and review of the properties on Willow
Drive that are enduring this drainage problem. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion.
No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
39.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Dupps the meeting was
adjourned at 9:05 p.m. Motion carried with all ayes.

OCTOBER 1, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES

1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Father Paul Berschied gave the invocation. Council Members Eric
Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi answered roll
call. Council Member Jim Bushong was absent. Also in attendance was City
Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.

2.   On behalf of Toyota North American Parts Center, Council Member, Eric
Dupps presented to Lt. Ed Bailey of the Police Department a donation check in
the amount of $500.00 in support of the DARE Project and Bike Helmet Safety
Program.

3.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to accept the minutes of the council meeting of
September 10, 2001 as amended. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with four yes votes, with Mr. Gabbard abstaining. Motion carried 4-

4.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Dupps for approval of the

carried 4-0 in favor.
Privileges of the Floor
5.   Rita King, 6523 Sugar Camp Road, addressed council regarding the plans for
a proposed municipal building. She asked if council had considered Independence
Park in the Hartland Subdivision as a possible site for the building. Mr.
Wendling replied that that site has been platted as a neighborhood park. Ms.
King asked if the master plan for Memorial Park was going to include a
municipal building. Mayor Kriege responded that nothing had been determined at

city building.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-09- Map Amendment for 77 Acres at Senior Rd. & Fowler
Creek Rd.
6.   Mayor Kriege explained there was a second reading and adoption of this
ordinance at the special council meeting of August 21, 2001. He stated that the
Kentucky Post/Enquirer failed to publish the ordinance within thirty days as
required which is the reason this ordinance is being presented for a new second
reading.
7.   Mr. Ellison made a motion for a second reading of Ordinance No. 2001-O-09
and Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Mr. Gabbard suggested adding the sidewalk
requirement to this ordinance. Mr. Walker explained that if any changes are
made to this ordinance now that it will regress to a first reading causing
another delay in the adoption process of this ordinance. He advised that if the
city made changes at this late date that the developer of this planned
subdivision would argue and go with the original recommendations by the
Planning Commission. He reminded council that this map amendment was approved
with more conditions than was recommended by the Planning Commission and
advised against abandoning this ordinance. Upon Mr. Walker’s advise, Mr.
Gabbard agreed that the ordinance should not be amended. Mr. Wendling commented
that the Planning Commission upheld the sidewalk condition for the development.
8.   Mr. Walker read Ordinance No. 2001-O-09 by title only. Roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2001-O-15 –2nd Reading – Dedicating a Parcel Adjacent to Scherry
Ave. as a Right of Way
9.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to have a second reading of a proposed ordinance
to dedicate a parcel of land adjacent to Scherry Avenue as a right of way. Mr.
Kudera seconded the motion. Mr. Walker read Ordinance No. 2001-O-15. There
being no discussion, roll call was taken and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0 in favor.
Discussion regarding the Maintenance of Justice Lane
10.   Ms. Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, addressed council requesting
clarification of a public record. More specifically the Ordinance (1-11-87)
accepting Justice Lane as a city street for maintenance purposes. She stated
that Jeff Smith of the Public Works Department informed her the city did not
maintain Justice Lane. She stated that Justice Lane is not restricted to public
access. City attorney, Lawson Walker advised the city has no record of this as
a public street. He went on to say that a resident on Justice Lane claims the
road is on his property and the city doesn’t have a plat indicating where the
private property and city property lines are located. He said this is something
the city will need to determine, as the current ordinance that was adopted in
1987 does not affirm the boundary lines. He stated the city should not dedicate
a road without owning it, and it is unclear from reading the ordinance to
determine the location of the right of way. Ms. Woolum argued that this road
has been unrestricted for many years and cited a state statute that provides
two means for dedication of a road; one formally and the other provision of
dedication would be informal for a road that has been open to public use for
more than five years, then it is presumed to be a public right of way. Ms.
Woolum presented research documents to Mr. Walker for his review. Mayor Kriege
stated this matter could not be resolved at this meeting and advised Ms. Woolum
the city would have legal counsel review the matter and notify her in
letterform.
11.   Mr. Gabbard stated that he felt the city had some obligation to maintain
Justice Lane due to the adoption of an ordinance. Mr. Walker asked if the city
had provided some maintenance to this street in the past. Mr. Jeff Smith,
Public Works crew leader, stated that his crew has filled some potholes on two
occasions. Mr. Walker stated he would review the matter and advise council.
Resolution No. 2001-R-12 – Approving Payment of CDBG Monthly Expenses for the
Senior Center
12.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to read Resolution No. 2001-R-12 approving the
monthly payment to Mark Spaulding Construction in the amount of $176,637.60.
Mr. Gabbard seconded the motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Ellison asked
if the building was close to completion. Mr. Wendling stated no specific date
has been set but it may be about two more weeks. Mr. Ellison asked if a
completion date was included in the contract. Mayor Kriege stated there was,
but that the date is not imminent and is not a cost concern. Mr. Gabbard asked
how the Board was doing on their fund drive to cover the cost of furniture. Mr.
Wendling stated the Board has raised over $50,000.
13.   Mr. Walker read Resolution No. 2001-R-12. Roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Resolution No. 2001-R-13 – Condemning September 11, 2001 Terrorist Attacks on
the USA
14.   Mayor Kriege presented to council a resolution condemning the terrible
terrorist attacks in Washington D.C. and New York City on September 11, 2001.
He said we should remember what our country has experienced these last several
weeks and show an expression of support.
15.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to read Resolution No. 2001-R-13, seconded by
Mr. Kudera. Mr. Moriconi suggested adding wordage that would support the
services of the men and women of the military. Mayor Kriege stated that could
be included by adding a Section IV. Mr. Walker read the Resolution in its
entirety. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Discussion of the September 11, 2001 Terrorist Attacks and Offering Financial
Support to New York City
16.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to contribute $5,000 to the New York City
Police and Firemen Survivor’s Fund and to host the Hoxworth mobile blood unit
and suggested the city officials head this project. Mr. Ellison stated that he
would second the motion as long as funds could be found in the budget. Mayor
Kriege asked Mr. Gabbard where in the budget he would pull the $5,000. Mr.
Gabbard suggested that funds be taken from the administration and police
training expenses. Mr. Kudera stated that while he supports community
involvement in the survivor’s fund he thinks the fire department and probably
the police department has incurred additional expenses due to extra security
measures being taken for our community and that additional costs may be
impending until the war is over. He stated that he feels that at this time the
city needs to focus on our local responsibilities as we may have future
unbudgeted expenditures before the end of the fiscal year. Mr. Gabbard
countered that thousands of lives have been lost in the September 11, 2001
terrorist attack, and he feels the city can and should make the extraordinary
effort to donate to this fund for the people who put their lives on the line.
Mr. Moriconi stated that he did not want to pull funds from the police training
as their budget is tight already, but he would be willing to donate to the
survivor’s fund if another funding source can be found. Mayor Kriege suggested
the staff could review their budget with a recommendation at the next council
meeting. Mr. Gabbard reiterated that he feels the city is obligated to
contribute to this fund. Mr. Dupps suggested the funds could come from the road
budget if the street repairs fall under budget. Mr. Wendling stated he would
review the budget tomorrow with the Finance Director to look for extra funds.
Mayor Kriege suggested tabling this matter until next month. Mr. Gabbard
amended his motion to table voting on the $5,000 contribution until next month
upon a report from staff on where funds can be pulled from in the budget, and
to proceed to move forward with contacting Hoxworth Blood Center to arrange to
have the mobile unit brought to the city. Mr. Ellison seconded the amendment.
Roll call was answered with four yes votes, with Mr. Kudera abstaining. Motion
carried in favor.
Miscellaneous
17.   Mr. Ellison advised that a No Parking sign needs to be installed on the
north side of Independence Station Road.
18.   Mr. Ellison stated that he has received a call from Owen Electric who
reports that house numbers are not being installed on the houses in the Battle
Ridge Subdivision. Mayor Kriege stated he thought the city had an ordinance
that requires house numbers be posted. Mr. Ellison stated he would like to see
the Zoning Administrator enforce this ordinance. Mr. Gabbard concurred and
