19.   Mr. Ellison advised that Webster Road, off of Cody Road, has a temporary
road, which has made access to those houses nearly impossible for emergency
personnel/vehicles. He stated this is a serious safety concern. Mayor Kriege
advised that Mr. Wendling would look into this tomorrow.
Naming of the Park in the Lakefield Subdivision to Marion Schadler Park
20.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to name the new park in the Lakefield
Subdivision after the former mayor, Marion Schadler who has dedicated many
years of public service to the City of Independence. Mr. Gabbard seconded the
motion. Mr. Gabbard stated that Mr. Schadler served as mayor of Independence
for sixteen years and two years as a council member. Mr. Ellison commented that
Mr. Schadler deserves this recognition. Mr. Dupps stated that he recalls in the
past the Independence Recreation Committee would compile a list of park names
and make a recommendation to council for approval. He also recalled the
Recreation Committee recommended against dedicating parks to individuals and
that Memorial Park was aptly named to encompass memorials to individuals. Mr.
Dupps stated that he does not object to naming the park after Mr. Schadler, but
feels the Building and Recreation Committee should review this matter and make
a recommendation to council. Mr. Gabbard stated that he feels anyone that
serves the community for such a lengthy period should have something named
after them. He stated that Mr. Schadler was mayor when the city was a smaller
community during tougher times.
21.   Mayor Kriege stated that regardless of the outcome of the vote on this
motion, that he feels this matter should be discussed by the Building and
Recreation Committee as suggested by Mr. Dupps. Roll call was answered with
three-yes votes cast by Mr. Ellison, Mr. Gabbard and Mr. Moriconi and two no
votes cast by Mr. Dupps and Mr. Kudera. Motion carried 3-2 in favor of naming
the park in the Lakefield Subdivision to Marion Schadler Park.
CITY ADMINISTRATOR’S REPORT – Mark T. Wendling
22.   Senior Center – Mr. Wendling reported the carpet is being installed and
the project is expected to be completed by the end of the week.
Street Repairs – Mr. Wendling reported that Beechgrove Drive has been milled
and that Adahi is approximately one-half completed. Mr. Smith reported the
faulty joints have been removed from Holton Drive and that the asphalt work
will begin on Beechgrove Drive. He stated that Roselawn Drive repairs would
begin soon. Mr. Smith stated that if good weather continues all road repairs
should soon be complete for the year. Mr. Gabbard commented about reports of
mail delivery being interrupted on Adahi during the street repairs. Mr. Smith
stated he is aware of these problems and will continue to monitor the situation
until the street repairs are complete.
Willow Drive – Mr. Wendling stated that progress is being made on solving this
drainage problem. The EPA tested the water and it appears to be ground water.
He stated he would meet with the Sanitation District next week to do an on-site
inspection.
Memorial Park Master Plan – Mr. Wendling reported the master plan
questionnaires have been prepared and are available at the city building and on
the city’s website.
Gunstock Court – Mr. Wendling reported that a letter has been sent to Ms. Tammy
Dorgan informing her of the city’s position on the lake on the common area
behind her house.
TEA 21 Grant – Mr. Wendling reported that the Department of Transportation has
notified the city that we can begin drawing on the grant any time. He will
begin working with the city engineer on this project of installing sidewalks
from Hartland Blvd. to Walnut Hall Drive. Mr. Gabbard asked when this project
would begin. Mr. Wendling stated it would be best to begin this construction in
the spring of 2002. Mr. Gabbard suggested bidding the project out prior to the
end of this year.
Lakefield Park – Mr. Wendling reported that the play equipment and sidewalks
have been installed. He stated when the park is completely constructed it will
be deeded to the city by the Drees Corporation.

NOVEMBER 5, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty gave the invocation. Council Members Jim
Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera, and Chris Moriconi
answered roll call. Also in attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and
City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the October 1, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to accept the minutes of the council meeting of
October 1, 200 with Mr. Dupps seconding the motion. Mr. Gabbard requested an
amendment of paragraph sixteen on an amendment to his motion regarding the
$5,000 donation to the New York City Police and Firemen’s Survivors Fund. He
stated that he has requested and the City Clerk has agreed to review the audio/
video tape for clarification of his motion and to make any needed changes. Mr.
Gabbard made a motion to make the changes to this section of the minutes if
warranted. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Motion carried with all ayes. Mr.

noted and Mr. Ellison’s motion and Mr. Dupps second carried unanimously. No
roll call.
Presentation of the 2000/01 Audit by Linda Chapman of Rankin, Rankin & Company
3.   Linda Chapman of Rankin, Rankin & Company presented the audit report with
council. She stated the audit was conducted in accordance with generally
accepted auditing standards. Ms. Chapman advised that the lease with the
Kentucky League of Cities for $450,000 for the Senior Center and the lease-
purchase debt for the cruisers of $172,781 was the reason for the increase in
fund balances. Also, the increase in fixed assets is due to the Senior Center.
Ms. Chapman advised council that the city’s prior years fund balance increased
by approximately $316,000 due to the implementation of GASB 33 as of June 30,
2001. She stated that this is a paper entry only and represents earlier
recognition of payroll and gross receipt tax received July, August and
September of this year and in future years. She stated that no major errors or
indications of fraud were found.
4.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to accept the audit as presented; seconded by Mr.
Ellison. Roll call was unanimous. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Keith Napier, 869 Stephens Road, addressed council concerning his desire
to subdivide 2.5 acres on Stephens Road, which is owned by his mother, in order
to build a house on 1.3 acres of this land. He stated that personal concerns
regarding the health of his mother and invalid sister necessitate his presence
to care for them. Mr. Napier stated that the city currently has in effect an
ordinance that prohibits flag lots, thereby prohibiting the variance needed to
divide this property so that he can build a house. He stated that he feels this
land has been rendered useless due to the ordinance prohibiting flag lots.
6.   Mr. Gabbard stated that the ordinance would not permit a variance. Mayor
Kriege suggested that the Planning & Zoning Committee review this ordinance for
a possible repeal or amendment. Mr. Gabbard expressed concern of repealing/
amending this ordinance as it may open the door for others in similar
situations that want flag lots.
7.   Mr. Wendling stated he has been working with the city attorney’s
associate, Jeffrey Smith, to modify the ordinance to accomplish the original
intention of the ordinance while helping Mr. Napier and others with similar
needs. He stated it would take some time to accomplish the presentation of an
amended ordinance. Mr. Napier stated that he is approaching a deadline, as he
needs to take possession of the modular house by February 2002.
8.   Again, Mayor Kriege suggested the Planning & Zoning Committee review this
ordinance for a possible amendment and bring a recommendation to the December
council meeting. Mr. Kudera suggested adding a grandfather clause to the
ordinance. City Attorney, Mr. Walker stated that he has looked into this matter
and advised there are some options to be looked at. Mr. Ellison suggested the
Planning & Zoning Committee meet on Wednesday, November 7 at 4:30 p.m. The
other committee members agreed.
9.   Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, addressed council requesting an update on
the matter regarding the maintenance of Justice Lane, which she presented to
council at last month’s meeting. Mr. Walker stated that he has provided to
council and mayor a written opinion on this matter, which he is reluctant to
discuss outside of an executive session. Ms. Woolum stated that she felt this
should be a public matter. Mr. Gabbard agreed this matter should be discussed
in open session. Mayor Kriege and Mr. Kudera agreed with the city attorney that
this should be discussed in executive session, which will be held at the end of
the regular session.
10.   Bill Ahearn, 2032 Mapletree Lane, addressed council regarding the zoning
violations at 11515 Madison Pike owed by Ted Davidson. He stated this property
is an eyesore with many junk cars including about ten tractor-trailers on a
gravel lot. He stated the smoke emission and noise from the running pay loaders
has become intolerable for the surrounding neighbors. He also mentioned the
sound of guns being discharged coming from this property. He stated that he has
spoken with Zoning Administrator, Rich McAllister on several occasions about
this property, and wants it to be public record that the neighbors in this area
want these violations to be abated. Mayor Kriege responded that this matter has
been an on-going situation and will notify Mr. McAllister to look into it.
11.   Raymond Kahrs, 2931 Senour Road, came before council to protest paying a
trash assessment for property he owns where the house is vacant. He stated that
since no one lives in the house and no trash is brought to the curb that he
shouldn’t be required to pay for a service that is not used. Mayor Kriege
explained that Rumpke (the trash pickup contractor) charges the city for each
house in the city. He stated that since the city is charged for this, it is a
pass-through expense to the property owner. Mr. Kahrs stated he should not have
to pay for two trash assessments when he only needs it for the house he lives
in. Mayor Kriege advised the city could not begin a precedent of waiving the
trash assessment charge, as others that choose not to use the service would
then expect this. Mayor Kriege suggested the city could make arrangements for
him to make payments on this assessment if it was a hardship for him to pay the
entire $91.16. Mr. Kahrs agreed to meet with the City Clerk to discuss options
for payment.
OLD BUSINESS
Discussion of Donation to NYC Police & Firemen’s Survivors Fund & Blood Drive
12.   Mr. Gabbard inquired on the status of his motion last month to donate
$5,000 to the New York City Police and Firemen’s Survivors Fund and if staff
was able to find the funds in the budget to fulfill this motion. He also stated
that he called the Hoxworth Blood Center to see if the city made arrangements
for the mobile unit to come to Independence for a blood drive (which was also
part of the motion last month) and was informed that such a request had not
been made by the city. Mayor Kriege stated that the timing was not as they were
scheduling people out. Mr. Gabbard stated he was advised by Hoxworth that they
are behind in scheduling the mobile units, but if the city can promise forty or
more donors that they will schedule a unit for the city. Mr. Wendling stated
that he did not call Hoxworth to arrange for a mobile unit due to media reports
saying that no blood was needed at this time. He stated that he had heard that
Hoxworth was turning people away. Mr. Gabbard stated that Hoxworth has a
regularly scheduled mobile unit coming to the Kroger parking lot on December
28, 2001 but that they would make a special trip before then if forty donors
would sign up. He stated he would handle the arrangements.
13.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to put Mr. Gabbard in charge of arrangements for
a special blood drive; seconded by Mr. Dupps. Mr. Moriconi stated that he read
an article a couple of weeks ago that the Red Cross was not accepting donors
and that blood has a shelf life of forty-two days. Mr. Gabbard stated that
certain, rare types of blood are always needed. He added, that as a city, we
should show our patriotism and urged all elected officials to get behind this
endeavor. Mayor Kriege reminded council there was a motion and second on the
floor. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
14.   Mr. Wendling stated that he felt with the city loosing two patrol
officers to active military duty that the $5,000 donation may be better spent
by picking up the difference in salary and military pay for these two officers.
Mr. Gabbard felt the city could still find $5,000 excess in the budget to
contribute to NYC. Mayor Kriege stated he did not feel the city could afford to
make that contribution, in addition to paying the salary gap to the two
officers, and the need to provide replacements in the police department for
these officers. Mayor Kriege cautioned that it is too early in the fiscal year
to estimate where the city will end up with regard to finances. Mr. Walker
advised there are legalities involved with the city making donations to
charities. Mr. Gabbard stated that he felt this type of donation was no
different than those given to the Independence Lions Club for the Easter Egg
Hunt or Simon Kenton High School for Project Prom. He stated the NYC Survivors
Fund is not a charitable organization. Mayor Kriege asked council how they
wanted to proceed. He stated they can review the budget or take Mr. Walker’s
advise. Mr. Moriconi stated he would like to contribute the $5,000 to the city
police officer’s that were called to active duty. Chief Butler stated that
federal law mandates that an employer pay a service member on a monthly basis
the lesser of (1) the difference between the gross monthly salary as an
employee and the sum of the gross military pay or (2) $500. Mr. Gabbard asked
what the term of duty was for each officer. Chief Butler replied that the
minimum duty term is six months; then it will be reviewed for a possible
extension. Mr. Gabbard stated that if council was willing to bridge the gap
between the employee’s salary and the military pay while on active duty that he
would agree to abandon this cause. Chief Butler advised that the continuation
of the health insurance for these employees is also an issue that needs to be
addressed.
15.   Mayor Kriege recommended that the council authorize payment of the
difference of salary for the active military duty employees in lieu of the
$5,000 donation to the NYC Police and Firemen’s Survivor’s Fund. Mr. Kudera
expressed concern that this may be premature, as the other patrol officers will
be working overtime to fill in for the loss of two patrol officers. He
anticipates that the police department’s overtime budget will be exceeded very
quickly and worries this will be an open ended situation.
16.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to authorize payment to active military duty
employees the difference between their military salary and city salary for the
next six months. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Mr. Bushong asked for
clarification on the ‘difference’. Chief Butler stated the difference would be
from the basic military pay. Mr. Ellison advised the city would need to get a
copy of the military pay voucher. He stated that he agreed the city needed to
do this so that the officers could continue to maintain their houses, cars,
etc. while on active duty. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0 in favor.

Proposed Ordinance – Creating the Position of Emergency Operation Director –
1st Reading
22.   Mayor Kriege stated the proposed ordinance would create the position of
an Emergency Operations Director for the city and called upon Chief Butler to
explain this position. Chief Butler informed council that having an Emergency
Operations Director would be necessary in case the city would experience an
emergency disaster and need state assistance. He explained that thirteen cities
in Northern Kentucky have established this position and then appointed the
Kenton County Emergency Operations Direction, Ed Burke to fill this position.
He explained there are several problems with establishing this department and
hiring a full time employee for the city, as this position requires extensive
training and the city would be required to purchase expensive equipment. He
stated that the county has graciously offered to provide this service to
Independence. He stated that Mr. Burke is a paid county employee and has a
trained staff. Chief Butler advised that this position and department is
necessary but is just not physically feasible for the city to operate and
maintain.
23.   Mr. Gabbard expressed concern that with so many cities being served by
the county how they would be able to assist everyone adequately. Chief Butler
stated he felt there would be a coordinate effort between the cities and the
county. Mayor Kriege stated that the intent of this ordinance is to create the
position and then appoint Mr. Burke. Chief Butler stated that he would invite
Mr. Burke to address council before appointing him as Emergency Operations
Director for the city. Mr. Walker stated the proposed ordinance is the same one
used by the other cities. Mr. Gabbard inquired about a compensation clause. Mr.
Walker stated that the county pays Mr. Burke, but that the city pay plan will
need to indicate that a salary was not set by ordinance.
24.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance to create the position of Emergency Operations Director; seconded by
Mr. Dupps. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes and Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance.

Discussion Regarding the Maintenance of Justice Lane
42.   Mayor Kriege asked Ms. Woolum if she had copies of the plats for the
properties on Justice Lane. She stated she gave her research findings to the
city attorney last month. She stated that part of Mr. Walker’s research should
have been obtaining copies of the plats. Mr. Walker asked her if Justice Lane
was shown on her plat. She replied no. Mr. Walker asked Ms. Woolum if Mr.
Scherder signed an easement for the road. She stated that she was unsure, but
that the sale of the property did not require it to be surveyed. She stated her
property had to be surveyed, as the other eighty-three acres was not platted.
43.   Mr. Walker stated that as he understands it, Justice Lane as used crosses
over Mr. Scherder’s property. Ms. Woolum stated that the original deed, which
was Mary Bannister’s farm, reserved a forty-foot right of way and that for
years this road has been unrestricted to public use. She stated that the
portion of the road shown on her plat was dedicated by the city.
44.   Mayor Kriege asked council how they wanted to proceed with this matter.
He stated the options are to affirm the maintenance of the road, repeal the
ordinance or do nothing at all. Mr. Ellison suggested reviewing both plots to
see what actually exists. Mr. Gabbard suggested obtaining a copy of the
Bannister farm plat so this could be reviewed also. Mr. Walker stated he could
get a copy of that if it is still on record at the courthouse, but advised that
he is advising council based on the current issues at hand. Mr. Walker went on
to say that the ordinance is the only thing stating this is a right-of-way and
that anything prior to that is a private matter between Ms. Woolum and her
neighbors. He stated a public right-of-way has to be owned by the public.
Again, Mayor Kriege suggested that the Planning & Zoning Committee review this
matter and make a recommendation to council.
45.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to, prior to dedicating Justice Lane, it should
be surveyed as prescribed and in a legal manner as a city street as it
presently exists. The motion died for lack of a second.
46.   Mayor Kriege suggested that Mr. Walker research this matter, then the
Planning and Zoning Committee review his findings and make a recommendation to
council. Mr. Ellison made a motion to have the city attorney obtain all plats
that touch Justice Lane and provide his research findings to council. Mr.
Bushong seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one
no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.

NOVEMBER 8, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the special meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the
Beechgrove Clubhouse. Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special
meeting was to discuss the following agenda items:
§   Discussion and Review of Potential Municipal Center Sites
§   Discussion and Review of Proposed Building Schemes
§   Discussion and Review of Financing and Budget Options
§   Discussion and Review of Design Proposal
§   Open the Floor for Citizen Feedback
2.   Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard. Jim
Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance was City
Administrator, Mark T. Wendling and City Attorney, Jeffrey S. Smith sitting in
for H. Lawson Walker.
3.   Mr. Wendling presented council with a summary report of the feasibility
study for a new municipal center that would house all city offices in one
central location. He stated that Matrix Architects was contracted to perform
the study, which was completed and presented to council in September. Mr.
Wendling stated that the study included evaluation of five proposed sites,
analysis of program requirements, building schematics and estimated costs of
construction. He stated that city staff members worked with Matrix on each
aspect of the study and that each potential site details the positive and/or
negative features. He stated that the positives to constructing a municipal
center at Memorial Park or Staggs Park is that these properties are owned by
the city, thus eliminating the added cost of purchasing land to build on. Mr.
Wendling examined each site in the Project Summary with council pointing out
the pros and cons of each site. He advised, that of the two building schematics
presented, that both staff and the architects recommended the split-level
design. He stated that the site of the current administration building was
briefly considered but it was determined to have too many expensive and safety
disadvantages to make it a viable site.
4.   Mr. Wendling reported that since the feasibility study was completed in
September, that council has suggested two other possible sites. The sites are:
5407 Madison Pike (at the corner of Peach Drive) owned by Taylor Smith and the
Masonic Lodge at 5403 Madison Pike. He stated that the Smith property is
currently for sale but that the Lodge property is not, and the trustees of the
Lodge may not be interested in selling the property. He stated the Smith
property would infringe upon the Peach Drive neighborhood, but that most of the
proposed sites would be in close proximity to a residential neighborhood.
5.   Mr. Wendling stated that the estimated construction costs range from $3.5M
to $4.3M and are detailed in the feasibility study report. He stated that the
data packets provided also include the building schematics and space needs
assessment. He stated that the space is less than what is actually needed and
it is recommended to construct a building large enough to withstand 10-20 years
of growth. He advised that adding on later would cost more in the long run.
6.   Also included in the data packet is the budget and financing options
available. Mr. Wendling advised that in order to move forward that council
would need to take measures to raise revenue. He stated the city could obtain a
loan through the Danville Bond Pool for a seventeen-year period or the
Jeffersontown Bond Pool for a twenty-seven year period. These pools are through
the Kentucky League of Cities. Mayor Kriege stated that the Jeffersontown Bond
Pool has fees associated with it because it is a relatively new pool; he feels
the cost incurred could be considerable over the life of the loan.
7.   Mayor Kriege stated that the Finance Director, Amy Guenther, has updated
the five-year projection. Mrs. Guenther reviewed the estimated fund balance
worksheet with council explaining the difference between the audited versus the
estimated figures. She stated that this worksheet looks at the trends over the
last three years. She reminded council that the city would be taking on the
added debt of the mortgage for the Senior Center and the smaller debt of the
cruiser lease-purchase payments. Mrs. Guenther stated that a certain amount of
additional revenue is predictable, but if a major corporation in the industrial
park would shut down, it would make a significant impact on the city’s revenue.
8.   Mr. Wendling suggested that as the economy grows and businesses expand
more development could come about, especially with the re-routing of State Hwy.
17 and other major road improvements. He went on to say that when comparing
Independence with other cities, similar in makeup, that we have the lowest
taxing revenue. Mrs. Guenther stated that Northern Kentucky Area Development
District did a similar comparison study and the results showed that
Independence was fifth lowest overall and second lowest in Kenton County. Mr.
Wendling reviewed the Household tax comparison by locality worksheet, which
compares the current makeup of revenue with other cities and shows potential
sources for revenue. The list of potential revenue sources include: insurance
premium tax, park tax, road tax, Senior Center tax, increase the property tax
rate at greater than the compensating rate, increase the payroll tax and non-
renewal of the cable board agreement would save the city $20,000. Mr. Wendling
stated that if the property tax rate was set at a rate greater than the
compensating rate plus 4% that it would be subject to voter recall. He also
suggested that the payroll tax, currently at 1.25 %, could be increased to 1.5%
or greater. Mr. Wendling advised that the Senior Center tax and the road tax
must be a referendum placed on the ballot at a general election.
9.   Mayor Kriege requested that council review the information presented and
be prepared to arrive at a conclusion by the December 3rd regular council
meeting. Mr. Moriconi inquired as to if the city could afford a $250,000 to
$300,000 annual mortgage payment without taking measures to adopt new or
increase current taxes to raise the revenue. Mrs. Guenther advised that was
uncertain, but that it may be possible to handle such a mortgage for a couple
of years, but probably not longer, without increasing the city’s revenue. Mr.
Kudera stated that other expenses would have to be considered, such as increase
in property insurance, etc. He stated that other related expenses could be
substantial. Mrs. Guenther advised that with the current level of revenue, the
Police and Public Works Departments would not be able to grow.
10.   Mr. Dupps asked Chief Butler if the current staffing of his department
could handle things. Chief Butler stated that calls are up 17% and he is
currently short in staff. He stated that he will feel compelled to ask for two
new officers next year and one every year thereafter. Chief Butler stated there
are many intangibles but is certain there will be a need for more officers in
the future.
11.   Mr. Wendling advised council that the Public Works Department also needs
to add staff in the coming year. He stated the growth in the city is becoming
very demanding on this two-man department. He also advised the administration
department will need additional staffing within the next five years. Mr.
Wendling stated that some issues couldn’t be answered until the fiscal budget
is reviewed each year but that it would be necessary to deal with one issue at
a time. Chief Butler said his department would continue to apply for grants to
offset some of the cost of staffing. Mr. Wendling commented on the dilemma
between adding staff and constructing a municipal center. He added that as far
as the police department’s prolonged rental of space from the county on the
second floor of the courthouse, the county has permitted the city to stay until
the process regarding the municipal center is complete. Mr. Wendling stated
that if the city does not move forward with this project, we will have to
discuss other options with the county to see if they will continue to lease
this space to the city. He stated they have expressed interest in using the
second floor of the courthouse for county offices and may not be agreeable to a
long-term lease for this space. Mr. Kudera stated that next year is an election
year and fears the next sitting Fiscal Court may not feel compelled to honor
the agreement with the city for this rental space.
12.   Mr. Kudera commented that he feels the site selection is important in
order to begin work on financing the project. Mayor Kriege stated that he feels
site selection and financing is an important package and advised council that
the Kentucky League of Cities has committed to lending the city the finances
needed to proceed. Mr. Ellison agreed that the city is in need of a municipal
building and informed council that this type of project was put off years ago
due to the need to build a sewer system. He questioned if the city knows how
much borrowing power we have. Mayor Kriege stated he has been assured KLC will
lend the city what we need. Mr. Ellison stated the debt from the sewer system
project might be a liability against our borrowing power. Mr. Kudera stated
that he feels the sewer system is self-sustaining and has no reflection on the
city tax rate.
13.   Mr. Moriconi expressed interest in purchasing only a section of the
Masonic Lodge property at 5403 Madison Pike instead of the entire property. Mr.
Ellison stated he doesn’t see the need to purchase this property. A lengthy
discussion ensued regarding possible sites, including the Smith property and
the Masonic Lodge property. Susan Keeny, project architect with Matrix, stated
there would be some work needed to the Smith property and that there would be
limited parking. She estimated the municipal center would need 3-4 acres for
building and parking space. She stated they have reviewed the Smith and Masonic
Lodge properties, but their findings are very preliminary. Mr. Ellison
questioned whether the buildings could fit on the Smith site. Ms. Keeny stated
that anything was possible when programming the spaces. Mayor Kriege stated
that square footage could be cut in the meeting room. Ms. Keeny also advised
that the lobby and council room could be tightened. She stated that it was
important to first determine a site and then the building schematic can be
adjusted to make it work on the site. Mr. Wendling stated that the actual
design phase will be where the details of the building will be more specific.
Mayor Kriege asked council if they were interested in obtaining the Smith
property. Mr. Moriconi stated that since the property abuts Memorial Park it is
a good location. He stated the property is for sale and he has talked with the
current owner and learned he will work with the city. Mr. Wendling asked the
city attorney to research as to whether the city can purchase property for more
than the fair market value. Mr. Kudera stated that the city could offer a price
and if the owner and the city couldn’t agree on price then the city could take
the property by eminent domain. Mayor Kriege stated he would like to look into
the purchase of the Lodge property also. Mr. Gabbard stated that he is a member
of the Lodge and said that he was not aware if they were interested in selling
the property. Mr. Bushong stated there is a lot behind the Lodge that may be
useful if needed. Mr. Moriconi asked Mr. Gabbard to ask the Lodge if they would
sell part of the lot. Mayor Kriege asked council if they wanted to consider
this site.
14.   Mr. Moriconi made a motion to move forward with the Smith property;
seconded by Mr. Ellison. City Attorney, Jeffrey S. Smith, stated that the
agenda does not specify that action would take place at this meeting and
recommended the motion be withdrawn. Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Ellison withdrew
their motion and second.
15.   Mayor Kriege asked if there was a consensus from council to move forward
with this by way of a cost analysis and site evaluation to see if the building
would fit on this site. Ms. Keeny said they could provide a proposal for a cost
estimate and evaluation for this site. Mr. Ellison stated he would like to see
the cost of moving the Memorial Park play equipment backed out of the original
estimate.
16.   Mr. Wendling stated the Memorial Park Master Plan is on hold indefinitely
with the introduction of these new sites that abut the park. Mr. Dupps asked if
the Smith site information would be prepared in time for the next special
meeting on November 26, 2001. Ms. Keeny did not promise but stated she would
try to be ready by then. Mayor Kriege asked if the design proposal could be
presented too. Ms. Keeny stated that a design proposal would be premature at
this time.
CITIZEN FEEDBACK
17.   Joanne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, spoke in favor of remodeling the
current Administration Building at 5247 Madison Pike next to her property. She
referred to Mr. Wendling’s opening remarks wherein he stated that the site of
the current Administration Building was considered early on in the feasibility
study for a possible site with the purchase of neighboring property and asked
why she hadn’t been contacted about this. Mr. Wendling stated this option was
discussed but was eliminated at the onset for various reasons. Mrs. Cobble
commented that she felt it was unnecessary to house both administration and
police in the same building and that the current administration building could
be easily added on to. She suggested renovating the old firehouse to house the
police department. Mr. Wendling explained that the county owns the old
firehouse, not the city, and the county has no interest in selling the building
to the city. He added that the city currently leases storage space in the old
firehouse, but is being evicted because the county is moving their Parks and
Recreation Department into the space. He stated the remodeling the current city
building might be more expensive in the long run. Mr. Wendling stressed the
need to concentrate all city offices in a campus type setting that would
produce better communications within the departments and serve the city for
many years. Mrs. Cobble stated the drive thru lane at the city building could
be easily converted and the building space doubled for considerably less than
the projected $4M for a new municipal center.
18.   Mr. Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, suggested the state might fill in the
hollow at Memorial Park (at the Madison Pike site) with fill dirt free of
charge. Mr. Wendling stated that the site would require a significant amount of
fill and work. Mrs. Cobble commented that she feels the area of the new
firehouse is a dangerous site in regard to traffic congestion. Again, she
suggested the city remodel the old firehouse into offices for the police
department. Mr. Wendling stated the county owns the firehouse. Mr. Dupps
explained that the city looked into the possibility of purchasing the old
firehouse a couple of years ago, but because the land that the firehouse sets
on was owned by the county the Independence Fire District accepted the county’s
offer to purchase the building. Mr. Kudera advised Mrs. Cobble that the lease
and ownership of the old firehouse building was never an option for the city to
purchase.
19.   Rita King, 6523 Sugar Camp Drive, suggested the city purchase the old
Ponzer’s Restaurant building at 5277 Madison Pike to renovate for police
department offices. Mr. Moriconi stated that he would like to see the city
avoid this type of ‘band-aid’ solution to this growing problem. He also
commented that the city doesn’t have time to coordinate obtaining fill-dirt for
the Memorial Park site. Mrs. King commented that she was not opposed to
building a new center, but that her main concern was how the city planned to
pay for a $4M municipal center.
20.   Mayor Kriege commented that a municipal center is a necessity and that it
can be funded if the city adds a revenue source. He stated that it is important
to move forward and that council will have to make some hard decisions. Mrs.
King commented that some of the council members promised not to raise taxes
when they were running for office. She stated that she wanted to see the
numbers on how the city planned to pay for this project. Mr. Kudera stated that
some of the council members may have promised not to raise taxes before
becoming familiar with the city finances and growing needs. He stated that
circumstances change and it is now time to reconsider, now that they know the
facts before them.
21.   Mrs. Cobble commented that she feels there should be a renovation plan
for the downtown area. Mr. Kudera commented that renovating the downtown area
would be expensive. Mayor Kriege stated that the city would soon be working
with the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission to design an individual
Comprehensive Plan for Independence, separate from the Kenton County Plan. He
commented that he cares very much about the future of the downtown area. Mr.
Kudera commented that he feels the downtown has moved to the Independence Towne
Center. He stated that many cities across the country are going broke trying to
revitalize their downtown areas and wondered how a city can bring people to the
downtown.
22.   Mr. Gabbard stated that he agrees with Mr. & Mrs. Cobble. He stated that
he would like to see the city purchase four or five acres from the Cobble’s,
fill in some of the low area, and remodel the current administration building,
and build a separate building to house the police department. He commented that
he would like to see the municipal center stay in the downtown area for
enhancement. Mr. Kudera stated that he feels the current administration
building would be better suited for offices, such as a dentist, doctor, etc.
that does not require a high volume of public traffic.
23.   Mrs. Cobble suggested using incentives to draw businesses to the downtown
area. Mr. Kudera stated that most businesses would request tax abatements,
which would take revenue away from the city, not add to it. Mayor Kriege stated
that the city originally had budgeted money for the Renaissance Program for the
downtown area, but had to withdraw the proposed funds, as there were other
pressing priorities that had to be met, specifically road repairs. Mr. Moriconi
stated that the good news for downtown is that the county is expanding their
offices, which will bring more people into the area. He also felt that when the
current city building is sold as office space that this would also keep the
downtown area vital.
24.   A member of the audience suggested applying for federal and state funds,
and soliciting private funds to revitalize the downtown area. Mrs. Cobble
commented that the emphasis should be on remaining in the downtown area to keep
it vibrant. Mr. Moriconi agreed that he would like to see the revitalization of
the downtown area, but stated that he is trying to look into the future of the
city. He stated that a municipal center should be functional for many years and
doesn’t feel the city offices moving down the street should hinder this, as a
business would occupy the building, keeping patrons in the area.
25.   Ms. Keeny commented that the administration building isn’t necessarily
the dependant factor that would keep the downtown alive; she stated that a
building couldn’t promise off shoots for future development. She stated that
working with preservation experts would provide more options. Mr. Kudera stated
that he and Mayor Kriege walked the downtown area looking for feasible sites
for a new municipal center and most possible sites were eliminated for one
reason or another.
26.   Mr. Perry Wing, 10734 Cypresswood Lane, shared his thoughts. He stated
that as things are evolving a lot of activity is currently being funneled in
the Towne Center area and that access to all with safety, as a basic concern
must be considered, no matter where the building is located. He stated there is
not a lot of flat land left in Memorial Park to develop, but he is in favor of
keeping the new building on Madison Pike and suggested downsizing some of the
building space. He commented that the Smith property will help with the
development of the building on the Madison Pike side of the park and suggested
phasing in the development over a 3-5-7 year plan. He stated that he sees the
city having many options and would like to see a plan initiated for the
renovation of the downtown area. He said that Independence is a small town with
big city dreams and believes the city is heading in the right direction.
27.   Mayor Kriege concluded by stating that council would need to review all
proposed sites and recommend the Memorial Park site off of Jack Woods Parkway
as the site he feels is best suited for development. He urged council to make a
decision that would take the city into the next 30-40 years. He stated the next
special meeting would be held on November 26, 2001 at the Kenton County
Extension Center on Marshall Road and asked council to be prepared to make some
decisions regarding this project so that the city can proceed. He stated that
if council had questions over the next couple of weeks to call him or Mr.
Wendling.
Adjournment
28.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Dupps the meeting was
adjourned. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 8:47 p.m.

Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
NOVEMBER 26, 2001
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the special meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. at the
Kenton County Extension Center. Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this
special meeting was to discuss the following agenda items:
§   Declare list of vehicles from the Police Department as Surplus Equipment
§   Resolution Approving the CBDG Payment for the Senior Center
§   Discussion and Possible Action Regarding Potential Municipal Center Sites
§   Discussion and Possible Action Regarding Proposed Building Schemes
§   Discussion & Possible Action Relating to Financing & Budget Options for a
Potential Municipal Center
§   Discussion and Possible Action Relating to a Design Proposal
§   Open the Floor to Citizen Feedback
§   Executive Session (if necessary)
2.   Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Jim Kudera and Chris
Moriconi answered roll call. Council Member, Ike Gabbard was absent. Also in
attendance was City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling and City Attorney, H.
Lawson Walker.
Declare List of Police Department Vehicles as Surplus Equipment
3.   Police Chief, Shawn Butler presented to council a list of three vehicles
that are no longer in service with the police department and requested they be
declared as surplus equipment so that the vehicles could be auctioned. He
stated that all three vehicles were 1994 Ford Crown Victorias having an excess
of 150,000 miles on each vehicle.
4.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to declare the three 1994 Ford Crown Victorias as
surplus equipment; the motion was seconded by Mr. Bushong. Roll call was
answered with five yes votes. Motion carried 5-0 in favor.
Resolution Approving the CBDG Monthly Payment for the Senior Center Expenses
5.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to read Resolution No. 2001-R-15 authorizing the
monthly CBDG payment for the Senior Center in the amount of $118,614.46. Mr.
Moriconi seconded the motion. Mr. Dupps asked where the current payment stands
on the schedule of payments. Mr. Wendling reported there has been an additional
change order regarding the ansul system in the kitchen which will amount to
approximately $6,000. He stated that the construction company will submit a
final payment request when the building is complete and a final certificate of
occupancy permit is issued. Mr. Bushong asked how the city would handle the
payment retainage. Mr. Wendling stated the retainage would be held until
everything is approved and all permits are issued. Mr. Walker read Resolution
No. 2001-R-15. Roll call was answered with five yes votes. Motion carried.
Discussion & Possible Action Regarding Potential Municipal Center Sites
6.   Mayor Kriege reported that he has worked with Matrix Architects to prepare
potential schemes for the expansion of the Route 17 Memorial Park site that
would include the Smith property at 5407 Madison Pike (at the corner of Peach
Drive) and the Masonic Lodge at 5403 Madison Pike as shown in the site
evaluation plans F-1 and F-2. He stated that since these sites were not
included in the original feasibility study contract, that Matrix has submitted
a project change notice in the amount of $1,750.00 for additional site
investigation and study of these two parcels of land. He requested council
approve this change notice for the feasibility study so that the city can
proceed with this project.
7.   Mr. Dupps asked if the existing building on the properties would be
demolished. Mr. Wendling stated the Smith house would be razed. Mayor Kriege
stated that if council wants to proceed with this site it would be necessary to
move forward with this parcel of land, as it appears the site would be feasible
for the building scheme. He stated that he felt the Masonic Lodge would also
need to be acquired. Mr. Ellison stated that he favors the F-1 scheme. He
stated that if the city pursues these parcels we should speak with a
representative of the Masonic Lodge to inquire interest in selling the
property. Mayor Kriege stated that parcel would be included in the additional
feasibility study and to proceed, council would need to approve the $1,750.00
feasibility change notice from Matrix.
8.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to proceed with the feasibility change notice to
approve the additional fee of $1,750.00 requested to Matrix Architects. Mr.
Moriconi seconded the motion. Mr. Bushong referred to the Site “F” evaluation
and asked if the future parking of sixteen spaces is the space currently
occupied by the mobile vehicle behind the Masonic Lodge. Mr. Kudera stated that
he believed it was. Mr. Moriconi asked if the split-level building design on
the F-1 site evaluation plan would accommodate another entrance. Mayor Kriege
advised this is a preliminary schematic and that details would be provided at a
later date when Matrix does an in depth study of the site. Mr. Kudera asked how
long it would take to complete the study of this additional site. Mr. Wendling
stated that he anticipated it would take two to three weeks. He stated that
Dugan & Meyers would provide the cost estimate, which would take some time to
determine. Roll call was answered with five yes votes. Motion carried
unanimously.
Discussion Regarding Proposed Building Schemes
9.   Mayor Kriege stated that the actual design of a building is a long way off
and addressed possible building schemes for consideration. He stated the staff
put forth a split level design as their recommended preference as it relates to
work flow and site position. Mayor Kriege stated the opportunity to solidify
office sizes, etc. would come at a later date. He asked council if there was a
consensus to look at other schemes for consideration during the design phase.
Mr. Dupps stated that he felt the office sizes presented in the preliminary
schemes were oversized, especially the council chambers. He stated that the
Senior Center could be utilized at times when more meeting space is needed. He
stated that a council chambers would be nice but felt that 250 seats was very
large and seemed redundant, since the Senior Center could accommodate large
crowds, when necessary. Mr. Kudera commented that the Building Committee would
consider the square footage cost estimates and decide if the reductions would
be necessary to reduce the overall cost of the building. Mayor Kriege commented
that during the design phase, the Building Committee could work through these
concerns. Mr. Moriconi voiced his concern about building the municipal center
to small to handle future growth. Mayor Kriege stated that Matrix Architects
met with city staff to determine office and other work area sizes taking future
growth into consideration.
Discussion Relating to Financing and Budget Options for a Proposed Municipal
Center
10.   Mr. Kudera reported that the Budget & Finance Committee met at 5:00 p.m.,
prior to this meeting. He stated the committee reviewed two critical issues.
Mr. Kudera commented that the present economy is good for the construction
industry and felt this would be a good time to assume this capital project. He
stated the other significant issue is to give Mayor Kriege the authority to
negotiate the necessary financing. Mr. Kudera recommended that council
authorize the mayor to secure a cap of $4.5-$5,000,000 in funds for this
project. He commented that that doesn’t mean the city will spend the entire
amount, but reminded council that funds will be needed to furnish the building
also. He recommended that a consensus be made to move forward with the project
and that council be prepared to act on this matter at the December 3, 2001
regular council meeting. Mayor Kriege commented that a plan would be difficult
to develop until the city secures the necessary financing for this project. Mr.
Kudera concurred and stated that the city needs to make a commitment to move
forward. He stated that there are options available to the city to generate
revenue and cited the option to increase the payroll tax and implement a road
tax, which would require a public referendum.
11.   Mayor Kriege advised he would try to bring good financing arrangements to
the December 3, 2001 council meeting along with the development of a good site
plan and schematics. Mr. Dupps commented that some financing options might not
be eligible until next August. Mayor Kriege stated it would be necessary to
address financing now in order to make the project work and start the process.
Mr. Dupps also was concerned that some financing may be eliminated. Mayor
Kriege advised that some revenues could be phased-in in proceeding fiscal years
and if referendums fail then other revenue options could be revisited. Mr.
Kudera advised the city has available revenues to proceed for some time, but
that currently, future revenues were not predictable. He felt that within six
months revenues would be more foreseeable. Mayor Kriege stated that Matrix
Architects has not provided the city with a full blown cost estimate, but hoped
to have it by the December 3, 2001 council meeting.
Citizen Feedback
12.   Joann Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, had several questions regarding the
Memorial Park Site #1 which included the number of acres that was to be used
for a city building and the size of the access road to the building and if
these structures would be calculated into the site plan. Mrs. Cobble also
questioned the acreage of some of the possible sites and why some sites were
eliminated and others were not considered. She expressed concern that some
property owners of proposed sites were not notified and implied that she may
have been willing to donate some of her land in order for the current city
building to expand at the current location. She also suggested that Rodney
“Biz” Cain might be receptive to donating the land he owns at Pelly Road and
Madison for a municipal center and asked if Mr. Cain had been approached about
donating this land.
13.   Mr. Wendling answered Mrs. Cobble’s concerns. He stated that the
schematics for a new building indicate the site would require approximately
three acres for a building and parking areas. He replied that an access road
would be a double lane road and that both the building and road would be
considered in the Memorial Park Plan. Mr. Wendling advised Mrs. Cobble that
specific sites were eliminated for various reasons, with size and/or cost to
purchase the land being the major factors.
14.   Mayor Kriege replied that Mr. Cain had not been contacted about donating
his land. Mayor Kriege and some of the council members pursued Mrs. Cobble
statement about donating some of her land to the city and pressed her for a
commitment of how much land she was willing to donate. She stated she would be
willing to give the city one acre. Mr. Kudera and Mayor Kriege stated that
would not be enough, as the city needs three acres of land. Mrs. Cobble
countered that her donation of one acre added to the 1.3 acres currently owned
by the city at that site would make for a 2.3-acre site. She stated that it was
unnecessary to construct a large parking area as she felt the city could use
the parking lot of Swindler & Currin Funeral Home and the Firstar Bank lot
adjacent to the city building. Mr. Kudera replied that it was unfair to
infringe upon private property owners neighboring the city building to provide
parking for city functions. He commented that he felt this was unacceptable.
Mrs. Cobble stated that she felt this could be mutually beneficial to both the
bank and funeral home. Mr. Kudera responded that Mr. Currin is currently in the
process of expanding his parking lot with the recent purchase of the land next
to the funeral home, as Mr. Currin doesn’t expect the city to provide parking
for his business.
15.   Mr. Kudera asked Mrs. Cobble what her objective is in this line of
questioning. Mrs. Cobble replied that she wanted to see the city building
remain in the downtown area of the city, which has indisputably been the heart
of town for the last 150 years. Mr. Kudera advised that that areas in the heart
of town are not large enough to be considered for this project. He went on to
say that the downtown area has shifted to the Towne Center. Mayor Kriege
interjected that he felt the downtown area was expanding and is now
encompassing a larger area of the Madison Pike corridor. Mrs. Cobble reiterated
that she feels the city hall should remain downtown and expressed concern that
two possible sites have not been fully investigated. She stated that half of
the downtown buildings were vacant or abandoned and with the city leaving the
area felt that this projects and image that the city officials don’t care. She
stated that if the two new buildings, specifically the Senior Center and the
new Firehouse would have been constructed in the downtown area it would have
been a $10M improvement to the area. Mr. Kudera stated that it was the city’s
responsibility to invest city funds the best way possible and the downtown area
is not the best way. Mayor Kriege shared Mrs. Cobble’s concerns and commented
that the downtown area is important to him and council, but advised Mrs. Cobble
that building in the downtown area is just not feasible. He stated that council
couldn’t solve the downtown problems and municipal building problems in one
step.
16.   Mr. Dupps asked Mr. Ellison how long the city building has been located
in the downtown area. Mr. Ellison replied the city offices have been in the
downtown area for the last 20+ years. Mr. Dupps asked Mrs. Cobble if the city
offices have been in this area for the last twenty years, how has this helped
the area remain vital. She replied that it has kept buildings from being
boarded up. Mr. Dupps stated that he was trying to understand her position and
asked how often she goes to the city building. She stated that was not a fair
question as she goes to the city building for other than business. Mr. Dupps
stated that he doesn’t see the need to locate the city building on the main
thoroughfare and many city buildings are not in the town area. Mrs. Cobble
countered that other cities do not have a prestigious courthouse in their city.
Mr. Dupps stated that most people only go to the courthouse once every four
years to renew their driver’s license. Mr. Moriconi commented that the city’s
vacating the current city building might be an incentive for another business
to occupy the space. He stated that it is not city government’s responsibility
to develop the downtown area, but felt it would take private enterprise to
vitalize the area. Mayor Kriege stated he would like to partner with the
business community in the task of revitalizing the downtown area. Mr. Moriconi
advised the city alone cannot save the downtown and felt it would take free
enterprise to do this.
17.   Mayor Kriege recapped the proposed building sites to include the
following: Memorial Park #1 (where the playground equipment is currently
located); Memorial Park #2 (facing Route 17) with the adjacent Smith property
at the corner of Peach Drive and Route 17; current city administration building
located at 5247 Madison Pike (at the corner of Carrie Way); Sterling Staggs
Park; the city’s Park & Ride lot located at 5292 Madison Pike; and Pelly Road/
Route 17 property. Mayor Kriege asked council if they would like more
information on the Memorial Park #2 and adjacent Smith property site. He
reiterated that the Sterling Staggs Park site would be eliminated at the land
was purchased with federal funds with a restriction that it was to be used as a
park. He stated this site would not have been proposed if he had been aware of
this restriction. Mr. Kudera stated that a deed restriction also exists for the
Independence Park in the Hartland Subdivision and if the city ever ceases using
the land as a park then the property would revert back to the donor, Arlinghaus
Builders, to use as residential building lots. Mayor Kriege stated his
preferred building site was Memorial Park #1.
18.   Mrs. Cobble asked who owns the existing Fire Stations #1 & #2. Mr. Kudera
replied that the Independence Fire District owns those buildings and advised
her that the city has no control or financial interest in the Fire District.
19.   Mrs. Linda Payne, 1832 Forest Run Drive, a resident and member of the
Independence Recreation Committee stated that it was a waste of tax dollars to
move the playground and shelter equipment from it’s current location in the
park to make way for a municipal center and showed a lack of planning at
Memorial Park. She stated that she felt the city needed a city planner to
address the growth concerns including the preservation of green space, which
she feels is being gobbled up. Mr. Kudera responded that the Independence
Tomorrow Committee had made recommendations regarding the growth issue to the
city council by way of a Strategic Plan, which was soundly rejected. He stated
that it might be possible to revive this committee. Mr. Ellison countered that
he felt the city has planned several capital improvements such as the Fowler
Creek Sewer Project, the Fire District’s new fire station and the restructuring
of Route 17. He stated the planning is there and that the city has too much
open land not to make plans for its development. Mr. Ellison stated the city
building should be near the new fire station even if the Masonic Lodge wants to
stay, as he does not favor taking the property by eminent domain. Regarding the
revitalization of the downtown area, Mr. Ellison stated that he did not want to
see the city disrupt the lives of the long-time residents in the poorer houses
along Madison Pike. He stated that most of those lots were designed too small
to even consider for today’s development. Mrs. Cobble interjected that she
feels the city is proposing an oversized city building, but agreed that she
would not want to see the city seize the resident’s property by eminent domain.
She felt the city should approach the property owners to see if they would be
willing to sell their land. She stated that she did not understand why
Independence needed to build a municipal center 26,000 square feet in size. Mr.
Ellison tried to explain the city needed to construct a building that would
accommodate growth for the next fifty years. He stated that other cities in
Northern Kentucky, more affluent communities, are landlocked and will not be
growing at the rate that Independence is and has been growing. Mr. Moriconi
concurred that other local cities are maxed out. Mr. Ellison stated that
Independence is geographically, the largest city in the state of Kentucky.
20.   Mrs. Cobble raised the issue of the city possibly raising the current
payroll tax rate. She stated she felt it was already higher than most other
cities in Northern Kentucky. Mr. Ellison and Mr. Kudera explained that
Independence does not have the industry the other cities have nor has
Independence imposed an insurance premium tax which most other cities have to
increase their revenue. Mrs. Cobble reminded council that some of them made
campaign promises not to raise taxes. Mr. Kudera stated that he would not make
a decision that he felt was necessary to make based on whether or not he would
be re-elected to this office.
Adjournment
21.   There being no further discussion, upon motion and second by Mr. Kudera
and Mr. Ellison the meeting was adjourned at 8:34 p.m. Motion carried with all
ayes.

PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
4.   Mrs. Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, addressed council about her previous
requests that the city provide street maintenance to Justice Lane. She
recounted her request and subsequent approval by council in December 1987 to
take over the maintenance of the street. She stated that since that time, on a
few occasions, at her request, the city filled some of the potholes with
gravel. She stated that she has also taken it upon herself to fill the potholes
with gravel on a few occasions. Mrs. Woolum reported that Mr. Smith of the
Independence Public Works Department recently informed her that he has been
advised not to treat the street as it is owned by Mr. Bobby Scherder. She
stated that she has appeared before council for the last couple of months
requesting a decision be made as to whether or not the city is going to honor
the ordinance passed in 1987 approving Justice Lane as a city maintained
street. She also reminded council that a state law exists that proclaims a road
can be dedicated informally when it has been open to public use for more than
five years thereby causing it to be presumed as a public right of way. She
stated that she feels the city has had ample time to review this matter and
would like the city council to uphold the city ordinance and K.R.S. regarding
public right of ways and resume maintenance of Justice Lane.
5.   Mr. Ellison, chairman of the Planning & Zoning Committee, reported that
the committee reviewed and discussed the matter with the city attorney and
determined the matter to be a neighborhood dispute and don’t agree with Mrs.
Woolum that Justice Lane is a public right of way. He stated this road and/or
right of way has never been measured for accuracy, nor does the city ordinance
establish the meets and bounds necessary to adopt the street for maintenance.
Mr. Ellison stated the committee believes that Justice Lane is a private
street. Mrs. Woolum replied that she believes the state statute should be
upheld by the city. She stated that she has never discussed this matter with
Mr. Scherder and that it is not a dispute between neighbors. Mr. Ellison stated
that Mr. Scherder staunchly objects to the city’s maintenance of his road. Mrs.
Woolum stated that she had hoped the city would thoroughly research the
Kentucky Revised Statute regarding public right of ways and come to the
realization that Justice Lane is not a private road so that the maintenance of
this street would be resumed. Mr. Ellison expressed concern that a decision
either way, for or against providing maintenance for the street, could possibly
result in legal action taken against the city. She asserted that she wanted for
her records, and has received, a final response from the city regarding their
position in this matter. Mayor Kriege advised the matter was discussed at the
last council meeting and the majority of council concurred that Justice Lane is
a private street.
6.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to not provide street maintenance to Justice
Lane; seconded by Mr. Kudera. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and
two no votes cast by Mr. Gabbard and Mr. Bushong. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.

2002 Minutes
JANUARY 7, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant from the Grace Community Church gave the
invocation. Council Members, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard,
Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance was City
Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the November 26, 2001 Special Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve the minutes of the November 26, 2001
special council meeting as amended. Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call
answered with five yes votes and one abstain from Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried
5-1 in favor.
Approval of the Minutes of the December 3, 2001 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of December 3, 2001 as submitted. Mr. Bushong seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Discussion Regarding the Financing/KLC Pooled Lease Program for a Proposed
Municipal Center
4.   Mayor Kriege introduced William Skees, attorney with Frost Brown Todd LLC,
and acting as bond attorney for the city. Mayor Kriege stated that Mr. Skees
was present to explain the proper financing of, answer any questions the
council members have regarding the Kentucky League of Cities Pooled Lease
Program, the 1989 Series, City of Danville Poole.
5.   Mr. Skees explained that as bond attorney, his role would be to ensure
that the bond is validly issued, not to advocate for or against securing the
bond. He advised that the Resolution presented would authorize the
participation in the Kentucky Municipal League Pooled Lease Finance Program,
Series 1989, for up to $5M for the construction of a proposed municipal center.
He stated that the way a bond works is that the city will deed the property to
the lien, and then lease it back for financing of the bonds. Mr. Skees stated
that the bond will be similar to the bonding of the Senior Center is that it
will be a variable rate debt. He stated the interest rate will vary and be set
on an annual basis and that the current rate today is 4.160%. He stated the
Senior Center rate was 4.9% and the city is currently at an advantage as the
rate has decreased significantly. Mr. Skees advised that PNC Bank would assess
fees to administer this program.
6.   Mr. Gabbard asked what the amount of interest would be over the seventeen-
year life of the bond. Mr. Skees stated this information is detailed in the
financial handout documents provided and stated the project assumption would
yield $1,971,000 in interest costs. Mr. Moriconi asked if there was a cap on
the interest rate over the life of the bond. Mr. Skees stated that if the
interest rate begins to creep up then council could choose to pay off the bond
without incurring prepayment penalties.
7.   Mr. Kudera reported that the Budget and Finance Committee reviewed the
pooled bond program and has agreed there is no better time than now to consider
a good finance package for this project. He stated that the bond would have a
$5M limit and suggested council approve this bond package with this limit, as
this is an excellent deal for the city. He stated that the Danville Bond Pool
which these funds will be derived from is nearing its’ end and other available
pools will be at a higher interest rate. He advised that the reason the
Danville Pool is cheaper is that the cost of issuance of the bonds have been
paid off. Mr. Bushong requested that the documents include wordage that would
limit the interest rate to 4.4% with council approval necessary to extend over
that maximum rate. Mr. Skees and Mr. Walker agreed that a section could be
added to the Resolution to stipulate that requirement. Mr. Ellison inquired if
there would be a maximum cap on points over the seventeen-year life of the
bond. Mr. Skees advised that the bank fees would be a constant and that the
interest rate will vary with the market but the city’s remedy to that will be
to refinance.
Resolution No. 2002-R-01 Authorizing Participation in the KLC Pooled Lease
Finance Program
8.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to read Resolution No. 2002-R-01 authorizing the
participation in the Kentucky Municipal League Pooled Lease Finance Program,
Series 1989, to include a section that would limit the interest rate to 4.4%.
Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Mr. Gabbard asked how the city would repay
this debt, as the funds were not in the budget. Mayor Kriege responded that the
Finance Committee has reviewed several funding options. Mr. Kudera stated that
there are some options available to increase revenues to fund this project and
advised that discussions have centered on increasing the payroll tax rate,
implementing a property tax rate of compensating plus four percent with an
additional two percent over that, and putting a referendum on the general
election ballot to implement an ad valorem property tax to be used for the
maintenance of roads. He stated the committee would begin to look at the
reserve funds and begin the process necessary to generate the needed revenue.
Mr. Kudera stated that he felt comfortable that the city could begin the
project without the necessary tax increases for a year or two. Mr. Gabbard
expressed concern that the council would bind future administrations to funding
this project. He stated that he felt the city should focus on and could afford
to construct a building for the Police Department and that the administration
department could exist in the current space for the next few years. He stated
that he felt a facility could be constructed for the police department for
about $1M.
9.   Mr. Gabbard reminded council that five members made campaign promises that
they would not raise taxes. Mr. Kudera stated that it is time to move forward
and advised Mr. Gabbard that the property tax rate has decreased every year for
the last several years. He disagreed that the city should focus only on a
facility for the police, thereby starting the process all over again in the
next few years when the administration department outgrows their current
facility. Mr. Gabbard stated that he felt it was important to keep one’s word
and that he will support a facility for only the police department.
10.   Mayor Kriege stated that the Finance Committee is not interested in
increasing taxes without voter input and would like to begin by placing the
referendum for a ad valorem (road) tax on the November ballot. He stated that
if the voters do not support this tax then the city would move forward with the
next plan to generate revenue by looking at the property tax or payroll tax.
Mr. Gabbard stated that he is not willing to bind the next administration to
funding this capitol project.
11.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Moriconi, Mr. Walker read
Resolution No. 2002-R-01 in title only. Roll call was answered with five yes
votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard citing that the city does not have
the revenue in hand to pay for the proposed building. Motion carried 5-1 in
favor.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
12.   Mr. Chuck Berling addressed council with a proposed Stage II development
plan for a section of the Villages of Beechgrove. He requested approval of a
zone change in order to change the Stage II plan from condos to single-family
construction. He stated the original plan called for 106 condos and he would
like to build 42 single-family homes instead. Mr. Moriconi wondered if this
request should be taken to the Beechgrove Homeowners Association. Mr. Berling
stated this approval would have to come from the city. Mr. Gabbard asked if
these houses would be starter homes and asked what the size of the lots would
be. Mr. Berling stated the lot size would vary but average out at fifty-foot
lots. He advised that the houses would cost between $110,000 and $130,000. Mr.
Moriconi asked if the houses would require a brick front. Mr. Berling stated
there would be alternate front elevations, but that materials were not
specified. Mr. Bushong asked if sewer and water lines were available for this
development. Mr. Berling stated that sewer lines were available along Bristow
Road, which they would tie into, and that new water mains are available that
they will access. He stated that the Planning Commission has reviewed the
preliminary plans and if council supports this zone change, it will go before
them for approval. Mr. Bushong stated that the Beechgrove Homeowners
Association is not aware of this proposed development. He asked Mr. Berling the
number of streets that will be constructed for this development. Mr. Berling
stated there would be one main road with two cul-de-sac streets and they will
be constructed to Kenton County specifications.
13.   Mr. Ellison stated that Mr. Berling has presented this proposed
development plan to the Planning & Zoning Committee and they are recommending
approval. He stated that he feels this plan reduces the number of living units
from 106 to 42 and that Mr. Berling will build a quality development. He stated
that changing this from multi-units to single family units was a fair trade
off.
14.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to approve the Stage II development plans
proposed by Mr. Berling for the specified section of the Villages of Beechgrove
permitting single family homes in place of the original plan to build 106 condo
units. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with all ayes.
Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
15.   Mitchell Wade, Willow Drive, addressed council regarding his longstanding
grievance regarding the swampy area of his yard that he asserts is the
aftermath of the sewer pipe construction several years ago. He stated that he
feels the city should support the residents and not the contractors employed to
perform this job. He reported that when a supervisor from the Sanitation
District recently inspected this swampy area of his property that he was told
that someone would do something to remedy the situation. He stated that now the
Sanitation District wouldn’t do anything to correct this problem. He requested
that the city provide to him in writing a letter stating the city was not
responsible for the drainage problem on his property.
16.   In an unrelated matter, Mr. Wade questioned the city’s law and
enforcement of roadside signs. He stated that his son owns an auto detail shop
and had placed a sign along the roadway advertising a special sale and was told
by the city that he had to remove the sign or he would be cited. Mr. Wade
expressed concern that his son was being singled out as he feels there are many
signs placed in the right of way throughout the city that have gone unchecked.
Mr. Wendling stated that about a month ago the Zoning Administrator, along with
the Public Works employees, did a sweep of the signs that were illegally placed
in the right of ways throughout the city. He stated that the enforcement of
this zoning violation was not biased. Father Berschied, Pastor of St. Cecilia
Church, commented that the church has recently had their signs pulled also.
17.   Mr. Wade’s last concern presented to council was in regard to the city’s
recent denial of a text amendment change that his brother has requested for the
property located at 6429 Taylor Mill Road (at the corner of Cox Road). He
stated his brother has requested the property be permitted to be used as a used
car lot and was told the city was not interested in this type of development.
He stated that the property was originally a gas station and did not understand
why a car lot business did not conform to this property. Mr. Gabbard commented
that the Planning & Zoning Committee met with Lance Wade and told him he did
not know how council would feel about this type of business in that location.
Mr. Wendling stated that the committee had expressed that they were not
interested in changing a NSC (Neighborhood Shopping Center) to include used car
lots. Mr. Ellison added that the committee felt it was difficult to control the
type of cars that would be for sale. Again, Mr. Wade requested the city put
their decision in the form of a formal letter. Mr. Wendling suggested that Mr.
Wade could expend the $150.00 fee and make application to the Kenton County and
Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission for a text amendment for this property,
then if approved it would formally come before city council for consideration.
Mayor Kriege stated that Mr. Ellison provided Mr. Wade with the reason the city
would not be favorable for this type of business in that location. He went on
to explain to Mr. Wade that when a text amendment is made it affects all like
properties, not just the property that requested the amendment. Mr. Wade stated
that he feels the text regarding this zone is evasive and has considerable
omissions, as it does not make sense to him that a gas station for cars is
permitted, but a used car lot is not permitted.
18.   Barbara Gabbard, 5140 Madison Pike, addressed council regarding her
concern that the city is taking on more debt than the citizens can handle with
the recent obligations of the new Senior Center and now the proposed Municipal
Center. She stated that she feared the taxpayers would be left to pick up the
bill with increased taxes to pay for these expenses. She encouraged the
citizens to express their feelings about the proposed budget deficit. She
stated that the Senior Center was larger and more costly than anticipated and
encouraged council to act responsibly and lookout for the city’s best interests
before proceeding with a municipal center. She stated that the citizens could
only pay so much in taxes as they have other expenses of growing families. She
stated that the city should be operated similar to a business. Mrs. Gabbard
stated there is no question that the city needs a police facility to fulfill
their special needs but questioned going into debt to build a municipal center.
She expressed concern that the city is proposing the hiring of a Senior Center
Director as a city employee and cited that the position does not even exist in
the Personnel Policy and wondered how the city was going to manage to pay for
this additional personnel and the expense of operating the Senior Center. In
closing, she commented that she felt the city was putting the cart before the
horse.
19.   Mayor Kriege responded that the Senior Center Board of Directors
encountered some stumbling blocks with the hiring of a Senior Director. He
stated that the final candidates for the position did not feel the Board of
Directors could provide job security, which made it difficult to fill the
position. Mayor Kriege stated that the city is working on the assumption that
the Board of Directors will provide the salary for the Director by way of
grants, etc. Mr. Kudera commented that while the city should not spend money
they don’t have, he felt the city should provide services to the seniors as
well as other residents.
