Award Bid for Sidewalk Construction from Hartland Subdivision to Walnut Hall
Drive
23.   City Engineer, Dave Whitacre presented a tabulation sheet and reported
that five bids were received by the city for this project. He stated that the
lowest bidder was RU-NIC who did not provide an adequate bid bond, but instead
provided a company check for only 7.85% of their bid, $39,906.75, which is less
than the 10% required. Therefore, Mr. Whitacre recommended that RU-NIC’s bid be
rejected. Mr. Whitacre stated that the second lowest bid was from Ray Prus &
Son, Inc. He stated he is familiar with this company, that they are well
qualified and recommended that council award the bid to Ray Prus as the lowest
and best bid. Mr. Gabbard asked if this company has constructed a lot of
sidewalks. Mr. Whitacre stated that this company does not bid a lot of
sidewalks, but stated that it is rare that they are a low bidder. He stated
that they are a large contractor and recently performed a good job for the City
of Fort Thomas. Mr. Gabbard asked if the bids came in lower than anticipated.
Mr. Wendling stated this project had been budgeted higher than the low bids
received. Mr. Whitacre stated that upon acceptance by council they would draw
up a contract with the bidder that would indicate a start date for the project.
24.   Councilmember Moriconi moved to award the sidewalk construction bid to
Ray Prus & Son, Inc. as the best and lowest bid in the amount of $44,827.00,
seconded by Councilmember Dupps. Roll call was answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 6-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Placing an Ad Valorem (Road) Tax on the November General
Election Ballot
25.   Mayor Kriege presented a proposed ordinance for council’s consideration
that would levy a special ad valorem tax on all taxable property within the
city in order to provide funding for the maintenance and repairs of public
streets. He stated the proposed tax would be placed on the November General
Election ballot for approval by the voters. Mr. Gabbard asked if enactment of
this ordinance would be contingent on the approval of the voters. City
Attorney, Mr. Walker advised that Section 65 of the K.R.S. provides for the
city to authorize commencement to propose this tax by ordinance then placed on
the ballot for passage in the general election. He stated that this ordinance
is nothing until it is passed in November. A suggestion was made to add a
section to the ordinance that would clarify the ordinance would be enacted upon
voter approval in the general election in November. Mr. Kudera stated the
Budget and Finance Committee suggested a rate of .06¢ per $100.00 of assessed
value for this tax.
26.   Councilmember Kudera moved, with second from Councilmember Gabbard, that
the proposed ordinance receive a first reading. Mr. Moriconi asked for
clarification that he is not voting to raise taxes, but agreeing to send this
proposed tax to the general election in November for endorsement by the voters.
Mr. Gabbard confirmed Mr. Moriconi’s analysis and suggested the need for
council to promote this ad valorem tax to the voters. Motion carried with all
ayes and Mr. Walker gave a first reading of the proposed ordinance that
included language stating the tax referendum would be placed on the November
ballot.
Discussion/Authorizing Mayor to Enter into a Contract with Cole+Russell
Architects, Inc. for Municipal Building

with Cole+Russell Architects for the design of a new Municipal Building. He
introduced David Acomb and John Russell, who were present from the architect
firm to answer any questions council might have regarding the contract. Mayor

Cole+Russell unanimously from three architect firms that were interviewed for
this project.
28.   Mr. Gabbard directed his question regarding Section 10.1 on page 13 of
the agreement for services. He stated this section regarded direct personnel
expenses and asked for an explanation of why the city would be obligated to pay
benefits for the architect’s personnel. Mr. Russell stated that this section
could be removed as the fee charged to the city is calculated and does not rely

fee would start at 8% (of the estimated construction cost) as the basis, then
go to a fixed cost from there. Mr. Russell concurred, and further explained,

City Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
30.   Mr. Wendling referred council to an inventory list of used sewer badger
meters and flow monitors, equipment the city is no longer utilizing, and a
letter from the City of Walton offering to purchase this equipment for $500.00.
Mr. Wendling asked the city engineer, Mr. Whitacre to expound on this
equipment. Mr. Whitacre stated the equipment is currently being stored at his
office. He said it was used from 1996 through 1999 and was originally purchased
to monitor the sewage flow as required by the Kentucky Division of Water. He
stated the city is no longer required to perform this monitoring and the
Sanitation District has indicated they are not interested in obtaining these
meters. Mr. Whitacre stated he was aware that the City of Walton occasionally
performs testing of their sewer system to identify and locate inflow and
infiltration problems and the equipment could be of benefit to them. He stated
that no other cities in Boone, Kenton or Campbell County have a need to perform
any sewer monitoring.
31.   Mr. Kudera moved to declare the five flow monitors, one 15-inch band, one
12-inch band, four 8-inch bands and one connector cable as surplus property.
Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
32.   Councilmember Bushong moved, with second from Councilmember Gabbard to
authorize Mayor Kriege to sell the surplus sewer monitoring equipment to the
City of Walton for $500.00. Mr. Ellison asked that we stipulate the sale to
allow Independence to borrow or rent the equipment from Walton if the need
would ever arise. Roll was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0

due to the additional evaluation of adjoining property.

Discussion of NKAPC Landscape Regulations – Mike Schwartz
7.   Mayor Kriege presented to council a proposed ordinance that would provide
landscape regulations in zones with the exception of single-family, two family
and agricultural areas. He introduced Mike Schwartz from the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning Commission who gave a more detailed explanation regarding this
proposal. Mr. Schwartz advised that the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission staff members drafted the proposed landscape regulations with
consultations from the Home Builders Association and other agencies. He stated
that the entire process took about one and one half years to complete and that
the Commission held several public meetings to hear comments and suggestions.
Mr. Schwartz stated the regulations would apply to industrial, commercial and
office building zones, not to single and duplex residential zones. He stated
the regulations are varied depending on the type of development. He stated that
the landscaping required for a commercial development situated next to a
residential property would be more stringent in order to provide a stronger
buffer between the two zones. He stated that the proposal addresses interior
landscaping for a development and that it would require five percent of a
parking lot to be landscaped and even specified the type of trees to be planted
that would control maintenance issues. Mr. Schwartz stated that landscaping
around dumpsters is also addressed so that the opening to the dumpster would
not be visible from the street. He stated the proposal also would require
certain landscaping for conditional use areas. Mr. Schwartz stated that other
guidelines are provided in the instruction manual and planting guide for
various alternatives. Mr. Schwartz stated that he has met with the city’s
Planning & Zoning Committee to discuss this proposal and stated the Planning
Commission is recommending that the landscape regulations be adopted by the
city. Mr. Ellison, Chairman of the Planning and Zoning Committee, stated that
the committee recommends the city attorney draft an ordinance, but would first
like the council to review the proposed regulations submitted by Mr. Schwartz.
Mr. Schwartz advised he has made presentations to several other Northern
Kentucky cities that are giving consideration to adopt these regulations as
well. Mr. Dupps suggested having a first reading of the ordinance prepared by
Mr. Walker, with amendments, if any, to be made next month after council has
had a chance to review the regulations.
Privileges of the Floor
8.   Mitchell Wade, 640 Willow Drive, stated that at the last council meeting
he had requested two letters from the city regarding two separate issues. He
stated that the first letter he received was regarding his request for a text
amendment to permit a car lot at the corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road
wherein the letter stated that the city doesn’t feel this text amendment was
needed. Mr. Wade stated that he did not ask for a letter stating the city does
not feel the “need”, but that the city refuses to support his request.

property has endured since the installation of the Fowler Creek Sewer lines
several years ago. He stated the other letter from the city regarding this
issue indicated the city feels there is no evidence the sewer lines were
installed improperly, which he disagrees with. He feels the city is not
accepting responsibility for the condition of his property.
10.   Mayor Kriege responded by stating that Mr. Wade has been given every
opportunity by this council to present his grievances. He stated that council
has given him numerous occasions to provide evidence that the current condition
of his property was a result of the installation of the sewer lines. Mayor
Kriege stated that council has heard all this before and asked council if they
wanted to continue to debate this issue with Mr. Wade. Hearing no assertions,
Mayor Kriege closed the discussion with Mr. Wade.
11.   Bob Dodson, 3921 Trappers Court, reminded council that the commercial
trucks parked in the Hunters Green Subdivision, which he reported at the
December meeting, are still in violation. He wondered why these violators have
not complied with the ordinance prohibiting this. Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Dodson
to submit the address to Mr. Wendling so that he can make inquires with the
Zoning Administrator about this violation. Mayor Kriege stated that the process
of ordering compliance should have already begun, but that it takes time.
12.   Keith Napier, 8976 Supreme Court, addressed council regarding the
amendment to the flag lots ordinance. He stated that the text amendment would
be discussed at the February 7, 2002 meeting of the Kenton County and Municipal
Planning and Zoning Commission and that council would not act on this until a
recommendation is received after that date. Mayor Kriege stated that he hoped
to have a first reading of a proposed ordinance that would amend the text
regarding this ordinance. Mr. Wendling stated that the proposed text would
require the flag lot to be one and one-half times the size of the front portion
of the property. He advised Mr. Napier that he might need to change the size of
his lot to conform to this text. Mayor Kriege recommended that Mr. Napier
attend the Thursday meeting of the Kenton County and Municipal Planning and
Zoning Commission.

Proposed Annexation of a 500 Acres area along Hogreffe Road/Maher Road/Bristow
Road
18.   Before Chuck Berling made his presentation regarding the proposed
annexation and development, Mr. Walker advised council that at one time he
represented one of the developers of this project, but wanted to clarify that
he no longer represents them.
19.   Mayor Kriege introduced Mr. Chuck Berling who would present an overview
of the proposed development of the west side area along Hogreffe, Maher and
Bristow Roads. He stated the developers would include Arlinghaus, Berling and
Glenhurst Development.
20.   Mr. Berling advised that approximately 440 acres would be developed in
the area and that the property owners are requesting the land be annexed into
the city of Independence. He stated there are four large parcels, which are
contiguous and would meet the at the city border by the Battleridge Subdivision
at Bristow Road. He stated that Phase I of the Glenhurst Development has been
approved and is under construction off of Maher Road at the Boone/Kenton County
line. He stated the Williams Woods subdivision along Bristow Road would have
80-foot lots and border the Glenhurst Development, which will have 50, 70 and
80-foot lots. He stated that a new elementary school would be located in this
area and they are currently working to designate a site for the school. He
stated it would take approximately a two to four year period to get the
approval and actually construct the school. He stated that the developers
originally planned to allocate thirteen acres for active recreational park use,
but has evolved to include a school in the area on five acres with the
remainder being developed for recreation. He stated the Glenhurst development
would have twenty to thirty acres available for the city to allocate for a park
system, but if the city did not want the area then they would approach Kenton
County for a county park. He stated that another significant part of this
development would be to construct a new connector road for Hogreffe and that
they are currently in preliminary agreement with the Kenton County Fiscal Court
to rebuild Hogreffe. He stated that long-term plans would be to eventually
connect Maher, Hogreffe and Bristow to ease transportation in this area. They
would also address the issue of the railroad tracks in order to access the
other part of the subdivisions. Mr. Berling stated that the development would
be phased over a ten to fifteen year period, depending on how quickly the
building lots are sold. He stated that overall density would be 2.4 units per
acre and that Arlinghaus Builders would develop three quarters of the lots with
other builders developing the remaining, smaller lots. Mr. Kudera asked if
there would be access to the Boone County industrial park. Mr. Berling stated
there would not be direct access as there is a building currently there that
cuts off access to the subdivision. But stated that there will be three ways to
access the development from Mt. Zion Road. Mr. Kudera asked if there were plans
for a firehouse in the area. Mr. Mike Schwartz interjected that the
Comprehensive Plan recommends a firehouse location, as well as an elementary
school, but that the Plan does not show an exact site for a firehouse.
21.   Mr. Wendling stated that the School Board has expressed excitement
regarding the offer of free land in this development and has stated that they
will definitely build a school on the site. He stated the city could develop
ball fields, but that it may require zone changes as it is close to a proposed
industrial area.
22.   Mr. Bushong asked what the cost of the homes would be. Mr. Berling stated
the smaller homes would be near the Boone County line and the original plan is
for a cluster overlay for the 50-80 foot lots in an R1-C and R1-D zones. Mr.
Wendling stated the Planning & Zoning Committee is recommending that the city
annex this development. Mr. Berling stated that Williams Woods construction
would begin this summer and that Glenhurst Development is already under
construction. Mr. Berling discussed layout of the development and the
connections of the various subdivisions with Mr. Moriconi. Mr. Bushong asked
how many lots would be developed. Mr. Berling stated that the development
originally planned for 1061 lots. Mr. Wendling stated that the school will take
a large area causing this number of lots to decrease and that some lot sizes
may be increased also affecting the final number of lots developed. Mr. Berling
stated that the home prices would range between $125,000 to $275,000. Mr.
Berling stated that the school board has very specific topography requirements
for the land in order to build a school. Mr. Berling advised that the final
layout of the development would change somewhat to accommodate the school needs
and design the infrastructure. Mr. Dupps asked what the square mileage of the
entire area would be. Mr. Berling replied it would be around 2/3 of a square
mile.
23.   Mayor Kriege presented to council a proposed ordinance that would start
the annexation process. Mr. Walker advised that the city has received
agreements from the various owners requesting to be annexed. It stated that
this is an annexation by agreement, but the owners are allowing the city to
annex the land in exchange for the city granting the zone change they are
requesting. Mr. Walker advised that the first step in the process would give
the city the ability to go to the Planning Commission to propose the
annexation. He stated this process would begin with the first reading of a
proposed ordinance pronouncing the intent to annex the land. He stated that
then the city would go back to the Planning Commission for a hearing for the
requested zone change, then the zone change request would be presented to the
council and a first reading of an ordinance agreeing to annex the land. Mayor
Kriege stated that the entire process could take until May to complete.
24.   Mr. Kudera made the motion, seconded by Mr. Bushong to have a first
reading of the proposed ordinance declaring the intent to annex the land. No
roll call; motion carried with four ayes, with Mr. Ellison abstaining. Mr.
Walker read the proposed ordinance.

they would be looking at ways to cut costs.

PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
4.   William Miller, 4394 Oliver Road, addressed council regarding the Annual
Planning Session that is scheduled for Saturday, March 16, 2002. He asked if
the agenda would include discussion about a proposed tax increase. Mayor Kriege
replied that the agenda had not been determined yet, and that no decisions are
made at the Planning Session just discussions on priority issues concerning the
city. Mayor Kriege stated that comments from citizens would be permitted. Mr.
Miller turned his remarks to the council members by reminding them that four of
the six current council members made campaign promises at the public forum held
at Summit View School that they would not vote to increase taxes. Mayor Kriege
disputed Mr. Miller’s assertion by stating that less than four of the council
made this promise. Mr. Dupps commented that it was possible that the
discussions at the Planning Session would revolve around tax decreases as well
as increases.
Discussion Regarding Intent to Annex Approximately 500 Acres Along West Side of
City
5.   Before this discussion began, Council Member Gabbard announced that
because a friend of his owned some of the property that may be annexed he would
not participate in this discussion, excused himself and vacated the room.
6.   Mayor Kriege introduced Chuck Berling who was the spokesperson
representing a group of developers that were requesting annexation into the
city. Mr. Berling stated that some loose ends have been tied up since last
month’s council meeting. He stated that they have received approval of the
school and it’s location of the site by the State Board of Education. Mr.
Berling distributed drawings for council to review. He pointed out that
Hogreffe Road has been realigned with placement of the proposed school at the
intersection. He also indicated that a site has been designated for a future
firehouse and police substation. Mr. Berling stated that sewer, water and gas
utilities will be run to the area. Mr. Bushong asked when the school would be
built. Mr. Berling advised that it would be approximately three years before
the site would be reconstructed and that the school board has agreed to build
the school within ten years. He stated that the school board’s bonding
capabilities will determine when they can build. He stated that the school
board anticipates building this in the next several years and that it will be
large enough to house six hundred students. Mr. Berling stated that they hope
to obtain some state funds to reconstruct the county roads.
7.   Mayor Kriege turned the floor over to City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker who
explained to council the procedure before them. He stated that in addition to
the request by this group to have this property annexed into the city, they are
also requesting a zone change. He advised that presently the zone change
request is before the Kenton County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission
who will hold a public hearing on this matter this Thursday and must first
receive approval by the Commission before being acted upon by City Council. Mr.
Walker stated that council should first complete the process of their intent to
annex by having a second reading of the ordinance to do so. He stated that it
was necessary to put the annexation in place in order to give the city standing
in this process. He explained that the blanks in the proposed ordinance would
be filled in with the date of publication. Mr. Walker explained that the intent
to annex allows the owners of the property sixty days to oppose the annexation;
although he does not anticipate this will happen, as this is an annexation by
request of the owners. Mr. Walker advised that in addition to a second reading
of the intent to annex ordinance, that a proposed ordinance to actually annex
the property is being presented to them tonight for a first reading. Mr. Dupps
expressed concern that the process may not proceed as outlined.
8.   Mr. Walker stated that a special meeting of council would be needed to
have a first reading of a zone change ordinance as requested by the group of
developers. He stated that the second reading of the ordinance would be at a
subsequent meeting probably sometime in April. He stated that first the city
would need to receive a recommendation from the Planning Commission regarding
the zone change request. Mr. Kudera questioned the need to have a second
reading on the intent to annex ordinance. Mr. Walker advised that it was
necessary to approve the intent to annex so that the Planning Commission can
deal with the city’s plan.
9.   Mr. Dupps stated that the Public Safety Committee has discussed the
additional burden this development would put on the police department. Chief
Butler concurred that this development will have a major impact in the future
with the addition of a new school and approximately 1100 homes.

10.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Dupps there was a second
reading, by title only, of the intent to annex Ordinance No. 2002-O-04. Mr.

1st Reading of Proposed Ordinance Annexing Approximately 500 Acres of
Unincorporated Area on West Side
11.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed
ordinance that would annex approximately 500 acres of unincorporated land lying
contiguous and adjacent to the city. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Mr.
Bushong questioned the difference in having a first and second reading of the
ordinance as opposed to one emergency reading. Mr. Walker advised that it is
not recommended to annex property by emergency. He stated that adopting certain

Ordinance No. 2002-O-05 – Adopting the NKAPC Landscape Regulations – 2nd
Reading
13.   Mayor Kriege presented Ordinance No. 2002-O-05 adopting landscape
regulations as recommended by the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission
for a second reading. He advised that the suggested planting manual would be
adopted by resolution as a supplement to the ordinance. He stated that it would
be easier to amend the planting manual in the future, if necessary, if adopted
by resolution.
14.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance No. 2002-
O-05 adopting landscape regulations. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. A brief
discussion ensued. Mr. Gabbard expressed his concerns that this ordinance was
too complex and felt it would be difficult to enforce these regulations. He
felt it would take a zoning administrator an inordinate amount of time to
ensure compliance of this ordinance. Mayor Kriege stated he felt that by
adopting this it was better than having no regulations at all. He stated that
he trusted that the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission staff members
put together a set of regulations that would be manageable. Mr. Gabbard agreed
that the city needs some kind of regulations, but felt it would be time
consuming for a zoning administrator to do this, as well as necessary for that
individual to be familiar with a variety of trees and plants. Mr. Bushong
stated that it has been his experience that the more regulations you have in
writing the better it will be. Mr. Kudera felt the proposed regulations were
not as strong as it could be especially in some areas, but overall he felt the
regulations would have a good effect. Mayor Kriege stated that the Planning
Commission staff worked with local developers for well over a year to draft
these regulations that would be practical and effective.
15.   There being no further discussion, Mr. Walker read Ordinance 2002-O-05.
Roll call was answered with four yes votes with Mr. Gabbard opting to pass.
Motion carried.
Resolution No. 2002-R-07 – Adopting a Landscape Planting Manual
16.   Mayor Kriege presented Resolution No. 2002-R-07 that would approve a
planting manual to be used in conjunction with the landscape regulations
adopted by Ordinance No. 2002-O-05. He advised that by adopting the planting
manual by resolution, separate from the landscape regulations ordinance, it

and Mr. Bushong seconded the adoption of Resolution No. 2002-R-07. No roll was
called; four ayes were cast with Mr. Gabbard opting to pass. Motion carried.
Resolution No. 2002-R-08 – Supporting the City of Taylor Mill Regarding Traffic
Flow Concerns in the Area of Route 16
17.   Mayor Kriege presented to council this resolution that would support the
City of Taylor Mill in their concerns regarding the increasing traffic flows
within southern Kenton County. He advised that representatives from the City of
Taylor Mill were unable to attend this evening. He stated that the City of
Taylor Mill is requesting that the state Transportation Cabinet research
alternative routes, more specifically the east/west corridor of Hands Pike (Ky
Rt. 1501). Mayor Kriege advised that the resolution supports their request that
funds allocated for the Ky 16 project is reallocated to the improvement of Ky
1501 (Hands Pike) instead.
18.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2002-R-08 supporting
the City of Taylor Mill in petitioning the Transportation Cabinet of Kentucky
to divert funds from the Route 16 Project to the Route 1501 Project. Mr. Kudera
seconded the motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Moriconi expressed concern
with reallocating funds away from the Route 16 Project. Mayor Kriege stated the
City of Taylor Mill would like to see Hands Pike widened to the intersection
with Route 17. Mayor Kriege stated that because this is a long-term project,
modifications would probably be necessary. He stated that the Route 16 Project
is not even on the list of future proposed state projects. Mr. Wendling stated
that Taylor Mill has requested support of this resolution from the Kenton
County Fiscal Court and the City of Covington. Mr. Moriconi was concerned that
support of this resolution may not be in the best interest of the City of
Independence as this basically is requesting that no funds be allotted for the
widening of Route 16 which runs through the east side of Independence. Mr.
Bushong concurred. He stated that a road widening of Hands Pike would not help
Independence. He commented that Route 16 is a major artery in the City of
Independence. He stated that he would have liked for a representative of Taylor
Mill to appear before council so he could have learned more of their reason for
requesting Independence’s support of this resolution.
19.   Mr. Kudera commented that there are critical issues concerning Taylor
Mill with the widening of Route 16. The state would have to dislocate too many
families along the road and the state cannot provide traffic data.
20.   Mayor Kriege advised that the City of Taylor Mill is in disagreement with
the Transportation Cabinet on the planned alignment of Route 16. Mr. Moriconi
reiterated that he doesn’t feel that diverting funds from the Route 16 Project
to the Hands Pike project is in the best interest of Independence. Mr. Gabbard
stated that currently no state funds have been allocated to the Route 16
Project, so all the city would be doing is supporting them by resolution.
21.   At this time, Mr. Walker read Resolution No. 2002-R-08 in summary. Mayor
Kriege suggested the city’s intent could be clarified by inserting another
section in the resolution that would add the following wordage, “provided that
this resolution does not adversely impact funding for future widening of
Kentucky 16 from Hands Pike south to Kentucky Route 536.” Mr. Walker advised
that a motion and second would be needed to amend this resolution. Mr. Gabbard
suggested not voting on this tonight, as he would like to see the final
resolution after the wordage is added. There was another brief discussion
regarding the flow of traffic in the Route 16, Route 17, Hands Pike and Route
536 areas. Mr. Gabbard stated that since no current state funds have been
allocated for the Route 16 Project, he has no reservations in supporting the
City of Taylor Mill with this resolution, as he too, does not want to take
anything away from Independence.
22.   Mayor Kriege proposed approving the amendment of the resolution with the
added language. Mr. Moriconi made a motion to amend Resolution No. 2002-R-08;
seconded by Mr. Kudera. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and one no
vote cast by Mr. Dupps. Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
23.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2002-R-08 as amended
to include the phrase “provided that this resolution does not adversely impact
funding for future widening of Kentucky 16 from Hands Pike south to Kentucky
Route 536.” Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with three
yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Dupps and Mr. Bushong. Motion carried 3-
2 in favor.
Annual Project Prom Donation – Simon Kenton High School
24.   Mayor Kriege advised council that the city has received the annual
donation request from Simon Kenton High School Project Prom Committee. He asked
Chief Butler to expound on Project Prom. Chief Butler advised that Project Prom
is an excellent arrangement wherein the students attending are locked down for
the event. He stated this is a good alternative to private parties after the
prom as it keeps the kids off the street. He stated that one-third of the
proceeds from the basketball event are donated to Project Prom also. Mayor
Kriege advised that last year the city donated $500.00 to Project Prom.
25.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Dupps, to approve a $500.00
donation to this years Simon Kenton High School Project Prom. Motion passed
with a unanimous roll call vote.
Award Bid for Production Court Storm Sewer Replacement
26.   City Engineer, Dave Whitacre reported to council that the city received
four bids for the storm sewer replacement on Production Court. He stated the
bids ranged from a low bid of $38,544.00 from JPS Construction to a high bid of
$60,255.02 from Hendy Incorporated. Mr. Whitacre advised council that this
replacement is not a permanent repair. He stated the project would include the
installation of 128 feet of concrete pipe. He also advised that Production
Court would have to be closed for two days while the work is performed. In
addition the pond will need to be drained to prevent water from going through
it while the work is being done. Mr. Whitacre stated they have been aware of
this problem for about a year and that there is no alternative than to replace
the line. Mayor Kriege advised this project had been budgeted. Mr. Wendling
stated that since the work will be done in July that the budgeted funds will
carry over into the next fiscal year. Mr. Dupps asked if the contractors were
aware of the time frame. Mr. Whitacre stated the time frame was clearly defined
in the bid packet. Mr. Dupps asked if the council could award a bid that would
be paid out of next years budget. Mr. Walker stated that this was acceptable to
pre-bind for the next fiscal year. Mr. Wendling advised that this is not an
uncommon practice as accepting bids early in the season results in better bid
prices for the city.
27.   Mr. Whitacre stated that the low bidder, JPS Construction has performed
other projects for the City of Independence. Mr. Wendling advised that LN
Concrete is currently suing JPS Construction and the City of Independence has
been named as a party in the suit. Mr. Walker explained this lawsuit to the
council and how the city has become party to this. Apparently JPS Construction
purchased concrete from LN Concrete that was used on some city streets. JPS has
an outstanding balance with LN Concrete, which is the reason for the lawsuit.
JPS contends that the concrete was substandard, resulting in the replacement of
certain sections of some of the newly cemented city streets and therefore has
not paid LN Concrete what is owed to them. Mr. Walker advised that since the
city has paid JPS in full, he feels the city will be dismissed as a party in
the lawsuit.
28.   Mr. Whitacre stated that the city has ninety days to award the bid. Mr.
Kudera made a motion to award the bid to JPS Construction as the lowest and
best bid. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with four yes
votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Bushong. Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the Flag Lot Ordinance No. 1999-O-11 – 1st
Reading
29.   In the absence of the Planning & Zoning Committee Chairman, Mr. Ellison,
Mr. Wendling explained that the proposed ordinance presented to council was the
result of the Planning & Zoning Committee’s many discussions regarding the ban
on flag lots as outlined by ordinance a few years ago. He stated that the
current ordinance’s intent was to curtail the numerous flag lots that were
appearing on new residential development plans. Mr. Wendling stated there are
some residents who are requesting approval to subdivide their property and the
current ordinance does not permit them to place a “flag lot” to the rear of
their property. He stated that the committee had worked with Scott Hiles of the
Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission to develop language to amend the
current ordinance. He stated that at the recent hearing by the Kenton County &
Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission the city was denied this text amendment
request. He stated their denial was determined largely on the feeling that the
city adopted the ordinance against their recommendation and they feel the city
should be following their recommendations on flag lots. Mr. Moriconi asked if
this amended ordinance would permit flag lots in new subdivisions. Mr. Wendling
stated that flag lots would be permitted in new developments but that the lots
would require more restrictions. Mr. Walker explained in detail the definition
of flag lots. He stated the lots would have to have 120 feet and be one and
one-half times the width of the lot, which will make it hard to comply with.
Mr. Wendling stated that the wording was done in such a way that it would help
residents to subdivide their land, yet not be attractive to developers. Mr.
Moriconi commented that he would hate to see them reappearing in the
subdivisions as people generally don’t like flag lots but sometimes they are
larger then the other lots. Mr. Walker stated that the Board of Adjustments
would consider the issue. Mr. Dupps questioned whether the current ordinance
permits the Board of Adjustments to rule on flag lots. Mr. Walker replied that
no prior ordinance states that flag lots are prohibited. During a lengthy
discussion on this matter Mr. Walker cautioned council on imposing stronger
restrictions. He stated that you should exercise caution when dealing with
setbacks. Mayor Kriege stated that the Board of Adjustments could make a ruling
to permit a structure to be closer but that it would not change the definition
of that zone. Mayor Kriege stated that it could be more restrictive and feels
it is necessary but it may not help the individual(s) who requested this
amendment and they may have to make modifications. He commented that he is not
sure the Board of Adjustments can approve a variance. Mr. Wendling reminded
council that the Planning & Zoning Committee supported the working in this
proposed amended ordinance.
30.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to have a first reading on the proposed
ordinance to amend the current Ordinance No. 1999-O-11 enacting a text
amendment to the zoning ordinance approving the definition and regulations for
‘flag lots.’ Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with four
yes votes, with Mr. Gabbard opting to pass, citing that he does not like flag
lots. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Text Amendment Permitting Riding Stables/Indoor Riding
Arenas as a Conditional Use in a Residential Zone – Presented for a 1st
Reading, But was Tabled
31.   Mayor Kriege presented to council a proposed text amendment to the zoning
ordinance that would add riding stables and indoor riding arenas to the list of
conditional uses within residential zones. He stated this text amendment is
being presented at the request of Marty Neltner, 6239 Taylor Mill Road who
would like to construct a riding stable and arena on the property. Mr. Gabbard
stated that he felt there was a problem with the ordinance in that no amount of
land is specified and he thinks it would be wise to have a minimum of three to
five acres stated in the ordinance. Mr. Wendling stated that that was a major
concern of the Planning & Zoning Committee also. Mr. Walker advised that this
text amendment has already gone before the Kenton County and Municipal Planning
& Zoning Commission for their approval and that changes cannot be made adding
text that was not discussed at their public hearing on this matter. Mr. Gabbard
stated that he felt there could be problems with the number of acres necessary
for such a development not being addressed in the ordinance. He also felt the
surrounding neighbors may complain regarding the odor, etc. if too many horses
were allowed to gather in a confined area. He asked Mr. Neltner how many acres
he had. Mr. Neltner replied that he has thirteen acres. Mayor Kriege asked Mr.
Neltner if he considered requesting a zone change. Mr. Neltner replied that he
doesn’t remember. He stated he would hire someone to care for the horses and
that the horses would be kept in stalls and not out in the pasture. Mr. Neltner
presented to council an aerial photo that indicates where he would place the
arena, etc. and the adjoining barn. Mr. Neltner stated that if council wanted
to send this proposal back to the Planning Commission to amendment for a
minimum acreage requirement that it would be okay with him.
32.   Mr. Walker advised council that any text amendment would have to go
before the Planning Commission, but reminded them that the ordinance being
presented to them requires the approval by the Board of Adjustments for a
conditional use. Mayor Kriege agreed that language requiring minimum acreage
should be added to this ordinance. Mr. Walker suggested that the minimum land
requirement be seven acres. Mr. Gabbard suggested there be a limit on the
number of horses and acreage. Mr. Dupps suggested looking at the zones. Upon
motion by Mr. Dupps and second by Mr. Kudera the matter was tabled. Motion
carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2001-02 Budget – 1st Reading
33.   Mayor Kriege presented to council an amended budget ordinance for the
2001/02 fiscal year. Mr. Kudera made a motion to have a first reading of the
amended budget ordinance; seconded by Mr. Bushong.
34.   A brief discussion ensued. Mayor Kriege referred council to Mr.
Wendling’s memo wherein he details the reasons for the amendment to the budget.
The memo cites several areas that the budget changed and included increased
health insurance costs, which were estimated; Zoning Administrator contract,
which was also estimated and the actual costs have been higher; PVA assessment,
which is also an estimate that cannot be determined until the property
valuations are complete in August; dog control contract, the authority raised
their fee of which we had no prior knowledge; police vehicle and property
insurance, the headquarters nor the contents was in the old contract; disparity
between prior year fund balances, due to required GASB 33 accounting
procedures; Senior Center fund, Director’s salary and other related expenses;
and, Municipal Center revenues and expenditures, due to the loan proceeds from
the bond issue and expenses associated with land acquisition.
35.   Mr. Gabbard questioned if the health increase was only for the Public
Works Department. Mr. Wendling replied no that it was due to the anticipated
increase in April. Mr. Gabbard also questioned the disparity of the prior year
fund balance. Mayor Kriege advised that revenue was collected after the fiscal
year for a period and then it is accrued back into the current year. He stated
that three months was accrued back. Finance Director, Janet Rebman, explained
this was payroll taxes. Mayor Kriege explained this was an adjustment and that
$350,000 spiked up the fund balance. Mr. Gabbard commented that the end of June
shows that but the city won’t actually have the funds.
36.   Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance amending the 2002/03 budget. Roll
call was answered with four yes votes, with Mr. Gabbard opting to pass. Motion
carried.

APRIL 1, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:02 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Lisa May from the Staffordsburg United Methodist Church
gave the invocation. Council Members Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim
Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Council Member Jim Bushong was
absent. Also in attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City
Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the March 4, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of March 4, 2002 as submitted. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with three yes votes and two pass votes cast by Mr. Gabbard
and Mr. Ellison. Motion carried.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
3.   Mayor Kriege introduced Gary Edmondson, Kenton County Attorney, who
announced that he would hold seminars on Elder Law and Neighborhood Law during
the months of April and May at two branches of the Kenton County Public Library
and the Kenton County Extension Center. Mr. Edmondson encouraged council and
the general public to attend these seminars, especially the Neighborhood Law as
it covers issues the city would be involved with regarding boundary lines, etc.
4.   Mayor Kriege informed the large audience in attendance that he assumes
they are present to address council regarding the proposed development along
Bristow-Hogreffe-Maher Roads. He stated that he would allow Mr. Chuck Berling
to make his presentation and afterward would allow public comments from the
audience.
5.   Mr. Gabbard recused himself from the discussion citing a possible conflict
regarding this matter and left the room. Mr. Ellison likewise excused himself
and left the room.
6.   Mr. Berling stated that he feels that the major objection of the proposed
development is the density. He stated that he is willing to agree to a formal
agreement with the city. He stated that the development proposes 2.5 units per
acre and that the numbers circulating are incorrect. He stated that the Falcon
Ridge Subdivision has a density of 2.5 units per acre and that the Hartland
Subdivision has 315 houses on 134 acres of land. Mr. Berling stated that the
R1-C zoning permits 3.5 units per acre and that the request for smaller lots
would create more open green space. He stated that he feels the density issue
is a mute point, as the development will not exceed 2.5 units per acre. He
stated the developers have committed land to the Kenton County School Board,
the Independence Fire District and the City of Independence for a police
station. He stated the densest area if R1-F which is still less than the
density of the Falcon Ridge Subdivision. He stated that the developers would
also upgrade Hogreffe Road and the School Board would pursue funds to upgrade
and widen the through lanes. He advised that the School Board has indicated
that the earliest they would be able to construct a school on the designated
property would be three years, which is also the earliest all utility lines
would be installed and road improvements made. The School Board also indicated
that it might be five years before they will have bonding capabilities
available.
7.   Mr. Berling sated he would be requesting plat approval from the Planning
Commission. He advised everyone that it is necessary to understand that this
development is a very long-term project, taking approximately twenty-two years
to build out.
8.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor for questions from the council members. Mr.
Moriconi asked what the maximum number of units for a R1-F zone. Mr. Berling
replied 2.69 units which is 150 lots on 130 acres and this area would be
adjacent to the industrial buildings. He stated the R1- zone would accommodate
smaller lots.
9.   Mayor Kriege stated that Frank Platek, 732 Hogreffe Road, was unable to
attend tonight’s meeting, but has presented a letter wherein he requests the
city to uphold the previous zoning rulings of the Planning Commission and not
permit the Hogreffe Road areas to be annexed at a higher density zone. He
stated Mr. Platek would like his letter to become part of the official record
of the minutes of this meeting. Mayor Kriege ordered the City Clerk to attach
the letter to the official minutes and copy to council.
10.   Mr. Ray Scarton, 496 Hogreffe Road, spoke against the proposed
development and stated that he was in agreement with Mr. Platek’s letter. He
advised council that on six separate occasions the Planning Commission has
endorsed the current zoning of this area. He questioned whether the developers
were talking about net density or gross density, as he is very familiar with
the area and said that much of it is steep, making it unbuildable. Taking that
into consideration, he fears there will be six or seven units per acre. Mr.
Scarton also expressed concern that the proposed housing would not be similar
to the subdivisions Mr. Berling referred to. Another concern was that the
residents of Hogreffe Road would have to submit a portion of their front yards
to widen the road. In closing, Mr. Scarton commented that he was not totally
opposed to expansion or development, he just wanted it to be consistent to
other quality homes in the area. He also stated that a four-lane road would be
necessary to accommodate the increase in traffic. Mr. Scarton encouraged
council to familiarize themselves with this area before coming to a decision on
this development.
11.   Teresa Kampsen, 991 Maher Road, addressed council regarding her
opposition to the proposed zone change. She stated that currently there is no
density in that area that is close to the one proposed and cited the Northern
Kentucky & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission’s disapproval of a zone
change request on two occasions. She stated that the proposed development and
zone change would drastically change this area and urged council to not permit
more than two houses per acre.
12.   Tom Messamer, 520 Hogreffe Road stated that he lives directly across the
proposed development site. He stated that he too agrees with the views
expressed in Mr. Platek’s letter to the city. He stated that he opposes being
annexed into the city, as he sees no benefits to it. He stated the city would
be annexing vacant land with the only people benefiting from this would be the
developers. He feels that as a property owner abutting this proposed
development he should have a say into this matter. Mr. Messamer stated that the
adjoining properties were not included in the annexation.
13.   Karla Palmer, 979 Maher Road stated that she is not opposed to
development in the area, just that she feels the development should be done
responsibly. She stated that the proposed zone change is not consistent with
the current zoning. She stated that the developers are not listening to the
residents in this area; the people that will be most affected by this
development. Ms. Palmer urged council to not allow the proposed development as
planned, but to insist on a higher density zone.
14.   Roger C. Bales, 801 Hogreffe Road, stated that he was born and raised in
Independence and has observed the growth over the years. As a property owner of
over forty years, he urged council to stick with the Planning Commission’s
recommendation to disapprove this zone change. He encouraged “smart growth”
with regard to the infrastructure, if not, he had concern that the ability to
commute would become stifled.
END - PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR

Maher & Hogreffe Roads
15.   Mayor Kriege pointed out that the city was prepared to have a first

§   Area “E” - approximately 175 acres located along the north side of Maher
Road, at the Boone/Kenton County border, from A-1, R-1B, R-1C (RCD) and I-1 to
R-1F.

19.   Mayor Kriege stated the city would place a notice in the newspaper if a

clarify the situation to the audience members. He advised that when two members
of council recuse themselves from voting that it is counted with the majority
vote. He explained that the majority of the quorum that existed at the

15.   Before continuing with the agenda, Mayor Kriege asked that Mr. Gabbard

Ordinance Number 2002-O-06 – Amending the 2001/02 Budget – 2nd Reading
16.   Mayor Kriege referred to Mr. Wendling’s memo outlining the reasons for
the proposed amendments to the 2001/02 fiscal year budget. Mr. Wendling
reviewed the memo with council and advised the amendments were due to increased
health insurance costs, expenses associated with zoning administration, which
had been underestimated, PVA assessment was higher than anticipated, the Dog

the Municipal Center revenue. Motion carried 4-1 in favor and Mr. Walker read
the ordinance.
Discussion Regarding the Purchase of Taylor Smith Property at 5407 Madison Pike
18.   Mayor Kriege informed council that funds to purchase the Taylor Smith
property would need to be split between the Building Fund and the Municipal
Center Fund accounts. He stated that the Building Fund account balance is not
sufficient to cover the full amount of the purchase of this property. He
proposed withdrawing $75,000 from the Building Fund and the remainder of the
purchase price from the Municipal Center Fund bond proceeds.
19.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to purchase the Taylor Smith property at 5407
Madison Pike from the Municipal Center Fund; Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion.
A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Gabbard asked if the city has closed on the
$5,000,000 loan for the Municipal Center project. Mayor Kriege replied that the
loan was closed last week. Mr. Ellison asked what the balance was of the
Building Fund. Mayor Kriege stated the balance was $12,500.00 as a portion
($75,000) was allocated as part of the purchase price of the Smith property. He
stated that the full purchase price of the property would have been taken from
the Building Fund but there was not a sufficient balance to do so. Mr. Wendling
stated the entire amount was not available as certain funds are obligated to
the amphitheater. Mr. Ellison stated that it is his understanding that the
amphitheater funds were donated and expressed his concern that there are not
adequate funds for the purchase of the Smith property from the Building Fund.
Mayor Kriege explained that unforeseen expenses for the Senior Center project
were paid for out of the Building Fund. Mr. Ellison asked if the property has
already been purchased. Mayor Kriege stated the closing on the property would
take place tomorrow. Roll call was answered with three yes votes and two no
votes cast by Mr. Gabbard and Mr. Ellison. Motion carried 3-2 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-07 – Amending Flag Lot Ordinance No. 1999-O-11 – Second
Reading
20.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to have a second reading of Ordinance No. 2002-
O-07 to approve and adopt regulations regarding flag lots. Mr. Ellison seconded
the motion. Mr. Walker read the ordinance. Mr. Walker explained that this
ordinance would permit flag lots on the condition that it contains the minimum
lot width at the minimum front yard setback line. He advised that every flag
lot would have to be one and one-half times the minimum lot area and width
contained within the area and height regulations for each respective zone. Mr.
Dupps asked for a definition of a minimum lot width. Mr. Walker explained that
a flag lot would have to be 75 feet wide and one hundred fifty percent of the
square foot minimum in that particular zone. He stated that the setback is how
you define the flag lot size. Mr. Ellison commented that this ordinance should
stop the cul-de-sac flag lots in subdivisions and these homes tend to become
retention areas. He stated this ordinance should address that problem and at
the same time assist residents with large lots that would like to subdivide.
Mr. Dupps asked if this ordinance addresses the problem for the resident who
originally came to council requesting this amendment. Mr. Wendling stated that
that resident might have to redraw the lot lines, but that this amendment
should meet his needs. Mr. Ellison advised that the resident would need to
apply for a map amendment with the Northern Kentucky and Municipal Planning &
Zoning Commission for approval. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and
one no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard.
City Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
21.   Mr. Wendling reported that the current contract with Rumpke for trash
pickup would expire at the end of this month, but that they have agreed to
extend the contract through June 30, 2002. He stated that the contract has been

22.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to approve a two-month extension of the current
contract with Rumpke for trash pickup; seconded by Mr. Dupps. No roll call;
motion carried unanimously.
23.   Mayor Kriege stated that the bids for trash pickup would be tabulated and
presented to council next month to award the bid. Mr. Gabbard asked how many
bids were received. Mr. Wendling stated that three bids were received; from
Rumpke, CSI and Bavarian.
24.   Mr. Ellison expressed some concern about the status of the Marion
Schadler Park in the Lakefield Subdivision. He stated that he appreciates Mr.
Wendling’s protecting the city’s interests, but feels the city should assist
Drees in getting the park development completed. Mayor Kriege reported that the
steps and drainage problems are currently being attended to and stated that the
city could not accept maintenance of this area until these matters were
resolved. Mr. Ellison reiterated that he felt that Drees has been willing to
work out an agreement with the city and have allocated funds into this project
and he would like to see the city lend a hand in an effort to get the park
completed. Mayor Kriege stated that liability issues existed that had to be
resolved before the city agrees to take over maintenance.
25.   Mr. Wendling stated that he met with Drees representatives and it was
their suggestion to remove the steps entirely and not replace them. Mr. Ellison
felt the removal of the steps would eliminate access to the upper part of the
subdivision. A discussion ensued regarding the easement that was obtained for
the installation of the steps. Mr. Ellison also feels the city can assist the
development of the park with other things, like signage, installing parking
curbs, and sowing grass. Mayor Kriege stated that the city is working with
Drees, but the weather has delayed some progress. Mr. Ellison stated there is
$3,500 in the capital improvements budget. Ms. Brake informed council that
those funds have been allocated for the installation of a water line.
26.   Mr. Moriconi wondered if the adjoining property owners would attain the
easement land since the stairs will not be replaced. Mayor Kriege stated the
property owners already own the easement area, as it is an overlay. He went on
to say that the hillside is very steep and the city is considering planting
crown vetch in that area to discourage foot traffic on this hill. Mr. Kudera
commented that he does not feel the removal of the steps will hinder access to
the park. Mr. Dupps asked who would own the hillside. Mayor Kriege stated this
area would be part of the park that the city will take over maintenance.
27.   Mayor Kriege asked council how they wanted to proceed. Mr. Ellison made a
motion to retain the easement for the stairway that is platted on the Marion
Schadler Park land; seconded by Mr. Gabbard. Roll call was answered with two
yes votes and three no votes cast by Mr. Dupps, Mr. Kudera and Mr. Moriconi.
Further discussion ensued. Mr. Dupps felt that developers sometimes want to
install a path after they see what paths gradually evolve from use by the
residents. Mr. Ellison stated the easement is laid out between two property
lines. Mr. Dupps suggested the Building and Recreation Committee work on
resolving this matter. Mayor Kriege felt this should be decided now as Drees
has been instructed to remove the stairway. Mr. Wendling stated that the park
should be completed by mid-April. Mr. Moriconi stated the stairway was a
complete disaster and expressed concern that it will be difficult for Drees to
market a property that has an easement that kids will use on a regular basis to
access the park. He stated that this easement basically goes nowhere and feels
it will become overgrown with weeds.
