MAY 6, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:04 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Bill Clark from the Hickory Grove Baptist Church gave the
invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard,
Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance was City
Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the April 1, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of April 1, 2002 as submitted. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Roll
call was answered with five yes votes and one pass vote cast by Mr. Gabbard.
Motion carried.
Introduction of New Police Officer, Amy Schworer
3.   Shawn Butler, Chief of Police introduced the newly hired police officer,
Amy Schworer. He stated that Officer Schworer is transferring from the City of
Fort Wright to Independence and comes highly recommended.
Agenda Amendment
4.   Mayor Kriege announced that Scott Layman of Cole + Russell Architects was
unable to attend the meeting to present a site rendering for the new municipal
center. He stated that Mr. Layman would be rescheduled to next month’s meeting.
Discussion Regarding the Zone Change Request for the Unincorporated Area near
Hogreffe Road
5.   Mayor Kriege announced to the assemblage that this meeting was not a
public hearing and that any decision made at this meeting must be decided based
on the facts that were presented at the public hearing held by the Kenton
County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission. He stated that Mr. Chuck
Berling was not present to review the proposed development plan for the
property for which a zone change has been requested but advised council that
they could proceed with a first reading of the proposed ordinance to approve
the zone change. City Attorney, Lawson Walker explained the procedures to
council.
6.   Council Member, Mr. Gabbard recused himself from the discussion of this
matter citing a possible conflict of interest and left the room during the
discussion. Mr. Bushong questioned this action by Mr. Gabbard. Mr. Walker
advised that there is no legal reason that would require Mr. Gabbard to leave
the room during the discussion and that Mr. Gabbard is free to do so. He stated
that Mr. Gabbard is also within his rights to recuse himself and refrain from
voting on this matter.
7.   Mayor Kriege advised that council would be considering the acceptance of
property parcels A & B, rejecting parcels C & D and denying parcel E. Mayor
Kriege acknowledged the audience and stated that he would allow everyone an
opportunity to address council concerning this matter. Mr. Walker explained in
detail the parcels of land that council would be considering for this zone
change request. He stated that in Exhibit A, the property along the south side
of Bristow Road between Banklick Road would be rezoned from R-1C (county) to R-
1C (city). He stated that the county and city zone requirements differ but that
the density is the same. The proposed change would rezone the parcel to R-1C
city conditions. Mr. Walker advised that Exhibit B would rezone the property
along the northeast corner of the intersection of Banklick Road and Maher Road
from A-1 and R-RE to R-1D. He stated the last two changes along Maher Road and
Hogreffe Road would change from A-1, R-RE and R-1B zones to an R-1D zone. He
stated there is no mention of Exhibit E, which had an R-1F and advised that if
that tract of land were annexed in the future then it would come into the city
as the current zone. Mayor Kriege stated that if council decides to approve
Exhibits C & D then the city would override the recommendation from the
Planning Commission to deny this zone change request. He advised that the
Planning Commission has also recommended disapproval of the zone change request
for Exhibit E. He stated that council would not be voting on this ordinance at
this meeting, as this would just be a first reading. He stated that the final
vote and possible adoption of this ordinance would come at the June council
meeting.
8.   Mr. Moriconi referred to the ordinance presented at the last council
meeting and asked if they would be starting over with the ordinance presented
tonight. Mr. Walker replied that changes were made to the previous ordinance
and the ordinance presented at this meeting reflects those changes and would
require a first reading. Mayor Kriege stated that the current ordinance
excludes the R-1F zone. He reiterated that there would be no vote on this first
reading and that action on this ordinance would take place at the regular June
council meeting. Mayor Kriege stated that basically this is a new start for
this ordinance.
9.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor to citizen comments on this subject.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
10.   Frank Platek, 732 Hogreffe Road, spoke in opposition to the re-zone
request. He stated that the Planning Commission has revisited this zone change
request on four other separate occasions and all four times has denied the
requests. He called attention to net versus gross acreage and stated that the
developer contradicted himself at the last council meeting with regard to
density. He stated that the area is currently undergoing heavy road
construction and that Hogreffe Road is in poor condition due to the heavy
equipment being used. He also expressed concern over the Glenhurst site area
and the current condition. He expressed dissatisfaction with the quality of the
homes proposed and the open area being converted to this density level with
less than quality structures. Mr. Platek cited that sites B and C narrow to a
pinpoint that enables sites C and D to be part of this development but was
concerned that realistically the areas are not connected and are not
functional. In closing, Mr. Platek stated that the annexation boundaries
totally exclude current residents. He stated that if the proposed property is
annexed the excluded residents will have to call county police if there is a
problem with a neighboring city resident. He also had a strong concern that the
only access for some current residents in the area will be the county road as
they will be surrounded by city areas. He stated that he feels this was done
purposely as current residents would have the power to have this annexation put
on the general election ballot that would require 51% approval to override the
annexation attempt by the city. He urged council to do the right thing by
denying this zone change.
11.   Tom Messamer, 520 Hogreffe Road, stated that he agreed with Mr. Platek
but added that he does not wish to be annexed by the city.
12.   Teresa Kampsen, 991 Maher Road, Walton, Kentucky stated she was in
agreement with Mr. Platek’s comments and had nothing new to add.
13.   Ron Yarnell, 320 Independence Station Road, was concerned about
accountability and who was going to take responsibility for all the debris from
the roadwork construction that is building up in the Banklick Creek. Mayor
Kriege advised that maybe the State was responsible for this. Mr. Yarnell asked
if a fund would be set up by the developers for any future problems that may
arise due to the development. Mayor Kriege advised him that the developer is
required to adhere to water retention requirements. Mr. Yarnell expressed
concerns that all the development in the area is changing Banklick Creek. Mayor
Kriege stated that the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission might be able
to address his concerns.
14.   Jerry Palmer, 979 Maher Road, Walton, Kentucky voiced his agreement with
Mr. Platek’s comments and added that he is concerned that all this development
is surrounding the farms in the area and forcing the farmers to move out of
Kenton County. He fears that the farmland will not survive all the residential/
commercial development.
15.   Sherry Carran, 927 Forest, Covington, Kentucky stated that she is a
member of the “Smart Growth Coalition” and that she attended the public hearing
at the Kenton County and Municipal Planning and Zoning Commission’s meeting.
She stated that the proposed development is an example of a compact
development, which is supported by the Coalition. She stated that the Glenhurst
development on Maher Road has ignored the creek area, which is the sites best
feature. Ms. Carran expressed concern about who would be maintaining the
detention ponds. She stated that other green space has been used for utility
lines and that the roads are not good. Mayor Kriege stated that the city is not
considering the site she is referring to. Ms. Carran urged council to make a
closer review of compact developments, as they need to be refined.
16.   In closing, Ms. Carran questioned Mr. Walker’s conflict of interest to
advise council on this matter since he was the attorney for the Glenhurst
Development. Mr. Walker made clear that at the onset he publicly disclosed at
the last council meeting that he was the former attorney for the Glenhurst
Development. He reiterated that he no longer represents this business and that
he has basically just drafted the documents the city has requested from him.
Map Amendment Approving Zone Change for Unincorporated Areas along Bristow,
Hogreffe & Maher Roads – 1st Reading
17.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Moriconi there was a first
reading of the proposed ordinance to approve a map amendment for a zone change
for unincorporated area along Bristow Road, Hogreffe Road and Maher Roads.
Motion carried with all ayes. Mr. Ellison clarified his favorable vote by
making a formal statement. In his statement he indicated that he would no
longer remain silent on the Glenhurst LLC 464-acre proposed annexation, because
his brother-in-law, Joe Arlinghaus is one of the builder/developers. He stated
that Mr. Arlinghaus has been his brother-in-law longer than he has been in the
land development/house building business. He stated that since he is not
employed by any of the Glenhurst builder/developers and would not receive any
financial benefits that he felt he would be usurping his elected duties as a
councilperson to remain silent on this issue before council and therefore has
decided to cast his vote to represent the citizens of Independence. Motion
carried 5-0 in favor and Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance by title only.
18.   Mayor Kriege advised the second reading would be on the agenda for the
regular council meeting on June 3, 2002 unless a special council meeting is
called before that date.
19.   Before continuing with the agenda, Mayor Kriege asked that Mr. Gabbard be
told that the discussion regarding the annexation issue had ended. Mr. Gabbard
re-entered the meeting room and participated in the rest of the meeting
Discussion Regarding Map Amendment for Zone Change for Flanagan Property at
5460 Madison Pike
20.   Due to the number of people in attendance regarding the zoning issues on
the agenda, Mayor Kriege moved up the discussion regarding the zone change
request for the Flanagan property at 5460 Madison Pike. Mayor Kriege advised
that the Kenton County and Municipal Planning Commission have rejected this
zone change request at their May 2, 2002 meeting; he stated it was rejected
based on NKAPC staff recommendation. Mayor Kriege allowed the developers to
make a presentation.
21.   Mr. David Wallace, with Cors and Bassett law firm, represented developer
Mike Helson. Mr. Wallace stated that the public hearing for the zone change was
held last week and they will not introduce any new facts as he feels the
evidence stands for itself. He stated they are requesting a zone change for an
approximate 36 acre tract of land located along the east side of Madison Pike
between Walnut Hall Drive and Harris Pike from R-1C (single family residential)
to NC (neighborhood commercial). He stated the property is currently bordered
by Route 17 and will be bordered by the new section of Route 17 to be
constructed in the future. He stated the zone change was denied by the KC&MP&Z
Commission primarily because it is not consistent with the recommended land use
map of the 2001 Comprehensive Plan nor the concept o a community service area
as defined in the Comprehensive Plan. He argued that the courts in Kentucky say
it is recommended. Mr. Wallace stated that the current residential zone of R-1C
permits a density ranging from 7.1 to 14.0 dwelling units per net acre and no
one in the area thinks there is a need for more apartments since there
currently are ample apartment units vacant in the development behind Krogers.
He stated the real need is for commercial development to help build the tax
base in the city. Mr. Moriconi asked if any of the proposed development would
include some multi family buildings. Mr. Wallace stated no, that it would all
be neighborhood commercial. Mr. Moriconi asked if the development would tap
into the sewer system. Mr. Murphy, engineer for the proposed development,
replied that the Sanitation District main lines are north of the property and
that a force main backup could be constructed in the vicinity of the cemetery
and St. Cecilia Church along Route 17. Mr. Gabbard asked what types of
commercial businesses would occupy this development. The engineer responded
that the front units would house restaurants and the rear units would have
generic office space. Mr. Gabbard asked if the office space would house
business headquarters, etc. Mr. Helson stated that professional office space
for doctors, etc. Mr. Gabbard asked if gas/service stations would be part of
the development. The developer’s engineer stated that service stations are
considered conditional uses and this type of building would need to go before
the city’s Board of Adjustment for approval.
22.   Mr. Kudera asked if they had considered developing at the Towne Center.
Mr. Helson stated that he had considered it but that the property has deed
restrictions. He stated that he feels they have clients that would come to
Independence if office space were available. Mr. Gabbard stated that he would
not be in favor of any development in the area that did not include plans for a
large buffer between the current residential properties. He asked if they have
included buffer plans. Mr. Helson stated that sidewalks and landscaping
requirements would be adhered to. Mr. Moriconi expressed concern for the steep
topography of the site area. Mr. Helson stated the state highway department
would be taking six acres of the land for the reconstruction of Route 17 and
they are currently negotiating with them to obtain fill dirt. He stated they
would also get topsoil from the rear of the property if necessary. Mr. Wendling
asked how they planned to restore that area. He stated they would bring in
topsoil.
23.   Mr. Kudera asked Mr. Helson if he had experience in this kind of
development that council could look at. Mr. Mike Brandy began to distribute a
client list to the council members. An audience member objected to this, citing
that this list was not introduced at the public hearing held by the Kenton
County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission. City Attorney, Mr. Walker
advised council that this list could not be considered and Mr. Brandy retrieved
the list from council. The attorney for Mr. Helson stated that without a public
hearing held by the city, further discussion on the zone change request would
be limited. Based on this, Mayor Kriege proposed a public hearing be held on
another date.
24.   Mr. Dan Koch, 29 Walnut Hall Drive, stated that he has been a resident
for thirty-nine years. He voiced objection that the City Administrator, Mr.
Wendling attended the public hearing held by the Planning Commission to speak
on behalf of the city. He stated that he felt Mr. Wendling did not have the
authority to speak on the city’s behalf, but was told by Mr. Wendling that the
Mayor had instructed him to attend that meeting. Mayor Kriege confirmed that he
did send Mr. Wendling to the meeting to act as the city’s representative. He
also stated that it has no relevance on the matter, as it will be the council
that will decide whether this development is approved or not. He stated that
the Kenton County & Municipal Planning and Zoning Commission as well as the
Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission have rejected the development plan.
He reiterated to council that they could set a date for a public hearing by the
city.
25.   Mr. Ellison commented that Mr. Wendling attended the Planning
Commission’s public hearing to represent the city and to obtain information for
council as to whether this development plan was feasible for the city, but was
not there to cast a vote for the city.
26.   Mr. Helson’s attorney stated that the city could hold another public
hearing, but felt that there is no additional evidence that would be heard to
cause council to disapprove the development plan. He expressed confidence that
there is plenty of evidence to support the plan.
27.   Mayor Kriege asked council what they would like to do. Mr. Moriconi
expressed an interest in obtaining more information regarding the development
plan. Mr. Gabbard stated he would like the city to hold a public hearing.
28.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to obtain the minutes of the public hearing for
the development plan for the Flanagan property on Madison Pike and to schedule
a date for a city public hearing on this zone change request. Mr. Dupps
seconded the motion. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 in
favor. Mayor Kriege stated that a date would be set for the public hearing and
the public would be notified.
Proposal by Martin Butler to Amend the Zoning Ordinance to Include an RC-2 Zone
29.   Mr. Martin Butler made a presentation to council on behalf of his client,
Bill Dehlinger, to encourage council to amend the current zoning ordinance by
adding an RC-2 zone. He stated his client is currently interested in property
located at the intersection of Richardson and Crowe Roads. He stated this six
acre parcel of land is currently zoned R-1A. He stated the need for this area
is for commercial and other appropriate uses for this area, which are not
currently in the city’s zoning text. He distributed a draft text to council for
their review. He stated that he prepared this document and that he has had it
reviewed by the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission. He commented that
other areas in the city could benefit from this zone and stated that the
proposed text would require that a zone change request be made of council,
thereby allowing council to keep this type of development under their control.
Mr. Butler requested that council take the initial step to adopt this text
amendment tonight and submitting it later for a final vote.
30.   Mayor Kriege advised council that the first step in implementing Mr.
Butler’s request would be to add this zone text to the zoning ordinance and the
second step would be for Mr. Butler to request a zone change for property. Mr.
Butler stated the he would like to make separate applications concurrently.
Mayor Kriege asked what type of development Mr. Dehlinger had planned for the
areas. Mr. Butler replied office warehouse storage and/or light assembly type
of facilities. He stated that a body shop is across the road.
31.   Mr. Gabbard commented on a problem the city had with a Dehlinger
Development off of Turkeyfoot Road. He stated that a core sample taken from the
street on Fox Run Drive did not meet specifications. There was a brief
discussion regarding this matter with the City Engineer, Dave Whitacre. Mr.
Gabbard stated that he would not vote for approval of another development by
Mr. Dehlinger when there are unresolved problems in his current developments.
Mr. Butler stated that he could not respond to this, as he had no knowledge of
this matter. Mr. Gabbard stated there were improper core samples and depth of
the street, Fox Run Drive. Mr. Butler stated he would bring this matter to the
attention of Mr. Dehlinger.
32.   Mr. Moriconi asked if the Richardson Road/Crowe Road area was in the
flood plain. Mr. Butler stated that this was one of his concerns also and has
learned that this area is not in the flood plain. Mr. Kudera asked how the
development would be accessed and if it would be necessary to use the old
bridge. Mr. Butler stated it would be accessed by Old Richardson Road and the
bridge would not be traveled.
33.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Walker how council should proceed. Mr. Walker
stated the text amendment would need approval from council and would not be
binding when it comes back for a final approval on the recommendation from the
Planning Commission. Mr. Ellison commented that this request was presented to
the Planning and Zoning Committee and the text has been drafted as promised. He
recommended that the city make application for the text amendment with the City
Administrator representing the city in this matter.
34.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to make application to the Kenton County &
Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission for a text amendment to the zoning
ordinance to add the R-C2 zone, with Mr. Wendling representing the city in this
matter. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. Mr. Dupps asked how close this
planned development was to residential areas. Mr. Butler stated that there is a
three to four football fields distance. Mr. Ellison stated that the property
would not be conducive to residential development. Roll call was answered with
four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Gabbard and Mr. Dupps. Motion
carried 4-2 in favor.
Discussion Regarding Memorial Park Amphitheater – Rendering Submitted by
Charles Deters
35.   Mr. Charles Deters presented to council a proposed design for Memorial
Park and the amphitheater. He stated that, at his own expense, he worked with
architect, Robert Hayes to re-design a master plan for Memorial Park. He stated
that this plan provides a vehicle roadway, which he feels, is critical for
access to all twenty-seven acres and will enable the city to develop the entire
park. He stated that currently only the front edges of the park have been
developed. He stated that this architect rendering provides for handicap
parking near the amphitheater, fixed seating and lawn seating for approximately
1000 viewers. He stated this amphitheater would be great for city events, like
concerts and the July 4th Celebration. Mr. Gabbard agreed that something more
is needed for the park. Mr. Moriconi asked if Mr. Deters’ plan would involve
moving the current shelter and playground equipment. He replied that the
equipment might need to be moved. He stated that this proposed placement of the
amphitheater faces the south and will accommodate a greater number of viewers
that the original suggested site for the facility. Mr. Deters stated that
another positive feature for this site would be that it provides a cost savings
measure for the sewer system for both the amphitheater and the new city
building. This way only one pump and force main would be necessary to service
both buildings. He stated that the city might need to acquire an area of land
from Peach Drive for another access road to the park. Mayor Kriege advised the
Building and Recreation Committee would discuss the proposal, as the issue of
providing access to the amphitheater has not been addressed. Mayor Kriege
thanked Mr. Deters for presenting this plan for the park and stated that it is
a step in the right direction.
Discussion Regarding the Kentucky Renaissance Program
36.   Mrs. Barbara Gabbard, 5140 Madison Pike, addressed council regarding the
status of the Renaissance Program. Mayor Kriege advised Mrs. Gabbard that
currently the city holds the Bronze level and that due to budgetary restraints
there were no plans to apply for the next level. Mrs. Gabbard asked how long
the city had to apply for the next level. Mrs. Nita Brake responded that the
city had until September 2002 to apply for the Silver level. Mrs. Gabbard
stated that the Renaissance program provides an 80% return on the city’s money
and she urged council to find the $8,000 - $10,000 from the proposed budget
that is needed to reach the Silver level. She felt it would be worthwhile to
divert funds from other areas in the budget to get an 80% return on the city
money, funds that could be used for sidewalk projects, etc. She stated she has
spoken to some of the businesses in the area that have voiced support for this
program. Mr. Wendling advised that the Silver level status would require the
city to hire an employee whose sole job duty would be to administer the
program. In closing, Mrs. Gabbard encouraged council to follow through with
this program. She felt it would be a shame not to revitalize the downtown area.
Proposed Ordinance – Text Amendment permitting Indoor Horse Arena/Riding
Stables – 1st Reading
37.   Mayor Kriege presented a proposed ordinance that would amend the text of

would require periodic inspections of the premises. Mayor Kriege stated that
Section C, Number 10 addresses this concern. Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance.

45.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Kudera, Resolution No. 2002-
R-10 was read and approved. Mr. Walker read the resolution; roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Discussion Regarding Bids Received for Contract of Trash Collection in the City
46.   Mayor Kriege remarked that representatives from the three trash
collection companies that bid on this contract were in attendance and moved
this item of discussion up on the agenda.
47.   Mr. Wendling stated that the city received three bids for trash
collection. The bidders are Rumpke of Northern Kentucky, Bavarian and CSI. He
reviewed the bid tabulation presented to council in their packets. He explained
that the city requested that bids be presented for four options. The options
included: once per week pickup; once per week pickup plus one curbside
recycling pickup; twice per week pickup; and twice per week pickup plus one
curbside recycling pickup. Mr. Wendling stated that CSI was the low bidder at
the once per week pickup; Rumpke was the low bidder for the twice per week
pickup; CSI was the low bidder for the once per week pickup plus once per week
curbside recycling. He also pointed out that CSI’s automated pickup was the
lowest of all the bids. He stated that automated pickup provides all homeowners
with a waste container and that special size pickups would need to be phoned
ahead. He advised that plastic bags left at the curb would not be picked up.
Mr. Wendling stated that the company representatives could answer any questions
council had.
48.   A lengthy discussion ensued. Mr. Moriconi directed his attention to CSI
with concerns regarding the requirement for a 95-gallon container, especially
for the elderly, and items that would not fit into a container. He also
wondered why CSI was interested in recommending automated pickup in
Independence since that type of pickup was not prevalent in this area of the
country. He also asked if automated pickup would impose parking restrictions on
pickup day. CSI representatives responded to Mr. Moriconi’s concerns. They
stated that three sizes of containers were available for the automated pickup –
95-gallon, 65-gallon, and 35-gallon, which would be more suited for the
elderly. CSI advised that automated trucks are one-man operated vehicles that
are only eighteen inches off the ground and the operator can get out of the
truck if necessary to retrieve items by hand. CSI stated they would like to
introduce automated pickup in this area and offers it as an effort to control
costs. CSI recommended that the council members view the video that has been
provided to the city on automation pickup. They advised that the automation
style of pickup is demonstrated and thoroughly explained on the video.
49.   Mr. Gabbard asked how branches would be picked up. CSI stated that
automation pickup is offered as a cheaper alternative, but that the city may
want to continue with the standard type pickup. Mr. Gabbard also expressed
concern with trash service beginning earlier than 7:00 a.m. He stated during
the current five year contract with Rumpke they have routinely picked up the
trash in front of his home on Madison Pike as early as 5:00 a.m. causing a
disturbance to the residents. CSI stated that they would abide by the bid specs
that require trash pickup to begin no earlier than 7:00 a.m. Greg Rumpke
responded to Mr. Gabbard’s grievance by stating the Independence Police
Department had requested his company to pickup along Madison Pike early, before
rush hour traffic gets heavy. Mr. Gabbard replied that the Police Department
did not have the authority of council. Mr. Wendling stated that he was not
aware of complaints in this area. Mr. Moriconi stated that he understands there
would be a problem with heavy traffic and school buses, etc. if trash was
picked up during the rush hours.
50.   Mayor Kriege advised council that Rumpke, as the current contractor with
the city for trash pickup, has agreed to extend the current contract for May
and June so that the city can get this contract on a fiscal year rotation. Mr.
Rumpke stated that his company has provided service to this city for years and
his company is here to stay in this area. He advised that he is very familiar
with the trash pickup route schedule. He also commented that he felt that one
trash container provided to each resident by CSI for automated pickup would be
inadequate especially at Christmastime.
51.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to award the trash collection contract to CSI
as the lowest and best bid for the two-year period from July 1, 2002 through
June 30, 2004.
52.   Mr. Rumpke commented that the cheapest is not always the best bid, that
people want dependable and on time service. Ms. Christy of CSI responded that
there is a $62,000 annual difference between their bid and Rumpke’s. Mayor
Kriege asked her how she arrived at this figure. She stated that once per week
pickup plus once per week curbside recycling pickup multiplied by twelve equals
$62,000. Mayor Kriege stated the motion to award the bid was for once per week
pickup – no recycling, at an annual cost of $93.60.
53.   Ms. Christy stated that she understands that there is a certain amount of
trepidation in changing from one company to another, but urged council to check
the references they provided the city. She stated that they provided smooth
transitions with Covington, Bellevue and Florence and they will provide quality
customer service to Independence, even on the city premises if so desired. She
stated that mistakes are a human factor, but promised they would provide
customer service reports to monitor their service.
54.   Mr. Ellison suggested the option of the contractor billing the homeowners
directly. Mr. Gabbard stated that he felt the cost was too high. Mr. Ellison
stated that he feels this is an option the city should look at it as the cost
for this service is a pass through cost to the resident. Mr. Gabbard stated
that it is $9.00 more per year for the contractor to bill the resident and he
felt it was not a big deal to add this assessment to the annual tax bill. Mr.
Ellison pointed out that in the long run the amount collected from this
assessment does not equal out due to the bills that go unpaid. Mayor Kriege
commented that having the contractor bill the resident directly was an option.
Mr. Ellison stated that taking this assessment off the tax bills would relieve
the burden of delinquent bills on the property owners who pay their taxes. Mr.
Dupps suggested not picking up the trash of the delinquent tax bills, but then
thought that this could become a problem for the zoning administrator. Mr.
Walker commented that eventually the taxes get paid.
55.   Mr. Gabbard reminded council that he had a motion on the floor for the
Option “A-1” bid. Mr. Moriconi stated this option would cost more for the
residents that recycle. Mr. Gabbard stated that he would be willing to amend
his motion. Mr. Dupps stated that he would second the motion if it were amended
to Option “A-3” for $115.44 (once per week pickup plus once per week curbside
recycling pickup). He stated that he felt more people would recycle if it were
offered universally as this would encourage recycling. There was a brief
discussion regarding individual subscription versus curbside recycling. CSI
stated that recycling makes for a better community, as it will meet guidelines
in the years to come.
56.   Mr. Moriconi asked if the city had to decide this matter tonight. Mayor
Kriege advised that this contract would be awarded anytime before July 1, 2002.
He suggested that the Public Works Committee view the videotape that CSI
provided on automated pickup, and review the three bids received. Mr. Moriconi
expressed concern that other cities (Edgewood, Lakeside Park, Cold Spring and
Alexandria) chose to opt out of the CSI contracts. Ms. Christy responded that
that was 2 ½ years ago when they lost the contracts with Cold Spring and
Alexandria and since then they have a new General Manager and other changes in
staff. She urged council to investigate their current contracts and excellent,
efficient service. Mr. Wendling advised council that he checked all references
and found there were no major issues and that the transition difficulties were
resolved. Mr. Gabbard stated that he is looking strictly at cost and is trying
to ensure the resident gets the lowest cost as long as the service is good.
Rumpke stated that Greg Rumpke has worked in this area for over twenty years
and that the bid submitted was based on the history of pickup in the city. They
stated that Rumpke pays their employees well, provides good benefits and has a
low turnover in staff. CSI encouraged council to try the automated pickup
service.
57.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to table this matter until the Public Works
Committee can review the bids submitted. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. No
roll call; motion carried unanimously.
58.   NOTE: Mr. Gabbard’s motion died for lack of a second.
Recess
59.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Dupps a brief recess was
called. Motion carried with all ayes.
60.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Ellison the council meeting
resumed. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Budget for 2002/03 Fiscal year – 1st Reading
61.   Mayor Kriege presented to council his proposed budget for the 2002/03
fiscal year. He stated that the Budget and Finance Committee members reviewed
the proposal and some revisions were made prior to this presentation. He stated
that this budget assumes that the revenue generated from the property tax rate
adopted will be the compensating rate plus four percent and that the payroll
taxes will see a twelve percent increase. He stated that the revenue shows an
overall increase of six percent. He advised that expenses in the administration
budget have been cut by $12,000 and that the police budget is up 5.7% mainly
due to salary increases. He stated the police chief has submitted a new pay
plan for the police department. Mayor Kriege advised that health insurance
costs came in at a thirteen percent increase, which was much lower than
anticipated. He stated that the Public Works budget is up by 12.7% mainly due
to the expenses associated with the Cox Road facility that is being rented from
the Fire District to house the public works equipment. Mayor Kriege stated that
the parks budget is up 18% due to maintenance and operational expenses. He
advised that Municipal Road Aid transfer from the general fund will be $70,000
less than last year and there will be a transfer of $128,894 to the Senior
Center fund. He advised that $240,000 is allocated for road repairs, $150,000
for crack sealing and $70,0000 for storm sewers work including Production
Drive. He stated that no funds have been allocated to the Building Fund. Mayor
Kriege advised that the revenue and expenses budgeted for the Senior Center is
$168,894. The Fowler Creek Sewer Fund expenses will run $409,400 with only
estimated revenue of $386,000, while the Sewer Fund will have revenues of
$259,000 and $20,322 in known expenses. He stated that the budget expenditures
would total $3,403,640 with a fund balance of $1,581,779 on June 30, 2003,
which is six months of reserves or 46% of the budget. Mayor Kriege advised that
the new municipal center revenue would be $4,525,000 with estimated expenses
totaling $3,167,300.
62.   Mayor Kriege advised that this makes up the general and special funds and
that the budget should be adopted prior to July 1, 2002. Mr. Gabbard stated
that he had several questions regarding the budget that Mayor Kriege has
presented but requested to reserve his questions until the next meeting, prior
to the second reading.
63.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to have a first reading of the proposed ordinance
to adopt the budget for the 2002/03 fiscal year; seconded by Mr. Moriconi. Mr.
Walker read the ordinance by title only.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a Pay Plan – 1 Reading
64.   Mayor Kriege submitted a Personnel and Pay Classification Plan ordinance
for a first reading. No motion or second; Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance.

JUNE 3, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard,
Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance was City
Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
2.   Mayor Kriege introduced Richard Noah, 1843 Forest Run Drive, a member of
the Citizens Police Academy Alumni, who presented a pepper ball gun to the
police department that the Alumni purchased with fundraising proceeds. Mr. Noah
stated the addition of this pepper ball gun would now provide for one gun per
shift. He stated this type of non-lethal weapon would give the police officer
an alternative to using lethal force on an offender. Chief Butler thanked the
Alumni for this and the other equipment they have purchased for the department.
He stated the next Citizens Police Academy will commence on September 5, 2002
and invited everyone to attend to see a demonstration of the equipment.
Approval of the Minutes of the May 6, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of May 6, 2002 as amended. Mr. Dupps seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with five yes votes and one pass vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion
carried.
Presentation of Memorial park Master Plan by Matrix Architects – Susan Keeney
4.   Mayor Kriege introduced Susan Keeney of Matrix Architects who would
present the recently completed master plan for Memorial Park. He stated that
the plan was presented at the Building and Recreation Committee last week.
5.   Ms. Keeney distributed a copy of the master plan to the council and
reviewed the highlights of the plan. She stated that input on the plan for this
park was obtained from a variety of ways; a citizen survey was conducted as
well as involvement from the city staff. She stated the citizen survey results
stressed the desire for a family oriented park. She stated that they tried to
adopt a vision for the future based on the survey results and taking into
consideration the irregular park terrain, trees and natural vegetation that are
present. She stated they worked with the existing features and have proposed
another egress via Peach Drive. Ms. Keeney stated that the citizen survey
revealed that additional parking, toilet facilities, play equipment for younger
children, water fountains and security police patrol were high priorities for
the park. She stated they tried to design a plan that would work with the
existing walking trails, provide an access road to the future amphitheater and
locate parking around the perimeter of the park. She advised that this plan
would not move the existing play area and shelter building.
6.   Ms. Keeney advised that the master plan is to be used as a tool for the
future development of the park and is not a construction document. Mr. Gabbard
stated that Mr. Charles Deters has submitted an alternate amphitheater plan to
the city for consideration. Ms. Keeney stated she was aware of this alternate
plan that suggests relocating the amphitheater further back from the Senior
Center and developing a road to access the amphitheater. She cautioned
placement of the access road in that section of terrain. Mr. Gabbard stated
that the lake shown on the master plan map is on the bordering property to the
park. Ms. Keeney stated that the city may desire acquiring that area in the
future as the lake provides a nice amenity.
7.   Ms. Keeney closed by informing council that the plan also gives a broad
look at how to implement the plan over time. Mayor Kriege encouraged the
Building and Recreation Committee to look at phasing in the plan over time, as
the budget will permit and suggested they make a recommendation to council.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
8.   Frank Platek, 732 Hogreffe Road, addressed council regarding the proposed
rezoning of the Glenhurst Development area that includes portions of Hogreffe
and Bristow Roads. He stated that he had new information to present. Mayor
Kriege interrupted him by advising that council would not be permitted to hear
any information that was not presented at the public hearing held by the Kenton
County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission. Mayor Kriege reminded Mr.
Platek and council that the city’s decision regarding this zone change had to
be based solely on the information that was presented at the public hearing.
Mr. Platek reminded council that on four previous occasions the Planning
Commission recommended to not expand this area beyond 2.4 units per acre. He
began to comment on conversations he has had with representatives of the city
and again Mayor Kriege cautioned him about revealing new evidence that was not
heard at the public hearing. Mr. Platek expressed his concern that a brother-
in-law of one of the council members is one of the developers of this land and
stated that he feels there is an appearance of a conflict of interest. Mayor
Kriege stated that it is up to the individual council member to decide if they
feel they have a conflict of interest. Mr. Platek requested that each council
member, when called upon to cast their vote, cite why they are voting for or
against the zone change. In closing, Mr. Platek stated that the watershed site
is worse than ever and that he feels the developers are railroading this zone
change. Mayor Kriege stated that council should not be hearing any new
comments, as the public hearing that was held by the Planning Commission was
the resident’s opportunity to voice their concerns.
9.   Russell England, 1 Stevens Road, addressed council regarding the excess
water run off that has been draining into his lake. He stated that he did not
see plans for water retention in the Memorial Park master plan presented
earlier. Mayor Kriege stated that it is not shown in the master plan rendering
but agreed that the city should consider why this flooding is occurring. Mr.
England stated that he is in favor of the park but would appreciate the city
looking into the flooding. Mayor Kriege asked Dave Whitacre, City Engineer to
inspect this area and advise council.
10.   Grace Wilson, 3735 Klette Road, addressed council regarding the re-zoning
of the Fornash property on Mills Road. She commented that the footnotes in the
Comprehensive Plan mention that the roads (Marshall, Mills and Decoursey) in
the area need a lot of attention. She stated she would like to see council heed
these footnotes when considering the zone change request. Ms. Wilson stated
that she understands the benefit of a zone change for the developers but sees
no benefit for her and other residents. She also expressed her frustration that
some of the council members campaigned against over development yet continues
to approve developments that she considers mediocre projects.
11.   Roger C. Bales, 801 Hogreffe Road, stated that he is an opponent of the
proposed development in the Hogreffe Road area. He stated that he wanted to
point out that two percent of the tax bill is designated to support the
Planning Commission, and that if the city has the power to override the
recommendations of the Commission that those tax dollars should be eliminated.
Mayor Kriege stated that he did not feel the council had the power to eliminate
the county taxes at the city level.
12.   Jim Knarr, 10157 Marshall Road, addressed council regarding his
opposition of the development of the Fornash property. Mr. Knarr’s main concern
was the creek flooding which gets worse every year. He stated that he spoke for
one half hour at the Planning Commission’s public hearing and realized when he
left there that this development was a ‘done deal.’ The developer’s plan for a
bridge on Marshall Road is acknowledgment that they are aware of the flooding,
which comes from the Mills Road Park area. Mr. Knarr was also concerned with
the number of units per acre, citing that 3.5 homes per acre is ridiculous in
this area. He stated that some of the 133 acres has a sloping terrain. He
expressed concern that the schools and infrastructure are not able to handle
this future growth. He stated that Governor Patton’s Smart Growth Task Force
establishes goals that include land use plans. In closing, he urged council to
keep in mind the flooding problem in the area when coming to a decision on this
development plan.
13.   Don Saylor, 6084 Taylor Mill Road spoke in favor of the Fornash
development and re-zoning. He stated that he moved here approximately thirty
years ago when the area was completely rural. He stated he has enjoyed the area
but realizes that change will take place. He stated that the Fornash’s have
been good stewards of their land and that poor health has forced Mr. Fornash to
eliminate his livestock. He stated that Mr. Fornash has hired the best
engineers to address the concerns of traffic, sewers and water runoff in order
to protect the neighbors. Mr. Saylor stated he would like to give support to
the Fornash project.
14.   Jeff Jarboe, 11466 Marshall Road addressed council in opposition to the
proposed development of the Fornash property on Mills Road. He stated that he
feels a violation occurred at the Planning Commission as a preliminary site
plan was not available prior to the meeting. He stated that this is not a
normal procedure and would like the matter to be resubmitted to the Commission
because of this violation. He also expressed concern with the plans to install
two pump stations and tie into the existing Marshall Road station. He stated
there are no plans for a gravity line and doesn’t believe this design will
allow the area to develop 1100 homes. He also objected to the main reason the
Planning Commission cited for approving this development plan, which was the
new designation of an Urban Service District. Mr. Jarboe was also concerned
that the plan indicates that forty acres will drain into the Decoursey Creek
instead of the ponds. In closing, he urged council to send this matter back to
the Planning Commission for reconsideration or to deny the zone change request.
15.   Richard Maines, 5254 Courtney Court, asked council what would be done
with the abandoned Everyday gas station at the corner of Madison Pike and
Independence Station Road as the property is looking shabby. Mayor Kriege
advised Mr. Maines that the property was in bankruptcy court. Mr. Maines also
suggested that council combine the commercial and residential trash rate in an
effort to get a lower contract rate.
END OF PRIVELEGES OF THE FLOOR
Award of the Bid for the Lawn and Park Maintenance Contract for Fiscal Year
2002/03
16.   Mr. Wendling informed council that the city is in receipt of four bids
for the maintenance of lawn and park grounds. He stated that the bids were
received from Quad Lawn Care Services, Jackson’s Lawncare Service, Dan’s Lawn
Care and Malco Services. Mr. Wendling stated that because the bid specs allow
the contractor to bid per time or by the hour it is difficult to determine
which bid is the lowest. He stated that some contractors quoted by the hour but
the majority quoted a bid per time each location was maintained. He stated that
the bids give the impression that Quad is the lower bidder and Dan’s is the
high bid. He advised that the contract for the last few years has been with
Malco Lawn Services.
17.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to award the lawn/ball park maintenance bid to
Malco Services as the best bid; seconded by Mr. Kudera. Mr. Ellison commented
that when looking at the bids submitted, that Malco appears high, but
considering that the city has received excellent service he agrees the contract
should be awarded to Malco as the best bid. Mayor Kriege concurred, and added
that Malco knows the area and has provided notable assistance with the
landscaping of the Senior Center building. Mayor Kriege stated that he feels
this is the lowest and best bid submitted. Mr. Gabbard commented that Barry
Malott (Malco) goes the extra mile for the city and that he can be counted on
to provide the needed services. Roll call was answered with six yes votes.
Motion carried 6-0 in favor of awarding the contract to Malco Lawn Services.
Award of Bid for Trash Collection
18.   Mayor Kriege stated that the Public Works Committee met on May 15th with
representatives of the three companies that bid on this contract to review the
bids received. Mr. Gabbard, Chairman of the Public Works Committee, stated that
the meeting lasted two hours with many questions presented and answered. He
stated that two thirds of the citizens favor Rumpke, but he feels there have
been a lot of problems with Rumpke and that concerns him. Mr. Gabbard cited
that his main concern in Rumpke’s bid was the section that would allow Rumpke
to levy additional fees on the city to cover any federal fees imposed on
Rumpke. He stated that the other bids received from Bavarian and CSI did not
include that provision. Moreover, Mr. Gabbard stated, CSI is the low bidder.
Mr. Ellison countered that Rumpke has serviced the city for a long time and in
all that time has never known them to implement this clause. Mr. Kudera
commented that under federal law the city would still have the right to refuse
any increase in fees; he stated that this is a common clause in this type of
contract and sees no reason to deny award of the contract for that reason. He
stated that in his opinion Rumpke has serviced the city very well. Mr. Gabbard
reiterated that he feels Rumpke is too high and this clause gives them the
opportunity to impose additional fees. Mr. Kudera stated that Rumpke could not
arbitrarily impose additional fees, but could come before council to negotiate
any increase.
19.   Mayor Kriege asked Greg Rumpke to clarify this clause in the bid package.
Mr. Rumpke advised that they have not used this clause in the past and would
only come before council if they felt they needed assistance with additional
federal fees that they incur. He stated that one time, some years ago, he
requested additional fees from the city council and was refused; and he
reiterated Mr. Kudera’s comment that, this clause could not be exercised
without agreement from the city council.
20.   Mr. Moriconi commented that the Public Works Committee spent two hours
talking about garbage. He stated that the bids were very professional. He
stated that he felt the automated pickup proposed by CSI was not something the
city was ready to try at this time. Mr. Moriconi commented that the city has no
complaints with Rumpke regarding current services provided to the city. In
addition, he felt that the $7.00 per year difference between Rumpke and CSI was
relative.
21.   Mr. Dupps stated he would like council to consider recycling as part of
the package awarded. He stated that he feels that few residents currently
subscribe to recycling, as it is an additional financial burden to them. He
commented that he feels the city would be encouraging more residents to
participate in recycling if this is a part of the program offered. Mayor Kriege
commented the he is probably right but that would add another $25.00 per year
to this assessment of each resident. He stated that hopefully the recycling
program could be added on in the next couple of years. Mr. Moriconi commented
that only 149 out of 5000 residences currently subscribe to curbside recycling.
Mayor Kriege suggested the city might want to promote this program to possibly
boost the subscription number of residents.
22.   Representative from CSI, Ms. Christy, thanked the city for giving them
the opportunity to bid on this contract. She stated they feel their bid is the
lowest with no additional charge for recycling. She advised that, per
legislation, the contractor is permitted to pass on the additional fees imposed
by the federal government without getting prior approval from the city council.
In closing, she stated that CSI provided the city with the best bid and hopes
that council will take that into consideration. Mr. Wendling clarified Ms.
Christy’s comment that there is no charge for the recycling bid, but that the
resident subscription rate is $4.00 per month for recycling pickup. Another
representative for CSI commented that their bid was submitted per the city
specifications and does not contain qualifications. A representative from
Rumpke commented that they feel Rumpke submitted the best bid based on the
quality of their current service and the past service they have provided the
city over the last decade. That withstanding, he feels this is a fair bid.
There was a brief discussion between Mr. Gabbard and the Rumpke representative
regarding the employee wages paid by Rumpke and CSI.
23.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to award the trash pickup contract to CSI, as
the lowest and best bid, Option “A-1”, for the period of July 1, 2002 through
June 30, 2004 at the rate of $93.60 per year, with the subscription recycling
rate of $4.50 per month. The motion died for lack of a second.
24.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to award the trash pickup contract to Rumpke as
the best bid, Option “A-1”, for the period of July 1, 2002 through June 30,
2004 at the rate of $100.80 per year, with the subscription recycling rate of
$3.50 per month. Mr. Bushong seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with
four yes votes and two no votes cast by Mr. Gabbard and Mr. Dupps.

Ordinance No. 2002-O-11 Adopting the Budget for the 2002-03 Fiscal Year – 2nd
Reading
36.   Mayor Kriege presented Ordinance No. 2002-O-11 for approval by council to
adopt the city budget for the 2002-03 fiscal year. Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance.
37.   Motion was made by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Dupps to adopt the
proposed budget.
38.   Mr. Gabbard stated that he had several questions regarding the budget
presented. He asked what property tax rate had been estimated for this revenue
line item. Finance Director, Janet Rebman stated that line item assumed a rate
of 1.49/1,000 of assessed value based on preliminary figures obtained from the
Property Valuation Assessor and assuming the city adopts the compensating rate
plus four percent. She stated that presently the rate is 1.47. Mr. Gabbard
asked if this would be corrected when the final totals were received from the
PVA. Mayor Kriege assured Mr. Gabbard corrections would be made if necessary.
39.   Mr. Gabbard suggested the city newsletter be published three times per
year instead of the proposed twice a year. Mayor Kriege stated if council
wanted to change this then the ordinance may require a second reading. Mr.
Walker stated that a line item could be changed. Mr. Gabbard stated he would
like to amend this line.
40.   Mr. Gabbard questioned the $27,000 reduction in the city attorney’s
expense line item. Mayor Kriege stated that he is confident that this line item
expense will decrease in the coming year due to the fewer number of lawsuits
Mr. Walker is handling.
41.   Mr. Gabbard questioned the expense budgeted for codification of the
ordinances. He advised that the codification is done every two years and that
this could save $2,000.
42.   Mayor Kriege voiced his concern that if council makes any changes in the
budget that has been presented, and then the reading tonight will revert back
to a first reading. Mr. Ellison commented that he felt the summary budget would
hold true regardless of individual line items. Mr. Gabbard stated that he is
asking that some changes be made to department budgets. Mr. Moriconi asked Mr.
Gabbard how many changes he was proposing. Mr. Gabbard stated he had several
change requests. Mr. Bushong objected to Mr. Gabbard’s waiting until now to
come forth with his requests for amendments. He stated that any proposed
changes should have been done in committee meetings. Mr. Gabbard stated that he
is not on the Finance Committee, but did attend a couple of the meetings. Mayor
Kriege advised that the proposed budget has changed very little from two months
ago when it was submitted to the Budget and Finance Committee.
43.   Mr. Gabbard proceeded with his questions. He asked what the $1,200 “rent”
line item was allocated for. Mr. Ellison advised this is the expense for the
use of the courtroom where the city holds their meetings. Mr. Wendling stated
this line item decreased since the city lost the leased space in the old
firehouse building. Mr. Gabbard asked why the line item for the auto lease for
Mr. Wendling’s car increased by $400. Mayor Kriege replied that the current
lease would expire by the end of this year and it was estimated that a new
lease or purchase would increase from the current rate.
44.   Mr. Gabbard questioned the need for a line item for a Public Works
seasonal employee and suggested the city utilize Kenton County jail inmates for
this type of labor. Mr. Wendling stated the city has used inmates in the past
but has found that this type of laborer is not always a reliable resource for
the city. Mr. Gabbard also questioned the capital expenditures line item in the
Public Works budget. Mayor Kriege advised that this is for equipment that is
not your average type of tool, such as a generator, etc.
45.   Mr. Gabbard was concerned that the road repairs budget was only $240,000.
Mayor Kriege advised he was backing down on the road budget for the coming year
as the city has spent a lot the last three-four years. Mr. Moriconi asked if
the Holton Drive project would come from the proposed budget. Mayor Kriege
stated that project would be paid out of the current 2001/02 budget.
46.   Mr. Gabbard asked about the T-21 Grant for the construction of sidewalks.
Mayor Kriege advised the $145,475 allocation was put into the budget in the
anticipation that city would be awarded the grant. He stated that the funds
would not be expended if the city does not receive the grant. Ms. Brake advised
the next section of sidewalks would proceed north on Madison.
47.   Mr. Gabbard expressed concern that the Senior Center budget of $168,894
seemed high in light of the fact that the building is open only three days per
week. Mr. Wendling advised that the goal of the Board of Directors is to open
five days per week by June or July of this year. He stated that currently the
Center is open three days a week from 9:00 am until 3:00 p.m. Mr. Gabbard asked
if kitchen equipment and furniture has been purchased. Mr. Wendling advised
that tables, chairs and some of the kitchen equipment has been purchased and
installed.
48.   Regarding the Municipal Center Fund, Mr. Gabbard noted the loan proceeds
revenue and asked how many years the city would pay on this loan. Mayor Kriege
advised the loan was for seventeen years with no penalty for early payoff
49.   Mayor Kriege advised council that the budget would be adopted using a
summary format so that changes on individual line items could be made
throughout the year. There being no further questions regarding the proposed
budget, roll call was answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr.
Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.

12; seconded by Mr. Bushong.

Discussion of Allocating Funds for the Kentucky Renaissance Program
53.   Mr. Gabbard stated he has a petition that requests the city to continue
with the Renaissance Program of the downtown area. Mayor Kriege stated that
during the budget process for next year he struggled with allocating funds for
this program but that there was only so much money to cover the various
departments and this program would require an employee be hired to administer
the program. Mr. Gabbard argued that the program has a return rate of 80%. Mr.
Gabbard made a motion to add the Renaissance Program to the 2002/03 budget by
allocating $12,000 to be taken from the general fund reserve. He stated that
then the city could apply for the Silver designation by the September deadline.
Mr. Moriconi stated the city would then be required to hire the employee to
administer the program. Mr. Wendling advised the city would have to hire within
a year or refund the money received from the state. Mr. Gabbard stated he felt
this was a good opportunity to revitalize the downtown area. Mr. Dupps seconded
the motion. Mr. Dupps asked what the $12,000 would finance. Mr. Gabbard
reiterated the city could get an 80% return on this money. Mrs. Barbara
Gabbard, who was in the audience, advised the $12,000 would be used for
whatever the city indicates in the written grant application; sidewalks, street
lighting, etc. Mr. Dupps stated that the city would need to push forward, as
putting this grant together with limited staff would take a lot of work. Mr.
Gabbard concurred that it would be a lot of work, but that it needs to be
started and that this is something the city should strive for. Mayor Kriege
advised that continuing the Renaissance Program would be a very large
commitment for the city. Mr. Kudera commented that continuing this Program
would be spending money the city doesn’t have as the city has quite serious
budget constraints. He stated there should be a master plan adopted prior to
continuing this program. Mayor Kriege stated that the Renaissance Program is
only one way that the area can be revitalized. He stated that private funds
would be another way to keep this program going and that support for the
program would be needed from the residents to assist in this endeavor. Mr.
Gabbard stated that the funds could be used to invest in sidewalks to help the
city have a nicer appearance. Mayor Kriege stated that Hometown Pizza and Huber
& Behle Contractors reconstructed the sidewalks in front of their
establishments. Mr. Kudera commented that several homes in the business area
are badly in need of repairs and asked council if the city should pay for that
as well. He stated that he feels the private sector should fund this. Mayor
Kriege stated that it is the homeowner’s responsibility to repair the sidewalks
in front of their property. Mr. Gabbard stated that he felt the city should try
to make an effort to upgrade the downtown area. Mr. Bushong asked who would
write the grant. Mayor Kriege advised that Ms. Brake wrote the original
application for the Bronze level. Mr. Wendling stated he would have to look at
the current staff workload before he could answer that. Mayor Kriege stated
that the city couldn’t go out and hire someone at this time. At this time roll
call was taken and answered with three yes votes by Mr. Ellison Mr. Gabbard and
Mr. Dupps and three no votes cast by Mr. Kudera, Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Bushong.
Mayor Kriege broke the tie by voting no. The motion was defeated 4-3.

JULY 1, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera
and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Council Member Jim Ellison was absent.
Also in attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator,
Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the June 3, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Moriconi made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of June 3, 2002 as amended. Mr. Bushong seconded the motion. No roll
call; motion carried with all ayes.
July 4th Celebration – Update Report by Nita Brake
3.   Ms. Brake gave a report for the Special Events Committee to Mayor Kriege
and council regarding the plans for the upcoming July 4th Celebration. She
stated the days events would begin with a parade at two o’clock commencing from
the Summit View Schools parking lot and ending at Memorial Park. She stated
that a Black Hawk would do a ‘’fly-over” during the parade. She stated that the
Grand Marshals of the parade this year would be Lt. Governor Steve Henry and
his wife, former Miss America, Heather French Henry, and Mr. James Simmons, a
city resident. She stated that on Friday, July 5th, at the Wright Patterson Air
Force Base, Mr. Simmons would be receiving a Purple Heart medal for his valor
demonstrated during World War II when the plane he was piloting was shot down.
She stated that several military vehicles would be on display at the Park
during the day’s event. Ms. Brake reported that approximately twenty booths
would be set up offering a variety of food and games, in addition to
fundraising booths manned by local organizations. She stated that the day’s
entertainment would include a variety of musical groups that would play from 3:
30 until 9:00 p.m., with kiddie rides and a fireworks display at 10:00 p.m. She
stated that because a large crowd is expected for the fireworks display, that
shuttle bus service would be provided from 8:00 p.m. until 11:45 p.m. along
Madison Pike at various parking lots.
4.   Mayor Kriege stated that he is looking forward to this year’s event, as it
would be bigger and better than last year. He encouraged everyone’s attendance.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-13 – Map Amendment for Zone Change of Fornash Property on
Mills Road – 2nd Reading
5.   Mayor Kriege advised that council has before them the minutes of the May
2, 2002 public hearing of the Kenton County & Municipal Planning & Zoning
Commission as well as the letter of recommendation relative to the request by
Mr. Clint Fornash for a map amendment for his property (approximately 130 acre
parcel) along the northeast side of Mills Road. Mayor Kriege reminded council
that any decision made regarding this zone change request would have to be
based on the information disclosed at the public hearing. He asked Mr. Martin
Butler, attorney for Mr. Fornash if he wanted to make a presentation to
council.
6.   Mr. Butler sated that he had nothing further to add and was here on behalf
of Mr. Fornash, who was also in attendance. He stated he would answer any
questions council may have regarding this request.
7.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor to Mr. Jim Knarr, 10157 Marshall Road, who
spoke in opposition to this zone change and planned development. Mr. Knarr
asked if council had received the map. Mayor Kriege replied they had. Mr. Knarr
reported that this area has a major flood every five years, the most recent
being on April 22, 2002. He stated that he feels the flooding is a direct
result of the development of Shaw Estates and Manor Hill subdivisions. He
stated that he has attempted to get an answer regarding a flood plain for this
area, but has been unable to get an answer. He asked if a study has been done
regarding this. Mr. Butler stated a study has not been conducted yet, but it
would be the next step in the process. He stated that Mr. Fornash was here to
request a zone change only, not for approval of a development plan. He stated
that catch basins would be a part of a plan. Mr. Knarr expressed his concern
regarding the flooding and felt the property could be developed after the flood
conditions are solved. Mr. Butler stated that the Planning Commission reviewed
this request and these issues were not raised. Mr. Bushong asked if the
property was in a flood zone. Mr. Butler stated that the property is not in a
flood plain as it sits on a hill. Mr. Knarr distributed maps to council that
were also presented at the public hearing held by the Planning Commission. He
stated that development of the Fornash property would add to the current
flooding on Marshall Road. Mr. Butler disagreed that the current flooding is
the fault of the planned development.
8.   Mr. Knarr stated that his objections to this development also include the
plans for 3.5 units per acre, which he feels is too high, only one ingress/
egress, which he feels could be a safety issue if Mills Road was blocked and
emergency vehicles could not access the area. Mr. Knarr also stated that he
feels the planned development would be unfair to the surrounding neighbors.
9.   Mr. Butler stated that he objected to the presentation of the photos
showing the flooding conditions, which he claimed were never presented to the
Planning Commission nor did the applicant see these photos. Mr. Butler
presented a packet to the mayor and council, which was also presented to the
Kenton County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission at the May 2, 2002
public hearing. He stated the zone change request would further a proposed
development of 137 acres to construct no more than 300 homes. He stated the
current zone permits 2 units per acre and the R-1C zone would allow 3.5 units
per acre. He stated the range planned that would not exceed the 300 homes would
be 2.4 – 2.5 units per acre. He stated this is very conservative considering
the number of units permitted; the plan is on the low end of the range. In
response to the plan for only one ingress/egress, Mr. Butler stated, that by
current law, they are not required to provide a second access unless the
development is over five hundred units. He stated the houses will be
constructed along the ridge top and the roads will be laid out so that the
water can be caught. He stated the catch basins would feed to a well-designed
retention area. Mr. Butler stated the development plan is well within the
regulations and that the driveway point access issue is not prohibited by the
subdivision regulations only that it is recommended. He stated the plans do not
include many lots on the Marshall Road side, with some lots on Mills Road that
are adequately spaced.
10.   Mr. Bushong asked where the nearest sewage plant was to the area. Mr.
Butler stated there was a force main on Marshall Road, which will provide for a
natural connection and with the ability to service 1400 homes is more than
adequate in size. He stated that this force main currently serves less than 400
homes in the area. He commented that the Sanitation District put a lot of
forethought into the design of this pump station regarding future needs of the
area. Mr. Moriconi asked how many years it would take to build out. Mr. Butler
stated that they have estimated it would take approximately six years to
complete the subdivision at fifty homes per year.
11.   Mr. Gabbard stated that the pump station on Marshall Road was installed
and is owned by the City of Independence and for which the city is currently
paying the debt. Mr. Gabbard read an excerpt from the letter from the Chairman
of the Kenton County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission dated May 6,
2002. He stated that page two; paragraph b referring to the need to upgrade
Marshall Road as a collector road, was specifically devoted to this
development. Mr. Butler commented that he feels this paragraph is a matter of
interpretation, but advised that Mills Road will be the main artery. He feels
the purpose of the Comprehensive Plan recommending that Marshall Road be
upgraded was for the eventuality of a larger development, over five hundred
homes. He stated that the neither Commission, nor staff raised this issue at
the public hearing.
12.   Mr. Gabbard raised some concerns he had regarding the three retention
ponds planned for the development, especially how they would effect the houses
that sit below the area. Mr. Jim Berling, engineer for this development
explained that the regulations allow for the detention area to be over-designed
so that it can detain more than necessary. Mr. Berling stated that the main
drain to Marshall Road would go under the road and into the creek. Mr. Gabbard
feared this would cause the creek to rise at a faster rate. Mr. Berling
explained that the water would be stored then released slowly. Mr. Gabbard was
concerned that with flooding already a problem that more homes would create
more flooding. Mr. Butler stated that the water would be directed into the
detention ponds then the catch basins would contribute to the lake at a slow
rate as opposed to the rapid rate that currently exists.
13.   Mr. Gabbard asked who would develop this subdivision and what builders
would be involved. Mr. Butler stated they have not yet contracted with a
developer, consequently they do not know what builders would be associated with
this development. Mr. Butler stated that Scheben has expressed an interest in
developing this property.
14.   Mr. Gabbard also had concerns for adequate thoroughfares in this
development. Mr. Butler stated that Mills Road is much larger than Marshall
Road and guessed it to be 28-30 feet in width. He stated that the Planning
Commission would require that main road be identified when the development plan
is submitted for approval. Mr. Gabbard was concerned that the lack of two
entrances into the development might hinder access for emergency vehicles. He
asked if the entrance would be well lit. Mr. Butler stated that an attractive
entrance would be included in the development plans. Mr. Gabbard stated he
would like to see one builder versus multiple builders in an effort to keep the
city free of smaller, poorly constructed houses. Mr. Butler stated that it
would be unfair to limit the developer to one builder, and assured council that
they would find very interested, good builders.
15.   Mr. Butler stated for the record that the application is for a zone
change; there is no request for a variance, homeowners’ association or mixed
land uses. He stated that there is nothing unique or extraordinary regarding
this rezoning request and that the recommendation of the Planning Commission is
consistent with the Comprehensive Plan.
16.   Mayor Kriege asked council how they would like to proceed. Mr. Dupps made
a motion to accept the recommendation of the Kenton County & Municipal Planning
& Zoning Commission’s decision to approve this request for a zone change from
R-RE to R-1C. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Roll call was answered with four
yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-13 – Approving the Map Amendment for the Fornash Property
along Mills/Marshall Rds.
17.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Bushong there was a second
reading of Ordinance No. 2002-O-13 amending the zoning map of the city changing
an approximate 137.5 acre area located along the northeast side of Mills Road
and northwest of Marshall Road from a R-RE to R-1C zone. Roll all was answered
with four yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 4-1 in
favor.

Discussion Regarding Adoption of an Ordinance to Require Developers to Present

24.   Mr. Bushong stated he has received calls regarding the abandoned Circle K
