City Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
Discussion Regarding Detention Basin Design as an Amendment to Cole+Russell
Contract
25.   Mr. Wendling stated that an amendment to the professional services
agreement with Cole + Russell Architects for the municipal center has been
presented for their review. He stated the amendment in the amount of $5,650 is
for the design of a detention basin that would accommodate the municipal center
as well as the amphitheater. Mayor Kriege stated the construction of the
detention basin would be added to the construction bids. Mr. Kudera suggested
the Memorial Park Master Plan should be approved before designing the detention
basin. Mayor Kriege advised it would be necessary to work around that project
and this would provide some preliminary analysis. Mr. Gabbard suggested the
city ask the Independence Fire District to assist in the cost of this detention
pond, as it will also retain drainage from their property. Mr. Kudera disagreed
that the Fire District building was contributing to the drainage condition.
Mayor Kriege stated that all contributing factors would be considered when the
system is designed. Mr. Kudera asked if there were other drainage problems in
the area. Mr. Wendling stated the playground area has a drainage problem, also.
Mayor Kriege stated the council could opt to do nothing as a detention pond is
not required, but the city has been informed there is flooding on the property
below this area. Mr. Whitacre, City Engineer, stated that he has not performed
a detailed analysis, but that drainage problems will increase as the area is
developed and that he is aware that overflow drainage is currently going onto
Mr. Russ England’s property. Mr. Kudera commented the he thinks it is
interesting how the city is just learning of these drainage problems when the
park has been there for three years. Mr. Whitacre stated the drainage problem
could be a combination of two or three factors. He stated that the lowest
portion of the area abuts Mr. England’s property and is probably the best area
for the detention pond. He advised that the Public Works staff recently
installed some surface drains that empty over the hill by the football field.
He stated that the park terrain is full of rock with so little soil atop. Mr.
Kudera suggested moving the play equipment to another location. Mr. Wendling
stated there are no plans to move the equipment now that the Municipal Center
will be located on Madison Pike near Peach Drive. Mr. Moriconi asked if Forest
Run Subdivision was contributing to the drainage problem. Mr. Whitacre stated
the water runoff from that subdivision drains into another ravine area. Mr.
England suggested that if the flooding problem continues that the culvert may
need to be enlarged.
26.   Mayor Kriege advised council that the proposal submitted would cost
$5,600 and would provide construction estimates for a detention pond. Mr.
Gabbard stated that he feels the city does not have an option as the city could
face liability issues in the future if this flooding continues. Mayor Kriege
stated that there are several options available: the detention pond could be
constructed with the municipal or the amphitheatre or with both, but that it
will become a city expense in any case. Mr. Gabbard suggested the detention
area be constructed along with the municipal center. Mr. Wendling stated that
the $5,600 is to design the basin. Mayor Kriege advised that the construction
cost could be ten times more that that. Mr. Moriconi asked if it was necessary
to decide this tonight. Mayor Kriege stated that a decision now is needed if
the municipal center is going to proceed on schedule. Mr. Moriconi suggested
the Building and Recreation Committee review the Memorial Park Plan from Matrix
before deciding this. Mayor Kriege stated this would delay the project by a
month and it may be too late to include this item as an alternate bid. Mr.
Bushong asked if the $5,600 would be taken from general funds. Mayor Kriege
stated this expense would be a part of the municipal center project funds.
27.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to authorize Mayor Kriege to sign the $5,600
amendment to the professional services contract with Cole+Russell Architects
for the design of a detention basin for the Municipal Center/Memorial Park
area; seconded by Mr. Moriconi. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and
one no vote cast by Mr. Kudera. Motion carried 4-1 in favor.
Continuation of City Administrator’s Report

29.   Mr. Wendling reported that the Dehlinger new zone request would be heard

Wendling attending the Planning Commission meeting to represent the city.

AUGUST 5, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian Church gave
the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike
Gabbard, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also in attendance
was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Presentation of the Mayor’s Choice Award to Farmers National Bank
2.   Mayor Kriege presented the first annual Mayor’s Choice Award to Nancy
Kenter and Terri Barnes, representatives of Farmers National Bank for the
bank’s exceptional float entered into the July 4th Celebration parade. Mayor
Kriege thanked them for this wonderful display and encouraged others to come
forward next year with unique and creative entries for the parade.
Approval of the Minutes of the July 1, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of July 1, 2002 as amended. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Roll call
was answered with five yes votes with Mr. Ellison opting to pass. Motion
carried 5-0.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-14 – Approving Parking Restrictions on Independence Rd. –
2nd Reading
4.   Mayor Kriege presented to council Ordinance No. 2002-O-14, an ordinance
that would prohibit parking on the north side of Independence Road from its
intersection with Madison Pike to the corporation line of the city. City
Attorney, Mr. Lawson Walker read the proposed ordinance.
5.   Mr. Kudera moved and Mr. Bushong seconded his motion to adopt Ordinance
No. 2002-O-14. There was a brief discussion wherein Mr. Dupps asked how this
restriction would affect the city. Mr. Wendling advised that because
Independence Road is a state maintained route this ordinance is required by the
state to identify the exact location where parking limitations will be
enforced. Mr. Dupps asked if the state would install the “no parking” signs.
Mr. Wendling replied that the local entity adopting the restriction would take
charge of installing the signs.
6.   Roll call on Mr. Kudera’s motion and Mr.Bushong’s second was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Update on Sidewalk Easement from 5407 Madison Pike – Nannie McIntosh
7.   Mr. Gabbard requested an update on the acquisition of a sidewalk easement
from Ms. McIntosh. Mr. Walker stated that the city was able to acquire this
easement for $1,000 from Ms. McIntosh.
Update on Liberty Orchard Subdivision Compliance with Road Improvements
8.   Mr. Ellison reopened the discussion regarding the lack of compliance for
road improvements from the Henry Fischer development at Liberty Orchard
Subdivision. He advised that the original plans for this development showed
that a third lane with sidewalk and curbs would be installed at the Madison
Pike and Patriot Way intersection. He stated that this requirement was tabled
until the reconstruction of this new section of Madison Pike was completed. Mr.
Ellison stated that the state has completed construction on this area of
Madison Pike and feels the city should follow up with the Fischer Company to
enforce the improvements per the subdivision plans. Mayor Kriege directed Mr.
Wendling to obtain a copy of the subdivision plans for the city to review. Mr.
Ellison suggested the city cease all construction in Liberty Orchard until the
developer complies with the road and sidewalk improvements.

Discussion Regarding the New Municipal Center Project
17.   Mr. Moriconi suggested that the council chambers section, along with the
lower level of that section, of the proposed design of the new Municipal Center
be deleted, in an effort to cut the construction cost of the building. He
stated that he could put that in the form of a motion. Mayor Kriege replied
that it would be necessary to re-design the plans that have been drawn to date.
Mr. Moriconi suggested that by deleting the council chambers the savings could
be used to build a restroom facility in Memorial Park and to pay off the loan
the city obtained to build the Senior Center.
18.   Mr. Gabbard commented that the city is facing the impending cost of the
Industrial Road Project, which will run $78,000 per year over the next three
years. Mayor Kriege advised that the city will have the option to bond the
Industrial Road Project over a ten year period and that the city is still
exploring this option. He stated there is a possibility there will be funds
available to apply to this road project after the municipal center is complete.
19.   Mr. Bushong concurred with Mr. Moriconi and stated he has devised a new
plan to get the total project goal to 3.5M. He stated that deleting the council
chambers would save $830,000, and then the savings could be used for other
projects. Mr. Moriconi stated that he felt, at the bare minimum, restroom
facilities should be constructed in Memorial Park.
20.   Mr. Kudera asked what the final position of the amphitheatre plans were
and suggested the two projects could be combined. He expressed a desire that
the funds for the municipal center should be spent wisely and felt that council
should be prudent in the plans for the Municipal Center, in light of other
outstanding debts.
21.   Mayor Kriege asked council for a motion to authorize him to instruct
Cole+Russell Architects to re-design the Municipal Center without a council
chamber. A brief discussion ensued regarding architect fees that might be
involved in this type of re-design. Mr. Moriconi suggested that removing the
council chambers would eliminate 30% of the project. He stated that the
mechanical room, which is currently designed under the council chamber, would
have to be moved elsewhere.
22.   Mr. Gabbard stated he felt the architect fees were included in the
initial bid. Mayor Kriege advised the architect fee ($316,000) was established
based on the original cost estimate for the project. Mr. Kudera stated that he
thought the design fee was contingent on the final plan approved by council.
Mayor Kriege stated that the architect’s position is that they are due the
established design fee for the original scope of the project and that any re-
design would involve additional fees. Mr. Moriconi suggested that the city
attorney review Cole+Russell’s contract. Mayor Kriege stated that he could not
sign the change order without council approval, so he will instruct Mr. Walker
to review the architect contract, then this discussion will be resumed at the
next council meeting. Mr. Gabbard asked that the re-design cost estimate be
available in time for the special meeting in a couple of weeks. Mr. Kudera
commented that time is of the essence and that he doesn’t want to keep adding
fees only to end up with nothing. Mr. Moriconi concurred that the taxpayer’s
dollars should be spent wisely. Mayor Kriege instructed the City Clerk to poll
the council members in the coming week to arrange for a special council meeting
later this month.
Discussion Regarding Property Located at 5209 Madison Pike
23.   Mr. Gabbard asked if there has been an outcome on the request for a text
amendment by the owner of the old schoolhouse (5209 Madison Pike) that would
permit a church on the first floor and a residence on the second floor. He
expressed some concern that because of the age of the building there may be
evidence of environmental hazards. Mr. Wendling stated that it is not the
responsibility of the city to oversee this concern, as it is private property.
Mr. Gabbard commented that he did not see how the city could approve a re-
zoning request if there may be a major problem with asbestos. Mr. Walker
advised that the request before the city is a zone change and granting a zone
change relates to the use of the building not the safety of the building. He
stated that the city approves zone changes all the time without inspecting for
environmental safety violations. Mr. Gabbard stated this might become a public
safety issue for the city. Mr. Walker reiterated that zone changes are based on
the use of the property. He asked if the building currently housed residents.
Mr. Kudera replied that there are people living there. Mr. Walker stated the
city has no authority, in connection with a zone change, to be concerned with
hazardous materials. He stated that that kind of matter is addressed under the
building code regulations. Mr. Ellison commented that he felt there was problem
in permitting residential in a commercial zone with a church. Mr. Gabbard
stated that he thought the city would be responsible or liable to inspect for
possible hazardous materials. Mr. Walker stated the building is currently being
used as a pre-existing non-conforming use and he assumes the building inspector
is enforcing current building codes regarding safety.
Discussion Regarding Service Cutbacks by the Transit Authority of Northern
Kentucky (TANK)
24.   Mr. Moriconi stated that he has recently been informed through articles
and correspondence that TANK’s bus service to the Independence area will be
drastically cut, especially with the elimination of route nine. He expressed
concern that this will have a negative impact on many students of Holy Cross
School who depend on this form of transportation to Latonia. He stated that
other residents would be affected as well. Mr. Moriconi suggested the city send
a letter to TANK requesting that they reconsider this decision to eliminate
current service routes to Independence. Mr. Ellison concurred and added that
the tone of the letter should be very firm. He stated the Park & Ride lot is
full every day and the growth in this city should support continued service to
this area. Mr. Moriconi agreed and stated the Park and Ride lot is in the heart
of the city and bus service to this area may be eliminated by TANK. Mayor
Kriege concurred and stated the city will contact TANK to see if a
representative would attend the September meeting to answer council questions
regarding their plans to service the city.
City Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
25.   Mr. Wendling reported that the sidewalk projects are complete. He stated
that another project that will soon be under way, hopefully within the next few
weeks, is the road improvements to Production Drive and Production Court. He
stated that he would meet with the businesses to brief them on the work to be
performed. Mr. Wendling advised that some of the banners along Madison Pike
were straightened today. Also, Malco Lawn Service will begin preparing the lawn
area at the Senior Center for reseeding. He stated that because the area is
filled with rocks, Malco would begin by removing as much rock as possible, and
then bring in some topsoil so the seed will take root. The reseeding will be
done sometime between mid-September and October.
26.   Mr. Gabbard asked when council could expect to receive a financial report

Mr. Wendling stated the auditor would be in the next few weeks, at which time
the actuals will be determined. Mr. Gabbard stated the city should have the
actual figures. Mayor Kriege advised that the auditor would determine the true
numbers. Mr. Wendling stated that the Finance Director is still in the process
of closing out the books for the 2001/02 fiscal year.
Discussion Regarding Hillcrest Subdivision – Phase II
27.   Mr. Ellison addressed council regarding the Phase II plan of the
Hillcrest Subdivision on Fleming Drive. He stated the original design was
presented in 1991 and he expressed concern that some conditions placed on the
development are not being met, since new construction has recently begun. His
main concern was adequate water flow in the event of a fire. Mr. Kudera stated
there are state mandates and a development procedure for every new hydrant. He
stated that hydrant tests are conducted at the time of installation. Mr.
Ellison stated that Fleming Drive also needs to be widened and a turn lane
installed. He stated that since new construction has begun he feels the city
needs to review the original plans to see that all conditions of the
development are being met.
COMMITTEE REPORTS
Budget & Finance Committee
28.   No July meeting. Next scheduled meeting is August 19, 2002
Building & Recreation Committee

AUGUST 29, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 6:02 p.m. Council Members
Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call.
Also in attendance was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator,
Mark T. Wendling. Council Members absent were Eric Dupps and Ike Gabbard.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   A proposed ordinance that would approve a text amendment to add an RC-
2 Zone
∙   A proposed ordinance that would approve a map amendment granting a zone
change request
∙   A proposed ordinance that would set the property tax rates for 2002
Proposed Ordinance – Approving Text Amendment to Add RC-2 Zone – 1st Reading
3.   Mayor Kriege presented this ordinance to council that would enact a text
amendment to the city zoning ordinance, Article VIII, Section 8.0 pertaining to
the establishment of zones and Article X, Section 10.19 providing for an
additional zone classification of RC-2 (Rural commercial two) zone and
permitted uses and Article XIV, section 14.7 pertaining to sign regulations and
permitted use and location of signs. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance by
title only.
4.   Mr. Kudera commented that he was concerned that only four council members
were present for this special meeting. He stated that he felt their absence may
be for political purposes and they did not want to be on record for voting for/
against important issues before the city, prior to the general election in
November. Mayor Kriege stated that Mr. Dupps called to say he had to work late.
The City Clerk stated that Mr. Gabbard had informed her after the August 5th
meeting that he would be available for a special meeting anytime in August
except for the last week, as he would be out of town that week. Mrs. Gabbard
was in the audience and concurred that her husband was out of town this week.
Mr. Kudera stated the he just wanted it very clear before votes were taken.
Mayor Kriege stated there would be no votes taken on the first reading of the
ordinances, only on the second reading at the September 9th regular meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Map Amendment approving a Zone Change – Richardson Road
Area – 1st Reading
5.   Mayor Kriege presented an ordinance to council that would amend the zoning
map changing an approximate 5.4-acre area located at the southwest corner of
the intersection of Richardson Road with Old Richardson Road from R-1A to RC-2.
Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance. No discussion by council. Mayor Kriege
informed Mr. Bill Dehlinger, who applied for this zone change, and his
attorney, Marty Butler that a second reading would come before council at the
next meeting on September 9, 2002. Mr. Ellison commented that the Planning &
Zoning Committee worked closely with Mr. Butler and the Northern Kentucky
Planning Commission to add the RC-2 zone classification. He stated that the
committee recommends that council give their approval for this matter.
Proposed Ordinance – Setting the Property Tax Rates for 2002 – 1st Reading
6.   Mayor Kriege presented an ordinance to council that would set the tax
rates for both real estate and personal (tangible) for the year 2002. Mayor
Kriege stated that the 2002/03 budget was based on the revenue that would be
raised taking the compensating rate plus four percent. He stated that rate has
been calculated at $1.56 per $1,000 of assessed property value for real estate
and $3.17 per $1,000 of assessed value for personal property.
7.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to set the rates using the calculation of the
compensating rate plus four percent; seconded by Mr. Bushong. Roll call was
answered with four yes votes. Motion carried. Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance.
ADJOURNMENT
8.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Moriconi the meeting was
adjourned. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting was closed at 6:17 p.m.

Thomas M. Kriege, Mayor

SEPTEMBER 9, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Thomas M. Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member, Jim Kudera, gave the invocation. Council
Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera and Chris
Moriconi answered roll call. Also present was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker
and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the August 5, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of August 5, 2002 as submitted. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. No
roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Approval of the Minutes of the August 29, 2002 Special Council Meeting
3.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve the minutes of the special council
meeting of August 29, 2002 as submitted. Mr. Moriconi seconded the motion. No
roll call; motion carried with four ayes. Mr. Gabbard and Mr. Dupps voiced a
pass, as they were not present at the special meeting.
PRIVELEGES OF THE FLOOR
4.   Bill Miller, 4394 Oliver Road, addressed council with his displeasure
concerning the unkempt condition of the Revere Crossing development across from
his residence on Oliver Road. He voiced his objection to the piles of dirt,
overgrowth of weeds and cut wood that has been shoved to the side of the road.
Mr. Miller stated that he is aware of the fact that Oliver Road is a state
maintained road, but felt that this poor condition is a direct reflection on
the City of Independence. Mayor Kriege advised Mr. Miller that he does not want
to appear that the city is passing this off, but the city would contact the
responsible agency to handle this problem. Mr. Wendling stated he would call
the state highway department to come out and make an inspection of the area.
5.   Kathy Howard, 1887 Freedom Trail, addressed council concerning TANK’s
(Transit Authority of Northern Kentucky) recent announcement that certain bus
routes to Independence will be eliminated. She expressed her displeasure that
bus Route 9, that services the Cherokee Shopping Center, would put a hardship
on Holy Cross High School students that use that route bus to get to the school
in Latonia. She stated that the students do not have an alternate way to get to
school. Ms. Howard reported that TANK had requested a 24% increase in funds
from Kenton County Fiscal Court, but only received 8% and that TANK has cited
the lack of funds as the reason for the cutbacks in services. She questioned
TANK’s motives in not eliminating express routes that transport riders to
Cincinnati. She stated that her taxes are paying for others working in
Cincinnati and paying Cincinnati payroll taxes. In closing, Ms. Howard
commented that TANK should be held accountable for the decisions they have made
to eliminate the planned service routes to this area. Mayor Kriege stated that
a representative from TANK was present and would speak later in the meeting
regarding this issue.
6.   Tony Stenger, 5188 Madison Pike, addressed council regarding the rundown
property located at 5190 Madison Pike. He stated that he has spoken to the City
Administrator and City Building Inspector who have inspected the deteriorated
condition of this property and advised him that the property owners would be
requesting a zone change from the city so that they can raze the house and
build a duplex unit in its place. Mr. Stenger was concerned that the property
in its current condition is decreasing the surrounding property values. Mr.
Wendling responded by advising Mr. Stenger of the process the property owners
will encounter to get the zone changed for a duplex unit. He stated the owners
will make an application for the requested zone change to the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning Commission, and then the staff will forward a recommendation to
the Kenton County Planning Commission, who in turn will make a recommendation
to the city, for either an approval or denial. He stated that the city would
then have ninety days to act on the recommendation by the Planning Commission;
and this is a three to four month process. Mr. Stenger stated that in the
meantime the house is falling apart. Mr. Moriconi asked if the house had
structural cracks. Mr. Wendling stated he would send the Zoning Administrator
to inspect it and have the Building Inspector collaborate to seek a temporary
remedy. Mr. Wendling assured Mr. Stenger that the city is making every effort
to rectify this eyesore.
TANK – (Transit Authority of Northern Kentucky) – Mr. Mark Donaghy, General
Manager
7.   Mayor Kriege introduced Mark Donaghy who is the General Manager of TANK.
He stated that Mr. Donaghy is present to inform, explain and answer any
questions council has concerning the recent service reductions on Route 9. He
stated that the budget request that they had submitted to the three counties
was not fully funded, nor has the state been matching the federal grants. He
stated they have also seen an increase in insurance premiums. Mr. Donaghy
stated that as a public agency their records are open for public review. He
stated that Kenton County contributed predominantly less this year and that
overall TANK is experiencing a $1.8M shortfall resulting in the elimination of
expansion plans, three management positions and the elimination of three bus
routes. He stated the deletion of the three bus routes would be effective on
Saturday, September 14, 2002. He stated that while Route #9 is productive, that
in comparison with other routes, its ridership is less. He stated that some
routes lost partial service while others were eliminated altogether. He stated
that during the budget process, they began with the idea of increasing
services, but was not able to achieve this due to the lack of anticipated
funds.
8.   Mayor Kriege asked when the ridership count was conducted. Mr. Donaghy
stated the most recent was taken in April. Mr. Moriconi asked if the current
growth in the Independence area was a consideration factor when deciding the
routes to be eliminated. Mr. Donaghy replied that TANK is not ignoring this
area, but with the revenue funds decreased by $1.1M that services had to be cut
back. Mr. Gabbard asked the daily start of the Day Tripper service could begin
at 7:00 a.m. instead of 8:00 a.m. Mr. Donaghy explained the Day Tripper service
is on a ‘first come, first serve” basis, and added that it is not designed for
“standing reservations.” He advised that the Covington School System purchased
$65,000 in bus service for the students.
9.   Mr. Bushong asked if TANK’s decision to cut services has been etched in
stone. Mr. Donaghy advised that the changes will take effect this Saturday and
noted that public hearings were held regarding these changes in service. Mayor
Kriege asked when the board would next review the services. Mr. Donaghy stated
that talks with the county officials should begin early next year and the
concern will be what funds will be available. Mayor Kriege asked what it would
cost to reinstate Route #9. Mr. Donaghy stated he would have to review that and
get back to the city with that information. Mr. Ellison asked when the board
would hold another public hearing. Mr. Donaghy stated it would not be necessary
to hold a public hearing until the next budget cycle. Mr. Ellison commented
that attendance at the public hearings is poor especially during the summer
months when ridership is down. Ms. Howard stated that the public hearing notice
was in the paper around July 4th when people are out of town for the holiday.
She stated she has requested the revised bus schedules so that they can try to
make other car-pool arrangements. Mr. Donaghy stated the schedules were just
received from the printer and he brought some to be distributed. Again, Mr.
Donaghy explained that the Day Tripper service is not designed for daily use
for an individual. Mr. Kudera commented that that service is expensive to
operate. Mr. Donaghy stated that it has a lower pay rate. Mr. Donaghy reassured
council that he hoped to be able to reinstate the bus services next year. Mayor
Kriege asked when the board holds its meetings. Mr. Donaghy replied that the
board meets on the second Wednesday of each month.
Discussion Regarding the Municipal Center and Additional Service Contracts
10.   Mayor Kriege introduced Mr. John Russell and Mr. Scott Layman from
Cole+Russell Architects who were present to explain the various additional
service contracts from which council could choose to modify the original
contract plans for the new municipal center. Mr. Layman informed council that
the service options include the following:
§   Amendment No. 1891-808 – Schematic re-design to remove the Council Chamber
wing from the original scope of work, including replacement of the break room
with the mechanical room. This additional contract service charge will be
$13,750.00.
§   Amendment No. 1891-809 – Design development and construction documents for
re-design to remove the entire Council Chamber wing from the original scope of
work, including replacement of the break room with the mechanical room. This
additional contract service charge will be $16,500.00.
§   Amendment No. 1891-810 – Prepare the construction documents to indicate the
Council Chamber wing as an Add-Alternate to the base construction bid. This
additional service will be a continuation of the building re-design from
Agreements 1891-808 and 1891-809. This additional contract service charge will
be $15,000.00.
§   Amendment No. 1891-811 – Schematic re-design and documentation to reduce
the size of the Council Chamber wing by approximately 30% on both the upper and
lower levels. The existing clerestory will be removed in the redesign.
Administration and Police offices, fitness and break rooms, lobby, council
conference room, public toilets and mechanical room are to generally remain as
currently designed. This additional contract service charge will be $15,000.00.
§   Amendment No. 1891-812 – Design development and construction document
services for re-design to reduce the size of the Council Chamber wing by
approximately 30% on both the upper and lower levels. The existing clerestory
will be removed in the redesign. Administration and Police offices, fitness and
break rooms, lobby, council conference room, public toilets and mechanical room
are to generally remain as currently designed. This additional contract service
charge will be $18,500.00.
Mayor Kriege reviewed with council each proposed service contract amendment.
Mr. Bushong asked what the overall cost would be. Mayor Kriege stated the cost
could not be determined until the architects redo the schematic design. Mr.
Russell advised that the cost estimate is based on square footage and reduced
cost can be achieved by eliminating or reducing it. Mr. Bushong stated that he
heard that the rough estimate to eliminate the council chamber wing was
$826,000. Mr. Layman stated that the estimators did not support that
approximation and that a firm construction estimate cannot be obtained until it
can be actually quantified. Mr. Moriconi questioned Amendment No. 810 that
would design the council chamber as an add on. Mr. Layman explained that it
would be similar to the clock tower in that it would be designed totally
separate from the rest of the building and then council could either accept or
decline the bid based on the funds available and the base bids received. Mr.
Moriconi commented that this Amendment makes sense to him to obtain bids to
construct the building with or without the Council Chamber. Mr. Wendling
commented that it will be complex to design the chamber wing as an add on
feature. Mr. Layman stated that the loss of the council chamber wing would
necessitate the mechanical room being relocated along with other re-design that
would be associated to facilitate loosing that wing. Mr. Moriconi voiced
concern in losing the fitness/exercise room for the police, which is currently
located under the council chamber; he suggested relocating the mechanical room
in the designated storage area for the administration department, as it appears
that department has lots of storage and future office space. Mr. Layman stated
that the elimination of the Council Chamber wing and consequently the
relocation of the mechanical room would affect the design of both sides of the
building. Mr. Russell concurred that losing the Council Chamber would
necessitate finding room for every essential element. Mayor Kriege advised the
break room would also be eliminated if the mechanical room had to be located in
its place. Mr. Moriconi questioned the need for a Planning Room. Mayor Kriege
explained that the Building Inspector would use the room to store flat plan
files and review plans. Mr. Gabbard emphasized the importance of adequate
storage space, which the city is currently lacking. He stated there is a real
need for storage now and for future expansion. He questioned the idea of
designing a building that would lack sufficient storage and other necessary
facilities.
Mr. Russell commented that he has never heard a client state that they regret
building extra storage space.
11.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Layman if the project was ready to put out to bid.
Mr. Layman stated that the construction documents are 95% complete. Mayor
Kriege asked council if they wanted to put the project out to bid. Mr. Kudera
replied yes. Mayor Kriege asked council if they wanted to proceed with the
original plan and put it out to bid. Mr. Ellison stated that they would be
deciding on a plan for a building that would last well into the future and that
it doesn’t make sense to him to build it without a council chamber wing. He
stated that he would agree that the size of the wing might need to be reduced
and that the niceties could be eliminated in an effort to control the cost.
Mayor Kriege stated that the extras, such as the clock tower, would be an add-
on bid so that council could add that feature if the overall cost of the
building is lower than projected. Mayor Kriege commented that the proposed
council chamber wing is smaller than the room in the courthouse where council
currently holds meetings. Mr. Russell advised the proposed council chamber
would accommodate sixty spectators.
12.   There was a discussion wherein the architects explained the difference
between the proposed amendments to the original service contract and that some
are continuations of the re-design from other amendments. Mr. Moriconi
suggested going with Amendment 810 that would indicate the council chamber wing
as an add-alternate to the base construction bid. Mr. Layman advised that
Amendment 810 is a continuation of Amendment 808 and 809. He stated that the
way it is structured is that it is a continuation of the design process and
that all three amendments would total $45,250. Mr. Gabbard commented that it
seems like a multitude of tasks. Mr. Russell advised that the re-design process
is much more complicated at this stage of the project than it would have been
if the plans had been outlined this way in the beginning. Mayor Kriege
commented that the project could be put out to bid as it is currently designed
and then there would be no additional fees; but if council were considering the
removal of the council chamber, then Amendment 808 and 809 would accomplish
that. Mr. Layman stated that Amendments 811 and 812 reduce the size of the
Council Chamber wing. Mr. Russell stated that would require the additional
Amendment 810 as well. Mr. Moriconi asked how the square footage of the council
chamber was determined. Mr. Russell stated that Mr. Wendling supplied the
information.
13.   Mr. Russell advised that the construction document phase is close to
completion and that the last estimate is consistent with the current estimate
so that the project should be right on budget, but he stated, it is only an
estimate. Mr. Gabbard asked if the design of the detention pond is included in
the bid document. Mr. Layman stated that the civil engineering is finished and
the drafting may be near completion. He stated that he thinks the cost of the
detention pond will be around $33,000.
14.   Mr. Moriconi commented that he would like to see some other projects in
Memorial Park, such as the construction of the amphitheater and restroom
facilities, shelter building and basketball courts accomplished in conjunction
with the construction of the Municipal Center, as well as eliminating the
Senior Center debt. Mr. Gabbard questioned eliminating a part of the Municipal
Center in order to save funds to pay off the Senior Center. Mr. Moriconi
replied that was his goal and recalled that he had proposed this at the last
council meeting. He stated that the city could save $60,000 per year. Mr.
Gabbard asked Mayor Kriege what the total payoff was on the Senior Center. Mr.
Wendling stated he did not know the exact figure but would get the information.
Mr. Kudera stated he was told the payoff was $410,000. Mr. Moriconi stated the
amphitheater would cost more to construct than the available allocation of
funds, as it will be necessary to put in an access road, etc. Mr. Gabbard
expressed concern that the city does not have the adequate funds to accomplish
all that Mr. Moriconi is proposing. Mr. Kudera stated that council needs
accurate figures to make these decisions. Mr. Bushong commented that he did not
feel that a Council Chamber wing was needed when the city has other facilities
available. Mr. Gabbard stated that he can’t make a decision regarding re-design
fees as the city needs to ensure there are adequate monies to do this. Mr.
Kudera expressed frustration that the original contract was $378,000 including
the $185,000 cost of the Taylor Smith property and yet the city is still not
committed and a building design has not been determined. Mr. Russell stated
that the original budget for this project was $3,800,000 and is now $3,867,000.
He stated that council is now considering a re-design of the project. He stated
that since the construction documents are ready to bid, he suggested putting it
out to bid at the present design and test it on the street. Mr. Layman advised
that the first design presented to the committee was estimated at $4,400,000;
the committee voluntarily made many revisions in order to bring it to the
current $3,800,000 cost. Mr. Gabbard commented that the architects have done
what was requested of them. Mr. Moriconi expressed concern that if the bids
received reach the $4,000,000 point then there will not be adequate funds to
eliminate the debt on the Senior Center and other things he would like to
accomplish in the Park. Mr. Bushong asked if eliminating the Council Chamber
would bring the project below $3,000,000. Mr. Layman stated the project is
within the budget now at only $250,000 over. Mr. Bushong stated that it has
been his position all along that the Municipal Center should be constructed for
under $3,500,000. Mr. Russell advised that the building would have to be
drastically reduced in size in order to see a substantial reduction in the
construction cost.
15.   Mayor Kriege expressed the need to finish up the project and put it out
to bid unless the council wants to take another direction. Mr. Moriconi asked
what the time frame would be for the re-design work. Mr. Dupps commented that
most of the amendments state twenty days. Mr. Layman stated they would request
an extension of thirty days. Mr. Moriconi asked if they could cut that time in
half. Mr. Russell explained that the re-design involved many aspects of the
building and would need the time. Mr. Moriconi stated he would like to see this
accomplished by the next council meeting so that a bid could be awarded at the
November council meeting. Mr. Layman advised the extension time would not be
more than stated. Mr. Bushong asked what other savings would be involved in the
re-design. Mr. Russell stated that many components make up the square footage
costs, including lights and plumbing. He stated that he would be happy to meet
with individuals to review this in detail.
16.   Mayor Kriege commented that he feels there is no support for the current
bid documents and advised that if council did not want to proceed with the
plans, that they would need to make a decision whether to re-design a smaller
council chamber or eliminate it entirely. Mr. Bushong asked what the savings
would be. Mayor Kriege stated approximately $225,000 to reduce the size of the
building. Mr. Bushong stated that would not be enough to do other projects. Mr.
Moriconi asked if the project cost included fees and soft costs. Mr. Wendling
stated that it did not. Mr. Russell advised the council chambers could be an
add-alternate on the bid and it could be reduced in size. Mr. Dupps stated that
he was in favor of that which is directed in Amendments 811 and 812. Mr. Layman
informed council that 811 and 812 was in conjunction with 810 for a total of
$48,500 in amendments. Mr. Russell encouraged council to build as much space as
possible. Mr. Gabbard recalled the city did not build storage space in the
past, which he felt was an oversight. Mr. Dupps commented that having a lot of
storage space for large items, such as Christmas decorations was one thing, but
he did not feel it was necessary to have a lot of archival space, as electronic
storage does not require a lot of space. Mr. Moriconi expressed the desire to
put this project to rest and move forward so that construction bids could be
presented in November.
17.   Mayor Kriege recapped the options available for re-design of the
building; he stated the project could be bid as is, reduce the size of the
council chamber along with the lower level of this wing or totally eliminate
the council chamber wing. He stated that re-design fees would be necessary for
all options. Mr. Wendling advised that the courtroom where the council meetings
are currently held is approximately 1,787 square feet in size.
18.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to go with Amendments 810, 811 and 812. The
motion died for lack of a second.
19.   Mr. Bushong made a motion to approve Amendments 808, 809 and 810 for a
total of $45,250; seconded by Mr. Moriconi. Mr. Ellison asked if these would
include a council chambers wing. Mr. Russell stated these amendments would
direct the re-design of the building without a council chamber and design the
council chambers as an add-on alternate, essentially requiring two sets of
construction plan documents. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and two
no votes cast by Mr. Gabbard and Mr. Ellison. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.
Recess
20.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Ellison council took a brief
recess. Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Dupps the regular session
of the meeting resumed.
Amendment to the Agenda
21.   Mayor Kriege asked that the agenda be amended to take care of the
business of the second readings regarding the text and map amendments regarding
Mr. Dehlinger’s property at the Richardson Road area.
22.   Mr. Ellison made a motion to amend the agenda per Mayor Kriege’s request;
seconded by Mr. Dupps. Motion carried with all ayes.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-18 – Text Amendment to Add an RC-2 Zone – 2nd Reading
23.   Mayor Kriege presented for a second reading, Ordinance No. 2002-O-18 that
would enact a text amendment to the zoning ordinance, Article VIII, Section 8.0
pertaining to the establishment of zones and Article X, Section 10.19 providing
for an additional zone classification of RC-2 (Rural Commercial Two) zone and
permitted uses, Article XIV, Section 14.7 pertaining to sign regulations and
permitted use and location of signs. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
24.   Council Member Kudera moved, with second from Council Member Ellison,
that Ordinance No. 2000-O-18 be approved. Roll call was answered with five yes
votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-19 – Map Amendment Approving a Zone Change Request – 2nd
Reading
25.   Mayor Kriege presented for a second reading, Ordinance No. 2002-O-19 that
would amend the zoning map of the city changing an approximate 5.4-acre area
located at the southwest corner of the intersection of Richardson Road with Old
Richardson Road, from R-1A to RC-2. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
26.   Mr. Ellison moved, with a second by Mr. Moriconi to approve for adoption
Ordinance No. 2002-O-19. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one no
vote cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Annexing Unincorporated Territory in the Bristow &
Hogreffe Road Area – 1st Reading
27.   Mayor Kriege presented for a first reading an ordinance that would annex
and make part of the incorporated territory of the City certain unincorporated
territory lying contiguous and adjacent to the City, specifically two tracts of
lands on Bristow Road totaling approximately 32 acres. Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance and added that the owner of the property has requested
annexation by the city.
28.   Mayor Kriege opened the floor for discussion. Mr. Gabbard asked what the
property was currently zoned. Mr. Wendling advised the property is currently
zoned RCD under the county definition. Mr. Gabbard asked if it would be re-
zoned to the city classification. Mr. Wendling explained that it can be but
would not be necessary and pointed out that a portion of the recently annexed
Glenhurst Subdivision was not re-zoned to city classification. Mr. Gabbard
expressed concern that the city did not have a zone to match that zone. He
asked if the property would be used to construct homes. Mr. Wendling replied
yes. Mr. Ellison advised that Mr. Brown is willing to drop some zones. Mr. Tony
Brown, an audience participant, advised council that he is purchasing the
property from Bill Dehlinger. He stated there are thirty-two acres, which he
plans to divide into seventy-two lots. Mr. Dupps asked Mr. Brown if he had a
schematic map of the planned development. Mr. Wendling stated that he has the
plans at the city building. Mayor Kriege advised council that the Planning &
Zoning Committee has reviewed this development plan. Mr. Brown stated he plans
to construct one and two story homes on this site.
29.   Mr. Bushong expressed interest in the Hogreffe Road bridge accessing this
development. He commented on Mr. Dehlinger’s development at the intersection of
Richardson Road and Old Richardson Road and asked if the bridge on Old
Richardson Road would be used to access the development. Mr. Wendling stated
that the development would have access from the new section of Richardson Road.
Mr. Ellison commented that the bridge on Old Richardson Road is the
responsibility of the city, as it is maintained by the city.
30.   Mayor Kriege advised this ordinance would be held for a second reading at
the next regular meeting of council.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-15 Setting the Trash Collection Assessment Rate – 2nd
Reading
31.   Mayor Kriege presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2002-O-15
providing for the payment of the costs of the collection and removal of solid
waste material from residences within the city by establishing an annual
assessment charge of $100.80 upon each mobile home and residential unit.
32.   Council Member Ellison moved, with second from Council Member Bushong
that Ordinance No. 2000-O-15 be approved. Mr. Gabbard commented that no date
was noted in the ordinance regarding the years this assessment charge would be
valid. The City Clerk advised that the contract that was recently entered into
with Rumpke for the collection of waste within the city limits was for a term
of two years. She stated that the rate of $100.80 would be in effect until June
2004, so that this rate would be applicable for two years; therefore, this
ordinance would remain valid until such time that the contract is renegotiated,
making it unnecessary to note a date in the ordinance. Roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-16 Setting the Property Tax Rates for the F/Y 2002/03 –
2nd Reading
33.   Mayor Kriege presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2002-O-16
providing for the annual assessment of all real estate and personal property
within the city that is subject to taxation for the fiscal year beginning on
July 1, 2002 and ending on June 30, 2003. He stated that the real property rate
is established at .156 dollars for each one hundred dollars of assessed value
and the personal property rate is established at .317 dollars for each one
hundred dollars of assessed value. Mr. Walker read the proposed ordinance.
34.   Council Member Kudera made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2002-O-16;
seconded by Council Member Dupps. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Gabbard stated
that this is the highest increase ever seen and wanted the residents to be
aware that the established tax rates are legal. Mayor Kriege countered that the
proposed rate for real property is not the highest as it was .160/100 when he
took office. Mr. Gabbard clarified that the rate proposed (at .156/100) was the
highest increase from one year to another, than at any other time, not the
highest rate. He was concerned that the city is asking the people to pay more
than in past years. Mayor Kriege advised that the average property owner, with
a house valued at $100,000 would see a $9.00 increase this year. He explained
that that compensating rate was lowered which resulted in a significant
increase for this year. Mr. Bushong questioned if other cities had higher
rates. Mr. Gabbard stated that when you take into consideration that other
cities have a fire department, and then factor in the Independence Fire
District tax rate, the residents in Independence are paying a higher tax rate
than other cities. Mr. Kudera stated that the city’s tax rates have reduced
substantially over the years. He commented that council would need to make use
of available revenue options or forget about capital projects. Mr. Gabbard
commented that the tax rates have decreased every year but one and based on the
loss of assessed values from businesses in the Industrial Park this year, it
has cost the real estate property owners more tax dollars. He stated he just
wanted to inform the public of this. Mayor Kriege advised council that he feels
adopting the established rates of .156/100 and .317/100, which is the
compensating rate plus four percent, is the appropriate thing to do. He advised
that is a common practice for cities to take the four percent additional, and
many cities do. Roll call was taken at this time and answered with five yes
votes, with Mr. Moriconi clarifying his vote by stating for the record that he
was voting in favor of the established tax rates as he felt it was the fiscally
responsible action to take, and one no vote was cast by Mr. Gabbard. Motion
carried 5-1 in favor.

Discussion Regarding an Interlocal Agreement with Boone County Fiscal Court for
Industrial Road Improvements
41.   Mayor Kriege presented to Council, for consideration an Interlocal
Agreement with Boone County Fiscal Court that would consent to an allocation of
$234,000 to the improvements to Industrial Road. He advised that the Kentucky
Transportation Cabinet has committed up to $10,000,000 in state and federal
funds to carry out the needed improvements and that this contract would require
a total local commitment of $2,000,000. He stated that Independence’s portion
of $234,000 would be payable over a three year period (at $78,000 per year) and
due on the first of January for the next three years (2003-2004-2005). He
stated the improvements to Industrial Road would benefit all the entities
(Boone County, Kenton County, City of Elsmere, City of Florence and City of
Independence) involved. Mayor Kriege requested a motion to authorize him to
enter into this agreement.
42.   Council Member Kudera moved, with a second from Council Member Gabbard to
authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into this contract with the needed funds being
taken from the fiscal year budget over the next three years. Mr. Bushong asked
how this would benefit the city. Mayor Kriege advised that the Industrial Park
is a major tax base for the city and is a good east/west thoroughfare that is
heavily traveled. Mr. Gabbard commented that the heavy tractor-trailers have
deteriorated this road and it needs to be improved. Mr. Kudera stated that this
is a small price to pay for these major improvements. Mr. Ellison commented
that the roads are old and was not originally designed to handle this volume of
traffic. Mr. Dupps asked if the future improvements to Turkeyfoot Road have
been considered. Mayor Kriege stated that he believed it had. Mr. Dupps asked
how each entity’s share was determined. Mayor Kriege advised that each entity’s
tax base was the basis to determine shares. Mr. Wendling stated the combination
of payroll and property taxes revenue was the basis. Mayor Kriege stated this
would be a state job the engineering firm of Bayer-Becker overseeing the
project.
43.   Roll call was taken and answered with four yes votes and two no votes
cast by Mr. Bushong and Mr. Dupps. Motion carried 4-2 in favor.

Discussion Regarding an Interlocal Group Study Regarding Sexually Oriented
Businesses
68.   Mayor Kriege presented to council the idea of joining a group effort with
other local cities and Kenton County to hire an outside agency to perform a
study of the area in an effort to assist and make decisions on where sexually
oriented business zones should be located. He stated that this is definitely a
controversial issue with all communities. He advised that Independence’s share
of this study would be $3,317.33. Mr. Moriconi commented that the Supreme Court
states that the city is required to provide a place for this type of business.
He stated that the study would define sections in the local areas. Mr. Moriconi
commented that all the local cities are on board with conducting this joint
study except Boone County, who opted out. Mr. Gabbard expressed concern with
joining this group effort, only to have the recommended site for this type of
business be located in Independence. Mr. Moriconi stated that if the city
conducts a private study then we would bear the entire cost of such a study.
Mayor Kriege was concerned that the city is currently unprepared for this type
of business locating in the city. He stated that the City of Wilder was not
prepared and was unable to prohibit the business when it arrived. Mr. Dupps
stated that the city needs to be ready, and commented that the City of
Covington was recently forced to act on this issue before the study was
completed. Mr. Ellison commented that addressing this matter is going to be a
challenge for the city and felt it would be more cost effective to be involved
in a group study. Mr. Wendling stated that if the city does not join the group
study then we would have no influence and the zone may well end up in our city.
Mayor Kriege stated that he recommends the city join this group study. Mr.
Gabbard asked where the funds would be taken to pay the city’s share. Mayor
Kriege stated he would review the budget.
69.   Mr. Ellison moved, with a second by Mr. Moriconi to join an interlocal
agreement for the study of sexually explicit zones in the area, with the cost
submitted at the next council meeting for a decision by council. Further
discussion ensued. Mr. Gabbard expressed his concerns. Mayor Kriege emphasized
the need to be a part of this study and see what the recommendation will be.
Mr. Bushong stated it will take three months to conduct this study and that an
ordinance format will be presented to each entity for adoption. Mr. Gabbard
stated that he felt the city should continue to look at this issue in the
interim even if we do participate in the joint study. Mr. Moriconi stated the
study would involve visits to every city in order to designate a site in each
city. Mr. Walker advised that he is of the understanding that every city will
not have a zone because of the definition of “community”, but did caution that
he feels Independence is at great risk of having an area in the city getting
this zone designation, mainly due to the size of the city and available green
space. He stated that Independence might be sidestepped if a zone is
recommended for South Covington or Taylor Mill. He stated that in other areas
of the state, such as Louisville, these types of businesses have been located
in the industrial zones where people work during the day and do not live in the
area. Mr. Dupps stated the city should join the study. At this time roll call
was taken and answered unanimously in favor.
Adjournment
70.   Upon motion by Mr. Bushong and second by Mr. Gabbard the meeting was
adjourned with unanimous approval of council, the time being 10:26 p.m.

OCTOBER 7, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Thomas M. Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Rev. Lisa May of Staffordsburg United Methodist Church
gave the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike
Gabbard, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also present was
City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 9, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mr. Dupps made a motion to approve the minutes of the regular council
meeting of September 9, 2002, seconded by Mr. Bushong. Regarding the suggestion
and ensuing motion by Mr. Ellison to retain one of the surplus police cruisers,
Mr. Ellison asserted that his intent was for that vehicle to be used
exclusively by Nita Brake, having all the privileges of a take home vehicle. He
requested that this be made clear in the minutes. Mayor Kriege stated that he
understood Mr. Ellison’s motion to declare the vehicle as a pool car. He stated
that take home vehicles should be for employees that are on-call for emergency
situations and recreation does not fall under this purpose. Mr. Gabbard
concurred with Mr. Ellison and stated that he thought Ms. Brake would have
exclusive use of the spare vehicle. After a brief discussion, Mayor Kriege
advised Mr. Ellison that he could re-address this matter later in the meeting
under old business. Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Dupps brought forth other amendments.
The amendments were noted and roll call was answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0 to approve the council minutes as amended.
Presentation of the 2001/02 Audit by Linda Chapman of Rankin, Rankin & Company
3.   Mayor Kriege introduced Ms. Linda Chapman of Rankin, Rankin and Company
who performed the audit of the city’s financial records for the year ending
June 30, 2002. He informed council that Ms. Chapman had met with the Budget &
Finance Committee to review the audit results and is here to present the
findings to the full council.
4.   Ms. Chapman distributed the presentation package of the audit and reviewed
the highlights with council. She reported that the city saw a cash decrease of
$598,000 due to general operations during the last fiscal year. She stated that
the investments increased by $4,700,000 due to the $5,000,000 loan proceeds for
the Municipal Center Fund and advised that as the money is spent on the project
that investment will decrease. Ms. Chapman indicated that the general fixed
assets, a GASB accrual requirement, is noted at $3,112,828, an increase of
$1,029,192. She reported that the city had a $192,207 decrease in
intergovernmental revenues because the grants for the Senior Center and the
COPS (Community Oriented Policing) expired. She also stated that the total
liabilities line increased from $7,500,000 to $12,100,000 due to the completion
of the Senior Center. She stated that the fund equity balance was inflated this
year due to the $5,000,000 municipal center loan proceeds, a temporary
condition that will decrease to a more normal level as the loan proceeds are
spent. Ms. Chapman advised that the overall revenues decreased 5% due to the
close of the Senior Center grant; in addition the city lost 49% of interest
income. She advised that the 2001 expenditures of $4,746,000 increased to
$5,655,000 in 2002 with capital expenses going from $871,000 to $1,244,000. She
stated the increase in capital expenditures was due to the three outstanding
leases on police vehicles and the first full year of mortgage payments on the
Senior Center. She advised that other losses included the $405,000 in general
funds, $633,000 funds transferred out of the general fund (due to the Senior
Center and Street repairs) and a loss of $117,000 in Municipal Road Fund
revenue. She stated that it is not unusual to see this type of loss for the
road fund.
5.   Ms. Chapman reported that the revenues were largely from real estate taxes
(55%), with 24% coming from charges for services and the remainder of the
revenue coming from grants. She stated that the debt service expenses are
creeping up mainly due to the additional leases taken out. The general fund
loss was anticipated to be $351,000 with the actual figure being $405,000.
Special revenues were anticipated to be $240,000 and actual was $123,000; debt
service funds were anticipated to be $151,000 with the actual being $235,000;
and, capital funds anticipated at $438,000 and the actual being $4,355,000 due
to the lease proceeds. Ms. Chapman explained that many of the variances were
attributed to the car leases and Senior Center expenses and municipal lease
proceeds.
6.   Mr. Gabbard questioned the notation on page 23 of the audit report
regarding compliance. Ms. Chapman stated that this is a repeat comment from
last year’s audit. She explained that the $210,000 lease obtained with Fifth
Third Bank for the purchase of police cruisers was money that was not
physically run through the city’s books. She stated that the bank holds the
funds until the vehicles are ready for delivery and when the bank obtains the
invoice from the car dealer, the bank issues a cashier’s check from a special
account set up to house the lease funds. She stated that this practice by the
bank results in the expense not showing up on the city’s financial records.
7.   Mr. Gabbard asked Ms. Chapman how long the city could make the payments on
the loans obtained for the Senior Center and Municipal Center at the current
level of revenue. Ms. Chapman replied that at the current rate of transfers-out
of the excess funds, that she would guesstimate 3-5 years, but emphasized that
is without crunching the numbers. Mr. Gabbard asked if a tax increase would be
necessary. Ms. Chapman stated that finding a revenue source or cutting expenses
could be a course of action.
8.   Mayor Kriege commented that the fund balance has grown over $500,000 and
feels the city needs to recognize the growth along with other factors that
could be considered. Ms. Chapman stated she was basing her response on the
current year results. Mr. Gabbard commented that the spurt of current
residential construction is not bringing in adequate revenue. He stated he had
reservations about paying off the debt on the Senior Center since the interest
rate is so low, at 4.16%. Ms. Chapman stated it could be an option and might
afford more concentration in reducing the debt on the $5,000,00 loan for the
municipal center.
9.   Mr. Bushong asked where the sewer fund balance was noted in the audit. Ms.
Chapman stated the sewer debt service funds were on page 19 of the full audit.
She stated the ending fund balance at June 30, 2002 was $1,194,450.
10.   There being no further questions or discussion, Mayor Kriege requested a
motion to approve the audit as presented. Mr. Bushong moved with second by Mr.
Moriconi to accept the audit for the year ending June 30, 2002 as presented.
Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
11.   Thelma and Robert Gibson, 5123 Madison Pike addressed council regarding a
letter they received from the city about property they own at 5190 Madison
Pike. Mrs. Gibson stated that the house is rental property, has not been
abandoned and there is no rubbish on the property. She stated the roof has been
repaired and they are aware the house is in need of additional repairs and are
trying to rectify the condition. She stated that this property was jointly
owned but have recently bought out the other owner and are currently the sole
owner of the property. She reported that they had made a down payment with a
contractor to do some renovations and the contractor did nothing, so they are
trying to recover this loss in small claims court. Mrs. Gibson stated that they
have met with the City Administrator and the Planning & Zoning Committee to
discuss their proposal to demolish the current house and build a two-family
house. She said there are two sewer taps on the property. She advised that they
have discussed their plans to construct a duplex with the adjoining neighbors
and did not receive any negative comments from them. Mrs. Gibson stated that
she has since heard that a neighbor has come before council to make a complaint
regarding the condition of the property. She also commented that the county has
increased the assessed value – from $40,000 to $60,000. Mrs. Gibson requested
council to grant an extension of 120 days to comply with this zoning violation
in order to arrange for the removal of the house from the property.
12.   Mr. Gabbard commented that he did not have a problem with Mrs. Gibson’s
request. Mrs. Gibson stated she has spoken individually with some of the
council members, whom also stated they had no problem with this request. She
stated that they are not slum landlords and feels if given time they could
build a new structure.
13.   Mayor Kriege advised that the Gibson’s would need to apply for a zone
change in order to build a two family structure in a single residential zone.
Mrs. Gibson stated she is aware of that, but has been informed that the final
approval for a duplex will be decided by the city council.
14.   Mrs. Gibson advised that her attorney has responded to the Building
Inspector’s letter regarding the zoning violation and to date has not received
a response. Mayor Kriege asked if the building was secure. She stated that it
is. Mayor Kriege asked Mrs. Gibson what alternate plans she had if the zone
change was denied. Mr. Gibson replied they would consider two smaller houses on
fifty-foot lots. Mr. Moriconi asked the Gibson’s if they had considered selling
the property. Mrs. Gibson stated that they had the property up for sale in the
past, but that it took some time to buy out the other owner. She stated that
they also have not been able to get good renters for this four-room house.
15.   Mr. Moriconi asked if they had received notice from the Property
Valuation Assessor’s office regarding the increase in assessment. Mrs. Gibson
stated they had not. Mr. Moriconi stated that he did not have an objection to
the demolition of the current building but inquired why they wanted to build a
duplex near single-family homes. She stated this would not be the usual square
duplex but a nice design.
16.   Mayor Kriege stated that the Building Inspector is willing to grant the
Gibson’s an extension to comply with this zoning violation, but has expressed
some concern regarding existing liabilities and has spoken to the City Attorney
regarding this. Mr. Wendling stated that the current state of the building
presents safety problems for future tenants. Mr. Bushong questioned the city’s
liability if a 120-day extension is granted. Mr. Walker advised that the city
is obligated to see that buildings are safe and inhabitable and determine if
the condition is dangerous or just an attractive nuisance, nevertheless, the
city’s liability would be secondary to that of the property owners. Mrs. Gibson
stated that the interior of the house is in no condition to be lived-in, but
felt the exterior was not any worse than others in the area.
17.   Mayor Kriege asked council if there were any objections to granting the
Gibson’s a 120-day extension. Upon motion by Mr. Gabbard and second by Mr.
Bushong a 120-day extension was granted to the Gibson’s to demolish the house
located at 5190 Madison Pike. Roll call was answered unanimously and the motion
carried 6-0 in favor. Mr. Kudera advised the Gibson’s that this extension does
not assure approval of a zone change for the duplex that they wish to build on
this site. He stated that they would need to go through the process and should
not assume the council will approve the zone change.
Ordinance No. 2002-O-20 – Annexing 2 Tracts (32.5 Acres) of Land in the Bristow
Rd/Hogreffe Rd Area

Proposed Ordinance Regarding the Pre-Submission of Subdivision Site Plans
21.   Mayor Kriege presented for a second reading an ordinance that would
establish a procedure for the submission and review of preliminary plats and
other matters that would be subject to approval by the Kenton County and
Municipal Planning and Zoning Commission. Mr. Walker read the proposed
ordinance and advised council that this ordinance would just formalize what the
Planning & Zoning Commission does. Mr. Kudera asked if this ordinance would be
enforceable, as it seems to him that this is redundant and impractical, as the
city already has the right to deny or approve development plans. Mr. Gabbard
stated that the city does not always have all the necessary information to make
the decisions, as most of council does not attend the public hearings held by
the Planning Commission. Mayor Kriege stated that council can attend those
meetings or choose to have a separate public hearing within the given time
period. He stated that the city’s Planning & Zoning Committee currently reviews
plans when they meet with the developers. Mr. Gabbard referred to a recent
development, which revealed many things, but not all the details needed for
council to make a good decision. Mr. Walker commented that this ordinance is
‘extra statutory’, adding to the process developers currently follow. He
advised that state statutes define the process for the developers and, in his
opinion; the city would not be able to stop a development if the developer has
acted in accordance with KRS. Mr. Gabbard stated that he felt it was worth the
effort. Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Walker if other cities have adopted similar
ordinances. He stated he did not know.
22.   Mr. Gabbard moved, with second by Mr. Ellison to adopt the proposed
ordinance to establish a procedure for pre-submission of subdivision site
plans. Roll call was answered with three yes votes and three no votes cast by
Mr. Kudera, Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Bushong. Mayor Kriege broke the tie vote by
casting a no vote, stating that he felt this legislation was unnecessary. The
proposed ordinance was defeated by a 4-3 vote.
Discussion Regarding Regal Ridge Drive – Steve Powell of Powell Homes
23.   Mr. Steve Powell addressed council regarding his plans to construct
thirteen single-family homes on Regal Ridge Drive. He informed council that the
Planning Commission has approved his plan with the stipulation that the street
be improved to meet subdivision standards. He stated that he assumed Regal
Ridge Drive was a city maintained street but has since learned that it is a
public dedicated right of way. He stated that he is here to seek assurance from
the council that the city will accept the street for maintenance, before he
makes the investment in upgrades to this road. He stated that this is not a
through street as it dead-ends into the Regal Ridge Apartment complex. He
advised the street is 1600 feet long and that the city currently maintains 143
feet. Mr. Dupps asked what the property is currently zoned. Mr. Powell stated
the property is R-1D. Mr. Ellison asked about the storm water drainage. Mr.
Powell responded that this is not a concern as there are two lateral lines
across the street and a ditch line. He assured council that everything has been
approved and in order with the Planning Commission and he plans to have the
road improvements completed in November. Mr. Gabbard expressed concern that
Area Planning (NKAP) does not have sufficient staff to oversee the road pours.
Mr. Moriconi asked if the street would be concrete or asphalt. Mr. Ellison
asked if the homes would be built first then the street poured. Mr. Powell
advised the street would be constructed of asphalt, and he would delay the
topcoat, until heavy equipment construction is complete. He stated that it
would take 2-3 years to finish the home building, mostly single story houses
ranging in price from $130,000 to $180,000. Mr. Kudera asked if the hillside
slippage was part of the development plans. Mr. Powell stated it was not.
24.   Mr. Gabbard moved, with second by Mr. Ellison to accept Regal Ridge Drive
for street maintenance after the improvements are complete and have been
approved. Roll call was answered unanimously with the motion carrying 6-0 in
favor.

fund revenue to pay down the sewer debt. Roll call was answered with four yes

favor.
