NOVEMBER 11, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Tom Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Council Members Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera
and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Council Member Jim Bushong was absent.
Also in attendance was attorney Jeffrey S. Smith sitting in for his associate,
City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
2.   Mayor Kriege stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   New Municipal Center
∙   Memorial Park Development Plan
∙   Scherry Avenue
∙   Ordinance No. 2-12-78 and the annexation of land in the Madison Pike area
as it relates to property owned by Karen and Greg Lipscomb and John Schoborg
∙   Fowler Creek Sewer Debt and Pay-off Options
∙   Executive Session
∙   Police Department School Resource Officer
∙   Zone Change on Cox Road
Discussion Regarding the New Municipal Center
3.   Mayor Kriege introduced Mr. Scott Layman of Cole+Russell Architects. Mr.
Layman presented to council for their review the Notice to Bidders
advertisement for bids for the construction of the new municipal center. He
stated the bid document would request a base bid and three alternate bids. The
three alternate bids are for a clock tower, storm water detention basin and
removal of the council chamber wing.
4.   Mr. Gabbard inquired about the removal of storage space. Mr. Layman stated
the reduced floor plan would result in the loss of storage rooms in the
alternate bid that removes the council chamber wing. Mr. Gabbard stated this is
not reflected in the notes. Mr. Layman advised that removal of the council
chamber would delete storage space on both floors. Mr. Ellison asked if the bid
specs contained a provision to add on the council chamber wing in the future.
Mr. Laymen stated that the council could decide when the bids come in whether
or not to delete that alternate bid.
5.   Mr. Moriconi inquired about the DD comparison column noted on the Opinion
of Probable Construction Costs document dated November 7, 2002. Mr. Layman
advised that this design development comparison was a gauge for evaluation
purposes only. Mr. Moriconi asked if the DD comparison changed any after the
project was pared back. Mr. Layman stated that it defines the construction
documents as designed and it was further refined.
6.   Mayor Kriege requested authorization from the council to advertise the
Notice to Bidders advertisement as presented. Mr. Wendling stated that the pre-
bid meeting noted in the advertisement would be changed to December 3, 2002
instead of November 29, 2002.
7.   Upon motion by Council Member Moriconi and second by Council Member
Kudera, council authorized the advertisement of the Notice to Bidders as
presented for the construction of the new municipal center. Roll call was
answered with four yes votes and one no vote cast by Mr. Ellison. Motion
carried 4-1 in favor.
Discussion Regarding the Memorial Park Development Plan
8.   Mayor Kriege introduced Ehmet Hayes of the architect firm of Robert Ehmet
Hayes & Associates. Mr. Hayes proposed taking a global look at the Memorial
Park Master Plan by creating a development plan that would provide more
detailed information as far as location of the pieces and their projected
costs. He stated the development plan would put a value on the components and
develop a sequence for the project. He stated that he is aware the city
currently has money set aside for the construction of an amphitheater and that
part of his proposal would be to provide information as to what type of
amphitheater could be constructed with the available monies, as well as the
addition of associated access roads. Mr. Hayes stated the plan would also
prioritize key features of the development of the park. Mr. Hayes stated the
proposed fee for this service would be $8,000 and advised that his firm could
have a preliminary development plan ready for initial review around the end of
December.
9.   Mayor Kriege stated that with the available funds set aside for the
amphitheater, a development plan would provide for a way to phase in this
aspect of the park.
10.   Council member Kudera made a motion to approve the fee of $8,000 to
contract with the architect firm of Robert Ehmet Hayes & Associates to design a
development plan for Memorial Park. Council Member Moriconi seconded the
motion. Mr. Dupps asked how the Master Plan developed by Matrix Architects
would tie into this plan proposed by Mr. Hayes. Mayor Kriege advised that the
Master Plan outlined a design for the park but did not provide cost projections
or phasing in the various features. He stated that the service proposed by
Hayes & Associates would bring the two together and identify cost amounts for
the key features. Mayor Kriege commented that the Matrix plan had good points
and the design would not be discarded, nor would Mr. Hayes’ proposal be a
reproduction. Mr. Hayes commented that his proposal would provide the city with
more detail on how to accomplish the design in the master plan by Matrix. Mr.
Ellison asked where the funds would be pulled from the budget to finance this
development plan. Mr. Wendling stated the expense could come from the Memorial
Park account. Roll call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 5-0 in
favor.
Discussion Regarding The Early Pay-Off of the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt
11.   Mayor Kriege announced that if no one had any objections that he would
like to move the discussion regarding the Fowler Creek Debt Repayment up on the
agenda. No one voiced objection to this request. Mayor Kriege introduced Janet
Rebman, Finance Director who presented detailed information regarding this
debt.
12.   Ms. Rebman stated that in response to the discussion at the last council
meeting she has prepared payoff schedules for council’s review. She stated that
on the Schedule I, Description of the Bonds, there is a penalty for early
payment anytime before December 1, 2010. Schedule II, indicates the annual due
date of the principal and interest. She stated the city still owes $5,000,000
at this time. Ms. Rebman stated that Schedule III, Fowler Creek Debt Repayment,
shows a projected fund balance for the two funds (General Sewer and Fowler
Creek Sewer) and indicates a $1,200,000 combined balance. She stated that
projecting the fund balance over a nine-year period would yield an estimated
$4,620,891 in the year 2011; enough to repay the entire balance of this debt at
that time. She commented that 4% is a very small interest growth.
13.   Mr. Gabbard commented that he hopes that Ms. Rebman was conservative in
her estimations and that here calculations are accurate. Mayor Kriege commented
that this fund should be tagged with the bank so that the city does not forget
that the intent is to completely pay off this debt in 2010. Ms. Rebman stated
she has spoken with the bank representative regarding this and they are
agreeable. Mr. Wendling commented that the accumulated fund balance would also
be available for emergency sewer repairs. Ms. Rebman stated that the city would
save $1,500,000 in interest by paying this debt in full by 2010. Mr. Kudera
stated that he agrees with Ms. Rebman’s calculations and feels this repayment
schedule is a good process for the city. Mayor Kriege stated that this bond
being issued in 1998 with the intent of taking 25 years to pay off would now be
repaid in thirteen years. Mr. Kudera commented that this projection will now
give the residents some hope that this debt will be retired much sooner than
the anticipated 25 years.
Discussion Regarding Scherry Avenue
14.   Mr. Glenn Ellison addressed council with a request for a letter of
acceptance on the paving and extension of Scherry Avenue. He distributed maps
of the street for council to review. Mr. Wendling provided some background
information regarding Scherry Avenue and stated that when this street was
platted in the 1980’s it was not built according to subdivision codes and the
road veers onto the right of way and private property. He stated that Mr.
Ellison has purchased a few lots with plans to construct single-family houses.
He advised that this matter has been discussed at the Planning & Zoning
Committee and he has met with Mr. Glenn Ellison, as well as the City Engineer,
several times regarding Mr. Ellison’s plans to construct the houses on this
street and his extension of the street to access the new houses. He stated that
Mr. Ellison installed the new section of Scherry Avenue before receiving
approval from the Planning Commission and that the new section does not meet
subdivision code. Mayor Kriege advised council that the Planning Commission
would not approve this street until the city advises them that it will be
accepted for city maintenance. Mr. Glenn Ellison stated that he could have
constructed only half of the road but decided to go down further. City
Engineer, Dave Whitacre, commented that although the newly paved section does
not meet subdivision code, it does meet the required thickness and strength and
is better than what was there.
15.   Council Member Ellison commented that it has been built to the same
standards and that Mr. Ellison agreed to remove the old pavement if the city
pays half the costs. Mr. Moriconi asked if the city should accept the newly
paved section of road. Council Member Ellison stated that he thinks the city
should accept the road for maintenance, as there is not much traffic in this
area with only a few homes. He stated the city should send a letter to the
Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission informing them the city would accept
this street for maintenance. He added that the problem for the city is to
decide whether to split the cost with the residents for removal of the old
section of the street. Mr. Dupps voiced concern that access for emergency
vehicles would be difficult and was concerned that this could be a safety
issue. Mayor Kriege stated that access for police vehicles should not be a
problem. Mr. Kudera stated that this street is no different from the various
other narrow streets throughout the city. Mr. Moriconi commented that this
street has a turn around area, which many streets do not have. Mr. Dupps
suggested ‘no parking’ signs be installed. Mayor Kriege stated this would be
addressed. Mr. Whitacre commented that because the street is only sixteen feet
wide, parking on either side should be prohibited.
16.   Council Member Ellison made a motion to accept Scherry Avenue as
constructed and that the city should inform the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission of this acceptance. Mr. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered unanimously; motion carried 5-0 in favor.
17.   Mayor Kriege addressed the other issue regarding Scherry Avenue, that
being the removal of the old section of the road and who should absorb this
cost. Two residents of Scherry Avenue were present to speak to this. Mr.
Richard Miller, 645 Marilyn requested that the old section of the street be
removed from his land, but wanted to be assured that the area would be covered
with seed and straw. Mr. Wendling stated that Riegler Paving has quoted a price
of $4,000 to remove the old section of roadway and Mr. Glenn Ellison has agreed
to split this cost with the city. Mr. Alvin Gibson, 764 Scherry Avenue, stated
he would like to see the section removed but then his access will be
terminated. Council Member Ellison stated that he was agreeable to splitting
the cost with Mr. Ellison. Mr. Moriconi asked if Mr. Gibson would be provided
with a new driveway. Mr. Whitacre advised that the paving of a new drive would
be at the expense of the residents, as the quote given by Riegler Paving was
for paving, a new culvert and hauling in dirt. The quote did not include
seeding and straw. Mr. Moriconi asked who has been maintaining the old Scherry
Avenue. Mr. Wendling stated that the street was a prescribed easement and has
been maintained by either the city and/or county for the last forty years. Mr.
Kudera asked how the maintenance situation of Justice Lane differed from this
street. Council Member Ellison stated that Justice Lane is not a dedicated
right of way and Scherry Avenue is a platted city street. Mr. Whitacre
concurred and added that Scherry Avenue is a platted right of way.
18.   Council Member Ellison asked how the cost would be split: Riegler Paving
and the City or Glenn Ellison and Riegler Paving. Mr. Kudera stated that he
felt the property owners should share a portion of this expense, as it will
improve their property. One of the residents stated that this was a mistake
made by the city when the road was placed on his property. Mr. Kudera
maintained that the city was making a generous offer and many residents would
like the city to pay for this kind of improvement.
19.   Council Member Ellison made a motion to share the cost (50/50) of
correcting the alignment of Scherry Avenue with Mr. Glenn Ellison, with the
residents absorbing the cost for seed and straw as this is not a part of the
quote by Riegler Paving. Mr. Gabbard seconded the motion. Roll call was
answered with three ayes and two nays cast by Mr. Kudera and Mr. Dupps. Motion
carried 3-2 in favor.
Discussion Regarding Ordinance No. 2-12-78 Annexation of Madison Pike Area As
it Relates to the Property Owned by Karen & Greg Lipscomb and John Schoborg
20.   Ms. Karen Schoborg Lipscomb addressed council regarding property tax
bills that she has been receiving each year for property she owns on Madison
Pike. She stated that this property is not in the city limits and that she is
receiving these bills in error since 1997. She stated that she has spoken with
the City Clerk, as well as Council Members Gabbard and Ellison. She stated she
has also discussed this with the Area Planning Commission who has told her the
annexation lines were drawn in error. She stated that the council members
assured her that the property is not in the city limits. She stated she wants
to be a good citizen and pay her taxes but would like this matter resolved.
21.   Mr. Kudera asked what the city could do. Mr. Smith, City Attorney, stated
that this is the first formal presentation regarding the matter before city
council. He stated he is not sure what has come about from Ms. Lipscomb’s
discussions with Area Planning. Council Member Ellison stated that several of
the Area Planning staff members are familiar with this matter and have
concurred that the lines were drawn in error and they want official word from
the city to correct this map. He stated that he feels the correction should be
made and allow the Lipscomb’s to pay the correct amount of taxes due the city.
Ms. Lipscomb stated she has been informed that the city has to make the
correction. Mr. Smith stated he has conducted some research into this matter
and has learned that an annexation ordinance cannot be corrected by a municipal
order. Ms. Lipscomb insisted that her property has not been annexed. Mr.
Ellison also agreed that it is not an annexation problem, but a simple matter
of correcting the line drawn on the map. Mr. Ellison and Ms. Lipscomb recalled
when Norb Schoborg spoke to the city prior to 1997 regarding this mapping
error.
22.   Mr. Gabbard stated he has spoken to Mike Schwartz of the Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission regarding this property, which is 150 feet
east of Madison Pike (Route 17). Mr. Ellison stated the city should get the
line corrected and refund any monies owed to the property owners. City
Engineer, Dave Whitacre advised that prior to 1978 the front section of this
property already existed within the city limits.
23.   Mayor Kriege directed Mr. Whitacre, Mr. Ellison and Mr. Smith to work on
resolving this matter and bring a recommendation to council next month.
Executive Session
24.   Mayor Kriege requested a motion to enter into executive session. Upon
motion by Mr. Gabbard and second by Mr. Dupps the council went into executive
session in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) and 61.810 (f) for the purpose of
discussing pending litigation and an employee contract, respectively. Motion
carried unanimously.
25.   Upon motion by Mr. Kudera and second by Mr. Ellison the council resumed
the open session of the council meeting. Motion carried unanimously.
Discussion Regarding the Hiring of a School Resource Police Officer
26.   A motion was made by Mr. Moriconi and seconded by Mr. Kudera to authorize
the Mayor to enter into a contract for the hiring of a school resource officer
for the Police Department. Mr. Ellison asked if this officer would be provided
a take home cruiser, as contract employees are not normally provided a vehicle.
Chief Shawn Butler stated that the department would provide this contract
employee an older cruiser (1995) that was retained for this purpose. He stated
that he feels it is a good thing to have a cruiser parked in the front of the
school building. Roll call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 5-
0 in favor.
Discussion of the Property Located at the corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill
Road – Zone Change Request by Scheben Development – 1st Reading of the Zone
Change Ordinance
27.   Mr. Moriconi made a motion to have a first reading of a proposed
ordinance that would grant a zone change for the property located at the corner
of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road with the three conditions recommended by the
Kenton County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission as well as a city
imposed requirement that sewer lines be made accessible to the residents on
Jimae. Mr. Kudera seconded the motion. Mr. Jeff Smith read the proposed
ordinance. Mayor Kriege stated this ordinance would be presented at the next
meeting for a second reading and vote and asked that the motions be withdrawn.
Mr. Moriconi and Mr. Kudera moved and seconded to withdrawn the motion on the
floor.
Adjournment
28.   Upon motion by Mr. Ellison and second by Mr. Gabbard the meeting was
adjourned. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting ended at 9:00 p.m.

DECEMBER 2, 2002
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   Mayor Thomas M. Kriege called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence Christian
Church gave the invocation. Council Members Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim
Ellison, Ike Gabbard, Jim Kudera and Chris Moriconi answered roll call. Also
present was City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker and City Administrator, Mark T.
Wendling.
Approval of the Minutes of the October 7, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Council Member Dupps moved, with a second by Council Member Bushong to
approve the minutes of the October 7, 2002 council meeting. Council Member
Kudera suggested that Mr. Gabbard’s statement on page two, paragraph seven
regarding the audit be deleted as he feels the question posed to the auditor by
Mr. Gabbard was for political reasons and was not part of the financial audit
of city records. Mr. Gabbard countered that he was asking for the auditor’s
opinion as to whether she felt a tax increase would be necessary. Mayor Kriege
advised that the minutes of a meeting is a synopsis of the dialogue that took
place. Mr. Kudera voiced his disapproval of the question that was asked of the
auditor and maintained that it should be stricken from the minutes. Mayor
Kriege advised that it could be stricken if council so chooses. Council took no
action to amend paragraph seven as recommended by Mr. Kudera.
3.   Mr. Ellison asked that paragraph thirty on page five reflect that the
zoning violation he reported in the Beechgrove Shopping Center was a trailer
‘type sign’, not a trailer. The change was noted. Mr. Ellison advised that the
situation still exists, as the sign has not been removed. Mr. Bushong stated
that the owner has a sign permit issued by the city’s Building Inspector. Mayor
Kriege advised that this matter would be reviewed.
4.   No roll call was taken; the motion to approve the minutes as amended
carried with all ayes.
Approval of the Minutes of the November 11, 2002 Special Council Meeting
5.   Council Member Kudera moved to approve the minutes of the November 11,
2002 special meeting, seconded by Council Member Moriconi. There were no
suggested amendments. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Privileges of the Floor
6.   Mr. Doug Eppenson, 5277 Cody Road, addressed council regarding the burning
of brush on Cody Road in the area of the Troopers Crossing Subdivision. He
complained that it is foul smelling. Mayor Kriege stated the city would contact
those responsible for the burning to get this matter resolved.
Update Regarding the Lipscomb/Schoborg Annexation Dispute
7.   City Attorney, H. Lawson Walker reported to council on his findings
regarding the 1978 ordinance that annexed properties along Madison Pike. He
advised that he believes the property in question has been legally annexed even
though some residents have contended over the last several years that their
property was never annexed. He stated the Planning Commission has drawn the
maps in accordance with the description in this ordinance and has published the
maps for more than twenty years. Mr. Walker addressed the suggestion by those
who think the problem can be resolved by simply switching one parcel for
another by advising that it would leave the city with no contiguous nature.
Mayor Kriege suggested annexing the right of way to keep the city contiguous.
Mr. Walker advised council to have the city engineer assess the situation and
bring a recommendation (s) on how to keep the city contiguous. Mr. Ellison
stated the ordinance was intended to annex 150 feet east of Madison Pike. Mr.
Walker stated that the description in the ordinance is the basis of the maps
drawn by the Planning Commission. He stated that if the property owners want
out of the city and the council agrees to that, a de-annexation process could
take place, but the city engineer would have to research ways to keep the city
contiguous prior to approving and beginning a de-annexation process.
8.   Mayor Kriege requested a vote from council on how to proceed with this
matter. Mr. Kudera stated that he felt this was not a course of action for
council and that it is up to the property owners to decide whether or not they
want to pursue this matter legally. Mr. Bushong asked how many residents were
affected. Mr. Wendling stated two. Mr. Gabbard suggested the council direct the
city engineer to research this and bring a recommendation to the new council
members that take office in January. Mr. Moriconi asked if a de-annexation
matter would have to be placed on the general election ballot. Mr. Walker
stated that it would not. Mr. Gabbard asked how far up Madison Pike was
involved. Mr. Walker stated that three lots were affected.
9.   Mr. Gabbard made a motion to authorize the city engineer to research ways
to de-annex the properties involved for the incoming council to take action on.
Mr. Ellison seconded the motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Dupps stated
that he did not feel this was necessary at this time, as he feels someone other
than the city should take the next step. Mr. Kudera concurred with Mr. Dupps.
Mr. Bushong stated that he felt that too much effort and valuable time would be
expended for two property owners. Mr. Moriconi asked when the residents first
approached the city. Mayor Kriege stated the residents have been disputing this
annexation for several years, but just last month brought the issue to the
council floor. Mr. Ellison stated the residents have been dealing with the city
office.
10.   Roll call on Mr. Gabbard’s motion and Mr. Ellison’s second was answered
with two yes votes and four no votes cast by Mr. Kudera, Mr. Moriconi, Mr.
Bushong and Mr. Dupps. Motion failed.
11.   Mayor Kriege stated that the city would notify the Lipscomb’s regarding
council’s decision to take no action regarding their dispute over this
annexation of their property in 1978.
Revised Interlocal Agreement for Improvements to Industrial Road
12.   Mayor Kriege presented to council for their approval a revised interlocal
agreement between the Counties of Boone and Kenton and the Cities of Elsmere,
Florence and Independence for the improvements to Industrial Road. He advised
that the date of the last installment payment for this project has been
changed.
13.   Mr. Wendling stated that in the previously approved agreement the final
payment is payable January 1, 2005. He stated that the final payment date has
been changed to July 31, 2004 at the request of the Boone County Fiscal Court
due to concerns that if construction begins next year and the final payment is
not received until January 2005, the county will not have sufficient local
funds to match the federal dollars on a timely basis. He advised council that
the final payment will still be taken from the same fiscal year as the original
agreement. Mr. Gabbard asked why this wasn’t a consideration before now. Mr.
Wendling stated that he did not know.
14.   Council Member Kudera moved and Council Member Moriconi made the second
to approve the revised Interlocal Agreement for the Improvements to Industrial
Road. Mr. Dupps expressed concern that the City of Florence was paying the
lowest percentage for this project than the other governmental bodies. Mr.
Wendling advised that the financial allocations were based on taxable income
from the Industrial Park and that the City of Florence had the lowest taxable
income. He stated that the majority of the Industrial Park businesses are
located in Boone and Kenton counties. Roll call was taken and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zone Change for Property located at Cox and
Taylor Mill Rds.
15.   Mayor Kriege acknowledge the residents in the audience who wished to
speak to council regarding the matter of the zone change requested by the
Scheben Group for property located at the corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill
Road.
16.   Mr. William Ruzinok, 6394 Jimae Court, shared with council his
disapproval of the Scheben Group’s plan to construct a three-story, 96-unit
condominium at this location. He provided council with a detailed history of
past development proposals for this property and the type of plans the
residents in the area feel would not be appropriate. He stated he doesn’t want
a development that would lower the resident’s property values or standard of
living. Mr. Ruzinok stated that Cherokee Bowl and the Regal Ridge Apartment
complex were bad developments for the area. He questioned the benefit this type
of development would provide the city and the residents, and the necessity of a
96 unit building on this corner, surrounded by residential, single family
homes. He stated he sees no advantages and fears this proposed development will
not have an adequate buffer zone and will ruin the neighborhood.
17.   Mr. Eric Thomas, 6406 Jimae Ct., advised that of the nine homes on Jimae,
that three have recently installed new septic systems, leaving only six
residents that might take advantage of tapping into the nearby sewer line that
this development would provide. He urged council to keep this property zone
single family residential.
18.   Mayor Kriege asked Mr. Jerry Dusing, legal counsel for the Scheben Group,
if he wished to address the residents’ concerns. Mr. Dusing stated it would be
inappropriate for him to debate this matter with the residents considering this
matter is being contested to settle a lawsuit. He did say that one of the main
attractions to this development was that the trees on the property would be
preserved and the plan would be very upscale. Mr. Gabbard commented that Mr.
Jim Berling had indicated that another entrance to the development could be
installed on Route 16. Mr. Berling advised that he would be agreeable to that
condition subject to approval from the State Highway Department with the
procurement of an encroachment permit. Mr. Moriconi asked Mr. Dusing if other
development options, other than the proposed condominiums, are being
considered. Mr. Dusing advised that Scheben had looked at possibly constructing
single-family detached dwellings but decided it was not an option. He added
that the city had suggested a commercial development, but advised that would
require his client to begin a whole new application process with the Kenton
County & Municipal Planning & Zoning Commission, with the possibility that such
a plan would be denied by the Commission. Mr. Moriconi asked if they had
considered patio homes. Mr. Berling replied no.
19.   Ms. Gail Wallace, 6396 Jimae Court, stated that she has lived at this
residence for twenty years and that her property abuts this proposed
development. She stated that previously when development plans were proposed
for the Cox Road/Taylor Mill Road location the adjoining residents were
notified. She expressed concern that this time the residents were not notified
and that she read about it in the newspaper. She stated that she disliked the
idea of looking out her rear window at a monstrous three-story building and
expressed concerns regarding storm water drainage. Ms. Wallace stated that she
was not totally against progress but urged council to consider the property
owners when deciding this matter.
20.   Mayor Kriege directed Mr. Walker to read the proposed ordinance as
presented at the first reading in November, granting the zone change for the
property located at the corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road. Mr. Dusing,
attorney for the Scheben Group, advised Mayor Kriege and council that the other
condition by council to add another access road could be agreed to tonight.
Council Member Dupps requested an executive session to discuss this matter.
Executive Session
21.   At 7:50 p.m., Mr. Dupps moved and Mr. Gabbard made the second to move
into executive session in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) for the purpose of
discussing pending litigation. Motion carried unanimously.
22.   At 8:15 p.m., Mr. Bushong moved and Mr. Dupps made the second to return
to the regular session of the meeting. Mayor Kriege stated that pending
litigation was discussed in the executive session and that no action was taken.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zone Change for Property located at Cox and
Taylor Mill Rds.
23.   Mayor Kriege directed Mr. Walker to read the proposed ordinance that
would approve the zone change requested by the Scheben Group for property
located at the corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road. Mr. Walker read the
proposed ordinance in its entirety.
24.   Mr. Kudera made a motion to approve the ordinance; seconded by Mr.
Moriconi. Council Member Bushong expressed confusion that the ordinance had
been amended since the first reading to add a fourth condition under Section
II. Mr. Walker responded that his associate, Jeffrey S. Smith, who attended the
meeting wherein a first reading of this ordinance was read, had drafted the
first reading of this ordinance by hand; therefore it was read in summary. He
went on to say that no substantial change has been made from the first to the
second reading, as the fourth condition providing sewer lines to the residents
on Jimae Ct. was a part of the ordinance at the first reading. Mayor Kriege
concurred that the first reading of the ordinance contained all four conditions
in Section II.
25.   At this time, roll call was taken and answered with two yes votes cast by
Mr. Kudera and Mr. Moriconi and four no votes cast by Mr. Bushong, Mr. Dupps,
Mr. Ellison and Mr. Gabbard. The motion was defeated by a vote of 4-2.
Shaw Road Repairs
26.   Council Member Moriconi asked if the Water District has addressed the
needed repairs on Shaw Road. Mr. Wendling stated the Water District has
encountered some issues with the contractor that installed the lines on Shaw
Road this summer. He advised Mr. Moriconi that he would follow up with the
Water District to see when the repairs can be made to Shaw Road.
Contract with Glenhurst Development for a New City Park on Glenhurst Drive
27.   Mayor Kriege presented to council for their approval a proposed Agreement
between Glenhurst Development LLC and the city regarding the transfer of
ownership of the parklands property in the Glenhurst Subdivision to the city.
He stated the agreement details the arrangement between Glenhurst Development
and the city regarding the land use and development of the park. Mr. Dupps
asked if this subdivision would have a Homeowners Association. Mr. Wendling
replied no. Mr. Dupps asked if the city’s insurance company had been contacted
to discuss possible liabilities with regard to the lake on this property. Mr.
Wendling stated he had spoke to the city’s insurance agent who assured him the
city would be covered under the Errors & Omissions Policy.
28.   Mr. Wendling advised council a motion would be needed to accept the
property. Council Member Moriconi made a motion to accept ownership of the
Glenhurst park property; seconded by Mr. Kudera. Mr. Dupps asked the acreage of
this property. Mr. Moriconi stated the property was sixteen acres. A
representative of Glenhurst Development stated that Glenhurst Drive runs
through the parcel. Mr. Ellison noticed an easement on the property for East
Kentucky Power and expressed some concern for a power line in a city park. Mr.
Bob Schroder, representative of Glenhurst Development, advised that it was not
a high-tension line. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
29.   Mayor Kriege requested authorization to enter into the agreement with
Glenhurst regarding the development of the park. Council Member Kudera moved
with a second by Mr. Ellison to authorize Mayor Kriege to enter into the
agreement regarding the development of the Glenhurst Park. Roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Lease Purchase Contract with Fifth Third Bank for Purchase of City
Administrator’s Vehicle
30.   Mayor Kriege presented for council’s approval a lease purchase agreement
with Fifth Third Bank for the financing of a replacement vehicle for the City
Administrator.
31.   Council Member Moriconi moved, with second by Council Member Kudera to
approve a 36-month lease purchase agreement with Fifth Third Bank for a 2003
Ford Taurus. Council Member Gabbard commented that there are not sufficient
funds in the car lease line item in the budget to approve this purchase. He
suggested purchasing a Kia for a significantly lower amount of money. Mayor
Kriege stated there are sufficient funds in the departmental budget. Mr.
Gabbard argued that even though the Kia is not on the state contract price
list, that the city could save $7,000 choosing a Kia over a Ford Taurus that is
on the state contract-pricing list. Mayor Kriege countered that $16,000 for a
vehicle is not an outrageous price and that the city is just replacing the
leased vehicle with a matching car. Mr. Gabbard responded that this vehicle has
already been delivered and in use by the City Administrator, without council’s
approval. Mayor Kriege contended that he had approval to take delivery of this
vehicle when this council passed the current budget and that this line item is
not depleted. He maintained that the new 2003 Ford Taurus is a replacement for
the expired lease, with no option to purchase, of the 1999 Ford Taurus.
32.   Roll call was taken and answered with five yes votes and one no vote cast
by Mr. Gabbard. Motion carried 5-1 in favor.
33.   Mr. Ellison noted the Bank Qualification section on page two of the
contract that states “the lessee will be required to certify that they do not
reasonably expect to issue more than $10,000,000 in tax-exempt debt during the
current calendar year as defined by the Internal Revenue Code.” He expressed
concern that the city may not qualify with the current debt owed on the Fowler
Creek Sewer Project and the Municipal Center. Mayor Kriege assured Mr. Ellison
that he would follow up on that requirement.
City Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
34.   Mr. Wendling announced that the Sixth Annual Christmas Walk & Tour would
be held on Friday, December 6, 2002 from 6-9 P.M. The Walk & Tour would cover
the area on Madison Pike between the Independence Christian Church and St.
Cecilia Church. He stated that there would be a variety of entertainment,
refreshments and carriage rides available. Council Member Moriconi acknowledged
the Special Events Committee and the Citizens Police Academy for all their hard
work on the city events. Allison Kriege added that there would also be various
crafters and food vendors at three locations: St. Cecilia Church, Independence
Christian Church and the Park & Ride lot.
Mayor’s Report – Thomas M. Kriege
35.   Mayor Kriege explained that since the committees did not meet last month
there would be no committee reports. Council Member Dupps announced that the
first school resource officer hired with the grant funds awarded to the city
would begin employment with the city after the first of the year.
36.   Council Member Moriconi acknowledged Mayor Kriege by stating that it has
been a pleasure to work with him and wished him the best as he steps down from
the position of Mayor. Applause followed.
37.   Mayor Kriege announced that the Appreciation Dinner and Swearing In of
the Newly Elected Officials would be held on Thursday, December 12, 2002 at 6:
30 p.m. at the St. Cecilia Church undercroft. He wished the new mayor and
council well.
Adjournment
38.   Council Member Bushong moved, with second by Council Member Moriconi to
adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 8:44 p.m.

2003 Minutes
JANUARY 6, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
January 6, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Father Paul Berscheid of St. Cecilia
Catholic Church gave the invocation. The roll was called and the following
Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison,
Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also present was City
Administrator, Mark T. Wendling. Mayor Moriconi introduced and welcomed each
new Council Member.
Municipal Order 2003-MO-01 - Appointment of New Legal Counsel – Jed K. Deters
2.   Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration and approval a
Municipal Order authorizing the appointment of Jed K. Deters of the Deters,
Benzinger & LaVelle law firm to the position of City Attorney. He stated the
Municipal Order would also authorize him to enter into a Professional Services
Agreement for Mr. Deters’ services, which would be for a term of one year and
would provide for a thirty day written termination notice by either party.
Mayor Moriconi requested Mr. Wendling to read Municipal Order No. 2003-MO-01.
Council Member Bushong moved, with second from Council Member Yeager that
Municipal Order No. 2003-MO-01 be approved as read. Council Member Ellison
questioned whether this appointment should be made with an Executive Order. Mr.
Deters advised that approval by council would call for a municipal order. Roll
call was taken and answered unanimously by council.
Recess
3.   Mayor Moriconi requested a motion to take a short break so that Mr. Deters
could take the city attorney chair and quickly review the agenda. Council
Member Bushong so moved, with second by Council Member Ellison. Motion carried
unanimously.
4.   Mayor Moriconi requested a motion to reconvene the regular meeting.
Council Member Ellison so moved, with second by Council Member Yeager. Motion
carried unanimously.
Approval of the Minutes of the December 2, 2002 Regular Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the December
2, 2002 regular meeting of Council. Council Member Ellison so moved, with
second by Council Member Franzen to approve. No amendments were noted and roll
call was answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
6.   Mayor Moriconi announced that no one signed up to address council.
Old Business
7.   Mayor Moriconi advised that discussion of Old Business items would be
deferred to the Special Council Meeting planned for next Monday (January 13,
2003) at 7:00 p.m. to be held at the Senior Center, if it is available.
Declare List of City Owned Property as Surplus Items to be Auctioned
8.   Mayor Moriconi presented a list of surplus items, most of which have been
acquired by the city with the purchase of the Taylor Smith property (5409
Madison Pike). The list includes house fixtures such as cabinets, ceiling fans,
windows, doors, vinyl siding and shutters, sinks, shelving, electrical and
plumbing fixtures, as well as items that were left behind, such as baseball
cards, household appliances, sports equipment and games, when the previous
owner vacated the building. Council Member Ketron moved to declare the list of
items as surplus property, seconded by Mr. Ellison. No roll call taken; motion
carried unanimously.
9.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for review and approval a contract
with Auctioneer, Jim Kannady for his services to auction the aforementioned
surplus items. Upon motion by Council Member Ellison and
10.   second by Council Member Yeager roll call was taken and answered
unanimously to approve the contract with Auctioneer Jim Kannady.
Proposed Ordinance – Setting the Time and Date of the Council Meetings – 1st
Reading
11.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for their consideration an ordinance
that would add a monthly caucus meeting. He stated that having a monthly caucus
meeting would eliminate the need for committee meetings. He stated that no
action would be taken at caucus meetings and that the meetings would be purely
for discussion purposes only and that action on issues would be reserved for
the business meeting on the first Monday each month. He stated that he feels
the caucus meetings, which will be held at the Senior Center, will enhance
communication in a more informal manner. Mayor Moriconi advised that the
proposed ordinance indicated that the caucus meeting would be held on the third
Thursday each month, but would like to change that to the third Monday instead.
City Attorney, Jed Deters read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi stated
the second reading would be placed on the agenda for the special council
meeting next Monday.
Administrator’s Report – Mark T. Wendling
12.   Mr. Wendling advised the Police Department has received a grant for the
purchase of a VideoDetective Interceptor. He asked Police Chief Shawn Butler to
speak to council on the benefits of this equipment. Chief Butler advised that
the VideoDetective is a $50,000 piece of equipment that has been purchased with
a federal grant. He explained that it is a portable video enhancement system
that will assist in the crime solving of robberies. He stated this equipment is
designed to provide clearer images on surveillance videos. Chief Butler stated
that Detective Amy Chapman has been trained on the equipment and advised that
an arrest warrant has been issued today for the recent robbery at the Ameristop
in the Beechgrove Plaza. Mayor Moriconi asked what procedure the department
used prior to acquiring this equipment. Chief Butler stated the Airport has a
similar piece of equipment they could use, but they had to make an appointment
and the resulting picture would not be clear enough. He stated the process
could take several months and by that time the suspect may be long gone. Mr.
Wendling asked if this equipment would be available for use by other
communities. Chief Butler stated the department would share this resource with
other law enforcement agencies.
Resolution No. 2003-R-01 – Approving the Payment of Monthly Expenses for the
CDBG Grant (Senior Center)
13.   Mr. Wendling advised council that Resolution No. 2003-R-01 is being
presented for approval of the final payment of the Community Development Block
Grant funds from the State for the Senior Center project. He stated this final
payment is to the Grant Administrator, Bryan Kirby of Community & Economic
Development Associates, Inc. in the amount of $3,500.00.
14.   The City Attorney read Resolution No. 2003-R-01. Council Member Bushong
moved, with second by Council Member Yeager to approve Resolution No. 2003-R-
01. Roll call was answered unanimously.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
15.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for their approval three executive
orders appointing individuals to various Boards.
Executive Order No. 2003-EO-05 – Appointing Margaret Anne (Annie) Wuestefeld as
Citation Officer
Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2003-EO-05 repealing the designation of
Mark Wendling, Rich McAllister, Jeff Smith, Kevin Barbian and Diane Collins as
appointed citation officers pursuant to KRS 83A.130(7) and appointing Annie
Wuestefeld as the sole Citation Officer for Independence. Council Member
Franzen moved, with a second by Council Member Ellison to approve this
appointment. Council Member Bushong asked why only one person would be the
designated citation officer. Mr. Wendling explained that in consulting with Mr.
Deters it was discovered that because the above mentioned people have not
received training necessary of citation officers that any citation given by
those would not be upheld in a court of law. Mr. Deters stated that the
appointment of a citation officer should be based on their qualifications. Roll
call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Executive Order No. 2003-EO-06 – Re-Appointing Tom Jump to the Board of
Adjustments
Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2003-EO-06 re-appointing Tom Jump to
the Board of Adjustments for a four-year term that would expire on March 14,
2007. Council Member Ellison moved, with second by Council Member Bushong to
approve this appointment. Council Member Ellison expressed gratitude for the
many years of service Mr. Jump has devoted to the city as a member of this
Board. Mr. Deters commented that Mr. Jump does an excellent job on the Board.
Roll was called; motion carried unanimously.
Executive Order No. 2003-EO-07 – Re-Appointing Scott Holten to the Board of
Adjustments
Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2003-EO-07 re-appointing Scott Holten
to a four-year term on the Board of Adjustments that would expire on March 14,
2007. Council Member Ellison moved, with second by Council Member Yeager to
approve this appointment. Council Member Ellison also expressed gratitude to
Mr. Holten for his years of dedicated service to this Board. Roll call was
answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Miscellaneous Comments
16.   Council Member Franzen asked if there was any development on the
possibility of changing the title of the Recreation Director as discussed at
the last caucus meeting. Mr. Deters stated that matter is being reviewed.
Adjournment
17.   There being no further business, Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to
adjourn. Council Member Ellison so moved, with second by Council Member Ketron.
Motion carried unanimously and the meeting adjourned at 8:52 p.m.

Christian J. Moriconi, Mayor

JANUARY 13, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special
Session on Monday, January 13, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Independence Senior
Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Chris Moriconi presiding in the Chair.
Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. The
roll was called and the following council members registered present: Mary Pat
Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager.
Also present was Jed K. Deters, City Attorney and Mark T. Wendling, City
Administrator.
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   Discussion of the Lipscomb Annexation Issue
∙   Discussion & possible Action Relating to the Re-Financing of the Loans for
the Senior Center and the Municipal Center
∙   Discussion & possible action regarding the new Municipal Center
∙   Discussion regarding an interlocal agreement with the Sanitation District
No. 1 for storm water regulations
∙   Discussion & possible action regarding City Engineer services contract
Municipal Order 2003-MO-02
∙   Discussion & possible action regarding caucus meetings – Ordinance No.
2003-O-01
∙   Executive Order 2003-EO-04 – Appointments to the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Council
∙   Executive Session (only if necessary)
Lipscomb Annexation Issue
3.   Mayor Moriconi reported that he is directing the city attorney to review
the annexation ordinance that was adopted in 1978 that affects properties owned
by John Schoborg and Karen Lipscomb as they are disputing this annexation. He
stated that at some point council would be presented with a report and asked to
vote on how the city should proceed with this matter. Mr. Wendling explained
that the property was annexed in 1978 and the question of whether or not it was
a proper annexation has resurfaced throughout the last couple of decades. He
stated that in recent months the city staff along with the previous city
attorney and city engineer have met with the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
staff members in an effort to get to the bottom of this annexation dispute. Mr.
Wendling advised that the previous council took some action in December of
2002.
4.   City Attorney, Jed Deters advised that he would review the documents
pertaining to this annexation ordinance and would present a recommendation by
the February caucus meeting. Council Member Ellison suggested that Mr. Deters
obtain 1976 and 1996 plotted maps from Area Planning, so that he can compare
the boundary lines. Mr. Wendling advised that the description in the annexation
seems to be a matter of interpretation. Council Member Ellison suggested that
Mr. Marshall Slagle at Area Planning could shed some light on this matter. Mr.
John Schoborg commented that he and his sister have inherited this land from
their father. Council Member Franzen asked if they want this land taken out of
the city boundaries. Mr. Wendling stated that part of their land was in the
city prior to the annexation and that the annexation affected the rear portion
of the parcel.
Discussion Regarding Re-Financing of the Loans for the Senior Center and the
Municipal Center
5.   Mayor Moriconi informed council that he would like to explore the
possibility of re-financing the loans the city currently holds on the Senior
Center and the Municipal Center in an effort to lower the annual mortgage
payments by $100,000. He stated that this would mean extending the life of the
loans, which would add more interest, but that a fixed rate would be available
for a thirty-year loan. He stated that a fixed rate would provide peace of
mind, as well as reduce the annual budgeted funds needed for these line items.
6.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a Financial Advisory Agreement between
the city and Seasongood & Mayer, a firm specializing in Public Finance, for
consideration. Mr. Robert Cooper, a Senior Principal with the firm, was present
to answer questions. Mr. Deters asked questions regarding the fees for services
section of the proposed contract. Mr. Cooper advised that minimum fees are
associated with a tiered fee schedule. Mr. Deters also noted that the annual
fee is not printed in the contract. Mr. Cooper advised there is no annual
advisory fee and that the line could be removed. Mayor Moriconi advised that
there would no be a prepayment fee after the first ten years. Council Member
Ellison asked if the Senior Center loan had a prepayment penalty. Mr. Cooper
stated that his preliminary research of the current loan with the Kentucky
League of Cities on the Senior Center shows no prepayment penalty would apply.
7.   Mr. Cooper stated that multiple scenarios on the concept of refinancing
have been considered, including a thirty-year loan on the Senior Center, which
he feels is not in the best interest of the city. He advised that interest
rates are at a forty-year low and stated that an in-depth analysis with some
modifications would result in the best deal for the city. Council Member
Franzen asked for clarification regarding one or two loans. Mr. Cooper stated
that it was unsure at this time if the loans would be kept separate or if it
would be more cost-effective to combine the loans, and that further review
would be necessary to make that determination. Mr. Wendling advised that even
if the loans were combined, the Senior Center would still be paid off in ten
years. Mr. Cooper advised that there are various factors to look at regarding
advantages and minimum costs for the city. Council Member Yeager asked if there
were one loan - would there be two payments. Mr. Cooper replied if there was
one, loan there would only be one payment. Council Member Ketron asked if the
Senior Center was paid off in ten years would the remaining loan on the
Municipal Center decrease. Mr. Cooper replied that it would.
Re-Financing the Loans
8.   Council Member Behler asked if they were being asked to vote on whether to
settle on a fixed or variable interest rate. Mr. Cooper agreed on a concept of
re-financing. Mayor Moriconi requested a motion to begin the re-financing
process. Mr. Cooper explained that the re-financing process and that it would
require two readings of an ordinance and would take approximately forty-five
days and that after the second reading of the ordinance they would authorize
the sale of the bonds. Council Member Franzen asked if this would be a lengthy
process. Mr. Cooper stated that it would take forty-five to sixty days for the
entire process, as the bonds would be bid out. He explained that the most
important motivation for re-financing would be to protect the city from the
volatility of the market. Council Member Ketron asked if the sample interest
rates that were provided were close to what the city could expect to obtain.
Mr. Cooper stated that conservative rates were used, but felt they were better
than close but still contained a cushion. Council Member Ellison asked if the
bond counsel fees were included. Mr. Cooper stated that those fees would be
additional. Mr. Deters advised that bond counsel fees were unavoidable and
explained to council that he is not a certified bond counselor, but will handle
the local issues regarding the bonding. Mr. Cooper advised there is several
bond counsel firms the city can choose from and that he has worked with
several. Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Cooper to disclose council of the other
Northern Kentucky agencies he has worked for. Mr. Cooper stated he has worked
with the cities of Erlanger, Edgewood, and Newport and St. Elizabeth Hospital,
the Sanitation District and the Airport.
9.   Council Member Yeager moved, with second by Council Member Franzen to
authorize Mayor Moriconi to enter into a financial advisory agreement with
Seasongood & Mayer regarding the re-financing of the bonds for the Municipal
Center and the Senior Center. Roll call was answered unanimously and the motion
carried 6-0.
Discussion & Possible Action Regarding the New Municipal Center
10.   Mayor Moriconi directed council to the bid tabulation sheet for the
Municipal Center. He stated the architects were present to answer any questions
regarding the bids received, contracts, etc. Council Member Behler asked the
architect to point out the location of the council chamber wing. Mr. Scott
Layman, Cole+Russell Architects, reviewed the building design and the bid
tabulation sheet with council. He explained that the contractors were asked to
provide a base bid for the entire building, two alternate bids, one each for
the addition of a clock tower (A-1 add B) and the addition of a detention basin
(A-2 add C) and one alternate bid that would be to construct the building minus
the council chamber wing (A-3 deduct D). He indicated that the low bidder was
Century Construction with Paul Hemmer Companies coming in second. Council
Member Bushong asked about the Century Construction bid which had a deduct bid
amount of $505,000 for the council chamber wing. Mayor Moriconi replied that
the original bid listed that amount, but Century stated after the bid opening
that there was a calculation error, with a corrected amount of $310,000. Mr.
Layman stated that since this is post-bid information, Century couldn’t submit
this information and will have grounds to withdraw their bid if Alternate A-
3 is a consideration by council. Mr. Layman stated that if council chooses to
construct the entire building the difference is $245,000 to keep the council
chamber wing. Mayor Moriconi advised that in effect Century Construction cannot
be awarded the bid if council chooses to remove the council chamber wing. Mr.
Layman explained that the next low bid from Paul Hemmer Companies would result
in a net savings of $245,000 if Alternate A-3 were part of the bid award.
Council Member Ellison asked if Century Construction was the lowest bid with
the council chamber wing. Mr. Layman replied that their bid was the lowest base
bid with the council chamber wing. Mr. Deters explained there was just an error
on Century’s bid in the calculation of the deduct amount for the council
chamber wing.
11.   Council Member Franzen expressed concern that if the project is delayed
and goes over budget the cost of the project could exceed available funds, and
the building would still need furniture, etc. She asked how likely this could
happen. Mr. Layman advised that a five percent contingency fund ($187,000) has
been built into the project costs. Mr. Deters stated that the city could incur
multiple change orders up to $187,000 and still come in at budget. Mr. Layman
also advised that the bid amounts came in as predicted and that the
construction contract will allow for the city to be compensated for each day
beyond the completion date as contracted. Mr. Lape of Cole+Russell commented
that Century Construction has stated in their bid that the project would be
completed within 400 days with the city being compensated $1,000 per day beyond
that. Council Member Franzen asked the architects to estimate the construction
cost of the council chamber wing if built ten years from now. Mr. Layman
replied that it would be difficult to predict but felt certain that the current
$62.49 per square foot cost would not be within reach in the future. Council
Member Franzen suggested that only the storage area below the council chambers
be built.
12.   Council Member Bushong asked about the detention basin. Mr. Layman
advised that technically the basin does not have to be constructed but that it
was added as an alternate bid at the direction of the former council. Mr.
Bushong asked if the detention basin was contingent on the placement of the
proposed amphitheater, as he thought it might be priced into the amphitheater
construction. Mr. Layman stated that Ehmet Hayes would design a preliminary
site plan. Council Member Yeager referred to a water problem with Mr. England’s
property that abuts the city park. Mr. Wendling stated that was an issue
presented by Mr. England at a council meeting several months ago. Council
Member Bushong commented that the construction of the detention basin would
drive up this project another $33,000. Mr. Layman stated that storm water
retention is always a good thing, but is not always necessary.
13.   Council Member Franzen asked how the size of the proposed council chamber
wing compares to the current meeting space in the courthouse. Mr. Wendling
stated that it is smaller. She asked the purpose of the executive session room
as observers could be asked to leave the room, as is the current practice. Mr.
Wendling stated the executive session room would allow private conversations
without violating the open meetings law and that the current arrangement is not
ideal as the conversations in the courtroom can be overheard in the lobby area
of the courthouse.
14.   Council Member Behler stated she was in favor of a council chamber wing.
She stated that the additional space for meetings would serve as a multiple
purposes and would be a resource for the community. She stated that free
meeting space is difficult to find and the Senior Center is being used a great
deal. Council Member Franzen expressed concern with building a grand council
chamber and commented that she had phoned about thirty people to gather input
on public preference – a council chambers wing or restrooms in the park. She
stated the overwhelming choice from those she polled was the preference for
restrooms in the park. Council Member Yeager advised that restrooms are already
planned for Memorial Park. Mayor Moriconi stated that the study of facilities
for Memorial Park might be ready and presented to council at the February
caucus meeting. He stated the study would offer various facilities with cost
estimates and that having sufficient funds would be key to the development
plans.
15.   Council Member Ketron commented that he felt the city would never again
be able to build the council chamber wing for $245,000 and that more than just
the council chamber room would be lost. He stated the space below the council
chambers would be lost, as well as the mechanical room, which takes up about
one-fourth of the area; it would have to be moved elsewhere in the building,
crowding the remaining lower level of the building. Council Member Bushong
stated the mechanical room was enlarged to have more storage of non-essential
items. He commented that he feels the public is upset with the $5M loan
obtained for this project and that he feels other things can be gained with
$245,000. He stated that the Senior Center has adequate meeting space and that
the city only pays $100 per month to the county for the use of the courtroom
for the council meetings. He stated he feels the city needs to do other things
for the residents and the he doesn’t feel a council chamber wing is needed. He
added that it might cost more to build ten years from now but that hopefully
the city will have more funds to pay for it in the future.
16.   Council Member Yeager commented that the city has already borrowed the
$5M and may as well continue the plans for the council chambers for only
$245,000. Council Member Bushong stated he sees no urgency for a council
chamber and that the city could add it later. Council Member Yeager responded
that the city shouldn’t have to run to the courthouse, to rent space for city
meetings. Council Member Ellison commented that city government centers around
the city building and that he feels the proposed cost of $62.49 per square to
construct this wing contributes to the urgency.
17.   Council Member Franzen asked if this wing would be used for meeting space
or only benefit the mayor and council. Council Member Yeager stated it would be
open to the public. Council Member Franzen suggested that Summit View Schools
and the Senior Center already provide plenty of meeting space available to the
public. Council Member Ellison stated that school facilities are only available
to organized groups. Council Member Franzen stated that what the community
needs are more sidewalks and restrooms in the parks. Council Member Ellison
commented that the development in the city of Independence has come a long way
in the last fifteen years and that public support won’t allow it to stop.
18.   Mayor Moriconi commented that this is a big decision. Mr. Tom Brinker, a
resident and member of the audience asked if the council chambers would be free
meeting space. Mr. Wendling stated it would be free to non-profit groups. Mr.
Brinker asked Mayor Moriconi if he could guarantee there would be funds left to
allocate for restrooms in the park. Mayor Moriconi said he felt he had to.
Council Member Yeager stated she felt there is no guarantee that the funds will
be available. Mayor Moriconi commented that the current Memorial Park fund
balance is $256,000 and that is not enough to construct the amphitheater.
Council Member Yeager commented if the amphitheater had been built three years
ago it wouldn’t have cost what it will now. Mr. Brinker commented that he feels
the city will never get this price again to build the council chamber wing.
Council Member Franzen stated that the only thing that concerns her with losing
the council chamber wing is the storage space below. Council Member Behler
countered that the city does not need the storage space now, but does need the
meeting space now and will in the future. Council Member Franzen argued that
she does not feel the need for meeting space justifies an additional $245,000
expense to this project. Mr. Wendling concurred that usage of the Senior Center
continues to climb.
19.   Mayor Moriconi commented that soft costs (furniture, telephone system,
etc.) are estimated to be about $275,000. Mr. Wendling stated that the audience
seating in the council chambers would be stack chairs so they could be stored
when not in use. Council Member Ketron inquired as to the balance of the $5M
that was borrowed for this project. Mayor Moriconi replied that the city has
been making monthly payments on this loan for about a year and have paid
architect fees and some soft costs with approximately $4.5 remaining for the
project. He stated the money is being invested and that in one month alone the
city earned $18,000 in interest, but the amount of interest will decrease as
expenses are incurred.
20.   Mr. Deters commented that the Fire District has regretted not adding a
basement area to the new firehouse. Council Member Yeager commented that the
Senior Center did not build a basement and needed one.
21.   Council Member Franzen maintained that she would like restrooms built in
Memorial Park, as well as the amphitheater, and was concerned this would not be
possible if the council chambers was added to the project. Mayor Moriconi
stated that he has reviewed the budget for the Municipal Center and feels if
the project comes in on budget there may be $50 - $60,000 left that could be
directed to Memorial Park. He advised that the amphitheater project now has a
fund of $256,000, but that additional revenue will be needed to accomplish this
project. Council Member Ketron commented that more parking spaces would be
needed if the park adds an amphitheater and restroom facilities. Mayor Moriconi
stated that Ehmet Hayes firm will supply a list of things for the park. Council
Member Franzen commented that it bothered her to build a council chambers wing
when there are no restrooms in the park. Council Member Ketron maintained that
it was not just about the council chambers, but the additional storage space
that the lower lever will provide.
22.   Council Member Behler moved, with second by Council Member Ellison to
award the construction bid of the Municipal Center including the council
chambers wing to Century Construction as the lowest bid. There was a brief
discussion regarding the retention basin and whether it was necessary to
include it in the bid. The architect advised it was not a requirement and
Council Member Ellison suggested the new Memorial Park design plans could
explore how a detention basin could fit in the plan. Mayor Moriconi asked for
the roll to be called. Roll call was answered for four yes votes and two no
votes cast by Council Members Bushong and Franzen. Motion carried 4-2. Mayor
Moriconi commented that the Municipal Center has been a long process and
thanked Mayor Kriege for getting the ball rolling.
Recess
23.   Council Member Yeager moved with second by Council Member Franzen to take
a brief recess. Motion carried unanimously.
24.   Council Member Ellison moved with second by Council Member Behler to
reconvene the meeting. Motion carried unanimously.
Discussion and Possible Action Regarding the City Engineer Services Contract
25.   Mayor Moriconi requested this item be moved up on the agenda. Hearing no
objections, he informed council that he would like to contract with CDS
Associates, Inc. for city engineering services. Council was presented with an
agreement for professional services with CDS for their consideration. He stated
that CDS would not do business with other clients in the city while they are
representing the city. He also commented that he would not require the city
engineer’s presence at all council meetings. Moriconi asked if council had any
questions.
26.   Council Member Yeager questioned Part IV of the agreement regarding
ownership of documents. President of CDS Associates, John Eisenmann, explained
that the ownership of documents is a legal issue and that the documents are a
product of their professional service. He advised the city would be provided
copies, but they would retain the official final document. Mr. Deters stated
that he sees no problem with this clause as long as the city has copies. Mr.
Eisenmann stated the city would have permission to utilize the document copies.
Mr. Eisenmann advised that CDS would designate Mark V. Brueggemann as the
principal engineer for the city with Jim Schumate as the backup. He stated they
see their firm as an extension of city staff and therefore will not work for
private developers that may conflict with the city’s interests. Council Member
Bushong asked what Mr. Brueggemann’s position would be. Mr. Eisenmann stated
that Mr. Brueggemann works out of the Florence office and would be the Senior
Manager for Independence. He advised that Mr. Brueggemann and Mr. Schumate
specialize in municipal engineering, with experience in twenty counties.
Council Member Ketron asked if CDS was a local firm. Mr. Eisenmann stated that
they are a local company with the main office in Blue Ash, Ohio. Council Member
Ellison commented that he knows Jim Schumate from his work with Estes
Engineering when that firm provided the City of Independence with engineering
services. He stated that Mr. Schumate is knowledgeable and helpful and feels
confident with his abilities.
Municipal Order No. 2003-MO-02 – Approving City Engineer Services Agreement
with CDS Associates
27.   Council Member Ellison moved to approve the contract agreement for city
engineering services with CDS Associates, with second by Council Member
Franzen. Council Member Bushong asked if the city paid an hourly rate to
Cardinal Engineering. Mr. Wendling responded yes as well as a $250 monthly
retainer. City Attorney, Mr. Deters read Municipal Order No. 2003-MO-02. Roll
call was answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Discussion Regarding An Interlocal Agreement with the Sanitation District No. 1
For Storm Water Regulations
28.   Mayor Moriconi advised council that representatives from the Sanitation
District, Jeff Eger and John Lyons, were present to explain the federally
mandated storm water regulation program and answer questions He advised that
all cities must comply with this mandate and the deadline for the
implementation of this program is March 10, 2003. He also advised that the
Sanitation District is proposing an Interlocal Agreement to provide the city
with storm water discharge permit services and other storm water related
services. Mayor Moriconi stated that this matter is being discussed for
information purposes; no action will be taken tonight, but will be deferred to
the business meeting on February 3, 2003.
29.   Mr. Jeff Eger (Sanitation District representative) advised council that
all cities are obligated to comply with this unfounded federal mandate. He
stated that the Sanitation District was asked to assist the local cities and
has been working with city leaders on a proposal to deal with the new
regulations and work out a transfer of ownership of the storm water system. He
advised that by March 10, 2003 an application and management plan must be
submitted to the Kentucky Division of Water for the thirty-three Northern
Kentucky communities, as well as the counties of Boone, Campbell and Kenton,
that were specifically listed in the EPA Phase II storm water regulations. Mr.
Eger advised that the proposed plan has addressed the following compliance
issues:
∙   Public education and outreach
∙   Public involvement and participation
∙   Illicit discharge detection and elimination
∙   Control of construction site runoff
∙   Post-construction storm water management
∙   Pollution prevention and good housekeeping
Mr. Eger advised that the cost per resident to maintain this storm water
management program is proposed at $5.00 per month which would be assessed on
the quarterly sanitation bill. He stated this assessment was based on square
footage. He stated they have estimated a $3,000,000 per year capital budget to
address the needs of this program and a $2,000,000 debt service at the end of
the five-year cycle to be used to operate and maintain the system.
30.   Council Member Ellison asked if every house would be billed the $5.00 per
month even if they did not have public sewers. Mr. Eger replied yes. Council
Member Bushong asked what other cities were doing. Mr. Eger stated that the
focus group, comprised of city representatives, has met for the last two years
to discuss and draft the proposed interlocal agreement, which has been provided
to Mr. Deters for review.
31.   There was a lengthy discussion regarding the assessment fee to the
residents and the feasibility of Independence handling this federally mandated
regulation without the assistance of the Sanitation District. Mayor Moriconi
commented that he felt there was strength in numbers. Council Member Franzen
felt if the city took on this responsibility, they it may cost the residents
more. Council Member Yeager expressed concern that the rates would increase,
just as the sanitation tap-in fees did when the Sanitation District took over
the maintenance of the city’s sewer lines several years ago; from $600.00 to
$1,800.00 for each tap-in. Mr. Eger countered by stating there has been no
increase in those rates in the past five years.
32.   Mr. Eger stated the survey work has been costly and that the District has
already invested $8,000,000 into this project and if the city chooses to go it
alone they would either have to compile their own inventory or buy it from the
District. Council Member Ellison took objection to Mr. Eger’s statement and
argued that the rate payers already paid this debt and suggested that maybe the
District was overcharging.
33.   Council Member Franzen asked if the city had to be in compliance by March
10. Mr. Eger advised that an application for a permit had to be submitted to
the Kentucky Division of Water along with a plan of action no later than March
10, 2003. He stated that the city does not have time to conduct an inventory of
the storm water system and develop a plan of action in time to meet the March
10th deadline. Council Member Yeager asked for assurance that there would be no
increase of the $5.00 assessment fee. Mr. Eger stated he could not promise
there would be no increase as the $5.00 is an estimated rate. He stated that a
Board of Directors would make that decision. He advised that the Kenton County
Judge Executive appoints the members on the Board of Directors. Council Member
Ellison commented that the county doesn’t protect the city funds. Council
Member Bushong asked if the $5.00 assessment fee could possibly be adjusted a
little lower. Mr. Eger stated they would continue to look at the costs
involved. Council Member Franzen asked if they could guarantee that assessment
fees from Independence residents would not fund the problems of other cities.
Mr. Eger stated they would address all the issues in a manageable manner and
lay out a plan. Council Member Ellison stated he would like the agreement to
provide the city with some control in negotiating the assessment rate charged
to the residents. Council Member Ketron asked if the city would have some
responsibility regarding maintenance tasks. Mr. Eger stated the city would have
to provide storm sewer maintenance for the first five years until the
Sanitation District takes over ownership of the city’s system. Council Member
Yeager asked what the District would do for the first five years. Mr. Eger
stated they would do all compliance, enforcement and permits.
34.   Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Eger when the Agreement would be ready for the
city to consider. Mr. Eger stated it is undergoing some minor language
amendments and should be ready later this week. Mr. Deters asked if there would
be opportunity for city amendments. Mr. Eger replied no, not with thirty-six
cities taking part in this agreement. Council Member Yeager reiterated her
concern with the proposed assessment rate of $5.00 per month per household.
Council Member Franzen proposed each city should agree to a rate charged to
their residents. Mr. Eger countered that city’s do not have input on the
sanitation rates and that state laws govern the rate review. Mr. Deters asked
if this could be delegated to each entity. Mr. Eger responded that it would be
reviewed y the Council of Local Government. Mr. Deters asked if the final draft
of the Agreement would have an “opt out” provision. Mr. Eger replied no, but
added that at the end of the five years, if a city wanted to keep their storm
water system they would be able to do that. Council Member Yeager suggested
that since the sanitation billing is done on a quarterly basis that the $5.00
per month proposed assessment rate be advertised as $15.00 per quarter.
35.   Council Member Behler asked if the city is expected to vote on this
Agreement at the next council meeting. Mayor Moriconi advised that when it
comes time for council to authorize him to enter into this agreement with the
Sanitation District a Resolution would be submitted to council for their
consideration. Mr. Eger mentioned that they would take over the plan review for
storm sewers in new construction and there would be no duplication of services
by the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission. There being no further
discussion, Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Eger for attending the meeting and
explaining this mandated regulation and the proposed interlocal agreement.
Ordinance No. 2003-O- 01 – Setting Council Meeting Date & Times
36.   Mayor Moriconi presented, for second reading the proposed ordinance
setting the dates and times for council’s regular monthly business meeting and
establishing and setting regular monthly caucus meetings on the third Monday of
each month. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Council Member Bushong
moved, with second by Council Member Ketron to adopt Ordinance No. 2003-O- 01
as read. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Executive Order No. 2003-EO-04 – Appointments to the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Council
37.   Mayor Moriconi read and presented to council for endorsement Executive
Order 2003-EO-04 designating himself as the principal representative for the
city on the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Council and Council Member Ellison
as the alternate representative. Council Member Bushong moved, with second by
Council Member Yeager to approve Executive Order 2003-EO-04 as presented. Roll
call was answered with five yeas, with Council Member Ellison voicing a pass
vote. Motion carried.
Adjournment
38.   There being no further business on the special meeting agenda, Mayor
Moriconi asked for a motion to adjourn. Council Member Bushong so moved, with a
second by Council Member Behler. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting
adjourned at 9:37 p.m.
