FEBRUARY 3, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
February 3, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the
Independence Christian Church gave the invocation and called for a moment of
silence in memory of the fallen Columbia space shuttle and the demise of all
seven astronauts on board. The roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol
Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K.
Deters and City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling.
Presentation of Proclamations
2.   Mayor Moriconi presented proclamations to Boy Scouts, Robert Graydon and
Gregory Benoit on their recent achievement of Eagle Scout rank. Mayor Moriconi
welcomed Boy Scout Troops Number 8 and Number 71 that were attending the
meeting to earn their communication badges. He encouraged them to continue
their good work and stated his appreciation of their community service.
Approval of the Minutes of the January 6, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the January
6, 2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Bushong so moved, with
second from Council Member Ketron. No amendments were noted and roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the January 13, 2003 Special Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the January
13, 2003 special meeting of council. Council Member Ellison moved, with second
from Council Member Bushong. Several amendments were noted and approved. Roll
call was answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
PRIVELEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Mr. Jeff Whorf, 5375 Valleycreek Drive addressed council regarding his
concern about the amount of garbage and litter that is strewn throughout the
city. He stated it is unsightly and decreases property values. Mr. Whorf
offered three suggestions to keep the city clean:
1.   Impose a fee or surcharge on direct mail companies that could be used to
clean up the fliers and pouches of information they leave on mailboxes that get
blown away and turn into litter.
2.   Pass an ordinance that would require all trash to be placed in a container
with a lid, when left at the curb for pickup. He stated this would prevent
animals from tearing apart plastic trash bags. He stated that other communities
in which he has lived had such an ordinance.
3.   Encourage the police to enforce existing litter laws. To raise awareness,
he suggested putting up no littering signs stating the dollar amount of the
fine.
Mr. Whorf stated that the trash collectors also spread litter when they dump
the can in the truck and then place the can back on the ground upside down
dumping leftover debris all over the ground. He stated it would only take the
truck attendant a couple of extra seconds to place the can upright and replace
the lid. He also suggested enlisting non-violent county jail prisoners to clean
up the side of the roads. He encouraged council to implement some of his
proposals that he feels will make a big difference over the long term in
keeping the city clean.
6.   Mayor Moriconi suggested the city might urge organizations to sponsor
designated highway sections to provide clean up along the roadways. He stated
the council could discuss this further at the caucus meeting, as this would
require many sponsors. He advised that the city would hold a spring clean up in
April that would provide large dumpsters for residents to dispose of large
items.
7.   Council Member Bushong commented that he thought all mail placed in
mailboxes was required to have postage affixed and suggested the city attorney
research this. Council Member Ellison suggested the city notify local carriers
that the city will not tolerate haphazard distribution of advertising
materials. Council Member Franzen suggested specific tubes designed to hold
this type of material would be affixed to all mailboxes to control this type of
litter. Mayor Moriconi directed the city administrator to contact a
representative of the Door-to-Door Advertising Company to convey the council’s
concerns.
Discussion of Zone Change Request by Thelma & Robert Gibson for 5190 Madison
Pike
8.   Mayor Moriconi informed council that Mr. & Mrs. Gibson were present to
request a zone change for property they own at 5190 Madison Pike. He asked Mr.
Deters to explain the matter. Mr. Deters explained that the Gibson’s have
applied for a map amendment to rezone this property from R-1D, a single-family
residential zone, to R-1DD, which is a single and two family residential zone.
This property currently has a deteriorated single-family structure on the site
and the Gibson’s would like to raze the house and build a two family duplex,
which would be rental property. He stated that the Planning Commission has
recommended that the zone change be denied based on the fact that the request
does not comply with the adopted comprehensive plan and that the approximate .3
acres would constitute “spot” zoning. He stated that the zoning ordinance
requires that zone R-1DD contain a minimum of five acres. Mr. Deters advised
council that they have four options
1.   Do nothing – which would essentially uphold the Planning Commission’s
decision
2.   Follow the recommendation without a hearing or only an argument-type
hearing
3.   Review the record of the hearing before the commission and determine from
that evidence adjudicative facts which differ from those found by the
commission, and then override the Commission’s recommendation based on those
facts
4.   Council could hold its own trial-type of public hearing and find as a
result thereof different adjudicative facts than those found by the commission
and then disapprove the recommendation based upon those facts.
Mr. Deters advised council that they should decide which option they would like
to pursue before entering into a discussion on this matter. Mayor Moriconi
advised council that they have been presented with the Planning Commission’s
minutes from the January 2, 2003 public hearing on this. Mr. Deters advised
that the council could hear point of opinion from the Gibson’s and the
neighbors, but they cannot present new evidence to council. He stated that in
order for council to override the Planning Commission’s recommendation, the
city would have to determine different facts.
9.   Council Member Ellison stated that he was prepared to follow option number
three. Council Member Franzen asked what would happen if council rejected the
recommendation. Mr. Deters advised that council would need to have a hearing to
obtain evidence to support that opinion. He stated it would be advisable to
review the actual transcript of the Planning Commission’s meeting and not just
the summary minutes. Council Member Franzen asked if this could be decided at
the caucus meeting later in the month. Mr. Deters stated no action could be
taken at the caucus meeting.
10.   It was decided to allow the Gibson’s and neighbors to address council,
but they were cautioned not to disclose any information that was not heard at
the Planning Commission’s public hearing on this matter. Mr. & Mrs. Gibson had
a prepared copy that they wanted to distribute to council. Mr. Deters denied
that request. Mrs. Gibson stated that their zone change request has been denied
in large part due to the size of the lot, which is noted as 0.3 acres, but in
fact is 0.34 according to the deed. She argued that the area does not lend
itself to high-end construction, with a vacant convenience store nearby. She
stated that there are other duplexes throughout the city, which does not
adversely hurt those areas. Mrs. Gibson also objected to the Planning
Commission’s report wherein it was repeatedly noted that they proceeded with
this zone change despite information and advise from the city that the request
did not meet the minimum size for a new zone. Mrs. Gibson advised council that
they now have a development plan prepared and are ready to proceed with the
construction of a ranch style duplex with a common driveway. She stated that
the proposed structure would be rental property with the option to buy. In
closing she stated the city’s deadline to raze the current structure is
February 20, 2003 and stated they would not be able to meet this time frame and
she asked for an extension.
11.   Tony Stenger, 5188 Madison Pike, spoke in opposition to this development
plan by the Gibson’s. He stated that he lives next door to the property. He
urged council to look at the facts and stated that ultimately, the neighbors do
not want a multifamily structure in this area.
12.   Pat McCleese, 5181 Madison Pike, stated she has lived there for 35 years.
She stated she has lived next to apartments in the past and that she was
concerned that this being rental property, it would not be maintained properly.
13.   There being no further comments, Mayor Moriconi asked council how they
wanted to proceed. Council Member Ketron moved, with second by Council Member
Behler to accept the recommendation of the Planning Commission, that being to
disapprove the zone change request. Further discussion ensued. Council Member
Ketron stated that based on the Planning Commission’s recommendation granting
this zone change would constitute “spot” zoning since the property in question
is less than the five acres necessary for the R-1DD zone. He stated that he
does not believe the city will uncover sufficient data to defy their
recommendation. He stated that he personally likes the two-family design, but
considering the size of the lot, and no supporting facts to grant this map
amendment, he feels the city has no choice but to support the Commission’s
recommendation. Council Member Ellison stated that the Comprehensive Plan is
just a guideline for development, not concrete. He stated that he does not feel
the minimum five acres requirement will support their recommendation to
disapprove this zone change request by the Gibson’s. He stated that further
evidence can be obtained from the Planning Commission’s own GIS system. Council
Member Yeager agreed that the city should have all information before voting.
Council Member Ellison commented that the Planning Commission is the research
body for the cities and they should provide all applicable info. Mr. Deters
advised the city could pay for a detailed transcript of the public hearing that
the Planning Commission held.
14.   Council Member Behler stated that she seconded the motion as she feels
making small zone changes will bring about a zoning hodgepodge, even if the
city opposed the Comprehensive Plan, or produced further evidence, the property
still does not meet the minimum five acres for the R-1DD zone that the Gibson’s
are requesting.
15.   Council Member Franzen stated that she hasn’t decided how to vote in this
matter, as she understands both sides. She stated she would like all the
necessary information, so as to have a well-informed opinion before taking
action on this matter.
16.   Council Member Ketron stated that council must look at the precedence
this would set if the city permitted this type of zone on a smaller lot. A
precedence that could be repeated throughout the years. Mayor Moriconi
commented that the size of the lot is 100 x 150 feet. Council Member Ellison
stated that the Planning Commission wasn’t established until 1966 and that the
Gibson property was probably plotted in the early 1940’s which would be
protected by the grandfather law. Council Member Ketron disagreed by stating
that the grandfather law would not apply to a new structure that the Gibson’s
are proposing.
17.   Council Member Bushong asked that the roll be called on the motion or
that it be withdrawn. Council Member Yeager felt since the lot is greater than
13,000 square feet that the disapproval by the Planning Commission is
questionable. Council Member Behler reiterated that the “spot” zoning for this
lot was the determining issue for her decision to uphold the recommendation of
the Planning Commission. Council Member Franzen commented that she is
interested in hearing more of Council Member Ellison’s position.
18.   At this time, Mayor Moriconi directed the roll to be called. The roll
call resulted in a 3-3 vote by council with Council Members Ketron, Behler and
Bushong voting ayes and Council Members Ellison, Franzen and Yeager voting no.
Mr. Deters advised that Mayor Moriconi has the authority to vote on this matter
in order to break the tie and distributed the state Attorney General’s Opinion
upholding stating this. Mayor Moriconi stated that based on Mr. Deters advise
he would cast a vote. He voted yes. Motion to approve the recommendation of the
Planning Commission to deny the zone change request for the property located at
5190 Madison Pike carried by a vote of 4-3.
19.   Mr. Deters advised he would draft a resolution regarding this decision
and will present it at the next council meeting.
Zoning Compliance Extension to 5190 Madison Pike Property Owned by Robert &

Resolution No. 2003-R-03 – Approving an Interlocal Agreement with the
Sanitation District No. 1 Regarding Storm Water Regulations
24.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-03 that would
authorize him to enter into, and execute on behalf of the city an interlocal
agreement with Sanitation District No. 1 to provide the city with Kentucky
Pollutant Discharge Elimination System (KPDES) storm water discharge permit
services and other storm water related services. Mr. Deters read the
resolution.
25.   Mayor Moriconi introduced John Lyons from the Sanitation District who was
present to answer questions council might have regarding this agreement. Mr.
Lyons advised that the Storm Water Management Plan could be viewed on the
Sanitation District’s website. He stated the Plan outlines capital improvements
of the storm water infrastructure. Council Member Ketron asked about the cost
to the residents. Mr. Lyons stated that initially the surcharge cost was to be
$5.00 per month but that amount has now been adjusted to $3.75 per month.
Council Member Ellison asked if the city could attach an addendum to this
agreement that would provide the city with input should the District ever
request an increase in this surcharge. Mr. Lyons stated that would not be
permissible. He stated that the Sanitation District has been committed to
consolidating the storm water system for the various cities and the first
priority will be to focus on Phase II regulations, which the individual cities
are not able to fund on their own. He stated that one of the goals would be the
ultimate transfer of the storm water system to the Sanitation District along
with providing more regional service to storm water management. He stated that
the federal deadline for the permit application is March 10, 2003. Council
Ellison asked if each city would be provided a copy of the permit to display in
a public place. Mr. Lyons replied yes. He informed council that for the first
five years the city will still be the owner of the system and will have certain
obligations. He stated that the Sanitation district will be responsible for the
operation and management of the system and that the revenue generated from the
surcharge will go toward the elimination of unlawful discharges found those
first five years. He stated that the District would prioritize improvement
projects with the excess funds generated from the surcharge. Council Member
Franzen asked if the surcharge would go into one fund or separated by city. Mr.
Lyons stated there would be one fund. Mayor Moriconi commented there is
strength in numbers. Council Member Yeager expressed concern that the surcharge
would be increased without city input. She also suggested, that since the
residents are billed on a quarterly basis, that the Sanitation District
publicize that the surcharge would be $11.25 per quarter.
26.   Mr. Lyons stated that initially the primary focus would be on water-based
issues. Mayor Moriconi asked if the Plan would cover flooding issues. Mr. Lyons
stated that the Plan was not setup to address flooding problems.
27.   Mr. Lyons informed council that the Sanitation District was not named on
the list of entities that had to comply with these federally mandated
regulations. The District was asked by some of the local cities to assist them
in this responsibility, and collectively the region is implementing this
agreement. Council Member Franzen commented that the city could not afford to
meet these federal compliances for $3.75 per month. Mr. Lyons advised that
unimproved parcels would be the only exception to the $3.75 per month
surcharge.
28.   There being no further discussion, Council Member Franzen moved, with
second by Council Member Behler to approve Resolution No. 2003-R-03. Roll call
was answered unanimously; motion carried.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the Codification of Ordinances – 1st Reading

and adopting the 2001 S-6 supplement to the code of ordinances. Mr. Deters read

Resolution No. 2003-R- 04 – Opposing Mandated State Health Insurance Coverage
30.   Mayor Moriconi presented for council’s approval a resolution that would
oppose legislation that would require local governments to pay an additional
monthly fee to the Kentucky Retirement System for each retired employee. Mr.
Wendling explained that the Kentucky League of Cities, who is concerned about
the effect this legislation will have on cities, has proposed this resolution.
He stated that the additional monthly fee that would be paid to the Retirement
System by the cities is an effort to combat the rising health insurance cost
for Kentucky teachers. He stated that this resolution is meant to send a
message of opposition of this mandate to the state legislators. Mr. Wendling
explained that while this will not affect Independence for a while, it could be
a hard hit in the future. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2003-R- 04.
31.   Council Member Bushong moved, with second by Council Member Yeager to
approve Resolution No. 2003-R-04 as read. Roll call was answered unanimously;
motion carried 6-0.

FEBRUARY 24, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL CAUCUS MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
24, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Independence Senior Citizens and Community Center
in Independence with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi
called the meeting to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. The roll was called
and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim
Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also present
was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters, City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling and
Finance Director, Janet Rebman.
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone to the first caucus meeting. He advised that
the caucus meetings would provide more flexibility for discussions and
basically be a pre-game for the regular business meeting on the first Monday of
each month.
Privileges of the Floor
Martin Neltner, 6239 Taylor Mill Road addressed council on three issues.
∙   Speed Limit on Route 16 – He expressed concern with the speed limit on
Route 16 (Taylor Mill Road). He feels the speed limit should be reduced to 35
mph and then enforced. Currently the speed limit fluctuates with most drivers
averaging 55 mph. There have already been a couple of fatalities on this road.
He suggested the city request the state highway department to do a study, as
something has to be done.
∙   Zoning Violations on his property located at 6445 Taylor Mill Road (the old
Cherokee Bowl) – Mr. Neltner expressed his frustration with the Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission and the hassle he feels they have unduly put
him through the past year regarding seeming zoning heating and air conditioning
unit violations at this location. He stated he has made $1,800,000 in
improvements to this building, and that the Planning Commission has cost him
dollars in construction delays, etc. He was upset that the Planning Commission
overlooked this aspect regarding the placement of these units when the
improvement plans were submitted to them for approval. This oversight cost him
an additional $4,000 for a fence to act as a buffer to the adjoining
properties. He wanted council to be aware of these issues that he has
encountered with the Planning Commission.
∙   Horse Arena on his property at 6239 Taylor Mill Road – He stated that he
initially received city support for this project but is currently been required
to go before the Board of Adjustments for a fifth time, which continues to
stall the project. He stated that he has not personally attended these meetings
as he is busy and has sent professionals to speak for him. He stated he has
never received the city’s concerns regarding this project in writing. He stated
this horse arena is not for profit. Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld,
commented that Mr. Neltner has received the general notifications of the Board
meetings.
Update on Lipscomb Annexation Issue
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters, provided a written report to council regarding
his research and opinion on Karen Lipscomb and John Schoborg’s dispute with the
city that their property (previously owned by their deceased father, Norb
Schoborg) was not annexed into the city in 1978. He advised that based on his
review of the city council meeting minutes of 1978, the map and legal
description of the annexed parcels, that everything looks to be in order. He
stated that the map that was attached to the ordinance on file at the county
courthouse removes any ambiguity even though the legal description of the
annexed parcels is a little irregular. But, he stated, that does not make it
invalid. He stated that in his legal opinion it is a valid annexation, which
includes the Lipscomb/Schoborg properties.
Ms. Lipscomb expressed some confusion with Mr. Deters findings and claims she
has been given conflicting information from the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission. Mr. Deters directed her to the County Clerk’s office and the
Planning Commission if she wants to pursue this matter and do further research.
Budget Amendment for Fiscal-Year 2002/03
Mayor Moriconi presented for council’s review a proposed budget amendment for
the current fiscal year. He advised he would like to have a first reading of
the ordinance at the March 3, 2003 regular council meeting, with the second
reading at the April meeting. He stated that Finance Director, Janet Rebman,
was present to point out the items that need to be amended.
Ms. Rebman pointed out the major amendments:
∙   Audited Fund Balances that were forwarded from the prior fiscal year – she
stated that these figures were estimated as the budget was adopted prior to the
city audit.
∙   Municipal Center Fund – big revision as the revenue was documented last
year and the carry forward amount reflects a $4,000,000 balance.
Mark Wendling pointed out other significant amendments:
∙   Resource Officer grants
∙   Amphitheater funds being transferred in to pay for design fees – he stated
that next year’s budget would provide for additional funds to be transferred in
to pay for the actual construction of the amphitheater.
∙   Snow Removal – budgeted $30,000, but to date the actual expenses well
exceed this amount. Mayor Moriconi advised that the city’s public works
employees clear approximately 25% of the city’s streets with the county
contracted to treat the remainder of the streets for the city. He stated that
he plans to offset some funds diverted from the Police Department salaries into
this line item, as the Police Department budget has surplus funds ($21,600) in
the personnel expenses due to employee’s absences due to workers compensation
and short-term disability leaves.
Police Chief, Shawn Butler pointed to some amendments in his budget:
∙   Increased revenues due to a grant received for the resource officers
∙   Over budget in Workers Compensation insurance – due to increase in premiums
∙   $109,000 in amendments will be pass thru expenses from the revenue received
from grants.
Mayor Moriconi advised council to review this proposed budget amendment in
preparation to have a first reading of the ordinance at next Monday’s business
meeting.
Mayor’s Priorities and Goals for 2003
Mayor Moriconi requested that each council member decide on his or her top two
goals to bring forth at the next caucus meeting.
He outlined his goals as listed below.
∙   Municipal Center
∙   Amphitheater

installation of sidewalks along the state maintained streets.
∙   Laptop Computers – to do away with council meeting packets, thereby

∙   Eliminate primary elections
∙   New “Welcome to the city” signs
∙   Random drug testing for employees
∙   Senior Center Sign
∙   City’s website – utilize more effectively
∙   Aggressively pursue light commercial development
∙   Recognition of Local Businesses – on a monthly basis, Mayor and each
council member will rotate each month a business they would like to acknowledge
by presenting a plaque or proclamation at each monthly business meeting. He
stated he would like to recognize Nick’s Grove Restaurant at the March meeting
Memorial Park Development Plan
Mayor introduced architects Ehmet Hayes and Joe Hayes, who made a Power Point
presentation of the plan they have developed for Memorial Park. Mayor Moriconi
advised he would like council to consider this Plan for adoption at the March
3, 2003 business meeting.
Mr. Ehmet Hayes advised this was a comprehensive plan that could be developed
in phases as the budget allowed. His proposal outlined cost estimates for
parking lots, access streets (a connector to Peach Drive and a new Memorial
Park Drive), improvements to the existing athletic (soccer/football) field,
playground, shelters, restrooms, lighting of Memorial Park Drive, amphitheater,
volleyball courts basketball courts, 8 foot asphalt walking trails, 4 foot
mulch trails, sidewalks, grading allowance, storm/sewer allowance, as well as a
contingency fund. Total cost $1,160,525.
Complete Master Plan for Memorial Park as designed by Robert Ehmet Hayes &
Associates Architects is attached to these minutes as part of the record.
Mayor Moriconi advised that the city currently has a fund balance of $256,000
reserved for the development of this park. He suggested using these funds to
proceed with the construction of the Phase I Platform Portion of the
amphitheater for $200,000, a restroom near the current shelter building and one
of the proposed parking lots.
Council Member Behler expressed concern that landscaping expenses were not part
of this proposal, as she feels this is an integral element to the
beautification of the park. Mr. Hayes stated no allowances were made for
landscaping, but it could be added.
Council Member Ketron asked if electric lines were currently in place. Mr.
Hayes advised electric lines are already in the park.
Mr. Hayes stated he would need an exact dollar figure from council in order to
develop the first phase of this development.
Council Member Bushong suggested that the city proceed with only two of the
facilities, as there will be architect fees associated with Phase I so that the
expenses do not exceed the current funds on hand. Council discussed the options
of constructing restrooms versus additional parking.
Mayor Moriconi advised council to review the enclosed contract for basic
services and associated fees proposed by the architect firm for Phase I of the
development plan that would include the amphitheater, restrooms near the
present shelter building and a parking lot east of the Senior Center.
Text Amendment for 5209 Madison Pike (Old Independence School House site)
The property owners addressed council regarding their development plans for
this building. Mr. Wendling advised council that the owners approached the city
several months ago with their plan for this building and the owners were
advised that there are no provisions in the city’s zoning ordinance that would
permit a church or mosque in a Neighborhood Commercial (NC) zone.
One of the owners, George Soister, advised that they would like to restore the
building and remodel to accommodate a residence for two Tibetan Buddhist Monks
as well as hold religious services in the building.
Mr. Wendling advised this property is not on the historical register and would
probably not meet requirements, as it does not have the original windows.
Council Member Ellison suggested the text amendment allow for a “conditional
use” and include a two-story dwelling. Mr. Deters agreed that it would be more
appropriate as a “conditional use.” Council Member Ellison agreed that making a
text amendment would give the city more control instead of the Planning
Commission.
Mr. Wendling stated the text amendment application fee is $150.00, which the
property owners have agreed to pay. He stated the process would take a few
months and that after the application is made it would probably be May before
the city receives a recommendation from the Planning Commission for approval/
disapproval of this request. Then council would act on that recommendation.
Appointment of Council Committee Chairs (Department Liaisons)
Mayor Moriconi appointed Department Chairs and stated he would ask for a report
from each at the caucus meetings.

contact – Annie Wuestefeld (NKAPC – contracted Zoning Administrator)

∙   Administration & Personnel - Council Member Jim Ellison with primary staff
contact City Clerk Patricia Taney
∙   Public Works - Council Member Carol Franzen with primary staff contact
Public Works Crew Leader Jeff Smith
∙   Parks & Recreation - Council Member Donna Yeager with primary staff contact
Recreation Director Nita Brake
Appointment of Citation Officer, Zoning Administrator – Annie Wuestefeld
Mr. Wendling advised the city needed to add to the list of current citation
officers for the city, Annie Wuestefeld who also acts as the city’s Zoning
Administrator. He stated that the former Zoning Administrator, Rich McAllister
had held this position, but Annie has taken his place. He stated that since she
has not been appointed as a citation officer for the city she currently has to
take a police officer with her to perform these duties. Mayor Moriconi advised
this is not a new position as she is already the Zoning Administrator for
Independence as a contracted service through the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission. Council discussed providing Ms. Wuestefeld with proper
identification.
Mayor Moriconi advised that the city attorney would draft the necessary
resolution to appoint her as a citation officer for the city and it would be
presented at the March 3, 2003 business meeting for council’s consideration.
Simon Kenton High School Project Prom Donation
Simon Kenton High School has made their annual request for this contribution to
their Project Prom party. The City Clerk advised they city has donated $500.00
each year for the last few years as well as donations to the Independence Lions
Club for the annual Easter Egg Hunt. City attorney, Mr. Deters expressed is
concern over the legality of using tax dollars to make these kinds of
donations. He will research this and report back to council at a future
meeting.
Miscellaneous Discussion
Council Member Bushong expressed concern that the Senior Center generated very
little revenue for rental of the facility last year and suggested the building
needed more paying customers to offset some of the expenses of the Center. He
reported that it was rented seventeen times and generated only $2,400.00. He
would like the city to come up with ideas to generate interest in renting this
building. The Senior Center Director, Joan Bowling stated she is working on
this.
Council Member Bushong addressed the issue of job titles for employees and
suggested looking into a change for the Recreation Director due to high workers
compensation insurance premiums for this position. He feels it could save the
city some money. Council Members Ellison and Yeager voiced their objection to
changing the job title of this position. Council Member Yeager stated the high
premiums are not just in this job position and was concerned if the title was
changed it may be a loss of a city department. Council Member Ellison commented
that the high premiums are based on claim experience.
Adjournment:
There being no further business to discuss, Council Member Franzen moved to
adjourn, with a second by Council Member Ellison. Motion carried and the
meeting adjourned at 9:35 p.m.

FEBRUARY 24, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special
Session on Monday, February 24, 2003 at 6:32 p.m. in the Independence Senior
Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Chris Moriconi presiding in the Chair.
Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. The roll was called and the
following council members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim
Ellison, Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also present was Jed K.
Deters, City Attorney and Mark T. Wendling, City Administrator.
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   Refinancing of the Municipal Center Bond – Ordinance No. 2003-O-02 – Second
Reading
∙   Adopting the Codification of Ordinances – Ordinance No. 2003-O-03 – Second
Reading
∙   Adoption of Resolution No. 2003-R-05 Regarding the Brent Spence Bridge
Ordinance No. 2003-O-02 – Authorizing the Issuance of Municipal Center Project
Refunding Bonds, Series 2003 – 2nd Reading
3.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for second reading of a proposed
ordinance that would authorize the issuance of general obligation public
project refunding bonds, Series 2003 in an aggregate principal amount not to
exceed $5,000,000. Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to read the ordinance.
Mr. Deters read the ordinance in summary and pointed out that there was a minor
change in the wording; that in fact the current bond lease is with the Kentucky
Municipal Finance Corporation and not Kentucky League of Cities Funding Trust.
He cited case law that supported his opinion that this change in wording was
not sufficient reason to warrant a new first reading of the ordinance.
4.   Mayor Moriconi asked for a motion on this second reading of Ordinance No.
2003-O-02. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by Council Member
Bushong. Roll call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2003-O-03 – Adopting the Codification of Ordinances 2001 S-
6 Supplement – 2nd Reading
5.   Mayor Moriconi presented for second reading a proposed ordinance enacting
and adopting the 2001 S-6 supplement to the code of ordinances. Mr. Deters read
the proposed ordinance. Council Member Yeager moved, with second by Council
Member Behler to approve the second reading of Ordinance No. 2003-O- 03. Roll
call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0. Mr. Deters advised
the code of ordinances is updated every two years.
Resolution No. 2003-R- 05 – Requesting Federal Funding for the Brent Spence
Bridge Replacement
6.   Mayor Moriconi presented for council’s consideration Resolution No. 2003-
R- 05 urging congress to provide full funding of the TEA-21 reauthorization and
funding for the Brent Spence Bridge replacement. He read the resolution and
requested a motion for adoption. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second
by Council Member Franzen. A brief discussion ensued wherein Council Member
Ellison commented that the language of the resolution contained generic
literature and he made suggestions to provide more personalization. Mayor
Moriconi stated that a draft resolution was supplied to the cities by way of
Bill Goetz, City Administrator of Ft. Mitchell. Mr. Wendling commented that the
resolution probably originated from OKI (Ohio-Kentucky-Indiana Regional
Council). Council Member Bushong moved to amend his motion to insert the
language suggested by Council Member Ellison, with Council Member Franzen
agreeing to amend her second. Council Member Bushong asked how the Brent Spence
Bridge project would be funded if the federal government does not agree to
provide the funding. Mr. Wendling commented that the responsibility might fall
on the local cities, although most do not have the adequate resources to fund
this sizeable project. At this time roll call was taken to adopt Resolution No.
2003-R-05 and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Adjournment
7.   Upon motion by Council Member Ellison and second by Council Member Ketron
the meeting was adjourned at 6:45 p.m.

MARCH 3, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
March 3, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with
Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant of Grace Community
Church gave the invocation. Mayor Moriconi congratulated Reverend Bryant on the
one-year anniversary of the establishment of the Grace Community Church in the
city. The roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters and City Administrator,
Mark T. Wendling.
Presentation of Business Award
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated he would like to initiate a new tradition by
recognizing the local businesses in Independence and has chosen Nick’s Grove
Restaurant as the first recipient of this tribute. He advised that he and the
council members would take turns designating a recipient of the business award
on a monthly basis to be presented at the first meeting of each month. Mayor
Moriconi introduced Becky and Vito Casullo, who are the proprietors of Nick’s
Grove, and presented them with a plaque in recognition of their civic and
economic contributions to Independence. Mr. Casullo said that Nick’s Grove
Restaurant has been a presence in the city since it’s opening fifty-seven years
ago by his father. He thanked Mayor Moriconi and council by saying that he was
honored to be the first business to receive this recognition and advised the
plaque would be proudly displayed in the restaurant.
Approval of the Minutes of the February 3, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February
3, 2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Bushong so moved, with
second from Council Member Ketron. No amendments were noted and roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the February 24, 2003 Special Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February
24, 2003 special meeting of council. Council Member Bushong moved, with second
from Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted and roll call was
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the February 24, 2003 Caucus Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February
24, 2003 caucus meeting of council. Council Member Bushong so moved, with
second from Council Member Franzen. City Attorney, Jed Deters, noted a
necessary correction in the last paragraph on page one. The amendment was noted
and roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
6.   Mayor Moriconi advised no one signed in to address council and moved on to
the business on the agenda
Resolution No. 2003-R-06 – Adoption of the Development Plan for Memorial Park
by Robert Ehmet Hayes Architects
7.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for consideration, Resolution No.
2003-R-06 that would adopt a master development plan for Memorial Park as
designed by Robert Ehmet Hayes & Associates and would enable the city to
develop individual aspects of the park as funds become available. Mr. Deters
read the resolution.
8.   Council Member Bushong moved, with second by Council Member Franzen to
adopt Resolution No. 2003-R-06. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member
Behler asked if this plan has been revised to include cost estimates for
landscaping in the park. Mr. Hayes stated that a $150,000 allowance has been
included in this Master Plan for landscaping expenses that could be phased in
as the various sections of the park are developed. He suggested that creative
solutions be applied with an emphasis on maintaining the natural landscape.
Council Member Bushong asked how the city’s current Memorial Tree Program would
work into the landscaping; would the trees be planted only in certain areas of
the park or throughout. Mr. Hayes stated that nothing is firm at this time, but
suggested it may be practical to identify key features of the park by
determining a landscaping design.
9.   There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi requested the clerk call
the roll. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2003-R-07 – Authorizing a Contract With Robert Ehmet Hayes &
Associates for the Design of the Proposed Amphitheater & Restroom Facilities of
the Memorial Park Master Plan
10.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for consideration, Resolution No.
2003-R-07 that would authorize him to enter into a contract with Robert Ehmet
Hayes & Associates for design services of the platform aspect of the
amphitheater and restroom facilities for Memorial Park. Mr. Deters read the
resolution.
11.   Council Member Yeager moved, with second by Council Member Behler to
adopt Resolution No. 2003-R-07. A lengthy discussion ensued regarding the
facilities that could be constructed with the existing funds that have been set
aside for the project. Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Hayes if he was able to
design a smaller restroom facility as discussed at the caucus meeting that
would fit into the city’s budget for this first phase of development in
Memorial Park. Mr. Hayes responded that he is conscience of the fact that the
city does not want to experience overruns on this project and has spoken to
local contractors to get a sense of current cost estimates. He recommended the
city take each fixture and scale it down to meet the budget allowance or place
focus on building each facility independently with minimal amenities, such as
landscaping around that facility. Council Member Bushong asked about building
the restroom feature on the rear of the amphitheater. Mr. Hayes advised that
that feature of the amphitheater would be costly as restrooms in that area of
the park would require a lift station over the hill. Mayor Moriconi commented
than an effort should be made to get the cost of restrooms down to about
$30,000. Mr. Hayes advised that a simple cement block structure, without
landscaping, would cost a minimum $40,000-$50,000.
12.   Council Member Yeager and Mr. Wendling discussed the current funds the
city has set aside for the construction of the amphitheater. Council Member
Yeager advised that the $200,000 granted to the city from the state has to be
used for the exclusive purpose of constructing an amphitheater. Council Member
Franzen commented that she would love to see an amphitheater built, but it
needs to be completed with restrooms. Council Member Yeager commented that the
funds for this project are not tax dollars, but donations that are designated
for the construction of the amphitheater, not restrooms. Council Member Bushong
stated he supports the construction of restrooms in the park, but also feels
the need for the amphitheater. He asked Mr. Hayes what it would cost to build a
small serviceable restroom facility near the amphitheater site. Mr. Hayes
stated he would have to take time to reassess that notion of a freestanding
restroom facility in the area.
13.   Mr. Wendling advised that the city received the $200,000 state grant
about three years ago and received a two-year extension last year that will
expire in June 2004. Mr. Hayes suggested that the amphitheater be downsized to
keep the building cost around $150,000. Council Member Yeager commented that
she would prefer not to build it at all, if a cheaper version of the design
plan is all the city can afford. Council Member Franzen suggested building just
the amphitheater and consider restrooms later. Mayor Moriconi commented the
city should proceed with the amphitheater, as the grant money has to be spent
by June 2004. Mr. Hayes suggested that both structures could be scaled back to
meet the budget constraints. Council Member Ellison voiced his objection to
scaling back on the amphitheater. He stated that the state grant of $200,000
was designated for the amphitheater and felt that the state may be critical of
a city that requests more funds than will be used for a specific project.
Council Member Behler suggested seeking additional funds, such as grants and/or
donations, or selling the naming rights of the amphitheater, to obtain the
extra revenue needed to develop this phase of the park so that downsizing would
not be necessary. Mr. Hayes suggested proceeding with the amphitheater as
designed and review other options for restrooms. Mayor Moriconi commented that
some citizens have come forward in the past with an interest in contributing
their labor to construct restrooms in the park, with the city just paying for
the cost of materials.
14.   Mr. Deters advised that the discussion has not resulted in any amendments
that would be necessary to the resolution as read. Mayor Moriconi requested the
clerk call the roll. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Budget Amendment
15.   Mayor Moriconi advised that he has decided to postpone a budget amendment
until all expenses for the snow removal have come to an end. He will present an
amended budget for the current fiscal year at a later date.
Random Drug Testing for City Employees
16.   Mayor Moriconi stated that at the last caucus meeting he mentioned that
one of his goals would be to establish a random drug-testing program for city
employees and has since learned there may be some legal issues with this type
of policy. Mr. Deters advised that random drug testing is legal and could be
implemented if accomplished pursuant to Kentucky Statute. Mayor Moriconi asked
the Chief of Police, Shawn Butler, to speak on this matter. Chief Butler stated
that currently his officers are only drug tested as part of the hiring process.
He stated that last year the city set up an EAP (Employee Assistance Program)
through St. Elizabeth Medical Center. He stated he would review options, such
as where the testing would take place and the costs associated with this type
of program. He stated he feels it is time to implement such a policy and the
goal would be to develop one that is legally defensible. Chief Butler stated he
would collect some information to present at the April or May council caucus
meeting.
City Administrator Report – Mark T. Wendling
17.   Mr. Wendling advised that the next meeting of the Municipal Government
League of Northern Kentucky would be held at the City of Wilder offices.
18.   He also reported that due to the inclement weather this winter, snow/ice
removal expenses have well exceeded the $30,000 that was budgeted.
Mayor’s Report - Christian J. Moriconi
19.   Mayor Moriconi advised of appointments to be made to the Board of
Adjustments as well as the appointment of a citation officer for the city, and
presented Executive Orders for council’s endorsement.
Executive Order No. 2003-EO-05 – Appointing Margaret Anne (Annie) Wuestefeld as
Citation Officer
Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2003-EO-05 repealing the designation of
Mark Wendling, Rich McAllister, Jeff Smith, Kevin Barbian and Diane Collins as
appointed citation officers pursuant to KRS 83A.130(7) and appointing Annie
Wuestefeld as the sole Citation Officer for Independence. Council Member
Franzen moved, with a second by Council Member Ellison to approve this
appointment. Council Member Bushong asked why only one person would be the
designated citation officer. Mr. Wendling explained that in consulting with Mr.
Deters it was discovered that because the above-mentioned people have not
received training necessary of citation officers that any citation issued by
those persons would not be upheld in a court of law. Mr. Deters stated that the
appointment of a citation officer should be based on their qualifications. Roll
call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0 in favor.
Executive Order No. 2003-EO-06 – Re-Appointing Tom Jump to the Board of
Adjustments
Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2003-EO-06 re-appointing Tom Jump to
the Board of Adjustments for a four-year term that would expire on March 14,
2007. Council Member Ellison moved, with second by Council Member Bushong to
approve this appointment. Council Member Ellison expressed gratitude for the
many years of service Mr. Jump has devoted to the city as a member of this
Board. Mr. Deters commented that Mr. Jump does an excellent job on the Board.
Roll was called; motion carried unanimously.
Executive Order No. 2003-EO-07 – Re-Appointing Scott Holten to the Board of
Adjustments
Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2003-EO-07 re-appointing Scott Holten
to a four-year term on the Board of Adjustments that would expire on March 14,
2007. Council Member Ellison moved, with second by Council Member Yeager to
approve this appointment. Council Member Ellison also expressed gratitude to
Mr. Holten for his years of dedicated service to this Board. Roll call was
answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Miscellaneous Comments
20.   Council Member Franzen asked if there was any development on the
possibility of changing the title of the Recreation Director as discussed at
the last caucus meeting. Mr. Deters stated that matter is being reviewed.
Adjournment
21.   There being no further business, Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to
adjourn. Council Member Ellison so moved, with second by Council Member Ketron.
Motion carried unanimously and the meeting adjourned at 8:52 p.m.
