MARCH 29, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
CITY COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
SPECIAL BUDGET SUMMIT
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special Session
on Saturday, March 29, 2003 at 9:00 a.m. in the Independence Senior Citizens
and Community Center with Mayor Chris Moriconi presiding in the Chair. Mayor
Moriconi promptly called the meeting to order. The following council members
were present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen, and
Donna Yeager. Council Member Otis Ketron was absent. Also present was City
Administrator, Mark T. Wendling and City Clerk, Patricia Taney. Mayor Moriconi
stated that the purpose of this special meeting was to review and discuss a
preliminary draft budget for the 2003/04 fiscal year. He stated that each
department head would present for council’s consideration a departmental budget
proposal, with explanations for special requests that would help them in
performing their jobs more effectively. Mayor Moriconi stated that this process
is an effort to keep everyone involved and informed along the way to adopting
the budget in June.
Mayor Moriconi advised that some increases in the draft budget couldn’t be
predicted, such as the 20% increase in the health insurance for employees. He
also advised that the current budget was adopted with the assumption that
implementing another tax, such as a road tax or insurance preminum tax, would
raise $200,000 in revenue. He advised that no additional tax was adopted as
assumed. Mayor Moriconi pointed to the Building Fund allocation was decreased
from $400,000 to $270,000 per year due to the re-financing of that loan. He
also advised that another expense that could not be foreseen was the increase
in the snow and ice removal from $30,000 to around $100,000 due to the severe
winter conditions.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that the budget process would be to have a first
reading of the ordinance at the May 5th business meeting with the second
reading and adoption of the ordinance at the June 2nd council meeting. In
closing he reiterated that this budget proposal is preliminary and wanted
everyone to have adequate time to review and discuss before voting for adoption
in June.
Police Department – Chief, Shawn Butler
Police Chief, Shawn Butler presented his budget proposal and pointed out the
following highlights –
∙   Total proposed budget $2,394,936.50 – Reflecting an 11.6% increase over
last year’s budget
∙   Employee salary - Increases – majority would receive only a 2.4% consumer
price index (CPI) increase. $212,693 of the salaries line item is funded by
outside sources
∙   School Resource Officers (SRO) – this budget will reflect the first full
year for these salaries
∙   2 Additional Police Officers – Maximum salary of $72,600 for two mid-level
officers. The salary is based on years of service as a police officer. He
stated that the last time the police department had an increase in staff was
1998. He stated the department has experienced a 127% increase in calls for
service and that the population has grown by 25%. He stated that resident
growth has the highest demand for police service. In addition, the city has
recently annexed over 500 acres of land that will be residential development.
Have not asked for additional officers before now, as the need for equipment,
especially a new fleet of cruisers, took priority. Equipment concerns has been
overcome and now feels the need to move forward with additional staff.
∙   Pointed out that volunteer service has increased and the department has
established cooperative efforts with the Kenton County Police to further
develop community programs.
∙   National police staffing levels is recommended at 2.6 officers for every
1000 residents. He recommends 1.9-2.0 per 1000 residents, as he is cognizant
there are revenue issues. Still, the city needs to look to the future.
∙   Salary raises should be 3% in salary scale steps.
∙   Health, Workers Compensation and property insurance premiums are uncertain
at this time. He expects that the price of gasoline may increase also, but this
too will be an uncontrollable expense Overtime pay for the city’s Special
Events have been a drain on the budget.
∙   Police Cruisers – this line item will be drastically reduced next year as
the leased and older fleet has been aggressively replaced with new cars and now
he will recommend that a rotation system be implemented to keep the fleet up-
to-date.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the proposed amount of wages for the request of two new
officers included the cost of two cruisers. Chief Butler stated that it did not
include vehicles, but felt he would only need to purchase one vehicle as he has
a spare older vehicle that could be used for a second new officer. Council
Member Bushong asked if the health insurance increase of 20% was definite. Mr.
Wendling replied that the city has received the renewal quote, which is 20%.
Council Member Behler asked if the two new hires that Chief Butler is
requesting would be School Resource Officers. Chief Butler said no, that the
SRO positions were funded by a state grant for the next three years. Council
Member Behler asked why Chief Butler wanted to hire mid-level officers versus
rookies. Chief Butler explained that hiring experienced officers provides an
immediate impact as they can be released onto the street sooner, after fifteen
weeks of field training. He stated that a recruit would have to be trained as a
police officer, which has associated costs for the city, then go through field
training, making it nearly one year before the city realizes a benefit from
that hire. Council Member Yeager asked how many police officers the city
currently has. Chief Butler stated he has twenty-three patrol officers and two
school resource officers for a total of twenty-five. He stated that school
resource officer Scott Paul will do patrol duty for a few weeks in the summer,
but not enough to make up the difference. Mayor Moriconi asked about the
cruiser lease payment that is proposed as $145,388.00. He asked how much this
would level off. Chief Butler replied that the following year there would be a
drastic reduction in this line item, by $72,000, and then future years the
amount should stay close to $65,000 annually. Mr. Wendling asked how many
cruisers would be replaced each year. Chief Butler replied that the plan is to
keep each vehicle seven years, with three vehicles replacement each year, but
that is dependent on staffing levels. Mayor Moriconi asked about property
insurance and if the proposed expense would change with the move to a new
building or was the budgeted amount for personal property that the department
currently has. Mr. Wendling advised that the cost of property insurance is
always divided between the departments and that the amount listed is for
contents of the rented space in the courthouse and auto insurance. He stated
that by dividing the expense between the departments it keeps each division
vigilant and responsible for that department’s personal property.
Senior Citizens and Community Center – Joan Bowling, Director
Senior Director, Joan Bowling presented her budget proposal and pointed out the
following highlights –
∙   Proposed budget is $171,937.00
∙   Rental revenue is currently up by 20% - Gradually this revenue is
increasing each year. She has budgeted this low but thinks it may come in
higher.
∙   Senior Board of Directors have committed to paying $20,000 toward her
salary next year.
∙   Utilities (gas/electric) are proposed at a 6.1% increase due to the cold
winter this year. Telephone expenses will also increase due to the city’s
Recreation Department housing its office at the Senior Center.
∙   Maintenance and Janitorial Services – estimated a 4.2% increase for
maintenance of the building and a 20% increase for the janitorial services. The
janitorial service cleans the building twice per week and provides setup and
breakdown, if needed, for the building rentals.
Mayor Moriconi commented that he will ask the Kenton County Fiscal Court
members to consider providing the Senior/Community Center with continued
financial support, as this Center is used by other county residents living
outside the city limits.
Council Member Franzen asked how the janitorial service charged the city, and
suggested the renters do their own cleanup. Ms. Bowling replied the service
charges by the hour and that each renter is informed they must clean up after
their event or risk losing their security deposit. Council discussed the
building maintenance issue as well as the opening/closing of the building for
every rented event and the option of continuing to hire this service out to a
company or hire personnel to perform these duties.
Ms. Bowling stated, that because of Health Department concerns, locks are
needed on the kitchen doors and that a food service window, that can be locked,
needs to be installed in that open space. She stated that currently renters are
told they are not permitted use of the kitchen, but without locks on the doors,
it is impossible to enforce. Council Member Ellison commented that fire codes
may prohibit the locking of the kitchen doors. Mayor Moriconi noticed that Ms.
Bowling budgeted $2,800.00 for the building expenses and wondered if that would
be enough to purchase a shutter for the food service window. Ms. Bowling stated
yes.
Mr. Wendling commented that a couple things the Senior/Community building is in
need of is an outdoor sign and the installation of cable television connection
lines, which have not been added to this budget proposal. He stated that the
Board has discussed the option of cable versus satellite hookups and have
concluded that the expense of $3,000-$4,000 to run the cable lines will be less
costly in the end as the building will receive free cable access. He stated
that they would investigate the possibility of the cable company absorbing the
expense of installing the cable lines to the building as the conduit has been
run from he building to the street. He advised that the Senior Board has
approved sharing this expense with the city if the cable company will not
install the line free of charge. Council Member Bushong advised that some
television signals can be accessed through telephone cable lines and suggested
that option be investigated.
The Council Members also discussed the significance of retaining membership
with the telecommunications board and consensus was that it might be worthwhile
and more profitable for the city to discontinue being represented by this
group.
Public Works Department – Jeff Smith, Crew Leader
Mr. Smith, Crew Leader for the Public Works Department presented his budget
proposal and pointed out the following highlights –
∙   Increase in salaries – 8% for himself and 6% for the other employee.
∙   Additional Staff – Is requesting one new full time employee at a salary of
$24,000. He stated the reason for a new employee is due to an influx of calls
for service and the increased amount of managerial duties he is faced with
every day. The additional employee could work along side of his current
employee (Ken Hicks) while he is doing paper work, attending meetings, etc. He
stated it is also a safety issue and that many of their tasks require a second
pair of hands. He stated that one of them works alone when the other is on
vacation or away at training, etc.
∙   Equipment – Mr. Smith is requesting an allocation of $29,000 to purchase a
bobcat and trailer. He stated this piece of equipment would have multiple uses,
from street cleaning to asphalt removal and restoration work, as well as work
in the parks. He stated that currently when the city needs this machine that it
is rented at a rate of $250 per day.
Council Member Yeager asked how much was spent this past year on the rental of
this type of equipment. Mr. Smith responded that because of the rental cost,
they did not utilize a bobcat very often. Council Member Franzen asked if the
purchase of a bobcat would save dollars in other areas of the budget. He
replied that the equipment rental line item could be reduced from $7,500 to
$2,000. Mr. Wendling asked what the average life span was for a bobcat. Mr.
Smith replied 15-20 years. Mayor Moriconi asked if Mr. Smith was capable of
performing the routine maintenance of this machinery. He replied that minimal
maintenance would be required. Mayor Moriconi asked what the cost would be for
a trailer to haul the bobcat. Mr. Smith stated that the requested amount of
$29,000 would include a trailer. Council Member Bushong asked about purchasing
a used bobcat. Mr. Smith replied that a used bobcat would cost around $10-
15,000, with an additional $5,000 for the trailer and stated that more
maintenance expense would be involved with a used bobcat. Mr. Smith advised
that the purchase of a bobcat, would realize a savings in other areas of the
budget, with the reduction or elimination of other line item allocations such
as street sweeping.
Mayor Moriconi commented that Mr. Smith is requesting a significant increase in
street repairs line item – from $240,000 to $750,000. Mr. Smith advised there
are currently 228 city maintained streets and that 15 of those are in desperate
need of replacement or partial repair. He stated that past citizen surveys have
concluded that the residents consider the streets to be a priority issue. Mayor
Moriconi stated that this proposed figure does not include Clubhouse Drive. Mr.
Wendling stated that the city engineer has advised that Clubhouse will not
require a sub grade as it has about ten years of life left.
Council Member Franzen asked if a part-time employee would fulfill his need for
additional help. Mr. Smith advised that the department currently has funds
allocated for seasonal help and that this position could be eliminated with a
year round full-time employee. Council Member Yeager suggested a part-time year
round employee that could work 20-25 hours each week. Council Member Behler
asked if the city could save on street repair expenses if the hiring of an
additional full-time employee is approved. Mr. Smith stated that major street
repairs are always contracted out, because it requires more people and large
equipment. He stated that he and Ken currently do some of the sectional street
repairs. He stated he is currently working with the city engineer to finalize a
street repair list. Council Member Bushong asked if it would be ready by the
next meeting. Mr. Wendling advised the city engineer is in the process of
updating the street inventory and he will provide an estimated cost of repairs
and/or replacements. He stated the engineer has suggested the city get on a
rotating basis of concrete repairs one year and asphalt the next, as this will
affect the repair quotes received. He stated that the city engineer has also
determined that the sub grade of some of the streets are in adequate condition
with several years of lifetime remaining. The discussion turned to Fleming
Drive and the need for major repairs. Mr. Smith commented that the city added
50 new streets last year and will probably add another 30 this year. Council
Member Ellison advised that the city should begin a program of sealing the new
streets to prolong the life. He stated that many of the older streets in the
city were not built to today’s specifications. There was a brief discussion
about who pays for the replacement of street lights (bulbs) and street signs.
Council was advised that the electric companies (Owen Electric and Cinergy)
replace street light bulbs and that the street signs are installed by the city.
Recreation Department – Nita Brake, Recreation Director
Ms. Brake presented her budget proposal for the 2003/04 fiscal year and pointed
out the following highlights –
∙   Proposed Salary Increase 33% - from $26,372 to $35,000. She stated she was
hired on as a part-time employee in 1998 at $13,000 and is only making $26,000
now, four years later. She stated that the average salary for her position, as
determined by the NKADD salary survey, is $36,378.
∙   Estimated increases for retirement and insurances (medical, workers comp,
etc.)
∙   Deleted seasonal employee – She stated she has used Kenton County inmates
this past year, but has been unable to obtain this help for the last few weeks,
so she now has a seasonal employee for this spring/summer.
∙   Added new line items – for the fuel and maintenance of the old cruiser that
is being used.
∙   Safety Surface for the parks – this would be to add new surface on top the
existing surface - $3,500
∙   New park in the Glenhurst Subdivision will probably require lawn
maintenance – but did not propose an amount in this budget.
∙   Special Events – increased this line item from $18,700 to $20,000. Will
attempt to get sponsorship of some of the events
∙   Seasonal Decorations – street banners for the Cherokee and Beechgrove
areas.
∙   Restroom Facilities in Memorial Park – proposed budget of $50,000
∙   Equipment purchase – Lawn Mowers $20,000 and Trailer $3,000. Would like to
purchase two large riding mowers and gas powered weedeaters. She stated the
city could discontinue contracting out lawn maintenance each year if these
items were purchased and the city hired part time help to cut the grass. She
stated that the city could hire local college students from March through
November to perform this labor.
Council Member Ellison asked if the fireworks expense has increased each year.
Ms. Brake responded that last year was the first increase since the inception
of this event. She stated that this year’s July 4th Celebration will include a
live broadcast on channel 106.5 playing music along with the fireworks.
Mayor Moriconi asked how she arrived at the $50,000 estimate for the restroom
facility in Memorial Park. She replied that the estimate was based on a smaller
building constructed of concrete block, which will also be low maintenance.
Council Member Bushong asked if this was based on the assumption that a water
line is already in place. Mayor Moriconi replied yes.
Mayor Moriconi questioned the need for lawn mowers and a trailer. Ms. Brake
replied that other cities do not contract out for lawn maintenance. She stated
that the lawn maintenance expense increases each year. She stated that the city
could hire seasonal help to do this work and it would be less expensive.
Council Member Behler asked if Recreation is requesting equipment for tasks
that should be performed by the Public Works Department. Ms. Brake stated that
other cities separate parks and public works responsibilities. Mr. Wendling
advised that the Public Works employees do assist Ms. Brake with various tasks
such as mulching and/or hanging the street banners.
Ms. Brake advised that she did not make budget allocations for some of the
parks. She stated that the newly acquired park in the Glenhurst Subdivision may
need lawn maintenance, but that the developer has not installed any park
equipment as agreed upon. Mr. Wendling stated the city would meet with the
developer to determine the equipment and/or facilities that they will install.
Administration Department – Patricia Taney, City Clerk
Ms. Taney presented a proposal budget for the 2003/04 fiscal year and pointed
out the following highlights –
∙   Salary adjustments for the Deputy Clerk and the Secretary positions. Ms.
Taney explained that these positions are 12-15% below average compared to other
local cities that have these positions on staff. She requested these positions
salaries be raised to other comparable wages.
∙   Other related personnel expenses – Ms. Taney noted these are expenses the
city has little control over. She stated that the state retirement program will
increase by 1% and the workers compensation premium for office employees will
increase by .03 cents.
∙   Medical Insurance – Have received a renewal quote of 20.56% increase for
all city employees (not just administration). Reported that the she and Mr.
Wendling will meet with the city’s insurance agent to review quotes that have
been proposed by other companies. Do not anticipate that these quotes will be
much lower that the renewal rate of 20.56%, but wanted council to know that the
city is shopping for the best possible insurance price without losing benefits.
∙   Utilities for the building – actual increase is unknown - guesstimated a
15% increase.
∙   Dues/Fees/Subscriptions – proposed a 15% increase, based on actual to date.
∙   PVA assessments – estimated an 8% increase (high) do not expect that much
∙   No other line items were increased. No requests for equipment this year,
will hold off until the offices are settled in the new Municipal Center.
Mr. Wendling commented that the line item for the city attorney reflects a
significant increase due to the on-going legal fees for the lawsuit for which
Lawson Walker is handling for the city. He also commented that the auto lease
for his car will reflect a 29% increase to make the second payment on a three
year loan to purchase the car.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the budget proposal does not reflect two months
of new expenses associated with the move into the new Municipal Center.
General Discussion on Expenditures and Department Budget Requests
Mayor Moriconi informed council that he recently met with a consultant who acts
as a lobbyist for various entities. He suggested it might be worthwhile for the
city to hire a lobbyist that could be a voice for Independence down state to
obtain funding for sidewalks, roads, etc. He asked council to consider
contracting with this lobbyist as an option to raising revenues; the cost of
the lobbyist would be about $10-$15,000 per year. Council Member Behler asked
what other businesses he represented. Mayor Moriconi replied that he worked for
non-profit, government and private businesses and named the City of Florence,
Tri-Ed and the Chamber of Commerce as a few of his clients. Mayor Moriconi
stated he would invite him to a caucus meeting so that he could explain his
services to council.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that if all department requests were approved
that the city’s reserve fund would be reduced to about $700,000 from the
current $1,500,000. Mr. Wendling informed council that the salaries in the
Mayor’s proposed budget only reflects a 2.4% cost of living increase and does
not reflect the department requests.
Council Member Bushong questioned the revenue shortfall of $200,000 in the
current budget. Mr. Wendling stationed that an amended budget would be
presented for council to adopt at the April or May meeting. Finance Director,
Janet Rebman advised that because the city experienced unbudgeted corresponding
income, ultimately there was not a significant shortfall.
Mayor Moriconi commented that he is hesitant to approve a budget that will
reduce the reserve fund so dramatically. Council Member Ellison commented that
the city might want to consider a hiring freeze. Council Member Franzen stated
that she feels council needs to approve at least one new police officer.
Council Member Ellison replied the he felt the city needed to get some current
salaries up to par before hiring additional staff. He voiced skepticism with
the salary survey conducted by the NKADD.
Council Member Franzen agreed that the employees in the Administration
Department should be brought up to comparable levels. She also stated she would
agree to a used bobcat for the Public Works Department. Council Member Bushong
questioned the possibility of consolidating some public services with Kenton
County, as well as Parks services. Mayor Moriconi stated he has recently
learned that Kenton County Public Works also subs out lawn maintenance
Council Member Behler suggested that police services could also be consolidated
with county. Council Member Ellison commented that Boone County recently
consolidated policing services. Mayor Moriconi stated that consolidating public
works services versus police services was like comparing apples to oranges.
Council Member Bushong commented that the city is too large to consider
consolidating police services. Council Member Ellison stated that he felt the
city could have contracted for snow removal services with someone other than
the county at a much cheaper rate.
Mayor Moriconi stated that the Police Department has not added a new officer in
five years. Council Member Behler responded that other departments have not
added staff either. Mr. Wendling commented that the Public Works department is
facing safety concerns by lacking the adequate staff to complete certain tasks.
Council Member Yeager asked if the crew leader performed tasks also. Mr.
Wendling replied yes, as well as managerial duties, but another person is
needed to assist the laborer when the crew leader is handling managerial
business. He advised that many of their tasks require two sets of hands.
Council Member Ellison stated he is not opposed to expanding the Public Works
Department but in light of the fact that the department does not have a
permanent facility to work out of he does not feel that expansion is reasonable
now. He stated he also does not want to get in a position that would
necessitate job layoffs. Council Member Franzen commented that the city has a
lot going on and cannot afford to initiate a hiring freeze. Mayor Moriconi
stated that this proposed budget includes the addition of two new police hires
and an additional $500,000 of road repair expenses. Council Member Ellison
asked Ms. Rebman to point out the areas of the budget that were excessive. Ms.
Rebman responded by saying each department knows the areas of their budget that
could be cut and suggested that each department be responsible for reducing
their budget to an established amount.
Discussion on Revenue Enhancement
Ms. Rebman advised council that the reserve fund will be down to zero unless
the revenues are increased or expenditures are decreased. Mayor Moriconi
informed council that information regarding the insurance premium tax was
inserted in their packet. Mr. Wendling gave a brief synopsis of this tax. He
stated that essentially this tax is an occupational license fee on insurance
companies and that all types of insurance premiums can be taxed. He discouraged
taxing life and health insurance premiums. He stated that the city could impose
a rate between 5% and 12%. He stated this tax could generate a minimum of
$600,000 revenue for the city. Mr. Wendling advised that the only other major
city in Northern Kentucky, besides Independence, that has a population over
5,000 that has not imposed this tax is Edgewood. He stated that Edgewood has
not found it necessary to impose the insurance premium tax as it receives a
high rate of occupational tax from the hospital that is located in their city.
Mayor Moriconi advised that a rate of 8% for insurance premium tax would
generate $1,000,000 – 5% would generate $600,000. Ms. Rebman advised that the
necessary documents would have to be filed with the state 100 days prior to the
end of the fiscal year in order to be effective by July 1, 2003 and it is
probably too late to meet that deadline this year.
Ms. Rebman also advised that this proposed budget assumes that the city will
adopt a compensating rate plus 4% property tax rate. Mr. Wendling advised that
anything over 4% would be subject to referendum. He stated that council could
also consider increasing the occupational payroll tax rate. It is currently set
at 1.25%. He advised that an increase in this tax could have an impact on
economic development.
Council Member Behler asked how Independence’s property tax compares with other
cities. Mayor Moriconi stated that Covington and Erlanger property tax rates
are the highest. Council Member Ellison stated that cities that have their own
fire departments tend to have a higher rate in order to support an additional
public safety department.
Council Member Bushong recognized that the city might have to look at revenue
options Council Member Behler agreed and voiced concern about how the city was
going to address infrastructure issues without some revenue enhancement. Mayor
Moriconi commented that the two concerns that residents have are police
protection and road maintenance. Council Member Franzen commented on the need
to bring some salaries up to comparable levels. She also expressed concern that
the city cannot continue to operate statuesque. Council Member Bushong voiced
his concerns about exercising a band-aid approach to fix big problems. Mayor
Moriconi advised that the intent of today’s meeting was to inform everyone of
the current state of affairs.
Mr. Wendling advised of the need to stay on top of the street maintenance. He
stated that funds spent on the streets in the Industrial Park area is money
well spent, as this area is a large revenue center for the city. Council Member
Bushong suggested the city might want to consider assessing the businesses in
the industrial park for street improvements. Mr. Wendling commented that Holten
Drive was not constructed to withstand the weight of the semi tractors that
travel that road.
Council Member Franzen commented that the council needs anticipate the city’s
future needs. Council Member Behler agreed that, as a growing community, an
increase in taxes is part of that growth.. Mr. Wendling advised that the city
will need to take control of a zoning plan for the city and recommended that a
comprehensive plan be developed. He stated that it would cost about $50,000,
which is not in this proposed budget, to get that accomplished, but he feels
the city needs to be very aggressive in this endeavor. Council Member Ellison
suggested imposing impact fees on developers. Mr. Wendling advised that
Homebuilders Association would probably declare opposition on that type of fee.
Council Member Bushong stated that he measures the wants and needs of the
public based on the calls he receives, 99% of which are regarding street
maintenance and police safety issues. Council Member Franzen stated that she is
receiving public input that does not necessarily oppose an increase in taxes as
long as in exchange there is an increase in services. Council Member Behler
stated that she feels that part of a safety concern is roads that are
maintained in good condition.
Mayor Moriconi voiced the possibility of exempting senior citizens over the age
of 65 if the insurance premium tax is adopted. There was general discussion
regarding this exemption, but Mr. Wendling advised it would be difficult to
accomplish for various reasons. Council Member Bushong suggested adding an ad
valorum road tax to the general election ballot. Mr. Wendling advised the city
had a first reading on a proposed ordinance for a road tax two years ago, but
then it was dropped. Mr. Wendling advised that there are other taxes that
council could consider, such as a Senior and/or Recreational tax to support
those programs, but like the road tax, they are also subject to referendum.
Council Member Bushong suggested the need to educate and market the need for
increased revenues. Council Member Yeager stated that Campbell County has an
“old age tax” that completely supports their Senior Center. Council Member
Bushong stated that he would not object to an insurance premium tax as long as
life and health insurances were excluded. He suggested that further discussion
of revenue enhancement be included on future meeting agendas. Mayor Moriconi
commented the city needs to raise $350,000 to $400,000 to build up the reserve
fund.
Mayor Moriconi advised that further discussion of the proposed budget would
take place at the next caucus meeting. Council requested that audience
privileges of the floor be given a three minute time limit to voice their
concern or request of council.
Adjournment
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi adjourned the meeting at 12:
38 p.m.

APRIL 7, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
April 7, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with
Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Lisa May of Staffordsburg United
Methodist Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Jim Bushong, Donna Yeager, Mary Pat Behler, Carol
Franzen and Jim Ellison. Also present was City Attorney, Jed Deters and Mark
Wendling, City Administrator. Council Member Ketron was absent.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated the first item of business is the recognition of our
local businesses, which is a tradition the city started last month. The Mayor
stated Council Member Behler selected Robinson’s Meats located on Taylor Mill
Road. The Mayor presented Jason and Chris Robinson with a plaque of
recognition. Jason Robinson thanked the city and gave a brief description of
the food services they have to offer.
Approval of Minutes /March 3, 2003 Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to approve the minutes of the March 3,
2003 Council Meeting. Council Member Bushong so moved with a second by Council
Member Yeager. Amendments were noted and approved. Roll call was answered
unanimously; Motion carried 5-0.
Approval of Minutes/March 17, 2003 Caucus Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to approve the minutes of the March
17, 2003 Caucus Meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second by
Council Member Bushong. Amendments were noted and approved. Roll call was
answered unanimously; Motion carried 5-0.
Approval of Minutes/March 29, 2003 Budget Summit Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to approve the minutes of the March
29, 2003 Budget Meeting. Council Member Behler so moved with a second by
Council Member Ellison. Roll call was answered unanimously; Motion carried 5-0.
Privileges of the Floor
6.   Linda Buchanan of 3946 Hunters Green Drive advised Mayor and Council she
has called the police numerous times regarding barking dogs next door. She
stated the police has spoke to her neighbors several times but advised her
there was nothing they can do until two separate complaints are received
according to the city ordinance. She stated as she understands it, the Dog
Warden cannot do anything but send letters but cannot issue any violation.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mrs. Buchanan if she had spoken to her neighbor regarding
the dogs. She stated she and her husband have spoke to the neighbor and the
only result they have gotten was the gentleman ringing their doorbell at 6:00
a.m. and leaving, blowing his horn, bending a post in their back yard and
telling his dog to “sic” her. Mr. Paul Buchanan, father of Mrs. Linda Buchanan
stated he is on the Code Enforcement Board in Boone County and stated they have
a Nuisance Ordinance, which is very effective and maybe the city should look
into something like that. Police Chief Butler stated as long as the Ordinance
the city has at the present is in effect, the police officers hands are tied.
He stated in order for a complaint to be filed in District Court, it would
depend on Gary Edmondson accepting the complaint. He stated two separate
residents would have to file charges before anything could possibly be done.
Council Member Franzen asked if Annie Wuestefeld, our Citation Officer could
site for a problem such as this. Attorney Deters advised she could. He stated
he could re-draft a new ordinance and bring back to the next meeting.
7.   Mrs. JoAnn Cobble of 5257 Madison Pike addressed Mayor and Council
regarding the condition of Madison Pike. She stated Madison Pike has not been
cleaned of debris in two years. She stated she and her husband cleaned up two
wheel barrels of debris including broken curb from in front of their home. She
stated she spoke to employees at the Administration Office and was advised that
Madison Pike was a state maintained highway. She also stated she feels the
streets are over treated during snow removal. She stated her lake is damaged
due to the salting of the streets. She feels it is a waste of money to put so
much salt on the streets, which is affecting our environment. Mayor Moriconi
advised Mrs. Cobble that Madison Pike is not a city maintained street but
maintained by the State, which salts that road during snow removal. He added
that the city does snow removal on city maintained streets. Mayor Moriconi
advised Mrs. Cobble the city will clean up the area in which she was speaking
of. Mr. Wendling advised Mrs. Cobble he would contact the State Highway
Department regarding these matters.
Old Business
8.   Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Robert Cooper with Seasongood and Mayer that
handled the bonding of the new Municipal Center to answer any questions Council
might have regarding the bond rating. Mr. Cooper stated he was asked to come to
recap the debt the city had with Kentucky League of Cities. He stated it is a
tedious process leading up to the sale of this bond issue mainly because the
city has never gone to market. Thanks to Janet Rebman and Mark Wendling, they
put a lot of information together that is required to go to Rating Agencies and
supply the information for an offering document that is sent out to the public.
This being the city’s first time in the market, Rating Agencies has a lot of
questions such as what their philosophies are, what their plans are; what kind
of problems they foresee and how are they going to address them. One of the
issues they recognized was the fact the city was growing and there were
questions about how the city is going to address the growth and infrastructure
the city would need. They were satisfied the city has recognized that and are
aware of what needs to be done to accommodate that growth. Some of the items
that were stated in the report by Moody were the ratings the city receives due
to the city’s growing tax base and above average wealth levels; satisfactory
financial operations and low debt burden. The other issue is they review this
rating every year based on the financials sent to the Rating Agencies. Anytime
something major occurs we must notify the Rating Agency of some event that
happened. They are always watching the rating in seeing how the city performs.
They were extremely impressed with the levels of fund balances. Another issue
is the region the city is located in. The city is located in Kenton County,
which is a double rated county. The rating was an A2 rating which is very good
and should improve over time. The result of the sale of the bonds was a 30-year
amortization with a net interest cost of 4.4%. The interest rates range from 2%
to 4.6% over that 30-year period.
Mayor Moriconi reiterated the city refinanced the New Municipal Center and was
able to get a fixed rate, which will drop the payment to almost half.
New Business
Proposed Ordinance – Regulating Garbage Containers and Curb Placement Times-1st
Reading
9.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a first reading of an ordinance that
would regulate the times for garbage can placement at the curb and return from
the curb and asked City Attorney, Jed Deters to read the Ordinance. Council
Member Bushong noted the word “by” should be added in Section 1 of the
Ordinance. Council Member Bushong asked if this Ordinance addresses the problem
with residents putting out plastic bags with grass clippings and leaves. City
Attorney, Jed Deters stated the contractor has provisions for yard waste. He
stated if Rumpke will pick up plastic bags with yard debris then it is okay.
Council Member Ellison stated the Ordinance allows for the pick up of yard
waste. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated this Ordinance is sort of subordinate
to their regulations and will require that trash be in a container with a
secured lid. Council Member Yeager stated another complaint was the trash
collectors turn the can upside down and any trash that did not get emptied then
gets blown into the street. She asked if this was reported to Rumpke and the
City Clerk advised that Rumpke had been notified. Mayor Moriconi stated this
Ordinance attempts to solve two issues; the times trash cans can be placed at
the curb and back in, and the containers have to have a lid so animals cannot
tear the trash up. Attorney Jed Deters stated he would make the amendment and
bring back to council. Mayor Moriconi stated the second reading would be placed
on the agenda for the next regular council meeting.
Resolution No.2003-R-08-Text Amendment to Zoning Ordinance Re: Churches in NC
Zones
10.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-08 requiring a
text amendment to the Zoning Ordinance relating to churches in Neighborhood
Commercial Zones and asked City Attorney, Jed Deters to read. Mr. Wendling
advised that Area Planning now requires a Resolution by council when applying
for a text amendment. The text amendment supports the zoning ordinance to add
churches, and other buildings for the purpose of religious worship, teaching or
education as a conditional use within the neighborhood commercial (NC) zone.
City Attorney, Jed Deters read Resolution 2003-R-08. Council Member Yeager
moved, with second by Council Member Franzen to approve Resolution 2003-R-08.
Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Resolution No. 2003-R-09-Declaring 1.23 Acres As Surplus Property
11.   Mayor Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2003-R-09 declaring 1.23 acres
off Oby Drive be declared as surplus property so the city can accept sealed
bids and asked City Attorney, Jed Deters to read. Council Member Ellison moved,
with second by Council Member Yeager to approve Resolution No. 2003-R-09. Roll
call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Resolution No. 2003-R-10-Termination of Participation in the Kenton County Dog
Authority
12.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-10 authorizing
the city to terminate its participation with the Kenton County Dog Authority
and support a merger with the Kenton County Animal Shelter and send written
notice no less than 60 days prior to July 1, 2003. Mr. Wendling also advised
that Kenton County Police would be overseeing the department, not the Animal
Shelter as originally thought. City Attorney, Jed Deters read Resolution 2003-
R-10. Council Member Bushong moved, with a second by Council Member Yeager to
approve Resolution No. 2003-R-10. Roll call was answered with four yeas and
Council Member Ellison voting no.
Proposed Resolution - Accepting “The Oaks” Subdivision detention basin for city
Maintenance
13.   Mayor Moriconi presented to a council for consideration a resolution that
would authorize the Mayor to execute documents to transfer ownership of the
detention basin for the development known as “The Oaks” located off Hogreffe
Road in Independence and asked City Attorney, Jed Deters to read. City
Attorney, Jed Deters read the Resolution and recommended that council not to
accept this detention pond due to liability. He stated even though the
Sanitation District has indicated they will take over the responsibility of the
detention pond in the future, there is no guarantee they will. He stated he
does not feel there is an upside to any of this. Council Member Behler stated
she thought one of the reasons the city would take over the detention pond was
because the developer was not caring for it now. City Attorney, Jed Deters
advised council if the city does not take over the detention pond, the
developer would have to assume responsibility unless a Homeowners Association
is formed. Council Member Ellison made a motion to table this issue until the
April Caucus Meeting, with a second by Council Member Behler. Mayor Moriconi
requested the clerk call the roll. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0.

classified as a “safety issue” which will allow the city to make a donation.
Council Member Yeager made a motion to donate $500.00 to Simon Kenton High

in Iraq on Thursday evening at 6:30 p.m. at Memorial Park and asked everyone to
come and show their support.
18.   Mayor Moriconi advised council that Skyline Chili had donated $800.00
toward the Easter Egg Hunt to be held April 13th at 2:00 p.m. at Memorial Park.
Miscellaneous Discussion
19.   Council Member Yeager asked the city clerk approximately how much money
was still owed on delinquent city taxes. City Clerk, Pat Taney stated
approximately $100,000.00 including more than one year of delinquency. Council
Member Yeager asked if there were further steps that could be taken to collect
some of the delinquent taxes. City Clerk, Pat Taney stated delinquent letters
are sent out in January and March after they have become delinquent.
20.   City Attorney, Jed Deters advised Mayor and Council that he could send a
letter including attorney fees would be added if not paid by a certain due
date.
21.   Council Member Ellison moved to have City Attorney, Jed Deters collect on
a contingency basis, delinquent tax bills and add legal fess as required by the
Ordinance with a second by Council Member Yeager. Roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 5-0.
22.   Mayor Moriconi stated if there were no further discussions he entertained
a motion to adjourn. Council Member Bushong so moved, with a second by Council
Member Ellison. Motion carried and the meeting adjourned at 8:10 p.m.

APRIL 21, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL CAUCUS MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 21,
2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Independence Senior Citizens and Community Center in
Independence with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called
the meeting to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. The roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol
Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Council Member Mary Pat Behler was
absent. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters, City Administrator, Mark
T. Wendling and Finance Director, Janet Rebman.
Privileges of the Floor
JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, addressed council with her concerns of a
reported tax increase, especially on insurance. She remarked that she was
prepared to work against any such increases in taxes. She stated that she hoped
that the council would adopt a balanced budget for the coming year and in
closing added that she would like to reserve additional comment after the
Mayor’s presentation of the proposed budget later in this meeting.
Lori Lucas, 1941 Freedom Trail and Toni Moriconi, 1899 Freedom Trail, addressed
council regarding their plans to organize a Stamping and Scrapbook Club for the
purpose of documenting photos of the city’s events. They stated that the club
would operate as a non-profit type organization and would require annual dues
from its members that would be used for the purchase of supplies and materials
needed to create the city scrapbooks. Mrs. Moriconi stated that the Club would
meet once every month and requested permission for complimentary use of a
meeting room in the Senior/Community Center. Mr. Bushong asked if this
organization would become a charter non-profit. Mrs. Moriconi stated that she
would look into it. Council conveyed that they would consider this request for
a complimentary meeting room at the Senior/Community Center at the May 5, 2003
council meeting.
Jeff Jarboe, 5468 Madison Pike and his attorney, David Davidson addressed
council regarding their request for a text amendment to the city’s current
zoning ordinance. They stated that Mr. Jarboe’s property located at 5468
Madison Pike is currently zoned R-1C. He stated that their proposal for a text
amendment would permit a conditional use for buildings in an R-1C zone to be
used as offices that are located in modified residences. He advised that this
modification would affect only a few parcels of property in the city.
City Attorney, Jed Deters, reminded council that the Kenton County Planning
Commission has recently began a requirement by cities that they adopt a
resolution to support a proposed text amendment to the zoning ordinance. Mr.
Deters asked what they mean by a “modified residence”. Mr. Davidson stated a
“modified residence” would describe any residence that was converted to
business offices. He also commented that the Comprehensive Plan does not
provide for commercial or office places. Mr. Deters explained that a
conditional use request would have to be applied for and granted by the city’s
Board of Adjustment. Mr. Davidson stated that if council approves the requested
text amendment then that would be their next step. Mr. Jarboe commented that
his property is essentially condemned, because under the current zoning it
cannot possibly come into compliance. Mr. Davidson stated that the structure is
no longer suitable for a residence as it is in an area that has become
predominantly commercial. He stated Mr. Jarboe’s mother has owned this property
since 1997, but that Mr. Jarboe has been living and working there and pays rent
to his mother. Mr. Deters advised that Mrs. Jarboe would have to be the
applicant for the conditional use request. Council Member Ellison suggested
adding the language “be adjacent to an arterial state highway route” to the
text amendment that Mr. Davidson is proposing. Mr. Davidson agreed to Council
Member Ellison’s suggestion. In closing, Mr. Jarboe stated that there are five
houses in the area of the Independence Towne Center that would be affected by
this text amendment. He stated that he would like to see council limit the
modification of these residences to professional offices.
Mayor Moriconi advised that this matter would be placed on the May 5, 2003
agenda for council to act on this text amendment request. He directed the city
attorney to draft a resolution for council’s consideration.
Discussion of the Detention Pond in “The Oaks” Subdivision
Mayor Moriconi advised that Tony Browne, the developer of The Oaks subdivision
was not present, but has requested that the city take over maintenance of the
detention pond in that subdivision. The Mayor advised that the city’s engineer,
Mark Brueggemann is present to report to council his assessment of this
detention basin.
Mr. Brueggemann advised that the basin was constructed by building a dam across
an existing creek with the existing plant life in the area remaining and
appears to have been constructed as per the approved construction drawings. He
stated this design is going to require more maintenance after substantial
rainfalls in order to remove any debris that will possibly collect and block
the inlet that is a six-inch orifice. Mr. Brueggemann stated that he recommends
the city request a compaction report from the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission to ensure that the dam was compacted properly. He stated that upon
inspection he observed a buildup of silt in front of the inlet to the control
structure and recommended the silt be removed. He stated this buildup is a
result of the design.
Mr. Brueggemann advised council that he recommends the city require the
developer to do the following three things before accepting this detention pond
for maintenance: 1) removal of the silt build up, 2) re-seed the embankment,
and 3) provide a dam compaction report.
Mayor Moriconi expressed his reservations on the city taking over maintenance
of this area. Council Member Franzen advised that the city’s Public Works Crew
Leader, Jeff Smith, videoed the area and presented the tape for possible
viewing by council. She stated she had viewed the video tape and state the area
is very wooded and that Mr. Smith submitted a list of reasons supporting his
recommendation to not accept this basin for maintenance. City Attorney, Mr.
Deters, concurred with Mr. Smith’s assessment of this matter and advised the
city would be assuming a big liability without any benefit. Mr. Wendling
commented that he does not believe the city’s acceptance of the detention basin
was part of the annexation agreement of this property, but he feels the
developer would not have asked to be annexed if the city was not going to agree
to assume maintenance of this basin. Council Member Bushong commented that he
sees no benefits for the city in accepting this area for maintenance. Council
Member Ellison disagreed with Mr. Wendling by stating that he feels Mr. Browne
would have still desired annexation regardless of whether or not the city
agreed to assume the liability for this detention pond. Mr. Brueggemann
commented that he is not aware of any city in Kenton or Campbell County that
have assumed the maintenance responsibilities of detention areas. Council
Member Bushong asked if the Sanitation District would assume this area for
maintenance. Mr. Wendling stated that he spoke to John Lyons of the Sanitation
District who stated they would not take over the maintenance of this area now,
as they are not currently in the storm water retention business. But advised
they would take it over if it is city owned in five years when the Sanitation
District takes over the storm water retention.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Brueggemann for his report and advised this matter
would be placed on the agenda of the May 5, 2003 business meeting for an
official vote to either approve or disapprove the acceptance of this detention
pond for maintenance.
Glenhurst Development – Regarding a Zone Change and Annexation Request – Chuck
Berling
Mayor Moriconi announced that Mr. Berling was not present and would postpone
the discussion of this matter until another time.
Discussion Regarding On-Street Parking in the Forest Run Subdivision
Mayor Moriconi introduced Robert and Ellen Wood, 10737 Bluespruce Lane, who
wrote to him regarding their concerns with the on street parking in the Forest
Run Subdivision. She stated that she feels the residents are using the streets
as parking lots. Mrs. Wood stated that she feels that a potential hazard exists
because the streets are not wide enough to allow two cars to pass each other
when one is going around a parked car. Mr. Deters advised that the subdivision
streets are constructed to meet the specifications of subdivision regulations
in place at the time the subdivision is developed. He also noted that double
car driveways were designed to alleviate on-street parking. Council Member
Franzen commented that when a snow emergency is declared parking on the streets
is prohibited. Mayor Moriconi commented that even then, the on street parking
is difficult to enforce without issuing tickets to every violator. Council
Member Franzen questioned whether covenants would be a solution. Mr. Deters
said that some subdivisions do this, but added that even if council considered
an amendment to the street widths, that it would not help with the current
streets. He stated that many older streets are much narrower than those in
Forest Run. Council Member Ellison suggested imposing a fee to purchase a decal
to permit a vehicle to park on the street as a possible solution. Mrs. Wood
commented that she feels that on-street parking devalues a neighborhood. Mayor
Moriconi directed the city administration to survey other cities to see how
they contend with on-street parking problems.
Presentation by Jeffrey Keener, President of the Northern Kentucky Little
League
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Jeffrey Keener, President of the Northern
Kentucky Little League who was proposing to form a partnership with the city
for exclusive use of Sterling Staggs Park as the home fields for their
organization’s ball games.
Mr. Keener shared with council the dilemma his organization is experiencing
with the increased number of teams and the lack of ball fields in Northern
Kentucky to play on. He stated that the Northern Kentucky Little League
currently has fifty teams in Boone and Kenton County and that Kenton County did
not provide Saturday playing fields or practice fields. He stated that it is
becoming increasingly difficult to find playing fields for the ages of eight
years and younger that meet the Little League requirements. Mr. Keener proposed
that the City of Independence partner with the Northern Kentucky Little League
to solve their problem of supplying ball fields next year, as he estimates
there will be close to one hundred teams. He advised it would be necessary to
convert some of the green space into parking spaces at Sterling Staggs Park.
Council Member Yeager expressed concern that this would eliminate green space.
Mr. Keener stated he would like to work with a city representative to begin the
process of making the necessary accommodations in time for next year, but only
if the city council was going to support this venture. Council Member Franzen
suggested that the city’s Recreation Director, Nita Brake attend the next
caucus meeting to meet with Mr. Keener. Mr. Keener stated he wanted council’s
commitment to his proposal before investing time into a venture that may not
come to fruition. Mayor Moriconi suggested that this might not be worth
pursuing, as the park is landlocked and it seems there may not be the full
support of the city council. In closing, Mayor Moriconi suggested that the
Glenhurst Subdivision area will be adding a park area with a school in the near
future and encouraged Mr. Keener to investigate that as an option. Mr. Deters
suggested the organization acquire and develop property for these purposes. Mr.
Keener commented that the high price of land would prohibit this as a solution
for their organization.
Proposal by Marc Wilson & Associates for Lobbyist Services for the City
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Marc Wilson. Mr. Wilson addressed council
regarding professional services he would like to provide the city as a paid
lobbyist. He stated he is a marketing/communications professional, registered
lobbyist and has worked in various capacities in politics. He stated he would
represent the city’s individual interests and provide protection against
discrimination. He advised he would pursue the political representatives of
this district and lobby for city project funding to alleviate the constraints
on the city budget. Mr. Wilson stated that the value of a paid lobbyist would
exceed the city’s investment for this service. He advised that he is proud of
his accomplishments with the Newport on the Levy development.
Council Member Bushong asked Mr. Wilson if he has been a paid lobbyist for
other cities. Mr. Wilson stated not yet, but has worked with Tri-ED. Mayor
Moriconi commented that Independence is a large city in Northern Kentucky, but
has been overshadowed by the large cities located on the Ohio River. Mr. Wilson
stated that the city should be receiving thirty cents back on every state tax
dollar collected. Council Member Yeager asked Mr. Wilson if he would assist
with state grants. Mr. Wilson stated that he could help track grants that the
city applies for. He also stated that U.S. Senator McConnell could be pursued
for federal funding. Mr. Wendling asked Mr. Wilson how he would handle possible
conflicts of interest with his other clients, like the Apartment Association.
He stated that would be a unique situation and if it would occur he would work
through it. Mayor Moriconi advised he would obtain some firm numbers from Mr.
Wilson and get back to council at a later date.
Discussion of Sunday Liquor Sales Hours
Mayor Moriconi reported that the city has received a request by the Kenton
County Golf Course to consider permitting alcohol sales at 11:00 a.m. rather
than the current onset of 1:00 p.m. He stated the Golf Course is losing
revenue, which has lead to this request. He requested input from council.
Council Member Yeager stated that she has no problem with allowing alcohol
sales to begin at 11:00 a.m. Council Member Ellison concurred that he had no
problem with this request but suggested that sit-down eating establishments
might be included. Council Member Ketron suggested the onset of sales be at
noon instead of 11:00 a.m. Council Member Franzen stated that she is strongly
opposed to granting this request by the Golf Course and felt that the city
should not permit alcohol sales until 1:00 p.m. Mr. Deters stated that whatever
is agreed on should be a citywide regulation. Police Chief Butler commented
that state law prohibits package liquor sales before 1:00 p.m. Council Member
Bushong questioned if the city would charge a fee. Mr. Wendling stated that the
city does not have a liquor license for businesses that sell alcohol and may
want to consider establishing one. Council Member Bushong replied that he would
be interested in knowing what other cities charge for a liquor license. Mr.
Deters advised that state law takes precedence with regard to liquor sales and
he would like to research this law and will present an opinion at the May
meeting.
Update Regarding the City’s Barking Dog Ordinance
Mr. Deters, City Attorney, presented a draft ordinance that would amend the
city’s current ordinance regulating barking dogs for council’s review. Chief
Butler commented that he suggest some amendment to the language in Section II
so that the police officer would have some discretion in issuing a citation. He
also commented that his department does not track warnings that they issue. In
addition, he stated that according to state law, the police officer would have
to actually witness the offense, before a citation could be issued. Chief
Butler commented that sometimes these types of complaints are the result of
petty neighborhood squabbles. Council Member Bushong asked how many dog calls
the police department receives. Chief Butler stated he would have to run a
report to obtain that figure. He commented that dog complaints seem to come in
spurts and that he feels that it is part of the growing pains the city is
experiencing. Mr. Deters stated he would review this draft ordinance with Chief
Butler to make the necessary revisions and submit it at the next caucus meeting
for council’s consideration.
Proposed Ordinance – Regulating Garbage Containers and Curb Placement Times
Council Member Franzen reported that she has received many phone calls from
residents opposing the proposed ordinance regulating garbage containers. (A
first reading of this proposed ordinance was at the April 7, 2003 council
meeting) She stated that the callers mainly object to the prohibition of
plastic trash bags being placed at the curb and being cited for the litter that
results from the torn bags. Mr. Deters stated the city already has a litter
ordinance. Council Member Franzen went on to say she has had 50-60 complaints
and feels this ordinance is redundant. Council Member Yeager stated that she
feels part of the problem exists with the garbage collectors, as they return
the cans on the curb upside down, thereby dislodging any remaining trash onto
the lawn areas. Council Member Franzen stated that additional cans that
residents will have to own to replace the prohibited bags, would only add to
this problem. She expressed concern that Independence, by mandating the
exclusive use of trashcans for curbside garbage disposal, might be viewed as a
socialist community. Council Member Bushong spoke in favor of the use of
trashcans versus bags as neighborhood dogs can be blamed for spreading the
refuse. Council Member Franzen maintained that she felt the ordinance was in
need of language revisions. Council Member Ellison commented that he felt the
ordinance would be used as a tool for enforcement when necessary for persistent
violations. Mayor Moriconi concurred with Council Member Ellison. In closing,
Council Member Franzen commented that the city currently has a leash law that
should be enforced and advised council to expect to be addressed by residents
opposing this proposed ordinance at the next council meeting.
Presentation of the Memorial Park Amphitheater Site Plan
Mayor Moriconi reported that the site plan for the amphitheater is complete and
here for review after the meeting. Mr. Wendling reported that he anticipates
the notice to bidders will be released very soon and that construction of the
amphitheater will begin sometime this summer.
Proposed Resolution of Support for the Northern Kentucky Regional Farmers’
Market
Mayor Moriconi submitted to council for their consideration a proposed
resolution that would support the creation of a regional farmers’ market in
Northern Kentucky. He stated it would be an in-door year round $7,000,000
facility located in downtown Covington. Mayor Moriconi voiced some ambivalence
in supporting this venture as he feels it might detract from local businesses.
Council Member Yeager commented that Independence attempted unsuccessfully a
few years ago to launch a farmers’ market. Discussion died; no one voiced
interest in supporting this resolution.
Discussion of a Proposed Budget for the 2003/04 Fiscal year
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed budget for the 2003/04 fiscal
year that included two options for their consideration. He stated that both
options reflect a balanced budget.
He stated that Option 1 specified the following:
∙   Adoption of a compensating property tax rate
∙   Adding two new police officers
∙   Adding one new Public Works laborer (with the additional duty of in-house
grass cutting)
∙   A 21% salary increase for the Recreation Director
∙   $50,000 improvements to Memorial Park
Mayor Moriconi advised that Option 2 specified the following:
∙   Adoption of a compensating property tax rate plus 4%
∙   Adding one new police officer
Mayor Moriconi advised the both options assumed cost of living salary increases
for the city employees, with the exception of a few that would receive a higher
adjustment. In addition, he stated that Option 1 would assume increased revenue
with the adoption of the insurance premium franchise fee. He advised that
adopting this fee would cost each resident about $80-$100 per year.
Council Member Bushong expressed concern on the Mayor’s Option 1 proposal to
eradicate the city’s entitlement to the additional 4% property tax. Mayor
Moriconi responded that he did not want to have a doublet-hit effect on the
residents. Mr. Deters advised that in the past when the city did not exercise
their option to adopt the compensating tax rate plus the 4%, it has had a
detrimental impact on the city’s budget and makes it difficult to recover from
the lost revenue. Council Member Bushong stated that a couple years ago the
city council made a commitment to get back on track with the 4% option. He
stated the city needs more than the bare bones amount allowed by law and urged
Mayor Moriconi to continue the practice of adopting a tax rate that includes
the 4% allowed by law. Mr. Deters agreed and commented that the plus 4% is an
option that is intended for growing communities like Independence. Council
Member Ellison also concurred that adopting the compensating tax rate plus 4%
was a necessary practice to keep revenues stable. Mayor Moriconi agreed to
include the 4% back into the revenue calculations.
Council Member Bushong questioned adding another employee in the Public Works
Department. Mayor Moriconi stated that he felt the additional person could
possibly be used for grass cutting thereby deleting the expense the city
currently has in contracting out this job.
Council Member Bushong asked Mayor Moriconi how the 21% salary increase was
determined for the Recreation Director. Mayor Moriconi responded that this
position requested a higher increase. Council Member Yeager commented that the
increase was to bring this salary up to a comparable salary for this position.
Council Member Bushong asked if the administration deputy clerks would be
getting the requested salary increases. Council Member Franzen stated the City
Clerk and deputy clerk positions need to be brought up to comparable rates.
Council Member Bushong commented that salary adjustments were approved for the
police department last year and asked what salary range was needed to get the
City Clerk at a comparable wage. Mr. Wendling stated the City Clerk position is
currently being paid $7,000-$10,000 less than comparable cities. Council Member
Bushong stated he would like to have some wage percentages and dollar amounts
to review and consider for a merit raise system. Mayor Moriconi stated that the
police salary adjustments were implemented last year in an effort to reduce
staff turnover. He stated he would look at a way to implement salary
adjustments for the administration department. Council Member Franzen stated
that in order to keep good employees they need to be well compensated.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the city is also committed to the Industrial Road
Improvement Project which will cost the city $75,000 this year. Council Member
Bushong asked when this project would begin. Mr. Wendling commented that the
commencement of this project has been delayed until the fall of 2003.
Mayor Moriconi permitted Mrs. JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, to make
comments to council regarding the presentation of the 2003/04 proposed budget.
Mrs. Cobble commended Council Member Bushong for his question of Mr. Marc
Wilson on what other cities he provides lobbyist services. She stated that Mr.
Wilson’s answer speaks for itself, and commented that the city does not need to
pay for the services of a middleman. She stated that if other cities felt the
need for a lobbyist, they would have engaged him by now.
Mrs. Cobble also commended Chief Butler. She commented that the proposed dog
ordinance needs to be looked at very closely and re-evaluated. She stated that
she could often hear animals in her neighborhood.
Council Member Bushong asked the timeline of adopting the budget. Mr. Wendling
advised the first reading of the ordinance is scheduled for the May 5th meeting
with the second reading and adoption at the June 2nd meeting. Mayor Moriconi
stated he would continue to review the proposed budget over the next two weeks
in preparation for presentation to council at the May 5th meeting. Council
Member Bushong asked if this timeframe would be sufficient if amendments to the
budget were made between the first and second reading. Mr. Deters advised that
if a significant change was made after the first reading it might delay the
schedule. Council Member Yeager stated a special meeting could be held if
necessary. Mayor Moriconi advised there was sufficient time prior to the next
caucus meeting to hold a special meeting if necessary.
Council Member Franzen asked if Option 1 included more than cost of living
(COLA) salary increases. Mr. Wendling stated only a couple of employees would
be given a salary adjustment higher than the cost of living. Mayor Moriconi
reiterated that he would work on making some incremental adjustments to some
administration positions.
Council Member Bushong asked what percentage was used to calculate a revenue
amount for the insurance premium tax. Mr. Wendling stated eight percent was
used and that the calculations were distributed at the Budget Summit held in
March.
Business Recognition
Mayor Moriconi asked Council Member Bushong if he had selected a local business
that he would like to recognize at the May 5th council meeting. Council Member
Bushong stated he would be recognizing Farmers National Bank with the new CEO
Mark Aulick attending the meeting to accept the plaque.
Miscellaneous Item of Discussion – Cluster Mail Boxes
Council Member Ellison commented that he has received a complaint that cluster
mailboxes are being installed in the Clover Ridge Subdivision. He stated the
city adopted an ordinance several years ago prohibiting these types of
mailboxes. Mr. Wendling advised he would look into this.
Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss, Mayor Moriconi adjourned the
meeting at 9:16 p.m.
