MAY 5, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May
5, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of Independence
Christian Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen, Otis
Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed Deters and Mark
Wendling, City Administrator. Council Member Bushong was absent.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated the first item of business would be the recognition
of Farmers National Bank, which Council Member Bushong has selected as
recipient of the Business of the Month tribute. The Mayor presented Mark
Aulick, President/CEO, with a plaque of recognition. Mr. Aulick thanked Mayor
Moriconi and Council for the opportunity to receive this honor. He remarked
that Farmers National Bank is a well-kept secret in Independence and because
they are a small bank they take pride in providing excellent service to their
customers. Mr. Aulick invited everyone to stop in.
Agenda Revision
3.   Mayor Moriconi advised that he would like to revise tonight’s agenda and
moved the matter of the proposed budget for the 2003/04 fiscal year to the
forefront.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a Budget for the Fiscal Year 2003/04 – 1st
Reading
4.   Mayor Moriconi presented for first reading a proposed ordinance adopting a
budget for the 2003/04 fiscal year. Mayor Moriconi advised that this proposed
budget did not include tax increases. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Mayor Moriconi stated that a second reading of this ordinance would take place
at the June 2, 2003 council meeting.
Approval of the Minutes of the April 7, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the April 7,
2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Yeager so moved, with second
from Council Member Franzen. Several amendments were noted and approved and
roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the April 21, 2003 Caucus Council Meeting
6.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the April 21,
2003 caucus meeting of council. Council Member Ellison moved, with second from
Council Member Franzen. Several amendments were noted and approved. Roll call
was answered unanimously; motion carried 5-0.
PRIVELEGES OF THE FLOOR
7.   Mr. Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike requested that he be allowed to reserve
his comments till the end of the meeting. Mayor Moriconi consented to Mr.
Cobble’s request.
8.   Pauline Judd, 11 Apple Drive addressed council regarding her concerns of a
reported tax increase and voiced a strong objection to new taxes. Ms. Judd
advised that she is 83 years old and is struggling on a fixed income to pay for
her necessities; she does not have cable television, etc. She commented that
she does not feel the city needs a new municipal building and accused council
of finding ways to spend the resident’s tax dollars.
9.   JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, presented Mayor Moriconi and Council
with a petition containing over 1,150 signatures of citizens who oppose an
insurance premium tax. She requested that the petition be included as an
attachment to the official council minutes of this meeting. Mrs. Cobble
commented that she was impressed by the tremendous response from the citizens
regarding this matter and stated that the flame of democracy is not completely
extinguished and it shows that democracy can and does work. . She stated that
the senior citizens can be a power force and thanked everyone who participated
in this effort.
10.   On a somber note, Mrs. Cobble expressed how troubled she was to find out
that a Council Member and one of her petition workers had been threatened. She
stated that this behavior goes against the laws of God and State and her intent
was to raise opposition against increased taxation in a peaceful manner. Mrs.
Cobble proclaimed shame on the people guilty of these threats. She asked Mayor
Moriconi to ask for a show of hands from the audience of those opposing any tax
increases. (Mayor Moriconi acceded this request and herein the minutes reflect
that the majority of the audience raised their hand in opposition to increased
taxes. Also this record will reflect that a few hands were raised in support of
increased taxes.) Mrs. Cobble thanked Mayor Moriconi and Council for the
opportunity to speak.
11.   Tom Brinker, 1192 Constitution Drive, stated that he is a regular
attendee of the city council meetings and was amazed that every available seat
was taken tonight due to the talk of a possible tax increase. Mr. Brinker went
on to say that he was in favor of a tax increase and advised that others should
know the facts behind council’s consideration before they voice their
opposition. He stated that the city is growing rapidly and there is a great
need to hire more police officers to ensure the safety of the citizens. He
stated that the last time the city hired a new officer was 1999 and during that
time many new homes have been constructed, which means that more residents have
moved in. Mayor Moriconi advised that an average of 300-400 homes are built
every year. Mr. Brinker directed his comment to the audience attendees by
stating they should attend the council meetings every month to learn the facts,
and not just when there is a threat of new taxes.
12.   Council Member Behler requested that respect be shown to all persons
taking the podium and that attendee’s refrain from expressing disparaging
remarks.
13.   Jim Reusch, 1775 Forest Run Drive, stated that he also is retired but is
concerned that the city can’t expand without additional revenue to support the
police and fire departments.
14.   Michael W. Little, 10897 Gristone Circle in the Shaw Estates Subdivision,
spoke against any proposed tax increase. He stated that any tax increase should
be put on the general election ballot. He stated he was against the way the
city tried to pass the proposed insurance premium tax. He stated that some
people live paycheck to paycheck and that the influx of new homes being
constructed should be producing adequate tax dollars for the city to operate.
15.   Council Member Franzen explained that the initial discussion of the
possibility of implementing an insurance premium tax was at the Budget Summit
held in March. She stated that if council had decided to proceed with such a
tax that it would have been publicized. She stated assuredly that there was
never any intent by the Council to try to implement this kind of tax in an
underhanded manner. She also advised that at the Budget Summit meeting in
March, Council Member Bushong proposed that the city schedule special town hall
meetings to give the residents an opportunity to voice their opinions on this
tax. Mayor Moriconi commented that no residents attended the Budget Summit that
was held in March.
16.   Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum Road, voiced his opposition to an insurance
premium tax, as it will hurt the elderly residents as well as those on a fixed
income. He stated when this matter was brought up last March that he called
some of the council members and found that most opposed this tax. He commented
that he felt that the payroll tax should be increased if additional revenue was
needed by the city, as the people who have jobs can afford to pay taxes.
17.   Jeanne Cooper, 14816 Decoursey, stated that she was here to speak on
behalf of Mr. Jeff Jarboe’s request to obtain a conditional use for his
accounting/tax service business in a residential zone. She commented that Mr.
Jarboe is an excellent financial planner and tax consultant and is a good
business for the city.
18.   Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, stated that he opposed the insurance
premium tax. He stated there should be other means to raise additional revenue
without putting a tax on insurance policies. He suggested to those in favor of
the city implementing this kind of tax, that they should make a voluntary
donation to the city. He went on to say that he has lived in the city for
thirty-two years and has yet to see the streets swept. He stated that the
deteriorating condition of the curbs and sidewalks in the city is a disgrace.
Mr. Cobble commented the city should get funds from state/federal grants to
make the necessary repairs without taxing the people. Mayor Moriconi advised
that the streets were swept two weeks ago. Mr. Cobble replied that the streets
were not swept in front of his house. Mr. Wendling disputed this comment and
advised the city rented a bobcat and swept the downtown area along Madison
Pike, even though the maintenance of this stretch of highway is the
responsibility of the State Highway Department. He stated that the
disintegrating condition of the curb is making it difficult to keep up. Mayor
Moriconi advised Mr. Cobble that the city is working on obtaining grants to
replace and install sidewalks along Madison Pike. In addition, Mayor Moriconi
has written to this district’s state representatives to enlist their assistance
in obtaining state and federal funds. Mayor Moriconi agreed that the curbs are
a mess, but advised that it may take an increase in taxes to help pay for those
kind of repairs.
End of Privileges of the Floor
Ordinance No. 2003-O-04 Regulating Garbage Can Containers and Curb Placement
Times – 2nd Reading
19.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2003-O-04 regulating the times for garbage can placement at the curb and their
return from the curb, requiring garbage containers to have secured lids during
such times and setting a penalty for violations of this ordinance. He stated
this ordinance was discussed once more at the April caucus meeting.
20.   Council Member Ellison moved, with second by Council Member Behler to
approve a second reading in summary only. Council Member Franzen stated that it
was discussed at the caucus meeting that the city already has a litter
ordinance in effect that should address the concerns that prompted this
ordinance. She stated that she felt this was unnecessary legislation. Council
Members Yeager and Ellison were of the opinion that this ordinance could be an
effective tool for the police department in extreme cases. Council Member
Behler commented that this ordinance was initiated because of a citizen’s
letter to council complaining about the litter throughout the city; and,
Council Member Behler suggested that perhaps the litter ordinance was not
sufficient. Mayor Moriconi commented that enforcement of the litter ordinance
is a problem. Council Member Franzen maintained that this ordinance was not
necessary with a litter ordinance already in force. Roll call was answered 4-
1 with Council Member Franzen casting the no vote. City Attorney, Jed Deters
read Ordinance No. 2003-O-04.
Authorization to Advertise Bids for the Construction of the Memorial Park
Amphitheater
21.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a draft copy of the bid packet for
the construction of the amphitheater in Memorial Park. Council Member Yeager
moved, with second by Council Member Ellison to approve the bid packet as
presented. Council Member Franzen asked if this project was fully funded. Mayor
Moriconi replied that the city had funds set aside for this project. She stated
that she thought the city lacked the total amount of funds needed to proceed
with this project. Mayor Moriconi advised that the size of the amphitheater was
scaled back to meet the reserved fund balance. Council Member Yeager commented
that the city does not have additional funds necessary to construct attached
restrooms and dressing rooms, so that section of the amphitheater was removed
from the original plans. She advised that the reserved funds being used for
this project is money that was derived from donations and grants. Roll call
resulted in a 4-1 vote with Council Member Franzen abstaining. Motion carried.
Update on the Fourth of July Celebration – Chairman, Larry Staverman
22.   Mayor Moriconi introduced Larry Staverman, Chairman of the Fourth of July
Celebration Committee.
23.   Mr. Staverman reported to council that since this year July 4th falls on
a Friday the Celebration would be a two-day event beginning on Thursday at 4:00
p.m. until 11:00 p.m. and continuing on Friday from noon until the end of the
fireworks display at nightfall. He stated that the parade would begin at 4:00
p.m. on Friday. He advised council that the committee is in the process of
making the following plans:
∙   Contracting with WNKR radio (106.5) of Dry Ridge Kentucky to synchronize
the fireworks to music and station a van on site on the 4th. WNKR will also
provide the event with on-air advertisement for which they will sell
sponsorships. They will recognize the sponsors right before the fireworks.
Categories for sponsorships are: soft drinks, banks, McDonald’s, supermarkets
and car dealers. WNKR has already sold spots to Farmers National Bank and are
working on Fifth Third Bank, Kroger’s, Robke Chevrolet and Coca-Cola.
∙   Recruiting several business sponsorships to help finance the event
∙   Street banners in four locations around the city to advertise the event.
The sponsors will have their business logos on the banners. The Lions Pride
Amusement s is again providing rides for this year’s event. They will arrive
early Monday morning for staging and will begin to assemble the rides on
Tuesday. A special handicap session with Redwood School on Thursday morning
from noon – 2:00 p.m. The radio station will provide funds for the handicap
session.
24.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the funds from the local businesses will make
it possible to have this as a two-day event this year. He thanked Mr. Staverman
for this report.
Resolution No. 2003-R-11 Supporting a Text Amendment Adding a Modified
Residence as a Conditional Use
25.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for consideration Resolution No.
2003-R-11 that would support a zoning text amendment adding a modified
residence as a conditional use within an R-1C zone. Council Member Ellison
moved, with second by Council Member Yeager to adopt Resolution No. 2003-R-11.
A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Jeff Jarboe and his attorney, David Davidson was
present to answer any questions regarding their request for this text
amendment. Council Member Ellison suggested deleting the word ‘arterial’,
pertaining to state routes, from the resolution as this section of Madison Pike
where Mr. Jarboe’s property is located may soon become a secondary route due to
the re-routing road improvements being made to Route 17. Council Member Yeager
concurred. Mr. Davidson stated he was not aware that that section of Route 17
may become a secondary roadway and since deleting the word ‘arterial’ does not
make a significant difference for their purposes, he had no objection to this
amendment to the resolution. The change in the wording of the resolution was
noted and roll call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 5-0 in
favor.
26.   Mr. Jarboe stated he has received a notice from the Zoning Administrator
to vacate the property and requested council grant a stay of enforcement until
after the text amendment process. Mr. Wendling advised council that since Mr.
Jarboe is operating a business in a residential zone, the zoning violation
notice was issued. Although Mr. Jarboe was issued a home occupation license,
that license does not allow additional employees at the location. Mr. Wendling
advised that the issue here is one of selective enforcement and that council
needs to consider setting precedence if they elect to grant Mr. Jarboe a stay
of enforcement. Mr. Davidson advised that the tax season has ended and that Mr.
Jarboe is attempting to rectify the violation and come into compliance. Mr.
Deters advised the council could delay enforcement until such time that this
matter is settled.
27.   Council Member Yeager motioned to grant Mr. Jarboe a stay of enforcement,
with second by Council Member Ellison. Roll call was unanimous and the motion
carried 5-0 in favor.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2002/03 Budget – 1st Reading
28.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading an ordinance that

discussion Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to read the proposed ordinance
amending the 2002/03 budget. Mayor Moriconi advised the final reading and
enactment of this ordinance would be presented at the next business meeting of
council.

MAY 19, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE
COUNCIL CAUCUS MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence met on Monday May 19, 2003 at 7:00
p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Moriconi presiding.
Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. The
roll was called and the following council members were present: Council Member
Jim Ellison, Council Member Donna Yeager, Council Member Carol Franzen, Council
Member Mary Pat Behler, Council Member Jim Bushong and Council Member Otis
Ketron. Also present was City Attorney, Mr. Charles Deters, and City
Administrator, Mark Wendling.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi stated Barry Malott of Malco Services signed in for privileges
of the floor and asked to address council.
Mr. Malott who currently holds a contract with the city for park and lawn
maintenance, asked council and mayor to go over the bids for maintenance very
carefully. He did point out that he does not charge for edging around sidewalks
or parking lots and noted the other bidders have added a fee for this service.
He feels his bid is very competitive with the other bidders and wanted council
to know he has been contracting with the city for over eight years and pays
over $460.00 yearly in taxes for his business. He advised council and mayor he
would answer any questions they might have and just wanted them to realize he
thinks his past record with the city speaks for his business.
Mr. Steve Rymarquis of 4744 Crowe Road advised mayor and council that Crowe
Road is slipping into the creek. He stated no repairs have been performed on
this road in years. He stated when Council Member Ellison was mayor, he did
move the shape of the creek but a flood washed that out again.
Council Member Behler asked if Crowe Road was a city road.
Mr. Wendling stated it was and our city engineer did look at.
Mr. Rymarquis stated that Estes Engineering inspected the road several years
ago but nothing was ever done.
Council Member Yeager stated that the Army Corp of Engineers also looked at
Crowe Road several years ago.
Council Member Franzen advised Mr. Rymarquis that she would get with Jeff
Smith, Public Works Department and make an inspection of the road.
Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Rymarquis he will be notified if they have all the
information gathered by the next council meeting.
Mr. Louis Enzweiler at 619 Independence Station Road advised mayor and council
that he received a letter in March 2003 inquiring as to the status of sidewalks
in front of this property. Mr. Enzweiler stated when the site plan was approved
by NKAPC, there were no sidewalks noted. He stated he has nothing against
sidewalks but there is a problem with the feasibility issue and the
construction of sidewalks. Due to the slope of the land, trees will have to be
removed along Independence Station Road. He stated after the trees are removed
he will have to shore up a portion of the property in order to level the
foundation of the sidewalk. He stated the Kenton County Golf Course drains on
to this property from the other side of the street and also the drainage ditch
line maintained by the county would flow across the sidewalk. He stated it
would cost around $5,000.00 to install sidewalks and is requesting a waiver so
he can obtain a final occupancy permit. He stated the county engineer inspected
the site and advised it would be impossible to put in a sidewalk.
Council Member Ketron asked Mr. Enzweiler how much road footage is in front of
the property.
Mr. Enzweiler stated there is 150 feet of road footage.
Council Member Bushong asked how a waiver would be granted.
Mr. Enzweiler stated that NKAPC told him it is a city issued waiver and if the
city doesn’t have a problem they can issue a certificate of occupancy.
Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Enzweiler if any of the adjoining property
owners have sidewalks.
Mr. Enzweiler stated there is not a sidewalk within a half-mile of this
property.
Council Member Franzen asked if none of the other properties were required to
install sidewalks, why does he have to.
Mr. Wendling stated the subdivision regulations require sidewalks on all new
development. When Mr. Enzweiler filed his plat with NKAPC, he did not have
sidewalks on the site plan, and they approved the site plan without the
sidewalks. He stated Mr. Enzweiler has built houses without sidewalks and he
was advised the houses have to have sidewalks before a final occupancy can be
issued. Mr. Wendling stated it is a steep terrain but as more development goes
around this property, the city would eventually have to pay to have the
sidewalks put in if Mr. Enzweiler does not have to.
Attorney Charles Deters asked if the present ordinance requires, under
subdivisions, to have sidewalks.
Mr. Enzweiler stated his interpretation of a subdivision is if you can
interpret a subdivision to one lot divided into two lots by definition.
Attorney Charles Deters asked Mr. Enzweiler when the lot split from the large
lot.
Mr. Enzweiler stated in August or September of 2001.
Mayor Moriconi stated they would bring this back to the June meeting for a
vote.
OLD BUSINESS
Zone Change and Additional Annexation-Glenhurst Development
Mr. Chuck Berling stated that NKAPC has advised him that the way the zoning is
set up, they cannot donate the 25 acres to the Kenton County Board of
Education. The acreage would have to go to the city first and then the city can
decide what to do with the green space before the subdivision gets completed.
Mr. Wendling asked Mr. Berling if he is correct in saying that the city can
deed the property over to the school district, but Glenhurst Development cannot
do it directly.
Mr. Berling stated NKAPC requires that the space must to go to a public entity.
The school board for some reason does not fall under that. He stated the
property has to come to the city first.
Attorney Charles Deters asked if the plat was originally designated to the
city. Mr. Berling stated it was. Attorney Charles Deters commented that is
probably the reason it has to go to the city first.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Berling if they are going to put in utilities on this
property. Mr. Berling stated they are going to put in the utilities, sewer,
water, and, provide sidewalks on both frontages of the site.
Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Berling if he felt the city should decide what
they are going to use it for. Mr. Berling stated the city should look at their
options. He stated the site plan does show a lake utilized for detention and is
sized big enough to serve the school board for their detention. If it stays as
recreational use, the city doesn’t necessarily need a lake. Those issues need
to be discussed.
Council Member Behler asked Mr. Berling how soon he would need a decision from
the city.
Mr. Berling stated they would need four to six months to submit the special
design plans.
FINAL REVIEW of the PROPOSED 2003/2004 BUDGET
Mayor Moriconi stated a few things have come up recently regarding the police
budget. He stated at the last mayors meeting they discussed lap tops that sit
in police cruisers that the officer can enter all the data on a vehicle
directly instead of going thru Kenton County Dispatch. The county has received
a $1,000,000.00 grant, which they will use to assist in the expense of some of
the MDT’s. He stated there would never be a better time or price to purchase
this equipment.
Mayor Moriconi asked Chief Butler to explain the importance of the Mobile Data
Terminals.
Chief Butler stated he would like to explain why this expense did not show in
the new budget. He stated the facts on the MDT’s have only unfolded in the last
two weeks. He stated this project has been worked on for the past three years,
countywide. He stated Kenton County Fiscal Court is willing to make up the
additional one third funding with the final one third funding being divided by
the cities. He stated the terminals are more than just a computer in their
cruiser. It actually entails building an entire infrastructure throughout the
county. In discussions with the mayor in regards to what is important to the
police department, Chief Butler stated he would like to have both a new officer
and the MDT’s but knows that is not possible. In an effort to make the
department more efficient and do a better job is to give officers the tools to
better use their time on the street and felt this is the best way to go for the
next budget year. Chief Butler stated this would take approximately $30,000.00
out of what the department has asked for. Chief Butler stated the terminals
should reduce the police officers time on a traffic stop from twenty-two
minutes to approximately nine minutes. As far as safety issues, the officer
will know what they are dealing with before they even stop a car in regards to
being stolen or warrants on the persons in the cars. Chief Butler stated it was
a tough decision foregoing an additional officer but he felt the city should
take advantage of this opportunity. He stated the cost would be approximately
$35,000.00 a year for ten years. It will cover all costs, all air time costs,
all upgrades to the system.
Council Member Behler asked if a terminal would go in each squad car.
Chief Butler stated there will be twenty terminals and would go in all patrol
cars and supervisor cars.
Council Member Ellison asked if ongoing training would be given.
Chief Butler stated the officer has to be certified by attending an eight-hour
training course given by the Kentucky State Police.
Council Member Franzen asked what else are the computers capable of.
Chief Butler stated the computers would allow the officers to literally do a
field report in the field instead of having to go back to the office to do the
paperwork.
Mayor Moriconi stated this information was received since the first reading of
the 2003/2004 Budget.
Mr. Wendling stated the budget would not have to be modified as long as the
monies come out of the police budget.
Council Member Bushong asked Janet Rebman, Finance Director why the decrease
under Tangible Property Taxes.
Ms. Rebman stated there is no certain percentage increase in tangible tax.
Tangible taxes are hard to predict and she was trying to be conservative.
Council Member Ellison asked Ms. Rebman if the $202,454.00 was also estimated
high and you budgeted less for 2003/2004, he did not see where the decrease
would apply.
Ms. Rebman stated the original budget for 2002/2003 was $179,000.00. She stated
she increased it on the amended budget because it was coming in higher. She
stated she did not increase it the second time because again she was being
conservative.
Council Member Bushong stated he was not comfortable in giving the elected
officials an increase in pay.
Mr. Wendling stated that raise was established by ordinance, and council would
have to pass another ordinance changing that.
Council Member Franzen and Council Member Behler both agreed with Council
Member Bushong.
Council Member Franzen stated under the Senior Center Fund there is a transfer
from the General Fund of $115,000.00. She asked why the Senior Center Board is
not taking in more money since they control the building and why is the city
paying $115,000.00.
Mr. Wendling stated the Senior Center Board and the city had an agreement on
the salary for the director. The first year they paid $40,000.00 and the second
year they paid $20,000.00 toward the director’s salary. He stated the Senior
Board does not control the center. They do have use of it between the hours of
9:00 a.m. and 3:00 p.m. but the city does set policy for the building. All
monies paid to use the building for whatever purpose is turned over to the
city.
Council Member Franzen stated she is having a problem with it because the city
is short of money and the Public Works Department needs another employee and
the police department needs another employee and the city is giving $115,000.00
to the Senior Center.
Council Member Ellison proposed that the city enter into a hiring freeze.
Council Member Franzen stated she takes issue with Council Member Ellison’s
suggested hiring freeze considering he voted to spend $245,000.00 of the city’s
money for a council chamber section in the new Municipal Center. She stated he
also voted for the construction of the Senior Center and now supports the
building of an Amphitheater, all of which the city cannot afford the associated
operational expenses of these buildings. Council Member Franzen strongly
disagreed with a hiring freeze, as she feels it would place the citizens and
police at risk.
Council Member Yeager stated the amphitheater would not cost the city anything
as the state has contributed $200,000 with another $75,000 of private donations
received for his project.
Council Member Franzen stated it has to be insured, it has to be maintained and
the city has to pay acts to perform and the police have to monitor the crowd.
She stated we haven’t hired a public works employee in four years and a police
officer in five years.
Council Member Behler stated she agrees with Council Member Franzen in that the
city needs to supplement the Public Works Department. She stated when she read
the information given to her by Jeff Smith she was appalled by how understaffed
that department is.
Council Member Franzen stated we have city streets that need repairs but we
keep building. She stated she is all for the buildings if the city has the
money to do it, but we don’t have the money to do it.
Mr. Bill Cobble addressed council on how many police officers are required for
a certain number of citizens.
Chief Butler stated that the norm is 2.6 officers per 1,000 citizens.
Mr. Cobble asked if the number of citizens that live in Harvest Hill
Subdivision is included in that count.
Chief Butler stated that subdivision is not in the city limits.
Mr. Cobble stated that Independence Police do go there to answer calls.
Chief Butler stated only in emergency situations.
Mr. Cobble stated if they do not pay city taxes then the Independence Police
Department should not respond to their calls.
Chief Butler stated if there is an emergency situation and one of his officers
is one minute away and the county police are twenty minutes away, then they
will respond. He stated the county police would do the same thing for them.
Mrs. JoAnn Cobble stated the city should bill the county police for answering
calls out of their jurisdiction.
Mayor Moriconi stated police try to back each other up when an emergency
arrives.
Mr. John Sanders of Pioneer Drive stated he had the opportunity to talk with
Council Member Franzen after she rode with one of our police officers. He
stated he was shocked when he was told there were only three officers on the
street for that shift. Mayor Moriconi stated he appreciates the comments and
technically the city should have thirty policemen and we only have twenty-
three.
Mayor Moriconi stated essentially there is no hiring in this budget.
Mr. Cobble asked why the new mayor and council did not put off building the
municipal center if the knew we were short on funds. Council Member Franzen
stated she suggested that. Mr. Cobble stated he is not against a new city
building if we have the money.
Mayor Moriconi stated that was hashed out two years ago as a campaign issue but
it is a done deal. The county wants the space back that the police department
is renting. He stated it is embarrassing for a city this size not to have a
permanent home for our police department. The fiscal court gave the city a
certain amount of time to vacate the space so the city decided if they had to
build a police building then we should consolidate everything under one roof.
Since that time the debt has been refinanced, the payment cut in half and now
has a locked interest rate. He stated the building is no longer an issue and
that is not why we are here today. He stated the city should have been hiring
police officers throughout the years. The city did not get into this situation
in the last six months or because we built that building. The city was not
taking the compensating 4% over the years for the taxes and no planning. This
all didn’t happen because we were elected, this goes back years. To answer your
question we were forced to do something and Mayor Kriege deserves a lot of
credit for getting all of this started. He stated he is proud of the way he
voted and he would not change it. Mayor Moriconi asked if anyone else had any
questions regarding the budget.
Council Member Yeager stated she has spoke to Mr. Wendling and Ms. Rebman
regarding the format of the budget and some changes are going to be made.
Council Member Ellison stated it is a little difficult to follow.
NEW BUSINESS
BIDS-LAWN MAINTENANCE
Mayor Moriconi stated under new business is the review of the lawn maintenance
bids. He stated five bids were received and Barry Malott of Malco Services
spoke earlier and gave us some paperwork on his pricing. He stated that Ridge
Runners of Dry Ridge had the lowest bid followed by Executive Lawn Care,
Jackson’s, Malco and then RPC.
Council Member Ellison noted that Ridge Runners quoted $40.00 per time at

some background references on the bids and find out if Jackson’s is located in
Taylor Mill.
Mayor Moriconi suggested that references be obtained from Ridge Runners and
Jackson’s and be brought back to the next council meeting.
Council Member Ellison noted Executive Lawn Care did not quote a price for
Glenhurst Park and did not feel that Glenhurst Park would require a lot of
mowing.
Mayor Moriconi stated this contract would take the mowing into late summer,
fall and next spring.
Mr. Wendling stated Glenhurst Park is ready for mowing at this time due to
grass seed being sewn earlier.
SPEED LIMIT-TAYLOR MILL RD
Mayor Moriconi stated Mr. Martin Neltner is asking the city to pass a
resolution lowering the speed limit from 45 mph to 35 mph on the stretch of
Taylor Mill Road that is in our city.
Mr. Wendling asked if council thought 45 mph on Taylor Mill Road is excessive.
He stated that Council Member Franzen rode with Officer Schultz and only one
person was pulled over for speeding, which was 51 mph.
Council Member Bushong stated until the new reconstruction of Taylor Mill Road
has started the city doesn’t really know what kind of plans they have regarding
the speed. He suggested that the city do nothing at this time.
Council Member Behler stated she travels Taylor Mill Road everyday and does not
feel anything needs to be done at this time.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Wendling to contact Mr. Neltner advising him council
does not feel the city needs to make any changes at this time.
SIDEWALK REGULATION-INDEPENDENCE ROAD
Mayor Moriconi stated new development is planned at the intersection of Cody
Road and Independence Station Road, to the northeast, which will have 228
homes. He stated NKAPC waived the sidewalk requirements for that part of
development that will front Independence Station Road.
Mr. Wendling stated what normally happens is a developer will request a waiver
on sidewalks. If it is requested in advance, it will go on the agenda so the
city or any other interested party can attend a public hearing and voice their
objections if there are any. This waiver was not placed on the agenda, so you
assume there is no waiver requested. Council then did not have an opportunity
to take a position on it. The developer brought it up at the hearing and
evidentially it was granted at the hearing.  
Council Member Ellison stated that Independence Station Road is dangerously
narrow, and he thought if they were to put in sidewalks, he was going to
suggest the developer be made to set enough land aside on Independence Station
Road down to the railroad tracks to widen the road.
Mr. Wendling stated the developer has just recently applied for a zone change
from R1-A to R1-C, which will go to the planning commission at its June
commission hearing and will come back to the city in July.
TEXT AMENDMENT-OUTDOOR DINING IN NC ZONE
Mayor Moriconi stated Pasquale’s Pizza had approached him regarding a text
amendment permitting the restaurant to do outdoor dining.
Mr. Wendling stated they want to put a couple of tables on their front porch
fronting Madison Pike for out door dining. Mr. Wendling stated he has advised
Mr. David Lee that the zoning ordinance prohibits this. He stated council would
have to do a text amendment for a conditional use in a neighborhood zone.
Council Member Ellison stated he felt the city should pass a text amendment but
needs to add conditions.
INTER-LOCAL AGREEMENT WITH KENTON COUNTY/ANIMAL CONTROL
Mayor Moriconi stated council was asked to review the Inter-Local Agreement
with Kenton County Animal Control Services. Council Member Franzen asked if
anything had changed in the agreement other than Kenton County Police
overseeing the dog authority. Mr. Wendling stated it was originally going to be
with the Kenton County Animal Shelter but the county felt the Kenton County
Police could better manage it because they are an enforcement agency and the
shelter is not. Council Member Ellison asked if the dog authority employees
would be able to keep their seniority, wages and benefits. Mr. Wendling stated
nothing would change for the employees.
CITY ATTORNEY REPORT – Jed K. Deters
SUNDAY LIQUOR SALES
Mayor Moriconi stated City Attorney Jed Deters reviewed the Kentucky Statutes
for liquor sales and the statutes do provide that each municipality may set its
own time for liquor and beers sales by ordinance.
Council Member Bushong asked if this was mainly to benefit Kenton County Golf
Course. Mayor Moriconi stated the golf course wants to be able to sell beer by
11:00 a.m. on Sundays.
Council Member Behler asked what is the benefit to the city.
Mayor Moriconi stated he was advised the golfers are bringing beer to the golf
course because they cannot buy it until l:00 p.m. so by changing the time the
golf course can generate more revenue.
Council Member Franzen stated if an ordinance is drafted, is the city going to
sell liquor licenses to generate revenue for the city. She stated she was not
in favor of changing the time but if the city can generate revenue she would
not be against the ordinance.
Mr. Wendling stated if the city proceeds to sell liquor licenses to
restaurants, it would also include stores that sell packaged liquor. Mr.
Wendling stated he would further research this matter regarding the fee for a
liquor license in other cities.
BUSINESS RECOGNITION OF THE MONTH
Council Member Ellison stated he would like to recognize State Farm Insurance
that has been in the since city November 1979.
ADJOURNMENT
Council Member Yeager moved to adjourn with a second by Council Member Ellison.
Motion carried and the meeting adjourned at 8:45 p.m.

JUNE 2, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June
2, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Mr. Jim Kudera gave the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler,
Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also
present was City Attorney, Jed Deters and Mark Wendling, City Administrator.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Ellison has selected State Farm
Insurance, Agent Greg Wermuth as recipient of the Business of the Month
tribute. Unfortunately Mr. Wermuth was ill and not able to attend this meeting.
Mayor Moriconi suggested presenting the plaque to Mr. Wermuth next month, along
with the July Business of the Month recipient.
Approval of the Minutes of the May 5, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the May 5,
2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Ketron so moved, with second
from Council Member Franzen. Several amendments were noted and approved and
roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the May 19, 2003 Caucus Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the May 19,
2003 caucus meeting of council. Council Member Bushong moved, with second from
Council Member Behler. Several amendments were noted and approved. Roll call
was answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
PRIVELEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Betty Eichelberger, 6258 Taylor Mill Road, addressed council regarding
several concerns. Her first concern was the recent activity on the property
located at the corner of Cox and Taylor Mill Roads. Mayor Moriconi advised her
that he believes that the owner is planning to construct about 38-40 new
single-family homes. Mr. Wendling stated that the land is being cleared, but
the developer has not yet filed a plat. Ms. Eichelberger was concerned about
the ingress/egress location on Cox Road. She also asked about the size of this
development. Mr. Deters, City Attorney, stated that the developer would have to
comply with the permitted use of that zone. Mayor Moriconi stated that he
thought the development would be 80-foot residential lots.
6.   Ms. Eichelberger reported that the property located at 6215 Taylor Mill
Road is operating a car repair shop. This property has an ever-present wrecker
with cars and a boat with for-sale signs parked in front. She reported that the
garage is being expanded. She complained that she has not been able to reach
the city’s Zoning Administrator. Council Member Behler requested that Mr.
Wendling make sure that the Zoning Administrator contacts Ms. Eichelberger.
7.   Ms. Eichelberger pointed out another high weeds and grass zoning violation
at the Shadybrook Trails Subdivision off of Taylor Mill Road. She stated that
the grass had not been mowed during the spring and was a foot tall before it
was recently cut. Mr. Wendling stated he would see that the Zoning
Administrator monitors this property.
8.   Ms. Eichelberger asked who would be inspecting Marty Neltner’s property to
ensure that the building codes will be adhered to. Mr. Wendling replied that
the building inspector will oversee this development during the construction
process and since this is a commercial development Northern Kentucky Area
Planning will perform the inspections.
9.   Ms. Eichelberger’s last concern was who was responsible for declaring a
‘burn ban.’ Council Member Yeager stated that the Fire Chief at the
Independence Fire District would be the person to issue a ‘burn ban’. She also
stated that at specific times of the year a ‘burn ban’ is routinely in effect.
10.   John Sanders, 5268 Pioneer Drive, read a prepared statement to council
wherein he expressed his concern regarding the city’s current level of revenue
and growing operational expenses. He stated the Senior/Community Center and
Memorial Park amphitheater are nice facilities to have, but questioned how the
city would provide future operational funding for these buildings. Mr. Sanders
suggested imposing a builder’s franchise fee of at least $200.00 per house. He
stated this would provide the city with the necessary funds to continue police
protection and other city services from the outset instead of cutting other
worthy items from the budget. Mr. Sanders also suggested enacting a city
alcohol sales permit, which he acknowledged would not generate a lot of
revenue, but felt would increase over time. He stated that city auto stickers
would also produce much needed revenue that would be another growth product.
Mr. Sanders stated that the residents primary public services concerns are
Public Works and Police Department related and urged council to address the
staffing needs in those departments. In closing, Mr. Sanders urged council to
dedicate their efforts in the coming year to finding innovative ways of raising
revenue without weakening the pockets of the senior citizens.
11.   Chuck Kahrs, 21 Oby Drive addressed council regarding the on-going
problem with speeding drivers on Oby Drive. He stated that he has been working
together with the Police Chief to solve this traffic problem on their street.
Chief Butler stated he has been there numerous times during the past month. Mr.
Kahrs requested that the city install speed bumps or a street sign midway along
the street.
12.   Another resident on the street, David Millward, 25 Oby Drive concurred
that the speeding has become a bad situation, stating this has become a problem
due to the increased traffic on this street coming from the development of the
Freedom Trail area. Council Member Behler asked if the city had a policy
regarding the installation of stop signs. Chief Butler stated that the city
recently passed an ordinance that would allow him to use his discretion in
considering a solution. He stated he will inspect the area to see if it
conforms to the guidelines as generally stop signs are not installed midway
through a street. Council Member Ellison agreed that in this particular
situation a stop sign might be warranted. Council Member Yeager also agreed
that if Chief Butler determines that the criteria support the need, that a stop
sign should be installed. Mayor Moriconi advised Chief Butler to make the
determination regarding this matter.
Ordinance No. 2003-O- 05 – Amending the 2002/03 Budget Ordinance No. 2002-O-11
– 2nd Reading

Ordinance that would approve a city budget for the 2003/04 fiscal year. Mayor

coming year. Companies submitting bids were Executive Lawn Care, Ridge Runners
Outdoor Home Care, RPC Mechanical, Inc., Jackson’s Lawn Care and Malco Lawn

He stated that the references checked for Jackson’s Lawn Care reported

Services has held the city contract for this service for the last several years

base bid with five alternate bids:
Alternate #1 – Concrete Pavement
Alternate #2 – Additional Grading & Seeding
Alternate #3 – 400 Amp Electric
Alternate #4 – 800 Amp Electric
Alternate #5 – Electric Line to Sanitary Lift Station

recommending that B.L. Spille Construction be awarded this project for the base
bid along with alternates 1, 2, 4 and 5 for a total contract amount of
$202,956.00.
20.   Council Member Bushong moved with second by Council Member Yeager to

$202,956.00. A brief discussion ensued wherein Council Member Ellison

stated that the electric line would not run from the Municipal Center. Council
Member Bushong asked if this change order for the Municipal Center would show
up as a credit. Mayor Moriconi stated the Municipal Center would be credited
for this expense. Roll call was answered with five yes votes and one no vote
cast by Council Member Franzen. Council Member Franzen clarified her vote by
asserting the amphitheater would cause operational expenses the city could not

Resolution No. 2003-R-12 – Interlocal Agreement with Kenton County for Animal

Council Member Bushong expressed concern that this consolidation of the Kenton
County Dog Authority and Kenton County Fiscal Court would have an adverse
effect on the number of dog handlers. Mr. Wendling advised that this concern
was addressed in the agreement. He stated there would be a total of four dog
controllers, which includes the two Dog Authority employees who would transfer

with the understanding that the employees working for the Kenton County Dog
Authority would not lose their job due to this merger. Motion carried 4-2.
Resolution No. 2003-R-13 – Supporting a Text Amendment to Add Outdoor Dining
Facilities in the NC and NSC Zones
22.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the owner of Pasquale’s Pizza, David Lee has
approached the city regarding his desire to set up an outdoor dining area at
the restaurant. He stated that the city’s current zoning ordinance does not
permit outdoor dining. He presented for council’s consideration a resolution
that would support a zoning text amendment that would permit outdoor dining as
a conditional use in the NC (neighborhood commercial) and NSC (neighborhood
shopping center) zones. Mr. Wendling stated that if council approves this
resolution it would be submitted to the Kenton County Planning Commission for
review at their July 10 public hearing. Mr. Lee stated that about two months
ago he spoke with Mr. Wendling and Mayor Moriconi regarding his plans for the
restaurant. He stated that he has had a successful first year and would like to
work with the city to continue the enhancement of the downtown area. He stated
that the downtown area is viable and growing and he has a good feel for the
area. He would like to set up a minimal outdoor dining area in the front to
provide another dining alternative for his customers. He stated his future
plans include the purchase of the building from Mr. Ponzer, a full service
alcohol bar and outdoor dining in the rear.
23.   Council Member Bushong stated that he endorses this text amendment. He
stated he has reviewed Mr. Lee’s outdoor dining plans and feels it will be a
good addition to the downtown area.
24.   Mr. Deters read the resolution. Council Member Ellison moved to approve
Resolution No. 2003-R-13, with second by Council Member Bushong. Roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.

Proposed Ordinance – Zone Change Request for 130 Acres of the Glenhurst

JUNE 16, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL CAUCUS MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 16,
2003 at 7:05 p.m. in the Independence Senior/Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and
Donna Yeager. Council Member Jim Ellison was absent. Also present was City
Attorney, Jed Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Public Comment on the Mayor’s Decision to Non-Renew the City Administrator’s
Contract
Sherry Carran, 927 Forest Avenue, Covington, Kentucky, introduced herself as
the Board Supervisor of the Kenton County Conservation District. She stated
that her work is mainly volunteer and that she addresses the concerns of
conserving natural resources. She stated she is very involved in land use
issues and has been active in raising awareness concerning the Banklick
Watershed.
Ms. Carran stated that she had discussed the Glenhurst Subdivision development
with Mr. Wendling on a couple of occasions and expressed concern how the city
would be able to manage the rapid growth without a full time city
administrator. She stated the elected city officials have limited time to
oversee these developments. She stated that she had also spoken to Mr. Wendling
about the deteriorating condition of Crowe Road, how it is falling into the
Banklick Creek, and how she had agreed to assist Mr. Wendling with finding a
solution for this problem.
Ms. Carran also spoke to the Independence Station Road project planned by Mr.
Berling. She stated that the city currently does not permit PUD’s (Planned
Urban Developments) and urged council to be more open to innovative approaches
in this city that is experiencing rapid residential growth. She pointed out
that the city has very little commercial development and advised the city will
always have budgetary constraints if commercial areas are not planned. She
stated the quality of life for residents is important, as is good roads,
adequate green space and a fiscally responsible budget. She stated that a city
administrator is valuable in this process.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the city is aware of the need for more commercial
growth and have avenues that will be followed for all developments. He advised
that the city council still has the final say for zone change requests. Mayor
Moriconi assured Ms. Carran that the city would continue to operate without a
city administrator.
Beverly Stewart, 808 Stephens Road, Independence, stated that she is a nursing
manager with St. Elizabeth Hospital South. She addressed council regarding her
concern over the loss of a city administrator. She stated that she called the
city office to request a copy of the job description for the city administrator
position and expressed displeasure that she was told she would have to complete
a public records request form and that it would take three days to obtain it.
She stated she does not find this procedure acceptable.
Ms. Stewart went on to say that she is concerned how the city will oversee the
new capital developments, such as the Municipal Center, parks and Amphitheater
as well as the tremendous residential growth without a city administrator on
staff. She stated that this position would oversee expansion, and fears the
city will be out of balance and will find incorporating these new projects
difficult.
Kari Ward, 10414 Calvary Road, Independence also addressed council regarding
the elimination of the city administrator position. She stated that having
three employees assume the duties of another person’s job is not effective
government, especially in light of the capital projects the city has recently
initiated. She stated that she felt it would be necessary to have one person to
communicate and coordinate these projects.
Ms. Ward also voiced her concern regarding the water drainage problem at
Memorial Park and felt that a city administrator could address this issue as
well as assisting in beautifying the city parks.
Council Member Yeager addressed Ms. Ward’s concern about the drainage problem
at Memorial Park by advising the city has had three engineers and the city’s
public works department try to solve that problem area in the park. Ms. Ward
stated the area is near the playground and is swampland. She also complained
that the park has no bathroom facility. Council Member Yeager reported that the
city has plans to construct a bathroom facility. Mayor Moriconi advised Ms.
Ward that the city is very aware of the drainage issue in Memorial Park and
will continue to assess this area to solve the swampy condition of the area
near the playground.
Mayor Moriconi also addressed the public concerns regarding the elimination of
the city administrator position. He stated it is not uncommon for a city to
function without a city administrator. He complimented the city staff by
stating they are very knowledgeable of their jobs and expressed confidence that
business would be handled effectively. He assured everyone that, if in six
months or so he finds it necessary, he will re-evaluate the situation. Council
Member Behler expressed her concern with the Mayor’s decision to eliminate the
city administrator position. She stated she has been doing some research
comparing Independence with other cities in the Kenton, Boone and Campbell
counties. She advised that Independence is a third class city along with
Erlanger and Florence: both Erlanger and Florence have a city administrator.
She stated that a third class city is one that has a population in the range of
8,000 and 19,999. She advised that she has learned that only some fourth-class
cities have administrators, mainly those with a higher population and larger
land area. Council Member Behler stated that she feels the city needs to look
at reducing other expenses and discussing possible revenue enhancements in
order to restore the city administrator position.
Council Member Franzen stated that she supports the Mayor’s decision and also
wants what is best for the city. She stated that she voted against the
amphitheater project, as she does not feel the city can afford to operate the
facility once it is built. She went on to say that all the residential growth
is added expense for the city because the cost to provide services to the
increased population is exceeding the revenue generated by these homes.
Council Member Yeager answered that the amphitheater isn’t costing the city;
the money to build it has come from the state and private donations. She stated
the city would work at acquiring sponsors for bringing in the various bands and
other entertainment, just as other cities and counties do.
Mayor Moriconi remarked that over the last six months he has made some changes;
hired a new attorney and city engineer. He stated it is his job to represent a
population of nearly 15,000 residents and that in a perfect world the city
would have employees such as an administrator or an economic developer. He
stated that Independence couldn’t be compared to Florence or Erlanger, who have
much larger tax bases. Council Member Behler countered that smaller fourth-
class cities have administrators and with Independence having 17.66 square
miles this city is bigger than other cities. She maintained that with a growth
average of 300 homes each year if will be difficult to take stock without a
city administrator.
Canberra Ridge Subdivision – Sidewalk Waiver Request on Independence Station
Road
Mayor Moriconi called on Mr. Jim Berling and Mr. Jim Wenstrup of the Scheben
Group who were present to discuss the sidewalk concern along Independence
Station Road where the Canberra Ridge development will be located. Council
Member Behler advised that a sidewalk along Independence Station Road was not
indicated on the preliminary plat that was approved by the Planning Commission.
She stated that the omission of a sidewalk was an oversight and has not been
officially waived by the city. Mr. Berling stated that the Planning Commission
staff recommendation included sidewalks for the streets within the subdivision
but due to the severe topography on Independence Station Road that sidewalks
were not recommended along that street. He stated that this was the initiative
of the Planning Commission, not theirs. He stated they would be working with
Kenton County to widen that section of Independence Station Road for safety
reasons. He stated the development of Canberra Ridge will bring about
intersection improvements to the area of Independence Station Road and Cody
Road and that a sidewalk is planned for the area between the intersection and
the entrance into Canberra Ridge. He stated there is a real safety concern in
developing sidewalks from the subdivision entrance on down toward the railroad
tracks.
Council Member Yeager stated that sidewalks would provide access to the
Banklick Woods Park, just up and over the railroad tracks. Mr. Berling
commented that the Scheben Group does not own the property along there. Mr.
Deters asked if the Planning Commission has approved the preliminary plat. Mr.
Berling stated it has and that he is before council to discuss the sidewalk
concerns on Independence Station Road. Council Member Franzen suggested that
the property owners along the road be required to install sidewalks. Mayor
Moriconi stated that Mr. Berling was present to discuss the concerns that were
raised at the last caucus meeting. Council Member Behler asked if the city
might install sidewalks in the future. Mayor Moriconi stated he does not
foresee this as the railroad crossing only has warning lights in that area. Mr.
Berling stated they would work with Kenton County on the necessary road
improvements in the area. Mayor Moriconi asked how long this development would
take to construct. Mr. Berling responded five to six years. Council Member
Franzen stated that she has concerns that someone would be struck by a car.
Discussion to Amend Ordinance No. 2000-O-02 Relating to Compensation of Elected
Officials
Mr. Deters stated that he was absent from last month’s caucus meeting when this
matter was initially introduced. He asked council what their desire was
regarding this legislation. Council Members Yeager and Ketron advised that
council discussed amending Ordinance No. 2000-O-02 to eradicate the scheduled
increase in compensation for council members that will become effective on
March 1,2004. Mayor Moriconi stated that keeping the current compensation is an
effort by council to cut back expenses due to budget constraints. Mr. Deters
advised that he will research the statutes, but stated that he has misgivings
that this ordinance is constitutional. He stated he would review and prepare a
proposal for an amendment.
Discussion Regarding Bids Received for the Sale of 68-A Oby Drive
Mayor Moriconi advised the city received two bids last week for city owned
property located at 68-A Oby Drive. The bids received were from Seaward and
Lori Padilla, 1866 Freedom Trail in the amount of $11,888 and Russell K.
Holloway, 68 Oby Drive in the amount of $1,601. Mayor Moriconi advised that the
award of this bid would be on the July 7, 2003 council meeting agenda.
Mr. Padilla addressed council regarding two concerns. He reported that Mr.
Holloway has cleared his property that adjoins the city lot and stacked the
trees and foliage onto the lot he has bid on. He stated he would like this
debris removed prior to the closing. Secondly he stated that he would like to
know the exact boundary lines of this property and therefore is willing to
assume the cost of having the land surveyed. He stated that if Mr. Holloway has
stepped over those boundary lines and bulldozed the trees and vegetation on the
city property he would like council to address that situation and replace the
trees that were destroyed. Mr. Padilla submitted photos of the land area that
Mr. Holloway has bulldozed for council’s inspection. Mr. Deters asked if the
trees stumps were also uprooted. Mr. Padilla replied yes.
Mr. Holloway responded by stating the area he cleared is within the boundary
lines of his property. He stated he would remove the debris when the area
dries. He stated the trees he removed were scrub trees and full of poison ivy.
He stated that this city owned property has never been maintained in the four
years he has lived there.
Mr. Padilla stressed that he would like the land cleared of any debris that may
have been stacked on this property prior to a closing with the city. Mr. Deters
advised that the area will be inspected and a contingency will be included in
the contract if necessary for the removal of the cleared trees and vegetation.
Mayor Moriconi reiterated that council would take action to award this bid at
the July 7th meeting.
Presentation by Barry Burke of NKAPC Regarding Proposed Street Name Changes
Mr. Burke stated that he was the Deputy Director of Engineering and Inspection
Services with the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission. He stated that
the recent state and county road realignments and improvements have resulted in
the formation of many spurs or remnant streets. Mr. Burke advised that it is
the governing body’s responsibility to approve re-addressing changes that are
necessary to provide for public safety for the residents.
The following streets have been identified as problems affecting traffic safety
and property locations:
1.   Hogreffe Road – The spelling has been revised to spell Hogreffe with one
‘f’ (Hogrefe)
2.   Old Bristow Road – This spur has resulted with the realignment of State
Route 536. Another street in the Battleridge Subdivision intersects to the west
enabling an existing street name (Battleridge Drive) to replace that portion of
Old Bristow Road. The affected residents in both Kenton County and Independence
will be surveyed for their input regarding a new road name. Battleridge Drive
will be suggested.
3.   Cody Road & Troopers Crossing – This area of Cody Road was relocated due
to a new subdivision collector street extension. The result has been two street
names and conflicting addressing (both odd and even numbers) along the same
sides of the road. The road in this area was widened which provided needed
improvement. Cody Road is county-maintained. City is being asked to re-name
this portion of Cody Road to Troopers Crossing. Additionally, the house numbers
will need to be changed.
4.   Pelly Road – The relocation of State Route 17 has created three separate
segments of the original unsegmented Pelly Road. It is recommended that on two
of the segments that the residents be surveyed to gain their input.
5.   Relocated Kentucky State Route 17 – Rename the new State Route 17
Alternate to the William W. Bowdy Highway in recognition of Mr. Bowdy’s thirty-
seven years of service to the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission and
his leadership in the planning for the future needs of Kenton County. Mr. Bowdy
recently retired from NKAPC. Each city that a portion of the highway passes
through has been notified of this new designation and since no resistance has
been received NKAPC will move forward at the District level. This should
resolve the naming of the various State Route 17 segments from Hands Pike to
the existing Pelly Road.
Council Member Behler asked if the surveys sent to the residents would explain
that it was necessary to re-naming the streets to avoid public safety concerns.
Mr. Burke stated that an explanation would be given to the residents.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the section of Cody Road near the creek/train overpass
would be permanently closed. Mr. Burke replied that the matter of closing the
area is still under discussion.
Council Member Ketron asked if the section of Cody Road was renamed Troopers
Crossing if Kenton County would continue to maintain the entire roadway. Mr.
Burke replied that the county would still maintain the street, as well as the
other county maintained streets that run throughout the city. Additionally, he
stated that signs would be posted.
Mr. Burke advised that changing street name is never popular with the
residents, but he stated, it is necessary to resolve public safety problems, as
well as plan for future growth and avoid duplications. When the results of the
surveys are compiled and recommendations will be forwarded to council for
consideration and endorsement.
Zone Change Request for 12.7 Acres at Senour Road and Mohawk Lane
Mr. Jerry F. Keith, on behalf of Tim Reese, addressed council regarding a
proposed zone change request for 12.7 acres from R-1C to R-1D at the southeast
corner of Senour Road and Mohawk Lane. Mr. Keith advised council that the
preliminary plat for this development has received recommendation for approval
from the Kenton County Planning Commission. He stated that the R-1D zone would
permit seventy-foot lots, which are more appealing to developers. Mr. Keith
added that intersection improvements are planned that will widen Senour Road to
twenty-two feet. This development will provide for thirty-nine lots that will
interconnect with Clover Ridge Subdivision located to the south of this site.
He stated that this development would also open Mohawk Lane to sanitary sewer
lines, which will benefit the residents in the area. Mr. Keith asked council to
take the initial step to approve this zone change at the July 7th council
meeting with final approval at a special meeting prior to the caucus meeting on
July 21, 2003. Mayor Moriconi stated that an ordinance approving this map
amendment would be presented to council for consideration at the July 7th
meeting.
Senior/Community Center Rental Agreement Update
Ms. Joan Bowling submitted to council the Senior/Community Center rental
agreement indicating some proposed revisions. She stated she has also made some
revisions to the Center’s information pamphlet adding the hours of operation
and rental availability. She stated that Monday through Thursday the Seniors
occupy the entire building from 9:00 a.m. until 3:00 p.m., although this may
vary. She stated that she does not get many requests for rentals during daytime
hours. Council Member Yeager commented that the seniors should have exclusive
daytime use Monday through Friday. Council Member Behler suggested that Ms.
Bowling exercise her judgment to allow use of the facility by others when
seniors will not be using it. Council Member Yeager asked if the Center would
be providing lunches to the seniors five days a week. Ms. Bowling stated that
was yet to be determined. Mayor Moriconi asked who should approve this rental
agreement. Mr. Deters advised that approval of the rental agreement should be
approved by whoever operates the Center. Council Member Yeager stated the
Center is a joint effort by the city and the Board of Directors. Mr. Deters
advised that both should approve the rental agreement. Mayor Moriconi advised
that council would take action on the revised rental agreement at the July 7,
2003 council meeting.
Discussion Regarding the Waiver of a Sidewalk Installation at 619 Independence
Station Road
Mr. Deters explained to council that in 1994 an application was submitted to
the Planning Commission requesting that a waiver for the installation of a
sidewalk be granted to the owner of 619 Independence Station Road. He stated
that the Planning Commission did not take action on this request. He stated
that the owner, Mr. Enzweiler has not been able to obtain a permanent
Certificate of Occupancy because the sidewalk was never installed. Mr. Deters
advised that this situation could be remedied by either re-applying to the
Planning Commission to request the waiver of this subdivision regulation or
request a variance from the city Board of Adjustment.
Mr. Enzweiler stated that everything was approved in 1994 and it was determined
that a sidewalk was not feasible due to the slope of the land. He stated this
issued resurfaced when it came time to obtain a Certificate of Occupancy. He
stated he has discussed this with the staff at Area Planning, who claim this is
a matter the city will need to decide. Mr. Deters responded that the Board of
Adjustment would then need to grant a variance. Mr. Enzweiler stated that the
engineering department at the Planning Commission does not feel that is
necessary and is of the opinion that the city council can grant this waiver.
Mr. Deters stated that the process to apply for a waiver is stated in the
subdivision regulations.
Mr. Deters advised Mr. Enzweiler that he should have no problem in getting the
Planning Commission to review this matter and make comment. Then he can proceed
to apply for a variance from the Board of Adjustment. Mr. Deters advised
council that Mr. Enzweiler has received from the city a temporary Certificate
of Occupancy, but must resolve this sidewalk matter in order to obtain a
permanent certificate.
Business of the Month for July
Council Member Franzen stated that she has chosen Hottees Silk Screen Design
and Apparel, located on Madison Pike, to be recognized at the July meeting.
Speeding on Oby Drive Update
Police Chief Butler reported that after reviewing the situation on Oby Drive,
he has determined that installing a stop sign midway on Oby Drive does not
follow the manual on uniform traffic control. He stated that council can
override this, but he is concerned that the city would be setting precedent by
installing a sign in the middle of a street that does not intersect with
another street. He recommends that the city install a “Children at Play” sign,
continue radar, and the city approve the purchase of a removable speed bump,
which could be used in other areas of the city as well, when speeding
complaints are received. He stated that a stop sign would only temporarily slow
the drivers but eventually they would just roll right through it. He stated
that in the long term the cost of the removable speed bumps would be cheaper
than paying patrol officers overtime pay. Consensus from council was to take
Chief’s Butler’s recommendation and approve the purchase of the removable speed
bumps.
Mayor’s Comments - Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi stated that he has received suggestions from some council
members to replace the current budget format with a user-friendlier one,
similar to that used by the Independence Fire District. He advised that he
would take it under consideration and evaluate a new format.
Discussion Relating to the Initiation of a new Commodities Program
Council Member Yeager stated that she has learned that the Southern Kenton
County area does not have a commodities program and would like to see the city
become involved in the distribution of available commodities. She stated that
she would need to find someone willing to pick up the food to be distributed in
Independence. Council Member Franzen suggested that one of the local churches
might provide space for the distribution. Council Member Yeager stated the food
would be picked up on Monday and distributed on Tuesday. There were suggestions
that the distribution could take place at the Senior/Community Center.
Discussion Relating to Zoning for Sexually Oriented Businesses
Council Member Bushong inquired about the status of designating a city zone for
sexually oriented businesses. Mr. Deters advised that Area Planning is working
on a proposal. The City Clerk stated the city is taking part in a regional
feasibility study that will review the Northern Kentucky area for possible
locations for these types of businesses so that each city does not have to have
a zone. Council Member Bushong stated that the “community area” idea is being
challenged in other areas and commented that it should be a city’s decision
where to locate this type of zone. Mayor Moriconi commented that right now the
city is wide-open, since no such zone has been designated by the city. Mr.
Deters stated this is not new ground and advised he would investigate the
situation.
Discussion Relating to Crowe Road
Council Member Behler asked if the city engineer had provided the city with an
assessment of the deteriorating Crowe Road and given possible recommendations
to correct this problem. Council Member Franzen stated she has inspected the
area and stated that the most cost-effective solution for the city may be to
buyout the property owners. Mayor Moriconi advised he would look into this
matter.
Discussion Relating to Personnel Matters
Council Member Behler asked if the city employees were clear about the
additional duties they would be asked to take on with the elimination of the
city administrator position. Mayor Moriconi informed council that he would
issue an official memo explaining the division of duties.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Bushong moved with second by
Council Member Franzen to adjourn. The meeting ended at 9:07 p.m.

JUNE 16, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special
Session on Monday, June 13, 2003 at 6:30 p.m. in the Independence Senior
Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding in the
Chair. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. The roll was called and the
following council members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong,
Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Council Member Jim Ellison was
absent. Also present was Jed K. Deters, City Attorney.
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   Adopting a Budget for the fiscal year 2003/04 – Ordinance No. 2003-O-06
∙   Resolution No. 2003-R-15 – Ratifying the Mayor’s Decision to Non-renew the
Contract of Mark T. Wendling, City Administrator
Ordinance No. 2003-O-06 – Adopting a Budget for the 2003/04 Fiscal Year
3.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading proposed
Ordinance No. 2003-O-06 that would adopt a city budget for the 2003/04 fiscal
year. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2003-O-06. Council Member Franzen moved
with second by Council Member Bushong to adopt Ordinance No. 2003-O-06. Council
Member Behler questioned if it would be necessary to change the salaries line
item to take out the wages budgeted for a city administrator. Mayor Moriconi
advised that the adjustment could be made later on in the fiscal year. The City
Clerk explained that since the amount budgeted for administration salaries
would not exceed the amount in this proposed budget that the revision could be
noted when the budget is amended. There being no further discussion, the roll
was called and answered with four yeas and one no vote cast by Council Member
Behler. Motion carried 4-1.
Resolution No. 2003-R-15 – Ratifying Mayor Moriconi’s Decision to Non-Renew the
Contract of the City Administrator, Mark T. Wendling
4.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a resolution that would support his
decision to not renew the employment contract of City Administrator, Mark
Wendling. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2003-R-15.
5.   Council Member Yeager moved to approve Resolution No. 2003-R-15, seconded
by Council Member Bushong. Council Member Yeager commented that she hates to
see anyone lose their job, but given the current budgetary constraints, she
supported the Mayor’s decision to non-renew Mr. Wendling’s contract. Council
Member Behler asked if Mr. Wendling would be receiving four months of severance
pay as specified in his contract. Mr. Deters advised that the four months of
severance pay that is referred to in his employment contract was to be paid if
he was terminated for cause prior to June 30, 2003. He stated that basically
Mayor Moriconi has opted to non-renew Mr. Wendling’s contract. Council Member
Behler stated she did not understand the reason council should vote to approve
this non-renewal if this is the Mayor’s choice. Mr. Deters explained that even
though the Mayor has the authority to terminate Mr. Wendling’s employment, the
fact that he had an employment agreement is a gray area, and that by ratifying
the Mayor’s decision both legislative and executive branches would be
integrated. Council Member Franzen expressed concern regarding the continuation
of medical insurance coverage for Mr. Wendling and asked if he would be
eligible for COBRA. Mr. Deters stated that he would, and advised that he wanted
to discuss this in detail in an executive session. Roll call was answered with
four yes votes and one no vote cast by Council Member Behler.
Executive Session
6.   Council Member Bushong moved to enter into executive session in accordance
with K.R.S. 61.810 (f) to discuss a personnel matter pertaining to an employee
dismissal, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
7.   Council Member Bushong moved to return to regular session, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
8.   It was announced that no action was taken.
Adjournment
9.   Upon motion by Council Member Franzen and second by Council Member Bushong
the meeting adjourned. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting ended at 7:00
p.m.
