City of Independence, Ky.
July 7, 2003
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July
7, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Randy McCafferty of the Independence
Christian Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol
Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed
Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Ellison had selected State Farm
Insurance, Agent Greg Wermuth as recipient of the Business of the Month tribute
for June. Since Mr. Wermuth was unable to attend the June meeting, he was
invited to this meeting and Mayor Moriconi presented him with the plaque. Mr.
Wermuth thanked Mayor Moriconi and Council and commented that he has operated
his business out of the same location on Madison Pike since 1979 and has seen
many changes in the city over the years.
3.   Mayor Moriconi presented Hot Tees Silk Screen Design and Apparel with the
July Business of the Month award. Mr. Pat Bradley thanked Council Member
Franzen for selecting Hot Tees as this month’s recipient as Business of the
Month. He stated Hot Tees specializes in business and team apparel, as well as
embroidery design. He stated they have been in operation for three years and
hope to be in business a long time.
Approval of the Minutes of the June 2, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the June 2,
2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second
from Council Member Ketron. One correction was noted and approved and roll call
was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the June 16, 2003 Special Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the June 16,
2003 Special meeting of council. Council Member Bushong moved, with second from
Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted and motion carried with five
ayes and one pass from Council Member Ellison.
Approval of the Minutes of the June 16, 2003 Caucus Council Meeting
6.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the June 16,
2003 caucus meeting of council. Council Member Yeager moved, with second from
Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted and motion carried with five
ayes and one pass from Council Member Ellison.
Privileges of the Floor
7.   Sherry Carran, 927 Forest Avenue, Covington, Kentucky addressed council
with her concerns regarding the planned development by Jim Berling known as
Canberra Ridge Subdivision, to be located off of Independence Station Road
contiguous with Banklick Creek and Brushy Fork Creek. She suggested an
alternative development plan that would decrease the number of homes by twelve,
thereby allow the storm water runoff to be controlled in a more natural way and
would conserve the environmental characteristics of this area. She stated her
plan would allow for a buffer along the Brushy Fork Creek area, but would be
more costly for the developer. Council Member Behler asked if Ms. Carran was
asking council to delay taking action to approve this development plan. Ms.
Carran stated that Mr. Berling has stated the city is not open to this kind of
development. Mayor Moriconi stated that a twenty-foot wide conservation
easement is one of the Planning Commission’s staff recommendations conditions
for approval of the plan. Council Member Behler commented that the Planning
Commission confirms that this planned development conforms to the Comprehensive
Plan. Ms. Carran maintained that this development plan can be improved upon and
would like the opportunity to show council how well a planned urban development
(PUD) can establish a more desirable and nature friendly environment. Mayor
Moriconi advised that the council would have a first reading tonight on an
ordinance to approve this development and that the matter could be discussed
further at the July 21, 2003 caucus meeting. Ms. Carran stated she would
provide Mr. Berling with her suggested alternatives to his development plan so
that he could review here proposal. Council Member Ellison commented that Ms.
Carran has apparently done her homework on this matter and feels she is
knowledgeable on natural conversation issues.
Ordinance No. 2003-O-07 – Glenhurst Subdivision Zone Change Request for 130
Acres – 2nd Reading
8.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Ordinance No. 2003-O-07 for a second
reading. He stated this ordinance would accept the recommendation of the Kenton
County Planning Commission to approve a request by Glenhurst Development
Company for a map amendment to the city zoning ordinance changing an
approximate 130-acre area located at the terminus of Hogreffe Road from A-1, R-
1B, R-1C, R-1D and I-1 to R-1D (PUD) subject to certain conditions. City
Attorney, Mr. Jed Deters read the proposed ordinance.
9.   Council Member Bushong moved for a second reading of Ordinance No. 2003-O-
07, seconded by Council Member Ellison. Mr. Ellison asked if the proposed
spelling of Hogreffe Road, to delete one of the ‘f’s has taken effect. Mr.
Deters stated the street name spelling has not been changed yet. Council Member
Ellison suggested the spelling be corrected before this is printed. Roll call
was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 – Establishing the Time of 11:00 A.M. for Liquor Sales
– 2nd Reading
10.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 for a second
reading. He advised this ordinance would establish the time of 11:00 a.m. as
the time that liquor and malt beverages may begin being sold and served on
Sunday within the city limits. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
11.   Council Member Ellison moved to approve Ordinance No. 2003-O- 08 as read,
seconded by Council Member Bushong. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member
Ketron stated that he has considered this matter and agrees with Council Member
Franzen. He commented that a primary reason for liquor sales to begin after 1:
00 p.m. on Sunday was the effect it would have on churches. Council Member
Behler stated she also opposed this time change, but for different reasons and
stated she would not vote to enact this time change. Mayor Moriconi advised
that the time change was a request by the Kenton County Golf Course. Council
Member Ketron commented that this ordinance opens up the sales to every place
that holds a liquor license, not just the golf course. Council Member Bushong
stated that he feels the same, but that other cities, such as Covington and
Taylor Mill, are passing similar ordinances that permit the 11:00 a.m. liquor
sales. Roll call was answered with three yes votes and three no votes; Mayor
Moriconi cast the tie-breaking vote by voting in favor. Motion carried 4-3.
Resolution No. 2003-R-16 – Accepting the Bid of Seaward and Lori Padilla for
the Purchase of 68-A Oby Drive and Authorizing the Mayor to Enter into a
Purchase Contract and Execute a Quit Claim Deed
12.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-16 accepting
the bid of Seaward and Lori Padilla, 1866 Freedom Trail, Independence, in the
amount of $11,888.00 for the purchase from the city the approximate 1.23-acre
parcel known as 68-A Oby Drive. The resolution authorizes Mayor Moriconi to
enter into a purchase contract and execute the Quit Claim Deed. Mr. Padilla
commented that he has had the property surveyed at his expense and advised that
the majority of the trees that Mr. Holloway had cleared from his adjoining
property have been cleared away. He stated he would like a couple of the trees
replaced but does not want to squabble over this minor issue. Mayor Moriconi
asked Mr. Padilla if he was ready to proceed with the purchase of this parcel.
Mr. Padilla stated he was. Mr. Russell Holloway, the adjoining property owner
confirmed that he has cleared the area of the trees he removed as evident in
the photos he presented a week ago. Mr. Jed Deters stated he has inspected the
parcel and found that it look as if the debris had been cleared. Mr. Deters
also advised that the proposed contract allows sixty days, which is plenty of
time to resolve any lingering issues. Mr. Padilla stated that he was willing to
proceed with the purchase of this property.
13.   Council Member Franzen moved with second by Council Member Yeager to
approve Resolution No. 2003-R-16. Council Member Bushong asked if it was the
city’s place to be the intermediary of this dispute between Mr. Holloway and
Mr. Padilla. Mr. Deters advised that since the city is selling this property it
is in the interest of the city to settle any outstanding issues related to this
property. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
14.   Mr. Holloway asked if the property would now become a parcel of Freedom
Trail, as there is no access directly from Oby Drive. Mr. Deters stated it
might have to be combined with Mr. Padilla’s property for access purposes. Mr.
Padilla stated he has no plans for making improvements to this parcel other
than a privacy fence, fire pit and perhaps a shed. He went on to say that he
became interested in purchasing the property when rumors began circulating that
Mr. Holloway was planning to build a large garage on it and the Freedom Trail
residents feared that would destroy the natural environment of the area.
Resolution No. 2003-R-17 – Granting a Sidewalk Waiver for 619 Independence
Station Road
15.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-17 that would
grant a waiver for the requirement for the construction of a sidewalk along the
area of 619 Independence Station Road. The owner,    Louis Enzweiler has been
denied a permanent Certificate of Occupancy, as the sidewalk was not
constructed in front of his residence in accordance with subdivision
regulations. The owner contends the severe slope of the terrain makes
compliance with this regulation difficult.
16.   Council Member Ketron moved with second by Council Member Ellison to
approve Resolution No. 2003-R-17. Council Member Behler asked what the Kenton
County Planning Commission meant when they denied to comment on the matter. Mr.
Deters stated, exactly that that it is their position that this is a decision
to be made by the city. Rolled was taken and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2003-R-18 – Approving the Senior/Community Center Rental
Agreement
17.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-18 that would
accept and approve the rental agreement for the Independence Senior Citizens
and Community Center. Council Member Bushong moved with second by Council
Member Yeager to approve Resolution No. 2003-R-18. Roll called was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – 1st Reading to Approve a Zoning Map Amendment Requested by
Independence Station Road LLC for a 50-Acre Area North of Independence Station
Road
18.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would
approve a map amendment for an approximate 50-acre parcel north of Independence

Brushy Fork Creek. The proposed map amendment would rezone the area from R-1A
to R-1C. Mayor Moriconi advised this would be the first reading of the first

Proposed Ordinance – 1st Reading to approve a Zoning Text Amendment adding

19.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would

Proposed Ordinance – 1st Reading to Approve a Map Amendment for 12.7 Acres
along Senour Road and Mohawk Lane
20.   Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that
would approve a map amendment changing an approximate 12.7 acre parcel located
at the southeast corner of the intersection of Senour road with Mohawk Lane
from R-1C to R-1D on the condition that the density of the site not exceed a
maximum density of 3.8 dwelling units per acre
21.   Mr. Jerry Keith addressed council with a request to hold a special
meeting prior to the July 21 caucus meeting in order to have a second reading
and adoption of this amendment to the zoning map. He stated that he makes this
request so that a closing date for the purchase of the property can be
scheduled. . Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
22.   Council discussed Mr. Keith’s request for a special meeting prior the
caucus meeting and agreed to hold a special meeting at 6:45 p.m. on July 21,
2003 to take action on this map amendment. Council Member Yeager suggested
placing on the special meeting agenda the other proposed ordinances. Mayor
Moriconi stated since there were several pending ordinances that he felt it in
the best interest of the city to maintain the normal timeframe to consider
them.
Proposed Ordinance – 1st Reading to Approve a Text Amendment Relating to the
Definition of “Family” and Relating to Manufactured Housing
23.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a first reading of an ordinance that
would approve a text amendment to the Zoning Ordinance that 1) deletes the
existing definition(s) of “family” and adds a new definition of “family”; and
2) adds compatibility standards for qualified manufactured housing along with
various cross references in other sections of the zoning ordinance. Mr. Deters
read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi stated this would be presented at
the August 4, 2003 council meeting for a second reading and adoption.
Proposed Ordinance – 1st Reading Regarding Compensation for Elected Officials
24.   Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed ordinance that effectively amends
Ordinance 2000-O-02 pertaining to compensation for elected city officials. He
stated that proposal eliminates the CPI (consumer price index) salary increases
as directed by council, which were scheduled to take effect on March 2004. Mr.
Deters read the proposed ordinance for the first time. Mayor Moriconi stated
this ordinance would have a second reading at the August 4, 2003 council
meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – 1st Reading Adopting the Updated Employee Pay Plan
25.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading an ordinance that
would update the current employee pay plan. He stated that the pay plan should
have been amended and enacted in correlation with the annual budget but was
overlooked. Council Member Franzen motioned, that since this is two months
behind, that perhaps council should consider adopting this by one, emergency
reading. Mr. Deters advised that he did not believe tardiness would qualify as
an acceptable reason to waive the second reading of this ordinance. Mayor
Moriconi expressed concern that by not enacting this ordinance on an emergency
basis that it may prevent employee raises that went into effect July 1 as
prescribed in the budget ordinance that was passed in June. Council Member
Franzen felt it would not be fair to the employees to delay their pay raises.
Council Member Yeager expressed concern for the minimum pay rate for some
positions. Chief Butler advised that the city adopts a range as guidelines and
that the 2003/04 salary increases are within the range. Council Member Yeager
also questioned why the Building Inspector, who is a contract employee, is
listed on the pay plan. The City Clerk stated that the pay plan lists all
positions for which the city has a job description. Council Member Ketron
pointed out that the position of City Administrator was omitted from the pay
plan submitted. Council Member Yeager voiced concern that she felt some of the
positions had high minimum rates and asked if a new employee would be paid the
minimum in the range for the position. Chief Butler replied yes. Council Member
Franzen maintained that since the pay range is a guideline for salaries and
that the employee raises have been adopted with the 2003/04 budget she saw no
reason to delay adopting the pay plan until August. She advised the pay plan
was adopted last year by an emergency reading of the ordinance. Council Member
Ellison stated that he did not see a reason to rush this through. He commented
that the seasonal positions that receive an hourly rate should be so noted on
the pay plan, that it is hourly and not an annual amount like the permanent,
full time positions.
26.   Council Member Behler suggested the pay plan could be discussed further
at the July 21 caucus meeting. Council Member Franzen withdrew her motion to
have an emergency reading of the proposed ordinance. Mr. Deters commented that
he would continue with the first reading of this ordinance and the see what
transpires at the caucus meeting discussion on this subject. Council Member
Yeager commented that she just wants the pay plan to be correct before adopting
it. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Resolution No. 2003-R-19 – Authorizing the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission to Proceed with the Proposed Street Name Changes
27.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-19 supporting
and authorizing the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission staff to proceed
with proposed street/road name and address clarifications or changes
necessitated by new developments within the city and county. Mr. Deters read
the Resolution 2003-R-19 as presented. Mr. Deters advised that Planning
Commission requested this resolution of support and stated that the street/road
name and address changes was necessary from a public emergency safety and
traffic concern perspectives.
28.   Council Member Bushong moved with second by Council Member Yeager to
approve Resolution No. 2003-R-19 as read. Roll call was answered unanimously;
motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2003-R-20 – Supporting an Emergency Medical Services Taxes
Referendum
29.   Mayor Moriconi presented for council consideration Resolution No. 2003-R-
20 that would support an EMS (Emergency Medical Services) tax referendum. He
advised that the Kenton County Fiscal Court has requested each city to support
their effort to enact a special ad valorem tax, subject to public referendum,
of two and one-half cents ($0.025) cents per $100 of assessed value on all real
property. He said the additional revenue would help meet the funding demands
and continue a high level of emergency medical services. Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2003-R-20.
30.   Council Member Bushong moved to approve Resolution No. 2003-R-20 as
presented with second by Council Member Behler. A brief discussion ensued.
Council Member Bushong asked if the increased tax was necessitated due to poor
handling of the ALS communication. Chief Butler responded that $600,000 will be
used for ALS needs with the remainder of the revenue to fund the BLS system
throughout the county. He stated that the county has not decided how the added
$1,200,000 will be divided. Mayor Moriconi commented that ultimately the
residents of Kenton County would decide in November whether or not they want to
support this tax. Chief Butler stated that if this tax is voted down at the
polls the county will cut emergency personnel staff. Roll call was answered
with five yes votes and one no vote cast by Council Member Ellison. Motion
carried 5-1.
Lease-Purchase Agreement with Fifth Third Bank for Police Cruisers
31.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposal with Fifth Third Bank for
the purchase of police cruisers in the amount of $86,936.00 to be paid over a
three-year period. He requested that council authorize him to enter into this
contract. Chief Butler stated that the 2003/04 budget that was passed in June
allotted funds for the lease-purchase of four new police cruisers. He stated
the city would realize a slight savings at the low interest rate of 2.940%. He
also advised that the bank requires council approval for the Mayor to sign this
proposal.
32.   Council Member Bushong so moved with second by Council Member Franzen.
Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Mayor’s Report
33.   Mayor Moriconi thanked the city staff and the many volunteers who helped
make the July 4th Celebration successful. He stated that since the fireworks
display was abruptly cancelled due to the onset of a thunderstorm, plans are
being made to re-schedule the fireworks display along with a free concert at
the opening of the Memorial Park Amphitheater in mid to late September.
34.   Mayor Moriconi announced that Chief Butler would be awarded the Police
Chief of the Year at the Northern Kentucky Area Development District’s annual
awards dinner that is scheduled for August 18, 2003. He also announced that the
department was won an award for the RAD program.
35.   Mayor Moriconi announced that the summer basketball camp was a success
with over 100 children attending. He stated the camp was held at Summit View
School.
36.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the city has received a tentative bid for the
amphitheater parking lot. He advised that Kenton County and city Public Works
employees would supply all equipment and man-hours.
37.   Mayor Moriconi reported that an update regarding the deteriorating
condition of Crowe Road would be announced at the caucus meeting. In closing,
he reported that Clubhouse Drive road repairs are progressing.
Executive Session
38.   Council Member Bushong made a motion to enter into executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss pending litigation. Motion carried
with all ayes.
39.   Upon motion by Council Member Ellison and second by Council Member
Franzen council returned to regular session. Motion carried with all ayes.
40.   Mayor Moriconi announced that no action was taken in executive session.
Adjournment
41.   There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved with second
by Council Member Bushong to adjourn. The meeting adjourned at 8:21 p.m.

July 21, 2003
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special
Session on Monday, July 21, 2003 at 6:45 p.m. in the Independence Senior
Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding in the
Chair. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. The roll was called and the
following council members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim
Ellison, Carol Franzen, Otis Ketron and Donna Yeager. Also present was City
Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for the
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   Discussion and possible action approving a map amendment for 12.7 acres at
Senour Road and Mohawk Lane. – Ordinance No. 2003-0-09- Second Reading.
∙   Discussion and possible action on updating the employee pay plan. –
Ordinance No. 2003-0-10.
∙   Executive Session (if necessary)
Ordinance No. 2003-0-09 – Approving Map Amendment for 12.7 Acres at Senour Road
and Mohawk Lane –From R-1C to R-1D - Second Reading
3.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading a proposed
ordinance that would approve a zoning map amendment for a 12.7 acre parcel
located at Senour Road and Mohawk Lane from an R-1C to R-1D zone. Mayor
Moriconi asked for a motion on this second reading of Ordinance No. 2003-0-09.
Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by Council Member Ketron.
4.   A brief discussion ensued wherein Council Member Yeager would like to make
certain there are two (2) egresses. Mr. Jerry Keith a representative for
Centerline Development responded to Council Member Yeager’s concern by advising
that the preliminary plan provides for one connector to Senour Road with
another route connecting through the Clover Ridge Subdivision.
5.   Council Member Jim Ellison voiced concerns that he would like this
development to provide widening of Senour Road with a left turn lane. He stated
that the Kenton County Planning Commission’s recommendation discusses this
condition but does not make a recommendation for it. Mr. Keith advised they
discussed a tapered lane, but that the plan was approved with a full
deceleration lane and widening of Senour Road. Council Member Ellison commented
that he feels that Planning Commission’s recommendation was unclear and did not
specify which condition was required. He stated that he wanted the conditions
to widen Senour Road, add a full deceleration lane and install sidewalks to be
a requirement for this map amendment.
6.   Attorney Jed Deters advised Council that he did not feel these changes
were significant enough to affect the second reading of this ordinance. Council
Members Bushong and Ketron agreed to amend their motion and second to include
Council Member Ellison’s recommendations. Mr. Deters read the ordinance in
summary to include Mr. Ellison’s recommendations. Roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2003-0-10 – Updating the Employee Pay Plan- Second Reading
7.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for second reading a proposed
ordinance that would update the employee pay plan. Council Member Franzen so
moved with second by Council Member Bushong. Council Member Franzen suggested
that the Administration Secretary and Police Clerk pay ranges should be the
same. Council Member Franzen stated that she has also been doing some research
with other cities regarding the pay ranges of public works and recreation
employees. Council Member Franzen believes that the Recreation Director should
be increased slightly and recommended a maximum of $36,000 opposed to the
existing $32,000. Council Member Behler suggested including the Deputy City
Clerk and Assistant City Clerk positions in this adjustment. Council Member
Ketron asked how these ranges would affect the current salaries. Mayor Moriconi
advised that the ranges in the salary pay plan are amended each year to
coincide with the pay raises. Chief Butler suggested increasing each range by
3% across the board. Council Member Ketron suggested indicating “hourly” on the
seasonal employee ranges in the Public Works and Recreation Departments.
Council Member Ellison stated that he would like the City Administrator
position to remain on the pay plan. Council Member Ketron concurred stating
that if the City Administrator position was re-established at a later time by
the Mayor that a range would be in place to use as a guideline for the salary.
Mayor Moriconi stated that none of this affects the current year’s budget. Mr.
Deters read ordinance 2003-0-10. Roll call was answered unanimously and the
motion carried 6-0.
Adjournment
8.   Upon motion by Council Member Jim Ellison and second by Council Member
Donna Yeager the meeting was adjourned at 7:01 p.m.

August 4, 2003
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
August 4, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Father Paul Berscheid of St. Cecilia
Catholic Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol
Franzen and Donna Yeager. Council Member Otis Ketron was absent. Also present
was City Attorney, Jed Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Ketron had selected Century 21 –
Garner Properties as recipient of the Business of the Month tribute for August.
Mayor Moriconi presented Tina Vogelpohl with the plaque.
Approval of the Minutes of the July 7, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the July 7,
2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Ellison so moved, with second
from Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted and roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the July 21, 2003 Special Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the June 21,
2003 Special meeting of council. Council Member Bushong moved, with second from
Council Member Yeager. No amendments were noted and roll was answered
unanimously with the motion carrying 5-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the July 21, 2003 Caucus Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the July 21,
2003 caucus meeting of council. Council Member Ellison moved, with second from
Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously; motion carried 5-0.
Privileges of the Floor
6.   Sherry Carran, 927 Forest Avenue, Covington, Kentucky addressed council by
stating that she is a member of the Banklick Watershed Council and shared her
concerns regarding the planned development by Jim Berling known as Canberra
Ridge Subdivision. She stated that at the last council meeting she informed
council that while she did not oppose this development she did feel that the
size of the planned conservation area needed to be larger. She stated that Mr.
Berling has begun grading this land and started the construction of a detention
pond. She stated that Mr. Berling had initially seemed willing to work with the
Banklick Watershed Council to address the environmental impact concerns this
development would have, but now feels he has not been forthcoming and that he
will not keep his promise. Ms. Carran recommended the city impose the following
additional conditions before approving this zone change:
1)   100 foot conservation easement along the Brushy Fork corridor
2)   Lot lines be modified to provide the 100 foot buffer
3)   A conservation easement be placed on the back portion of the development
4)   Get this agreement in writing before the final site plan is approved.
7.   Ms. Carran stated that she does not feel the conditions are unreasonable.
She reported she has obtained a model ordinance that protects watersheds and
advised that the standard buffer is 100-150 feet.
8.   City Attorney, Jed Deters cautioned council and Ms. Carran that the city
could not hear new evidence regarding this matter that was not provided at the
public hearing which was held by the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC).
He advised council they would need to make a decision based on the facts that
were presented at that hearing and the recommendation by the KCPC. He went on
to instruct those who wished to speak on this matter that they would be limited
to oral statements and stated they could not introduce new evidence.
9.   Ms. Carran stated that council should personally review this matter in
order to make an informed decision, as she feels the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission (NKAPC) and the KCPC has simplified the issue. Mr. Deters
stated that the Planning Commission performs this plan review process for the
city so that there would be no duplication of information.
10.   Mr. Martin Butler, attorney for Jim Berling, advised that his client has
not made a formal presentation to council, as this is not a public hearing. Mr.
Deters stated that Mr. Berling deserves due process.
11.   Ms. Carran stated that the Sanitation District is now reviewing the
watershed plan and advised the District has informed her that they have not
reviewed this particular development plan. Mr. Deters stated that the District
has not fully accepted the sewer system from the city yet.
12.   Mr. Butler stated that of the 140 acres of this development, his client
is only requesting that 50 acres be re-zoned from R-1A to R-1C as the remaining
acreage is already zoned R-1C. He stated that Ms. Carran is referring to what
is a standard subdivision regulation review. Mr. Butler said that his client’s
position in agreeing to make this a preservation area is that the area should
remain private. He advised that no mechanism has been put forward that would
provide for maintenance of this area if it was made public. Mr. Butler stated
that this could become a safety issue as the city has not assumed liability for
a large conservation easement. He stated that his client is willing to preserve
an area, but passive recreation implies the general public would have access
and he doesn’t think the city was to assume maintenance. Mr. Butler also
commented that the storm water drainage has been addressed in the development
plan and his client does not consider this to be a valid issue and it is not a
condition before the city.
13.   Marc Hult, 322 East 3rd Street, Covington, Kentucky stated that he is the
Executive Director of the Banklick Watershed Council. He stated that Mr.
Berling’s development site is located in the Brushy Fork Creek area where it
meets with Banklick Creek. He stated that he feels there is much work to be
done before the city approves the recommendation of the KCPC, as it should be
determined whether this development will result in more flooding downstream.
Mr. Hult stated that an adequate plan to address downstream flooding should be
established before approving this development.
14.   Al Carson, 4015 Old Ky. 17, stated that he felt the city would approve
this project based on money and the tax dollars this development would be
generating. He stated that Ms. Carran not only addresses the conservation
concerns but also the storm water runoff. Mr. Carson stated that these projects
continue to affect his property as well as his neighbors. He stated that
Banklick Creek is three feet from the edge of his yard. He urged council to
look at this more closely and find a way to prevent additional storm water
runoff that will affect neighboring communities.
15.   Susan Cross, 5045 Madison Pike, stated that she has lived in Independence
since 1988 and as a science teacher and concerned citizen urged council to 1)
maintain the green space and the quality of life in Independence, which she
feels is in jeopardy with the influx of developments. Secondly, Ms. Cross
stated that she fears that the back section of this development will destroy
the water flood plain area and cause more flooding downstream. She urged
council to plan growth intelligently and with regard to Independence’s
neighbors.
16.   Bill Schneider, 2034 Cruise Creek Road, stated that council should delay
deciding this zone change until the city has a consolidated plan with
understanding to watersheds, and then make an informed decision.
17.   Jim Hendricks, 3972 Old Ky. 17, advised council that he has four sump
pumps to prevent his basement from flooding. He stated that in 1996 flooding
resulted in $40,000 damage to his property causing his property insurance
premium to triple. He urged council to look at this carefully and make
provisions to help the downstream residents.
18.   Mark Bergman, 57 Apple Drive, commented that he is a student of the
environment and as such felt council would be making a serious mistake to
approve this zone change. He stated that by removing the flood plain area the
storm water would not have an area to pond before it hits the creek. He stated
that it is bad stewardship to create problems for others outside of the city
limits.
19.   George Wolsing, advised council that he was born and raised here and
owned this property for fifty years. He stated that the flooding in this area
has been going on for seventy years. He commented that he would like to know
where all these people were when he was trying to protect it. Mr. Wolsing
stated he felt compelled to sell the property due to the rising frequency of
vandalism to his property, including having his cows shot several times. He
stated that the point he wanted to make was that the flooding is no worse now
than it was fifty years ago.
20.   Mr. Butler commented that there are systems in place; an improvement plan
was reviewed and approved by the Planning Commission. He stated they couldn’t
change the fact that there is going to be water runoff from this development
but the issue has been given a lot of attention and they feel they have
addressed this concern adequately. He stated that Mr. Berling is willing to
preserve a conservation easement, but one of a private nature, not a public
green space that would be accessible to the public and require public (city)
maintenance. In closing, Mr. Butler commented that the hillside will still be
there and that Mr. Hult presented no evidence that the flooding will increase
and provided no reasonable argument for council to oppose this development.
21.   Mayor Moriconi closed the discussion on this matter and advised that that
matter would be presented for a second reading and vote later in the meeting.
22.   Thelma Sams, 6209 Taylor Mill Road, presented council with a petition
signed by eleven property owners in the Taylor Mill Road/Rusconi Drive area who
would like the city to provide public sewer service. She advised that she has
been working with the Sanitation District since August of 2002 and it took an
entire year for the Sanitation District to advise the project will cost each
property owner $17,932. Ms. Sams stated the estimated expense of this project
is causing them to seek assistance from the city.
23.   Council Member Bushong explained that the $18,000 would be spread out
over a twenty year period, which would make this more affordable for most, and
for those unable to pay it off, then a lien would be placed against the
property to be paid off in the event of a property transfer. Ms. Sams commented
that the assessed value of some of the properties is too low. She stated the
surrounding properties have public sewers and urged the council to assist them.
28.   Mr. Deters commented the city has the same cost prohibitive as the
Sanitation District. Mayor Moriconi advised he would have the city engineer
review this request.
29.   Sara Gadzala, 91 Fleming Drive submitted a petition to council signed by
116 citizens that do not support Council Member Ketron’s presence on city
council and called for his resignation. In addition Ms. Gadzala read a prepared
statement wherein she requested the resignation of Council Member Otis Ketron
on behalf of the citizens and in light of pending criminal charges against him.
She stated it is in the best interest of the city for Council Member Ketron to
relinquish his council seat and urged the city leaders to pressure him to
resign. Ms. Gadzala stated that others in the community she has spoken to agree
it would be the only responsible thing for Mr. Ketron to do. She stated
residents feel the city’s name should not be linked with an elected official
who is facing such repulsive and abhorrent charges.
24.   Mr. Deters, City Attorney, responded to Ms. Gadzala’s statement by
advising her that since Council Member Ketron was absent from this meeting she
should return at a time when he is present to direct her concerns and request
to him. Ms. Gadzala countered that the city council should be concerned about
his continued presence on the council and the citizens want Mr. Ketron to
understand that they are not content with his decision to remain on council.
Council Member Bushong requested the petition submitted by Ms Gadzala be
attached as a part of the official minutes of this meeting.
25.   Chuck Kahrs, 21 Oby Drive thanked the city council and Chief Butler for
addressing the speeding concerns on Oby Drive. He stated that the temporary
speed bump that was installed has been a big help in slowing the traffic.
26.   Council Member Yeager also thanked the Police Department and the
Independence Fire District for the quick response she received when the meter
on her house set off.
27.   Charles Deters, Independence Towne Center stated he wanted to comment on
his opposition to the proposed ordinance that would approve a text amendment
adding professional offices as a conditional use in the R-1C zone. He requested

Ordinance No. 2003-O-11 – Approving a Zoning Map Amendment Requested by
Independence Station Road LLC for a 50-Acre Tract North of Independence Station
Road (part of the Canberra Ridge Subdivision) – Second Reading
28.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading a proposed
ordinance that would approve a map amendment for an approximate 50-acre parcel
(in the Canberra Ridge Subdivision development) north of Independence Station
Road contiguous to the west with Banklick Creek and northeast with Brushy Fork
Creek. The proposed map amendment would rezone the area from R-1A to R-1C. Mr.
Deters read Ordinance No. 2003-O-11.
29.   Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2003-O-11 as read,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Council Member Bushong asked Ms. Carran how
many of the citizens were present here tonight also attended the NKPC public
hearing. Ms. Carran responded that she was the lone person and Mr. Berling had
agreed to work with her on establishing a conservation easement. She stated
that at the time of the public hearing she voiced her viewpoint but did not
have all the information put forth tonight. Mr. Butler commented that there
were two hearings before the KCPC wherein there were full blown presentations
and extensive discussion
30.   Council Member Behler asked if a grading permit and a clearing permit
were two different things. Mr. Berling stated that the project is divided into
phases and that he is now in Phase I where the general clearing and grading of
the land is allowed by means of one permit. Council Member Behler asked how
many natural ponds were on the property. Mr. Berling stated there were two. She
asked if he would add retention ponds. Mr. Berling responded yes.
31.   Council Member Franzen stated she is concerned that the city is allowing
new evidence at this meeting. Mr. Deters assured her that the discussion to
this point has been proper. Mr. Butler stated that he feels they have simply
responded to the statements made.
32.   Council Member Ellison stated that the Wolsing’s who are the former
owners of this property were excellent neighbors of his for many years, and the
Wolsing’s have struggled for the past 15-20 years to care for their property.
He stated he does not see a valid reason to oppose this development by Mr.
Berling and feels the city should allow him to proceed.
33.   Council Member Yeager commented that she concurred with Mr. Wolsing in
that the flooding has been occurring for many years. She stated that this is
nothing new and that Sanfordtown has always had flooding problems and that she
believes the flooding has lessened in recent years.
34.   Council Member Behler stated that she is at the low end of the learning
curve when it comes to planning issues and in this particular case feels that
she does not have enough information at this time to vote to approve or
disapprove this development. Council Member Franzen commented that the city
should follow the KCPC’s recommendation on this development.
35.   There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi called for a vote. Roll
call was answered with four ayes, with Council Member Behler recusing. Motion
carried
Ordinance No. 2003-O-12 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment adding Religious
Worship Institutions as a Conditional Use in the NC (Neighborhood Commercial)
Zone – Second Reading
36.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.

Ordinance No. 2003-O-13 – Approving a Text Amendment Relating to the Definition
of “Family” and Relating to Manufactured Housing – Second Reading
38.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2003-O-13 that would approve a text amendment to the Zoning Ordinance that 1)
deletes the existing definition(s) of “family” and adds a new definition of
“family”; and 2) adds compatibility standards for qualified manufactured
housing along with various cross references in other sections of the zoning
ordinance. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
39.   Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2003-O-13 as read,
seconded by Council Member Ellison. No discussion; roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 5-0.
Ordinance No. 2003-O-14 – Regarding Compensation for Elected Officials and
Amending Ordinance No. 2000-O-02 – Second Reading
40.   Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2003-O-14
that effectively amends Ordinance 2000-O-02 pertaining to salary compensation
for elected city officials. He stated that as proposed by this council,
Ordinance No. 2003-O-14 would eliminate the CPI (consumer price index) salary
increases, which were scheduled to take effect in March 2004. Mr. Deters read
Ordinance No. 2003-O-14
41.   Council Member Franzen moved, with second by Council Member Behler to
adopt Ordinance No. 2003-O-14 as read. . He stated that the previous Ordinance
No. 2000-O-02 was essentially unconstitutional as there is no reference to CPI
increases in the constitution. Council Member Behler asked Mr. Deters why it
was unconstitutional. Mr. Deters explained that by providing for built in
salary increases based on the cost of living, eventually the elected officials
salaries would exceed the salary limits set by Kentucky statute. There being no
further discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 4-
1.
Discussion Regarding the Recommendation by the Kenton County Planning
Commission (KCPC) to Disapprove a Text Amendment Adding Professional Offices as
a Conditional Use in the R-1C Zone
42.   Mayor Moriconi advised the next agenda item before council is the
consideration of a zoning text amendment proposed by Mr. Jeff Jarboe which
would add professional offices as a conditional use in the R-1C zone. He stated
that the KCPC has recommended the city disapprove this text amendment. City
Attorney, Mr. Jed Deters explained the process of a text amendment. He stated
that in this particular case the KCPC has recommended that the city disapprove
this request as it would allow for incompatible land use in the R-1C zones with
offices locating in residential areas all around the city which is not
appropriate planning. Mr. Deters advised that ultimately the city council has
the authority to either support the recommendation of the Planning Commission
or override their recommendation. He stated that if council chose to override
the recommendation by the Planning Commission, it would require two readings of
the proposed ordinance to approve the zoning text amendment.
43.   Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Mr. Charlie Deters who wished to
voice his opposition to the city approving this text amendment. Mr. Charlie
Deters stated he is the developer of the Independence Towne Center, which is
directly across from Mr. Jarboe’s property. He stated that the Towne Center was
a 250-acre parcel, which is a well-thought out development that includes
neighborhood commercial, residential and multi-family, with twenty-seven acres
given to the city for the development of a park and municipal center and two
acres to the Fire District to build a new firehouse. He stated the development
is public and accessible; he built public streets and sewers. He stated that he
opposes this text amendment, as he feels it is does not provide an overall plan
to better the community. He stated it is nit picking to change a zone in order
to permit an office building in a residential area. Mr. Deters stated that it
offends him to change the words in the zoning text to modify the planning
process and permit rinky-dink growth. He stated that when he set out to
construct the Towne Center he had to follow the rules and create a sound
development plan and it took substantial effort to do a nice project for the
city. He urged council to uphold the recommendation of the Planning Commission
because to allow this type of conditional use is bad planning.
44.   Mr. Frank Wichmann, legal counsel for Mr. Jarboe, responded that while he
appreciates Charlie Deters’ comments, he disagrees with his view. He
complimented Mr. Deters’ on the Towne Center development, but stated that Mr.
Jarboe’s property is not shabby. He stated that Mr. Jarboe would be willing to
sell his property for the replacement cost, but no one would purchase the
property in the manner that the Comprehensive Plan identifies this area for
commercial use. Mr. Wichmann stated that the Planning Commission suggested the
method used by Mr. Jarboe as a means to bring his home business into compliance
in this residential area. He cited that the issue here is whether Mr. Jarboe
can use this residential property for a commercial purpose and he feels he
should be able to considering the surrounding properties are zoned commercial.
45.   Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Jarboe how long he has operated at this
property. Mr. Jarboe stated that he has been there for four years operating as
a financial planner with no customers on site and for one year with customers.
He stated that prior to that time, he operated his offices above Nie’s
Pharmacy.
46.   Council Member Ellison stated that he feels the confusion stems from the
Planning Commission. Mr. Jed Deters commented that the NKAPC staff took one
position, while the KCPC members made two recommendations to Mr. Jarboe.
Council Member Yeager agreed with Council Member Ellison. She stated that after
reviewing the zoning map she obtained from the Planning Commission and reading
the information she feels bad for Mr. Jarboe that he has received conflicting
information.
47.   Mayor Moriconi stated that ultimately the council needed to decide
whether or not they want Mr. Jarboe’s business to remain in it’s present
location. Mr. Charlie Deters commented that by approving the text amendment
proposed by Mr. Jarboe it will affect other properties throughout the city as
long as the request meets the conditions set forth. Mr. Wichmann objected to
Mr. Deters’ assessment, citing that very few properties would be affected by
this change in text. Council Member Ellison commented that he agreed with Mr.
Deters that many properties would be affected. Mr. Jarboe stated that the only
areas designated in the Comprehensive Plan to as neighborhood shopping centers
or professional office spaces are properties across from the Towne Center. Mr.
Charlie Deters replied that a text amendment opens up the possibility for all
properties in the city to seek a conditional use.
48.   At this time, Council Member Franzen made a motion to accept the
recommendation of the KCPC to disapprove the proposed zoning text amendment
that would permit professional offices as a conditional use in the R-1C zone.
Council Member Behler seconded the motion and commented that she is very
conflicted. She stated that she hates to see the city loose a business, but is
compelled to agree with the Planning Commission. She suggested the city might
help Mr. Jarboe relocate in the city. Roll call was answered with four ayes and
one no vote cast by Council Member Ellison. Motion carried 4-1.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Text Amendment Providing for a Moratorium on
the Establishment of a Sexually Oriented Business – 1st Reading
49.   Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading an ordinance that would
enact a proposed text amendment to the zoning ordinance adding Article XX that
would provide for a moratorium on the establishment of a sexually oriented
business and provide that no application shall be processed and no permit
issued for such an establishment. He stated the Kenton County Planning
Commission has proposed this moratorium be in effect until May 15, 2004 or upon
the adoption of a new ordinance in response to the regional study regarding
sexually oriented businesses is complete. The City Attorney, Jed Deters read
the ordinance.
Resolution No. 2003-R-21 Declaring 5247 Madison Pike Surplus Property and

accept sealed bids for the sale of the property to the highest and best bidder.
Council Member Ellison questioned accepting bids instead of placing the
property on the market with a realtor. Mr. Deters advised it is first necessary
to declare the property as surplus, before taking sealed bids. Council Member
Behler asked what would happen if the sealed bids were well below the actual
market value. Mr. Deters advised the city would have the right to reject the
bids received and then perhaps the city would list the property with a realtor.
Mayor Moriconi advised that a market analysis has been completed.
51.   Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Resolution No. 2003-R-21 with second
by Council Member Behler. No roll called; motion carried with all ayes.

Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
54.   Fleming Drive Repairs - Mayor Moriconi reported that the city is in
receipt of bids to make road repairs to Fleming Drive. Chief Butler stated a
copy of the city engineer’s report was provided in the council packets. He
stated that the engineer is recommending that the city delay commencement of
this road work until next year, because of concerns that this project will take
several weeks to complete and may run into the onset of winter weather. Council
Member Franzen stated she spoke with Jeff Smith of the Public Works Department
who feels it will cost more to repair next year, as additional damage will
occur over the winter months. Chief Butler reiterated that the city engineer is
concerned that if this project is started in September it will not be completed
before the start of winter. Mayor Moriconi advised delaying this project until
next spring. Council Member Ellison stated that he feels the city should follow
the recommendation of the city engineer even though additional maintenance may
be necessary until spring. Council Member Behler expressed concern that the
city could not afford to add an additional $100,000 to delay these repairs
until spring.
55.   Police Grants – Chief Butler reported that the department has received a
$10,000 grant to combat illegal prescriptions as well as a $10,000 grant from
the state for the installation of video camera.

Executive Order No. 2003-EO-10 – Appointing Dr. Craig Sanders to the Senior

City of Independence, Ky.
September 8, 2003
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
September 8, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Lisa May Staffordsburg United
Methodist Church gave the invocation. Mayor Moriconi asked for a moment of
silence in remembrance of the approaching two-year anniversary of the September
11 (2001) tragedy.
2.   Following the moment of silence, roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Carol
Franzen and Donna Yeager. Council Member Otis Ketron was absent. Also present
was City Attorney, Jed Deters.
Presentation of the State Flag by Senator Damon Thayer
3.   Mayor Moriconi introduced State Senator Damon Thayer who presented the
City of a state flag that was flown over Frankfort earlier this summer. Senator
Thayer stated that it is an honor to be in Independence where he received much
support during his bid for the senate seat during a special election held in
January. He stated that he lives in Georgetown, and much like Independence it
is one of the fastest growing communities in the state. Senator Thayer stated
that he formerly lived in Crittenden and is familiar with the needs of the
citizens in Independence. He advised that he will actively support the road
improvements to St.Route17 and continue to make a great effort to ensure that
it will remain on the six-year road improvement plan for the state. He stated
that he sees this as an important issue for the future of Independence as well
as addressing other traffic plans. He also mentioned that he is not in favor of
increasing the gas tax and expressed confidence that the next governor will
hopefully be able to find waste in the current budget, thereby properly funding
the areas that need it.
4.   Mayor Moriconi advised Senator Thayer that Independence is lacking
sidewalks along State Routes 17 and 536 and would like state funding to assist
the city in achieving these improvements. Senator Thayer agreed that the
schools and subdivisions warrant that need. He stated that the economy is on
the rebound, which will help the state budget and create jobs. He stated that
the state has four major areas (Medicaid, education, public protection/
correction and health and human services) that consume 80% of a $13,000,000,000
bi-annual budget. The Senator advised that he felt the state needed to do a
better job funding those areas and then look at assisting with the funding of
community projects.
5.   Council Member Yeager stated that the city has sent a letter to Senator
Bunning requesting his support for the second phase of the construction of the
city’s Memorial Park Amphitheater. She stated that the city would also
appreciate his endorsement in this community project. Mayor Moriconi stated
that he would provide Senator Thayer with a detailed list of future needs for
Independence and thanked the Senator for his presence and support.
Recognition
6.   Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Yeager had selected Dr. Molly King of
the Associated Spine and Headache Centre as recipient of the Business of the
Month tribute for September. Mayor Moriconi presented Dr. King with the plaque.
Dr. King thanked everyone, including her staff. She stated this was an honor as
she has been a business owner in this location for five years but has been a
part of this community for many years as she has grew up in Independence.
Approval of the Minutes of the August 4, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
7.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the August 4,
2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second
from Council Member Franzen. Council Member Ellison noted two amendments; roll
call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Privileges of the Floor
8.   Bob Exeler, 5296 Fowler Creek Road, addressed council about his desire to
obtain public water service to the Fowler Creek Road area. He wondered about
the status of the Sycamore Creek Estates development as it appears to be
delayed due to the fact that the developer (Fischer) has filed suit against the
Planning Commission, as they are requiring the water lines be constructed to
the end of the property. Mr. Exeler asked what effect this has on the city.
Both Mayor Moriconi and City Attorney, Jed Deters stated they were not aware of
this issue
9.   Mr. Exeler asked how the city could help the Fowler Creek property owners
obtain water lines. He stated he has requested this service for years and would
appreciate any assistance the city can offer. Council Member Ellison confirmed
that Mr. Exeler has made several appeals to the city for assistance in
obtaining water lines in that area of the city. Mayor Moriconi advised that he
would need to work with the Northern Kentucky Water District and/or Taylor Mill
Water, whichever agency supplies water to that area.
10.   Chuck Kahrs, 21 Oby Drive, addressed council in a recurring appeal for
the city to provide a permanent solution to solving the speeding problem on Oby
Drive. He stated that he appreciates the Police Chief’s past efforts to solve
this problem, but that it is worse now than before. He stated the portable
speed bump helped while it was in place, but when it was removed the speeding
continued. He stated that he feels a permanent solution would be to install a
stop sign or permanent speed bump. Chief Butler stated his department has
worked very hard at trying to solve this problem. Council Member Ellison stated
he feels it is time to take care of this problem and suggested that Chief
Butler check with the City of Edgewood on the cost of speed bumps. Chief Butler
replied that they are very costly – anywhere from $3,000 to $10,000 per bump.
Mr. Kahrs asked why a stop sign couldn’t be installed. Chief Butler stated that
a stop sign couldn’t be used as a traffic control device midway through a
street that does not intersect with another street, but that council can
override this. Council Member Yeager suggested leaving the portable speed bump
permanently in place on Oby Drive. Chief Butler stated that Clubhouse Drive is
also experiencing speeders and the bump was being installed there for a time.
He stated that the other option of running radar costs the department
considerable man-hours in overtime pay. Council Member Ellison stated that
while he is normally against using a stop sign to control speed, he felt the
city may need to employ this in order to resolve this matter. Council Member
Franzen asked if purchasing another portable speed bump would be cheaper than
installing a permanent one. Chief Butler stated the cost of adding another
speed bump was a budget concern.
11.   Council Member Ellison made a motion to install a stop sign on Oby Drive.
Council Member Behler suggested this matter be discussed further at the caucus
meeting. She stated the city should review all options to resolving this
matter, such as different types of speed bumps and the associated costs as well
as the ramifications of a stop sign. Council Member Franzen asked if “Children
at Play” signs are posted on the street. Mr. Kahrs stated that Chief Butler has
those signs installed. Council Member Bushong questioned why speeding on Oby
Drive was worse than other city streets. Mayor Moriconi commented that other
streets have speeding problems as well as Oby Drive. Chief Butler stated that
one contributing factor was that Oby Drive did not have another egress for the
Freedom Park subdivision, which is accessed by Oby Drive. Hearing no second to
Council Member Ellison’s motion, he withdrew his motion from the floor. Mayor
Moriconi advised more information would be provided at the caucus meeting.
Ordinance No. 2003-O-15 – Approving a Text Amendment Providing for a Moratorium
on the Establishment of a Sexually Oriented Business
12.   Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2003-O-15
that would enact a text amendment to the zoning ordinance adding Article XX
that would provide for a moratorium on the establishment of a sexually oriented
business and provide that no application shall be processed and no permit
issued for such an establishment. City Attorney, Jed Deters read Ordinance No.
2003-O-15.
13.   Council Member Ellison moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2003-O-15 as read,
seconded by Council Member Bushong. Council Member Franzen asked if the
moratorium would be in effect for six months. Mayor Moriconi stated it would be
in effect until May 2004. Roll call was answered unanimously; motion carried 5-
0.
Proposed Ordinance – Prohibiting the Keeping or Harboring of Barking Dogs – 1st
Reading
14.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading, a proposed
ordinance that would address the problem of frequent and habitual barking of
dogs that disturb the peace of residents. Council Member Bushong stated that
there are rules in place that need to be enforced and while he is in favor of
making an effort to address this problem he is not sure that it will have the
desired effect. Mayor Moriconi commented the current laws are difficult to
enforce and that the purpose of this ordinance is to oblige the responsibility
of the dog owner. Mr. Deters stated that the prior ordinance required the
responding police officer to witness the dog barking. He stated that this
ordinance allows the complaining party to start the process of citing the
offender to the Kenton District Court for prosecution under this ordinance
through the county attorney’s office. Mayor Moriconi advised the city receives
numerous calls complaining about persistent barking dogs.
15.   Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi advised the
ordinance would be presented for a second reading and adoption thereof at the
October business meeting of council.
Award Bid of Municipal Center Telephone & Security Support System Equipment &
Wiring
16.   Mayor Moriconi reported that the city was in receipt of four bids for the
installation of the telephone and security system for the new Municipal Center.
Bidders include: ICS, Atkins & Stang, NorCom and Cincinnati Bell. The bids
include all wiring and equipment needed for the system. First Chief Butler
thanked Dave Millward for his time and dedication in facilitating the city in
bringing this project to completion. His experience and knowledge of this type
of equipment proved invaluable to the city. He stated that the project was bid
out based on equipment specifications and support services. Chief Butler stated
the funds for this expense is budgeted in the Municipal Center project. Council
Member Ellison pointed out that there is a notation that one of the bidders did
not fulfill the bid specs. Chief Butler stated there were exceptions to that
particular bid, but council can ultimately decide if this bidder met all areas
of the specifications.
17.   Chief Butler stated that he is most familiar with the Cincinnati Bell
bid. He stated the city currently utilizes Cincinnati Bell systems and have
been happy with the equipment and service. He advised that NorCom and
Cincinnati Bell had worked with the city to arrive at the specs for the bid of
this equipment. He stated that those two bids received had been considerably
reduced from the initial estimates they provided to the city. Council Member
Franzen noted that NorCom’s maintenance costs increased each year, whereas
Cincinnati Bell quoted a fixed maintenance cost up to five years. Chief Butler
stated that he felt that was an important factor to consider when awarding this
bid.
18.   Council Member Franzen moved to award the bid to Cincinnati Bell as the
best bidder, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Declare Surplus Property – One Police Cruiser
19.   Mayor Moriconi advised that the police department had an old cruiser that
needed to be declared surplus. It is a 1994 Ford Crown Victoria. Council Member
Bushong moved to declare the 1994 Ford as surplus property to be auctioned,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. No roll call was taken; motion carried
unanimously 5-0.
Resolution No. 2003-R-24 – Providing for the Appointment of Interim Successors
as Directed by Kentucky Emergency Management to Update the Emergency Operation
Plan
20.   Mayor Moriconi presented for council’s consideration Resolution No. 2003-
R-24 that would approve and adopt the statewide emergency management mutual aid
and assistance agreement, appointing primary and alternate representatives for
Independence in the event of an emergency. He advised that the city is being
asked to provide for the continuity of government throughout the duration of a
state of emergency by appointing emergency interim successors in the event that
the Mayor, as the primary representative for the city, is not available. Mayor
Moriconi stated the alternate representatives would be Shawn Butler, Police
Chief, Dave Nichols, Assistant Chief and Patricia Taney, City Clerk
respectively.
21.   Council Member Ellison moved to adopt Resolution No. 2003-R-24 as read,
seconded by Council Member Bushong. Roll call was answered unanimously and the
motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Text Amendment to Add Outdoor Dining as a
Conditional Use in the NC and NSC Zone – 1st Reading
22.   Mayor Moriconi presented for first reading a proposed ordinance that
would approve a text amendment to add outdoor dining as a conditional use in
the NC and NSC zone. He stated this would be in keeping with the recommendation
made by the Kenton County Planning Commission. Mr. Deters read the proposed
ordinance. Mayor Moriconi advised this ordinance would be presented for a
second reading at the next regular meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a 2003 Tax Rate for Real & Personal Property –
1st Reading
23.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would adopt
tax rates for real and personal properties for the year 2003. He advised the
proposed tax rate for real estate is .169 for $100 of assessed value and the
proposed rate for personal property is .465 for $100 of assessed value. Mayor
Moriconi stated these rates are four percent over the compensating rate, which
was calculated at .163 and .447 respectively. He reminded council that the
current budget was adopted with the assumption that the city would be adopting
a compensating plus four percent tax rate. He stated that he would call a
special meeting prior to the September 15th caucus meeting so that a second
reading and enactment of this ordinance could take place. There being no
discussion, Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
24.   Council Member Franzen requested that a second reading of the proposed
ordinance to approve the text amendment to add the outdoor dining language to
the zoning ordinance also be included on the agenda for the special meeting.
Mayor Moriconi approved this request.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
25.   Resignation of Council Member Otis Ketron - Mayor Moriconi stated the
city is in receipt of Council Member Otis Ketron’s resignation. Council Member
Bushong moved, with second by Council Member Franzen to accept Mr. Ketron’s
resignation from council. Roll call was answered unanimously; motion carried 5-
0
26.   Mr. Deters advised council that the statute states they must appoint a
successor to this council seat within thirty days. Mayor Moriconi commented
that the city has received some applications already and that he will provide
copies of each in time for the caucus meeting. He advised he would like to
schedule a special meeting near the end of September to review the applications
and narrow it down to a few candidates for the position. Council discussed
imposing a deadline for accepting applications and decided on September 15 at
the close of business (4:30 p.m.). Mayor Moriconi suggested interviewing the
candidates in executive session at the planned special meeting at the end of
the month. Mr. Deters advised that council could conduct the interview in an
open forum. Council Members Ellison and Yeager rejected the idea of
interviewing in an open session. Council Member Franzen concurred. Council
Member Bushong stated that he shares the feelings of the other council members
and felt the candidates may be uncomfortable being asked general questions in a
public session. He asked that Mr. Deters research the legalities of conducting
the interviews in closed session to see if council would be within their rights
to do so.
27.   Providing Public Water Services – Mayor Moriconi revisited the issue of
water lines in the Rusconi Drive/Taylor Mill Road area as requested by Ms.
Thelma Sams. Council Member Ellison advised that he told Ms. Sams that he would
inspect the area and asked the Mayor if he would authorize the city engineer to
review this location. He commented that even though the city has turned over
the city owned sewer lines to the Sanitation District, he feels the city can
still be of assistance to the residents in their effort to connect into the
public sanitation lines. Mr. Deters advised the city has the reserve right to
expand the public sewer system. Council Member Ellison stated the city could
finance the cost over a twenty-year period, whereas the Sanitation District
will not finance. Council Member Yeager stated that Senour Road residents have
also had a problem with obtaining public water/sanitation services. Council
Member Bushong advised there are pocket areas like this all over the city. He
stated that the Sanitation District is very cooperative with the residents and
will assist with financing over a 15-year period at 4% interest and are happy
to do so, but it is a lengthy process and they prefer to deal with thirty or
more properties. He also stated that a lien can be placed on the property if
they are unable to pay the financing, then when the property is sold the lien
would be paid at the time of the property transfer. Mayor Moriconi commented
that he would contact the Northern Kentucky Water District regarding this
issue.
28.   Memorial Park Concert & Fireworks – Mayor Moriconi announced that the
city would hold a special grand opening of the new amphitheater in Memorial
Park with a concert and fireworks, weather permitting. He stated the event
would be held on September 27, 2003 with the ribbon cutting at 7:00 p.m. and
the fireworks at 9:00 p.m.
29.   VoiceStream - Council Member Ellison advised that the Kenton County
Planning Commission has approved a cellular tower to be constructed on Maher
Road. He stated that although this property is in unincorporated Kenton County,
he feels in the interest of air safety, that the city should exercise their
five-mile option and request this tower be lighted at night. He stated this
could have an effect on the residents of Independence as there is an air
landing strip on nearby property that is in the city limits, as well as
emergency Air Care helicopters.
30.   Council Member Ellison made a motion that the city send a letter to
Planning Commission requesting the VoiceStream cellular tower be required to
install day/night lights, seconded by Council Member Yeager. No roll call;
motion carried unanimously. Council Member Bushong commented that he agrees
with Council Member Ellison, but advised that the Planning Commission has
already voted and approved this plan by VoiceStream. Council Member Ellison
stated that he feels they will have to re-open this issue. Mr. Deters stated he
was not familiar with the “5-mile option” of which Council Member Ellison
mentioned.
Adjournment
31.   There being no further business, Council Member Bushong moved with second
by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. The meeting ended at 8:22 p.m.
