SEPTEMBER 15, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL CAUCUS MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence met on Monday September 15, 2003
at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Moriconi
presiding in the chair. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Roll call was answered and the following Council Members
were present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Jim Ellison, Donna Yeager and Carol
Franzen. Also present was City Attorney, Jed Deters.
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mrs. Teresa Hudson as the city’s new Finance Director
and welcomed her to the city.
Privileges of the Floor
Don Nienabor asked if the applications for the vacant council seat would be
made public. Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Nienabor that he could obtain a list
from the Administration Office.
Chuck Kahrs, 25 Oby Drive, inquired as to the update for the speed bumps on Oby
Drive. Chief Butler stated he is in the process of compiling the information he
has obtained to submit to council.
Mayor Moriconi advised Mrs. Joan Bowling, Senior Center Director would like to
address Council regarding the rental of the Senior and Community Center on
Holidays because she has received phone calls from residents inquiring as to
rental of the hall for the holidays. Mrs. Bowling advised Mayor and Council she
has a request to rent the hall on Christmas Eve. She stated she had e-mailed
council members and felt the general consensus was to rent the center for to
obtain the needed revenue. She stated there are several different ways to
permit rentals on holidays but there are problems that could be associated with
holiday rentals. Mrs. Bowling stated the Cities of Wilder and Southgate do rent
out their facility on holidays, but provide the renter with a key to the
building.
Council Member Yeager stated the city could easily solve that problem by having
the center closed on those holidays. Council Member Franzen asked if a code has
to be used in addition to a key to open the building. Mrs. Bowling stated they
must have a key to enter the building and a code to turn off the alarm.
Mrs. Bowling stated it is not a problem to change the security code and she can
also check to see what time the center was opened and what time it was closed.
She stated if someone does not enter the code correctly the alarm will go off
and the police will be dispatched to the center and then someone will have to
reset the alarm.
Council Member Franzen stated she felt it should be tried for the revenue.
Council Member Behler asked Mrs. Bowling what the experience has been with the
City of Southgate renting their Center on a holiday. Mrs. Bowling stated
Southgate has never had any problems but that doesn’t mean Independence won’t
have a problem.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the renters would have to clean up the room and lock
the building when they left or would someone from the city have to come and
lock the building. Mrs. Bowling stated they do not have to clean the room but
their trash has to be picked up and the building has to be left in the same
condition as when they arrived. It would be cleaned the next day.
Council Member Bushong stated he did not know what holidays it would include,
but felt Thanksgiving and Christmas were the most important holidays and he did
not feel the center should be open to anyone on those holidays. Mrs. Bowling
stated to rent one room the charge is only $60.00 and $300.00 for the whole
building.
Council Member Behler stated she did not feel the amount of revenue generated
is enough to make it worthwhile during the major holidays. Council Member
Bushong asked Mrs. Bowling what holidays did she feel the center should not be
available for rental. Mrs. Bowling stated Easter Sunday, Thanksgiving,
Christmas Eve, Christmas Day, New Years Eve and New Years Day.
Attorney Jed Deters stated the rental agreement could be amended to reflect the
changes. Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated the amended rental agreement would be
ready for the October 6, 2003 Council Meeting.
Mrs. Bowling advised council that she has received a request by Jazz R Size, a
non-profit organization, to use the Center on a weekly basis donating 20% of
the profits to the city in lieu of paying a rental fee each time they use a
room in the Center. Council Member Bushong stated a 20% profit might not be
worth the trouble. Mayor Moriconi suggested no special considerations should be
allowed.
Sidewalk Waiver Requests
Mayor Moriconi stated Kevin Barbian, Building Inspector, per his memorandum in
the packets, has advised that two new homes being built on Cody Road and Oliver
Road are requesting sidewalk waivers. Mayor Moriconi advised Council that Mr.
Barbian can attend the October 6, 2003 Council Meeting to answer their
questions and added this request is similar to the Independence Station Road
sidewalk waiver request that was recently granted.
Council Member Ellison stated he feels the sidewalk waivers could become a
problem and felt sidewalks should be installed where required. Council Member
Franzen stated she agreed with Council Member Ellison. Council Member Behler
stated she looked at Cody Road and Oliver Road and is not convinced sidewalks
need to be installed on either road because they are dangerous and questioned
if sidewalks need to be installed on roads that do not lead anywhere but to
another subdivision. Council Member Ellison stated that the city probably did
not want sidewalks on Madison Pike fifty years ago, but they are needed today.
Attorney Jed Deters stated a temporary waiver could be added and if development
does occur, they could be required to go back and install sidewalks at a later
date. Council Member Bushong asked who determines the future need of sidewalks.
Attorney Jed Deters stated Council could make that determination and can lift
the waiver. He stated No. Ky. Area Planning does not issue waivers for
sidewalks that it is left up to the individual city.
Mayor Moriconi stated a Resolution could be discussed for a temporary waiver at
the next council meeting on October 6, 2003.
NEW BUSINESS
Damage to Subdivision Curbs
Mayor Moriconi stated Mr. Jeff Smith of the Public Works Department has
reported that contractors are damaging concrete curbs in new subdivisions. He
stated Mr. Smith is on vacation and this matter could be put off until another
meeting if Council agrees.
Council Member Franzen stated she has talked to Mr. Smith regarding this matter
and also viewed photos and would like an Ordinance created that would make
contractors liable for damages to the curbs. Mayor Moriconi stated if the city
accepts the street and the curbs are damaged the city would have to absorb the
expense of repairing them.
Council Member Bushong asked what position the city has taken up to now.
Council Member Franzen stated the city has repaired them and the cost has been
approximately $1,000.00.
Council Member Ellison stated he has also spoke to Mr. Smith regarding this
problem and he has visited some of the sites with him and advised when the
curbs are damaged they are not repaired properly. He stated they patchwork the
concrete in the part they have broken. Mayor Moriconi asked if the damage is
happening after the city has accepted the street. Attorney Jed Deters stated it
was. He stated this is happening when the contractors are doing their back
filling and final grading.
Council Member Franzen stated she would obtain information for Attorney Jed
Deters to prepare an Ordinance for the October 6, 2003 meeting.
Vacant Council Seat
Mayor Moriconi stated to date the city has received thirteen resumes regarding
the vacant council seat. He stated a Special Meeting could be held September
24, 2003 to speak with the applicants. Council Member Bushong stated it might
help if Council had a set of maybe 10 questions to ask each applicant to help
in their decision.
Council Member Ellison stated he feels Council should decide on four or five
applicants to interview. Attorney Jed Deters asked what would be the purpose
for a Special Meeting on September 24th. Mayor Moriconi stated it would be to
possibly go into Executive Session and let Council interview the applicants
individually and ask them the questions they agreed upon. He also stated they
could go into Executive Session at this meeting and then decide on the number
of applicants they want to interview.
Revenue Options Package
Mayor Moriconi stated the package shows in great detail where and how much
revenue the city is receiving with the largest amount being payroll taxes with
a close second being property taxes. Council Member Behler stated she is
concerned with Payroll Taxes decreasing to 51% from 56% in the last two fiscal
years.
Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated she would speak to the Occupational License
Director at Kenton County and ask him to search for companies located in the
city to see if there has been an increase in layoffs but as of now the current
layoff rate is up nationally.
Mrs. Terri Hudson stated from the Revenue Options report it does appear that
there was a drop based on percentages but if you look at the monies received,
there was an increase. She asked Council to remember Tangible Taxes and
Property Taxes did increase. Mayor Moriconi stated that collections are still
down about $30,000.00 from two years ago.
Mayor Moriconi stated property taxes from new homes just this year will bring
in more than $70,000.00 in additional revenue.
Mrs. Taney, City Clerk advised that the calculation formula for the tax rate is
designed to keep cities that are having so much development from collecting too
much in taxes.
Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated the Bank Deposit tax that was implemented in 2000
was researched by a council member and discovered that it is a tax that was
being collected by Kenton County and they were getting that money because they
had that tax and Independence didn’t and all we had to do was establish it and
adopt it and set a tax rate in order to obtain this revenue for the city. It is
a minimum of 1 percent that comes to about $30,000.00 annually
Mr. Bushong asked what a Franchise Tax was. Mrs. Taney, City Clerk advised it
is the utility companies and cable companies that pay taxes on their cable
lines throughout the city and we generally have a twenty to thirty year
contract agreement with the company.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mrs. Taney to verify how much money is owed in delinquent
property taxes. Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated there are sixty delinquent tax
bills to date, which is about $40,000.00 to $50,000.00 out of approximately,
six thousand property tax bills.
Council Member Yeager asked if liens had been filed on these properties. Mrs.
Taney, City Clerk stated delinquent notices are automatically sent out. Council
Member Yeager asked if foreclosure has been placed on these properties.
Attorney, Jed Deters stated that PVA would file the foreclosures. He stated
delinquent property taxes are a lien against any property they are assessed
against. If the taxes are not paid, and the property sells all taxes will be
paid at the time of the closing, or you can let the taxes accumulate for eight
years which will generally make it worth your while to foreclose on the
property.
Council Member Franzen asked if anything could be done to change the eight-year
waiting period. Attorney, Jed Deters stated you do not have to wait eight years
to file foreclosures but it is better economically to file suit after eight
years due to the amount that can be collected after that period of time.
Council Member Yeager asked if the property owner would have to pay court
costs. Attorney, Jed Deters stated that is not quite so clear at this time.
Council Member Behler asked Mrs. Taney how it was decided what cities were to
be listed on the Occupational License Fee Rates Sheet and Payroll and Gross
Receipts. Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated she obtained the info from the website
of the Kenton County Occupational License Director. She stated the county
collects for a number of cities in Kenton County for a fee of 1% of the revenue
collected.
Council Member Behler stated from the spreadsheet it shows Independence has the
second highest payroll tax in Kenton County. Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated that
Covington is the highest and Taylor Mill is the second highest. She stated that
Mr. Rollie Richardson, of Kenton County, the Director of the Occupational
License Department advised her that changes are being proposed by the state
legislature regarding the laws for Occupational Licensing. He stated one of the
changes would be that cities could no longer tax net profits, just gross
receipts. She stated this will not affect Independence, as the city already
taxes the gross receipts. She asked council and mayor to note at bottom of
spreadsheet that Independence receives 6.7313 % of the countywide license of
$150.00 which equates to $11.78 for each business that buys a countywide
license. Council Member Yeager asked if the sub-contractors are paying payroll
taxes. Mrs. Taney advised Kevin Barbian, Building Inspector does get a list of
the sub-contractors from the contractor obtaining the permit.
Attorney, Jed Deters stated the question posed to him was can the city hold up
a building permit until the contractor submits a list of all sub-contractors
and you have time to verify if all the sub-contractors were listed. He stated
the answer was “no” because there is nothing in the current Ordinance about
issuing building permits that states it is a “condition of issuance”.
Council Member Yeager asked if the Ordinance could be changed. Attorney Jed
Deters stated one way to make a change is to enlarge the building permit
application to allow for the listing of all contractors and sub-contractors and
proof of a business license.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mrs. Taney what impact this could have on the building
inspector by adding additional work for him. Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated it
might just slow him down if he is going to hold up on issuing building permits
if some of the sub-contractors drag their feet on obtaining a license and they
have work to do in another city.
Council Member Yeager suggested we obtain a list from Kenton County and forward
a letter to the sub-contractors that has not purchased a license. Mrs. Taney,
City Clerk stated the office receives a monthly list of every business that has
paid and how much they have paid along with the remittance check. She also
stated the problem with that is by the time they get the letter, they have
already been in the city and has moved on to another job out of the city.
Council Member Franzen asked if the City could charge builders an Impact Fee.
Mrs. Taney, City Clerk stated she had spoke with Dan Dressman of the Homeowners
Association and was advised that an impact fee was illegal in the state of
Kentucky. Council Member Franzen asked Attorney, Jed Deters to look into the
legality of this fee and if it is legal then Council should look into charging
developers $500 to $600 per home.
Mayor Moriconi stated he did not think anything could be done on the building
permit fee.
Attorney, Jed Deters stated there is a schedule under the Subdivision
Ordinances that Council would have to change to increase the fees.
Council Member Franzen asked if the payroll tax is increased one-quarter of a
percent how much would that bring in. Council Member Yeager stated it would
bring in $200,000.00.
Council Member Franzen stated the increase of payroll and the compensating rate
would bring in about half a million dollars. Chief Butler stated the budget was
based on the compensating plus four, so you will still have a revenue gap. When
the projections for revenue were made they were made on compensating plus four.
Mrs. Taney, City Clerk advised Council if they want to have an increase of one
quarter percent a first reading will need to be done at the October 6, 2003
meeting with a second reading in November because Kenton County will need the
information by mid November. Council Member Yeager requested that the Ordinance
be ready for the October 6, 2003 meeting. Council Member Behler stated she was
not in favor of the payroll tax because we want to bring new businesses into
the city and we need to look at the long term effects of such an increase, not
just the short term. She stated an insurance premium tax is probably how they
are going to have to go.
Council Member Franzen stated what Mrs. Behler is saying is right. She stated
the city is running on their reserves, which are going to be gone. Council
Member Yeager stated there are still some things that can be done within. She
stated it was discussed about getting a custodian and doing away with cleaning
services, including the mowing. Council Member Bushong stated he did not see
where that would bring in $700,000.00 that is needed.
Council Member Behler asked Mrs. Hudson if she could explain the projections
with the revenue that way it is now, how soon is the city going to be operating
in the red. Mrs. Hudson stated she did not know at this time but could have
some projections ready for the next Council Meeting.
Council Member Franzen stated she would like to explore the franchise fees and
sub-contractor payroll, which will not bring in enough revenue, but it would be
a start and will help people be more comfortable to know we are looking at
other options.
Mrs. Taney, City Clerk clarified to Mayor Moriconi she will bring the
information to increase the payroll tax twenty-five cents. Mayor Moriconi
stated that was correct.
CITY ATTORNEY REPORT
Attorney, Jed Deters stated he had nothing to report at this time.
MAYOR COMMENTS
Mayor Moriconi stated Chief Butler has to declare a horse as surplus property.
Chief Butler stated in the past the city had two horses, one of which died this
past year He stated since then the program has been done away with we have an
officer that has been caring for the horse. He stated what he would like to do
is sell the horse for $1.00 to the officer that has been caring for him the
last nine months including paying all of the expenses on the horse. Attorney,
Jed Deters stated the officer legally has an “agister lien” to care for the
horse. Chief Butler stated he would be bringing this issue back to the council
meeting in October for a vote.
Mayor Moriconi asked Chief Butler if there was an update on Crowe Road Bridge.
Chief Butler stated it was still pending. He stated they are trying to get
money from the State Emergency Disaster Fund but it could be several months or
the first of the year before anything is done.
Mayor Moriconi stated another issue that has come up is the Policy and
Procedures that will be discussed at the October Caucus Meeting. Council Member
Yeager asked what issue he referring to. Mayor Moriconi stated the annual paid
leave that is accumulated monthly.
Council Member Behler stated Kroger will be having a Fall To Do on October 25,
2003 and would like members of Council to judge the costumes.
BUSINESS RECOGNITION OF THE MONTH
Council Member Behler stated she would like to recognize Kroger.
Executive Session
Council Member Franzen made a motion to go into Executive Session in accordance
with KRS 61.810 (f) with a second by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried
with all ayes.
Council Member Ellison made a motion to return to regular session; seconded by
Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
ADJOURNMENT
Council Member Yeager made a motion to adjourn, with second by Council Member
Franzen. Motion carried and the meeting was adjourned at 8:30 p.m.

September 24, 2003
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special
Session on Wednesday, September 24, 2003 at 6:30 p.m. in the Independence
Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding
in the Chair. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. The roll was called
and the following council members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim
Ellison, Carol Franzen, and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed
K. Deters. (Note: Council Member, Jim Bushong was not present during roll call,
but was a late arrival.)
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the purpose of this special meeting was for the
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   To enter into an Executive Session for the purpose of conducting individual
interviews of the candidates for the vacated council seat and related
discussion thereof.
∙   To discuss an unrelated personnel issue
∙   Discuss and possibly take action on appointing a replacement for the
vacated council seat.
3.   Mayor Moriconi advised that the city received thirteen applications for
the council seat and that the top three finalists would be interviewed
individually in executive session. He stated that council has selected him to
be the moderator and that each candidate has been allotted twenty minutes time
during which he will ask each the ten questions assembled by the council
members.
Executive Session
4.   Council Member Yeager moved to enter into executive session according to
KRS 61.810 (f) for the purposed of discussing personnel issues, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
5.   Council Member Franzen moved to return to the regular session, seconded by
Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
Appointment to Fill the Vacated Council Seat
6.   Mayor Moriconi expressed gratitude to the three candidates: Tom Brinker,
Eric Dupps and David Millward for their time and involvement in this process.
7.   A motion was made by Council Member Ellison and seconded by Council Member
Bushong to appoint Eric Dupps to the position of Council Member thereby filling
the seat vacated when Otis Ketron resigned. Roll call was answered unanimously.
Motion carried 5-0.
8.   Mayor Moriconi advised that Mr. Dupps would take the Oath of Office prior
to the next meeting of council. He advised there may be a special meeting
scheduled for next week and if so the swearing-in of Mr. Dupps would be at that
time, and if not, it would take place at the October 6th meeting.
Adjournment
9.   Upon motion by Council Member Ellison and second by Council Member Yeager
the meeting was adjourned at 8:15 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.
October 6, 2003
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
October 6, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant of the Grace
Community Church gave the invocation.
2.   Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Eric Dupps as the candidate selected by
Council to serve out the unexpired term of Council Member Otis Ketron who
resigned in August. Mayor Moriconi welcomed and congratulated Mr. Dupps. Mayor
Moriconi administered the Oath of Office to Mr. Dupps as an Independence City
Council Member.
3.   The following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim
Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present
was City Attorney, Jed Deters.
Recognition
4.   Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Behler had selected Kroger’s food
store as recipient of the Business of the Month tribute for October. Mayor
Moriconi presented Kroger’s manager, Mr. John Dubrocq with the plaque of
recognition.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 8, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September
8, 2003 regular meeting of council. Council Member Bushong so moved, with
second from Council Member Ellison. Council Member Ellison noted amendments;
roll call was answered with five yeas with Council Member Dupps passing. Motion
carried.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 15, 2003 Special Council Meeting
6.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September
15, 2003 special meeting of council. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second from Council Member Bushong. Roll call was answered with five yeas with
Council Member Dupps passing. Motion carried.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 15, 2003 Caucus Meeting
7.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the caucus
meeting held on September 15, 2003. Council Member Behler so moved, with second
from Council Member Franzen. Roll call was answered with five yeas with Council
Member Dupps passing. Motion carried.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 24, 2003 Special Council Meeting
8.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September
24, 2003 special council meeting. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second
from Council Member Franzen. Council Member Ellison noted an amendment. Roll
call was answered with five yeas, with Council Member Dupps passing. Motion
carried.
Privileges of the Floor
9.   Wanda White, 5220 Madison Pike requested JoAnne Cobble be permitted to
speak on her behalf.
10.   Mayor Moriconi stated that in the interest of fairness, that he would not
permit everyone to give his or her three minutes speaking time to Mrs. Cobble.
He advised that council is not required to permit public addresses and that
yielding the floor to the spectators is considered a privilege. Council Member
Behler stated that she would prefer to hear individual opinions and not the
viewpoint uttered through one person, that being Mrs. Cobble. Council Member
Franzen agreed, stating that others too may want more speaking time. Mayor
Moriconi asked if there was anyone in attendance that wanted to address council
on a matter other than the proposed adoption of additional taxes.
11.   Kathy Eggleston, 6336 Taylor Mill Road, addressed council regarding a
proposal to construct storage units on her property. She stated that she feels
there is a need for this type of facility in the city so that residents can
park and store their boats, campers, etc. She stated she has 15 acres and the
property is bordered by Ponzer’s golf driving range. Ms. Eggleston stated that
the rear section of this property is currently zoned RRE which does not allow
this type of facility. City Attorney, Jed Deters advised that two options were
probably available to her; 1) apply for a text amendment that would provide for
a permitted or conditional use, or 2) apply for a zone change. Council Member
Bushong suggested that she check into the options before deciding the best
course of action. Mr. Deters stated he could draft a resolution of support for
council’s consideration at the caucus meeting.
12.   Robert McCubbin, 33 McMillan Drive, addressed council regarding speeding
cars on his street. He stated he has lived there for two years and has
complained to the Police Department. He stated it has become a safety concern
for the children playing in the area and requested that police run radar to
catch the violators. Mayor Moriconi advised that Chief Butler would look into
the matter.
13.   Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum Road, addressed council expressing his
opposition to the proposed enactment of an insurance premium tax. He stated he
objects to this type of tax, as it cannot be taken as a tax deduction at year-
end. He asked that council give the citizens the opportunity to vote to enact
such a tax during a general election.
14.   Council Member Behler asked Mr. Nienaber if he was under the assumption
that the city would tax health insurance. Mr. Nienaber commented that every
city that has the insurance premium tax also taxes health insurance, except the
City of Fort Wright. Council Member Behler assured Mr. Nienaber that
Independence was not proposing to tax health and life insurances. Council
Member Franzen corroborated Council Member Behler’s statement and pointed out
that the proposed ordinance specifically exempts health and life insurance from
this tax.
15.   Vic Morrison, 100 Roselawn Drive, advised council that the audio doesn’t
work making it difficult for television viewers at home to hear the
conversation. He urged the council members to listen to the people that
supported and voted them into office. He stated that council should first prove
this tax is needed and then put it on the general election ballot for voter
approval.
16.   John Little, 6413 Jimae Avenue, addressed council regarding the proposed
insurance premium tax by saying he would support the tax if it was really
needed, but he felt that the council was presenting this tax wrong. Mayor
Moriconi stated that he felt the citizens have heard inaccurate information
with regard to the actual dollar amount that would be realized.
17.   Glenna Faulkner, 22 Carrie Way, addressed council to oppose the proposal
of new taxes. She stated she is 69 years of age, in poor health and on a fixed
income. She stated she pays $220 per month for just one prescription and after
paying her monthly expenses she has nothing left to live on.
18.   Lin Lucas, 5196 Madison Pike, expressed her opposition to the enactment
of an insurance premium tax. She stated she doesn’t see where it would be spent
on needed items, just wants. She stated the city needs basics, like sidewalks.
19.   Council Member Bushong advised that the city is trying to raise revenues
so that we can discontinue the practice of drawing from the reserve account to
make ends meet.
20.   Karl Lucas, 5196 Madison Pike, addressed council by stating he opposes
the tax. He stated people spend their lives working hard and the last thing
they need is more taxes. He stated that if the city can’t afford new things why
is a new police department building being constructed.
21.   Council Member Behler encouraged the citizens to talk to the members of
council so they can have the opportunity to explain the deficit the city is
facing in the near future.
22.   Tom Brinker, 1192 Constitution Drive, encouraged council to provide
copies of the budget to those who oppose raising taxes so that they can
contribute their suggestions for possible cuts. He advised the citizens that
the new city administration building that is under construction couldn’t be
blamed on the current administration.
23.   Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, stated she would like this council to
consider the matter of making needed street repairs to Justice Lane. She stated
that she also opposes the insurance premium tax. She stated the city recently
imposed the bank deposit tax and increased the payroll taxes and that her
personal opinion is that the citizens should not have to pay more. Mayor
Moriconi advised Ms. Woolum to contact the city attorney regarding repairs to
Justice Lane.
24.   Donna Miller, 4394 Oliver Road, expressed her opposition to the insurance
premium tax proposal by council by stating that the city has a champagne taste
on a beer pocketbook. She stated the tax should be placed on the ballot for the
people to decide.
25.   Doris King, 1906 Independence Road, stated she opposed the tax based on
her belief that it is an unfair tax. She stated that a family consisting of
mainly male drivers would pay a higher premium. She stated this community has
always been known for caring about it’s people. She stated she can’t believe
the city has needed to pull $500,000 from the reserve account each year. Mayor
Moriconi stated it has been necessary to keep up with street repairs. Ms. King
stated the city should be more vigilant with the subdivision developers.
Council Member Franzen commented that this problem didn’t just happen
yesterday, it has been coming for some time and the city is now faced with no
other choice but to raise revenues. She stated they have been left with no
other choice and is open to suggestions from the citizens on how the city can
save $600,000 each year. Council Member Franzen commented that this council has
been put in this leadership role to do what is right for the city even if
voting in favor of new taxes is not the popular choice to make.
26.   Carol Bach, 5287 Madison Pike, stated that she has been a business owner
in Independence for thirty-five years and she realizes that because she is not
a resident that she will not have a vote regarding the tax issue. She stated
that she opposes the tax increase as citizens are taxed to death. Ms. Bach
stated that the city has done nothing to develop the downtown area. She urged
council to put any new tax increases on the ballot for the people to decide.
27.   Kermit Ballmer, 689 Independence Station Road, commented that three
months ago petitions opposing increased taxes were being circulated to submit
to the city leaders. He asked how often it would be necessary to present such
petitions to the council. He stated he also opposes the vehicle sticker tax as
any additional tax will be a hardship to the senior citizens who are already
burdened by the cost of prescriptions
28.   Eric W. Thomas, 6406 Jimae Court, addressed council by stating they have
a fiscal responsibility to balance the city’s budget. He stated the city should
not spend money they do not have and then raise revenues to cover the
shortfalls in the budget. He stated that with the property tax base continuing
to rise, city officials must learn to manage the related costs. Mr. Thomas
commented that as the parent of teenage children, his automobile insurance
premium increased drastically last year and he feels that he shouldn’t have the
additional burden of a tax on this premium just because the city can’t balance
the budget. He went on to say that if the city needed additional revenue to
maintain the streets that they should implement a road tax.
29.   Council Member Franzen commented that not everyone on council is fiscally
irresponsible and urged the citizens to check her voting record.
30.   Cecilia Dennis, 4975 Oliver Road, stated that she has been talking to
council members for years about what she wants and they listen but don’t act on
her suggestions. She commented that sidewalks are badly needed in the downtown
business area as well as other improvements. She commented that the sidewalks
are in such bad condition that it is dangerous to travel them at night during
the Christmas Walk event in December. She expressed concern on how the tax
dollars are being spent and stated that she feels the city should find ways to
cut expenses.
31.   Aaron J. Wayman, 7 Apple Lane, informed council that he opposes
additional taxes. He advised that the city should not spend money until they
have the funds to do so. He urged council to figure out how to give tax cuts
instead of increasing taxes.
32.   J. George Sanders, 5268 Pioneer Drive, stated that he too does not like
taxes and he wonders how the city has found itself in this position. He stated
that with the exception of council members Behler and Franzen, the other four
members have previously held a seat on the council when the excess funds were
spent. He stated that the city needs the basic services that he believes are
police and fire protection and public works and everything else is gravy. He
stated that last year the city spent $120,000 for the Senior Center expenses
and suggested this building be rented as often as possible. In closing, Mr.
Sanders urged council to limit unnecessary spending to make an effort to
rectify the current budget deficit and after that is done and they find it is
still necessary to impose additional taxes perhaps the citizens will be
supportive of council.
33.   Fred White, 5220 Madison Pike, commented that he has lived in
Independence since 1936 and feels that taxes are already too high.
34.   Michael W. Little, 10897 Griststone, stated that he moved to Shaw Estates
subdivision about four years ago and the low property tax rate was a
consideration when re-locating to this area. He stated that he opposes the
insurance premium tax and the insurance companies will tack on an additional
administration fee. He stated that it doesn’t make sense to construct new city
buildings when the city is experiencing a budget shortfall. He stated that
there is a trust issue here as the residents feel their current tax dollars
have not been spent wisely and deserve an explanation as to where the funds
have been spent. Mr. Little stated that the seniors especially cannot pay more
taxes and that council should make more of an effort to correct the
overspending.
35.   Council Member Bushong asked what kind of fee Mr. Little was referring
to. Mr. Deters advised that the insurance companies are entitled to charge an
administration fee to collect and remit the taxes to the city. Mayor Moriconi
explained that it is the insurance companies that the city is taxing, but that
they pass this tax onto their customers, the policyholders.
36.   JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, addressed council by stating she was
opposed to increasing taxes and asked why council felt it was urgent to act
now. Mayor Moriconi advised that three proposed ordinances imposing a new tax
or increasing a current tax was on the agenda for first readings. He stated
they would not become law until the second reading and that there are state
and/or county clerk deadlines for submitting the information regarding the
taxes. He stated the insurance premium tax requires the ordinance information
be submitted 100 days prior to July 1. Mrs. Cobble commented that 100 days
would permit the city until March 23, 2004 to pass this ordinance. Mayor
Moriconi responded that council was originally informed that the effective
deadline was January 1. Council Member Dupps commented that the urgency was two
years ago when the city was beginning to experience the budget shortfall and
raising additional revenue should have been discussed at that time.
37.   Mrs. Cobble commented that the time limit was noted in the Revenue
Options report they were presented. Council Member Behler commented that they
are given a lot of information to review and sometimes they will overlook a
particular piece of data. Council Member Franzen stated that the consideration
of raising revenue is not a sudden idea as it was discussed at an open budget
summit in March of this year. She added that no residents attended this open
meeting, which was held on a Saturday.
38.   Mrs. Cobble pointed to the May 5th council meeting minutes wherein
Council Member Franzen is recorded as explaining that council never intended to
adopt the insurance premium tax ordinance in an underhanded manner and would
hold town hall meetings to garner citizen input. Council Member Franzen took
issue with Mrs. Cobble’s suggestion and countered that the tax issue has been
discussed many times in open council meetings, which have been advertised to
the public.
39.   Mrs. Cobble stated that the she does not believe the city is under a time
deadline, and has six months to give this more consideration. Council Member
Behler concurred with Council Member Franzen and again pointed out that the
city held a Budget Summit in March and no citizens attended to offer their
input regarding the city’s financial situation. Mayor Moriconi advised that at
the time of the caucus meeting the city was under the assumption that January
1, 2004 was the deadline to provide the information to the state agencies. He
also addressed Mrs. Cobble’s allegation that the meetings are not effectively
advertised on the city’s marquee sign. He asserted the city has advertised the
meetings on the sign to generate public awareness.
40.   Mrs. Cobble read excerpts from the Revenue Options report that was
provided to council. She expressed concern that the estimated revenue that
would be generated by imposing a 5% insurance premium tax on all insurance
policies except health and life was $659,681.00. She stated that compared to
the $1,042,571 revenue generated from the property taxes, the insurance tax was
63%; and argued that this would be the tax percentage increase the residents
would face.
41.   Council Member Franzen encouraged public attendance at the next meeting
wherein these ordinances will be presented for second readings. Mrs. Cobble
argued that she felt it was wrong to impose taxes that are not permitted as a
tax deduction.
42.   Mrs. Cobble stated that the property tax rate couldn’t be increased more
than 4% over the compensating rate without being subject to voter recall. Mayor
Moriconi stated the property tax ordinance for 2003 was adopted and that it
will not be subjected to voter recall, as the city did not exceed the 4%
allowed by law. Mrs. Cobble asked the Mayor what he feels was the intention of
the state legislators when the 4% cap was enacted by K.R.S. Council Member
Behler asked Mrs. Cobble where she was going with this line of questioning.
Mrs. Cobble stated that her point was that by imposing a 5% insurance tax the
revenue produced would be a 63% increase to the taxpayers. City Attorney, Jed
Deters, advised that a 4% increase over the compensating rate of property taxes
is an ad valorem on the value of property and there is no correlation between
the two types of tax. He stated that she is comparing apples to oranges. Mrs.
Cobble argued that if this council enacts the insurance premium tax they would
be increasing the tax burden on the residents by 63%.
43.   Mrs. Cobble referred to the Revenue Options report wherein the insurance
premium tax revenue projections estimated that a 5% tax would be $44.03 per
capita. She stated that, per the 2000 census, the average family consisted of
4.2 people and at $44.03 per capita would realize $176; coupled with the 2%
administration fee charged by the insurance companies, the average family would
pay $202.40 in additional taxes. Council Member Franzen disagreed, and advised
that she called her insurance company and as informed she would pay an
additional $100 per year. She urged everyone to discuss this with his or her
insurance company and get the correct information based on their current
premium payments.
44.   Mrs. Cobble stated that last year’s revenue generated from property taxes
was $1,042,571 and that the estimated revenue that would be received by
imposing a 5% insurance premium tax would be $659,681; a 63% tax increase that
will be a burden on many of the residents.
45.   Council Member Behler stated that she feels the numbers being cited by
Mrs. Cobble are being taken out of context. She stated that if she is wrong
about this she will admit it at the next caucus meeting, but asserted that she
did not agree with Mrs. Cobble’s conclusions regarding the financial effect
this tax would have.
46.   Again, Council Member Franzen urged everyone to check with his or her
insurance company for an accurate quote regarding the additional dollars they
would pay if this tax was imposed. Mayor Moriconi commented that he, too,
called his insurance company and was informed that he would pay an additional
$100 per year.
47.   Mrs. Cobble stressed that the city council needs to know all the facts
before having a first reading of this ordinance. She stated that when she spoke
to the state Attorney General’s office today that she learned that the
insurance premium tax does not permit special exemptions, such as senior
citizens. She also questioned if the Kenton County Fiscal Court and other
agencies such as the School Board were considered in the projected revenue
figures, as this tax could be costly to these agencies. She stated that she
felt the city attorney should research all possibilities before the first
reading of this ordinance. Mrs. Cobble stated that she was not here to
criticize so much as she wanted to ensure that council is aware that the facts
need to be addressed and urged council to table the first reading of the
insurance premium tax.
48.   Mrs. Cobble stated that she has learned that Independence’s property tax
rate ranks in the top five cities of the fifteen cities in Kenton County.
Council Member Franzen countered that most other cities have imposed the
insurance premium tax and while other cities may have a lower property tax rate
they have higher taxes overall.
49.   Council Member Bushong stated that it is possible that the Fiscal Court
is self-insured, in which case they would not pay insurance premium taxes.
Recess
50.   Council Member Franzen moved to take a brief recess, seconded by Council
Member Yeager. Motion carried.
51.   Council Member Yeager moved to resume the regular session of the meeting;
seconded by Council Bushong. Motion carried.
52.   Council Member Ellison suggested tabling the insurance premium tax first
reading. Mayor Moriconi stated that could be discussed under new business.
Recognition of Police Chief, Shawn Butler
53.   Mayor Moriconi stated that some citizens have come forward with a request
to be given the opportunity to commend Chief Butler at tonight’s meeting. He
introduced Mr. Vic Morrison.
54.   Mr. Morrison stated that he is a long time resident and has supported
both local and state police departments for over twenty-five years. He stated
he wanted to compliment the Independence Police Department and Chief Butler. He
presented Chief Butler with a certificate from the Natural Resources and
Environment Cabinet commissioning him the rank of admiral, a certificate
recognizing him as a Kentucky Colonel and a Certificate of Appreciation from
the House of Representatives, with sincere congratulations to Chief Butler for
his public safety efforts both on the state and local level. Mr. Morrison
stated that October 10, 2003 has been declared Chief Butler Day. Chief Butler
thanked Mr. Morrison and stated that receiving this recognition makes the job
worthwhile.

incurring an expense to repair damage done to the sidewalks, curbs and streets

60.   Council Member Franzen stated that it has been suggested that

Declare Surplus Property – Police Department Mounted Patrol Horse

as surplus property and allow the current caretaker to keep the horse.
62.   Council Member Ellison moved to declare the horse as surplus property,

would not be put up for bids. Mr. Deters advised that the current caretaker
basically has what is called an adjister lien against the city for the expenses
that have been incurred for providing food and shelter to the horse. He stated
that it has been determined that the value of the horse is less that the lien.

Proposed Ordinance – Imposing An Auto Sticker Tax
65.   Mayor Moriconi presented the proposed ordinance that would impose an auto
sticker fee for council’s consideration. Mr. Deters stated that he has
submitted a rough draft for this ordinance but that it does not have enough
substance to warrant a first reading, unless council can establish the

66.   Council Member Yeager asked Mr. Deters if he review similar ordinances

residents of the city. Mr. Deters stated he would also need to know what the
collection process would be so that it could be stated in the ordinance.
67.   Council Member Bushong stated he believes that the sticker fee and a

proposal is not an ad valorem tax. Council Member Ellison commented that it is
yet to be determined.
68.   Mr. Deters advised that the proposed ordinance, at this time is a

tax, he suggested postponing the first reading until a more definitive
ordinance can be submitted.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 1997-O-27 the Business License,
Fees, Payroll and Gross Receipts Tax

license payroll tax increase and the insurance premium tax at a special
meeting. She stated that hopefully council would be able to find solutions that
will determine the new tax unnecessary. Council Member Behler concurred.
Council Member Yeager commented that the revenue generated by the vehicle

revenue.

73.   Council Member Yeager stated that she is not in favor of any new tax or
tax increase but prefers the payroll tax rate increase to the insurance premium
tax. Council Member Behler stated that it is shortsighted of the city to look
to the payroll tax as the leading solution to the revenue shortage.
74.   Mr. Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, criticized council for not presenting

dollar amount. Council Member Ellison and Mayor Moriconi tried to explain that

protested that others should share part of the tax burden and not just the
residents. Council Member Behler stated that the city has to provide services

this ordinance would be presented for a second reading at the November meeting
of council.

Discussion Relating to Street Construction
81.   Council Member Franzen proposed that an ordinance be drafted that would
require new streets to be constructed of concrete versus asphalt in the new
residential developments. Council Member Ellison commented that he partially
agrees with Council Member Franzen, but blacktop is easier to maintain. He

OCTOBER 20, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY.
COUNCIL CAUCUS MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence met on Monday, October 20, 2003 at
7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Council Members Eric Dupps, Donna Yeager, Mary Pat Behler, Jim
Bushong and Carol Franzen answered roll call. Council Member Jim Ellison was
not present. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters and Finance
Director, Teresa Franklin Hudson.
Mayor Moriconi stated before privileges of the floor are permitted Council
Member Franzen asked to present to the audience her view of the different tax
options being considered and the shortfalls of each.
Council Member Franzen stated the fiscal year budget has a shortfall of
$610,826.00 and in order for the city to stay in the “black” the city had to
transfer approximately $600,000.00 out of the general reserve fund. She advised
that at that rate the reserve fund will be depleted by the summer of 2005.
Council Member Franzen stated the Kenton County Clerk advised her there are
approximately 14,005 cars in the City of Independence. At an annual charge of
$12.00 per car with the county charging $1.00 per car collection fee, the
revenue generated would be $154,055.00. That will leave a shortfall of
$456,771.00 in the general operating fund. Other options to consider would be
to close the Senior Citizens Center and sell it, or ask the Senior Board of
Directors to be responsible for the entire expenses of the building. She stated
another option would be to eliminate the Parks and Recreation Department,
thereby saving the city $251,081.00. She stated if we add $251,081.00 to
$154,055.00 there would still be a budget shortfall of $205,690.00. Another
option, if legal, would be to charge a vehicle sticker fee of $46.00 per
vehicle which would generate $630,225.00, which would allow the city to keep
the Senior Center and Parks/Recreation Departments. She stated that would cover
the shortfall for this year, however there are legal issues with this and the
tax dollars could only be used for certain things. She stated the fee could be
raised to $55.00 per car at a later date, but the shortfall continues. The last
option would be to close or sell the Senior Citizen Center and close the Parks
and Recreation Department and charge $27.00 per car that would generate
$364,130.00 tax dollars per year. That amount, added to the $251,081.00 for the
two closures, would cover the shortfall for this year. Council Member Franzen
stated another tax to consider would be the payroll tax. She asked everyone to
keep in mind if the payroll tax is increased the city has the potential to lose
business in the city. She stated the current rate being considered is ¼% or
.25, which would generate $218,353.00 in additional revenue. She stated adding
that amount to the current deficiet the city would still be $392,473.00 short.
She stated if the city increases the payroll tax and imposes the motor vehicle
tax to $12.00 per car, revenue would be increased by $372,408.00. She stated
there would still be a shortfall of $238,418.00. If the city increases the
payroll tax and imposes the vehicle sticker fee, eliminates the Senior Center
and Parks and Recreation Departments the city will be in the “black”
$12,663.00.
Council Member Franzen stated the other option is the insurance premium tax.
She stated it is estimated that a 5% raise on all insurance premiums, except
health and life insurance, would generate $659,681.00. She stated these are her
calculations but will not know the exact amount generated until the tax is
actually collected. She stated this money would cover the city’s shortfall.
Council Member Franzen stated she has calculated some sample insurance premiums
that include the tax premiums along with the collection fees. She stated the
collection fee charged by insurance companies is permitted by state law and the
city has no control over this, except contact our state representative and ask
him or her to lobby for a change to this law.
1.   A premium of $500.00 for 1 year would have a tax of $25.00 plus a 15%
collection fee of $3.75. The collection fee would be 15% of the total tax,
which would be $25.00 or 2% of the total premium, whichever is less. That would
be a total of $28.75 per year or $7.18 per quarter.
2.   A premium of $1,200.00 per year at 5% would be $60.00 with a $9.00
collection fee or $17.25 quarterly.
3.   A premium of $3,000.00 per year at 5% would be $150.00 plus a collection
fee of $22.50 for a total of $172.50 or $43.15 quarterly.
4.   A premium of $5,000.00 per year at 5% would be $250.00 per year plus a
collection fee of $37.50 or $287.50 a year a year or $71.88 quarterly
5.   A premium of $8,000.00 per year at 5% would be $400.00 per year plus a
collection fee of $60.00 or $460.00 a year or $115.00 quarterly.
Council Member Franzen stated she has heard comments that the insurance premium
tax will cost the citizens thousands of dollars a year. She explained that In
order to pay $1,000.00 per year in tax, you would have to be paying on a
premium of $20,000.00 per year.
Council Member Behler stated she spoke with the Chamber of Commerce and their
feeling is that most businesses prefer a premium tax in lieu of a payroll tax.
Council Member Behler stated she also spoke to Dr. Susan Cooke, Superintendent
of the Kenton County Board of Education and was advised they are coming up with
a response regarding the proposed tax options.
Council Member Franzen stated that other pending matters before the city that
needs to be taken into consideration is that the city has $400,000.00 in bridge
repairs on Crowe Road that does not include needed repairs to the road that
currently is slipping into the creek. She stated she has spoken to Jeff Smith
of the Public Works Department and was informed there are nineteen new streets
this year and next year the city will probably take over maintenance of twenty
more. All of these streets have to be maintained and plowed in the winter. She
stated Mr. Smith also informed her that Kenton County has lost a truck from
their fleet and in order to keep up with the street plowing, with the addition
of the new streets the city may have to purchase a new truck.
In closing, Council Member Franzen asked the audience to please keep in mind
that the budget shortfalls did not occur overnight.
Council Member Yeager stated she would like to make a comment. She stated that
“hell hath no fury like seniors and children” if you take away the Senior
Center and Parks Departments. She stated with the payroll tax and the vehicle
sticker fee, along with the compensating property tax rate plus the additional
4%, together with tightening our belts the city can make it.
Council Member Franzen commented that it will not stop the “bleeding”.
Privileges of the Floor
Kermit Ballmer, 689 Independence Station Rd, Mr. Ballmer stated in regards to
the ordinance on the car sticker, there are people living in condos and rental
property that the insurance tax will not affect. He stated his concern with the
payroll tax is current unemployment is over 6% and if you raise the payroll tax
there is no reason why the businesses in the industrial area and in the city
would not look for other tax free areas to relocate. Mr. Ballmer stated if the

going to move to the residential areas in the unincorporated areas of the

stated there is a state law that says a city cannot file bankruptcy but if

staff at the city building for being so professional and courteous. He stated
he obtained a copy of the finance reports for years ending June 2002 and June

a large part of the budget and in seeing that he looked at the population,
number of employees and police officers in the Kenton County and in doing so he
found per capita the city is not the highest or the lowest but somewhere in the
middle. He stated that safety for his family is very important to him and also
community safety is very important. He stated he wants the best equipped, best

impose any changes at this time. He stated in looking at the other numbers he
felt the amounts appeared to be reasonable but the fact remains the
expenditures for this fiscal year are projected to be $600,000.00 more than

the Senior Citizens Building as well as the Municipal Building. He stated he

fine police force and a place for our senior citizens to go, but at the same
time he wants to live in a community where the taxes are low and his property
values aren’t decreasing because of taxes. He stated in looking at the budget
this fiscal year he would ask three things of council when considering these
taxes. He would like council to consider areas to reduce costs to as much as
$300,000.00. He stated he would request the Finance Director make a detailed
forecast for the next five years. He stated he did not feel a major tax
increase is needed at this time and felt the insurance tax is too much and is
too open ended. He stated Independence should be a city where wealth is
generated, property values increase and where people want to come to work and
live and spend their money. He stated he appreciated Council Member Franzen’s

Mr. Little stated when Council Member Franzen brought up the fact that the

George Sanders, 5268 Pioneer Drive, stated the deficit spending has been going

receive.

democracy at work. He stated it was good to hear comments and suggestions and

New Business
Proposed Text Amendment to add Parking Garages as a Permitted Use in NSC Zone
Mayor Moriconi stated there is a proposed Ordinance to approve a Text Amendment

Elimination of Primary Elections
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that he has been made aware that primaries
cannot be eliminated in a third class city. He stated Bill Aylor, County Clerk
read the KRS stating it only applies to fourth thru sixth class cities.
Legal Review of Accrued Paid Leave Policy for City Employees
Council Member Yeager asked if the entire personnel policy would be reviewed.
City Attorney, Jed Deters stated all of the personnel policy would be reviewed.
He stated there have been some legal changes since the last time it was
updated. Council Member Behler asked if Council would vote on the changes.
Mayor Moriconi stated it would have to be voted on at the next Council Meeting.
Council Member Bushong asked if this was for the entire policy and procedures
or just accrued leave. Mr. Deters stated it would be a legal review of the
entire policy.
Council Member Bushong asked who would review the policy and how long will it
take. Mr. Deters stated his office would do the reviewing and it should take a
month, possibly longer. Council Member Bushong stated he agrees the policy
should be reviewed but is concerned with prolonging the discussion much longer
on the accrued leave situation. Attorney Deters stated recommendations have
been made on those issues. Council Member Bushong asked what recommendations
were made. Chief Butler stated he did not have the recommendations with him but
there was a recommendation on a cap for accrued leave. Council Member Behler
stated Mr. Deters recommended changes in how much time can be accrued. Council
Member Bushong asked if Mayor and Council were going to look at dollar figures
regarding accrued time. Chief Butler stated the recommendation on accrued time
did not include dollar amounts. Mr. Deters stated when the policy is reviewed
completely he will look at possible avenues in buying out overtime. Council
Member Yeager stated she had suggested 240 hours as a maximum carry over.
Council Member Bushong stated he was given information on how much accrued time
each employee has and if something happened to the employee with a high amount
of accrued time, the city could be out $48,000.00 or more. City Clerk, Patricia
Taney stated it is more like $134,000.00 as of June 30, 2003. Mr. Deters stated
it is a significant liability. Mayor Moriconi stated at the next Council
Meeting a Resolution could be presented. Council Member Bushong stated he has a
problem with having discussions when he does not have any paperwork to absorb.
Council Member Dupps asked if it would be a legal review or an administrative
review. Mr. Deters stated it would be both.
Old Business
Proposed Ordinance Relating to Sidewalk Waiver Requests
Mayor Moriconi asked if Council had any questions on this proposed ordinance.
Council Member Behler stated she is concerned with placing a lien on a piece of
property if the amount if not known. She stated if we put a lien on this
property and eight years later we need a sidewalk, how the city would know
there has been enough money put on that lien to add a sidewalk. Mr. Deters
stated he did not feel liens need to be updated yearly based on the engineers
projection. Council Member Bushong asked if a lien is placed based on the
situation knowing it will be a good amount for eight years, could we make it
subject to a cost of living adjustment every year. Mr. Deters stated an
interest rate could be added to the lien yearly. He stated engineers are able
to estimate pretty close on the cost of sidewalks. Council Member Franzen asked
if she were correct in saying the city would not be actually collecting any
money, just placing the lien so it can be adjusted.
Mr. Deters stated it could be adjusted. He stated for the publics information,
several people have asked the city for a sidewalk waiver. The subdivision
regulations require if a house is built you must install a sidewalk in front of
the house. He stated there are certain circumstances that would prevent you
from doing that. Sometimes it is topographically impossible to install
sidewalks or there are no other streets or sidewalks around so they are asking
for a waiver to that requirement. The city is concerned primarily due to
changing circumstances as years go by. He stated the city does not just want to
say “no” but if the city files a lien and in the future circumstances change
then the city can enforce the installing of a sidewalk. Mayor Moriconi stated
the lien is not so much for a subdivision but for example Independence Station
Road by Cody Road. He stated due to the increase of homes on these main roads
you might have a sidewalk that goes nowhere. Council Member Franzen asked if
the city engineer could help to determine the percent to be placed on the lien.
Mr. Deters stated he could.
Business Recognition for the Month of November
Mayor Moriconi asked Council Member Bushong what business he chose to recognize
at the November meeting. Council Member Bushong stated he did not know yet but
will let the City Clerk know.
Crowe Road Update
Mayor Moriconi stated the city has applied for state emergency funds to assist
with the repairs needed on Crowe Road.. He stated the estimate on replacing
that bridge is approximately $400,000.00 according to the city engineer. Chief
Butler stated a letter was received October 10th from Robert Hayes, the
district engineer for the state. He basically reaffirmed that the bridge is in
poor condition and in order to be considered for federal funds, we were in
compliance with the posting. He stated it could still be several months before
we hear what we might get or not get from federal funds. He stated these funds
would be for the bridge only.
Mrs. Cobble asked if the city has applied for a grant to help with the cost of
the bridge. Chief Butler stated the city is trying to get federal emergency
funds to replace the bridge but it is a very lengthy process. Mrs. Cobble asked
Mayor Moriconi is he has asked Senator Thayer for his assistance. Mayor
Moriconi stated he has asked Senator Thayer as well as Tom Kerr for their
assistance in obtaining state funds.
Council Member Franzen stated she spoke to Jeff Smith, Public Works and was
advised there is a storm sewer pipe that is rusting out on Production Drive and
he estimates a cost of $167,000.00 to replace the whole thing. She stated Jeff
Smith is filling out requisition forms to the Sanitation District for
assistance in all, if not some of the cost. Chief Butler stated there are some
questions as to replacing the pipe in sections. Council Member Franzen stated
it would cost $22,000.00 just to replace the section that has rusted out. She
stated the rusted pipe is creating sinkholes and the engineer is going to
inspect it.
Council Member Dupps asked if the city has looked at reopening the old section
of Richardson Road that exits on to Old State Route 17. Mayor Moriconi stated
irregardless if the city has to go to Plan B and we do not get any funds for
repairs is to close it and open up Old Richardson but that road is slipping
down the hill. Chief Butler stated in order to open up Old Richardson the state
has been less than enthusiastic about allowing that to be reopened. Chief
Butler stated one of the problems with applying for grants; the state always
takes into consideration the number of homes, which may not have an economic
impact to invest that amount of money. He stated that is a big problem when the
city applies for emergency money or grant money they look at the economic
impact as a whole and they weigh that very heavily on the project.
Council Member Franzen stated when she revisited Crowe Road there is an
abandoned house with trash piled in the driveway and what appeared to be stray
dogs. She asked if we could get Annie Wuestefeld, Zoning Administrator to
inspect it.
Discussion Regarding the MPG Stores
Council Member Yeager stated she drove by the MPG Store at the corner of
Richardson and Beechgrove and saw they are tearing it down. She asked if the

OCTOBER 20, 2003
CITY OF INDEPENDENCE, KY
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special
Session on Monday, October 20, 2003 at 6:30 p.m. at the Independence Senior
Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor
Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Donna Yeager, Mary Pay Behler, Eric Dupps, Carol
Franzen and Jim Bushong. Council Member Jim Ellison was not present. Also
present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the purpose of the special meeting was to
discuss and have a first reading of a proposed ordinance that would impose a
vehicle sticker fee. City Attorney, Jed Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Discussion
3.   Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion of this matter. Council
Member Behler asked if the Kenton County School Buses would have to pay a
vehicle tax. City Clerk, Patricia Taney stated that any vehicle that has an
official tag on it, would not pay the fee. Council Member Behler asked if a
resident has a vehicle registered in another community, perhaps a company car,
would they have to pay for an auto sticker. Mrs. Taney stated the vehicle has
to be registered in the state of Kentucky and reside in the city of
Independence. Mayor Moriconi stated that an actual sticker would not be issued.
Council Member Franzen stated the Kenton County Clerk has estimated there are
14,005 vehicles registered in Independence.
4.   Mayor Moriconi stated if there was no more discussion on this matter, a
second reading of the ordinance would be presented at the November 3, 2003
Council Meeting.
5.   Council Member Behler asked how this ordinance would be enforced. Mayor
Moriconi stated the vehicle sticker fee would be placed on the annual
registration notice. Council Member Behler asked if the vehicle owner would
have the option of not paying this tax. Mayor Moriconi stated no, it will be
listed as a line item just like the taxes for the Independence Fire District,
Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission, Kenton County Library, and Health
District.
Adjournment
6.   There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to
adjourn the meeting.
7.   Council Member Yeager so moved with a second by Council Member Franzen to
adjourn. Motion carried and the meeting adjourned at 6:38 p.m.
                     ________________________________
                     Christian J. Moriconi, Mayor

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk

Kathy L. Stenger, Asst City Clerk
November 3, 2003
City of Independence, Ky.
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
November 3, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Revered Charles Steger of Hickory Grove
Baptist Church gave the invocation. An audience member asked everyone to
remember the seventeen soldiers that lost their lives in Iraq this past week.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat
Behler, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Jim Ellison, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager.
Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Bushong had selected Swindler and
Currin Funeral Home as recipient of the Business of the Month tribute for
November. Mayor Moriconi presented Stephanie Currin and her sister with the
plaque.
Approval of the Minutes of the October 6, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of October 6,
2003 regular council meeting. Council Member Bushong so moved, with a second
from Council Member Mary Pat Behler. No amendments were noted and roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the October 20, 2003 Special Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the October
20, 2003 Special Council Meeting. Council Member Yeager so moved, with a second
from Council Member Dupps. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
with 5 ayes and 1 pass by Council Member Ellison.
Approval of the October 20, 2003 Caucus Meeting Minutes
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the October
20, 2003 caucus meeting of council. Council Member Franzen moved, with a second
by Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
with 5 ayes and 1 pass by Council Member Ellison.
Privileges of the Floor
6.   Rick Jordan, President of LSI Industries, 3871 Turkeyfoot Road addressed
council by stating LSI has paid over $274,000.00 in taxes and of that amount
Independence was paid an excess of $50,000.00. He stated two years ago they
employed over 200 employees in their facility and then the recession hit and
their orders dried up resulting in them eliminating eighty positions which
substantially reduced their work force. He stated they found it was necessary
to cut their costs and renegotiate with their suppliers. He stated they also
had to change some supplies due to their refusal to reduce their costs. He
stated a “Cost Committee” was formed to implement ideas on how to examine cost
saving measures to reduce their operating expenses. He stated LSI is returning
and just recently became the largest supplier for interior parking lot lighting
for the world’s largest retailer. He stated they are now beginning to increase
their workforce. Mr. Jordan advised LSI Industries is against any proposed
raise in taxes, both the payroll and insurance tax. He stated the insurance tax
is not just a 5%, but the insurance companies add administration fees for
processing this tax. He stated it is important not to raise payroll taxes as
this would hinder their ability to get qualified workers. He stated since they
have been through a recession, the city should cut their expenses and live
within the current budget. He stated LSI does not agree with the idea to
increase taxes in order to maintain a surplus.
7.   Charlene Case-522 Rice Road addressed council regarding storm water
drainage onto her property. She advises she has lived on Rice Road forty-years
and in that time fourteen new homes have been built on the street. She feels
this has contributed to the drainage problem. Ms. Case referred to a letter she
received from the City Engineer wherein he has determined the water drainage is
a result of the change in her driveway. She argued there have been no changes
in her driveway. She stated the city engineer came over to inspect it and
stated it was not a condition that required city maintenance, but was personal
property maintenance. She advised that Jeff Smith of the city Public Works
Department has also inspected the area. She stated they are in the city limits
and they pay city and county taxes and so far they have received no services,
just higher taxes. She stated if Rice Road is in the city limits then it should
be treated for maintenance. She stated she should not have to put a swale or a
ditch from the top of the road down to the bottom. She stated the water is
running from the top of the road due to heavy trucks traveling on it and it has
shifted the road and now the water travels down her driveway instead of in the
ditch. She stated if she has to change the flow of the water she will have to
cross private property. She stated the city advised her they cannot cross
private property but why do they think she can do it. She stated her neighbors
will not want a ditch four to six inches deep on their property when they don’t
need it.
8.   Mayor Moriconi explained to council that Mrs. Case lives on Rice Road and
water is running down Rice Road across her gravel driveway and washes out the
gravel. Mayor Moriconi stated the city engineer inspected the site and advised
it was not a city problem. He stated council can decide what to do but the
Public Works Department will have to go on private property to solve the
problem by building a swale.
9.   Mrs. Case asked if the city has a certain amount of right-of-way on every
road in the city. Mayor Moriconi stated they are finding there are different
right-of-ways for different roads. Mrs. Case stated she knows Rice Road has
been in the city for at least forty years and all she is ever told is there is
not enough money in the budget. She stated there is money in the budget to
