November 17, 2003
City of Independence, Ky.
CAUCUS COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, November
17, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong,
Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager answered roll call. Council Member
Jim Ellison was absent. Also attending was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Judy Kite, 708 Independence Station Road, stated she lives on a flag lot and
addressed council regarding a problem she is having a builder (Steve Amann) who
has damaged a section of her property while in the process of constructing a
new home. Mayor Moriconi explained there is an easement that runs across Ms.
Kite’s property which the developer used and then did not return the land to
it’s original condition. Ms. Kite stated that she has spoken to Mr. Amann and
has not been successful in getting him correct the problem.
Mr. Deters advised Ms. Kite that the developer had no right to encroach onto
her property and that because this is a private, civil matter she should retain
an attorney to help her resolve this matter.
Chuck Kahrs, 21 Oby Drive, addressed council again about the persistent
speeding problem on Oby Drive. He urged council to install a permanent speed
hump/bump or a stop sign on Oby Drive, as he feels this will resolve the
speeding problem. Mr. Kahrs distributed a report that he obtained from the
Police Chief that proves that speeding vehicles are a frequent occurrence.
Chief Shawn Butler stated that considering the other speeding complaints he
receives for other areas of the city, if council would set forth guidelines for
speed humps/bumps that would be adopted for the entire city then he would be
agreeable to installing them. He stated that the cost for the permanent humps/
bumps should be considered.
Mr. Kahrs stated a stop sign would have the same effect. Chief Butler stated
that installing a stop sign in the middle of a street that does not intersect
does not meet the criteria of the current city ordinance. Mr. Kahrs suggested a
temporary stop sign. Council Member Franzen said that drivers might ignore the
stop sign and drive right through it. Council Member Yeager commented that this
might be a temporary solution until a permanent resolution can be found for
controlling the speeders on this street. She asked Chief Butler what he
recommended to resolve this ongoing situation. Chief Butler reiterated that he
felt the current speeding problem on Oby Drive was a result of the increased
development of the Freedom Trails Subdivision. He stated this subdivision had
no other egress than Oby Drive and that Oby Drive was not constructed to handle
this volume of traffic. He requested time to respond until after he reviewed
the traffic report and assured Mr. Kahrs that he would continue to work with
him until this speeding problem is finish.
OLD BUSINESS
Building Permits In Relation to the Business License
Mayor Moriconi advised that an issue has been presented as to whether or not
the city can withhold or deny a building permit if the sub-contractors do not
possess a current business license with the city.
Mr. Deters explained that withholding the building permits until all sub
contractors have a city business license is an attempt to ensure that
occupational license and related payroll taxes are being paid to the city. He
stated that the city’s zoning ordinance requires a building permit application
be completed and submitted for approval and if there are blanks for which the
sub-contractor names are to be listed then the permit could be denied for
failing to list the subs. But he stated that in his opinion he does not feel a
permit could be denied if it is discovered that one or more of the sub-
contractors listed do not have a license, unless there was a text amendment
providing that as a condition of issuance of a permit. He stated the current
language of the zoning ordinance does not provide for the denial of a building
permit based on sub-contractors being licensed prior to issuance of a permit.
He concluded that in his opinion it would be inappropriate for the city to deny
a building permit on the basis that a subcontractor is not license.
Council Member Yeager stated that when she requested the city ensure that all
the sub-contractors were paying payroll tax it was not her intent to withhold
building permits. Mr. Deters stated that it would be difficult to police the
sub-contractors and the general contractor cannot be held responsible for the
subs. The City Clerk advised the office would implement a procedure to forward
the list of sub-contractors to the Kenton County Occupational License
Director’s office who would then verify the businesses that were licensed and
send notices to the sub-contractors that needed to obtain a license.
Discussion Regarding the Proposed Ordinance Relating to Sidewalk Waiver
Requests
Mr. Deters advised that he met with the city engineer and building inspector to
review the proposed ordinance that would provide a sidewalk waiver to
properties that have unusual topographical conditions as well as ensuring that
construction of a sidewalk would be done at a later date if there were physical
changes to the land. He stated that the ordinance has been revised to
incorporate everyone’s concerns. He advised that the waiver would be considered
temporary and a lien would be recorded to ensure that construction of a
sidewalk would be completed at a later date should the city later deem it
necessary due to a change in circumstances. Mr. Deters stated that the lien
would be an amount deemed appropriate by the building inspector and city
engineer together with a three percent per annum interest rate which would
cover the cost of the construction of the sidewalk in the future.
Council Member Dupps asked how this would be handled in the future should it be
determined a sidewalk should be construction. Mr. Deters advised that notice
would be given to the property owner and the lien enforced at that time.
Council Member Dupps commented that sometimes the sidewalks that are being
constructed now appear to go nowhere but years from now they will connect. Mr.
Deters advised that the proposed ordinance would ensure that sidewalks would be
installed in the future if it the landscape is altered to accommodate one.
Discussion Regarding the Glenhurst Park Development Plan
Mayor Moriconi asked Chief Butler to explain the status of the development of
the Glenhurst Park. Chief Butler stated the developers of the Glenhurst
Subdivision, along with the land for the park area, are also contributing
$25,000 for the development of the park. He stated he met with Council Member
Yeager to review the possible options available to the city. Chief Butler
advised that a sidewalk has been constructed around the lake area, which cost
$8,000, so the balance of $17,000 is available for other improvements to the
park area. He stated the developer would like the city to select the other

Council Member Bushong expressed concern with the lake area, which he stated is
actually a retention pond. He stated that he disagrees with the city’s decision
to assume responsibility of this retention pond and calling it a lake. Mr.

the city in December 2002. Council Member Franzen also expressed concern with

Chief Butler suggested the city use the remaining $17,000 to have the developer
install electric for the placement of security lights. Council Member Yeager
agreed with the installation of electrical lines as well as suggested water

for playground equipment. Council Member Franzen asked if the land was

Mayor Moriconi advised the park area in the subdivision is a facility that

Council Member Franzen commented that she was in favor of keeping this park as
passive recreation and installing the water and electric lines. Council Member
Yeager advised the city would reap more of a benefit by having the developer
install the utility lines while the area is being developed. Council Member
Behler concurred by commenting that the utility lines sounds like the best plan
for the area.
Mr. Deters commented that hopefully when the Sanitation District assumes full
responsibility of the storm water utility over the next several years that the
retention pond will be part of the takeover. Council Member Bushong agreed that
the utility lines were the best way to spend the remainder of the donation by

remainder of the money would be presented for council to accept at the December
1, 2003 council meeting.
New Business
Request for Water Service on Webster Road by Michelle and Michael Herrman
Michelle and Michael Herrman addressed council with a request for assistance in
obtaining water service and fire protection for property located at 345 Webster
Road. They submitted an estimate obtained by the Water District’s engineer
(Viox & Viox, Inc.) in the amount of $72,531.00. Mrs. Herrman stated the Water
District is requiring the installation of an eight-inch water main as well as
four fire hydrants along the 1720 linear feet of service line. She stated that
she petitioned the other property owners in the area to see if there was any
interest in obtaining public water service. Only one other property owner (399
Webster Road) was interested, the others stated that they were not interested
due to the extreme cost.
Mrs. Herrman stated that they felt the Water District’s requirements for an
eight-inch water main and four fire hydrants were excessive considering Webster
Road is a dead-end street. She also felt the residents should not have to pay
for the engineering costs. Mrs. Herrman stated that the District also requires
the main extend across the full road frontage of their parcel which she feels
is excessive considering the property owners at 431 and 5025 have stated they
do not desire water service. She stated that the District has said that there
are some exceptions to their requirements and would like the city to intervene
in an effort to obtain a more affordable price for this service.
Council Member Yeager asked what the city could do to assist the Herrman’s.
Council Member Franzen pointed to page two of the Herrman’s letter that
requests the city assist in obtaining low-cost financing.
Chief Butler commented that other areas of the city are dealing with the same
issues. He stated that the Water District has established a twenty-year plan
and if their area is a low priority on the plan they may not get service any
time soon. He stated the city has not control over the Water District’s
procedures for providing water service to their customers.
Mrs. Herrman stated the Water District recommended they approach the city for
assistance. Chief Butler asked what type of assistance they would like to
obtain from the city. She stated that she did not expect the city would foot
the bill for the entire project but suggested the city may assist by applying
for a grant or paying a portion. There was some discussion regarding a ‘spider’
line, which Mrs. Herrman advised the Water District has stated they would not
permit that type of connection. Council Member Bushong suggested a double meter
that could be tapped onto a neighbor’s line.
Mayor Moriconi advised the Herrman’s that he would be willing to set up a
meeting with representatives of the Water District or write a letter of support
if it would help. Chief Butler stated it comes down to money and if the city
provides financial assistance to the Hermann’s then it would set precedent for
future requests. Council Member Franzen suggested inviting the Water District
to the next caucus meeting to discuss this matter. The City Clerk asked the
Hermann’s if they were in the process of building their house. Mrs. Hermann
stated they have prepared the building plans and have contracted a builder, but
the water lines have the construction start date on hold until they can find a
resolution. Mr. Deters suggested they install a cistern and move on. Chief
Butler stated he would invite the Water District to the December caucus
meeting.
Discussion Regarding the Banklick Watershed Study – Melissa Jort, NKAPC
Mayor Moriconi introduced Melissa Jort, from the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission who was present to speak about the Banklick Watershed
Study.
Ms. Jort stated she wanted to familiarize the city with the Banklick Watershed
Council, which has recently received a grant to conduct the study. She stated
the project would be looking for ways to improve the watershed, which are
natural catch basins, both visible and invisible and will link this to urban
forestry. The project will help make the community healthy and attractive She
stated that the urban forest provides a number of functions that are vital to
the health of cities – trees absorb pollutants, cleanse our water supply,
provide shade to cool the city’s temperature in summer reducing energy demands,
provide flood control and enhance our landscape. She advised that Banklick
Creek, which is surrounded by steep slopes, has been identified as an impaired
waterway.
Ms. Jort stated that the Council was originally formed to educate the public on
the importance of clean water for the public health and welfare. She stated
that currently the Council’s overall goals for this project are to identify
‘’hot spots’’ along the watershed where urban forestry techniques could be
effectively implemented to improve the water quality, public education and
input and finally, produce a manual for other Watershed Councils. She stated
the project schedule is now through the end of 2004 to gather data, identify
issues and develop the manual with the promotion and distribution of the
published report in 2005.
Ms. Jort requested support on this project from the city by communicating the
importance of this project to the citizens. She asked for a city representative
that would act as a liaison to receive information as well as help in promoting
the results of the study.
Council Member Bushong asked if the citizens should report areas of erosion
and/or flooding. Ms. Jort replied yes, as well as providing information about
the location of stream areas. Council Member Bushong asked if the Council would
be conducting surveys as part of the project. Ms. Jort stated they may, but are
planning public forums where focus groups will speak face to face with the
citizens.
Mayor Moriconi advised Ms. Jort that Council Member Dupps has volunteered to be
the city’s contact person with the Banklick Watershed Council, and Council
Member Behler has volunteered to be the alternate. Mayor Moriconi asked Ms.
Jort if she knew of any grants available for the purchase of property along the
watershed area. She replied that she was not aware of any grants available to
acquire land, but would check into it. Mayor Moriconi thanks Ms. Jort for
addressing council on this matter.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Ordinance to Approve a Text Amendment
(Application No. 1640R by Martin Neltner)
Mayor Moriconi advised this ordinance for this zoning text amendment would be
presented for a second reading at the December 1, 2003 council meeting. He
stated Mr. Neltner was in attendance to present a proposed site plan for the
development that prompted his appeal for this text amendment.
Mr. Neltner advised he met with the neighboring property owners last week to
inform them of his plans for the property behind the Cherokee shopping center
and gather their input and address their concerns. He stated he would like to
install a storage facility with an attractive buffer to make this structure
less offensive to the neighbors. He stated their concerns were too much
security lighting and having the facility designed so that it would not be too
obtrusive. Mr. Neltner advised that he has not received formal approval for
this development, as the area needs some improvement. Mayor Moriconi asked if
he planned on parking garages, as the recommendation handed down from the KCPC
makes it sound if he wants a text amendment to add parking garages. Mr. Neltner
stated he does not plan parking garages, just storage garages. He would like to
utilize a few of the garages for his own property maintenance type of
equipment. Mr. Deters stated that KCPC recommendation terms the facility as a
parking garage for which they have recommended approval, but had recommended
disapproval for the storage garage. Council Member Behler asked if the area
already had a natural barrier. Mr. Neltner stated there are a lot of scrub
trees, which will be removed, but the other trees will be reserved, as well as
the additional installation of shrubs, etc.
Council Member Franzen stated she would like to hear from any of the residents
who live in that area.
Mr. Lancaster, 733 Cox Road, stated that Mr. Neltner did not submit a
definitive plan to the residents. He stated some approved of Mr. Neltner’s
proposal, and others were unsure since he did not submit a site plan. Mr.
Lancaster stated that he feels this type of storage facility should be
permitted in an industrial zone, not a neighborhood shopping center. He urged
the city to inspect the site, as the area slopes and this may cause water
drainage problems.
Mrs. Walker, 6446 Shawnee Court, stated she has lived there since 1973 and in
recent years the area was allowed to become overgrown in an effort to
discourage foot traffic behind the shopping center. She stated she is concerned
as the site is surrounded on three sides that are residential property. Mrs.
Walker expressed concern that they will loose their privacy and that her
property value will decrease.
Mr. Deters advised that the city’s current zoning ordinance permits storage
facilities in the IP (Industrial Park) zone only. Council Member Bushong asked
how the Richardson Road storage facility as able to come about. Council Member
Dupps stated that that particular area on Richardson Road is zoned IP.
Mr. John Huffman, introduced himself as the owner of the storage facility on
Richardson Road. He stated that he does not live in Independence, but runs his
office out of the Richardson Road self-storage facility. He expressed concern,
that in permitting Mr. Neltner to develop another storage facility in the city
there would be excess storage available, and not enough demand, leaving these
facilities unoccupied. Council Member Dupps asked Mr. Huffman what his
occupancy rate was. Mr. Huffman replied that it was 25% less than he was
assured it would be.
Lola Belville, 741 Cox Road, expressed concern that a storage facility would
devalue her property.
Karyl Shouse,737 Cox Road, told council that she does not want a storage
facility in her back yard.
Mike Walker, 6446 Shawnee, stated he was concerned about the noise pollution by
the cars that would enter the facility. He also pointed out that the site was
surrounded by residential properties.
Mr. Neltner commented that the adjoining property owners all had the
opportunity to purchase the land, but did not. He stated the property is zoned
commercial and he is entitled to develop it as it is currently zoned in a
commercial way that could generate even more traffic than a storage facility.
He stated that he feels this is the most logical development for the site and
would work with the neighbors and city to develop an attractive facility. He
stated the site is now housing some debris, as it has become a dumping ground
by some of the abutting property owners.
Mr. Deters advised Mr. Neltner that the city had a first reading of the
proposed text amendment ordinance at the November 3 council meeting. He stated
that the proposed ordinance accepts the recommendation as submitted to the city
by the KCPC. Mr. Deters advised council that the city needs more zones than
just the IP zone designated to house these types of uses.
Mayor Moriconi asked council if they wanted to move forward with a second
reading of this ordinance. The majority of the council members indicated they
did not want to proceed with the ordinance as it has been presented at the
first reading. Mr. Deters suggested a zoning text amendment to permit storage
facilities in the IP and NSC zones. Council Member Franzen stated she would
like to inspect Mr. Neltner’s property. Mr. Deters advised that council had
plenty of time to act on a proposed text amendment recommendation. A member in
the audience suggested the site should be returned to the original residential
zone. Mr. Deters advised the property is zoned commercial in keeping with the
Comprehensive Plan that was adopted. Mayor Moriconi stated that in order to
return the zone to residential Mr. Neltner would have to make application to
have it re-zoned residential again.
Mayor Moriconi advised that this proposed text amendment ordinance will not be
presented for a second reading at the December 1, 2003 council and will be
postponed indefinitely. Mr. Deters advised everyone that this property owned by
Mr. Neltner, with the commercial zoning, allows him forty-five other uses which
could generate a lot more traffic in the area. Mayor Moriconi reiterated that
this matter would be postponed until a later time and after the council members
look over the area.
Proposed Ordinance that would Repeal Ordinance No. 1-11-87 Pertaining to
Justice Lane
Mr. Deters explained that he has drafted an ordinance that would repeal
Ordinance No. 1-11-87, which was adopted in 1987 to accept Justice Lane as a
city maintained street. He stated this ordinance was adopted at an emergency
reading because a resident on Justice Lane needed it to meet a deadline for a
loan closing since the house on Justice Lane did not have frontage on a public
dedicated street. He stated apparently the bank providing the loan to the
resident required Justice Lane to be approved for maintenance by the city. He
stated that the problem is that Justice Lane was never dedicated for acceptance
and was never platted for dedication, nor was it improved to city standards
therefore making Ordinance No. 1-11-87 invalid. Mr. Deters also advised the
city has never provided maintenance of the street. He stated that the ordinance
should be cleared off the books so this matter can be put to rest.
Mayor Moriconi stated the ordinance would be presented for a first reading at
the December 1, 2003 council meeting.
Proposed Executive Order Appointing Additional Citation Officers
Mr. Deters advised that an Executive Order has been drafted that will appoint
additional citation officers for the city. He stated that several months ago it
was noticed that the city had several people who had citation authority and
that some might not have been as knowledgeable of the code restrictions to
shoulder the full responsibility that this authority requires. He stated that
currently the Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld is the only citation
officer for the city. Mr. Deters advised that the current citation process has
been reconsidered and it has been determined that the Building Inspector and
the Public Works Crew Leader should be appointed citation officers so they
would have the authority to cite violations of other city ordinances. He
advised that Annie Wuestefeld mainly cites zoning ordinance violations and by
authorizing the personnel of Building and Public Works Departments the issues
dealing with streets and building violations could be handled more efficiently.
Council Member Yeager expressed concern that anyone could issue citations and
suggested it is specified the type of citation that each citation officer would
be empowered to issue. Mr. Deters assured her that the appropriate person would
handle the necessary citation most compatible with each department. He stated
this will provide more time to analyze the citation needs of the city.
Mayor Moriconi stated the Executive Order appointing the additional citation
officers would be presented at the December 1, 2003 council meeting.
Discussion Regarding Establishing Property Condemnation Procedures
Mr. Deters advised council the city has some properties that need to be
condemned as they are structurally unsound and in violation of the property
maintenance code. He stated the city cuts the grass and does some basic
property maintenance and then places a lien on the property. He stated that the
property at 5220 Belle Drive is a public safety hazard, for which the city
could initiate condemnation proceedings and order the structure to be razed. He
advised that if the property owner disregarded the order, then the city could
level the property and place a lien on the property for the cost to do the
work. He stated that this would be an expense to the city, which may not be
reimbursed to the city until a later date when the property is sold. Mr. Deters
recommended before condemning a property that it be inspected by the building
inspector and city engineer to ensure it is structurally unsafe and the provide
a short abatement period to the property owner. Mayor Moriconi concurred that
the property on Belle Drive is a safety concern for the city. Mr. Stan Kahrs, a
resident of Belle Drive, informed council that the residents on Belle Drive
have tolerated this blighted property too long. There was a brief discussion
whether or not the property could be used by the Fire District as a training
tool for a controlled burn. Mr. Deters advised that appropriate notice should
be sent to the property owner.
Business Recognition for the Month of December
Mayor Moriconi stated he would select a business for the month of December.
Crowe Road Update by City Engineer, Mark Brueggemann, CDS Associates, Inc.
Mr. Brueggemann advised council that several months ago he reported to the city
the cost to replace the bridge over Richardson Road. He stated that this bridge
has an eight-ton limit, which is being exceeded by the Rumpke trash hauling
trucks. He advised that it has been determined that it would be more economical
to replace the bridge than to restore it to its original condition. The bridge
replacement cost would run about $440,000 and there is no inexpensive option to
make the current bridge safe other than re-opening the intersection of
Richardson Road and Old Route 17, and even though traffic in that area is
considerably less now that Route 17 has been re-routed it is not really a safe
option. He stated that another issue that needs to be addressed is the
landslides occurring in the same area of the bridge. He advised that Crowe Road
has active slides occurring along the bank of the creek, which presents another
potential issue of conserving access to the properties on Crowe Road. Mr.
Brueggemann guestimated that the cost to repair the landslides would be around
$700,000.
Council Member Yeager commented that Richardson Road is state maintained.
Council Member Bushong asked if the city has looked into the cost to buy out
the property owners on Crowe Road, as it may be a more cost effective option
for the city compared to the estimated cost to replace the bridge. Chief Butler
commented the city needs to move forward with some option so as to limit the
excess liability. Council Member Bushong asked if the property owners on Crowe
Road have been surveyed. Mayor Moriconi advised that he would be contacting the
City of Erlanger in an effort to share the cost of repairing the bridge, since
Erlanger residents that border the area use the bridge. Chief Butler stated
this issue has been talked to death and advised the city needs to begin
allocating funds in the next budget. Council Member Yeager inquired about help
from the Corp of Engineers. Chief Butler stated the Corp has denied the city
assistance on this matter. Council Member Behler commented that the city needs
to decide a plan of action. Council Member Franzen asked about applying for a
grant to help defray the cost of this project. Chief Butler stated it is
several months out, but feels the city needs to show an effort is being made to
deal with this liability. Mr. Deters stated that if the city decides to buyout
the property owners on Crowe Road, then perhaps an option would be to demolish
the bridge.
Mr. Brueggemann advised that it would be advisable to study the long-term
effect of the current erosion problem of the creek bank, as it could migrate
down stream. Chief Butler stated the city should pursue contacting the property
owners to see if there will be objections to the buyout and then pursue all
other options. Mr. Deters advised the city is obligated to maintain the street
and the buyout could be private or by eminent domain if there are those who
raise objections. Mayor Moriconi stated that he would first like to discuss the
bridge matter with the City of Erlanger to see if they would be agreeable to
sharing the expense, then contact the homeowners on Crowe Road.
Discussion Regarding a Street Repair Plan
Mr. Brueggemann stated he has been asked to give an opinion on whether the city
should require developers to install concrete streets or asphalt. He stated
that pavement sections, regardless of the material are required to carry a
given umber of vehicles over the lifespan of the street. He stated that
concrete is more rigid, but if the sub grade fails due to lack of proper
compacting or if water infiltrates this will cause weakness and it will not
hold up as long as it should. He advised that asphalt is not as rigid giving
way to potholes. He stated that the key to either material is protecting the
sub grade. Mr. Deters commented that the sub grade surface is designed to work
with the topcoat and often weakens over the time period before the topcoat is
put down. Council Member Behler asked if the city should be requiring the
developers to install an under drain. Mr. Brueggemann that could be a solution,
but there would still be side entry water conditions. Mr. Deters stated that
requiring under drains would probably have to be an amendment to the
subdivision regulations. Mr. Brueggemann concurred that it would be an
amendment to the subdivision regulations as well as costly for the developers
to install, probably about $20 per foot. He stated he felt there were other
options that could be considered. Mr. Deters stated that in order to amend the
subdivision regulation the city would have to obtain approval from KCPC. Mr.
Brueggemann stated that the solution to a successful pavement is the base. He
advised he would investigate all options and report back to council by the next
caucus meeting.
Discussion Regarding Rice Road Storm Water Drainage Problem
Mayor Moriconi stated Mr. Brueggemann has inspected the storm water drainage
condition on Rice Road that was brought to the city’s attention by Mrs. Case.
Council Member Yeager asked if Rice Road was a platted street. Mr. Brueggemann
stated that he has not checked at the courthouse, but that the road is
indicated on the GIS map as a platted street. Mr. Deters commented that it is a
public road.
Mr. Brueggemann reported that Rice Road has an asphalt pavement and is twenty
foot wide. He inspected the road and specifically Mrs. Case’s property at 522
Rice Road. He stated that storm water flows off the pavement and into her yard
which then flows to the existing creek. Mr. Brueggemann stated the storm water
has flowed this way for many years and the pavement in the areas of Mrs. Case‘s
property does not appear to have been changed. He state the erosion occurring
along her driveway is a result of the construction of the driveway and that it
acts to intercept the water that sheets off the pavement. He stated there is a
small area washed out with some minor erosion. He stated that the city could
place some gravel to rebuild the shoulder area and then the owner should
construct a small swale along the upper side of the driveway, as the channel is
not silted up. Mr. Brueggemann advised if the city does the shoulder work,
which is in the right of way, and the owner does some minor clean out to
develop a swale to access the culvert area this should solve the problem.
Council Member Bushong commented that Jeff Smith has a video that he shot
during a rain storm that is available for viewing that clearly indicates this
problem is minor. Mr. Brueggemann advised that if the city installs a curb then
the water would just be re-directed to another pointed location. He stated the
city is only responsible to improve the shoulder area. Mr. Deters concurred and
added that beyond the right of way, it is the property owner’s responsibility.
Cross Walks Repainted on Madison Pike
Council Member Dupps advised that he has requested Chief Butler to contact the
state highway department to see about having the cross walks on Madison Pike
re-striped. He stated they were covered when the street was blacktopped.
Executive Session
Council Member Bushong made a motion to enter into executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss pending litigation, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes.
Upon motion by Council Member Behler and second by Council Member Franzen the
meeting returned to regular session. Motion carried with all ayes.
Mayor Moriconi announced that no action was taken in executive session.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Yeager moved with second by
Council Member Behler to adjourn. The meeting adjourned at 9:50 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.
COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
December 1, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. In the absence of Reverend Eric Bryant
of Grace Community Church, Mr. Jim Kudera gave the invocation. Roll was called
and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim
Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City
Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated that LSI Imaging has been selected as the recipient
of the Business of the Month tribute for December, but since a representative
from the company was not present to receive the plaque, he would invite them to
the January meeting.
Approval of the Minutes of the November 3, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of November 3,
2003 regular council meeting. Council Member Dupps so moved, with a second from
Council Member Behler. Amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Approval of the November 17, 2003 Caucus Meeting Minutes
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the November
17, 2003 caucus meeting of council. Council Member Yeager moved, with a second
by Council Member Bushong. Amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Privileges of the Floor
5.   Mayor Moriconi announced that no one signed up to address Council.
Proposed Ordinance Providing for Sidewalk Waivers – 1st Reading
6.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance relating to the construction of sidewalks in the city and providing
for waivers with the use of a property lien. Mr. Deters read the proposed
ordinance. He explained that some property owners have approached the city
seeking waivers of the subdivision regulation that requires the construction of
a sidewalk prior to being given a certificate of occupancy. He stated that in
exceptional instances extreme sloping of the property would prompt the request
of a sidewalk waiver. Mr. Deters stated that this ordinance would ensure that
construction of the sidewalk would be done in the future if conditions of the
topography change so as to accommodate a sidewalk. He stated that a lien would
be placed on the property to cover the cost of the sidewalk construction in the
future.
7.   Council Member Yeager asked if an extension was included. Mr. Deters
advised that the city has granted a couple of sidewalk waivers recently; not
extensions.
Resolution No. 2003-R-26 – Glenhurst Park Improvements by the Developer
8.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2003-R-26 that notifies
the Glenhurst Subdivision’s developer of the city’s direction for the
appropriation of the donated funds for the development of the Glenhurst Park.
9.   Chief Butler stated he discussed with Council Member Yeager the park
improvement options available to the city. He stated they would like to
eliminate the request for a shelter and replace that with some playground
equipment. Council Member Yeager stated she also feels the city should be
specific on which utilities the city would like the developer to install. Chief
Butler stated the water and electric utilities could be provided at a lesser
cost to the developer than if the city had to do so in the future. He stated
the developer could handover the remainder ($10,000) of the allocated funds to
the city so that the city could purchase the playground equipment. He stated
that since the city is tax exempt, the play equipment could be purchased for
fewer dollars.
10.   The amendments were recorded and Council Member Yeager moved to approve
Resolution No. 2003-R-26, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll call was
answered unanimously and the motion carried 5-0.
Presentation of the 2002-03 Audit by Jim Sparrow of Rankin, Rankin and Company
11.    Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Jim Sparrow of Rankin, Rankin and Company
who was present to review the 2002/03 fiscal year audit report of the city’s
financial records.
12.   Mr. Sparrow distributed the presentation package of the audit report and
reviewed the highlights with council. He advised that the first page of the
report states that the general purpose financial statements are the
responsibility of the city management and the auditor’s responsibility is to
express an opinion on the financial statements based on the audit. He stated
that page two was the combined balance sheet of all the city funds – general,
special revenue, debt service and capital projects. He advised that the capital
projects included the Senior Center, Building Fund and Municipal Center.
13.   Mr. Sparrow advised the city had a little over $7,000,000 in cash and
investments during this period, which decreased somewhat due to the
expenditures on the Municipal Center. He stated the general fixed assets, such
as the Municipal Building, parks and vehicles and equipment amounted to a
little over $4,000,000. He stated the accounts payable saw an increase of
$237,000 largely due to the payables related to the Municipal Building.
14.   He advised that there was a $300,000 debt reduction on the bonds. He
stated that the Capital Projects funds were issued during the 2001/02 fiscal
year for the construction of the Municipal Center, but the proceeds from the
bonds had not begun to be spent until 2002/03 and that most will be expended by
June 30, 2004. Mr. Sparrow advised that total revenue in the general fund for
2002/03 was $3,718,079 with expenditures of $3,682,975; the excess was due to
vehicle lease proceeds. He stated that the special revenues, including
municipal road aid totaled $237,038.00 and expenditures of $397,732.00, but
that the city had carried a fund balance from the prior year so that the
balance broke even for 2002/03.
15.   Mr. Sparrow pointed out that the debt service fund proceeds exceeded the
amount of debt services fees for that year. He stated that the city’s revenues
are comprised of taxes at 54%, charges for services at 26%, intergovernmental
at 11%, licenses and permits at 5% and fines, interest and miscellaneous at 4%.
He advised that General Government expenditures increased by $110,000, police
by $187,00, sanitation by $95,000 and debt services payments increased by
$342,000. He stated that the debt service is a little high due to the Municipal
Center and Fowler Creek Sewer bonds. He indicated that while the police
department is the largest city expense that it is in line with what is
considered normal.
16.   Council Member Bushong asked about the expenses for the Memorial Park
Amphitheater and if city funds were added to the state and private donations.
Mr. Sparrow stated that the private and grant money was still being spent.
17.   Council Member Bushong inquired about the trash assessment revenue/
expenditures pass through. Mr. Sparrow indicated that the trash assessment
revenue was $516,997 and expenditures of $555,761. He stated that the revenue
shortfall might be due to delinquencies or a rate change sometime during the
fiscal year. Council Member Bushong suggested the city should coordinate the
trash contract to coincide with the fiscal year. Council Member Yeager
commented that the trash assessment revenue will never be equal with the
expenditures as there are delinquent tax bills. Finance Director, Teresa Hudson
commented that she is tracking suggested changes to the budget for future
amendments. Mr. Sparrow advised that the trash assessment revenue/expenditure
pass through should be shown in the budget and not just a bookkeeping entry.
18.   There being no further questions, Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Sparrow for
his presentation. Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to adopt the audit.
Council Member Bushong so moved with second by Council Member Yeager. Roll call
was unanimous and the motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Map Amendment Application No. 1643R
19.   Mayor Moriconi advised council that the map amendment for twenty acres on
the south side of Bristow Road is not in the city, therefore this item is not a
city matter and is deleted from the agenda.
Proposed Ordinance – Map Amendment Application No. 1648R – 5298 Madison Pike
from R-1C to NC – 1st Reading
20.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed

located at 5298 Madison Pike from R-1C to NC. Mr. Deters read the proposed

reading at the January 5, 2004 meeting.
21.   Council Member Dupps asked if this zone change was for only one parcel.

building on Madison Pike. Council Member Dupps suggested the city discuss the

to continue this type of revitalization. Mr. Deters commented that the

Deters stated that the last two zone changes have certainly changed the type of
uses for the properties, which would be cause for the Planning Commission to

this.
Contract with the Independence Senior Center Board of Directors for Use of the
Independence Senior/Community Center
22.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a lease agreement that has been

Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
23.   Chief Butler gave an update to council regarding the ongoing speeding
problem on Oby Drive. He stated that he stands by his initial report to council
and supports the continued use of radar and additional patrolling in the area.
He reiterated that installing a stop sign in the middle of Oby Drive does not
meet state guidelines for traffic control. He stated he recommends against that
as an enforcement measure to control speeders and stated he would prefer to
look at the cost to install speed humps.
24.   Mr. Chuck Kahrs, 25 Oby Drive, commented that he appreciates the efforts
of Chief Butler, but the current measures are not working. Chief Butler stated
he has tried to resolve this problem with radar enforcement and doesn’t know
what else to do. He advised council that they could override his recommendation
and go ahead and install a stop sign, which would satisfy Mr. Kahrs. Mr. Kahrs
stated this problem has been unresolved for six months and asked council to
install a sign, even temporarily. Council Member Yeager expressed concern that
this situation could be a liability for the city especially since the matter
has been brought to the city’s attention; it should be resolved to everyone’s
satisfaction. Council Member Franzen stated she was not sure that a stop sign
was the solution to this situation. She stated that many neighborhoods have
similar problems with speeders and was concerned that installing a stop sign in
the middle of the street that does not intersect would be setting a precedent.
Chief Butler stated that installing a stop sign is not even one of expense, but
that stop signs are not supposed to be used as speed enforcement. Mr. Deters
stated that passing a new law would not stop those already breaking the law.
Chief Butler stated that he supports the installation of speed humps but that
first he would insist that the city formulate the criteria for them to be used
citywide. He stated he would continue to run radar while studying the speed
hump solution.
25.   There was a discussion with regard to amending the current ordinance,
changing the specifics to regulate the entire city or drafting an ordinance
that would pertain to Oby Drive only. Mr. Deters advised that a stop sign on
Oby Drive would be easier than installing a speed hump. Council Member Yeager
urged the council to do something right away, even if it is a temporary stop
sign. Mr. Deters stated he could draft an ordinance to present at the next
meeting. Chief Butler stated that state law might prohibit this, although it is
a practice used in some areas. Council Member Behler commented if state law
prohibits the use of stop signs to control speeders, how would the Chief feel
about enforcing a city ordinance that is contrary to the state law. He stated
he would prefer not to use a stop sign in this situation and is continuing to
research the state statute. Council Member Franzen stated if the speeders are
not slowing down, how the city can expect they will observe a stop sign. She
stated if a sign is installed, that it should only be a temporary measure until
a more permanent resolution can be found. Chief Butler asked council to send
their comments regarding this matter to him by e-mail.
26.   Chief Butler stated the department held a successful food drive and if
anyone knows of needy families to call his office. He stated that last year
they were able to supply food to thirty families and hoped to increase that
number this year.
27.   He reported that the construction of a restroom facility in Memorial park
was progressing. Chief Butler also reported that the Christmas Walk and Tour
would be this Friday, December 5, 2003 from 7 – 9 p.m.
28.   Chief Butler reported that Ken Hicks of the Public Works Department
recently achieved the designation of road scholar.
MAYOR’S REPORT - Christian J. Moriconi
Accept Resignation of Council Member Jim Ellison
29.   Mayor Moriconi stated that Council Member Jim Ellison has submitted his
resignation from council. Council Member Dupps moved to accept Mr. Ellison’s
resignation, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Roll call was answered

Executive Order No. 2003-EO-12 – Appointing Additional Citation Officers

December 15, 2003
City of Independence, Ky.
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, December
15, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Mary Pat Behler, Donna Yeager,
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen and Eric Dupps answered roll call.
Privileges of the Floor
Sandra Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, stated she was there to address council once
again on behalf of Justice Lane. She stated Justice Lane was on the agenda
earlier but was removed from the last council meeting. She stated that the city
ordinance that is in place should be upheld. She stated she has retained an
attorney, Mr. Tim Theisen. She stated that Mr. Theisen has already spoken to
City Attorney, Jed Deters. She stated she would like the matter settled and get
a commitment from the city to maintain the road. She stated according to her
counsel she does have a strong case but does not want to sue the city if she
doesn’t have to. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated on behalf of the city he has
spoke to Mrs. Woolum’s attorney and advised council not to speak of this. He
stated he has been instructed by the city that the matter will not be on the
agenda until he and Mr. Theisen resolve the matter. Mrs. Woolum asked if she
would be notified when this matter comes back on the agenda. City Attorney, Jed
Deters stated her attorney would be notified when it comes back to council.
Mrs. Woolum asked if the city is going to maintain the road until the matter is
resolved.
City Attorney, Jed Deters stated he could not answer that at this time. Mrs.
Woolum asked how she gets council to answer that question. City Attorney, Jed
Deters stated she would have to speak to her attorney.
Mayor Moriconi asked City Attorney, Jed Deters if all communication will be
handled thru Mr. Theisen and himself. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated as the
city attorney he is advising Mayor and Council not to discuss the issue because
of the legal process.
Mrs. Woolum asked City Attorney, Jed Deters because he has a personal interest
in the matter, should the city retain other legal counsel. City Attorney, Jed
Deters stated not at this time. He stated he has a dower interest of 1/9th of
twenty-five acres. Mrs. Woolum stated the dower interest of 1/9th of the
twenty-five acres is the whole issue because you are saying the person that
passed away was the owner of the road in some way or another. City Attorney,
Jed Deters stated he was a co-owner of the road. Mrs. Woolum stated if City
Attorney, Jed Deters has a personal interest is it ethical to be representing
the city. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated that at this time he is not
conflicted and if it arises, he would advise the city to seek other counsel.
Mrs. Woolum asked if she should have her attorney proceed in a different
direction because she wants to settle this matter before 2010. City Attorney,
Jed Deters stated this has been going on since 1987 and he will contact Mr.
Theisen very soon.
Johnny Sue Bauer, 4920 Justice Lane, stated she is confused as to why council
cannot discuss the Justice Lane matter. She stated the city public works
department had maintained in the past but who will maintain it now that Mr.
Scherder has passed away. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated there is threatened
litigation. Mrs. Bauer stated she has not retained an attorney at this point
and felt Mr. Deters should be able to discuss the matter with her.
Mr. Jed Deters stated the issue of whether or not Justice Lane is a city street
and whether or not Justice Lane should be maintained by the city is a legal
issue and he is working on it. Mrs. Bauer stated she has a letter dated 1989
from the city attorney telling her Justice Lane had been accepted by the city
so she could get a loan from her bank. Mayor Moriconi asked the length of
Justice Lane. Ms. Bauer stated it is 6/10ths of a mile.
Executive Session
Council Member Dupps made a motion to enter into Executive Session per KRS
61.810 with a second by Council Member Franzen. The motion carried.
Council Member Yeager moved with a second by Council Member Franzen to resume
the Caucus Meeting. The motion carried.
City Attorney, Jed Deters advised he would be meeting with Mr. Theisen and will
have an answer for council by the first meeting of 2004. Ms. Bauer asked if she
needed to retain an attorney. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated he did not feel
she needed an attorney and could contact Mr. Theisen.
OLD BUSINESS
New Street Requirements
Chief Shawn Butler stated the City Engineer, CDS has supplied information
regarding pavement issues for new streets. He stated the city is looking at an
8% to 10% increase to developers. Chief Butler asked City Attorney, Jed Deters
if it would be legal for a city to supersede Area Planning Subdivision
Regulations. City Attorney, Jed Deters he felt it could be done but not without
the process of changing the text. Mayor Moriconi stated he will be attending
the Mayors Group Meeting and will get feedback from them and bring back to
council.
Oby Drive-Traffic Control Options
Chief Shawn Butler stated a proposal was obtained from Haines Contracting in
the amount of $5,375.00 to install a 12’ by 24’ speed reduction strips. He
stated stop signs could not be installed due to various reasons. He stated he
needs council to direct him on what direction they would like to pursue.
Council Member Franzen stated some of the residents from Freedom Trail told her
they do not want speed bumps on Oby Drive because they do not see a problem
with speeders. Council Member Behler stated she feels an ordinance needs to be
passed regarding when and where speed bumps could be constructed and in the
meantime alternate between speed bumps and radar until the January 2004 Caucus
Meeting.
Mr. Chuck Kahrs thanked Chief Shawn Butler for helping and working on this
matter with him.
Crowe Road Update
Chief Shawn Butler stated in regards to Crowe Road he was able to speak to
Erlanger but was advised they would have to get back to him at a later date.
NEW BUSINESS
Storm Sewer Issues
Chief Shawn Butler stated CDS has viewed the videotape of the Production Drive
Storm Sewer and opined the cost to be $54,000.00. The process will have to be
bid out for acceptance. He stated there are several streets throughout the city
that need storm sewer repairs. He stated grants have been applied for but it
might be spring 2004 before an answer is received.
Chief Shawn Butler also advised council that the new restrooms at Memorial Park
are now under roof and are to open in early spring.
Council Member Yeager stated if the city is going to apply for a grant for
sidewalks, it must be in by February 1, 2004. Chief Shawn Butler stated that
would fall under the T21 grant and the only thing council has to do is decide
what section of sidewalk they want to install first but must realize it is
cheaper to install new sidewalks than to replace old sidewalks due to the old
sidewalks having to be torn out first. Council Member Behler asked if the city
is liable if someone falls on the sidewalks. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated
there is no “black and white” answer to that. Council Member Brinker stated
they would get more sidewalks for the dollar where there is no sidewalk and
make the downtown area a priority. Mayor Moriconi stated there would be some
money in the budget for sidewalks next year whether the city gets grants or
not.
Mayor’s Comments
Mayor Moriconi stated the city has approximately $50,000.00 in delinquent tax
collection. He stated he has someone that would like to solely collect these
taxes. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated he found in his research that only the
county sheriff or county attorney’s office could collect delinquent taxes. He
stated a city is allowed to levy and collect taxes why can’t they collect
delinquent taxes. He stated he would have a definite opinion by the January 5th
meeting. Council Member Yeager asked if the city could print the names in the
city newsletter. City Attorney, Jed Deters stated it could be done or find out
who the first mortgage holder is on the property at the Kenton County
Courthouse and if there is an escrow account, they will pay the taxes.
Miscellaneous Discussion
Council Member Behler stated in reading the Kentucky League of Cities
newsletter she learned there will be three key legislative issues affecting
cities. She asked Chief Shawn Butler if he could explain the Community
Investment Act. Chief Shawn Butler stated the Community Investment Act allows a
city to pass an Ordinance, levying a 3% tax on all restaurants in the city. He
stated 75% of the money raised would then come back to the city for the Parks
and Recreation Program and 25% of that would go to Northern Kentucky Convention
and Tourism Center.
Council Member Behler congratulated Patricia Taney, City Clerk on applying for
and receiving grant funds for the archival of permanent city records.
Chief Shawn Butler stated council has received a new Work Order Form to be used
when the public is requesting public services.
Mayor Moriconi stated he and Chief Shawn Butler have met with Mr. Richard
Harrison of the water district regarding Webster Road. He stated the grant that
was applied for did not meet the criteria nor did any area in the city due to
financial income. He stated it is a matter that is between the water district
and the property owner.
Adjournment
Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to adjourn the meeting. Council Member
Dupps so moved, with a second by Council Member Yeager. The motion was passed
with all ayes and the meeting ended at 8:30 p.m.

DECEMBER 15, 2003
City of Independence, Ky
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in Special
Session on Monday, December 15, 2003 at 7:00 p.m. in the Independence Senior
Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Chris Moriconi presiding in the Chair.
The roll was called and the following council members registered present: Donna
Yeager, Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Eric Dupps and Jim
Bushong. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
2.   Mayor Moriconi stated the purpose of the special meeting was for
discussion and possible action on the following agenda items:
∙   Discussion and possible action relating to a lease agreement between the
Senior/Community Center and the Senior Center Board of Directors.
∙   Discussion and possible action relating to a proposed ordinance approving a
map amendment for property located at 5298 Madison Pike.
Lease Agreement with Senior Board of Directors
3.   Mayor Moriconi stated the lease is being presented as the Senior Board
plans to establish and operate a bingo as a means to raise funds for
programming at the Center.
4.   Council Member Behler stated in Item 5 of the lease agreement it states
the lessee agrees to maintain liability insurance. City Clerk, Patricia Taney
stated the city carries insurance on the building. City Attorney, Jed Deters
stated both parties are to carry insurance. Council Member Yeager stated the
Senior Board does not carry liability insurance. Mayor Moriconi stated the
lease agreement states the lessee or lessor must have liability insurance.
Mayor Moriconi stated this lease is a formality to help the Senior Board obtain
a license to have bingo at the Senior Center.
7.   Council Member Franzen moved with a second by Council Member Dupps to
accept the lease agreement with amendments. Roll call was answered unanimously;
motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance for Map Amendment located at 5298 Madison Pike
10.   Mayor Moriconi stated this could be a new first reading based on a change
Mr. James Bertram, the developer is requesting for a zone change from R-1C to
NC subject to three (3) conditions.
∙   The location of the proposed access point is subject to approval of a
variance being granted by the Independence Board of Adjustments.
∙   Landscaping is provided in accordance with Section 9.17 of the zoning
ordinance.
∙   Two twenty-four foot wide access easements are provided on site to allow
for future interconnection with the property to the south, front and to the
rear of the property.
11.   Mayor Moriconi stated Northern Kentucky Area Planning did approve the
change without a separate road coming out to the property. They wanted to
connect it with the one they just did and have it all come out to the same
driveway. He stated the developer does not want to have all of the front
property as concrete, but would like to have a separate entrance with green
space.
12.   Mr. Bertram stated they have purchased the adjoining property and will
construct another two-story office building. He stated they went before area
planning and asked for a zone change because it is currently zoned residential.
He stated one of the requirements was the driveway space. He stated according
to their regulations it has to be 100 feet from end of curb return to the curb
return. He stated there is 100 feet from center of drive to center of drive and
he is talking about 15 feet roughly. He stated one of the conditions for the
approval would have to be going before the Board of Adjustments to get the 100-
foot driveway condition waived. He stated they would like to keep the green
space with the new building.
13.   City Attorney, Jed Deters advised council they would essentially be
overriding Northern Kentucky Area Planning recommendation and they would need a
majority vote to pass. Council Member Bushong asked if the state has approved
this recommendation. Mr. Bertram stated the curb cut would have to be approved
by the state. Mayor Moriconi stated council would actually be eliminating
condition number one of the ordinance because the curb cut is already there.
14.   Council Member Franzen moved with second by Council Member Yeager to
adopt the ordinance eliminating #1 under Section 1. Roll call was answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0. City Attorney, Jed Deters read the first
reading of the ordinance with amendments.
15.   Mayor Moriconi stated a second reading would take place at the January 5,
2004 council meeting.
Adjournment
21.   There being no further business on the special meeting agenda, Mayor
Moriconi asked for a motion to adjourn. Council Member Dupps so moved, with a
second by Council Member Behler. Motion carried unanimously and the meeting
adjourned.

2004 Minutes
January 5, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
January 5, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant of Grace Community
Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps,
Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Mayor Moriconi welcomed new council member Tom Brinker and all those in
attendance.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi presented Mr. Rick Jordan, President of LSI Imaging, with a
plaque of recognition as the business of the month honoree and thanked him for
doing business in the city. Mr. Jordan stated that LSI has been it’s present
location since 1954 and that the company produces plastic products used by fast
food restaurants, as well as metal fabrication products for both exterior and
interior lighting for retailers. He stated the company has three shifts of
employees and while the economy saw a slow down in recent years the economy is
now turning around and business is picking up. Mr. Jordan stated he appreciated
the recognition and thanked Mayor Moriconi and council.
Approval of the Minutes of the December 1, 2003 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the December
1, 2003 regular council meeting. Council Member Bushong so moved, with a second
from Council Member Dupps. No amendments were noted. Roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the December 15, 2003 Special Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the December
15, 2003 special council meeting. Council Member Behler so moved, with a second
from Council Member Bushong. Amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the December 15, 2003 Caucus Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the December
15, 2003 caucus council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second
from Council Member Dupps. No amendments were noted. Roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
6.   Chuck Berling, 1835 Beacon Hill, Fort Wright Ky., developer of the
Shadybrook Subdivision, addressed council regarding a proposal to donate a
parcel of land that the city could develop as a community park that would
include hiking trails and a soccer field. He stated that three subdivisions,
Shadybrook, Clover Ridge and Sycamore Creek will be linked and that a community
park maintained by the city could be an alternative to establishing a
homeowners association. He stated he is presenting this offer to the city prior
to submitting this plan to the Kenton County Planning Commission for approval
so that he would know if this donation of green space for a park would be
accepted by the city. Mr. Berling presented to council an exhibit of the
property to be considered.
7.   Council Member Dupps asked the time frame for this project. Mr. Berling
stated the preliminary plan would be submitted to the purview Commission in a
couple of months, but that the area that would be deeded to the city for a park
would not be ready until the year 2005. Council Member Behler asked the length
of the hiking trails. Mr. Berling replied about one-half mile but that it would
tie into the sidewalk system.
8.   Council Member Yeager asked if Mr. Berling would consider installing a
restroom facility. Mr. Berling stated it is an option but cautioned council
that a restroom facility would require more maintenance expenses for the city
and that the city would need to determine if they want this additional cost. He
advised that portable facilities could be utilized during the busy times of
year and that an enclosure could be constructed for aesthetic purposes. Mr.
Deters commented that the city’s liability might increase with the addition of
a restroom facility.
9.   Council Member Brinker commented that the city presently has several parks
and not sufficient funds to adequately maintain or improve them. Council Member
Franzen asked Mr. Berling what would be done with the land if the city did not
want to accept it for maintenance. Mr. Berling advised it may go as unused
space. He stated that homeowners associations typically would not maintain
sports fields that would be used by non-subdivision residents.
10.   Council Member Dupps suggested that Parks/Recreation review this proposal
presented by Mr. Berling and make a recommendation to council. Mayor Moriconi
asked if any of the council members were opposed to the proposal. Council
Member Dupps stated the property that would be accepted is the best he has
seen, as usually developers offers of green space are hillside areas of the
subdivision. Mayor Moriconi advised that Parks/Recreation would consider the
matter and provide a recommendation for council to act on at the February 2,
2004 council meeting.
11.   Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, addressed council regarding her previous
request for the city to repair Justice Lane. She stated that her attorney has
called the city attorney several times to discuss this matter. She stated that
she feels the ordinance adopting Justice Lane for maintenance is valid and that
the city should provide the maintenance as the residents on the street are tax-
paying citizens. Mayor Moriconi advised Mrs. Woolum that discussion of Justice
Lane is not on the meeting agenda. Mrs. Woolum stated that Mr. Deters promised
he would have an answer regarding this street maintenance issue at this
meeting. Mr. Deters advised that he has spoken to Mrs. Woolum’s attorney
(’’Tim’ Theissen) once and that since this matter has become threatened
litigation against the city that it would not be discussed in an open forum.
12.   Johnny Sue Bauer, 4920 Justice Lane, also addressed council regarding the
maintenance issue of Justice Lane. She stated that she was told by the Mayor
and Mr. Deters they would have an answer for the Justice Lane residents at
tonight’s meeting. She stated she is concerned about snow removal during the
winter months and how the residents are supposed to deal with this. Mr. Deters
stated there has been a misunderstanding, as he did not convey there would be
resolution to this matter at tonight’s meeting. He reiterated that he has
spoken to Mrs. Woolum’s attorney and sent written correspondence on December
16, 2003. He advised no action has resulted and that he would not discuss this
matter in an open forum, considering one resident on Justice Lane has
threatened litigation. Ms. Bauer went on to say that she feels Mr. Deters has a
conflict of interest. Mr. Deters advised that his wife has an interest in
property on Justice Lane which is part of her deceased father’s estate. He
stated if he was operating in his wife’s interest he would want the city to
maintain the street, too; but he is not. Mayor Moriconi supported Mr. Deters
and assured Ms. Bauer that if there appears the resolution of this matter will
pose a conflict of interest that Mr. Deters will recuse himself. Council Member
Franzen requested an executive session as she had some questions. Council
Member Bushong requested the executive session take place at the end of the
regular meeting.
Ordinance No. 2004-O-02 - Approving a Map Amendment for 5298 Madison Pike -
(KCPC #1648R)
13.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2004-O-02 that would approve a map amendment for property located at 5298
Madison Pike from zone R-1C to NC. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2004-O-02.
14.   Council Member Dupps moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O-02, with second
by Council Member Bushong. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Ordinance No. 2004-O-01 - Providing Sidewalk Waivers with the Use of Liens
15.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2004-O-01 that would provide for sidewalk waivers with the use of a property
lien. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2004-O-01.
16.   Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O-01, with second
by Council Member Bushong. There was a brief discussion. Council Member Behler
asked if a resident would oppose the Building Inspector’s denial of a request
for a waiver, would the matter then come before the council. Mr. Deters stated
it would. Mr. Brinker expressed concern there could be a delay in the
construction and stated it may be necessary to clarify this for the property
owner. Council Member Franzen asked if a property owner would be able to obtain
a clear title with this lien attached. Mr. Deters stated the city would have
the authority to subordinate the lien for the transfer of property.
17.   Roll was called and the motion carried with five yes votes and one no
vote cast by Council Member Behler. Motion carried 5-1.
Renewal of City Attorney’s Contract
18.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for their approval the professional
services agreement with the city attorney. He stated this would renew Mr.
Deters agreement to provide the city with legal counsel.
19.   Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve the renewal of Mr. Deters
Agreement with the city, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Police Chief Report
20.   Mayor Moriconi announced that Chief Butler was absent due to illness and
that Assistant Chief Dave Nichols would give the report. Assistant Chief
Nichols advised that during the month of December 2003 the police department
responded to 1,692 calls for service, made 34 physical arrests and issued 133
state citations.
21.   He also reported that the annual Christmas Walk and Tour was well
attended and that the construction of the restroom facility in Memorial Park
will be complete by spring 2004.
22.   Assistant Chief Nichols advised that the street repairs for the Fleming
Drive will be put out to bid with the bids being submitted to the city by
March. He also wanted to remind the citizens that if two inches of snow falls
that all vehicles must be moved from the roadway for snow removal by the Public
Works Department.
City Attorney’s Report on the Issue of Delinquent Property Taxes
23.   Mr. Deters directed council’s attention to the memo he drafted regarding
his research of the collection process of delinquent property taxes. He stated
that the most efficient thing to do would be to amend the current ordinance
that would add a reasonable attorney fee to the cost of collection of the tax
bill. Or the city could initiate the process used by the county by creating a
delinquent certificate that could be sold at auction. Council Member Bushong
suggested the council leave it at the current $300 attorney collection fee. Mr.
Deters stated that the ordinance that established the $300 attorney collection
fee was adopted in 1978 and that fee would not begin to cover the cost of a
foreclosure suit today. He advised that it currently costs over $200 just for
filing and service fees. Council Member Bushong suggested that an outside
organization could collect the back taxes for a fee. Mr. Deters stated this is
not an option for the city unless the ordinance is amended; in addition any
outside service would need to be approved by the Department of Revenue. Council
Member Bushong stated he did not agree.
24.   Council Member Yeager asked what fees are associated with collecting the
delinquent taxes using the same process as the county. Mr. Deters stated he did
not know. Council Member Franzen commented that she, as well as most residents
pay their taxes, and feels others should pay too. Council Member Bushong stated
he is open to hiring an outside source to collect the back taxes. Council
Member Brinker concurred, but suggested we check with other cities that use
outside sources to collect this revenue. Council Member Yeager stated she would
also like information regarding the county’s process of collection.
Executive Order No. 2004-EO-01 - Establishing the Citizens Budget & Economic
Development Committee
25.   Mayor Moriconi presented Executive Order No. 2004-EO-01 establishing the
criteria for the Citizens Budget & Economic Development Committee and
appointing seven citizen members to the committee. Mayor Moriconi advised that
twenty candidates submitted a letter of interest to serve on this committee,
but he felt the make up of the committee should be a realistic number of
members.
26.   Council Member Yeager asked when the committee would meet. Mayor Moriconi
stated the committee would have the freedom and flexibility to decide of
meeting dates. He stated the function of the committee would be to make
recommendations and suggestions to the mayor and council regarding city
finances and the economic growth of the city. He stated the committee would
serve as an advisory panel with the committee chairman presenting the
committee’s recommendations for action at city caucus meetings.
27.   Council Member Dupps asked about the term limit of the committee. Mayor
Moriconi advised he would review the progression of the committee at six
months, but that ultimately he was looking at one year appointments. Mr. Deters
advised it was not necessary to indicate the terms of the committee members in
the executive order. Council Member Yeager commented that she felt bad that not
more than seven people were appointed to the committee as there were twenty
great candidates. Mayor Moriconi agreed but feels the seven citizens he has
selected is a good mix of the city’s residents and that is essential that the
group be a manageable size. He announced the seven citizens he has selected to
serve on this committee: Cindy Dobias, Darrel Herald, Jim Kudera, Michael
Little, Dave Millward, Tom Nicodemus and Larry Staverman. Mayor Moriconi read
Executive Order No. 2004-EO-01 and advised the committee would have its first
meeting in January. In closing, he thanked all who had volunteered to serve on
the committee.
Executive Order No. 2004-EO-02 - Appointing the City Clerk as the City’s ABC
Administrator
28.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council and read Executive Order No. 2004-EO-
02 appointing City Clerk, Patricia Taney as the city’s ABC Administrator.
Cancellation of the January 19, 2004 Caucus Meeting
29.   Mayor Moriconi advised he had a scheduling conflict and would like to
cancel the January 19, 2004 caucus meeting. Council Member Dupps made a motion
to cancel the January caucus meeting, seconded by Council Member Franzen. No
roll called; motion carried with all ayes.
Executive Session
30.   There being no further business, Mayor Moriconi requested an executive
session in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss pending litigation.
Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by Council Member Dupps. Motion
carried with all ayes.
31.   When the executive session ended, Council Member Yeager moved to
reconvene the regular session with second by Council Member Brinker. Motion
carried with all ayes.
32.   Mayor Moriconi announced there will be no action resulting from the
executive session.

Franzen the meeting was adjourned at 8:27 p.m.
