February 2, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
February 2, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council member Jim Bushong gave the
invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen
and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the Minutes of the January 5, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the January
5, 2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Bushong so moved, with a second
from Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted. Roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 6-0 to accept the minutes as presented.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
3.   Johnny Sue Bauer, 4920 Justice Lane, requested to reserve her comments
until the discussion is held on the Justice Lane matter on the agenda.
4.   Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane also requested permission to service her
comment until the discussion is held on the Justice Lane matter.
5.   Don Nienabor, 66 McCullum Road, addressed council regarding his concern
that the Citizens Finance and Economic Development Committee meetings would not
be open to the public. He stated that he has reviewed the K.R.S. and doesn’t
see where these committee meetings would be exempt from the open meetings law
6.   Mr. Nienabor also expressed concern that if a resident was registered to
vote as an independent that he would be unable to vote for the city council
candidates in the primary election to be held in May. Council Member Behler
commented that this once happened to her, but since the council race in
Independence is non-partisan and that any citizens registered as independents
should be able to vote in the primary election.
7.   Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Nienabor that the Citizen Budget & Economic
Development Committee is not requested to be open to the public. He stated that
the chairman of that committee will present the recommendations of the
committee to council at the monthly caucus meetings. Mayor Moriconi compared
this committee to the Garden Club and commented that the committee will have
the freedom to open the meetings to the public or not. Council Member Yeager
commented that she felt the meetings should be open to the public. Mayor
Moriconi disagreed and reiterated that he felt this would be the decision of
the committee.
OLD BUSINESS
Maintenance of Justice Lane
8.   Mayor Moriconi advised that Mr. Tim Theissen was present on behalf of
Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane. Mr. Jed Deters, City Attorney, advised Mr.
Theissen that he has advised council that the matter of Justice Lane
maintenance should not be discussed or debated in an open forum since it has
become threatened litigation. Mr. Theissen disagreed with Mr. Deters and stated
he felt it would be inappropriate not to discuss this matter in open session.
Mr. Deters reiterated that he has instructed the council not to discuss this.
9.   Mr. Theissen explained that according to records Justice Lane was
initially created as an easement to serve one house and currently there are
nine residents that access the road. He stated that it was not built to meet
the current subdivision standards. Mr. Theissen stated that Mrs. Woolum’s house
is the most recent development on the street and explained that in 1987 when
Mrs. Woolum was building her house she was having trouble conveying that lot
because there was no public road that would serve her property, therefore she
asked the city council to help her. He stated the city council then voted to
make Justice Lane a street and passed the ordinance on an emergency basis to
meet the deadline of Mrs. Woolum’s loan closing.
10.   Mr. Theissen stated Justice Lane is recognized as a public street and
that the city has, on a couple of occasions, provided some maintenance. He
stated that a street sign identifies it and there is no guard at the entrance.
Mr. Theissen stated that when a plat was conveyed a strip was dedicated
indicating additional action that it is recognized as a city street. He
commented that Mr. Bobby Scherder, another property owner on Justice Lane had
made it difficult for the city’s Public Works Department employees to come onto
the property to provide maintenance.
11.   He advised that Mrs. Woolum has requested the city since October/November
2003 to provide maintenance and since then council has begun discussions to
repeal Ordinance No. 1-11-87. Mr. Theissen insisted that Ordinance No. 1-11-87
is a valid ordinance and while this may be a complicated issue as to whether or
not it met the requirements to be declared an emergency, the fact that the
street has been publicly used for a period of time would be reason that the
city can assume that it is a publicly dedicated street. In addition, Mr.
Theissen argued there has been no legal challenge over the years. He stated
there is a procedure to follow for a street to be closed to the public, such as
a paper street or an undeveloped street.
12.   Mr. Theissen objected to Mr. Deters proposed procedure to repeal
Ordinance No. 1-11-87 saying that it was an inappropriate course of action to
repeal an ordinance that adopted a public street. He stated there is a separate
process for doing that.
13.   Mr. Theissen asserted that the residents on Justice Lane are taxpayers
that are asking that a service be provided for their tax dollar. He stated that
council should not take this as a threat of litigation, moreover a plea; but
when on to say that this issue is so important to Mrs. Woolum that she feels
duty bound to ask the court system to judge what she feels is inappropriate
action by the city. He stated that repealing Ordinance No. 1-11-87 could
adversely devalue Mrs. Woolum’s property and hinder subdividing her land. He
stated that other residents of Justice Lane would be party to the lawsuit
against the city including Bobby Scherder’s estate, which would then cause Mr.
Deters to have a conflict of interest, placing the city in the situation of
hiring another attorney to litigate this matter. Mr. Theissen suggested that
council seek independent legal advice, other than Mr. Deters before getting
into a lawsuit.
14.   Council Member Brinker stated that he does not feel that silence by the
council members is conveying the proper message to the residents. He stated he
has remained quiet about this matter but he wanted the residents to know that
he is trying to do what is right for the city. He stated he wanted the
residents to know that council is in a difficult situation and is very
concerned and he will support a speedy resolution to this matter. Council
Members Franzen and Yeager concurred with Council Member Brinker.
15.   Johnny Sue Bauer, 4920 Justice Lane, corrected Mr. Theissen in that her
parents built a house on Justice Lane in 1997 making it the most recent
development, which was approved by the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission. Mr. Deters advised that property has adequate frontage on
Independence Road and is not dependent on Justice Lane. Ms. Bauer questioned
the urgency to repeal Ordinance No. 1-11-87 now. She urged council to consider
the facts and make a thorough evaluation before taking any drastic action.
Council Member Franzen advised Ms. Bauer there would be no vote taken on the
first reading of the proposed ordinance to repeal Ordinance No. 1-11-87.
16.   Mrs. Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, made an appeal to council to postpone the
first reading of the proposed ordinance until council had adequate time to
review the information provided by Mr. Theissen. She stated she would like to
assist council in clearly understanding the issue at hand and how valuable
Ordinance No. 1-11-87 is to the residents on Justice Lane. She stated that the
threat of litigation would disappear if the city would uphold Ordinance No. 1-
11-87 and agree to maintain Justice Lane.
Executive Session
17.   Council Member Yeager moved to go into an Executive Session in accordance
with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss threatened litigation, seconded by Council
Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes.
18.   Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with al ayes.
Continuation of the Discussion of the Maintenance of Justice Lane
19.   Mr. Deters advised that it was determined during the executive session
that since there is the appearance that he may have a conflict of interest,
given that his wife is heir to property located on Justice Lane, the city
council will consult with separate counsel. He stated he has recommended
attorney Ed Lanter to the council and will ask him to be present at the
February caucus meeting, but will advise the matter should be discussed in an
Executive Session at that meeting.
20.   Mayor Moriconi advised that the caucus meeting will be held on the fourth
Monday, February 23, 2004 due to President’s Day on the third Monday which is
the normal meeting day for the caucus meeting.
21.   Council Member Bushong questioned Mr. Theissen that he too may have a
conflict of interest in this matter since he was on the Planning Commission in
1987 when Mrs. Woolum’s plat was approved. Mr. Theissen advised that he did not
join the Planning Commission until February of 1990 and stated that he did not
feel this was an issue since it did not affect the Planning Commission. Council
Member Bushong suggested that as this issue progresses it might become a
conflict. Mr. Theissen reiterated that he did not feel this would become a
conflicted issue for him. Mr. Deters suggested that Mrs. Woolum could
ultimately subdivide her property for future development purposes. Mr. Theissen
stated that if that should happen, then he would withdraw from the case. Mrs.
Woolum stated she wants Justice Lane to be a city maintained street as no one
can propose future development of the land unless it is a city street. Mr.
Deters stated that the street is only forty feet wide, which is not sufficient
for future development. Mr. Theissen countered that forty feet is sufficient
width for it to be a public street and that if future development was approved
the street could be constructed to fifty feet wide which would bring it up to
regulations to meet current building codes. He stated that fifty feet could
then provide on-street parking.
22.   Council Member Franzen stated that Ordinance 1-11-87 states the
maintenance purposes, as the street presently exists. She asked what kind of
maintenance Mrs. Woolum was expecting from the city. Mrs. Woolum stated the
street is constructed of gravel, but the city should look further into
providing practical maintenance. Ms. Bauer commented that she is not expecting
the city to provide security lighting by installing lampposts, but would like
the street to be smooth and level. Mr. Theissen stated the 1987 ordinance meant
the residents didn’t have to improve the condition of the street to get the
city to take over the maintenance, but at present the street desperately needs
gravel. Ms. Bauer stated that she expects the city to do more than just install
gravel as the gravel just runs into the gully.
23.   Mayor Moriconi asked the length of the road. Mrs. Woolum stated Justice
Lane is 7/10 of a mile long.
24.   Mr. Theissen stated that they appreciated being given the opportunity to
be heard by council with their concerns. Mayor Moriconi advised there would be
a first reading of the proposed ordinance to repeal Ordinance No. 1-11-87, but
there would not be a vote until the ordinance was presented for a second
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Repealing Ordinance No. 1-11-87 Regarding the Maintenance
of Justice Lane – 1st Reading
25.   Upon motion by Council Member Behler and second by Council Member Dupps
there was a first reading of a proposed ordinance that would repeal Ordinance
No. 1-11-87 that accepted Justice Lane as a city maintained street for the
purposes of meeting a deadline for a real estate closing. City Attorney, Jed
Deters read the proposed ordinance in its entirety.
NEW BUSINESS
Discussion Regarding Park Shelter Rentals
26.   Council Member Yeager introduced a suggestion regarding the park shelter
rental fees. She stated that a rental fee for the shelter at Memorial Park has
not been established and that the rental fee for the shelters at Sterling
Staggs Park needs to be increased. She proposed adopting a fee schedule similar
to that of the Kenton County Parks. She stated they have a rain or shine rental
fee of $35.00 excluding a refund with rental fee for larger special events at
$100.00. Council Member Franzen suggested that the elimination of a deposit fee
could cut down on paper work. Mr. Deters advised the fee schedule should be
adopted by ordinance. Chief Butler stated there would not be a deposit held for
clean up, just a flat fee for the rental of the shelter and the city would
clean up after each event. He stated if the city eliminates the deposit fee
there will be no incentive by the resident to clean up the shelter area.
Council Member Bushong asked if Mr. Deters would draft an ordinance. Mr. Deters
reiterated the fees should be established by ordinance and he would review the
way they are currently set up.
27.   Council Member Bushong made a motion to establish a shelter rental fee of
$35.00 per shelter at Sterling Staggs park and a $50.00 shelter fee for
Memorial Park. Mr. Deters stated he would draft an ordinance for council’s
review at the caucus meeting. Council Member Yeager stated she would like the
rental fee for the larger events, such as weddings to be higher than $50.00.
Mayor Moriconi suggested the rental contracts be reviewed by Mr. Deters. Roll
call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Discussion Regarding Development of a Park in the Shadybrook Subdivision
28.   Mayor Moriconi reported that Council Member Yeager and Chief Butler met
with the developer of the Shadybrook Subdivision regarding a proposal to
develop a park area complete with ball fields and turn it over to the city.
29.   Chief Butler stated that they met with Mr. Berling regarding the
development and he has done some preliminary operational cost estimates, which
the city would incur, should council decide to accept this park area for city
ownership and maintenance. He advised his estimate includes the expense to mow,
provide electricity, insurance coverage, etc. and would be around $8,000 to
$10,000 annually. He stated that Mr. Berling proposes the development of a ball
field, soccer field, walking trails and parking lot.
30.   Council Member Bushong asked about a restroom facility for a park of this
size. Chief Butler stated that Mr. Berling would attend the next caucus meeting
to discuss development details, such as a restroom facility, and irrigation for
the soccer field. Council Member Behler expressed concern that a restroom
facility and irrigation of the soccer field would just increase the annual
operational expenses. Chief Butler stated that he felt a restroom would be an
essential facility for a park with ball fields. Council Member Brinker asked
that Chief Butler provide a written cost estimate for the operation of this
proposed park before the caucus meeting. Chief Butler stated this park would
not have playground equipment, just ball fields, walking trail and parking lot.
Mayor Moriconi advised that this matter would be discussed further at the
caucus meeting. Chief Butler stated there is no rush to act on this matter.
Discussion Regarding HB 413
31.   Chief Butler reported that the Committee Safety Act introduced HB 413
last week. He advised that if this bill were passed it would provide a
significant amount of revenue for the city. He stated that if this bill were
passed that the city would receive $20 on all criminal convictions, which he
estimates could amount to $180,000 annually for the city, helping to offset
current expenses. He advised that the city currently receives no portion of
revenue from the state for writing state citations while the city bears all the
associated expenses. He encouraged everyone to contact the state
representatives and urge them to support this bill. He stated that council may
also want to take an official position by adopting a Resolution in support of
this bill. Council Member Behler advised it was introduced in the House of
Representatives and will go before the Senate next.
Update on Bids to be Let
32.   Chief Butler advised that the bids for the repairs on Fleming Drive have
been let out, and that the bids for the computers and audio-visual equipment
for the Municipal Center will be released soon.
Update on Collection of Delinquent Taxes
33.   Mayor Moriconi directed council’s attention to the report in the council
packets outlining the procedures for collecting delinquent property taxes in
other local cities as well as the county. Council Member Yeager stated she
favors the collection procedure used by the county. Council Member Behler asked
if the county’s procedure is mandated by state statute. Mr. Deters stated that
it is but felt the city could probably establish a similar system for the
collection of delinquent property taxes. He stated he would check into it and
report back at the next caucus meeting.

Discussion Regarding the Possible Sale of the Park and Ride Municipal Parking
Lot
36.   Mayor Moriconi reported that he has been approached by a person
interested in purchasing the Park and Ride lot for the purpose of constructing
an office building. Council Member Yeager stated that she objected to selling
this property as it will be the only land the city will own in the downtown
area after the move to the new Municipal Center and the sale of the current
Administration Building. She stated the city worked hard to get this parking
lot for the TANK bus riders. Mayor Moriconi stated that if council decides they
would like to declare the lot as surplus property, then Chief Butler would meet
with TANK to discuss another location for a park and ride lot. Mr. Deters
suggested that council first have the property appraised before declaring it
surplus property. He advised after it is declared surplus property the city
would take bids for the sale. Council Member Yeager expressed concern regarding
relocation of the park and ride. Mayor Moriconi stated he has had preliminary
discussions with the management of the Towne Center who seemed receptive to the
idea of relocating the park and ride lot at the Towne Center. Council Member
Yeager stated that the Towne Center is not located in the downtown area of
Independence and expressed concern for the downtown businesses as well as the
courthouse, whose patrons use the park and ride lot. Council Member Brinker
concurred with Council Member Yeager and suggested getting information from
TANK about rider ship to determine the use of the lot. He stated he would not
want to relocate the lot until an alternate plan was in place. Council Member
Bushong asked where TANK would stop. Mayor Moriconi advised it would run down
Route 17 to Declaration. Chief Butler advised the current park and ride lot is
at capacity and the Towne Center would be able to offer more parking spaces.
Council Member Bushong asked if the city would have to lease space for the park
and ride lot from the Towne Center. Mayor Moriconi stated that he has spoken to
Mr. Charlie Deters about relocating the park and ride lot at the Towne Center
and Mr. Deters did not take issue with the arrangement as it has the potential
of providing more traffic to the businesses at the Center. Council Member
Yeager reiterated that the downtown area needs more parking for the business in
that area of the city. Mayor Moriconi stated that the person interested in
developing the land has stated that there should be no problem for patrons of
Pasquales to park there after regular business hours. Council Member Yeager
also expressed concern about having a location for the lighting of the
Christmas tree for the annual Christmas Walk & Tour if the city does not own
land in the downtown area. Council Member Bushong commented that selling the
park and ride lot would be potential income for the city and agreed that the
city should have the property appraised.
37.   Council Member Bushong made a motion to have the Park and Ride lot
appraised, seconded by Council Member Behler. Council Member Yeager advised
that when the city approached TANK with the plan to construct a park and ride
lot for bus riders in Independence TANK had wanted the city to enter into a 20-
year lease and she was able to talk them out of a lease providing they supply a
bus shelter and signage. Roll call was answered with three yeas by Council
Members Bushong, Behler and Brinker and three nays by Council Members Yeager,
Dupps and Franzen. Mayor Moriconi broke the tie by casting a yea vote. Motion
carried 4-3 in favor.
Condemnation of Property Located at 5220 Belle Drive
38.   Council Member Behler asked for an update on the procedures the city
would be using to condemn blighted property, more specifically 5220 Belle
Drive. Mr. Deters explained the process, and advised council they should take
into consideration, when condemning a property, the possibility that city money
expended to demolish blighted private property might not be recouped. Mayor
Moriconi asked Chief Butler if the Public Works employees could take down this
property if the city condemns it. Chief Butler stated he spoke to Jeff Smith
who advises they could probably handle this. Mr. Deters advised that the city
still has a process they must follow before sending city employees onto private
property and removing the blighted structure. Council Member Behler requested
the city begin the necessary process to condemn this property and remove the
rundown building.
39.   Council Member Franzen made a motion to begin the process necessary to
condemn and raze the house located at 5220 Belle Drive. No roll call; motion
carried with all ayes.

40.   There being no further business, motion was made by Council Member

City of Independence, Ky.
February 23, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
23, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Christian J. Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Mary Pat Behler, Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager answered roll
call. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Tom & Sharon Creamer, 10736 Chinkapin Circle, addressed council with their
request to purchase city owned land that abuts their property on Chinkapin
Circle in the Glenhurst Subdivision. They proposed the city sell them a small
triangular shaped parcel that is part of the Glenhurst Park. Mr. Creamer stated
that the area is basically unusable to the city and he is having his property
surveyed as groundwork before he installs a fence and stated he was willing to
pay to have the city owned section surveyed as well if the city would agree to
sell him the piece. He invited the city to inspect the area.
Mayor Moriconi advised the Creamer’s that the land was donated to the city for
recreational green space and that the city would need to research the deed to
see if there were any restrictions. Mr. Deters concurred and added that the
city could not selectively sell the property, and explained the city is
required to advertise for sealed bids so that anyone that may also be
interested would have the same opportunity. Mayor Moriconi stated the city
would review the matter over the next couple of weeks and then contact the
Creamer’s with the findings.
Betty Eichelberger, 6258 Taylor Mill Road, addressed council with a concern she
has with the property located at 6290 Taylor Mill Road. She stated that the
owner had come before the city recently with a proposal to construct self-
storage units on the property. She advised that the land is being cleared and
asked if the city had approved this type of development. Mr. Deters stated
there is no proposal pending before the city council and if the property owner
submits a development plan to the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission,
the Commission would then notify the city.
JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, conveyed that there was a toll free number
available to the citizens of the state wherein they could leave comments for
the representatives regarding pending legislation. She encouraged everyone to
use this toll free number to convey support for HB 413 relating to a law
enforcement fee, which would be revenue for the city. Chief Butler advised that
there have been some changes to HB 413, which will decrease the initial amount
of revenue he reported to council, which was approximately $180,000. He stated
the revenue expected now will be around $60,000, which is more base court
revenue than the city is currently receiving.
Mrs. Cobble asked Mayor Moriconi if he would be scheduling a Budget Summit
soon. Mayor Moriconi stated that he might not hold a Budget Summit this year.
He explained that he would be working with the Police Chief and the City Clerk
to establish the preliminary budget figures. In addition, he stated that he did
not feel a Budget Summit would be needed due to the establishment of the
Citizens Budget and Economic Development Committee who would be submitting
their budget recommendations to the council.
NEW BUSINESS
Presentation of a Future Senior Retirement Village by Kudera Development LLC
Jerry Dusing, legal counsel for Jim Kudera introduced himself and P.J. Hannon,
the architect of the development. Mr. Dusing stated that Mr. Kudera is planning
to develop a retirement village on the rear section of his property at the end
of McMillan Road. He stated that the development would be on nine acres, eight
of which are within the city limits and one acre, which is presently in
unincorporated county. He stated that they would request annexation for the one
acre coupled with a zone change request for the entire acreage. Mr. Dusing
advised that this development is being planned around the future road
improvements to State Route 17, which will provide direct access to the
retirement village and that the project would not proceed until such time the
road improvements move forward. He stated the village would consist of six
multifamily buildings, each providing thirteen units and three to four single
story structures with attached garages and additional parking. He stated that
two years of research has gone into the planning of this development, which
will be independent living restricted to those aged fifty-five and up. Mr.
Dusing advised that this development is consistent with the current countywide
Comprehensive Plan and is a type of housing that is needed in Independence. He
stated there would be quite a demand for independent living units with the
“baby boomers” approaching retirement age. Mr. Dusing assured council that this
development would not become government assisted housing, as it will be a “for
profit” privately owned community. He stated the community will be a unique
concept to Northern Kentucky and while it will be independent living, it will
include community activities and provide some basic services.
Mr. Deters advised Mr. Dusing that it would be inappropriate for the council
members to voice their comments before the recommendation from the Kenton
County Planning Commission formally comes before them, as they are the final
arbiters of a proposed zone change. Mr. Dusing replied that they were making
this presentation to the council as a courtesy before they proceed with
submitting the application of a development plan to the Planning Commission.
Council Member Franzen asked if the city would have to decide on the annexation
request first. Mr. Dusing advised that they would request annexation of the one
acre at the same time they request a zone change. Mr. Deters explained that it
would be an annexation by consent. Council Member Behler asked the number of
total units. Mr. Dusing replied 92 units would equal 9.4 units per net acres.
Council Member Yeager commented that she has heard many requests for this type
of housing from the senior members that frequent the Independence Senior
Center.
Williams Woods Subdivision Green Space
Bob Schroeder, representative for Williams Woods subdivision development
addressed council with a proposal to give the city a four-acre parcel of land
located in the Williams Woods Subdivision. Council Member Behler reported that
she inspected the area and voiced concerns with a small retention pond that she
noticed. Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Schroeder what would be done with the parcel
if the city did not want to accept it. Mr. Schroeder advised they would
increase the size of the individual lots. Council Member Franzen stated she was
not in favor of accepting this property, considered it a liability and felt the
land should be used to increase the size of the lots. Council Member Bushong
stated he was not in favor of accepting the land. Council Member Yeager
commented that she appreciated their offer, but since the property would abut
property owners who would assume the property was theirs, that the city should
probably not accept it. Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Schroeder that the council
comments were not in favor of accepting this land, but thanked him for the
offer.
Discussion Regarding Shadybrook Park
Mr. Chuck Berling addressed council and submitted a site plan for their
inspection of the proposed park in the Shadybrook Subdivision. Mr. Berling
stated the park would be for active recreation, having a soccer field and a
baseball field, walking trail and fifty-nine parking spaces. He advised the
park area sits on a separate plateau, with the parking lot separate from the
subdivision. He reported that they would install a water line tap so the city
would have the capability of adding a restroom facility in the future. Chief
Butler stated that he has estimated that it will cost the city $10,000 per year
to operate this park, mainly the expense of utilities and mowing the land.
Council Member Behler asked which road would access the park. Mr. Berling
stated it could be accessed from three directions, which would include Senour
Road, Fowler Creek Road and Route 16. Mayor Moriconi stated that this park
would tie three residential developments together. Mr. Berling reported that
the land would be graded this year with utility lines being installed and then
sow seed and lay straw the following year. He advised that sometime in the year
2005 the property would be ready to deed over to the city. Council Member Dupps
asked if the Clover Ridge subdivision ever developed the ball fields that were
planned for the community. Council Member Yeager stated the fields were never
built. Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Berling if they would construct a
restroom facility. He stated they would only supply the rough service lines.
Chief Butler stated he has discussed with Mr. Berling the irrigation of the
ball fields and went on to introduce the idea of establishing fees of the
sports leagues similar to those of the Kenton County Parks and Recreation
Department to help the city offset the expenses of maintaining the fields. He
urged the city to install a restroom facility in this park due to the large
number of people that would be using this park. Council Member Behler stated
that she would be more favorable of accepting this proposed park if she knew it
would generate the operational fees for the upkeep. Council Member Franzen
stated that the Northern Kentucky Little League and the Independence Soccer
Club may consider contributing to the operational fees. Chief Butler stated
these organizations want exclusive use for their contribution. Council Member
Yeager commented that other cities have similar type of ‘pay to play’ programs.
Council Member Behler asked Chief Butler if he had law enforcement concerns
with the location of the proposed park. Chief Butler stated that it is in a
remote area and suggested that security lighting be installed, especially in
the parking area. Council Member Franzen stated that she did not think that
fifty-nine parking spaces would be adequate for both fields when games are
being played simultaneously. Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Berling if they could
enlarge the parking lot. Mr. Berling stated it was a possibility and would look
into it.
Mr. Berling stated that they felt that the city would benefit from a park in
this area but if the city did not want the land for a proposed park, that they
would form a homeowners association. Council Member Brinker stated that he
would like the city to explore charging the teams a usage fee. Mr. Berling
reminded council that they would not be taking on the expense of this park
until late 2005. Council Member Yeager commented that the park probably
wouldn’t be ready for ball games until early 2006. Council Member Dupps
wondered if the Citizens Budget Committee should look into this matter. Mayor
Moriconi felt that was not necessary. Council Member Franzen stated that adding
a restroom facility should be seriously addressed, as it will be an enticement
to the ball teams.
Mr. Berling stated that this development has already received approval from the
Planning Commission, so council’s decision will not hold up the construction.
Council Member Bushong commented that he feels that restrooms are a more
important amenity than a shelter. Council Member Franzen suggested contacting
the Northern Kentucky sports teams to discuss agreements for exclusive use of
the fields. She suggested that Independence should propose user fees that would
be competitive with fees charged by other cities.
Council Member Dupps asked Chief Butler to provide council with a breakdown of
the projected expenses that will be associated with this park. Chief Butler
read from his list. Council Member Behler suggested he would need to increase
his estimate by 6% considering the year 2006 cost factor.
Discussion Regarding the Maintenance of Justice Lane
Mr. Deters advised council that he has invited Ed Lanter, a colleague of his,
who has agreed to represent the city in the matter of Justice Lane. He
suggested that council enter into an executive session to discuss the matter
with Mr. Lanter.
Executive Session
At 8:02 p.m. Council Member Dupps moved to enter into an executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) for the purpose of discussing pending
litigation. The motion was seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried
with all ayes.
At 8:21 p.m. Council Member Brinker made a motion to reconvene the regular
session of the meeting; seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with
all ayes.
Resume Discussion Regarding the Maintenance of Justice Lane
Mayor Moriconi announced that Ed Lanter would provide legal counsel for the
city in the matter of the maintenance of Justice Lane. Mr. Lanter explained to
the members of the audience that reside on Justice Lane that he has been
contracted to represent the city regarding the validity of Ordinance No. 1-11-
87. He stated he would review the ordinance and personally meet with the
Justice Lane property owners and/or their legal representative in an effort to
resolve this matter in an amicable manner. He advised council that he would
report back in a few weeks.
Traffic Speed Hump Program
Mayor Moriconi thanked Council Member Bushong and Chief Butler for preparing a
thorough report to establish a traffic speed hump program defining speed bumps,
lumps and humps. He suggested that council might want to adopt this program by
ordinance. Council Member Yeager asked if this program was going to help the
residents on Oby Drive. Chief Butler stated they would need to go through the
process as outlined in the program and suggested the city could install
temporary white striping with the word ‘slow’ on Oby Drive.
Mr. Deters concurred with Mayor Moriconi and advised that this program should
be adopted by ordinance. Council Member Brinker suggested the city make this
document available to the citizens. Chief Butler suggested posting it on the
website as this will be the guideline the city will use when residents request
this type of traffic control devise. Mr. Deters advised he could draft an
ordinance for a first reading at the March 1, 2004 meeting next week.
Bids Received for the Fleming Drive Repairs
Mayor Moriconi advised the city receive sealed bids on February 6, 2004 for the
Fleming Drive repairs. He directed council to the correspondence from City
Engineer, Mark Brueggemann of CDS Engineers who is recommending the city award
the contract to the low bidder, Hendy, Inc. in the amount of $160,984.00. Mayor
Moriconi stated the bid received is lower than the amount that was anticipated.
Council Member Behler asked if the city engineer feels comfortable that Hendy
would provide satisfactory work. Mayor Moriconi replied yes. He stated that
formal award of this contract would be on the agenda for next Monday’s regular
meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Relating to the Code Enforcement Board & Amending
Ordinance No. 1999-O-02
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would amend the
current ordinance relating to the Code Enforcement Board. He stated this would
be presented for a first reading at the March 1st regular meeting of council.
Mr. Deters advised council that this amendment was the result of a meeting with
the Zoning Administrator, Building Inspector and City Clerk. He stated the
Zoning Administrator has been having some difficulty in getting enforcement
assistance from the county attorney’s office as the current ordinance lacks the
necessary enforcement language, which this amendment will provide.
Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Park Shelter Rental Fees & Amending Ordinance
No. 1998-O-05
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would amend the
current ordinance relating to the reservation of the park shelters and the
associated fees. Attached to the ordinance are the application forms for the
shelter permits. Council Member Yeager commented the fee schedule needed to be
revised, as the maintenance of the parks is a lot of work and the city needed
to discontinue the practice of a refundable $15.00 fee. Mayor Moriconi asked if
the applicant’s social security number should be included on the form. Mr.
Deters stated that name and address should be adequate. There was a brief
discussion and it was decided to add a line for the applicant to provide his/
her driver’s license number. Mayor Moriconi stated this ordinance would be
presented for a first reading at the March 1st regular meeting.
Report on Establishing a Procedure for the Collection of Delinquent Taxes
Mr. Deters reported that in order for the city to have the county collect it’s
delinquent taxes the county would have to be in charge of the billing and
collection of the city’s taxes, similar to the Independence Fire District,
Kenton County Library, etc. He stated this might reduce delinquent bills, as
the county does not accept partial payments. Mr. Deters also stated that
another option would be to change the language of the current ordinance that
would provide for a ‘reasonable fee’ for city attorney collection. He stated
the current ordinance only provides a flat fee of $300.00, which by today’s
standards does not begin to cover the cost of foreclosure, filing fees and
other associated attorney expenses. Mayor Moriconi asked what the county fee
was. Mr. Deters stated the county charges 4%. Council Member Brinker asked if
the county should collect the city property taxes. Mr. Deters suggested the
city might want to take the most economical route. Chief Butler commented that
the county might only be able to recoup their costs for the service. Council
Member Franzen suggested the city amend the ordinance in the meantime.
Discussion Regarding the Renewal of the Contract with Rumpke for Trash
Collection
Mayor Moriconi reported to council that the city’s two-year contract with
Rumpke was due to expire on June 30, 2004. He stated that the term of the
contract provides the option for four two-year extension periods upon mutual
agreement of both parties. He advised the rates for the next two-year extension
would increase by .42 cents per month making that an annual increase of $5.04
each year for the next two years for a total annual assessment of $105.84.
Council Member Yeager stated that while she has no complaints with Rumpke’s
service, she is concerned that the trash assessment is on the tax bill and if a
bill is delinquent so is the trash assessment. Council Member Franzen asked if
the city could provide a list of delinquent property tax residents to Rumpke so
they could discontinue service to that property.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that they could choose to stay with Rumpke and
extend the contract period with Extension #1 for a term from July 1, 2004
through June 30, 2006 or they could decide to bid out the service. Council
Member Bushong suggested not bidding this out again. Council Member Franzen
asked if CSI submitted a lower bid two years ago. Mayor Moriconi replied that
CSI did submit a lower bid but that they were proposing a mechanical arm type
of truck, which was cheaper to operate, and the city had concerns that there
might be some difficulty for the senior residents to use the trash containers
that were required by CSI for this type of collection. Council Member Dupps
concurred and added that the mechanical arm trucks was not a viable option for
Independence terrain. Council Member Brinker suggested that if the city did re-
bid this service that the bids could come in higher than Extension #1. Council
Member Franzen agreed. Mayor Moriconi concluded that it appeared that the
general consensus of council was to continue service with Rumpke by opting to
extend the contract for another two-year period. He stated this matter would be
presented at the March 1st meeting when this decision would be ratified.
Discussion Regarding the Simon Kenton High School Project Prom Donation
Mayor Moriconi announced that Simon Kenton High School has requested a donation
for the after prom event again this year. He stated that council would
officially act on this at the regular business meeting on March 1st. He stated
there was some question last year as to whether the city could make these types
of donations. However the donation was made last year in the amount of $500 as
the event was considered a public safety related concern as it is dedicated to
providing a drug and alcohol free environment for the teenagers of the city.
Chief Butler suggested that in place of making a cash donation to the school
that instead the police could provide in-kind services in the form of police
security for the event. He stated the school customarily provides police
security, but this year the city could provide that in place of the cash
donation. Council Member Yeager asked how many officers the city would provide.
Chief Butler stated one or two officers would be on hand for the event. Mayor
Moriconi stated the city would go with Chief Butler’s suggestion.
Business Recognition for the Month of March
Mayor Moriconi suggested that new Council Member Tom Brinker should select a
business to recognize at the March 1, 2004 council meeting. Council Member
Brinker stated he would like to recognize the new Subway that has opened in the
Beechgrove Plaza.
Discussion Regarding Contracting with a Realtor to Sell the City Building
Mayor Moriconi advised council that since the City Building has not sold that
it may be time to contract with a real estate agency. Council Member Yeager
suggested working with a local agency, Bonnie Garner Century 21. Mayor Moriconi
stated that the local Century 21 office did not have a commercial realtor; but
had one in their Florence office. Council Member Bushong commented the city
could contract with the Florence office and the Independence office could
handle the sale. Mayor Moriconi stated he would contact the Century 21 office
and negotiate a commission percentage.
Report on the Park & Ride lot Appraisal
Mayor Moriconi directed council’s attention to the appraisal report for the
Park and Ride lot. Council Member Yeager expressed concern about selling this
property. She stated that a new Municipal center was not constructed on this
property due to the sewer easement that runs on the property. Mayor Moriconi
stated he believes the lot was too small and would not be suitable for a large
building. Council Member Bushong asked what the next step would be. Mr. Deters
stated that the lot would have to be declared as surplus property. Council
Member Bushong asked if the appraisal amount would be the minimum sale price.
Mr. Deters advised that the city should go through the bid process, but that it
could be set as the minimum price. Mr. Deters advised the city may want to
verify whether or not the sewer line runs perpendicular on the property. He
stated if the sewer line is a simple lateral line it could be relocated. Mayor
Moriconi stated the city would contact One Eleven Engineers.
Discussion Regarding ALS – TransCare
Chief Butler reported that TransCare is seeking funding from the county and
cities. This is a matter the Mayor’s Group has been reviewing and that the City
of Covington has decided they will pull out and will provide their own
ambulatory life support to their residents. He stated that TransCare has
indicated they need $55,000 - $83,000 per year to continue operation and has
asked that this revenue be raised by implementing a tax and would like a
referendum placed on the general election ballot. Chief Butler advised that
providing this service has never been a city matter as the Independence Fire
District handles this service. Mr. Deters stated there is a legislative bill
(HB 406) pending regarding this and it is possible that the Fire District may
establish an ambulance district. Mayor Moriconi stated that if a tax is passed
for this service it would be collected by the county and be a line item on the
county property tax bill.
Discussion Regarding Changing the Caucus Meeting Format
Council Member Brinker suggested changing the caucus meeting format that would
allow the audience members to have more participation other than the privileges
of the floor as an item on the agenda. Mayor Moriconi commented that there may
be a downside to this for the citizens that want to speak at the top of the
meeting so that they can leave before the end of the meeting. Council Member
Bushong asked if this meeting could be televised. Mayor Moriconi advised the
Senior Center building is not equipped for a live broadcast. Council Member
Franzen stated it could be taped and replayed at a later date.
Discussion Regarding Production Drive
Council Member Behler asked if the Sanitation District share part of the
expense of repairing the sinkhole on Production Drive. She stated she is
concerned the city should not make the necessary repairs on Production Drive
until the sinkhole is repaired. Mayor Moriconi advised the repairs the city
will be making to Production Drive are not affected by the section containing
the sinkhole.
Personnel Policy Update
Council Member Yeager asked about the progress on the update of the employee
Personnel Manual. Chief Butler stated that a draft would soon be available.
Crowe Road Update
Council Member Behler asked for an update on the Crowe Road matter. Chief
Butler advised that he attempted to get some grant money to help fund repairs
as well as emergency funds, but to no avail. He stated he had also been working
with the county, but that the county has had some recent changes in public
works personnel and a new county judge executive has recently been appointed to
fill the unexpired term of Judge-Executive Murgatroyd. Chief Butler stated he
also approached the City of Erlanger to get some assistance, but the city has
been non-responsive.
Adjournment
There being no further business, motion was made by Council Member Franzen and
seconded by Council Member Brinker to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 9:20 p.m.

March 1, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
March 1, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with
Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant of the Grace
Community Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric
Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K.
Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi presented Mr. Bob Wade of Bob & Lorraine’s Subway with a
plaque of recognition as the business of the month honoree and expressed the
city’s appreciation for recently locating his business in the city. Mr. Wade
stated that they opened their Subway in the Beechgrove Plaza on October 29,
2003 and that business has been good.
Approval of the Minutes of the February 2, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February
2, 2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Bushong so moved, with a second
from Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted. Roll call was answered
unanimously and the motion carried 6-0 to accept the minutes as presented.
Approval of the Minutes of the February 23, 2004 Caucus Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February
23, 2004 caucus council meeting. Council Member Yeager so moved, with a second
from Council Member Bushong. One amendment was noted by Council Member Yeager.
Roll call was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0 to accept the
minutes as amended.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Brett Ross, 720 Independence Station Road, representative of the South
Kenton Peewee Football organization, addressed council with their concerns
about the possibility that the city may implement team usage fees. He advised
council that the South Kenton Peewee football is a non-profit organization with
current expenses around $22,000 - $24,000 per year and that prior to using the
field at Memorial Park, they held practices at Simon Kenton High School. He
stated that they have invested several thousand dollars in the maintenance of
the field at Memorial Park, as well as man-hours, in order to keep the field in
good, safe playing condition for the children. He stated they do not have the
additional funds to pay the city for exclusive user privileges. Mr. Ross stated
the only recreation available to the children in the city is the ball fields.
He stated their organization is having a difficult time to cover the cost of
re-seeding the field each year and that imposing a user fee would be an added
hardship.
6.   Council Member Franzen advised Mr. Ross that council did not discuss user
fees for the football teams using the Memorial Park field. She advised that the
discussion at the caucus meeting centered on the two fields being proposed by
the developer of the Shadybrook subdivision; a soccer field and a baseball
field. She stated that council discussed offering exclusive rights as a means
to support the maintenance of an additional city park. She concurred that
sports activities for our children can get expensive, but the city was
discussing a ‘pay to play’ format as a way to offset the expenses associated
with the maintenance of the parks.
7.   Council Member Dupps commented that the football organization donated
$6,000 to refurbish the field. Council Member Yeager advised that the city
funded $14,000 of the overall expense to get this field in good playing
condition.
8.   Mayor Moriconi assured Mr. Ross that the city would give notice to the
football organization if the city should decide to enact a user fee. He advised
that the idea of a ‘pay and play’ program was just in the discussion stage.
9.   J. David Rabe, 529 Independence Station Road requested that he be able to
reserve his comments for later in the meeting when the subject of the Park and
Ride parking lot is discussed. Mayor Moriconi granted this request.
10.   Kevin O-Hara, 2092 Patriot Way, addressed council regarding his concerns
that the city may impose user fees for the use of the football field in
Memorial Park. He stated that he heard there was a deadline. Council Member
Yeager reiterated that this possibility is still in the discussion stage. She
advised that the discussion was prompted because a developer wants to give the
city green space that will be developed as a park with soccer and baseball
fields. She stated the city could not impose user fees on just soccer and
baseball teams.
11.   Rita King, 5966 Taylor Mill Road, President of the Independence Soccer
Club stated that they are also a non-profit organization. She advised council
that they are in desperate need of practice and playing fields, as they have
lost two fields this year. She stated they would be willing to lease the city
fields if they could have input into the construction and maintenance of the
fields. She stated that the field at Sterling Staggs Park will be unplayable
for the spring season as it has been destroyed during the winter months when it
was used by people playing flag football when the land was saturated. She
stated she has spoken to Nita Brake about the possibility of using the Memorial
Park field for their spring season. They are also looking into the possibility
of playing at Summit View Schools. She stated they do not have a huge fund to
work with, but they are willing to help the city with the field maintenance.
Council Member Yeager asked what the city could do to help the Independence
Soccer Club. Ms. King stated they would like to have an agreement with the city
to have priority for use of the new field. She stated that due to the
unplayable condition of the field at Staggs Park, they would like the use of an
alternate field, such as the field at Memorial Park for the March 27 – June 8th
spring season. Council Member Yeager stated the football season would not begin
until July. The representatives in the audience from the Peewee football
organization expressed concern that the soccer players would destroy the field
that they have worked so hard to maintain. Mayor Moriconi stated the city is
working on the condition of the fields and stated the soccer teams would just
use the Memorial Park field during the football off-season. Council Member
Franzen reiterated that football practice begins in July. The representatives
from the Peewee football were adamant that the field should not be used by the
soccer teams as they were concerned the field might be damaged during games
that are played during inclement weather.
12.   Council Member Brinker suggested that a representative from each
organization attend the March 15th caucus meeting so this matter could be
discussed further and hopefully a resolution to everyone’s satisfaction. Mayor
Moriconi concurred and advised this matter would be placed on the March 15th
caucus agenda.
Park & Ride Lot – Discussion to Declare it as Surplus Property and Authorize
Taking Bids for the Sale of the Property
13.   Mayor Moriconi advised that with the receipt of the recent appraisal
report that council had requested on the Park & Ride lot, the next step would
be to declare the property as surplus and authorize taking bids for the sale of
the property. He stated that council needed to determine what direction they
wanted to take and called for a motion. With no motion placed on the floor,
Mayor Moriconi stated that three members had voted in favor of getting the
property appraised.
14.   Council Member Brinker stated he feels that the appraisal came in under
market. He stated he would like more research, i.e. who currently uses this
parking lot and how they would feel about the park and ride lot being relocated
to the Towne Center. Mayor Moriconi stated that a solution has been initiated
for the relocation, which will provide more parking spaces at the Towne Center.
He stated the current property has been appraised as a buildable lot. Council
Member Brinker asked if the city received bids for the sale of the property how
would the proceeds be spent. Mayor Moriconi advised the use of the proceeds
would be decided by council. He suggested that council authorize taking bids
and depending on the amount of the bids received, council could then decide how
to proceed, as they would always have the option to reject all the bids. He
stated a final decision would take place at the April or May meeting. Council
Member Yeager stated the Park & Ride lot is part of the downtown area and was
reluctant to sell this property, especially since the City Building will be
relocating south of the downtown area.
15.   Mayor Moriconi expressed his disappointment and stated this was a waste
of the money spent for an appraisal.
16.   J. David Rabe, 529 Independence Station Road, addressed council with
comments that he was in favor of keeping the Park & Ride lot in its present
location. He stated that with gasoline prices escalating, TANK may begin to see
an increase in ridership. He stated that the city has already invested in this
property and feels it would be a waste to sell this property with the only
benefit being payroll tax if a business would build on the site. He feels it
would be a long time for the city to recoup the loss. In closing, Mr. Rabe
commented it would be more positive to add another park and ride location at
the Towne Center.
17.   Council Member Behler commented that she visited some of the downtown
businesses to ask if their customers used the park and ride lot and they
responded that their customers do not use the lot.
18.   There being no further discussion nor a motion/second to declare the park
and ride lot as surplus property the matter was closed.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment (1658R) Shadybrook Subdivision –
1st Reading
19.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that would approve a map amendment (application number 1658R) for
property changing an approximate 65-acre area located approximately 600 feet
south of Senour Road between Clover Ridge Drive and Fowler Creek from R-1C and
R-1C (RCD) to R-1C (PUD) with two conditions.
20.   Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi advised this would
be presented for a second reading and enactment at the April 5th council
meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Relating to the Code Enforcement Board & Amending
Ordinance No. 1999-O-02 – 1st Reading
21.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that amends the language of Ordinance No. 1999-O-02 that established
the Code Enforcement Board. The amendments will correct content errors and
provide a new section that would assist the Zoning Administrator with code
enforcement. City Attorney, Jed Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Park Shelter Rental Fees and Amending
Ordinance No. 1998-O-05 – 1st Reading
22.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that amends Ordinance No. 1998-O-05 relating to the rental fees and
deposit rates for the park shelters. The proposed ordinance will eliminate
refundable deposit fees and increase the rental fees for the park shelters. Mr.
Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Establishing a Traffic Speed Hump Program – 1st Reading
23.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that will create a new section of traffic laws dealing with speed
humps, their classifications and the requirements for determining their
locations, installation, maintenance, removal, necessity and funding. Mr.
Deters read the proposed ordinance.
24.   Mayor Moriconi stated that the four ordinances would be presented at the
April 5, 2004 business meeting for a second reading and enactment.
Discussion regarding the Renewal of the Rumpke Waste Hauling Contract
25.   Mayor Moriconi advised that the current contract with Rumpke for
residential trash pick up would expire on June 30, 2004. He stated that the
contract provides for two-year extensions through June 30, 2012. He advised
that Extension #1 would increase the resident’s annual trash assessment by
$5.04 for each of the next two years, taking the annual assessment from $100.80
to $105.84. Mayor Moriconi advised that opting to extend the current contract
with Rumpke would save the city time and money that would be expended going
through the bidding process.
26.   Council Member Behler made a motion to select Extension #1 of the current
contract with Rumpke for residential trash collection, seconded by Council
Member Franzen. Council Member Bushong asked what the increase percentage
amounted to. Council Member Dupps advised that on page two of the current
contract it states that the two-year extensions calculate a 5% increase for
each extension. Shawn Butler commented that it amounts to 2.5% for each year.
Council Member Yeager asked if the city would still collect this trash
assessment from the residents. The City Clerk commented that the rate would be
higher if Rumpke would be asked to direct bill the residents. Council Member
Yeager expressed concern that since the assessment is added to the annual
property tax bill, if the bill is delinquent then the city ends up paying for
the trash pick up for those residents. Mayor Moriconi advised the current
contract extension rate is based on the city collecting the trash assessment
from the residents.
27.   There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 to select Extension #1 of the Rumpke contract
for trash pick up for the period beginning on July1, 2004 and ending on June
30, 2006.
Award Bid for Fleming Drive Repairs
28.   Mayor Moriconi advised that the city is in receipt of bids for the street
repair of Fleming Drive. Chief Butler stated that the city engineer, CDS
Associates, is recommending the city award the bid to Hendy, Inc., who
submitted a low bid of $160,984.00
29.   Council Member Yeager made a motion to award the Fleming Drive repairs
bid to Hendy Inc. as the lowest and best bid; seconded by Council Member
Brinker. Council Member Bushong asked if this company has been used by the city
in the past. Chief Butler stated that Hendy has not performed work in
Independence, but that CDS is familiar with their work and is confident they
will do a good job. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-
0.
Discussion Regarding the Development of a City Park in the Shadybrook
Subdivision
30.   Chief Butler reported that Mr. Berling has not completed the development
plan of this proposed city park yet, but hopes to make a presentation to
council at the April meeting. Council Member Bushong stated that he would like
to go on record as requesting that a restroom facility be an essential part of
the development of this park. Council Member Yeager asked if Mr. Berling was
able to provide more parking spaces as requested. Council Member Behler asked
that field irrigation be considered also. Chief Butler advised that Mr. Berling
was trying to consider all the amenities that council would like to see
developed in this park. Mayor Moriconi advised that Mr. Berling would be at the
next caucus meeting to discuss the development plan in detail.
Adjournment
31.   Mayor Moriconi advised since he had nothing to report and there was no
need for an executive session he called for a motion to adjourn. Motion to
adjourn was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 7:40 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.
March 15, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 15,
2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker,
Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager answered roll call.
Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Diana Walker, 6446 Shawnee Court, Independence, Kentucky addressed council
regarding her concerns about a request by Mr. Marty Neltner for a text
amendment that might permit him to construct a self-storage facility behind the
Cherokee Shopping Center. She stated that the subject property owned by Mr.
Neltner is bordered on three sides by property zoned residential. She stated
that she is concerned they will loose their privacy and that this type of
structure will devalue their property. She stated that the subject property is
less than three acres and wondered if there was a minimum acreage requirement
for his proposed development. Ms. Walker also stated that the security lighting
for this kind of structure would annoy the residents.
Mayor Moriconi explained that the proposed ordinance to approve this text
amendment had a first reading in November 2003 and that since that time the
matter has been postponed. Ms. Walker commented that the Planning Commission
actually did not approve a text amendment that would permit self-storage units
in that zone. Council Member Franzen advised that the text amendment that was
approved would allow parking garages, which Mr. Neltner did not want. Mr.
Deters advised that since Mr. Neltner owns the adjacent property, it can be
considered with the smaller parcel for a “total site area” as one development.
Ken Lancaster, 733 Cox Road, Independence, Kentucky asked if any of the council
members had inspected the area that Mr. Neltner would like to develop. Some of
the council members indicated that they had inspected the area. Mr. Lancaster
reiterated that the parcel is small, a little over two acres and expressed his
opinion that this type of facility does not belong in this mostly residential
location. He also expressed concern regarding ‘unknown’ contents in the rental
units. In closing, Mr. Lancaster reminded council that the Planning Commission
voted to disapprove a storage unit facility in this zone.
Mayor Moriconi commented that there is no council support to approve Mr.
Neltner’s request for a storage unit facility in this location and that the
matter was a dead issue. Council Member Franzen stated that the current zoning
allows Mr. Neltner thirty-four other development uses for this property and
that she does not support a plan for a storage unit facility. Council Members
Yeager and Behler concurred. Council Member Yeager stated that the Planning
Commission had good reason to deny this request and feels the city should not
override their decision. Council Member Dupps concurred and added that Mr.
Neltner has other less obtrusive options available to him for development of
this property.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters if the council should have the second reading
of the proposed ordinance that would approve the text amendment as recommended
by the Planning Commission. Mr. Deters replied yes. Council Member Dupps
informed the residents that Mr. Neltner’s property is zoned commercial and he
can put other types of commercial structures on that parcel.
Mayor Moriconi commented that Mr. Neltner was not in attendance nor was there a
representative for him in attendance. He went on to say that he did not think
Mr. Neltner was interested in developing the land other than for the self-
storage units.
Council Member Brinker explained to the residents that a development plan is
only submitted to the city for approval when the property owner is requesting a
zone change to enable him to use the property for a purpose other than that of
the current zone. He stated that if the property owner wants to develop the
land for a purpose under the current zone then it would only need approval from
the Planning Commission and would therefore not come before the city council
for approval.
Mr. John Huffman, 4290 Richardson Road, Independence, Kentucky commented that
he has been required to comply with the zoning laws and feels the city should
follow the recommendation of the Planning Commission.
Mayor Moriconi advised the second reading of the text amendment as recommended
by the Planning Commission would be on the April 5, 2004 council meeting
agenda.
Update on the Proposed City Park in the Shadybrook Subdivision
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Chuck Berling, developer of the Shadybrook
Subdivision. He stated that the last time Mr. Berling appeared before council
with the plan for the development of a park in the subdivision, the council had
requested he add more parking spaces to the parking lot. Mr. Berling stated
that he was able to accomplish that by replacing a portion of the street
pavement to increase the size of the parking lot to accommodate 74 spaces. He
stated that this amount of spaces should be adequate but that overflow parking
for about twenty cars could be at the far end of the Clover Meadow subdivision.
In addition, stated that ball games should be staggered to prevent parking
problems.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that this park plan would be a turnkey project
wherein it would be completely developed by the time it is deeded over to the
city. Mr. Berling advised that if the city would like the city engineer or an
architect to review the development plan for the park then they would build it
according to that approved plan. Council Member Brinker stated that he would
like principal representatives from the ball leagues to have some input into
the design of the fields. Mayor Moriconi agreed that the city engineer could
meet with the league reps. Mr. John Huffman stated that he runs Huffman
Sportscape and he could offer suggestions about the kind of materials that
should be mixed with the soil for the ball fields.
Mr. Berling advised that a shelter house and restroom facility would be
included in this development plan. Mayor Moriconi confirmed that Mr. Berling
was agreeing to construct a restroom facility. Mr. Berling said that, yes, he
would work that out with the city. Council Member Behler asked if irrigation
for the fields would be part of the plan. Mr. Berling advised that irrigation
lines would not be expensive to install but would be costly for the city to
maintain as a separate water meter would be necessary. Mr. Berling also
conveyed that there would be security lights in the parking lot as well as
streetlights along the corridor to the lot. An audience member suggested the
installation of boundary fences around the fields. Mr. Berling did not commit
to providing for fencing in the development plan. Mayor Moriconi recommended a
coordinated effort be made to obtain everyone’s input on the development plan.
Mr. Berling commented he would need to finalize the plan as soon as possible
prior to grading the land. He stated they would complete a rough grading this
year to determine how well it will hold water.
Walkable Communities Workshop –Larisa Keith of the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission
Mayor Moriconi introduced Larisa Keith of the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission. Ms. Keith advised council that Independence has been selected to
participate in the Walkable Communities Initiative which is an effort to make
the city and region more pedestrian friendly. She stated the program is being
funded by the National Center for Bicycling and Walking, OKI Regional Council
of Governments and NKAPC. Ms. Keith invited the city officials and other
interested citizens to participate in a 4-hour “Walkable Community” workshop to
be held on April 20, 2004 at the Independence Fire Station located at 1980
Delaware Crossing, from 1:00 – 5:30 p.m. She advised that the workshop would
identify the needs of the community, highlighting land use, transportation
overview, assessment of the area as well as learning about pedestrian design
and safety. During the workshop solutions will be proposed to address problem
areas.
Council Member Bushong asked if this program has been done in other
communities. Ms. Keith replied no, but that the cities of Erlanger and Florence
are planning to. Council Member Bushong commented that he plans to attend and
expressed concern that many areas of the city do not have sidewalks. Ms. Keith
advised the participants in the workshop would be discussing those areas and
how to create a walkable community. She stated that the workshop would also
discuss funding solutions and how to obtain grants.
Council Member Dupps asked who they hoped would attend this workshop. Ms. Keith
replied that the workshop schedule was not set by NKAPC, but that it is geared
toward policymakers and because it is a public meeting the public is invited to
attend as well. She recommended viewing the website to learn more about this
program.
Council Member Behler asked how Independence was chosen to participate in this
program. Ms. Keith stated that the city was recommended by NKAPC. Mayor
Moriconi cautioned the workshop attendees to be careful walking along Madison
Pike as there are some areas that do not have sidewalks. He also commented that
he would be very interested in learning more about grant money that might be
available for the construction of sidewalks.
Report on Establishing a Procedure for the Collection of Delinquent Property
Taxes
Mayor Moriconi requested a report from the City Attorney and City Clerk on the
procedure for the collection of delinquent taxes. City Clerk, Patricia Taney
reported that delinquent property owners will receive two delinquent notices
from the Clerk’s office, with a third notice from the City Attorney. If the
taxes are not paid by May following the tax year, the attorney will begin
foreclosure proceedings. She stated that many delinquent bills have been paid
since the attorney’s letter was mailed last week. Ms. Taney stated she met with
representatives of the Kenton County Sheriff’s office earlier today to discuss
the request by council to obtain a proposal from the county to bill and collect
city taxes. She advised the county stated it would take a week or so to submit
a proposal. Ms. Taney also stated that Mr. Deters has submitted a proposed
ordinance that will amend Ordinance No. 3-5-79 establishing city attorney fees
for the lien enforcement. She stated this would be presented for a first
reading at the April 5, 2004 meeting, with a second reading at the May meeting.
After the ordinance is enacted, then the city attorney will be able to proceed
with foreclosure action on the delinquent properties.
City Attorney Report on the Lawsuit – Howard v City
City Attorney, Jed Deters advised council that Judge Steven Jaeger has ruled in
favor of the city in the Howard v City lawsuit. He stated that Captain Bill
Howard, who was dismissed from the Independence Police Department, will now
have thirty days to file an appeal.
Discussion Regarding the Memorial Park Ball Field
Council Member Franzen stated that she heard that the football field at
Memorial Park has been lined for soccer play. She stated that she thought this
was going to be discussed before deciding whether or not the soccer teams would
be able to play on this field. Mayor Moriconi stated that soccer starts in two
weeks and will be finished in May allowing plenty of time (7 weeks) to prepare
the field for football play. Council Member Dupps stated the field would need
to be repaired and seeded to prepare it for the football season and if a
drought hits, the field may not be ready when football practice begins in July.
Mayor Moriconi advised that the Independence Soccer Club was donating $1,000
for the maintenance of each field. Council Member Franzen commented that the
football league has already spent several thousand dollars maintaining the
football field at Memorial Park. Rita King, President of Independence Soccer
stated that she has discussed the use of the field with Dave Martin of the
football league and Nita Brake and understood that everything had been cleared
for the soccer teams to use the field. Mr. Martin of the football league was
concerned that the soccer teams would play on the field during rain. Mayor
Moriconi advised that Nita Brake, the city’s Recreation Director would be the
person to determine if the ground was too wet to play on the field, which
should ease the concerns of the football league. Council Member Brinker
suggested the leagues providing the city with their game schedules. Mayor
Moriconi advised that the city would work out a solution that everyone could
abide by. Council Member Brinker suggested the council get a report on the
condition of the fields from Ms. Brake. Mayor Moriconi agreed that with the
soccer season quickly approaching that the schedules need to be finalized.
Council Member Bushong commented that he feels there should be more of an
agreement between the two organizations and not the city. Rita King reiterated
that she had spoken to both ’’Nita Brake’ and the President of the football
organization who both stated they didn’t mind if the soccer teams played on
that field. Mr. Thomas stated that he did not have a problem with it as long as
it was not a permanent arrangement. Mayor Moriconi stated that they should work
a schedule out with ’’Nita Brake’ then she can report back to council.
Report on HB 413
Council Member Franzen advised that HB 413 passed the house and has moved to
the Appropriations Committee in the Senate. She stated that she has spoken to
Senator Dick Roeding who has advised that the bill has become a political game
between the democrats and republicans. Council Member Franzen encouraged the
residents to contact their legislatures and urge them to vote for this bill.
She stated there is a possibility that the bill will die, but there seems to be
consensus in the senate to pass it, but first it has to make it out of the
Appropriations Committee.
Discussion Regarding City Maintenance of County Roads
Council Member Behler expressed some concern regarding information she has
learned that the city will now be responsible for maintaining county roads
within the city limits and wondered how that would affect the city budget. Mr.
Deters advised that this is not new, but clarified that it only relates to
county roads that are annexed into the city, as then the county street would
become a city street.
Discussion of Sidewalk Installation at the Brentwood Apartments along Delaware
Crossing
Council Member Brinker stated he received a call stating that a section of
sidewalk along Delaware Crossing in front of the Brentwood Apartment was
missing. Mayor Moriconi advised the new owner has been notified that the
sidewalks are a requirement and they have promised to get them installed.
Adjournment
There being no further discussion, Council Member Yeager moved to adjourn with
second by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting
adjourned at 8:09 p.m.
