April 5, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
April 5, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with
Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Charles Steger gave the
invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen
and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member Eric Dupps had chosen
Valvoline Instant Oil Change as the recipient of the Business of the Month. He
presented owner, Dan Childress with a plaque of recognition. Mr. Childress
thanked Mr. Dupps and his store manager, as well as the Independence community.
Approval of the Minutes of the March 1, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the March 1,
2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second
from Council Member Yeager. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the March 15, 2004 Caucus Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the March 15,
2004 caucus council meeting. Council Member Behler so moved, with second from
Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 to accept the minutes as presented.
Guest Speaker – Diane Brumback of ––––Kentucky–– Women In Action
5.   Mayor Moriconi introduced Diane Brumback, President of the Kentucky Women
in Action organization. Ms. Brumback explained that she has been visiting local
governments to promote awareness about this new political organization that
will focus on issues important to women and work to see that there are equal
representation of men and women on local boards and commissions. She stated
that the group would be endorsing candidates for office as well as collecting
resumes of qualified individuals who represent the group’s mission of promoting
equality for women. She advised the group would also provide assistance in
filling vacant political positions throughout the state. Ms. Brumback stated
that ’’’’Kentucky’’ Women In Action currently have four hundred members
throughout the state. She encouraged everyone to visit their website at http://
kywomeninaction.homestead.com to learn more about the organization.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
6.   William Edmondson, 4931 Oliver Road, Independence addressed council to
voice his objection to the new vehicle sticker tax. He was upset that he
received a letter from the city stating the unpaid tax was subject to a $50.00
fine when he did not pay the tax. He stated that the courthouse clerks did not
inform him of the fine when he chose not to pay the tax at the time he renewed
his vehicle registration. He stated that the vehicle he was registering had
originally belonged to his sister who recently died. Mr. Edmondson went on to
say that he felt this was an unfair tax, especially since he lived on a county
maintained road and mainly traveled on county or state maintained roads. He
stated that he felt the only service he received from the city was the trash
collection.
7.   Mr. Deters commented that this type of scenario is very likely since the
owner of record as of January 1 of each taxing year would be the name listed on
the vehicle registration card. Mayor Moriconi asked the City Clerk to contact
Mr. Edmondson to discuss a resolution to the matter.
8.   JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, Independence addressed council regarding
her view on the possible sale of the city’s Park and Ride municipal parking lot
on Madison Pike. She stated that she had hoped there would be more discussion
by council on this matter at the last meeting, since the city had the lot
appraised with the intent of possibly selling it. She stated that she believes
the city should consider selling the property if they are offered a fair and
good price. Mrs. Cobble commended Mayor Moriconi for working with Mr. Charlie
Deters to relocate the park and ride lot to the Towne Center, which she feels,
would be a better and safer location for bus riders to embark and disembark a
bus. She stated that the Towne Center’’ would also offer a retail convenience
to the commuters. Mrs. Cobble also commended Council Member Behler for speaking
with the downtown business owners to ask how or if the relocation of the park
and ride lot would affect their businesses.
9.   Mrs. Cobble stated that she felt the new construction of an office
building on the park and ride lot would make a nice appearance in the downtown
area as well as promote other community interests. She stated it could bring
new life to the downtown area along with the new Victorian style building
recently constructed by One-Eleven Engineers.
10.   In closing, Mrs. Cobble presented to council a listing of the expenses
paid by the city to maintain this lot on an annual basis as well as estimated
revenue that could be generated if the property was sold and developed. She
encouraged council to re-consider selling the property if they could get a fair
and good price.
11.   Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum Road, Independence advised council that he was
not here to discuss the Park and Ride lot, which he opposes the sale of, but
commented that Mrs. Cobble made some good points in her presentation.
12.   Mr. Nienaber advised council that he was against the city supporting a
tax increase for TransCare, a private ambulance service. He stated that he
voluntarily supports TransCare through it’s annual membership drive, but is
against any tax that would be mandated on the citizens.
13.   Chief Butler advised everyone that he has attended numerous regional
meetings on this tax proposal and he has informed the other local agencies that
Independence will not be contributing to this. Mayor Moriconi also commented
that he has been attending meetings for the last two years where this matter
was discussed. He advised that Independence is on record by way of adopting a
Resolution that would support putting the tax proposal as a referendum on the
general election ballot, but does not support annual contributions from the
city budget directly to TransCare.
14.   Pat Walton, 2610 Harris Pike, Independence introduced herself as an
active member of the Independence Senior Citizens Center. She stated that she
and some of the other senior members have been planning for the fundraising
events they will be organizing during the city’s July 4th Celebration when they
recently learned that they will no be permitted to use the Senior Center
building on July 4th. She stated they have learned that the Special Events
Committee will have use of the building for a VIP reception, with the seniors
being allotted a certain number of VIP reception tickets that they can sell.
She stated many seniors have spent the last several months planning this
fundraiser with a silent auction, quilt raffle, etc. and now they feel excluded
from the building.
15.   Mayor Moriconi explained that the July 4th Celebration events and
expenses have been expanding each year and the city is making an effort to wean
the expenses off the city budget. He stated that the VIP reception will only
last four hours on the night the fireworks are displayed, which will be July
3rd this year. He advised they will not need use of the entire building and
there was never the intent to exclude the seniors.
16.   Chief Butler advised that the Chairman of the Senior Center Board of
Directors was informed last December of the city’s plan to hold a VIP reception
on the day of the fireworks display. He stated that the seniors would get one-
third of the total tickets that will be available for the reception. Ms. Walton
stated the seniors were not informed of this decision until March of this year.
17.   Ms. Walton stated that the seniors’ objective is to assist the city in
providing funds to maintain the Center. Chief Butler explained that the Special
Events Committee is attempting to make the July 4th Celebration self-sufficient
by soliciting private donations from corporate sponsors and that providing a
VIP reception area for the sponsors is a way the city can express gratitude for
their donation. Mayor Moriconi advised the seniors could still hold a silent
auction. Ms. Walton was concerned that they would not be able to generate a
large enough crowd. Mayor Moriconi commented that it will be a two-day event
and should be well attended.
18.   Council Member Brinker commented that the Special Events is a volunteer
group and open to all citizens. He suggested the seniors attend a meeting to
present their ideas. Chief Butler stated he would contact Ms. Walton to inform
her of the next scheduled meeting of the Special Events Committee.
19.   Council Member Behler thanked Ms. Walton for her spirit of cooperation
and willingness to work. She commented that the Special Events Committee and
the members of the Senior Center should work together to arrive at a mutually
beneficial resolution.
Ordinance No. 2004-O-03 – Approving a Map Amendment for Shadybrook Subdivision
– 2nd Reading
20.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2004-O-03 that would approve a map amendment for a 65-acre section located in
the Shadybrook Subdivision approximately 600 feet south of Senour Road between
Clover Ridge Drive and Fowler Creek Road from R-1C and R-1C (RCD) to R-1C
(PUD), with certain restrictions.
21.   Council Member Behler moved to table the second reading approving this
map amendment until the council has reviewed the proposed budget. She stated
she is uncomfortable taking on the maintenance of a new park, which is included
in the proposed map amendment for this subdivision until there is assurance the
city will be able to support the maintenance. Council Member Franzen asked if
approving this map amendment would be approving the park plan also or if that
would be presented later. Mr. Deters advised that the park is not developed
yet. He presented council with a commitment letter from Mr. Chuck Berling of
Shadybrook, LLC wherein he agrees to convey to the city approximately seventeen
acres that he will develop as a park. He stated that Mr. Berling is committing
to develop two athletic fields, a parking lot to hold seventy-two vehicles and
a handicap accessible restroom building. Mr. Deters advised the city would not
accept maintenance of the park until after it is developed and that the map
amendment was approving the zone change to permit this mixed development.
22.   Council Member Behler’s motion died for lack of a second.
23.   Council Member Behler made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O- 03;
seconded by Council Member Franzen. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member
Dupps expressed some confusion regarding the city’s elimination of RCD’s not
PUD’s which he discussed with Mr. Barbian, the city’s Building Inspector. He
stated that more caution should be exerted with greater density developments.
There being no further discussion, the motion was called to a vote and roll was
answered unanimously with the motion to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O-03 approved
6-0. Mr. Deters gave a final reading of Ordinance No. 2004-O-03.
Proposed Ordinance Approving a Zoning Text Amendment for Parking Garages and
Self-Storage Facilities – New 1st Reading
24.   Mayor Moriconi explained that this proposed text amendment was presented
for a first reading in November 2003 accepting the recommendation of the KCPC
approving a text amendment to add parking garages as a permitted use in the NSC
zone and denying self-storage facilities and warehouses as a conditional use in
the NSC zone. He advised the second reading has been delayed for some time, as
there was a general consensus of council regarding approval of garages and
self-storage facilities in the NSC zone. Mayor Moriconi stated the ordinance is
now being presented for a second reading.
25.   Council Member Yeager moved to have a second reading of the proposed
ordinance; seconded by Council Member Behler. A brief discussion ensued.
Council Member Franzen stated she was concerned about adding parking garages as
a permitted use in the NSC zone. Mr. Deters advised that removing this language
from the proposed ordinance would be a significant change that would
necessitate a new first reading of the ordinance. He stated that if council
wanted to uphold only part of the KCPC’s text amendment recommendation he would
modify the ordinance language to deny parking garages in the NSC zone. Mr.
Deters made the changes and gave a new first reading to the proposed ordinance.
Council Members Yeager and Behler withdrew their original motion/second to have
a second reading of the original proposed ordinance.
Ordinance No. 2004-O-05– Relating to the Code Enforcement Board & Amending
Ordinance No. 1999-O-02 – 2nd Reading

2004-O-05 amending the language of Ordinance No. 1999-O-02 that established the
Code Enforcement Board. The amendments will correct content errors and provide

27.   Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O-05; seconded

Ordinance No. 2004-O-06 – Relating to Park Shelter Rental Fees and Amending
Ordinance No. 1998-O-05 – 2nd Reading
28.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2004-O-06 that amends Ordinance No. 1998-O-05 relating to the reservation of
city park shelters and establishing rental fees and deposit rates. Ordinance
No. 2004-O-06 eliminates refundable deposit fees and increases the rental fees
for the park shelters. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2004-O-06.
29.   Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O- 06 as read;
seconded by Council Member Franzen. Council Member Bushong commented that if
future amendments are made that council should consider imposing a higher
rental fee for non-residents. He stated that he has recently learned that this
is a common practice in other cities. He stated that he would also like to see
a future amendment have additional language that would state that the rental
agreement would be revoked if any rules were violated. He also feels that the
renter should sign a form stating they have received a copy of the park rules
and regulations and is aware of the conditions imposed. Mr. Deters commented
that he feels it goes without saying that violation of any law would result in
the immediate discontinued use of the park shelter. Mayor Moriconi stated that
the amendments in this ordinance deal strictly with the establishment of the
rental fees that the city will charge. Council Member Bushong stated that he
felt the permit form should include park rules that would include no
skateboarding or rollerblading, no loud music, no firearms, fireworks or open
fires. Mayor Moriconi stated that the reservation rental permit form could be
amended to include Council Member Bushong’s recommendations, but would have no
effect on the language of the ordinance. Council Member Yeager agreed with
Council Member Bushong’s recommendations. There being no further discussion,
the roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.

Resolution No. 2004-R-01 – Approval of the Revised Personnel Policy
35.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2004-R-01 that adopts
a revised Personnel Policy. Chief Butler explained to council that the policy
manual was reviewed by Deters, Benzinger & LaVelle law firm with regard to
legal compliance of applicable state and federal laws. He stated the sexual
harassment policy was broadened to include all types of harassment and made
clear the process in handling those situations.
36.   Chief Butler also reported that another major change was regarding the
number of hours an employee could accrue paid leave. He stated the revised
policy will permit an employee to accrue up to 480 hours of paid leave but will
only be paid 240 hours upon separation with the city. He stated that more than
240 hours would only promote absenteeism during the last days of employment
with the city. He stated the maximum accrual of 480 hours should be permitted
as employees do not get sick time. Council Member Yeager asked if there would
be a grandfather clause that would permit employees that currently have more
than 480 hours to be paid for that additional time. Chief Butler replied that
he planned to buy down some of his employee’s accrued paid leave time. He
stated that Mayor Moriconi has directed him to fund this out of the current
budget. He stated that he has worked hard to address this concern that was
expressed by the council earlier this year.
37.   Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2004-R-01; seconded
by Council Member Yeager. City Attorney, Jed Deters read the resolution. Roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Police Chief Report – ––Shawn Butler
   Rejection of Bids Received for Computer and Audio/Visual Equipment for new

Council Member Bushong. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
   Enter into an Agreement with Telecommunication Board for Purchase of Audio/
Visual Equipment and Labor
40.   Chief Butler requested authorization to enter into an agreement with the
Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky for the labor and purchase of
audio/visual equipment for the audio/visual equipment for the council chambers
of the new Municipal Center building. He stated the city could save $33,000 by
having the Telecommunications Board supply this equipment and perform the labor
to install it. He stated that basically the labor is free and is a service they
provide to the city as part of the franchise fees the city pays to the Board.
He stated they would provide a good system as it is a system they would be
operating when televising the council meetings.
41.   Council Member Bushong asked if they would be televising the caucus
meetings. Council Member Brinker stated he would be in favor of changing the
format of the caucus meetings and would like to see the caucus meetings
televised. Mayor Moriconi advised that the caucus meetings may be taped for
delayed playback.
42.   Council Member Bushong moved to enter into an agreement with the
Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky for the purchase of the audio/
visual equipment, to include labor, in an amount not to exceed $30,000; motion
was seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll call was answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
   Update on Proposed Road Repairs
43.   Dalewood Drive and Thomas Drive - Chief Butler advised that resurfacing
of Dalewood Drive and Thomas Drive has been put out for bids with a bid opening
scheduled for May 7, 2004. He stated the bid specs states the road work should
be completed no later than June 30, 2004. He advised the city engineer has
estimated the repairs will cost $33,600 for Dalewood Drive and $69,500 for
Thomas Drive.
44.   Regal Ridge Drive – Chief Butler advised he has been approached by the
developer of Regal Ridge Drive regarding the street repairs that the city has
required before accepting this private drive for maintenance. He stated that
the city engineer is inspecting the street and has noted a few repairs still
needed by the developer. He stated that most requirements have been met by the
developer thus far.
45.   Walnut Hall Drive – Chief Butler reported that this street will be
resurfaced with funds from the next budget cycle (2004/05) and that bids will
be sought in June with award of a contract at the July 5th meeting.
46.   Crowe Road – Chief Butler advised that he has been in contact with state
representatives to discuss the deteriorating condition of Crowe Road. He stated
he has asked them to consider funding the stabilization of the entire road
which would be a huge savings for the city. He advised that the State feels the
Old Richardson Road Bridge is safe as long as vehicles maintain the 8-ton
weight limit. He stated the State suggested the city re-open the old entrance
off of Madison Pike since there is now less traffic in that area of Madison.
Mayor Moriconi commented that Ex-Kenton County Judge Executive Dick Murgatroyd
taking the position of Deputy of the Transportation Cabinet may be an advantage
for this area of Kentucky.
   Update on HB 413 Law Enforcement Bill
47.   Chief Butler reported that HB 413 has passed the Senate and will be
signed into law. He stated the city could potentially acquire $45,000 - $55,000
in revenue.
   Child Safety Seat Fair
48.   Chief Butler advised the police department will sponsor a Child Safety
Seat Fair on April 25, 2004 from 12:30 – 2:30 p.m. at the Senior Center. He
stated they will inspect child restraint seats.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
49.   Mayor Moriconi announced the city has been awarded a $250,000 grant to
fund the hiring of School Resource Officers for three years. He stated that
Independence is one of only four cities in the state to be awarded this grant.
50.   Municipal Center Update - Council Member Behler asked for an update on
the construction of the new Municipal Center. Chief Butler stated the new
completion date is May 24, 2004. He stated the contractor has requested
additional days, which the architect is requiring documentation before
recommending whether or not to grant this extra time. He stated if the
contractor cannot document the need for additional time they will be subject to
a $1,000 per day penalty. Chief Butler stated he would be able to report more
at the caucus meeting.
51.   Justice Lane Report - Mr. Deters reported that the dispute between the
residents on Justice Lane and the city regarding street maintenance may now
subside as the Scherder property owners have signed a contract to sell to a
developer who will upgrade the road to subdivision standards.
52.   Mayor Moriconi announced that Chief Butler has received the Greater
Cincinnati Public Employees award as Chief of the Year. He stated there will be
a ceremony on May 5, 2004.
Adjournment
53.   There being no further discussion or business Mayor Moriconi called for a
motion to adjourn. Council Member Behler so moved, with second by Council
Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 8:40 p.m.

April 19, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
April 19, 2004
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 19,
2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members, Carol Franzen, Eric Dupps, Tom
Brinker, Donna Yeager and Mary Pat Behler answered roll call. Council Member
Jim Bushong was not present. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters,
Finance Director, Teresa Franklin Hudson, Chief Shawn Butler, City Clerk,
Patricia Taney and Assistant City Clerk, Kathy Stenger.
Mayor Moriconi stated there would be no privileges of the floor, due to the
Citizens Finance and Economic Development Committee giving a Power Point
presentation regarding their suggestions for the 2004/05 budget. He asked that
all questions be held until the end of the presentation. Mayor Moriconi thanked
the Citizens Committee for all of their time and hard work they put into the
presentation. He also asked if the committee would take their group into an
Economic Development Committee and Mr. Darrel Herald chair the committee. Mr.
Herald stated he would. Mr. Jim Kudera gave an opening statement to Mayor and
Council in regards to their recommendations. He stated the presentation
consisted of recommendations based on department figures, previous city history
and functions of the city. He asked that Mayor and Council review all issues in
depth. He stated after the presentation, a hard copy of the report would be
given to Mayor Moriconi, Council Members, Chief Butler and City Clerk, Patricia
Taney. It would be at their discretion as to whom they choose to give a copy
to. He stated this committee should be held harmless in any decision the city
makes. Mr. Herald stated the committee’s part was easy, relatively speaking but
it was going to be tough on the Mayor and Council to decide on which, if any,
of the recommendations will be implemented.
CITIZEN FINANCE POWER POINT PRESENTATION
Mr. Darrel Herald was the spokesman for the Committee and advised the current
situation is a result of inactions on certain circumstances that occurred by
previous administrations that has created a challenge for the city. He stated
that failure to react to these situations at this time may have grave
consequences for the city. He suggested the reluctance of the previous
administrations has placed a serious operating burden on the city for
maintenance and upkeep of the Senior Center and which could carry over to the
opening of the new city building. He stated the Committee feels the present and
future administrations will be faced with the financial task of meeting these
obligations. The Committee conducted their research through interviews,
analyzing data from other cities and their own work related work experiences.
He stated the Committee feels the recommendations presented tonight do not
completely solve the city’s financial outlook but will help in starting the
process. He stated it was difficult for the Committee to come up with these
suggestions because many deal with the livelihood of individual employees and
the current administration will have difficult decisions to make in that
regard. Mr. Herald stated that the following are the recommendations submitted
by the Citizens Budget Committee as possible ways to cut budget expenses:
·   Eliminate Contracted Service for Zoning Administration and Bring this
Service In-House
Bring code enforcement in house and combine with the position of Parks and
Recreation Director, and can be handled by one individual. It is the
committee’s position and feeling this department would be placed under a
Department of Public Services in the future with an estimated savings of
$30,000.00.
·   Eliminate the Position of Senior Center Director
Eliminate the Senior Center Director position. While the Senior Center was a
noble idea, the committee looks at it as a failed experiment and needs drastic
changes. The committee feels that volunteers could handle managing the Center
on a day-to-day basis. The city would continue to be responsible for the debt
and insurance on the building, but all other costs would be the responsibility
of the Senior Board. The city would be responsible for all costs for events
that use the facility for city business. The committee suggests that City
Officials meet with the Senior Center Board to determine an acceptable
percentage between senior and city activities. The city would stand ready to
provide assistance to the Senior Board if they fall short of the ability to
meet their financial commitment. The Senior Board should have a date for which
it fulfills its obligation to the city. If the Board cannot fulfill the
obligation, the city would then have the option to take control of the
facility. Estimated savings would be $51,000.00.
·   Outsource the Property Tax Billing to Eliminate Administration Clerical
Positions
The committee recommends that the billing and collection of all property taxes
be outsourced. By doing this, one clerical position could be eliminated in the
Administration Office. The committee understands that would leave three
employees in the administration department and recommends that one of the
employees would spend twenty hours per week assisting the police department and
twenty hours per week at the city office. Estimated savings would be
$50,000.00.
·   Sale of Park & Ride Municipal Parking Lot
The immediate sale of the Park and Ride parcel and combine the sale of both the
present city building and Park and Ride parcel at a reduced purchase price for
economic development. The Park & Ride would then be moved to the town center
where TANK agrees that it would be a safer place to pick up and drop off.
Estimated revenue for the sale of the Park and Ride would be $75,000.00 with an
increase of $10,000.00 annually.
·   Implementation of Parks Usage Fees
The committee suggests that a fee be assessed to all participants using city
parks for recreational activities. Estimated annual increase would be
$20,000.00.
·   Establish a Modified Zero Based Budgeting System
The committee recommends using a modified zero based budget using actual
figures based on known costs for each line item. All other costs would be
placed in the budget after extensive research and documentation for items and
needs of each department. Estimated cost would be $50,000.00.
·   Road Repairs
The committee recommends that all major road repairs only be done by revenue
allocated by the state and perform only minimum maintenance to the road system
of the city. The committee recommends the hiring of a city engineer to do an
immediate study of the city streets and prioritize them according to repairs
needed. This would assist the city on estimated road repairs in the future.
Estimated savings would be $250,000.00.
·   Public Works
Rename the Public Works Department to Public Services Department and hire a
Director of Public Services that has a financial and engineering background.
This would expand to provide more quality services to an effective and
efficient manner. This department would have responsibility for all areas of
the city over three to five years.
·   Elimination of Some Contracted Services
Contracted services are currently costing the city more than $150,000.00.
Included but not limited to be snow removal, mowing, small and medium blacktop
repairs, building and maintenance repairs, storm sewer repairs and electrical
work that could be brought in house. The committee has come up with an overall
cost savings of $556,000.00 for fiscal year 2005.
Council Response to Citizens Finance Committee Presentation
Council Member Behler stated it seems they have looked at changing or
eliminating staff in all departments but the police department. She asked if
the police department operation and budget was reviewed and was there any fluff
in it. Mr. Herald stated they did look at the police budget and compared it to
other cities in Northern Kentucky and the Committee felt the police budget was
in line or the same as other police departments. He stated they felt there were
no major areas that needed to be changed with the exception of sharing one of
the clerk positions.
Mr. Kudera stated the police department has a lot of area to cover
geographically and is effective with the amount of officers they have, and the
committee feels the police department needs to add one or two more officers to
the force. Council Member Behler asked if the committee had looked at the
Administration and Public Works staff, like they did the Police Department. Mr.
Herald stated the committee looked at the total staff for Administration and
Public Works Department and compared them with other cities. Council Member
Yeager stated she sees no method of handling the Senior Citizens Center without
a Director, other than volunteers. She stated volunteers could not detect

Public Services to include Public Works and Parks. Mr. Kudera stated with the
new Municipal Building being so close, one of the city employees could open it,
close it and set up scheduling for events. He stated, like it or not, the
Senior Center is a significant part of the city’s financial problem. Council
Member Yeager asked where the $70,000.00 comes in for the Park and Ride. Mr.
Herald stated it would be for the sale of the property and an estimated
$10,000.00 yearly for payroll taxes that would be generated revenue.

Council Member Franzen stated she is aware there are problems with the Senior

Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May
3, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant of Grace Community Church
gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps,
Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Recognition

Independence Wendy’s Restaurant as the recipient of the Business of the Month.
He presented Jim Rogers with a plaque of recognition.

3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the April 5,
2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Behler so moved, with a second
from Council Member Dupps. One amendment was noted by Mayor Moriconi and roll
call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.

Council Member Franzen. Mayor Moriconi noted a couple of amendments and roll
call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 to accept the minutes as
amended.
Presentation by Citizens Police Academy Alumni
5.   Dave Millward, President of the Citizens Police Academy Alumni was present
as the spokesperson for the alumni and to present Mayor Moriconi on behalf of
the city a gift to the police department. Mr. Millward stated the ninety-member
alumni held several fundraisers over a two-year period that enabled them to
donate this gift of $7,200 to be used to purchase exercise equipment. He stated
the alumni will be holding a rummage sale this spring as well as having a
fundraising booth at the July 4th Celebration this summer and is active in
assisting the police department with their annual golf outing and preparing
meals for various civic meetings. Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Millward and the
entire alumni, many of whom were present. He stated this all-volunteer group’s
fundraising efforts has saved the city money. Chief Butler also thanked the
alumni on behalf of the police department. He stated they have assisted the
department in various ways and he appreciated all they do. He also commented
that the exercise equipment would be available for use by all city employees.

Resolution No. 2004-R-03 – Partially Accepting KCPC Text Amendment
Recommendation Relating to Self-Storage Facilities & Parking Garages
8.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2004-R-03 that would
reject in part a recommendation by the Kenton County Planning Commission
relating to self-storage facilities and parking garages. City Attorney, Jed
Deters read Resolution No. 2004-R-03. He explained the application for the text
amendment was made by resident, Martin Neltner to add to the zoning text the
addition of the use of self-storage facilities in the NSC zone. He advised that
the recommendation of the Planning Commission was to deny self-storage
facilities and warehouses as conditional uses in the NSC zone, and to permit a
text amendment to add parking garages as a permitted use in the NSC zone. Mr.
Deters advised council that Resolution No. 2004-R-03 addresses the council’s
desire to partially accept and partially deny the KCPC recommendation of
application 1640R, thereby upholding the disapproval of self-storage facilities
and warehouses as a conditional use in the NSC zone and disapproving their
recommendation to add parking garages as a permitted use in the NSC zone. He
stated this resolution would take the place of a proposed ordinance, which had
a first reading at the November 3, 2003 council meeting.
9.   Council Member Dupps moved to adopt Resolution No. 2004-R-03, seconded by
Council Member Bushong. Council Member Yeager questioned the language of
paragraph two, stating that she did not feel it was clear. Mr. Deters provided
further explanation. There being no further discussion, roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Discussion of Bids Received for the Sale of the Municipal Park & Ride Lot
10.   Mayor Moriconi announced that only one bid was received for the sale of
the city’s park and ride lot located at 5290 Madison Pike. He stated the
bidder, James Bertram submitted a bid price of $60,000. Mayor Moriconi
entertained a motion to accept the bid and sell the lot to Mr. Bertram. Council
Member Dupps asked the zone of the property. Council Member Bushong asked if
the bid was over or under the appraised amount. Mayor Moriconi stated that at
$60,000, the bid amount was slightly under the appraisal of $67,700. He stated
that he felt the bid was a realistic amount, as the developer will have the
expense of relocating sewer and other utility lines. In responding to Council
Member Dupps question regarding the current zone, Mr. Deters advised that the
developer might need a zone change. Mayor Moriconi commented that now is the
time to sell this property for development. Council Member Bushong commented
that he understands there is a sewer easement road on the lot, which must be
preserved. Mayor Moriconi stated that the bidder is aware of the easement and
that he will be required to provide access. Council Member Brinker commented
that he thought the bids would be in the $50,000 range so he is pleased with
the $60,000 bid considering the preparation work that will be necessary to
relocate the utility lines. He stated the budget is in need of the revenue that
will be generated by this sale and the city is collaborating with the Town
Center to relocate the TANK Park and ride facility. Council Member Bushong
asserted that any agreement with the Deters Company be a binding permanent one.
He stated that he hates to relocate the park and ride facility, but if the
decision is to move it, then he would like an official agreement in place. Mr.
Deters agreed that the city should seek an irrevocable lease with the Town
Center.
11.   Council Member Brinker asked if TANK was in agreement with the relocation
of the facility. Chief Butler advised TANK has requested a 120-day notice from
the Town Center if, sometime in the future, they would rescind the agreement.
Council Member Brinker asked if the city has received any negative feedback
regarding the plans to relocate. Chief Butler stated he has not heard any
negative comments, but did get a positive e-mail message from the city’s
website. Council Member Yeager stated she has heard negative comments. Mayor
Moriconi stated he received a comment that indicated the TANK stop would be
safer taken off of Route 17 (Madison Pike).
12.   Council Member Bushong moved to accept the bid from James Bertram in the
amount of $60,000 for the purchase of the park and ride lot located at 5290
Madison Pike and authorize Mayor Moriconi to enter into a contract for the sale
of the property; seconded by Council Member Franzen. Council Member Yeager
asked how the city would utilize the $60,000. Mayor Moriconi replied it would
be put into the general fund. Council Member Yeager asked that it be used to
pay down the mortgage debt on the Senior Center building. Council Member Dupps
commented there might be expenses associated with relocating the bus shelter.
Mayor Moriconi asked council if there was a consensus to use the revenue to pay
down the debt. No one voiced objection to Council Member Yeager’s suggestion.
Roll was called and answered unanimously. Council Member Yeager clarified her
vote by stating that she was voting yes only if this revenue would be used to
pay down the debt on the Senior Center. Motion carried 6-0. Council Member
Dupps stated that the TANK bus riders should be given adequate notice of the
relocation of the facility.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2003/04 Budget – 1st Reading
13.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that would amend the current, 2003/04 fiscal year budget. Mr. Deters
read the proposed budget. No discussion ensued.
Proposed Ordinance – Establishing a Trash Assessment Rate Effective from 7-1-04
through 6-30-05 – 1st Reading
14.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that would establish a trash assessment rate for the period of July
1, 2004 through June 30, 2005. He stated the new rate would be $105.84, an
increase of $5.04. There being no discussion, Mr. Deters read the proposed
ordinance.
Executive Session
15.   Before moving on to the next agenda item regarding the proposed ordinance
adopting a 2004/05 budget, Mayor Moriconi requested a motion to enter into
executive session for the purposing of discussing a personnel issue. Council
Member Franzen moved for an executive session in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810
(f), with second by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes.
16.   Council Member Brinker moved to return to regular session; seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2004/05 Budget – 1st Reading
17.   Mayor Moriconi stated that he was pleased to present to council for a
first reading a proposed ordinance adopting a budget for the 2004/05 fiscal
year. He thanked the members of the Citizens Budget Committee for working so
hard on the budget recommendations they presented to council. He stated that
Committee would now continue to function as an Economic Development Committee,
to be chaired by Darrell Herald.
18.   Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance adopting the 2004/05 budget.
19.   Council Member Yeager stated that she did not feel it would be practical
to purchase mowing equipment and other related lawn maintenance equipment this
year. Council Member Behler commented that while she feels it is necessary to
increase the public works staff, she has concerns with bringing the grass
cutting in house. She stated she spoke to Jeff Smith, the Public Works crew
leader who is concerned it will be difficult to find good reliable part time
laborers, since no benefits are provided for part time help. And that in fact
it may be more of a burden on him, if his department spends all their time
mowing grass in the summer months. She stated that even Malco Lawn Service, who
the city currently contracts with for this maintenance, expressed difficulty in
obtaining good reliable laborers and he offers full time work. Council Member
Brinker asked if the lawn equipment would be a lease-purchase, so that the
equipment could be returned if the part time staffing does not work out. Chief
Butler replied no, that the equipment would be purchased outright, but if the
city did work out a lease-purchase agreement with the bank, there might be
penalties involved if the city would back out of the agreement. Council Member
Yeager commented there would still be the difficulty in hiring good part time
laborers. Council Member Brinker stated he felt there are plenty of people
looking for jobs. Council Member Behler expressed concern how it would be
handled if, after a short period of time, the situation was not working well.
She asked where the new public works equipment would be stored when no in use.
Mayor Moriconi replied the equipment would be stored at the Cox Road facility.
Council Member Brinker stated he would like the Citizens Budget Committee to
supply council with the supporting data used to recommend that grass cutting
would be more cost effective if done in house. Council Member Yeager commented
that the city tried bringing this job in house before and it didn’t work out.
Council Member Bushong asked why it didn’t work out. Council Member Yeager
explained the city had used other contractors in the past that did not perform
as well as Malco. Council Member Brinker stated it was never brought in house.
He expressed concern that in future years, with the addition of a new park, the
expense of park and other lawn maintenance will continue to increase.
20.   Council Member Bushong asked if the purchase of a new public works truck
was in this budget. Chief Butler commented that Barry Malott of Malco Lawn
Services does a great job, but adding two part time employees to the Public
Works department is about growing the department, not just about saving
dollars. He stated he feels that adding two part time employees to cut grass in
the summer months and help out with the snow removal in the winter months will
cost no more than is currently being expended to outsource this type of work.
He stated he was confused why Jeff Smith would feel adding two additional
employees would be a burden to him. Chief Butler suggested at the very least
the city should hire one additional full time employee and purchase one more
truck for the public works department. He stated the city is adding more
streets each year and more patching is required each year. Council Member
Behler stated that while she agrees that the public works needs additional
staffing, she also looks at it as increasing the level of responsibility onto
that department.
21.   Council Member Franzen asked if hiring one full time employee and
purchasing one truck would keep the proposed budget balanced. Chief Butler
stated the budget would remain balanced, as it would just require moving some
figures from one line item to another. Council Member Franzen suggested the
addition of one full time employee could assist with snow removal help in the
winter. Mayor Moriconi advised the city currently has a 75/25 split arrangement
with Kenton County for snow removal; they maintain 75% of the city streets with
the city’s two public works employees handling the other 25% of the streets. He
stated that as the number of city streets increases, there will be a need to
offset the growth. Council Member Bushong commented that he feels the city
should proceed with plans to purchase another public works truck and another
snow blade for the winter months. Chief butler commented that the cost of a
snow blade has been calculated in the proposed budget. Council Member Franzen
commented that she feels it was a good idea to bring the grass maintenance in
house, but that the timing may not be right. She stated that adding staff to
the public works department is a first step to eventually handling the
responsibility of all the lawn and park maintenance in future years. Council
Member Brinker concurred with Council Member Franzen.
22.   Mayor Moriconi stated the grass cutting issue is resolved for now, as
everyone has had two weeks to review the proposed budget. He commented that the
proposal to bring the grass cutting in house was not meant to suggest that
Malco Lawn Service is not doing a good job for the city, quite the contrary.
Council Member Bushong stated that he favored hiring one additional full time
public works employee while continuing to outsource the lawn maintenance for
now.
23.   Chief Butler commented this change will just require shifting numbers
from one line item to another and will have no material affect on the proposed
budget.
24.   Council Member Dupps asked if the outsourcing of the property tax billing
and collection has been determined. Mayor Moriconi stated he has not received
information regarding this from the county yet and hoped to have something to
report by the caucus meeting. Council Member Bushong stated he has reviewed
this and would welcome the possibility of having this revenue collected by the
county. Mayor Moriconi stated the purpose of outsourcing this collection would
be to save money.
25.   There being no further discussion regarding the proposed budget, Mr.
Deters suggested a motion would be in order to amend the first reading. Council
Member Bushong so moved, with second by Council Member Behler. Motion carried
with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a Pay Plan for the F/Y 2004/05 – 1st Reading
26.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would adopt
an employee pay plan for the 2004/05 fiscal year. Mr. Deters gave a first
reading of the ordinance. No discussion ensued.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
27.   Chief Butler reported that the Public Works department is making repairs
to Richardson Road. He also reported that he would like to have the City
Engineer prepare a street assessment proposal, wherein they will inventory
every street and make recommendations for future maintenance/repairs. Chief
Butler advised this will be a long process, taking about seven months for the
engineer to complete. He stated he would like to pay the engineer for this
project out of the current budget. Mayor Moriconi advised the city currently
has forty-two miles of streets. Council Member Dupps commented that the former
city engineer had prepared a similar street assessment and wondered if the city
was currently working from that report. Chief Butler stated that he does not
believe the previous report had been updated on an annual basis. After a brief
discussion, the consensus of council was to obtain a proposal from the city
engineer.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
28.   No Report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
29.   Mayor Moriconi reported that the city has been contacted by Burgess &
Niple on behalf of Cingular Wireless with a proposal to lease a 100 x 100 sq.
ft. area at Sterling Staggs Park. He stated they would like to install a 150
foot cell tower in the southwest corner of the park. Council Member Franzen
stated she would recuse herself from the discussion on this matter, as her
church, Independence Christian on Madison Pike, has been approached with a
similar offer and are in the process of considering it. Council Member Bushong
commented that he heard four other cites are being considered and he opposes
the idea of locating a cell tower in the park. Council Members Behler and
Yeager agreed with Council Member Bushong. Council Member Dupps stated he felt
a cell tower would be too obtrusive in the park. Since the general consensus of
council was to deny this proposal by Cingular Wireless, Mayor Moriconi
requested the City Clerk to contact Burgess & Niple to advise them the city is
not interested in leasing space for a cell tower.

Fiscal Court Town Hall Meeting which is scheduled for May 18, 2004 at 7:00 p.m.
in the Courthouse. He encouraged the council members to attend this meeting. A
comment was made that May 18th is Election Day and wondered if the meeting
would still take place. Council Member Behler urged registered voters to go to
the polls in this primary election to cast their votes for city council
candidates. She stated the council race is non-partisan election and there was
some confusion two years ago when many voters, who were registered as
independents, were turned away at the polls, but this should not occur this
year.
Adjournment
31.   There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Council
Member Dupps and seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 8:10 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.
May 17, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 17,
2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker,
Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager answered roll call.
Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Mike Harmon, 81 Sherwood Drive, Independence, Kentucky addressed council
regarding a proposal to set up a mobile concession to sell Hawaiian shaved ice
cones at Memorial Park and Sterling Staggs Park. He stated the Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission has advised him that mobile concessions are
not permitted on private property, and since the city is exempt from zoning
laws, he thought the parks would be an ideal location for this type of
concession. He stated that Hawaiian ice is a great summer treat for families.
He stated that he and his wife operate Special Occasions Catering, which is
licensed and insured, and that the mobile concessions is just one of the
services they offer. He assured council that his workers would inspect the park
area each day and dispose of any litter resulting from the concession.
Mr. Harmon stated that he also hopes to implement a program that will help fund
the local youth sports organizations. He stated he would give the parents and
supporters of the sports organizations the opportunity to help work the
concession and in return earn a share of the profits to help fund the football,
baseball and soccer teams. He stated he would also like to provide concession
at the upcoming summer concerts at the Memorial Park Amphitheater.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Harmon if he wanted authorization to set up the mobile
concession at both Sterling Staggs Park and Memorial Park. He stated yes, at
least initially, so that he could determine which location would be best. Mayor
Moriconi asked what he would charge for the Hawaiian ice. Mr. Harmon stated he
would charge around $2.00 - $2.50 which is the average rate, but that part of
the concept is that a portion of the charge will be going to the sports
organizations. Council Member Behler asked if the fund raising for the sports
teams was the primary reason for the mobile concession. Mr. Harmon stated no;
that the mobile concession will be an extension of his catering business and he
is unsure how profitable it will be.
City Attorney, Jed Deters advised council that he is inclined to think that
granting a concession/vending agreement for profit on city property is a
situation that should be bid out so that others have the same opportunity.
Council Member Behler asked if the city did not bid this service out could the
city be open to a lawsuit. Mr. Deters stated it could be a possibility. Council
Member Yeager commented that she thought it might fall under the $20,000
bidding regulation. Council Member Dupps stated that he felt the city would
only be open to a lawsuit if they denied other mobile concessions the same type
of agreement. Mr. Harmon stated the he was not asking for exclusive rights to
provide concessions in the parks. Mr. Deters stated that he felt bidding out
concession services was the easiest thing to do.
Council Member Bushong asked if the ball teams would earn a specific percentage
of the profits produced by the concession. Mr. Harmon stated that teams who
have supporters work the concession would receive 20% of the net profits.
Mayor Moriconi commented that during Amphitheater performances, it could become
a problem if other vendors would want to set up. Mr. Harmon stated he has not
purchased the mobile concession trailer yet and it may be June or July before
he could be in operation.
Council Member Behler asked how the city could oblige Mr. Harmon and protect
the city’s interests. Mr. Deters advised the city could consider a zoning text
amendment to allow these types of businesses. Council Member Franzen suggested
starting the bid process while concurrently applying for a text amendment.
Mayor Moriconi commented that he thinks a mobile concession is a great idea and
would like to find a way to permit this without a lot of bureaucracy. Council
Member Bushong asked how often Mr. Harmon would set up the mobile concession.
Mr. Harmon stated that he would like to be open from mid-week through the
weekend.
The consensus of council was to temporarily allow Mr. Harmon to set up the
mobile concession at the two parks, with the city applying for a text amendment
during the interim. Mr. Deters stated he would draft a resolution for council
to consider at the June 7, 2004 council meeting. Council Member Behler asked if
the city would ask for compensation from Mr. Harmon. Council Member Brinker
stated that if the city does receive compensation that the revenue should be
directed into the Parks and Recreation budget. Mayor Moriconi advised the city
could consider compensation later.
Discussion of Proposed 2004-05 Budget – Final Review and Comments
Mayor Moriconi presented a final review of the proposed 2004-05 budget. He
stated that the budget ordinance is scheduled for a second reading and adopting
at the June 7, 2004 council meeting.
Council Member Dupps expressed concern that the courthouse rent line item had
zero budgeted funds and since it looks like the construction of the new
Municipal Center will not be completed by July 1, thought that the budget
should reflect two or three months of rent.
Council Member Yeager questioned the Public Works line item for the lease of a
dump truck. Chief Butler explained that this item has to be shown as both a
revenue and expense. He stated the full estimated cost of the truck will be
$54,000, but the city will only expend $18,000 each year for the term of the
three-year lease purchase loan.
Council Member Bushong asked if the mowing equipment that was originally
proposed has been withdrawn. Chief Butler stated that all the mowing equipment
has been deleted, since the proposal to bring the grass mowing in house has
been rejected.
Council Member Franzen asked if the Senior Center Director salary should be
eliminated since the Director has resigned. Mayor Moriconi advised that he
wanted to keep the salary in the proposed budget until a decision is made about
the Director position. Council Member Behler asked if the mayor intended to
hire another Director. Mayor Moriconi advised that Recreation Director, Nita
Brake would temporarily assume the duties of the Senior Director until a
permanent situation is decided. He advised that it may be difficult to fill the
position since the city in recent months informed the Senior Board of Directors
that the city intended to relinquish full financial responsibility of this
position to the Board over the next three years.
There being no further questions, Mayor Moriconi advised the budget ordinance
would be presented at the June 7, 2004 council meeting.
Review Bids Received for the Resurfacing of Thomas and Dalewood Drives
Mayor Moriconi presented the City Engineer’s correspondence and spreadsheet
regarding the five bids received for the resurfacing of Thomas Drive and
Dalewood Drive. He stated that the street repair bids have been coming in lower
than estimated which will enable the city to repair more street than expected.
Chief Butler stated that the City Engineer is recommending that the bid be
awarded to Barrett Paving who submitted a low bid of $67,120.00. Council Member
Behler commented that she was surprised at the wide range from a high bid of
$117,540.00 to the low of $67,120.00. Mr. Deters stated that often times the
smaller companies need the work and are willing to work for less money. Council
Member Bushong asked if a performance check would be done by the engineer.
Chief Butler stated yes, that the engineer would do periodic quality checks on
the work being performed. Mr. Deters advised that the company that is awarded
the bid, be it a small company or large, is required to follow the bid specs
and it is the engineer’s job to oversee that.
Chief Butler advised that council will be asked to authorize a contract with
CDS Engineers for a five-year street repair projection. He also advised that
repairs to Walnut Hall Drive have been let for bids.
Mayor Moriconi stated that he would like to use the remaining street repair
funds toward the installation of sidewalks in the downtown area. Chief Butler
stated that the Public Works staff would be able to supply the labor.
City Attorney – Jed K. Deters
No report.
Miscellaneous
Council Member Dupps suggested the city sponsor a city-wide yard sale in
September. He stated the city could advertise the event. Council seemed open to
this suggestion.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Business of the Month - Mayor Moriconi advised that Council Member Yeager would
select the business of the month for June and asked that she advise the City
Clerk of her selection prior to the June 7th meeting.
Sale of the City Administration Building - Mayor Moriconi advised council that
the city is in receipt of a contract to purchase the city administration
building. He stated that Mr. Eric Deters is offering the city $260,000 for the
building. The city attorney advised that council could ratify this purchase to
offer at the June 7th council meeting.
Adjournment
There being no further business, motion was made by Council Member Franzen and
seconded by Council Member Brinker to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:52 p.m.

June 7, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June
7, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant of Grace Community Church
gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps,
Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member Yeager had chosen Malco
Services as the recipient of the Business of the Month. He presented owner,
Barry Malott with a plaque of recognition and stated the city appreciated his
business. Mr. Malott thanked Mayor Moriconi and council for the honor and
stated he has lived in Independence all his life and is proud to call it home.
Approval of the Minutes of the May 3, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the May 3,
2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Bushong so moved, with a second
from Council Member Franzen. Amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the May 17, 2004 Caucus Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the May 17,
2004 caucus council meeting. Council Member Behler so moved, with second from
Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 to accept the minutes as presented.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Pat Walton, 2610 Harris Road, Independence addressed council regarding
several issues relating to the Senior Center. She informed them that the Senior
Center Director had not been notified that the seniors would not have use of
the Senior Center for their fundraising events during the July 4th Celebration.
She stated this could affect the seniors fundraising plans, which have been in
place for several months.
6.   Ms. Walton also commented that several seniors were offended by Jim
Kudera’s remarks at the May caucus meeting. She stated that many of the seniors
feel the operation of the Center getting more political than they can handle.
She stated they feel they are being overrun and they want to continue with
their fundraising.
7.   Ms. Walton expressed concern that she heard the grant funds the city
received for the Senior Center were used for the general fund of the city and
not paid on the Senior Center building debt. She stated she is concerned that
the money is not being handled property. She stated the seniors are worried
they will loose the Center due to a lack of funds.
8.   In closing, Ms. Walton stated that it was announced at the last Senior
Board meeting that the commencement of a Bingo and the selling of tear-offs
would be postponed. She stated the seniors are concerned about this
postponement as they feel this would be moneymaking venture for the Center.
9.   Mayor Moriconi asked Chief Butler to respond to Ms. Walton’s concerns.
Chief Butler stated that there is no truth to the rumor that the Center will be
closed due to lack of funds. Chief Butler and Mayor Moriconi advised they were
not aware of the Board’s decision to postpone the Bingo and other gaming
fundraising.
10.   Council Member Brinker asked Chief Butler if the seniors had received
written notification that the Center would be used for a private party on the
fourth. Chief Butler stated that the Mayor and him met with the Chairman of the
Senior Center Board to advise him of the Special Events Committee’s plan to
hold a private party for the sponsors of the July 4th Celebration. Ms. Walton
stated the seniors did not learn of the Committee’s plans until recently, after
they had spent months in planning their fundraising events, and then they were
told they would not have use of the building. Chief Butler stated the Chairman
was told of the plans well in advance of July 4th; he does not known when the
Senior Director was informed.
11.   Mayor Moriconi responded to Ms. Walton’s assertion regarding the loan
proceeds for the construction of the Senior Center. He stated that the rumor
that the funds were misused is a big misconception. He also commented that if
the city was going to abandon the Senior Center, that it would have been closed
by now. He stated the city does not have plans to close the Center. Ms. Walton
voiced her concern about the Board postponing the commencement of the Bingo,
which was the senior’s primary way to raise funds for the continued operation
of the Center. Council Member Behler commented that the Bingo issue needs to be
resolved. Council Member Yeager stated that the Board has not been issued a
gaming license from the state yet. There was a brief discussion about the
gaming license. The City Clerk stated that the license application has been
returned on a couple of occasions due to requests for more information, such as
budget and other financial information and information needed regarding the
Board members.
12.   Council Member Bushong asked if it was too late for the seniors to
proceed with their plans for the fourth. Ms. Walton said they would not be able
to do all they normally do, but that they would open the Center on July 2nd and
hold a quilt raffle. Council Member Yeager stated the seniors will also sell
drinks and hotdogs and metts on July 2nd.
13.   Council Member Brinker stated he would like the Senior Board members to
attend a caucus meeting. He feels the Council Members should meet with the
Board members and work together. Council Member Franzen asked if the Board was
a requirement to keep the 501-3(c) status. Council Member Yeager replied yes.
Mayor Moriconi encouraged the council members to attend the Senior Board
meetings. Council Member Yeager stated the meetings are the fourth Tuesday of
each month at 8:30 a.m. at the Senior Center.
14.   In closing, Mayor Moriconi commented that the seniors have the building
available to them every day of the week, and he stated it shouldn’t be a
problem for the Special Events Committee to have use of the building for one
evening, July 3rd, from 5-10 pm.
15.   Vic Morrison, 100 Roselawn, Independence, Ky. commented that the primary
election, with sixteen candidates for city council, made history as a record-
setting number of interested residents for a council seat. He thanked Council
Member Brinker for acting as an interim council member, when Jim Ellison
vacated his seat. He stated that even though he did not win a position on the
November general election ballot, he should be proud of his time spent on the
council. Mr. Morrison also complimented Council Member Yeager for all she has
done; stating that she has proven she cares about people, and he complimented
the entire city council for their efforts.
16.   Council Member Brinker thanked everyone who voted for him in the primary
election and stated that it has been a great honor to act as an interim council
member. He stated he would continue to volunteer his time in other ways to make
this city a great community.
Ordinance No. 2004-O-09 – Adopting a Trash Assessment Rate – 2nd Reading
17.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2004-O- 09 that would adopt a trash assessment rate of $105.84. City Attorney,
Jed Deters read the proposed ordinance.
18.   Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O-09, seconded
by Council Member Dupps. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.

Request for Annexation by Freedom Park LLC
25.   Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Mike Duncan, attorney for Diversified
Builders and Freedom Park LLC.
26.   Mr. Duncan addressed council with a request for annexation and rezoning
of approximately fifty-six acres located at 11527 Wilson Road. He stated that
this property would be the next phase of development of the Freedom Park
subdivision, which is located entirely within the city boundaries. He stated
the developers plan to purchase the fifty-six acres from Margaret Mullins,
which is currently not within the city limits. Mr. Duncan advised that since
this development will be an extension of the Freedom Trail subdivision that it
makes sense to request the city to annex this property. He stated the
developer’s layout plan for the fifty-six acres proposes 158 lots, most 70-80
foot with some of the lots even larger than 70-80 foot and a 2.8 per net acre
density. He stated they are requesting a R-1D zone, which would give the
developer flexibility while not adversely affecting the theme of the Freedom
Trail subdivision. Mr. Duncan advised the R-1D zone would permit the builders
to offer a more diverse community and present a product to empty nesters who do
not want a large lot to maintain. Mr. Duncan advised the development would not
contain any manufactured, duplex or slab homes and they would range in price
from $170,000 to $250,000. He stated the smaller lots would allow the buyer to
put the majority of their purchase dollars into the house versus the lot.
27.   Mr. Duncan advised that KRS100.209 (1) permits the city to annex the
unincorporated territory and amend the zoning map (rezone) simultaneously. He
stated the developers have contracted with Ms. Mullins and would like to
proceed in making application to the Kenton County Planning Commission right
away. He stated the deadline to make application is Wednesday. Mr. Duncan
advised the annexation/map amendment would require two ordinances and if the
city council agrees to support the developer’s request to move forward with
this process, would like to propose a first reading of the ordinances at the
July council meeting. He stated that he is requesting the city proceed with the
voluntary annexation process tonight and then ask the Kenton County Planning
Commission recommend the appropriate zoning for the property upon annexation.
28.   Mayor Moriconi stated that Freedom Trail Drive could be continued out to
Wilson Road. Council Member Yeager asked if this development would be providing
another egress for the subdivision. Mayor Moriconi stated yes. Council Member
Brinker stated this would give some relief to Oby Drive, which currently is the
only ingress/egress for the Freedom Park subdivision. Mayor Moriconi concluded
that this proposed plan is a positive phase for the ongoing development of this
subdivision.
29.   City Attorney, Mr. Deters commented that it is his policy of advising
council not to discuss a zone change before it is officially before the council
to act on. He advised council they should only discuss whether or not they want
to pursue the annexation aspect of the development. Council Member Yeager
stated that she feels the extension of this subdivision is a good thing.
Council Member Franzen stated that the city police officers would be patrolling
the area, so it should be annexed into the city. Mayor Moriconi commented that
having another ingress/egress would alleviate the traffic off of Oby Drive and
State Route 17. Council Member Brinker asked when the road leading out to
Wilson Road would be developed. Mr. Duncan advised that Ms. Mullins, for tax
purposes, wants to stage the sale the fifty-six acres in three separate tracts
and that the tract that directly abuts the Freedom Park subdivision would be
the first phase developed.
30.   Council Member Bushong asked if the annexation was desired if the
developer did not get the requested R-1D zone. Mr. Duncan stated probably not.
Council Member Bushong asked why the developer did not want to stay with the
current R-1C zone of the Freedom Park subdivision and would they be interested
in staying with the current zone. Mr. Duncan responded that the developers
would probably not be interested in building under the current R-1C zone, as
they want to have more flexibility provided in the R-1D zone so they could
offer a product that the public wants to purchase.
31.   Mr. Deters asked Mr. Duncan what he would like from council at this
meeting. Mr. Duncan stated that they would like the council to approve an
application for the KCPC to consider the property for voluntary annexation and
make a recommendation to amend the comprehensive plan and official zoning map
to incorporate and establish zoning or other land use regulations for the
property proposed for annexation.
32.   Council Member Franzen moved to recommend annexation of the Mullins
property, located at 11527 Wilson Road, and ask the Kenton County Planning
Commission to recommend a building zone. Council Member Yeager seconded the
motion. Council Member Dupps asked if the development would contain unused
green space. Mr. Duncan advised there would be large rear yards with hillsides,
with many trees left untouched. He stated these green spaces would be owned and
therefore maintained by the individual property owners. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 1997-O-13 Relating to Building
Codes – 1st Reading
33.   Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance
relating to the adoption of the building codes. He yielded the floor to Mr.
Deters for further explanation. Mr. Deters advised council that the city adopts
the uniform building codes and that this proposed ordinance would adopt the
most recent updates, that being the 2002 Kentucky Residential Code; in effect
keeping the city current with operating under the uniform codes. Mayor Moriconi
stated it is a formality to adopt the building codes by ordinance and basically
a little ‘housekeeping’ of the ordinance currently in effect. Mr. Deters read
the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi advised this ordinance would be on the
agenda of the next regular business meeting for a second reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 1-7-89 Adopting the International
Property Maintenance Codes – 1st Reading
34.   Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance
relating to the adoption of the 2003 International Property Maintenance Code.
He asked Mr. Deters to explain this proposed ordinance to council. Mr. Deters
stated that again, this proposed ordinance is needed ‘housekeeping’ to keep the
city current with regulations for control of buildings and structures.
Discussion Regarding “Gang/Cluster” Mailboxes and Amending Ordinance No. 1993-
O-01
35.   Mayor Moriconi directed council’s attention to a memo in their packet
from the city’s Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian. He stated that Mr. Barbian
is requesting that council consider amending Ordinance No. 1993-O-01, which

to allow these mailboxes for shopping centers. Council Member Brinker suggested

Member Franzen commented that most apartment complexes have the cluster mailbox
located inside the front door of each building unit, which she considers to be
reasonable. Council Member Yeager stated she is concerned that the senior
citizens would be burdened if they had to walk a long distance to retrieve
their mail, especially in inclement weather. Mr. Deters stated he would draft
an amended ordinance for their consideration at the next caucus meeting
