June 21, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 21,
2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor,
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Donna Yeager, Eric Dupps, Jim
Bushong, Tom Brinker and Mary Pat Behler answered roll call. Council Member,
Carol Franzen was not present. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
No one signed in for privileges to address council.
OLD BUSINESS
Discussion for Acceptance of Regal Ridge Drive for Maintenance
Mr. Steve Powell of Powell Homes Development revisited an issue that was
brought before council on October 7, 2002. He stated that at that meeting he
had requested a commitment from the city to accept Regal Ridge drive for
maintenance purposes after he completed the planned improvements to bring the
street up to building code specifications. Mr. Powel advised that Council
Member Jim Ellison made a formal motion to accept Regal Ridge Drive for
maintenance after improvements were made. Mr. Powell stated the road was in
poor condition and was actually dedicated in 1982, but for unknown reasons it
never became a city maintained street. He stated they worked with the Planning
Commission and rebuilt the street, including the replacement of curbs and
gutters, all completed in May 2003. He stated the City Engineer made an
inspection of the street improvements and noted a couple of deficiencies that
have now been fixed to the engineer’s satisfaction. Chief Butler confirmed the
city engineer’s findings. City Attorney Deters asked if the street had been re-
platted. Mr. Dwight Clayton stated the city never accepted the street but it
was platted in 1982 as a dedicated public right-of-way. Council Member Dupps
asked if an ordinance would be needed. City Attorney Deters stated it would.
Mr. Powell stated that they felt this was the best way to do it and that is why
they are bringing this before the city. City Attorney Deters stated it might be
overkill since the city engineer and NKAPC have approved this street for city
maintenance, but felt it would be prudent to do an ordinance. Mayor Moriconi
stated an ordinance would be prepared for a first reading at the August 2nd
meeting with a second reading of the ordinance at the first business meeting in
September.
NEW BUSINESS
Proposed Ordinances relating to Gang Mail Boxes
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would amend
Ordinance 1993-O-01. He explained that this ordinance established a ban on
cluster/gang mailboxes in the city limits. He stated that the building
inspector has received requests from developers of multi-residential complexes,
such as condominium and apartments, permission to install the cluster/gang
mailboxes. Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for questions from council on this
proposed ordinance amendment. Council Member Yeager asked if some wording
relating to a “limit of footage between the residence and the mail box could be
no further than 100 feet” due to some residents, especially senior citizens
might not be able to walk that far to retrieve their mail. City Attorney Deters
stated in speaking with the Post Office, he was told the postal carriers would
deliver to someone’s door under certain circumstances. Mayor Moriconi stated
the goal of the gang mailboxes is for convenience. Council Member Yeager stated
she had discussed this with the Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian, and he tends
to agree with her. City Attorney Deters stated Mr. Barbian would have that
discretion. Council Member Behler stated another building inspector might not
be so generous. Council Member Dupps stated he is concerned that would create a
need for variance requests, which would have to go before the Board of
Adjustments for a determination. City Attorney Deters stated the gang mailboxes
could be constructed according to an agreement with a developer. Mayor Moriconi
stated the mailboxes would be hard to regulate, but a developer should want to
offer conveniences. Council Member Behler stated that if in the future problems
arise, due to a lack of a definite distance between each cluster mailbox unit
in this ordinance then it could be amended at a later date. Council Member
Yeager asked how the gang mailboxes currently located at the park and ride lot
would be handled once the city sells this property. City Attorney Deters stated
he did not know and that this may be an issue between the resident box holders
and the postmaster.
Discussion Regarding the Creation of a Part-Time Building Custodian
Mayor Moriconi stated this position has been added to the 2004/05 budget and
would combine the duties of cleaning the new Municipal Center and the Senior
Center He stated the goal is to hire one custodian to maintain both buildings
as well as assist in the opening/closing of the Senior Center when it is rented
for private meetings and events. Mayor Moriconi stated the City Clerk was in
the process of a job description and pay scale. Attorney Jed Deters stated he
would draft an ordinance to create this position. Council Member Behler asked
why the city was not remaining with the contracted personnel that is currently
performing these duties at the Senior Center. Chief Butler stated there has
been an issue raised regarding overtime pay for a city employee and that Owings
Construction, who had assisted with the opening/closing of the Senior Center
when the director was unavailable has advised the city they will no longer
supply this service. He stated it might be more economical to hire a part-time
employee to perform the maintenance of both buildings and assist with the
openings/closings. Council Member Dupps asked if the job duties would include
cleaning the park shelter restroom facilities. Mayor Moriconi stated that the
Public Works Department would take over that job. Council Member Dupps asked if
the intent is to pay a part-time employee to be available 24/7, without the
added benefit of fringe benefits. Chief Butler stated the Senior and Community
Center is rented every weekend and there are events taking place there every
night so this would be a cost savings for the city. Mayor Moriconi stated the
consensus seems to be to move forward with the creation of this position.
City Attorney Report
Mr. Deters advised he did not have anything to report.
Police Chief Report
Chief Butler advised he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Moriconi asked Council Member Behler whom she had selected to receive the
Business Recognition for the month of July. Council Member Behler stated she
would like to recognize Chambers and Grubbs Funeral Home.
Mayor Moriconi stated the next scheduled council meeting will be cancelled and
the caucus business meeting will be held on July 19, 2004 at the Senior and
Community Center.
Discussion Regarding the Decision by Kenton County to Discontinue Maintaining
County Roads in City Limits
Mayor Moriconi stated he was just advised about two hours ago that the county
has decided they would no longer maintain county roads that are located within
city boundaries. He stated this information is according to the county
attorney. Chief Butler stated he received verbal notice today, and that a
formal (written) notice has not been sent to the city yet. He stated that the
county attorney, Garry Edmondson is recommending the Kenton County Fiscal Court
take action to discontinue maintaining all county roads that run through any
incorporated city boundary based on a recent court ruling. Chief Butler stated
he believes this could become a legal issue, as it would be devastating to our
budget, as well as other cities. Council Member Behler asked if any other
cities are involved in this issue. Chief Butler stated they were. City Attorney
Jed Deters stated that in his opinion the case being cited is a “real stretch”
and did not feel it would “fly”. Council Member Brinker stated Independence
stands to be hurt the most due to being the largest city in Northern Kentucky.
Chief Butler stated there are many county roads in the city. He added that it
is believed the original intent of the court ruling is that county roads
annexed into the city limits it the future would be subject to city
maintenance. City Attorney Deters stated should this become a lawsuit against
the county that one or two attorneys should represent all of the cities.
Council Member Dupps asked if KLC could provide any input. Mayor Moriconi
stated he would continue to check into this matter and provide updates to
council. Council Member Behler asked how many miles of county roads are located
in the city limits. Chief Butler stated he would have Public Works do a count.
Discussion Regarding TransCare ALS (Advanced Life Support) Services
Mayor Moriconi stated the next issue for discussion is the Advanced Life
Support (ALS) issue. He stated this issue has been a topic of discussion over
the last two years between TransCare and city and county officials. Mayor
Moriconi asked if council was interested in funding a temporary fix for the
next six t twelve months until a permanent solution can be made regarding this
service. Council Member Bushong asked what the approximate cost would be. Chief
Butler stated it would cost approximately $77,000.00. Council Member Yeager
asked what the Independence Fire District contribution would be. Chief Butler
sated as of July 1, 2004, ALS will no longer service Independence. Chief Butler
stated he spoke to the Fire District and they have stated they will not split
this expense with the city. He stated TransCare is signing with several cities.
He stated that over the last two years many proposals have been discussed
regarding the best way to handle this service to the residents, as well as a
way to fund the cost of the service. He stated Erlanger and Elsmere will remain
until February when they will start their own. Council Member Yeager asked if
Covington would temporarily fund this service with TransCare until February
when they will launch their own. Chief Butler stated legislation is involved as
to whether another district can come into the county. Chief Butler stated if
the city opts to do this, and if the fire department implements this program,
then we could ask them for reimbursement. Council Member Bushong asked if
TransCare will not do for less than one year. Chief Butler stated this is a one
year deal and it may be revisited next year but this will allow the
continuation of service until the issue is decided. Council Member Brinker
asked how many runs are done in the city. Chief Butler stated it would be
difficult to obtain that information because that data is lumped in with other
cities. Council Member Brinker stated the city might need to do a public
hearing to get citizen input. Chief Butler stated there is not time for a
public hearing, and council needs to decide tonight. Council Member Yeager
stated she would prefer an agreement with the Independence Fire Department. Mr.
Kudera stated the tax has not been approved but there could be a void in
service. He stated the fire department will not have this service up and
running for a while. Chief Butler stated there could be a six to seven month
span where the city would be without service. Mr. Kudera stated the city does
not have a good ALS service until we have our own. Council Member Yeager asked
what would be the cost. Mr. Kudera stated this is not a simple process but they
are working on numbers and cannot make a commitment at this time. Chief Butler
stated the issue may be revisited next year but this will allow continuation of
service until the issues are decided. Council Member Behler stated this is a
service to the citizens and Chief Butler concurred, but felt the fire
department should be responsible for the ALS service. Mayor Moriconi stated he
approached the fire department twice and both times requested they pay half.
Mr. Kudera stated the fire department does not have to provide medical service
as they are classified as fire protection. Mr. Kudera stated if the tax passes
and there is a voter recall, the fire department will not realize the funds to
fund ALS and they may not be able to do. Chief Butler asked council if they
wanted to provide this service to the citizens. Council Member Yeager stated
this will be hard to explain to the citizens. Mayor Moriconi stated Council
Member Brinker brings up a good point that St. Elizabeth is not able to provide
this service when they have a huge expansion and decorate plus one-million
dollars to Gateway. Council Member Brinker asked if citizens subscribe for this
service. Council Member Behler asked if the fire department would still provide
ambulance service. Mr. Kudera stated the fire department will still have EMT’s,
just not paramedics. Mr. Kudera stated in July, 2002 TransCare made a proposal
to the Mayor’s Group and Kenton County Fiscal Court and they are still no
closer to a solution. Mayor Moriconi stated they passed a Resolution to put
this on the ballot but then it was decided not to put it before the voters.
Council Member Yeager stated hopefully the fire department will decide to
provide this in the near future. Mayor Moriconi stated for July 1, 2004 thru
June 30, 2005 the city will remain with TransCare and will check on the current
cost to provide this service. Council Member Brinker stated that you can’t put
a price on a person’s life, and does not like that the city has fund this, but
we will have to find money to provide this service to the citizens. Mayor
Moriconi stated this is a very important issue and he will bring numbers back
to council.
Citizen Comments
Leon Myers, 10805 Autumnridge Drive stated that EMT’s do not have the authority
to administer drugs and feels the city must supply this service to the
citizens.
Marcus Cook, Carrie Way asked if the city could be sued if they don’t provide
this service and someone dies. Mr. Deters stated the city has immunity.
George Sanders, 5268 Pioneer Drive asked if the fire department has ever lost a
life. Mr. Kudera stated he has no statistics on that information. Mr. Sanders
stated the city needs to find a way to assist the fire department.
Chief Butler stated everyone would like to have this service; so does the city
provide no ALS service or enter a one year contract with TransCare. Council
Member Dupps stated he is concerned with issues that could arise later on if
the city agrees to this and then discovers the charge for this service is out
of sight. Mr. Kudera stated this is a community problem and the issue is bigger
than just providing paramedic services to a stroke victim. He stated the fire
department will be meeting on June 30th to look at their budget and are
postponing other agenda items to discuss the ALS issue earlier. Chief Butler
asked if the Fire Board passes this tax, would they come back and negotiate
this service with the city. Mr. Kudera stated he will take these questions to
the Fire Board. Mr. Kudera stated the Fire Board has $300,000 in reserves and
they refuse to touch this money. He stated they also have to consider the
unincorporated areas covered by the Fire District. Council Member Bushong asked
if the $77,000.00 includes providing ALS service to the unincorporated areas.
Chief Butler stated that would be provided by the county. Mayor Moriconi stated
the county is out of this. He stated this service is only for the cities. He
stated he would get a firm money figure and advise council members to get a
consensus. Mr. Deters stated they could ratify this at the next regular
meeting. Council Member Bushong asked where in the budget the money would come
from. Chief Butler stated they would have to make even deeper cuts in the
current budget. Mayor Moriconi stated the money would be taken from the reserve
account if necessary. Council Member Brinker asked how they arrived at the
city’s fair share. Chief Butler stated it was based on population. He stated if
any of the cities drop out, the remaining cities shares get higher.
Discussion Regarding the Senior Center Gaming License
Council Member Yeager announced she has obtained the gaming permit for the
Senior Center. Mayor Moriconi complimented Council Member Yeager, City Clerk,
Patricia Taney and staff. Council Member Yeager stated they should have pull-
tabs available for the July 4th Celebration events on July 2nd and 3rd. She
stated the Senior Center Board of Directors and senior volunteers would begin
the process of establishing a Bingo as well as holding 50/50 raffles at the
various senior events. Mrs. Joann Cobble advised of the state requirement to
keep accurate figures to report. Council Member Yeager stated, Pat Walton will
chair the committee and will speak with representatives of St Cecelia Church
that will assist them with establishing the Bingo. Council Member Behler stated
that she recalls at the last meeting council discussed the gaming license and
she was under the impression that members of the Senior Board of Directors
would be invited to speak with council regarding this new venture. Council
Member Brinker stated it might be hard for some of the Board members to attend
evening meetings. Council Member Yeager stated the next Senior Board meeting is
June 22, 2004 in the morning. Council Member Yeager expressed confidence that
the Senior Board would feel more financially independent now that they have
received the gaming license, thus having a viable way to raise their own
revenue. Council Member Behler stated that many of the seniors have expressed
that they feel the Senior Board is not supporting them. Mayor Moriconi stated
some of the board members have not taken active roles on the Board have poor
meeting attendance records. Council Member Behler stated she did not understand
why the board members do not contribute more. Council Member Yeager stated
maybe the meetings should be changed from mornings to evenings. Council Member
Behler stated the seniors need a Board that is going to actively participate in
the success of the Center and she hopes these discussions will continue.
Adjournment
There being no further business, motion was made by Council Member Bushong and
seconded by Council Member Behler to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:22 p.m.

July 19, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 19,
2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor,
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker,
Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager answered roll call.
Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Michelle Herrman, 345 Webster Road, Independence stated that she would like to
address the zone change request by Wolsing, Hasekoester-Reese, LLC for property
located along Independence Station, Webster and Cody Roads. She requested the
opportunity to reserve her comments until have they made their presentation to
council. Mayor Moriconi granted this request.
Mr. Deters advised council they would be able to ask questions of the
developer, but reminded them this is not a public hearing forum and that new
evidence that was not heard at the official public hearing held by the Kenton
County Planning Commission could not be presented. Mr. Deters asked Mrs.
Herrman if she spoke at the public hearing, she replied that she did. Mayor
Moriconi advised council to limit the discussion to the Planning Commission’s
recommendation to the city.
Sherry Carran, 927 Forest, Covington, Kentucky stated that Mr. Jim Berling
asked her to share the comments that she made the Kenton County Planning
Commission’s public hearing regarding the Wolsing, Hasekoester-Reese, LLC
development on Independence Station Road. She stated she spoke in favor of the
development plan. Again, Mr. Deters advised that all discussion should pertain
to the Planning Commission’s recommendation. Mayor Moriconi stated the matter
was on the agenda and would be discussed later.
Discussion Relating to an Addition to the - Freedom Park Subdivision
Annexation/Zone Change for Mullins Property, 11527 Wilson Road – KCPC
Application No. 1682R
Mayor Moriconi presented for discussion a zoning recommendation the city has
received from the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) for property located
at 11527 Wilson Road upon annexation by the city. He stated that Mr. Mike
Duncan and Mr. Erpenbeck were present to answer questions council may have
regarding this recommendation.
Mr. Duncan stated that the developer is requesting voluntary annexation of the
Wilson Road property into the city limits, as this will be an extension of the
Freedom Park Subdivision, which is currently within the city boundaries. He
stated it makes sense to have the entire subdivision within city limits. He
stated the recommendation by the Planning Commission suggests the property be
zoned R-1D as part of the annexation process.
Council Member Behler asked if another access road would be constructed for
this development, as currently Oby Drive is the only egress for the
subdivision. Mr. Duncan advised that eventually there will be access to Wilson
Road, as they have that land under contract to purchase in the future, but the
development will not begin in that area.
Council Member Yeager asked if they could establish a gravel road during the
construction phase so that the heavy equipment could access the construction
sites instead of using Freedom Trail and Oby Drive, which is so narrow. She
expressed concern for the children playing on Oby Drive. Mr. Erpenbeck stated
they had not considered and does not anticipate it would be a problem, but that
he would review this request to see it a temporary egress could be installed.
Regarding lot sizes, Mr. Duncan advised they had requested an R-1D zone so they
could build 70-foot lots. He stated that the NKAPC staff recommendation was for
an R-1C (PUD), which would permit the flexibility, the developer request. Mr.
Duncan stated this zone would allow fifty foot lots with twenty-percent of the
development left as green space. He stated the green space could be maintained
by either a homeowners’ association or the city and he has the senses the city
does not want the maintenance of more green space. He stated that the Planning
Commission expressed concern about the area along the creek but they will
designate the area as a conservation easement. Either way, Mr. Duncan said they
would be willing to work within the requirement of an R-1C zone as they like
the flexibility this zone would provide. He advised that they propose a
development plan of 3.02 net units per acre, with forty-one 80-foot lots and no
lots lower than 70 foot. Council Member Yeager asked the lot sizes currently in
’’’’Freedom’ ’’Park’’ subdivision. Mayor Moriconi stated the lot sizes are 80
foot. Mr. Duncan advised the development will limit the number of lots to 156,
which is less density than is allowed. He stated that some people do not want
big lots to maintain and they wish to satisfy the needs of those buyers. He
stated the smallest lot will be 70 feet and they feel this mix of lot sizes
will strike a good balance.
Council Member Bushong stated that callers have expressed to him a desire to
keep the minimum lot size at 80 feet continuing the uniformity of the
subdivision. Council Member Behler asked if the callers understood the
developer would be building fewer homes than permitted. Council Member Bushong
stated the callers are adamant the lot size should not be less than 80 feet.
Council Member Franzen asked if they would be willing to revise the plan to
develop more of the 80-foot lots. Mr. Duncan commented they have the irregular
topography to deal with that would make it difficult. Mr. Tom Schreiber, one of
the developers, commented that all the houses planned for this development
could easily fit on a 70-foot lot. Council Member Franzen expressed concern
regarding the minimum space between each house regardless of whether it is a
ranch or 2-story structure. Mr. Duncan stated that the R-1C zone requires 20-
feet total between houses.
Council Member Behler stated she wonders if others have concerns regarding the
aesthetics or change in the configuration of the neighborhood. Council Member
Dupps commented that is typically a density concern but that doesn’t apply in
this situation.
Mr. Duncan stated the developers would discuss making the changes that council
has suggested: a temporary access road for the construction vehicles, spacing
between the houses and lot sizes. He stated that they have the terrain of the
property to consider. Council Member Yeager stated she would like to see more
80-foot lots on the same number (156) of planned lots. Mr. Duncan stated they
would loose a third of the planned houses if they would increase all the lot
sizes to 80 foot.
Council Member Dupps expressed concern about a detention pond on the other side
of the development. Mr. Erpenbeck advised they would take that under
consideration when they get into the design phase of the project.
Mr. Duncan stated that the Planning Commission has placed five conditions on
the zone change. Those conditions include: a maximum of 156 lots, a maximum
density of 3.02 dwelling units per net acre, a minimum of 41 lots with 80 foot
frontage at the setback line, no lots under 70 foot frontage and there is to be
a 200 foot conservation easement placed along the stream within the site. Mayor
Moriconi asked who would maintain the conservation easement. Mr. Duncan advised
the property owner would have that responsibility.
Mayor Moriconi advised a proposed ordinance for the zone change would be
presented for a first reading at the August 2nd council meeting. He stated that
a vote is not usually taken on the first reading of a proposed ordinance, but
in this case he may call for a vote to see if there is interest in moving
forward for a second reading and enactment. In closing, Mr. Duncan stated he
would consult with the developers and afterward contact Mayor Moriconi
regarding council’s changes/suggestions they may be able to satisfy.
Discussion Regarding a Map Amendment for Property Located on Independence
Station Road by Wolsing & Hasekoester-Reese LLC – KCPC Application No. 1683R
Mayor Moriconi presented for discussion a recommendation the city has received
from the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) for a zone change request by
Mr. Jim Berling, on behalf of George and Laverne Wolsing and Hasekoester-Reese,
LLC for a 170-acre parcel located on Independence Station Road between Webster
Road and Cody Road. He stated that Mr. Marty Butler and Mr. Jim Berling were
present to answer questions council may have regarding this zone change. Mayor
Moriconi advised that the KCPC has recommended the property be changed from an
R-1C to an R-1C (PUD), subject to nine conditions.
Mr. Marty Butler distributed copies of the packets that were provided to the
KCPC at the public hearing. He stated the maximum number of homes in this
development will be 415 with 33% of the subdivision designated as open green
space, which addresses the concerns of the conservationists. Mayor Moriconi
advised that he has informed the developers that the city has currently reached
the maximum number of parks that we are able to maintain. Council Member
Brinker concurred that the city could not afford to maintain another park. Mr.
Butler stated they have approached Kenton County to see if they are interested
in maintaining this area as a park. Council Member Yeager commented that if the
county does not want the land and it would become the responsibility of a
homeowners’ association, she would like the deed to delegate the property to
the city in the event that the homeowners’ association would dissolve. Council
Member Behler suggested it would be better to establish a homeowners’
association that would impose property assessments and provide professional
management. She also suggested hillside trusts to ensure the conservation
easements remain in their natural state. Mr. Butler stated that, owner George
Wolsing has expressed his desire that the 100-year-old trees be preserved as
part of a naturalist park area.
Council Member Dupps expressed concern regarding access roads for this
development. Mr. Butler commented that concern has been addressed. Mr. Jim
Berling advised they met with John Scheben to address the access roads and they
have developed a loop system within the development.
Mayor Moriconi advised a proposed ordinance would be drafted for presentation
at the August 2nd meeting for a first reading.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Ordinance that would Create a Building
Custodian Position and Job Description
Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed ordinance that will create the position of
part-time building custodian. He advised this position would be responsible for
the cleaning and maintenance of the Senior/Community Center and the new
Municipal Center, as well as assist with the opening and closing of the Senior/
Community Center when it is rented for events. Council Member Bushong asked how
much assistance would be provided to the Senior/Community Center for the
opening and closing of the building and how that would be specified in the job
description. Chief Butler stated this position would assist Nita Brake about
fifty percent of the time and that it would be by mutual arrangement. He stated
the person hired for this position would have to be able to offer the city
flexible working hours. Council Member Yeager stated the working hours should
be specified in the classified advertisement to fill this position. She
wondered if they could find a person to work ten hours per week. Mrs. Taney,
City Clerk advised that it is estimated that this position would be working 20-
25 hours per week, with no benefits other than retirement. Chief Butler
commented that bringing this position in house should be less expensive than
the current outsourcing for this service.
Mayor Moriconi advised this ordinance would be placed on the August 2nd agenda
for a first reading.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Ordinance to Amend the Personnel and Pay
Classification Plan to Add the Position of Part-Time Building Custodian
Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed ordinance that will amend the current pay
plan to add the position of part-time Building Custodian and setting the
minimum and maximum pay range. Council Member Behler asked if a salary
comparison was performed for this position. Mrs. Taney advised that a
comparison was not done but that she could ask the Northern Kentucky Area
Development District if they had information on this position.
Chief Butler advised that he would like to amend the minimum salary range for
the Public Works maintenance worker position, as it is a little higher than it
should be. No objections were noted from the council members to this change.
Mayor Moriconi advised this ordinance would be placed on the August 2nd agenda
for a first reading.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Ordinance to Accept Regal Ridge Drive as a City
Street for Maintenance Purposes
Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed ordinance that will accept Regal Ridge
Drive as a city street for maintenance purposes. He stated this would honor an
agreement between the developer and the city that was made last year when the
developer approached the city with a plan to construct several houses on the
street and stated he would bring the street up to construction code if the city
would accept it for future maintenance. Council Member Dupps asked if the City
Engineer has inspected the street. Mayor Moriconi confirmed that the City
Engineer had conducted a site visit in March and found some deficiencies in the
concrete curb, which he recommended should be replaced. He stated that the City
Engineer reinspected the site on June 16, 2004 and has reported that the curb
has been replaced according to subdivision regulations and did not notice any
further defects.
Mayor Moriconi advised this ordinance would be placed on the August 2nd agenda
for a first reading.
Discussion Regarding the Maintenance of County Roads Within the City Limits
Mayor Moriconi reported that the city has been notified by Kenton County that
they will immediately discontinue maintenance of county streets within
incorporated areas. He stated that the Public Works Department has conducted a
street audit of the county streets within Independence limits and have reported
there are fifteen miles of county roads in our city. Council Member Dupps asked
the total number including the city streets. Mayor Moriconi advised there are a
total of sixty-four miles of streets.
Chief Butler advised that he has requested this mandate in writing from Deputy
Judge Executive, Scott Kimmich as currently the city has only received a verbal
notice from the County Attorney. He reported that this situation has already
caused some problems regarding whose responsibility it is to remove dead
animals from the county roads, etc. He stated that a more serious problem would
be the closing of the Cody Road underpass during a flash flood, as the city
does not possess the keys needed to lock the floodgates. Chief Butler went on
to say that this mandate handed down from the county is going to have an
immediate impact on the city budget especially with the job of snow removal, as
the majority of the main roads in the city are county roads. He stated the
2004/05 budgets that was just passed has only allocated $50,000 for snow
removal and now the city is faced with the possibility of this amount doubling
before the end of winter.
Council Member Franzen stated she has spoken to county officials who indicate
they are willing to make a deal. Council Member Bushong stated he also has
spoken to county officials who stated the will continue to mow and deal with
slippage conditions on some of the roads.
Mayor Moriconi expressed a desire to request that Kenton County relinquish the
portion of taxes they collect that are allocated to the maintenance of roads
and give that money to the cities that will now be responsible for providing
this service to the residents. Mr. Deters, City Attorney, advised that a
portion of taxes collected by TANK (Transit Authority of Northern Kentucky)
goes toward the maintenance of roads. He stated that these funds should be
appropriated to the city as they cannot collect for roads they do not maintain.
Council Member Behler commented that she attended the Mayor’s Group meeting on
Saturday and it was suggested that all the city’s attorneys review the Kentucky
Supreme Court ruling that is being cited by Kenton County and give the mayors
an opinion. She stated it was also suggested that the cities collectively ask
the Attorney General for an opinion on this matter. Council Member Behler
stated that many feel that County Attorney Garry Edmondson has a loose
interpretation on this ruling by the Supreme Court. Mr. Deters stated that he
feels that may be the reason the city has not received this mandate in writing
yet from the county. Council Member Behler stated that the Mayor’s Group
discussed acting as a body to oppose this decision by the county. She stated
that the City of Taylor Mill has requested specific information from the county
with regard to which roads they are now expected to maintain, etc. She also
reported that the county has scheduled a meeting to discuss this matter with
city representatives for July 29, 2004, but that no one has been advised of the
time or location of the meeting.
Mr. Deters stated that he too feels the County Attorney has loosely interpreted
this court ruling. Mayor Moriconi stated that the county might now be able to
offset their deficit since they will not be expending funds for the maintenance
of roads within incorporated areas.
Council Member Franzen stated the city should look into the legality of the
state allocating municipal road aid to the county if they will no longer
provide maintenance to the streets in incorporated areas. She suggested city
officials schedule a meeting with county officials to work on an agreement.
Council Member Behler advised that the Mayor’s Group will be doing this;
representing all cities. Council Member Franzen suggested that council members
address the Fiscal Court at one of their meetings. Mayor Moriconi advised he
would provide updates to council as this matter progresses in an effort to keep
everyone informed. He stated he would learn more about the July 29th meeting
and let everyone know the details.
Discussion of Miscellaneous Matters
Council Member Behler commented that she feels it is important that the city
always have representation at the Mayor’s Group meetings and suggested a
rotation schedule for the council members. She stated she would like to see the
city more represented and perhaps a report could be provided to the entire
Council. Mayor Moriconi commented that the Mayor’s Group has had the same
agenda for the last year or so, mainly discussing the ALS issue. He stated he
would gladly provide everyone with a copy of the group’s meeting agenda and
instructed the City Clerk to copy the council members.
Council Member Bushong requested the council members be included on the website
comments routing list. Mayor Moriconi stated that he did not have a problem
with this if council would agree to not respond to the sender’s comments or
questions. He stated that multiple respondents with varying responses might
cause confusion to the person making the comment or inquiry. He advised that
currently he, Chief Butler or the City Clerk, gives answers and/or comments to
the senders. He stated he would instruct the website administrator to add the
six council members to the routing list.
Discussion Regarding the Calvary Road Survey Results
Mayor Moriconi advised that a survey was mailed to the residents on Calvary
Road to see if there was interest in changing the spelling to C-a-v-a-l-r-y in
keeping with the theme of the Battleridge Subdivision. Mrs. Taney reported that
of the seventy-four surveys mailed that forty were completed and returned to
the city. She stated that the overwhelming response was to keep the original
spelling of C-a-l-v-a-r-y. She advised that the survey respondents felt the
change would be problematic, inconvenient and costly. Mrs. Taney stated that
some residents had their address permanently etched into a cornerstone
installed on the brick of their house. The consensus of council was to keep the
original spelling as favored by the majority. Mrs. Taney stated she would send
a follow up letter to the Calvary Road residents to inform them of the survey
results and that new street signs would be installed.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Resolution Supporting Rumpke Corporation’s
“Slow Down to Get Around” Safety Campaign
Mayor Moriconi advised that Rumpke has approached the city with a request to
adopt a resolution supporting their “Slow Down to Get Around” safety campaign
they are promoting. Mrs. Taney stated that Rumpke has begun this campaign after
recent incidents where a couple of their trash collector truck drivers were
struck while on the job by passing motorists. This resulted in one fatality and
one serious injury. She stated this campaign is an effort to educate the
motoring public about safety standards and promote awareness to exercise
caution when passing all services workers, which include postal workers,
package delivery workers, municipal workers making repairs to the roadway and
other various service providers. Council Member Yeager commented that she feels
this is a good idea.
Mayor Moriconi stated the residents should be aware of this safety campaign and
it would be a good article for the city newsletter. He stated a resolution
supporting this would be presented at the August 2nd council meeting for
approval.
Discussion Regarding Proposed Regulations on Political Signs
Council Member Brinker introduced a discussion regarding regulations on
political signs. He stated the he feels that political signs should not be
erected prior to forty-five days before the Election Day. Mr. Deters stated
that he is not aware of city provisions on political signs except for the a
condition that the signs must be removed the day after the election. It stated
that a simple ordinance could be established to impose restrictions. Council
Member Yeager stated that she would like to see a 30-day provision on the
signs. Council Member Bushong stated that he feels 60 days would be more
appropriate with five days after the election to remove the signs. A brief
discussion ensued regarding the time frame needed over the next several weeks
to enact such an ordinance with a provision of a 45-day or 60 day period prior
to the general election in November. There was a consensus to move forward with
this type of legislation and the city attorney stated he would draft an
ordinance for council to consider at the August 2nd meeting.
Discussion Regarding Advanced Life Support (ALS) Services
Council Member Behler advised that the Mayor’s Group discussed the Independence
Fire District ‘s decision not to house the ALS personnel. She stated that she
feels the city should approach the Fire District to discuss an agreement for
the benefit of the citizens. Council Member Brinker stated he would like to
invite members of the Independence Fire District Board and ALS to a city caucus
meeting so that this matter can be discussed. Council Member Bushong commented
that the ALS issue was discussed for a year with an effort to arrive at a
solution for providing this service, including sleeping quarters for the
personnel.
Chief Butler suggested the city request the Independence Fire District to
assist the city, by paying half of the $68,000 the city has pledged to
contribute to ALS for continued service to the citizens. He stated that in
light of the Fire District’s recent increase in the tax rate they would be
imposing this year, which will double their current revenue. They concurred and
directed Mayor Moriconi to send a written request to the Fire District Board.
Council Member Franzen suggested council should communicate to the citizens
that the city council has no control over the tax rate that has been imposed by
the Fire District. Mayor Moriconi stated he would address this in the next city
newsletter.
Discussion Regarding the Bids Received for the Resurfacing of Walnut Hall Drive
Chief Butler advised council that six bids were received for the Walnut Hall
Drive resurfacing project. He stated that the low bidder was Barrett Paving
Materials at $90,299.75. He advised that Barrett has done work previously in
the city on Fleming Drive. Council Member Yeager commented that they did a good
job on Fleming Drive. Chief Butler stated that the City Engineer is
recommending that the bid be awarded to Barrett and council will be asked to
award the bid at the August 2nd meeting.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler reported that Patrol Office Greg Hallau has been called to active
military duty and will be leaving for Kuwait this weekend.
Chief Butler reported that he has purchased a new computer software program for
the Public Works Department that will provide for online complaint forms and
track complaints.
Chief Butler reported that on July 14, 2004 the police department received
their re-accreditation for a second 5-year term.
Community Yard Sale
Council Member Dupps announced he is organizing a citywide community yard sale,
which is scheduled for September 11, and 12, 2004.
Discussion Regarding a Road Tax
Council Member Behler suggested the city look into establishing a road tax to
fund the maintenance of the county roads that the city is now being expected to
care for. Mr. Deters advised that since the city has not received written
notice from the county that it may be premature to take this kind of action.
Council Member Behler advised that the City of Taylor Mill has already had a
first reading of a road tax ordinance. She stated that if the city wants to
proceed with proposing a road tax to the voters that there is a deadline for
this information to be delivered to the County Clerk. Mr. Deters advised he
would speak with the city attorney for Taylor Mill to obtain some information.
Proposed Resolution Supporting the Reauthorization of a Federal Six Year
Surface Transportation Bill – (TEA-21 Grant)
Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed resolution for council’s consideration that
would request the U.S. Congress to pass, and the President to sign a six-year
transportation reauthorization bill that would be no less than $318 billion. He
stated these funds are used to improve the nation’s transportation
infrastructure. He asked council to review the proposed resolution and advised
it would be put on the August 2nd agenda.
Resolution Honoring Former President Ronald W. Reagan
Council Member Franzen stated that she has been approached by a City of Fort
Wright council member who is requesting the city pass a resolution honoring
former President Ronald W. Reagan. Council Member Brinker requested she obtain
a copy for council to consider passing.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Yeager moved to adjourn,
seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes and the
meeting ended at 8:48 pm.

July 19, 2004
Special Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
of the Council on Monday, July 19, 2004 at 6:45 pm in the Senior Citizens and
Community Center, 2001 Jack Woods Parkway in Independence with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps,
Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced that this special meeting of the city council was
called to discuss and possibly take action on the following agenda items:
·   A lease-purchase agreement with Fifth Third Bank for the purchase of four
police cruisers and a Public Works truck and other equipment
·   Award the bid of the Park and Lawn maintenance contract
Lease-Purchase Agreement with Fifth Third Bank for Cruisers & Public Works
Equipment
Chief Butler presented to council two separate tax-exempt lease-purchase
financing agreement proposals from Fifth Third Bank. He stated the first
agreement is for the purchase of four police cruisers in the amount of
$83,019.36 ($20,754.84 per vehicle) for a lease period of 36 months at a 3.86%
interest rate. He stated that Assistant Chief Dave Nichols handled the vehicle
purchase and was able to acquire them at an excellent rate, saving $2,000 on
each. Chief Butler stated that the second lease purchase total was for
$65,275.00 for a Public Works truck ($47,345), bobcat and trailer. He stated
this was a 48-month lease at a 4.10% interest rate.
Chief Butler requested that council authorize Mayor Moriconi to enter into
these financing agreements with Fifth Third Bank.
Council Member Yeager moved to authorize Mayor Moriconi to execute the
financing agreements for the purchase of the four cruisers and the public works
truck and equipment, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Award of the Bid of the Park and Lawn Maintenance Contract
Mayor Moriconi advised that the city received four bids for the lawn and park
maintenance. He stated that the bid that is awarded would be for a two-year
contract period with the option of a two-year extension. Bids were received
from Professional LawnCare, Gary Adams, Multi Service Group and Malco Services.
Council Member Brinker commented that he recently observed Malco working in the
parks over the last couple of weeks and they appeared to be good workers with a
genuine interest in the city. He stated that if the city is not able to have
city employees perform this job that it’s good to have a city resident awarded
the contract.
Council Member Behler moved to award the lawn/park maintenance contract to
Malco Services, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to adjourn.
Council Member Bushong so moved, with second from Council Member Yeager. Motion
carried with all ayes.

August 2, 2004
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 2,
2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance led by Cub Scout Troop 808, Den 12. Mayor
Moriconi presented the Troop with city maps and lapel pins. Council Member
Bushong gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps,
Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Recognition
Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member Mary Pat Behler had chosen
Chambers and Grubbs Funeral Home as the recipient for the Business of the Month
Plaque. Mr. Chris Grubbs thanked mayor and council for the recognition and
stated it was an honor. Mr. Grubbs stated they have been operating in
Independence since 1963 and plan on enlarging the funeral home and add
additional services for the residents in the future. Council Member Yeager
asked that it be noted that Mr. Grubbs also serves on the Senior Board of
Directors.
Approval of Minutes for June 7, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting.
Council Member Bushong so moved, with a second by Council Member Dupps as
amended. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of Minutes for June 21, 2004 Caucus Council Meeting
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting.
Council Member Behler so moved with a second by Council Member Bushong as
amended. Roll call was answered and Council Member Franzen passed. Motion
carried 5-1.
Approval of Minutes for July 19, 2004 Special Council Meeting
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting.
Council Member Behler so moved with a second by Council Member Franzen. Roll
call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of Minutes for July 19, 2004 Caucus Council Meeting
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the meeting.
Council Member Bushong so moved with a second by Council Member Franzen as
amended. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi requested that everyone addressing council keep his or her
speech limited to three minutes due to a full agenda.
Mrs. Joanne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike asked Mayor Moriconi if she could take
seven minutes to make her speech. Mayor Moriconi advised Mrs. Cobble she would
have three minutes to address council. Mrs. Cobble, in her speech read the
first amendment rights, freedom of speech and cited court cases regarding
political signs. Mayor Moriconi thanked Mrs. Cobble. Mr. Deters asked Mrs.
Cobble if she has threatened litigation against the city. Mrs. Cobble stated
that was true. Mr. Deters stated he should have advised her not to speak but
that would not have done any good. Mrs. Cobble stated the quote in the

Annexation Request-Maher Road Development
Mayor Moriconi stated Bayer and Becker is requesting annexation of property
located off Maher Road, which consists of fifty-five acres with the
construction of new homes starting at $200,000.00 and up, are making this
request. Mayor Moriconi stated they have not been before NKAPC but first wanted
to see if the city supports this annexation before it goes before NKAPC for a
zone recommendation. Council Member Yeager asked if the city has any property
on Maher Road at this time. Mayor Moriconi stated the city does. Council Member
Franzen asked Mr. Deters if council was legally permitted to discuss this
issue. Mr. Deters stated this request is only for annexation, so anything in
that regard is permitted. Council Member Franzen stated she is not opposed to
more growth in the city but the city has more than it can support now. Council
Member Behler stated there are still a lot of areas within the city limits that
could be developed. Council Member Bushong stated he feels it should go to the
Planning Commission before council agrees or disagrees with the annexation
request. Council Member Yeager asked who the owner of record is for this
property. Mayor Moriconi stated the name “Parker” is in the letter from Bayer
and Becker. Council Member Franzen stated the property they want to annex has
to be connected with the city but does not see where it would connect to any
city property. Mr. Deters stated this property is abutting city property on the
north side which does make it contiguous, so it could be annexed into the city.
Council Member Dupps stated he did not feel the city can continue to annex
property and not gain anything from the tax receipts that will pay for the
services the city would provide. Council Member Franzen stated it appears it
would put the city in more of a financial bind. Council Member Yeager stated
she does not have enough information to make a decision. Mayor Moriconi stated
Area Planning will kick it back to the city eventually for the annexation. Mr.
Deters stated Area Planning will only suggest what the appropriate zoning
should be so it can be changed during the annexation process. Mayor Moriconi
stated since there are different opinions then maybe it should go to the
Planning Commission first. Council Member Brinker stated they are the
professionals for these matters and we should wait for their recommendation.
Council Member Franzen stated that regardless of the zone it will still be
residential property for which the city would have to provide services.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Gephardt from Bayer Becker engineering firm if he
would like to speak. Mr. Gephardt stated the plans are very preliminary at this
time and they are in the process of creating a plat. He stated the developer
just wants to get council opinion regarding their request for annexation into
the city. Council Member Brinker expressed concern that council might be
setting precedent for the future and council needs to decide which way they are
going to go. Council Member Bushong asked Mayor Moriconi if he wants an opinion
or a vote from council. Mayor Moriconi stated they just wanted to see if the
majority of council favored the annexation. Council Member Bushong stated the
city is already looking for financial ways to pay for the roads that county
wants to turn over to the city. He stated he would be against any annexations
at this time. Council Member Yeager stated that is why she asked if the city
has any property on Maher Road. Council Member Franzen stated that she did not
think Maher Road was one of the roads included in the list from the county that
we now have to maintain. She stated she did not think the city had any property
on Maher Road. Mayor Moriconi stated Glenhurst Subdivision was on Maher Road.
Mr. Deters stated he has not received anything in writing as of yet. Council
Member Yeager asked Mr. Gephardt if they could discuss this again at the August
Caucus Meeting. Mr. Gephardt stated he was not sure of the nature of the
developer’s contracts and negotiations with the owners but time is of the
essence and that is why they wanted to get council opinion as soon as possible.
Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Gephardt if there was a reason they did not
want to build in unincorporated Kenton County. Mr. Gephardt stated he was not
sure.
Mr. David Rabe, 529 Independence Station Rd asked if the (56) fifty-six acres
with one hundred-twenty (120) homes at (12,500) twelve-thousand five-hundred
square feet, is consistent with the current zoning. Mayor Moriconi stated that
is what the Planning Commission will tell them. Mr. Rabe stated Mr. Gephardt,
an engineer, already knows what the existing zoning for that property is and he
knows if it is(12,500) twelve-thousand five-hundred square feet. Mayor Moriconi
stated the acreage at this time is zoned agriculture. Mayor Moriconi advised
that it appears that four members on council do not wish to annex this
property. Council Member Franzen stated they are just letting him know so he
can decide if he wants to move forward with the zoning issue. Mayor Moriconi
stated they will need a zone change from the city or the county.

Proposed Ordinance-Map Amendment of 170 acres on Independence Station Road-1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading for a map amendment for
170 acres on Independence Station Road. Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters to read
the ordinance. Council Member Yeager stated it was brought to her attention
that some of the lots did not meet the zoning requirements of (12,500) twelve-
thousand five-hundred square feet. Mr. Dave Rabe residing at 529 Independence
Station Road stated there are no lots in this development that meet the
existing zoning of (12,500) twelve-thousand five-hundred square feet, but
(12,000) twelve-thousand square feet. He stated there are (416) four-hundred
sixteen homes that do not meet the present zoning and there are (163) one-
hundred sixty three lots that are (50) fifty-feet wide. He stated he resides
between Independence Station Road and Cody Road and that section of the land
does not have any lots close to that size. He stated he could not understand
why the city would want to lower the zoning requirements to make it less than
the existing (12,500) twelve-thousand five-hundred square feet. Mr. Rabe stated
there are already enough starter homes in Independence. Mr. Rabe stated he has
no problem with building on lots of (12,500) square feet, but a (50) fifty-foot
lot only has (25) twenty-five feet of front yard. He stated the planning
commission passed this zoning, but he feels there is no planning regarding
traffic or lights.
Mr. Tom List, 5005 McHugh Lane stated his property is located at the very
bottom of the development and he would like a “stub” to come down on to his
property so in the future if he opts to develop this land, this will enable him
to do so. He stated if there are no park land set aside for this development
then he feels that each home needs one-half acre of ground for children to
play.
Council Member Brinker asked if the map amendment has been to the Planning
Commission for their recommendation. Mayor Moriconi stated it has. He asked if
council turns this down, does the developer have other options. Mr. Deters
stated council can hold its own public hearing and have different findings or
the majority can overrule the Planning Commission’s recommendations. Mr. Martin
Butler stated it was the recommendation of the Planning Commission that they
look at the R-1C PUD as opposed to the R-1C. He stated this property is
currently zoned R-1C, and under the R-1C zone you are permitted 3.5 units per
acre. The net of right of way for this development, without a park area is
(150) one-hundred fifty acres that would allow (525) five-hundred twenty-five
lots without the park. He stated they are only asking for (416) four-hundred
sixteen homes. He stated if you look at the traffic issues, there will be (100)
one-hundred plus units less than they are proposing for the development. He
stated the average square footage per lot, if you take into the park is over
(15,000) fifteen-thousand square feet per lot. He stated because of the nature
of a PUD development, when you do a diversity of lots, given the parks and
given the open areas, that you come up with these numbers, but the numbers
aren’t really what is being presented. When you look at the net affect of the
park taken into consideration, you then have an access of (15,000) fifteen-
thousand square feet. He stated two parking spaces have been committed for each
lot. Council Member Yeager asked if there has been any thought to increasing
the size of the (50) fifty-foot lots. Mr. Butler stated economically, if you
are going to give the acreage that is being allotted to for green space, which
is (58) fifty-eight acres that will be totally undeveloped. Council Member
Yeager stated she wanted to make it clear if the map amendment is passed, and
the Homeowners Association or the company handling the association goes
bankrupt, that the park area would be added to the deed that the land would
revert back to Mr.& Mrs. Wolsing. Mr. Butler stated they will be able to come
up with covenants that city council could review and be comfortable with that
would not necessitate the property reverting back to the Wolsing’s. Mr. Deters
stated the city had one Homeowners Association go defunct and the city did not
have any easements to do what they needed to do on the property. Council Member
Bushong asked if this was going to be a bona fide Homeowners Association that
will maintain the green space and park. Mr. Butler stated the current proposal
has an area between the public-park, and residential area to create a buffer.
That area would clearly be the responsibility of the Homeowners Association.
There would not be any maintenance in that area because the intent is to keep
that area as a natural space. Mr. Butler stated Mr. Wolsing wants to keep the
green space area natural for walking, and bird and animal observation. He
stated the Wolsing Park area would be the responsibility of the county or the
Conservancy. Mr. Rabe stated that it was noted at the Planning Commission
meeting that “we” do not want this development to go through unless the City of
Independence or Kenton County will fix up and maintain the park area forever.
Mr. Rabe stated he was at that meeting, and he can get a tape of the meeting.
Mr. Rabe stated the park area is in a flood zone. Mayor Moriconi stated the
developer did approach the city regarding a park and they were advised the city
does not need anymore parks right now. He stated that Mr. Butler said they
would go to Kenton County and ask if they would maintain this park. Council
Member Yeager asked if they did go to county and were they told that the county
will maintain the park. Mr. Butler stated there have been several meetings with
the county and discussions are still proceeding with questions as to whether
the county will maintain the property or whether it will be dedicated to the
Conservancy. Mr. Butler stated this is consistent with the park link design the
Planning Commission has been promoting for years.
Mayor Moriconi advised this proposed ordinance will come back for a second
reading in September. Council Member Brinker asked if the city will have it in
writing if the county will maintain or a conservatorship is established, and
what their responsibilities will be to maintain the park. Mr. Butler stated
they will put that in writing and will present a proposal on the restrictions
for the green space and also the park. Council Member Behler stated she also
has concerns regarding how much added traffic this is going to add to
Independence Station Road. She stated at this point she is not sure what can be
done about it but does feel the city needs a City Planner to help make
recommendations on these sorts of problems. Mr. Rabe stated that council has
everything to do with it. He stated you as a council can either let it go
through or you can keep the lot size at (12,500) twelve-thousand five-hundred
square feet that the surrounding residents can live with. He stated (416) four-
hundred sixteen homes cannot be built in this area because it is a flood zone
and that is why they are leaving it as a park because nothing else can be done
with it.
Proposed Ordinance-Creating Position of Part-Time Building Custodian-1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance creating a part-time
building custodian position. Council Member Yeager stated she did not feel a
custodian should be responsible for the removal of spoiled food or wiping out
refrigerators. She stated each department should be responsible for their own
food disposal. She also stated that the custodian should not have to wash
dishes. She stated that sweeping of sidewalks and keeping entrances clear was
okay but picking up litter in the parking area and plant islands, should be one
of the Public Works duties. She stated they will be responsible for the
opening, closing, setting up and tearing down of tables and chairs at the
Senior Center. She stated that she checked into the lifting of objects of less
than 25 pounds and found that either a woman or man must be able to pick up 70
pounds but was okay to leave at 50 pounds. Council Member Franzen stated she
was not sure it was the Public Works responsibility to pick up trash in the
parking area and felt it would come under the Custodian Job Description. Mayor
Moriconi stated to just leave it in there will leave it open so everybody can
pitch in and help if someone was busy. Council Member Bushong stated since this
was a new job for the city they need to come up with a basic description and it
can be amended as needed. Mayor Moriconi stated some of the changes can be made
at this meeting before Mr. Deters does a first reading. Council Member Brinker
stated since this person will report to the City Clerk, she should be able to
use common sense and determine what modifications need to be made instead of
coming to council. Council Member Yeager stated she did not know who would
supervise this position. Mayor Moriconi stated it would be the City Clerk.
Council Member Franzen stated this is only a part-time position and there will
be a limit to how much this person can get done. Council Member Yeager stated
when the job is advertised, there should be a minimum of (24) twenty-four hours
worked each week. Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters to read the ordinance as
amended.

Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance amending Ordinance No.

the ordinance. Mr. Deters read the ordinance in its entirety. Mayor Moriconi
stated the original ordinance was established to keep gang mailboxes from being

mailboxes. Mr. Deters stated there is a “grandfather clause” built in under
Section II that states,” any future installation will continue to be
prohibited.”
Proposed Ordinance-Levying a Road Ad Valorem Tax-1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance levying a road tax. He
stated a vote will have to be taken in order to have a first reading. He stated
if the ordinance is passed by the voters, a second reading will take place. He
stated council will have to set a tax rate per $100.00 of assessed valuation.
He asked council if they would like to suggest a rate, if this should go on the
ballot. Council Member Yeager stated she did not want this on the ballot.
Council Member Franzen stated the citizens would be paying double taxes because
they are already paying taxes to the county for their roads and now they would
be paying the city for county roads. Mr. Deters stated the problem is the
timing. He stated in order to get it on the ballot in November council would
have to vote on a tax rate now. Council Member Yeager stated she did not want
to put another tax on the ballot. Mr. Deters asked what will happen if the city
does have to maintain the county roads that are in the city. Council Member
Yeager stated the city will keep its roads clean and the residents that live on
county roads can complain to the county. Council Member Behler stated she feels
it should go on the ballot because she cares for the residents of the city and
she would like their opinion. She stated the county is putting the city in a
terrible situation because there has been no written notification. She stated
if the road tax does not go on the ballot, and the city has to do the
maintenance on the county roads, where does that leave the city financially.
Council Member Brinker stated the city needs a plan, which is what the road tax
is, just in case. We want to make sure the county is aware that we are not
giving in to this, and we are going to challenge their decision, but it would
be foolish to do that and not have a backup plan. He stated the residents need
to be made aware of why the city is in this position. Mr. Deters stated at this
point he has nothing to challenge. He stated he has received nothing in
writing, only rumors. Council Member Yeager asked if the money the county is
collecting for roads from Independence residents will come back to the city.
Mr. Deters stated the county cannot collect taxes for services that they do not
provide. Mayor Moriconi stated the city now pays the county $1.31 per
$1,000.00, or about $900,000.00 per year for county roads. Mayor Moriconi asked
Mr. Deters if the city could request a pro-rated share of that money to come to
the city. Mr. Deters stated it is unconstitutional for the county to collect
taxes for a particular purpose, and not use the money for that particular
purpose. If part of that tax is for roads, then the money should be refunded or
they should no longer collect it. Council Member Bushong stated he has had no
cooperation with the county in his phone conversations and wonders how
difficult if would be to separate what goes for road maintenance. Mr. Deters
stated the response would probably be they do not have enough money to begin
with. Mayor Moriconi asked why would the city continue to pay the county when
they are no longer going to do snow removal or repairs on (15) miles of roads.
Council Member Bushong stated he had written a letter to the Kentucky League of
Cities, Attorney and his response is he disagrees with the county’s
interpretation of the law. He stated the only portion that could be
appropriated is the money going into the county road fund. He stated they might
be able to argue that money, but all other money can be spent as they see fit.
Mr. Deters stated until the city receives a letter from the county he can do
nothing. Council Member Bushong asked if he had gotten any feedback from other
Mayors. Mayor Moriconi stated some of the other cities are not going to be
affected like Independence. He stated Villa Hills and Taylor Mill are going to
put a tax on their ballot. He stated the other cities will not be impacted like
Independence. Council Member Behler stated maybe we should work with other
cities on these issues and not go it alone. Council Member Franzen stated Judge
Drees advised her he did not want to meet with the cities together because
nothing would be accomplished. Council Member Brinker stated the city needs to
be prepared and place the tax on the ballot. Mayor Moriconi asked council if
they had a rate they would like to place on the ordinance. Council Member
Brinker asked how much money does the city need to compensate the additional
maintenance for the county roads. Mayor Moriconi advised council the first
reading of the ordinance has to be at the County Clerk’s Office by August 10,
2004 at 4:00 p.m. Council Member Behler stated she is disappointed because no
research was done before this meeting on how much it cost to maintain the city
roads. Council Member Franzen stated the City of Taylor Mill is asking for 10-
cents per $100.00 but they also have a lot less roads to repair than we do.
Mayor Moriconi stated there are some estimates in your packet on what a rate
per $100.00 would bring in. Mr. Leon Myers, 10805 Autumnridge Drive, stated
council is trying to impose a tax and they do not know if it is a requirement.
He stated if the tax is not specifically stipulated for county roads only, then
it is wrong. Mr. Deters stated that is so stipulated in the Ordinance. Council
Member Behler stated she will suggest .06 cents per ($100.00) one-hundred
dollars. Council Member Bushong suggested .03 cents per ($100.00) one-hundred
dollars. He asked if the .03 cents is approved and things change, can the city
withdraw it from the ballot in the future. Mr. Deters stated the city could.
Council Member Dupps asked if the city can go back and lower the rate if
necessary. Mr. Deters stated that could also be done. Mayor Moriconi asked Mr.
Deters to read the ordinance. Council Member Behler moved to adopt a first
reading of the ordinance, seconded by Council Member Dupps. Roll was called and
the ordinance was defeated with a tie vote of 3-3 vote by council and 1 no vote
by Mayor Moriconi.
Proposed Ordinance-Regulating the Use of Campaign & Politically Oriented Signs-
1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance regulating campaign
and politically oriented signs. Mr. Deters stated there was some talk about
making changes and he was not sure it was ready for a first reading. Mayor
Moriconi stated the ordinance also states that signs cannot be displayed more
than (45) forty-five days but was not sure how council stood on that. Council
Member Franzen stated she checked with other cities and most of them require
(60) sixty days. Council Member Bushong stated that most of the council is
comfortable with (60) sixty days. He stated the ordinance should be very
specific that it only reflects on political signs that are up in yards and
right-of-ways. Council Member Franzen stated she received many complaints
regarding political signs that were posted during the July 4th parade. Mayor
Moriconi asked council if there were anymore comments besides changing the
requested number of days from (45) forty-five days (60) days. Council Member
Behler stated she would like the word “mechanism” taken out of the ordinance.
Mr. Deters stated the word “mechanism” is in the ordinance to cover the
unknowns. Mayor Moriconi asked if there were any other changes besides the
number of days and replacing the word “mechanism” to “medium.” Mr. Deters read
the ordinance as amended. Council Member Franzen made a motion to accept the

with 5 ayes and 1 nay by Council Member Yeager.
