Kathy L. Stenger, Assistant City Clerk
August 16, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August
16, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor,
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker,
Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager answered roll call.
Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Michael Warth, 1897 Bridle Path, Independence read a prepared statement
declaring his opposition to a proposed ordinance relating to political signs.
He stated he does not feel that political signs have become a nuisance and that
restricting the time that they can be posted is violating one’s freedom of
speech. He stated that he feels that ‘for sale’ signs are a greater problem
throughout the city. Mr. Warth urged council to vote down the proposed
ordinance and find a better solution that would guarantee free speech rights.
Discussion Regarding a Map Amendment for 11527 Wilson Road (KCPC Application
No. 1682R)
Mayor Moriconi asked if council had any questions regarding the proposed
ordinance for a map amendment of 11527 Wilson Road before the second reading,
which is scheduled for September 13, 2004. Council did not have any questions.
Discussion Regarding a Map Amendment for Property Located on Independence
Station Road by Wolsing & Hasekoester-Reese LLC – KCPC Application No. 1683R
Mayor Moriconi asked council if they had any questions regarding the proposed
ordinance for a map amendment for the 170-acre parcel located on Independence
Station Road between Webster Road and Cody Road.
Council Member Franzen stated that while she feels that Scheben develops a good
subdivision, she expressed concern with the total number of homes planned for
this parcel, as well as the plans that some of the lots will only be fifty feet
wide. She stated that she would like this concern discussed with the developer
in an effort to increase the size of the lots or decrease the number of
proposed homes. Council Member Behler concurred with Council Member Franzen and
added that roads in the area are a safety concern and has reservations about
adding more traffic in that area. Council Member Dupps stated that he also
agreed and felt the terrain would not support more houses. Council Member
Brinker stated that he would like to do away with the fifty-foot lots.
With four Council Members voicing concerns, Mr. Jed Deters, City Attorney,
questioned why there was a first reading of the proposed ordinance approving
this development at the last council meeting. He advised that council should
attempt to negotiate with the developer in an effort to address these concerns.
Council Member Behler stated she does not have an issue with the fifty-foot
lots, as many retirees prefer smaller lots to maintain. She also feels it is a
good idea to have a variety of sizes of houses in a development. Council Member
Franzen stated she is more concerned with the number of homes planned for this
area. Council Member Dupps stated that he would like to see more of the larger
lot sizes that would benefit the city.
Mayor Moriconi suggested discussing these concerns with the developer at the
next caucus meeting in September and that the second reading of the ordinance,
scheduled for September 13, 2004 be postponed. Mr. Deters advised council that
the city has ninety days from the date that the Kenton County Planning
Commission made their recommendation to the city. He stated that council would
need to take action to either approve or disapprove the recommendation.
Council Member Bushong commented that many of the houses that have not sold in
the various subdivisions have become rental properties. He stated that he likes
that this planned development has a whole range of lot sizes. Council Member
Yeager expressed concern about the planned recreational open space as the
developer had stated the area would be natural open space, not recreational.
Council Member Dupps commented that a homeowners association would maintain the
common use areas. Council Member Yeager stated that the development plan calls
for a hiking trail and bike path. Mayor Moriconi stated that when the city and
county advised the developer they were not interested in taking over the common
areas for maintenance; the developer redesigned it to be natural open space.
Mr. Deters stated that ownership of the common areas would revert to the Kenton
County Conservancy to fund and maintain. Council Member Behler commented that
no decision has actually been made about this. Council Member Yeager stated
that much of the area is in a flood plain.
Mayor Moriconi stated that the Conservancy sounds nice, but if it is not
maintained then the city will get calls from residents. He stated he would
contact the developer (Berling) to discuss council’s concerns, as the city will
need to act on the KCPC recommendation no later than October 1, 2004.
Proposed Ordinance – Annexing 11527 Wilson Road
Mayor Moriconi asked if council had any questions regarding the proposed
ordinance that would annex 11527 Wilson Road, a parcel that would extend the
Freedom Trail subdivision, which is within the city limits.
Council Members Dupps and Bushong commented that they were not in favor of
annexing this property into the city. Council Member Behler stated she was in
favor of the annexation as it would be an extension of the Freedom Trail
subdivision. Council Member Yeager expressed concern that by annexing this
property the city might be taking on the added responsibility of maintaining
Wilson Road. Mayor Moriconi agreed that he does not want to accept maintenance
of Wilson Road, but there may be police department issues with responding to
calls for service. Council Member Behler asked if similar issues exist in other
areas of the city. Chief Butler replied that it could cause some problems but
the city officers would work with the county police department to handle the
calls.
Council Member Brinker suggested the city review a map for possible areas to
annex in the future. Mr. Deters commented that this is a function of the Kenton
County Planning and Zoning Commission. Mayor Moriconi stated that the city’s
Budget and Economic Development Committed is currently looking at areas of the
city that can be annexed, especially along SR. 536 where development for light
industrial could be located. They will be meeting with the Transportation
Cabinet to discuss this matter. Council Member Behler stated she spoke with
Mike Schwartz of the NKPC about unincorporated areas that are already zoned for
businesses. Council Member Brinker asked if it was difficult to annex
commercial properties. Mr. Deters advised there are fewer property owners
involved but they are generally more prominent.
Discussion of a Proposed Ordinance Creating the Position of a Part-Time
Building Custodian
Council Member Dupps asked if it was necessary to require a bond for this
position since they would have access to the police department offices. Chief
Butler stated the access would be minimal.
Council Member Yeager stated she would like the job description for this
position to include language that ensures the hours worked would be in the
evenings to open and close the Senior Center for the renters of the building.
Chief Butler commented that there will be no guaranteed working hours for the
position and should be considered a scheduling issue not part of the job
description. Council Member Yeager suggested deleting the lifting weight limit.
She stated that she also wanted it clear that this position would be
responsible for the set up and tear down of the tables/chairs for the various
events and not just an assistant in performing this duty.
Discussion Regarding the Maintenance of the County Roads Within the City Limits
Chief Butler stated that the county is recommending that Cody Road be closed
and the county is willing to fund the construction of a cul-de-sac. He stated
that the county has studied the problem, laid out all the options and discussed
the situation with all the effected parties. Chief Butler also stated there is
a slippage problem on Cody Road. He stated that Kenton County now feels this
problem on Cody Road is a city issue and they believe the road needs to be
closed to through traffic due to safety concerns.
Chief Butler introduced two gentlemen from the Kenton County Public Works
Department, Charlie Meyer and Joe Murphy. Council Member Bushong asked what
portion of Cody Road that would be closed. They replied the bridge area, past
Upton Drive. Council Member Brinker was concerned how this closing would affect
the residents and asked if a traffic survey had been performed. They replied
that a traffic survey had been done and there was a daily count of 3,800 cars.
Council member Brinker wondered if this was high, low, or average. Chief Butler
stated that he had a copy of the traffic study and would provide council with a
copy of it.
Mr. Murphy advised they were here on behalf of the county regarding the Cody
Road issue and stated that the county is willing to pay the costs associated
with the closing, if the city will agree to close the road. Mr. Murphy advised
there is a site distance problem and initial studies indicate it will cost
millions of dollars to repair the bridge area as the water table is a major
problem. He stated that construction a new road connecting Upton Drive (which
is a private drive) and Troopers Crossing is also an expensive option. He
stated that with more traffic from the new subdivisions using Cody Road the
effectiveness of the floodgates is declining as people move the gates.
Mr. Deters advised council that it would take court action to close a street.
Mr. Murphy advised it would take a public hearing and stated the county had
been working on that and would like the city to continue with the county’s
plans to close the road.
Council Member Bushong asked about the mowing along the county roads. Mr.
Murphy advised the city should be receiving a letter from the county asking if
the city wants to join in a mowing contract, as it will be re-bid in the fall.
Chief Butler stated that the debate is on-going as to who is responsible for
the maintenance of the county roads running through incorporated cities. He
stated if we proceed with the closing of the road at the urging of the county
then we will be effectively accepting it as a city maintained road. Mayor
Moriconi commented that now was the opportunity to get this completely funded
by the county. Mr. Murphy stated it would run around $50,000-$70,000 to
construct a cul-de-sac. He stated the road slippage repairs have been estimated
at $500,000 - $600,000.
Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Deters how this issue would affect the city if
it winds up in court. Mr. Deters advised that in the interest of public safety
the city and county would need to come to an agreement outlining a game plan on
handling this particular road problem, then deal with the other road
maintenance issue separately, at a later time. Council Member Yeager stated she
would not agree to accept Cody Road for city maintenance.
Council Member Brinker stated he feels there will be strong opposition from the
residents on closing the road. Council Member Dupps stated he has many concerns
with regard to traffic flow. He stated that emergency vehicles would have to
take a longer way around. Chief Butler stated that emergency vehicles should be
stationed in the area.
Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to draft an agreement between the city and
county for the necessary repairs for Cody road for council to consider. Mr.
Deters stated that he is certain that a public hearing will be necessary to
close the road, but that he will research the matter further and advise council
how to proceed.
Request for Annexation by Dr. Dean Skinner
Mayor Moriconi introduced Dr. Dean Skinner who has eleven acres adjacent to the
Freedom Park subdivision that he would like to request the city annex. Dr.
Skinner stated that he has two reasons that he would like the city to annex his
property; the first reason being that he would like to tap into city water, and
the second reason is to construct his driveway accessing Tremont Drive in the
Freedom Park subdivision. Mayor Moriconi stated that from Tremont Drive it
would just appear like another driveway in the cul-de-sac, which would lead to
the house that Dr. Skinner wants to build.
Council Member Bushong advised Dr. Skinner that he would have to request water
lines from the Sanitation District. Mr. Deters asked what the current zone is
for the property. Dr. Skinner stated he did not know. Mr. Deters advised that
if he needed to modify the zone it could be done along with the annexation
process. He stated the city would want to control the zoning during annexation
in case he sells the property later. Council Member Brinker stated the city
would need to know what the current zone is as it may be appropriate as is.
Council Member Dupps asked the linear footage between the driveways. Dr.
Skinner did not know. Council Member Franzen asked if this would place another
house on the cul-de-sac. Mayor Moriconi stated it would not. Dr. Skinner stated
he would need to purchase a piece of land from a cul-de-sac owner in order to
construct a driveway. Mr. Deters asked if the property fronted on a dedicated
right-of-way and gave an explanation for this.
Council Member Brinker stated he would be in favor of this annexation as he
feels it is a no brainer. Council Member Yeager stated she would need more time
to consider this request. Council Member Behler stated she does not have enough
information to make a decision; she would like to know the current zone and if
it should be changed.
Mr. Deters advised Dr. Skinner that if he is contemplating annexation he should
ask the KCPC for a zone recommendation. He stated that Dr. Skinner would need
to get a map and a legal description of the parcel to file with the application
for the map change.
Discussion Regarding the NKAPC Building and Zoning “One Stop Shop Codes
Admininstration” Proposal
Mayor Moriconi advised council that the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission (NKAPC) has proposed a “One Stop Shop Codes Administration” program
that would require the city to enter into an interlocal agreement for zoning
administration, as well as building inspection and related services. He stated
that the proposal is an all or nothing plan, wherein the city would be required
to contract for the building services in order for NKAPC to handle the zoning
administration services for the city. He stated that in doing this the NKAPC
would assume all the city’s building inspection services as well as the fees
associated. Mayor Moriconi stated the residents would have to drive to
’’’’Fort’ ’’Mitchell’’ to obtain permits for pools, fences, decks, etc. He
stated that he did not feel this proposal was appropriate for
’’’’Independence’’ with the residential growth the city is experiencing. He
stated that if NKAPC will no longer contract with the city for zoning
administration, then he would like the city to hire its’ own zoning
administrator and bring this service in house for the residents.
Mr. Deters advised that the NKAPC is statutorily required to provide specific
services to the cities, one being subdivision review. Council Member Franzen
asked if Annie Wuestefeld, who is currently the NKAPC employee assigned to
Independence to provide zoning administration would be discontinued should the
city elect not to agree to NKAPC’s proposal. Mayor Moriconi replied yes.
Council Member Brinker commented that basically the city would not be permitted
to contract with NKAC for ‘ala carte’ services. He asked if NKAPC submitted a
formal proposal for the One Stop Shop Codes Administration service. Mayor
Moriconi stated that he was provided with a four-tier level of service
proposal. Council Member Behler stated she would like to see the proposal that
NKAPC submitted to the city.
Council Member Franzen asked the Mayor if Ms. Wuestefeld would consider coming
to work for the city. Additionally, she stated that she did not see the city
benefiting from letting the current building inspector, Kevin Barbian; go in
favor of contracting this service out with NKAPC. Council Member Yeager
commented that she felt the city would need to fill this position with a full-
time employee.
Mayor Moriconi agreed with Council Member Franzen and reiterated that he did
not feel this proposal was suitable for Independence. He advised that NKAPC
wants the city’s decision about this proposal by October 1, 2004. Mayor
Moriconi directed the City Clerk to provide each council member and the city
attorney with a copy of the One Stop Shop Codes Administration proposal that
was submitted by NKAPC.
Council Member Franzen asked how this proposal was supposed to benefit the
city. Mayor Moriconi stated that NKAPC feels their proposal will save the city
money by allowing them to collect all the associated fees and provide the
services. He stated that Mr. Barbian’s salary is paid entirely with the
building fees the city collects. He stated that his position is that he would
prefer to move in the direction in keeping Mr. Barbian on staff and hire an in
house zoning administrator. Council Members Yeager and Brinker stated they
would prefer to keep the building and zoning services in house. Council Member
Franzen agreed, and stated that she felt this was ultimately the Mayor’s
decision. Council Member Behler reiterated that she would like to review the
proposal before making a decision.
Discussion Regarding the Adoption of the Real and Personal Property Tax Rates
for 2004
The City Clerk, Ms. Taney presented for council’s consideration a proposed
ordinance that would adopt the real and personal property tax rates for 2004.
She stated the proposed rates are .184 per $100.00 of assessed value for real
property and .615 per $100.00 of assessed value for personal property other
than motor vehicles. Ms. Taney advised that these rates are the compensating
rate plus the four percent, which is the maximum allowed. She reminded council
that the 2004/05 budget adopted in June was based on the revenue that would be
generated by adopting the compensating rate plus four percent. Ms. Taney
explained that the required public hearing on the proposed tax rate would be
held at 6:30 p.m. on September 13, 2004 prior to the regularly scheduled
council meeting at which time a first reading would be presented for this
ordinance. She stated that in order to get the tax bills printed and mailed on
schedule it would be necessary to hold a special council meeting on September
20, 2004 at 6:45 pm, prior to the regularly scheduled caucus meeting at 7:00
p.m.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters reported that he sent a letter to Kenton County Judge-Executive
Ralph Drees regarding the county road maintenance issue and to date has not
received a reply.
Regarding the proposed political sign ordinance, Mr. Deters reported that he
has been inundated with calls and correspondence regarding the language content
and the constitutionality of this type of ordinance. He stated that the
ordinance language that was presented at the first reading needs to be
reconsidered for possible problems and perhaps needs more language in the
preamble than has currently been proposed. He advised council that he would do
further research on this as there are more stringent requirements with regard
to political and protected speech. He stated he would need additional time to
do this research so that he can be sure any ordinance that is adopted can
holdup in a court of law if challenged. Council Member Bushong asked if similar
ordinances adopted by other cities have ever been challenged. Mr. Deters stated
he is not aware of any. He stated there is no case in the Sixth Circuit Court
that addresses this issue. Mayor Moriconi advised the second reading of the
proposed ordinance would be postponed until Mr. Deters has researched this
further.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler stated he did not have anything to report, but requested an
Executive Session to discuss a personnel matter.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi announced that Chief Butler was awarded the Kentucky Police
Chief of the Year award and extended congratulations. Chief Butler stated it
was quite an honor and a highlight of his career. He stated the city has many
excellent employees and receiving this was an honor for the city. Mayor
Moriconi stated he was very proud of the Chief and said his receiving this
award is a big achievement.
Discussion of Miscellaneous Matters
Hawaiian Ice Vendor - Council Member Bushong asked if the city was monitoring
the mobile Hawaiian Ice vendor with regard to complying with payroll tax for
employees working the mobile unit. City Clerk, Ms. Taney advised that the
business license administration was handled through the Kenton County
Occupational License Director’s office. She stated that Mr. Harmon holds a
current city business license, but would check with the License Director’s
office to see if he was reporting payroll tax for employees. She reminded
council that Mr. Harmon had stated that volunteers from the football teams, who
in turn would receive a percentage of his profits, would most likely man the
mobile unit. This would be an opportunity for the football teams to raise funds
to support their team.
Kenton County Library - Council Member Dupps suggested that the city make a
formal request that the new library branch that is being constructed in the
unincorporated area in Southern Kenton county, just outside the city limits,
not be referred to as the Independence Library. He wondered if there was
anything the city could do to prevent this.
Kenton County Taxes – Council Member Yeager suggested the city send a letter to
the Kenton County Fiscal Court requesting the .133 tax rate that Independence
residents are assessed for road maintenance be provided to the city, since the
county now feels the city should take over maintenance of the county roads
within the city limits. She stated that if they are not going to maintain the
roads, and expect the city to do so, then they should give up the revenue to
the city. Mayor Moriconi commented that he has received many calls about this.
Council Member Behler asked if the city has commenced maintaining the county
roads within the city limits. Chief Butler replied that the city has only
responded to safety related matters on those roads. Council Member Behler
commented that if the city later learns that we are not required to maintain
the county roads, then we should back bill the county for these expenses. Chief
Butler commented that the city needs a resolution to this disagreement with the
county before winter, when snow removal will become a major concern.
Executive Session
Council Member Bushong moved to go into an executive session to discuss
personnel issues, in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (f), seconded by Council
Member Dupps. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of the council
meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
It is noted that no action resulted from the executive session discussion.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Bushong moved to adjourn,
seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting
ended at 8:55 p.m.

                     Christian J. Moriconi, Mayor
ATTEST:
_____________________________________
Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
September 13, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
September 13, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant of Grace Community
Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps,
Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the Minutes of the August 2, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
2.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the August 2,
2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Dupps so moved, with a second from
Council Member Bushong. Amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the August 16, 2004 Caucus Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the August
16, 2004 caucus council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
from Council Member Behler. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0 to accept the minutes as presented.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
4.   Mayor Moriconi announced that eighteen people signed in to address
council. He advised that everyone would be allotted three minutes to speak.
5.   Sherry Carran, 927 Forest, Covington, addressed council regarding the
development (Meadow Glen Subdivision) of the George Wolsing property on
Independence Station Road. She stated she is a representative of the Kenton
Conservancy and was speaking on behalf of the proposed Berling development. Ms.
Carran informed council that she has a letter of intent stating that the Kenton
Conservancy will take over the maintenance of the forty-three acre easement.
She stated that this forty-three acres of green space is a great addition for
Independence and Kenton County and that the Kenton Conservancy, a land trust
group, will workout the appropriate land restrictions for the maintenance of
this area. She stated that she supports the smaller lots proposed in this
development as it helps preserve the areas that need it.
6.   Council Member Bushong asked if the maintenance agreement that the
Conservancy is presenting would be perpetual. Ms. Carran responded that it
would be a permanent agreement and in the event that the Conservancy would
dissolve then another land trust would take over. Council Member Yeager asked
if the Conservancy would be taking over maintenance of the entire green space
in this development or just the nature area. Ms. Carran advised that the actual
boundaries had not yet been determined. She stated that a section of the green
space would be maintained by a Homeowners’ Association, including the retention
pond.
7.   Martin Butler, legal counsel for the Meadow Glen Development, presented
council with a list of conditions that his clients (Berling and Wolsing) are
submitting, the first six being the recommendations made by the Kenton County
Planning Commission (KCPC) and an additional ten provisions which were in
response to the concerns of the residents and city council. Mr. Butler stated
the additional conditions include:
·   A reduction of 35 lots; reducing the total number of lots from 415 to 385
·   Minimum lot size will be 60 feet in width at the building set back line
·   Lots located adjacent to the western boundary line will not be less than 80
feet in width at the building set back line
·   Upgrades to Webster Road to carry the additional traffic that will result
from the development
·   No curb cuts will be made from Webster Road to lots abutting upon the
western right of way line of Webster Road
·   The minimum rear yard set back line will be increased from 25 feet to 50
feet on those lots only whose rear lot line abuts along the western right of
way line of Webster Road including a 15 foot wide greenbelt area
·   The addition of a greenbelt area along the most easterly rear 15 feet of
the lots abutting along the western right of way line of Webster Road (“Webster
Greenbelt”). The establishment of a natural greenbelt area will prohibit the
removal of trees and shrubbery from within the area.
·   The establishment of a HOA (homeowners’ association) with an annual
assessment on lot owners to assure the maintenance and repair of the common
areas, exclusive of Wolsing Woods Park, with provisions that in the event of a
default of the HOA that title to the common areas shall automatically revert to
the developer, its successors and assigns.
·   Developer will plant pine or evergreen trees at least 4-6 feet in height
within the areas of Webster Greenbelt area within six months of commencement of
grading on the Wolsing property
·   Wolsing Woods Park will be subjected to a perpetual Declaration of
Restrictive Covenants restricting the use of the park property to green space
and a natural preservation area
8.   Council Member Bushong stated that he appreciated all the revisions they
made, addressing all the city’s concerns. He asked what the development time
frame would be. Mr. Butler stated that it was hard to predict, but they have
estimated it may take five years to complete the development. Council Member
Franzen asked if the retention pond would be maintained by the HOA. Mr. Butler
replied yes.
9.   Council Member Yeager asked the number of lots for each lot size. Mr.
Butler advised the breakdown is shown in the legend on the plat he distributed.
He stated the breakdown is: 80-foot lots 99, 70-foot lots 55, and 60-foot lots
218, for a total 372 lots.
10.   Mr. Deters informed council that he has reviewed the provisions of the
Homeowners’ Association restrictions and considers it much better than the
original one that was submitted to the city.
11.   Council Member Yeager express concern that Webster Road would not be
widened until nearing the completion of the development. She wondered why this
road improvement was not planned early in the development of this subdivision.
Mr. Butler advised that it is the logical direction of a development to
construct the roads as the development evolves. Mr. Jim Berling interjected
that the road could be widened midway through the development of the
subdivision.
12.   Greg Bridges stated he was a local builder and was speaking on behalf of
the Meadow Glen development. He stated he builds in this type of development
for moderate-income families, and that housing jumps in price on the larger
lots. He advised that a sixty-foot lot should be as marketable as a fifty-foot
lot.
13.   Scott Workman, 1049 Wedgewood Drive, Independence stated he is the owner
of Scott’s Towing Service. He stated he is taking issue with the policy the
city’s Police Department has with regard to the towing service. He stated that
he feels the city should change their policy by either bidding out this service
or using a rotation system similar to the county. He stated that he would like
to be a provider of the towing services needed by the city.
14.   Chief Butler responded to Mr. Workman’s concerns. He stated that the city
only using towing services when there is an arrest or an accident. He advised
that the city does not get part of the towing fee from the provider. Chief
Butler stated that he feels the rotation system is problematic, and while he is
satisfied with the service of the current towing provider, he would be glad to
use Mr. Workman as a backup. Mr. Workman was unwavering is in disagreement with
Chief Butler and stated that he should be given the opportunity to provide this
service. Council Member Bushong advised Mr. Workman that this was not a council
matter as the decision on which towing service to employ is an administrative
concern. Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Workman that his concerns are noted but
cannot be resolved at this meeting.
15.   Janine Moeller, 2789 Senour Road, stated she was here to speak on behalf
of the Meadow Glen development, advising that she supported it and believes
Fisher builds a nice community.
16.   Robert Sharpe, 5545 Cody Road, addressed council by stating that he would
like to tie into the water line that will be installed for the Meadow Glen
development. He stated that currently it has been cost prohibitive for some of
the residents on Cody Road.
17.   Mayor Moriconi advised that Kenton County has plans to repair the road
slippage on Cody Road and close the road on both sides of the train trestle. He
stated that Mr. Berling would have to address Mr. Sharpe’s request for water
lines.
18.   Mr. Jim Berling responded by saying the Northern Kentucky Water District
regulates the water lines, but that the lines would need to be extended
further, about 1500-2000 feet or more. He stated there are water lines on both
sides but they have never been connected.
19.   Council Member Dupps added that the city is not in the water business and
suggested Mr. Sharpe contact John Scheben at the Northern Kentucky Water
District. Mayor Moriconi asked how many homes on Cody Road might be interested
in public water service. Mr. Sharpe stated there are about 15 homes.
20.   Kip Mueller, 10386 Bugle Court, Independence, addressed council regarding
the Meadow Glen development by stating that he supported the zone change, and
as a subcontractor that has worked in many new developments he feels that
Fisher Homes builds nice communities. He stated that the smaller lots and homes
are affordable for firemen, nurses, teachers and policemen.
21.   David Rabe, 529 Independence Station Road, stated that his property (33
acres) adjoins the proposed subdivision. He stated that the people in
attendance at this meeting who are speaking in favor of the development don’t
even live in the area. He urged council to adhere to the 12,500-foot lots. Mr.
Rabe stated that the PUD zone was the worse thing to happen to Independence
zoning. He urged council not to grant the zone change being requested.
22.   Brian Fannin, 5152 Dana Harvey Lane, stated he is an employee of Fisher
Homes Company and supported the proposed zone change for the Meadow Glen
development. He stated he sees this as an opportunity to do something good for
Independence. He stated that people should have the opportunity to purchase
affordable, new housing. He also commented that the land use changes proposed
makes a model design which best utilizes the land for the residents who will
live there. Mr. Fannin stated this type of planned community appeals to a broad
spectrum of buyers as it meets the needs of new first time buyers as well as
retirees.
23.   Dan Arlinghaus, 400 Webster Road, Independence, spoke in support of the
Meadow Glen development and commented that Fisher Homes builds nice houses and
neighborhoods.
24.   Dave Arlinghaus, 551 Webster Road, Independence, stated that his property
adjoins the proposed development site of Meadow Glen subdivision. He stated he
has been in the construction business for thirty years and knows that Fisher
Homes does a good job and he welcomes Fisher Homes to his neighborhood.
25.   Michelle Herman, 345 Webster Road, Independence, addresses council
regarding the proposed Meadow Glen development. She stated she has been
struggling with this issue and is encouraged by the concessions made to the
plan by the developer. Ms. Herman informed council that the intent of a PUD
overlay is to provide diversification to a development plan. She advised that
the plan should be a mixed development that would include town homes, etc.;
that it should encompass more and she feels this plan clearly does not meet the
intent of the PUD zone as a PUD zone should enhance an R-1C zone. She stated
that she also has concerns about the strains on the public safety service
departments. Ms. Herman stated that she feels Independence already has an
abundant of starter homes for small families and needs more “move up” housing.
She stated the abundance of starter homes might make Independence a transient
community, without the next step up in housing.
Ordinance No. 2004-O-15 – Map Amendment 170 Acres Independence Stat. Road –
Meadow Glen Subdivision – (KCPC Application No. 1683R) – 2nd Reading
26.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2004-O-15 that would approve a map amendment changing an approximate 170-acre
area located along the south side of Independence Station Road between Webster
Road and Cody Road, approximately 800 feet west of Webster Road from R-1C to R-
1C (PUD). Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2004-O-15 which included the six
conditions recommended by the Kenton County Planning Commission and
incorporating the additional ten development conditions consented to by the
developer.
27.   Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O-15, seconded
by Council Member Bushong. Council Member Dupps asked if the additional
stipulations would necessitate a new first reading of the ordinance. Mr. Deters
advised that he did not deem the additional language to be significant enough
to revert to a new first reading. He stated that the type of zone request did
not change and the developer consented to the additional restrictions. Council
Member Brinker commented that since the developer has compromised and addressed
the city’s concerns regarding the surrounding infrastructure he feels the
development plan/map amendment is better than it was when first submitted to
the city for approval. Council Member Yeager asked if the recreational park
area was taken care of. Mr. Deters responded that the additional HOA provisions
would ensure that the park area is maintained. Council Member Yeager stated she
is still concerned that some of the lots are not 12,500 feet. Council Member
Behler commented that she feels the developer did an excellent job listening to
the city’s concerns. She added that the infrastructure issues need to be
improved sooner than later and urged the developers to ask the local
legislators to support state funding for city road improvements. There being no
further discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-
0.
Ordinance No. 2004-O-16 – Map Amendment of Mullins Property on 11527 Wilson
Road (KCPC Application No. 1682R) – 2nd Reading
28.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.
2004-O-16 that would approve a map amendment changing an approximate 56-acre
area located along the east side of Wilson Road and between Shaw Road and
Bramlage Road, approximately 1500 feet north of Bramlage Road, unincorporated
Kenton County, as a part of the annexation process, from R-1C and R-1B to R-1D.
Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2004-O- 16.
29.   Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O- 16, seconded
by Council Member Franzen. Council Member Yeager commented that she does not
see the language in the ordinance that will ensure the city does not end up
with street maintenance responsibilities for Wilson Road. Mayor Moriconi stated
he spoke to the attorney for the property owner who assured him that no houses
would face Wilson Road. Council Member Franzen stated she wanted to be sure of
this condition. Council Member Yeager stated she did not want the city to end
up annexing Wilson Road. Mr. Deters recommended adding an eighth condition that
inserts the appropriate language. He stated this has been discussed with Mr.
Mike Duncan, the property owner’s attorney, and will not constitute a
significant change to the ordinance.
30.   There being no further discussion, the roll was called and answered with
five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Dupps. Motion carried 5-1.
Ordinance No. 2004-O- 17 – Annexation of 11527 ––Wilson– Road – 2nd Reading
31.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading Ordinance No.

17.
32.   Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O- 17, seconded

also be incorporated into this ordinance. Council Member Bushong wondered if
this ordinance would counteract Ordinance No. 2004-O-16 approving the zone
change. Mr. Deters responded no to both concerns, adding that the two

Council Member Behler stated she agreed with council Member Dupps and advised
that the only reason that she supported this map amendment and annexation was
that is was the extension of an existing city development. She stated that it
was reasonable for the developer to request that the entire subdivision be
within the incorporated boundaries. She commented that she also favored the
addition of another egress for this subdivision. Council Member Franzen
concurred with Council Member Behler. Council Member Dupps commented that
Wilson Road will still be there. There being no further discussion, roll was
called and answered with five ayes and one dissenting vote cast by Council
Member Dupps. Motion carried 5-1.

City of Independence, Ky
September 20, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday September 20, 2004 at
7:00 pm at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Council Members Donna Yeager, Eric Dupps, Tom Brinker, Mary Pat
Behler and Carol Franzen answered roll call. Council Member Bushong was not in
attendance. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
No one signed in for privileges to address council.
OLD BUSINESS
There was no old business to be discussed.
NEW BUSINESS
Development Proposal by Fifth Third Bank
Mayor Moriconi advised council that he met with representatives of Fifth Third
Bank a few months ago to discuss their interest in adding another branch in
Independence. He stated they are looking at property located at the corner of
Independence Station Road and Turkeyfoot Road. He stated he has invited them to
attend this meeting to present their proposal to the entire council. Mayor
Moriconi introduced Mr. Jeff Smith, a Corporate Facilities Project Manager with
Fifth Third Bank.
Mr. Smith informed council that the property they are interested in acquiring
is not currently zoned for a bank. He stated they have already been told they
would be turned down by Northern Kentucky Area Planning for a re-zoning as the
property is less than the required minimum five acres. He stated the Planning
Commission considers this “spot zoning.” Mr. Smith stated with the planned
widening of Turkeyfoot Road, a deceleration lane would be added. Mr. Smith
stated Fifth Third Bank wants to be a good neighbor and provide products and
services to the citizens of the community. He stated their building design fits
very well into a residential community that resembles a cape-cod style of home.
He stated their proposal would also make it safe and easily accessible for
their customers. He stated a traffic study has been performed and a view of
what Turkeyfoot Road will look like as a four lane road. Mr. Smith stated they
have looked at the property from both a practical and commercial standpoint and
they do not feel anyone would have interest in developing this property at its
current residential zone since it is so close to the road.
Mr. Smith advised council they are before them to ask what they felt would be
the best avenue to pursue when making application to the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission. He asked if the city would be more inclined to consider a
zone change for this property that is less than five acres or a text amendment
with more restrictive conditions. He stated eventually the zoning may change in
the area when the Comprehensive Plan is updated. Mr. David Curle, a Senior
Project Architect with K4 Architecture, LLC stated that Fifth Third has found
this to be a good site. He stated there are several challenges with the
widening of Turkeyfoot Road that will reduce the lot size and the only egress
location for the bank would be close to the intersection. He stated they would
provide upkeep of site and good landscaping with a generous buffer. He stated
due to the narrow lot site the building would be squeezed in and permission
would be needed to place it as to not diminish the required buffer.
Council Member Behler asked how many feet they wanted to reduce the buffer. Mr.
Curle stated the normal buffer is 10 to 15 feet and they would like to reduce
it to 5 feet and add a decorative fence.
Mr. E.J. Foltz, an engineer with Cartec Engineering Corp. stated this site is
in the R-1D zone and the amount of the land needed for the bank structure is
1.4 acres. He stated he is aware that NKAPC will deny a zone change request
because the parcel is smaller than five acres.
Mr. Foltz stated they would like to request the city to consider a text
amendment with conditions that would be restrictive. He read the list of
current permitted businesses in the R-1D zone, which include libraries and
funeral homes. He stated he feels that eventually the zoning may change in the
area with the updates to the Comprehensive Plan. Mr. Foltz stated they would
like to see the city allow banks in this zone as a conditional use with
restrictions as they propose in the text they submitted to council to review.
Mayor Moriconi stated that Fifth Third Bank is essentially asking for a text
amendment so restrictive that things can’t just pop up anywhere or a zone
change which NKAPC will probably reject just based on the current Comprehensive
Plan. Mr. Foltz stated that he felt the lot was not conducive for the
construction of a residential building. He stated there is a high volume of
traffic in the area. He advised council that with a text amendment, the city
would still have control as they would be required to get approval for the
conditional use from the city’s Board of Adjustment.
Mr. Deters cautioned the discussion with council should stay within the realms
of a possible text amendment.
Council Member Behler asked why they feel this is a good location. Mr. Smith
stated Independence is a growing community and they look at many factors,
including population and location, as they prefer to be on an arterial street.
He stated they also like to locate in a community close to where people reside
which helps them forge good relationships with their customers.
Council Member Yeager asked when the five lanes on
Turkeyfoot Road would be constructed. Mr. Smith stated the year 2005, but that
is subject to change by the Department of Transportation. Council Member
Franzen asked if a traffic light will be installed at the intersection. Mr.
Smith stated there would be a light, along with two lanes in each direction
with a turn lane onto Independence Station Road. Mayor Moriconi asked if
Richardson Road will be rerouted to the north. Mr. Smith stated it would. Chief
Butler asked if their building plans would coincide with the road improvements,
because, from a safety standpoint, that intersection is one of the toughest in
the city. Mr. Smith stated they hope to have the bank constructed before the
road improvements are completed.
Mayor Moriconi stated they must decide if a bank is the best use for this land.
He stated he did not feel someone would want to build a home on this property.
Council Member Franzen expressed concern about the additional traffic the bank
may generate as it is already a dangerous intersection and more traffic will
only make it worse. Mr. Smith stated there is a very good chance there is
already a temporary construction easement on Independence Station Road that
could make the construction of the bank very difficult. He stated they may have
to postpone their construction until the fourth quarter of 2005.
Mr. Deters stated that while the council cannot discuss a possible zone change,
he recommended that Fifth Third Bank should submit double application, one for
a text amendment and one for a zone change and then the Planning Commission
staff can recommend on both, thereby incorporating all concerns.
Council Member Brinker stated he is not in favor of having banks in that area
even if the entrance is on Independence Station Road. He stated he is in favor
of a text amendment because it will be controlled through the Board of
Adjustments. Mayor Moriconi stated with the restrictive conditions language in
the proposed text amendment, it will let make the NKAPC aware of their
intentions.
Council Member Dupps stated he is not in favor of spot zoning, but agreed that
the planned road improvements will change the traffic conditions. He stated
there are already other businesses in the area.
Mayor Moriconi stated they could possibly have a proposed text amendment in
conjunction with a possible zone change at the same time. Council concurred
that Fifth Third Bank should apply for both a text amendment and zone change
concurrently. Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters to prepare a resolution to be
presented to council at the October 4, 2004 council meeting indicating the
city’s support of a text amendment application to the Planning Commission.
City Attorney Report - Jed K. Deters
No report
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
No report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Brinker has chosen Beechgrove Self-Storage
for the business of the month award.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that he attended a meeting on Saturday regarding
the county road maintenance issue. He stated the Kenton County Fiscal Court is
proposing to provide snow removal on the county roads that are within the
corporate limits of the city for a fee of $1,000.00 per mile. He stated they
estimate there is 16.9 miles of county streets in Independence and for
$16,900.00 the county will plow county roads for snow removal in the city. He
stated this is for snow plowing only, not regular street maintenance. Mr.
Deters stated regardless of how much it snows, if this is a package deal, then
it is a good deal if it covers the entire season.
Mayor Moriconi stated that minus the county roads the county is covering 75% of
our city streets and our public works is covering 25% of city streets during
snow removal. He stated this is a separate issue. He stated this is an
additional 16.9 miles that were county roads and that the county is now
considering to be the city’s responsibility. Mayor Moriconi stated when he
questioned the maintenance of the roads he was told by Judge Drees when it
comes time for maintenance on the county roads then the city should come back
to the county and advise which county roads are in need of repairs and they
will give us a bid.
Council Member Franzen expressed concern that if the city accepts this
agreement for snow removal they the city may be sending the message to the
county that we are going to accept the responsibility of these county roads.
Council Member Yeager agreed. Mr. Deters advised there are some questions as to
whether the city inherited the streets. He stated there are issues to be
resolved and during his research to date, wherein he has read the opinion
numerous times and while he does not agree with the opinion, he has not been
able to find holes that the city could use in a legal argument.
Mayor Moriconi distributed paperwork from the county showing the breakdown of
fees the county would charge the city for various road services. Chief Butler
stated the city does not have the staff to handle all of the roads and if it is
put out to bid, the county will be able to under bid any individual contractor.
Mayor Moriconi stated he feels the city could not beat this deal, $16,900 for
the entire snow season, if they did bid it out to a private contractor. He
expressed concern that the snow season was looming and that the city needed to
make preparations for the coming winter season. Council Member Yeager was
concerned that the city may pay $16,900 and then it wouldn’t snow all season.
Mr. Deters stated the city could enter into separate interlocal agreements with
the county; one for snow removal and one for road maintenance. Council Member
Yeager stated she still does not like the situation the city has been put in by
the county. Mayor Moriconi stated that the whole situation began when the
county advised the cities that they learned it was illegal for them to spend
funds on maintenance of county roads running through corporate city limits
without an agreement with the city. Council Member Franzen expressed concern of
how the city was going to have the funds to maintain this additional 16.9 miles
of streets on a budget that is already stretched.
Mr. Dennis Redmond, 1792 Forestrun Drive stated in 1985 there was a law passed
regarding the LGEA funds and asked if the county was going to get a reduced
amount now that they are turning their roads over to cities for maintenance.
Mayor Moriconi stated the county has indicated they would not surrender the
municipal road aid they currently receive as they indicate they are currently
operating at a loss. Chief Butler stated the county’s portion of state funds is
probably not much more than the city’s portion which is about $200,000.00
annually. He stated the law is clear that there is an increase/decrease change
every ten years, based on the census.
Mr. Dennis Koch asked if the county will take care of the side streets like as
they have in past years. Mayor Moriconi stated the city has a separate
agreement with the county that encompasses the maintenance of the city streets.
He stated the county has also agreed to handle the repairs of the Cody Road
slippage issue.
Mr. Mike Little stated he feels the county is using this for revenue
enhancement. He asked if the city is still going to pursue legal action against
the county and if other Northern Kentucky cities plan to fight this issue.
Mayor Moriconi stated no other city has been impacted like Independence. He
stated Taylor Mill has put a road tax referendum on the November general
election ballot. He stated no other city has attempted any legal action.
Council Franzen stated if the city accepts this snow removal agreement then the
city is allowing the county to do what they want. Mr. Deters advised that to
some extent, the city is agreeing with their decision that the county roads are
the responsibility of the city. Council Member Yeager stated the city did not
have to do this last year for the county to plow the county roads. Mr. Little
stated that if no other city is going to take legal action then the
repercussions of being able to sue is slim to none.
Council Member Brinker stated he feels our only hope is to work with Taylor
Mill. Mayor Moriconi stated they have a road tax on the ballot and have pretty
much said they are preparing to take over the county roads within their city if
the referendum fails.
Mr. Deters stated he disagrees with what the county is doing but cannot come up
with a legal argument to get around it. Council Member Franzen stated she
believes the city should ask the court for clarification on the issue.
In closing the discussion, Mayor Moriconi advised council that a snow removal
interlocal agreement with the county will be drafted for their review.
Zoning Violation – Old Circle K Store on Madison Pike at Independence Station
Road
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters to expand on the status of the Circle K on
Madison Pike.
Mr. Deters stated the owners are in Chapter 7 of Bankruptcy Court. He stated if
the city wants to enforce a cleanup of the site the owner can be notified and
then a lien can be placed on the property and when it sells the city will
recoup its money. He stated the Zoning Administrator can send a zoning
violation notice and then we can proceed. He stated that any condemnation
cannot be done at this time due to the bankruptcy. Council Member Yeager
suggested the city condemn the property and raze the building. Mr. Deters
advised the city cannot do that as the building would have to be declared
structurally unsound, which it is not. City Clerk, Patricia Taney stated there
are also underground gas tanks on this property.
Council Member Brinker expressed concern regarding the set back line and that
it may not be useable property. Council Member Brinker suggested the zoning
enforcement officer keep check on the site and submit monthly update reports to
council.
Adjournment
Mayor Moriconi stated there being no further action, he entertained a motion to
adjourn.
Council Member Franzen so moved to adjourn, seconded by Council Member Behler.
Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 8:00 p.m.

September 20, 2004
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, September 20, 2004 at 6:30 pm in the Senior Citizens and Community
Center, 2001 Jack Woods Parkway in Independence with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called
and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom
Brinker, Eric Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Jim Bushong was not in
attendance. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the city council was called to
discuss and possibly take action on the following agenda items:
·   Adoption of the 2004 property tax rates – Ordinance No. 2004-0-22 – Second
Reading
·   Zoning Administration – Executive Order No. 2004-EO-05
Ordinance No. 2004-0-22 - Adopting 2004 Real & Personal Property Tax Rates -–
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would adopt the property tax rates for 2004. Council Member Dupps moved to
adopt Ordinance 2004-0-22, setting the 2004 real estate tax rate at .184 per
$100.00 of assessed value and the personal property tax rate at .615 per
$100.00 of assessed value; seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called
and answered unanimously and the motion carried 5-0.
Executive Order No. 2004-EO-05 - Zoning Administrator Position
Mayor Moriconi stated this position came up when Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission advised the city that they would cease providing the city
with zoning administration services unless the city also contracted for
building inspection services. He stated that basically it had to be an “all or
nothing” contract with the Planning Commission. Mayor Moriconi advised he plans
to bring the zoning services in-house and announced that Annie Wuestefeld could
continue to do the zoning for the city, as a city employee. Council Member
Yeager asked if she would resign from her position at the Planning Commission.
He stated that he has discussed the position with her and she has agreed to
take the position with the city. Council Member Yeager asked if she would work
a 5-day week. Mayor Moriconi stated that Annie would be available four days
each week instead of the current three days she is now working and added that
it would be exclusively for Independence unlike her current situation with the
Planning Commission where she also provides zoning service for other
municipalities. He stated she will report to Mr. Kevin Barbian, Building
Inspector and assist him when needed as she is a certified building inspector.
Mayor Moriconi clarified that while he did not actively pursue this change of
contracting out the zoning administration to bringing the service in-house, he
reminded council that having a staff member perform this service was a
recommendation made by the Budget and Finance Committee last spring. He stated
there will not be a big change in the budget but it will have to be amended
$2,000.00 to $4,000.00 later this year.
Council Member Dupps asked if a regional building/zoning service was initiated
by the county. Mr. Deters responded that the “one stop shop” concept was
initiated by the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission. Mayor Moriconi
stated that the Planning Commission wanted Independence to be a part of this
interlocal service they were proposing. He stated that bringing Annie on board
as a city employee will be a win/win for the city. Council Member Franzen asked
if Annie will be able to be of assistance to Kevin Barbian, Building Inspector.
Mayor Moriconi advised that Annie would report directly to Mr. Barbian and
would assist him as needed.
Council Member Dupps asked if Mrs. Wuestefeld would receive benefits. Mayor
Moriconi stated she would be considered a part-time employee and as such would
only receive retirement benefits. He stated Chief Butler has an older, spare
cruiser available for that would be assigned to Annie.
In closing, Mayor Moriconi advised that as of October 1, 2004 the Planning
Commission will no longer perform zoning administration services for the city.
He stated that the Building Inspector could use some assistance and he feels
the addition of Annie to the city staff would be a natural fit. He stated it
could be difficult to fill this position with the appropriate person; one that
has all the necessary qualifications to perform this job and one that wants
only part-time work.
Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2004-EO-05, appointing Annie Wuestefeld
as the Zoning Administrator for the city and requested a motion to approve the
appointment. Council Member Behler moved to adopt Executive Order No. 2004-EO-
5, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Adjournment
Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to adjourn the special meeting. Council
Member Franzen so moved, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with
all ayes and the meeting ended at 6:35 p.m.

October 4, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
October 4, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Kenton County Courthouse in Independence
with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting
to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Lisa May of Staffordsburg
Christian Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric
Dupps, and Carol Franzen. Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member Donna
Yeager’s mother passed away about two hours ago and that she would not be
attending tonight’s meeting. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Recognition
2.   Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member Brinker had selected
Beechgrove Self-Storage as the recipient of the Business of the Month, but
since the owner was not present, we would present the plaque at next month’s
meeting. He advised two businesses would be recognized next month.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 13, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September
13, 2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Behler so moved, with a second
from Council Member Bushong. There being no amendments, roll call was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Approval of the Minutes of the September 20, 2004 Special Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September
20, 2004 Special council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
from Council Member Dupps. No amendments were noted and roll call was answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0 to accept the minutes as presented
Approval of the Minutes of the September 20, 2004 Caucus Council Meeting
5.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September
20, 2004 caucus council meeting. Council Member Behler so moved, with second
from Council Member Brinker. No amendments were noted and roll call was
answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0 to accept the minutes as presented.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
6.   Mayor Moriconi announced that no one signed in to address council under
Privileges of the Floor, so they would proceed with the agenda.
Resolution No. 2004-R-10 – Supporting a Text Amendment to Permit Banks as a
Conditional Use in the R-1D Zone
7.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2004-R-10 that would
support a text amendment to the Zoning Ordinance to permit banks and banking
institutions as a conditional use in the R-1D zone. Mayor Moriconi reminded
council that this proposed text amendment comes at the request of Fifth Third
Bank who presented a plan to the city at the last caucus meeting to construct a
bank at the intersection of Turkeyfoot Road and Independence Station Road.
8.   Council Member Behler moved to adopt Resolution No. 2004-R-10, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Franzen asked
if the city was going to stipulate that a traffic light had to be installed at
the intersection before the bank is construction. Mr. Deters advised that
council would have the opportunity to impose that condition when the zone
change request is presented to the city for approval. Council Member Dupps
asked about the current traffic plan for Turkeyfoot Road. He stated that he did
not think Fifth Third Bank would want to wait too long to construct this
branch. Police Chief Butler stated that he believes the reconstruction of
Turkeyfoot Road is still on schedule, but that it will probably be two years or
so before a traffic light will be installed at that intersection. Council
Member Franzen stated that the city needs additional businesses in the city,
but this particular intersection is already hazardous and wondered if the city
could get the traffic light installed sooner. Council Member Bushong advised
that the road plans call for the intersection to be relocated and he thinks it
will be a long time before the corner will be completed. Chief Butler suggested
the text amendment language include both banks and professional office
buildings. Council agreed. Council Member Bushong commented there are several
areas in the city that could benefit from this type of development. Mayor
Moriconi instructed Mr. Deters to add the additional language to the text
amendment proposal. No roll was called; the motion to adopt Resolution No.
2004-R-10 was passed with all ayes. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2004-R-10
including the additional language as discussed.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 Establishing Sunday
Liquor Sales – 1st Reading
9.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that would amend Ordinance No. 2003-O-08. He asked Mr. Deters to
explain why it was necessary to amend the current ordinance regulating Sunday
liquor sales. Mr. Deters advised that the current Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 does
not make a distinction of liquor sold by the package or drink. He stated that
the amendment specifies the difference and clarifies by the drink after 1:00
p.m. Council Member Bushong asked if there was a difference for establishments
like Kroger’s or a regular liquor store. Mr. Deters replied no, that all
businesses that possess a liquor sales license fall under the same state laws.
There being no further discussion Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Mayor
Moriconi advised the second reading would be held at the next council meeting.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
10.   Chief Butler reported that Northern Kentucky University donated a ten-
piece nautilus set to the city for use in fitness room of the new Municipal
Center. He thanked NKU.
11.   Chief Butler reported that Scott Kimmich, Kenton County’s Deputy Judge-
Executive, has advised that the county will charge the city $1,000 per road
mile for snow removal maintenance of the sixteen miles of county roads which
may or may not be the responsibility of the city. He stated that Mr. Kimmich
advised the county would be sending written notice of this proposal. Council
Member Bushong asked if the county is proposing a flat $16,000 for the entire
winter season, regardless of the number of times it becomes necessary to treat
the roads due to snow and/or ice this winter. Chief Butler responded yes, that
is how he understands the county’s proposal. He stated he hopes to have a
written proposal soon.
12.   Council Member Franzen asked if this expense would come from regular tax
dollars or the state Municipal Road Assistance fund. Mr. Deters advised he has
sent a letter to the county regarding the issue of state funds but has not yet
received a reply.

Pembroke Village Subdivision – Developer Request for Waiver of Turn Lane on Cox
Rd
26.   Mayor Moriconi reported that the city is in receipt of a copy of a
correspondence that the state Highway Department has sent to the developer of
Pembroke Village subdivision, wherein it is stated that the imposed condition
of a turn lane on Cox Road does not meet state requirements for such. He stated
that Mr. Berling, representing the developer for Pembroke Village has made an
appeal of the Kenton County Planning Commission requesting a waiver the imposed
condition for a turn lane on Cox Road. Mayor Moriconi advised council that
residents in the area object to the possibility that this turn lane may be
waived and are requesting the city take an active role in ensuring that Cox
Road will have adequate improvements to handle the additional traffic this
development will produce. Mayor Moriconi advised the matter will be considered
at the Planning Commission’s Subdivision Review Committee on Thursday, October
7, 2004.
27.   City Attorney, Mr. Deters advised council that the city couldn’t force
the state to alter their highway. Council Member Bushong asked how the city
could become involved in this issue. Mr. Deters commented that the city does
not have a right-of-way and essentially no control in the dispute. Council
Member Bushong suggested the city send a letter to the state Highway Department
expressing future traffic concerns. Mayor Moriconi stated that when the Kenton
County Planning Commission approved the development plan submitted by the
developer, constructing a turn lane on ’’’’Cox Road’’ was a condition that the
Planning Commission imposed when approving the plan, and which the developer
agreed to comply with. Council Member Franzen suggested the city ask the
developer to uphold his agreement to install a turn lane. Council Member Behler
suggested the city speak with the state representatives to get the state
highway department’s decision overturned. Council Member Brinker stated that
the turn lane was a condition of the re-zoning that was approved by the
Planning Commission and city. Council Member Behler stated it shouldn’t be any
different if it is a state maintained road. Mr. Deters advised that since it is
a state road, that the state has the right to override a city-imposed
condition.
28.   Mayor Moriconi directed the City Clerk to check with the Planning
Commission to inquire if the city has the final approval and what options may
be available to the city. Council Member Franzen suggested sending a letter to
the Planning Commission requesting they uphold the condition of the approved
plan that includes the installation of the turn lane on Cox Road. Council
Member Bushong suggested the letter be hand-delivered. Mayor Moriconi stated
the letter could be faxed to the Commission.
29.   Council Member Behler moved to support the construction of a turn lane on
Cox Road by the developer of the Pembroke Village Subdivision as was a
condition of the original plan approval by the Planning Commission, seconded by
Council Member Dupps. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss, Council Member Franzen moved to
adjourn the meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with
all ayes and the meeting ended at 7:50 pm.
