October 18, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
18, 2004 at 7:00 pm at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Donna Yeager, Mary Pat Behler,
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric Dupps and Carol Franzen answered roll call. Also
present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
Mike Little, 10987 Griststone Circle addressed council regarding a call from
Diane Glaser advising him that the Scherry Drive street sign does not have a
“c” in the spelling. City Clerk, Patricia Taney stated she would see how the
street name was platted and get back to him.
Ken Lancaster, 733 Cox Road addressed council regarding zoning violations
behind Cherokee Shopping Center. He stated according to zoning regulations,
dumpsters are required to be screened on at least three sides and there are
also four dumpsters there. He presented to Mayor and Council photos of trash on
the site. He also stated the streetlights glare on his property. He stated with
the storage of parked trucks, they should also be screened. Mayor Moriconi
stated he would advise the zoning administrator to make an inspection of the
site.
OLD BUSINESS
Discussion Regarding a Proposal from Kenton County Fiscal Court for Various
Services
Mayor Moriconi stated the city has received a letter from Kenton County Fiscal
Court defining the proposals and related costs for providing the city with
various services such as snow removal, fleet vehicle maintenance, etc. He
advised that the letter from Judge-Executive Drees states that fleet
maintenance gasoline will be increased by 3 cents per gallon surcharge plus a
15% handling charge. The rate for culvert, ditch work and patching road holes
is being raised from $52.50 to $67.00 an hour. He stated all the services that
the county provides will be substantially increased. Mayor Moriconi advised
council that he has discussed this proposal with Chief Butler and they have
decided they will look into the possibility of eliminating county services and
may bid out for services, including snow removal.
Council Member Bushong asked Mayor Moriconi if he had spoke to Jeff Smith,
Public Works about a survey on additional staff to his department so that some
of these services could be handled in-house. Chief Butler stated they are
looking into that possibility but even though it might be cheaper than using
the county we have to factor in the cost of wages, including benefits to hire
additional Public Works personnel. Mayor Moriconi stated with a normal snowfall
of three to five inches, the county sends out four trucks, plus our two trucks
and it takes about five hours with those six trucks. Chief Butler stated some
switch of services has already taken place, as the police cruises are now
having oil changes done at the Valvoline on Madison Pike as they charge less
than the county garage. He advised he is also looking into fleet management
services for the purchase of gasoline. He stated he is also checking into car
dealer’s hourly rate for vehicle maintenance and repairs. Chief Butler
expressed concern on whether the county could legality charge the cities a 15%
handling fee on vehicle parts that are state contract bid and asked City
Attorney Deters to research this.
Council Member Bushong asked Mayor Moriconi if this proposal by the county for
these services was discussed at the recent Mayor’s Group meeting. Mayor
Moriconi stated that the other cities are not getting hit as bad as
Independence, as Independence is much larger than many of the other cities in
Northern Kentucky.
Council Member Yeager stated that she checked on fuel prices that large
corporations like Cinergy, Cincinnati Bell and UPS are paying and feels the
city needs to get look into acquiring the state road funds the county is
receiving. Mayor Moriconi stated it would probably take a court action to
handle the road situation. Chief Butler stated from an employer standpoint,
there are two issues to address; one being the roads and the other is fleet
maintenance and fuel. He stated they need some guidance from council on whether
to challenge the county on the road maintenance issue, or move on and do what
we need to do to get cheaper prices and discontinue reliance on the county for
various services. Council Member Franzen asked if the city could contract out
other areas of services. City Attorney Deters stated he did not feel it was
feasible to challenge the road issue, but feels the city could challenge other
duties the county, which are currently performed on the city’s behalf. Chief
Butler stated he would look at all of the issues very carefully. Council Member
Bushong asked if the county is going to dictate the services the city would
have to contract with them for and would the city be able to select the
services we actually need from them. Mayor Moriconi stated the Scott Kimmich,
Deputy Judge-Executive, is going to send a memorandum of understanding breaking
down the various services that will be offered and the associated costs and the
cities can choose the services they need from the county.
Mayor Moriconi stated that City Attorney Deters will research the municipal
road aid monies the city and county are receiving and maybe the city can obtain
a portion of the funds that the county is currently receiving from the state.
Council Member Dupps asked if the city does not contract with the county garage
for vehicle maintenance then who would do the maintenance. Chief Butler stated
the city would solicit several Ford Dealers in the area for contract prices to
see if they are compatible or comparable to what the city is presently paying
the county. Council Member Bushong asked if the city could opt out of county
services after one year with a 30-day option. City Attorney Deters stated it is
his understanding that the proposal submitted by the county would not be an
exclusive service contract, therefore the city would be able to obtain other
services elsewhere. Mayor Moriconi stated he would keep everyone updated on the
situation.
NEW BUSINESS
Proposed Zoning Text Amendment in the NSC Zone - NKAPC Application No. 1697R
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed text amendment would add
automobile laundry as a permitted use or conditional use within a neighborhood
shopping commercial zone. Council Member Yeager stated she had spoken to a
resident regarding this and they felt it would attract a criminal element.
Council Member Franzen stated she also spoke to the same resident regarding the
entrance and exit to the car wash being on Cox Road due to new residential
construction entering and exiting from Cox Road. Council Member Bushong stated
the Planning Commission thought this car wash was going to be constructed in
the Independence Town Center area. Mayor Moriconi asked City Clerk, Patricia
Taney if the city was the applicant for the text amendment and if the Planning
Commission has had the public hearing on this application yet. Ms Taney stated
the application had gone before the Planning Commission and it had been
partially approved and disapproved. She stated the request was for a text
amendment as a permitted use or a conditional use in the NSC zone and that the
Planning Commission has denied approval of adding text that would allow it to
be a conditional use, which then would have allowed the city’s Board of
Adjustments to decide each individual application. She stated the Planning
Commission has recommended approval for adding text to the zoning ordinance
that would allow an automobile laundry as a permitted use, thereby making it
unnecessary to go before the Board of Adjustments and would only need approval
from the city’s Zoning Administrator.
Ms. Blanche Bedell, 6402 Jimae, asked who requested the city to make
application for this text amendment. Ms. Taney stated no one came before
Council, but instead stopped by the city office and requested a signature on
the text amendment application. She stated she did not know the person. Ms.
Taney stated the city is being asked to either approve or disapprove a text
amendment that would affect the entire city, not a particular individual’s
building plan. Mrs. Bedell stated if this is for Mr. Neltner, he could go
either place in the shopping center. She also asked if City Attorney Deters was
also the attorney for Mr. Neltner. City Attorney Deters stated he was not.
Mayor Moriconi stated this would be voted on at the Special Council Meeting
scheduled for November 8, 2004.
Fischer Homes-Clover Ridge Subdivision-Request for a Waiver of Cluster
Mailboxes
Mayor Moriconi stated a packet from Fischer Homes was received for council to
review and introduced Mr. Greg Fischer, the construction manager at Fischer
Homes. Mr. Fischer stated he was new to the community as the Construction
Manager for Clover Ridge Subdivision. He stated he was not familiar with the
city’s ordinance banning cluster mailboxes. He stated that the entire
development has cluster mailboxes and with the subdivision in the last phase of
construction, he would like to continue to install the last three cluster
mailboxes and requested the city to waive enforcement of the ordinance that
prohibits them. Mayor Moriconi asked how the mailboxes were approval to be
installed. Mr. Fischer stated these cluster mailboxes were obviously installed
by Fischer without notice and was not aware of an Ordinance that was passed in
1999 to ban cluster mailboxes. City Clerk, Ms. Taney stated the original
ordinance banning cluster mailboxes was enacted in 1993 and has since been
amended.
City Attorney Deters asked if it was possible to change the mailboxes by way of
the Homeowners Association. Mr. Fischer stated that in some Homeowner’s
Associations you would need 70% approval to change the mailbox styles. Council
Member Franzen stated Fischer Homes was the major developer in her subdivision
(Liberty Orchard) and they installed $12.00 mailboxes in everyone’s front yard
and they were all uniform. She stated when other builders developed the back
end of the subdivision the property owners were permitted to install their own
mailboxes. She stated she did not feel that should be an issue and that Fischer
should remove all the cluster mailboxes in Clover Ridge and individual mail
boxes be installed. Mr. Greg Fischer stated since he learned about the
ordinance, Sycamore Creek has already been changed to individual mailboxes.
Terry Laughlin, 9653 Cloveridge Drive stated she has a degenerative muscle
disease and it is painful for her to stand for long periods of time. She stated
she did not see any cluster mail boxes when they visited the subdivision before
buying their home. She stated that she favors individual mailboxes over the
cluster mailboxes that Fischer has installed.
Leslie Balch, 3046 Saddlebred Court addressed Mayor and Council regarding the
installation of cluster mailboxes installed by Fischer Homes. She stated she is
a post office employee and she knows the cluster mailboxes should not have been
installed. She stated the cluster boxes are tacky looking and also a hazard for
residents during bad winter weather.
Mayor Moriconi stated the mailboxes are actually illegal, and asked Council how
they would like to proceed, given Mr. Fischer’s request for a waiver. Council
Member Franzen stated to Mr. Fischer that she understands that he has inherited
this dilemma, but Fischer Homes has illegally installed these postal units. She
stated they need to removed and let the residents install their own individual
mailboxes. Mr. Fischer stated he did not know the procedure on removing the
cluster mailboxes. Mayor Moriconi stated the post office owns the cluster
mailboxes and will remove them at Mr. Fischer’s request.
Council Member Yeager asked if there was a form letter available for all the
developers and builders making them aware of this ordinance. City Clerk, Ms.
Taney stated she has discussed this with the Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian,
and the city is going to devise a way to contact each developer or homebuilder
of this ordinance. Mrs. JoAnne Cobble stated she feels this is a major problem
that has slipped through the cracks and there is a problem with our building
and zoning. Council Member Franzen stated she did not feel cluster mail boxes
present a “major problem” in the city. Ms. Taney stated cluster mailboxes are
not one of the construction requirements that the Building Inspector checks.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he had nothing to report.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Shawn Butler reported to Mayor and Council that Officer Kevin Gill
resigned as of today. He stated we do wish him well but he was injured in the
line of duty some time ago and will be applying for his state pension. He
stated with the injuries he received, Officer Gill can never return as a police
officer. Chief Butler stated again everyone wishes him and his family well.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi asked Council Member Bushong to select a business of the month
for November. Council Member Bushong stated he would get back to the Mayor on
his choice.
Memorial Park Practice Field Agreement
Council Member Franzen stated she had received a letter from the South Kenton
Lions asking for a more permanent arrangement with the city for the use of the
fields at Memorial Park. She stated they do not want to change any terms on the
agreement, but want to extend the arrangement for three to five years, instead
of a yearly arrangement. Mr. David Nolan stated they just want to be assured of
a place for the kids to practice. City Attorney Deters stated there is a
premise in the law regarding municipalities not being allowed to bind future
public entities for too long. He stated this council couldn’t make a decision
that would normally bind future decisions like this request, for a new council.
Mr. David Nolan stated he has heard from numerous people that in the “past
minutes” the park was given to them to use as a practice facility. City
Attorney Deters stated he would see if a long-term agreement could be drawn up.
Budget Amendment
Mayor Moriconi stated coming up there will be a first reading to amend the
budget to account for the T-21 Grant, which are for the installation of
sidewalks. He also stated that the budget amendment would note snow removal
expenses will be changed to $1,000.00 a mile and the $68,000.00 that was
allocated for ALS (Advanced Life Support) services to the residents.
Mayor Moriconi stated that Chief Butler has informed him that the Public Works
Department will have to vacate their headquarters on Cox Road that is currently
being leased from the Independence Fire District sometime in 2005. He stated
the Fire District would be bulldozing the building to construct a new fire
station on the east side of town.
Selling of Old Administration Building
Mayor Moriconi stated the old city building has been sold and the closing would
be Wednesday, October 20, 2004. He stated the ribbon cutting for the new
Municipal Center would be held on October 23, 2004 at 4:00 pm and invited
everyone to come and tour the new building.
Adjournment
There being no further business, motion was made by Council Member Brinker and
seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion was carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:15 pm.

November 8, 2004
Special Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
of the Council on Monday, November 8, 2004 at 7:00 pm in the Senior Citizens
and Community Center, 2001 Jack Woods Parkway in Independence with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric
Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K.
Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced that this special meeting of the city council was
called to discuss and possibly take action on the following agenda items:
·   A proposed design of a Cox Road turn lane
·   Voluntary annexation request by Jim and Helen Kudera for property located
on McMillan Drive – Resolution No. 2004-R-11
·   A proposed zoning text amendment that would add ‘auto laundry’ in the NSC
zones – Resolution No. 2004-R-12

1st Reading of the Proposed Ordinance
·   An executive session (only if necessary)
Proposed Design of a Turn Lane on Cox Road
Mayor Moriconi presented to council the idea of widening Cox Road at the
intersection of Taylor Mill Road (St. Rt. 16). He stated this proposal would
address the residents concerns that were voiced at the last meeting regarding
the Pembroke Village developer’s request to waive the turn lane on Cox Road’’
that was a condition of the development plan approved by the Kenton County
Planning Commission. Council Member Bushong commented that the original turn
lane proposed on Cox Road at the subdivision entrance would only accommodate
three cars. Mayor Moriconi stated that the proposal to extend the turn lane to
the intersection of Taylor Mill Road would be a separate issue. He advised that
it might be possible to acquire state funds that are specifically used for
congested intersections. He stated he would like to direct the city engineer to
actively work on a design to improve traffic flow at that intersection. Council
Member Dupps commented that it makes sense to look at improving the roadway, as
the traffic conditions will only worsen in the future. Council Member Behler
asked if state funds are available and if the city would have to fund some of
the improvements. Mayor Moriconi stated he was not sure, but it was a
possibility that the city may have to fund one-half of the project. He stated
he would like to direct the city engineer to design a turn lane then the city
could submit the proposal to the state with a request for assistance. Council
Member Brinker asked if the city engineer would charge an hourly rate to do the
design work. Chief Butler commented that the developer has already done a
traffic study, so it would only be necessary to fund the design work by the
engineer at his regular hourly rate.
Council Member Yeager asked when the developer was scheduled to have the public
hearing on the request for a waiver for installing a turn lane into the
Pembroke Village subdivision. Council Member Bushong stated that the public
hearing was postponed until next month. Mayor Moriconi commented the short turn
lane that the developer has been required to install on Cox Road may only
worsen the traffic flow at that site. Council Member Behler asked if a traffic
light could be installed at the intersection of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road.
Chief Butler replied that although the city has been denied a request for a
traffic light in the past that it may possibly be granted this time.
Council Member Behler made a motion to direct the city engineer to review the
Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road intersection and design a turn lane on Cox Road
between Taylor Mill road and the entrance into the Pembroke Village
subdivision. Council Member Bushong seconded the motion. Council Member Yeager
commented that she favors requesting funds from the state and possibly the
developer of the subdivision. Council Member Dupps asked what other recourse
would be available to the city if the developer does not install the turn lane
into the subdivision as he previously agreed. Mayor Moriconi stated the city
would proceed in trying to get state assistance. Chief Butler commented that
both roads are state maintained. Council Member Franzen expressed concern that
since the state does not feel this development will generate the additional
traffic that would meet their requirements for a turn lane; they probably will
not be willing to fund road improvements to the site. Council Member Bushong
stated at the last public hearing regarding the developer’s request to waive
this condition of the subdivision development, the developer had stated that
the state did not feel a turn lane was necessary. There being no further
discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2004-R-11 – Supporting a Voluntary Annexation of Property
Located on McMillan Drive, Owned by James and Helen Kudera
Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2004-R-11 that would support
a voluntary request by Jim and Helen Kudera for annexation of a parcel of
property they own on McMillan Drive. He stated that the parcel is nine-tenths
of an acre and is adjacent to property owned by the Kudera’s, which is already
within the city limits. Mayor Moriconi introduced Jerry Dusing, legal counsel
for the Kudera’s who would present the request and answer any questions council
may have.
Mr. Dusing stated that his clients would be requesting a zone change along with
the annexation so that they can utilize the property for the development of an
independent living retirement village for residents over the age of fifty-five.
He stated the units would be purchased outright with a pro-rated buyout.
Council Member Bushong asked if an egress would be made possible onto the new
section of Route 17. Mr. Dusing replied yes and that it would be the main
public access to the development with an emergency access onto McMillan Drive.
Mayor Moriconi asked if they would be requesting a re-zoning of the property
along with the annexation. Mr. Dusing stated yes.
Council Member Dupps moved to adopt Resolution No. 2004-R-11, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Council Member Bushong asked if the state has approved
an egress onto the new section of Route 17. Mr. Dusing advised that they have
presented their plans to the state but have not received an official approval
as yet. He stated that they did not anticipate any problems with obtaining
approval for the egress. Mayor Moriconi read Resolution No. 2004-R-11. Roll was
called and answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2004-R-12 – Denying a Recommendation by KCPC to Support a Text
Amendment to the Zoning Ordinance Adding Automobile Laundry in the NSC Zone
Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2004-R-12 that would
disapprove a recommendation by the Kenton County Planning Commission to amend
the zoning text to add automobile laundry as a permitted use in the NSC zone
and disapprove an automobile laundry as conditional use in the NSC zone. He
stated that this resolution would reject the entire proposed text amendment.
Council Member Yeager stated she did not understand why the city would apply
for a text amendment, and then deny approval of the recommendation by the
Planning Commission. Council Member Franzen stated that it was explained at the
last meeting that the city was approached by a citizen who stopped in the city
office requesting this amendment and that the city followed procedure to be the
official applicant as is required. Mr. Deters reminded council that this
Resolution is being presented to them based on the discussion on this issue at
the last meeting. He reminded council that the general consensus was that the
city did not want to add automobile laundries in the NSC zones; neither as a
permitted or conditional use. He stated the proposed resolution formally
concludes the issue before them. Council Member Brinker stated that making
application on behalf the citizens reduces the time it would take if they had
to come make a formal request of the council before getting a recommendation
from the Planning Commission. Mr. Deters informed council that the Planning
Commission requires the city to be the sponsor and would not consider a
proposed text amendment unless the city is the applicant. Council Member Yeager
commented that she feels the location for which a text amendment is intended
should be an important factor before submitting the application.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi read Resolution No. 2004-R-
12. Council Member Franzen moved to approve Resolution No. 2004-R-12, seconded
by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously; motion
carried 6-0.
Shadybrook Trails Subdivision – Approval of the Stage II Development Plan
Mayor Moriconi directed council to the correspondence inserted in their packets
from the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission regarding the Stage II
development plan for an approximate 65-acre area in the Shadybrook Trails
subdivision. The property is located approximately 600 feet south of Senour
Road between Cloverridge Drive and Fowler Creek Road. The development plan
includes 140 detached single-family residential lots with provisions for open
space and recreational areas. Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Chuck Berling to
answer any questions that council may have regarding the plan.
Mr. Berling advised council that the Stage II development plan adds
recreational amenities that will include two soccer fields, a restroom facility
and additional parking for the sports fields. He stated that the recreational
amenities for this development were established earlier this year after
collaborating with the city. He stated that the Planning Commission has
thoroughly reviewed the plan and has recommended approval. Mr. Berling advised
that the land has been graded, utilities lines will be installed this winter so
that construction of the houses will begin in the summer of 2005 and the park
areas ready by the spring of 2006.
Council Member Yeager moved to approve the Stage II Development Plan for the
Shadybrook Trails subdivision, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance amending Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 Establishing Sunday Liquor
Sales – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance 2003-O-08 that established the Sunday Liquor Sales. He ceded
the floor to Mrs. JoAnne Cobble, who asked to address council on this issue.
Mrs. Cobble provided some history on the adoption of the original ordinance
(Ordinance No. 2003-O-08). She stated that, as she understands it, the Sunday
liquor sale was prompted by a request by the Kenton County Golf Course. She
stated the golf course possesses a beer license and wanted to be allowed to
begin selling beer at 11:00 a.m. on Sunday’s to their patrons.
Council Member Brinker asked if the golf course was in the city limits. Chief
Butler advised that it is.
Mrs. Cobble went on to say that she discussed this with Mr. Jim Ellison, who
was on council when Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 was enacted and that he conveyed
that the intent of the ordinance was to allow alcoholic drinks (beer only) in a
sit down establishment only. She questioned the city attorney and council why
the language of the ordinance was written to include hard liquor. Council
Member Yeager commented that the 2003 ordinance was not intended specifically
for the golf course but was enacted city-wide. Mrs. Cobble questioned why it
included the sale of hard liquor when the golf course only sells beer. Mayor
Moriconi expressed concern that the city would not enact an ordinance that
would show favor to a particular establishment. Mrs. Cobble informed council
that when the original ordinance was enacted in 2003, and that it was in direct
conflict with state laws regarding the sales of hard liquor before 1:00 p.m. on
Sunday. She suggested more restrictive language that the proposed amended
ordinance contains.
Council Member Franzen advised Mrs. Cobble that Mr. Ellison voted in favor of
the ordinance that is currently in effect regarding Sunday liquor sales and
commented that she is not sure why he says the language is not what he
intended. Council Member Franzen informed Mrs. Cobble that she personally
opposed Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 and voted against its approval. Mrs. Cobble
stated that if this council adopts the proposed language amendment before them
that they would be permitting hard liquor to be sold at 11:00 a.m. on Sundays.
Council Member Dupps asked if there was a difference between beer and malt
beverages. Mr. Deters advised council there are two state statutes regulating
the sale of beer and distilled spirits and wine. He stated the laws regarding
distilled spirits and wine are more restrictive as they are considered more
‘evil’ than beer. Mrs. Cobble expressed intense concern that if council enacts
the ordinance before them with the proposed language, that they would dilute
the standards of this community.
Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Deters how the original ordinance would stand
if the proposed language amendment were not approved. Mr. Deters stated the
proposed language eliminates serving by the drink prior to 1:00 p.m. Mrs.
Cobble countered that the proposed language still permits the sale of packaged
hard liquor at 11:00 a.m. on Sunday. Council Member Yeager commented that it
also includes all other days, resulting in only a two-hour difference per week.
Mr. Deters stated that a city ordinance could not trump a state law. He stated
that Beechgrove Liquors contacted the city regarding Sunday sales. Mayor
Moriconi stated that since the state statute was amended, the City of Bellevue
has permitted Sunday liquor sales. Mrs. Cobble reiterated her concern that hard
liquor sales were permitted in the original ordinance. Mayor Moriconi stated
that the ordinance was drafted to be general for all businesses throughout the
city that hold liquor licenses and not just to accommodate the golf course.
Council Member Dupps asked Mr. Deters what text would be amended in the current
ordinance. Mr. Deters stated that the language “serve” would be eliminated.
Council Member Dupps asked if the state permits the city to establish the time
for sales and service of alcohol. Mr. Deters advised that the state draws a
distinction between the two types of alcohol. Mrs. Cobble commented that she
does not feel the parameters set forth would have been prohibitive to other
businesses in the city. She concluded by stating that she wanted council to be
certain that they are aware of exactly what they are voting for if this
ordinance is enacted. She stated that she knows of no other city that permits
hard liquor sales before 1:00 pm on Sunday and that she felt there was a moral
and family issue at stake and that the proposed ordinance would weaken the
community standards if passed.
Council Member Dupps countered that even if the city did not permit liquor
sales on Sunday until 1:00 pm., there are other religions that hold services on
other days besides Sunday mornings. Council Member Franzen stated she voted
against the ordinance in 2003. Council Member Behler stated that her position
as a substance abuse professional she does not favor earlier sales on Sunday.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that if the proposed ordinance is voted down,
than the original ordinance will remain. Mr. Deters stated this proposed
ordinance is meant to clarify the language of Ordinance 2003-O-08. Mayor
Moriconi read the proposed ordinance number 2004-O-23. Council Member Yeager
moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2004-O-23, seconded by Council Member Dupps. A
brief discussion continued. Council Member Dupps asked if this proposed
ordinance is not approved would Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 be upheld. Mr. Deters
replied yes, but that the interpretation of serving before 1:00 pm would be
incorrect. He stated the proposed ordinance would clarify that language by
eliminating the word “serve.” He reiterated that state law draws a distinction
between selling and serving by the drink. He stated if council does not adopt
this amendment, then the other option would be to repeal Ordinance No. 2003-O-
08. Council Member Brinker suggested the newly elected council members taking
office in January 2005 could propose changes to the ordinance. Roll call was
answered with two yes votes and four no votes cast by Council Members Franzen,
Behler, Brinker and Bushong.
Mr. Deters advised council that the current ordinance (Ordinance No. 2003-O-08)
is in conflict with state law. Council Member Bushong stated the Council taking
office in January would need to amend the current ordinance. Mr. Kent Kelso,
spoke from the floor to comment that if the current ordinance is in conflict
with state law then it is basically null and void. Mr. Deters agreed that that
section of the ordinance would be null and void.
Mrs. Cobble commented that the owner of Beechgrove Liquors called the city
office and spoke with the City Clerk, Ms. Taney, who is also the ABC
Administrator for the city regarding the sale of liquor at 11:00 a.m. She
stated that Ms. Taney told the storeowner he was permitted to sell. Ms. Taney
responded by advising council that she did speak to the storeowner, read the
ordinance to him over the phone, and then faxed Ordinance No. 2003-O-08 to him
and advised he have his personal attorney review the ordinance for legal
counsel regarding it’s content. Mrs. Cobble commented that the ordinance should
be clearer.
Proposed Ordinance Amending the 2004-05 Budget Ordinance – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would amend the
current fiscal year’s budget. He explained the main changes included the
following: adding the expense of $68,000 for the city’s share to fund the
TransCare ALS (Advanced Life Support) service to the citizens; insurance line
items - property, general liability and workers’ compensation insurance actuals
came in higher than estimated; eliminated the zoning contract line item and
added the recently hired zoning administrator’s wages to administrative
personnel salaries; adding $50,000 to Memorial Park land improvements line item
to install basketball courts in the Spring of 2005; eliminating the salary and
benefits of the Senior Center Director, since Nita Brake, the Recreation
Director assumed those duties when ’’Joan Bowling’ resigned from the position;
adding the $160,000 revenue the city will receive for the T-21 sidewalk grant
and the twenty percent the city will match; and, increasing the snow removal
expense to cover the maintenance of sixteen miles of county roads. Council
member Franzen commented that considering the city may have to assume the
additional maintenance of county roads that are within city boundaries, now may
not be the time to take on the expense of adding basketball courts to Memorial
Park. She suggested the city try to get a developer to donate this amenity to
the Park. Mayor Moriconi stated that could be a possibility. Council Member
Yeager stated she would attempt to get some private donations to fund the
basketball courts. Chief Butler advised that some of that $50,000 land
improvements is to cover some outstanding expenses that were carried over from
the 2003-04 budget when it was closed out. Council Member Behler asked how
much. Chief Butler stated between $10,000 - $12,000. He stated the remainder
would include parking lot lights, as well as the basketball courts. Council
Member Behler favored deleting the courts, and preferred installation of
lights. Chief Butler advised that last year’s bills would have to be paid
first, and of course lights would be a priority over courts. Council Member
Behler asked the cost of lights. Chief Butler stated he did not have an
estimate yet. Council Member Yeager stated that council was informed about the
plans to install basketball courts. Council Member Franzen asked if the council
would vote on the installation of the courts. Chief Butler advised that if the
bids were over $20,000 the council would vote on the award of the bid. Council
Member Dupps asked the planned location of the courts. Chief Butler explained
where they would be placed. Council Member Behler stated she would like the
explanation of that line item to include ‘pay outstanding bills and lighting’.
Council Member Yeager asked that the Park and Recreation Donations Revenue line
item reflect the actual of $4,000, which is an increase of $1,000 over the
estimated amount.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance
amending the 2004/05 budget. Mayor Moriconi advised that it would be presented
for a second reading at the December 6, 2004 meeting.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to adjourn.
Council Member Franzen so moved, with second from Council Member Bushong.
Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting adjourned at 8:00 pm.

City of Independence, Ky
November 15, 2004
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, November
15, 2004 at 7:00 pm at the Senior Citizens and Community Center with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Members Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric
Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager answered roll call. Also present was City
Attorney, Jed K. Deters. Mayor Moriconi advised council that Council Member
Behler was absent due to illness.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi announced that the citizens signed in to address council are
reserving their privilege to speak regarding specific agenda items at the time
the issue is presented.
NEW BUSINESS
Voluntary Annexation Request by Freedom Park, LLC
Mayor Moriconi advised that the developers of the Freedom Park subdivision are
requesting the city annex an unincorporated portion of land to the east of the
existing platted subdivision. He stated the area proposed for annexation is a
little over 8.5 acres and will take the subdivision out to State KY 17 at the
point of relocation. Mayor Moriconi introduced the developer, Tom Schreiber and
his legal counsel, Mike Duncan.
Mr. Duncan explained that the property is located along the south end of
Freedom Trail Drive that currently is a dead-end. He stated that the property
is currently outside city limits, is zoned R-1C and they will develop the
property as is currently zoned. He stated that annexation would ensure all
property owners in the subdivision have city services and suggested it would be
difficult for the city to monitor which properties are within city limits and
which are not if part of the subdivision is outside city limits. Mr. Duncan
stated that since the property will abut KY 17 when it is relocated, this would
provide another egress for the subdivision.
Council Member Yeager asked the location of the exit point onto KY 17. Mr.
Duncan advised that the street would feed out to KY 17 directly across from
Maple Tree Lane. Council Member Brinker asked the time frame for the
development, specifically when the egress onto KY 17 would be constructed. Mr.
Schreiber stated that the state highway department has granted them permission
to construct a temporary drive to access KY 17 until the relocated section is
constructed, so that the new property owners could utilize this egress. He
stated that the highway department has indicated that the construction of that
section of KY 17 would be let out for bids the first of the year (2005).
Council Member Franzen asked if they would be developing the land even if the
city does not grant their request for annexation. Mr. Schreiber replied yes;
that they have already begun development. Council Member Yeager stated she
would like the city to have a copy of the permit issued by the state granting
Freedom Park LLC access onto KY 17. Mr. Schreiber advised they did not have the
permission in written form yet, but stated he would request this from the
state. Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Schreiber if he would be able to obtain
a written permit before a first reading of the annexation ordinance at the next
meeting on December 6, 2004. Council Member Dupps expressed concern with having
a first reading of this annexation ordinance with the current council and then
the second reading with the new council in January. Mr. Deters advised that it
was an acceptable procedure. Council Member Franzen suggested the first reading
could be delayed until January 2005.
Mayor Moriconi advised this issue would be presented at either the December 6th
or January 3rd council meeting for a first reading.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Map Amendment – Flanagan Property 26 Acres on
Madison Pike - KCPC Application No. 1698R
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a recommendation from the Kenton County
Planning Commission approving a map amendment for a 26-acre parcel on the east
side of Madison Pike owned by Nancy and Everett Flanagan. He stated the
proposed map amendment would rezone the property from R-1C to R-2 (PUD). Mayor
Moriconi introduced Jim Bertram from One Eleven Developers, LLC and his legal
counsel, Tim Theissen.
Mr. Bertram distributed a detailed development plan to Mayor Moriconi and
council. Mr. Theissen made an in-depth presentation of the proposed development
plan for the 26-acre parcel. He advised council that the proposed map amendment
went before the Planning Commission on November 4, 2004 and received a
unanimous favorable recommendation for approval subject to four conditions. Mr.
Theissen advised that the parcel of property for the proposed development would
run between old KY 17 and the new section of KY 17. The development plan
identifies a through street that would connect both the old and new sections of
KY 17. He stated that due to elevation drops, the connector road should
discourage traffic speeding violators. Mr. Theissen stated that the PUD plan
would be part residential and part commercial with condominiums on the north
side and six commercial outlots on the south side. He stated the commercial
lots would be small retail, restaurants, gas station and a bank. He stated the
development would be a walkable community with sidewalks throughout. Mr.
Theissen stated that the developers have been working on the plan for a year
and are now marketing the concept with intended users lined up. He advised that
a PUD requires twenty percent open space, which is included, providing walking
trails along the creek area, and two retention ponds for storm water drainage.
He stated that a gravity sewer system would hook into the Hartland Subdivision.
He advised that the proposed plan provides a nice tree buffer along the Walnut
Hall properties. Mr. Theissen also indicated that the plan would provide a
driveway to connect future development of the adjoining parcel at the corner of
Madison Pike and Harris Road, as well as providing access for the Jarboe
property next door. Mr. Theissen advised council that this proposed development
is consistent with the recommended Land Use map of the 2001 area-wide
Comprehensive Plan.
Mr. Theissen commented that he is aware that Mr. Charlie Deters is concerned
about the undeveloped lots he has available at the Towne Center. He stated he
doesn’t know why the lots are still vacant along ’’’’Shaw Road’’ (St. Rt. 536),
unless it is because it is a 2-lane road.
Mr. Theissen advised council of the four conditions that the Planning
Commission imposed upon approval of the development plan and to which they have
no objections. He stated the four conditions are: 1) a traffic study be
prepared to assess the north-south and east-west movement of traffic as well as
needs for possible intersection improvements in the area, crosswalks and
traffic control devices; 2) landscape screening along the existing KY 17 and
the proposed new section of KY 17 as well as areas adjacent to residential
zones; 3) only one pole sign will be permitted and located at the east end of
the development; and 4) a provision be made for a future connection to the
property to the south by way of an access drive between the proposed two-level
commercial building and the building to the east. He stated that they are
certain the traffic study will reveal that they will need to add turn lanes on
KY 17, but expressed concern that they would install the turn lanes only to see
them torn out in the future when Charlie Deters complies with the Towne Center
development conditions. Mr. Theissen requested specific text be included in the
ordinance the city would adopt approving this map amendment that would not
require compliance of improvements to Madison Pike until the time of and in
coordination with other improvements by the developer (Charlie Deters) of the
Independence Towne Center. He also requested specific text included in the
ordinance that would stated that no screening would be required to roadways,
internal to development, nor to future commercial sites to the south.
Council Member Yeager asked if Mr. Theissen had an overlay for the commercial
development that council could view. Mr. Theissen stated he did not prepare an
overlay for viewing, but the commercial uses are limited to, and are identified
as banks, professional offices, service stations and restaurants. Council
Member Brinker asked the time frame for the construction/opening of the new
section of KY 17. Mr. Bertram responded that they have been informed by the
state that construction would be put out to bid in January 2005, but since a
state budget has not yet been adopted, the state is hesitant to provide an
exact time frame. He stated that the state has acquired property and the design
plans are complete. Council Member Brinker asked the developer’s time frame.
Mr. Bertram advised they would like to commence development of the land in 2005
before moving forward. Mr. Theissen stated the development would not move
forward without the new section of KY 17 underway.
Mayor Moriconi asked about the sanitation tie in for this development. Mr.
Bertram stated that they would install a gravity line by acquiring easements
from the adjacent property owners, which will allow them to provide sewer
service to the residents on Walnut Hall Drive. Mayor Moriconi asked if these
users would be tied into the Fowler Creek system. Mr. Bertram stated he was not
sure. Council Member Franzen asked if the proposed sewer lines would be able to
service the properties along Madison Pike across from the new city building.
Mr. Bertram replied yes, as well as the properties on Peach Drive.
Mayor Moriconi commented that this development being proposed by One Eleven
Developers LLC is the most major development in the city since the Independence
Towne Center. Council Member Brinker expressed reservations about proceeding
with a commitment on this zone change request since the second reading of an
ordinance would not be held until January 2005, when a new group of council
members will take office. Mayor Moriconi stated that a first reading that would
be held on December 6, 2004 would not require a vote by this council, but
acknowledged Council Member Brinker’s concern and suggested that the first
reading of the ordinance could be delayed until January 3, 2005. Mr. Jed Deters
advised that the city council had ninety days to act on the KCPC’s
recommendation on this map amendment. Mr. Bertram stated that since the KCPC
recommendation was made at its November 4, 2004 meeting, the city has until
February 4, 2005 to take action.
Council Member Bushong questioned whether or not this proposed development
would be tied into the Fowler Creek Debt Reduction assessment. Mr. Bertram
stated that the system would tie into the trunk line of the pump station on
Fowler Creek Road, but did not know if the assessment would apply to this
development. Council Member Yeager commented that perhaps the Sanitation
District should attend a city council meeting to explain if this development
will be tapping into the Fowler Creek lines. Mr. Jed Deters advised that the
development would be subject to the assessment if they use the system.
Mayor Moriconi advised that the sewer tap in information should be obtained
from the Sanitation District prior to the January 3, 2005 council meeting when
they will schedule a first reading of an ordinance to approve this map
amendment. Council Member Yeager stated she did not see a need to delay the
first reading until January and suggested having the proposed ordinance
prepared in time for a first reading at the December 6, 2004 meeting.
Council Member Brinker asked Mr. Bertram if he had commercial tenants
contracted yet. Mr. Bertram advised that while he does not have formal
contracts signed yet, he has had more interest than he has available lots. He
suggested that this development could help bring more business into the area
thereby helping the Independence Towne Center also.
Citizen Comments Regarding the Map Amendment Request for the Flanagan Property
Jerry Zimmerer, 2340 Harris Pike, Independence – Mr. Zimmerer stated he opposed
the planned development for the Flanagan property. He stated as his concerns
were with increased traffic congestion in the vicinity of the Harris Pike/Shaw
Road/Madison Pike intersection. He pointed out there are several vacant
commercial buildings/property already in the local area, including Nicholson,
which could be utilized. Mr. Zimmerer also suggested that the proposed
development’s connector road would be a headache for the residents due to
speeders.
Charlie Deters, developer of the Independence Towne Center – Mr. Deters stated
that he was reluctant to speak against the proposed development across from the
Towne Center, but felt it necessary to re-examine the planning principles with
regard to zoning which the Planning Commission adopted in the 1998
Comprehensive Plan. He read an excerpt from the Plan that outlined the
philosophy. Mr. Deters stated that the proposed map amendment is contrary to
the Planning Commission’s own philosophy regarding zoning.
Mr. Deters advised council that when he devised a development plan for the
Towne Center, he tried to build a comprehensive site and of the original fifty
acres, twenty acres are still undeveloped. He also stated that twenty-six acres
was donated to the city for the development of recreational facilities. Mr.
Deters went on to say that the area currently has adequate food service and
that most are having financial difficulties. He advised that the Courthouse
Restaurant has never made a profit.
Mr. Deters advised council that the reason for zoning is to create an orderly
progression in the city. He stated that he feels they have tried to do that in
the Towne Center. He stated the Towne Center has wide streets and the best and
only retention system in the area, which was very expensive to construct. He
stated that the proposed development plan submitted by One Eleven LLC has a
thoroughfare that is too narrow and in his opinion is the weakest part of the
plan.
Mr. Deters stated that when the city recently sold the municipal park and ride
lot to make way for commercial development he was asked to allow the TANK
busses to use a section of the parking lot at the Towne Center for a park and
ride for the bus patrons. He stated that at first he was hesitant to do this,
but having the city’s best interest at heart, and in the spirit of cooperation
he consented to the request. Mr. Deters commented that he believe the
construction of the new Wal-Mart on KY 17 in Fort Wright will hurt commercial
development in Independence for some time. He stated that he feels the proposed
development on the Flanagan property is an attempt to piggyback off the Kroger
anchor store at the Towne Center, which generates the majority of the traffic
in the area. In closing, Mr. Deters commented that there is no demand in
Independence for the proposed residential section of the development.
Mr. Bertram commented that he was the buyer of the city’s municipal park and
ride lot. He stated construction on the lot will begin in 2005 of a 3500 square
foot building and that he already has 2500 square feet of it leased. He stated
he would also begin the process of applying for a zone change on the property
adjacent to his office building at 5294 Madison so that he can continue the
commercial development of that area. He stated that as a business owner
operating in Independence he has an interest in this community and he is trying
to grow this area by marketing a theme. He stated he wants to succeed and grow
his business and be a part of the planned growth in the city.
Council Member Yeager asked which part of the development he would begin with –
residential or commercial. Mr. Bertram replied that he planned to develop both
residential and commercial simultaneously. He stated the condos would be sold,
not leased.
Council Member Brinker commented that council has to look at each development
objectively and not favor one or the other. Mr. Charlie Deters asked how he
would answer the planning principles he quoted directly from the Planning
Commission. Council Member Brinker stated that it appears there has been a
change in their philosophy in recent years. Mr. Theissen commented that he held
the position of Chairman on the Planning Commission when the 1996 Comprehensive
Plan was drafted. He stated that the Plan was adopted prior to the re-routing
of KY 17. He went on to say that he agrees with the planning philosophy that
Mr. Deters quoted, but that the current section of KY 17 wil become a collector
road with the new KY 17 improvements are made. Mr. Theissen stated that the
development plan for the Flanagan property is designed exactly as is outlined
in the updated 2001 Comprehensive Plan.
Mayor Moriconi suggested that council may need some time to digest the proposed
development plan and could have more questions prior to the first reading of
the ordinance, which might be delayed until January 2005. Council Member
Franzen asked Mr. Bertram if this proposed development was contingent on the
construction of the new section of KY 17. Mr. Bertram stated that the back
section of the development would not be constructed until the new section of KY
17 is completed and he is confident that the state will make the road
improvements in two or three years. He stated that the entire development would
be constructed in phases over several years. Council Member Franzen commented
that she thought it would be a good idea to make the connector road three
lanes. Mr. Bertram stated that the connector road is designed to be twenty-
eight feet wide, but a traffic study may determine a third lane may be merited.
He went on to say that they are attempting to make it a well balanced
development and will take it into consideration. Mr. Zimmerer asked about
parking for the condos. Mr. Theissen stated that each condo will have a two-car
garage plus two additional parking spaces which is a requirement of
Independence codes. Mrs. Cobble asked if anyone knew the width of Cody Road.
Mr. Bertram advised that Cody Road is about 21-22 feet wide and that many of
the old county roads vary in width from 17-22 feet.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi advised this issue would be
revisited either in December or January.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Text Amendment – Request by Fifth Third Bank -
KCPC Application No. 1702R
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed text amendment, prompted by
Fifth Third Bank, that would amend the current zoning ordinance to add “banks
and other financial institutions” to the list of conditional uses within the R-
1D zone. He stated that Fifth Third Bank had simultaneously applied for a map
amendment for property owned by Thelma Stein, located at 4118 Richardson Road,
containing approximately 1.5 acres at the southeast corner of the intersection
of Independence Station Road. Mayor Moriconi advised that Fifth Third Bank has
since withdrawn their request for the map amendment and is looking for approval
of the text amendment.
Tim Garry, legal counsel for Thelma and Lawrence Stein advised that his clients
would like to sell the property to Fifth Third Bank and concurred that the
request for the map amendment has been withdrawn in hopes that the city will
approve a text amendment that would permit banks in the current zone. He stated
this property has been in the Stein family for fifty years and the Stein’s are
relying on the sale of this property for their retirement. He said that many
family members live in the vicinity of this parcel. Mr. Garry advised council
that the KCPC has recommended approval of the proposed text amendment.
Council Member Yeager commented that she had requested that the text “and
professional office buildings” be included in this proposed zoning amendment.
Mayor Moriconi advised the city could add that before the first reading.
Council Member Franzen commented that there are presently only two locations
within the city that this proposed text amendment would affect – the
intersection of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road, as well as Richardson Road and
Independence Station Road. Council Member Yeager stated that the text amendment
would still require the applicant to go before the city’s Board of Adjustment
to get approval for the conditional use. Mr. Deters concurred with Council
Member Yeager.
Mrs. Cobble commented that the text “and professional office buildings” was not
considered by the KCPC and expressed concern regarding the city adding this
text without the Planning Commission’s recommendation to do so. Council Member
Yeager commented that the city had agreed to this by resolution. Mrs. Cobble
expressed displeasure with the city going outside of the text that was
considered by the KCPC and felt the city should not add extra text without
making re-application. Mr. Deters advised that the city makes the final
decision and even though the application submitted for the KCPC’s
recommendation did not have all the proposed text the city wanted to include,
it contained sufficient text for consideration and he is comfortable with the
additional text if this is what council desires. Council Member Franzen
commented that even if the city has included “and professional office
buildings” in the text amendment application and it was recommended for
disapproval by the KCPC, the city would have the authority to override that
recommendation. Mrs. Cobble stated that she feels the residential zones should
be protected and that the property owners should not have to defend their
properties. She reiterated that she didn’t feel the city should be permitted to
make a text amendment without getting comment and recommendation by the KCPC.
Council Member Bushong asked why Fifth Third Bank withdrew their application
for a map amendment. Mr. Garry advised that they felt they do not need the map
amendment and that their use can be satisfied with a text amendment. Mr. Deters
commented that the city recommended that Fifth Third apply for both the text
amendment and the map amendment simultaneously so that KCPC could consider them
side by side.
Council Member Franzen commented that she feels a traffic light will be needed
at that busy intersection and suggested the bank lobby the state officials to
provide a signal. David Curle, architect for Fifth Third Bank, commented that
they spoke with the Transportation Cabinet who advised road improvements will
begin the spring of 2005. He said that the state will not provide an exact
starting date for the road project. Mr. Curle commented that when recommending
the text amendment language, it was for specific limited use on an arterial and
collector street. He stated that within a five mile radius of the project site,
there are other like business services within that circle of use.
Mayor Moriconi stated this proposed text amendment ordinance would be discussed
further at the December 6, 2004 meeting. Mr. Deters advised council there is no
time limitation for the city to adopt a text amendment like there is for a map
amendment, so they will have all the time they need to consider this issue. Mr.
Curle commented that Fifth Third Bank was intent on the city having a first
reading of a proposed ordinance to adopt this text amendment at the December 6,
2004 council meeting. He stated they would like to have final approval on the
ordinance before the end of the year and hoped this would be workable for the
city to accomplish. Council Member Brinker commented that he would be agreeable
to resolving this issue before the end of the year. Council Member Dupps
commented that the December 6, 2004 meeting will determine if this can be
resolved by year end. Mayor Moriconi stated that the city will decide at the
December 6th meeting if it will be necessary to schedule another meeting to
finish some of the outstanding issues begun by this council before the end of
their term.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler advised he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Bushong who he would select to receive the December
Business of the Month award. Council Member Bushong advised he selected
Deaton’s Nursery and Greenhouse.
Mayor Moriconi announced that the Christmas Walk & Tour would be held on
Friday, December 10, 2004 from 7-9 pm. He encouraged everyone to attend.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that he is having some of the sidewalks
repaired/replaced in the downtown area in preparation for the Christmas Walk
this year. He stated the sidewalks have been in a deteriorating condition for
many years and have become a safety issue.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Yeager moved to adjourn,
seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes and the
meeting ended at 8:35 p.m.

December 6, 2004
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
December 6 2004 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with
Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Charles Steger of Hickory rove
Baptist Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Eric
Dupps, Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K.
Deters. Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone in attendance and stated this was a
historical meeting as it is the first official meeting of the City Council
being held in the new Municipal Center
Presentation to the Police Department by the Kentucky Crime Prevention
Coalition
2.   Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Bob Douglas, Director of the Kentucky Crime
Prevention Coalition. Mr. Douglas stated that each year the Coalition
recognizes an agency they feel is worthy of the outstanding local crime
prevention project. He stated that this year the Coalition was presenting the
Independence Police Department with this recognition due to the active Citizens
Police Academy alumni members and the committed level of volunteer involvement.
Chief Butler thanked Mr. Douglas for his support and he also thanked all the
CPA Alumni volunteer for their many hours of service.

Nursery and Greenhouse as the recipient of the Business of the Month and
presented a plaque to Mr. Darrell Deaton. Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Deaton for
operating his business in the city.

Proposed Ordinance Approving a Map Amendment for 26-Acres owned by Nancy and
Everett Flanagan Located along the Eastside of Madison Pike – KCPC Application
No. 1698R – 1st Reading
8.   Mayor Moriconi stated that he would extend privileges of the floor to
those who signed in to speak on this proposed map amendment. He yielded the
floor to Mr. Charles Deters, developer of the Independence Towne Center.
9.   Mr. Deters spoke in opposition to the proposed re-zoning of the Flanagan
property. He stated that in 1998 Mr. Gene Daniels filed a zone change
application for the five acres at the corner of Harris Pike and Madison Pike,
where the Deaton’s Nursery is currently located. He stated that the Kenton
County Planning Commission (KCPC) recommended against the zone change citing
many reasons, one of which was they felt there was sufficient commercial
property at the Towne Center and in the Nicholson area to sufficiently handle a
future population of 20,000 to 75,000 people. Mr. Deters stated that the KCPC
felt there should only be commercial development along one side of the highway,
with no commercial development beyond the Shaw Road/Harris Pike/Madison Pike
intersection that would be near the Simon Kenton High School’’ as it was
consider that commercial development near an educational facility was not
conducive to the educational system. He stated those were considered to be the
essential differences in denying Mr. Daniels a zone change in 1998. Mr. Deters
stated that Mr. Tim Theissen, who is currently representing the developer for
the Flanagan’s property, was the chairman of the KCPC in 1998 and is the person
that communicated that recommendation to the city at the time.
10.   Mr. Deters went on to say that the Towne Center property had been for
sale for a long time when he expressed an interest in purchasing it. He stated
that he went before the Planning Commission to get a recommendation for a zone
change. He stated that the Planning Commission suggested the large parcel be
zoned for multiple uses that would include fifty acres of multi residential
units, along with commercial lots. He stated they also questioned and suggested
future need for municipal space for a firehouse and city building and open
green space. Mr. Deters stated he agreed with the Planning Commission’s
recommendation for the rezoning of the property and the development plan was
approved unanimously by the KCPC.
11.   Mr. Deters pointed out that the Independence Towne Center is only
partially developed and with adequate commercial space available, and utilities
already installed and a large retention basin in place, questioned the need for
more. He stated the Towne Center has a four-lane wide connector road from
Madison Pike to Shaw Road and the traffic move nicely because of the width of
the road. He stated it was expensive to construct, but it made the development
much nicer. Mr. Deters stated that he feels the city is not following through
with it’s commitment to the Towne Center. He stated that from the outset it was
considered to be an extended, long-range development plan, which is not yet
complete. He stated that the Planning Commission has now altered their criteria
regarding commercial development on one side of a highway.
12.   In closing, Mr. Deters distributed to council a proposed ordinance that
he drafted that would deny the zone change recommendation by the KCPC and urged
council to consider this option due to the adequate commercial land currently
available on the west side of Madison directly across from the proposed re-
zoning site.
13.   Council Member Brinker commented that Mr. Deters deserves a lot of credit
for the development of the Independence Towne Center, and while he often
frequents Mr. Deters restaurant and other retail shops, he feels it is not his
position to protect the interests of one developer. Council Member Brinker went
on to say that he feels the relocation of the new St. Rt. 17 has changed the
position of the Planning Commission with regard to commercial development along
Madison Pike. He stated that as he sees it, the city has two options in
building up the tax base; either rely on the residents by increasing their
property taxes or build up the commercial tax base. He stated he feels the city
needs to do whatever it can with regard to commercial economic development and
he sees this as the right approach to holding down property taxes.
14.   Council Member Yeager stated she wanted a guarantee that the developer
would have twenty-five percent of the residential development started before
beginning the development of the six commercial lots. Council Member Franzen
voiced disapproval of Council Member Yeager’s suggestion, stating that she
feels it would be a mistake that may cost the loss of the commercial tenants
the developer has secured. Council Member Yeager asked if the developer has
secured residential sales also. Mr. Jim Bertram of One Eleven Developers
advised that the secured developers of the commercial lots may withdraw their
commitment if they will be delayed from beginning their project for two or
three years. He stated he fears the residential developers may also pull out if
limitations are set that will delay the commencement of either section of the
development.
15.   Mayor Moriconi asked what percentage would be residential and commercial.
Mr. Bertram advised there would be eighteen acres of residential units and
eight acres of commercial parcels. He stated the commercial lots would be at
the south end of the development. Council Member Behler asked if the
development would be constructed in phases. Mr. Bertram advised it would, over
the span of several years. He stated they would begin by constructing the
connector road between Madison Pike and the new re-routed KY 17, and then they
would begin construction of the residential units and three commercial lots
simultaneously.
16.   Council Member Yeager asked what percent would be residential. Mr.
Bertram advised about thirty percent of the development would be residential.
Council Member Yeager stated she would like some assurance that the residential
units would be constructed before the commercial lots are developed. Mr.
Bertram advised that this development plan is a ‘package deal’ that he has been
working on for the past year. He stated he is unable to get firm commitments
from builders until the city approves of the proposed rezone and development
plan. He stated he does not want to be committed to complying with twenty-five
percent of the residential development before he can begin the commercial
development. He stated it may take two or three years for a prime corner
commercial lot to be developed. He reiterated that development of both the
residential and commercial sections needed to be constructed simultaneously.
17.   Mayor Moriconi asked the council how they wanted to proceed. He reminded
them that this was just a first reading of the proposed ordinance and would not
require a vote. He asked council if they wanted to have a first reading of the
proposed ordinance that would approve the recommendation by the KCPC to permit
the zone change or if they wanted to have a first reading of the ordinance that
was drafted and presented by Mr. Charles Deters that would deny the zone
change. City Attorney, Jed Deters advised council that they would need to take
action either to approve the zone change or deny it. Council Member Brinker
stated that he did not feel comfortable approving an ordinance that has not
been drafted by the city attorney. Mr. Jed Deters stated he has read through
the proposed ordinance that Charlie Deters presented and the language is
appropriate. Council Member Yeager suggested not voting on either proposed
ordinances. There was a brief discussion regarding the ordinances presented.
Council Member Dupps asked City Attorney, Jed Deters why the proposed ordinance
to approve the zone change has blank spaces. Mr. Jed Deters responded that
there were concerns expressed at the caucus meeting and he thought there was a
possibility that council may want to add additional language so he provided
some blank spaces in case more conditions on the zone change were added.
18.   Mayor Moriconi commented that since there did not seem to be an interest
in reading the proposed ordinance submitted by Mr. Charles Deters to deny the
zone change, that he will proceed with the first reading of the proposed
ordinance to accept the recommendation from the KCPC to approve the zone change
for the Flanagan’s twenty-six acres. Mayor Moriconi read the proposed
ordinance. There was no vote on this first reading. Mayor Moriconi advised the
proposed ordinance would be presented for a second reading at the next meeting.
Proposed Ordinance Approving a Text Amendment to Add “Banks and Other Financial
Institutions” to the list of Conditional Uses within the R-1D Zone – KCPC
Application No. 1702R – 1st Reading
19.   Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to JoAnne Cobble who wished to ask a few
questions on this issue before council.
20.   Mrs. JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, asked Mr. Jed Deters why the
proposed ordinance that he drafted for council’s approval did not include the
entire language recommended by the Planning Commission. She requested that “and
a collector street, and are located within a Community Service Area as defined
in the adopted comprehensive plan” be included in the ordinance text. She
stated that the incomplete language of the proposed ordinance does not meet the
parameters outlined and in effect will not meet Fifth Third Bank’s needs. She
stated that Mr. Deters missed two very important factors of the text amendment.
Council Member Franzen stated adding the language is easily remedied. Council
Member Brinker moved that the ordinance include the additional language as

21.   Regarding the previous issue before council, the rezoning of the Flanagan

for discussion before the second reading.

Update on Post Office cluster mailbox issue in the Clover Ridge/Sycamore Creek
subdivision
30.   Council Member Brinker asked for an update on the Clover Ridge/Sycamore
Creek Subdivisions cluster mailbox issue with the Post Office. Mr. Deters
advised he has received correspondence from the U.S. Post Office’s legal
counsel. Council Member Brinker stated the legal counsel has cited cases. Mr.
Deters advised they have insinuated things they feel support their position,
but he feels they have no legitimate grounds to support their position. He
advised council that he has responded to the correspondence from the Post
Office’s legal counselor, but he has not received a reply yet. Council Member
Brinker asked how the residents were receiving their mail. Mr. Deters assumes
the cluster mailboxes are still being used until the issue is resolved. Council
Member Franzen commented that she was under the impression that the
Independence post office had no preference regarding the type of mail
receptacles used in the city. Chief Butler stated he would check into the mail
delivery receptacles being used in the Clover Ridge/Sycamore Creek subdivision.
Council Member Bushong asked Mr. Deters if the U.S. Post Office had the
authority to trump a city ordinance. Mr. Deters stated that he feels the U.S.
Post Office statement and position on this issue is very broad. Council Member
Brinker stated that he feels since the developer of the subdivision violated
the city ordinance that they are the one that should be held responsible. Chief
Butler suggested they could be cited to court. Council Member Franzen stated
she feels this issue is between the city and the U.S. Post Office. Mr. Deters
advised he would try to get this resolved, but since his reply letter was sent
on November 22, 2004 it is too early to have expected a response from the Post
Office. Mayor Moriconi commented that the important thing is that the residents
continue to receive their mail while the city is awaiting a response from the
Post Office legal counselor.
Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky – Cable Access to the Senior
Center
31.   Council Member Franzen referred to a copy of a letter received from the
Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky regarding running cable lines to
the Senior Center for broadcast purposes. She wondered why this was necessary
since all future meetings would be held and broadcast from the new Municipal
Center Council Chambers. Mayor Moriconi stated that she was correct, that all
future council meetings would be held in the new Council Chambers, but advised
installing cable lines to the Senior Center would provide the opportunity to
broadcast events, such as concerts at the Memorial Park Amphitheater as well as
July 4th Celebration events. Chief Butler also added that it would provide
future options of live coverage of other public meetings held at the Senior
Center.
Discussion Regarding Maintenance of Green Space in Future Developments
32.   Council Member Brinker commented that the maintenance of green space in
new developments should be addressed when a developer is applying for a zone
change. He stated that he would like to see the city look at developers’s track
record with regard to previous developments in the city before granting them a
zone change. He stated that he feels this will help in the prevention of the
maintenance of green space problems in the future. Mr. Deters advised this
should fall under the building permit ordinance wherein a condition could be
imposed that building permits could be denied if there are outstanding zoning
violations in the development. He stated that currently this is not a condition
of building permits. Council Member Yeager suggested that penalties should also
be included if they don’t maintain their green space. Mr. Deters advised he
would work on drafting an amendment to the current building permit ordinance
for council’s consideration.

Report on the proposed Cox Road turn lane at the Intersection of KY 16
35.   Mayor Moriconi reported that he attended a meeting with the State Highway
Department, along with the City Engineer and Zoning Administrator. He stated
they discussed a right and left turn lane, heading east at the intersection of
Cox Road and KY 16. He stated that at first the Highway Department
representatives suggested they would make the road improvements if the city
would assume future maintenance of Cox Road, but he did not feel this was a
feasible option for the city. He said that the Highway Department advised they
would be willing to work with the city on the road improvements and check into
the possibility of obtaining some state funding for the project. He stated it
might be difficult to obtain state dollars since the state officials have yet
to adopt a budget. He stated that large utility poles would need to be
relocated making the project costly. Mayor Moriconi stated that this would be a
separate issue from the turn lane that Mr. Berling has been instructed to build
at the intersection to the Pembroke Subdivision off Cox Road. Council Member
Dupps asked if the state highway representatives supported the city’s assertion
that a turn lane is needed. Mayor Moriconi replied they somewhat agreed, but
was against the installation of a traffic light at that intersection as they do
not feel the current traffic flow warrants one. Council Member Behler commented
that she feels that is part of the problem now with regard to visibility at
that corner. Council Member Franzen stated she has heard concerns from
residents in that area they the state may take part of their property for the
road improvements. Mayor Moriconi advised there was no mention of eminent
domain for this project. He stated he would keep council advised of any
progress on this possible future road project.
Closing Remarks from Outgoing Council Members & Adjournment
36.   Council Member Bushong stated since this was the last live meeting of his
term that he wanted to let everyone know that he appreciated the citizens
support that allowed him to serve on council for the last four years. He
stated, that for the record, he wanted to apologize for allowing candidates for
council in this past general election to use the city council meetings as a
public forum to verbally attack members of the city council. He stated that
even if someone doesn’t respect the person sitting in the council seat, then
they should at least respect the position. In closing, he moved to adjourn the
meeting. Council Member Brinker also thanked council for the opportunity to
fill the unexpired term of Council Member Ellison when he resigned. He stated
that he has tried to respect everyone’s opinion.
37.   Council Member Brinker seconded Council Member Bushong’s motion to
adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting adjourned at 8:07 pm.
