City of Independence, Kentucky
December 20, 2004
Special Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
of the Council on Monday, December 20, 2004 at 7:00 p.m. at the Municipal
Center. Mayor Christian J. Moriconi called the meeting to order with the Pledge
of Allegiance. Roll call was taken and the following Council Members registered
present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Donna Yeager, Carol Franzen
and Eric Dupps. Also present was City Attorney, Mr. Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced that the special meeting of the city council was
called to discuss and possibly take action on the following agenda items:
·   Ordinance No. 2004-0-25 – Second Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2004-0-26 – Second Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2004-0-27 – Second Reading
·   Approving development plan for parcel of the Meadow Glen Subdivision
·   Executive Order No. 2004-EO-07 appointing Kent Kelso to OKI
·   Executive Session (if necessary)
Ordinance No. 2004-O-25 - Approving a Map Amendment from R-1C to R-2(PUD)-2nd
Reading
Mayor Moriconi stated One Eleven Developers, per Jim Bertram, on behalf of
Nancy and Everett Flanagan has made application asking Kenton County Planning
Commission to review a proposed map amendment changing an approximate 26-acre
area located on the east side of Madison Pike between Walnut Hall Drive and
Harris Pike from single-family residential zone to a two and multi-family
residential zone with a planned unit overlay.
Council Member Bushong made a motion, with a second by Council Member Dupps, to
open the meeting for discussion. Council Member Yeager asked Mr. Jim Bertram to
give a summary of the schematic drawing presented to them from the Sanitation
District. Mr. Bertram stated the new development will tie into Hartland
Subdivision and a gravity sewer will run along Fowler Creek that will also
serve Walnut Hall residents. Council Member Yeager asked who would bare the
expense of putting in more sewers. Mr. Bertram stated it would be up to the
Sanitation District. Council Member Franzen asked if the new sewers would also
service some residents on Madison Pike and Peach Drive. Mr. Bertram stated it
would. Council Member Yeager asked if the streets in the new development would
be considered private streets. Mr. Bertram stated the streets would be private
which will be north of the connector street and only the main connector drive
would be maintained by the city.
Mr. Bertram stated he did not want to divulge his source, but has received a
letter of intent for all (102) one-hundred two units. With no more questions,
Mayor Moriconi asked Attorney Jed Deters to read the ordinance.
Mr. Tim Theissen stated when he spoke to Mayor Moriconi; he advised him there
were two conditions that would be added to the ordinance. Mr. Theissen stated
in regards to the traffic study requested by the planning commission, he asked
if the study could be held off until Madison Pike is widened and also would
like to wait on the turn lane until the improvements are completed to the Towne
Center by Mr. Charles Deters or by the State of Kentucky.
Mayor Moriconi stated the wording in the ordinance states, “substantial
completion”. Council Member Brinker asked if a date had been specified in the
ordinance. Council Member Bushong asked who would make the “judgment call” on
the date. Mayor Moriconi stated that would be up to Mr. Charles Deters.
Council Member Brinker asked if Mr. Charles Deters had a certain amount of
years for the completion.
Mayor Moriconi stated if a time limit was not established, the city will have
to wait.
Mr. Theissen then stated they are required to put a buffer between residential
and commercial properties. He stated Mr. Toebben’s property is zoned
residential but if he changes to a commercial development then screening would
not be required between the two properties.
Council Member Behler stated commercial areas never use enough landscaping
which makes the area ugly and asked if they are required to use a buffer, to
contact the Kenton County Extension Center for free help on what to use as a
buffer.
Council Member Bushong stated he would like the developer to consider adding a
ranch type structure on some of the two story condos. He stated there is also a
parking problem in the Beechgrove area and hopes they will consider additional
type parking for guests in this development.
Mr. Bertram stated they will take all considerations to heart. Council Member
Dupps stated from the drawing there is no room for parking on the private
streets. Mr. Bertram stated he would prefer more off street parking rather than
everyone parking on the street which is the purpose of the driveways. He stated
he would like to keep the streets down to (22) twenty-two feet which would
deter on street parking. He stated there will be guest parking around the
clubhouse and will take into consideration adding additional parking among the
buildings to provide additional parking.
Mayor Moriconi stated Mrs. JoAnn Cobble would like to speak. Mrs. Cobble stated
the drawings behind Tab 3 showed no garages nor does the floor plan show any
stairs to the garages.
Council Member Franzen stated those units will be facing the roadway and the
plan was to put the garages in the back so you would not see the garages from
the front. Mr. Bertram stated it is a concept and the garages will be under the
living space with parking in the rear. He stated the final drawing will show
the garages and also steps into the living space.
He stated these drawings are showing the type of architect of the buildings
they want to use more than anything.
Mrs. Cobble stated the units that face the new section of SR 17 also face a
steep embankment and asked if all storm water runoff, erosion and slippage had
been addressed.
Mr. Bertram stated a GEO Technical Engineer will be hired to help with the
design plus there will be two retention ponds.
Mrs. Cobble stated the drawing shows only four parking spaces around the
clubhouse and pool area and felt more parking spaces would be needed. She
stated that the (28) twenty-eight foot connector street is not narrow relative
to other city streets and one citizen had expressed concern regarding waste
pickup on the connector street. She stated it looks as though the drawing is
showing dumpsters for the commercial sites and asked what the plans are for
residential waste pickup.
Mr. Bertram stated they are looking into a community dumpster but may not be
the best solution as residents like to have their trash picked up at the end of
their driveway.
Mrs. Cobble asked that in the future, the print on the drawings be made larger
for easier reading and also asked that they plant Aristocrat pear trees.
Mayor Moriconi stated these are valid points regarding parking spaces mainly
for the police department.
Chief Butler stated that these streets are private and if there is a parking
issue that will have to be handled between the residents because the police
cannot enforce parking issues on private property.
Mayor Moriconi asked City Attorney Deters with the additional proposals to the
map amendment, does that need to be included in the motion to approve.
City Attorney Deters stated if those proposals are added, it is not substantial
enough to do another first reading. He stated the ordinance should be read with
the additional proposals.
Mayor Moriconi asked City Attorney Deters to read Ordinance #2004-0-25 to add a
clarification and a modification of the ordinance.
Council Member Franzen asked how the issue of the buffer between the
residential and commercial areas will be handled.
City Attorney Deters stated that is being done by saying “no screening”.
Council Member Dupps stated they want to say no screening will be required on
roadways internal to the development.
Mr. Bertram stated that is fine. City Attorney Deters again read the ordinance
with the additional proposals.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2004-0-25, with a
second by Council Member Behler. Roll was called was answered with Mr. Bushong
voting no. The motion carried 5-1.

2005 Minutes
January 3, 2005
Opening
1.   The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday,
January 3, 2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with
Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order with the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend John Cheadle, the new pastor of
Independence Christian Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook,
Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
2.   Mayor Moriconi welcomed the four new council members as well as returning
members Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager.
Approval of the Minutes of the December 6, 2004 Regular Council Meeting
3.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the December
6, 2004 regular council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second
from Council Member Yeager. Council Member Yeager stated that during this
meeting she had requested a representative from the Sanitation District attend
a council meeting to explain if the development on the Flanagan property would
be taping into the Fowler Creek sewer lines. Council Member Franzen stated she
thought that request was made at another meeting, but that Council Member
Yeager had requested the developer construct twenty-five percent of the
residential section at this meeting. Council Member Yeager stated she had made
the request again at this meeting. There being no further discussion, roll was
called and answered with three yeas and three abstains by Council Members
Cobble, Cook and Little. City Attorney, Mr. Jed Deters explained that the three
abstentions are counted with the majority votes. Motion carried.
Approval of the Minutes of the December 20, 2004 Special Council Meeting
4.   Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the December
20, 2004 special meeting. Council Member Yeager so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. Council Member Cobble and Council Member Franzen noted
amendments. There being no objections to the amendments, roll was called and
answered with three yeas and three abstains by Council Members Cobble, Cook and
Little. Motion carried.
PRIVILEGES OF THE FLOOR
5.   Ken Lancaster, 733 Cox Road addressed council regarding an on-going zoning
violation behind the Cherokee Shopping Center. He submitted photographs that
showed debris, including construction materials as well as large items that
have been left by the dumpsters by unknowns. Mr. Lancaster advised council that
this constant discarding of large items and recurring debris continues every
week.
6.   Mr. Lancaster stated that he would like the city to have a professional
landscaper look at the area to suggest cleanup options. Mr. Lancaster feels
this would be a permanent clean up of the area and deter passersby from
discarding their unwanted large items.
7.   Council Member Yeager told Mr. Lancaster she was sorry he had to bring
this issue before council again. She stated she feels the Zoning Administration
should be there to do something about this ongoing problem. Council Member
Cobble asked Mayor Moriconi the status of this zoning violation and if the
Zoning Administrator had inspected the area. She stated Mr. Lancaster sent a
very courteous letter to the city asking that this problem be addressed.
8.   Mayor Moriconi advised council that the owner of the property has been
cited. He asked Mr. Deters to comment on available options for this type of
persistent violation. Mr. Deters advised that there is a process the city has
to follow when dealing with these violations. Council Member Cobble suggested
citing the violator to the Code Enforcement Board. Mr. Deters advised it would
have to go through the appeal process first. Council Member Cobble expressed
concern that Mr. Lancaster has not received a progress report from the Zoning
Administrator. Mayor Moriconi directed the City Clerk to obtain an update on
the progress of this violation from the Zoning Administrator. Also, Mayor
Moriconi advised Mr. Lancaster he would receive a call from the Zoning
Administrator this week.
9.   Ike Gabbard was next to address council. Mr. Gabbard declined to provide
his address and cited state statute that supports he is not required to provide
his address.
10.   Mr. Gabbard stated he just wanted to congratulate the voters for electing
this council. He stated he feels they will do great things for the city.
11.   Jeff Hemsath, 728 Stablewatch, Independence, addressed council regarding
the terrible condition of the roads after the recent snowstorm. He stated he
could understand to a point the impact this storm had on the city, but he
stated there was a obvious separation line between the city boundary of Taylor
Mill and Independence.
12.   Chief Butler responded that the city would be meeting with the county
officials this week to discuss better solutions in handling future storms. He
stated that the city heard from may complainants. He advised that the city
contracts with the county to handle seventy percent of the city streets for
snow removal. He also advised that two of the city’s three trucks had
transmissions go out which hampered an effective treatment of the roads. Chief
Butler stated that this storm exposed the weakness that exists in the city’s
Public Works Department due to lack of personnel and equipment. He stated that
the three Public Works employees were working sixteen-hour shifts trying to
keep up with the snow removal. Mayor Moriconi commented that additionally, this
storm occurred during Christmas week. Council Member Franzen commented that she
received calls from residents; some lived on streets that the city personnel
handle and some lived on streets that the county employees handle. She
commented that when she called the city employees to respond to the complaint
that she received good response and that she couldn’t say the same for the
county. Council Member Cobble suggested being watchful of the county to ensure
the city is getting a good value for the $16,000 the city paid. Council Member
Yeager stated that she was housebound for four-five days and as a council
member did not get any favors in having her street cleared of the snow and ice.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2003-O-01 – Setting Time and Place
of the City Council Meetings – 1st Reading
13.   Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed
ordinance that will amend the current Ordinance No. 2003-O-01 that sets the
time and place of the city council meetings. He stated that now that all
meetings will take place in the new Municipal Center Council Chambers it has
caused the amendment of this ordinance as a matter of ‘housekeeping’.

observed” in Sections I and II. There being no objection to this suggestion,
Mr. Deters added the language and gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Mayor Moriconi advised the ordinance would have a second reading at the
February 7, 2005 meeting.

prohibits the installation of cluster mailboxes, and to date, has not received

Mayor’s Report - Christian J. Moriconi
Executive Order No. 2005-EO-01 – Citizens Budget & Economic Development
Committee Appointment
18.   Mayor Moriconi read Executive Order No. 2005-EO-01 appointing Mary Pat
Behler to the Citizens Budget & Economic Development Committee. He stated that
Ms. Behler would be replacing Mike Little. He thanked Mr. Little for serving on
this Committee the past year.
19.   Council Member Cobble read a prepared statement wherein she commented
that while she did not object to the Mayor’s appointment of Ms. Behler to the
Committee, as believed she was a good choice, she reminded Mayor Moriconi that
it has been requested by former council members that he provide a brief bio of
his appointees. She requested that he continue that procedure in the future.
20.   Council Member Cobble went on to make comments regarding the Committee’s
practice of having their meetings in private and stated that she believes the
Committee should adhere to the Open Meetings Act as mandated in KRS Sections
61.800 through 61.850. She stated that the argument used in the past that the
Committee is just an “ad hoc” committee, which has no budgetary or legislative
powers, is irrelevant with regard to the statutory requirements of the open
meetings laws. (For the official record, Council Member Cobble’s full statement
is attached to these minutes). Council Member Cobble requested this subject be
open for discussion and added that she would be in favor of tabling the
appointment to the Committee until the next meeting if the majority of the
council would like more time to research the issue she brings forth.
21.   Council Member Kelso asked if this Committee was acting outside their
scope, by making policy or in violation. Council Member Cobble reiterated the
Committee was in violation of state statutes regulating open meeting laws.
Council Member Kelso asked if the Committee has made budget decisions. Mayor
Moriconi stated the Committee was just a group of volunteers that serves as an
advisory group to the Council. He stated that have no authority and only make
recommendations. Mayor Moriconi suggested he should just dissolve the Committee
if Council had objections to their meetings taking place in non-public
locations. Council Member Franzen stated the committee members usually meet in
one of their homes, in a relaxed atmosphere, but that they present their
recommendations to Council at an open, public meeting. Council Member Kelso
stated he would hate to see the Committee dissolved and stated he would be
concerned if they were making city budget decisions. Council Member Cobble
stated that while the Committee has no power, that is a moot point, and she
agreed with Council Member Kelso that the Committee should not be dissolved, as
she feels they serve a great purpose.
22.   Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters if the Committee is required to keep
minutes of their meetings. Mr. Deters stated they should be keeping some form
of minutes. Mayor Moriconi asked the Committee Chairman, Darrel Herald if he
would like to address Council’s concerns. Mr. Herald stated the Committee would
be presenting an Economic Development report at the January 24, 2005 caucus
meeting. With regard to the open meetings concern, Mr. Herald stated that
nothing they discuss would be considered confidential information, except
budget issues that deal with staffing positions. He stated the Committee only
consists of seven people and that he agreed with Mayor Moriconi that perhaps
the Committee should be dissolved and then residents can present their
individual ideas and comments directly to the Council at the public meetings.
He stated that he feels the Committee would not be productive in an open forum.
23.   Council Member Cobble stated that it is possible that the public would
not even attend the open meetings of the Committee, but that the Committee has
to comply with state statute regarding open meeting laws. Mr. Herald asked why
this concern is just now being brought up. Council Member Cobble stressed the
importance of following the rules. Mayor Moriconi closed the discussion by
advising Council that he would take the issue under consideration. He advised
Council that the Citizens Budget and Economic Development Committee would
present their recommendations at the caucus meeting which will be held on the
fourth Monday of this month – January 24, 2005 – as the third Monday is a
federal holiday (Martin Luther King Day).
24.   Council Member Kelso asked if they had resolved the issue of the
Executive Order. Mr. Deters advised that the Mayor’s Executive Order does not
require Council’s approval. Council Member Cobble suggested deleting the text
in the Executive Order that reads “approved by council”.
Announcement
25.   Mayor Moriconi announced that Chief Butler would leave on Saturday for

Discussion Regarding Adopting Rules of Order for the Council Meetings
26.    Council Member Kelso presented looking at adopting Rules of Order to run
the council meetings. He stated that most councils including federal and state
agencies run their meetings with Robert’s Rules of Order. He suggested that
some of the issues address at this meeting could have been handled under

Discussion Regarding the Flanagan Property Re-zoning at the December 6, 2004
Meeting
29.   Council Member Cobble read a prepared statement expressing concerns she
and others had with regard to Charles Deters presentation to Council and the
legality of the prepared ordinance he submitted opposing the proposed
development of the Flanagan property, which is located directly across from the
Independence Towne Center. In the prepared statement, she also expressed that
she felt this situation created a conflict of interest for Jed Deters, the city
attorney whose is the son of Charles Deters, owner of the Towne Center. She
stated that she feels a person should have recused himself from giving legal
counsel to the city regarding the ordinance presented by his father relating to
the Flanagan property zone change. She stated that in the future, should a
conflict of interest arrive for Mr. Jed Deters, that the Council should request
that he recuse himself (For the official record, Council Member Cobble’s full
statement is attached to these minutes).
30.   Mr. Jed Deters responded to Council Member Cobble’s assertions by stating
that Charles Deters, his father, was looking to find the support of a council
member to sponsor the ordinance he presented, but no council member came
forward to present the ordinance for a first reading. Secondly, he advised
Council Member Cobble that Charles Deters is not his boss as his father is
retired from the law firm. Mr. Deters advised Council Member Cobble there is no
“heir” until there is a death, and just because he is Charlie’s son does not
guarantee him the right to be an heir to his father’s estate.
31.   Council Member Cobble countered that many people recognized there was a
clear conflict for Mr. Deters. Mr. Deters stated that he knows full well when a
conflict exists for him and he does not feel there was a conflict in this
matter. Council Member Franzen stated that since the vote favored One Eleven
that this is a moot point. Council Member Cobble stated if this situation
happens again she will advise council of Mr. Deters conflict of interest. Mr.
Deters stated that it is not council’s decision to determine if a conflict of
interest exists for him; it will be his decision to determine if one exists.
Council Member Yeager stated she supports Jed Deters in this situation as she
feels he did not express his views regarding the proposed development of the
Flanagan property. She stated that Charles Deters was well aware that he needed
to have one of the council members sponsor the ordinance he was trying to
submit. Council Member Cobble stated that no one but a council member could
sponsor proposed legislation; that people cannot draft their own ordinances and
present to the council for adoption. Mayor Moriconi stated that any council
member could motion to have a reading of an ordinance presented to the Council.
Mr. Deters stated that both ordinances for the proposed development of the
Flanagan property were properly introduced before council. Council Member
Franzen reiterated that the issue is a moot point and asked that the discussion
of the issue be put to rest.
Discussion Regarding the Maintenance of the County Roads Within Incorporated
City Limits
32.   Council Member Little advised he has been researching the decision handed
down by the Kentucky Supreme Court affirming that county roads annexed into the
city become the maintenance responsibility of the incorporated city. He stated
he would like to discuss what he has learned about this issue at a future
meeting. He stated that as he sees it, there might be a couple of ways to
benefit the city that would assist with the maintenance of the seventeen miles
of county roads that run through the city. He distributed copies of the Supreme
Court decision to the council members.
33.   Mayor Moriconi advised the city is requesting some clarification from the
county attorney regarding particular streets that divide city and county
boundaries. Mr. Deters advised that the city has not yet received an interlocal
agreement proposal from the Kenton County Fiscal Court. Chief Butler stated the
county has submitted a price list and it is up to the city if we want to
exercise the proposed options. He stated he feels there are some issues worth
challenging, as he does not see how the city is entirely responsible for a road
when only a portion is part of an annexation. Council Member Little feels the
city may have some leverage in a challenge if it can be established that a
particular street is used for a specific county purpose. Council Member Franzen
suggested that the Deputy Judge-Executive, Scott Kimmich be invited to speak to
Council about this at a future meeting. Chief Butler stated that he does not
think Mr. Kimmich will be receptive to addressing Council on this issue as the
county’s position is that the Supreme Court decision is very clear in that the
county legally cannot maintain roads that have been annexed into incorporated
areas. He stated the county has provided the city with a price list for
specific services ranging from road maintenance to vehicle maintenance and it
is up to each city to decide if they want to continue receiving services from
the county or contract elsewhere. Council Member Little commented that he feels
the city can nail it down, but will have to follow-up. Chief Butler advised
that the various cities did not get an opportunity to meet with county
officials until December 11, 2004, when a joint meeting was held. He stated it
was a very long meeting wherein all the county services provided to the cities
was discussed. He stated that all county fees have been raised as well as the
addition of new fees, such as surcharges, etc. Chief Butler reported that he
has begun getting gasoline and fleet maintenance services elsewhere as he feels
it will be more cost effective for the city than the new fee schedule the
county has proposed. He advised that he has been involved in some discussion
with other cities regarding a collaborative bid to contract out the vehicle
maintenance. Mayor Moriconi stated that since all the cities had adopted their
budgets last June, the county might delay implementation of the new service
rates until July 1, 2005 to give the cities an opportunity to work the new fees
into the next budget cycle. Chief Butler commented it is believed that the
county is not concerned if the cities obtain service elsewhere. Council Member
Little commented that this is having a greater impact on ’’’’Independence’’
than on the other cities and he sees the county trying to operate as a private
business instead of the government agency that it is. Council Member Cobble
expressed concern that the county has their maintenance garage located on
’’’’Independence Station Road’’, over which their heavy trucks travel every day
and then expect the city to be entirely responsible for the maintenance of that
road. Council Member Yeager commented the same could be said for Richardson
Road on which the Kenton County Golf Course is located or Mills Road, which is
highly traveled by visitors to the county owned Mills Road Park.
34.   Council Member Little asked that everyone review the copy of the Supreme
Court decision he distributed, and then they can collectively consider possible
options that may be available to the city. Council Member Cobble asked Mr.
Deters to obtain a copy of OAG 68506 (Opinion of the Attorney General). Mr.
Deters advised that the 68 in that particular reference number tells him that
the opinion was rendered in 1968 and since that was thirty-seven years ago the
opinion is probably irrelevant today especially regarding the recent Supreme
Court decision. Council Member Little suggested the city might be able to
impose usage restrictions if we are exclusively providing maintenance of the
street.
Adjournment
35.   There being no additional issues presented for discussion, Mayor Moriconi
entertained a motion to adjourn. Council Member Kelso so moved, with second by
Council Member Cobble. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting adjourned
at 8:02 pm.

City of Independence, Ky
January 24, 2005
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
24, 2005 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent
Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K.
Deters.
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone to the caucus meeting and announced that no
formal action would be taken at this meeting.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi announced that no one signed in to address council.
Presentation by the Citizens Budget & Economic Development Committee
Mayor Moriconi introduced Darrell Herald, Chairman of the Citizens Budget &
Economic Development Committee, who would present the Committee’s Economic
Development Report to Council. (A complete copy of this Report is attached to
the official minutes of this meeting)
Mr. Herald began by saying it was an honor and privilege to serve on this
Committee and thanked the other Committee members for contributing many hours
of research that was necessary to assemble this report.
Mr. Herald stated that he acknowledges that the report is not a comprehensive
report, but rather a practical guide. He stated that one critical element of
their research was that the road system was not well developed. He stated the
committee also was recommending adding a Marketing or Economic Development
Director to the city staff. Mr. Herald stated that with the submission of this
report that the committee has completed their work.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Herald and all the committee members. He stated he
appreciated the time they put in to research the economics of the city. He
stated putting these ideas together would provide the city with a road map with
resolutions. Mayor Moriconi stated two interesting notes in the report was,
when looking at economic development the goal should be to provide community
services to the residents and not try to develop a shopping mecca. The other
was the recommendation to rezone some areas on the west side of town to light
industry and retail.
Council Member Cobble thanked Mr. Herald and the Committee. She asked Mr.
Herald for some specific suggestions to implement their recommendations into
policy. Mr. Herald stated the Committee feels the city should urge state
legislators to make improvements to SR 536 a high priority, as well as the
completion of SR 17. He stated that when the improvements are made the city
leaders should encourage businesses to locate along these thoroughfares. He
stated the city needs to continue to encourage commercial development by
rezoning more commercial areas in the city and consistently support businesses.
Council Member Cobble asked when the committee members spoke with political
leaders if they received any encouragement. Mr. Herald replied yes. He stated
they received positive feedback from Senator Damon Thayer, who is working with
the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet Secretary on some beneficial road
improvements for Independence. Mr. Herald also stated that that had spoken to
State Representative Tom Kerr who also promised to help in any way he could.
Council Member Cobble asked if the Committee had investigated rezoning options
for the Turkeyfoot Road/Richardson Road intersection. Mr. Herald indicated they
had not reviewed that area and were not able to exhaust every opportunity in
the city. He reiterated that the report is not comprehensive, only that they
tried to convey some options that are available. Council Member Cobble thanked
Mr. Herald
Council Member Kelso also thanked the committee. He asked Mr. Herald what he
perceived to be the city’s next logical step upon receipt of this report from
the committee. Mr. Herald commented that he felt the city needs to communicate
to the business community that the city was open for business. Council Member
Kelso commented that this goes along with the vision he has for the city and
that he will address this issue later on in the meeting.
Again, Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Herald and the Committee for all their hard
work.
Proposed Map Amendment Submitted by Fowler-Reese LLC for 88 acres Along the
east side of Fowler Creek Road – KCPC Application No. 1717R
Mayor Moriconi introduced for discussion an application for a map amendment
submitted by Timothy Reese, Fowler-Reese LLC, on behalf of owners Lewis W. and
Barbara A. Moore, Mark E. and La Deana Exeler, Robert E. and Ruth C. Exeler,
Trustees, Martin E. Neltner, Marjorie K. Neltner, Charles Thomas Neltner and
Penelope Jo Neltner. He stated the request is for a zone change from R-1A and
R-1C to R-1D for approximately eighty-eight acres located along the east side
of Fowler Creek Road between Sycamore Creek Drive and Cox Road. Mayor Moriconi
advised that the Kenton County Planning Commission has recommended approval of
the requested zone change and that an ordinance accepting that recommendation
will be presented at the February 7th council meeting for a first reading.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Don Stegman who was representing Fowler
Reese LLC.
Mr. Stegman introduced himself as a civil engineer with Cardinal Engineering.
Mr. Stegman presented a video presentation of the site for which a single-
family development is planned. He advised that the site is surrounded by other
new developments – Sycamore Creek, Claiborne and Lakefield by Drees. He stated
that the R-1D zone they are requesting is consistent with the Comprehensive
Plan. He stated they do not have a Stage I development plan in place yet but
advised the builders would be Keystone Builders, Dixon Builders and Ryland
Homes.
Council Member Cobble asked Mr. Stegman if they would be installing a street
extension stub to access the Carr property for possible future development. Mr.
Stegman confirmed they would be doing so.
Council Member Yeager asked if the sewer lines for this development would be
tapped into the city’s Fowler Creek main. Mr. Stegman stated yes. Council
Member Cobble stated that the she would definitely want that as a condition of
the development. Mayor Moriconi asked how many houses were planned for this
site and what the price range would be. Mr. Stegman advised that the
preliminary plan calls for 206 lots with a starting price of $165,000-$170,000.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the houses would have a first floor brick wrap. Mr. Tim
Reese advised that a house feature, such as brick wrap has not been established
yet. Council Member Cobble asked what percentage of the development would be a
PRDA (Physically Restrictive Development Area). Mr. Stegman advised that 20-25%
would be PRDA and they would follow the Kenton County Subdivision Regulations
regarding theses areas. Council Member Cobble asked why they did not plan to
use zone parameters of the surrounding areas. Mr. Stegman advised that the site
was a physically tougher site to develop. Council Member Cobble asked if they
would be putting in a turn lane on Fowler Creek Road. Mr. Stegman stated they
would install a turn lane on Fowler Creek Road and that there would be an
interior street network as well. Council Member Cobble also asked if the houses
would have a brick wrap. Mr. Reese advised they would address that request with
the builders if the city wants this as a condition of the zone change. Council
Member Cobble commented that she liked the 2.5 dwelling units per net acre much
better than the 2.7 units. Mr. Stegman stated it is a net density, which does
not include the streets. Council Member Cobble asked if the development would
have public/open space or common grounds. He advised that most of the open
space would be the hills and creek area, which would be platted on individual
lots or maintained by a homeowners association, which has yet to be determined.
He commented that an adjoining property owner has requested they not establish
a homeowners association. Council Member Cobble stated that she would like a
time frame to be established for the construction of the turn lane on Fowler
Creek Road.
Council Member Little asked if some lots would be more than 2.7 in density. Mr.
Stegman advised that 2.7 is the maximum net density. Mr. Reese advised most
will be 2.1 – 2.4 as they are attempting to stay below the 2.7 net density. Mr.
Stegman stated that the R-1D permits the lots to be reduced in size to enable
the preservation of tree areas. Mr. Reese commented that he was involved in the
development of the Meadow Glen subdivision and is aware that the city opposes
fifty-foot lots.
Council Member Franzen asked if all the lots would be seventy foot wide. Mr.
Stegman stated that the minimum lot size would be seventy foot with some lots
larger. Council Member Franzen commented that she also would like to see brick
wrap on the houses in this development.
Mayor Moriconi asked if this development would tie into the Shadybrook
Subdivision. Mr. Reese stated that eventually it would. Mayor Moriconi
commented that the Shadybrook Subdivision would have a large park that will
include athletic fields, a restroom facility and parking. Council Member Little
asked if there would be green space they would want the city to take over. Mr.
Stegman stated they will either develop shorter lots for a homeowners
association to maintain or they will develop larger lots for the individual
property owners to maintain; they would not be asking the city to take over
common green space areas. Mr. Reese stated they would probably plan for larger
lots for the individual property owners.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Stegman and Mr. Reese for a very thorough
presentation. He stated that an ordinance would be prepared and presented for a
first reading at the February 7, 2005 council meeting. Council Member Franzen
requested that a first floor brick wrap be a condition of the zone change. Mr.
Jerry Dusing, legal counsel for Fowler-Reese, LLC commented that he would
discuss the issue with the city attorney. Council Member Yeager requested that
tapping into the city’s Fowler Creek sewer line also be a condition of the zone
change. Mr. Dusing commented they would take these conditions under
consideration.
Request for City to Sponsor a Text Amendment -– Regarding Indoor ––––Shooting–
––Range––
Mayor Moriconi stated that the city is being asked to sponsor a zoning text
amendment that would add an indoor shooting range as a permitted use in the RC-
2 zone, which the current text does not address. He stated that the property in
question is located at 3456 Richardson Road and is owned by Bill Dehlinger.
Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld stated that the future tenant would be a
gun store with the shooting range in the lower level of the building. She
advised that new legislation mandates if a gun shop holds a federal license
then they are exempt from zoning laws. She said the prospective tenant holds a
federal license and would operate a gun shop, but would like to also operate an
indoor shooting range in the lower level of the building.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that a text amendment application has to be
sponsored by the city. Council Member Little asked if this property is located
at the end of Crowe Road. Mr. Dehlinger stated the property is at the
intersection of Richardson Road and Old Richardson Road near Banklick Creek.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the building had a full basement. Mr. Dehlinger said
yes and that they would control access to the lower level shooting range from
the top floor. Council Member Cobble asked if they would install acoustics. Mr.
Dehlinger stated they have not discussed that yet. Mr. Alex Logsden, the
prospective tenant stated that since the shooting range would be sub-level that
acoustics would probably not be necessary. He advised council that all the
range equipment would meet noise regulations relating to shooting range codes,
as well as bullet entrapment. Mr. Logsden commented that presently there is no
other shooting range in this area of Kenton County. He said their business
would encourage shooting as a sport and promote gun safety. He stated the
shooting range would safely accommodate five or six people.
Council Member Cobble expressed concern that this property is located in a
flood plain. Mr. Dehlinger stated a flood plain exists along the banks of
Banklick Creek. Mayor Moriconi asked if other council members had any comments.
Council Member Little commented that he thinks an all-in-one facility of this
type is a good concept. He stated that this might be a facility the city’s
police department could utilize. He stated he liked the idea of the range being
located in the basement area of the building, so that any shooting noise should
be minimal. He stated in keeping with the current vision for the city to
encourage more retail areas in the city, he would approve of sponsoring this
text amendment application.
Council Member Yeager stated she would also support this application. Council
Member Franzen stated she had no problem with approving this request and liked
that fact that the location was not a highly populated residential area.
Council Member Kelso asked if the business would be providing gun license
certification programs. Mr. Logsden replied yes; they will have a classroom and
will provide this program. He also stated they plan to target women and the
younger people to introduce them to gun safety and shooting as a sport. Council
Member Kelso stated he was in agreement to sponsor this amendment. Council
Member Cobble stated she had no objection to supporting this text amendment
application but was concerned about the flood plain and wondered if they would
be able to obtain insurance. Mayor Moriconi stated the lender may also have
some concern about the flood plain. Council Member Franzen commented they would
probably be required to purchase flood insurance. Council Member Cook stated
she was also in favor of supporting this text amendment application. Mr. Deters
advised he would prepare a resolution supporting this and submit it to council
for approval at the February 7, 2005 council meeting.

Discussion Regarding the Adoption of Rules of Order for the Council Meetings
Mayor Moriconi presented a draft Executive Order that would establish rules of
order for conducting city council meetings as suggested by Council Member Kelso
at the last meeting. Mr. Deters advised the language of the Executive Order
being presented are rules the Mayor considers beneficial.
Council Member Kelso had requested the Rules of Order be adopted by Municipal
Order and questioned the binding effect of an executive order on the Council.
Mr. Deters advised that it depends on the subject it addresses. He advised that
KRS says that the mayor runs the meetings. Council member Kelso countered that
KRS says that the mayor is the presiding officer, but it is the legislative
body that enacts the laws of the city. He stated that just as ordinances are
binding on the citizens, a Municipal Order would be binding on the Council.
Council Member Kelso stated he was not confident that an Executive Order was
the proper way to adopt the Rules of Order. Mr. Deters advised that he feels it
should be an Executive Order as it will be up to the mayor to enforce the
rules. Mr. Deters also expressed concern that this council should not bind
future mayors, as the next sitting mayor may not want to enforce such rules for
conducting the meetings. Council Member Kelso stated that he disagreed with Mr.
Deters and feels the KRS is very specific. He suggested getting together to
review the draft copies and determine an outline to submit to council at a
future meeting. Mr. Deters commented that when the legislative body dictates to
the executive authority then they are doing his job. Council Member Kelso
asserted that the draft Rules of Order that he submitted does not exceed or
conflict with KRS. Mr. Deters stated that the original draft that he reviewed
had KRS conflicts. He stated he would be willing to sit down and review the
content of the document in more detail. Council Member Franzen asked why Mr.
Deters felt the Rules of Order should be adopted by Executive Order. Mr. Deters
advised that it should be an Executive Order as it is the function of the mayor
to run the city and the city meetings. He stated it is inherently wrong for the
council members to tell the mayor how to run the city. Council Member Franzen
commented that she thought the Rules would be a tool for the mayor in running
the meetings and actually give him more authority. Mr. Deters stated it would
not give him more authority; it would only spell out the rules. Council Member
Kelso commented that an Executive Order does not give flexibility to the
Council to enforce. Mayor Moriconi commented that he is not convinced that the
Rules of Order is needed to conduct the meetings. He stated he would like to
review a final draft. Council Member Kelso commented that he feels the Rules
are necessary as he is not happy with the decorum exhibited at some meetings in
the past and feels it is time to control the meetings to achieve a more
professional code of conduct from everyone in attendance. Council Member Little
stated he agreed with Council Member Kelso and suggested reviewing all three
drafts that have been presented. Mayor Moriconi suggested Council Member Kelso
schedule a meeting with Mr. Deters to review the drafts. Council Member Cobble
commented that she partially agrees with Mr. Deters and does not want to
relinquish the Mayor’s executive powers. She also expressed reservations on
imposing criminal penalties for those who do not comply with the Rules. Council
Member Kelso stated that KRS imposes criminal fines. Mayor Moriconi advised
that a revised draft would be submitted at a future meeting.
Discussion Regarding a Vision Statement for the City
Council Member Kelso distributed “A Vision of Independence” statement to all in
attendance and presented this to Council for their consideration. He presented
this as a formal request to adopt a resolution that would approve the
establishment of a citywide initiative to develop a strategic vision for the
city. He proposed that a citizens committee be established to lead the process.
He stated that he has begun to collect a lot of information from the residents
and business owners and has come to the conclusion that a strategic vision
would guide the city leaders in making important decisions. He stated that the
committee could help the city set plans and goals relating to recreation,
transportation, safety and security that could be accomplished over the next
10-20 years. He stated that organizations that have a vision and specific goals
tend to be successful. He stated both the elected officials as well as the
citizens should share the goals.
Council Member Yeager suggested the city have a meeting with the public to
garner interested individuals, before making hand-selected appointments to this
committee
Council Member Little suggested inserting a citizen survey in the city
newsletter.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that a few years ago a strategic committee
called “Independence Tomorrow” was established. He stated they met for a year
and compiled a report, which was presented to the city council, which the
council would not adopt. He stated that strategic plan is basically collecting
dust. Mayor Moriconi expressed some doubt about appointing another committee to
accomplish the same goal unless some concrete results could be achieved and the
council would act on the results of the strategic plan produced by the
committee. Council Member Kelso stated the success of the process would depend
on the city leaders. He stated it was too bad that the former strategic plan
was not adopted.
Council Member Yeager stated she feels that every individual that asks to serve
on the committee should be welcomed. Mayor Moriconi advised council that he
would take the request under consideration.

that this new Council Chambers has the ability to televise the meetings live to

Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi advised that the next recognized business of the month would be
at the February 7th meeting. He asked Council Member Cobble to let the City
Clerk know of her selection as soon as possible so that a plaque could be
ordered. Council Member Cobble stated she would like to select Carol’s
Hairstyling as the recipient of the Business of the Month for February.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that the snowstorm the week of Christmas
practically wiped out the snow removal budget. Council Member Cobble asked if
that included the $17,000 that was allotted for payment to the county for the
county roads that run throughout the city. Mayor Moriconi stated the $17,000
was over and above the snow removal budget amount.
Mayor Moriconi reported that he attended a recent Mayor’s Group meeting wherein
it was discussed that the Kenton County Fiscal Court is considering the
adoption of an ordinance that will establish an 8% insurance premium tax on
auto and property insurance policies. He stated the tax would not apply to
health and life policies. He stated the cities in the county that already
collect the insurance premium tax will continue to receive that revenue. If a
city has not enacted the tax then the county will collect the revenue that
would otherwise go to the city. Mayor Moriconi advised that the ordinance will
need to be enacted by the county no later than March 23rd and they are
considering a first reading of the proposed ordinance at tomorrow’s meeting.
Council Member Kelso stated that he is very concerned about this and that we
need to let the citizens know we are not in favor of this. He stated the city
would need to educate the citizens about what is happening with this tax. He
expressed concern that the county would turn over the maintenance of their
roads that run through incorporated areas and now propose to increase their
revenue base as well as increasing the cost of the services they provide the
cities. He stated he feels the county is generating revenue on the backs of the
cities and that the city needs to take firm stance. He stated if the county
enacts this ordinance he would submit the same for the city so that the revenue
generated from the city residents would stay in the city and not spent
elsewhere in the county by the Fiscal Court. Mayor Moriconi reported that
originally the county wanted to impose the tax on just the unincorporated areas
of the county by they learned they had to impose the tax countywide. Mayor
Moriconi advised county the city may have to have a first reading of a proposed
insurance premium tax ordinance soon as we would be held to the same time
deadline as the county, which is March 23rd. Council Member Cobble stated that
Kenton County cities that already have an insurance premium tax, but at a lower
rate than 8%, would find it necessary to increase their rate to that equal of
the county, or the county would get the difference.
Council Member Kelso stated the citizens should be encouraged to get involved
and let the county know they do not support this tax increase. Council Member
Franzen stated she would urge everyone to attend the Fiscal Court meeting
tomorrow night.
Marcus Cook, 96 Carrie Way, addressed council to say he thinks they need to
look at what they are suggesting, as they campaigned door-to-door and learned
from the residents, that eight out of ten don’t want to pay this insurance
premium tax. Council Member Little commented that several council members here
opposed the insurance premium tax when the city proposed enacting it back in
2003. He stated he hopes the county does not impose this tax, but it sounds
like they will. He stated this needs to be explained to the citizens. He stated
that if the city does enact this tax, it would be done because the city had no
other choice. Council Member Cook commented that she campaigned against this
tax and wants the opportunity to explain in detail why the city would now be
compelled to enact it.
Mayor Moriconi suggested the city have a first reading of an ordinance to
establish this tax at one of the future meetings, then before having a second
reading and enactment, we could wait to see if the county adopts it. He stated
if the county does not adopt the ordinance then the city would not have a
second reading.
On another subject, Mayor Moriconi gave the city council an update regarding
the outstanding zoning violation behind the Cherokee Shopping Center, which was
discussed at the January 3rd council meeting. He stated at the January 3rd
meeting that one might have thought no action has been taken in correcting the
problem, but it would have been a wrong impression. He stated that a timeline
relating to communication and action relating to the violation has been
provided in their packets. Mayor Moriconi stated that he did not have that
information with him at the last meeting to support the Zoning Administrator’s
efforts to correct this problem. He said there was some miscommunication
regarding the extent of what Mr. Lancaster expected the city to accomplish.
Mr. Lancaster asked Mayor Moriconi if the owner of Cherokee Shopping Center
(Mr. Meyers) has let the city know what he is willing to do regarding a long-
term solution to cleaning up the area. Mayor Moriconi stated he has not heard
back from Mr. Meyers, nor has the Zoning Administrator. Mr. Lancaster asked if
the city would follow up with Mr. Meyers in a couple of months. Mayor Moriconi
advised the city would follow up in the next thirty days.
Adjournment
There being no further business, motion was made by Council Member Kelso and
seconded by Council Member Little to adjourn. Motion was carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 9:05 pm.

January 24, 2005
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, January 24 2005 at 6:45 pm in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook,
Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the city council was called to
discuss one agenda item which was a grant application to the Land & Water
Conservation Fund Program to assist the funding of the construction of
basketball courts in Memorial Park and the adoption of a Resolution supporting
the application.
Resolution No. 2005-R-01 – Approving the Grant Application to the Land & Water
Conservation Fund for the Construction of Basketball Courts in Memorial Park
Mayor Moriconi stated the application is for a 50/50 grant which means the city
would have to fund 50% of the project cost if awarded the grant. He stated the
estimated project cost is $87,330.00. He presented Resolution No. 2005-R-01 and
directed City Attorney, Jed Deters to read the Resolution.
Council Member Cobble moved to approve Resolution No. 2005-R-01, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.

Member Franzen so moved, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with

Mayor Moriconi stated it was brought to his attention a few months ago by Nita
Brake that she has been recommending some changes on some of the rental
agreement issues. Mayor Moriconi asked Mrs. Brake to present her
recommendations to council. Mrs. Brake stated she would like to amend the
rental agreement.
Council Member Yeager stated before Mrs. Brake speaks she would like to point
out that the addendum states under paragraph #3 it states it “is seeking
approval from the City and the Senior Center Board of Directors.” She stated
the Senior Center Board of Directors does not have anything to do with renting

Council Member Franzen asked Mrs. Brake if she was looking to council to

Council Member Kelso stated that our citizens are already paying taxes that

Council Member Kelso stated he feels the fees should be low to encourage people
