February 28, 2005
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
28, 2005 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent
Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K.
Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi advised that those who signed in for privileges of the floor
will reserve comment until the agenda item is presented for discussion.
Discussion Regarding the 1998 Interlocal Agreement with the Sanitation District
No. 1
Mayor Moriconi introduced and welcomed Mr. Jeff Eger, General Manager of
Sanitation District No. 1. He stated that he invited Mr. Eger to this meeting
to provide this Council with some history regarding the 1998 Interlocal
Agreement between the City and District that effectively turned over the
maintenance of the city sanitation lines to the District. Mayor Moriconi stated
that he appreciated Mr. Eger coming to the meeting and being so accessible to
the city.
Mayor Moriconi stated he would begin the questioning with Council Member Kelso.
Council Member Kelso stated he did not have any questions at this time.
Council Member Cobble stated she would suggest that Mr. Eger first provide
Council with some history of the Agreement and then she would like to ask a few
questions.
Mr. Eger stated the part of the 1998 merger Agreement included the directing of
the city to pay their portion of the GRW study, which was $203,220 over a ten-
year period. He stated that GRW is an engineering firm that Sanitation District
No. 1 (SD1) has used on many projects. He stated that prior to legislation that
was adopted in 1994 many cities owned and operated their own sanitation lines.
He stated the 1994 legislation allowed the cities to get out of the sewer
business and turn over their lines to SD1. He stated the KRS 220.135(a)
mandates that the cities shall pay 50% of the cost of repairs and the GRW study
revealed that the estimated cost of the repairs of Independence lines would be
$203,220. He stated this was based on the findings of the televising of 10% of
Independence’s system. Mr. Eger advised that SD1 agreed to honor that number
for each city, even though the repairs exceeded GRW’s study findings in many
cases. He stated that SD1 allowed the city to pay this amount to them over a
ten-year period interest free. He stated the current balance is $81,288. He
stated that to date, SD1 has spent $3,560,887 in repairs and upgrades to the
Independence sanitation system, as well as negotiated storm water management.
Mr. Eger stated that initially in 1994 when the cities were first able to merge
their sanitation systems with SD1, only three cities opted out of the merger
agreement. He stated those cities were Alexandria, Florence and Independence.
He advised that five years later when Independence city leaders approached SD1
requesting to opt in to the merger agreement, the conditions of that agreement
were different from what had been established in 1994. He advised that had
Independence opted in to the merger agreement in 1994 SD1 would have assumed
all the city’s capital debt, including the Fowler Creek sewer debt. He stated
that condition was not available to Independence in 1998; but that it was
negotiated that SD1 would give Independence a $300 credit for each tap in fee
collected by SD1 for properties within the city limits. He stated that other
cities did not get this tap in fee credit.
Mr. Eger stated that he feels the city has a legal question that may have
surfaced regarding the maintenance fee currently charged to all Independence
system users. He cited KRS 220.135(b) wherein it states the fee may continue
until such time the debt is paid off. He stated that it needs to be determined
if that statutes applies in this situation. He stated that SD1 is essentially
‘leasing’ the lines until the city pays this debt in full. He stated that if
the city currently has adequate funds to pay off the GRW study, then
technically the debt has been satisfied.
Mayor Moriconi asked, for clarification purposes, if the $6,000,000 Fowler
Creek sewer debt the city currently owes would have been assumed by SD1 in
1994, but not five years later when the city leaders finally opted for the
merger agreement. At that time, in 1998, when SD1 took over, they only took
over the maintenance of the city lines and the city retained the obligation of
paying off the debt. Mr. Eger confirmed that Mayor Moriconi’s statement is
correct.
Council Member Cobble asked when the new Fowler Creek gravity line was
installed. Mr. Eger stated that the gravity line was connected this past year.
Council Member Cobble asked if SD1 notified the city. Mr. Eger stated that SD1
is not required to notify the city as they have all rights of ownership.
Mr. Eger presented a map to illustrate to the council members the location of
the new gravity line and treatment plant on the east side of the city in the
vicinity of the Shadybrook and Clover Ridge subdivisions. He advised that the
Fowler Creek Road and McMillan Drive pump stations were removed and replaced
with the gravity lines. He stated that SD1 negotiated with the developers of
those subdivisions to run the gravity lines to allow for expansion in the area.
He stated that pump stations are inferior and costly to operate, so it was in
the best interest of the community to replace the pump stations. He stated the
Fowler Creek system runs by gravity. Mr. Eger went on to say that the Lakeview
pump station has problems during wet weather and with future growth projected
for the area, their long-range plans call for half of that to be diverted. He
stated that if the Independence system had remained a separate system new flow
could not have been taken.
Council Member Cobble expressed concern that with the pump stations being
removed new development is not able to tap into the Fowler Creek system and
those three new subdivisions are not paying the debt reduction assessment. Mr.
Eger stated the city is being compensated $300 for all new homes tapped into
the system, irregardless of whether it is into the Fowler Creek system or not.
Council Member Yeager expressed concern that there was no longer a Fowler Creek
system in that area. Mr. Eger explained that anything south of that pump
station goes into the SD1 system. Council Member Franzen commented that if SD1
installed their own system then those affected users should not be charge the
city fee. Council Member Cobble stated the users should pay if they are tapped
into the old Fowler Creek line. Mr. Eger stated that the Agreement directs SD1
to charge the properties as advised by the city.
Council Member Cobble referred to Section 3 of the Agreement regarding the $300
tap in credits that SD1 would remit to the city. She commented that since this
was mandated by statute that should not be considered a negotiable part of the
agreement as state statute is not negotiable. Council Member Franzen commented
the statute applied to counties and only by the good graces of the SD1 it was
granted to Independence. Council member Cobble suggested the $300 per house tap
in fee should continue for the life span of the Fowler Creek sewer debt. Mr.
Eger stated he did not believe it would be permitted for more than ten years.
Council Member Yeager stated SD1 raised the tap in fee shortly after the
Agreement was made with the city. Council Member Cobble concurred saying it was
six months later. She went on to say that of the $3,000,000 that Mr. Eger
asserts SD1 has expended on repairs over the last several years that it should
be noted that amount was offset by approximately $2,500,000 in revenue
generated by the tap in fees they collected.
Council Member Cobble referred to page one of the Agreement and asked who the
American Skandia Life Assurance Company was. Mr. Eger stated he was not sure,
but that it may have been the underwriting bond company.
Council Member Cobble referred to “repairs that remain for completion” – stated
very specific – thought the city was paying for repairs that…Mr. Eger asked if
there were areas in the city that were in need of repairs and if complaints
have been received from the residents, as he was not aware of any outstanding
repairs. Council Member Cobble the GRW study was conducted to identify the
necessary repairs that needed to be made to get the sewer system up to SD1
standards. She stated that if KRS 220.135(a) mandated that the city should pay
50% of the necessary repairs, why the city was required to pay the full
$203,220 in the GRW report.
Mr. Eger replied that since the city of Independence did not opt in at the
inception of the merger, it was one of the negotiations made in 1998 that
became part of the Agreement. In addition, SD1 has remitted the $300 tap in
fees, which was also part of that Agreement. He stated he is not aware of any
resident complaints regarding needed repairs to the system. Mr. Eger stated it
was a give and take agreement and reiterated that SD1 has increased the
capacity for future growth in Independence with the investment of $3,000,000 in
improvements including a new treatment plant.
Council Member Franzen recapped that if the city leaders in 1994 had opted into
the merger agreement with SD1 at the inception, then the city, and the
residents would not be burdened today with the Fowler Creek sewer debt. Mr.
Eger stated that was correct. Council Member Yeager commented that the
residents were told they would only have to pay the debt reduction for ten
years or so and now hears it is scheduled to be paid off in the year 2023.
Council Member Franzen stated she pays this assessment and that she was advised
it would be a twenty-year assessment and that she could pay it up front if she
wanted to.
Council Member Franzen asked it the city is responsible for any sanitary sewers
now. Mr. Eger stated no. She asked what the city could do with the remaining
funds once the GRW study obligation is paid. Mayor Moriconi wondered if the
funds could be used to pay toward the Fowler Creek debt. Mr. Eger suggested Mr.
Deters review the statutes to answer that question. He also stated there may be
some legal questions regarding the continuation of charging the maintenance
fee.
Mayor Moriconi stated that everyone pays the maintenance fee including Fowler
Creek system users, which are primarily east of Madison Pike. Council Member
Cobble stated that in her opinion the maintenance fee should have been
discontinued when the city entered into the merger Agreement with SD1. Council
Member Franzen suggested that since everyone is paying the maintenance fee that
the excess funds, over and above what is owned toward the GRW study, should be
used to pay down the Fowler Creek sewer bond debt.
Council Member Cobble suggested the city needed to come to a conclusion on this
issue as she feels that two years into that Agreement the maintenance fee
surcharge should have been taken off, because at that time there should have
been adequate funds to pay off the GRW study. Council Member Little asked when
the maintenance fee was established. Council Member Yeager stated it was
established by ordinance in 1978. Mr. Eger stated that many cities had
maintenance fees and that state statute permitted the cities to maintain that
fee. Council Member Cobble asked what percent of the maintenance fee was usage.
Mr. Eger advised that a maintenance fee or surcharge is generally a set amount
and whatever the city directed SD1 to charge is the amount that would be on the
user’s bill. Council Member Cobble asserted that in 1998 someone had to submit
a written directive regarding the amount of the surcharge. Mr. Eger suggested
that the fee schedule that was already in place at the time of the merger
Agreement in 1998 was automatically continued. He stated since it was
established in 1978 no change was made to it in 1998 and it was continued to be
charged to pay off the GRW study.
Council Member Franzen commented that she feels the maintenance fee should be
discontinued if there is enough to pay off the GRW study. But she stated she
agrees that those not tied into the Fowler Creek system should not have to help
pay down the debt. She suggested the Council has the authority to stop charging
the fee now. Mayor Moriconi agreed that it appears the city needs to rescind
the ordinance that established the maintenance fees as the city can effectively
fund the pay off of the GRW study. He stated this needs to be resolved and
directed Mr. Deters to review that possibility.
Council Member Yeager commented that she feels it is wrong that the users of
the Fowler Creek system have to continue paying the debt assessment until the
year 2023. Mr. Eger commented that the city is faced with two issues; whether
or not to continue the maintenance fee charged to all users of the sanitation
system and the other issue is the Fowler Creek. He suggested the city attorney
review the statutes. Mr. Eger also advised council that it is not uncommon to
levy an entire customer base to make improvements that benefit the entire
community.
Council Member Cobble thanked Mr. Eger from attending the meeting and providing
an account of the 1998 merger Agreement. In closing she referred to Section 7
of the Agreement wherein it states “the city shall send a written report to the
District after July 31 and before December 31 of each calendar year which will
identify” all debts as outlined in paragraphs A, B, C & D, and relating to the
operational sanitary sewer system of the city. She asked if SD1 would want the
city to provide that. Mr. Eger stated that it is in the city’s best interest to
resolve and eliminate any outstanding debt, and that he doesn’t feel it
necessary to know the city’s outstanding debt.
Council Member Cobble stated that she feels the lease merger was signed in good
faith and she would like to think SD1 would not intentionally undermine the
city if they can help it, but she feels there has been a negative impact of the
retirement of the Fowler Creek debt. Mr. Eger asserted that he feels the
installation of the treatment plants and gravity lines enhanced the city and
permitted future growth of an overloaded system. He stated he apologized for
not providing better communication to the city. Council Member Franzen
commented that the improvements made by SD1 did not undermine the city. She
stated SD1 had no choice as the Fowler Creek pump stations were at capacity.
Council Member Cobble stated she still feels the city should have been notified
that the pump stations were being removed. Mr. Eger stated the residents
benefited from the improvements and more can pay into the debt reduction
assessment. Council Member Yeager commented that she thought he said the city
could not feed into the old system. Mr. Eger stated that anything south of the
area could be charged the assessment.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Eger for his
time.
Request for City to Sponsor a Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Automobile
Laundries
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that a request is being made for the city to
sponsor a zoning text amendment that would add automobile laundries as either a
permitted use or conditional use within the NSC zone. He introduced Mr. David
Stanfield, with Radius Construction Company who was present to make this
request. Mayor Moriconi advised council that it would be necessary to adopt a
Resolution authorizing the application of this text amendment. Mr. Stanfield
stated that he was making this request on behalf of Martin Neltner who would
like to construct a car wash facility on the front section of the property he
owns at 6463 Taylor Mill Road in the Cherokee Shopping Center. He stated the
area is currently serving as a parking lot for Mr. Neltner’s employees of his
billing service company. He directed council to the preliminary drawing of the
plans for the property that was inserted in their council packets. He stated
that vacant lot behind the building would be made into a parking lot for the
employees.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the car wash would be automatic or self-spray. Mr.
Stanfield replied that their preliminary plans would be to install one
automatic (tractor pulled) and two or three self serve units.
Council Member Cobble commented that this same request was introduced about
four months ago. Mayor Moriconi confirmed that an application had been made
last fall, but that on one attended the council meeting to elaborate on that
request. He stated that the Council had the impression that the request was
being made so that the car wash could be constructed in the vicinity of Cox
Road and Jimae. Council Member Cobble commented that there needs to be a
consensus of Council if this text amendment is desired, and she feels there
needs to be parameters set for this type of structure. She expressed concern
that the requester may present preliminary plans that Council would be in favor
of, only later to learn that the final plans changed drastically. Mr. Stanfield
stated that if they are able to get an approved text amendment, then they would
submit a site plan to the city.
Mayor Moriconi asked Council if there was a consensus to move forward with the
text amendment application. Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Stanfield that approval
by Council to sponsor the text amendment application does not mean they will be
in favor of the recommendation by the Planning Commission.
Council Member Cobble commented she did not feel the city should sponsor the
text amendment application if a majority would not favor adopting it if the
Planning Commission’s recommendation is for approval. Council Member Franzen
stated that while she likes knowing who is behind the application request, she
is less than thrilled with the proposed location for this car wash facility.
Don Barnett, 788 Jimae, stated that he feels Mr. Neltner has a nice building
and there is adequate parking in front which is also used by customers of the
other businesses in the shopping center. He expressed discontent with the poor
condition of the adjacent building that houses Robinson’s Meats and feels, that
in general, blight is settling into the east side of the city. Mayor Moriconi
advised Mr. Barnett that Mr. Neltner does not own the building that houses
Robinsons’ Meats.
Council Member Yeager stated that she has received phone calls regarding Mr.
Neltner’s plans for a car wash in that area and all the callers she spoke with
oppose the idea. She stated she feels it is a bad location.
Mr. Stanfield commented that Mr. Neltner’s employees own most of the cars in
the front parking area. Mayor Moriconi asked how many parking spaces are
planned for the rear parking lot. Mr. Stanfield stated there would be between
100-120 parking spaces. Council Member Yeager wondered how close the parking
lot would be to the adjoining properties. Mr. Stanfield advised the parking lot
would utilize the greater part of the lot. Mayor Moriconi asked if the cars
would be parked there mainly between 9:00 am and 5:00 pm. Mr. Stanfield replied
yes. He commented that Mr. Neltner is trying to improve the aesthetic of the
shopping center and if he could purchase the other building that houses
Robinson’s Meats, he would. Council Member Franzen stated that Mr. Neltner has
done a wonderful job with his building, but she doesn’t like the idea of a car
wash in the front lot. Council Member Yeager stated she also couldn’t vision a
car wash in that area.
Council Member Little asked the distance between the front of Mr. Neltner’s
building and the proposed location of the car wash. Mr. Stanfield stated they
only have conceptual plans at this time.
Council Member Cobble expressed concerns that an empty parking lot at night
would attract loiters after regular business hours. Mr. Stanfield advised they
would provide adequate lightning that would be shielded so that it would not
reflect on the surrounding residential properties.
Mr. Ken Lancaster, 733 Cox Road, commented that Mr. Neltner has done a
wonderful with the improvements he has made to the shopping center, but a car
wash in front of the other buildings would make mess of the whole area. He
stated that people go to a neighborhood shopping center to shop not wash their
car. He stated he strongly recommends that Council not approve this request, as
it is not the right location for this type of structure.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the rear parking lot could be gated to deter nighttime
loiters. Mr. Stanfield replied yes and advised that a parking lot would
actually clean up the area.
Council Member Cobble asked if they were prepared to address storm water
drainage issues. Mr. Stanfield stated they would look at all the issues during
the design of the parking lot. She stated she feels the lot should be 150 feet
from the residential property.
Mr. Deters stated he would prepare a resolution that would approve the
sponsorship of this text amendment application for presentation at the next
meeting. He asked if anyone had suggestions for conditions that they would like
to have imposed to send them to him and he would include these in the
resolution. Mayor Moriconi advised the proposed resolution would be presented
at the next business meeting, which is scheduled for next Monday, March 7, 2005
at 7:00 pm.
Proposed Map Amendment – for 5298 & 5302 Madison Pike from NC and R-1C to NC
KCPC Application No. 1722R
Mayor Moriconi advised representatives from One Eleven Engineering & Surveying
were present to submit their development plan for two parcels located at 5298
and 5302 Madison Pike. He stated that One Eleven has applied for a map
amendment requesting the current zones of NC and R-1C be changed to NC which
has received a recommendation for approval from the Kenton County Planning
Commission (KCPC). Mayor Moriconi advised if Council decides to accept that
recommendation from the KCPC, there would be a first reading of the ordinance
at the March 7th meeting with a second reading and enactment at the April 4th
meeting. He stated Mr. Jim Bertram and Mr. Darren Eyre would answer any
questions Council had regarding this zone change and development plan.
Council Members Yeager and Cobble asked if there will be two or three houses on
the site. Mr. Bertram replied there are two parcels that currently have three
houses, which will be razed to ready the property for two new structures. Mr.
Bertram distributed copies of the site plan to the Council. Mr. Bertram advised
the property addresses are 5298, 5302 and 5302 Madison. He stated that the 5298
Madison parcel was approved with a driveway that will serve both planned
structures, which will reduce space by providing joint parking and access
points for both buildings. He stated that the 5302-5304 parcels will be
constructed right away, but that the current house on 5298 Madison will be
rented until development plans can be finalized. Mr. Bertram advised council
that he would not be constructing this development so he was unsure of the
building design, but that he thought it would be colonial style or similar to
the design of the new buildings and would be in keeping with the current theme
he has begun in this section of the downtown area. He stated he would keep some
green space and that the signage and lighting will be similar. He stated the
concept plan distributed for the 5302-04 lot will provide office spaces on the
first floor. Mr. Bertram stated that KCPC only imposed one condition on the
zone change, which was to amend the Stage I development plan to meet the
minimum requirements of the city’s zoning ordinance.
Council Member Cobble asked if the city should consider holding a public
hearing as part of the due process. Mr. Deters advised that would not be
necessary if the consensus of council was to approve the recommendation made by
KCPC.
Mayor Moriconi commented that he appreciated the Victorian/Colonial theme being
continued and is contributing to the revitalization of the downtown area. He
advised council that an ordinance would be prepared to accept the
recommendation from the KCPC and submitted for a first reading at the March 7,
2005 meeting.
Discussion of Lease Proposal by Cingular Wireless to Install Cell Tower at
Sterling Staggs Park
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council an offer from Cingular Wireless for a lease
agreement to rent an approximate 100x100 parcel in the Sterling Staggs Park to
erect a cell tower disguised as a flagpole. He stated the document before them
is not an actual contract. Mr. Deters advised it is basically a letter of
intent from Cingular. Mayor Moriconi stated Cingular is proposing a flagpole
similar to the photo enclosed in the packets. He stated the letter of intent
proposes a lease amount that ranges from $1,500 per month for the first five
years to $5,277 per month for the last five years over a fifty-year term. Mayor
Moriconi stated that Mr. Deters had dealt with this type of business contract
in the past for the flagpole cell tower that was erected on the property of
Scott High School.
Council Member Yeager asked what section of the Park Cingular wanted to lease.
Mr. Deters advised that hasn’t been determined yet. He stated that accepting
the letter of intent would allow Cingular to conduct a study to determine that.
Mayor Moriconi stated that when the study is complete and if the city is not in
agreement with their final proposal then we would have the option to reject
their final offer. Council Member Cobble stated she would want to know the base
dimensions of the flagpole and wanted to suggest some bargaining tools. Mr.
Deters advised the city should not expose it’s had in an open forum. He
suggested they inspect the flagpole that has been constructed on the property
of Scott High School.
Council Member Franzen stated that Cingular had expressed interest in and had
been negotiating with Independence Christian Church, of which she is a member.
And she stated she was not aware whether or not those negotiations had ceased.
She wondered if she should recuse herself from discussions on this issue.
Council Member Yeager commented that this offer is hard to turn down. Since the
consensus of the Council was to move forward with this offer, Mayor Moriconi
advised he would keep Council informed of the negotiations. Mr. Deters stated
he would prepare a Resolution for Council to approve at the March 7, 2005
meeting.
Discussion Regarding the Adoption of Rules of Order for the Council Meetings
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Rules of Order and Procedures for the
council meetings as submitted for consideration by Council Member Kelso. Mayor
Moriconi asked Mr. Deters if this should be adopted by Resolution or Ordinance.
Mr. Deters suggested Council Member Kelso explain his proposal.
Council Member Kelso advised that this document will dictate conduct of both
the council members and the public and that since there are sections that will
apply to the citizens it will be required to be adopted by ordinance. He stated
that if it was just dealing with parliamentary procedures to could be adopted
by municipal order. Mr. Deters suggested he explain the purpose of adopting
this document. Council Member Kelso stated that he would challenge anyone to
tell him this city’s rules of order, to conduct efficient, effective and kindly
meetings. He stated that he believes this document will assist with that
process in running smoother meetings.
Council Member Cobble stated that he hoped they would adopt a document that
would deal with ten or fifteen parliamentary procedures and not encompass
statutes. She stated that she believes you cannot have a document that
summarizes statutes. Council Member Cobble stated she has strong reservations
regarding Section 6.3, Violation of Rules of Order, especially with imposing
penalties. She stated the city has a sergeant-at-arms that could handle order,
as well as the mayor. She stated that she feels those measures are already in
place.
Mr. Bill Cobble interjected that since the city has two meetings per month that
both should be business (voting) meetings. He stated he feels it takes too long
to get some of the business accomplished.
Council Member Kelso stated that he strongly disagrees with Mayor Moriconi’s
assertion. He stated at times the meetings have been out of control with some
people acting inappropriately. He stated everyone needs to know the protocol of
the meetings. Council member Franzen stated that everyone should act like
adults. Council Member Kelso replied that doesn’t work.
Council Member Little stated, that at first glance the document appears a
little lengthy and he feels like 90-95% of the content of the document is
already being accomplished as mandated by statute. Mr. Deters stated the
statute was restated in simpler terms in this document. Council Member Little
commented that while he really doesn’t have an issue with the document, he
questions the need for this in an organized form. Council Member Cobble
commented that it is probably not necessary if it is redundant. Council Member
Franzen stated that some of the content she liked, but that some is redundant
and she feels the violation penalties is a bit stiff.
Council Member Kelso commented that as a newly elected official, he feels this
document would have been helpful.
Mr. Deters advised the council members to discuss their proposed changes with
Council Member Kelso, and then he will review the legalities of any changes.
Mayor Moriconi stated this would be presented at the March 7, 2005 council
meeting.

Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Report on Kenton County Road Issue
Mayor Moriconi thanked Council Member Little for the in-depth report he
compiled and presented to Council regarding the Kenton County road issue. He
stated this report required extensive research by Council Member Little,
wherein he has surmised that the seventeen miles of county roads that are
within the incorporated city limits should actually be reduced to only five
miles that the city should be responsible for maintaining. Mayor Moriconi
directed Mr. Deters to review the report and then draft a letter to the Kenton
County Fiscal Court advising them of the city’s findings and facts on this
issue.
America Supporting Americans – Adopt a Military Unit Program
Mayor Moriconi stated that Council Member Kelso has suggested the city adopt a
military unit, which is the focus of an organization known as America
Supporting Americans. Council Member Kelso stated he would like the city to
adopt the Walton Military Police unit who is currently serving in Iraq. He
stated that many of the unit’s members live in Independence and some of their
family members contacted him about this program. He stated he thinks this will
be a good program for the city to actively support. Mayor Moriconi suggested a
Resolution be presented at the March 7, 2005 meeting for Council’s approval.
Council Member Cobble stated this should meet with unanimous approval. She also
suggested announcement of this adoption of a military unit be in the next
newsletter to encourage a letter writing campaign.
Update on Proposed Cox Road Improvements
Mayor Moriconi reported that the original estimates for improvements to the
intersection of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road (SR 16) was considered to be
around $150,000. He stated the estimate has now been determined to be half that
amount, with $30,000 being funded by the developer of the Pembroke Subdivision,
which will have egress onto Cox Road. Mayor Moriconi advised Council that the
city has contacted Dick Murgatroyd of the state Transportation Cabinet
requesting assistance with the funding of this project. He stated that if the
state does not assist with the project, then the additional project of
extending the turn lane to the intersection of Taylor Mill Road would be
withdrawn.
Council Member Yeager stated she noticed cable being installed in that area.
Mayor Moriconi advised a utility pole would need to be moved on the south side,
so the cable lines may not be impacted.
Mayor Moriconi advised he would keep Council informed of any developments of
this issue as they become know.
Business of the Month
Mayor Moriconi stated that Council Member Cook would select the business of the
month to be recognized at the March meeting. Council Member Cook stated he has
chosen US Bank.
Miscellaneous
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mrs. Brown’s class at Beechgrove Elementary for all
their thank you cards they sent him.
Council Member cobble requested that future agendas be considerate of those who
have attorney’s present to represent them and permit those agenda issues to
take priority over issues being presented by city staff members and/or regular
orders of business. Mayor Moriconi concurred.
Council Member Cobble also thanked everyone that assisted with contesting the
proposed insurance premium tax that was being proposed by the Kenton County
Fiscal Court.
Adjournment
There being no further business, motion was made by Council Member Little and
seconded by Council Member Kelso to adjourn. Motion was carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 9:10 pm.

March 7, 2005
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky. met on Monday, March 7,
2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Doctor Will Lange Ford, Pastor of Hickory Grove Baptist
Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso,
Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.

Mayor Moriconi presented a Proclamation to the Simon Kenton High School
Academic Team and their coaches. The Proclamation was in recognition of winning
first place in the KAAC Governor’s Cup Ninth Region competition on February 19,
2005. Mayor Moriconi proclaimed March 9, 2005 as “Simon Kenton Academic Team
Day.” Mayor Moriconi wished the team luck at the KAAC Governor’s Cup all-state
competition March 12-14, 2005.
Business of the Month Recognition
Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member Margaret Cook had chosen US Bank
as the recipient of the Business of the Month. He presented a plaque of
recognition to the bank’s Assistant Vice President, Sandra Woolum.

Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February 28,

Ordinance No. 2005-0-02-Approving Map Amendment-KCPC Application No. 1717-R-2nd
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading an ordinance approving
a proposed map amendment for an approximate 88-acre area located on the east
side of Fowler Creek Road between Sycamore Creek Drive and Cox Road from R-1A
and R-1C to R-1D, under KCPC Application No.1717R. Mayor Moriconi directed City
Attorney Deters to read the ordinance.
Mayor Moriconi asked for a motion on the second reading of Ordinance No. 2005-
0-02. Council Member Kelso so moved, with second by Council Member Little. A
discussion ensued.
Council Member Yeager stated she would like to add that after speaking to the
City Attorney, she stated some wording regarding the Fowler Creek debt
reduction needs to be added to future ordinances regarding new subdivisions
that will tie into the Fowler Creek sewer system. City Attorney Deters stated
that he recalls from previous discussions that there are fifteen houses that
will tie directly into the new Fowler Creek line installed by the Sanitation
District and the remainder of the development would go into the city’s Fowler
Creek sewer system.
Mr. Don Stegman with Cardinal Engineering representing Centerline Development
stated he did not have any objections with the city adding this as a condition
of the development regarding the Fowler Creek sewer line. City Attorney Deters
stated he did not feel this additional language to the ordinance was
significant enough to require a new first reading because it was discussed at a
prior meeting and it could be added as an eighth condition to the ordinance
stating the “development will be a part of the Fowler Creek Debt Reduction area
which will require the residents to participate in the $280.00 yearly debt
reduction assessment”.
Council Member Cobble expressed concern that since the current ordinance
relating to cluster mailboxes has come under legal scrutiny that it might be
wise to add another condition on approving this development and include
language in this ordinance that would prohibit the cluster mailboxes in this
development. Council Member Kelso questioned the need to do this since there is
already an ordinance prohibiting gang mailboxes in single family developments.
Council Member Cobble also suggested in the form of a request of the developer,
with regard to proposed Resolution No. 2005-R-08 “Vision of Independence” that
has been listed on the agenda for this meeting, since it is her personal
vision, and in honor of a former Kenton County Extension agent, Mr. William
Straw who propagated the Aristocrat Pear Tree, that they plant a couple of the
trees in the common spaces of this development.
Council Member Franzen stated the Planning Commission recommended the city give
consideration to providing a street extension to Mr. & Mrs. Carr adjoining
property. She asked if that would also be a condition or is the developer going
to do that himself. Mr. Stegman stated the whole intersection would be
accommodated so the extension can be provided in the future.
There being no further discussion roll was called and answered unanimously.

NEW BUSINESS
Resolution No. 2005-R-05-Adopting a Military Unit
Mayor Moriconi stated it has been brought to his attention and a request has
been made that the city adopt a military unit. He advised that Council Member
Kelso has suggested a particular military unit for the city to adopt. He asked
Council Member Kelso to address this issue. Council Member Kelso stated
residents Harold and Phyllis Pettit brought this issue to his attention and
thanked them for taking the time to bring it to the city’s attention and push
forward with this. He stated they are members of the Family Readiness Group for
the 940th Military Unit. He stated Goldie Lakes and Jenny Shalfeld were present
in the audience and noted Jenny is president of the Family Readiness Group and
Goldie is the vice-president. He stated Mr. John Stein is the field liaison for
“Kentucky for America Supporting America” which is the organization the city
will be collaborating with. He stated Mr. Stein is also a city councilman for
the City of Alexandria.
Mr. Stein stated they are a 501C organization that seeks to develop ties
between the community and the military that started in 1967. Mr. Stein gave a
brief narrative of ASA history and purpose of their program and stated its
history can be read on their website at www.asa-usa.org. He stated there is
several different ways to engage your community and by acting as a conduit of
information the city can get churches involved and organizations such as the
American Legion. He stated the city newsletter is a good vehicle to communicate
information to the citizens. He stated other ways of getting the community
involved are letters from school children, care packages, surplus law
enforcement equipment and school supplies can also be shipped. He stated there
are ten other Northern Kentucky cities that have adopted a military unit. He
stated if there is information that you would like to share on the ASA website
there is an agreement form that needs to be completed and also donation
agreement forms along with more information could be obtained on the website.
Mayor Moriconi stated this information will go on the city’s website and also
in our next newsletter. He stated everyone is excited to support this mission.
Council Member Cobble stated the Resolution was lacking a zip code for the
Walton military unit, and it needs to be included since the post office will
not deliver without a zip code.
Mr. Stein stated the commander from the Kentucky National Guard which is the
940th Military Police Unit out of Walton, Ky. has contacted ASA and asked them
attempt to find cities willing to adopt all their units within the National
Guard. Mayor Moriconi stated he would like to have the 940th MP Company in the
July 4th parade, which will be on Saturday, July 2nd. Mr. Stein stated the unit
might still be deployed in July. Mayor Moriconi stated any members that could
represent them would be great. Council Member Yeager stated she would like to
thank them for all the past years they have helped the city and now appreciated
the opportunity to help them.
Mayor Moriconi read Resolution 2005-R-05. Council Member Kelso moved to adopt
Resolution 2005-R-05 as read, with a second by Council Member Cobble. Roll call
was answered unanimously and the motion carried 6-0.
Council Member Kelso stated he would again like to thank Harold and Phyllis
Pettit for bringing this to the city’s attention and making sure this happened.

Proposed Ordinance Adopting Rules of Order for Council Meetings - 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance adopting rules of
order for council meetings. Mayor Moriconi stated before the ordinance is read
he would like to add some changes. City Attorney Deters stated he has received
some suggested changes from Council Members Cobble and Franzen. Mr. Deters
recommended this ordinance be added to the agenda in April so he can discuss
these changes with the council members. Council Member Kelso recommended a
first reading at this meeting. Mayor Moriconi stated if a first reading is done
at this meeting, there might be substantial changes to the ordinance at the
next meeting that would require a new first reading. Council Member Kelso
stated the changes could be addressed at the second reading. City Attorney
Deters stated the changes that were discussed were not substantial enough to
stop a first reading.
Council Member Cobble commented she feels there are substantial changes that
have been recommended by herself and Council Member Franzen. Council Member
Yeager stated she feels some of the changes are pretty substantial with regard
to state statute and city ordinances. Council Member Kelso stated there are
suggested changes which is the only thing that could be substantial but other
things are just questions. Council Member Kelso stated he has read what Council
Members Cobble and Franzen have suggested, and he has no objections with the
majority of the recommended changes.
Council Member Cobble stated the substantial changes she is concerned with are
the criminal penalties. She stated she has a very big problem with putting
criminal penalties in the rules of order. She stated under “Violations of
Rules”, we are using that mandatory language that says, “shall” instead of the
permissive language, which is “may”. She quoted from the K.R.S. 83A.0656(2)
“authorize a city to punish those who violate city ordinances and failure to
abide by the terms and conditions set forth in these Rules of Order “shall”,
again that word should be “may” constitute either a “Misdemeanor or a
Violation.” She asked who would define the “failure to abide by the terms and
conditions.” She questioned if someone exceeded the time limit for addressing
council by more than five minutes, are they failing to abide. She also asked
who would inform the people addressing the council of the rules. She asked the
Mayor if he is going to advise anyone that comes to speak, of the rules that
only permit someone to speak five minutes or less. Mayor Moriconi stated under
the agenda’s Privileges of the Floor, if there are more than five people signed
up to address the council, he will ask that they keep their comments to three
minutes or less.
Mr. Deters stated the purpose of adopting this as an ordinance, puts the city
on notice that these rules are a newly enacted legislation that they are to
take notice of. He stated he was sure Council Member Kelso planned on having
copies of the rules available to anyone to obtain. He stated the process of
doing the ordinance in passing the law basically puts the community on notice.
Council Member Franzen stated she thinks the spirit of the rules of order was
to place some sort of punishment for those who are unruly. Council Member
Cobble stated we already have an ordinance regarding disorderly conduct.
Council Member Franzen stated she did not think it was a bad idea to have fines
for someone who is blatant. Council Member Cobble stated to get a fine, it has
to go through the District Court and that the city would not receive any monies
from that fine. Council Member Franzen stated she would look at it as teaching
someone a lesson. Council Member Cobble asked what crime she deems necessary to
occur to fine someone a $100.00 penalty. Council Member Franzen stated if
someone screams or slanders someone in the council chambers during the meeting.
Again, Council Member Franzen stated the city already has an ordinance
regarding disorderly conduct. Council Member Little stated if someone is close
to breaking the rules; it would be brought to their attention.
Council Member Yeager asked Mr. Deters if these changes discussed would be
considered substantial. Council Member Franzen asked if they needed a vote to
remain or delete text from the proposed rules. City Attorney Deters stated you
either adopt the Ordinance or you don’t, adopt as amended, or you don’t. Mayor
Moriconi stated Council Member Kelso has worked on these rules for a month and
is sure Council Member Kelso would like to have a first reading to proceed with
getting this adopted.
Council Member Yeager made a motion to have a first reading, seconded by
Council Member Little. Council Member Yeager asked if there will be more
discussion prior to the next vote. Council Member Kelso stated he did not have
a problem with striking section 6.3 completely because whether this council
wants it or not, KRS gives the authority to implement these rules. He stated it
gives the city the authority to implement and that authority still resides
within the Mayor and Council but it can be deleted. Mayor Moriconi concurred
with council that it was permissible to remove section 6.3 of the Rules of
Order.
Roll call was answered unanimously and motion carried 6-0. Mayor Moriconi asked
City Attorney Deters to read the proposed Rules of Order ordinance.
Discussion Regarding a Proposed Ordinance to Approve a Text Amendment to Add
Indoor Shooting Range as a Permitted Use in the R-C2 Zone
Mayor Moriconi stated this ordinance is not on the agenda, as the information
was not received from the Kenton County Planning Commission prior to
distribution of the council packets. He stated the property owner, Mr. Bill
Dehlinger, who requested the city sponsor this text amendment is present and
has requested the city have a first reading of a proposed ordinance to act on
the KCPC recommendation that was decided at their meeting last Thursday. Mr.
Deters explained a Resolution was approved to get the Planning Commission to
comment on amending the city zoning ordinance to add language that would permit
an indoor shooting range as a permitted use in the R-C2 zone. He stated the
KCPC has recommended approval of a text amendment for an indoor shooting range
be allowed in the R-C2 zone as a conditional use; not as a permitted use the
city applied for. Mr. Deters explained that a conditional use would require the
property owner to get approval from the city’s Board of Adjustment who could
add some conditional parameters on the request. He distributed an ordinance he
prepared according to the Planning Commission’s recommendation, which changes
the text and makes the indoor shooting range a conditional use and not a
permitted use. He stated council needs to vote on whether they want this
shooting range to be a permitted use or a conditional use.
Council Member Kelso moved for a first reading of the proposed ordinance to
approve the zoning text amendment as recommended by the KCPC. Council Member
Franzen seconded the motion.
Mr. Bill Dehlinger stated they did request a permitted use. He stated currently
the only zone that an indoor shooting range would be allowed is the RC-2 zone
and it is only at the Richardson Road site. He stated the mere fact the city
has that zoning, gives the city that measure of control where it would be at
another location if someone else applied for another shooting range. He stated
at the KCPC meeting it was discussed as to whether we need to do that and the
county attorney deemed it conservative in making it a conditional use.
Mayor Moriconi asked if that was the only RC-2 zone in the city and that in and
of itself restricts it because there are no other RC-2 zones in the city. Mr.
Deters advised that as a conditional use this would give the Board of
Adjustments the authority to impose additional conditions on indoor shooting
ranges. Council Member Franzen asked if the Board of Adjustments could stop the
shooting range itself. Mr. Deters stated they could choose to attach so many
conditions to the conditional use that it might deter someone from doing it.
Council Member Yeager stated the city could choose to disregard the KCPC
recommendation to add this text as a conditional use and opt to add the text as
a permitted use. Council Member Cobble asked if the Council needs to be
concerned, as this is just a text amendment, of any adjudicated process being
violated. City Attorney Deters stated they did not.
Mayor Moriconi asked if, as a conditional use, how that affects the process and
getting the information back to the city. City Attorney Deters stated the
property owner would have to submit an application for a hearing before the
city’s Board of Adjustments. Council Franzen stated she is okay with a
permitted use if this is the only R-C2 zone in the city. Mr. Deters stated
there is already a motion and second on the floor to approve this text
amendment as a conditional use. Council Member Kelso withdrew his motion to
approve the KCPC recommendation to add this text as a conditional use. Council
Member Franzen followed by withdrawing her second.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to change the text of the proposed
ordinance to make this zoning text amendment to allow an indoor shooting range
as a permitted use in the R-C2 zone. Council Member Yeager seconded the motion.
Mr. Deters stated the wording of the proposed ordinance would have to be
changed from a conditional use to a permitted use. Roll was called and answered
with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Cobble stated since the ordinance was given to the Council
Members prior to this meeting and was not able to read the ordinance until
tonight and while she gives great weight to the Planning Commission’s opinion
and recommendations she stated in the future she would prefer to have more time
to review the KCPC recommendation prior to voting on an issue. She stated when
council is given something at a business meeting and expected to vote on it at
that meeting, she feels it should be part of the rules that council will not
vote unless it is deemed an emergency.
Police Chief Report - Dave Nichols, Assistant Chief
Mayor Moriconi asked Assistant Police Chief Nichols if he had anything to
report. Mr. Nichols stated the Citizens Police Academy has begun classes again.
He also thanked the VIPS (Volunteers in Policing) volunteers who are citizens
willing to volunteer their time to the police department to do various clerical
tasks when they need the assistance. He stated it has been a major benefit to
the department.

Update on the Cluster Mailbox Issue

to contact to discuss the cluster mail box issue and he is in the process of
scheduling a meeting with this representative and the developer of the Clover
Ridge Subdivision to discuss a resolution to cluster mail box violation in that
development.
Discussion Regarding the Discontinuation of the Sewer Maintenance Fee
Council Member Cobble stated she is prepared to make a motion to have Mr.
Deters prepare an ordinance to consider terminating the sewer surcharge that
was initiated to pay the GRW debt. She asked if that could be done by ordinance
or municipal order. City Attorney Deters stated it should be an ordinance. She
then requested he prepare an ordinance to terminate the sewer surcharge for
consideration at the caucus meeting. Mr. Deters asked if that was to include
the Fowler Creek charge. Council Member Cobble stated everyone pays the
surcharge and that is added to all city residents billing to pay the GRW debt,
which now has an excess of $846,000.00. She stated the properties connected to
the Fowler Creek sewers would then just be paying the debt reduction. Council
Member Franzen stated the Fowler Creek charge is added to the property tax
bills, and not on the sewer bill. Mr. Deters asked if council was aware the
maintenance surcharge was added in 1978 and the GRW debt was not in existence
at that time. Council Member Little stated it was for maintenance of the sewer
system and since the city no longer provides maintenance for the sewer system
it is not needed. Mr. Deters stated the Fowler Creek ordinance allows the city
to use that surcharge also for the payment of the Fowler Creek bond debt. He
stated if the surcharge was kept in place it would help reduce the debt
reduction. Council Member Yeager stated she would like to transfer the monies
from the general sewer fund to the Fowler Creek fund until such time it can be
paid down. She stated there needs to be a history maintained of this project
and a forecast to assist future elected officials. Council Member Kelso stated
he would like this discussed more at the caucus meeting. He stated if a surplus
exists he would like to review that situation in more detail.
Discussion Regarding the Discontinuation of a Caucus Meeting in order to have
two Business Meetings
Council Member Cobble suggested the city Council hold two business meetings
each month and eradicate the caucus meeting format. She requested that Mr.
Deters prepare an amended ordinance regarding the city meetings so this can be
put to a vote.
Adjournment
There being no further business to discuss, Council Member Kelso moved to
adjourn the meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 8:36pm.

Resolution No. 2005-R-06-Cingular Wireless Tower at Sterling Staggs Park

Proposed Ordinance-Adopting Rules of Order for Council Meetings-1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance adopting rules of
order for council meetings. Mayor Moriconi stated before the ordinance is read
he would like to add some changes. City Attorney Deters stated he has received
some suggested changes from Council Members Cobble and Franzen. City Attorney
Deters recommended this ordinance be added to the agenda in April so he can
discuss these changes with the council members. Council Member Kelso suggested
a first reading. Mayor Moriconi stated there might be substantial changes to
the ordinance. Council Member Kelso stated the changes could be addressed at
the second reading. City Attorney Deters stated the changes that were discussed
were not substantial enough to stop a first reading.
Council Member Cobble noted there being substantial changes between herself and
Council Member Franzen. Council Member Yeager stated she feels some of the
changes are pretty substantial regarding KRS and Ordinances. Council Member
Kelso stated there are suggested changes which is the only thing that could be
substantial but other things are just questions. Council Member Kelso stated he
has read what Council Members Cobble and Franzen did, and is fine with the
majority of the changes.
Council Member Cobble stated the substantial changes she is concerned with are
the criminal penalties. She stated she has a very big problem with putting
criminal penalties in the rules of order. She stated under “Violations of
Rules”, we are using that mandatory language that says “shall” instead of the
permissive language which is “may”. She quoted from the K.R.S. 83A.0656(2)
“authorize a city to punish those who violate city ordinances and failure to
abide by the terms and conditions set forth in these Rules of Order “shall”,
again that word should by “may” constitute either a “Misdemeanor or a
Violation” . She asked who is going to define a failure to abide by the terms
and conditions. She asked if someone goes over the time limit of speaking more
than five minutes, are they failing to abide. She also asked who will tell
someone that is going to speak, what the rules are. She asked the Mayor if he
is going to advise anyone that comes to speak, there a rule that only allows
someone to speak five minutes or less.
Mayor Moriconi stated under Privileges of the Floor, if there are more than
five people signed up to address them, he will ask that they keep their
comments to three minutes or less.
City Attorney Deters stated the purpose of adopting this as an ordinance, puts
the city on notice that these rules are a newly enacted legislation that they
are to take notice of. He stated he was sure Council Member Kelso planned on
having copies of the rules available to anyone to obtain. He stated the process
of doing the ordinance in passing the law puts the community on notice.
Council Member Franzen stated she thinks the spirit of the rules was to place
some sort of punishment for those who are unruly. Council Member Cobble stated
we already have an ordinance regarding disorderly conduct. Council Member
Franzen stated she did not think it was a bad idea to have fines for someone
who is blatant. Council Member Cobble stated to get a fine, it has to go thru
the District Court which the city would not receive any monies from that fine.
Council Member Franzen stated she would look at it as teaching someone a
lesson. Council Member Cobble asked what crime she deems necessary to occur to
fine someone a $100.00 penalty. Council Member Franzen stated if someone
screamed at someone or calls someone a name. Council Member Little stated if
someone is close to breaking the rules; it would be brought to their attention.
Council Member Yeager asked City Attorney Deters is this issue is substantial.
Council Member Franzen asked if they needed a vote to remain or delete from the
rules. City Attorney Deters stated you either adopt the Ordinance or you don’t,
adopt as amended, or you don’t. Mayor Moriconi stated Council Member Kelso has
worked on these rules for a month and is sure Council Member Kelso would like
to have a first reading. Council Member Yeager made a motion to have a first
reading, seconded by Council Member Little but asked if there will be more
discussion prior to the next vote. Council Member Kelso stated he did not have
a problem with striking section 6.3 completely because whether this council
wants it or not, KRS gives the authority to implement these rules. He stated it
gives the city the authority to implement and that authority still resides
within the Mayor and Council but it can be deleted. Mayor Moriconi concurred
with council that it was permissible to remove section 6.3 of the Rules of
Order.  
Roll call was answered unanimously and motion carried 6-0. Mayor Moriconi asked
City Attorney Deters to read the Ordinance.

March 21, 2005
Caucus Council Meeting Minutes
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 21,
2005 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso,
Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi advised that those who signed in for privileges of the floor
would reserve comment until the agenda item is presented for discussion.
Request of City to Support Zoning Text Amendment to Add Medical Office
Buildings as Permitted Use in NC Zone
Mr. Jim Bertram addressed council with a request that the city sponsor a zoning
text amendment that would add medical office buildings as a permitted use in
the NC zone. He stated that currently only the PO (professional office) zone
allows medical office buildings. Mr. Bertram advised that he will be
constructing an office building on the old Park and Ride lot at 5294 Madison
Pike and currently has a doctor that is interested in locating there.
Hearing no objections to this request, Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Deters to
draft a Resolution approving the sponsorship of this text amendment application
and it would be presented at the April 4, 2005 meeting for council’s
consideration.
Road Inventory Summary Report – Presented by City Engineer, ––Mark
Brueggemann–, CDS Engineers
Mayor Moriconi stated that several months ago the city council authorized an in
depth road inventory of all the city streets. He stated the city engineer has
compiled his findings and has presented a report, which Mr. Brueggemann will
review with council.
Mr. Brueggemann stated the results of this road inventory lists every city
street and provides detailed information such as the length and width, type of
pavement, curbs (if there are any) and the type of curb and whether or not the
street has sidewalks. He stated that each street was visually inspected and
evaluated. The report also estimates which streets need to be reconstructed and
when with an opinion of construction costs for each fiscal year through the
year 2009 for the city’s budgeting purposes. He stated the recommendations were
made based on needs and conditions.
Mayor Moriconi stated this report now provides the city with a guide to use
over the next five years. Council Member Little stated this report is
excellent. He asked if the cost estimates were figured at today’s prices. Mr.
Brueggemann replied yes and that adjustments for inflation would be necessary.
He stated his ballpark estimate would be 2-3% per year or the CPI (consumer
price index).
Council Member Kelso asked if this five-year plan was based on current budget
assumptions and if this would be reflected in the 2005/06 budget, as he feels
the city should not have studies conducted and then not implement the results
of the study. Chief Butler stated the city did not have a street program in
place when he assumed supervision of the Public Works Department. He stated he
feels this is a critical step; obtaining the data needed to develop a plan for
future repairs.
Mr. Brueggemann stated that based on the number of roads in the city, the
absolute minimum the city should be budgeting for road repairs each year is
$300,000 to $500,000. Mayor Moriconi commented some of the repairs could be
accomplished in the 2005/06 budget or a plan could be developed to fund a
portion of the major repairs.
Council Member Cobble asked if some of the streets with major problems could be
attributed to storm water runoff. Mr. Brueggemann replied yes. She commented
that if this is the case then the city might want to approach the Sanitation
District (SD1) with a request to help fund fifty percent of the repairs. Mr.
Brueggemann advised that since SD1 has a pending lawsuit that has been filed
against them regarding the storm water management program surcharge they
oversee for the local cities, they are suspending future storm water system
repair projects. Chief Butler commented that the city and Sanitation District
have already collaborated on two repair projects. Chief Butler asked if SD1 was
honoring prior commitments. Mr. Brueggemann stated SD1 is only honoring the
projects that have already been bid out.
Council Member Yeager stated she noticed the recommended depth of concrete is
one inch and in some cases one and one-half inch. She asked if the depth was
increased to two inches if it would increase the life of the street. Mr.
Brueggemann advised increasing the depth of the street to two inches would
decrease the height of the street curbs.
Council Member Cobble asked if stricter subdivision regulations would help
increase the life of the streets. Mr. Brueggemann advised some things could be
implemented, but that the city’s regulations are currently the same as the
other local cities. Council Member Franzen asked which was a better material
for the streets - asphalt or concrete. Mr. Brueggemann advised that asphalt is
easier to maintain, both wear well and have their pros and cons and that the
sub grade is very important for both materials.
Mayor Moriconi advised this street inventory report would be posted on the city
website or that residents could get a copy from the city office. Council Member
Cobble asked that the City Clerk be responsible for informing future elected
officials that this report exists.
OLD BUSINESS
Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Rules of Order for Council Meetings – Review
of Latest Draft
Mayor Moriconi presented the latest revision of the Rules of Order ordinance
and asked for any comments or proposed amendments. He stated if there are no
requested changes then this would be presented at the April 4th meeting for a

ordinance. Council Member Franzen suggested moving Mr. Jim Bertram’s agenda
item up to let him make his presentation regarding his map amendment request.
Mayor Moriconi agreed that was a good idea.
NEW BUSINESS
Proposed Map Amendment – KCPC Application No. 1728R – An Approximate 50-Acre
Area along the South Side of Cody Road between the CSX RR and Upton Drive from
R-1C to R-1C(PUD) – Carol Ann Subdivision
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Mr. Jim Bertram who distributed a handout
to council that included a Stage I development plan for “Carol Ann
Subdivision.” Mr. Deters asked if the information he was distributing were the
same documents reviewed by the Planning Commission (KCPC). Mr. Bertram replied
yes.
Mr. Bertram advised he was requesting a map amendment that would change the
current zone of R-1C to R-1C (PUD) as it would allow the developer a more
flexible design and preserve Banklick Creek by providing more open space. He
stated they will be approaching the Kenton County Conservancy to take over the
maintenance of the open green space. He stated the development plan calls for
117 lots; 78 single family parcels, which would be consistent with the type of
houses in the Troopers Crossing and Battleridge subdivisions. He stated the
remaining 39 lots would be developed as duplexes (two units per lot) and would
probably be rental properties, but not a section 8 development.
Mr. Bertram stated the KCPC has approved this map amendment and development
plan contingent on the following four conditions:
·   The City of Independence determine whether or not to close Cody Road at the
Banklick Creek/CSX railroad crossing.
·   That an HOA (homeowners association) or the Kenton Conservancy be assigned
the responsibility for the maintenance and management of the open space areas.
·   That each single family dwelling unit is provided with a minimum of 2 off-
street parking spaces and each 2-family dwelling unit e provided with a minimum
of 4 off-street parking spaces.
·   That additional pedestrian’s access to the proposed open space area be
provided in the vicinity of lots 88 and 89.
Mr. Bertram commented that he doesn’t know how the city feels about closing
Cody Road. It would be realigned to produce a T-intersection. He stated there
is slippage condition before the low water area and the development would
alleviate the slippage. A lengthy discussion ensued regarding options to repair
this portion of Cody Road. Chief Butler advised the Kenton County School Board
has sent correspondence to the city expressing their opposition to closing Cody
Road. He stated there is also the issue of whether it is the city or the county
that is ultimately responsible for the maintenance of Cody Road. He stated last
year Kenton County representatives attended a city council meeting to discuss
options for improving Cody Road, but they have not followed up with the city
since then. He stated that he believes the state provided funds to the county
to make improvements to Cody Road.
Council Member Cobble expressed concern regarding the proposed small lot sizes
and the duplex style houses. Mr. Bertram stated the R-1C (PUD) allows a more
flexible development and the smaller lot sizes will maximize the ridge and
leave the creek area undisturbed and the duplexes will provide a good mix of
residential units. He stated the larger lots by the railroad tracks might prove
to be unmarketable as a single-family parcel. He stated the frontage on the
smaller lots would be sixty-five feet, but that the PUD designation would
permit fifty-foot lots
Council Member Franzen suggested an all brick front on the duplexes. Mr.
Bertram was agreeable to that suggestion. Council Member Cobble asked the price
range of the homes. Mr. Bertram stated the prices would range from $150,000 -
$190,000 for the single-family structures and $200,000 for the duplexes. He
stated that one builder would develop all the duplexes and probably manage them
as well.
Mayor Moriconi questioned cluster mailboxes. Mr. Bertram stated he was not a
fan of cluster mailboxes and that the development would have consistent boxes.
Mr. Bertram stated that the site distance issue would need to be resolved
before this development can proceed.
Council Member Cobble asked about providing water access lines to Upton Drive
residents and Council Member Yeager asked the sewer system and if it would tie
into the Brushy Fork lines. Mr. Bertram replied that water lines would have to
be extended from the Battleridge subdivision as it currently stops one-quarter
mile from the site. He stated both water and sewer services would be provided
closer to Upton Drive and they would have to look at the possibility of
servicing the other residents in that area. He also advised that the sewer
system has not yet been determined, as they would be done in the design phase
of the development. Council Member Yeager stated she would like the builders to
provide that information to the city. He stated he would try to make a judgment
call in time for the first reading of the ordinance at the next meeting.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the subdivision would have an HOA. Mr. Bertram replied
no, that the developers, in an effort to be environmentally friendly wanted to
preserve the Banklick Creek, will be donating the open green space to the
Kenton Conservancy. Council Member Cobble asked if the Conservancy has agreed
to accept this. Mr. Bertram replied yes.
Council Member Cook advised she is not happy with the size of the lots. Mr.
Bertram commented that the sixty-five foot lots are a step up from the fifty-
foot minimum lot size permitted with a PUD zone. Council Member Franzen asked
how many lots are planned to be sixty-five feet. Mr. Bertram replied the
majority of the development would be sixty-five foot lots. Council Member
Franzen asked if he could increase the size of the lots. Mr. Bertram stated
that would be difficult in order to make the development feasible. Mayor
Moriconi advised Mr. Bertram there appears to be considerable concern from the
council regarding the small lot sizes and asked if he would like to make an
attempt to re-configure the lot sizes. Council Member Cobble also expressed
concern regarding the duplexes that would become rental property appealing to
lower income families.
Mr. Bertram stated he would try to get more information from the builder prior
to the next council meeting as well as some answers about the plans for the
rental property. Council Member Yeager commented that she has several concerns
and would like to negotiate some of the details of this proposed development.
Mr. Bertram stated he would look into some other options to present to council,
hopefully before the April 4, 2005 meeting.
Mayor Moriconi advised this proposed map amendment would require two readings
of an ordinance and suggested additional comments and concerns could be
addressed prior to the first reading at the April 4, 2005 meeting.
OLD BUSINESS (Continued)

Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Repealing Ordinance No. 12-1-78 that
Established the Sewer Maintenance Fee (Surcharge)
Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed ordinance that would repeal Ordinance No.
12-1-78 which established the general sewer maintenance fee (surcharge) in
1978. He advised the interlocal agreement with the Sanitation District (SD1) in
1998 relinquished maintenance of the city sewer lines to SD1 and since the city
has adequate funds to effectively pay the balance of the GRW debt it is no
longer necessary to impose this maintenance fee. He stated this proposed
ordinance is a result of Council’s discussion at the last meeting.
Council Member Kelso asked the amount of the fee. Council Member Yeager advised
the fee varies as it is based on water usage in each household. He asked if the
funds generated had ever been used to reduce the Fowler Creek Sewer debt.
Council Member Yeager stated she is attempting to gather more information about
the two sewer funds. Council Member Cobble distributed a copy of the KRS
regarding user fees and commented she feels this ordinance should have been
repealed in 1999. She stated if the fee is a surcharge, as considered by Mr.
Eger (General Manager of SD1) then it is a legal charge. She stated she feels
it was just a bookkeeping mistake and that the surcharge should have been
removed.
Mayor Moriconi commented that it seems everyone is in agreement that the
maintenance fee (surcharge) should be discontinued so this proposed ordinance
would be presented for a first reading at the April 4, 2005 meeting. Council
Member Cobble suggested the city notify SD1 that the fee will be discontinued.
Mayor Moriconi directed the City Clerk to draft a letter to SD1 for his
signature.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2005-O-01 and Eliminating the
Caucus Meeting Format
Mayor Moriconi presented for council’s consideration a proposed ordinance that
will amend Ordinance No. 2005-O-01 setting the times, places and purposes of
city council meetings. He stated the amended ordinance would eliminate the

The comments expressed by the council members were in favor of this change.

council meetings are established in the Rules of Order ordinance the city is in
the process of adopting. Mr. Deters suggested that since the Rules of Order
ordinance would be in conflict with this ordinance that council may want to
just repeal Ordinance No. 2005-O-01
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Update on Cluster Mailbox Issue in the Clover Ridge Subdivision
Mayor Moriconi reported he has been informed that the U.S. Post Office Director
of Operations has visited the Clover Ridge subdivision and has determined the
cluster mailboxes can be retained. In addition, a Fischer Homes representative
has also confirmed they plan on keeping the cluster mailboxes in place. Mayor
Moriconi advised that Fischer Homes is adamant in their position on this issue.
Council Member Yeager asked that Mr. Deters go to the Director of Operations’
supervisor. Council Member Cobble commented that since Mr. Deters is of the
opinion that the city ordinance prohibiting cluster mailboxes is valid, then
she would like to see specific federal law the U.S. Post Office cites the city
is violating. Mr. Deters stated he has researched this issue and could not find
any laws the city is violating and the legal counsel for the Post Office has
not provided any. He stated he feels since the city is not restricting the Post
Office’s delivery of the mail then the city has the authority to impose the ban
on cluster boxes
Mayor Moriconi asked council how far they wanted to go in pursuing this issue,
as it may be necessary to file a lawsuit if they want to move forward with
enforcing the ordinance. Mr. Deters advised the next step would be to file an
injunction in court. Council Member Cobble suggested Mayor Moriconi personally
call Henry Fischer. Mayor Moriconi informed council that he spoke with Steve
Feldman of Fischer Homes.
Mr. Steve Fischer (no relation to Fischer Homes), a resident in the Clover
Ridge subdivision addressed council by informing them that he has learned that
Fischer Homes has signed an agreement with the Post Office to install cluster
mailboxes in the last phase of the subdivision. He stated he has also learned
that once the cluster mailboxes have been established as the mode of delivery
they cannot change. He stated some individual curbside mailboxes have been
installed. Mayor Moriconi commented that developers prefer to install the
cluster mailboxes in subdivisions that have fifty-foot lots – for aesthetic
reasons.
Council Member Cobble commented that she feels the city needs to stand up and
enforce the city ordinances.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler stated he had nothing to report.
