NEW BUSINESS
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment for a 50-Acre Tract on the South
Side of Cody Road – KCPC Application No. 1728R – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would approve a map amendment (KCPC Application No. 1728R) changing an
approximate 50-acre area located along the south side of Cody Road between the
CSX Railroad and Upton Drive, approximately 500 feet west of Upton Drive from
R-1C to R-1C (PUD). Mr. Deters read the ordinance.
A lengthy discussion ensued. Council Member Cobble advised she has discovered
the density for this development has been calculated incorrectly and she has
spoken to Mike Schwartz of the Planning Commission about this and he has
confirmed the density is wrong. Council discussed the possibility of reviewing
the Planning Commission’s entire record on this application or the city
possibly holding it’s own public hearing. Mr. Deters submitted a memo outlining
the council’s three options when confronted with a map amendment proposal.
Chief Butler voiced his concern that approving this map amendment and
development plan might send an incorrect message to the county that the city is
accepting maintenance of Cody Road. He cautioned council the city is still in
dispute with the county over the maintenance of some of the county roads within
city limits. He stated he is of the opinion that the city will not get
assistance from the county for the needed improvements of Cody Road. Mr. Deters
stated he did not feel the proposed ordinance contained any language that could
be interpreted that the city was automatically accepting full maintenance of
Cody Road.
Mr. Jim Bertram, developer of the proposed map amendment presented to council
and distributed a revised development plan. He stated that he tried to address
all of council’s concerns that were voiced at the last meeting, which included:
·   larger lot size – from the proposed 65’ to 70’ with some lots deeper
·   fewer lots – from 117 to 110
·   35 duplexes will now be sold as condo units, rather than the initial
proposal of rental units
·   eliminated the flag lots
·   no cluster mailboxes
·   duplexes will have an all brick front and will provide this on the single
family, if requested
Mr. Bertram stated he was unaware of the incorrect density issue and informed
council that he would contact Mr. Schwartz at the Planning Commission to
resolve this.
Mr. Deters advised council that since the lot sizes have change and the density
was calculated inaccurately, he feels the first reading of this proposed
ordinance needs to be repealed. He stated council has ninety days from the time
of the KCPC recommendation to act on the map amendment and in this case that
will be June 3, 2005.
Council Member Cobble moved to not accept the first reading of the proposed
ordinance approving a map amendment, KCPC Application Number 1728R, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 6-0.
Mayor Moriconi advised this proposed map amendment would be presented at a
future meeting for a new first reading as soon as the density concern is
resolved, possibly for the April 18, 2005 meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending (Repealing) Ordinance No. 2005-O-01 Relating to
Council Meetings – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a first reading an ordinance amending
Ordinance No. 2005-O-01 setting the times, places and purposes/subjects of the
city council meetings. There was a brief discussion relating to the meetings
now being addressed in the Rules of Order Ordinance No. 2005-O-04 that had the
second reading earlier in this meeting. The consensus of the council was to
repeal, not amend Ordinance No. 2005-O-01.
Council Member Yeager moved to repeal Ordinance No. 2005-O-01, seconded by
Council Member Little. Motion carried all ayes.

Establishment of a Sewer Maintenance Surcharge – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
repeal Ordinance No. 12-1-78 effectively eliminating the sewer maintenance
charge. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Resolution No. 2005-R-08 – Adopting a City Vision and Planning as Proposed by
Council Member ––––Kent–– Kelso
Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2005-R-08 that would call
for the establishment of a citywide initiative to develop strategic priorities
for the city and a citizens committee to lead the process. Mayor Moriconi
directed Mr. Deters to read Resolution No. 2005-R-08.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve Resolution No. 2005-R-08, seconded by
Council Member Kelso.
A lengthy discussion ensued. Some members of the council expressed concerns
regarding the citizen committee setup, how it would be implemented, how this
proposal differed from the “Independence Tomorrow” committee that submitted a
strategic plan proposal a few years ago and the use of surveys to gather
information. Council Member Kelso reassured the council that the volunteers
serving on this committee would go into the community and gather information
from the residents about their dreams for the city. He stated the volunteer
committee meetings would be open to the public. Mayor Moriconi stated that the
Council never adopted the five-year strategic plan proposed by the

Member Yeager expressed her desire that any one that volunteered to be a member
of this committee should not be turned away. Council Member Kelso stated the

Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2005-R-09 that would support

Resolution No. 2005-R-10 Waiving the City Attorney’s Conflict of Interest
Regarding Litigation against the Sanitation District No. 1
Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2005-R-10 that would waive
any conflict of interest created by the law firm of Deters, Benzinger &
LaVelle, P.S.C. by making the City of Independence a party defendant to legal
action against the Sanitation District No. 1 on the condition that no claim for
damages, monetary or otherwise will be sought or pursued against the city. The
law firm of Deters, Benzinger & LaVelle, P.S.C. also represents certain
plaintiffs who have initiated litigation against the Sanitation District
regarding the collection of storm water fees/taxes and the validity of certain
interlocal agreements entered into between the Sanitation District and various
municipalities including Independence. It is the desire to add Independence as
a party defendant only to ensure that the issues in said litigation can be
fully adjudicated.

Little to approve Resolution No. 2005-R-10, seconded by Council Member Yeager.
Roll was called and answered with all ayes. Motion carried 6-0.

KCPC Application No. 1728R - 1st Reading

May 2, 2005
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 2,
2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend Eric Bryant gave the invocation. Roll was called
and the following Council Members registered present: Donna Yeager, Mike
Little, Kent Kelso, Carol Franzen, Margaret Cook and JoAnne Cobble. Also
present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Presentation of Municipal Road Funds by Senator Damon Thayer
Mayor Moriconi introduced Senator Damon Thayer who was present to give a report
on the 2005 General Assembly Session and present a check in the amount of
$198,150.38 for road funds.
Council Member Kelso moved to allow Senator Thayer more time to speak than the
usual five minute allowance. Council Member Franzen seconded the motion. Motion
carried with all ayes.
Senator Thayer thanked Mayor Moriconi and Council for the opportunity to speak
about the very productive session just finished by the Assembly. He reported
the highlights of the Session included the passage of a balanced budget, an
overhaul of the tax code, several important pieces of legislation, economic
development of water, sewer and road projects, as well as cutting taxes across
the board.
Senator Thayer stated that he served on the Transportation Cabinet and that a
supplementary pool of funds has been allocated to cities for road improvements/
repairs. He presented Mayor Moriconi with a check in the amount of $198,150.38
in Municipal Road Aid from the State. Senator Thayer went on to report that he
will continue to work on getting the State to allocate funds for the east/west
connector (SR 536) which is critical for economic development. He stated he
will make this one of his priorities while serving in the Senate. He also
announced that the next phase of the new section of SR 17 will soon be
underway, as $18,000,000 has been allocated and bids will be let in June with
construction beginning approximately 2 months later. He stated the next phase
will run from Pelly Road to Apple Drive. Senator Thayer stated that when this
section is complete it will bypass Independence and provide access to the
rapidly growing surrounding areas.
Senator Thayer also mentioned that Mayor Moriconi had called him asking for
assistance with the deteriorating condition of Senour Road. He advised that he
has arranged for a short-term solution – heavy patching – which will be
accomplished in the next month or so, even tough it was not on the state’s
short term repair list. He advised that the city will need to apply for funds
for future major repairs.
In closing, Senator Thayer stated, that all-in-all, Northern Kentucky had a
very good year in Frankfort as millions of dollars was allocated to several
large projects in this area of the state.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Senator Thayer for the report as well as the extra road
funds.
Recognition of Business of the Month – ––––Independence–– Cleaners, Jeff
Bolger, Proprietor
Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member Kelso had chosen Independence
Cleaners as the recipient of the Business of the Month. He presented a plaque
of recognition to the owner, Jeff Bolger.
Approval of April 18, 2005 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the April 18, 2005
council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second from Council
Member Cobble. Amendments were noted; roll was called and answered 6-0. Motion
carried.
Privileges of the Floor
Thomas Schonecker, 638 Madison Avenue, addressed council regarding the
deteriorating condition of Senour Road. He advised he is the Chief of Police/
Acting City Manager for the City of Covington. He stated that Senour Road is
unique as it borders both Independence and Covington, yet is a state maintained
road. He stated that Covington residents in the Senour Road area have
petitioned the City of Covington to do something to improve the condition of
the street. He stated he was present to ask Independence to support Covington
in their efforts to get the State to make repairs to the street and to reduce
the speed limit to a safer 35 mph. He asked that Independence write a letter to
the Highway Department, District 6 to petition the street repairs and reduction
of the speed limit.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that he has spoken to Covington Mayor Callery
regarding this issue. He also thanked Senator Thayer for arranging for

builders to repair the road damages they created.

in the military. She stated that the names they were able to get were provided
by Nita Brake. Mayor Moriconi stated he appreciated all their work.

mailboxes in the Clover Ridge Subdivision. He stated everyone is working on

cluster mailboxes there.

prohibiting the cluster mailboxes and whether it would be the responsibility of
the Zoning Administrator, Police Department or the Code Enforcement Board. City

Ordinance No. 2005-O-18 - Map Amendment for 50-Acre Parcel South side of Cody
Road-KCPC Application No. 1728R – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would approve a map amendment changing an approximate 50-acre parcel
located along the south side of Cody Road between the CSX Railroad and Upton
Drive from R-1C to R-1C (PUD) with certain conditions.
Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Council Member Kelso moved to adopt
Ordinance No. 2005-O-08, seconded by Council Member Cobble. A brief discussion
ensued wherein language was added to condition number two and amended in
condition number four. Condition number two added language that would state the
developer would be responsible for resumption of the maintenance of the open
spaces if the HOA (homeowner’s association) or the Kenton Conservancy became
defunct. Condition number four changed the lot numbers from 88 and 89 to 94 and
95. This was to accommodate the revised development plan which was requested of
the developer by the city Council.
Council Member Cobble expressed concern regarding the safety of children, as
this development is very near the railroad tracks. Mr. Bertram advised they
would provide a type of landscape barricade, with a mound and trees. Council
Member Cobble urged him to install a fence in that area to provide another
safety measure for the children in the area. He stated he would look at doing a
fence. She stated she would beg him to install a fence to deter the children
from playing near the tracks.
Mr. Deters advised a motion was needed to amend the original motion to include
the two minor changes of the proposed ordinance. Council Member Kelso so moved,
with second by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
Mayor Moriconi directed the Clerk to call roll on the original motion by
Council Member Kelso and second by Council Member Cobble to adopt Ordinance No.
2005-O-08. Roll was called and answered with four ayes and two no votes cast by
Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion carried 4-2 to adopt Ordinance No.
2005-O-08.

Ordinance No. 2005-O-10 - Amending Ordinance No. 1997-O-06 Relating to Mud and
Debris on Streets – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
amending Ordinance No. 1997-O-06 relating to mud and debris deposited on city
streets and right of ways and providing for penalties. Mr. Deters read the
proposed ordinance.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2005-O-10, seconded by
Council Member Kelso. A brief discussion ensued regarding which city employees
would be responsible to enforce this ordinance and the fine being increased
from $250 to $500. Mr. Deters advised this ordinance is currently being
enforced by city personnel and is being amended to include additional language
to assist them doing so more efficiently and effectively. He also assured
Council that city personnel currently issue warnings before a citation is
actually issued. Some council members expressed concern in raising the fine to
$500 and that enforcement would not be arbitrary.
Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no vote cast by Council
Member Cobble, stating that she has concerns regarding enforcement and feels it
should be under zoning. Motion carried 5-1.

Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would amend Ordinance No. 1999-O-02 relating to the Code Enforcement

NEW BUSINESS
Crowe Road Repairs
Mayor Moriconi advised council that due to the rapidly deteriorating condition
of Crowe Road, he would forego the bid process for the needed repair work and
stabilization. He stated that KRS 424.260 allows him to certify that an
emergency exists and that the regular procedure of seeking bids for materials,
supplies, equipment and services will not be followed. He stated he would file
a signed Certificate of Emergency (a copy is attached) document with the city’s
Finance Director as required by KRS 424.260.
Council Member Yeager moved to support the Mayor’s declaration of an emergency
to forego the bid process to make the necessary repairs and stabilization of
Crowe Road. Council Member Franzen seconded the motion. At council’s request,
Mr. Deters composed an impromptu resolution (a formal Resolution does not
exist). No roll call vote; motion carried with all ayes.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler advised the Crowe Road repairs would begin sometime during the
next 30-60 days.

May 16, 2005
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 16,
2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso,
Mike Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the May 2, 2005 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the May 2, 2005
council meeting. Council Member Yeager so moved with a second from Council
Member Franzen. Amendments were noted; roll was called and answered 6-0. Motion
carried
Privileges of the Floor
No one signed in to address the Council.
Discussion of a Lease Proposal by Cingular Wireless
Mayor Moriconi presented for discussion a lease agreement proposal by Cingular
Wireless for a tract of land located in the Sterling Staggs Park (5103 Madison
Pike). He stated that Cingular would like to lease a 100 foot by 100 foot area
in the park for a cellular tower. Mr. Deters advised that it would be more
appropriate to discuss the proposed contract in executive session. He advised
that council should only discuss the proposed location in open session. Some
council members expressed opposition to leasing this area and voiced concern
regarding the proposed location of the tower citing that the park was too small
and that the playground equipment would have to be moved. They also had
concerns regarding fencing and/or landscape buffers. Other council members
spoke in favor of leasing the space but had concerns with the terms of the
proposed lease, including the financial package. It was decided to discuss the
terms of the proposal in more detail in executive session.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2004/05 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend the 2004/05 budget. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion and/or questions from council.
Chief Butler stated that the major amendments included the addition of the MDT
(mobile data terminals) revenue that was previously omitted. He stated this is
just a pass through revenue/expense. He stated the amended budget also
reflected the additional principal payment on the Senior Center bond based on
the proceeds of the sale of the Park and Ride municipal parking lot.
Council Member Cobble voiced concern regarding the sewer tap in fees. She noted
the amended budget shows the tap in fees being moved from the general sewer
fund into the Fowler Creek fund as suggested by Rankin & Rankin (the city’s
auditing firm). She stated that according to the lease-merger agreement with
SD1 and in keeping with KRS 220.135 (5d) the tap in fees collected should have
been applied to the GRW debt. She stated she wanted it noted that she feels
this amendment is erroneous but it can be corrected at a later date after the
council meets to discuss this issue.
Council Member Franzen asked why funds were being transferred from the general
fund to balance the Senior Center budget. Chief Butler commented that this is
done each year to cover the debt retirement and operational expenses of the
Senior Center. She asked what the balance was of the Senior Center bond. The
City Clerk advised the principal balance would be approximately $240,000 after
the extra principal payment of $59,600 that will be paid in June.
Mayor Moriconi advised the amended budget ordinance would be presented for a
second reading at the June 6, 2005 meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a 2005/06 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented the proposed budget for the 2005/06 fiscal year along
with his budget message. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi
stated that his budget message highlighted the major changes from last years
budget and commented that property tax revenue has surpassed the occupational/
payroll license tax revenue, now making it the city’s largest revenue source.
He advised council that he would submit the proposed budget for a second
reading at the June 20th regular meeting and encouraged council to use next
thirty days to meet with him, Chief Butler or the City Clerk to address any
specific questions or concerns regarding this budget.
Proposed Ordinance – Creating the Position of Public Services Director – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed ordinance creating the position of a Public
Service Director. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi
advised creating this position is a result of one of the recommendations to the
city from the Citizens Budget & Economic Development Committee. He stated the
creation of a Director position for public services would encompass public
works and building and zoning services. There was a brief discussion regarding
the need for this position versus a city administrator.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler stated he had nothing to report.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi announced that he has a meeting scheduled with the director of
the State Highway Department District 6 regarding the Cox Road turn lane
improvements. He stated that hopefully he will be able to provide an update in
a couple of weeks.
Mayor Moriconi announced that the Memorial Day Parade is Monday, May 30th at
10:30. He stated the parade would begin at the Firehouse on Delaware Crossing
and Madison Pike and end at the Kenton County Courthouse. He encouraged
everyone to attend.
Executive Session
Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to go into executive session pursuant to
KRS 61.810 (b), to deliberate possible property acquisition and (c) possible
litigation. Council Member Cobble so moved, with a second by Council Member
Franzen. Motion passed 6-0.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to return to the regular council meeting,
with a second by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
Council Member Kelso made a motion to adjourn the meeting, with a second by
Council Member Franzen. Motion carried and the meeting adjourned at 8:13 p.m.

Deters was also absent; his associate Jeremy Deters of Deters, Benzinger &

No one signed in to address the Council.
Ordinance No. 2005-O-14 – Amending the 2004/05 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for a second reading an ordinance that
would amend Ordinance 2004-O-24 and the annual budget for the 2004/05 fiscal
year. Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to read Ordinance No. 2005-O-14. After
Mr. Deters gave the second reading of the ordinance, Council Member Yeager
moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2005-O-14, seconded by Council Member Franzen.
There being no discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0.
Resolution No. 2004-R-14 – Authorizing the Mayor to enter into an Agreement
with The Transportation Cabinet for Reimbursable funding up to $40,000 for the
Installation of a turn lane on Cox Road
Mayor Moriconi advised council that the Kentucky Transportation Cabinet has
agreed to provide funding, up to $40,000 for the installation of a turn lane on
Cox Road at the intersection with SR 16. He stated that the developer of the
Pembroke Subdivision off Cox Road will provide an additional $30,000 for a
section of the turn lane that provides egress into the subdivision. He also
stated that the city will incur the cost of the city engineer’s fees to design
the turn lane. Mayor Moriconi stated members of the council pointed out the
proposed agreement contained language stating the city would be responsible to
maintain this state road upon completion of the project. He stated he has
requested a corrected agreement deleting that condition. He stated he would
like to move forward with the adoption of this Resolution. He assured council
that he would not be signing the agreement until he receives the corrected
copy.
Council Member Kelso moved to approve Resolution No. 2004-R-14, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. A brief discussion ensued wherein Council Member Cobble
stated she opposed the city providing partial funding for this project since
Cox Road is a state maintained road. Mayor Moriconi advised that the city
approached the state to assist with this project and the state did not entirely
agree that this turn lane was necessary, but due to a rare collaborative
agreement between the developer, city and state this project can be realized,
providing a safer intersection for the residents. Council Member Yeager agreed
this project would not be realized without some city support. Council Member
Franzen stated she feels since Cox Road runs solely within the city limits that
the city needs to cooperate with the state. Council Member Cook commented that
she thought the turn lane was supposed to be the responsibility of the
developer. Mayor Moriconi advised that the developer was only responsible to
install a turn lane into the Pembroke Subdivision and that extending the turn
lane up to the intersection with SR 16 was proposed to the state by the city.
Council Member Kelso commented that sometimes give-and-take is necessary to
accomplish the needs for the residents, but that the city should clarify its
position to the state. Resident, Ken Lancaster commented that the left turn
lane is needed and while he does not like that the city has to partially fund
this project he feels it is needed.
Council Member Kelso moved to amend his motion to include the language
amendment of the first sentence in paragraph two on page two of the agreement.
Council Member Franzen seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
In closing the discussion on this subject, roll was called on the original
motion made by Council Member Kelso and second by Council Member Franzen to
approve Resolution No. 2005-R-14. Roll was answered with four ayes and one no
vote cast by Council Member Cobble. Motion carried 4-1.

the list of Permitted Uses within the NC Zone – KCPC Application Number4 1735R

Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2005-O-17, seconded by
Council Member Kelso. There being no discussion, roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2005-O-18 – Adopting a Budget for the 2005/06 Fiscal Year – 2nd
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading an ordinance that
would adopt a city budget for the 2005/06 fiscal year. He commented that the
budget he is presenting is a balanced budget despite dealing with a 15%
increase in employee health care costs as well as retirement increases. He
stated this budget grows the reserve fund, expands the public works department
and invests almost a half million dollars in street and sidewalk improvements.
Mayor Moriconi thanked the council members that met with him to ask questions
and/or discuss their concerns.
Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2005-O-18. Council Member Yeager moved to adopt
Ordinance No. 2005-O-18, seconded by Council Member Franzen. A discussion
ensued. Council Member Cobble commented that she believes the $27,000 surplus
is artificial. She also stated she could not justify adopting a budget that
assumed the enactment of a 2005 property tax compensating rate plus four
percent that would support a budgeted 5% salary increase for employees. Council
Member Cook concurred. She stated that the resident’s property values were re-
assessed this year and she could not see adopting a compensating tax rate plus
four percent then give it away by providing five percent salary increases to
the city employees. Council Member Franzen commented she felt the proposed
budget was great. She stated she felt that five percent raises were typical and
it compensates the employees for a job well done. Mayor Moriconi commented that
he feels the employees deserve the proposed raises, especially considering that
for the first time ever they are paying a portion of their health insurance
premium this year. Council Member Little stated that a city budget differs from
a personal budget, taking into consideration that the city is trying to provide
as many services as possible with the current sources of revenue. He stated he
believes it is crucial to grow the Public Works Department.
Mayor Moriconi stated that the state statute allows the city to adopt a
compensating tax rate plus four percent in order to keep up with inflation. He
stated employee raises are part of the city’s inflation costs. He stated that
he feels this keeps city salaries competitive and reduces turn over in staff.
Council Member Yeager agreed and added that the citizens want more services and
the city needs to take the additional four percent over the compensating rate.
Council Member Cobble commented that she did not say the employees are not
doing a good job, only that she would want to give cost of living (COLA)
increases. She stated she did not feel the city employees should receive more
than the members of the United States military. Council Member Yeager commented
that federal government employees also get step raises and awards and often
receive other types of compensation. Council Member Kelso commented that he is
not comfortable using federal guidelines.
Council Member Kelso commented he is not prepared at this time to discuss the
2005 tax rate, since the tax rate would not be proposed until August, and this
proposed budget does not affirm the compensating rate plus four percent.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi asked the Clerk to call the
roll. Roll call was answered with four yes votes and two no votes cast by
Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion carried 4-2.
Ordinance No. 2005-O-19 – Amending Ordinance No. 1999-O-02 Relating to the Code
Enforcement Board – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2005-O-
19, which has been tabled since April, since some of the council members wanted
to review with Mr. Deters regarding some of the changes. He stated the Zoning
Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld is present to address any questions from
Council. Mr. Deters stated that he changed the ordinance to include the
appropriate “amending” language but it did not make it in the packets. He
stated the final, signed version would. Mayor Moriconi advised before Council
begins discussion on this issue, he would like to yield the floor to Mrs.
Ronnie Riley, who had signed in under Privileges of the Floor to address
Council.
Ronnie M. Riley, 4284 Richardson Road provided a narrative of the on-going
zoning violations of the property next door (4290 Richardson Road) to her and
the trials and tribulations she has encountered with efforts to get the
property owner to comply to the city’s zoning regulations. She stated the
troubles with this property began in 1998 when this property built a batting
cage which was not approved for this development (storage units facility). She
stated the batting cage finally came down in 2003. She stated the property
owner continues to violate zoning code and has said he can do what he wants and
nothing will be done. She stated she has seen first hand how difficult it has
been for the Zoning Administrator, Police and Building Inspector to enforce the
Code. She stated she would like to encourage Council to adopt the proposed
ordinance, which she believes will give the city employees the tools they need
to enforce the regulations.
Mayor Moriconi advised that the most significant change to this ordinance would
be the increase in fines to the violators. He said currently the violator will
just pay a small fine and not rectify the violation. He stated when the
proposed amendments to the 1999 ordinance was first presented to Council in
April, it was agreed that the council members would meet with Mr. Deters to
iron out their concerns. He stated some of Council discussed these concerns.
Mr. Deters stated he discussed three concerns with Council Member Yeager and
she was okay with the legalities.
Mr. Deters stated Council Member Cobble wrote a three-page memo that was
distributed to everyone and he addressed those concerns. Council Member Cobble
stated she never received an answer to her memo. Mr. Deters commented that most
of the comments in her memo, which raised several legal issues, did not warrant
a response. Council Member Cobble expressed concerns that this ordinance
violates state statutes. Mr. Deters and Council Member Cobble engaged in a
debate regarding KRS and whether or not this ordinance violates state laws.
Mayor Moriconi interrupted the debate and asked Mr. Deters to read the proposed
ordinance. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2005-O-19. He advised Council that
this proposed ordinance amends the fines, addresses requirements for posting,
findings by the Board, if there is a violation; it includes a $50 appeal fee,
and makes it easier for the code enforcement officers to issue a second
violation for continued violations.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve Ordinance No. 2005-O-19, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for any further
discussion before the vote. Council Member Cobble stated she would like her
memo she sent to everyone regarding this issue to be attached to the minutes of
this meeting as part of the official record. She continued the debate with Mr.
Deters regarding the legalities of the amendments proposed in this ordinance.
Mrs. Wuestefeld commented that she went to a code enforcement seminar wherein
she learned it is legal to post a citation on the property as long as it is in
a visible location. A brief discussion ensued regarding this. Council Member
Franzen and Yeager requested that a written notice be sent by mail in addition
to posting a notice on the property.
Council Member Kelso suggested that language amendments by the Council be posed
in the form of a motion in lieu of circular discussions. Council Member Yeager
moved to amend the language to add “regular mail”, seconded by Council Member
Kelso. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Cobble stated this is
violating state statute which will make this ordinance null and void. She
stated she is aware problems exit with zoning code enforcement but she feels
this ordinance will not do it, because she believes it violates state law. Mrs.
Wuestefeld stated she consulted an attorney with the Kentucky League of Cities
who advised that posting the notice on the property and taking a photo of it is
as good as sending the notice by certified mail. She went on to say that the
KLC attorney said it provides immediate notice by posting it on the property.
Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Deters if he feels this ordinance is in
violation of state law. Mr. Deters replied that he does not feel these
amendments violate state law and for clarification purposes explained that
there is a difference between initiating due process and completing the due
process. He went on to say that when citations are issued we comply with
statute by doing all, and the section Council Member Cobble is referring to is
with respect to posting the final orders which does not violate the statute. He
stated there are two separate statutes and he is perfectly comfortable with the
language of this ordinance. Council Member Yeager suggested taking a vote and
if we find it is wrong then we will amend. Mayor Moriconi directed the Clerk to
call the roll on Council Member Yeager’s motion to amend the language to add
“regular mail”. Roll was called and answered with four ayes and two no votes
cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion carried 4-2.
Mayor Moriconi resumed the discussion on the main motion on the floor to adopt
the ordinance. A brief debate ensued between Council Member Cobble and Mr.
Deters regarding her memo. Mayor Moriconi closed the floor to further
discussion and directed the Clerk to call the roll. Roll was called and
answered with four ayes and two no votes cast by Council Members Cobble and
Cook. Council Member Cobble explained her vote by stating she would not violate
the oath she took to uphold the laws of this state and this country. Motion
carried 4-2.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler announced the Independence July 4th Celebration to be held on
Friday and Saturday, July 1 and 2. He advised shuttle busses would be
transporting people from overflow parking at the Summit View Schools and he
encouraged everyone to use this service to avoid parking hassles and traffic.
Also on June 29 he would be participating in the MDA (Muscular Dystrophy Assn)
Lock-Up and would appreciate any donations to ‘raise bail’ to get him out of
jail.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he had nothing to report. He requested an executive session.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi

recognized for the Month for July. Council Member Yeager stated she would
decide then let the City Clerk know for the July 11th meeting
Mayor Moriconi encouraged everyone to attend the July 4th Celebration. He
stated the parade will begin at 3:30 on Saturday and fireworks scheduled for
10:00 pm.
Executive Session
Council Member Kelso made a motion to enter into executive session in
accordance with KRS 61.810 (c) for the purpose of discussion pending litigation
and KRS 61.810 (b) to discuss possible property acquisition, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of the meeting,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Results of the Executive Session

piece of real estate. He stated that Council has also authorized him to
initiate a lawsuit regarding property rights as soon as possible.

Cingular attend one of the July Council meetings to answer questions regarding
the proposed cell tower in Staggs Park.

Staggs Park Cell Tower Proposal – Tim Sturm of Burgess & Niple Engineers
Mayor Moriconi introduced Tim Sturm with Burgess & Niple Engineers, who was
representing Cingular Wireless in their proposal to lease space from the city
in Sterling Staggs Park for a cell tower disguised as a flagpole. Mayor
Moriconi commented that Mr. Sturm inspected the park area prior to the meeting
and advised that a third location has been looked at that might be more
suitable than the first two proposed areas. He stated the site was on the north
side (Sylvan Drive) of the park near the basketball fields.
Mr. Sturm advised that Cingular uses his firm to locate possible sites for
their cell towers. He stated they now must determine a site before proceeding
with terms of a lease agreement. He stated that he feels the site area near the
basketball fields can be reduced from the proposed 100x100 feet to 50x50 feet
as they just need an area large enough to install the tower and a 10’ x 20’
equipment building. He stated they usually prefer a larger space, and then it
would not be necessary to negotiate for additional space in the future, but if
other carriers wanted additional space they could negotiate for it. Mr. Sturm
advised the basketball courts and ball field would not be disturbed. He also
commented that they could forego the installation of a fence around the area.
Council asked if some of the parking spaces along the Sylvan Drive side of the
park would be taken. Mr. Sturm stated the city could not loose any of the
parking slots, but that Cingular would probably desire a reserved spot ‘of
record’ for access to the equipment building.
Some issues were raised regarding the proposed lease agreement. Mr. Deters
advised council that the details of the lease agreement could be resolved later
and it may be necessary to sort out the terms in an executive session.
Council Member Cobble asked Mr. Sturm to address the safety issue of cell
towers. Mr. Sturm advised that cell towers are regulated by the FCC (Federal
Communications Commission) and that Cingular follows these regulations
regarding the amount of emissions they transmit. He stated there have been
numerous reports and studies regarding the safety of the towers which can be
found on the internet. He stated they are installed in football fields and atop
hospitals.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that a site would need to be agreed upon at this
meeting. Mr. Deters stated that Cingular would need to perform tests on the
site area and if they tests failed the site would be abandoned.
After some discussion, Council Member Yeager moved to tentatively approve the
site location near the basketball courts on the north side of Sterling Staggs
Park for the cell tower lease area pending all the other conditions. Council
Member Franzen seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered with all ayes.
Motion carried 5-0.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Strum for attending the meeting. Council Member
Cobble thanked Mr. Sturm for negotiating with the city regarding the fence and
size of the lease area.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 18,
2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Mayor Moriconi called for a moment of silence for Army
Spc. Ronnie D. Williams who died on July 17th while on active duty in Iraq.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: JoAnne
Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso, Mike Little and Donna Yeager.
Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the July 11, 2005 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the July 11, 2005
council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second from Council
Member Little. Council Member Cobble stated that she was correct in stating at
the July 11th meeting that her memo of May 12, 2005 could be entered into the
record as part of the July 11th meeting minutes without actually being read
into the record. She read Section 4.19 of the Rules of Order ordinance which
she stated supported her position and advised her memo should be attached to
the June 20th meeting minutes. Mayor Moriconi asked for Council comments
regarding Council Member Cobble’s statement. There being no expressed comments,

answered with four ayes and two nays cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook.

Proposed Ordinance – Zoning Text Amendment Proposal to increase the Minimum
Planting Strip for Developments within the NSC Zone – KCPC Application No.
1739R
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to the citizens signed in to address Council
regarding this issue.
Diana Walker, 6446 Shawnee Court, Independence addressed council, speaking on
behalf of the Cherokee Acres Neighborhood Residents and in support of a
proposed zoning text amendment that would increase the minimum planting strip
for developments within the NSC zone. She submitted a petition signed by
residents supporting the approval of the text amendment and urged Council to
approve this proposed text amendment.
Ken Lancaster, 733 Cox Road, also addressed council regarding the proposed text
amendment and urged Council to approve this. He read a prepared statement
wherein he outlined the reasons that KCPC has recommended the city disapprove
this and the reasons he feels the Council should approve it.
Marty Neltner, 6239 Taylor Mill Road, Independence addressed Council voicing
his opposition regarding the proposed text amendment. He stated that while he
understands the residents concerns with regard to development possibilities of
his property (731 Cox Road) behind the Cherokee shopping center, he feels that
it has become personal and prejudicial. He stated he has the right to develop
that property and in the past has tried to consult with the surrounding
residents to foster a conciliatory resolution regarding the commercial develop
of this property. He stated he is still willing to work with the residents, and
with the guidance of the Planning Commission develop this land in an
appropriate way that would be considerate of the adjoining property owners. He
stated that he was not opposed to the idea of a 50 foot buffer, if it was
feasible, as he currently did not have a development plan.
Lola Belville, 741 Cox Road, commented that she did not want to see a parking
lot adjoining her property.
A lengthy discussion ensued between Council, Mr. Neltner and Mr. Lancaster,
which concluded with Mr. Neltner agreeing to work with the residents to
consider a development plan that would be acceptable to the property owners
adjacent to Mr. Neltner’s property located behind the Cherokee shopping center,
known as ’’’’731 Cox Road’’. Some council members expressed a willingness to
act as an intermediary with the residents and Mr. Neltner in an effort to
resolve this issue. Mr. Deters advised the Council that doing so could present
some conflict issues later.
In closing the discussion on this issue, Council decided to table, for an
indefinite period of time, any action on the recommendation of the KCPC for the
proposed text amendment, therefore a first reading of the proposed ordinance
did not take place.
Request by Helen & Jim Kudera for the City to Sponsor a Text Amendment
Mayor Moriconi advised council that the city has received a request that the
city request assistance from the NKAPC staff in drafting a text that would
create a new zone for a retirement village
Mayor Moriconi said the possible development of a retirement home was brought
before the Council last year and a zone change and development plan submitted
to the Planning Commission (KCPC), but they did not recommend approval of this
type use in the R-2 zone and the city does not have an appropriate zone that
would regulate retirement home uses.
Jay Bayer, Engineer/Surveyor with Bayer-Becker reiterated they went through the
application process last year and the city agreed to annex part of the
development property. He stated they requested the R-2 zone as it was the best
zone they could use, which would solve their needs, but would leave the
neighborhood up for some exposure to other developments that were permitted in
that zone. He stated that the KCPC denied their zone change request. Therefore
they are requesting the city ask the NKAPC staff for assistance in drafting
proposed new text for the official zoning ordinance to create a new zone that
would best suit retirement housing along with the appropriate language that
would regulate circumstances, conditions and regulations.
Mr. Jim Kudera advised the development he is proposing would be unique in
Northern Kentucky as it would be an independent living retirement village that
would be individually owned but would have covenants and restrictions that
would include resident minimum age and transfer of ownership should a resident
require assisted living.
There was a brief discussion regarding the location of the planned development
(McMillan and the new SR 17)
Council Member Kelso moved to request assistance from the NKAPC staff in
creating a new zone and related language that would best suit retirement
housing for consideration by the city to possibly submit for a zoning text
amendment. Council Member Franzen seconded the motion. There was a brief
discussion wherein the Council Members expressed a desire to review the NKAPC
staff recommendations for the new zone and related language before they
actually approve submitting a text amendment application. Mr. Deters advised
that the NKAPC staff results would be presented to the Council for
consideration before proceeding with the process.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered with five ayes
and one no vote cast by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 5-1.
Proposed Ordinance – Prohibiting On-Street Parking on Don Victor Drive
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
make it unlawful to park any motor vehicle, trailer, truck, motorcycle, or the
like, at any time, on any portion of Don Victor Drive. He stated this ordinance
is being proposed at the request of Council Member Cook at the last meeting.
Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to the citizens in attendance that wished to
address Council regarding this issue.
Linda Boggs, 914 Don Victor Drive stated she opposed the proposal to prohibit
parking on her street. She expressed concerns that she would not have a place
to park their van which they use to transport her to her doctor appointments.
She suggested the city install speed humps as a speed deterrent.
Tonya Williams, 957 Don Victor Drive, submitted a petition signed by citizens
who opposed prohibiting on-street parking on Don Victor. She expressed concern
where the visitors of the residents would park as well as additional parking
spaces for the residents. She suggested if the city wants to fix the speeding
problem and address safety issues on the street that it should be dead-ended or
made into a one-way street. She stated that prohibiting on-street parking will
hurt many of the residents who have teenagers with vehicles that need to be
parked on the street. Ms. Williams requested that Council reconsider this
proposed ordinance.
Karen LeMaster, 940 Don Victor Drive, stated she has never lived anywhere that
did not allow on-street parking. She stated that the driveways on the street
only hold two vehicles
Mayor Moriconi suggested the city survey the residents on Don Victor Drive to
solicit input before proceeding with this ordinance. A brief discussion ensued.
It was noted that a developer will be constructing nineteen new homes on the
street which will affect the traffic. Also mentioned was this was one of the
county maintained streets that was turned over to the city and since the city
has initiated legal proceedings against Kenton County regarding this issue, it
was decided to table any action until the lawsuit is settled.

as well as the city employees who worked extra hours.
Chief Butler also announced that a benefit event would be held on July 24, 2005
to raise funds to purchase a defibulator for the Senior Center.

Mr. Deters stated he had nothing to report.
Miscellaneous
Council Member Yeager commented that all the correspondence the city receives
from the NKAPC regarding the approval of preliminary plats specifies that the
approval includes “public improvements, such as streets, storm drains, sanitary
sewers and water systems” and she would like for them to add ‘sidewalks’ to
that. She feels that the term ‘public improvements’ may include sidewalks, but
she is not sure and would like NKAPC to add that language in the future so the
city is aware that it is included in the approval of the plat. Mayor Moriconi
directed the City Clerk to convey this request to the NKAPC.
Council Member Cobble made a motion to establish a three-member committee to
investigate why it took five years to resolve the zoning violation regarding
the batting cage at the Beechgrove Storage property located at 4290 Richardson
Road and to make a recommendation to ensure that doesn’t happen again. Council
Member Yeager seconded the motion. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Deters
advised that this committee would not be appointed by the Mayor, but that
Council would be acting independently in exercising their legislative
authority. Council Members Cobble, Yeager and Franzen volunteered to be on this
committee. Roll was called and answered with three yes votes and three no votes
cast by Council Members Kelso, Little and Cook. Mayor Moriconi broke the tie by
casting a no vote. Motion defeated 4-3.
Executive Session
Council Member Kelso moved to enter into an executive session in accordance
with KRS 61.810 (c) for the purpose of discussion pending litigation and KRS
61.810 (b) to discuss possible property acquisition, seconded by Council Member
Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Kelso moved to reconvene the regular session of the meeting,
seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.

Independence Fire District with a maximum purchase offer of $180,000. Council

next meeting. The motion died for lack of a second.
Council Member Cobble announced that she would leave the meeting and that the
record should reflect that the Council was now a quorum of five.
Mayor Moriconi directed the Clerk to call the roll. Roll was called and
answered with four ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Cook. Motion
carried 4-1.
Adjournment
Council Member Franzen made a motion to adjourn the meeting, with a second by
Council Member Little. Motion carried and the meeting adjourned at 10:05 p.m.

August 1, 2005
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 1,
2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The Reverend Eric Bryant of Grace Community Church gave
the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters. Council Member Little
was absent.
Approval of the July 11, 2005 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the July 18, 2005
council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second from Council
Member Kelso. One amendment was noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Discussion of City Tax Bill Collection by Kenton County Sheriff Department
Mayor Moriconi introduced Kenton County Sheriff Chuck Korzenborn who was
present with a proposal to bill and collect the city’s property taxes. Mayor
Moriconi presented this idea for discussion and suggested it may be more
convenient for the residents as they will have several locations available for
payment of the tax bill. He stated the deadline for electing the county to
provide this service expired in June; too late for the 2005 tax season, but it
could be effective for the 2006 tax year.
Sheriff Korzenborn distributed a handout of his proposal to the council. The
handout included a copy of KRS 91A.070, a cost comparison, a list of associated
expense savings and a list of advantages that might be realized by having the
Sheriff’s office collect the city taxes. He advised that other city charges
currently on the tax bill would have to be mailed separately as they could only
place ad Valorem taxes on the bill. He suggested the city have Rumpke bill the
residents directly. Mayor Moriconi advised that Rumpke would charge the
residents more to do that. During the discussion the Sheriff’s associate from
the county attorney’s office advised that while they could collect the
delinquent city taxes as part of this proposal, they could not, per KRS,
collect the delinquent trash and sewer assessment charges, but that they would
have the city sign off on any suit before it was dismissed. He stated that
would ensure all other fees charged by the city had been satisfied. Sheriff
Korzenborn advised that the residents would have 35+ locations, some with 7
days per week operating hours, to pay their bill.
When Council Member Cook asked the Sheriff’s fee to collect the city taxes, he
advised his office would take 4.25% of all city tax revenue collected. Mayor
Moriconi asked if a discount period would be offered. Sheriff Korzenborn
replied yes. They advised that tax collection periods would coincide with that
of the county and that the delinquent taxes would be handled the same as the
county taxes and would be sold April 1 of each year with an automatic lien
placed on the property.
Council Member Cook asked if the Sheriff’s office collected any other city
taxes. He replied no, but that he expected other cities would follow suit..
A brief discussion addressed the 4.25% collection rate that is set by KRS and
the comparison figures provided in the Sheriff’s proposal. The proposal used to
calculate collection cost savings was for the tax year of 2003. Council Member
Cobble stated she believed the figures were not accurate since the city had
tightened its tax collection policies. She asked how the tax collections would
be remitted to the city. The Sheriff’s associate advised that the county would
remit, on a monthly basis, to the city the taxes collected along with a detail
report.
Mayor Moriconi commented that since this proposal could not be implemented
until 2006 there was no urgency in acting on this proposal until next May with
a deadline of June 30, 2006. The Sheriff’s associate advised the city should
have the city’s finance director formulate more up to date revenue and expense
analysis to ensure this would be beneficial to everyone.
Proposal to Repeal the Vehicle Sticker Fee Ordinance
Council Member Yeager stated she would like to initiate proceedings to repeal
the Vehicle Sticker Fee effective December 31, 2005. City Attorney, Jed Deters
stated he would prepare an ordinance for the Council’s consideration at the
next meeting, August 15, 2005.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler, Police Chief
No Report.
City Attorney Report – Jed. K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he had nothing to report, but requested that Council hold an
Executive Session to discuss some litigation issues.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi stated he would like to compliment the residents of the
Glenhurst Subdivision for maintaining a well kept landscape in their community.
Mayor Moriconi also announced that the city would hold a “Clean-Up
Independence” day on September 17, 2005. He urged individuals and organizations
to sign up to volunteer for this event on the city website.
Mayor Moriconi announced the city would hold a Support our Troops Rally on
Sunday, September 11, 2005 at the Memorial Park Amphitheater from 4:00 – 6:00
pm. He stated following this event, there would be a performance by St.
Patrick’s Church “Joyful Noise” choir.
Executive Session
Council Member Cobble moved to enter into an executive session in accordance
with KRS 61.810 (c) for the purpose of discussing pending litigation, seconded
by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of the meeting,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
Council Member Franzen made a motion to adjourn the meeting, with a second by
Council Member Cobble. Motion carried and the meeting adjourned at 7:54 p.m.

Center Project. Mayor Moriconi explained to Council that the city has been

Mayor Moriconi presented to council Resolution No. 2005-R-18 that would adopt

18.
Council Member Cobble moved to adopt Resolution No. 2005-R-18, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Chief Butler explained that by adopting this system it

Resolution No. 2005-R-19 – Supporting a Text Amendment Application Relating to
Recreational Vehicles
Mayor Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2005-R-19 that would authorize the
application of a text amendment to the zoning ordinance seeking recommendations
on the updating of the requirements for recreational vehicle parking, including
boats, their sizes and weights and also the temporary storage facilities. He
advised that the current language in the zoning ordinance regarding
recreational vehicles is antiquated and does not even address heavy cars and
the use of temporary storage units. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2005-R-19.
Council Member Little moved to adopt Resolution No. 2005-R-19, seconded by
Council Member Kelso. There was a brief discussion wherein Mr. Deters advised
that since the NKAPC has access to broader standards that the city should ask
for their comments that would be more relevant to current standards regarding
trailers, recreational vehicles and temporary storage units. Zoning
Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld commented that the smallest trailer in today’s
market is twenty-eight feet. Council Member Little commented that he concurs
with the outdated language as a new full size pickup truck weights over 6,000
pounds and violates the current ordinance. Council briefly discussed the
definition of PODS, which are temporary storage units.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered with five yeahs
and one no vote cast by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 5-1
Resolution No. 2005-R-20 – Petitioning the State to Install a Traffic Light on
SR 17
Mayor Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2005-R-20 that would support the
installation of a traffic light on SR 17 at the intersection with Declaration
Drive and convey this desire and support to the state. Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2005-R-20.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2005-R-20, seconded by
Council Member Kelso. There was a brief discussion regarding the development
plans in this area, across from the Independence Towne Center. Council Member
Cobble asked developer, Jim Bertram, the time frame for this new development.
Mr. Bertram stated two years. He stated he has currently sold 102 units and has
only one commercial outlot remaining. He stated he plans to begin residential
construction in the spring. He stated the completion date for the connector
road is planned for June 2006 and hope to coincide that with the installation
of the traffic light at that intersection. When asked about the installation of
a deceleration lane, he stated it was a requirement of the development plan and
would be done in conjunction with the Independence Towne Center.
Mayor Moriconi commented that Walgreen’s is planning to construct a store at
this intersection and the installation of a traffic light is a condition of
that plan. Council Member Yeager asked how far this intersection would be from

is roughly 650 feet from the intersection of Harris Pike and SR 17 and meets
the state requirement. He presented a traffic study for Council’s review. Mayor
Moriconi commented that the addition of a Walgreen’s in the city would be an
economic boost for the city. There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2005-R-20. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.

Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2005 Real & Personal Property Tax Rates – 1st

Mayor Moriconi presented to council a proposed ordinance that would set the
real estate and personal property tax rates for the year 2005. He stated he is
proposing the city adopt the compensating rate which has calculated to be .177
per $100.00 of assessed value. He stated this rate is down from the 2004 rate

Terri Hudson, Finance Director for doing a great job. Mayor Moriconi advised
the proposed ordinance and adoption of the tax rates would be placed on the
agenda of the September 12, 2005 council meeting.

September 12, 2005
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
12, 2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Father Jeff Von Lehman from St. Patrick’s
Catholic Church gave the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent
Kelso, Mike Little and Donna Yeager. City Attorney, Jed K. Deters was also
present.
Approval of the August 15, 2005 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the August 15,
2005 council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second from
Council Member Yeager. Amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Maura Snyder, 5129 Dana Harvey, Independence, addressed council regarding an
incident that took place last month in the parking lot of the Municipal Center
after the city meeting. She alleged that a verbal exchange took place between
herself and Council Member Cook that ended with Council Member Cook making an
obscene gesture toward her in the presence of her eight-year old son. Ms.
Snyder demanded an apology from Council Member Cook. Council Member Cook
objected to Ms. Snyder’s public attack on her and stated she had no intention
of apologizing to anyone.
Ordinance No. 2005-O-21 – Repealing Ordinance No. 2003-O-21 Establishing a
Vehicle Sticker Fee – 2nd Reading
Mayor presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2005-O-21
repealing Ordinance No. 2003-O-21 which provided for the classifying and
licensing of motor vehicles. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2005-O-21, seconded by
Council Member Kelso. There was a brief exchange of comments by Council Members
Cobble and Yeager. Council Member Cobble stated she was glad the sticker fee
would be eliminated as she had opposed any new taxes two years ago, and instead
had proposed $192,000 in budget cuts. She asked Council Member Yeager if she
believed the city had sufficient revenue to operate without this revenue and
wanted assurance that a more heinous tax would not be proposed in the future to
replace this lost revenue. Council Member Yeager replied yes, that this was
discussed at prior meetings; and, how the city departments operated well within
their budgeted funds last year. Mayor Moriconi commented that the former
Finance Director had predicted a gloomy financial picture which, two years ago
prompted the Council to find alternate sources of revenue to balance the
budget.
There being no further discussion, the roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2005-O-22 – Adopting 2005 Real Estate & Personal Property Tax
Rates – 2nd Reading
Mayor presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2005-O-22
adopting the 2005 real estate and personal property tax rates. Mr. Deters read
the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2005-O-22, seconded by
Council Member Little. Council Member Cobble commented that most of the city’s
property values were reassessed this year and because of that most property
owners would not see a decrease in their property tax bill. She stated the city
could not take credit for lowering the tax rate (from .184/$100 in 2004 to
$.177/$100 in 2005) because the compensating rate is statutorily formulated
using the PVA assessed values. Council Member Kelso stated that the increased
assessed value of a property also increased the actual cash value of the
property for resale. Mayor Moriconi commented that he felt the city could take
credit for lowering the tax rate and attributed this to the city departments
that operated within their budgets. Council Member Little stated that not every
property in the city was reassessed this year, so some property owners will see
a decreased tax bill. He stated the city has been running efficiently and with
the influx of new properties, he sees this as a good sign the city is in better
financial shape than a couple of years ago. Council Member Yeager commented
that she feels the city can also be credited with lowering the tax rate,
because by law the city could have adopted the compensating tax rate plus 4%,
but instead opted to adopt the compensating rate only.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Ratify Stage II Development Plan – Meadow Glen Subdivision
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council correspondence from the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning Commission that recommended approval of the Stage II development
plan for an approximate 10.5 acre area located approximately 200 feet south of
the terminus of Meadow Glen Drive (Z-05-08-05/1764R) subject to the conditions
set forth. He stated this recommendation from the Planning Commission needed to
be ratified by the Council before it would be final.
Council Member Cobble moved to approved the Stage II development plan for this
10.5 acre area located at the terminus of Meadow Glen Drive as recommended on
page three of the NKAPC letter dated August 8, 2005 and in compliance with the
conditions set forth. Council Member Yeager seconded the motion. Roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2005-R-21 – Supporting Proposed KRS Amendments Regarding Storm
Water Management
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for their consideration, Resolution No.
2005-R-21 which would support proposed changes to KRS Chapter 220 to allow
Sanitation District No. 1 (SD1) to better serve the public by more clearly
integrating storm water management into KRS Chapter 220 and updating sections
that have become outdated as a result of changes within the industry and
clarifying ambiguities. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2005-R-21.
Council Member Little moved to adopt Resolution No. 2005-R-21, seconded by
Council Member Cobble. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Franzen asked
if this related in any way with the pending lawsuit against SD1. Mr. Deters
replied possibly and suggested attorney, Chris Mehling could discuss this with
the council in executive session later in this meeting. Council Member Kelso
expressed concerns about supporting this legislation. Mr. Deters suggested that
council table this agenda item until after the executive session.
Council Members Little and Cobble withdrew their motion and second to adopt
Resolution No. 2005-R-21 from the floor,
Council Member Kelso moved to table Resolution No. 2005-R-21, seconded by
Council Member Cobble. Roll call was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2005-R-22 – Supporting Opposition to Senate Bill 1504 relating
to the Broadband Investment & Consumer Choice Act
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration, Resolution No.
2005-R-22 that expresses opposition of Senate Bill 1504 known as the “Broadband
Investment and Consumer Choice Act”. This Bill introduced by U.S. Senators John
Ensign and John McCain would preempt all local authority over the provision of
cable and video services within the community, including the ability of the
local government to provide appropriate oversight to entities conducting
business within their jurisdiction and in the local public rights-of-way. Mr.
Deters read the proposed Resolution.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2005-R-22, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. A brief discussion ensued. Mayor Moriconi and Council
Member Cobble conveyed they had spoken to Tim Broering of the
Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky about this Bill. Council Member
Cobble stated that this proposed legislation would basically eliminate the
“home-rule” and local control of cable services. She stated that Mr. Broering
has advised he will attempt to get the city more information. Council Member
Kelso stated he would not vote to adopt Resolution No. 2005-R-22 as he would
like information on the other side of this issue. Council Member Cobble stated
she would like the pros and cons of any issue to make a vote. He stated the
Resolution makes a strong argument opposing the Bill but he would like to see
the defense for the Bill.
Council Member Kelso moved to table this issue until such time council has the
information for both sides of the argument, seconded by Council Member Cobble.
Roll call vote was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Mayor Moriconi advised council that Tim Broering of the Telecommunications
Board has stated he would be glad to attend a council meeting to discuss this
issue.
Police Chief Report – Dave Nichols, Assistant Police Chief
Assistant Chief Dave Nichols gave a report on his trip to Prague,
Czechoslovakia where he attended the International Police Executive Symposium,
along with Tom Brinker, President of the Independence Citizens Police Academy
Alumni. He stated while there, they presented a report on the Independence
community programs, such as the Citizens Police Academy and Volunteers in
Policing (VIPS). He stated this program’s funding was supported 100% by Eastern
Kentucky University’’ with the Citizens Police Alumni Association funding
additional expenses. He stated this was a positive experience for the city and
a rewarding one for him and Mr. Brinker.
City Attorney Report – Jed. K. Deters
Mr. Deters advised council that citizen questions has arisen involving the
relocation and rededication of a dedicated right of way on Far Hills Drive and
he would like council‘s authorization to refer this on to the city engineer for
review and comment. He stated the dedicated right of way runs through two lots,
but a street was never built and the proposal would be to cut it off at the end
of one of the lots not improved on and redirecting it in another direction. Mr.
Deters stated he is not sure if this proposal would be beneficial to the city
to have that right of way continuing on as it currently does. Mayor Moriconi
asked if council would have to approve a change. Mr. Deters replied yes, as it
will involve a street closing and a rededication of a new right of way if done
as proposed. Council Member Yeager commented there are a lot of changes going
on in that area. Again Mr. Deters advised he did not want to send the engineer
to review this proposal, thereby incurring expenses without council’s knowledge
and approval. No one voiced objection to this proposal.
Mr. Deters distributed the (NKAPC) Planning Commission’s initial draft of a
retirement community development regulations per the resolution the city
submitted asking them to propose some language for this new zone as a text
amendment to the current city zoning ordinance. Mr. Deters asked everyone to
review the document and submit any comments/suggestions so that he can get back
with the planning commission. He stated there is no deadline, but the Planning
Commission is waiting for the city’s comment. Mayor Moriconi asked council to
submit their comments to Mr. Deters within ten-fourteen days. Council Member
Kelso asked if this proposed text amendment had been sent to Mr. Jim Kudera,
the developer of the proposed retirement community. Mr. Deters stated he asked
the Planning Commission representative if it had been sent to Mr. Kudera and
they replied that it had not, as they felt it would be more appropriate if the
draft would be presented to the city for first review. Council Member Kelso
asked that Mr. Kudera be given a copy to review. Mr. Deters stated he would get
a copy to Mr. Kudera.
Mr. Deters also submitted a couple of court pleadings, one filed by Kenton
County and the other filed by the city in the lawsuit involving the maintenance
of the county roads that run within the city limits.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
