The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
19, 2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent
Kelso, Mike Little and Donna Yeager. City Attorney, Jed K. Deters was also
present.
Approval of the September 12, 2005 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September 12,
2005 council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second from
Council Member Kelso. Amendments were noted; roll was called and answered with
five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried 5-1.
Council Member Cook stated that the statements made by Mrs. Maura Snyder at the
September 12, 2005 council meeting were inaccurate in all aspects. She went on
to say that Mayor Moriconi should have enforced several sections of Robert’s
Rules of Order, specifically Sections 5.1(c) (e) and 5.4. Council Member Cook
also asserted that a Council Member made inflammatory remarks that were also in
violation of Robert’s Rules of Order. She stated the Council spent a lot of
time reviewing these Rules of Order before adopting them and they need to be
adhered to or thrown out the door. Mayor Moriconi responded that Robert’s Rules
of Order, as he understands it, is applied to personal attacks and he did not
hear any personal attacks. He stated Mrs. Snyder asked for an apology three
times and he did not interpret that as an attack, just a request for an
apology. Council Member Cook stated he should read the Robert’s Rules of Order.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the Rules would not permit a person to ask for an
apology. Council Member Cook maintained Mrs. Snyder’s request for an apology
was a personal attack which had absolutely nothing to do with the business of
the Council at that meeting.
Privileges of the Floor
No one signed in to address Council.
Request for City to Sponsor a Zoning Text Amendment Application Relating to
Fences
Mr. Craig Hadley, 5720 Cody Road, addressed Council with a request for the city
to sponsor a zoning text amendment application relating to fence regulations.
He stated that the language in the current zoning ordinance does not permit
fences to be erected in a front yard. He stated that his property is located at
the corner of Cody Road and Independence Station Road and that he has lived
there for five years. He stated he recently acquired a section of land from
Kenton County along Cody Road. Mr. Hadley stated he has a lake in his front
yard and for safety reasons would like to install a fence along the Cody Road
side of his property. He said he has to carry extra liability insurance as the
lake attracts kids that want to fish in the lake. Mr. Hadley distributed photos
of his property. He stated he worked with the staff at the NKAPC (Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission) to draft zoning text that would allow a
class 4 fence to be installed, for security purposes, on property that has a
minimum one acre body of water.
There was a brief exchange of comments. Mr. Deters stated he could draft a
resolution to present to Council at the October 3rd meeting that would support
this zoning text amendment application to the Kenton County Planning Commission
so they can officially comment on this request.
Council Member Cobble moved to support the text amendment application, seconded
by Council Member Kelso. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no
vote cast by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 5-1.
Request for City to Sponsor a Map Amendment Application by Bill Toebben for
Property Located at 5490 Madison Pike
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Bill Toebben who was present to request the city
act as applicant for a map amendment for twenty-five acres located at the
northwest, northeast and southwest corners of SR 17 and Harris Pike. Mr.
Toebben stated the northeast corner is currently zoned for multi-family
residential and the northwest corner is zoned residential. He stated the
southwest corner is part commercial, part residential. Mr. Toebben stated only
about 20 acres will be usable as the rest will be state highway right-of-way,
detention areas, etc. He stated if he was the applicant, the Planning
Commission would require a Stage I development plan be submitted with the
application. He stated the city, as the applicant, is not required to submit a
development plan. Mr. Toebben stated he is making this request as he needs a
zone in place in order to attract potential users to this property. Otherwise
he would have to make a best guess for potentials users. He stated once the
commercial zone is in place on all three corners, when a development plan is
decided on, it would be submitted directly to the city for approval.
A discussion ensued. Council Member Cobble commented that she agreed that the
entire site should be zoned commercial, but questioned if the city had been the
applicant in the past, as the city attorney usually advises Council not to
comment on a map amendment prior to a recommendation from the NKAPC lest the
process be contaminated. Mr. Deters stated the city could make the application
but generally the property owner applies for the map amendment as it could
later pose a problem for the city if they support/sponsor the application.
Council Member Kelso stated that a clear message from the city’s Vision
Committee is the need for a master plan with regard to zoning. He stated he
feels the city should be proactive in planning for economic development.
Council Member Yeager stated she has no problem rezoning the site to
commercial, but feels apprehensive at the City being the applicant for this map
amendment. Council Member Little stated he agreed the city had a definite need
for more commercial retail space and understands the marketability of it to
potential developers.
Mr. Deters questioned the lose of control by the city on the development of
this property without a development plan being submitted with the map amendment
application. Mr. Toebben stated he feels the city would still have control as
the site plan would be submitted directly to the city for approval instead of
going through the Planning Commission. Mr. Deters advised that once the zone
change is effected, the city would lose controls that might otherwise be
available to them.
Council Member Franzen asked if the city could predispose the process by
applying for the map amendment. Mr. Deters stated he thinks so, especially if
the city does not approve the zone change recommendation by the Kenton County
Planning Commission.
Council Member Kelso made a motion to support Mr. Toebben’s request for the
city to be the applicant for the map amendment, seconded by Council Member
Cobble. Council Member Yeager commented that the city would be opening the door
by doing this. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Council Member Cobble asked if Mr. Toebben would be responsible for all fees
related to the application. Mayor Moriconi replied yes.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler reported that the Crowe Road slippage has been shored up and that
the piering is complete.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters reported that to date he has not received any feedback from anyone
regarding the proposed zoning text amendment relating to the addition of a
retirement community zone. Council Member Cobble asked if this text would add a
new zone. Mr. Deters stated yes along with the regulations to accompany the new
zone. Council Member Yeager stated she needs some additional time to review the
proposed language.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi

event. Mayor Moriconi advised he would like to make this a bi-annual event each
spring and fall.
Comments on 2005 Property Tax Rates
Mayor Moriconi stated that he would like to respond to the discussion that took
place at the last council meeting regarding the 2005 property tax rates. He
stated that he feels that Council Member Cobble’s statement that he and Council
had nothing to do with lowering the tax rate is inaccurate. Mayor Moriconi
commented this is not about who gets credit for lowering the tax rate but
asserted that much effort has been put forth which has contributed to being in
a position to adopt a lower tax rate for 2005. He stated he has merged city
positions in the last few years which has saved the city money. He also thanked
the city staff for continuing to find ways to save money and the city’ s
Finance Director for effective management of the city funds.
Council Member Cobble countered that since the compensating rate is statutorily
formulated using the state office property assessment values the rate would
have been .177 regardless of the city’s cost saving efforts. She stated she
commends everyone for the role they played in recent cost saving measures, but
reiterated it had no effect on the calculation of the tax rates. Council Member
Franzen stated she disagreed with Council Member Cobble, also asserting that
the Council had everything to do with not adopting a compensating rate plus the
additional 4% which is allowable by law. She stated the city adopting just the
compensating rate and not the additional 4% was a win-win for the residents.
Support the Troops Rally
Mayor Moriconi advised the TBNK filmed the Support the Troops Rally that was
held at the Memorial Park Amphitheater on September 11 and it will be televised
on cable several times over the coming weeks.
Miscellaneous

committee will meet with the Citizens Police Academy Alumni Association
tomorrow. He advised the open meeting with all interested residents will be
held on November 7, 2005 at 5:30 p.m., probably at the Senior Center.
Adjournment
There being no further business before council, Council Member Cobble made a
motion to adjourn the meeting, with a second by Council Member Little. Motion
carried and the meeting adjourned at 8:00 p.m.

Resolution No. 2005-R-22 – Opposing Senate Bill 1504 Known as “Broadband
Investment & Consumer Choice Act”
Mayor Moriconi presented to council for their consideration, Resolution No.
2005-R-22 which would support the opposition of Senate Bill 1504 known as the
Broadband Investment & Consumer Choice Act. He reminded Council that this
Resolution was tabled at the September 12, 2005 meeting to give them time to
research the pros and cons of this issue. Mayor Moriconi introduced Tim
Broering, Executive Director of the Telecommunications Board of Northern
Kentucky (TBNK) who was present to answer any questions Council may have about
this bill. A brief discussion ensued wherein Mr. Broering explained that U.S.
Senator John McCain’s bill (S. 1504) known as the Broadband Investment and
Consumer Choice Act would strip local government of imposing local franchise
fees and control of the rights of way. He stated that the Kentucky League of
Cities and National League of Cities have voiced their opposition to this bill.
Council Member Cobble commented that she would like this issue remain tabled
until Council Member Kelso was present to comment. Mayor Moriconi stated he had
no objections. Council Member Yeager stated that Council Member Kelso received
all the research information on this issue, as did all the Council Members.
Mayor Moriconi, hearing no support to keep the issue tabled, directed Mr.
Deters to read Resolution No. 2005-R-22. Council Member Cobble commented that
the issue should first be removed from the table. Council Member Franzen made a
motion to remove Resolution No. 2005-R-22 from the table, seconded by Council
Member Yeager. No roll called, motion carried with all ayes.
Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2005-R-22. Council Member Franzen moved to
approve Resolution No. 2005-R-22, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Council
Member Cobble commented that she has contacted the offices of Senator McConnell
and Senator Bunning and was advised that they have taken no position yet on
this issue. There being no further discussion, roll was called and was answered
with four ayes and one pass vote cast by Council Member Cobble. Motion passed.
Resolution No. 2005-R-23 – Supporting the Sponsorship of a Zoning Text
Amendment Relating to Fences

read Resolution No. 2005-R-23.

November 7, 2005
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, November
7, 2005 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent
Kelso, Mike Little and Donna Yeager. City Attorney, Jed K. Deters was also
present.
Approval of the October 3, 2005 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the October 3,
2005 council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second from
Council Member Cobble. One amendment was noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Introduction of New Public Services Director
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Gary Cooper as the newly hired Public Services
Director. He stated Mr. Cooper began employment with the city on October 31st
and will oversee public works, building and zoning employees. Mr. Cooper
thanked the Mayor and Council for the opportunity to serve the citizens of
Independence.
Privileges of the Floor
Tom Schoborg, 49 Walnut Hall Drive, informed Council that he has heard rumors
that Walnut Hall Drive will be extended to connect with the adjoining new
development. He asked if the city was aware of this. Mayor Moriconi stated he
asked the developer and was told “absolutely not”. He stated he would ask
again. Council Member Cobble commented she did not recall seeing an extension
of Walnut Hall Drive on the Stage 1 development plan for the Independence
Village. She stated it was possible that sewer lines would be extended to
Walnut Hall Drive Mr. Deters advised that in order for the developer to extend
the street it would be necessary to acquire right-of-way (private property).
William E. Miller, 4394 Oliver Road, addressed Council regarding the proposed
zoning text amendment, specifically Section 9.23(d) relating to the parking/
keeping of recreational vehicles. He stated he feels the section should remain
intact and, if anything, strengthened. He expressed concern to increasing the
permitted length of an RV from 20 feet to 39 feet. He stated that 39 feet is
three-fourths as long as a semi-tractor trailer. He urged Council not to impose
these larger vehicles on the citizens of Independence.
Donna Miller, 4394 Oliver Road, addressed Council with a request to provide
more ‘open time’ for the audience to provide input at the meetings prior to
voting on issues. Mayor Moriconi replied that he often calls on audience
members with raised hands, allowing them to comment. Mr. Deters advised that
council meetings are open for public viewing, they are not a public forum and
that ‘privileges of the floor’ is designed to allow for public comment. He
stated that the time to address the Council regarding proposed legislation is
prior to the second reading of an ordinance.
Ed Smith, 1177 Constitution Drive, addressed Council with a zoning complaint.
He stated that the entrance to his subdivision (Independence Pointe) has gone
uncut since late August/early September. Council Member Cobble commented that
this is a repeated violation by the developer and recalled the city adopted an
ordinance that would permit the Building Inspector to withhold issuance of
future building permits when outstanding violations exist. Mayor Moriconi
advised that since Independence Pointe was built-out, he would inquire if this
developer was building elsewhere in the city and if so, check the possibility
of withholding permits until the grass cutting violation is resolved.
OLD BUSINESS
Status Report Regarding the Cingular Cell Tower Proposal at Sterling Staggs
Park
Mayor Moriconi reported that Cingular representatives have completed the site
review for the proposed cell tower location in Staggs Park and have reported
the sanitary sewer lateral line cannot be located without actually digging or
acquiring as-built drawings. The City Clerk reported that she has contacted the
city engineer to conduct a site review on the city’s behalf and report back to
Council with their findings, either confirming or rejecting Cingular’s report.
She stated that Cingular will need Council’s final approval of the proposed
site before proceeding with lease negotiations.
Mr. Deters commented that the underlying question is whether the city is
satisfied with the proposed location and if so, then the cell tower could
probably be constructed around it. Council Members Cobble and Cook stated they
were in favor of the site. Council Member Yeager commented that she would only
agree to this location if the equipment was installed underground and they did
not install a fence around the area. Mr. Deters reminded Council that Cingular
has advised they cannot use underground utilities for this type tower.
Mayor Moriconi advised he would request that Mr. Tim Sturm attend the December
5, 2005 meeting to wrap-up discussions of the site location. He advised Council
to be prepared with their questions of Mr. Sturm.
Audience member, Mr. Bill Cobble commented that he feels this is a great
opportunity for the city to finance the operation of the city parks with the
revenue that would be generated by leasing this property.
Discussion Relating to Proposed Zoning Text Amendment Regarding Recreation
Vehicles
Mayor Moriconi introduced discussion regarding a possible text amendment of
Section 9.23(d) of the city’s Zoning Ordinance which regulates the parking and/
or storing of recreational vehicles. He stated the current text is antiquated
and it has been suggested the city review this for possible amendments
regarding the length and weight of recreational vehicles. Mayor Moriconi also
stated that regulations need to be established for portable storage units
(PODS), which are becoming commonplace. He stated the purpose of the text
amendment would be to strengthen, not weaken the ordinance, by adopting
regulations that would accommodate current standards. Mayor Moriconi yielded
the floor to Annie Wuestefeld, Zoning Administrator for further explanation and
to answer questions from the Council and audience. A lengthy discussion took
place between the audience, council members and Mrs. Wuestefeld, which resulted
in several people (including Council Members Franzen and Little) volunteering
to sit on a committee to review Section 9.23(d) and present to the full Council
a proposed text amendment that would be practical for this community. Mayor
Moriconi requested they address the issue of establishing regulations for PODS
also.
NEW BUSINESS
Request by Sam and Sharon Beach and Jerry Sanders for the Waiver of Subdivision
Regulations for the Extension of McKim Drive
Mayor Moriconi stated the next item of business was a request by Sam and Sharon
Beach and Jerry Sanders for a waiver of subdivision regulations for the
extension of McKim Drive. Mayor Moriconi asked Mrs. Wuestefeld why this was
necessary. Mrs. Wuestefeld stated that the Beachs’ and Sanders’ want to build
homes at the dead end section of ’’’’McKim Drive’’ and in order to make the
lots buildable the road will have to be extended by twenty feet. She stated the
road would have to be constructed to current subdivision regulations which
would require curbs, gutters and sidewalks. She stated that since McKim is an
older city street that does not have these modern features it would be unfair
to enforce current street construction regulations. Mrs. Wuestefeld stated that
the Council has the authority to waive this regulation and allow them to build
the new section of roadway to like conditions of the existing portion of McKim
Drive. She stated that if the Council does not waive this regulation, then the
Planning Commission will enforce the subdivision regulations.
After a brief discussion, Council Member Kelso moved to waive the subdivision
regulations relating to the construction of the extension of McKim Drive as
requested by the Beachs’ and Sanders’; seconded by Council Member Franzen.
Prior to the vote, there was a brief discussion regarding the placement of a
sidewalk lien in the event that McKim Drive received major street improvements
in the future. Mr. Deters advised the lien would not be enforced until such
time, if ever, that the street would be reconstructed to meet current
subdivision regulations. Council Member Kelso amended his motion to include
requesting a sidewalk lien be filed as a condition of the waiver being granted
by the city. There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Municipal Order No. 2005-MO-02 – Approving Mayoral Appointment of Phyllis
Vetter to the Board of Ethics/Code Enforcement Board
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Municipal Order No. 2005-MO-02 that would
approve his appointment of Phyllis Vetter to the Board of Ethics/Code
Enforcement Board. Council Member Franzen moved to approve Municipal Order No.
2005-MO-02; seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered
with five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Margaret Cook. Motion
carried 5-1.
Municipal Order No. 2005-MO-03 – Approving Mayoral Appointment of Dave Millward

Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Compensation for Elected City Officials – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
set the compensation of the elected officials beginning January 2007. Mr.
Deters read the proposed ordinance. A lengthy discussion ensued. Council Member
Cobble questioned which Council Member was sponsoring this ordinance and also
expressed concerns about the attached salary comparison with other third-class
cities. She stated she felt other factors should be taken into consideration.
She stated she was absolutely opposed to approving an increase and was not
motivated to be in this position for the monetary compensation. Council Member
Franzen commented that she feels the compensation for the Mayor position should
be increased as it requires a lot of time. She stated she didn’t have a problem
if an increase for the council members was excluded, because the position is
not as time consuming as that of the mayor. Council Member Yeager concurred.
Council Member Little commented that the proposed increases were based on
averages of other third-class cities in the state. Council Cobble also
expressed concern about sufficient funds to handle these salary increases in
light of the fact the city recently eliminated three revenue items from the
budget. Council Member Little stated the ordinance would not be effective until
January 2007. Council Member Franzen commented that taxes would not have to be
increased to cover the additional compensation to the elected officials.
Mayor Moriconi advised the proposed ordinance would be presented for a second
reading at the December 5th meeting.

the Kentucky League of Cities for $2,500 for the purchase of safety related
equipment.

Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.

selected.

screening around dumpsters in retail/commercial areas. She stated she feels
this would resolve the open area behind the Cherokee shopping center which has
caused many complaints by the neighbors. Council Member Cobble stated that
existing businesses would be ‘grandfathered’ thereby exempting them from the
requirement. Mayor Moriconi suggested Council Member Franzen discuss her
suggestion with the Zoning Administrator.

meeting on Tuesday, December 6, 2005 at the new auditorium in Simon Kenton High
School from 7-9 p.m. He stated this meeting is an open invitation to the
general public and will be an opportunity for the citizens to provide the

years.

––––Kenton– ––County–– Attorney, Garry Edmondson

OLD BUSINESS:
Status Report Regarding the Cingular Cell Tower Proposal at Sterling Staggs
Park by Tim Sturm of Burgess & Niple
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Tim Sturm from Burgess & Niple who was present to
provide a status report regarding Cingular’s proposal to lease space for a cell
tower in Sterling Staggs Park. Mayor Moriconi commented that the main issue
before the city is whether or not to proceed with this proposal. He stated
there is concern that sewer lines are in the vicinity of the proposed site.
Mr. Sturm reported that after approaching the city and agreeing on an
appropriate site, they have conducted a basic study and are not able to find
sewer utilities in the area. He stated the lease area would be 50x50 feet
instead of the usual 100x100 feet, the building would be 20x11 feet and
Cingular has agreed to forego the installation of a fence around the structure
as requested by the city. There was a brief discussion between Council Member
Yeager, plumber Dave Arlinghaus and Mr. Sturm regarding sewer lines in the
area. Mr. Arlinghaus stated he installed sewer lines which run under the sand
volleyball court and exits along Sylvan Drive. Council Member Yeager stated she
also feels the cell tower would take up a lot of space and ruin the look of the
park. She stated she also wanted the tower equipment buried. Mr. Sturm stated
Cingular has a policy that they will not install their equipment underground.
Council Member Cobble and Council Member Cook made an announcement that they
have a vision to mark the 25th anniversary of the Simon Kenton High School
tragedy that killed one student at the school by having a glazed ceramic
memorial drawn on the cell tower equipment structure to camouflage the
building. Council Member Cobble stated she has discussed this vision with Mr.
Sturm who has agreed to permit this. Council Member Cook stated donations would
be sought to put up the ceramic memorial with a bronze plaque. She stated the
cell tower would be a great revenue source for the maintenance of the city
parks. Council Member Cobble stated she has spoken to school representatives
and after having done that, feels confident that the cell tower would not
present a health hazard to children. Council Member Yeager commented that
Memorial Park was so named to have all memorials at that park.
Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Sturm why they did not approach private
resident owners for lease space. Mr. Sturm said they prefer to lease municipal
property as local government is generally looking for revenue sources. Council
Member Franzen stated she received 31 e-mail messages from citizens opposing
the installation of a cell tower in the park. She stated she has to consider
more than the possible revenue that would be generated.
Council Member Cobble made a motion to move forward with the proposal by
Cingular Wireless to lease a 50x50 square foot parcel at the current site in
Sterling Staggs Park. Council Member Cook seconded the motion. Council Member
Little stated he has received 15 e-mail messages from concerned parents that
oppose a cell tower in the park. Council Member Cobble stated she only received
one objection, but many more that were in favor of it. Roll was called and
answered with four no votes cast by Council Members Franzen, Kelso, Little and
Yeager and two yes votes cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion failed
4-2.
Council Member Kelso stated that he believes that the citizens did not have
correct information and that he voted against the cell tower proposal because
he disagrees with a cell tower. He stated he does not have concerns about
radiation, but was concerned about the effects if the tower fell over. He
stated he favored the revenue that would be generated by leasing the space, but
he was not comfortable that there was so much disagreement associated with this
proposal. Council Member Kelso requested the Mayor have an open session for the
citizens to attend so that they can be shown what is being proposed by
Cingular. He stated that even though he voted against this issue he does not
think it is time yet to put it to rest. Council Member Cobble stated that he
should have put a motion forth to table the issue, as the vote just effectually
defeated the proposal. Council Member Kelso disagreed that it was a dead issue.
Discussion Relating to Proposed Zoning Text Amendment Regarding Recreational
Vehicles
Mayor Moriconi presented for discussion a proposed text amendment to the
official zoning ordinance as it relates to the parking or storage of
recreational vehicles in residential zones. Mayor Moriconi thanked the
volunteers who met to discuss the text amendment and make the proposal
presented to council. Mr. Deters stated that a proposed text amendment
ordinance is being presented to council to show the actual language amendment
to the zoning ordinance. Mayor Moriconi read the changes in language that is
being proposed indicating that the significant changes would be an increase in
the gross vehicular weight from 6,000 to 18,000 pounds, the removal of a length
requirement on the recreational vehicles and the addition of language that
would regulate the use of PODS (Portable On Demand Storage Facilities). Mr.
Deters advised that an application for a text amendment would have to be
submitted to the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission, who would then
comment and submit a recommendation to the city.
A lengthy discussion ensued with the council members asking questions about the
proposed text amendments and making suggestions. Annie Wuestefeld, Zoning
Administrator stated a permit fee for PODS was being proposed, as it would be
considered an accessory structure. Council Member Cobble asked if a
construction dumpster should be considered as an accessory and charged a permit
fee as well, so as not to be discriminatory. Mr. Deters stated that dumpsters
are not problems as they are hauled away when they become full. The discussion
also touched on the number of RV's that would be permitted on any lot or
parcel. Council Member Franzen stated the committee considered one or even two
vehicles to be a reasonable number. Council Member Cobble submitted a letter
from Realtor Rebecca Coates Burris, which she read into the record of this
meeting. Ms. Burris' concerns were of an aesthetics nature, which she asserted
affect the market value of resident's homes. (Ms. Burris' letter is attached as
part of the official minutes of this meeting and is noted as “Attachment-A”).
Council Member Little stated that former Council Member Jaimie Henson was at
the committee meeting and shared information that stated the Supreme Court has
ruled that the city cannot pass an ordinance completely on concerns of
aesthetics. He also commented that the concern that market values are affected
is subjective. Council Member Franzen commented that a run down house will also
affect market values in a community. When discussing length restrictions, Ms.
Wuestefeld advised that she can not legally go onto private property to measure
an RV.
Jerry Saylor, 5140 Madison Pike, addressed council by stating that he recently
moved to the city. He stated he lives on a corner lot and went to the expense
of pouring a $4,000 concrete pad for his trailer and is now being told it is an
eyesore and that he can't store it on his property. A lengthy discussion ensued
between Mr. Saylor, Ms. Wuestefeld and Council Member Cobble about this
reported violation.
Council Member Little moved to submit the text amendment language to NKAPC as
proposed, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Council Member Franzen suggested
adding text proposed by Mr. Ken Lancaster. After a brief discussion it was
decided to submit the text as presented. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0. Mayor Moriconi advised a text application
would be submitted to NKAPC for a recommendation.

January 9, 2006
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
9, 2006 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Resident, John Little gave the invocation. Roll
was called and the following Council Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble,
Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. City Attorney,
Jed K. Deters was also present. Mayor Moriconi announced that Council Member
Kelso called to say he would not be present at the start of the meeting, but
would be arriving late.
Mayor Moriconi stated he would be implementing a couple changes in the meeting
procedures to make the meetings run smoother. He advised he would refrain from
yielding the floor to audience members wishing to participate in council
discussion. He stated he would also stay more focused on the agenda items and
avoid straying into other issues not on the agenda.

Hudson, Finance Director
Mayor Moriconi directed council to a Summary of Bank Proposals submitted by the
city’s Finance Director, Teresa Hudson. He stated that the city received six
bid proposals from the following banks: US Bank, The Bank of Kentucky, Fifth

week that Council Member Cobble, on January 9th submitted a two page statement
to the City Clerk and asked that it be attached to the December 5th minutes
after they had already been voted on and approved. Ms. Cobble cited that under
Section 4.19 of the Rules of Order ordinance that this is allowed. However,
since he is responsible to run the meetings and enforce the rules he has read
the statement and finds it does not meet the requirements of this rule and,
therefore Ms. Cobble’s statement will not be allowed to be attached to the
minutes of the Dec. 5th meeting

Proposed Ordinance - Relating to the Regulation of Portable Storage Units – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance amending
Section 92.10 of the official zoning ordinance that would create a new
definition for the regulation of portable storage units. Mr. Deters explained
that it was recommended by the Planning Commission that a separate ordinance
should be adopted to regulate the temporary use of portable storage units and
that the Zoning Administrator has suggested they be classified under the
nuisances section of the zoning ordinance. There was a brief discussion prior
to the first reading wherein further amendments to the proposed text were
noted.
Mayor Moriconi asked for a motion to approve the amendments. Council Member
Yeager so moved seconded by Council Member Little. No roll call; motion carried
5-1, the nay vote being cast by Council Member Cobble. Mr. Deters gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading. Further discussion centered on the need to
require a permit, but that no fee should be associated with a permit. The
permit would be used strictly as a tracking devise.

Mitigation Plan
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2006-R-01 that would approve

official Hazard Mitigation Plan for the City. He advised that under the
Disaster Mitigation Act of 2000, the U. S. Federal Emergency Management Agency
(FEMA) requires that local jurisdictions have in place a FEMA-approved
Mitigation Action Plan as a condition of receipt of certain future funding. Mr.
Deters read Resolution No. 2006-R-01.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Resolution No. 2006-R-01, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.

Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. City
Attorney, Jed K. Deters was also present.

Franzen selected One Eleven Engineering and Surveying as the recipient of the
Business of the Month for January and Council Member Kelso selected SMI New
Home Solutions as the recipient for February. Mayor Moriconi presented the
plaques to Jim Bertram of One Eleven and Mark and Susie Wheatly of SMI New Home
Solutions.
Approval of the January 23, 2006 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the January 23,
2006 council meeting. Council Member Little so moved with a second from Council
Member Franzen. Council Member Cook read a prepared statement regarding the
January 23, 2006 meeting. Council Member Little asked if her statement was a
motion to amend the minutes. Council Member Cook so moved, with second by
Council Member Cobble. No roll was called; motion failed 2-4. Council Member
Cook asked that a copy of her statement be attached to the minutes of this
meeting.
Council Member Cobble stated she wished to make a statement which she had
prepared in Resolution form. Council Members Little and Kelso called for point
of order citing that the reading or discussion of a Resolution should not be
done while there is a motion on the floor to approve the minutes from the last

more appropriate under new business.

necessary. Council Member Franzen so moved, seconded by Council Member Kelso.
Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Kelso moved to adopt Resolution No. 2006-R-04, seconded by
Council Member Cobble. There was a brief discussion regarding the proposed text
relating to screening of parking lots, service areas, etc. from view of
adjacent residential properties. Council Member Yeager made a motion to add
language that would designate the Zoning Administration as the person to
determine the appropriate screening, seconded by Council Member Little. No roll

Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2006-R-04 and afterward advised that, if
approved, this text would establish a new zone in the city and provide
regulations for the zone. Mayor Moriconi called for a vote to adopt Resolution
No. 2006-R-04. No roll call; motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-03 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment – KCPC Application
Number 1789R - Relating to Recreational Vehicles (RV’s) – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve an amendment to Section 9.23 of the official zoning ordinance that
would prohibit the parking of vehicles with a gross vehicle weight of 18,000 or
more pounds and modifying the length requirement on recreational vehicles. Mr.
Deters gave a second reading to Ordinance No. 2006-O-03.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-03, seconded
by Council Member Little. Council Member Cobble asked which council member was

the sponsor. A discussion ensued. Council Members Cobble and Cook voiced their

Executive Order No. 2006-EO-01 – Establishing Continuity of Government
Administration in the Absence/Vacancy of the Mayor
Mayor Moriconi presented Executive Order No. 2006-EO-01 that would establish
the continuity of government administration in the event of a vacancy in the
office of the mayor due to absence or disability. Executive Order No. 2006-EO-
01 establishes that the responsibilities of the office of mayor would be
delegated to first, the Police Chief, second the Assistant Police Chief and
third would be the Council Member as designated by city ordinance. There was a
brief discussion wherein it was decided to eliminate the third designee, as it
was pointed out that state law does not permit a council member to handle the
day to day responsibilities of the mayor. Mayor Moriconi agreed to eliminate
the third designee and the change was noted.

February 27, 2006
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
27, 2006 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent
Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. City Attorney, Jed K. Deters was also
present.
Approval of the February 6, 2006 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February 6,
2006 council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved with a second from
Council Member Yeager. Council Member Little voiced his objection to the
attachment of Council Member Cook’s statement that she read at the February 6
meeting and a debate ensued. In due course, roll was called to approve the
minutes with the statement attached, and answered 4-2, with Council Members
Little and Kelso casting the dissenting votes. Motion carried.
Privileges of the Floor
John Bach, 427 Independence Station Road, Independence – addressed Council
regarding the Meadow Glen Subdivision Stage II development plan, which is on
the agenda for Council to consider the recommendation of the Planning
Commission. Mr. Bach advised that in order for the developer to adhere to one
of the sixteen conditions imposed on this development plan would involve the
acquisition of a portion of his property to widen ––––Webster Road––. He feared
this would be taken from him by eminent domain. Mr. Deters advised that the
Planning Commission cannot force the city to condemn private property for
private use and that in his opinion the condition imposed on the developer
(Berling/Fischer) to widen a portion of ––––Webster Road–– to twenty-two (22)
feet is unenforceable.
Mary Yost, 3988 Thomas Drive, addressed Council regarding a concern she has
with her grandchildren’s use of dirt bikes. She stated her grandchildren have
told her the police officers have told them the bikes are not allowed. She
asked if there was an ordinance prohibiting dirt bikes. Mayor Moriconi advised
Ms. Yost he would have the Police Chief call her this week to discuss her
concern.
JoAnne Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, Independence - Mayor Moriconi advised that
Council Member JoAnne Cobble wished to address the Council under the Privileges
of the Floor. Council Member Cobble read a prepared statement wherein she
protested the adoption of Resolution No. 2006-R-02 and Resolution No. 2006-R-
03.
Proposed Ordinance - Relating to the Regulation of Portable Storage Units – New
1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a revised draft of a proposed ordinance
that would establish the regulation of portable storage units. There was a
brief discussion to add language providing currently existing portable storage
units a period of sixty days in which to come into compliance with this new
law. The amendment was noted and Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Prohibiting Disclosure of Information Discussed In
Executive Session – New 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a new first reading a revised draft of a proposed
ordinance that would prohibit the disclosure of any information divulged or
discussed in an executive session of the city council and providing that a
violation would be a Class A misdemeanor. There was a lengthy discussion with
differing opinions on this proposed ordinance.
Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Ratify the KCPC Recommendation to Approve the Stage II Development Plan of
Meadow Glen Subdivision
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for discussion the correspondence from the
Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission dated February 7, 2006 wherein they
recommend approval of the Meadow Glen Subdivision Stage II development plan for
an approximate 20-acre area, subject to one additional condition. (Note: City
Ordinance No. 2004-O-15 was adopted on 9-13-04 approving the rezoning of the
area from R-1C to R-1C (PUD) subject to sixteen conditions). A discussion
ensued wherein there was some hesitancy by some Council Members who voiced
their concerns in approving this based on Mr. John Bach’s property being taken
for the widening of ’’’’Webster Road’’. (Condition number 10 of Ordinance No.
2004-O-15). Mr. Deters restated that it was an unenforceable condition.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to resident, Michelle Herrmann who pointed out
that condition number ten was imposed at the time of the zone change, and a
condition that she feels is necessary. Mr. Deters stated the developer would
have to condemn the private property needed to adhere to this condition. A
lengthy discussion ensued. Ms. Herrmann commented that Webster Road would need
to be widened even before the construction trucks could access it. Mr. Deters
advised that Council that Mr. Bach is requesting the city provide him a
promissory letter that we would not pursue the widening of Webster Road. In
closing the discussion, Mr. Deters stated that the bottom line is that
condition number ten effectively doesn’t hurt either Mr. Bach or Ms. Herrmann.
Council Member Kelso moved to ratify the NKAPC recommendation to approve the
Meadow Glen Subdivision Stage II development plan (Z-06-01-05/1769R), seconded
by Council Member Yeager. No roll call; motion carried 4-2 with Council Members
Cobble and Cook casting the dissenting votes.
Resolution No. 2006-R-05 – Petitioning the State to Lower the Speed Limit on
––––Fowler Creek Road––
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration Resolution No.
2006-R-05 that would petition the state to lower the speed limit on Fowler
Creek Road. Chief Butler cited numerous traffic incidents on Fowler Creek Road
and advised Council that in the interest of public safety he felt it would be
prudent to lower the speed limit, but that since it is a state maintained road,
the city would need to make this request to the state highway department.
Council Member Cobble moved to adopt Resolution No. 2006-R-05 for all the
reasons cited by Chief Butler. Council Member Yeager seconded the motion. No

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 6,

J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the

Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the February 27,

Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum Road, Independence – Asked Mayor Moriconi if the
Fowler Creek Sewer Assessment audit had been completed yet. Mayor Moriconi
advised the report would be ready for presentation to the Council sometime in
March or April.
Discussion Regarding the Tabling of Map Amendment Application No. 1798R –
Bridges & Smock Properties on Madison Pike
Mayor Moriconi advised that after the February 6, 2006 council meeting, wherein
the Council agreed to sponsor a zoning map amendment for properties along
Madison Pike owned by Mr. Gailen Bridges and Ms. Vicki Smock, he received calls
from citizens and council members who had concerns over this proposed zone
change. He stated that it became clear to him that the concerns were sufficient
enough to warrant having the Kenton County Planning Commission table the matter
until such time that concerns could be addressed and resolved. A lengthy
discussion ensued. Some Council Members stated they had received complaints
from residents on Sidney Drive. Also, Council Member Franzen stated she had
learned that the Kenton County Board of Education was in negotiations with the
property owners to purchase the land. Mr. Bridges confirmed there had been some
discussion with the Board of Education. Mr. Jeremy Deters, legal counsel for
the Board of Education, stated the Board had interest in the property as it
will be the new entrance into the school from the newly routed section of SR
17. He stated the Board has concerns of the property being zoned commercial and
the type of businesses that could possibly be developed on the land.
Ray Baldwin, 34 Sidney Drive, addressed council by stating he did not think it
was appropriate to zone this property commercial. Further discussion centered
on the possibility of amending the current application for the zone change.
City Attorney, Mr. Jed Deters advised the application could continue being
tabled, modified with conditions, or completely withdrawn. He stated if the
city decided to withdraw the application, then the property owners could apply
for the map amendment themselves. Mr. Bridges stated if he and the other
property owners made the application they would be required to submit a
development plan, which he currently does not have.
Mayor Moriconi asked Council how they wanted to proceed. Mr. Bridges expressed
displeasure at the possibility that he would be out the application fee
($1,250) if Council would decide to withdraw the application. Mr. Deters
advised Council that the application fee is non-refundable.
Council Member Kelso moved to untable the map amendment application and
proceed, but the motion died for lack of a second. Council Member Kelso
questioned why it would even be necessary for the Council to untable this issue
since the Mayor had exercised his executive authority to table it.
Council Member Yeager moved to withdraw the map amendment application, seconded
by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered with two yeahs and four
nays. Motion was defeated 2-4. A brief discussion ensued regarding the time
frame the city had to work within to untable the application with the Planning
Commission. Mr. Deters advised the Planning Commission deadline to submit new
information, untable or withdraw the application was August 2, 2006. Mayor
Moriconi advised Mr. Bridges that the city would take all the comments and
discussion tonight under consideration.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-04 – Establishing Regulations of Portable Storage Units –
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2006-O-
04 establishing the regulation of portable storage units. Mr. Deters gave a

carried 4-2.

Executive Session – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2006-O-05, an
ordinance that would prohibit the disclosure of any information divulged or
discussed in an executive session of the city council and providing that a

Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-05, seconded by

enforceability of such an ordinance. Roll was called and answered with four
ayes and two nays cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion carried 4-2.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to De-Annex 4946 and 4948 Madison Pike – 1st

state the city’s intent to de-annex a part of the property owned by Greg and

the meeting ended at 8:08 p.m.

Discussion of Rumpke Contract Renewal
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that the current contract with Rumpke for waste
removal will expire on June 30, 2006. He advised that the current contract has
an option for a 2-year extension that would increase the current monthly rate
by .44 cents for a total of $5.28 annually. He stated the trash assessment per
unit would go from $105.84 to $111.12 per year. The $111.12 assessment would be
set for two years – 2006 and 2007.
There was a brief discussion about having Rumpke directly bill the property
owners, and then if the trash bill is not paid, Rumpke could discontinue
service to the property. The pros and cons of this were discussed. The City
Clerk advised that the option before the Council was whether or not they would
like to extend the current contract which provides that Rumpke bill the city
directly and not the property owners. She stated that if they wanted to deviate
from the current service being provided under the current contract that Rumpke
would probably want to re-negotiate the rates, taking into consideration
today’s high fuel rates, cost of postage to every property owner, etc.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve extending Rumpke’s contract for the
next 2-year period of 2006/2008 providing for an annual rate of $111.12,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.

of the month recognition for April.

There being no further business, Council Member Cobble made a motion to adjourn
the meeting, with a second by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried and the
meeting ended at 7:26 p.m.

May 1, 2006
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 1,
2006 at 7:00 p.m. in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council Members

Mayor Moriconi stated he would personally meet with Mr. Ahearn to inspect the

Independence Courthouse/SR 17 Corridor Area Study Proposal by NKAPC
Representatives Dennis Gordon & Keith Logsdon
Mayor Moriconi introduced Dennis Gordon, Executive Director of the Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission who presented a proposal that the city
partner with the NKAPC to conduct a market analysis and area study to determine
sites for future commercial development which would also include a strategic
plan for the new development. Mr. Gordon stated their proposal consisted of a
two-part plan; part one would be a market/economic analysis and part two would
be a downtown Independence small area study. Under part one of the proposal
they would suggest contracting with GEM Public Sector Services of Dayton, Ohio
to conduct the market study and detailed retail analysis. He advised that NKAPC
would contribute $13,000 toward this part of the project of the total estimated
cost of $24,500 which includes the detailed retail analysis at approximately
$4,000. He stated the second part of this proposal would consist of a detailed
plan to include proposals for land use, transportation and community facility
issues in a newly defined downtown area. He advised this would include the
selection of a planning consultant to partner with the NKAPC staff on the
downtown Independence small area study portion of the project. They stated the
project would be a collaborative effort in which input would be sought from
residents, business leaders and elected officials. It was also suggested that
the city create an advisory committee to work on the study.
Mr. Gordon stated they have partnered with other cities on similar projects.
When questioned on the appropriate time frame to complete this project, Mr.
Logsdon stated the goal would be to complete the study before the new section
of SR 17 is open. Council Members questioned Mr. Gordon on the dollars spent by
other cities on this type project as well as the cost of part two of this
proposal. Mr. Gordon advised the cost varies based on the extensiveness of the
services requested. Mr. Gordon stated he would provide council with a copy of
the study conducted for the City of Fort Wright so they could review a finished
product. The consensus of Council was to take this proposal under
consideration. Mayor Moriconi advised that action on this proposal would be
placed on a future agenda.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving the De-Annexation of Lipscomb/Schoborg Property
on ––Madison– Pike – 1st Reading

At 8:49 p.m. Council Member Cobble moved to return to regular session, seconded

Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment Changing Approximately 64 Acres
Along the North Side of Mt. Zion Road from R-1C to R-1C (PUD) – KCPC
Application No. 1810R
Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion and possible action on a
proposed map amendment for an approximate 63-acre area located along the north
side of Mount Zion Road, approximately 800 feet west of Bristow Road. The
developer is requesting the zone change from the current R-1C to R-1C (PUD). He
advised Council that the residents of Timber Lane, as well as other adjoining
property owners in the vicinity of the proposed development site have expressed
concerns over the PUD designation. Mayor Moriconi stated the residents have
provided written correspondence outlining their concerns and many are in
attendance at tonight’s meeting. Mayor Moriconi also advised that developer,
One-Eleven and their legal counsel, Tim Theissen are present to discuss the
development plan and answer any questions.
Mr. Theissen advised Council that the KCPC (Kenton County Planning Commission)
has recommended approval of this zone change subject to compliance with ten
conditions; one being that there is no vehicular connection between the
internal street system of the proposed development and Sawmill Drive which
connects to Timber Lane. Mr. Theissen advised the developer is happy to do
either – connect or not connect to Sawmill. Mr. Theissen and Jim Bertram of
One-Eleven presented a rendering of the proposed Stage I Development Plan. He
stated the proposed development would consist of nineteen acres residential,
twenty-five acres commercial and the remaining acreage would be open/green
space. He stated the commercial development, probably a grocery store, would
face SR 536 and the residential development would consist of ranch condominiums
and patio homes in the $200,000 price range.
Mr. Tim Kappas, 731 Timber Lane, Independence - spoke on behalf of the Timber
Lane and surrounding property owners. He asked that the Council reject the KCPC
recommendation to approve this zone change. He stated they have several
concerns with this proposed development and feel that some criteria have not
been met to warrant a zone change. Some of the concerns cited by the residents
were traffic congestion and safety , as well as the magnitude of the planned
commercial development which they feel is not consistent with the PUD zone and
in fact exceeds PUD goals.
Scott Holten, 853 Bristow Road, Independence – spoke in opposition to the
planned development and zone change. He stated that 41% retail space for a PUD
development is unusually high and feels this bends the intention of a PUD zone.
He also expressed concern that the area cannot support such a large retail
development. Mr. Holten also had signage concerns and who would maintain
fourteen acres of open space – would there be an HOA (homeowners’ association).
After discussing this for some time, Council Member Franzen moved to table this
issue until the June 5th meeting to give everyone more time to review all the
information submitted. Council Member Yeager seconded the motion. No roll call,
motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment Changing Approximately 2.4 Acres
Along the East Side of Madison Pike from R-1C to NC – KCPC Application No.
1798R
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
accept the KCPC recommendation to approve a zone change to an approximate 2.4
acre area located along the east side of Madison Pike between Harris Pike and
Sidney Drive, approximately 500 feet south of Harris Pike from R-1C to NC.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Mr. Rob Haney, Director of Support
Operations for the Kenton County School District. Mr. Haney stated that Dr.
Susan Cook, Superintendent of the School District submitted a letter to the
KCPC wherein she expressed the District’s concern with expanding the commercial
zone so near a school facility. Mr. Haney stated it is the opinion of the Board
of Education and the ’’School District’ staff that the zone change request
should be denied. Council Member Cobble wanted to know which parcels the school
wanted and the intended use by the school. Mr. Bridges objected to this and Mr.
Deters concurred stating that the intended use by someone that may be
condemning a property is not relevant, and probably inappropriate, to whether
this recommendation is in conformance with the plan.
A discussion ensued between the Council and property owner, Gailen Bridges.
Council expressed concerns that retail businesses would go in. Mr. Bridges
asserted he would be using the two existing houses on his property as
professional office space and that he did not seek PO (professional office)
zone as that zone requires a minimum of five acres. Council discussed with Mike
Schwartz about imposing a condition that only professional offices be
permitted. Mr. Schwartz advised that the city could clarify that any change of
use, other than professional office would be considered a major change, thereby
requiring an application be made.
Council Member Cobble commented that while she agrees that this zone is in
agreement with the Comprehensive Plan, as does the NKAPC Staff and KCPC, her
only concern is that she never wants to see commercial/retail development
across from the school. She is concerned about the students, parents and
faculty, being attracted to stores selling pop, candy, etc. She stated since
the Stage I plan is for professional offices, which she feels would have a low
impact on the area; she is moving to read the proposed ordinance to approve the
KCPC recommendation. Council Member Kelso agreed and seconded her motion. She
stated she would like conditional language regarding professional office use in
the ordinance.
Roll was called and answered with three yeahs and three no votes cast by
Council Members Franzen, Little and Yeager. Mr. Deters stated that since the
Mayor cannot vote on zoning issues that the tie vote amounts to no action.
There was some objection voiced by some of the Council Members regarding this
counsel as they felt this was just an underlying motion, not the enactment of
the ordinance.
Mayor Moriconi advised the issue would be brought back for a second reading at
the May 15, 2006 council meeting.
Award Bid for the 2006 Street Repairs Program
Mayor Moriconi presented the bid tabulation results for the Independence 2006
Street Program for repairs to Kimberly Drive, Kimberly Place and Elizabeth
Drive. He stated that Prus Construction’s base bid was the lowest submitted at
$299.511.20. Contractors were asked to provide both a base bid for a basic
overlay and an alternate bid which consisted of a total reconstruction of the
street. Chief Butler explained this was done to see if it would be affordable
to do a complete reconstruction, but the alternate bids have come in higher
than expected. He stated the base bid came in as estimated by the city
engineer.
Council Member Cobble moved to award the 2006 Street Repairs Program base bid
to Prus Construction in the amount of $299,511.20, seconded by Council Member
Little. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Award Bid for the Madison Pike Sidewalk Project
Mayor Moriconi presented the bid tabulation results of the Madison Pike
Sidewalk Program. He stated two bids were received with the low bid of
$123,505.00 being submitted by RFH Construction. He stated the city engineer is
recommending the bid be awarded to RFH. Council Member Kelso moved to award the
Madison Pike Sidewalk Project to RFH Construction, seconded by Council Member
Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler had nothing to report.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi stated the Business of the Month for May would be selected by
Council Member Cobble. Council Member Cobble stated she has chosen Wicklund
Florist to be the recipient.
Mayor Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Discussion Regarding Common Areas in New Developments
Council Member Cobble introduced discussion regarding the common areas,
detention ponds, etc. in the new residential developments. She expressed
concern that this could become a problem and expense in the future if the city
would become responsible for the maintenance of these areas. Council had a
brief discussion about measures that could be put in place to prevent problems
in the future.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Kelso made a motion to adjourn
the meeting, with a second by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried and the
meeting adjourned at 10:48 p.m.

Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Relating to the
Regulation of Sexually Oriented Businesses – 1st Reading
Council Member Cobble made a motion to move the proposed ordinance regarding
sexually oriented businesses to the next item for discussion before Old
Business is discussed with second by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried 6-0.
Mayor Moriconi stated a few years ago a number of cities came together and
contributed to a fund to help regulate sexually oriented businesses. He stated
Mr. Gary Edmondson, County Attorney and Mr. Mike Schwartz from NKAPC are in
attendance to speak on this subject.
Mr. Edmondson stated the hearings have been held and Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission has recommended what the cities involved need to do in
terms of zoning and the ordinance will require city approval. He stated it is
long in language but is required to make it legally binding.
Mr. Schwartz stated the Industrial Park Zone has been removed from the list of
permitted zones wherein the businesses would be located. He stated as of now
the city has no zones that these uses would be applied to but because of size,
growth, and potential future annexations, NKAPC feels it is important to adopt
the full text of the regulations opposed to the “no zone scenario”.
Mr. Deters read the summary of the proposed ordinance.

NKAPC Proposal to Conduct an Independence Downtown Small Area Study
(Courthouse/SR 17 Corridor Area) - Keith Logsdon, NKAPC Representative
Mayor Moriconi stated that Mr. Keith Logsdon from the Planning Commission was
present to respond to any questions Council might have regarding their proposal
to partner with the city in conducting a market/economic analysis and land use
plan for the downtown area. He stated this proposal was first introduced at the
May 1, 2006 meeting. Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor for Council’s comments
and questions. A lengthy discussion ensued wherein Council members expressed
interest in reviewing the Visionary Committee’s report prior to accepting this
proposal. Discussion also centered on the cost. Mr. Logsdon confirmed that the
Planning Commission would contribute $13,000 of the estimated $24,500 for Part
I of the proposal; Part I being the market/economic analysis, leaving the city
with a contribution amount of $11,500. He stated the estimated cost to the city
for Part II, a land use plan, would be approximately $80,000. Also discussed
was the time frame to conduct the analysis and land use plan. Mr. Logsdon
indicated the project would take ten months from August 2006, so they would
need to commence as soon as possible.
Council Member Franzen moved to accept both Parts of the Downtown Small Area
Study proposal submitted by NKAPC in an amount not to exceed $91,500, seconded
by Council Member Yeager. Further discussion ensued. Council Member Kelso
suggested the motion be withdrawn. He stated he feels the Vision Committee will
save some time and he did not think it would hurt to wait a couple of months
before acting on this proposal. Council Member Little suggested the City pay
the full amount of $24,500 for Part I and ask if the Planning Commission would
contribute $13,000 to Part II instead of Part I. Mr. Logsdon stated he was not
authorized to make that decision and would have to see if that was acceptable
to the Planning Commission.
Council Member Franzen amended her motion by moving to accept Part I of the
Downtown Small Area Study proposal submitted by NKAPC in the amount of $24,500
with the city paying the full amount, if necessary. Roll was called and
answered with two yes votes by Council Members Franzen and Yeager and four no
votes cast by Council Members Cook, Kelso, Little and Cobble. Motion defeated
4-2.
Mayor Moriconi advised this issue would be placed on the June 19, 2006 meeting
agenda, if the city received an answer from the Planning Commission regarding
the request by the city to re-direct their $13,000 contribution to Part II of
the proposal.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment Changing Approximately 64 Acres
Along the North Side of ––––Mt. Zion Road–– from R-1C to R-1C (PUD) – KCPC
Application No. 1810R
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve a map amendment for a 63-acre parcel located along the north side of
Mount Zion Road approximately 800 feet west of Bristow Road. The applicant, One
Eleven Developers, LLC is requesting the zone be changed from R-1C to R-1C

Proposed Ordinance - Hickory Valley Subdivision – Amendment to Ordinance No.
2005-O-02
Pursuant to a request by Tim Reese of Centerline Development at the May 15,
2006 council meeting, Mayor Moriconi presented a proposed ordinance to Council
that would revise Condition 5 imposed on the Hickory Valley Subdivision. Mr.
Reese addressed Council by stating that this subdivision has been awarded the
“Parade of Homes” location and the builders must be ready to begin construction
of ten homes by June 1, 2006 with a completion date by the first week of
October 2006. He stated the builders who will be constructing the houses are
requesting that the conditional brick wrap be changed in the ordinance to allow
them to construct a brick front instead of a complete first floor wrap.
There was a brief discussion by Council wherein some Members expressed concern
that if this request is granted for one developer then other developers will
follow suit and the city will be flooded with requests to eliminate the
condition of first floor brick wraps in other developments.
Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to give the proposed ordinance with the
amended text as requested by Mr. Reese a first reading. Mr. Deters read the
proposed ordinance that would strikethrough condition number five and insert
new language for condition number five. The proposed amendment is as follows:
5.   That the first floor of all dwelling units built in the development shall
be brick wrapped, except for isolated areas not directly supported by a
concrete foundation- an example of such isolated area would be cantilevered
walls, bay windows and the like.
5 .   That the first floor of all dwelling units built in the development shall
have a brick front. That the units on Lots 1 and 203 shall have a first floor
brick wrap. That the dwelling units on all corner lots shall have a first floor
brick front on the bottom half of both sides of the first floor of the dwelling
unit. These requirements for brick wrap apply except for isolated areas not
directly supported by a concrete foundation – an example of such isolated areas
would be cantilevered walls, bay windows and the like.
Mayor Moriconi stated the proposed ordinance would be presented for a second
reading and vote at the next council meeting.

Ordinance No. 2006-O-10 - Approving the Amended 2005/2006 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would amend Ordinance No. 2005-O-18 adopting the 2005/06 fiscal year
budget for the city. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2006-O-10.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-10, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. A brief discussion ensued wherein Council Member Cobble
and Council Member Cook expressed some concerns they had with overruns in some
line items. Council Member Little responded that many line items budgeted more
funds than was actually spent. Mrs. Terri Hudson, Finance Director explained
that to operate efficiently, it was not practical to present each and every
possible line item overrun to the Council for an amendment to the budget. Mayor
Moriconi also advised that each amendment would then require two readings of an
ordinance and publication costs of the ordinances would be incurred. Mrs.
Hudson also commented that the total revised budget saw an increase of $18,000
in revenue. She also informed Council that the figures in this amended budget
are projections for expenses through June 30, 2006.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered four ayes and
two no votes cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion carried 4-2.

Council Member Cobble stated that because this is a zoning issue, she does not
believe the Mayor is eligible to vote. Mr. Deters stated he would research the
matter and report to the Mayor.
Proposed Ordinance - Approving the 2006/2007 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve the city budget for the 2006/07 fiscal year. Mr. Deters gave the
ordinance a first reading. Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion.
Council Member Cobble moved to abolish the building and zoning revenue line
items and contract for the city’s building and zoning services with NKAPC’s
“One-Stop Shop” service, seconded by Council Member Cook. A brief discussion
ensued, roll was called and answered with two yes votes and four no votes cast
by Council Members Kelso, Little, Yeager and Franzen. Motion defeated 4-2.
Council Member Cobble also voiced concerns with the proposed budget,
specifically employee health insurance benefits, janitorial services for the
Senior Center and Municipal Center and street sign expenses. Chief Butler
advised Council that the city is actively shopping health plans for the
employees with the emphasis being on keeping the premium costs down, which will
effectively raise each employee’s out of pocket expenses with higher co-pays
and annual deductibles. Council Member Franzen commented that she supports this
budget and feels it is important to provide good wages and benefits to maintain
good employees.
Council Member Cobble moved to require all employees to pay ten percent toward
the cost of their health insurance premium, seconded by Council Member Cook.
Roll was called and answered with two yes votes and four not votes cast by
Council Members Little, Yeager, Franzen and Kelso. Motion was defeated 4-2.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi advised the second reading of
this proposed budget would be presented at the June 19th council meeting.

(Courthouse/SR 17 Corridor Area) - Keith Logsdon, NKAPC Representative
Mayor Moriconi re-introduced the proposal by the Northern Kentucky Area
Planning Commission to conduct a “Downtown Independence Small Area Study” and
yielded the floor to Keith Logsdon of the Planning Commission. Mr. Logsdon
reported the $13,000 the Planning Commission would contribute for this project
had to be specifically used for the market/economic analysis portion of the
study and could not be used for the land use study. He stated the funds would
not have to be allocated right away, but it would be necessary to begin the
process of selecting a private consultant that would work with the NKAPC staff
on the land use plan. Mayor Moriconi advised that the City could begin the

Proposed Ordinance - Hickory Valley Subdivision – Amendment to Ordinance No.
2005-O-02
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2005-O-02. The proposed amendment would change condition
number five, under Section I, that currently requires a brick wrap on the first
floor of all dwelling units. Mr. Tim Reese of Centerline Development requested
that condition five be amended to require a brick front, with only certain lots
being required to have a first floor brick wrap. He stated this request was
being made at the urging of several builders in the development, who feel this
requirement significantly increases the cost of the houses and noted that many
homebuyers would prefer to add other amenities rather than a brick wrap. Mayor
Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to read the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Kelso moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-12, seconded by
Council Member Cobble. A discussion ensued. Mr. Reese distributed photos of
houses with both brick fronts and brick wraps. Council Members voiced their
concerns about rescinding a condition of this development that has been imposed
on other developments as well; and shared their concern that if this request
was granted that other developers would make the same request of the City.
Other issues discussed were lot sizes, the connector street to the adjoining
subdivision that does not have the brick wrap as a condition of the
development, and adhering to building standards the City has put in place.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi asked the Clerk to call the
roll. Roll was called and answered with two ayes cast by Council Members Kelso
and Cobble, and four nays cast by Council Members Cook, Franzen, Little and
Yeager. Motion was defeated 2-4 and Ordinance No. 2006-O-12 was not enacted.
