July 24, 2006
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING MINUTES
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, July 24,2006 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center, 5409
Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook,
Carol Franzen, Kent Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
§   Resolution No. 2006-R-11 – Authorizing and Approving an Interlocal
Agreement with the Sanitation District No. 1 Transferring the Fowler Creek
Sewer System Along with All Associated Funds
§   Ordinance No. 2006-O- 16 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Relating to
Retirement Communities – 2nd Reading
§   Ordinance No. 2006-O-17 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Day
Care Facilities as a Permitted Use in the NC Zone – 2nd Reading
Resolution No. 2006-R-11 – Authorizing and Approving an Interlocal Agreement
with the Sanitation District No. 1 Transferring the Fowler Creek Sewer System
and Associated Funds
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2006-R-11 that would
authorize and approve an Interlocal Agreement with the Sanitation District
whereby the Fowler Creek Sewer System is transferred to the District along with
the associated funds, with the District assuming the responsibility for the
bond obligations. Mayor Moriconi read a prepared statement (attached herewith)
wherein he stated this proposed Agreement is the result of several months of
discussions with the District officials that would offer the City an
opportunity to transfer full ownership of the sewer system to the District
along with the responsibility of the remaining debt of the Fowler Creek Sewer
System. He stated the city would continue to collect the assessment and remit
the funds to the District for repayment of the debt and the District would
agree to make the final bond payment on this project. Mayor Moriconi stated he
is excited about this proposed Agreement as he feels this is a win-win
situation for everyone. He introduced Mr. Jeff Eger, General Manager of
Sanitation District No. 1.
Mr. Eger provided some history on the 1998 Lease/Merger Agreement with the City
wherein the District agreed to lease the sanitary sewer system from the City
while the City maintained ownership and the outstanding bond debt on the Fowler
Creek Sewer System. He also mentioned the GRW Report debt obligation and
initial estimate of $203,220 as the city’s share. He indicated that during the
last several years the District has spent an approximate $4,000,000 in
infrastructure improvements. Mr. Eger stated the Independence lines drain into
the Lakeview Pump Station, which is one of the largest in the District and will
require upgrades to handle the growing community. He stated a conservative
estimate would be several million dollars. Mr. Eger stated that he feels the
District can offer continuity in the handling of the debt, unlike the City
which often experiences changes in leadership. Mr. Eger stated that the current
schedule for the payoff of the debt is the year 2023, but he believes that the
District will be able to pay it off several years earlier than that.
Mayor Moriconi stated that by entering into this Agreement with the District
the city will be 99% out of the sewer business; the 1% being that the City will
collect and remit the Fowler Creek Sewer assessment for the District. Mr. Eger
commented that the City’s continuation of the billing will allow the residents
to escrow this assessment each year.
Council Member Cobble asked Mr. Eger to elaborate on how the District would use
the sewer funds the City would relinquish. Mr. Eger stated the District would
upsize the lines to the Lakeview Pump Station, and also extend present lines,
perhaps to the Courthouse Estates subdivision and Peach Drive areas. He stated
that due to the dynamic growth that Independence is experiencing it is hard to
be specific as more pressing needs may come along, so the District would need
to prioritize the projects.
Further discussion centered on maintenance fees collected and the city’s
outstanding balance of the GRW Study obligation. Mr. Eger also advised Council
that one of the conditions of the 1998 Agreement - wherein the District
provides the City a $300 share for each tap-in permit issued - will expire in
2008. Also discussed was future growth and providing sanitary sewer service to
pocket areas throughout the city.
Mr. Deters advised Council the Agreement would still require the approval of
the Sanitation District Board and the Kentucky Division of Water. Council
Member Cook asked if the City would continue to file liens on the properties
being assessed the debt reduction. Mr. Deters replied that the District would
notify the city of the new tie-ins and he would file the liens. Council Member
Cobble expressed some concern about the City absorbing the cost of filing the
liens. Mr. Deters said that the liens could be bunched together when filing to
keep the cost minimal.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to read
Resolution No. 2006-R-11. Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Resolution No.
2006-R-11, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered
with four ayes and two nays cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion
carried 4-2.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-16 – Approving a Text Amendment Relating to Retirement
Communities – KCPC Application No. 1807R – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2006-O-16 that
would approve a zoning text amendment relating to the establishment and
regulation of a retirement community zone. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2006-
O-16.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-16, seconded by
Council Member Kelso. A brief discussion ensued wherein Council Member Cobble
voiced her objection to the language in Section D that grants final approval of
the Stage II development plan to the legislative body. She expressed concern
about potential litigation against the city, however, the city attorney made it
clear that it would be more of a potential that the ordinance would be thrown
out as opposed to monetary damages being sought. She went on to say that she
felt the legislative body, by assuming this role, would jeopardize the city,
because it was stated in previous meetings by both Mr. Deters and Mr. Schwartz
of the Planning Commission that it was highly inappropriate for the legislative
body to assume this role as it should be an administrative function of the
Planning Commission staff.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered with four ayes
and two no votes cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Motion carried 4-2.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-17 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Day
Care Facilities as a Permitted Use in the NC Zone – KCPC Application No. 1818R
– 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2006-O-17 approving
a text amendment to the zoning ordinance adding day care facilities to the list
of permitted uses within the NC (neighborhood commercial) zone. Mr. Deters read
Ordinance No. 2006-O-17.
Council Member Kelso moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-17 seconded by Council
Member Cobble. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no vote cast
by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 5-1.
Executive Session
At 7:35 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to enter into an executive session to
discuss pending litigation in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c), seconded by
Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 8:07 p.m., Council Member Kelso moved to return to reconvene the regular
session, seconded by Council Member Cobble. Motion carried with all ayes.
Update on County Road Maintenance Issue
Mayor Moriconi announced that the Council discussed the judge’s ruling on the
city lawsuit against the county. He stated the city looks forward to a quick
resolution of this issue and has directed the city attorney to contact the
county attorney to discuss the possibility of an out-of-court agreement.
Adjournment
Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to adjourn the special meeting. Council
Member Cobble so moved, seconded by Council Member Kelso. Motion carried with
all ayes and the meeting ended at 8:08 p.m.

Lisa Placke, 112 McCullum Road, Independence – submitted to council photographs
of ––––McCullum Road––. She stated the photos show the damaged roadway which
has been caused by the heavy construction vehicles making improvements to the

Sandy Woolum, 4880 Justice Lane, Independence – addressed Council with her
request to waive a sidewalk lien on her daughter’s property on Justice Lane.
She stated that the city’s building inspector will not issue the Certificate of
Occupancy for her daughter’s new house until the notice of lien is signed. Ms.
Woolum feels her daughter should not have to sign a lien, as she feels there
are legitimate reasons that would permit the city to grant a waiver. She stated

Peggy Justice – ––––36 Fleming Drive–, ––Independence – addressed Council

the debt would be retired.
Jim Bertram, 5290 Madison Pike, Independence, - Mr. Bertram addressed Council
regarding two issues. He stated that his development site on Carol Ann Drive is
being delayed as he needs a decision from either the Kenton County Fiscal Court
or the City regarding the Cody Road situation. He stated that he has two
development plans ready; one that would develop the site based on Cody Road
being closed and the other based on realigning the road and keeping it open to
through traffic. He said he cannot make application to the Planning Commission
until the city and/or county make a decision on whether to realign or close the
road. He stated he has approached the County regarding this issue and their
position is that Cody Road is a city maintained street and therefore the City
must decide. He stated he feels the Carol Ann Drive development is “caught in
limbo” and is looking for some guidance from the City on how best to proceed. A
lengthy discussion ensued. Some Council Members expressed concern on taking any
action with regard to Cody Road as it is one of the streets that are part of
the lawsuit the City has filed against the County regarding maintenance of
county roads that run through incorporated areas of Independence. Council
advised Mr. Bertram did not want to take any action at this time regarding Cody
Road that might jeopardize the lawsuit.
Mr. Bertram stated his other issue that he needed help with was the Stage II
development plan for the Independence Village. He stated that he would like the
City to approach the State Highway Department with a request to install a
temporary traffic light at the intersection of Centennial Drive across from the
Kroger’s access road. He stated he is aware the State has agreed to install a
permanent light after the new section of SR 17 is open for traffic, but the
intersection is already experiencing heavy traffic flow, especially during
school bus hours. He advised that the State is also running about 6-8 months
behind schedule on the construction of SR 17 and it could be Spring 2008 before
the road is completed. He requested the City submit a resolution to the State
supporting a temporary traffic light at this location.
Council Member Cobble moved to have the city attorney draft a Resolution to
request the State to install a temporary traffic light at the intersection of
Centennial Blvd. and Madison Pike, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion
carried with all ayes.
Linda Skelton, 10437 Sharpsburg Drive, Independence – addressed Council
regarding several lots on their street that have been neglected by the
builders. She stated the construction of the houses is not complete and the
lots are overgrown with vegetation and strewn with building debris. Mr. Deters
advised the city must send notice to the owner of record and then if no action
is taken the City can go in and clean up the properties. Ms. Skelton also
advised that their street does not have street lights installed yet and
wondered who was responsible for this. Mayor Moriconi advised the developer was
responsible to install the lights and would have city staff check into this.

Minutes of August 28, 2006
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, August 28,2006 at 6:30 pm in the Independence Municipal Center, 5409
Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Carol Franzen,
Kent Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Council Member Margaret Cook was
absent. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
1.   Ratify Stage II Development Plan for Independence Village (Walgreen’s)
2.   Cody Road – Discuss road improvements as it relates to the Development
Plan by One Eleven Engineers for ––––Carole Ann Lane––
3.   Ordinance No. 2006-O-18 – Text Amendment Relating to Fences – 2nd Reading
4.   Ordinance No. 2006-O-19 – Establishing a Trash Assessment Rate for 2006 &
2007 – 2nd Reading
5.   Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2006 Tax Rates for Real and Tangible
Property – 1st Reading
6.   Resolution No. 2006-R-13 Supporting the early Installation of a Traffic
Light on SR 17 at the Intersection with Declaration Drive
7.   Personnel Appointment
8.   Executive Session (if necessary)
Ratify Stage II Development Plan for Independence Village (Walgreen’s) for an
Approximate 2.1 Acre area located at the Southeast Corner of the Intersection
of Madison Pike with Proposed Centennial Blvd. (NKAPC No. Z-06-06-02/1821R)
Mayor Moriconi directed Council to the correspondence from the NKAPC
recommending approval of the Amended Stage II development plan for the
Independence Village (Walgreen’s site) subject to three conditions. He stated
Mr. Jim Bertram was present to answer any questions. Mr. Bertram asked Council
to waive condition number three which would only permit one forty square foot
sign. Council Member Cobble commented that she did not feel the signage and
landscape conditions recommended by the Planning Commission would be consistent
in this area of development. Therefore, Council Member Cobble moved to approve
the Independence Village Stage II development plan for the Walgreen’s site and
waiving the landscaping and sign conditions (Number 1 and 3). Council Member
Franzen seconded the motion.
A discussion ensued. Mr. Bertram presented a rendering of the Walgreen’s
signage for Council to review. He advised Council that Walgreen’s stores have
signage on two sides of the building, therefore they were requesting 159 square
feet of signage for both the north and west elevations and consisted of four
signs on those elevations of the building. Council also discussed condition
number one, which required a minimum of five percent interior landscaping be
provided. Mr. Bertram stated the adjacent property is no longer zoned
residential and therefore he feels the landscaping condition is not necessary.
Council Member Yeager expressed her concern that the city would open a
Pandora’s Box by permitting the larger signs in a PUD zone. There being no
further discussion, roll was called and answered with four ayes and one no vote
cast by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried 4-1.
Cody Road – Discussion or Road Improvements as it Relates to the Development
Plan by One Eleven Engineers for ––––Carole Ann Lane
Mr. Jim Bertram of One Eleven Engineers addressed Council regarding the road
improvements for Cody Road. He stated he is ready to begin development and is
preparing to submit a development plan and he would like some direction from
the City regarding Cody Road and whether it will be closed or remain open to
through traffic. Council Member Cobble suggested the city hold a public hearing
to get citizen input on whether or not the city should close the road. Mr.
Bertram asked if the city was assuming jurisdiction of Cody Road. Mr. Deters
replied yes. A brief discussion ensued and the consensus of the Council was to
keep Cody Road open. Mr. Bertram stated as part of his development plan for
Carole Ann Lane he will design a new alignment for Cody Road.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-18 – Text Amendment Relating to Fences – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2006-O-
18 that would approve a zoning text amendment amending the height and location
of fences within residential zones. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2006-O-18 a
second reading.
A discussion ensued. Council Member Little expressed concern that this
ordinance was a tool to bring properties into compliance that are currently in
violation. He stated he would like the Board of Adjustment members to provide
the Council with a formal recommendation and their reason for the
recommendation. Mayor Moriconi advised that he has spoken with some of the
Board members who stated they did not understand the basis of the current
ordinance which limits the locations of fences on corner lots. Mr. Deters
commented that the Board reaches their decisions based on current ordinances
and they requested the city apply for the text amendment. He said the Board has
had several non-compliance cases come before them and they have been upholding
the ordinance, but see no rationalization in the current ordinance. Council
Member Cobble stated there is concern of obstructed view for vehicles. Further
discussion ended in a Council consensus to request input from the Board members
as to why they don’t grant a variance.
Council Member Franzen moved to table the adoption of Ordinance No. 2006-O-18
until they hear from the Board of Adjustment members on this issue, seconded by
Council Member Little. No roll call; motion carried with all ayes.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-19 – Establishing a Trash Assessment Rate for 2006 & 2007
– 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented Ordinance No. 2006-O-19 for a second reading. This
ordinance would establish the trash assessment rate for 2006 and 2007. Mr.
Deters gave the ordinance a second reading.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-19, seconded by
Council Member Cobble. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2006 Tax Rates for Real & Tangible Property – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance adopting the
2006 tax rates for real and tangible properties. A brief discussion centered on
the compensating tax rate that had been calculated at .185 for real property
and .662 for tangible property. The consensus of Council was that the rates
seemed high and that the rates should have decreased not increased and that
keeping the 2005 rates would still provide an increase in revenue for the city.
Council Member Little moved to maintain the 2005 tax rate of .177 for real
property for the 2006 tax year, seconded by Council Member Cobble. Roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0
Council Member Franzen moved to maintain the 2005 tax rate of .578 for tangible
property for the 2006 tax year, seconded by Council Member Yeager. A brief
discussion ensued which resulted in Council Member Little amending his original
motion and Council Member Cobble amending her original second to include
maintaining the 2005 tax rate of .578 for tangible property for the 2006 tax
year. Council Members Franzen and Yeager withdrew their motion and second. Roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0. Mr. Deters read the
proposed ordinance.
Resolution No. 2006-R-13 – Supporting the early Installation of a Traffic Light
on SR 17 at Centennial Drive
Mayor Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2006-R-13 supporting the early
installation of a traffic light on SR 17 at Centennial Drive. Council Member
Cobble moved to approve Resolution No. 2006-R-13, seconded by Council Member
Franzen. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2006-R-13. No roll call; motion carried
with all ayes.
Municipal Order 2006-MO-04 – Approving Appointment of Shawn Butler as Chief of
Police
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Municipal Order No. 2006-MO-04 that would
approve his appointment of Shawn Butler as Chief of Police. Council Member
Franzen moved to approve Municipal Order No. 2006-MO-04, seconded by Council
Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Cobble moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:25 p.m.

September 18, 2006
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
18, 2006 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Kent
Kelso, Mike Little, and Donna Yeager. City Attorney, Jed K. Deters was also
present.
Approval of the August 7, 2006 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the August 7, 2006
council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by Council Member
Cobble. There being no amendments, roll was called and answered unanimously;
motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the August 28, 2006 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the Special
Council meeting held on August 28, 2006. Council Member Yeager so moved, with
second by Council Member Franzen. Amendments were noted by Council Members
Cobble and Yeager. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no vote
cast by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 5-1.
Privileges of the Floor
Tom Spurlock, 580 Skyway Drive, Independence – addressed the Council with a
request to close the portion of Skyway Drive that runs from Sugar Tree Drive to
the Blau property. He stated he built his house in 1959 and put in a gravel
driveway back to their house. He stated he would like the street permanently
closed as he has concerns this could become a thoroughfare for planned
development that adjoins his property. A discussion with Council ensued. Mr.
Deters explained the process to close a public right of way. He stated that Mr.
Spurlock has provided the City with letters from two adjoining property owners
who stated they have no objections to closing the street. In closing, Council
requested that Mr. Spurlock speak to the developer of the Blau property to get
his consent in closing the street. Mr. Deters stated if all the adjoining
property owners consent to closing the street, then the City could do so by
ordinance.
Brett Ross, 720 Independence Station Road, Independence - addressed Council on
behalf of the South Kenton Lions Football League, regarding a letter sent to
them by the City’s Recreation Director, Nita Brake. He stated the letter
concerned trash left in Memorial Park after the football practices. He stated
their organization has used the field for nine years and that they appreciate
the use of the park and do not want to lose this facility. He said they pickup
the park area after each practice, seed the field every year at their expense
and always work hard to keep it well maintained. Mayor Moriconi stated the
letter was sent after receiving numerous complaints from the City’s Public
Services personnel who stated they are spending a lot of time cleaning up the
field after the practices. He assured Mr. Ross the Football League would not be
prohibited from using the field.
Glenna Faulkner, 22 Carrie Way, Independence – addressed Council with a
complaint that a resident that lives on Madison Pike has been parking his
vehicle on ––––Carrie Way–– adjacent to the Swindler & Currin Funeral Home. She
stated the truck is parked in close proximity to the stop sign at the
intersection of ––––Carrie Way–– and Madison Pike and feels this is a safety
issue. Council Member Cook submitted a three page petition (attached to these
minutes) signed by residents of Carrie Way and Cheyenne Court who are
requesting a No Parking sign be erected to prohibit parking from 21 Carrie Way
to the intersection with Madison Pike. After a brief discussion, it was decided
that the city attorney would draft an ordinance that would prohibit parking in
this specific area and that it would be presented at the next meeting.
Interlocal Agreement with NKAPC for Downtown Small Area Study
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council an Interlocal Agreement with the NKAPC for
the Independence Downtown Small Area Study. He stated Mr. Keith Logsdon would
answer any questions they might have regarding the Agreement. A discussion
ensued with Council Member Cobble sharing her comments regarding the Market
Analysis; she stressed that recently the NKAPC has been remiss in requiring the
developers to comply with the existing zoning ordinance that states a market
analysis must be made to justify the need for commercial uses in a PUD zone
that are intended primarily for the service and convenience of the residents in
the permitted project area. She stated that since the developer of the
Independence Village was not required to conduct a market analysis, the city is
now engaging in a contract to do so. She state that she does not feel it is
right to stick the bill to the taxpayers. . She also expressed concern that
zone changes would be recommended and she did not want to see the City force
zone changes on the residents in the study area. Council Member Little
commented that this study was a larger project than just zoning recommendations
and would include other items of focus. Further discussion included development
possibilities along the new section of SR 17 and the parameters of the study
area. Mr. Logsdon advised they would focus on a five to eight mile area.
Council Member Franzen commented she feels the City cannot continue to ‘piece-
meal’ development and a professional planning firm would make recommendations
the City could use in making good decisions.
Mr. Logsdon stated there would be key components of this study, including
citizen input, which will result with actual implementation strategies the City
can use in the future. Mr. Logsdon went on to introduce the project team
members: Clete Benkin and Sukirti Ghosh with the professional planning firm of
Kinzelman Kline Gossman (KKG), Doug Harnish of GEM and Paul Sloan with URS
Corporation.
Mayor Moriconi asked for a motion to authorize him to execute the Interlocal
Agreement with the NKAPC to proceed with the study. Council Member Franzen so
moved, seconded by Council Member Kelso. Roll was called and answered with four
ayes and two no votes cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Council Member
Cobble clarified her vote by stating she objected to the taxpayers footing the
bill for this project.
Contract with KKG Professional Planning Firm for Downtown Small Area Study
Project
Mayor Moriconi advised that the professional planning firm of Kinzelman Kline
Gossman (KKG) has been selected to be the consultant for the Downtown Small
Area Study. Mr. Clete Benkin addressed Council by stating there will continue
to be more development pressure in the future and now is a good time for the
City to forecast ahead and protect the City’s identity. He stated this study
will cast a wide net and will consider surrounding influences outside the scope
of the study area. Mr. Paul Sloan stated he is a Senior Transportation Engineer
with URS Corporation. He stated he has worked extensively in transportation
planning on SR 536 and SR 17 redevelopment plans.
A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Cobble expressed concern that the
city did not have jurisdiction over the state routes within the city limits,
some of which are in the study area. Council Member Cobble also stated she
objected to spending public funds for this study.
There being no further comments or discussion, Mayor Moriconi entertained a
motion to authorize him to execute the contract with KKG for their consulting
services on the Downtown Small Area Study. Council Member Franzen so moved,
with second by Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered with four
ayes and two no votes cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Council Member
Cobble clarified her vote by stating she felt this was a waste of taxpayer’s
money.
Proposed Street Name Changes by NKAPC – ––––Bristow Road–– Area
Emalee Listermann of the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission addressed
Council with a request to consider renaming the remnants of roadway created by
the reconstruction of Bristow Road. She stated emergency services are having
difficulty in locating some of the addresses. She stated that NKAPC is
suggesting the following possible solutions to resolve this situation.
1.   Rename the old Bristow section to Battleridge Drive where it aligns with
same. This would also require the renumbering of the residences currently on
the old Bristow section.
2.   Rename the old Bristow section to something else entirely. NKAPC would
coordinate with the city to identify three options for a new street name and
then send a questionnaire to each resident that would be affected advising them
of their choices for a new street name. They would then compile the results and
announce the street name that received the most votes.
There was a brief discussion which resulted in Mr. Logsdon stating he would
discuss the matter further with Scott Hiles at his office and get back to
Council.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-18 – Text Amendment Relating to Height & Location of

reconsideration, after this Ordinance was tabled at the August 28, 2006 special

Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2006-O-18 a second reading. Council Member Kelso

Brinker, a member of the Board of Adjustments, was in attendance and advised
Council that the Board has been enforcing the current ordinance, but could not
understand the reason that it exists. Mayor Moriconi stated the Kenton County
Planning Commission has recommended approval to make this change that would
allow a corner lot to extend the fences in the rear yards. There being no
further discussion, roll was called and answered with four ayes and two no
votes cast by Council Members Cobble and Cook. Council Member Cobble clarified
her vote by saying she feels that extending the corner lots fences could be a
traffic safety issue.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-20 – Adopting 2006 Property Tax Rates – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2006-O-
20, an ordinance that would adopt the real and personal 2006 property tax
rates. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a second reading. There was no discussion.

October 2, 2006
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
2, 2006 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: JoAnne Cobble, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike
Little, and Donna Yeager. Council Member Kent Kelso was absent. City Attorney,
Jed K. Deters was also present.
Approval of the September 18, 2006 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the September 18,
2006 council meeting. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by Council
Member Yeager. Amendments by Council Member Cobble were noted; roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi announced that no one signed in to address the Council.
Award Bid for Production Drive Repairs
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received for the
Production Drive Resurfacing Project. Bids were received from six contractors.
Mayor Moriconi stated that Len Riegler Blacktop was the low bid at $95,422.00.
There was a brief discussion, after which a motion was made by Council Member
Cobble and seconded by Council Member Little to accept the recommendation of
the City Engineer to award the bid to the low bidder, Len Riegler Blacktop.

Proposed Ordinance – Relating to a Request for a Map Amendment for an
Approximate 2-Acre Area Located Along the East Side of New SR 17 Approximately
900 Feet North of Harris Pike from R-1C to NC – KCPC Application No. 1837R –
1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council proposed ordinances – one to approve and
one to deny – a map amendment for an approximate two-acre area located along
the east side of new SR 17, approximately 900 feet north of Harris Pike that
would change the zone from R-1C to NC. Mayor Moriconi asked Council if they had
any questions. Council Member Franzen expressed concern that the applicant –
One Eleven Engineering – was not present to present their request. She
suggested postponing this matter until they could be present. Mr. Deters
advised that was not an option as the City has to act within ninety days of
receiving the recommendation from the Planning Commission. He went on to say
that the City really has four options: 1) do nothing and it passes by operation
of law within ninety days, 2) to approve the ordinance and it passes by
operation of law within ninety days, 3) to review the transcript of the public
hearing held by the Planning Commission, which was included in this meetings’
packet, and reach different conclusions and deny it, and 4) the City could hold
it’s own public hearing and reach different conclusions and deny it. Mr. Deters
advised Council the ninety day period will expire on December 6, 2006 so the
City will need to take action to either deny or approve the zone change request
before then or it will automatically pass by operation of law. In closing, he
advised Council they would need to decide whether they wanted to approve or
deny this and have a first reading of the appropriate ordinance.
Council Member Little commented that based on reading the transcript of the
public hearing and the NKAPC staff recommendation wherein the staff expressed
concerns with the landscape screening where commercial and residential zones
adjoin, the lighting of off-street parking areas onto adjacent property, the
number of off-street parking spaces and the lack of information regarding
signage, he is inclined to feel there is not sufficient information to approve
this request. Based on this, Council Member Little made a motion to deny the
request for this map amendment and do a reading on the proposed ordinance to
deny this map amendment. Council Member Yeager seconded the motion. Mayor
Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to read the proposed ordinance to deny the KCPC
recommendation (1837R) that would approve the map amendment. Mr. Deters read
the proposed ordinance. Roll was called and answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 4-0.

November 27, 2006
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, November 27,2006 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky. City Clerk Patricia Taney announced
that Mayor Christian J. Moriconi would not be present for this meeting and
stated city Ordinance No. 2005-O-04, Section 2.14 on Replacement of Presiding
Officer, directs that the Council Member who received the most votes in the
last election shall serve as Mayor Pro Tem and preside at meetings in the
Mayor’s absence, but may decline the Chair and request the Council to select
another Council Member to preside. Ms. Taney advised Council the Mayor Pro Tem
is Council Member Donna Yeager and that she has declined to Chair the meeting
and desires the Council to select another Member to preside at this meeting.
Motion was made by Council Member Franzen to have Council Member Kelso, as
resident Parliamentarian, to Chair the meeting. Council Member Yeager seconded
the motion. Roll was called and answered with four ayes and one no vote cast by
Council Member Cook. Motion carried and Council Member Kelso took the Chair’s
seat. Prior to beginning the meeting, Chairman Kelso led with the Pledge of
Allegiance. Chairman Kelso called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen,
Kent Kelso, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Council Member JoAnne Cobble was
absent. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Chairman Kelso announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss and take action on the following agenda items:
·   Presentation of the November 20, 2006 council meeting minutes for approval
·   Ordinance No. 2006-O-22 – Setting Dates and Times of Regular City Council
Meetings – Discussion and Possible Action for a second reading of the Ordinance
·   Ordinance No. 2006-O-23 – Map Amendment on an Approximate 2-Acre Site
Located along the east side of the New section of SR 17 approximately 900 feet
north of Harris Pike from R-1C to NC – KCPC Application No. 1837R – Discussion
and Possible Action for a second reading of the Ordinance
·   Discussion and Possible Action to Ratify the Recommendation from NKAPC for
Stage II Development Plan for Bristow Village
·   Discussion and Possible Action Relating to the Interlocal Agreement with
Sanitation District No. 1
Approval of the Minutes of the November 20, 2006 Council Meeting
Council Member Cook questioned why the minutes were being presented at a
Special meeting when in the past were usually presented for approval at the
regular meetings. The City Clerk stated she thought it would be logical to
present the minutes at this meeting since it was nearing the end of the year as
well as terms of office for half of the Council. Council Member Cook made a
motion to table approval of the November 20, 2006 council meeting minutes,
seconded by Council Member Kelso. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Deters advised
that he is not aware of any prohibition against the approval of the minutes
being placed on a Special meeting agenda. No roll was called; motion failed
with two ayes and three nays.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve the minutes of the November 20, 2006
council meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. No roll was called; motion

Ordinance No. 2006-O-22 - Setting Dates and Times of Regular City Council
Meetings – 2nd Reading
Chairman Kelso presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2006-O-22. Mr.
Deters read Ordinance No. 2006-O-22 which modified the regular meeting schedule
of the City Council effectively continuing the first Monday meeting and
eliminating the meeting on the third Monday of each month.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-22, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. A brief discussion ensued wherein Council Member
Franzen asked Mr. Deters if the schedule could be amended at any time to resume
two regular meetings per month if it was deemed necessary by the Council. Mr.
Deters advised that at any time, the Council could amend the Ordinance if they
felt it was necessary. Roll was called and answered with four ayes and one no
vote cast by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 4-1.
Ordinance No. 2006-O-23 – Denying a Map Amendment for 2-Acre Site Located Along
the East side of the New SR 17 approximately 900 Feet north of Harris Pike from
R-1C to NC – KCPC Application No. 1837R – 2nd Reading
Chairman Kelso presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would
deny the recommendation of the KCPC (Application No. 1837R) to approve a zoning
map amendment for an approximate two-acre site located along the east side of
the new SR 17 approximately 900 feet north of Harris Pike. Mr. Deters gave
Ordinance No. 2006-O-23 a second reading.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2006-O-23, seconded by
Council Member Little. Chairman Kelso opened the floor for discussion. Mr.
Bertram of One-Eleven Engineering and Surveying addressed concerns Council
Member Yeager had with the five exceptions to the plan’s minimum requirements
that are noted in the recommendation from the Planning Commission. Mr. Bertram
went through each exception noted in section three of the recommendation and
agreed to the following:
a.   Landscape screening – He stated they will comply and provide screening
along the property line which abuts any R-1 zoning – he stated he is aware of
the requirement and will adhere to it.
b.   Parking Spaces – He stated they know they are a little lacking in having
the adequate number of parking spaces, so they will probably reduce the size of
the building to meet that zoning requirement and will supply the number of
spaces needed for the commercial use.
c.   Lighting of Off Street Parking Lots –Mr. Bertram advised they will keep
the lighting of the off street parking areas on their property, as there are
ways to do that, and stated this is usually handled at the Stage II Plan and
assured Council they will comply to the city zoning regarding lighting
regulations.
d.   Off Street parking – will adhere to that
e.   Sign Regulations – will adhere to the NC signs. Mr. Bertram stated that it
is hard to determine in the Stage I plan what will be on that sign, so this is
usually handled in Stage II. He stated they are aware of that and assured
council the signs will adhere to the city’s sign regulations.
He advised the original development plan submitted was a concept and as the
development progresses into Stage II that is when all the details are outlined.
He stated they would not circumvent the city’s zoning ordinance and that it is
typical for the details to be inserted as the Stage II development plan
evolves. He stated they will also provide an ingress/egress easement to the
adjoining property in order to limit the number of curb cuts onto SR17. (Mr.
Bertram presented a map to the Council to review.) He stated a 4-way
intersection would be constructed in this area. He also advised Council that
this particular two-acre parcel is sold.
Chairman Kelso stated that some of Council’s concerns at the last meeting were
how this development would affect the Downtown Small Area Study which the City
is currently conducting. Mr. Bertram stated that the application for this
development plan was submitted prior to the City initiating the Small Area
Study and he feels this plan should be grandfathered in and should not be an
issue.
Council Member Franzen asked if the ordinance is voted down and the KCPC
recommendation stood firm would this development still be required to meet the
City’s zoning ordinance requirements. Chairman Kelso said that was correct.
Council Member Franzen commented that she isn’t too concerned about the effect
this development will have on the Downtown Small Area Study as this is a just a
continuation of the plan the City approved two years ago. Chairman Kelso
advised the City has to act on this recommendation no later than December 6 or
the KCPC recommendation will go into effect.
There being no further discussion, Chairman Kelso advised Council that a vote
in favor of this ordinance would effectively kill the zone change and a vote
against this ordinance could result in going with the recommendation to the
KCPC, roll was called and answered with four nays and one yes vote cast by
Council Member Little. The motion was defeated 4-1 and the ordinance was not
adopted.
Bristow Village Stage II Development Plan – Discussion and Action to Ratify
Recommendation from NKAPC (Z-06-10-04/1852R)
Chairman Kelso presented to Council the Stage II Development Plan review for an
approximate 63 acre area located along the north side of Mount Zion Road,
approximately 800 feet west of Bristow Road.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to ratify NKAPC’s recommendation, seconded
by Council Member Little. Mr. Deters explained that the recommendation was to
disapprove the submitted development plan. Chairman Kelso asked Council Member
Franzen if she was aware that the recommendation was to disapprove. She stated
she overlooked that and asked why it has been recommended for disapproval.
Council asked Mr. Bertram to explain. He distributed site plan maps, both the
original and the proposed Stage II, for Council to review. Mr. Bertram advised
Council that the Planning Commission recommended disapproval based on the fact
that the interconnection to the adjoining subdivision and a pocket park was
eliminated from the original plan approved by the Planning Commission. He
stated this was an agreement with the adjoining property owners and the City
Council. He stated that when the Planning Commission made their recommendation
they were not aware that the city had approved the revisions from the original
development plan approved by the Planning Commission. He stated that the
signage and fencing plans are preliminary, but will be what the City requested
and approved during the original plan review. Mr. Bertram stated that if the
City agrees with the Planning Commission’s recommendation to disapprove, then
they will have to resubmit and this will delay the project which is currently
under construction.
Council Members Franzen and Little withdrew their motion and second. Council
Member Franzen moved to approve the Stage II Plan as presented and based on the
conditions that the street stub be removed, brick wrap be included, fences and
signage be provided as well as all other conditions as stated on the original
development plan as agreed upon by the City. Roll was not called; but the
motion passed by a vote of four ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member
Cook.
Interlocal Agreement with Sanitation District No. 1
Chairman Kelso presented to Council for consideration the amended Interlocal
Agreement with the Sanitation District for the transfer of the City’s sanitary
sewer system along with related funds and debt obligations under the bond
indenture issued by the City. Mr. Deters advised that this Agreement was
originally sent to the Sanitation District some months ago and after reviewing
it have added another condition to the closing of the transaction; that
condition being, that “Filing of a final and unappealled judgment in the case
of William Cobble, et al vs the City, et al, Kenton Circuit Court, Case No. 06-
CI-01975, dismissing the claims of Plaintiffs, and under such other terms as
are satisfactory to District.”
Council Member Yeager made a motion to ratify the amendment to the Agreement,
seconded by Council Member Franzen. There was a brief discussion. No roll
called; motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Little moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:43 p.m.

2007 Minutes
January 3, 2007
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Wednesday, January 3, 2007 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then called the
meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters. Mayor Moriconi announced
that a quorum was present for this special meeting regarding the six items
posted on the Agenda. He welcomed everyone to the first meeting of 2007.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
·   Accept the resignation of Council Member-Elect Jeb Holbrook with discussion
and possible action to appoint a new Council Member to fill the Vacancy
·   Request by Bill Roberts to support a zoning text amendment to add a used
car lot as a conditional use in the Neighborhood Commercial Zone
·   Resolution No. 2007-R-01 Disapproving the Proposed location of the New
Kenton County Jail
·   Discussion and Possible Action relating to the “Intent to Annex” the future
site of the new Kenton County Jail
·   Meadow Glen Subdivision Stage II Development Plan – Ratify Recommendation
from NKAPC
·   Independence Village Stage II Development Plan – Ratify Recommendation from
NKAPC for the 1.0 Acre site for the new National City Bank
Mayor Moriconi stated that he would modify the order of the Agenda items to
begin with Resolution No. 2007-R-01 and then the discussion relating to the
possible annexation of the future site of the Kenton County jail. No objections
were voiced from the Council Members.
Resolution No. 2007-R-01 – Disapproving the Proposed Location of the new Kenton
County Jail
Mayor Moriconi read Resolution No. 2007-R-01 which disapproves the actions of
the Kenton County Fiscal Court relating to the site chosen for the construction
of a new jail to be located on the new section of SR 17 which is adjacent to
the incorporated areas of the City. Motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Behler to approve Resolution No. 2007-R-01. Roll
was called and answered unanimously; motion carried 5-0. The audience applauded
this action taken by the Council. Mayor Moriconi stated that a copy of this
Resolution would be forwarded to the Fiscal Court.
Discussion & Possible Action Relating to the Intent to Annex the Proposed
Location for the new Kenton County Jail
Mayor Moriconi advised that if the Jail would be constructed on the proposed
site, then the City could take a pro-active position by proceeding with
annexation of the property so that the City could reap some financial benefits
of collecting payroll taxes. He advised the revenue could be used to hire new
police officers. He anticipated that Council might want to direct the City
Attorney to draft an “Intent to Annex” ordinance to start this process. Since
an ordinance requires two readings, the first reading could be done in February
and the second reading in March. Council Member Yeager concurred and stated she
feels the land should be annexed even if the Jail is not constructed on the
site.
A discussion ensued regarding the annexation of the jail site and surrounding
areas. Mr. Deters suggested the City just deal with the jail site for now as
there are no homeowners involved that would file a remonstrance that would
cause the annexation to be put on the general election ballot. He suggested if
the city wanted to annex other areas along the new SR 17 that they do it as a
separate annexation. Mr. Deters went on to explain the process of annexation
and if more than 50 percent of the property owners challenge (protest) the
annexation then it would be put on the ballot.
There being no further discussion, Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion for the
Council to direct the City Attorney to draft an ordinance of the City’s intent
to annex this tract of land. Council Member Yeager so moved, seconded by
Council Member Bushong. Council Member Franzen and Council Member Behler
expressed concern that Covington would also attempt to annex the proposed jail
site. Mr. Deters stated that Covington was not contiguous with the jail site so
they would have to annex other parcels to reach the jail site. Roll was called
and answered unanimously; motion carried 5-0.
At this time Mayor Moriconi opened the floor to any citizens who wished to make
comments regarding the jail site.
Catherine Wilson, 10316 Savannah Court, Independence – expressed concern
regarding the expenses the City would incur by annexing the proposed jail site
versus the amount of revenue that would be generated with the collection of
payroll taxes from the jail. She wondered if it would be worth it.
Mayor Moriconi advised the revenue would be based on the number of jail
employees, but he has heard that payroll taxes could be between $30,000 -
$50,000 per year and if the jail expands this amount could go as high as
$80,000 per year. He said the Fiscal Court would be exempt from paying property
taxes. Mr. Deters advised that the city expenses associated with the annexation
would be approximately $2,000 for surveying the property, advertising, etc.
Council Member Franzen commented that Kenton County Jailer, Terry Carl, has
reported that his payroll budget is currently over $2,000,000.
Jason Riley, 4947 Open Meadow Drive (Harvest Hill Subdivision) – asked the
difference between a jail and a prison. Assistant Police Chief Dave Nichols
explained that both terms are interchangeable and have the same meaning.
Jean Schultz 6213 White Bark, Independence – asked if the annexation was a last
resort. She expressed concern that the City may not pursue trying to stop the
jail being constructed on the proposed site as she feels strongly that the jail
will have a negative impact on the community. Mayor Moriconi assured her that
the annexation is a preemptive and proactive move by the City and will be used
as a last resort. He stated the Fiscal Court has been receptive to listening to
everyone’s concerns and the City is not yet waiving a white flag. He added that
the City will continue to do everything possible, as he does not want to see a
jail/detention center the first thing you notice at the gateway to the City
along the new section of SR 17.
In closing, Mayor Moriconi advised that city officials have been receiving many
email messages from citizens that want to help. He thanked everyone and asked
that suggestions for other more suitable, viable sites for the jail be emailed
to him via the City website. He stated he feels it would be more effective if
he sends a list of the alternative sites to the Fiscal Court rather than the
Fiscal Court being inundated with numerous emails regarding this matter. He
stated he thinks the City is united on this issue and appreciates all the work
and support of the citizens.
Accept the Resignation of Council Member-Elect Jeb Holbrook with Discussion &
Possible Action to Appoint a New Council Member
Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to accept the resignation of Council
Member-Elect Jeb Holbrook. Council Member Behler so moved, with second by
Council Member Little. Mr. Deters advised this would not be effective until the
meeting following this meeting. Roll was called and answered unanimously;
motion carried 5-0.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters to explain the procedure for the City to fill
this vacancy on the Council. Mr. Deters explained there would not be a vacancy
until the next meeting as the state statute mandates that once the resignation
is tendered to the legislative body then it is effective at the next regular
meeting following that. He stated he feels the Council can go ahead and accept
the resignation and then proceed with filling the vacancy with an effective
date of the next meeting, as there is no statutory procedure mandating the
process by which the Council has to accomplish filling the vacated seat.
Council Member Little moved to nominate Tom Brinker as he was the next person
receiving the most ballots on the November 2006 general election and to make
this appointment effective at the next regular meeting of the Council. Council
Member Franzen seconded the motion. There was a brief discussion. Mr. Bushong
stated that the last time this situation occurred the Council did this in
Executive Session under the vote principle. Mr. Deters stated the last time
this occurred, it was not so close following a general election and the Council
decided to take applications and do a review and interview process. He stated
that Council Member Little is suggesting that since this vacancy has occurred
so close to the election that Council should just follow the will of the people
by selecting the person with the next highest votes. He advised that Council
does not have to take applications and go through the interview process.
Council Member Little stated that he feels the Council has a lot of business to
conduct and does not feel the need to prolong filling this vacancy. Council
Member Franzen asked Mr. Brinker, who was in the audience, if he was still
interested in taking the seat on Council. Mr. Brinker stated he was.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously;
motion carried 5-0. Mr. Deters advised this appointment should be made official
with an Order, which can be presented at the next meeting. He also advised that
Mr. Brinker can take the Oath of Office at the next meeting as well.
Request to Sponsor a Zoning Text Amendment Application to add Used Car Lots as
a Conditional Use in the NC (Neighborhood Commercial) Zones – Bill Roberts
Mayor Moriconi stated the City is being asked to sponsor an application for a
zoning text amendment that would permit used car lots in the NC (neighborhood
commercial) zones. He advised Council that currently our NC zone does not allow
car lots and reminded them to keep in mind that any text amendment would apply
city-wide for that zone. He stated that the council packets contained
information about Mr. Robert’s proposal for a used car lot he plans for
property located at 5061 Madison Pike, formerly known as “Fedders Feed and
Seed.” He opened the floor for Council discussion and questions of Gary and
Bill Roberts who are making this request. Council asked several questions and a
brief discussion ensued. Council Member Little expressed concern that the
property was not owned by the Roberts’. Council Member Behler reminded the
Council that the City adopted a Vision for the City in 2005 and that part of
the Vision was the City having an identity and establishing that identity was
to have nice signage at the various entries to the City and she questioned this
particular location as a good place for a used car lot. She stated that does
not deny the Roberts’ good intentions; she just does not feel the location they
have selected is the best place in the city for a used car lot.
A brief discussion ensued with Mr. Deters regarding the procedures of
sponsoring a zoning text amendment. Mr. Deters advised they could sponsor the
application and then the Planning Commission would make a recommendation to the
City which then the Council would approve or disapprove.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to sponsor a zoning text amendment
application to permit used car lots as a conditional use in the NC zones. There
being no second to her motion, the motion died for lack of a second.
Meadow Glen Subdivision Stage II Development Plan – Discussion and Possible
Action to Ratify the Recommendation from the NKAPC (Z-06-11-02/1854R)
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the recommendation from the NKAPC to
approve the Stage II development plan in the Meadow Glen Subdivision. Council
Member Little stated he was concerned with the language in Condition number two
(2) under the Recommendation to approve section on page four (4). He stated he
feels that allowing a Homeowner’s Association to be “established prior to, or
simultaneous with a subsequent final plat” is too much of a gray area. He
suggested deleting the words “or simultaneous with.” He stated this type of
gray area has presented problems in the past. Mr. Deters advised it is within
the City’s purview to change that language and approve this with the language
modification. Mayor Moriconi stated that this amendment to the development plan
is for the addition of a swimming pool and clubhouse, which was always the
intent of the developer, but somehow was erroneously omitted from the original
plat.
There being no further discussion Council Member Little moved to ratify the
recommendation from NKAPC to approve the Stage II Development Plan with the
deletion of the words “or simultaneous with” from Condition Number two (2).
Council Member Behler seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 5-0.
Independence Village Stage II Development Plan – Discussion and Possible Action
to Ratify the Recommendation from the NKAPC for the National City Bank site (Z-
06-11-05/1857R
Mayor Moriconi stated he was pulling this agenda item at the request of the
developer, National City Bank. The information was just received yesterday and
this will give the Council time to review. He stated representatives from
National City Bank will be at the next regular meeting to address this
development.
Executive Session
At 7:40 p.m. Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to move into an executive
session. Mr. Deters stated the executive session would be pursuant to KRS
61.810 1(c) to discuss pending litigation, specifically the road case with
Kenton County and to entertain a settlement proposal. Council Member Bushong so
moved, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of the meeting,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Mayor Moriconi announced that no action was taken in executive session.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Little moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:11 p.m.

February 5, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
5, 2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance
and then Council Member Bushong gave the invocation.
Municipal Order No. 2007-MO-01
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a Municipal Order that would prospectively
appoint Tom Brinker to the City Council to fill the vacancy of the unexpired
term of Jeb Holbrook. Mr. Deters read Municipal Order No. 2007-MO-01. Council
Member Yeager moved to adopt Municipal Order No. 2007-MO-01, seconded by
Council Member Bushong. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0.
Official Swearing In of Council Member Tom Brinker
City Attorney, Jed Deters performed the Swearing-In of Tom Brinker to the City
Council. Mr. Brinker took his seat at the Council bench.
Roll Call of Members
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat
Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters. Mayor Moriconi announced
that a quorum was present for this meeting and welcomed everyone.
Approval of the November 27, 2006 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the Special
meeting held on November 27, 2006. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
by Council Member Little. There being no amendments noted; roll was called and
answered with five ayes and one abstain cast by Council Member Brinker. Motion
carried 6-0.
Approval of the January 3, 2007 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the Special
meeting held on January 3, 2007. Council Member Behler so moved, with second by
Council Member Bushong. There being no amendments noted, roll was called and
answered with five ayes and one abstain cast by Council Member Brinker. Motion
carried 6-0.
Discussion with Kenton County Commissioners Regarding the Proposed Site for a
new Kenton County Jail
Mayor Moriconi welcomed Kenton County Commissioners Chris Knochelmann and Sara
Voelker and thanked them for attending the City meeting to share a dialogue
with the Council regarding the County’s plans to construct a new jail on the
new section of SR17 adjacent to the incorporated boundaries of the City. He
stated that a Committee of citizens have met and come up with a list of ten
questions they would like to pose to the Commissioners in an effort to learn of
the ’’’’Fiscal Court’’’s reasons for choosing the proposed site. Mayor Moriconi
thanked the citizens for all the time and input they have given in working on
this issue and submitting alternative sites for the Fiscal Court to consider.
For the next, approximate hour, Mayor Moriconi posed each question to
Commissioners Knochelmann and Voelker. The Commissioners were unable to give
definite answers to many of the questions since they just took office on
January 1, 2007. Mayor Moriconi announced that he spoke to Commissioner Dan
Humpert who wanted to attend this meeting, but was unable to due to a prior
commitment.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2006/07 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration a proposed
ordinance to amend the 2006/07 budget. In a memo attached to the amended budget
Mayor Moriconi outlined several key changes necessitating the amendment, those
being: $142,000 in police grants revenue, additional funds received from the
State to make repairs on Production Drive, $130,000 in revenue for sidewalk
grants, $86,500 expense for Downtown Small Area Study and $50,000 additional
street repairs to be done in the Spring, and department expenses for health
insurance were combined into one line item as a result of the city’s conversion
to a self-funded policy last September. He also pointed out that the City
currently has a healthy fund balance in excess of $1,939,000. There being no
discussion by Council, Mayor Moriconi directed the city attorney to give the
ordinance a first reading. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance to amend the
2006/07 budget.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex Approximately 25 Acre Parcel along the New
SR17 (Proposed Kenton ––County– ––Jail– Site) – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration a proposed
ordinance of the City’s intent to annex approximately 22 acres along the
easterly side of the relocated SR17, south of Pelly Road, which is the property
owned by the Kenton County Fiscal Court and which has been designated as the
proposed site of the new Kenton County Jail. Mr. Deters gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading. Mayor Moriconi stated this ordinance is a pro-active
move that would ensure the city would reap the benefits of having a Jail in the
city if efforts to find another location fail. Council Member Franzen added
that regardless of the type of facility or future development on this site the
city would want to be in a position to collect business taxes. Council Member
Little suggested the City look at other areas along the new section of SR17 as
well and move forward with annexation of those areas. Council Member Behler
concurred and moved to direct the city attorney to look into the other sites
along SR17 and begin annexation proceedings. Council Member Bushong seconded
her motion. A brief discussion ensued regarding the best way to proceed. Mr.
Deters stated he would look into the annexation laws; he will also need legal
descriptions and certified surveys for each parcel. Roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2007-R-02 – Authorizing a Text Amendment Application to Amend
Section 9.23 of the Zoning Ordinance Relating to RV’s
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council and read Resolution No. 2007-R-02 that
would support an application for a zoning text amendment to the official Zoning
Ordinance. He stated this application would seek a recommendation from the
Planning Commission on updating the requirements for recreational vehicle
parking, specifically establishing criteria that must be met before the Zoning
Administration can permit parking of an RV on private property.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-02, seconded by
Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered unanimously; motion carried
6-0.
Police Chief Report – ––Shawn Butler–
Chief Butler advised that snow is in the weather forecast and reminded everyone
to get their vehicles off the street so the snow plows can maneuver without
delays or problems.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters requested the Council hold an executive session at the end of the
meeting.

30, 2006 is in their packets for review. He advised if they had any concerns or
questions regarding the Audit that they should direct their questions to the
city’s Finance Director, Teresa Hudson. Council

already answered and they were satisfied.
Mayor Moriconi announced he had some appointments that he would like the

March 5, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 5,
2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then
called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen,
Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters
Approval of the February 5, 2007 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on February 5, 2007. Council Member Little so moved, with second
by Council Member Franzen. Amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
with all ayes; motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2007-O-01 – Amending the 2006/07 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2007-O-
01 which would amend the 2006/07 budget. Mr. Deters gave the Ordinance a second
reading. Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-01, seconded
by Council Member Behler. Council Member Franzen asked about the significant
increase in the repairs line item for the Parks budget. Mayor Moriconi advised
this was revenue from an insurance claim the city filed due to vandalism damage
to playground equipment in the Glenhurst Park. There being no further
discussion by Council, roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Request by David Hill for City to Vacate a Paper Street at the End of Jimae
Court
Mr. David P. Hill, 10682 Kelsey Drive, Independence, Kentucky stated he is
interested in purchasing a vacant parcel at 6393 Jimae Court to build a house.
He stated a ‘paper street’ that was originally intended to connect to Regal
Ridge Drive runs along the property. Mr. Steve Powell, representing the owner –
Harold Clayton – suggested the City divide the ‘paper street’ area evenly
between 6395 and 6393 Jimae Court, thereby closing off this street that was
platted but never formed or used as a street. Mr. Powell stated that currently
the area is littered with debris which cost the City money to clean up each
year. A lengthy discussion ensued regarding this request and how it will affect
the residents of the Regal Ridge Apartments that use this ‘paper street’ as a
shortcut when going to the Cherokee Shopping Center. Mr. Powell stated that
while this area was intended to be a right-of-way, it was never meant to become
a pathway for foot traffic to and from the apartment complex. Council Member
Yeager stated that some of the residents on Jimae Court fear their backyards
may become a new pathway if the City closes off the ‘paper street.’ Further
discussion centered on trying to improve the situation to eliminate the through
traffic and the littering of the ‘paper street’ area and possibly enlisting the
owners of the Regal Ridge apartments to help resolve the problem.
Council Member Brinker moved to table this issue until the City has the
opportunity to speak with the management of the Regal Ridge apartment complex,
as well as notifying all property owners on Jimae Court to make them aware of
this request, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Robert Reusch, Independence Cleaners, 1904 Declaration Drive addressed Council
to request a 5-minute drop-off/pick-up parking area in the fire zone for his
customers. Council advised him to speak to the owners of the Independence Towne
Center and/or the Independence Fire District.
Resolution No. 2007-R-03 – Approving Amendment to MRA Bond Fund Agreement CC04
to Include ––––Kimberly Drive–– and ––––Elizabeth Drive
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2007-R-03 that would amend
the original agreement with the Transportation Cabinet to add Kimberly Drive
and Elizabeth Drive to the list of streets to be funded by Agreement CC04. Mr.
Deters read Resolution No. 2007-R-03. Council Member Franzen moved to adopt
Resolution No. 2007-R-03, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Council Member
Franzen asked if the funds would be increased/decreased. Mayor Moriconi advised
the fund amount would stay the same. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2007-R-04 – Declaring Old Pump Station parcel on ––––Fowler
Creek Road–– as Surplus Property
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2007-R-04 that declares the
land known as 0.0574 acres on the east side of Fowler Creek Road (PIDN 046-00-
00-072.01), which was previously used by the City as a sanitary sewer pumping
station, to be surplus property and authorizes the City administration to
accept sealed bids for the sale of the property to the highest and best bidder.
Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2007-R-04.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-04, seconded by
Council Member Bushong. Audience member, Mr. Don Nienaber, suggested the
proceeds from the sale of the property be applied to the Fowler Creek debt
retirement fund. Council was in agreement and Council Members Franzen and
Bushong amended their motion to include the provision that the proceeds from
the sale would go toward paying off the Fowler Creek debt. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Authorizing & Approving Mayor to Enter into an Agreement with Special Counsel
to Represent the City in a Proposed Commercial Development by Neyer Properties
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed Agreement for special legal
counsel from Taft, Stettinius and Hollister LLP. He stated the City has been
approached by Neyer Development Company who is planning a large commercial
development for property in the area of the new SR 17 and McCullum Road. He
advised that this law firm has assisted other cities with negotiations
regarding large shopping center developments and feels their expertise in this
area would be very valuable to the city.
Council Member Bushong moved to authorize Mayor Moriconi to enter into an
Agreement with Taft, Stettinius and Hollister for special counsel services
regarding the Neyer Properties development, seconded by Council Member Little.
Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Police Chief Report – Dave Nichols, Assistant Chief
Mr. Nichols stated he had nothing to report.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters reported that he has prepared legal descriptions for the other areas
along the new section of SR 17 that Council expressed interest in annexing. He
stated along with the larger section, there were two other smaller areas that
needed to be annexed, one of which was the back end of the Post Office parcel
which is completely surrounded by the City. Mayor Moriconi advised that meant
there would be three separate annexation ordinances. Mr. Deters went on to
explain the annexation process the City would undertake if they decided to
proceed. Mayor Moriconi advised that being annexed into the City could be seen
as an advantage for the unincorporated property owners that will soon be paying
an insurance premium tax that the Kenton County Fiscal Court just enacted. Mr.
Deters stated that if Council wants to proceed with the annexations then he
will prepare the three ordinances needed.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi reported that a status report on the Downtown Small Area Study
was available on the city’s website. He also announced that the Independence
Day Celebration would be held this year on June 29th and 30th. He stated the
Grand Marshall of the parade on Saturday, June 30th would be Army Sgt. Tommy
Rieman a Simon Kenton High School graduate who was acknowledged by President
George Bush in his State of the Union Address. Sgt. Rieman was awarded the
Silver Star for his exceptional courage during his reconnaissance mission in
Iraq.
Report on Kenton County Jail Site
Council Member Franzen reported that the Collaborative Citizen Committee who
has been researching alternative sites for the new Kenton County jail has
submitted a list of sites to the Kenton County Fiscal Court and she stated
things look cautiously optimistic that one of the proposed sites will be a
better choice.
Executive Session
At 8:00 p.m. Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to move into an executive
session. Mr. Deters stated the executive session would be pursuant to KRS
61.810 1(b) to deliberate acquisition of real property. Council Member Franzen
so moved, seconded by Council Member Brinker. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of the meeting,
seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
Resolution No. 2007-R-05 Directing the Condemnation of 157 Sq.Ft. of Land on
the Corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road for Necessary Public Improvements
to the Intersection
Mayor Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2007-R-05 which would authorize and
direct the condemnation, by eminent domain, of 157 square feet of land on the
corner of Cox Road and Taylor Mill Road for public improvements to the

moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-05, seconded by Council Member Behler.

Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:16 p.m.
