April 2, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 2,
2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then
called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Michael Little
and Donna Yeager. Council Member Tom Brinker was absent. Also present was City
Attorney, Jed K. Deters
Approval of the March 5, 2007 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on March 5, 2007. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by
Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered with all ayes; motion
carried 5-0.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Council Member Franzen who asked to make a
statement. Council Member Franzen stated that at the March 5, 2007 meeting of
the Council during the second reading of Ordinance 2007-O-01 that would amend
the 2006/07 budget, former Council Member Margaret Cook asserted that a first
reading had not been done. Council Member Franzen wanted the record to show
that the City Clerk and some members of the Council reviewed the meeting video
and saw that in fact a first reading of the ordinance had taken place at the
February 5, 2007 meeting, indicating that Mrs. Cook made an erroneous
statement.
Privileges of the Floor
Sheila Adams, 36 Walnut Hall Drive, Independence, Ky. – addressed Council with
a request to support a zoning text amendment that would permit fences in front
yards. She stated she has to let the dogs out in the front yard as she has no
rear door to let them out back. She stated she is not able to get an invisible
fence as one of her dogs has a trachea problem and cannot wear a collar. A
general discussion ensued with the Council wherein they discussed possible
solutions. Mr. Deters advised the Board of Adjustments would not be able to
issue a variance to allow a fence as it would be in violation of the zoning
ordinance. He also advised that even if the City applied for a zoning text
application that they would not get a position recommendation from the Planning
Commission as fences in front yards pose site distance issues, etc. which is
one reason they are generally not allowed in most communities. Mr. Deters
directed Ms. Adams to seek further information as to why front yard fences are
prohibited from the Northern Kentucky Planning Commission.
Doris Wicklund, 1906 Independence Road, Independence, Kentucky – addressed
Council with a request for the City to support an application for a zoning text
amendment that would permit a Bed & Breakfast as a permitted use in the R-1C
zone. She stated she has two bedrooms on the second floor of her house at 1906
Independence Road that she would like to rent out. She stated she also has a
wildflower walking trail on her property that will be open to the public free
of charge. There was a brief exchange between some of the Council and Ms.
Wicklund.
Council Member Yeager moved to support an application for a zoning text
amendment that would permit a Bed and Breakfast in the R-1C zone, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0. Mayor Moriconi directed City Attorney, Jed Deters to draft a
Resolution authorizing this application for presentation to the Council at the
May 7, 2007 meeting.
Ordinance No. 2007-O-02 – Intent to Annex 22.5 Acres along Eastside of New SR17
– 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2007-O-02 that
declares the city’s intent to annex a 22.53 acres parcel which is the proposed
Kenton County Jail site on the new section of SR17. Mr. Deters read Ordinance
No. 2007-O-02.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-02, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
5-0.
Discussion to Vacate a Paper Street at the end of Jimae Court
Mayor Moriconi advised Council of the letter from Mr. David Hill that was
included in their Council packet. He stated Mr. Hill was not able to attend
tonight’s meeting, but wanted Council to know that he will need twenty-five
feet of the paper street in order to build a house on the adjoining property –
6393 Jimae Court.
Council Member Behler submitted a petition with eighteen signatures of
residents that are in favor of the city vacating (closing) the paper street.
Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion. Ms. Gail Wallace, 6396 Jimae
Court, stated she has lived on the street for twenty-three years and has
endured years of vandalism in their neighborhood. She stated the paper street
has become a shortcut for the residents living in the Regal Ridge Apartments
who walk to the Cherokee Shopping Center. She stated the pathway is always full
of litter. She stated she would love to see a house built there.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Deters what the City’s options are. Mr. Deters stated
the paper street can be closed by consent or by a court action. He stated to
close it by consent would require all three adjoining owners to agree. A
discussion ensued. Susan Curran, ’’’’6401 Jimae Court, expressed her concerns
that if the City closes the ‘paper street’ then the Regal Ridge residents will
cut through their property. Council discussed closing a portion of the ‘paper
street’ and building a walkway on the remaining area. Mr. Deters stated he
feels this is impractical for the City to do this and will open the city to
liability if it is maintained as a public walkway. He advised that it is a
matter of either closing it or keeping it open. Council Member Franzen stated
she does not feel that closing the ‘paper street’ will stop people from
trespassing. Council Member Bushong commented that he thought HUD housing have
rules they have to abide by in order to keep their certification and wondered
if a high amount of crime was an issue that should be discussed with the owner
of the apartment complex. Mayor Moriconi stated they could set up a meeting
with the owners to discuss, but that Council needed to take some action tonight
with regard to Mr. Hill’s request.
Council Member Behler made a motion to vacate a minimum of twenty-five (25)
feet (east side) of the Jimae Court paper street and authorize any court action
to achieve that. Council Member Franzen seconded the motion. Roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0. Council Member Yeager commented
that she wants to see the City address the problems voiced by the residents of
Jimae Court.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex ––––4545 Oliver Road–– – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would approve an intent to annex 4545 Oliver Road (PIDN 046-00-00-096.00).
Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading. He explained that this parcel is
an island surrounded by city boundaries.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex 5106 ––Madison– Pike – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would approve an intent to annex the remaining section of 5106 Madison
Pike (PIDN 046-00-00-021.01). Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading. He
explained that this parcel is owned by the United States Postal Service and the
front 150-foot strip already lies within the city boundaries. This ordinance
will place the entire parcel within the city limits.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex areas north of McCullum, East of Old SR17,
Both Sides of Pelly Road and West of Fowler Creek Road – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would approve the City’s intent to annex approximately sixty parcels
bounded on the west by SR17, on the east by Fowler Creek Road, on the South by
Oliver Road and to the north, just north of Pelly Road. Mr. Deters gave the
ordinance a first reading. He advised Council that if more than fifty percent
of the property owners protest the City’s intent to annex, then the issue would
be placed on the General Election ballot in November where the issue would be
decided.
Proposed Ordinance – Text Amendment Pertaining to Floodplain Regulations &
Enclosure Requirements for Swimming Pools – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would approve a zoning text amendment accepting the recommendation of the
Kenton County Planning Commission’s recommendation (Number 1688R) and approve
text amendments to the City’s zoning ordinance modifying flood plain
regulations and enclosure requirements for swimming pools. Mr. Deters gave the
ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2007-R-06 – Authorizing Mayor to Enter into MRA 2007/08 Co-op
Agreement with the State
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2007-R-06 which would
approve the execution of a Municipal Aid Coop Program contract with the State
Transportation Cabinet for the 2007-2008 fiscal year. Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2007-R-06.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-06, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
5-0.
Mayor Moriconi stated that by entering into the MRA Co-op, the city will be
eligible to apply for emergency funding. He advised he planned to apply for
emergency funding for repairs needed for Cody Road due to slippage.
Police Chief Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler stated he had nothing to report.
City Attorney Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Municipal Order No. 2007-MO-06 – Approve Re-appointment of Mary Hellman to
Senior Board
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Municipal Order 2007-MO-06 that would re-
appoint Mary Hellman to the Senior Board of Directors. Council Member Bushong
moved to adopt Municipal Order 2007-MO-06, seconded by Council Member Behler.
Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
General Discussion – Dogs Running Loose
Council Member Franzen stated she has been receiving complaints about dogs
running loose in neighborhoods. She stated she spoke with the County Animal
Control and learned they only work Monday-Friday, 8 a.m. – 5 p.m. A discussion
ensued. Chief Butler advised that if the dog is vicious the animal control will
respond after hours. He stated the County only has four wardens to cover the
entire county area Council Member Franzen stated she would like to sponsor an
ordinance that would ban ownership of pit bulls; one similar to the one adopted
by the City of Covington. Mr. Deters stated he would research the issue and
draft an ordinance for the Council to consider.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Yeager moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:59 p.m.

May 7, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 7,
2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then
called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen,
Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the April 2, 2007 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on April 2, 2007. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. There were no amendments noted. Roll was called and
answered with five ayes and one abstain by Council Member Brinker. Motion
carried.
Presentation by Michael Strohm – Land Uses for Proposed Jail Site on New SR17
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Michael Strohm, a professional museum
interpreter. Mr. Strohm conducts Audubon field programs for elementary school
classes in rural Kenton County with a focus on wildlife art, natural resources
conservation and Kentucky history.
Mr. Strohm stated he has lived on Pelly Road for twenty-five years and
expressed concern about the impact the proposed Kenton County jail would have
on the Fowler Creek corridor. He stated the area is a discovery zone for young
children and would like to see it developed as a nature preserve and resource
center. He stated he has discussed the possibility of this type of land use
concept with Kenton County Commission Dan Humpert and wanted to present the
idea to the City to see if they would be receptive as well. He stated that
Kenton County does not have this type of facility and if the Fiscal Court finds
another viable site for the new jail, then this property would be an excellent
use for a nature preserve.
Update on Downtown Small Area Study by Keith Logsdon, NKAPC Planner
Mr. Keith Logsdon provided the Council with an update of the Downtown Small
Area Study. He distributed a calendar of the remaining activities beginning May
14, 2007 and ending August 2, 2007. Activities include a real estate
roundtable, public open house on May 31, 2007, draft presentation of the
project to the City Council at the June 4, 2007 meeting and final draft by June
18, 2007. Mr. Logsdon stated that City Council will be asked to review the
final document for adoption sometime between June 25 and July 2, 2007 so that
it can be presented to the Kenton County Planning Commission at their August 2,
2007 meeting with their recommendation back to the City and on the City’s
September meeting agenda.
Proclamation – Building Safety Week
Mayor Moriconi read a Proclamation declaring the week of May 6, 2007 as
Building Safety Week.
Ordinance No. 2007-O-03 – Zoning Text Amendment Modifying Flood Plain
Regulations and the Requirements for Swimming Pool Enclosures – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading, Ordinance No. 2007-O-03, which
would approve a zoning text amendment modifying flood plain regulations and the
requirements for swimming pool enclosures. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2007-
O-03.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-03, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Closing a Portion of Apple Drive – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
close a portion of Apple Drive. He advised Council that a section of Apple
Drive has been rerouted due to the road improvements to SR17 (Madison Pike) Mr.
Deters stated the leftover portion of Apple Drive would serve no purpose and
the abutting property owners (James D. Grubbs Trust and Grubbs Properties, LLC)
have submitted a notarized request and consent to the proposed closing. He
stated the property owners will be expanding their business and will need to
have this section of Apple Drive closed before a building permit can be issued
by the City. Mr. Deters read the ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Budget for 2007-2008 Fiscal Year – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed budget for
the 2007/2008 fiscal year. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
In his attached budget address, Mayor Moriconi stated that the budget assumes
the adoption of a compensating rate for property taxes. He also highlighted the
major expenses which included: $600,000 for an aggressive street repair
program, two additional police officers – one to be hired in July and one in
January, the purchase of a dump truck for the Public Services Dept., storm
sewer project on Production Drive which will be a collaborative effort with the
Sanitation District, and a $15,000 increase in the park improvements. In
addition, Mayor Moriconi advised council that the employees would begin paying
a portion of their health insurance.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a Pay & Classification Plan – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance to
update the personnel and pay classification plan. He stated this is updated
each year along with the budget. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Award Bid for Fowler Creek Pump Station Parcel
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the one bid that the City received for the
purchase of the old pump station property on Fowler Creek Road (PIDN 046-00-00-
072.01). The bid was submitted by Tim Reese of Centerline in the amount of
$200.00. This parcel adjoins land that is being developed by Centerline. There
was a brief discussion by Council regarding the low bid as PVA has the parcel
valued at $1,000. Council asked the city attorney to look into the possibility
of the City asking for a minimum bid amount in the future when these parcels
are declared surplus and sold. Mr. Deters stated that he felt sure that the
City could require all fees associated with the sale and transfer of the
property to be paid for by the purchaser.
Council Member Bushong moved to award the bid of $200.00 to Centerline,
seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered with four ayes
and two nays by Council Members Yeager and Little. Motion carried 4-2.
SD1 Agreement for Storm Sewer Repairs on Production Drive
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed Agreement between the City and
The Sanitation District relating to the Production Drive storm sewer
replacement project. The project has an estimated cost of $427,686 of which the
SD1 Board of Directors has approved up to a 50% cost share amount of $213,843.
A brief discussion ensued regarding Section 26 of the Agreement wherein the
City would acknowledge that the funding is being supplied from the SD1 Storm
Water Surcharge account which is currently involved in a lawsuit (Wessels
Company LLC et al v. Sanitation District No. 1, et al, Boone Circuit Court,
Case No. 05-CI-299) and in the event that SD1 should lose this lawsuit the City
would be required to refund the amount SD1 contributed to this project. Further
discussion resulted in Council reaching a consensus that the project was
necessary and decided to authorize the Mayor to enter into the Agreement.
Motion was made by Council Member Franzen, seconded by Council Member Bushong
to authorize the Mayor to enter into the Agreement with SD1 to share the cost
of the Production Drive storm sewer replacement project. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2007-R-07 – Declaring 4406-A Oliver Road as Surplus Property
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2007-R-07 that would declare
4406-A Oliver Road (PIDN 406-40-00-044.00) as surplus property. This property
was originally used to house a sewer pump station which is no longer in use.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-07, seconded by
Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.

Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi

Adjustments
Mayor Moriconi presented and read to Council Municipal Order No. 2007-MO-07
appointing Catherine E. Wilson to the Board of Adjustments. Council Member
Bushong moved to adopt Municipal Order No. 2007-MO-07, seconded by Council

Update on New Section of SR17
Mayor Moriconi reported that the construction of the new section SR17 is on

by the end of this year.
Discussion Regarding Vicious Dogs
Council Member Franzen reported that she is working on drafting a vicious dogs
ordinance for the City Council to consider adopting. She has been reviewing

to review it.
Kenton County Proposed Jail
Council Member Franzen also reported that the possible alternative sites for

optimistic that the proposed jail will not be built at the new SR17 and Pelly
Road site that was originally announced by the Kenton County Fiscal Court.
Executive Session

with K.R.S. 61.810(c) to discuss sewers and condemnations, seconded by Council

June 4, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 4,
2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then
called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen,
Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the May 7, 2007 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on May 7, 2007. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by
Council Member Little. No amendments were noted. Roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Downtown Small Area Study by Keith Logsdon, NKAPC Planner
Mayor Moriconi introduced Keith Logsdon of the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission who provided Council with a brief update on the Downtown Small Area
Study project and distributed an activity schedule with revised dates to get
the draft of the study submitted to the Council and the Kenton County Planning
Commission for their recommendation. Mr. Logsdon advised the final phases of
the study would include an open house at the Senior Center, as well as a public
display in the lobby of the Municipal Center of information compiled to date.
He stated comment sheets would be available to obtain citizen input. Mr.
Logsdon advised that the Council would receive a preliminary draft by June 18,
2007 so they could provide him with their input prior to the presentation of
the final document to Council at the July meeting. Emily Listerman, NKAPC
advised that they have received good feedback from the citizens. Council Member
Behler stated she has heard some negative comments from the public that are
afraid the study results will “be written in stone” and that their taxes will
increase. Ms. Listerman advised that this document should be considered as and
used as a reference guide for future planning, but that nothing in the study
should be considered concrete. Council Member Behler stated that she hoped that
the new businesses would come into the city which would increase the commercial
tax base, thereby increasing the City’s tax revenue.
Ordinance No. 2007-O-06 – Intent to Annex areas north of McCullum, East of Old
SR17, both sides of Pelly Road and West of Fowler Creek Road
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that he would move discussion of Ordinance No.
2007-O-06 up on the Agenda, as many of the property owners were present and had
legal counsel here to address Council.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Mr. Dennis Williams, a Covington attorney
representing approximately forty-two property owners on Pelly Road, Fowler
Creek Road, Oliver Road, Jimmie Lane and McMillan Drive. Mayor Moriconi advised
Council that the property owners are protesting the City’s intent to annex
their parcels. Mr. Williams submitted a petition with forty-three signatures
declaring that they do no desire to be annexed. He stated these citizens were
against the proposed annexation and reminded Council that state law requires
the issue to be put on the general election ballot for those in the affected
area. He stated that this election would be at the City’s cost and would fail
as these forty-three residents represent sixty-nine percent of the area’s
total. Mayor Moriconi advised that the main reason the City was proposing to
annex this area was to close the gaps in the city boundaries. Mr. Deters
advised Council that if more than fifty-percent of the property owners file the
petition protesting the annexation, then it would be put on the ballot for a
vote.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Yeager to table the second reading of Ordinance No. 2007-O-06. A discussion
ensued wherein Council reached a consensus to withdraw their interest in
annexing this area. Council Members Franzen and Yeager withdrew their motion
and second.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Yeager to not adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-06. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. The motion carried 6-0 and Ordinance No. 2007-O-06 was not
adopted. (Clerk’s note: Ordinance No. 2007-O-06 will be noted as ‘number
skipped’ in the city records.)
Ordinance No. 2007-O-04 – Intent to Annex 4545 Oliver Road – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2007-O-
04 which would approve the Intent to Annex 4545 Oliver Road. Mr. Deters read

July 2, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 2,
2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then
called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Michael Little
and Donna Yeager. Council Member Carol Franzen was absent. Also present was
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the June 4, 2007 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on June 4, 2007. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by
Council Member Behler. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 5-0.
Ordinance No. 2007-O-10 – Closing a Portion of Jimae Court – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2007-O-10 that
would close a portion of Jimae Court, which is considered no longer, needed for
future development. The area being closed is the fifty (50) foot by one hundred
thirty-three (133) foot portion of Jimae Court lying and being directly between
lot numbers 36 and 37 of the Beauty View Acres subdivision. Mr. Deters read
Ordinance No. 2007-O-10.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-10, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Council Member Yeager commented that with the closing of
this paper street, the property owners on the left side of Jimae Court would
have more trespassers using their yards as a shortcut to the Cherokee Shopping
Plaza. She stated she would like to see the City come up with a solution to
prevent the trespassing. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0.
Award Bid of Surplus City Property at 4406-A Oliver Road
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the lone bid received for the sale of a
parcel of land located at 4406-A Oliver Road that used to house a sewer pump
station and is no longer in operation. He stated the bid was received from
Glenn S. Pryor at 4406 Oliver Road in the amount of $300.00. Mayor Moriconi
asked for a motion to accept the bid.
Council Member Behler moved to accept the bid received from Mr. Pryor for
$300.00 plus the expenses associated with the publication of the legal notice
accepting bids and all other related costs and that the $300.00 should be
credited to the Fowler Creek Sewer debt. Council Member Little seconded the
motion. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Award Bid for Oliver Road and Stephens Road Street Repairs
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the bid tabulation sheet from the city
engineer (CDS Associates) for the street resurfacing of Oliver Road and
Stephens Road. He stated that five bids were received with the low bid being
from Barrett Paving in the amount of $145,065 and the high bid from Paul
Michels & Sons in the amount of $176,525. He stated the city engineer is
recommending the City award the bid to Barrett Paving. Council Member Little so
moved, with second by Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered with
all ayes; motion carried 5-0. Mayor Moriconi commented that the engineer’s
estimate for this project was approximately $200,000 so with the low bid coming
in approximately $50,000 lower than that estimate the City will have extra
funds to repair another street this year.
Award Bid for Phase I of the Production Drive Storm Sewer Project
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the bid tabulation sheet from the city
engineer for the Phase I portion of the Production Drive Storm Sewer Project.
He stated that ten (10) bids were received with the low bid of $266,357 from
Bray Arnsperger and the high bid of $419,643 from Larry smith Contractors.
Council Member Yeager moved to award the bid to Bray Arnsperger in the amount
of $266,357, seconded by Council Member Behler. Council Member Behler commented
that the second low bid was $310,613 and wondered why the disproportion. Mayor
Moriconi could not say but advised that the project’s estimated cost was much
higher than the low bid received and that even if change orders are requested
by the contractor, that it should not reach the city engineer’s original
estimated costs for this project. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Recreational
Vehicles – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend the city’s zoning ordinance, Section 9.23, regarding the regulations for
the parking or storing of trailers, recreational vehicles, campers, boats and
other similar equipment in all zoning districts. Mr. Deters read the proposed
ordinance.
Resolution No. 2007-R-12 – Accepting Recommendation of KCPC 1873R to Deny Text
Amendment Adding “Bed & Breakfast” Establishments as a Permitted Use in the R-
1C Zone & Supporting an Application as a Conditional Use
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a recommendation by the KCPC (Kenton County
Planning Commission) to disapprove the City’s application for a proposed text
amendment adding “bed and breakfast” to the list of permitted uses within the
R-1C zone. A discussion ensued about the City’s options with regard to this
recommendation from the KCPC. Mr. Deters advised the Council could adopt a
Resolution to accept the recommendation to deny the text amendment as a
permitted use and make a new application requesting that “bed and breakfast”
establishments be added as a conditional use.
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-12 accepting the
KCPC recommendation to disapprove a “bed and breakfast” as a permitted use and
to make a new application for a text amendment allowing this type of
establishment to be a conditional use. Council Member Little seconded the
motion; roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi announced that the City Clerk has been accepted into the
Leadership Northern Kentucky program sponsored through the Northern Kentucky
Chamber of Commerce.
Mayor Moriconi stated that the City’s July 4th Celebration held on June 29th
and 30th was a huge success with a record crowd for the fireworks display on
Saturday night. He thanked all the sponsors and everyone who worked to make it
a success.
Executive Session
There being no further regular business to discuss, Mayor Moriconi entertained
a motion to enter into an Executive Session in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810
(c) to discuss pending litigation on a sewer related issue and a right-of-way
issue. Council Member Bushong so moved, seconded by Council Member Little
Motion carried with all ayes. At 7:14 p.m. Council retired to the Executive
Session room.
At 7:30 p.m. Council Member Yeager moved to reconvene the regular session of
the Council meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with
all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Little moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:31 p.m.

July 23, 2007
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, July 23, 2007 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center, 5409
Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then called the
meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Michael
Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters. Mayor
Moriconi announced that a quorum was present for this special meeting regarding
the items posted on the Agenda. He stated he would like to change the order of
a couple of items on the Agenda. No objections were voiced.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
·   Recognition of Twenhofel Students chosen to attend the Junior National
Youth Leadership Conference in Washington, D.C.
·   Presentation and Discussion of the Downtown Small Area Study
·   Discuss a Proposed Ordinance to approve a map amendment of an approximate
30-Acre area located on the east side of Turkeyfoot Road across from Industrial
Road – Possible 1st Reading
·   Discuss a Stage II development plan for an approximate 1.5 Acre area
located along the south side of Centennial Blvd. approximately 800 feet east of
Madison Pike (NKAPC No. Z-07-06-06/1882R
·   Ordinance No. 2007-O-11 – Approving a Text Amendment relating to
Recreational Vehicle Regulations – 2nd Reading
·   Discuss a Proposed Ordinance to Adopt the 2007 Supplement to the Code of
Ordinances – Possible 1st Reading
·   Executive Session (if necessary)
Recognition of Twenhofel Students
Mayor Moriconi introduced Taylor Zumwalt & Sydney Schuler of Twenhofel Middle
School who have been chosen by their teachers, along with four other students,
to attend the Junior National Youth Leadership Conference to be held in
Washington, D.C. He also introduced their teacher and chaperone Beverly
Johnson. Mayor Moriconi presented the students with a bag they could take on
their trip to remind them of their hometown.
Proposed Ordinance to approve a map amendment of an approximate 30-Acre area
located on the east side of Turkeyfoot Road across from Industrial Road, KCPC
No. 1874R – Possible 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance to approve the
recommendation of the KCPC (Kenton County Planning Commission) to approve a
zone change for an approximate 30-acre area located on the east side of
Turkeyfoot Road, across from Industrial Road, from R-1B, R-1C and R-3 to an NC
(neighborhood commercial). Mayor Moriconi introduced Mike Schwartz of the NKAPC
(Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission) who was present to answer any
questions that Council may have. Mr. Schwartz advised that the KCPC held a
public hearing on the requested zone change on June 7, 2007 and that Council
has ninety days to take action or the KCPC recommendation to approve the
request will go into effect. Council Member Yeager asked if there would be
egress onto Thomas Drive and Mr. Schwartz stated no; that the KCPC imposed a
condition that egress would not be allowed onto Thomas Drive.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Justin Verst of Viox & Viox Engineers who
conducted a fifteen minute 3-D animation power point presentation of the
proposed site layout plan by Eagle Development Company. Mr. Verst advised that
Eagle Development has mainly worked in the Louisville area and that this would
be their first development in Northern Kentucky. He stated that the KCPC
recommendation was to approve the zone change subject to three conditions; two
being there would be no connections to Thomas Drive or Turkeyfoot Road. He
stated they would try to get an egress onto the LSI driveway. He stated that
the third condition imposed by the KCPC related to making the pedestrian access
more amenable. Mr. Verst advised that Eagle Development is also working with
the adjacent property owners – Remke’s and Huntington Bank – to assist them in
relocation to the new site and then renovate the existing building to update
the entire area.
Mr. Jerry Dusing, legal counsel for Eagle Development, stated that he would
like to emphasize that the current Comprehensive Update has the site earmarked
for expansion of the Southern Wood Village apartment complex as it had access
off of the old Turkeyfoot Road. Currently there is no physical access so it was
assumed there is no reasonable way to develop. He stated that this proposed
development plan provides the City with an opportunity for a nice mixed use
development. Mr. Dusing also advised that a traffic study was conducted and
presented the City with that report and stated that the traffic engineer is
present at this meeting to address any concerns that Council may have.
Council Member Bushong asked if the Remke grocery store would be relocating to
this planned development site. Mr. Ken Holiday of Huff Commercial Group advised
that Eagle Development has already purchased the Remke store site as well as
the Huntington Bank property, which are the north and south corners of
Industrial Road and Turkeyfoot Road, directly across from the planned
development site. He stated Eagle plans to expand and/or relocate the
businesses. He advised Council that Eagle would not market the other retail
sites until the zone change is approved. Mr. Verst commented that the north
side of the development is targeted for a professional office building that
would house doctor’s offices, etc.
Mr. Wardell Wilcox of Jacobs Engineering Group, 895 Central Avenue, Cincinnati,
Ohio, submitted for the City’s record a comprehensive traffic engineering
study. A lengthy discussion ensued about the traffic control and designating
the main street as a sub-collector road. Council expressed concerns about this
becoming a through street which could present safety issues for the residents.
The consensus of Council was that this road should be designated as a sub-
collector.
Other concerns that Mayor Moriconi and Council Members discussed were landscape
buffers for the adjacent/adjoining residential property owners, providing a
rear entry to the development that could be used by the nearby apartment
complex residents, geographic issues, detention ponds and a de-acceleration
lane to keep the traffic moving. Mayor Moriconi commented that the residents
have waited twenty years to get the needed road improvements to Turkeyfoot Road
and he is concerned this development may result in new traffic congestion.
Mr. Verst commented that they have agreed to the conditions imposed by the KCPC
and will do whatever the City requires as well. Another Eagle Development
representative commented that there has been a major physical change in this
area of Turkeyfoot Road since the Comprehensive Plan was last adopted.
Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for citizen comments on this planned
development.
Raymond Kerl, 3933 Thomas Drive, Independence – expressed concerns regarding
––––Richardson Road–– traffic. He stated that he feels the apartment owner will
eventually sell. He stated he currently has a lot of foot traffic from the
apartment complex crossing his yard and feels this retail development will only
make matters worse.
Further discussion ensued about the traffic issues and designating the road as
a sub-collector. Council Member Little commented that there are a number of
methods to control traffic concerns as a part of the preliminary plat approval.
Council Member Franzen commented that she feels this is an important gateway
into the City. She moved to have a first reading of the proposed ordinance that
would approve this map amendment as recommended by KCPC and subject to the
additional condition that the street is designated as a sub-collector road.
Council Member Bushong seconded the motion. A brief discussion ensued about
finding a solution to discourage the use of shortcuts by surrounding residents
when accessing the retail development area. Suggestions included privacy fences
and elimination of walkways which the developer will take under consideration.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Franzen’s motion carried with
all ayes and Mr. Deter’s read the proposed ordinance approving the map
amendment with the added condition that the street will be designated as a sub-
collector.
Recess
Council Member Bushong moved to have a brief recess, seconded by Council Member
Little. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene; seconded by Council Member Little.
Motion carried with all ayes.
Presentation and Discussion of the Downtown Small Area Study
Mayor Moriconi introduced Craig Gossman of KKG of KKG Architects and Keith
Logsdon of NKAPC who presented the results of the Downtown Small Area Study.
Mr. Gossman distributed a handout which provided details of the study process,
which included public input and the recommendations for implementation for the
City. He stated the Study includes a plan to help guide future development in
order to stay ahead of the growth. He stated that they looked at the north and
south gateways into the City as well as the McCullum Pike area. Mr. Gossman
stressed that this Study was merely a land use concept plan and is not intended
to mandate zone changes within the City. He stated the Plan calls for more
mixed use developments. He stated that the results of the public input were
that the people wanted to retain the rural, small-town feel of the City and
preserve historic downtown. He stated the residents would also like buffers
from the commercially developed area, more restaurant and entertainment
choices, wayfinding and more sidewalks throughout the City. Mr. Gossman
concluded by saying that the Plan also provides design recommendations,
transportation recommendations, economic development initiatives and an
implementation plan.
Mayor Moriconi thanked everyone who participated in this Study. There was a
brief exchange of questions and answers after which Mayor Moriconi asked for a
motion to adopt the Study, which would then be presented to the KCPC for an
approval to include the results of this Study as part of the Comprehensive
Update for Independence. Council Member Franzen commented that one of the
recommended initiatives of this Study was to hire a City Administrator,
Economic Development Director or Professional Planner to assist in implementing
this Plan. She stated she would like to work toward that goal and hopes this
Study will not sit on a shelf like prior studies the City has done. Council
Member Behler concurred.
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt the Downtown Small Area Study, seconded
by Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0. Mayor Moriconi thanked everyone for their involvement in the study
and commented that he feels this is a great investment in the City’s future.
Stage II Development Plan for an approximate 1.5 Acre area located along the
south side of Centennial Blvd. approximately 800 feet east of Madison Pike
(NKAPC No. Z-07-06-06/1882R
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the recommendation from NKAPC for a Stage
II Development plan from Ashley Development for an approximate 1.5 acre area
located along the south side of Centennial Boulevard, approximately 800 feet
east of Madison Pike.
Mr. Bill Kreutzjans of Ashley Development Group addressed Council and advised
that the NKAPC has reviewed their application and recommended denial based on
lack of information attached to their application. He stated that at the time
of the application they had not identified the use and did not have signage
information.
Mike Schwartz of the NKAPC explained to Council that if they don’t know what
all the uses will be they can’t know if they will meet parking requirements,
etc. Mr. Kreutzjans stated this will be a retail strip center that will house a
coffee shop, bank and other unknown retail space. He stated the structure will
be approximately 13,280 square feet, with six tenants. Currently they only have
two committed tenants.
A discussion ensued wherein Council Member Little commented that if the City
approves a Stage II development without more details, then zoning issues could
fall through the cracks when each thing has to be addressed individually which
results in ten times the work for the City. Council Member Behler stated that
NKAPC is paid to review the plan, which they have denied and she is not
comfortable approving this until the revised plan is re-submitted for another
review. Mr. Jim Bertram attempted to explain that it is difficult to determine
uses when they are in the process of leasing space which has to be set up
specifically for each tenant.
Council Member Behler moved to accept the NKAPC staff recommendation to
disapprove the Stage II Development plan and that Ashley Development re-submit
their plan to NKAPC, seconded by Council Member Little. A brief discussion
ensued wherein Mr. Bertram asked for a postponement to give them time to revise
the plan and get it back to NKAPC. Council Member Little expressed concern that
an attempt should not be made to try to circumvent the plan review system.
Council Member Franzen asked how they could help speed up the process since the
developer want to get this development started next month. Roll was called on
the motion and resulted in a tie vote; Council Members Behler, Little and
Bushong voicing yes votes and Council Members Franzen, Yeager and Brinker
voting no. This vote resulted in no action taken.
Council Member Franzen moved to table the issue so Ashley Development can re-
submit their plan to NKAPC and then back to the City. Further discussion
between Mr. Schwartz and the Council resulted in Council Member Franzen
withdrawing her motion and Mr. Schwartz suggesting the Council approve the
Stage II development plan subject to compliance with the following conditions:
1.   That all uses be from the list as identified in Section 10.12, E. of the
Independence Zoning Ordinance.
2.   That all required off-street parking spaces be provided, pursuant to
Section 11.2 of the Independence Zoning Ordinance.
3.   That each façade sign not exceed 40 square feet in area and that each
ground sign not exceed 60 square feet in area.
4.   That each off-street parking space be a minimum of 9 feet in width and a
minimum of 18 feet in length.
5.   That the paving of the off-street parking area meet the minimum
requirements of Appendix A of the Independence Zoning Ordinance
Council Member Franzen so moved, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2007-O-11 – Approving a Text Amendment relating to Recreational
Vehicle Regulations – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2007-O-11 which
would approve a text amendment to Section 9.23 of the official Zoning Ordinance
regarding the parking or storing of trailers, RV’s, campers, boats and other
similar equipment. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a second reading.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-11, seconded by
Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Proposed Ordinance to Adopt the 2007 Supplement to the Code of Ordinances –
Possible 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would adopt the
2007 supplement to the Code of Ordinances. Mayor Moriconi advised this is a
housekeeping ordinance that effectively incorporates all ordinances enacted the
last two years into the current Code. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Executive Session
At 10:23 p.m. Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to move into an executive
session. Mr. Deters stated the executive session would be pursuant to KRS
61.810 1(b) and (c) to discuss acquisition of real estate and pending
litigation. Council Member Franzen so moved, seconded by Council Member Yeager.
Motion carried with all ayes.
At 10:35 Council Member Little moved to reconvene the regular session of the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Authorize Mayor to Negotiate the Acquisition of Real Property
Mr. Deters announced that as a result of the discussion in Executive Session,
the Council has decided to authorize Mayor Moriconi to negotiate a purchase
price for a parcel of real estate. Council Member Franzen moved to authorize
the Mayor to begin negotiations at $70,000 for this purchase of land contingent
on obtaining an appraisal of the property. Council Member Behler seconded the
motion. Motion carried with all ayes
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Bushong moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 10:37 p.m.

August 27, 2007
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, August 27, 2007 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance and then called the
meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Michael
Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters. Mayor
Moriconi announced that a quorum was present for this special meeting regarding
the items posted on the Agenda.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
·   Ordinance No. 2007-O-12 – Discussion & Possible Action to Annex 22.53 Acres
Along new Section of SR17 (Proposed Kenton County Jail Site ) – 2nd Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2007-O-13 - Discussion & Possible Action Approving a Zoning
Map Amendment of an Approximate 30-Acre Area located on the East Side of
Turkeyfoot Road across from Industrial Road – 2nd Reading
·   Proposed Ordinance - Discussion & Possible Action – Approving a zoning text
amendment Relating to Bed & Breakfast Establishments – 1st Reading
·   Proposed Ordinance – Discussion & Possible Action – Adopting 2007 Property
Tax Rates – 1st Reading
·   Resolution No. 2007-R-13 - Discussion & Possible Action – Supporting the
Application of a Grant for Body Armor
·   Resolution No. 2007-R-14 – Discussion & Possible Action – Authorizing a
Lease-Purchase Agreement with Fifth Third Bank for a New Public Works Vehicle
·   Executive Session (if necessary)
Ordinance No. 2007-O-12 – Annexation of 22.53 acres Along the New Section of
SR17 (Proposed Kenton County Jail Site) – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2007-O-12 annexing
the 22.53 acre parcel (PIDN 046-00-00-025.02) on the easterly side of relocated
SR17, south of Pelly Road, and currently owned by the Kenton County Fiscal
Court. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2007-O-12.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-12, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Council Member Franzen commented that she wanted
residents to know that while the City is annexing this property to reap the tax
benefits, she will not give up the fight to prevent the Fiscal Court from
building the new jail on this site. She stated she feels that everyone should
continue exerting pressure on the county commissioners to look elsewhere for a
more appropriate site. Mayor Moriconi agreed that they would not give up the
fight. Council Member Brinker wondered if there was a way to make this site
less attractive to the county. There being no further discussion, roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2007-O-13 – Approving Map Amendment (KCPC 1874R) of an
Approximate 30-Acre Site Located on the East Side of Turkeyfoot Road across
from Industrial Road – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2007-O-13, but
before having the reading said he would allow comments from anyone in
attendance that would like to address the Council on this issue.
Bob Morehead, 4070 Richardson Road, Independence – voiced his opposition to the
proposed development. His major concerns was increased traffic in the area,
adverse topographical conditions and that he feels that residents do not want
this retail area so close to their homes and they feel this will devalue their
properties.
Richard (Rick) Hill, 4048 Richardson Road, Independence – voiced his opposition
to the proposed development. He expressed concern about the area between the
apartments and the proposed development site. He wanted to know if there were
alternate plans for the apartments. Mr. Deters commented that this was not part
of the proposal by Eagle Development and suggested he speak to the owner of the
property he was referring to.
Betty A. McGee, 4013 Turkeyfoot Road, (Erlanger) Independence – voiced her
opposition to the proposed development. She stated that she is concerned this
development will increase traffic congestion and fears that her quality of life
will go down. She was also concerned that the road would be a through road.
Council informed her that the City has made that a condition of the development
Linda Morehead, 4070 Richardson Road, Independence – spoke in opposition to the
proposed development. She also stated that she is concerned how this
development is going to generate increased traffic to the area and the impact
that will have. She stated that she feels this will be nothing more than a
strip mall.
Barry Bonneville, 377 Florence Drive, (Erlanger) Independence – voiced his
opposition to the proposed development. He stated he would like to see the city
impose a greater buffer zone between the residential properties. He stated he
would also like the city to require an embankment and walls that would prevent
him from viewing this development from his property.
Kathy Espelage, 11513 Staffordsburg Road, Independence (unincorporated) –
stated that she is not a resident of the City, but that she took interest in
the City’s Downtown Small Area Study and she feels this development is in
conflict with the results of the study.
Raymond Kerl, 3933 Thomas Drive, (Erlanger) Independence – expressed concern
about the nearby apartment complex owned by Lanny Holbrook and said he didn’t
see why the City didn’t condemn the buildings. Mayor Moriconi advised him that
was an entirely different issue and could not be discussed at tonight’s special
meeting due to state laws regulating special meetings.
Representatives from Eagle Development responded to the concerns expressed by
the residents that addressed Council. Realty broker Ken Holiday, commented that
the property, as currently zoned would allow twenty apartment units per acre,
up to six hundred apartments which he feels would be an ugly alternative to
this proposed commercial development. He advised that with this development the
City can expect to see upscale restaurants and stores that will have imposed
architectural controls. He also stated that Eagle Development has already
purchased the commercial properties across the street (currently Remke’s retail
center and Huntington Bank which are located at the north and south corners of
Industrial Rd and Turkeyfoot Rd.), which will be re-developed. Jonathan Brown,
traffic engineer with Viox & Viox Engineers advised that a traffic study was
conducted which has determined that the traffic this development will generate
will not be a detriment to the area in general.
Council Members Yeager and Franzen asked if the developers had met with the
residents beforehand to get their input regarding the plans for this
development. Mr. Holiday stated they had met with some individual residents
when requesting to purchase their properties, but other than that the residents
had opportunities to share their concerns at the public hearings. Council
Member Bushong stated that the Planning Commission sent letters to the adjacent
property owners notifying them of the public hearing.
Ms. McGee asked if the road was denied by the city. Council advised her that
the road will be deemed a sub-collector and not be a through street to
Richardson Road.
At this time Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to give the Ordinance a second
reading. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2007-O-13.
Council Member Yeager moved to postpone the adoption of this ordinance until
the developers could sit down with the residents to address some of the
concerns they expressed. Council Member Franzen agreed. Mayor Moriconi advised
Council that this special meeting was called in order to take action on this
map amendment request as the deadline for the City to do this is September 5th.
Council Member Yeager’s motion died for lack of a second. A lengthy discussion
ensued.
Mr. Deters advised the Council that they had three options; those being:
1)   They could follow the KCPC recommendation without a hearing or only an
argument-type hearing.
2)   They could review the record of the KCPC public hearing and determine from
that evidence adjudicative facts which differ from those found by the
Commission and then disapprove the recommendation based on those facts, (this
means only the record and no additional evidence) or
3)   The City could hold its own trial-type public hearing and find as a result
thereof different adjudicative facts than those found by the Commission and
then disapprove the recommendation based upon those facts. (this means making a
totally new record). Mr. Deters advised that in order for the City Council to
deny or go against such a recommendation, there must be a majority vote of the
entire legislative body. This means the vote has to be at least 4 to 2 and does
not mean a majority of members present. Four members must vote against the
proposed change.
He went on to say that the City must act on a recommendation for a map
amendment within 90 days of the recommendation. If they do not, the KCPC
recommendation becomes final by operation of law. He stated that the City is
running out of time as the 90 day time frame will end on September 5, 2007.
Council, the developer representatives and the residents in attendance
continued this discussion. Mr. Deters explained that the city would not have
time to hold its own public hearing, and then have two readings of an ordinance
prior to September 5th on this issue due to the legal advertising requirements
for public hearings. Council Member Franzen suggested delaying action on this
second reading of the Ordinance for thirty minutes or so, so that the
developers and residents could retreat to the conference room to discuss their
concerns to see if they could come to an agreement.
Council Member Behler made a motion that the City obtain of copy of the tape of
the KCPC public hearing on this issue to determine any facts which would differ
from those found by the Planning Commission that could be use to adopt an
ordinance opposing the zone change. Council Member Yeager asked if we couldn’t
oppose it tonight. Mr. Deters advised the Council would still need two special
meetings prior to September 5th to perform two readings of an ordinance to
oppose the zone change. Council Member Franzen stated she would like the
developers to speak with the residents to see if they can provide them some
assurances and give them some satisfaction. Again, Mr. Deters advised they have
limited time to act on this issue. Council Member Little commented the City
faced a similar situation a year or so ago and after developers met with the
residents they were able to resolve some issues. Mayor Moriconi commented that
it may not be possible to resolve their differences within thirty minutes or
so, but agreed to delay the vote on this ordinance for that amount of time and
permitted the residents and developers to go into the executive session room to
discuss their concerns. Mayor Moriconi stated they would continue on with the
other agenda items, including an executive session of the Council and then
resume this issue later in the meeting. Council Member Behler withdrew her
motion. The residents and developers went into the executive session room to
confer on this issue.
PROPOSED ORDINANCE – Adopting 2007 Property Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
establish the 2007 tax rates for real and tangible properties in the City. He
stated the rates before them are the compensating rate and proposed is $0.186/
$100 of assessed value for real estate and $0.575/$100 of assessed value for
tangible properties. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance that would adopt
the rates presented.
PROPOSED ORDINANCE – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Bed &
Breakfast Establishments – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
adopt the recommendation of the KCPC to approve a zoning text amendment adding
a definition for “Bed and Breakfast Establishment” and adding “Bed and
Breakfast Establishments to the list of conditional uses within the A-2 zone
and all of the residential zones. This amendment would also add developmental
controls to each of the zones listed. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance
for a first time. Mayor Moriconi stated this would be presented for a second
reading at the September 10, 2007 regular council meeting.
RESOLUTION NO. 2007-R-13 – Supporting an Application for a Body Armor Grant
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2007-R-13 which would
authorize him to enter into an Agreement with The Governor’s Office for Local
Development to participate in the Kentucky Body Armor Program. This authorizes
the execution of any documents necessary to facilitate this project and act as
the authorized correspondent.
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-13, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
RESOLUTION NO. 2007-R-14 – Authorizing a Lease-Purchase Contract for a new
Public Works Vehicle
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2007-R-14 that would approve
a master lease-purchase agreement with Fifth Third Bank for the financing of a
new dump truck for the Public Services Department. Mayor Moriconi read
Resolution No. 2007-R-14.
Council Member Little moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-14, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
EXECUTIVE SESSION
At 8:08 p.m. Mayor Moriconi asked for a motion to enter into an executive
session in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (b) to deliberate the possible
acquisition of real property. Council Member Behler so moved with second by
Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 8:44 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of
the council meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with
all ayes.
(Discussion Continued) on Ordinance No. 2007-O-13 – Approving Map Amendment
(KCPC 1874R) of an Approximate 30-Acre Site Located on the East Side of
Turkeyfoot Road across from Industrial Road – 2nd Reading
After the residents and developer representatives finished their discussion in
the executive session room everyone reassembled in the Council Chambers. Mayor
Moriconi announced that one of the ideas presented in the discussion between
the developers and the citizens was that the citizens be involved in the
development agreement process wherein they would have a say in how it would
look, the buffers installed, etc. He suggested they could have a committee as
they move forward with this. A brief discussion ensued. Mayor Moriconi offered
the use of the city building for the citizens and developers to meet. Mr.
Deters advised this should not be a city sponsored committee or meeting, but
that Council could mandate that a condition of their approving this map
amendment would be that the developer works with the citizens to address their
concerns which could be so stated in the Ordinance. Mr. Deters added the
appropriate language to Ordinance No. 2007-O-13 and gave it another second
reading.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2007-O-13 with the added
condition drafted and read by Mr. Deters. Motion seconded by Council Member
Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
ADJOURNMENT
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn,
seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting
ended at 9:03 p.m.

September 10, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
10, 2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance
and then called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol
Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed
K. Deters.

Resolution No. 2007-R-15 – Regarding Proposed Moratorium on Electronic Message
Boards
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for discussion a Kenton County Planning
Commission recommendation to disapprove a proposed zoning text amendment that
would provide for a moratorium through December 31, 2007 on the issuance of
building and other related permits allowing the installation of any new message
board, changeable copy sign, electronic message board, tri-vision sign, nor to
all the installation of a portion of a sign that is a message board, changeable
copy sign, electronic message board, or tri-vision sign or the conversion of
any existing sign that would include these type signs. A brief discussion
ensued. Mayor Moriconi advised that the NKAPC staff is working on a model
Zoning Ordinance which has a section that regulates signage. He stated the
staff recommendation was to impose a short-term moratorium until the model
Zoning Ordinance was complete. He stated that the issue of freedom of speech
was brought up during the KCPC public hearing and because of that the KCPC
postponed taking any action on this until the Commission’s legal counsel could
advise them on the legal ramifications of a moratorium. Council Member Franzen
commented that this issue could possibly be re-presented to Council at a later
date after legal review.
Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2007-R-15 that would accept the KCPC
recommendation (Application No. 1885R) to not impose a moratorium through
December 31, 2007 on the issuance of permits for signage. Council Member
Bushong moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-15, seconded by Council Member
Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2007-R-17 – Authorizing the Sponsorship of a Text Amendment
Application that would Allow Class 7 signage as a Permitted Use in the NC Zone
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a request by Atwell-Hicks, a development

would permit Class 7 signs in the NC zone. Tom Musgrove, representing Atwell-
Hicks addressed Council regarding this request. He stated that their client is
proposing the construction of a Rite-Aid pharmacy store at the southeast corner
of Harris Pike and Madison Pike where Deaton’s Nursery is currently located. He
stated that the city’s current zoning regulations do not permit class 7 signs
in the NC (neighborhood commercial zone). Mr. Musgrove presented development
plan drawings of the Rite-Aid building which included the signs they would like
to install along with this development. Council Member Franzen advised Mr.
Musgrove that any text amendment that would be adopted by the city would not be
site specific but would affect all NC zones. Mr. Deters commented that the
Planning Commission would make a recommendation to the City. Council Member
Little asked who would pay the application fee for the text amendment. Mayor
Moriconi advised that Atwell-Hicks would pay the fee.
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Resolution No. 2007-R-17 approving the
City’s sponsorship of an application for a text amendment that would permit a
Class 7 sign in the NC zone, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was
called and answered with five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member
Yeager. Motion carried 5-1.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
1, 2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance
and then called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council

K. Deters.
Approval of the September 10, 2007 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on September 10, 2007. Council Member Little so moved, with second

answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Jim Bertram of One Eleven Engineers addressed Council on behalf of White Castle
restaurants with a request of the City to sponsor a zoning text amendment that
would modify parking space requirements for certain eating establishments. He
distributed a handout to the Council that outlined the City’s current off-
street parking regulations for establishments that sell food and refreshments
for consumption on the premises or for take home food service. He stated that
their text amendment request follows the mixed use developments as suggested in
the Downtown Small Area Study recently adopted by the City. Mr. Craig Eilers,
representative for White Castle stated that this parking requirement is making
it difficult to get this building constructed as they only need half of the
parking spaces that the City’s zoning requires (30 of 60). He stated that fast
food restaurants generally need less parking. A brief discussion ensued
resulting in a general consensus of the Council to review the information given
to them by Mr. Bertram and then take action on this issue at the next regular
meeting which is November 5, 2007.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting new Building & Zoning Fee Schedule – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would adopt a new
schedule of fees for zoning and building permits. He introduced the City’s
Building Inspector Kevin Barbian who answered questions from the Council.
Council Member Behler asked how the permit increases were determined. Mr.
Barbian stated that the increases would now cover the actual costs involved and
allow the City to break even. He stated that obviously the industry is down,
but that the fees being proposed will be comparable to the fees charged by
other communities in the region. Mayor Moriconi commented that the proposed fee
schedule is in line with the staff and other expenses for this department.

accept the KCPC’s recommendation to approve a map amendment (KCPC Application
Number 1889R) changing an approximate 4-acre area located approximately 500
feet east of the terminus of Apple Valley Drive from R-1EE to R-2 (PUD).
Council Member Brinker stated he met with some residents in the area of this
proposed zone change. He stated their concerns were that an adequate buffer be
imposed as a condition and that no through street be constructed. Bob Buten,
the developer who plans to add on to the Apple Valley Apartment complex stated
that he did not object to the conditions imposed by the KCPC. He stated the
other apartment buildings are fifteen years old and the additional buildings he
has planned will be as nice, or nicer that the existing buildings. There was a
brief discussion about the conditions that KCPC has imposed and which include
1) a 20-foot planting strip along the north and east sides of the site, 2)
pedestrian access be provided from the site to the community center of the
existing apartment development, 3) that all fences and walls meet the
requirements of the underlying R-2 zone, 4) that signage be prohibited on the
site, and 5) that provisions for a secondary access point be provided to the
south of the site. All was in agreement that the conditions were similar to the
concerns voiced by the residents and that no additional conditions needed to be
imposed by the City. There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.

November 5, 2007
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, November
5, 2007 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance
and then called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol
Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed
K. Deters.
Approval of the October 1, 2007 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on October 1, 2007. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
by Council Member Yeager. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Kentucky Department of Veteran Affairs – Dennis Glacken
Mayor Moriconi introduced Dennis Glacken from the Kentucky Department of
Veteran Affairs. Mr. Glacken introduced several veterans – hometown heroes –
with the 275th American Legion Post. He stated these veterans, four of which
are recipients of the Purple Heart award, represented our nation in World War
II, the Korean War, the Viet Nam war and the War in Iraq. Mr. Glacken presented
the Mayor with a Certificate of Recognition for the City’s adoption and support
of the Kentucky National Guard, 940th MP Company of the Walton Armory. Mr.
Glacken introduced Mr. Alvin Duncan, Director of the Veterans Cemetery in Grant
County. Mr. Duncan announced that the new veterans’ cemetery in Grant County
will be called “Kentucky Veterans Cemetery North” is under construction with an
anticipated completion date in the Fall of 2008. He stated that all veterans
and their spouses will be eligible for free burial in this cemetery.
Proposed Ordinance Defining and Regulating the Keeping of Vicious Dogs – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading an ordinance being sponsored by
Council Member Franzen which will define vicious dogs and put guidelines on the
keeping of vicious dogs. He stated that council Members Franzen and Little have
more information to present based on the research they have done regarding
vicious dogs. Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to the Council Members for
discussion of this proposed ordinance.
A lengthy discussion ensued resulting in changes to the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Little distributed the research he found on the internet from
other cities that have adopted legislation to regulate vicious dogs, but that
legislation should be non-breed specific. He stated if a dog exhibits vicious
behavior as defined in the legislation then fines could be imposed to penalize
the dog owners. Council Member Franzen said that a dog would have to exhibit
behavior that would require it to be registered with the city as a vicious dog.
Council Member Little moved to remove the breed specific language from the
proposed ordinance, seconded by Council Member Behler. No roll call, motion
carried with all ayes.
Council went on to discuss first and second offense fines that would be imposed
on the dog owners. Council Member Franzen suggested the first offense should
require the dog to be registered as a vicious dog with the City and carry a
$500 fine. Council Member Little stated that the City of Chicago has a $10,000
fine for a second offense and it has been very successful in going after
irresponsible owners. Council Member Bushong commented that insurance coverage
for this type of injury would only be paid out for one incident. Council Member
Little stated that one of the regulations would be that the owner would have to
carry liability insurance. Chief Butler expressed concern that if the second
offense is not serious that the courts would look upon a $10,000 fine as
excessive. Mr. Deters agreed that it could be challenged in court, but that the
place to appeal the fine would be the Code Enforcement Board. Council discussed
imposing a fine “….up to $10,000” but was concerned that a variable fine amount
decided by the issuing officer may appear arbitrary. Council Member Brinker
stated he felt that $10,000 seemed extreme to him. He asked Chief Butler the
statistics on vicious dog attacks in the City. Chief Butler stated there were 3
cases reported in 2006 and 4 to date for 2007. He stated that state law
requires that dog bites be reported. Council Member Behler stated she too was
uncomfortable with the vagueness of “up to” and suggested the maximum fine be
set at $5,000.
Council Member Little suggested that after a dog has a second or third offense
that the dog would have to be removed from the City. Council Member Franzen
concurred and moved that the proposed ordinance text be amended to read that
the first offense would carry a fine of $500 and the second offense carry a
fine of $10,000 with removal of the animal from the City by the dog warden.
Roll was called and answered with four ayes and two no votes cast by Council
Members Behler and Bushong. Motion carried 4-2.
Council Member Behler asked about the license fee and if it would cover the
City’s costs. Council Member Franzen stated the City could issue a paper
registration and a dog tag and that the ordinance could be amended if the City
finds that the actual costs are higher.
There being no further discussion by the Council, Mayor Moriconi opened the
floor for citizen comments on this proposed legislation. Taylor Priest (Dayton,
Ohio) speaking on behalf of Sarah Peed, 602 Berlander Drive, Independence –
stated he was glad to see the Council remove language that would name specific
breeds of dogs as vicious. He stated that other communities struggle with this
complex issue and he thanked the Council for setting an example for other
communities.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading
Privileges of the Floor
Cass Ruhlman, 277 Buttermilk Pike, Fort Mitchell, Ky. – representing
Congressman Geoff Davis addressed Council to inform them that Congressman Davis
provides many services including assistance with federal grants. She encouraged
them to contact her if they can be of help with anything.
