Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on November 5, 2007. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
by Council Member Behler. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Occupational License Fee Changes per HB 107 and HB 458 –
1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi introduced Larry Klein, City Administrator of Fort Wright, who
was present to explain the changes that need to be made to the City’s current
regulations of Occupational License fees which have been State mandated in
accordance with HB 107 and HB 458 and become effective July 15, 2008. Mr. Klein
stated that he was a member of the Task Force of Occupational License Fee
Administrators from across the state who discussed a wide array of rules,
forms, methods and the confusion among the taxpayers, businesses as well as the
tax preparers. He stated he held the position of Kenton County Occupational
License Inspector from 1988-1998 and is a member of the Kentucky Occupational
License Association. He stated that since the bill goes into effect July 15,
2008 he is recommending that all cities and counties that impose this tax to
adopt this by January 1, 2008 so there is less disruption and confusion to
businesses and payroll services from changing rules on payroll and net profits/
gross receipts in the middle of a tax year. He stated that a model ordinance
has been developed by the state Task Force and that a scaled down version has
been drafted for their consideration by local attorney Frank Wichmann who
represents several cities in Northern Kentucky. Mr. Klein stated that it is
unique to Northern Kentucky cities that the county collects and administers
this tax for most cities in this area so additional language giving this
authority to the Kenton County Occupational License Inspector’s office is
provided in this ordinance the City is being asked to adopt.
Mr. Klein pointed out some of the changes brought about by HB 107 and HB 458
and incorporated into the model ordinance include:
·   Uniformity in administration among cities, counties, school districts with
occupational license fees
·   Maintain local control of tax rates, caps, minimums, maximums, net/gross,
etc.
·   Make collection of this tax “business friendly”
·   Increased compliance = increased revenue
·   The use of prevalent methods
·   Avoid double taxation
·   Make model ordinances and tax forms available
He advised that late filing penalty will be mandatory across the state with an
interest rate of 12% per annum, which is the same as property taxes. He stated
that this ordinance will put more teeth in imposing liens on personal property
for non-payment of the occupational license tax. It also clarifies where a sale
occurs for the business and provides definitions of businesses and employees.
This ordinance will also provide that there will be a 5-year statute of
limitations and that a business has up to two years after a tax was due to
request a refund if paid in error. He stated the previous ordinance did not
address refunds.
After a brief question and answer session with Mr. Klein and there being no
further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Klein for attending the meeting and sharing his
knowledge of these state mandated changes. Mayor Moriconi advised Council that
a special meeting would be held on Thursday, December 6th so that this
ordinance could be presented for a second reading and adoption to meet the
January 1, 2008 deadline recommended by Mr. Klein.
Neyer Development – Power Point Presentation regarding a Revised Site Plan for
New SR17 and McCullum Road
Mayor Moriconi introduced Dan Neyer of Neyer Development who was before the
Council to present a revised site plan, based on the Downtown Study, for the
new SR17 and McCullum Road intersection.
Mr. Neyer stated that the revised plan addresses the City’s concerns that the
original plan did not adhere to the results of the Downtown Study that was
recently adopted into the City’s comprehensive plan. He stated they are
presenting this revised plan and would like input from the Council before
making an application with the Planning Commission. He introduced Development
Manager Pete Mallow. They presented a power point presentation of the revised
plan which will be a mixed use incorporating retail, office space and high
density residential. Mr. Mallow suggested that the features and benefits of
this revised plan include 1500 new office and retail jobs, $750,000 in
projected payroll taxes for the city, $175,000 in projected property taxes and
gross receipts taxes for the city and provides an attractive gateway entrance
into the City.
After the power point presentation a discussion ensued, with some Council
Members stating they were hesitant to provide Neyer input before following the
proper application process with the Planning Commission. Mr. Deters advised
that because the City Council is the final arbiter, to comment in advance of
obtaining a recommendation from the Planning Commission could give the
impression of a pre-disposition and could make it difficult to give a fair and
impartial decision. Council suggested that the revised plan be submitted to the
Planning Commission for review and recommendation to the City.

January 7, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
7, 2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance
and then called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol
Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed
K. Deters.
Approval of the December 3, 2007 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on December 3, 2007. Council Member Behler so moved, with second
by Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the December 6, 2007 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the special
meeting held on December 6, 2007. Council Member Little so moved, with second
by Council Member Yeager. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Chris Francis, 10316 McCauley Drive, Independence, stated he is the YMCA
Independence Branch Director. He addressed Council regarding plans to expand
the YMCA. He stated he has met with Mayor Moriconi to discuss a joint
collaboration with the city to establish a Youth Advisory Council, which will
be modeled after the Cincinnati YMCA program. He stated this Advisory Council
will provide reports to the City Council.
Mike Warth, 1897 Bridle Path, Independence – addressed Council regarding the
speed humps recently installed in the Ridgeway Farms subdivision. He thanked
the City for establishing this program by which citizens can petition the City
for this type of traffic control device. He stated that he felt the program was
easy to use and worked effectively.
Presentation of the Market Study Conducted as Part of the Downtown Small Area
Study
Mayor Moriconi introduced Doug Harnish of GEM Public Sector Services. He stated
that Mr. Harnish would provide an overview of the market study that was
conducted in collaboration with the Downtown Small Area Study which was
completed and presented to the Council in July 2007. He stated Mr. Harnish was
unable to attend the July meeting, therefore the report was never officially
presented to the Council, so he is here tonight to go over the results of his
study with Council.
Mr. Harnish gave a condensed overview of the market study which included the
objectives that would help the city to identify sources of current and future
demand, project future growth and evaluate current capacity to meet current and
future demands for services. He stated another objective of the study would be
to identify business opportunities for the future. He stated that the City has
the unique ability to pick and choose future developments and this study will
assist them in addressing development proposals from an informed and market
based viewpoint.
Mr. Harnish advised the study revealed that the City has seen a significant
growth rate in population over the last ten years and although 2008 will be
sluggish they will continue to see the population grow at a higher rate than
other communities in the area. He stated that people move to Independence for
lifestyle but work in other communities. He stated that since all age brackets
are growing, this growth will put pressure on the public services to keep pace
as rooftops always precede commercial demands. He stated it is estimated that
the City’s population will brow by nearly 5000 residential units between 2000
and 2011.
Mr. Harnish went on to say that Independence is not a major employment center
and currently 64¢ of every dollar earned is leaving the City. He stated that
medical and health care services are underserved with less than 6% of the
market demand being captured in 2006.
In closing, Mr. Harnish shared some of his final observations from the market
study:
·   Independence is undergoing unprecedented growth which will continue in the
near future
·   Continue to maintain much of the character and vitality of the city’s
traditional “downtown” but this could change with the relocation of KY17
·   City should direct efforts to revitalize and restore the historical section
of the Madison Pike corridor and implement a mix of land uses in the future.
·   Need to focus on the parking problem in the historical downtown area by
securing reciprocal easements for shared parking.
·   Keep in mind that revitalization, reuse and redevelopment projects are
long-term projects
·   City should plan for future growth before the growth takes the City where
it wants to go
·   Define what it is that Independence wants to be in the future.
·   Develop policies and programs to help facilitate business development and
land uses the city wants to have in the future.
Mr. Harnish said the City should think aggressively but act conservatively and
think about the long-term sustainability of all future new development.
Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion. Council Member Behler asked Mr.
Harnish what type of staff member he would recommend to oversee the
implementation of the Downtown Study. Mr. Harnish commented that often two
employees, one from city administration and the other a city planner or
economic developer, would work together to recruit and enforce development
designs. Council Member Behler also asked the life span of this market study.
Mr. Harnish responded that a market study is usually good for 2-5 years, but
due to the growth rate in Independence, this study material will probably
become outdated sooner than that. Mayor Moriconi commented that he is
assembling a volunteer advisory group that will work on the implementation of
the Downtown Study which he will present at next month’s meeting. Council
Member Behler commented that the advisory group would be one component, but
feels the City needs to fund the hiring of a staff member in the next budget. A
discussion among the Council Members ensued about the hiring of a staff member
to oversee this study; suggested positions included a City Administrator, City
Planner or a Director of Economic Development. There was a consensus that the
City needed an actual employee and that funding for this position needed to be
a priority in the coming fiscal year budget.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Harnish for presenting the data in the market study.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving Zoning Text Amendment relating to Off-Street
Parking – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
accept the recommendation of the Kenton County Planning Commission and approve
a zoning text amendment for off-street parking requirements for restaurants
(KCPC Application No. 1898R). Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Police Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler stated he did not have anything to report.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Park Improvement Discussion –Mayor Moriconi directed Council’s attention to the
document in the Council packets provided by the Finance Director regarding loan
debt information for proposed park improvements as well as a proposed addition
to the Public Services facility on Richardson Road. He stated that it appears
that a bank line of credit would not be a viable option
Council Member Little reminded the Council that the Small Area Downtown Study
revealed that while the City has several parks that there will continue to be a
need for adequate recreational amenities as discussed on page 60 of the Study.
He stated the City needs to begin to look at improving the quality instead of
creating more parks. He stated that the Memorial Park site designated for a
skate park by the Committee has not yet been adequately compacted but that
other alternative amenities can be put in place such as basketball courts,
additional shelters and walking trails. He also mentioned needed improvements
for Staggs Park and Independence Park. A lengthy discussion ensued regarding
the various improvements that are needed to the existing parks. It was decided
to eliminate the plans for a skate park which would decrease amount of a
possible loan to $400,000 from the original $700,000. Council Member Behler
concurred with Council Member Little but stated that she felt the more pressing
priority for the City was to hire a staff member to lead the implementation of
the Downtown Study. She expressed concern about the City’s ability to fund a
new staff member as well as a new loan for Park and Public Services
improvements. Council Member Yeager agreed, but added that she still feels an
obligation to fix up the parks for the children. She stated she feels the
elimination of the proposed skate park, which reduces the park improvements
budget to only $250,000 is a compromise, as well as a loan amount the City
would be able to afford. Council Member Franzen stated she would be agreeable
to borrowing the lesser amount of $400,000. As Council discussed a lesser
amount it was suggested by an audience member to fund the improvements out of
the annual budget without borrowing money. Mayor Moriconi commented that he
feels the City’s revenues will be increasing due to the future commercial
growth on the horizon. He stated that he is committed to hiring a City
Administrator or Economic Development Director as well as making improvements
to the City’s parks and that he feels there are various options available to do
both. Council Member Brinker wondered if it would even be possible to set aside
funds in future budgets when you have the possibility of administrations
changing ever other year. Council Member Behler stressed that she was not
against park improvements, just against obtaining a loan at this time, when
additional staff is needed.
Mayor Moriconi urged the Council to take some sort of action since this
proposal was first presented last fall and he felt it was time to decide if the
City would or would not proceed in obtaining a loan to finance these
improvements. Further discussion by Council centered on having more accurate
numbers for each project before deciding on obtaining a loan. Mr. Deters
advised that Council should get bids before deciding to take out a loan so
there is a more detailed cost analysis. Final decision by the Council was to
get actual cost estimates for one Public Works building, 2 full basketball
courts, 2 half basketball courts, 2 play ground equipment, 2 shelters and 2
hiking trails.
Presentation of 2006/07 Audit
Mayor Moriconi presented the 2006/07 annual audit to the Council and stated
they should direct any questions about the audit to Finance Director, Teresa
Hudson or the City Clerk.
Sidewalk Construction
Council Member Brinker asked about the next sidewalk project along Madison
Pike. Mayor Moriconi reported that the next phase will begin at US Bank at the
intersection of Madison Pike and McCullum Road and head north to Independence
Station Road, cross the street and head south along Madison Pike and end at Big
Bone Turnpike. He stated that the City is in the process of obtaining easements
and hopes to put the project out to bid in a couple months.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:37 p.m.

regarding a zoning violation notice he received about his RV (recreational
vehicle) that he has parked in his driveway. He stated city staff has informed
him that he has to move the RV around to the rear of his property. He stated he
is unable to do this due to the size of the RV. He stated he has lived here for
twenty-four years and is upset he is being asked to move the RV. He stated he
feels the City is against RV owners.
Mr. Niece’s comments commenced a lengthy discussion among the Council members
regarding the current ordinance that regulates the parking and storing of RV’s.
Council Member Little advised that when the ordinance was amended in 2006 and
again in 2007 that it actually relaxed the old ordinance by increasing the
allowable weight and length of trucks, RV’s, trailers, etc. Mayor Moriconi
commented that the City has received numerous anonymous complaints in recent
years that have prompted a more pro-active approach in the enforcement of this
ordinance, so we now find that we are in a no-win situation. He suggested that
the City either continue to enforce the ordinance or rescind it and allow the
residents to park these vehicles anywhere they want on their property. He
stated he feels that while Mr. Niece’s situation is unique, for the majority of
the City the ordinance is relevant. Council Member Franzen stated that the
current ordinance provides that the property owner can make application with
the Board of Adjustments for a conditional use. Council Member Yeager commented
that the application fee is $500, which many people cannot afford to pay. Mr.
Deters commented that Council could review the current ordinance to consider
amendments, but the last amendment by Council was very thorough. Council
Members Little and Franzen, who worked on the amendments to the current
ordinance explained that allowing or not allowing RV’s, based on lot size, etc.
is not legal. Council Members Bushong and Brinker commented they would like to
take another look at the ordinance for possible revisions. Council Member
Little stated he would locate the information they used last year when the last
amendments were made and get it to Council Members Bushong and Brinker.
Resolution No. 2008-R-01 – Amending Job Description for Crew Leader Position
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2008-R-01 amending the job
description for the Public Services Department Crew Leader position. Mr. Deters
read Resolution No. 2008-R-01. A brief discussion ensued regarding the general
supervisor of this position and amendments were noted. Council Member Little
moved to approve the amendments noted in the job description, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2008-R-01, seconded by
Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 6-0.
Municipal Order No. 2008-MO-01 – Establishing Strategic Action Committee for
Downtown Area Study
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Municipal Order No. 2008-MO-01 that would
establish the Community Small Area Study Strategic Action Committee. He thanked
Mr. Keith Logsdon of the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission for
providing his input for this municipal order. Council Member Little commented

action on the recommendations in the Downtown Small Area Study, so that it
doesn’t become another Study that will just sit on the shelf without being
implemented. Mr. Deters read Municipal Order No. 2008-MO-01.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Municipal Order No. 2008-MO-01, seconded
by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.

March 3, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 3,
2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance. Reverend
Lisa May, Pastor of Faith Community United Methodist Church gave the
invocation. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom
Brinker, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City
Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the February 4, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on February 4, 2008. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second
by Council Member Behler. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Request for City to Sponsor a Zoning Text Amendment
Mike Martinelli of Triumph Energy and representing the Sunoco service station
at the intersection of Turkeyfoot Rd and Independence Station Road addressed
the Council with a request for the City to sponsor a zoning text amendment that
would add service stations to the list of conditional uses within the R-1D
zone. He stated that with the renovation of Turkeyfoot Road, they would like to
give an updated look to the Sunoco station at this intersection, by adding
another gas dispenser and new canopy. He stated that the current zoning does
not allow any improvements because the business is a non-conforming use in this
zone. A brief discussion ensued regarding the current zone and that the
proposed text amendment for a conditional use would mean that the request would
go before the Board of Adjustment for approval or disapproval.
Resolution No. 2008-R-02 – Support of Zoning Text Amendment Application
Council Member Franzen made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 2008-R-02 that
would support the application for the text amendment as requested by Mr.
Martinelli, seconded by Council Member Brinker. Roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment for the ––––Independence–
––Village––KCPC Application No. 1904R – 1st Reading
Presenting the revised development plan for the Ashley Commercial Group was Jim
Bertram of One Eleven Developers and legal counsel Tim Theissen. They
distributed the plan revisions report to the Mayor and Council Members which
outlined the changes to the original approved plan which increased the open
space from 5 acres to 9.8 acres and the residential dwellings from 102 to 108.
A lengthy discussion ensued with questions from the Council regarding lot sizes
and the number of signs for each commercial lot. Mr. Bertram stated that each
lot needed two signs so there would be better traffic visibility, but that it
would be possible that some businesses will only require one sign. Council
Member Little expressed concern that the residential section of this PUD plan
would not materialize. Mr. Bill Kreutzjans of Ashley Construction stated that
while they could not guarantee the speed at which the residential units would
be built they were projecting three years. Council Member Behler stated she was
concerned that they would return in the future to request for more commercial
lots. Mr. Theissen stated that they couldn’t provide a timetable for the
development, but explained that a PUD development must have a section that
includes residential. Mr. Bertram stated that if they attempted to change the
PUD status they would have to get approval from the adjoining residential
property owners. Mr. Theissen also stated that a number of development
contracts have fallen through since the original development plan was approved
in 2004, mainly because the numbers didn’t work, both financially and
development-wise. Council discussed installing a buffer now so as to appease
the residents on Walnut Hall Drive.
In closing the discussion, the Council Members agreed to impose two more
conditions, along with three conditions recommended by the Kenton County
Planning Commission, and would be subject to the development plan being
revised. The two conditions imposed by the City will include the following:
·   Condition 4 – Ten Percent (10%) of the residential development is to be
completed within two years from the adoption of this ordinance
·   Condition 5 - A buffer zone completed before a Certificate of Occupancy can
be issued on the north side of the development
Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance, to approve a map amendment for the
Independence Village, KCPC Application No. 1904R, a first reading including
text to add the above referenced conditions number 4 & 5.
Police Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler thanked all the volunteers and businesses that supported the
annual Women’s Wellness Fair.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report, but would need to request
an executive session to discuss pending litigation.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Memorial Park Development Update - Mayor Moriconi informed Council that the
city engineer was preparing a design and cost estimate for improvements to
Memorial Park which would include an access road off of Peach Drive, two full
and one half basketball courts, a 20-space parking lot, shelter building and
walking trail system. Chief Butler commented that the next step will be to
obtain financing for the project. He stated that in working on next year’s
budget the staff would need direction from Council regarding funds to support
this project. A brief discussion ensued regarding how much of the labor could
be provided by the Public Services employees and/or volunteers, installing a
buffer along the adjoining properties on the south side of Peach Drive and
funding the project, i.e. take out a loan or use reserve account. Council also
discussed breaking up the project into several alternate bids, so the
improvements could be done in phases based on the costs and the City’s ability
to fund each separately, if necessary. Mr. Deters advised Council that they
always have the right to reject any and all bids received and that bidders know
that the award of the bid is contingent on the city obtaining financing of the
project.
Council Member Bushong moved to begin the bid process for the Memorial Park
improvements, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes.
Update on Downtown Study Advisory Committee
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that the kickoff, informational meeting for the
Downtown Study Advisory Committee will be on Tuesday, March 18, 2008 at 6:00
p.m. in the Council Chambers. He stated the following people have volunteered
to serve on the committee: Chris Reinersman, Jake Stremmel, Donna Brautigan,
Paul Metzger, Rodney Crice, Mackey McNeill and Mike Warth. He thanked everyone
for their willingness to serve on this committee.
Discussion Regarding the Hiring of a City Planner (Economic Development
Director or City Administrator)
Mayor Moriconi asked Council if they had any questions regarding the position
of City Planner. Council Member Behler commented that she feels that Council
needs to decide which position is really needed. Council Member Franzen stated
she fears the need for an Economic Developer Director may fizzle out over time
and believes the city would be better off hiring a City Administrator. These
comments prompted an exchange of ideas among the Council regarding the best
position to be filled. Council Member Franzen stated she hoped to get a City
Administrator that would also be able to perform the duties of a Planner/
Economic Development Director as needed. Council Member Behler commented that
she felt an Economic Development Director could generate much needed revenue
for the City. She stated that while she also believes the City needs an
Administrator as well, she does not believe the City can afford both positions
at this time. She also is concerned that the City will expect too much from
someone that would take the City Administrator position. Council Member Yeager
commented that she likes the idea of an Economic Development Director but
believes that the current City Administrator job description includes some
development director duties. She stated she would like to review the current
City Administrator job description. She also suggested a college intern could
provide some assistance to a City Administrator. Council Member Little
suggested that a City Administrator could contract out Planning and Economic
Development jobs. Council Member Bushong stated the City could hire consultants
for planning needs, but that the City needs to move forward so we can begin the
search to fill the position. Council Member Behler stated that she does not
believe the City can afford to hire a City Administrator and contract out
planning and economic development services as well.
Mayor Moriconi suggested creating the position of Economic Development Director
just to get it on the books. Council Member Brinker moved to create a job
description for Economic Development Director. Mayor Moriconi asked if any of
the Council Members provided feedback to the City Clerk on the job description
she provide for the position. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Bushong
seconded the motion made by Council Member Brinker. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Mayor Moriconi encouraged Council to provide their input on the job description
as soon as possible so that it would be ready for the April 7th council
meeting.
Meeting to Discuss Zoning Ordinance that Regulates Recreation Vehicles
Mayor Moriconi reported that three members of the Council will be meeting with
the Zoning Administrator and the City Attorney on Monday, March 10th at 6:00
p.m. to discuss the current ordinance regulating recreational vehicles. He
stated that they will review the current regulations and discuss ideas for
possible revisions. Mayor Moriconi stated the public is invited to attend.
Announcement – Easter Egg Hunt
Mayor Moriconi announced that the annual Easter Egg Hunt is scheduled for
Saturday, March 15 at noon at Memorial Park.
Executive Session
There being no further business for the regular meeting of Council, at 8:27
p.m. Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to move into an executive session. Mr.
Deters stated the executive session would be pursuant to KRS 61.810 1(c) to
discuss pending litigation, specifically Cobble v City. Council Member Bushong
so moved, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 9:10 p.m. Council Member Bushong moved to reconvene the regular session of
the meeting, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
Cobble v City

of settlement until after the Judge ruled on the pending issues in the Cobble v

the City and the Independence Senior and Community Center. He advised that the
proposed changes are in bold text. Chairman of the Senior Center Board of
Directors, Dave Millward addressed Council regarding the amendments to the
agreement. He stated that the current lease agreement was written as if the
Board was a self sustaining organization that would require them to have their
own liability insurance, etc., when in actuality the City provides the
liability insurance and pays the utilities. He also stated that this lease will
specify the hours and days that the Center is leased to the Board and would
also allow the Board to sub-lease the Center during those specified hours to
others as a way to generate revenue for Senior programming.

generated. Mayor Moriconi advised that Nita Brake would oversee the operation
of the building. He also advised that the City has always subsidized the
expenses association with the operation of the Center.

Discussion Regarding the RV Regulations
Council Member Brinker resumed the discussion from previous meetings regarding
the possibility of making some revisions to the current regulations for the
parking and storing of recreational vehicles. He stated he feels there is
enough support to make some changes. Council Member Yeager suggested adding
language that would give city staff the discretion to waive the current
regulation if a property owner’s land has topography conditions that would
warrant the waiver. She stated that she felt there would not be many owners
that would have special conditions to warrant a waiver, but the staff would
have this available to them if necessary.
Council also discussed waiving the $500 Board of Adjustment fee for RV owners
that would apply to the Board for a variance and conditional use. Council
Member Franzen expressed reservations about waiving this BOA fee for some and
not others. She stated that this could have a snowball effect with everyone.
She also expressed concern that waiving the fee would then have to be
subsidized in the general budget. Council Member Yeager suggested this could be
avoided if the applicant was piggybacked onto another BOA meeting schedule.
Some council members debated the fairness of this suggestion.
Council Member Behler made a motion to add language changes to the current
ordinance that would permit staff members the discretion to waive the RV
regulations if a property owners’ land had topography conditions that would
warrant a waiver and that the amended ordinance be presented at the May
meeting. Council Member Brinker seconded the motion. Roll was called and
answered with five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Franzen. Motion
carried 5-1.

May 5, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 7,
2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance. Council
Member Jim Bushong gave the invocation. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the April 7, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on April 7, 2008. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by
Council Member Behler. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Trash Assessment Rate
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance to adopt an assessment
rate for the curbside collection and removal of solid waste. He advised council
that the current contract with Rumpke would expire on June 30, 2008 and that
the city could opt to continue the contract for the next two-year extension. He
stated that he met with a Rumpke representative to discuss Council’s suggestion
that Rumpke directly bill the residents. He advised that Rumpke is willing to
bill directly, but for a higher price than the next two-year extension rate. He
stated the other option was to keep the assessment on the city tax bill and
charge an administration fee or bid the contract out again. Mayor Moriconi
stated that due to the significant increase in fuel costs that any new bids
received would come in much higher than the rates that Rumpke is offering to
renew the current contract regardless of whether the city or Rumpke does the
billing. He stated that Rumpke would bill the residents on a quarterly basis.
A discussion ensued relating to the problem of assessing the trash on the
annual property tax bill and how delinquent bills result in the city paying out
more for the trash pick up than is being received in revenues. Council Member
Little stated that a vast majority of the delinquencies are due to property
foreclosures and bankruptcies which will be recouped in the future, but are
causing an imbalance in this source of revenue which should equal the
expenditure in the budget.
Council Member Bushong moved to renew the current contract with Rumpke at the
rate of $132.00 per year with the residents being billed directly by Rumpke,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Don Nienabor, 66 McCullum Road, expressed
concern that if Rumpke discontinued service to a resident do to non-payment of
the quarterly bill, then who would pick up the trash. Mayor Moriconi stated
that if a property becomes littered with trash then it would become a city
property maintenance/code enforcement issue. Rose Hofstetter, 146 McCullum
asked if the residents would be permitted to choose a different waste hauler,
such as Bavarian. The City Clerk responded by saying that Rumpke would be
awarded an exclusive franchise for service to all residential properties,
thereby prohibiting another carrier to service those properties.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a Map Amendment for a Stage I Development Plan in
the ––Independence– ––Village– – KCPC Application No. 1918R (White Castle
Restaurant – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve an amended Stage I development plan, submitted by White Castle
Kentucky, LLC, for an
approximate two-acre area located along the east side of new KY17,
approximately 900 feet north of Harris Pike and is part of the Independence
Village development. Mr. Dick Hauber, representative for White Castle stated
the parcel they will purchase is 2.3 acres, but they will not need the entire
area for the restaurant, so they will be splitting the lot. Also he advised
council that they need to have a closing on the property transfer by the end of
May which is before the council’s next regular meeting, so he asked council if
they would be willing to have a special meeting sometime in May so that a
second reading and adoption of the ordinance could be held. Council agreed to
hold a special meeting on Tuesday, May 13, 2008 at 6:30. Mr. Deters gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Accept Zoning Text Amendment Recommendation No. 1916R from KCPC that would
Disapprove Adding Service Stations as a Conditional Use in R1-D Zone
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the KCPC Statement of Recommendation for a
zoning text amendment application that the sponsored on behalf of the Sunoco
station at the intersection of Turkeyfoot and Independence Station Roads. He
stated that the Planning Commission has recommended disapproval of the proposed
text that would add service stations, with certain restrictions, to the list of
conditional uses within the R-1D zone, citing that service stations are not an
essential use in that zone and that they felt it was an unreasonable attempt to
circumvent the map amendment process. Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld
commented that advised council that Sunoco representatives have decided to not
pursue this text amendment by asking the Council to override the KCPC
recommendation. She stated that Sunoco has decided to keep the current
footprint of the store, but will not add a new gas pump or expand the building.
She stated they have advised her they will focus on updating the facade of the
building.
Council Member Franzen moved to accept the recommendation of the KCPC regarding
the zoning text application number 1916R, seconded by Council Member Behler.
Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting an Amended 2007/08 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would amend the 2007/08 budget. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a 2008/09 Fiscal Year Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would adopt a budget for the 2008/09 fiscal year. In his prepared budget
message he stated that despite rising health care, fuel costs and flat revenues
that he was presenting a balanced budget which will include funds to hire the
City Administrator which Council requested. He stated that $70,000 has also
been allocated to be put back into the reserve account. Mayor Moriconi
indicated that the revenue projections in this budget are based on the adoption
of a compensating tax rate later this summer. Mr. Deters gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Creating the Position of Director of Economic Development
& Planning – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would create the position of Director of Economic Development & Planning.
A brief discussion ensued as to whether this job description was for a part-
time or full-time position. Mayor Moriconi advised that the proposed Pay Plan
was a wide pay range to accommodate either part or full time. Mr. Deters
advised that the job function and duties will be the same regardless of the
number of hours the position works. There being no further discussion Mr.
Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting a Pay & Classification Plan for 2008/09 Fiscal
Year – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that will
adopt a Pay and Classification Plan for the 2008/09 fiscal year. Mr. Deters
read the proposed ordinance.
Police Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler reported that Officer Hobart Strange, for the second consecutive
year, has received Outstanding Student Resource Officer (SRO) of the Year.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi stated he did not have anything to report.
Discussion Regarding the RV (recreational vehicle) Ordinance
Council Member Brinker asked about the status of a zoning text amendment
application regarding the regulations for the parking and storage of
recreational vehicles. Mr. Deters stated there was some confusion at the last
meeting when Council directed him to prepare an ordinance with the text
revisions they had discussed. He went on to advise Council that all zoning text
amendments have to go through the Planning Commission for review and
recommendation back to the City before the City can proceed with making any
changes. Mr. Deters stated that he is of the opinion that the City will get a
negative response from the Planning Commission for the text changes the City is
considering. Mr. Brinker suggested that the City allow a side yard setback when
a property owner cannot get the RV in the rear yard. Zoning Administrator,
Annie Wuestefeld commented that the language Council Member Brinker is
suggesting is already in the zoning text and is considered a conditional use
thereby requiring the property owner to make an application to the Board of
Adjustments for approval. Council Member Little commented that therein lies the
concern, which is the $500.00 application fee to the Board of Adjustment. He
stated that Mr. Deters has recommended to this Council that it is not possible
to give relief from this fee to some and not others. In closing this
discussion, Council Member Brinker commented that he wanted to try to help the
property owners that had extenuating reasons why they couldn’t comply with the
current regulations, but that sometimes the City cannot make changes if the
changes won’t be fair to all.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:40 p.m.

June 2, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 2,
2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance. Council
Member Jim Bushong gave the invocation. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the May 5, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on May 5, 2008. Council Member Behler so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the May 13, 2008 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the special
meeting held on May 15, 2008. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by
Council Member Little. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Don Nienabor, 66 McCullum Road, Independence – stated he would like to address
Council during the discussion of the Neyer Development.
Steven McGuire, 10667 Sinclair Drive, Independence – addressed the Council
regarding a drainage issue on his property. He stated he has lived at the
property for one year, presented photos to the Council and stated that his sump
pump runs constantly. Mr. Deters advised that since the house was built in
accordance with subdivision regulations, that this water runoff from his
neighbor’s property would be a civil matter. He suggested that Mr. McGuire meet
with the city’s Building Inspector to confirm that it was built according to
the plans.
Charles Deters, Independence Towne Center – stated he would like to address the
Council during the discussion of the Neyer Development.
Neyer Development – Proposed Ordinance Relating to Zone Change & Development
Plan
Mayor Moriconi submitted to Council the Kenton County Planning Commission’s
Statement of Recommendation to disapprove Neyer Properties, Inc. proposal for a
map amendment for an approximate 24.4 acre area located along the south side of
McCullum Pike, at its intersection with the new KY 17 from R-1C to NSC. He
stated that the City has a ninety day window to take action on this
recommendation. He advised the City could accept the recommendation to
disapprove this proposed zone change or can override the recommendation and go
ahead and approve the plan. A brief discussion ensued. Council Members Little
and Franzen expressed some concern that this recent proposed development plan
did not include the development of the north side of the intersection. They
stated they did not feel comfortable approving this zone change since it does
not comply with the recent Downtown Study adopted by the City and does not
include a development plan for the north side.
Council Member Behler moved to accept the recommendation of the Kenton County
Planning Commission to disapprove the map amendment, seconded by Council Member
Bushong. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to citizens who wanted to address the Council
on the Neyer Properties development plans.
Don Nienabor, 66 McCullum Road, Independence – commented that there is an old
cemetery on the north side and may be the reason Neyer did not provide a
development plan for that area. He stated they will have to deal with the
cemetery issue first. Mr. Nienabor also stated that he does not feel the
intersection will be able to handle the additional traffic that will be
generated by a shopping center. He also expressed concern that the development
plan did not include a retention pond and fears flooding will occur without it.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the development plan rendering that he has
includes a retention lake.
Charles Deters, Independence Towne Center – addressed Council regarding the
proposed commercial development on the new section of KY 17 and along the south
side of McCullum Pike by Neyer Properties, Inc. Mr. Deters provided a history
of the 250-acre development plan of the Towne Center which included land
donated for the construction of a fire department, city building and city park.
He stated that he believes the City needs good planning and that the Downtown
Study should be considered in the planning process when new proposals are
submitted, but he is concerned that the City will forget about the current
commercial property owners. He urged Council to make the future developers do
the appropriate planning.
Lawn/Park Maintenance – Award Bid
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received for the
lawn and park maintenance. He stated that a total of three bids were received
from Malco Services, Merkle Lawn Care and HHA Property Management. He stated
the City is currently in contract with Malco Services and the contract will
expire on June 30, 2008. Council reviewed the breakdown of the bid.
Council Member Yeager moved to award the lawn and park maintenance contract to
Malco Services, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Cox Road Turn Lane Construction Project – Award Bid
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received for the
Cox Road Turn Lane Project. He stated the City received five bids from the
following companies: JPS Construction, Inc. (low bid at $101,286.50), Paul
Michels & Sons, Len Riegler Blacktop, Eaton Asphalt Paving Co., and Barrett
Paving Company and that the City Engineer is recommending that the contract be
awarded to JPS Construction.
Council Member Little asked if the City would be receiving grant money for this
project. Mayor Moriconi advised that the state has agreed to contribute $40,000
and the developer of the Pembroke Subdivision, located at that intersection,
will be contributing $30,000.
Council Member Franzen moved to award the bid to the low bidder, JPS
Construction in the amount of $101,286.50, seconded by Council Member Yeager.
Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Interlocal Agreement with Kenton County for Collection of Occupational License
Fees
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council an Interlocal Agreement for the collection
of the City’s occupational taxes and related license fees. He stated this was
submitted by the County to the Mayor’s Group. He stated the county officials
advised the need to increase their collection fee to the cities from 1% to 2%
in order to cover the actual costs to provide this service to the participating
cities. This increase would necessitate that the current agreement be amended.
He stated that this fee increase will be a $20,000 hit to the budget.
Council Member Little moved to authorize Mayor Moriconi to enter into the
Interlocal Agreement for the collection of the City’s occupational taxes and
related fees, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered
with five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried
5-1.
Ordinance No. 2008-O-07 – Adopting the 2008/09 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2008-O-
07 adopting a budget for the 2008/09 fiscal year. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No.
2008-O-07 a second reading. Mayor Moriconi commented that this is a no frills
budget. There being no discussion, Council Member Franzen moved to adopt
Ordinance No. 2008-O-07, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Police Report – Shawn Butler
Chief Butler announced the July 4th Celebration this year will be held on
Friday and Saturday, July 4th & 5th.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report, but requested the need
for an executive session to discuss pending litigation.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Richardson Road Bridge - Mayor Moriconi directed the Council’s attention to the
letter in their packet from the state Transportation Cabinet advising that the
minimum load posting for the Old Richardson Road Bridge should be at 3 tons. He
stated that the state is also recommending that the bridge be closed and
barricaded to traffic given that there is an alternate access for motorist
using that bridge. He stated the City has changed the load posting from 8 ton
to 3 ton as recommended by the state but feels the City should consider closing
this bridge as well. He stated the City would need to get consent to close the
bridge from the property owners that would be affected by the closing. A brief
discussion ensued regarding the possibility of getting a police order to close
it right away until consents could be obtained. Also discussed was the
intersection of old SR17 and Old Richardson Road and the safety issued there
when making a right turn onto old SR17. Chief Butler stated he would look into
getting a police order to close the bridge immediately He commented that if the
residents don’t provide consent to close the bridge that the City would then
have to go through circuit court to get a judge’s ruling to close it, which
could take months. Council decided to provide written notice to the residents
right away and request they provide the City consent to close the bridge.
Re-Naming of old SR17 - Mayor Moriconi reported that the State has approached
him about renaming the old section of SR17 “Business 17”.
Miscellaneous
Council Member Behler announced the Northern Kentucky Health Department would
be holding a “Growing Livable Communities” workshop at Simon Kenton High School
on June 12 and 13, 2008. She stated this will be a good program to attend for
those interested in the Downtown Study. She urged everyone to attend and stated
that the first 100 registrants will attend for free.
Executive Session
There being no further business for the regular meeting of Council, at 7:47
p.m. Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to move into an executive session. Mr.
Deters stated the executive session would be pursuant to KRS 61.810 1(c) to
discuss pending litigation regarding the sewers. Council Member Bushong so
moved seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 8:17 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular session of
the meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:17 p.m.

August 4, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 4,
2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor Christian
J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance. Council
Member Jim Bushong gave the invocation. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the June 2, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on June 2, 2008. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by
Council Member Behler. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Executive Session
At 7:05 pm Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion to move into an executive
session. Mr. Deters stated the executive session would be pursuant to KRS
61.810 1(c) and (f) to discuss pending litigation regarding the sewers and to
discuss a personnel issue. Council Member Bushong so moved seconded by Council
Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 7:20 p.m. Council Member Bushong moved to reconvene the regular session of
the meeting, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
Municipal Order No. 2008-MO-06 – Appointment of City Administrator
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Municipal Order No. 2008-MO-06 that would
approve his appointment of Dan Groth to the position of City Administrator.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Municipal Order No. 2008-MO-06, seconded
by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one
no vote cast by Council Member Behler. Motion carried 5-1.
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Groth, saying that he comes to Independence with
twelve years experience as a City Administrator, first with the City of Dayton
and most recently with the City of Crestview Hills. He stated he is a former
police officer and Solid Waste Coordinator with the Northern Kentucky Area
Development District. He stated Mr. Groth was instrumental in the development
of the Crestview Hills Town Center and is accomplished in grant writing and was
able to secure grant dollars for the City of Dayton. Mr. Groth thanked everyone
and stated he is anxious to begin work with the City next week.
Discussion of Richardson Road Bridge
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mark Brueggemann, City Engineer with CDS &
Associates. He stated he asked Mr. Brueggemann to inspect the Richardson Road
Bridge and report to Council regarding its condition. Mayor Moriconi explained
that the City is considering closing the bridge as recommended by the State due
to its deteriorating condition.
Mr. Brueggemann reported that he estimates the replacement cost for the bridge
would run about $600,000. He suggested that if the bridge is closed that the
City could consider the realignment of the intersection of Old Richard Road and
Old SR 17. He stated that the intersection is currently on a skewed angle with
sight distance problems. He stated the intersection could be shifted to obtain
a 100 foot site distance and the profile of the road could be modified to
replace 500 feet of the road and install a retaining wall. He stated this
option would not be without problems as there is some evidence of hillside
instability and he estimates the cost to do this project would also run
approximately $600,000 to $625,000. He also advised that he has not performed a
detailed analysis so there may be more cost factors.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the bridge could be repaired. Mr. Brueggemann replied
no, as there is exposed rebar and significant cracks of the piers. He stated it
would not be cost effective. Council Member Bushong asked if the City could
possibly obtain some funding from other agencies to assist with the replacement
cost. Mayor Moriconi advised that while we will look for some funding, that it
doesn’t look promising and that ultimately it is the City’s responsibility.
Further discussion centered on placing more signage in the area, the City’s
liability in keeping the bridge open to traffic, doing a traffic count and more
discussion on replacing the bridge. Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for
comments from the residents.
Steve Rymarquis, 4744 Crowe Road, Independence – stated that currently Rumpke
trucks and City dump trucks do not even observe the signs posted on the bridge.
He suggested the City replace the current bridge with a new one-lane bridge if
the savings would be significant. He stated his greater concern is that if the
bridge is closed there will be safety issues that will exist when more traffic
uses the intersection of Old Richardson Road and old SR 17.
Dave Murphy, 4794 Crowe Road, Independence – stated he would like to see the
bridge remain open and feels the City should build a new bridge even if it is a
costly option. He expressed concern that the City neglected the maintenance
throughout the years and are now looking at closing it or total replacement.
Council Member Little asked the City Engineer what the time frame would be if
the City would consider building a new bridge. Mr. Brueggemann stated it would
be an approximate six month process that would include design, bidding out the
project and construction. Mayor Moriconi stated the City might contact
Congressman Davis for possible federal grants.
Michelle Reinhart, 3124 Summitrun Drive, Independence – stated the bridge
currently has a weight limit posting of three tons and wondered how emergency
vehicles such as fire trucks would access the area.
Paul Bledsoe, 3512 Richardson Road, Independence – challenged the City
Engineer’s cost estimate of $600,000 for a new bridge. He stated he feels it
would be much less as he thinks the abutments are in good condition.
After hearing the City Engineers assessment of the bridge condition and
comments from the residents, Council Members Little and Yeager concurred that
they feel the best solution would be a total bridge replacement. Council
discussed looking for possible grant funds to build a new bridge as well as
establishing some temporary safety precautions until a permanent solution can
be found.
Charlie Birkenhauer, 922 Collins Rd, Villa Hills (business located at 4758
Crowe Road, Independence) – stated he has an auto body business on Crowe Road
and since he has deliveries to his shop from roll-offs he is constantly using
the bridge and asked that the City did not install any traffic control devices
on the bridge that would hurt his business.
Mayor Moriconi closed the discussion and advised more information would be
forthcoming regarding any funding opportunities that may be available to the
City and possible solutions regarding the bridge replacement.
Request for City to Sponsor A Text Amendment Application Relating to Outdoor
Music/Entertainment in the Outdoor Dining Area in the NSC Zone
Mr. Eric Deters, 5247 Madison Pike, Independence – addressed the Council on
behalf of Bill Cunningham and Willie’s Restaurant in the Towne Center by
requesting the City sponsor the application for a zoning text amendment that

the restaurant has an outdoor dining area where they would like to provide

a small bakery in the Towne Center that would produce home style baked cookies.
He stated they would want to be able to package the cookies for resale
elsewhere. A brief discussion ensued about the text amendments. Council Member
Bushong moved to sponsor the zoning text amendment(s) for Mr. Deters, seconded
by Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Award Bid for the Madison Pike Sidewalk Project
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received for the
Madison Pike Sidewalk Phase III Project. He stated that four bids were received
and the City Engineer has recommended awarding the contract to the low bidder,
R.A. Miller Construction at $207,725.00. He stated that 60% of this project is
being funded by grant dollars
Council Member Franzen moved to award the bid to R.A. Miller Construction in
the amount of $207,725.00, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2004-O-01 Regarding Sidewalk
Waivers – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would amend
Ordinance No. 2004-O-01 that permits property owners waivers for the
construction of sidewalks. Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to the City’s
Building Inspector, Kevin Barbian, who is proposing this ordinance be amended.
Mr. Barbian explained there are various areas of the City that most likely will
never be able to have sidewalks constructed due to the topography of the land,
etc. He stated he feels it is an undue burden to the property owner to require
them to request a temporary waiver and execute a lien against the property. He
stated he has received a lot of negative feedback from residents about this
requirement. He stated he would like the ordinance to be amended to allow for a
permanent waiver of the provision that requires the construction of sidewalks
when the building inspector finds that there are no existing sidewalks in the
vicinity and that it is highly unlikely that sidewalks will be constructed in
the vicinity in the near future. Mayor Moriconi commented that it makes sense
to him and that a permanent waiver could be a collaborative decision with the
Zoning Administrator and Public Services personnel. A brief discussion ensued.
Council Member Yeager expressed concern regarding others that have paid for the
temporary waiver. Council Member Franzen asked the cost of the lien. Mr.
Barbian replied that the cost is $20 per linear foot. Council Member Little was
concerned about possible legal issues. Mr. Deters commented that this amendment
would give Mr. Barbian some discretion in granting either a permanent or
temporary waiver. Mayor Moriconi suggested having a first reading of the
ordinance and then look into the issue more before the second presentation at
the September meeting. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Text Amendment Regarding Shared Parking – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would approve a
zoning text amendment to make provisions for shared parking for off-street
parking facilities. Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld advised Council that
the Planning Commission made a recommendation to the City in February 1990 to
approve this provision, but it was not adopted by the Council. Council Member
Little asked which zones to which this would apply. Mrs. Wuestefeld stated it
would apply to all commercial zones, individual parcels and owners that share a
parking lot. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Franchise with Rumpke for Curbside Trash Pickup – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
relating to the contract renewal of the curbside collection of solid waste and
providing for an exclusive franchise to Rumpke of Northern Kentucky. Mr. Deters
read the proposed ordinance. There was no discussion.
Resolution No. 2008-R-06 – Authorize ––––Kentucky–– Office of Homeland Security
(KOHS) Application for P-25 Radio Project
Mayor Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2008-R-06 authorizing him to make
application for a grant, and upon approval, enter into an agreement with the
Kentucky Office of Homeland Security for the acquisition of P-25 radios for the
police department. Assistant Police Chief, Dave Nichols stated this project
stems from the September 11 terrorist attack in New York City when it became
apparent of the inoperability between agencies. He stated this grant will
supply digital radios that are more advanced and will be a step toward better
operations between other agencies in our community.
Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2008-R-06. Council Member Little moved to adopt
Resolution No. 2008-R-06, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2008-R-07 – Authorize ––––Kentucky–– Office of Homeland Security
(KOHS) Application for MDT Project
Mayor Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2008-R-07 authorizing him to make
application for a grant, and upon approval, enter into an agreement with the
Kentucky Office of Homeland Security for the acquisition of Mobile Data
Terminals (MDT) for the police department. Assistant Police Chief, Dave Nichols
stated this grant would provide in car computers, hardware, etc.
Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2008-R-07. Council Member Behler moved to adopt
Resolution No. 2008-R-07, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Police Report – Dave Nichols, Assistant Chief
Mr. Nichols stated he did not have anything to report.

August 28, 2008
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Thursday, August 28, 2008 at 6:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker,
Carol Franzen, and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
·   Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2008 Property Tax Rates – 1st Reading
·   Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2001-O-11 Relating to Fowler
Creek Sewer Debt Reduction Assessment specifically Amending the Time of
Periodic Payments – 1st Reading
·   Award Bid for Production Drive Resurfacing
·   Executive Session (only if necessary)
·   Adjournment
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2008 Property Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
set the 2008 tax rates for real and personal property. Mr. Deters read the
proposed ordinance establishing the ad valorem tax on real estate property at
$0.200 dollars for each one hundred dollars ($100.00) of assessed value and a
personal property tax rate of $0.596 dollars for each one hundred dollars
($100.00). Mayor Moriconi stated that the rates presented are the compensating
rate and does not include the 4% allowed by law and that the estimated revenue
for this tax was based on the adoption of the compensating rate for the 2008/09
budget. He stated this would be presented for a second reading and adoption at
the regular meeting of September 8, 2008.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2001-O-11 Relating to Fowler Creek
Sewer Debt Reduction Assessment specifically Amending the Time of Periodic
Payments – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2001-O-11 relating to the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt reduction
schedule. The proposed ordinance would specifically amend the time of the
periodic payments of the assessment. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. A
discussion ensued regarding a billing time and the consensus was to mail the
assessment bills in January with a payment due date of March 31 each year.
Council also added language to provide for penalty and interest to be affixed
to delinquent assessments; the penalty and interest to be calculated in the
same manner as the City’s property tax bills.
Council Member Franzen moved to accept the first reading as amended to add the
language discussed, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all
ayes.
Award Bid for Production Drive Resurfacing
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received on August
14, 2008 for the Production Drive Resurfacing Project. The City received six
bids which ranged from a low of $66,875.00 to the high bid of $88,696.00. He
stated the City Engineer has recommended the contract be awarded to Len Riegler
Blacktop in the amount of $66,875.00.
Council Member Behler moved to award the low bidder, Len Riegler Blacktop, the
contract, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 4-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business before the Council, Council Member Yeager moved
to adjourn, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting adjourned at 6:17 p.m.

September 8, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
8, 2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Council Member Jim Bushong gave the invocation. Mayor Moriconi called the
meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Michael
Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Presentation by Senator Damon Thayer
Senator Damon Thayer presented a check to the City in the amount of
$25,398,267.00, which represented the amount of State funds used for the road
improvements to the new section of SR17. He stated that five years ago he
committed to see that the improvements were funded and the road completed and
within two weeks the road will be finished which will benefit the City in
relieving traffic congestion and create some economic development opportunities
in the area. He stated the road project took longer than anticipated but that
it is a nice stretch of road. He stated that he also noticed the sidewalk
improvements along the old section of SR17 in which he assisted the City in
obtaining State and Federal funds. Mayor Moriconi thanked Senator Thayer and
added that the City appreciates funding assistance with these projects. He
stated that the City would like his assistance with obtaining funds for bridge
repairs and other needed projects.
Mayor Moriconi asked Senator Thayer if he could give an update on future road
improvements for SR536. Senator Thayer explained that the road projects are
funded in phases and advised that the current state budget has funded the
design phase. He state the next phase would include right of way purchases and
relocating utilities.
Council Member Bushong mentioned that that new intersection of SR17 and
McCullum Road has become a traffic safety concern and suggested a traffic light
be installed. Mayor Moriconi stated that the State will perform a traffic study
to determine the need for a light in that area. Senator Thayer advised he would
also check into it.
Approval of the August 4, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on August 4, 2008. Council Member Behler so moved, with second by
Council Member Little. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the August 28, 2008 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the special
meeting held on August 28, 2008. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
by Council Member Brinker. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered with four ayes and two abstentions from Council Members Bushong and
Little. Motion carried 4-2.
Privileges of the Floor
John Richardson, 10782 Cypresswood Drive, Independence – appeared before the
Council to let them know that he was launching the Independence Business
Association. He stated the time is right to start this association to get small
business owners involved with the City in an effort to keep them and attract
more business to the City. He stated the meetings will be held on the fourth
Monday each month and that more information can be found on the website –
indepba.org . Council Members commented that the formation of this organization
was a good idea and applauded his efforts.
Francie Allison, 786 Ackerly Drive, Independence – addressed Council with a
request to allow in home child care in her subdivision. Zoning Administrator,
Annie Wuestefeld advised Council that the Glenhurst Subdivision is a PUD
development that did not include in home child day care businesses on the Stage
I development plan. She stated this now becomes a legislative function that the
Council will need to authorize. She advised that the State has recently changed
their licensing procedures and is requesting written authorization from the
City before providing Ms. Allison with a state license. Mr. Deters advised that
if Council so desired to grant this request this could be accomplished by a
Resolution and would only pertain to the Glenhurst Subdivision. There was a
brief discussion that resulted in a consensus to grant Ms. Allison’s request.
Resolution No. 2008-R-10 – Relating to Day Care Facilities in the Glenhurst
Subdivision
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Resolution No. 2008-R-10 that would
authorize State certified in- home day care facilities, serving not more than
six children (in addition to any children related to the day care provider for
a maximum of 10 children) as a permitted use within the Glenhurst Subdivision
Planned Unit Development and such facilities shall be deemed minor adjustments
from the original Stage I development plan. Council Member Bushong seconded the
motion. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Michelle Fails, 2816 Sycamore Creek Drive, Independence – addressed Council
with request to support the lowering of the speed limit on Fowler Creek Road
between Sycamore Creek Drive and SR17. She reported that she had been in a bad
car collision several months ago that resulted in injuries to her and her
child. She stated this stretch of road is the scene of many accidents including
one fatality. She stated she is asking the State to lower the speed limit to 35
mph.
There was a brief discussion that concluded with Council Member Franzen making
a motion to authorize the Mayor to send a letter to the State Transportation
Cabinet petitioning them to lower the speed limit. Motion was seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0. Mayor Moriconi commented that the Kenton County Fiscal Court was also in
favor of lowering the speed limit.
Proposed Ordinance – Zoning Text Amendment Adopting Model Sign Regulations –
1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mike Schwartz, staff Deputy Director for Current
Planning with the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission who provided
Council with some background regarding the proposed zoning text amendment that
would adopt new model sign regulations. He advised that the Planning Commission
hired a consultant two years ago to assist the Planning Commission staff in
drafting model sign regulations. He stated the proposed draft is content
neutral using knowledge of the most recent court cases. It also maintains
certain decade old policies, but does now allow any new billboards. Mr.
Schwartz stated that this text change stems from the submission of text
applications from some cities requesting new billboards which they disapproved.
A lengthy discussion ensued regarding billboards and other new features of the
model sign regulations. Council Member Behler suggested that the Council
postpone a first reading of the proposed ordinance until the Independence
Strategic Action Committee (ISAC) has time to review the proposal and provide
their feedback to the City. In an effort to move forward with the approval
process, the consensus of the Council was to proceed with a first reading and
if ISAC made recommendations for text changes, then a new first reading could
be done. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance to adopt model sign
regulations.
Award Bid for 2008 Street Repairs Project
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received for the
2008 Street Repairs Project. Five bids were submitted with the low bid being
from Barrett Paving in the amount of $98,540.00 and the high bid from Eaton
Asphalt in the amount of $111,540.00. He stated this project would resurface
four streets: Gary, Marilyn, Rusconi and Sherry drives. He also advised that
the Public Services maintenance staff would be working on Sherwood Drive and
Gunstock Drive.
Council Member Little moved to award the bid to Barrett Paving in the amount of
$98,540.00, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2004-O-01 Regarding Sidewalk
Waivers – Motion to Table 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would amend Ordinance No. 2004-O-01 which permits property owners waivers
for the construction of sidewalks. Council Member Franzen moved to table the
