possibility of a more viable solution with the city attorney and building

Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2008-O-08, seconded by

Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2008-O-09, seconded by

Ordinance No. 2008-O-10 – Adopting 2008 Property Tax Rates – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2008-O-
10 that would adopt the 2008 property tax rates, both real estate and personal
properties. He stated the proposed rates are the compensating rates and have

Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2008-O-10, seconded by

Ordinance No. 2008-O-11 – Amending Ordinance No. 2001-O-11 Relating to Fowler
Creek Sewer Debt Reduction Assessment – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2008-O-
11 that would amend the time of periodic payments of the Fowler Creek Sewer

October 6, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
6, 2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following
Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Carol
Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Council Member Jim Bushong was
absent. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the September 8, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on September 8, 2008. Council Member Yeager so moved, with second
by Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 5-0.
ISAC (Independence Strategic Action Committee) Report – Chairman, Rodney Crice
Mayor Moriconi introduced Rodney Crice, Chairman of the ISAC who was present to
report the Committee’s activities. Mr. Crice stated that the members are
getting acquainted and have selected officers and divided into sub-committees.
He stated there are three sub-committees for historic preservation, zoning
update and city beautification. He stated they are focusing on short term
goals. He reported that the Committee is in the process of reviewing the
proposed Model Sign regulations and will have a recommendation to Council at
the next meeting.
City Administrator Dan Groth commented that the sub-committees meet at 6 pm
prior to the ISAC meeting at 7 pm on the third Thursday of each month. He
stated most meetings are held at the Senior Center, but occasionally they meet
in the Council Chambers. Mr. Groth also reported that the ISAC Committee
originally had seven members, but that two members have resigned. He stated
that the remaining Committee members have asked to be permitted to move on with
the five remaining members and not replace the two vacated positions at this
time.
Mayor Moriconi asked Mr. Crice if he would bring the Committee’s recommendation
to Council regarding the Model Sign regulations at the City’s next meeting. Mr.
Crice replied yes, that is their goal.
Ratify Independence Village Stage II Development Plan – United Dairy Farmers –
NKAPC 1942R)
Mayor Moriconi presented for Council’s consideration a Stage II development
plan for the Independence Village for an approximate 1.6 acre area located at
the southwest corner of the intersection of Centennial Blvd. with the new SR17.
He stated this plan would involve the construction of a United Dairy Farmers
(UDF) convenience store with eight gasoline pumps and a canopy. He stated the
revisions to this plan would be the removal of a car wash, the addition of a
patio, additional signs on the canopy, as well as set back changes and a change
in the position of the structure on the lot. Mr. Groth advised Council they
were sent a booklet on the proposed development plan prior to tonight’s
meeting.
Representatives for UDF present at this meeting included architect John
Johnston, real estate developer Tim Kling and Don Stegman of Cardinal
Engineering. They advised that UDF entered into a contract with the developers
in 2005 and that the proposed development will be for the construction of 5300
square feet of retail space with eight fuel dispensers, an ice cream parlor and
attached outside patio. The plan would include extensive landscape. He stated
that the proposed signage is two square feet over what is permitted by the
City. They provided prototype photographs that would be used as models for the
Independence structure and indicated that the building would face north and
therefore requested four Mobile logo signs on the fuel pump canopy. He stated
they were also requesting a landscape monument sign at the entrance/exit to the
site. A discussion ensued regarding the signage, setbacks and obtaining a land
disturbance permit from SD1. Mr. Johnston advised that they have applied for
and submitted a bond for the land disturbance permit. Ms. Behler commented that
she was impressed with the extensive landscape design and asked if the greenery
would be replaced if ruined by drought, etc. Mr. Johnston stated that a full
irrigation system would be installed on the site to maintain the landscape.
There was discussion regarding a portion of the building that would be occupied
by a tenant. Mr. Kling advised that they would attempt to occupy that space
with a “high traffic driven” business, such as a pizza place or sandwich shop.
Final discussion regarding this development was the color of the roof. Council
expressed a desire to be consistent with the Independence Towne Center (green
roof) which has set the trend in the City. Mr. Johnston stated he would work
with the City on roof color. He stated they have owned the property for some
time now and would like to proceed with the construction as soon as possible.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve the Independence Village Stage
II development plan for the UDF parcel contingent on the following four
conditions:
·   Obtaining a land disturbance permit
·   Submitting the construction plans to the City’s Zoning Administrator prior
to issuance of a zoning permit
·   Approval of the roof color by City Council
·   Development must be completed within 12 months
Council Member Brinker seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered with
all ayes. Motion carried 5-0.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth reported that Council Member Behler has been awarded the Frank M.
Gaines Professional Award for her contribution made in the promotion of mental
health, prevention of mental illness and the improvement of diagnosis and
treatment of people with mental illness. He congratulated her and commented
that her achievement bodes well for the City of Independence.
Mr. Groth thanked the Public Works and Police department’s personnel for their
professionalism in handling calls the week following the windstorm on Sunday,
September 14, 2008. An area in Memorial Park, behind the Municipal Center, was
designated as a tree and yard debris drop off site for residents.
Mr. Groth reported that in response to the City’s request the state has
approved a speed limit reduction on Fowler Creek Road – from 45 mph to 35 mph.
He also announced that the City would be sponsoring a Howl-O-Ween event on
October 18, 2008 from noon to 6 PM at Memorial Park and that the City would
observe trick-or-treating on Friday, October 31, 2008 from 6:00-8:00 PM.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi stated he did not have anything to report.
Executive Session
At 7:41 p.m. City Attorney Jed Deters requested an executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss pending litigation, specifically
Cobble v City relating to the sewer maintenance fees. Council Member Yeager so
moved, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 8:16 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:17 p.m.

November 10, 2008
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, November 10, 2008 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker,
Carol Franzen, and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
§   Approval of October 6, 2008 Meeting Minutes
§   Independence Village Development Stage II Revision (United Dairy Farmers) –
Discussion & Possible Action
§   Independence Village Development Stage II Revision (Republic Bank) –
Discussion & Possible Action
§   Proposed Ordinance – Establishing Speed Limits on Roads acquired from
Kenton County – 1st Reading
§   Proposed Ordinance – Occupational License Regulations Amendment – 1st
Reading
§   Ordinance No. 2008-O-12 – Relating to Sidewalk Waivers – Possible 2nd
Reading
§   Ordinance No. 2008-O-13 – Adopting Model Sign Regulations – 2nd Reading
§   Resolution No. 2008-R-11 – Designating an Agent for a Grant Application for
Federal Disaster Assistance
§   Executive Session in accordance with KRS 61.810 to discuss pending
litigation
Approval of the October 6, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on October 6, 2008. Council Member Behler so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
with five ayes and one abstain by Council Member Bushong; motion carried 5-1.
Independence Village Development Stage II Revision (United Dairy Farmers)
Mayor Moriconi stated that when the UDF representatives last appeared before
the Council there was some discussion regarding the roof color of the store
planned for the intersection of Centennial Blvd. and the new section of SR17.
He stated that Mr. Johnston is here to present some sample colors for the roof.
Mr. Johnston presented four roof samples in shades of blue and green for
Council’s consideration. He also advised that they decided to eliminate the
extra retail space in this structure they had originally planned to lease. He
stated they feel this store will be successful at this location and they will
probably need the extra space for the UDF store. Council briefly discussed the
roof colors.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve the Stage II development plan, without
the retail rental space and with a blue roof color. Council Member Yeager
seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered 6-0.
Independence Village Development Stage II Revision (Republic Bank)
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Carol James, representative of Republic
Bank. Ms. James stated she was appearing before the Council regarding the
signage of this bank. She advised that the signs were installed before a City
permit was obtained. She stated that the directional signs are in violation of
the Stage I plan requirements and is asking the Council to allow them to keep
the signs in place. She stated they also have also applied for another sign
permit which would be attached to the building. She said the proposed sign
exceeds the permitted square footage by two feet and is asking the City to
waive this. She stated the directional signs are illuminated and aid the
customers in navigating the property. She stated the traffic on the property is
one-way and the signs are a safety issue. Ms. James apologized for the mishap
in installing the signs before a permit was obtained. She stated their vendor
used a sub-contractor and there was some miscommunication.
Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld advised Council that in the approved
Stage I development plan each tenant in this strip mall was permitted two 60-
square foot monument signs and one 40-square foot façade sign. If they submit
anything different from the approved Stage I plan then it goes back for a Stage
II plan review. She stated that since this development is a PUD the Council has
to give final approval.
Council Member Behler expressed concern that the bank was asking for
forgiveness instead of getting permission. Council Member Franzen stated she
was willing to allow the signs that have already been installed but that the
building sign would need to comply with the Stage I plan requirements and not
the 42 square feet that was being proposed. A brief discussion ensued.
Council Member Yeager moved to approve all the signage currently installed at
the site, including the directional signs and to disapprove the additional
proposed 42 square foot façade sign on the east elevation of the building.
Council Member Franzen seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered with
four ayes and two no votes cast by Council Members Behler and Bushong. Motion
carried 4-2.
Proposed Ordinance – Establishing Speed Limits on Roads acquired from Kenton
County – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
establish new speed limits on the following streets: 25 mph for Stephens Road
and Pelly Road; and 35 mph for Oliver Road, Hogrefe Road, Marshall Road, Mills
Road and Cody Road. Mr. Groth, City Administrator advised that all city streets
have an automatic 20 mph speed limit unless otherwise established by ordinance.
He said the county has asked the City to allow the speed limits as proposed in
the ordinance. There being no discussion, Mayor Moriconi directed Mr. Deters to
give the ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Occupational License Regulations Amendment – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for Council’s consideration a proposed ordinance that
will amend the current Occupational License regulations. Mr. Groth explained
that the City of Covington would like to be a part of this interlocal agreement
with Kenton County who administers and collects the occupational license fees
for many of the cities in Northern Kentucky. He stated that the current annual
county-wide license fee is $185.00 which is divided among the participating
cities. He went on to say that to accommodate Covington joining the agreement
the county-wide license fee would increase to $225.00. He stated that
Covington’s share of the county-wide license fee would be $25.00 with the
remainder of the increased amount to be placed in an escrow account until such
time that an equitable division calculation could be reached. Mr. Groth
commented that any new calculation will be favorable for Independence as the
old calculation was based on outdated factors. Since Covington would like to
join effective January 1, 2009 each city is being asked to pass an updated
ordinance that would include Covington in the multi-jurisdictional agreement by
December 31, 2008.
Council Member Franzen expressed some reservations with raising the rates in
this sluggish economy. Mr. Groth advised that the rates have not been raised
since 1993 and that the realtors have been actively petitioning the State to
adopt a central collection of this tax which would not benefit the cities.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Sidewalk Waivers – Second Reading of Proposed Ordinance – Postponed
Indefinitely
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would amend Ordinance No. 2004-O-01 that provides for sidewalk waivers
with the use of property liens. Council Member Franzen advised that she has
discussed this at length with Mr. Deters and Kevin Barbian (Building
Inspector). She stated that she does not like the idea of a property lien as
they cause problems at the time of a property transfer. She stated she would
prefer language that would permit the City to assess the property owner at the
time when sidewalks are installed. Mr. Deters stated that sidewalk projects are
considered a public improvement and the City would always have the right to
assess the property owner if and when sidewalks are constructed. A lengthy
discussion ensued about the pros and cons of liens and assessments. In closing,
Council was unable to reach a consensus. Council Member Franzen moved to
indefinitely table the second reading of the proposed ordinance, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Model Sign Regulations Text Amendment – Second Reading of Ordinance Postponed
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would amend the zoning text adopting new model sign regulations. He
stated, as directed by the Council, the Independence Strategic Action Committee
(ISAC) has reviewed the text changes and submitted their recommendations,
meeting minutes and notes for Council’s consideration. Council Member Franzen
stated that since ISAC has proposed numerous text changes that a new first
reading should be done on this ordinance. A discussion ensued. Mr. Groth
advised that a few cities have made some minor changes to the text that has
been proposed by the Planning Commission and only one local city has not
adopted these regulations. He stated if the Council decides not to adopt these
model sign regulations then we would just keep the regulations currently being
used.
After some discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Behler to have the
City Attorney review the proposed model sign regulations as well as the
proposed ISAC recommended changes before Council makes any changes. Council
Member Franzen seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2008-R-11 – Designation of Applicant Agent for FEMA Disaster
Assistance
Mr. Groth, City Administration advised Council there were federal funds
available for damages from the September 14, 2008 windstorm that struck this
area. He stated this resolution would authorize him to execute an application
and file it in the appropriate State office. He stated our damage expenses were
minimal, but we could apply for reimbursement from FEMA. Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2008-R-11.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2008-R-11, seconded by
Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Executive Session
There being no further business to discuss, Mayor Moriconi entertained a motion
to enter into an Executive Session in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to
discuss pending litigation on a sewer related issue, specifically Cobble v
City. Council Member Little so moved, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion
carried with all ayes. At 8:08 p.m. Council retired to the Executive Session
room.
At 9:30 p.m. Council Member Behler moved to reconvene the regular session of
the Council meeting, seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all
ayes.
Cobble v City – Motion to Appeal Judge’s Ruling
Council Member Brinker moved to direct the City Attorney to pursue an appeal of
the recent decisions in the Cobble matter. He stated that while it is his
desire and that of this Council, to return to the citizens of Independence
every dollar that should be refunded to them that he wants to ensure that it is
all accomplished in a legal and appropriate manner. He stated that he is not
just convinced that this will be accomplished under the current decision and
the parameters set forth therein. He stated this is especially true in light of
the latest lawsuit which challenges the Fowler Creek assessment process.
Council Member Bushong seconded the motion. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business before the Council, Council Member Little moved
to adjourn, seconded by Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting adjourned at 9:31 p.m.

December 1, 2008
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, December
1, 2008 at 7:00 pm in the Municipal Center Council Chambers with Mayor
Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi led the Pledge of Allegiance
and the invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong. Mayor Moriconi
called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen,
Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Mayor Moriconi stated that we have a lot of good things happening at tonight’s
meeting and that the City has the pleasure of recognizing several members of
the Independence Police Department for jobs well done this year. In addition,
the Police Department has re-established the Police Chaplain Program. He stated
he would first swear-in the Police chaplains.
Swearing-In of Police Chaplains
Mayor Moriconi administered the Oath of Office to, and introduced James Gentry
of the Mt. Zion Baptist Church, Charlie Steger of the Hickory Grove Baptist
Church, Dr. Gary Wilson, Counselor and Evangelist, Wilbert Ellis of Grace
Baptist Church and Lisa May of Faith Community Church. Chief Butler distributed
to each Chaplain a framed plaque of the Oath document. Mayor Moriconi thanked
each of them for their service to the community.
Awards Recognition for City Police Officers and Members of Police Explorers
Program
Mayor Moriconi stated that the Police Department has several officers that are
members of the Northern Kentucky Emergency Response Unit (NKERU), otherwise
known as S.W.A.T. He advised that the NKERU recently took first place in the
annual competition of KTOA (Kentucky Tactical Officers Association), which is a
statewide competition that involves other tactical groups and that the first
place status was for overall performance by the team.
Mayor Moriconi stated that the members of the Independence Police Explorers
participated in the 2008 Bowling Green Police Explorers competition in
September. He stated the Explorers are a group of local 14-21 year olds
learning about law enforcement. He stated the Independence Explorers members
are: Ben Bridges, Matt Hard, Cody Miller, Cody Cioffe, Dustin Jones, Joe
Portwood, Sara Chard, Drew Lucas and C.J. Whittenberger. Mayor Moriconi
congratulated them on taking third place in the active shooter competition, a
simulated training exercise.
Mayor Moriconi asked everyone to join him in honoring Officer Todd Bennett and
Officer Russ Woods who were involved in a tragic incident on Freedom Trail in
October. In recognition of their unselfless actions during an emergency
situation, which resulted in the saving of a human life, Mayor Moriconi
presented each Officer with a life saving award for their heroism and a silver
star for their bravery which has been granted by the American Police Hall of
Fame. Mayor Moriconi commented that all the City’s police officers never
panicked and quickly took control of the situation that night. He applauded
their work and stated it was an honor to have them on the Independence Police
force.
Next, in recognition of their outstanding investigation in an unusual and
difficult criminal case where they displayed officer’s skills and dedication to
the City, Mayor Moriconi presented Officer Mike Thatcher, Detectives Jim Moore
and Mike Richman and Officer Matt Hicks an award for their achievement in
criminal investigation.
Mayor Moriconi then presented each of the following with an Outstanding
Commendation Award for their performance of duties as a police officer and for
their actions during the tragic incident that occurred on Freedom Trail in
October: Assistant Police Chief Dave Nichols, Captain Bailey, Captain Lucas,
and Sgt. Lonaker, Sgt. Paul, Sgt. Schultz, Sgt. Schworer and Officers Todd
Bennet, Nathan Fuson, Tony Hill, Ron Hutchinson and Russ Wood.
Certification of Public Works Employees
City Administrator, Dan Groth announced that two of the City’s Public Works
personnel recently received their Road Master certification from the University
of Kentucky Transportation Center. He stated that Ken Hicks and Tom Robke will
be receiving their awards at a special luncheon December 16, 2008 at the
Executive Inn in Louisville.
Approval of the November 10, 2008 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the special
meeting held on November 10, 2008. Council Member Behler so moved, with second
by Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered with five ayes and one abstention from Council Member Bushong. Motion
carried 5-1.
Privileges of the Floor
Vic Morrison, 100 Roselawn, Independence – commented that he has supported the
police department for many years and was proud to see them honored for their
service to the City.
Twenhofel Middle School – Students Energy Wise Team
Mayor Moriconi stated he has received emails from some students of Twenhofel’s
Energy Wise Team. He introduced eighth-grader Blake Emmons who was present to
talk to Council about the Energy Wise team, what it would mean to the City and
how the City can help.
Mr. Emmons addressed Council by explaining the school’s Energy Wise team
promotes the saving of energy and helping the environment. He stated that they
would like to propose that the City lower the recycling rates paid by the
residents or provide incentives to participate in recycling such as giving tax
breaks. He stated they have implemented a recycling program at school and it
seems helpful. Mayor Moriconi advised that Rumpke sets the recycling rates.
Mayor Moriconi suggested the students submit an article for the City’s spring
newsletter that would provide information about their Energy Wise team and give
the residents advice on how they can help the environment and save energy. Mr.
Groth reported that currently only 6% of the property owners participate in
curbside recycling and that if the City did provide for the cost of recycling
the participation would still be relatively low at an estimated 20%. He stated
he agrees that recycling saves space in landfills and ultimately helps our
environment. Mr. Emmons thanked Mayor Moriconi and Council for allowing him to
speak about this issue. Mayor thanked the students and applauded their efforts.
Again Mayor Moriconi encouraged the students to submit an article for the next
newsletter.
Simon Kenton High School – Engineering Students “Safety Zone” Proposal
Mayor Moriconi stated he went to Simon Kenton HS a few weeks ago and met with
some engineering students who have created a type of a safety zone in front of
the high school along the new section of SR17 from the area of Chambers &
Grubbs funeral home to the intersection of SR 536. He stated the students have
created a schematic drawing of the area and have proposed ideas that include
lowering the speed limit to 35 mph, installing grooves in the road, electronic
flashing speed sign. Mayor Moriconi stated he has advised the students that
SR17 is a state maintained road and the City is limited by what the State
agrees to regarding the road, but that we would be happy to petition the State
on behalf of the students.
A lengthy discussion ensued. Student, Chelsea Williams stated a lady was
recently struck while crossing the road in front of the school and they feel
that lowering the speed limit and adding more signage could make the school
zone area safer. Ms. Williams reported that many students that cannot afford a
school parking pass park at the Independence Towne Center parking lot and then
walk to the school. Council Member Brinker stated he would also like to see
sidewalks constructed in the area. Mayor Moriconi suggested that the City might
be able to partner with the Kenton County School Board for the installation of
the sidewalks and stated he would arrange a meeting with them to discuss these
issues. Further discussion centered on the sidewalks along the old section of
SR17, SR536 and the vicinity of the Towne Center. Mr. Deters advised that
undeveloped lots in the Towne Center do not have to install the sidewalks until
the lots are sold and developed. Mr. Groth stated that a preliminary estimate
to install sidewalks from SR536 to the school would be approximately $88,000.
Mayor Moriconi stated this cost could be discussed with the School Board
representatives. Council Member Franzen asked when McDonald’s would be
installing the section of sidewalk on their property. Mr. Groth advised this
would be installed in the near future.
Council Member Brinker made a motion to move forward with installing sidewalks
along the old section of SR17 from McDonald’s to Simon Kenton High School as
soon as possible and before the start of the next school year beginning in
August 2009. Council Member Little seconded the motion. Council Member Yeager
stated she feels the State should install sidewalks on the lot they own.
Council Member Behler stated that while she fully supports the installation of
the sidewalks, this is not a simple project and she would like to know where
the funds will come from to pay for this project. There being no further
discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Council Member Behler commented that she feels the City will agree to do its
part to make this a safe zone, but that it is also important that the students
develop a safety awareness program within the school that will compliment the
City’s efforts. Mayor Moriconi stated that we might need a motion based on
their key points to send to the State regarding the speed limit. Mr. Deters
stated he would draft a Resolution to be presented at the January meeting that
would outline the City’s support of the student’s proposal. Council Member
Yeager so moved, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2008-R-12 - Requesting State Hwy Dept to Reduce Speed Limits on
Certain Streets & Install traffic light on new SR16 and Cox Road
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2008-R-12 that would support
the installation of a traffic light at the intersection of SR16 and Cox Road as
well as reduce the speed limit to 35 miles per hour on Cox Road. Mr. Groth
stated that residents have petitioned the City to reduce the speed limit and to
look into the feasibility of a traffic light. He stated the State will make a
study and report back to the City. Council Member Behler asked if the City
would have any other options if the State does not meet the City’s request. Mr.
Groth stated that other safety measures could be implemented such as additional
signage, speed humps, etc.

every day and that visibility is impeded by vans parked in the old gas station
lot on the corner. Mr. Groth stated he would have the Police Chief looked into
it to see if a code violation exists.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Bushong moved to adopt
Resolution No. 2008-R-12, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.

Resolution No. 2008-R-14 – Approving a Revised Personnel Policy handbook

2009 Minutes
January 5, 2009
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
5, 2009 at 7:00 pm in the auditorium of Simon Kenton High School, 11132 Madison
Pike, Independence, with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi
called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called
and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Margaret
Cook, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Council Member Jim
Bushong was absent. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Proclamation presented to Simon Kenton High School Football Team
Mayor Moriconi presented a Key to the City and Proclamation to the Simon Kenton
High School football team to commend them on their successful season winning
the regional championship trophy and going on to compete in and win the
school’s first ever semi-final championship game which qualified them to play
in the state championship game held on December 13, 2008. Mayor Moriconi
applauded the team members and head Coach Jeff Marksberry and his coaching
staff on their achievements and the positive recognition they brought to our
community. Coach Marksberry thanked Mayor Moriconi and the City Council.
Approval of the December 1, 2008 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on December 1, 2008. Council Member Behler so moved, with second
by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered with four ayes and one
abstain voiced by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 4-1.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex New Section of SR17 – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would document
the City’s intent to annex approximately fifty-three acres of ground being the
right of way of relocated KY17 south from Fowler Creek Road. He stated that by
annexing these right of way parcels the City would control future developments
on this road. Mr. Groth, City Administrator, commented that the annexed areas
total five sections along the new SR17 starting at the southerly corporation
line of the City of Covington and continuing on past McCullum Road.
There being no comments from Council, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading. Mayor Moriconi advised that the City would not be annexing
private properties along this road, just the right of way.
Resolution No. 2009-R-01 – Approving a Revised Personnel Policy Handbook

a revised Personnel Policy handbook. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2009-R-01.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2009-R-01, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Council Member Little asked a couple of questions
regarding probationary periods and cell phones as a taxable employee fringe
benefit. There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.

Engineering Class “Safety Zone” Project

for the installation and initiation of a “safety zone” on SR17. Mayor Moriconi

5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Zoning Text Amendment to Adopt Model Sign Regulations
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would adopt a zoning text amendment deleting current sign regulations and
inserting new model sign regulations. He stated that due to the length of the
document, lingering concerns by Council regarding some of the proposed text
changes, and the seating of a new member of Council at this meeting that it may
be best to delay the second reading of this ordinance until next month. He
stated that Council needs to be comfortable in adopting these proposed
regulations and suggested that Council send all their concerns and/or questions
to the City Administrator who will meet with the NKAPC staff to get answers.
Mayor Moriconi stated that most of the cities in Northern Kentucky have adopted
this model sign text, except for the City of Independence. He stated he is
comfortable with holding off on taking action on this until next month.

Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi announced that he would be hosting the Northern Kentucky Mayor’s
Group for their monthly meeting on Saturday, January 16th at 9:00 a.m. at the
Senior Center and encouraged the Council Members to attend this meeting.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:31 p.m.

February 9, 2009
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, February 9, 2009 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong,
Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi announced this special meeting of the City Council was called to
discuss the following agenda items:
·   Approval of January 5, 2009 Meeting Minutes
·   Independence Village – KCPC W-649 Waiver Request
·   Ordinance No. 2009-O-01 – Text Amendment Approving Model Sign Regulations –
2nd Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2009-O-02 – Intent to Annex a Total of 53.267 Acres, More or
Less, and being the Right of Way Area of Relocated KY-17 – 2nd Reading
·   Proposed Ordinance – Approving Cincinnati Bell Cable Franchise – 1st
Reading
·   Accept Property Transfer of Land Known as Shadywood Park and Authorize
Mayor to Sign Property Deed
·   Municipal Order 2009-MO-02 – Appointing Mary Pat Dressman to Senior Board
·   City Administrator’s Report
o   Additional street lights to be installed on new section of SR17
·   Mayor’s Report
o   Presentation of 2007 Annual Audit
o   Update on Old Richardson Road Bridge
·   Executive Session in accordance with KRS 61.810 (if necessary)
Approval of the January 5, 2009 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on January 5, 2009. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
by Council Member Yeager. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered with five ayes and one abstain by Council Member Bushong; motion
carried 5-1.
Independence Village – KCPC No. W-649 Waiver Request
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council correspondence from the Kenton County
Planning Commission relating to an application by Ashley Commercial Group
requesting waivers for two subdivision requirements. The first waiver request
was for the requirement that curb cuts along Madison Pike be located at least
400 feet away from the intersection of Madison Pike and Centennial Blvd and the
second waiver request was the requirement of the private street be provided to
interconnect Centennial Drive opposite Everett Drive with the private street
east of Lot #12 and require sidewalks along both sides of this private drive as
shown on the approved amended Stage I development plan. Mayor Moriconi asked
Mike Schwartz, Chief Planner with the Planning Commission to comment on these
waiver requests. Mr. Schwartz advised that the Planning Commission has approved
the first request regarding the curb cut and permitted the proposed access
point along Madison Pike as a right-in/right-out access point only. He stated
this would prohibit left turn ingress/egress. He stated the second waiver
request to eliminate the private street and sidewalks has been denied. Mr.
Schwartz stated that the correspondence was sent to the City for informational
purposes and that no action by the Council was necessary as these were
subdivision regulation waiver request which are handled by the Planning
Commission staff.
DEFEATED Ordinance No. 2009-O-01 – Text Amendment Approving Model Sign
Regulations – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2009-O-01 which
would approve a text amendment that would eliminate the current sign
regulations in the City’s zoning ordinance and adopt new model sign
regulations. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2009-O-01 a second reading.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2009-O-01, seconded by
Council Member Behler.
Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for comments and discussion. Council Member
Little distributed a handout he compiled that contained a sampling of photos of
current signs throughout the City that would not be legal to erect under the
new regulations in the model ordinance. He stated that his concerns were that
the new sign regulations would be difficult to enforce as they seem too
complicated and intrusive. He stated many of the signs were on church and
school properties NKAPC Planner, Mike Schwartz stated that public schools are
exempt from zoning regulations. Another concern expressed by Council was the
limit of 4 political signs per property. Mr. Schwartz stated the City could
place a higher limit of political signs. Council Member Franzen express
concerns that the new regulations would limit free speech. Mr. Schwartz advised
that adopting the new regulations would provide a better legal foundation. He
stated that the Planning Commission hired a consultant who worked on this
document for approximately a year and that many of the new regulations were
drafted based on current federal court cases. There was discussion about making
several text changes, but Mr. Schwartz cautioned that changing one element of
the document could affect the whole. Mr. Little stated he understood that and
would rather vote it down than to make a lot of changes. Council Member Behler
expressed concern about keeping the current regulations if they were not up to
the current legal standards.
Roll call vote was taken and answered with two ayes and four no votes cast by
Council Members Bushong, Cook, Little and Yeager. Motion failed.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt the proposed model sign regulations in
Ordinance No. 2009-O-01 without limits on political yard signs for single
family and multi-family residential properties, seconded by Council Member
Behler. Roll was called and answered with two ayes and four no votes cast by
Council Members Cook, Little, Yeager and Bushong. Motion failed and Ordinance
No. 2009-O-01 was defeated on the second reading.
Ordinance No. 2009-O-02 – Intent to Annex a Total of 53.267 Acres, More or
Less, and Being the Right of Way Area of Relocated SR17 – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2009-O-

Mr. Groth reported that he met with representatives of the State highway
regarding the City’s concern with lack of adequate street lighting on the new
section of SR17. He stated that since poles are already in the area, Duke
Energy has agreed to install the light fixtures and then the City would just
have to pay the monthly electric charges.
Council Member Yeager moved to approve the installation of the lights on the
poles and pay the electricity bills, seconded by Council Member Little. No roll
call; motion carried with all ayes.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Presentation of 2007 Audit -  Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the 2007
Audit report for fiscal year ending June 2008. He asked the Council to review
the document and direct any questions about it to Finance Director, Teresa
Hudson or to City Administrator, Dan Groth.
Update on Old Richardson/Crowe Road Bridge
Mayor Moriconi reported that action needs to be taken regarding the Old
Richardson Road Bridge. He advised that research has provided some cheaper
alternatives and consideration is being given to replacing the current bridge
with a one lane suspension bridge. He stated the bridge would cost
approximately $100,000 and the installation of the bridge would run between
$50,000 - $150,000. He stated that the City could realize some savings if the
Public Services employees dismantled the old bridge. Mr. Groth commented that a
realistic estimate for the bridge replacement would be between $175,000 -
$250,000. Mayor Moriconi stated this option is more cost effective than the
original estimate of $600,000 and bids may come in much lower than our estimate
due to the economic recession.
Mr. Groth commented that during the interim, and since the State has advised
the City that it is their recommendation that the bridge be closed, on April 1,
2009 the bridge will be closed until a replacement can be installed. He stated
that the he will be working with Kenton County officials to make application
for a bridge enhancement grant. He stated that while Kenton County is not
responsible for this bridge they have to apply for the grant on behalf of the
City.
A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Deters advised that by law if the residents that
are serviced by the bridge will not give their consent to close the bridge,
then the City will have to file suit against them. It was decided to send
another letter to the residents in the area of the bridge to inform them of the
April 1 Bridge closing and the City’s plans to replace the bridge if grant
money can be allocated from the State.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:27 p.m.

Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the special

Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment (KCPC No. 1952R)
Regulation Changes in NSC Zones – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would accept the
recommendation of the Kenton County Planning Commission for a zoning text
amendment that would modify the NSC (Neighborhood Shopping Center) zone that
would allow bakery and bakery goods stores to sell their products elsewhere off
the premises where they are baked and to disapprove outdoor dining areas, as a
conditional use, to have entertainment, music and sound amplifying systems. Mr.
Deters commented that he drafted a proposed ordinance pursuant to the KCPC
recommendation. Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion on the
recommendation.
A discussion ensued with Mr. Eric Deters, owner of the Bulldog’s Roadhouse
restaurant, who had requested Council consider these amendments to the zoning
regulations. Council’s main concern was that the outdoor music could be a
nuisance to the adjoining residential areas. Mr. Eric Deters stated that the
outdoor music would be mainly easy listening and acoustical types during the
warmer months – May through September. Council discussed imposing some
restrictions that included distance from residential zones and hours that music
could be played. Council Member Yeager suggested that the music could be played
until 10:00 p.m. on weekdays and 11:00 p.m. on weekends. Further discussion
identified weekends as Friday and Saturday nights and weekdays as Monday
through Thursday. Mayor Moriconi asked for a motion to indicate if the proposed
ordinance should be amended to permit the outdoor music.
Council Member Bushong moved with second by Council Member Yeager to add as a
conditional use, entertainment, music, and sound amplifying systems within the
outdoor dining areas, with the additional conditions that the same is only
permitted during the months of May through September, acoustical music shall be
permitted Sunday through Thursday until 10:00 p.m. and until 11:00 p.m. on
Friday and Saturday. No roll call; motion carried with four ayes and two no
votes.
The City Attorney gave the proposed ordinance a first reading as amended by
Council. Mayor Moriconi stated the ordinance would be presented for a second
reading at the April 6, 2009 meeting.
Occupational License Fees
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a revised Interlocal Agreement with Kenton
County for the collection of the City’s Occupational License Fees and Taxes.
The revised agreement would incorporate the City of Covington into the county-
wide business license, and in doing so would raise the county-wide license fee
to $225.00. Also the county would increase their collection fee from 1% to 2%.
Mr. Groth commented that the fee has not been increased since the inception of
the original agreement which was approximately fifteen years ago.
Council Member Franzen expressed concern that the agreement allows the County
to increase the collection fee in any even numbered year. Mr. Groth advised the
County would have to notify each participating City prior to any increase,
along with documentation of increased costs incurred by the County in providing
the services to justify the increase.
Council Member Little questioned language in the agreement wherein the County
would charge a consultation fee of $75.00 per hour. Mr. Groth stated the City
would have to request special consultation over and above the services
otherwise provided in this agreement.
Mr. Groth suggested that he address Council’s concerns with a representative
from the County office. Mayor Moriconi stated this issue would be tabled until
the April meeting.

April 6, 2009
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 6,
2009 at 7:00 pm in the Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike,
Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor
Moriconi called the meeting to order with the Pledge of Allegiance. An
invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong,
Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Michael Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was
City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the March 2, 2009 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on March 2, 2009. Council Member Behler so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi announced that the people registered to speak regarding the zone
change on Turkeyfoot Road would be allowed to address Council when the agenda
item is discussed on the floor.
Sanitation District No. 1 Regarding Rate Increase – Jeff Eger, General Manager
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Eger, General Manager of Sanitation District
No.1. He stated that Mr. Eger has been addressing the cities in Northern
Kentucky regarding the District’s rate increase. Mr. Eger advised the
District’s rate increase was effective on April 1st. He reported that the
District will be working on a plan to correct overflows and the deplorable
conditions of the underground infrastructure. He stated they will be addressing
the EPA’s twenty year plan to correct the overflow situation and that they will
deliver this program for one-third of the cost of the national average. He
stated that he wanted to assure everyone that they are working hard to manage
the rates, implement cost saving measures and acting in a progressive manner.
Mr. Eger stated he welcomed email messages with any questions the City has
regarding their rates and programs and would also be happy to meet with them
and the residents. Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Eger
Independence Strategic Action Committee Report – Rodney Crise & Chris
Reinersman
Mayor Moriconi directed Council’s attention to the four reports submitted by
ISAC in their council packets. He yielded the floor to ISAC Chairman Rodney
Crise.
Mr. Crise stated that ISAC has existed over one year now and reported they meet
monthly, as well as four sub-committees. He stated they have come up with some
guidelines of the Downtown Study conducted a couple years ago by the City. Mr.
Crise requested that the Council take some time in reviewing their
recommendations as contained in the reports so they could discuss in more

City budget so they can begin implementing some of the recommendations in the

·   Begin establishing “branding” with the downtown “Courthouse Square”
·   Engage NKAPC in establishing zoning codes for the south gateway and central
core areas of the Study
Mayor Moriconi commented that the research and work performed so far by ISAC is

Hickory Valley Subdivision – Potterhill Homes request for Waiver of Brick Wrap
on Houses – Andrew Temmel, Representative of Potterhill Homes
Mr. Andrew Temmel of Potterhill Homes addressed Council with a request to waive
a condition that was placed on the map amendment approval for the Hickory
Valley Subdivision, specifically the condition that all houses were to have a
first floor brick wrap. He stated that Potterhill Homes, previously Signature
Homes, purchased the remaining 135 lots from Centerline. He stated they are
requesting that the brick wrap condition be waived due to the unique
architecture designs of the Potterhill homes which provides more character to
the community.. He stated that a strong selling point of their houses is the
feature of energy efficiency which they feel is necessary to be competitive. He
stated this energy-star rating feature costs $4,000 per house and that plus the
cost of a brick wrap could have a negative impact on the marketing of the
houses, making them unaffordable to some consumers.
A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Temmel was asked if he was aware of the brick
wrap requirement when they purchased the lots from Centerline. He stated he was
aware of the condition. Council Member Behler commented that some of the
current residents in the subdivision are concerned that the Potterhill Homes
will be smaller in size and lower values of the established houses in that
community. Mr. Temmel responded that the prices of the houses are higher than
the Ryan Homes and they will be equal in square footage. It was pointed out to
Mr. Temmel that this is the third time a request has been presented to Council
to waive this brick wrap condition. Council Member Cook commented that an
additional $4,000 for brick wrap should not be a deterrent to a serious buyer.
Mr. Temmel responded that during the current economy the market is very
competitive and a sale can be lost over $1,000.
Mayor Moriconi ended the discussion by advising Mr. Temmel that there seems to
be a consensus that the Council has no interest in waiving the brick-wrap
building condition and wished him good luck.
Ratify Independence Village Stage II Development Plan - Buffalo Wild Wings
Restaurant
Ashley Commercial Group (ACG) representative Bill Kreutzjans Jr. addressed
Council regarding a Stage II Development Plan for the Independence Village for
the construction of a Buffalo Wild Wings restaurant. He stated they reviewed
the comments submitted by the NKAPC staff regarding the development plan and
stated they have responded to those concerns.
(The NKAPC has advised that the submitted Stage II Development Plan for the
Buffalo Wild Wings restaurant is consistent with the existing approved Stage I
Development Plan and meets the minimum requirements of the City’s Zoning
Ordinance except for five (5) deficiencies, those being: (1) outdoor patio was
not approved in the Stage I plan, (2) insufficient information on the enclosed
dumpster area, (3) two ground signs exceed the 40 square feet limit previously
approved, and an off-site ground sign that was not approved in the Stage I
plan, (4) submitted Stage II plan provides for three building facade signs,
black and white facade markings on all four building elevations and an LED
lighting band on all four building elevations which can be interpreted as
signs, all of which were not approved in the Stage I plan, and (5) a full
movement curb cut onto Madison Pike when a waiver had been previously granted
by KCPC for a right-turn-in and right-turn-out movement only, ADA curb ramps at
the intersections are not in accord with the required design and the curb,
gutter and sidewalk along Madison Pike is referenced to be in accord with city
standards rather than the Kenton County Subdivision Regulations.)
Mr. Kreutzjans stated the first issue the Planning Commission had was the
outdoor patio which was not part of the Stage I Plan, but BWW feels that
outdoor seating is an asset to this area. He advised that the front of the
building would face Madison Pike and the patio would face the direction of
Walgreen’s on Centennial Blvd. He stated another concern for the Planning
Commission was the monument signs. He stated they have actually proposed two of
the signs to be less that the forty feet which is permitted in this
development. He stated that Planning Commission also has interpreted the black
and white LED band mounted on the outside of the building as signage. Mr.
Kreutzjans stated that the black and white lighted banding is a component of
the building and trademark of the Buffalo Wings and feels this issue should not
be considered as signage. He stated the other issues were the ADA curb ramps ,
curb, gutter and sidewalk along Madison Pike which they have redesigned to come
into compliance with subdivision regulations.
Council Member Little initiated a discussion regarding this PUD development and
reminded Mr. Kreutzjans that when the City approved the revised development
plan last year one of the conditions imposed was that ten-percent of the
residential units had to be constructed within two years before any more
commercial lots could be developed. Mr. Kreutzjans stated that currently Ashley
Commercial Group (ACG) only owns the commercial lots. He stated they had a
contract with a residential builder which has fallen through and while they
have been actively searching for another condo developer they have not yet been
successful in doing so. Council Member Little stated that he is concerned that
they are only interested in commercial development and not pursuing the
residential part of the development. He said the entire site has been graded
with no developer for the residential area and now the Walnut Hall residents
are looking at a mud hole. Mr. Darren Eyre of One-Eleven Engineering stated
that the residential will be developed when they get a buyer. Council Member
Little stated that ten-percent will not be completed in two years with only
twelve months left in this time frame. He asked why the lake on the site was
drained. Mr. Eyre advised the lake had to be drained to put in the storm sewer
and grade the site properly.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the City wants to be sensitive to the residents
on Walnut Hall Drive and ensure that the site stays residential and to provide
a buffer from the commercial area. He stated that the clock is ticking. Council
Member Little commented that the intent of the ordinance was to build the
commercial and residential simultaneously and the City has an obligation to the
citizens, particularly to those of Walnut Hall Drive. Council Member Yeager
concurred.
Mr. Kreutzjans stated that this is two different issues and asked that they did
not hold up the development of the Buffalo Wings restaurant because of the
residential part of this site.
A lengthy discussion ensued. Council members were concerned that due to lack of
residential development the developers were possibly circumventing the
simultaneous development of this PUD zone by focusing on the commercial lots.
Council Member Little expressed concern that the developer is overpromising and
under-delivering.
City Attorney Mr. Deters advised that the City could opt to vote this
development down over the residential unit concern, but that he feels the City
would lose if challenged. He stated that the City has to wait until the two
years’ time frame has expired and not act ahead of that time limit.
Mr. Eric Deters, owner of Bulldog’s Roadhouse restaurant approached the podium
to comment on this issue. He stated that Ashley cannot possibly accomplish ten
percent of a residential development over the next twelve months. He stated
that he does not feel that the City can support three “Wings” restaurants and
the solution to this is for Council to vote down this Stage II development plan
and went on to assert that he would file a lawsuit to stop this process if
approved by the Council. City Attorney Mr. Deters advised that Council has the
option to vote this down but felt that decision would not be supported and able
to stand up if challenged. He stated that Council should wait until the two
year deadline runs out.
Council Member Yeager asked if Ashley Commercial Group purchased the entire
site. Mr. Eyre stated they were originally going to buy all the lots but ended
up purchasing the three commercial lots. Mr. Kreutzjans stated they originally
had an agreement with Ameritech Homes, but that Ameritech pulled out. Mr. Eyre
stated there were contingencies in the agreement.
Council Member Franzen commented that even if Council does not approve the
Stage II plan that will not change the situation with the residential part of
the development. She stated she is ready to vote on this, but admonished One-
Eleven by stating they should not return to this Council requesting another
commercial development until they have ten-percent of the residential
completed.
City Attorney Mr. Deters expressed concern that One-Eleven and/or Ashley
Commercial Group may not have actually had a valid contract/agreement with a
residential builder as they stated a year ago.
Council Member Yeager asked why the ponds on the development site had been
drained. Mr. Eyre advised they had to move the existing storm sewer and will
relocate the pond as part of the grading process. She also asked if they could
install the residential buffer now. Mr. Eyre stated that buffer is included
with lot 11. City Attorney Mr. Deters stated the buffer should be installed
before Buffalo Wild Wings gets a certificate of occupancy.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to override the staff recommendation of
the NKAPC and approve the Stage II development plan for the construction of
Buffalo Wild Wings restaurant, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was
called and answered with three ayes from Council Members Franzen, Behler and
Cook and three no votes cast by Council Members Bushong, Little and Yeager.
Mayor Moriconi stated that since the developer still has twelve months to get
ten-percent of the residential parcel completed that he would vote in favor of
approving this Stage II plan. Motion carried 4-3.
A discussion ensued as to whether or not a Stage II development plan is
considered a zoning issue. City Attorney Mr. Deters advised that the Mayor
cannot break a tie on a zoning issue, but questioned if this qualifies as a
zoning issue. Council Member Little asked the City Attorney if the Mayor’s vote
does not count then would the NKAPC recommendation to disapprove the Stage II
Plan become operational by law. City Attorney Mr. Deters replied yes. A brief
discussion ensued wherein several people gave their opinion on whether or not
the Mayor could vote on this issue. City Attorney, Jed Deters advised he would
officially find out tomorrow if the Mayor’s vote was valid.
Proposed Ordinance – Regarding Map Amendment (KCPC 1957R) for 11-Acre Area at
Turkeyfoot Road and Richardson Road (UDF) – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi announced that several people have registered to speak on this
issue. Mr. Joseph Hayes was the applicant on behalf of Eastgate Village Ltd.
and made the presentation to the Council. Mayor Moriconi asked how many
properties would be acquired by the developer. Mr. Hayes stated that only two
properties with houses would be purchased as the rest of the property was
vacant land. He stated they have an agreement with the Wren family, but no
agreement has been made with the McGee’s yet. He stated this development is
unique as they have a tenant (UDF) ready to go into the one building in the
development plan. He stated the other buildings on the development plan are
concept drawings. He stated the development site is for the north and south
sides of the Turkeyfoot/Richardson Road intersection, but that they would not
develop the north side until they get tenants. The south side would contain the
UDF store.
Mayor Moriconi gave privileges of the floor to three residents who were present
to speak on this issue.
Robert Morehead, 47 Richardson Road – voiced his opposition to approving the
map amendment by stating that everything in this area is residential and they
will no longer have any privacy at night. He stated that when the Eagle
development on Turkeyfoot Road was approved, it was his understanding that UDF
was going there. He stated he is also concerned that there isn’t space on this
development site to put in an adequate buffer zone between the residential and
commercial areas. He is concerned about the commercial sprawl in this area of
Turkeyfoot Road and doesn’t see why another eleven acres needs to be zoned
commercial when the Eagle development has thirty acres available. He stated
that traffic congestion is already a problem. In closing, he commented that the
Kenton County Planning Commission voted unanimously to disapprove this map
amendment.
Steve Rickey, 4081 Richardson Road – stated he was not in favor of this
development, feels it is a bad idea and will be able to see this development
from his back yard.
Betty McGee, 4013 Turkeyfoot Road – Ms. McGee stated she is a twenty-year
resident of Independence. She stated she met with Mr. Hayes and he advised they
do not want to purchase her property. She asked the Council to review the taped
meeting on the public hearing held by the Planning Commission. She stated that
not one member of the Planning Commission was in favor of this development. She
also reminded Council that the connector road from the Eagle development was
eliminated. Council Member Franzen responded that the City eliminated that road
at the urging of the citizens and not because the City did not want future
commercial adjacent to the Eagle development site. Ms. McGee also cited that
this proposal presents mobility and safety issues for the area and the school
buses. She stated this plan is not consistent with the Comprehensive Plan and
there will be a non-conforming island left in the road.
David Wren, 4011 Turkeyfoot Road – stated he was in favor of the development as
his house doesn’t fit in that area any longer since the commercial development
is changing the area.
Mr. Hayes advised Council that Mr. Lanny Holbrook owns the south side property
of this development and that they have not purchased the two additional parcels
as that is contingent on the approval of the zone change.
Mayor Moriconi opened the floor to Council for questions. Attorney for Eastgate
Ltd, Jerry Dusing responded to Council Member Franzen’s question about
developing the south side and not the north side. He stated there is a minimum
size needed to apply for the NC (neighborhood commercial) zone so they need
both sides to be eligible for the zone. He stated the north side zone is R-
3 which is the same as the adjacent apartment buildings and feels this zone
change would prevent the apartments from expanding in the future. He stated the
logical zone for this area would NC. Mr. Dusing commented that the merits of
the development, as outlined on page seven of the KCPC recommendation, were
derailed from the get-go at the public hearing of the Planning Commission. He
also said that the City had approved the amended Stage I development plan for
the Eagle site that permitted the removal of the connector road.
Council Member Little asked if Lanny Holbrook, who currently owns the
development site was in favor of this zone change. Mr. Hayes responded that
they have a contract to purchase the property from Mr. Holbrook if and when
then zone change is approved. Mr. Deters commented that it would be a package
deal.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters advised Council they have ninety
days to take some action on this. He stated they could take no action on this
recommendation from the Planning Commission, in which case their recommendation
to disapprove the zone change would in effect by operation of law, or the
Council could override their recommendation and approve the map amendment.
Council Member Yeager made a motion to override the disapproval recommendation
of the Planning Commission and to approve the submitted map amendment (KCPC
1957R) changing an approximate 11-acre area located at the northeast and
southeast corners of the intersection of Turkeyfoot Road with Richardson Road
from R-1C and R-3 to NC, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Although a roll
call vote is not usually taken on a first reading of an ordinance Mayor
Moriconi requested a roll call or voice vote to see if there was a consensus of
the Council to move forward with the motion to override the KCPC
recommendation. No roll call; all ayes and the motion carried. Mr. Deters gave
the proposed ordinance to approve the map amendment a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Closing a Portion of Richardson Road, Specifically the
Bridge Thereon – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
close a portion of Richardson Road, specifically the bridge area. He reported
that the City has received $175,000 from the State to be used for repairs or
toward the replacement of the bridge. He stated the bridge would need to be
closed during repairs or replacement. Mr. Groth commented that core drilling
would be conducted to see if the area can handle a steel bridge. It may be
possible that a second reading of this ordinance would not occur if the results
of the core drilling indicate that the area will not support a steel bridge.
Council Member Franzen asked if the residents have been notified of the
closing. Mr. Groth advised that if and when the time comes to close the bridge
for repairs/replacement the residents will be informed in advance. Mr. Deters
gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amendment to Ordinance No. 2003-O-04 – Relating to
Curbside Trash Pickup & Providing for Property Lien for Non-Payment of Penalty
for Non-Compliance – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2003-O-04 that regulates the times for garbage can
placement at the curb, requiring garbage containers to have lids. He stated the
amendment includes setting times for the removal of junk, trash and debris
placed on the curb for pickup, provides for posting notice of violations and
setting a monetary penalty for violations and also provides for a property lien
for non-payment of the imposed penalties. Mayor Moriconi advised this proposed
amendment is a direct result of taking the trash assessment off the property
tax bills. He stated that the City has found this amendment necessary due to
the many complaints called in regarding excessive trash accumulating at the
curb because residents have not paid Rumpke for their trash pickup. This
amendment will provide the City staff some recourse when we have to go out and
remove the trash. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Mayor Moriconi commented that he has received letters from residents regarding
the recent newspaper article that reported Rumpke’s rate for the City of
Florence was quite a bit less than the rate being paid by Independence
residents. He stated that the contract with Florence includes commercial pickup
as well as the residential pickup so the businesses are basically subsidizing
the residential cost. He stated that on the surface it may appear unequal, but
Independence does not have the amount of commercial properties that would allow
this lower rate here.
Proposed Ordinance– Approving Two Zoning Text Amendments (KCPC No. 1952R)
Modifying the NSC Zone Relating to Bakery Goods Stores and Music & Amplifying
Systems in Outdoor Dining Areas – New 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading an ordinance that would accept
the recommendation of the Kenton County Planning Commission for a zoning text
amendment that would modify the NSC (Neighborhood Shopping Center) zone that
would allow bakery and bakery goods stores to sell their products elsewhere off
the premises where they are baked and to override the recommendation to
disapprove outdoor dining areas, as a conditional use, to have entertainment,
music and sound amplifying systems. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
second reading.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt the proposed ordinance, seconded by
Council Member Little. Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for discussion before
voting on the ordinance. Council Member Bushong expressed concern about
allowing the amplifying systems close to residential property and suggested
that a distance restriction be imposed in the ordinance. City Attorney, Mr. Jed
Deters advised that because this will be a conditional use, a business would
have to apply to go before the Board of Adjustment to get approval and the
Board could impose distance restrictions. Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld
voiced her agreement with Mr. Deters. Mr. Deters advised that imposing distance
restrictions can become problematic and in some zones it won’t be possible.
Council Member Bushong stated that he doesn’t want to allow blaring music
within a certain distance and would feel better if the city would impose a
distance restriction in the ordinance.
Further discussion centered on deciding an appropriate distance restriction.
City Administrator Dan Groth commented that he would recommend not imposing a
distance restriction and if a business was permitted this conditional use by
the Board of Adjustment and then the music sound level prompted complaints from
the residents, the City would then just use the nuisance ordinance to resolve
the complaint(s).
Mr. Eric Deters, who had requested this text amendment so that he could have
outdoor music on the patio of his Bulldog’s Roadhouse restaurant (formerly the
Courthouse restaurant) commented that he planned to have acoustical, relaxing
type of music and that he would only hire bands during the holiday weekends,
such as the City’s July 4th two-day celebration. Council Member Behler stated
that she felt there would be less chance of the music becoming a nuisance from
acoustical music. Council Member Cook stated that five hundred (500) feet would
eliminate Bob’s Family restaurant from outdoor music. Council Member Franzen
stated she is not in favor of imposing stipulations on one restaurant and not
another and that the ordinance will affect the entire City, not just Mr.
Deters’ restaurant.
City Attorney Mr. Deters, suggested adding the new language to include a
distance restriction to the ordinance, but then they should do a new first
reading of the ordinance. Eric Deters expressed concern that a new first
reading would delay his application to the Board of Adjustment for the
conditional use by another month. City Attorney Mr. Deters commented that the
Mayor could approve the outdoor music for the holiday special event.
Council Member Little expressed his concern that imposing a distance
requirement could penalize some neighborhood commercial areas like the Cherokee
and Beechgrove plazas. He stated that he believes the zone has an impact and
that a five acre development would be more intrusive than a forty acre
development. He asked how the nuisance ordinance would take effect. Mr. Groth
responded by a reasonable person test wherein it only takes one person to be
affected.
A discussion ensued about adding a 200 feet distance requirement language in
the ordinance. Council Member Cook commented that she feels that a distance
requirement will cause problems. Council consensus was to add the new language
and have a new first reading of the ordinance. The City Attorney gave the
ordinance a new first reading.
Approving Interlocal Agreement with Kenton County for the Collection of
Municipal Occupational License Fees
Mayor Moriconi resubmitted to Council the Interlocal Agreement with Kenton
County for the collection of occupational license fees and taxes. He stated
approval of this Agreement was tabled at the March meeting. The City
Administrator was able to speak to a representative at the County office who
answered a few questions posed by the Council at the last meeting and the
answers have been conveyed to the Council.
There being no discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Little and
seconded by Council Member Yeager to authorize the Mayor to enter into the
Agreement with the County for the collection of the city occupational license
fees and taxes. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no vote
cast by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried 5-1.
Resolution No. 2009-R-04 – Designating an Applicant Agent for FEMA Assistance
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2009-R-04 that would
authorize him as the City’s agent for FEMA for all matters pertaining to
Federal disaster assistance. He reported that the City has applied for
reimbursement for expenses incurred from the ice storm in February. He stated
that the City is applying for a reimbursement of approximately $45,000.
A motion was made by Council Member Yeager and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to adopt Resolution No. 2009-R-04. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Municipal Order No. 2009-MO-03 – Re-Appointments to the Board of Adjustment
Mayor Moriconi presented to the Council a Municipal Order that would re-appoint
members to the Board of Adjustment. The members are Jim Brewer, Eric Dupps and
Darrel Herald. Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Municipal Order No. 2009-
MO-03, seconded by Council Member Little. Roll was called and answered with
five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Cook. Motion carried 5-1.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth submitted a written report to the Council. He commented that the new
Senior Center director is doing a good job and the membership is up to 175
seniors.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi reported that the City anticipates receiving approximately
$45,000 in reimbursement from FEMA for expenses from the ice storm in February.
He said a check should be forthcoming.
Miscellaneous
Council Member Bushong announced that Independence resident, Mary Beth Hall who
is a breast cancer survivor has written a new book “Lessons From a Bald Chick”
which helps people understand what cancer patients go through and how to do it
with a positive attitude.
Council Member Franzen congratulated the basketball teams at Summit View Middle
School for winning the Conference championship games. She also acknowledge the
winning teams at Twenhofel School too.
Council Member Cook acknowledged four girls from Summit View Middle School for
being chosen for the Children’s All-State Choir. She stated these four students
were chosen from 212 children statewide.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 9:54 p.m.
