February 1, 2010
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of February 1, 2010
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
1, 2010 at 7:00 pm in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. An invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the January 4, 2010 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on January 4, 2010. Council Member Little so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0
Privileges of the Floor
Mr. Larry Hamilton and Ms. Leslie Knight came before the Council to request the
City sponsor a zoning text amendment application that would add pawn shops to
the list of permitted uses within the NC (Neighborhood Commercial) zone.
Mr. Hamilton stated he has looked at the Beechgrove Shopping Plaza as a good
location for a pawn shop. He had four pawn shop locations in Lexington and
while he is aware that this type of business can be perceived negatively, they
provide loans to people struggling to meet their bills as well as sell items.
Council Member Bushong asked if they would sell weapons. Mr. Hamilton stated
they usually sell used and new weapons, but would be willing to not sell
weapons. He stated that when he operated the pawn shops in Fayette County the
county police would come in every day to check the inventory. A brief
discussion ensued. Council Member Behler expressed concern that some residents
would not welcome this type of business in their neighborhood. Council Member
Yeager stated she would like to hear from the residents of Beechgrove as she
would like their input.
Mr. Deters advised Council that sponsoring the text amendment would just be the
first step in the process of adding this type of business to the NC zone. He
stated the Planning Commission would make a review and then a recommendation to
the City as to whether or not they feel this should be a permitted use. Mayor
Moriconi advised that if this was approved that it would affect all NC zones
not just the Beechgrove Plaza.
Council Member Franzen stated she did not have a problem sponsoring the
application to the Planning Commission to get their recommendation and
therefore made a motion to do so, seconded by Council Member Cook. Roll was
called and answered with three ayes and three no votes cast by Council Members
Behler, Bushong and Yeager. There being a tie vote of the Council, Mayor
Moriconi broke the tie by voting yes. Motion carried 4-3 in favor of sponsoring
a text amendment application. Council Member Franzen announced she would also
be interested in hearing from the residents on this issue.
Traffic Signal at the Intersection of McCullum and New SR17
Council Member Yeager asked what the status was regarding the City’s request to
the State to install a traffic signal at the McCullum Road/New SR17
intersection. Mr. Groth advised he spoke with Rob Hans, District 6 Chief
Engineer for the Transportation Cabinet, who stated that
the preliminary tests indicate there is no change from the prior tests they
performed, but they are continuing to study the area. A discussion ensued with
some Council Members in favor of going to Frankfort to lobby for a traffic
light at this intersection. Council Member Bushong suggested that maybe the
State would consider installing a caution light. Council Member Yeager stated
that she feels a traffic light would be the best solution for this
intersection. Mr. Groth will keep Council informed of any developments on this
issue.
Privileges of the Floor (continued) – Discussion Regarding Plans for a “Welcome
to the City of Independence” Monument Sign
Mayor Moriconi advised that people signed in to address the Council regarding a
proposed “Welcome to the City of Independence” monument sign. He stated he
wanted to clear up a misunderstanding and make it clear that the City did not
budget $25,000 for this sign. He stated the amount budgeted in the 2009/10
budget is $10,000. He stated that those who still wished to speak on this issue
were welcome to do so, but he just wanted to make that clear.
Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, Independence – addressed Council regarding his
feelings about the proposed monument sign. He stated that he is not against
‘welcome’ signs but is not in favor of building four of these monument signs,
at four different locations, at the cost of $25,000 each. Mr. Cobble went on to
express concerns he has for raising taxes, cutting waste in the budget and
fixing city roads. He opined that the Council should do the right thing and get
the City’s priorities in order. Before yielding the floor, Mr. Cobble presented
to the Mayor petitions (attached hereto) signed by the residents who are
against the monument signs.
Again, Mayor Moriconi advised the audience that the City has budgeted $10,000,
not $25,000, for one monument sign, not four, which is planned to be
constructed at the intersection of the new section of SR17 and Pelly Road.
Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview Court, Independence – stated she did not feel the City
needed to spend $10,000 on one sign that would be surrounded with landscaping
and lightning. She stated she feels that landscaping is a maintenance expense
which is a waste of money. She went on to express concerns that the City needs
to be more conservative with the taxpayers’ money and that Council should
buckle down in the budget.
Mayor Moriconi explained that the committee (ISAC) of volunteers just presented
a sign concept to the Council at the last meeting. He stated he feels this sign
concept has been blown out of proportion as the City, other than setting aside
$10,000 in the current budget, has not acted on the concept. He stated that no
elected official has been quoted as saying the City will be spending $25,000 on
this monument sign. He stated the City has not taken bids for the sign and that
it is possible that the Public Works employees would construct the sign.
Mr. Jim Caldwell, 850 Independence Station Road, Independence – stated that
while he is not against the monument sign, he does feel that $10,000 is a lot
for one sign. He asked that the Council provide the exact plans for the sign to
the residents when the plans become available.
A brief discussion ensued among the Council Members. Council Member Little
tried to provide some history regarding the idea behind the monument sign. He
stated it was an idea that came from citizen input during the Small Area Study.
He stated that the citizens that participated in the Study considered signage a
priority. He also informed the audience that the City wasn’t actually certain
of the cost for this type of sign, but decided to set aside $10,000 in the
budget. Council Member Yeager commented that people have told her that when
driving along the new section of SR17 that they don’t know they have arrived in
Independence and end up in Nicholson. Council Member Behler agreed that
visitors to the City cannot find the City when using the new SR17, which is a
reason that installing signage is an important priority for the City.
Privileges of the Floor (continued)
Tom Daniels, 25 Carrie Way, Independence – addressed Council regarding two
issues, the first being that he lives on a dead end street and cars are parked
on one side and the other is speeders on his street. He stated he has talked to
the police about this and a cruiser will come by but does not stay and run
radar.
Mr. Daniels also complained that he has been notified by the City that he is
not permitted to keep his trailer, yet he notices other properties that have
campers and boats and he feels that nothing is being done about them. He
specifically mentioned the property across from the new office building in the
downtown area.
Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld responded to Mr. Daniels by stating that
the cars parked in violation on the street are a police issue that would be
handled by the Police Department. She also advised Council that in 2009 the
City notified 1300 property owners regarding zoning violations on their
property. She stated that all but forty-five owners came into compliance with
the City zoning laws. She went on to say that sometimes a violation will go
unnoticed by City staff, but the City has continually worked to get the
violations under control.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving Zoning Text Amendment for Sign Regulations – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would amend the
text of the current zoning ordinance to delete all current definitions and
regulations regarding signage and adding new definitions and regulations for
signage. He thanked Council Member Little for the time he spent on the
revisions to this ordinance.
Council Member Little led the discussion with Council in reviewing the proposed
revisions. After the revisions were made and agreed upon by the Council, Mr.
Deters gave the ordinance its first reading. Mayor Moriconi advised the
ordinance would be presented for a second reading at the next meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving Map Amendment to Amend Stage I Development Plan
for the Independence Village – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first a proposed ordinance that would approve an
amended Stage I map amendment to change an approximate 13.3 acre area located
at the northwest corner of the intersection of the new Madison Pike and
Centennial Blvd. from R-2 (PUD) to R-3(PUD).
Mayor Moriconi commented that this amendment would change the density of the
multi-family section of this PUD development so that the residential
construction could begin. A brief discussion ensued. Developer, Jim Bertram
advised they would like to begin the development by Spring, but still needs to
get the preliminary plat approved and then begin the Stage II approval process.
Mr. Bertram handed out an informational packet for this planned apartment
community to be called Independence Oaks. He advised Council the information
contained in these packets was the same information presented at the Kenton
County Planning Commission public hearing. He stated that this amended Stage I
Plan for the apartment development received unanimous approval from the
Planning Commission. He stated that part of the amended proposal would include
two ground signs and two directional signs. Council Member Bushong asked what
the rent would be for the apartments. Mr. Bertram advised that a two-bedroom
would rent for $875/month and a 3-bedroom would rent for $1,025/month. When
asked about the common space and if there would be any changes, Mr. Bertram
advised that most of the common area would be left in its natural state. Mr.
Bertram asked the Council if they would consider having a special council
meeting later this month to get final approval of this amended Stage I
ordinance so that they could then move on to getting the preliminary plat
approved before the end of February. He stated after the preliminary plat is
approved, and because this is a PUD development, they must then submit a Stage
II application and the builder would like to begin construction in April.
After a brief discussion regarding a date and time for a special council
meeting, the Mayor and Council Members agreed to hold a special meeting on
Thursday, February 11, 2010 at 7 p.m. at which time a second reading of the
ordinance would be presented.
Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance that would amend the Stage I map
amendment for the Independence Village development a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving the Closing of a Portion of Lily Drive – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
close a portion of Lily Drive no longer being needed since the relocation of
Richardson Road, with adjoining two property owners having provided the City
with notarized requests and consent for the proposed closing. Mr. Deters gave
the ordinance a first reading.
Discussion Regarding Lawn Maintenance Contract
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration the current
contract for lawn maintenance with Malco Services and asked if they wanted to
extend the current contract per the price schedule as outlined in the original
bid or if they wanted to put this service out for bid again. He stated that
Malco does a good job for the City. A brief discussion ensued.
Council Member Behler moved to put the lawn and park maintenance services out
for bid, seconded by Council Member Cook. Roll was called and answered with
three ayes and three no votes cast by Council Members Bushong, Franzen and
Yeager. Mayor Moriconi broke the tie by voting yes. Motion carried 4-3 to re-
bid the lawn/park maintenance services.
City Administrator’s Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth stated that he did not have anything to report.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Presentation of the Annual Audit – Fiscal Year ending June 30, 2009 – Mayor
Moriconi advised Council that a copy of the annual audit was provided to them
in the meeting packet and if they have any questions about the audit they
should contact the Finance Director.
Mayor Moriconi advised that he has received a lot of calls regarding a letter
many residents have received about the repair of public water lines. He advised
everyone to be cautious of acting on this notice as it is a scam and the
company that sent this notice is not associated with the City.
Marshall Road
Council Member Cook stated that she wanted to clarify the reason she voted
against the Marshall Road repairs at the December meeting. She stated she was
not a member of Council when the City finalized the agreement with the county
on taking over maintenance of certain roads which included Marshall Road. She
stated she agrees that the road needs to be repaired, but she feels the City
should not have accepted maintenance of Marshall Road. Mayor Moriconi advised
that the City assumed the ownership and maintenance of Marshall Road as part of
a lawsuit settlement with the County. Council Member Cook reiterated that she
feels the City should not have agreed to the responsibility for that street as
it does not touch city property. Council Member Little advised that Marshall
Road does touch the city and that the City accepted maintenance of this road in
exchange for the County taking maintenance of Independence Station Road which
was part of the lawsuit settlement.
Noise Nuisance Ordinance Discussion
Council Member Cook advised she has spoken to the Police Chief regarding loud
cars and motorcycles and she is looking into proposing an amendment to the
City’s current noise nuisance ordinance at a future council meeting. She stated
she is reviewing other cities noise ordinances and the City of Covington has a
good one.
Board of Ethics Ordinance Discussion
Council Member Cook stated she recently attended a Board of Ethics meeting
where they discussed the question of hiring practices, specifically employee’s
relatives. She advised that the Ethics Board has recommended that the City
update the Ethics ordinance to remove any vagueness. She stated the City
Attorney will speak with the Ethics Board chairman to propose amendments to the
current ethics ordinance.
Adjournment
Before closing the meeting, Mayor Moriconi advised that a March 1, 2010 regular
meeting would only be held if needed. There being no further business before
the Council, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the meeting, seconded by
Council Member Behler. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 9:
18 p.m.

February 11, 2010
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of February 11, 2010
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Thursday, February 11, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called
and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim
Bushong, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Donna Yeager. Also
present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone and announced this special meeting of Council
was being held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
·   Ordinance No. 2010-O-02 – Approving a Map Amendment for the Independence
Village – 2nd Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2010-O-03 – Approving Zoning Text Amendment Sign Regulations
– 2nd Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2010-O-04 – Approving the Closing of a Portion of Lily Drive
– 2nd Reading
·   Executive Session (only if necessary)
Ordinance No. 2010-O-02 – Approving a Map Amendment for the Independence
Village – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2010-O-
02 that would approve a zoning map amendment, KCPC Number 1995R, that would
change approximately 13.3 acres in the Independence Village development located
at the northwest corner of the intersection of Madison Pike (new SR17) with
Centennial Boulevard from R-2 (PUD) to R-3 (PUD). Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No.
2010-O-02 a second reading.
Council Member Bushong made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-02, seconded
by Council Member Franzen. There being no discussion, roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Developer, Jim Bertram, stated they would proceed with the next step which
would be to go before the Planning Commission with a Stage I development plan
application.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-03 – Approving Zoning Text Amendment Adopting New Sign
Regulations – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2010-O-03 which
would approve a text amendment that would eliminate the current sign
regulations in the City’s zoning ordinance and adopt new sign regulations. Mr.
Deters gave Ordinance No. 2010-O-03 a second reading.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-03, seconded by
Council Member Behler. A brief discussion ensued regarding the number of
permitted temporary signs in the various zones. The Council Members agreed to
change the proposed text to decrease the number of temporary signs from fifteen
to twelve.. Mr. Deters advised this was a minor change from the first reading
of the ordinance. Council Members Franzen and Behler consented to amending
their motion/second to include the amending of the number of temporary signs.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-04 – Approving the Closing of a Portion of Lily Drive –
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2010-O-04 that
would approve the closing of a portion of Lily Drive no longer being needed
since the relocation of Richardson Road, with adjoining two property owners
having provided the City with notarized requests and consent for the proposed
closing. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a second reading.
Council Member Behler moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-04, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. No discussion. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business before the Council, Council Member Little moved
to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with
all ayes and the meeting ended at 7:13 p.m.

March 22, 2010
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of March 22, 2010
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, March 22, 2010 at 6:45 p.m. in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong,
Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Donna Yeager. Also present was
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone and announced this Special meeting of Council
was being held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
·   Request by Farmers’ Market Vendors to Waive Occupational License Fees
·   Resolution No. 2010-R-03 – Authorizing the Application to the Department of
Local Government for Assistance Under the Land & Water Conservation Fun for a
Proposed Recreation Project
Request by Farmer’s Market Vendors to Waive Occupational License Fees
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that the Farmers’ Market vendors are requesting
that the City waive occupational license fees. He stated that this waiver could
be accomplished by amending Chapter 112 of the code of ordinances that regulate
peddlers, itinerate merchants and solicitors to include vendors participating
in the Farmers’ Market as an exemption. He commented that the Farmers’ Market
is a great program in the City which only operates on Saturdays from April
through October each year. Mr. Deters advised that this section of the code of
ordinances also provides exemptions for churches and educational institutions.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Chapter 112 of the Code of Ordinances and
Providing for an Exemption for Vendors of the Farmers’ Market – 1st Reading
After a brief discussion, Mr. Deters composed an ordinance amending Chapter 112
of the code of ordinances providing an additional exemption to include vendors
participating in the Farmers’ Market. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading. Mayor Moriconi advised that the second reading of the ordinance
would be presented at the regular meeting of April 5, 2010.
Resolution No. 2010-R-03 – Authorizing the Application o the Department of
Local Government for Assistance under the Land & Water Conservation Fund for a
Proposed Recreation Project
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2010-R-03 that would
authorize the application of a grant with the Land and Water Conservation Fund
for a proposed recreational project in Memorial Park. The grant would fund
fifty-percent of the estimated project cost of $102,000. The project is for
terracing the hillside between the Amphitheater and the Senior Center building.
Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2010-R-03.
Council Member Behler moved to adopt Resolution No. 2010-R-03, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Bushong stated
he would like to clarify that the City would only spend $10,000 as part of the
City’s fifty-percent and that the remainder of the City’s contribution would be
in-kind services. Council Member Cook stated that she does not approve of the
City spending any money on this project. She cited budget problems, recent
termination of two staff members and needed road repairs as reasons why she
felt this project should not be considered. Mayor Moriconi countered that this
is an opportunity for the City to get a valuable, capital park improvement
project completed for a fraction of the actual cost. He stated the City cannot
let an opportunity like this go by when there is a strong chance that an agency
in Northern Kentucky could be awarded this grant. There being no further
discussion, roll was called and answered with four ayes and two no votes cast
by Council Members Cook and Franzen. Motion carried 4-2.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 6:56 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 5,
2010 at 7:00 pm in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the

Behler, Jim Bushong, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.

Ordinance No. 2010-O-05 – Amending Ordinance No. 1-10-84 that Regulates
Solicitor’s License and Fees & Amending Same to Exempt Farmers’ Market Vendors

Award Bid for Lawn Maintenance Contract
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received for the
lawn and park maintenance. He stated that a total of ten bids were submitted.
He advised the City is currently in contract with Malco Services and while the
bid submitted by Malco was not the lowest, it does reflect an overall decrease
from the current 2010/2012 contract extension rates that were submitted in June
2008. Mayor Moriconi commented that Malco has provided good service for the
City.
Council Member Franzen moved to award the lawn and park maintenance contract to
Malco Services as the best bid, seconded by Council Member Yeager. A brief
discussion ensued. Some of the Council Members agreed with Mayor Moriconi that
Malco has provided the City with good service over the years. Council Member
Behler commented that the low bid is not always the best bid. Mayor Moriconi
stated that Malco is a business located in Independence and the owner takes a
personal interest in doing a good job for the City and at times does not charge
for some of the services he renders. He also commented that some of the bids
submitted seemed unrealistically low. Council Member Cook asked if it was legal
to not accept the low bid. Mr. Deters advised that the low bid is just one of
the criteria considered when awarding a bid and the City is not legally
obligated to award the contract to the lowest bidder. Mr. Groth commented that
the City has awarded bids in the past that were not the low bid.
In closing Mayor Moriconi commented that the processed work; in choosing to re-
bid this service instead of extending the current contract the City was able to
save money by receiving bids that were lower overall. There being no further
discussion roll was called and answered unanimously to award the bid to Malco
Services. Motion carried 6-0.
Independence Village – Stage II Development Plan (NKAPC # 10-02-05/2002R)
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a recommendation from the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning Commission to disapprove the Stage II Development Plan for an
approximate 13.3 acre area located at the northwest corner of the intersection
with Madison Pike (new) and Centennial Boulevard. It is being presented to the
City for final action to approve or disapprove the plan. Mayor Moriconi opened
the floor for discussion.
Developer Jim Bertram explained to Council that the Planning Commission
recommended disapproval because of the following three issues:
·   The plan indicated off-street parking spaces directly in front of rental
detached garages
·   The plan omitted a section of the walking trails that were included in the
Stage I development plan
·   The plan indicates an emergency access gate which would be contradictory in
providing vehicular access throughout the development.
Mr. Bertram advised that they have removed the off-street parking spaces that
were directly in front of the garages and still have the required number of
parking spaces for this development. He stated the walking trails were
inadvertently left off of the plan rendering submitted to the Planning
Commission and would be developed in its entirety as shown in the Stage I
Development Plan. Regarding the emergency gate, Mr. Bertram advised that this
gate was on the Stage I Plan, but they would like to control public access to
this residential section of the development. He stated this could deter
criminal activity yet still provide access for public safety (police/fire)
vehicles. There was a brief discussion on how the gate would be controlled. Mr.
Bertram stated the police and fire agencies will have keys for the gate lock.
He stated that criminals don’t like to have only one way in and one way out, so
this gate could deter vandals/robbers in this private community. Captain Tony
Lucas advised Council that the owners of this development have been meeting
with the police depart to review various types of locks to determine which
would work best for this gate. Council Member Little asked if this would be a
liability for the City. Mr. Deters advised it would not and commented that the
fire department carries big universal keys.
Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld advised Council that the three issues,
which Mr. Bertram has addressed, would be considered minor changes.
Mr. Bertram advised that improvement drawings would be submitted to the
Planning Commission after approval from the City on this Stage II Plan. He
stated they hope to begin the construction of this project in a couple of
weeks.
There being no further discussion and having received satisfaction regarding
the three issues discussed Council Member Yeager moved to override the Planning
Commission’s disapproval of the Stage II Development Plan by approving the Plan
based on the following:
1.   A section of the proposed walking trail along the new Madison Pike was
inadvertently omitted from the Stage II Development Plan submitted to the
Planning Commission. The developer has agreed to develop the walking trail in
its entirety.
2.   To waive vehicular access throughout the proposed development thereby
permitting an emergency access gate in the vicinity of Lot 12/Building #4.
3.   The developer has agreed to remove the inappropriate off-street parking
spaces directly in front of any detached garage.
A second was made by Council Member Behler. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment (KCPC 200R) Adding Pawn
Shops to the List of Permitted Uses within the NC Zone – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would

Proposed Ordinance – Establishing Rental Dwelling Licenses – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
create a new chapter of the code of ordinances (Chapter 99) concerning rental
dwelling licenses. He stated this ordinance will pertain to both residential
and commercial rental properties. Mayor Moriconi stated that this is more than
just establishing a rental fee but will lay out standards for maintaining
rental property. He stated that one issue that prompted the proposal of this
ordinance is the inordinate amount of calls for service received by the Police
Department at rental properties. He stated that he does not want to put rental
property in a negative light, but the majority of the police calls are from
apartment complex units. Mayor Moriconi stated that other cities have this type
of ordinance.
Mr. Bertram expressed his concern about adopting this ordinance and commented
that this license and associated fees will affect him and others that own
rental property. Police Captain Tony Lucas advised Council that his department
would submit an exact breakdown of calls for service to the various apartment
complexes at the next Council meeting.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Code of Ethics, Chapter 38 Codes of Ordinances –
1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Chapter 38 relating to the Code of Ethics by amending the definition of
“family member.” Council Member Franzen asked the Mayor who was sponsoring this
proposed amendment. Council Member Cook responded that she requested this
amendment. She stated she attended a recent Board of Ethics meeting where this
was discussed and it was the Board’s recommendation that this definition be
updated to include more family members. Mr. Deters commented that the proposed
amendment expands the definition of family member. There was a brief discussion
wherein Council Member Little suggested changing the proposed amendment to
include all “step” relations. The Council Members concurred. There being no
further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Nuisance Ordinance, Chapter 93 of the Code of
Ordinances – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Chapter 93 of the code of ordinances relating to nuisances by clarifying
and more specifically defining activities to be considered a nuisance. A brief
discussion ensued. Some Council Members questioned the need for the additional
text and whether it would be enforceable. Council Member Behler commended that
she understood that the Police Chief approved this text and that the department
had an instrument that would register decibel levels. Captain Tony Lucas
advised that they have reviewed the proposed text and it is comparable to other
cities, such as Covington and Erlanger. He stated that Chief Butler is
comfortable with this proposal. He stated they would need to purchase the
decibel meter equipment, but advised having the equipment would not prevent all
noise.
Mr. Deters commented that the proposed text better delineates nuisance types
and provides specifics on what can be declared a nuisance and that it all comes
down to establishing reasonable standards. Council Member Little expressed
concern that the proposed text may be too specific and stated that he feels the
current laws, if enforced could do the same. Captain Lucas commented that the
current ordinance is not specific enough and because it is too broad would get
thrown out of court. Council Member Franzen suggested postponing the first
reading so Council would have more time to review the proposal. After a brief
discussion it was decided to go ahead with the first reading of the proposed
ordinance. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading. Mayor Moriconi
advised Council that Chief Butler would be at the next meeting and give his
input on this proposed ordinance before the second reading.
He stated that the Police Chief feels comfortable with this proposal
Resolution No. 2010-R-04 – Supporting Federal Legislation that would Require
EPA to Consider Affordability and the Financial Capabilities of Communities
when Implementing its Combined Sewer Overflow Control Measures
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2010-R-04 that would support
federal legislation that would require the EPA to consider affordability and
the financial capabilities of communities when implementing Combined Sewer
Overflow control measures. Mr. Groth advised that this resolution basically
opposes unfunded mandates which forces communities to pass on the costs of
conforming to federal law to the consumers by way of increasing taxes and/or
utility rates. He stated this resolution supports the need for communities to
have more flexibility in the development and implementation of long-term
control measures for combined sewer overflow. Mr. Deters read Resolution No.
2010-R-04.
A motion was made by Council Member Behler and seconded by Council Member Cook
to adopt Resolution No. 2010-R-04. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2010-R-05 – Accepting Ownership & Maintenance Responsibility for
the By-passed Segments of KY 1829 (Turkeyfoot
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2010-R-05 that approves the
City accepting title to ownership and maintenance responsibility for the
bypassed segments of KY 1829 (Industrial Road) and reconstructed city streets,
which include West Richardson Road, Beechgrove Drive, Wedgewood Drive,
Clubhouse Drive, Fox Run Drive, Hunters Green Drive, Independence Station
Drive, Lily Drive and East Richardson Road due to the reconstruction of KY 1303
(Turkeyfoot Road).
Mr. Groth advised Council that City staff has met with the State to review the
sections described in the Resolution. He stated that while the City would
assume ownership there would be no real maintenance of these sections of
roadway. There was a brief discussion regarding the section of Independence
Station Drive. Mayor Moriconi stated that this section is maintained by Kenton
County and should be stricken from the Resolution. All were in agreement and
the Independence Station Drive section was stricken from the Resolution.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Franzen moved to adopt
Resolution No. 2010-R-05, seconded by Council Member Behler. Roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.

Executive Order No. 2010-EO-01 – Appointment to Senior Board of Directors
Mayor Moriconi presented Executive Order No. 2010-EO-01 appointing Tom Collins
to the Independence Senior Center Board of Directors.
Mayor Moriconi shared some good news - that he received a letter today from the
State Transportation Department notifying the City that they have re-evaluated
the intersection of SR17 (new) and McCullum Road and based on the present
factors they have determined that the intersection warrants a traffic signal.
He stated they did not provide a date by when the signal would be installed but
said it would be in upcoming months. Mayor Moriconi stated that he received
several scary letters about “near misses” at that intersection and thanked

insurance underwriting. He stated that residents will benefit by this good
rating in the form of a reduction in their property insurance rates.

COUNCIL MEETING

City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 3,
2010 at 7:00 pm in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. An invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat
Behler, Jim Bushong, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the April 5, 2010 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, April 5, 2010. Council Member Behler so moved, with
second by Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Privileges of the Floor
Gailen and Debra Bridges – addressed Council about their plans to work with
Arcadia Publishing on writing a book on the history of the City of Independence
and Southern Kenton County. Mr. Bridges stated they will be soliciting from the
public memorabilia, historic photos and other material for inclusion in the
book. He stated they would like and encourage participation from the community.
The Bridges can be contacted at independencebook@ymail.com.
Bob Schroeder, Arlinghaus Builders – addressed Council with a request for the
City to sponsor a zoning text amendment that would permit wider driveways (as
wide as the width of the opening of a three-car garage). He stated that current
regulations permit a maximum width of 20 feet and would like to see this
increased to 30 feet. Mr. Schroeder stated that his current recourse for
putting in a wider driveway is to go before the City’s Board of Adjustment to
request a variance. He stated it makes more sense to permit this wider
driveway, especially for a three-car garage, and therefore would like to see
the City change this zoning regulation.
A brief discussion ensued. General consensus of the Council was that an
application should be made with the Board of Adjustment for the variance.
Council Member Little felt confident that this type of variance would be
approved by the Board. Council Member Behler agreed and commented that the City
recently upheld the current regulations and ordered several properties that had
unlawfully increased the size of their driveways to come into compliance. Mr.
Schroeder’s request was denied due to lack of consensus to support a text
amendment.
Candace Klein, Graydon Head & Ritchey LLP – Ms. Klein addressed Council on
behalf of her client, Robert Meyers who owns property in the Cherokee Shopping
Center. Ms. Klein stated that Mr. Meyers is working with a potential renter –
Custom Outdoor Creations – who would like to run a seasonal flowers/plants
business between the LaRosa’s and the drugstore. She stated that since this is
a dimensional issue they cannot request a variance from the City’s Board of
Adjustment. Ms. Klein requested the City sponsor a zoning text amendment that
would amend Section 10.15 (E6) to add seasonal garden supply stores as an
exception.
Resolution No. 2010-R-06 – Supporting Text Amendment Application
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Resolution No. 2010-R-06 that would
support a zoning text amendment application that would amend Section 10.15 (E6)
adding as an exception “seasonal garden supply stores.” Motion was seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-06 – Establishing ABC Regulations and License Fee Schedule
– 2nd Reading

establish an alcoholic beverage control license and the respective fees and
licenses required for alcohol sales within the City limits and revising the
hours when alcohol sales are permitted. Mr. Deters read the ordinance.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-06, seconded by

Proposed Ordinance – Amending Code of Ethics, Chapter 38 Codes of Ordinances –
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would

Ordinance No. 2010-O-07 – Amending Nuisance Ordinance, Chapter 93 of the Code
of Ordinances – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Chapter 93 of the code of ordinances relating to nuisances by clarifying
and more specifically defining activities to be considered a nuisance. Mr.
Deters gave the proposed ordinance a second reading.
Motion was made by Council Member Cook and seconded by Council Member Behler to
adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-07. A lengthy discussion ensued. Council questioned
the police chief about the current nuisance regulations and the lengthy
proposed changes which include definitions of noise nuisances. Chief Butler
advised that the current regulations do not provide definitions of what
constitutes a noise nuisance; only saying “obnoxious emission of noise.” He
stated the courts will not prosecute as it is too vague. Council Member Little
stated he felt that some of the proposed text was good while other sections may
be difficult to enforce. Council Member Behler commented the City’s nuisance
ordinance needs more substance as several complaints received over the last few
years have not been resolved due to the current inadequate regulations. Council
Member Yeager commented that she likes some of the proposed changes, but not
all and she is not prepared to vote in favor of this as presented. Council
Member Franzen agreed that some of the noises, such as loud horns, would be
difficult to enforce as it would be gone by the time the police arrived. Zoning
Administrator Annie Wuestefeld agreed that there is a lot of proposed text, and
that much of it won’t be needed, but if it is then it will be defined in the
City ordinance. She agreed that often times we need to be there to witness the
violation. Council discussed making some changes, but there was concern that it
was important to move forward quickly with summer approaching. Mr. Deters
advised the proposed amendment has eliminated a lot of unknowns by being all-
inclusive. Chief Butler stated his department will not unreasonably enforce any
parts of this proposed ordinance.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered with five ayes
and one no vote cast by Council Member Little. Motion carried 5-1.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment (KCPC 200R) Adding Pawn
Shops to the List of Permitted Uses within the NC Zone – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve a zoning text amendment adding “pawn shops” to the list of permitted
uses within the NC (Neighborhood Commercial) zone.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Tom Nienaber who wished to address Council
as a proponent of this text amendment. Mr. Nienaber advised he was an attorney
representing his client Larry Hamilton who had requested that Council sponsor
this text amendment. Mr. Nienaber stated that the proposed text amendment has
received a recommendation for approval from the staff of the Northern Kentucky
Area Planning Commission and the Kenton County Planning Commission. He advised
that with the exception of alcohol sales there is not a more regulated business
by statute than pawn shops. He stated that historically there have not been
many pawn shops in Northern Kentucky, but they are starting to pop up in more
areas. He stated that when looking at existing land uses permitted in this
neighborhood commercial zone many of the uses already allowed are things that
pawn shops deal with and the vast majority of items are purchased and sold in
retail to the general public. In closing, Mr. Nienaber asked that Mr. Hamilton
be permitted to open the pawn shop at the location in the Beechgrove Shopping
Center. He stated that Mr. Hamilton has experience in this type of business
having operated six pawn shops in Kentucky.
Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a second reading. Council Member Cook
made a motion to adopt the proposed ordinance. Council Member Franzen stated
she opposes this text amendment that would allow pawn shops as a permitted use
in the Neighborhood Commercial zone. She stated she spoke with many residents
about this issue and not one person was in favor of this. No one put forth a
second to Council Member Cook’s motion, therefore the motion died for lack of a
second.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-08– Establishing Rental Dwelling Licenses – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a proposed ordinance that would
create a new chapter of the code of ordinances (Chapter 99) concerning rental
dwelling licenses.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-08 seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Mayor Moriconi then opened the floor for discussion
prior to a vote.
A lengthy discussion ensued. Council Members had questions and concerns
regarding the enforcement and annual inspections of the rental property, both
single family houses and multi-family complexes. Zoning Administrator Annie
Wuestefeld advised that it would take some planning for the annual inspections
before issuing a license, but that she and the Building Inspector would work it
out. Mr. Groth suggested that the police could help out if necessary. Council
Member Behler suggested the police are not trained in building code to assist
with inspections. Mayor Moriconi referred to a report supplied by the Police
Chief regarding the number of police calls for service to apartment complexes;
citing 2321 police calls which the Police Chief calculated to equate to an
annual expense of $183,000 police time. Council Member Behler stated that it is
difficult to determine if that is excessive since there is no comparison to
single family rental properties. Chief Butler replied that he had no way to
capture info on single family house rentals. Council Member Cook asked how the
City planned to license rented single family houses if we don’t know which
houses are rentals. Mrs. Wuestefeld advised that initially it would have to be
treated as an honor system and that it would take time before all single family
rentals could be determined.
Council Member Franzen expressed concern that the City is providing services to
renters who don’t pay any city taxes yet take advantage of all City services.
Council member Cook commented that many people cannot afford to purchase a
house and that renters support local businesses and pump their earned dollars
into the City’s economy.
Fred Burns, Green Road, Walton – addressed Council regarding this proposed
rental license and fees. He stated he is currently developing an apartment
complex in the Independence Village. He stated he studied this area and chose
to build here as he knew this was a strong area for this type of complex. He
expressed concern that this licensing fee will cost him an additional $6,000
per year. He didn’t see the need for this program as typically this would be
geared at low income housing and that there is already a federal inspection
program in place for the low income housing. He suggested the City consider a
flat fee charge for properties that require more police services. He stated
that this license and fee seems punitive to him. He stated the City will
collect a significant amount of property taxes for this development than for
the vacant land.
Doug Hauke – Also addressed Council regarding his opposition to this ordinance.
He expressed his displeasure that the vast majority will have to pay for the
few that don’t keep their properties up to code.
At this time there was a discussion on the extensive report provided to the
Council by the Police Chief. He advised that the report was for the 2321 calls
for service to 1300 apartment units citywide.
Council Member Behler commented that she understands this is a challenging year
for the budget but doesn’t want to pass this just for the revenue it would
generate. She stated she is concerned that it will cost more to enforce than
the revenue it will generate. She stated she would only vote for this if it
would be instrumental in keeping the citizens safe. She wondered if $40.00 per
unit would even be enough to accomplish all that was actually needed to do
that. Mayor Moriconi commented that it would be a net loss if taking into
consideration all the police time spend on calls for service.
Council Member Behler also expressed concern that this license/fee would not be
fair, since there will be no way to determine all the single family houses
being rented. Council Member Cook stated that the inspection part of the
licensing bothers her. She discussed the HUD inspection process and how
escrowed funds are withheld causing the property owner to lose subsidy from
government. She stated that additional inspections by the City would be
redundant in subsidized complexes and would run off good landlords. Council
Member Little asked how long it takes to inspect a unit. Council Member Cook
responded 10-15 minutes per unit and that HUD requires only 10% of a complex to
be inspected. Council Member Franzen commented that the HUD system does not
work.
Council Member Behler asked that the second reading of this ordinance be tabled
til next month until she could obtain more information. She would like to know
what percentage of the rental housing in the city is subsidized, etc. She
stated she feels that the way the ordinance is written that it cannot be
enforced fairly. Council Member Behler made a motion to table this until the
June meeting. The motion died for lack of a second.
Council Member Behler asked Mrs. Wuestefeld to look over the Police Chief’s
report and cross reference with the zoning/building code complaints she has
received. Mrs. Wuestefeld commented that the last couple years she has not
received any complaints. Council Member Little asked the Police Chief for stats
on drugs and theft. He replied that the stats could have been driven higher but
they were cautious in their reporting.
The discussion ended and Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2010-O-08 a second
reading. Roll was called and answered with four ayes and two no votes cast by
Council Members Behler and Cook. Motion carried 4-2
Award Bid for Arbor Court Road Repairs
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the tabulated results of the bids received
by the City for the road improvements for Arbor Court.
City Administrator Dan Groth reported that the improvements to Arbor Court were
in two parts. He stated that Part A was the City road improvements and Part B
was the water main improvements that would be funded by Northern Kentucky Water
District. He advised this was a collaborative bidding process with the Water
District. The City received five bids for the road improvements and he, along
with the Public Works Director, is recommending that the City award the project
to Len Riegler Blacktop who placed the low bid of $131,087.50. He stated the
City Engineer is recommending under-surfacing, but he feels that it is not a
necessary expense and would cost an extra $38,000. Mr. Groth stated that that
money could be better utilized elsewhere in the city, such as the sidewalks in
the area of Simon Kenton High School.
Council Member Franzen moved to award the Arbor Court road improvements project
to Len Riegler Blacktop in the amount of $131,087.50, seconded by Council
Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no cast by
Council Member Cook. Motion carried 5-1.
Amendment to Rental Agreement for the Senior Center
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for consideration a revised Senior Center
Rental Agreement. He stated that Nita Brake has been researching similar
agreements with other cities and the proposed amendments are a result of this
research.
Mr. Groth stated the proposed increase of rental fees would cover the actual
cost of cleanup of the center after each event. Ms. Brake commented that this
rental agreement was last updated in 2005 and the City has seen an increase in
maintenance charges over the last five years. She stated that the fee charged
to residents has not been increased in eight years.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the City should not lose money on rentals which
would be subsidizing private parties and events in the center. Ms. Brake stated
the proposed fee increase would take effect on July 1, 2010 but would not
affect existing signed agreements as the City will honor those. She distributed
to Council a list of fees charged by other cities that own a Senior Center or
Community Center.
A motion was made by Council Member Behler and seconded by Council Member
Little to approve the amended Senior Center Rental Agreement. Roll was called
and answered with five ayes and one no vote cast by Council Member Cook. Motion
carried 5-1.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Chapter 91 of the Code of Ordinances Adding a New
Section Dealing with Removal of Dog Excrement – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would amend
Chapter 91 of the code of ordinances by adding a new section dealing with dog
excrement removal. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Mr. Groth explained to Council the City has received several complaints this
past winter that pet owners would allow their dogs to go on the sidewalks and
then not clean it up.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending the 2009/2010 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would amend the 2009/10 budget. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2010/2011 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would adopt a budget for the 2010/2011 fiscal year. In his prepared budget
message he outlined the key elements of this budget which included the
following:
·   The proposed budget is based on maintaining the current property tax rate
·   No raises will be given to the employees
·   No new capital projects
·   No new fleet vehicles for the Police Department or Public Services
Department
·   Expenses have been reduced by over $400,000 compared to the current year
amended budget to offset declines in projected revenues from single family
building permits
·   Projected reserves at the end of the budget year are $1,844,482.
·   The proposed budget is balanced
Mayor Moriconi stated he feels this proposed budget maintains quality services
for the citizens and continues to maintain sufficient reserves for emergencies.
Council Member Cook asked if Council Members could have individual meetings
with staff to review the budget closer. Mr. Groth and Mayor Moriconi commented
that meetings could be arranged. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.

Reading

year. Mayor Moriconi advised Council that there is no change in the employee
pay ranges this year as no pay raises will be given this year. Mr. Deters read
the proposed ordinance.

Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi

Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2010-R-08 that would

an opinion.
Adjournment

the meeting ended at 9:27 p.m.

June 7, 2010
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of June 7, 2010
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 7,
2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. An invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat
Behler, Jim Bushong, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Proclamation presented to Marian Cummins, Independence Resident and The
Enquirer’s Women of the Year
Mayor Moriconi introduced and welcomed Independence resident Marian Cummins. He
stated that the City is excited and honored to have Mrs. Cummins here. He
stated that Mrs. Cummins has been recognized as one of ten women chosen by The
Enquirer to be awarded the honor of Women of the Year. Mayor Moriconi presented
Mrs. Cummins with a Proclamation expounding on her long and distinguished
career in private business and public service. Mrs. Cummins’ personal and
professional achievements include being a co-founder of the Nurse Advocacy
Center for the Underserved at Northern Kentucky University which provides nurse
volunteers to social service agencies as well as a mentor to nursing students,
volunteer and part time educator at NKU.
Mrs. Cummins thanked Mayor Moriconi and Council and stated that she has lived
in this community for thirty-four years and to receive this special recognition
from her community is particularly rewarding to her.
Presentation by Ann Brandon, Senior Public Education Specialist of the Women’s
Crisis Center Regarding Green Dot Intervention Program
Mayor Moriconi welcomed and introduced Ms. Ann Brandon who is the Senior Public
Education Specialist of the Women’s Crisis Center who would speak about the
Green Dot Intervention Program.
Ms. Brandon informed Council that Independence will be in the national
spotlight as Simon Kenton High School has been chosen to be part of the Green
Dot intervention program which is a national study that will train the students
to recognize violent situations. She stated this is a program that is funded by
the CDC. Ms. Brandon added that while Independence is not a violent community
this program will engage the high school students through education and skills
practice regarding violence and teach intervention techniques with the hopes of
reducing violence in our society. She stated that Phase 1 & 2 have been
completed at the school. In closing, Ms. Brandon stated that Simon Kenton High
School will be the national model and that Kenton County is the first county in
the nation that has done this.
Approval of the May 3, 2010 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, May 3, 2010. Council Member Bushong so moved, with
second by Council Member Yeager. One amendment was noted by Council Member
Behler; there being no objection roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-09 - Amending Chapter 91 of the Code of Ordinances Adding
a New Section Dealing with Removal of Dog Excrement – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2010-O-09 that
would amend Chapter 91 of the code of ordinances by adding a new section
dealing with dog excrement removal. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2010-O-09 a
second reading.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-09 seconded by
Council Member Behler. Council Member Cook asked how the ordinance would be
enforced. A brief discussion ensued and everyone concurred that the dog/owner
would have to be caught in the act in order to enforce this ordinance. There
being no further discussion roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-10 - Amending the 2009/2010 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2010-O-
10 that would amend the 2009/10 budget. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2010-O-10
a second reading.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-10 seconded by
Council Member Little. There being no discussion, roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-11 - Adopting the 2010/2011 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2010-O-11 that
adopts a budget for the 2010-2011 fiscal year. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No.
2010-O-11 a second reading.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-11, seconded by
Council Member Bushong. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Behler
expressed concerns that the projected revenue for the rental unit fee will not
cover the cost to administer and collect. She stated she is concerned that the
City will expend more funds in staff labor to make annual inspections to
enforce the fee/license than the City will receive in revenue that will be
collected from the fee. Mayor Moriconi stated for the record that he doesn’t
want to expend more than the City would collect, but that collection and
enforcement would not even begin until 2011. Council Member Behler stated that
she also believes the licensing of rental units will be hard to enforce. Mayor
Moriconi stated that he feels a system is in place that will enable us to
locate most properties that are rentals. He stated that if the license/fee does
not accomplish the goals the City hoped for then the Council may want to
reconsider this next year. Council Member Bushong suggested tracking staff
hours to get an idea of the amount of hours it costs to enforce this ordinance.
He stated he would be willing to look at this in a year to see if it is paying
for itself. Council Member Behler commented that it was mentioned at the last
meeting that the projected revenue would not even cover the police calls for
service hours spent at the apartment complexes. Mayor Moriconi stated that
while it will not fully cover the police time that it will somewhat offset the
police expense. Mr. Groth commented that the rental unit license will require
landlords to meet minimum building code standards before a license will be
issued to permit the unit to be rented. Council Member Behler advised that she
would be voting no on the budget ordinance and just wanted to say that she
believes this revenue line item will effect the budget in the long run. Mayor
Moriconi commented that he did not believe it was hurting the budget and would
actually provide some enforcement and offset some of the expense of police time
spent at the rental complexes.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered with five ayes
and one no vote cast by Council Member Behler. Motion carried 5-1.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-12 - Amending the Employee Pay and Classification Plan –
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading a Ordinance No. 2010-O-12 that
will adopt a Pay and Classification Plan for the 2010/2011 fiscal year. Mr.
Deters gave Ordinance No. 2010-O-12 a second reading.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2010-O-12, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2010-R-09 – Sponsoring a Text Amendment Application Regarding
Off-Street Parking Regulations
Mayor Moriconi introduced Resolution No. 2010-R-09 that would support the City
making application for a zoning text amendment to amend Article 11 Off-street
parking and access control regulations, Section 11.2. The text amendments would
affect Section 11.2 (T) Offices for professional, business, financial, real
estate and other business: Section 11.2 (W) Retail and personal service, and
Section 11.2 (Z) Shopping Centers by decreasing the number of parking spaces
required for those affected zones
A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Yeager asked what prompted these
proposed text changes. Mayor Moriconi advised that he has had several
businesses approach him about these parking regulations. He stated he has
discussed this with Mrs. Wuestefeld and learned that the City’s parking
regulations are more restrictive that other communities in this area. He stated
that the proposed changes have been modeled after the City of Fort Wright. Mr.
Deters advised that developers pay high dollar for commercial property and a
portion of that is higher price for more parking areas. Mrs. Wuestefeld
commented that the developers can’t meet the parking requirements for the
current available lots in the City. She stated that many prospective developers
leave when they become aware they can’t meet the City’s parking requirements.
She stated that only three types of business uses would be affected in this
section of the zoning text.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Cook moved to approve
Resolution No. 2010-R-09, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth reported that Simon Kenton High School is undergoing a complete
renovation of their parking lot area in the front of the school building. He
stated they will be installing a side walk area as well. Mr. Groth advised that
the City would complete the sidewalk area from the school to the intersection
of Shaw Road and Madison Pike.
Mr. Groth announced that the Police Department’s new recruit - Jeff Young - has
graduated from the Police Academy last week and was valedictorian of his class.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi reported that this year’s July 4th fireworks celebration will be
held on July 2 & 3 and that the City has received $29,500 in corporate/business
donations to offset the cost of this event. He stated this is an increase of
$5,000 over last year’s donations, which is incredible considering the weak
economy. Mayor Moriconi advised he would recognize these sponsors in the June
newsletter. He thanked Tony Lucas, Nita Brake, Shawn Butler and Council Member
Yeager for all their efforts in soliciting the private donations for the
fireworks.
Mayor Moriconi reported that the restrooms located in the Shadybrook
subdivision has been the target of vandals so it has been decided to keep the
restroom building locked unless there is a sport activity taking place at the
park.
Mayor Moriconi advised that Flag Day is June 14th and there will be a flag
burning ceremony held at Sterling Staggs Park at 7:00 p.m. on that day.
In closing, Mayor Moriconi announced and congratulated the seniors at the
Independence Senior Center who are the proud champs of this year’s Wii bowling
tournament.
Miscellaneous
Council Member Behler reported that the monument sign at the entrance of the
Lakefield subdivision is currently being maintained by the City as the property
on which the sign is located has been vacated. She stated these monument signs
are not a problem if they are maintained by a Homeowners’ Association, but are
a problem when they are located on private property, which concerns her.
Mrs. Wuestefeld advised that most monument signs are located on private
property and the property owner generally signs an agreement to maintain the
area. If not maintained, then the City mows the area and liens the property
owner as it is the property owners responsibility to maintain this sign area.
Council Member asked if July 12th would be the next meeting. Mayor Moriconi
advised that the City observes the July 4th holiday on Monday July 5th and the
City’s ordinance states that if the regular meeting falls on a holiday or
observed holiday, then the meeting would fall to the second Monday of the
month.
Executive Session
At 7:43 p.m. Mr. Deters requested an executive session in accordance with
K.R.S. 61.810 (b) for deliberations on possible future acquisition or sale of
real property. Council member Franzen so moved, seconded by Council Member
Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 7:57 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to resume the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. The motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Behler moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:57 p.m.

Mr. Groth reported that the Kenton County Planning Commission will hold a

to be located behind the Cherokee Shopping Center near the LaRosa’s
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters

successful July 4th Celebration. He commented that many people work behind the

virtually problem free, with no police arrests, which speaks highly of this
family-friendly event. He stated the police estimate that 15,000-18,000 people
came out to watch the fireworks display on Saturday night. Council Member
Franzen thanked Captain Tony Lucas for spearheading this event each year.
Executive Session

with K.R.S. 61.810 (b) for deliberations on possible future acquisition or sale
of real property, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all
ayes.
At 7:38 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to resume the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. The motion carried with all ayes.
No action resulted from the Executive Session
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Behler moved to adjourn the

COUNCIL MEETING

City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 2,
2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. An invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Mary Pat
Behler, Jim Bushong, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen, and Donna Yeager. Council
Member Mike Little was absent. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the July 12, 2010 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, July 12, 2010. Council Member Behler so moved, with
second by Council Member Franzen. There being no amendments noted, roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Presentation of Proposed Beck Financial Center at Independence Towne Center
Mayor Moriconi introduced Mr. Richard Wuest with K4 Architecture, LLC who would
present a proposal for a professional office building (Beck Financial Center)
in the Independence Towne Center.
Mr. Wuest distributed a design concept of the professional office building
which included a vicinity map, site plan and front elevation rendering. He
stated the three-story; 36,000 square foot building would be located off of
Declaration Drive. He stated the location would have good sight flow and have
two locations for ingress/egress. Mr. Wuest pointed out that all four
elevations of the building have unique architectural design consisting of a cut
stone base and federal style windows which will be consistent with the
historical elements seen in existing structures in this area. He stated it will
also have a cupola as required on all the structures in the Towne Center
development. He stated the proposed building will also have tower elements on
all four corners of the building.
Mayor Moriconi commented that no action is being asked of the Council at this
time. He stated he is excited about this proposal and wanted to share this plan
with everyone. Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Wuest for his informational
presentation and hoped to see the realization of his development plan in the
near future.
Presentation
Mayor Moriconi welcomed back Gailen and Debbie Bridges who were present to
provide the City Council with an update on their progress in compiling photos
and other information for the history book on Independence they are writing in
collaboration with Arcadia Publishing.
Mr. Bridges stated they commenced this book project approximately three months
ago and has compiled a good collection of old photographs that local citizens
are finding in old dresser drawers and stored in attics and basements. He
stated they are having fun and getting a lot of good documents and photos to
include in this publication. He stated they have received so many pictures of
the Independence High School that he could probably do a separate book just on
the high school building. Mr. Bridges presented a slide show of some of the
photos he has collected so far. He reminded everyone that they can send
information or contact him at independencebook@ymail.com. Mayor Moriconi asked
when they could expect the book to be published. Mr. Bridges advised that he
believes the book will be published and available by Memorial Day of 2011.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-13 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Permitting Exterior
Sales of Seasonal Garden Supplies and Plantings in the NSC Zone – 2nd Reading

garden supplies and plantings. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2010-O-13.

Award Bid for 2010 Street Repair Project

2010 Street Repairs. He stated the Public Services employees did the curb tear
out and restoration and the City received five bids for the resurfacing of

August 31, 2010
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of August 31, 2010
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Tuesday, August 31, 2010 at 6:00 p.m. in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Mary Pat Behler, Jim Bushong, Margaret Cook, Carol Franzen,
and Donna Yeager. Absent was Council Member Mike Little. Also present was City
Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone and announced this Special meeting of Council
was being held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
·   Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Property Tax Rates for 2010 – 1st Reading
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Property Tax Rates for 2010 – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
adopt the 2010 real estate and personal property tax rates. He stated the
proposed ordinance establishes the ad valorem tax on real estate property at
$0.200 dollars for each one hundred dollars ($100.00) of assessed value and a
personal property tax rate of $0.596 dollars for each one hundred dollars
($100.00). He advised these are the same rates adopted last year (2009). He
advised that this year’s real property compensating rate was calculated to be
$0.220 which would bring in $269,565 and a mid-way rate of $0.210 would produce
$133,676 in additional revenue. Mayor Moriconi commented that the City has
refrained from taking the compensating rate for the last few years due to the
downturn in the economy, but that, at some point it will no longer be
sustainable for the City to continue to adopt prior year’s tax rates.
Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance. Mayor Moriconi advised that the
ordinance would be presented for a second reading at the regular meeting of
September 13, 2010.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 6:04 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
4, 2010 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.

Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
