Steering Committee Update – Jenna Haverkos, NKAPC Principal Planner & Chris
Reinersman, Committee Vice-Chairman
Ms. Haverkos reported the Steering Committee is working on form based zoning
codes for the Downtown Study area and held a public meeting on August 31, 2010
to obtain citizen input on form based zoning codes. The Committee heard
suggestions from the citizens on their desires for future zoning for the area
as well as zoning they do not desire for this area of the city. They discussed
identifying the boundaries of the area and preferred zoning tools. She stated
that staff will work on a draft of text changes that will be proposed and will
update the Kenton County Planning Commission.
Mr. Reinersman reported that the major recommendation of the Small Area Study
was to update the zoning along the new (re-routed) section of SR17 and McCullum
Road area. He stated the Planning Commission staff has been helpful in guiding
the Steering Committee in this process and working with them in proposing a
zoning code that meets the desires of the City. He stated they have general
ideas for proposed regulations and will begin to narrow down the plans. He
stated that Council can expect to have the Committee’s recommendations in March
of 2011.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Reinersman, Ms. Haverkos and the Committee members
for their time and dedication to this project.
Privileges of the Floor
Mr. Joe Gormally, General Manager of Snap Fitness on Declaration Drive – Mr.
Gormally gave a presentation to Council on the new Snap Fitness that has opened
on Declaration Drive. He stated this is a 3300 sq. ft., 24-hour facility which
is staffed from 6:00 a.m. until 10:00 p.m. each day. He spoke to Council about
the Snap Fitness worksite health promotion and the benefits of a proactive
health management program for City employees. He stated there is a high rate of
return on the investment thereby decreasing the City’s employee healthcare
costs. He advised the Independence Snap Fitness would open on October 15th and
is the first of several that will be opening in this area. He invited everyone
to attend the Open House on October 22nd, with the ribbon cutting ceremony at
1:00 p.m.
Henry Covey, 16 Alvin Drive, Independence – Mr. Covey addressed Council
regarding the problem he is having with people on Shaw Road riding four-
wheelers (Quads) on his property. Mayor Moriconi advised that Quads are allowed
in the City. Mr. Covey asked that they be restricted to a certain amount of
acreage.
Council Member Little stated that he considered this disturbance to Mr. Covey
to be enforced under the City’s nuisance ordinance. A brief discussion ensued
with Mr. Covey regarding his concern and it was decided that the nuisance
ordinance would be used to enforce this and the City’s patrol officers would be
advised.
Rita Hauck, 5246 Oakview Court, Independence – advised Council that the
Hartland Subdivision has experienced a recent influx of door-to-door sales
people who are very persistent and won’t take no for an answer. She stated that
when police officers are called the sales people produce a county business
license but not a license from the City. She stated she is concerned for the
safety of the residents. Mr. Groth and Mayor Moriconi explained that the sales
people should be able to show a City solicitor license in addition to an
occupational license. The City Clerk provided a brief explanation of the
difference between a “solicitor” license for door-to-door sales and an
occupational license issued by the County office. Ms. Hauck asked that the
police officers be informed of the solicitor license. Council Members and the
Mayor agreed that this information about a solicitor license would be
publicized on the City’s website, Facebook page and City newsletter.
Ordinance No. 2010-O-15– Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Reducing the Number

2010-O-15, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Discussion regarding Zoning Violation Process
Mayor Moriconi advised Council there have been some concerns expressed to him
regarding the City’s zoning violation process with particular concern regarding
the chronic violators. Council Member Little stated the current process for
violations gives the owner thirty days to come into compliance, which they do
and the violation case is closed out and then within a few weeks the violation
re-occurs and the process starts over again. He stated this seems to be an on-
going process with several property owners who are aware of the loop hole in
the law. Mr. Groth advised that the City’s process is mandated by State law, so
the City’s options in changing this process may be very limited. A brief
discussion ensued resulting in the City Attorney advising he would research
possible options for the City regarding the repeat offenders of zoning
violations.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth announced the State Highway Department has installed a traffic light
at the intersection of the new SR17 and McCullum Road. He also announced that a
household waste collection event would be held on Saturday, November 6th at
Turfway Park in Florence.
Mr. Groth reported that upcoming City events are the Howl-O-Ween Pet Costume
Contest on Saturday, October 16 at 10:00 at Memorial Park and the F.O.P Haunted
Trail on October 23rd at 6:00 p.m. at Memorial Park.
Council Member Behler announced that a free concert would be held at the
Memorial Park Amphitheater on Saturday, October 30th from 3-6 pm in celebration
of Make a Difference Day supporting Milestones Equestrian Achievement Program
which is a not for profit therapeutic horseback riding program for individuals
with disabilities.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi announced that Trick-or-Treat hours for Halloween this year
would be from 6-8 pm on Sunday, October 31st.
Mayor Moriconi also announced that the Tea Party of Northern Kentucky would
hold a Rally on Saturday, October 23rd from 1-5 pm at the Memorial Park
Amphitheater.
Mayor Moriconi stated that he will possibly cancel the November meeting due to
lack of business. He stated he would let Council know as soon as possible if
the meeting will be cancelled.

meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:40 p.m.

Declare Surplus Property
Mayor Moriconi advised Council the City administration office has two pieces of
outdated office equipment no longer being used and need to be declared surplus.
The items to be disposed of are a Lanier 5635 Copier and a Brother 4100
Intellifax Fax machine. Mr. Groth advised that KRS 82.083 regulates the
disposition of City property and allows the City to take bids or transfer with
or without compensation to another governmental agency. He stated that the City
of Ryland Heights is in need of a copier and fax machine and ask that Council
consider donating the equipment to them.
Council Member Behler made a motion to declare the copier and fax machines as

Proposed Ordinance – Changing Speed Limit on Centennial Blvd., Declaration
Drive & Delaware Crossing – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would change the speed limit on Centennial Boulevard as it extends between
Old KY17 and the new relocated KY17 and the speed limit on Declaration Drive,
both from 20 miles per hour to 30 miles per hour. Mr. Groth advised that
Kentucky state law allows a speed limit of 35 mph in a commercial district.
Council Member Cook suggested that Delaware Crossing also be changed to 30 mph.
There was consensus among Council to include Delaware Crossing as well. Mr.
Deters made the change to the proposed ordinance and then gave it a first
reading. Mayor Moriconi advised the ordinance would have a second reading in
January.
Proposed Ordinance – Amend Current Building Fee Schedule to Include a Fee for
HVAC Inspections – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would repeal Ordinance No. 2007-O-21, which regulates the schedule of
building and zoning permit fees, and adopt a new schedule of permit fees that
will include permit fees for HVAC inspections. He stated this new fee schedule
will become effective January 1, 2011.
Mr. Kevin Barbian, the city’s Building Inspector, advised Council that HVAC
inspections is a new state requirement and will be regulated in a similar
manner to that of electric and plumbing. Council Member Bushong asked if the
fees/inspections would be for new or upgraded items. Mr. Barbian advised that
both new and upgraded systems would require a permit and inspection.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance to
adopt the new schedule of building and zoning application fees.
Proposed Ordinance – Amend Current Sidewalk Maintenance – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that will amend Chapter 95 of the code of ordinances by adding a new section
delegating responsibility for sidewalks to the property owners. Mr. Groth
advised Council that he contacted twelve local cities regarding this proposal
and learned that half of the cities take care of the sidewalks and the other
half require property owners to provide the upkeep of the sidewalks that abut
their property. Council Member Bushong questioned the liability aspect. Mr.
Deters advised that it would have no effect whatsoever as both the property
owner and City would probably be involved in a liability lawsuit if one should
arise. Mr. Groth commented that for a City the size of Independence it is a
financial hardship to undertake full responsibility of all sidewalk
infrastructures. In response to Council Member Yeager’s question, he advised
that this would apply to all new subdivisions. There being no further
discussion, Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading.

COUNCIL MEETING

City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
10, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with

Mayor Moriconi welcomed new Council Members Tom Brinker and Chris Reinersman.
He stated the City would make a couple of special presentations tonight.
Presentation to Senator Damon Thayer
Mayor Moriconi introduced Senator Damon Thayer and presented him a key to the
City to officially thank him for all the assistance with infrastructure
projects throughout the City. Mayor Moriconi stated that for the last several
years Senator Thayer has successfully supported the City’s efforts to get
traffic signals installed at the intersection of new SR17 and McCullum Road as
well as funding for the construction of new SR17.
Senator Thayer stated that he was honored to be recognized in this manner and
has not been bestowed in this way by other cities that he represents. He stated

Mayor Moriconi commented that the City will be requesting another traffic
signal at the intersection of Centennial and SR17 and would appreciate his
support again. Senator Thayer advised that the Transportation Department -
District 6 – would do a study to determine the need but assured Mayor Moriconi
that he would call the District and make sure they know that this traffic
signal is a priority of his and his constituents.
Again, Mayor Moriconi thanked Senator Thayer and presented him with a key to
the City.

Kenton High School, for her act of heroism on October 21, 2010 when confronted
with a life and death situation, she selflessly came to the aid of her friend
who was attacked by dogs. Ms. Kahrs quick reactions and instant decision to get
her friend to the hospital as soon as possible saved her friend’s life. Ms.
Kahrs thanked Mayor Moriconi and advised that her friend is doing well and even
returned to her volleyball team.

Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2008-O-11 Relating to the time of
Annual Payments of the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt Reduction Assessment – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2008-O-11 relating to the time of annual payments of the
Fowler Creek Sewer debt reduction assessment. He commented that staff has
recommended that this assessment be put back on the annual property tax
billing. He stated that this is just a first reading and no decision is
expected tonight.
Council Member Yeager stated she respects KLC legal counsel J.D. Chaney, but
disagrees with his opinion of this. She stated she feels it is not legal to add
this assessment to the tax bills and would like the City to obtain an opinion
from the State Attorney General before deciding on this issue. Council Member
Franzen agreed that the City should seek an opinion before the second reading
of the ordinance. She also expressed concern that the 2010 and 2011 fiscal
years would actually be billed in the beginning and end of 2011 which could
cause confusion to those paying the assessment. Mayor Moriconi advised that a
separate billing of the assessment has associated mailing costs and has caused
a decrease in the collection rate. He stated the full amount of the annual debt
service payment is being collected but the additional amount that is building
up the reserve balance is not increasing at a rate that will allow the City to
pay the full debt retirement earlier than expected. Council Member Little asked
what recourse or action is available to the City in collecting the delinquent
assessments. Mr. Deters stated that is a gray area now. Mr. Deters advised that
it would take several months or longer to obtain an opinion from the Attorney
General. Council Member Reinersman commented that he has heard complaints that
the separate bill cannot be included in a mortgage escrow account and now the
resident gets one big bill.
Mayor Moriconi advised that he would go ahead with a first reading of the
ordinance and further questions and concerns could be addressed prior to a
second reading. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.

February 28, 2011
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of February 28, 2011
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky held a Special Meeting
on Monday, February 28, 2011 at 6:00 p.m. in the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol
Franzen, Chris Reinersman and Donna Yeager. Council Member Mike Little was
absent. Also present was City Attorney, Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone and announced this special meeting of Council
was being held to discuss and take action on the following business item:
·   Road Improvement Projects – Discussion and possible Action
Road Improvement Projects
Mayor Moriconi stated that this meeting has been called to discuss the
possibility of borrowing funds for street projects. He introduced Todd Cooney
and Chris Bell of Fifth Third Bank. Mayor Moriconi advised that with interest
rates being at historical lows they began contacting various banks to seek rate
information and found some very competitive rates with Fifth Third Bank
presenting the lowest rate. He stated he is proposing borrowing funds to begin
making repairs and reconstruction of the most deteriorated streets in the City.
He stated that Fifth Third Bank has proposed a 10-year loan for 1,500,000 at a
fixed rate of 3.46%. He stated the point of this meeting is to lock in this
rate as the rates are fluctuating daily and the bank has advised they would
hold this rate until our March 7th meeting when a final vote would be taken on
issue.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that the City currently receives an annual
average of $303,000 in Municipal Road Aid (MRA) funds from the state. The MRA
amount fluctuates from year to year so this average was arrived from the last
five years receivables. He stated that the projected annual payment on the loan
would be approximately $180,000 which would leave an adequate amount for other
road projects. He stated it would be important to continue to allocate
additional funds to the road repair budget each year as well. Mayor Moriconi
advised that a scoring system is used for the streets and the $1,500,000 will
put a dent in the list of the lowest scoring streets. He stated that the road
repairs would also be coordinated with any work/repairs to be done by the
Sanitation District and/or Water District.
City Attorney, Jed Deters asked if the City would earn interest on the unused
funds as repairs are made to the streets. Mayor Moriconi advised the interest
would accrue on the remaining loan balance as each phase of the street project
was completed. He said it could take 2-3 years to complete the repairs and
exhaust the borrowed funds.
Mr. Groth reported that 150 streets were graded in the street inspection
summary report of 2009. He stated the City would coordinate repairs of 8
streets; four with the Sanitation District and four with the Water District.
Mr. Groth advised that coordinating with other agencies for repairs to
infrastructure is becoming commonplace through the Envista program. He stated
that all eight streets scored 75 or below. He stated that he feels the City
could receive good competitive bids for these street projects as the
contractors are eager to schedule work for their crews.
Council Member Reinersman commented that he is not totally opposed to this
proposal, as he knows there is a lot of merit to this street project. He stated
he is concerned that using a large portion of the MRA funds received from the
State for a ten-year debt service would not leave adequate funds to keep up
with maintenance and repairs of other City streets. He commented that he knows
it is hard to pass up this low interest rate, but he fears the City will not
get far enough ahead of the curve and then find in a few years we are unable to
maintain this aggressive program.
Mr. Deters asked if there was any risk of losing the State MRA funds. Mayor
Moriconi responded that the annual funds from the State are known to fluctuate,
but he does not foresee that they would eliminate this funding to the cities.
Mayor Moriconi went on to advise Council that this aggressive street program
will only work if we continue to apportion some of the general funds into the
street repair budget line along with the MRA funds from the State.
Mayor Moriconi stated that it his job to present ideas to Council for
consideration. He stated he feels this is a win-win situation and an
opportunity to obtain low interest rates on a loan, get good bids for the
construction projects and take care of some of the most deteriorated streets in
the City. He stated the other option is to do nothing. Mr. Deters commented
that in the long run, delaying road repairs will cost more in the long run.
Public Works Director commented that the annual budget for street repairs
should be around $500,000 and that in past years this has been underfunded. He
said it would be beneficial to fund this more each year to catch up on the road
repairs. He stated it would allow them to provide more maintenance to the
highest scoring streets which would add to the life of the street.
Mayor Moriconi stated that some cities have placed a road tax on the ballot
only to have it fail in the general elections. He stated the option he is
presenting will allow the City to take advantage of historical low interest
rates to get the project done without raising taxes. Mr. Groth commented that
the City of Cold Spring recently borrowed money to do a similar street
reconstruction/repair program for several of their streets and they report they
have been happy with the result.
Council Member Bushong asked how the City would be able to get the annual
street repair budget line item up to $500,000 if only receiving $300,000 from
the State. Mayor Moriconi replied that it would be taken from the reserve
account or by adopting the compensating property tax rate.
Council Member Franzen commented that the City’s job is to maintain services to
the community and that tax dollars should be spent in providing those services
and citizens are more uncomplaining of paying their taxes if they can see
something happening, such as their streets being repaired and maintained. Mayor
Moriconi commented that the City could remain taking a slower approach to the
needed repairs, but would rather not be short-sighted in this area.
In turning the conversation to the loan terms and process, Mayor Moriconi
advised that he did not recommend going with a seven year term as the annual
payment would increase about $60,000/year. He stated he would be more
comfortable keeping the annual payment well below the allocation of MRA funds
received each year. Council Member Franzen asked about paying off the loan
earlier than the ten years. Fifth Third Bank representative Chris Bell advised
that the loan agreement has a 2% penalty for an early pay off.
Council Member Brinker brought up the issue of Cody Road, which has been
slipping and in general disrepair for many years. Mr. Groth advised that Cody
Road and Marshall Road are separate issues for which he would consider apply
for emergency funds from the State Transportation Cabinet. He said these two
roads need to be approached separately. Mayor Moriconi commented that the City
could opt to borrow $2,000,000 and put $500,000 into the reconstruction of Cody
road, but he too feels that this road could qualify for emergency funds from
the State. He stated he is not really comfortable borrowing more than the
$1,500,000 for now. Mr. Cooper advised that the City was able to stabilize Cody
Road a few years ago and it has held up. He stated that the flooding in the
Cody Road creek is also another problem. Mayor Moriconi reminded everyone there
has been a lot of talk over the last several years about Cody Road situation
and that at one time a developer was going to make the necessary reconstruction
of the road as part of a residential development in the area, but the
development fell through. Mr. Groth stated he feels that State and/or federal
funds should become available within the next two-three years.
Mayor Moriconi stated that if Council was not supportive of this proposal he
would not move forward. He stated he feels this loan proposal is a good
opportunity to take advantage of low interest rates and is better than
proposing a road tax. He stated the City could take care of the most
deteriorated streets now and then get on a better maintenance schedule in a few
years.
Council Member Franzen stated she would like to see a seven and ten year loan
proposal before taking a vote on this at next week’s meeting. She stated she
believes it is trending down and would like to consider a seven year loan. Mr.
Bell from Fifth Third Bank commented that the bank is at risk as well. He
stated that time is of the essence in getting the low interest rate locked in.
He stated the rate has the potential to go up or down, but will now be a huge
swing either way. Mr. Deters advised the term of the loan would not make a
difference in the first reading of the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Yeager commented that she thinks this will be a good project for
the City.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Lease with Fifth Third Bank to Finance
$1,500,000 for the Construction of Streets and Other Infrastructure
Improvements – 1st Reading
Before having a first reading of the ordinance that would approve a lease with
the bank to finance the construction of streets for a principal amount not to
exceed $1,500,000, Mayor Moriconi asked for a show of hands by those Council
Members that favor moving forward. For the record, Council Members Brinker,
Franzen and Yeager raised their hands in approval to move forward.
Mr. Deters gave the first reading of the ordinance approving a lease to finance
$1,500,000 for road improvements.
Adjournment
There being no further business before the Council, Council Member Franzen
moved to adjourn the meeting, seconded by Council Member Reinersman. Motion
carried with all ayes and the meeting ended at 6:42 p.m.
                     ___________________________________
                     Christian J. Moriconi, Mayor

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
March 7, 2011
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of March 7, 2011
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 7,
2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters. Mayor Moriconi advised
Council they have before them an updated Agenda as two items of discussion have
been added.
Approval of the January 10, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, January 10, 2011. Council Member Reinersman so moved,
with second by Council Member Franzen. Amendments were presented without
objection, roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried.
Approval of the February 28, 2011 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the Special
meeting held on Monday, February 28, 2011. Council Member Bushong so moved,
with second by Council Member Yeager. Amendments were presented without
objection; roll was called and answered with five ayes and one abstention
voiced by Council Member Little. Motion carried
Privileges of the Floor
Mayor Moriconi called upon Mark Sennet of Beckmark, Inc. who did not answer.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that Mr. Sennet wanted to request that the City
sponsor a zoning text amendment that would allow an auto parts type of business
in the PUD development off of Centennial Blvd. He stated that current zoning
regulations do not allow this type of business in a PUD zone. Council Member
Bushong suggested that since Mr. Sennet failed to appear at this meeting that
this should be tabled until the April meeting or later on in this meeting if
Mr. Sennet arrives later.
Rokvic Family – Request for a Zoning Text Amendment – Mayor Moriconi asked
Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld to provide information for this request
from the Rokvic Family. Mrs. Wuestefeld stated the Rokvic’s came to her
requesting a permit to install a fence in the front yard of their property at
4224 Richardson Road. She stated she feels some special circumstances exist
that may give merit to applying for a text amendment to allow fences in the
front yard. Council Member Little asked which zone this property is located in
and if this type of request could be considered a variance that the Board of
Adjustment could decide. She stated she thinks it is an R-1C, but that fences
are not actually regulated by zone. She stated that the Board of Adjustment can
provide a variance for the height of a fence, but the Board cannot contradict
an ordinance regulation that currently prohibits fences in the front yard. Mrs.
Wuestefeld suggested allowing fences in the front yard when the property fronts
an arterial street and has four or more acres. Council Member Franzen suggested
adding a set-back requirement. Mrs. Wuestefeld stated a sixty-foot set-back and
limit the fence height to four feet in the front yard. She stated the type of
fence should also be specified.
Resolution No. 2011-R-03 – Supporting the Application of a Zoning Text
Amendment Relating to Fences in Front Yard Areas of Single Family Residential
Zone
There being no further discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Yeager
and seconded by Council Member Brinker to adopt a Resolution supporting the
application of a zoning text amendment that would allow fences in the front
yard area of single family residential properties if certain criteria are met.
Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one abstention cast by Council
Member Jim Bushong.
Proposed Ordinance – Authorizing the Financing of Road Improvement Project
Mr. Groth re-introduced the discussion from the special meeting held on
February 28, 2011 about the possibility of borrowing $1,500,000 for street
improvement projects. He advised Council that Fifth Third Bank has locked in at
today’s rates of 2.93% fixed for a 7-year and 3.48% fixed for a 10-year loan.
He stated the annual loan payments would be $233,289 and $174,121 respectively.
Mr. Groth advised that the average Municipal Road Aid (MRA) received from the
State is around $300,000 each year which would more than cover the annual loan
payment and leave extra funds for other street repairs and maintenance. Mayor
Moriconi commented that the rates have not changed much since the meeting last
week. He stated the funds would be expended over a 2-3 year period as the road
projects would be accomplished over that time period. Council Member Reinersman
expressed concern that the City would have to cut back or raise taxes to meet
this payment. He stated he would be more comfortable if it were only $500,000
this year. Council Member Franzen wondered how the City would meet the annual
loan payment if the State discontinued the distribution of MRA funds. Mr. Groth
explained that seems unlikely considering that the MRA allocation is based on
population and is derived from gas taxes collected by the State.
Council Member Reinersman expressed some concern that with recent skyrocketing
gas prices that this will affect the gas tax revenue collected by the State.
Council Member Franzen suggested putting a limit on the amount spent each year
from the $1,500,000 loan, such as $500,000 per year. Council Member Little
expressed concern that the State MRA funds would be committed to a debt payment
in final years of a 7-10 loan term that would leave a hole in the City’s road
repair fund. Mayor Moriconi countered that only half of the annual State MRA
funds would be allocated to the debt service of this loan leaving the other
half for continued road maintenance and repairs. Mayor Moriconi stated with the
historic low interest rates he felt this proposed loan was worth consideration.
Council Member Bushong commented this may not be the right time to borrow
money. He suggested supplementing the MRA funds with the City’s reserve account
until things turn around and perhaps look at taking out a loan at a later date.
Council Member Franzen commented that when the economy gets better the interest
rates will increase.
At this point in the discussion Mayor Moriconi advised the Council Members that
he would not break a tie vote on this issue. He stated he feels the majority of
the Members need to be in favor of this loan to move forward.
Council continued the discussion with focus being on the loan term – seven
versus ten years. While some Council Members voiced a preference for a seven
year loan, Mayor Moriconi stated the annual payment for a seven year loan would
consume most of the MRA funds and not leave enough funds to do other in-house
projects, such as sidewalks, etc.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to citizens who signed in to speak on this
issue.
Frank Halpin, 10326 Limerick Circle, Independence – voiced his objection to
taking out a loan for street repairs. He stated the City should not depend on
State MRA funds to make a loan payment and that if the City cannot repay the
loan from the general fund then the City shouldn’t be borrowing money. Mr.
Halpin described MRA funds as a gift from the State. Mayor Moriconi explained
that the MRA funds is not a ‘gift’ but is a portion of the gas tax revenue
collected by the State which is apportioned throughout the State for local
street repairs and maintenance. He commented that he feels taking out a loan is
a better option than putting a road tax on the general election ballot.
Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum Road, Independence – stated he is in favor of fixing
the roads, but against borrowing money to do it. He stated he does not think it
makes sense to borrow money when the City has a reserve fund.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence – also objected to borrowing money for
road repairs and paying loan interest each year. She also stated that she felt
the money should come from the City’s reserve account.
At this time the City Clerk explained the purpose of a reserve account and that
in keeping with government accounting standards a City the size of Independence
should maintain a four to six month reserve account to be used in the event of
a natural disaster or time of dire emergency. She stated the reserve account
should not be used for annual operational expenses. Mayor Moriconi asked what
was the current balance of the reserve fund. The City Clerk advised that the
balance is approximately $1,800,000 which is about a four month reserve.
Mayor Moriconi stated that taking out a $1,500,000 loan would allow the City to
repair five streets a year instead of two which could bring lower bid prices as
well. Mrs. Cook commented that the City has already saved money by doing some
of the road projects with in-house public works staff. Mayor Moriconi stated
that the City does most of the concrete replacement with the public works staff
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Lease with Fifth Third Bank to Finance
$1,500,000 for the Construction of Streets and Other Infrastructure
Improvements – 2nd Reading
At this time, Mayor Moriconi directed the City Attorney to give a second
reading to the proposed ordinance that would approve a lease with Fifth Third
Bank to finance the road project for a maximum principal amount of $1,500,000.
Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Further discussion ensued about possibly borrowing a lesser amount or
allocating more to the road repairs account from the general fund.
Council Member Yeager moved to have a second reading of the ordinance to
approve the borrowing of $1,500,000. Council Member Reinersman suggested that
if the City does borrow this money, that it would require additional action by
the Council to be expended and not a part of the annual budget. Mayor Moriconi
stated that the money could be kept in the reserve account and then amounts
transferred into the general account as repairs are done. Discussion ended; no
one was forthcoming with a second to Council Member Yeager’s motion, therefore,
the motion on the floor died for lack of a second.
Mayor Moriconi thanked the Fifth Third Bank representatives for the time and
effort they put into this proposal, but that the Council does not feel
comfortable at this time to borrow funds to do the street repair project. He
suggested that maybe this issue could be re-visited in coming months and
hopefully the interest rates will still be low.
Proclamation – Brain Injury Awareness Month
Mayor Moriconi presented a Proclamation declaring March as National Brain
Injury Awareness Month. He stated this proclamation was presented at the last
Mayor’s Group meeting with the request that each city adopt it.
Proposed Ordinance – Zoning Text Amendment Amending Regulations for Temporary
and Detached Signs – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
override the recommendation of the Kenton County Planning Commission (Number
2027R) and thereby approve a text amendment that would amend the regulations
for non-residential temporary and detached signs. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance
a first reading. Council Member Reinersman questioned some language that seemed
unclear on page two, section 1A. Mrs. Wuestefeld explained that the intent is
for “each” individual sign. The text will be revised for the second reading of
the ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Zoning Text Amendment Adding “Pawn Shops” to List of
Permitted Uses in the RC-2 Zone – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would

Proposed Ordinance – Amending 2010/2011 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would

budget of $75,000. There being no questions by Council, Mr. Deters gave the

Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Police Impoundment of Vehicles – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
allow for the collection of a $75.00 handling fee for vehicles impounded by the
Police Department. Council Member Bushong asked if a fee had been charged in
the past. Police Chief Shawn Butler replied they have not charged fees and this
new fee will only be charged in criminal related offenses and not for auto
accidents, etc. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Award Bid – Street Repairs Project for Catalpa and Chestnut
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a report and recommendation from the City
Engineer regarding the bids received for the Catalpa and Chestnut Street
improvements. He reported that the City received eight bids for this project
and that the recommendation is to award the bid to TMS Construction who
submitted the lowest bid at $219,247.00. Mr. Groth advised that this will be a
joint project with the Northern Kentucky Water District as they will be
replacing a water main and then the City will make the road improvements after
they complete their work which will be sometime after July 1.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to award the bid to TMS Construction in the amount of $219,247.00.
Council Member Bushong asked if the City Engineer checks the company’s
references or just recommend the lower bidder. Mr. Groth assured Council that
the engineer always check the references of the company’s bid before making a
recommendation to the City. He stated that the low bidder in this case is the
best bid as well. There being no further discussion, roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried.
Resolution No. 2011-R-02 – Authorizing a Lease Purchase Agreement with Fifth
Third Bank for the Purchase of Police Cruisers
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2011-R-02 that would approve
a lease-purchase agreement with Fifth Third Bank for the financing of the
acquisition of four new police vehicles. A brief discussion ensued. Police
Chief Butler advised they would purchase four Dodge vehicles at State bid
pricing and they would request that three or four of the older fleet vehicles
be declared as surplus property to be auctioned off. Mr. Deters read Resolution
No. 2011-R-02.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve Resolution No. 2011-R-02, seconded by
Council Member Brinker. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth announced that bids were received for installing an irrigation system
to two areas of Memorial Park. The two areas are the football/soccer field and
the playground. He said that last year’s draught has caused the areas to become
rutted which make the ground unsafe. He advised that several people came
together to discuss a solution and it was decided that topsoil, re-seeding and
an irrigation system would be a long-term solution. He stated that two bids
were received with the low bid from Malco Services at a total cost of
$26,198.66.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that this project would be taken out of the
amended budget and it would not be necessary to go into the reserve account. He
said it will be necessary to close the fields for a time to allow the new seed
to grow and the lawn area to get well established. He stated that he has
received calls from people that feel the City is kicking the teams off the ball
field, but the City is making improvements to the field for the safety of the
team players. He stated that the City is giving six months notice to the teams.
Dave Nolan, 1070 Oakgrove Ct. – stated he is a member of the South Kenton
Football. He stated the football league offered to do the repairs to the field
at no cost to the city. He stated that they met with the City in 2008 and
wanted a 5 year exclusive use commitment and in exchange they would haul in
topsoil and re-seed the field. Mayor Moriconi replied that he doesn’t remember
them offering the City money to make repairs to the field, but the City does
not want to restrict the use of the field to any one sport. Mr. Nolan stated
they offered to do the work not make a monetary donation to the City. Council
Member Franzen stated she didn’t want to see a clash with the Independence
Soccer league for use of the field. A lengthy discussion ensued. Mr. Nolan
expressed two additional concerns, the first being that he feels the football
league contributes to the success of the local restaurants during their season
and they will loose their business for four months if they need to practice
elsewhere. His other concern is about the $10/child fee the City will be
charging next year. He wanted to know why this fee will be charged. Mayor
Moriconi advised that the fee will help offset the cost of water to run the
sprinkler system. Mayor Moriconi stated the field will be closed this spring
and he discussed in detail the work that would be done to the two areas in the
park. He stated that after the work is complete that the areas would be
cordoned off until the lawn is well established. Council Member Yeager agreed
that she did not feel the City should provide exclusive use of the field to one
sport.
Further discussion centered on the $10/child fee to play on the field that
would take effect next year. Some residents expressed concern that this would
be burdensome to some families that have 2- children playing football.
Recreation Director Nita Brake commented that Independence Soccer leases a
county owned field in Mills Road Park on the condition they pay for all
maintenance including the monthly water bill which runs about $1,000 per month
during the summer and early fall months. Council Member Franzen commented that
Boone County charges $20/child and expressed some concern that $10/child per
season could be burdensome to families. Since football only has one season this
is not a problem, but soccer has two seasons. Council Member Little stated this
would involve some record keeping. Mayor Moriconi advised that this pay to play
fee was not a voting issue at this meeting and this could be re-visited at a
later date.
Award Bid for Memorial Park Irrigation System
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion on awarding the bid for the irrigation
system. Council Member Franzen so moved, seconded by Council Member Yeager.
Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried and the bid was
awarded to the low bidder, Malco Services.
City Administrator Report (continued) – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth announced that the Kenton County Spring Cleanup program is scheduled
for April 6, 7 and 8 from 8:00 a.m. until 6:00 p.m. Large items can be dropped
off at the Kenton County Public Works Dept on Independence Station Road.
Mr. Groth also announced that the Senior Center would be holding a fundraiser
at Skyline Chili on March 17th serving green spaghetti for St. Patrick’s Day.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report but requested an executive
session to discuss possible/pending litigation.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi – no report.
Executive Session
At 8 51 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to go into an executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss possible/pending litigation. The
motion was seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 9:05 p.m. Council Member Reinersman moved to reconvene the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 9:05 p.m.

COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of April 4, 2011
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 4,
2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters, City Administrator Dan
Groth and Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld.
Proclamation – Recognition of Military Careerist Rusty E. Mardis
Mayor Moriconi presented a Proclamation to the family of military careerist
Rusty E. Mardis commending Captain Mardis for his long military career in the
United States Air Force. Captain Mardis began his military service in 1990 and
is currently deployed in Kabul, Afghanistan serving in the War in Iraq.
Approval of the March 7, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, March 7, 2011. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Little . No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried.
Privileges of the Floor
Mark Sennet of Beckmark, Inc – addressed Council with a request to support a
zoning text amendment to add “automotive parts and accessories” as a permitted
use in the PUD zone. He stated he would like it to possibly include a fast food
restaurant with a drive up window. He said it would actually be two free
standing buildings, but this is a preliminary concept. Mr. Sennet advised
Council that he wants to commit to purchase the property in the PUD zone but
that AutoZone has to approve the site first. Council Member Bushong asked if he
would be the owner of the AutoZone. Mr. Sennet advised that he generally puts
the deals together, but he may retain ownership of the building and lease the
space. Council Member Franzen commented that the City is looking to add more
sit-down restaurants such as Applebee’s; not more fast food. Mr. Sennet advised
that not all restaurants are currently expanding. He stated he would like to
work with the City on other sites in the City. He stated he has done several
developments in the tri-state area. Council Member Bushong asked if he was
concerned that a new Advanced Auto was located in the same area that he is
proposing an AutoZone. Mr. Sennet did not seem concerned and responded that
competition keeps prices in check when there is a shared marketplace. Mayor
Moriconi asked the City’s Zoning Administrator for her thoughts on this
proposal. Mrs. Wuestefeld reported that the City’s current zoning excludes auto
service businesses in the PUD zone. She advised that if the zoning text is
changed to add this type of business as a permitted use in the PUD zone, this
change will still be required to submit a Stage II development plan to the
Planning Commission for approval. Council Member Little asked if this text
amendment would apply to all PUD zones. Mrs. Wuestefeld advised that it would
apply to all PUD zones and would still be required to go through a Stage I or
Stage II development plan review by the Planning Commission who would then make
a recommendation back to the City to approve or disapprove.
Resolution No. 2011-R-04 – Supporting a Text Amendment to Add “Automotive Parts
and Accessories” as a Permitted Use in the PUD Zones
There being no further discussion on Mr. Sennet’s request, Council Member

parts and accessories” as a permitted use in the PUD zone, seconded by Council

has accomplished some impressive projects and has a good track record.

May 2, 2011
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 2,
2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters, City Administrator Dan
Groth and Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld.
Approval of the April 4, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, April 4, 2011. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2011/2012 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would adopt a budget for the 2011/2012 fiscal year. He gave the ordinance
a first reading and commented that over $500,000 would be allocated to street
repairs and that later he would be seeking emergency road aid for repairs/major
improvements to some roads.
Cody Road – CDS Engineers to Present Repair/Rehab Options
Mayor Moriconi introduced Martin Hellmann with the City Engineer’s office who
presented to Council three options to permanently address the slide issue on
Cody Road. The options presented are as follows:
Option 1 – Roadway Relocation: Relocate the roadway to the south, parallel to
and just uphill from the existing road, between Upton and the railroad
underpass (approximately 1125 ft.). This will allow us to move the roadway out
of the slide area, and address sight distance and roadway width issues.
However, this option does not improve the flooding roadway or the geometry at
the railroad underpass. Additionally, this would require the City to purchase
additional right-of-way from the adjacent property owner. The cost to purchase
the necessary right-of-way is not included in the total project cost below.
Opinion of Probable Project Cost: $650,000.00
Option 2 – Drilled Shaft Wall: Construct approximately 550 ft. of drilled shaft
retaining wall along the north side of the existing roadway. The road would
remain on its current alignment at its current width. The wall could be
constructed within the existing right-of-way. This would address the landslide
problem, but would not address the flooding and sight distance concerns at the
railroad underpass, or the narrow roadway width and sight distance concerns
that currently exist along this section of Cody Road.
Opinion of Probable Project Cost: $480,000.00
Option 3 – Close Cody Road and Construct Cul-de-Sacs: Permanently close Cody
Road between Upton Drive and the Railroad underpass. A T-turnaround would be
constructed at the west end would be approximately 100 feet west of the
railroad underpass. A new section of driveway would be constructed to connect
the turnaround to the existing driveway at 5500 Cody Road. At the east end
Upton Drive would be used as a turnaround. The existing road would be
reconstructed and/or widened through the existing slide area up to Carole Anne,
where it would be maintained only as an access to Carole Anne. This section of
roadway would be shifted slightly to the south, but still within the right-of-
way, narrowed down to 16 feet wide and graded off to the north to provide a
more stable slope. With this option it will be crucial to provide adequate
signage to notify motorists of the roadway closure.
Opinion of Probable Project Cost: $125,000.00
After the options were explained by Mr. Hellmann, the floor was open for
discussion. Council Member Franzen asked if these repairs options would
guarantee no slides in the future. Mr. Hellmann responded that there would
always be that potential, but they would address the potential slide areas and
engineer it with an effort to avoid that potential. Mayor Moriconi commented he
will pursue emergency road aid for this project from the State, but it is
unknown how much the City could possibly obtain from that fund, if any. He
advised that FEMA funds don’t qualify for this but we will make a request on
the chance that it would. Council Member Reinersman asked if it was possible to
get emergency funds from the State again since we have been granted funds in
the past. Mr. Groth responded that we contribute to the fund each year which
would make us eligible so we will apply again. Council Member Brinker asked how
soon it would take to get a reply on the application for the emergency funds.
Mr. Groth stated it should be fairly quick.
Mayor Moriconi suggested installing a steel bridge under the railroad trestle
as part of this repair to Cody Road. He said it would be an additional cost of
approximately $86,000 and would be similar to the metal grate bridge recently
installed on Crowe Road. He advised the bridge would not stop the flooding in
this area but rebuild that portion of roadway under the railroad trestle.
At this time, Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to anyone who wanted to address
the Council about the Cody Road project.
Brad Jones, 1244 Cynthiana Court, Independence – voiced his request to keep
Cody Road open and not permanently close the road.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence – stated she feels that the City should
keep the road open as this road is used by the school busses. She also wondered
if the railroad (CSX) would have some liability.
Mayor Moriconi commented that he will be talking with the Kenton County
officials to request some road assistance for this project. He also responded
to Ms. Cook’s concern about CSX railroad liability. He said it was a valid
question, but didn’t know if they would have any liability in assisting the
City with this project.
Pat Dressman, 10366 Corinth Ct., Independence – asked Council to keep this road
open. She stated it is used all the time and would hate to see the west side of
the city cut off. She stated this would alienate those business, etc. She
stated she thought installing a bridge under the trestle would be a good idea
as well.
Greg Rehkamp, 10415 Lynchburg Drive, Independence – stated he was in favor of
keeping the road open. He stated there is fifty-three acres for sale for future
development and closing the road would hamper effort to build and bring in
future property taxes.
Further discussion among the Council centered on applying for emergency funds
with the State and which option to pursue. Mr. Hellman advised that option 1 or
2 were good long-term solutions.
Council Member Franzen moved to proceed with Option 1 for an estimated project
cost of $650,000 and to make application for State emergency road funds,
seconded by Council Member Reinersman. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Mayor Moriconi suggested pulling $86,000 from the reserve account to cover the
cost of the steel grate bridge under the railroad trestle.
He advised Council that a portion of Marshall Road that was fixed last year is
deteriorating again so that is an issue that will also need to be addressed.
Mr. Groth reported that he has met with Kenton County’s Emergency Management
Director and FEMA representatives. He stated they came out and inspected three
sections of Marshall Road and one section along Webster Road that need to be
fixed. FEMA program requires the City to make the repairs and then request
reimbursement. He stated that Mr. Cooper, Public Works Director, did a good job
compiling the information that FEMA needed to go ahead and get work done.
Council Member Bushong asked if the work could be done with in-house labor. Mr.
Groth stated that we could do concrete replacement but not blacktop; blacktop
work would have to be contracted out.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2011 Code of Ordinances Supplement – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
adopt the 2011-S-10 supplement to the Code of Ordinances as submitted by
American Legal Publishing Corporation. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Business License Regulations to Exempt Vendors
Participating in the Farmers Market – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Chapter 110 regulating the licensing of businesses by exempting vendors
participating in the Farmers’ Market. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Fence Regulations – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance for a zoning
text amendment that would override the recommendation of the Kenton County
Planning Commission (Number 2032R) thereby approving an amendment of the
regulations for fences, subject to restrictions, within the front yard of
residential properties. A brief discussion ensued about the height of the
fences and class 3 fences was removed. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first
reading with the amendment made on the floor.
Proposed Ordinance – Fireworks Regulations – 1st Reading

that would prohibit the storage for sale of any fireworks in any residential

could be considered permanent if it was in a location for a long time. There
being no further discussion Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading.

in Erlanger. He also announced a free forum looking at demographic and economic

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
June 6, 2011
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 6,
2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters, City Administrator Dan
Groth and Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld.

that would adopt the budget for the 2011/2012 fiscal year. City Attorney, Mr.

Yeager to adopt Ordinance No. 2011-O-09. There being no discussion roll was

Advance Auto Parts – Mike Nevil, General Manager

Parts store on the new section of SR17. Mr. Nevil announced to Council the
store would open on Monday with a grand opening at 11:00 a.m. on Thursday, June
16th. He invited everyone to attend. Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Nevil and
stated the City was excited to have Advance Auto Parts in Independence. Mr.
Nevil stated the store would employee ten people at this location. Mr. Groth
advised the new traffic signal at the intersection of SR17 and Centennial Blvd.
should be fully functioning by the opening of this store.
Approval of the May 2, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, May 2, 2011. Council Member Reinersman so moved, with
second by Council Member Brinker. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky – Tim Broering, Executive
Director
Mayor Moriconi welcomed the Telecommunications Board’s Executive Director, Tim
Broering. He reminded Council that during the budget discussions the topic came
up regarding the fees paid to the Telecommunications Board and what services
they provide for those fees. Mayor Moriconi stated Mr. Broering would explain
the function, role and value they provide the City for the fees paid to the
Board.
Mr. Broering distributed a copy of the franchise agreement that the Board
negotiates and manages for the City. He advised that the Board was established
and an interlocal agreement was adopted in 1980 between several cities for the
purpose of negotiating and administering the cable service agreements. He
stated this regional approach provided a cost savings to the cities as the
special legal counsel fees alone, to negotiate the franchise agreements
generally run over $100,000. He stated that negotiations is a long involved
process, taking as long as 3+ years to complete and involves community needs
assessments, holding public hearings and testing signal areas.
Mr. Broering advised Council that facilitating the monthly City meetings is
just one of the advantages of being a member of this interlocal agreement. He
stated the camera equipment in this room is provided by the Board and the Board
staff assisted with the purchase and installation of the other video equipment
in this room. Mr. Broering also advised the Board televises the City’s July 4th
events each year, recently televised the Memorial Day Oaks Re-dedication
ceremony, has installed a live line at the Senior Center, the Independence
Cemetery history piece and other special events like Clean-up America and a
salute to the troops and also provides live election coverage.
A discussion ensued with a question and answer period between Mr. Broering and
the Council. Mr. Bushong asked what other cities were part of the interlocal
agreement. Mr. Broering responded that most local cities were part of the
agreement except Erlanger, Florence, Walton and Union. In response to Council
Member Little’s question about cable versus satellite, he advised that cable
has 60-80% of the market while general satellite has about 13-20% of the
market. Council Member Yeager commented that the election coverage was lacking
as she couldn’t find the station for election results for the City. Mr.
Broering advised the results are on channel 16 every year. Mayor Moriconi
commented that it takes a long time for them to obtain the election results and
he volunteered to get those results to him quicker. Mr. Broering agreed that in
the past it has taken a long time to get the results from the clerk and he is
hoping the new clerk will release those results to him earlier in future
elections.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that in order to pull out of the interlocal
agreement it requires providing one year notice to the other member cities of
the agreement, so that would need to be done by June 30, 2011 in order to be
effective July 1, 2012. Mr. Broering commented that the City would realize a
savings just in the legal fees that would be expended for the negotiation of a
franchise agreement. He said the average cost for franchise negioation and
administration is approximately $80,000 per year with some years being higher.
Council Member Reinersman stated that with Cincinnati Bell now holding a
franchise in Northern Kentucky, as well as Insight Communications, there is now
two franchise agreements to negotiate. He also commented that his wife works in
the customer service department for Insight and knows firsthand how seriously
they take the agreement and what a valuable service they provide to this area.
Mr. Groth advised Council that the City receives approximately $165,000 in
telecommunications tax revenue each year of which the City pays $54,000 to the
Telecommunications Board for services. Mr. Broering commented that they lobbied
to get that tax passed.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Broering for all the good information and advised
him that he would let him know of any action the City would or would not take
on the interlocal agreement.
Resolution No. 2011-R-05 – Authorizing Homeland Security Grant Application for
Law Enforcement Protection Program Funds
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2011-R-05 authorizing the

Cody Road – Discussion Relating to Options to Repair or Close the Road Due to
Slippage
Mayor Moriconi reported that he recently met with representatives of Kenton
County Fiscal Court to discuss the deteriorating condition of Cody Road and
request some assistance from the County in repairing this road in an effort to
keep it open to traffic. He stated that the County said they could not help
financially but would assist the city with in-kind services. He advised Council
that the City has been awarded $100,000 in emergency road aid from the State so
we will move forward with some action; repairs or closing the road. Council
Member Brinker stated he was hoping more from the State and that he feels the
only option at this time would be to temporarily close the road and plan future
repairs to re-open it. He asked if the County’s offer of in-kind services
applied to any of the options Council would choose. Mr. Groth replied that it
did. Council Member Franzen stated she was in favor of keeping the road open
and expressed concern that postponing the needed repairs would cost even more
in five years. Council Member Little suggested a more detailed breakdown of the
costs to grade and move a section of the road. Mr. Groth stated that the best
solution would be to move the road out of the slippage area. Mayor Moriconi
commented that the retaining wall slid down and is a safety issue. Council
Member Franzen stated that drivers are already using it as a cut-through, so it
should be permanently closed to prevent this until such time as it can be
repaired.
Council discussed acquiring land from a resident in the area that would be used
to move a section of the road. The land is currently for sale and keeping the
road open would make the land more marketable. Council Member Yeager questioned
whether the City could afford this project, even with receiving $100,000 in
emergency road aid. Mayor Moriconi stated that the bids could come in lower
than the City Engineer’s estimated cost. Council Member Bushong asked about
exercising eminent domain to take the land needed to move the road. Mr. Deters
provided the legal procedures the City would have to abide by in exercising the
eminent domain process. Mayor Moriconi advised the City would need 1000+ feet
(less than an acre) of land.
There was a brief discussion about taking out a loan to fix the road. Council
Member Little commented that he felt the first step was to talk to the property
owner about acquiring a portion of their land. Council Member Reinersman
suggested the owner may be willing to give the City an easement or donate the
land. Mayor Moriconi agreed that we should first approach the owner about the
land and also check into borrowing money for the road repair/improvement. He
cautioned against taking funds from the reserve account that would take the
balance to an impractical low.
In closing the discussion, Council directed the City Administrator to contact
the property owner about acquiring a portion of their land to move the road,
check into some funding sources, discuss repair options with the City Engineer
and then determine if it will be necessary to take out a loan. Mayor Moriconi
commented that the interest rates have gone down since the last loan proposal
submitted in February of this year.
Independence Point Subdivision – Discussion About Developer Maintenance
A group of residents from the Independence Point Subdivision addressed Council
about the on-going maintenance violation of four lots, specifically high weeds
and grass, at the entrance of the subdivision and owned by the developer, Finke
Homes (aka Burlington Estates & aka G&T Excavation). Residents expressed their
frustration with the City’s violation process. Council Member Brinker commented
that it was the intent of Finke Homes to develop those lots, but they have not
been developed. Mayor Moriconi thanked the residents for coming and shared his
concerns as well with developers building nice monument signs at the entrance
to the subdivisions and when the subdivision is built out and they leave town
then the problems with maintenance begin for the City.
Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld explained the City’s violation process
is on a complaint basis only and that the property owners are given five days
from the time they receive the violation notice to get their grass cut. After
that time period, if the owner has not cut the grass, then the City can have it
mowed and file a lien on the property. She stated that Finke Homes did cut the
grass, but they did not do a very good job. She re-inspected the property and
advised they needed to cut it again. She stated the City mowed the area several
times last year. Mayor Moriconi commented that the excessive rains this year
have hampered the mowing schedule, so it has been a challenge to keep up.
There was some discussion about the entrance sign being in disrepair. Mayor
Moriconi advised he would have the City’s Public Works department inspect the
sign for repairs needed.
Council had a brief discussion regarding these chronic zoning violations and
adopting stricter regulations for habitual offenders by amending the nuisance
ordinance. Mr. Deters advised would review State laws and get with Ms.
Wuestefeld to propose an amendment to Council.
Ordinance No. 2011-O-10 – Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Fences in Front
Yards – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2011-O-10, that
would approve a zoning text amendment and would override the recommendation of
the Kenton County Planning Commission (Number 2032R) for an amendment of the
regulations for fences, subject to restrictions, within the front yard of
residential properties.
Mayor Moriconi stated he received an email from another property owner on Cody
Road with a similar issue regarding the placement of a fence in the front yard.
Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld advised that the Cody Road property is
actually a separate issue because Cody Road is not an arterial road. She
advised that if a parcel has more than five acres and has a horticultural use
then it would be eligible for a PVA exemption from zoning regulations. A
property with 10 acres that has an agricultural use can also be exempt from
zoning.
Recess

Ordinance No. 2011-O-10 – Zoning Text Amendment Relating to Fences in Front
Yards – 2nd Reading – (discussion continued)
Mayor Moriconi resumed the discussion regarding the second reading of Ordinance
No. 2011-O-10. Mr. Deters advised the proposed ordinance is to over-ride the
Kenton County Planning Commission’s recommendation which was to disapprove the
proposed text amendment.
A discussion ensued wherein Ms. Wuestefeld explained that the proposed text
amendment would allow a maximum height of six feet for class 2 and class 4
fences in the front yard, but only on arterial streets. She stated that hedges
are permitted in the front yards with a maximum height of thirty-six (36)
inches. Council Member Franzen suggested changing the maximum height to four
feet and wondered if that would require a new first reading of the ordinance.
Ms. Wuestefeld stated that if front yard fences were permitted then the Board
of Adjustment could allow a variance on a dimensional issue such as height of
the fence. She stated that the property owner on Richardson Road that is
requesting this text amendment has already been before the Board to obtain the
variance for the six foot fence on the rear and sides of his property, but it
was beyond the scope of the Board to allow a fence in the front yard.
Council Member Little advised the City has nine arterial State roads and that
approving this would not be for just one property but for all properties on
nine arterial roads in the City He stated he is not in favor of allowing fences
in the front yard. He stated he also feels restricting to acreage is unfair if
the parcel has adequate frontage. Council Member Reinersman commented that he
looked around the City and he feels this proposed text amendment could be
opening a door.
At this time, Council Member Franzen moved to have a second reading of
Ordinance No. 2011-O-10. The motion died for lack of a second. Council Members
suggested that the property owner requesting this text amendment consider
planting shrubs and tried to explain that it is difficult to pass legislation
as a solution for one situation.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 11,
2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Chris Reinersman and Donna Yeager. Council
Member Little was absent. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters and City
Administrator Dan Groth.
Presentation – Independence History Book, Gailen & Debbie Bridges
Mayor Moriconi welcomed Gailen and Debbie Bridges. He stated the Bridges’ have
completed their work on the Independence history book, which is now being
distributed. He stated it looks great. Mr. Bridges thanked everyone that
assisted with the creation of this book. He stated everyone was so supportive
of this effort which is a positive celebration of the City’s history. Mr.
Bridges commented that he hoped this book would express civic pride and be a
tool for economic prospects. He invited everyone to attend the formal
presentation of the book’s distribution which will be held on September 22,

stated he has provided a complimentary copy of the book to the City Clerk for

stores and that Walgreen’s has a supply of the books available as well.
Approval of the June 6, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular

Reinersman with no objection from the other members. Roll was called and

Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2004-O-15, Map Amendment Conditions
for Meadow Glen Subdivision – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would amend
Ordinance No. 2004-O-15 (relating to a zoning map amendment for the Meadow Glen
Subdivision) that would amend development condition number ten (10) requiring
the developer to make improvements to Webster Road in conjunction with the
development of the subdivision. He stated the developer will still make the
improvements to Webster Road, but would like to change the condition from being
half of the lots being developed to there being only fifty (50) lots remaining
to be developed in the subdivision. Mayor Moriconi stated that Mr. Jim Berling
was here to answer any questions they may have regarding this change.
Council Member Yeager asked how many lots were remaining. Mr. Berling advised
that 190 lots have been developed, which is close to the half way mark. He
stated the downturn in the economy has made it difficult to market the parcels
off of Webster Road but they continue to market from the model home off of
Independence Station Road. He stated they have 135 lots left to develop. He
stated they only built twelve houses in this subdivision last year, so at this
rate it could take some time to market the remaining lots, especially with so
much land available in Independence right now.
Council Member Reinersman advised that because he has done business recently
with Mr. Berling he would be abstaining from any action that Council would take
on this request. There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Award Bid – Historic Downtown Study, ISAC Recommendation
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that the City has received five RFP’s (Request
for Proposal) to conduct a Historic District Study of the downtown area. He
stated this project would be funded by the $7,000 donation the City received
from AT&T. He advised that four members of the ISAC Steering Committee have
unanimously selected to recommend that the study be performed by Taylor &
Taylor Associates out of Brookville, Pennsylvania in the amount of $6,750.
Council Member Reinersman advised that conducting this survey is an effort to
protect the downtown area and was recommended by the Kentucky Heritage Council.
He stated that he along with Dan Groth, John Richardson and Rodney Crice
reviewed the proposals received and agreed that Taylor and Taylor had the
qualifications they were looking for. Mr. Groth advised they looked at all the
qualifications of the companies and would like Council to approve their
recommendation to award the proposal to Taylor and Taylor based on this
company’s history of having performed similar surveys. He said the survey would
include forty properties in the downtown area between Independence Station Road
and Hartland Blvd. Council Member Brinker asked how long it would take to
conduct this survey. Mr. Groth advised it would take six months.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Reinersman moved to award the
proposal to conduct a Historic District survey to Taylor and Taylor Associates
in the amount of $6,750. Council Member Bushong seconded the motion. Roll was
called and answered unanimously; motion carried 5-0.
