Cody Road Update
Mayor Moriconi reported to Council that pursuant to the City’s request for
emergency funding for Cody Road repairs/improvements, the City has received
$100,000 from the Transportation Cabinet’s Municipal Road Aid cooperative
program. He advised that he and Dan Groth met with the listing agent (Mike
Parker of Huff Realty) for the property owner on Cody Road for which the City
would need to acquire land in order to bypass the slippage area on Cody Road.
He stated they discussed the City’s need for approximately 2.5-3 acres to make
the improvement to the road. He commented that he felt it was a good meeting
and the owner seems receptive to donating the land to the City. Mr. Groth
advised the realtor suggested moving just inside the current property line so
that a turn lane could be constructed. He stated that the City Engineer would
need to revise his estimates to accomplish this type of improvement. He said
the cost would probably be in the area of $250,000 - $300,000, which is quite a
bit of money, but it would be up to Council to make this decision.
Council Member Franzen expressed her concern that this was more expensive to
move the road over and asked if the property owner’s donation of land to the
City was contingent on construction of a turn lane. Mr. Groth stated he did not
know. Council Member Yeager stated there was still the issue of flooding under
the train trestle. Going back to the discussion of acquiring land from the
property owner, Council Member asked if they would deed over a permanent
easement. Mr. Deters advised it would not require a permanent easement as it
would become a dedicated city street and right of way.
Mayor Moriconi commented they have been given a verbal loan interest rate of
2.1% if Council was interested in taking out a loan to make these permanent
improvements to Cody Road. Council Member Reinersman stated that currently the
City Engineer’s estimates for repair/improvements are the best figures they
have to take action on. Council Member Bushong commented that it is difficult
to make a decision if we don’t have a firm project cost. Council Member Brinker
suggested that the next step would be to have the City Engineer submit an
updated proposal and then put the project out for bid. He stated that if the
bids come in too high and is unaffordable for the City then we can reject all
the bids. Council Member Bushong asked about getting some in-kind services from
the County road department. Mayor Moriconi commented that there are too many
unknowns right now for them to commit to in-kind services. He said we would
need scope of work specs, bids, etc. before that could be determined. He also
commented that three acres is a lot of land to move. Council Member Brinker
suggested the bid specs be broken down into alternate bids so that City and
County public works department employees could provide some of the labor.
Council Member Brinker asked that the City Engineer re-inspect the area and
make a cost estimate proposal for putting in a turn lane for the next Council
meeting. Council Member Franzen agreed that we need updated figures to
determine whether the City can afford to move the road over. She stated she
needs more info before considering borrowing money for these road improvements.
Mayor Moriconi advised he would set up some meetings to discuss what could be
done with in-house labor and what parts of the project would need to be
contracted out. Council Member Yeager suggested the City and County officials
meet first to discuss available labor and equipment they have in-house.
Council Member Bushong commented that at the opening of the discussion he had
the general feeling that if Council was going to make repairs to the road that
it would be done right. Mayor Moriconi said he may have made that comment at
the last meeting, but it was just his opinion that if the Council would decide
to make repairs then it should be lasting repairs and not just patched.
Council Member Franzen asked what the benefit would be to move the road. Mr.
Groth advised that by moving the road it would take it out of the slide area.
Council Member Yeager commented that was the City Engineer’s most expensive
option, with a project estimate of $640,000. Council Member Franzen commented
that the City Engineer said the road only needed to be moved a little – a few
feet – and if the other option is too expensive then the City needs to only
move it a little.
Mayor Moriconi commented that because of the flooding under the railroad
trestle, he struggles with whether or not the City should repair this road or
just permanently close it to through traffic. Council Member Franzen commented
that the area has only flooded six times in the last 8-9 years. Mayor Moriconi
advised that the Engineer’s cost estimates are hypothetical at this point.
Council Member Reinersman stated that he agrees with Council Member Franzen in
that he would like to find a way to keep Cody Road open to traffic, but he
feels there is not enough information being presented now to make that
decision. Mayor Moriconi stated he would get with the City Engineer for some
preliminary numbers. Council Member Franzen stated she remembers asking the
engineer at the meeting a few weeks ago if repairs were made to pier up the
slippage area if that would be a permanent fix. She recalled that the Engineer
stated that there was no guarantee that piering up one area would not cause a
slide in another area of the road.
Mr. Groth advised that the City Engineer would attend the next meeting of
Council to continue this discussion.
Public Questions and Comment
Brenda Chasteen, 1281 Victory Lane , Independence – addressed Council about the
overgrown grass on Flagstone Drive that is the entrance into the Independence

A brief discussion ensued. Mayor Moriconi commented that this economy has

5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi

Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters and City Administrator Dan
Groth.

Cody Road Proposal by City Engineer, CDS & Associates
Mayor Moriconi introduced City Engineer Mark Brueggemann who was present to re-
address the options submitted to Council at the May 2, 2011 meeting regarding a
permanent solution to the hill slide issue on Cody Road. The slippage area of
Cody Road has been closed since mid April. Mr. Brueggemann reviewed the options
being proposed as:
·   Option 1 – Roadway Relocation: This option would move the roadway out of
the slide area and improve the sight distance and roadway width issues. At a
probable project cost of $600,000 it is the most expensive option. The negative
issues with this option would be the purchase of addition right-of-way
acquisition, which is not included in the cost estimate and this option does
not address the flooding area or the geometry at the railroad underpass.
·   Option 2 – Drilled Shaft Wall: This would stabilize the current road within
the existing right-of-way by constructing approximately 550 ft. of drilled
shaft retaining wall. This option does not address sight distance problem or
flooding area under the railroad underpass. Probable cost estimate for this
option is $480,000.
·   Option 3 – Close the road permanently and construct cul-de-sacs: For
probable costs estimate of $125,000 this is the least expensive option. The
section to be closed is between Upton Drive and the railroad underpass. Then
construct a turn around to the existing driveway at 5500 Cody Road. This option
eliminates the need to solve the hill slide problem and it also addresses the
flood problem area and eliminates the safety problem of sight distance due to
geometrics.
Mr. Brueggemann stated that both the police and fire departments have provided
written statements stating that the closure of this section of Cody Road will
not have an adverse effect on response time for emergency services they provide
the City residents. He stated since Option 1 and Option 2 do not address all
the issues it would be his recommendation to close the road as it is the most
economical solution for the City and it addresses all the safety issues.
Mr. Groth advised Council that he, along with the Public Works Director and
Crew Leader met with the County Public Works Department and the bottom line is
that the County nor the City has the necessary heavy equipment needed to move
20,000 yards of debris and dirt to move the road. Danny Koch, Public Works Crew
Leader commented the flood gates had to be raised several times each year due
to heavy rains. He stated he agrees that the most logical thing for the City to
do would be to close this section of Cody Road permanently.
Mayor Moriconi commented that it might not have to be closed permanently if the
adjacent property is developed in the future. Mr. Groth stated the City has
received $100,000 in emergency road aid from the Kentucky Transportation
Department which could be used to close the road. Mr. Brueggemann advised that
the opinion of probable costs were based without sending out survey crews, so
it is possible that the costs could come in lower than their projections.
Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum Road, Independence – stated he thinks the City should
fix the road and keep it open. He expressed concern that some residents would
have restricted access. Mayor Moriconi assured everyone that the City cannot
cut off access to their property.
Dorsey Chasteen, 1281 Victory, Independence - stated the alternate route of
taking Independence Station Road adds another 1.5 miles. He expressed concerns
that the school busses are crossing the railroad tracks.
Mayor Moriconi stated that the cost of Option 1 is too great and questioned how
the City would pay for this. He stated he is not comfortable taking this amount
of money from the City’s reserve fund which would take that fund below what is
recommended to keep the City fiscally responsible and in keeping with
government accounting standards.
Council Member Reinersman commented that if the City would opt to fix the road,
while it makes sense to go with Option 1 and do it right, the probable cost
estimate exceeds the City’s entire annual road repair budget to fix one street.
He stated that even if the City fixes the slippage there is still the problem
of flooding and railroad trestle.
Mayor Moriconi addressed Mr. Chasteen’s concern about the school buses by
advising that the Kenton County School District is okay with the road closure.
Mr. Koch commented that the school buses have been traveling Bristow Road as a
safer, alternate route.
Council Member Bushong stated that he agreed the City could not reasonably
afford to repair the slippage on Cody Road. He made a motion to accept the City
Engineer’s recommendation to close the road using the $100,000 emergency road
aid provided by the Kentucky Transportation Department and authorize the city
attorney to initiate the necessary proceedings to close the road. The motion
was seconded by Council Member Reinersman.
Further discussion ensued. A member of the audience asked about using the
County’s equipment. The Mayor explained that initially the County offered to
assist the City with in-kind services of labor and equipment before learning
the magnitude of the project. Council Member Brinker commented that he would
like to keep the road open but the cost is making it prohibitive and there is
not enough support from the community asking the City not to close the road.
Margaret Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence – suggested the road be closed for
now and then re-open when the area is developed. Council Member Franzen stated
she would like to explore other options to keep the road open.
Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum, Independence – suggested holding a public hearing to
get input from the citizens. Mayor Moriconi commented that everyone that would
attend a public hearing would be the proponents for keeping the road open and
if the City would decide to keep it open then the City still has the dilemma of
how to pay for the repairs.
City Attorney, Mr. Deters advised that in order for the City to close the road,
all those affected would have to give their consent. He stated that anyone who
wants to challenge this would get a hearing before the district court judge.
Mr. Deters stated that the road is currently closed under a temporary order by
the Police Department. He stated they have that authority to provide safety to
the citizens.
Council Member Franzen suggested that additional right-of-way that would be
needed for Option 1 might be donated to the City by the property owners. Mr.
Groth stated the owners realtor suggested this might be a possibility but that
the owners would want a turn lane constructed in exchange for the donated land.
He stated this would still be very costly. Council Member Little asked if there
have been any major issues or problems or concerns from the School Board since
the road was closed four months ago. Mr. Groth stated he had one inquiry from
the Post Office wanting to know when the road would be re-opened, but no calls
from the schools. Council Member Franzen commented that she doesn’t think the
residents of Troopers Crossing and Battle Ridge subdivisions are aware the City
is discussing a permanent closure of the road and she feels certain they would
like to have it remain open.
There was a brief discussion on ways to finance the road repairs in order to
keep the road open. The Mayor said that $200,000 could be taken from the
reserve fund. There was also the $100,000 received from the State emergency
road aid. Mayor Moriconi wondered if the railroad would have any culpability to
help the City pay for the road repairs to keep it open as the vibrations to the
ground area from the passing trains may have contributed to the road slippage.
Mayor Moriconi stated there was a motion and second on the floor (Bushong/
Reinersman) to select Option 3 as submitted and recommended by the City
Engineer to close Cody Road. Council Member Reinersman suggested the City could
re-open the road in the future. Mr. Deters advised that when a road is closed
the land reverts to the owners on either side of the road, so if the City
should decide in the future to re-open the road they would need to reacquire
the land from the property owners. Council Member Reinersman asked if the City
had any other options. Mr. Deters advised it could be kept closed temporarily.
Jim Berling, developer of Troopers Crossing, stated he would like to see the
road kept open. He stated he still owns 4-5 acres on the other side of Upton
Drive and he would be happy to take a look at this and see if there is
something they could work on jointly with the City. Council Member Reinersman
commented that the land in this area will be more appealing to developers if
the road is open. Council Member Little commented that if the road is closed
the right-of-way will go to the railroad and if the railroad would ever change
the bridge structure then the city would never be able to re-open that section
of Cody Road. Council Member Reinersman stated that up till now all his
opinions were predicated on the possibility of re-opening the road some day.
There being no further discussion, roll was called which resulted in a tie
vote; three ayes were cast by Council Members Bushong, Little and Yeager and
three nays were cast from Council Members Reinersman, Brinker and Franzen.
Mayor Moriconi cast the tie breaking vote by voting in favor of the road
closure. Motion carried 4-3. Mayor Moriconi commented that while he would like
to see the road kept open he does not know how the City can pay for it.
Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth stated he did not have anything to report.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that he has provided them a copy of the Kenton
County Mayor’s Group Subdivision Regulation Review Committee recommendations
for the proposed update of the Kenton County Subdivision Regulations. He stated
the proposed changes would require developers to construct roadways with
thicker concrete, drain tiles, etc. Mr. Groth advised that the goal is to
finalize the new regulations in a couple of months and have in place by late
fall of this year. Mayor Moriconi advised this is just a draft copy of the
proposed recommendations. He stated we deal with a lot of concrete and blacktop
street failures and these proposed regulations should lengthen the life of new
streets. Council Member Bushong asked if the City had any recourse. Mayor
Moriconi stated the City has to object to any deficiencies within 45 days of
the inspection and after that time we have no recourse.
Brenda Chasteen, 1281 Victory Lane, Independence – stated the grass problem
continues at the entrance to the Independence Pointe subdivision off Cody Road.
She said it was cut today, but the area was not trimmed. Council Member Franzen
commented that a group of them met last week to work on a document that would
allow the City to deal with the chronic offenders of the zoning laws. She
stated they are trying to work something out but the City has to keep in line
with the state law as well. Mayor Moriconi stated the City is limited on what
can be legally done so we are doing due diligence to draft something that will
hold up. Council Member Little stated he feels we have worked out a resolution
that will deal with the chronic violators. Mayor Moriconi stated he hopes to
have something to present to Council at the next meeting.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the

August 29, 2011
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August
29, 2011 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters. City Administrator
Dan Groth was absent.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone and announced this Special meeting of Council
was being held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
·   Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Property Tax Rates for 2011 – 1st Reading
·   Award Bid – Mid-Size Dump Truck for the Public Works Department
·   Award Bid – Drilling & Placement of Rails for Marshall & Webster Roads
·   Declare Surplus Property – List of Vehicles & Miscellaneous Property
·   Resolution No. 2011-R-08 Supporting a Planning Grant Application with NKAPC
as Co-Applicant
·   Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Code Enforcement by Allowing Issuance of a
Citation without First Issuing a Notice of Violation – 1st Reading
·   Cody Road Information
·   Executive Session (only if necessary)
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Property Tax Rates for 2011 – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
adopt the 2011 real estate and personal property tax rates using the
compensating rates that have been calculated by the Area Development District
(NKADD) and confirmed by the City’s Finance Director. The proposed compensating
rates are .224/$100 of assessed value for real estate property and .737/$100 of
assessed value for personal property. Mayor Moriconi opened the floor for
discussion.
Council Member Little stated he took information from the calculation sheets
prepared by the City’s Finance Director and condensed the information down. He
distributed to the Council Members documents he prepared that illustrated the
current (2011) property values times last year’s tax rate of .200/$100 of
assessed value which would generate additional revenue of $102,584. He stated
the assessed property values increased $12,000,000 over last year. He stated
that this is a 2011-12 budget shortfall of about $168,678 and that in order to
collect enough revenue to fund the budget passed in June the City would need to
adopt a higher rate than .200/$100. Mayor Moriconi commented that he was
surprised to see the property assessments increased over last year.
Council Member Bushong stated he thought the budget was based on increasing the
payroll tax to 1.5% (up from 1.25%) and questioned how the revenue was
estimated. Mayor Moriconi explained that the budget was based on the assumption
that there would be an adjustment of the property tax rates or the payroll tax
rate. Council Member Little stated it is hard to guess at the exact revenue
when the City doesn’t have the assessed values at the time the budget is
prepared. The Mayor said the budget projections for the payroll revenue were
based on the current payroll tax rate which brought in $1,800,000 last year.
Mayor Moriconi stated in preparing the budget the assumption was that the
Council would adopt the compensating property tax rate not increasing the
payroll tax rate. Council Member Bushong wondered if some of the figures were
overestimated. Mayor Moriconi stated that since Council did not favor taking
out a loan for needed street repairs, that he chose to propose an aggressive
budget for street repairs. Council Member Reinersman agreed that the 2011-12
budget provided a significant increase in street repairs.
Mayor Moriconi stated he appreciated the good information compiled by Council
Members Little and Reinersman with the tax calculations and chart comparing
Independence to other cities. He stated that by holding the property tax rate
the same the last couple years it is starting to have a backward effect and
hindering the City’s ability to keep up with inflation as many expenses
continue to rise such as insurance and utilities. He stated it is becoming
unsustainable to keep the same tax rate and the City will have to dip into the
reserve account just to make ends meet.
Council Member Little also provided projections on tax revenue that could be
generated if the City would opt to increase the payroll tax. He stated since it
would not take effect until January 1st it would only benefit six months of
this budget which would not make up for the shortfall in revenue. Council
Member Reinersman expressed concern in raising the payroll tax rate as he feels
it would be a detriment in attracting new business to the City at a time when
we are trying to focus on economic development. He stated he would not be in
favor of a payroll tax increase.
Council Member Little stated that taking the proposed real property
compensating rate of .224/$100 would yield $350,412 in revenue. In an exhibit
he provided to Council he indicated that this City’s real estate tax rate is on
the lower end in comparison to other cities in Northern Kentucky while our
tangible (personal) property tax rate is much higher that other cities. Council
Member Reinersman suggested adjusting the property tax rate and leaving the
tangible tax rate the same as last year at .596/$100 of assessed value. Council
Members Little and Franzen concurred. Council Member Franzen suggested keeping
both tax rates the same as last year and then making up the shortfall next year
when the economy improves.
A discussion ensued on a property tax rate that would fund the budget adopted
in June. Mayor Moriconi suggested half of the compensating rate which would be
.212/$100. Council Member Little commented so much depends on how the budget
expenses are going so far this year. Mayor Moriconi commented that one of his
concerns is the unknown amount that could be spent on snow/ice removal during
the winter months.
Margaret Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence – commented that if a resident can’t
afford an additional $28-$30 per year in property tax increase then perhaps
they can’t really afford to own property. She stated she feels the City has
done a wonderful job on the budget and the City is not in debt except for the
Municipal Center building. She stated she did not want to see the City slide
backward by not raising the revenue needed.
Council Member Brinker wondered how the tangible tax rate was so much higher
than other cities. Mayor Moriconi stated the rate builds over time. Council
Member Brinker asked Mayor Moriconi how he would use the additional revenue if
Council would take the compensating rate. Mayor Moriconi advised his preference
would be to use any additional revenue on repairs and maintenance of the
streets.
Council Member Little commented that the City has not taken the compensating
rate for the last two years and over all the rate has remained pretty steady
for the last six years. Mayor Moriconi again commented that the 2011-12 budget
was based on assumptions of increased revenue and prior history of revenue and
expenses. Further discussion centered on a property tax rate that would be mid-
way between last year’s rate of .200/$100 and this year’s compensating rate of
.224/$100. Council Member Little suggested a real property rate of .210/$100
would provide enough revenue to balance the budget without tapping into the
reserve fund.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt a real estate tax rate of .215/$100 of
assessed value and a tangible (personal) property rate of .596/$100 (same as
2010), seconded by Council Member Reinersman. Council Member Franzen commented
that she didn’t expect the assessed values would come in as high as they did.
Mayor Moriconi stated that we don’t usually take a roll call vote on a first
reading, but he would like to see if a majority of Council agrees with these
rates before a second reading at the next meeting. The Clerk called the roll
and it was answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0. Mr. Deters gave a first
reading of the proposed ordinance to adopt the tax rates as stated in the
motion by Council Member Yeager. Mayor Moriconi advised the ordinance would be
presented for a second reading and adoption at the September 12th meeting.
Award Bid – Mid-Size Dump Truck for the Public Works Department
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council three bids that were received for the
purchase of a midsize dump truck. He stated that the Public Services Director
has recommended the bid be awarded to Peterbilt of Cincinnati in the amount of
$58,664.06. Council Member Little stated he spoke with the Public Services
Director who advised that the Peterbilt dealer attended the bid opening and has
been very responsive in answering questions and because of this service feels
this is the best bid. He stated there is only a $300 difference between the
Peterbilt bid and the low bid from Woody Sander Ford.
Council member Yeager moved to award the bid for the purchase of a mid-size
dump truck to Peterbilt of Cincinnati in the amount of $58,664.06, seconded by
Council Member Brinker. There being no further discussion, roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.

Declare Surplus Property – Vehicles and Miscellaneous Items to be Auctioned
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a list of City property that staff is
recommending to be declared as surplus so that these items can be included in
the Kenton County auction to be held on September 17, 2011. He stated the list
includes seven old model cruisers dating between 2000 and 2002 and about twenty
miscellaneous items. He stated the miscellaneous items include portable
heaters, wrist watches, MP3 player, portable game system, CD player, speakers
sets, etc. Police Captain Tony Lucas advised the miscellaneous list is

Council Member Little moved to declare the vehicles and miscellaneous list as

Resolution No. 2011-R-08 – Supporting a Planning Grant Application with NKAPC
as Co-Applicant
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a Resolution that would support an
application for the U.S. Department of Housing and Urban Development’s fiscal
year 2011 Community Challenge Planning Grant Program as a co-applicant with the
Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission (NKAPC). This program will aid in
the exploration of design and economic feasibility of redevelopment for focused
areas within the City. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2011-R-08.
A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Reinersman stated this is a new grant
possibility that would provide federal dollars to regional and local planning.
He stated that NKAPC staff has been working with the City’s Steering Committee
on an update to the City’s zoning code and the NKAPC staff will write the
grant. Council Member Bushong asked if this was a matching grant. Council
Member Reinersman stated the City’s match would be 20% which could be with in-
kind services. Council Member Yeager asked the total grant amount. Council
Member Reinersman replied that the total grant amount would be in the ball park
of $400,000-$500,000. He said the deadline for the grant application is Friday,
September 9, 2011. He went on to say that considering the brief time frame they
had to work within; the NKAPC staff compiled some approximate figures. Council
Member Yeager expressed some concern at not having some concrete figures
regarding the City’s share of the grant. Council Member Franzen suggested the
City could refuse the grant if it was awarded and the 20% exceeded the City’s
budget. Council Member Yeager advised that anytime a grant is awarded and
refused it can have a detrimental effect on future grant applications/awards.
Council Member Reinersman commented he understands and shares the concerns
about such an open-ended proposal.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve Resolution No. 2011-R-08, seconded by
Council Member Reinersman. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one
no vote cast by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried 5-1. Mayor Moriconi
advised Council he would get more clarity on this grant application and report
back at the next meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Code Enforcement by Allowing Issuance of a
Citation without First Issuing a Notice of Violation – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Section 39.09 of the City’s Code of Ordinances by allowing a code
enforcement officer to issue a citation without first issuing a notice of
violation. Mayor Moriconi stated this amendment would be a way to better deal
with the chronic violators. Council Member Little commented that he feels this
amendment will give the City’s code enforcement officer more muscle. There
being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Cody Road Information

September 12, 2011
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
12, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters and City
Administrator Dan Groth.
Approval of the August 1 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, August 1, 2011. Council Member Reinersman so moved,
with second by Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Approval of the August 29, 2011 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the Special
meeting held on Monday, August 29, 2011. Council Member Yeager so moved, with
second by Council Member Little. One amendment was presented without objection
by Council Member Little; roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2011-O-16 – Adopt Rates for 2011 Real & Personal Property Taxes –
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2011-O-16 that
would adopt the 2011 property tax rates for real estate and personal property.
Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2011-O-16 establishing the ad valorem tax on real
estate property at $0.215 dollars for each one hundred dollars ($100.00) of
assessed value and a personal property tax rate of $0.596 dollars for each one
hundred dollars ($100.00).
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2011-O-16, seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
6-0.
Ordinance No. 2011-O-17 – Relating to Code Enforcement by Allowing Issuance of
a Citation without First Issuing a Notice of Violation – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2011-O-17 that
would allow a code enforcement officer to issue a citation without first
issuing a notice of violation. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a second reading.
There being no discussion, Council Member Little moved to adopt Ordinance No.
2011-O-17 seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Allowing for Temporary Off-Site Vehicular Sales or Display
Events by Dealers – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration a proposed
ordinance that would allow for temporary off side vehicular sales or display
events by dealers.
Mr. Groth advised Council that the City has been approached by a dealer
representative who would like to have a “tent” sale to sell cars in the Towne
Center by Kroger’s. He stated that our current zoning regulations do not allow
tent sales. Council Member Reinersman asked if this would be for a single
event. Zoning Administrator, Annie Wuestefeld stated it could be more
than one event, but only if the City adopts this proposed ordinance. Mr. Deters
advised that the vehicle dealers also have to hold a State license in order to
have these special sales events. Ms. Wuestefeld advised that the City’s zoning
regulations do not allow car sales or tent sales. A brief discussion ensued
with regard to zones these events would be permitted in and the time frame for
each event. Mr. Deters stated he thinks that the length of each event is
stipulated in the KAR (Kentucky Administrative Regulations). Council Member
Reinersman suggested limiting the number of events that a dealer could hold
each year.
Council Member Brinker suggested tabling any action on this proposed ordinance
until more information could be obtained. Mr. Groth stated he would check with
the City of Florence to see how they handle this type of outdoor/tent sales.
Mr. Deters stated he would get a copy of the KAR. Ms. Wuestefeld stated the big
difference between Independence and some other cities, like Florence, is that
most other cities allow outdoor sales and/or permit auto sales in some of their
zones. She stated the dealer has State regulations to follow and has to submit
an application – a 45-day time period – to get approval. Mr. Deters commented
the dealer would not have time to have a sale event in this calendar year.
Mayor Moriconi suggested obtaining a copy of regulations imposed by other
communities, such as Florence and Campbell County, and present more information
on this at the October 3rd meeting.
Resolution No. 2011-R-09 – Adopting a Military Group – Ky National Guard, 1204
Aviation Group
Mayor Moriconi reported that the City has been approached with a request to
adopt a military unit – Kentucky National Guard, 1204 Aviation Group. He
advised a Resolution is being presented for their consideration in adopting
this unit. Mayor Moriconi stated the City will solicit corporate sponsors to
pay the shipping costs of care packages sent to the soldiers. Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2011-R-09. Mr. Groth advised the unit has just been deployed and
is currently stationed in Fort Hood before going overseas.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Yeager to adopt Resolution No. 2011-R-09. Roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried.
Resolution No. 2011-R-10 – In Support of First Responders & Honoring the 10th
Anniversary of 9/11
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2011-R-10 in support of
first responders and honoring the tenth anniversary of the terrorist attacks on
the United States on September 11, 2001. He reported that he read this
Resolution at yesterday’s Patriot Day memorial service held at the Senior
Center. He stated a good crowd attended the service. Mayor Moriconi read
Resolution No. 2011-R-10.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Little to adopt Resolution No. 2011-R-10. Roll was called and answered
unanimously; motion carried.
Declare Surplus Property – Fleet Vehicle to be Auctioned
Mayor Moriconi reported that at the last meeting of Council several City
vehicles were declared as surplus property and were scheduled to be auctioned

Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi

Cody Road Update – Mayor Moriconi reported that a local developer has
approached the City with a proposal to reconstruct the section of Cody Road
where the slippage occurred. The developer will work with the abutting property
owner to acquire the needed land for the road work. He reported that he met
with the engineers to discuss the realignment of the road, constructing a
shoulder area and installing drainage pipes. Mayor Moriconi advised that the
developer would handle this project, acquire the needed land and once the
roadway is finished would then turn back to the City for $300,000. He stated
this cost is half the original estimate the City received to realign the road
and make the necessary repairs. A brief discussion ensued. Mayor Moriconi
stated the reconstruction would involve the entire slippage area. He presented
to Council a proposed purchase agreement with Jim Berling wherein both parties
agree that the improvements shall be constructed according to plans and
specifications approved by the City Engineer and wherein the City agrees to
purchase the improved right-of-way in the amount of $300,000 when the project
is completed.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to authorize the Mayor to enter into the
purchase agreement with Jim Berling for the construction of a new and relocated
right-of-way on Cody Road. The motion was seconded by Council Member Yeager.
Roll was called and answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.

the meeting ended at 7:34 p.m.

October 3, 2011
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
3, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman
and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters and City
Administrator Dan Groth. Mayor Moriconi advised Council that Council Member
Bushong had an excused absence from tonight’s meeting.
Proclamation – Recognition of Veterans Day
Mayor Moriconi proclaimed the week of November 6 through November 12, 2011 as a
week-long celebration honoring all veterans and urging the community to honor
the dedicated men and women who currently serve or have served in defense of
the United States.
Approval of the September12, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, September 12, 2011. Council Member Yeager so moved,
with second by Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted; roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Allowing for Temporary Off-Site Vehicular Sales by Auto
Dealers – 1st reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
allow for temporary off-site vehicular sales or vehicular display events by
dealers in the NSC (Neighborhood Shopping Center) zones. He reminded Council
this was first presented at last month’s meeting and action was postponed. He
stated the ordinance has been revised to include the concerns discussed last
month.
Council Member Reinersman stated he would like the schools to be included in
allowable zones. Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld stated that schools are
considered a conditional use in the R1-C zones and the R1-C zone would need to
be added to this ordinance to allow the schools to hold car display events. A
brief discussion ensued with Ms. Wuestefeld responding to Council’s questions.
Ms. Wuestefeld responded that the property owner would be the applicant to hold
this type of temporary sale on their property – not the vehicular dealer – and
a stipulation in the City ordinance is that each location could only hold this
type of sale no more than three times each year. She stated that KAR
regulations allow each event to be held a maximum of five days. She stated the
City ordinance would require the dealer to obtain a permit for the off-site-
sale with a site plan attached to the permit application. Ms. Wuestefeld also
advised that the City only has two locations that would have adequate parking
for these types of events; being the Independence Towne Center and the Cherokee
Shopping Center.
There being no further questions or discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Text Amendment to the Flood Plain Regulations
– 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve a text amendment to the City’s zoning ordinance amending the flood
plain regulations for the City. Mrs. Wuestefeld advised Council that this text
amendment is in keeping with current State regulations. She stated that the
NKAPC noticed inconsistencies in the current flood plain regulations and
submitted the proposed changes. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading. He commented that this proposed ordinance will abolish the current
regulations and adopt the new regulations pursuant to Kentucky law.
Resolution No. 2011-R-11 – Authorizing Mayor’s Group to Donate the City’s
Portion of Funds to the Upkeep of the Kenton County 9/11 Memorial
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2011-R-11 that would
authorize the Kenton County Mayor’s Group to donate the City portion of the
checking account funds to the upkeep of the Kenton County 9/11 Memorial.
He explained that the Mayor’s Group opened this checking account many years ago
in anticipation of needing funds to fight a consolidation proposal by the
County. He stated the Mayor’s Group has decided to close this inactive bank
account and discussed options to disperse the funds. He stated that each City
would only be refunded approximately $34.00. After some discussion at the
Mayor’s Group meeting a motion was made to donate the money to the new Kenton
County 9/11 Memorial located in Veterans Park in Crescent Springs. He advised
Council that each City is being asked to approve this donation.
Council Member Franzen moved to approve Resolution No. 2011-R-11 authorizing
the Kenton County Mayor’s Group to donate the City’s portion of the bank funds
to the upkeep of the Kenton County 9/11 Memorial. The motion was seconded by
Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
5-0.

Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi

November 7, 2011
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, November
7, 2011 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Bushong gave an invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Jim
Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna Yeager. Also
present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters and City Administrator Dan Groth.
Captain Rusty E. Mardis, U.S. Air Force
Mayor Moriconi introduced and welcomed United States Air Force Captain Rusty E.
Mardis. Captain Mardis thanked Mayor Moriconi and Council for the Proclamation
he received from the City in April in recognition of his military service to
this country. He stated he was very appreciative of this Proclamation, sent a
letter to the City and advised that when he was back in the States he would
come to a meeting to personally thank everyone. Captain Mardis stated the
City’s token of recognition of his military career was greatly appreciated by
him and his family. He stated that he bragged about receiving this Proclamation
to his military friends while stationed in Afghanistan and they were shocked
that the City extended this honor. Captain Mardis presented the City with an
American flag that was flown in Afghanistan, which represents all the men and
women serving this country. Mayor Moriconi thanked Captain Mardis for his
service and the gift to the City.
Comprehensive Plan Update – Jenna Haverkos, NKAPC & Maura Snyder, KCPC City
Representative
Mayor Moriconi introduced Jenna Haverkos, Principal Planner with the Northern
Kentucky Area Planning Commission and Maura Snyder who serves as the City’s
representative on the Kenton County Planning Commission. He stated they will
present information on the county-wide Comprehensive Plan Update. Mayor
Moriconi advised that updating the Comprehensive Plan is a lengthy process and
will take approximately 1-2 years. Ms. Snyder advised Council on the important
reasons for the new Comprehensive Plan which is being called “Direction 2030.”
She stated the new Plan will be a twenty year vision for land use, housing and
transportation needs. She stated that heavy emphasis will be on obtaining
public input. She encouraged participation in the process by attending one or
more of the three rounds of public meetings that will be held at various
locations throughout the county. Ms. Snyder asked the Council Members and Mayor
to share their ideas and vision for the next twenty years. Ms. Haverkos stated
this round of public meetings is a separate process from the City’s current
committee meetings regarding the zoning update meeting that will be held on
November 14, 2011.
There was a brief question and answer session, wherein Ms. Haverkos explained
that the Comprehensive Plan is updated every five years and that “Direction
2030” will create a new vision for the Comprehensive Plan. Mayor Moriconi
advised that basically the Comprehensive Plan will be completely overhauled
with a new foundation for a twenty year vision that will then be updated every
five years. Ms. Haverkos advised that the foundation of the current
Comprehensive Plan originated in the 1970’s and that “Direction 2030” will
establish a whole new vision for the county. Mayor Moriconi advised Council
that NKAPC will periodically provide updates during this process. He stated the
second round of public meetings will be after the first of the New Year. Ms.
Haverkos also advised current information on this process can be obtained on
the Planning Commission’s website as it will be updated often.
Approval of the October 3, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, October 3, 2011. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Reinersman. No amendments were noted; roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.

Resolution No. 2011-R-12 – Approving the Transfer of Control of Insight
Communications, Inc. to Time Warner Cable, Inc.
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2011-R-12 that would approve
the transfer of control of Insight communications, Inc. to Time Warner Cable,
Inc. He introduced Dave Millward who serves as the City’s representative on the
Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky (TBNK). Mr. Millward advised
Council that he has served on the Board for the past eight years and is
currently the Chairman. He advised that Insight has held the cable franchise in
Northern Kentucky since 1997 and the Board has been in the process of
negotiating the contract renewal for the past three years which should be
finalized in the next few days.. He stated that Time Warner Cable announced the
purchase of Insight and since Time Warner is the fourth largest cable company

Council Member Yeager asked Mr. Millward if he would recommend the City approve

Authorize Revised Interlocal Agreement with Kenton County for Animal Control
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a revised interlocal agreement with Kenton
County for animal control services.
City Administrator, Dan Groth advised Council that the original agreement was
entered into ten years ago. He stated the proposed agreement has two major
revisions. He advised that the rate would stay the same but would be based on
the most current census population and given the City’s population increased in
2010 that will produce a significant increase in the fees the City will pay the
County for this service. The City will go from $22,000 per year to $33,000
which he feels is still a good deal since a vast majority of calls for animal
control service are being provided to Independence. Mr. Groth advised this
increase will be adjusted in next year’s budget. He stated the other revision
in this agreement will be that the City of Covington will be joining in along
with the other seventeen (17) cities.
Council Member Bushong asked how many animal control officers the County has on
staff. Mr. Groth advised the County has a total of four officers with two
officers on each shift. He stated that Covington will be funding a fifth
officer. Mayor Moriconi reported that Independence has twenty-eight percent
(28%) of all calls received by the County’s animal control department. Mr.
Groth stated that Independence had over nine hundred (900) calls last year and
one-third of those calls resulted with the animal being taken in. Council
Member Franzen asked if it would be necessary to amend the City’s current
budget. Mr. Groth stated it would not be necessary since this agreement would
take effect on July 1, 2012.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Bushong moved to approve the
proposed interlocal agreement and authorize the Mayor to sign the agreement,
seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously;
motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2011-R-13 – Authorize Lease-Purchase Agreement with Huntington
Bank for Police Cruisers
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2011-R-13 that would approve
a lease in the amount of $70,000 with Huntington National Bank to finance the
acquisition of three police cruisers. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2011-R-13.
Council Member Reinersman moved to adopt Resolution No.2011-R-13, seconded by

Proposed Ordinance – Requiring Annexation of Real Estate into City Prior to
being Permitted Access to a City Street – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration a proposed
ordinance that would require annexation prior to being granted access to any
City street or right-of-way. He stated this proposed ordinance is the result of
a request by an owner of real estate in an unincorporated area that abuts
parcels in the Williams Woods subdivision. The owner would like to access
Gatewood Drive. Mr. Deters advised the City has a similar ordinance regarding
sewer tap-ins. Council Member Little commented that even though this proposed

entire City. Council Member Reinersman asked if the City would be able to
review each request, on a case by case basis, as it pertains to specific issues
and what would be needed to accommodate specific access. Mr. Deters responded
that the specifics would be addressed under the subdivision regulations.
There being no further discussion Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.

Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.

2012 Minutes
January 9, 2012
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
9, 2012 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the December 5, 2011 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, December 5, 2011. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Yeager. Council Member Reinersman requested amendments
on page two; with no objections from Council, roll was called and answered
unanimously to adopt the minutes with corrections. Motion carried 6-0.
Recognition of Mr. Jim Berling
Mayor Moriconi stated that last year when Council had decided to permanently
close Cody Road due to the costly repairs needed as a result of a slippage, Mr.
Jim Berling just happened to be at that Council meeting. Mayor Moriconi went on
to say that Mr. Berling offered to assist the City in finding a more affordable
resolution in making the necessary repairs in order to re-open Cody Road. He
said Mr. Berling was able to make the repairs for half the estimated cost and
Cody Road has now been re-opened. Mayor Moriconi stated he has received fifty
to sixty emails from residents who are excited that the road has been re-
opened. He stated he asked Mr. Berling to attend this meeting so that he could
thank him for the reconstruction of Cody Road. He presented Mr. Berling with a
key to the City. The Mayor advised that while the road repairs are complete,
topsoil, seed and straw will be laid in the spring.
Presentation of the Downtown Area Form Based Codes – Part I
Mayor Moriconi advised that the Steering Committee has been meeting for the
past several months working on form based zoning codes as recommended in the
Independence Downtown Study. He stated that this has been a lengthy process for
the committee which has included public hearings to get citizen input. He
stated the committee’s findings and recommendations will be presented to
Council in three parts over the next few months and then go to the Kenton
County Planning Commission in April or May. He stated the information for each
part of the recommendation will be submitted to Council in advance of each
meeting. Mayor Moriconi advised committee members are here to present Part I of
their recommendation but that no action will be necessary tonight. He asked
that they listen to the presentation, ask any questions they may have and then
take the coming month to review the material and then act on the recommendation
at the February meeting.
Rodney Crice, 5105 Wooddale Drive – introduced himself as the Chairman of the
Independence Strategic Action Committee (ISAC). He provided some history on the
Small Area Study which Council approved in July 2007 and how the Committee was
formed to implement parts of the Study. He stated one aspect of the Study was
to create new zones as some of the current zones do not comply with the
recommendation in the Study. He stated in 2009/2010 the Steering Committee was
established to work on the on the zoning update process. Mr. Crice advised they
will present several design recommendations within three new zones – the
Downtown Independence zone, the Gateway mixed use zone, and the subdivision
conservation development single-family zone. He stated the committee has held
monthly meetings since early 2010 as well as public forums to get citizen input
whose comments have been incorporated into the proposal.
Mr. Alex Mattingly, introduced himself as the Vice Chairman of the Zoning
Update Steering Committee. He stated the zoning code update includes land use
recommendations for commercial developments, civic uses and providing open
green space. He stated the proposal develops a social core with specialized
markets in the downtown zone which they tried to balance based on the Study
recommendations and public comments. He stated the zone will establish design
guidelines, setbacks, streetscape and fill in building gaps. Again, he stated
they took comments from the citizens into account when proposing these designs.
Mayor Moriconi advised that the Council Members received a copy of all the
comments collected from the public forum meetings.
Andy Videkovich, senior planner with the NKAPC, addressed Council regarding the
downtown zone and the recommendation for a Design Review Board (DRB). He stated
that several tools were used to accomplish the vision for the downtown zone
which encompasses the area between Independence Station Road and Locust Lane.
This area will have two sub-districts: the Courthouse Square and the Transition
Corridor. He stated this will be a mixed use zone with residential only on top
floors and town houses and row houses allowed in outlying areas. Mr. Videkovich
advised that projected and ground signs will be regulated in the areas as well.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the proposed sign regulations would deviate much from
the City’s current sign regulations. He stated there was no difference.
Mr. Videkovich presented a recommendation for the formation of a Design Review
Board (DRB). He stated that not all development plans will need to go before
the DRB as long as they meet all the regulations for the zone. He suggested
that this would be a five member board that should include knowledgeable
individuals in the field of architecture, engineering and builders. He stated
the board should also include a council member and two at-large members. He
stated the board members should be appointed by the Mayor with Council
approval. Mr. Videkovich advised the board would ensure that designs are being
met with the zone’s intended purpose. He stated that under normal circumstances
the board would take final action, but the applicant could appeal to the City
Council and Circuit Court.
Council Member Franzen expressed some concern with the creation of the Design
Review Board. She stated it seems the City’s Zoning Administrator and/or Board
of Adjustment could oversee the regulations of the new zone. She wondered what
the benefits would be for having a DRB if the standards are set. Mr. Videkovich
stated the zones will have higher design standards and the DRB could be more
assistance with creative solutions and similar to the Board of Adjustment the
DRB would have final action. Council Member Franzen again expressed concern
about creating a whole new board which would probably require an application
fee, enlisting volunteers to serve on the board and the need to keep minutes of
all meetings. Mr. Videkovich advised the duties of the Board of Adjustments is
regulated by Kentucky State law (KRS).
Council Member Bushong asked how the new regulations would affect a current
building if destroyed by fire. Mr. Videkovich responded that as long the exact
same footprint was rebuilt – no expansion – then the new regulations would not
affect the rebuild.
Council Member Reinersman explained that the DRB would be different from the
Board of Adjustments in that they would look at creative options with expertise
in the industry. He stated that there would probably be a fee associated with
an application to this board. Council Member Franzen stated she feared this
would add another level of bureaucracy. Council Member Brinker asked if any
other local cities had a DRB. Mr. Videkovich responded that Covington had a
review board for their historic overlay zone.
Council Member Little stated there are twenty parcels involved in the downtown
area and he asked if the owners were consulted about the proposed land use. Mr.
Videkovich advised there was a general ad for the first public meeting and the
property owners were contacted about the second public meeting. Council Member
Little also asked if a change of zone would be necessary prior to any
development. He expressed some reservations about this and cited some examples
in recent years where the City granted a zone change for a proposed development
without firm commitments and the land has never been developed, so if it is
ever sold again, there will probably be another request for a zone change. . He
stated he would prefer that any zone change be requested by the current owner.
Council Member Little also expressed some concern about the creation of a
Design Review Board and the expenses that will be associated with this board.
Council Member Franzen stated she was also concerned property rights and
designating the land use of some parcels as conservation which could decrease
the owner’s property value. Mr. Videkovich stated they received many public
comments about this. Council Member Reinersman commented that any existing use
will remain so until the property is sold and that any parcels with a proposed
conservation land use are a pro-active direction to work toward the vision for
that area.
Mayor Moriconi commented that he understands that Council wants to take a
cautious approach toward this goal. Council Member Franzen stated she
appreciated the committee’s hard work and consideration put into this proposal.
Mayor Moriconi commented there is a lot of information to review and advised
Council to take their time and ask questions. He stated if they are not ready
in February to act on this that will be okay, but asked that they consider
everything presented. Mr. Videkovich stated they will attend the February
meeting to address any additional comments or questions Council has on Part I.
Mayor Moriconi asked Council to direct any questions to Mr. Groth via email.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-01 – Requiring Annexation of Real Estate into the City
Prior to Being Permitted Access to a City Street – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2012-O-01 that
would require the annexation of real estate into the City prior to such real
estate being permitted access to a City street.
Mr. Deters reported that Public Works Director Gary Cooper and the City’s
Building Inspector Kevin Barbian met with a representative of a citizen (Toby
Carpenter) who lives in the unincorporporated area that would like access onto
Gatewood Drive (in the Williams Woods Subdivision). He stated they all agreed
to a road development concept that would provide the City a T-turnaround, which
the City employees indicated they would need in order to provide access onto
Gatewood Drive. Mr. Deters advised he just received a letter today from Mr.
Carpenter’s attorney about finalizing an agreement with the City for this
street easement. Mr. Deters asked the Council if they wanted to postpone the
second reading of this ordinance and move forward with the proposed agreement
by Mr. Carpenter that would not require annexation. Council Members Reinersman
and Yeager indicated they felt it would be in the best interest of the City to
adopt the ordinance that would require annexation into the City prior to
accessing any City street.
Mr. Toby Carpenter stepped up to the podium to address Council about his
request. He stated the City allowed the developer of Williams Woods subdivision
to construct a dead-end street for no apparent reason. He stated that he did
not want to annex into the City.
Council Member Little stated that apart from this particular situation the City
has approximately one hundred similar situations and so this is a City-wide
concern. He stated adopting this ordinance would alleviate further problems in
the future.
Mr. Carpenter commented that property splits are approved by the NKAPC
(Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission). Council Member Brinker advised
that NKAPC is responsible for ridge continuity planning and therefore the City
doesn’t approve or disapprove the placement of street stubs.
Mr. Deters commented that the City would be getting a benefit from having a T-
turnaround as the Public Works department would have a place to push snow.
Mayor Moriconi stated the City is not trying to be difficult but must determine
a solution that would be in the best interest city-wide and not address this
situation based on one location. Council Member Reinersman agreed with the
Mayor and stated the City must protect the City interests as a whole.
Mr. Carpenter said he has subdivided from his property (that faces Maher Road)
two 10-acre parcels at the rear of his land which will front Gatewood Drive.
Mr. Groth asked why he did not want to annex those parcels into the City. Mr.
Carpenter stated he would just pay more taxes with no benefits and therefore
didn’t want to be annexed. Mr. Deters suggested these two parcels would
restrict access to a future, larger development.
Mayor Moriconi asked Council if they wanted to move forward with the second
reading of the Ordinance. Council Member Yeager so moved, with second by
Council Member Bushong. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no
vote cast by Council Member Franzen. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2012-O-01.
Resolution No. 2012-R-01 – Supporting the REINS (Regulations from the Executive
In Need of Scrutiny) H.R. 3765
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-01 that would support

and would require Congress to affirmatively approve any new major rule (over
$100,000,000) proposed by the executive agencies before it can be enforced on
the American people and requests our State and Federal representatives to
strongly support this Act and actively oppose unfunded mandates in any and
every form.
