Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
6, 2012 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the January 9, 2012 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, January 9, 2012. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Yeager. Council Member Reinersman requested amendments
on page two; with no objections from Council, roll was called and answered
unanimously to adopt the minutes with corrections. Motion carried 6-0.
Approving Application for Zoning Text Amendment – Part I
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that each part of the form based code being
proposed for the Downtown Study area, some of which was presented at last
month’s meeting, will be presented and considered by Council in parts and then
all parts will go to the Kenton County Planning Commission for their
consideration and recommendation back to the City for final approval. He asked
Council for their input regarding the presentation of the subdivision
conservation development zone and the Design Review Board that was presented at
last month’s meeting. He stated they are being presented with three proposed
Resolutions each pertaining to the first part of this project which would
approve applications being made to the Planning Commission for the following:
·   A text amendment to add the DI (Downtown Independence) zone including sign
regulations for the DI zone
·   A map amendment changing an approximate 60-acre area on the east and west
sides of Madison Pike from R-1C, R-1D and NC to a new DI zone
·   A text amendment to add Design Review Board (DRB) regulations and
procedures
A brief discussion ensued. Andy Videkovich, senior planner with the NKAPC,
advised that the intent of three separate resolutions being presented in the
event that Council was in favor of moving forward with certain parts of last
month’s proposal but not all of it. Council Members Franzen and Little
expressed some concerns regarding the DI zone and parcels that would have that
designation. Council Member Reinersman explained that there are actually three
different zones in that area. Council Member Franzen stated certain areas are
covered in Part II of this project and suggested she would prefer to vote on
this along with Part II at the March meeting.
Council Member Franzen moved to table acting on the proposed (3) resolutions
until the March meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. No roll was
called; motion carried with all ayes.
Presentation of the Downtown Historic Survey by David Taylor
Mayor Moriconi introduced David L. Taylor, a Historic Preservation Consultant
of Taylor & Taylor Associates out of Brookville, Pennsylvania who was awarded
the bid to conduct a historic resource survey of the City’s downtown area.
Mr. Taylor presented the City Council with a survey summary report of his
findings. He advised that the survey area included a ten-acre area along
portions of Madison Pike and McCullum Pike. He reported that the National
Register has designated a 50-year age threshold and so the houses prior to 1962
would be considered eligible for historic designation. He stated that each year
more buildings will become eligible as they reach the 50-year threshold. He
advised that he prepared individual survey forms for forty-nine properties in
the area that would be known as the “Independence Courthouse Square Historic
District.” He reported that this area has a mix of residential, commercial and
institutional architecture between the 1880’s to the 1960’s. He reported that
oral history was a part of his research as he had the opportunity to speak with
some of the property owners and that many of the photos he used came from Mr.
Bridges recently published book on the history of Independence. He said these
historic photos are a wonderful road map. Mr. Taylor advised that he looked at
the various properties, the integrity and overall character of the study area
and recommends preparing a nomination to the National Register of Historic
Places for the survey area that would be known as “Independence Square Historic
District.”
Mr. Taylor went on to recommend the City adopt a local ordinance designating
this area as a historic district which will not impose any restrictions on
private property owners’ rights. He advised that one of the benefits of the
historic district designation is the ability to apply for State and Federal tax
credits for the rehabilitation of buildings in the district.
Mr. Groth reminded Council that this historic survey was possible as the City
received funding for this project from AT & T. Mr. Taylor suggested the next
step would be to contact the Kentucky Heritage Council’s National Register
staff to discuss this undertaking and then allocate funding for the nomination
to the National Register. He advised there are statutory requirements and it is
a year long process that includes the preparation of a nomination and holding a
public hearing. In response to a question from a property owner, Mr. Taylor
advised that having this designation will not increase property values, but
would never decrease the value either. Council Member Reinersman commented that
it could incentivize people to rehab their properties. There was a brief
question and answer session with Mr. Taylor. Mayor Moriconi thanked him for his
report and presentation.
Presentation of the Downtown Area Form Based Codes, Part II – Steering
Committee and NKAPC Staff
Mayor Moriconi introduced Rodney Crice, Chairman of the Steering Committee who
would present the concept of the conservation development overlay zone for the
downtown area as Part II of the form based codes project.
Mr. Crice stated that the conservation development single-family (CD-SF)
overlay zone seems to be the most controversial zone but an important component
of the downtown study. He advised the two main issues of this zone is the
density and conservation of the rural area and keeping the small town feel. He
stated this zone does not currently exist in the City. He stated he feels that
the overall vision of the project will be difficult to achieve without it. He
cited various statements from the Downtown Study that recommended the
modification of the local zoning code to include a conservation development
model and the principles of mixed use development. Mr. Crice stated that the
Comprehensive Plan and current zoning regulations help guide development and he
hopes that adopting the proposed form based codes for the downtown area will
achieve the desired results.
Alex Mattingly, Vice Chairman of the Zoning Update Steering Committee reported
that the guiding factor for their committee was addressing the conservation
development overlay zone. He stated a higher density residential area would
support the conservation district subdivision with more green space and also
support nearby commercial land uses. He reported the committee focused on
public comments and found that no one wanted this to be mandatory, so it is
being proposed that the conservation area development be optional. He stated
the committee initially proposed the conservation area be fifty percent but
decreased it to thirty percent with density bonus incentives to the developers.
He said the current zoning has a density penalty. He stated some advantages of
a conservation development is that rights-of-way can account for 10% of the
land area, topography where physical features restrict can result in larger
lots, and the development of other residential amenities such as parks. Mr.
Mattingly said the CD-SF overlay protects the rural character and uses the land
more efficiently. He went on to explain the density calculations and
incentives, such as more permitted lots in the development, for providing open
space. He stated this concept would allow more people to be served thereby
using land more efficiently.
Mr. Mattingly explained the options of ownership and maintenance of the green
space with a detailed management plan that might include City maintenance, a
Homeowners’ Association, donate or sell to the Kenton Conservancy or the
designation of conservation easements which would be part of private platted
lots within the subdivision.
Mr. Mattingly advised the process for the developer would be to submit a Stage
II Development Plan and have the Plan reviewed and approved by the Design
Review Board as well.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the conservation development has been implemented
elsewhere in Kenton County. Mr. Mattingly responded that Kenton County and
Edgewood have adopted the text amendment but no development yet. He went on to
say that many cities have PUD and cluster developments throughout the County.
Council Member Franzen addressed the Hartland Subdivision residents in
attendance that had some concerns about Chateau Court, which is currently a
stub street, being opened as a through street to connect future development on
McCullum Road. He stated an option to consider would be to permanently close
the stub. He explained that the property along McCullum Road is currently zoned
R-1C which would permit the development of a couple hundred single family
houses. He said if the property owners sell to a developer the City would have
no control over a zone that is currently in place. He went on to explain that
if the City adopts the conservation development in that area that it may be
possible that the City would have more control of the development.
Mr. Videkovich advised that stub streets fall under the subdivision regulations
and are intended to allow for another egress so as not to overload main roads
and address safety issues. City Attorney informed Council that ultimately the
City does have authority to close a stub street and he explained the process to
do so. He stated that when a street is permanently closed the sides become the
property of the adjoining properties
Council Member Franzen explained the purpose of the Downtown Study was to
facilitate planned development and not piece meal development of the
residential and commercial in a haphazard manner.
Council Member Brinker expressed some concern with higher density lots and
feels that most people move here looking for larger lots. Council Member
Reinersman commented that the committee was looking at a way to get a
sufficient number of rooftops to support local business, yet keep a rural feel.
Council Member Reinersman explained that the conservation area supports higher
density single family construction such as town homes and patio homes without
large yards. He stated this is a new single family development style that would
be marketed in the mid to high price range.
Council Member Little addressed the various references made to the Small Area
Study during this discussion. He stated he feels the intent may be somewhat
misconstrued as the City felt it was important to plan for future development
by conducting the Study. He went on to say that although the Small Area Study
was adopted by the Council, it must be noted that the Study was adopted as a
whole, but that does not mean every Council Member agreed with all parts of the
Study. He further commented that he does not believe, if a developer is given
the option that a conservation development will ever happen, so therefore, he
doesn’t understand the point of doing this. He stated he sees this as a
hindrance to the developer. He stated he feels the best time to propose a zone
change is when a development plan is being proposed. Council Member Little also
expressed concerns about the maintenance of all the green space and mentioned
the City expense to mow subdivision entrances. In closing, he stated that he
would not support any proposal that would restrict a property owners rights and
reiterated that he did not understand an optional conservation area that
developers would probably not opt for since it would involve more cost and
impose more restrictions on a development. He also commented that every big
business wants to locate in the Towne Center area making the chances of new
development in the downtown area less competitive.
Council Member Reinersman cited other cities were this type of development has
been successful and commented that it’s finding the right businesses for the
downtown area. He stated that while he does not agree with every part of the
concept he likes the idea of laying the groundwork for future development and
feels this plan allows more options for developments.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Videkovich, Mr. Crice and Mr. Mattingly for their
presentation. Council Members urged citizens to provide their input on this
proposal to them via email or phone calls. Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor for
comments from some audience members.
Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview, Independence – commented that she attended the
committee meetings and public hearings on this issue and heard the suggestions
offered by residents. She stated she lives in the Hartland Subdivision and is
opposed to this proposal. She stated the committee members could not solve all
the concerns the residents put forth.
Robert Dupuy, 5325 Chateau Court, Independence – shared some of his feelings on
the proposal for a conservation area and said he would like it to remain a
historic district. He asked if it would be possible to keep Chateau Court a
stub street. Mr. Deters advised he would check on the legalities of closing the
street.
Margaret Powers, 2919 Westridge Ave., Cincinnati, Ohio 45238 – commented that
the property owners on McCullum Road have rights and if they decide to sell
their land to a developer she does not feel it is fair that they have to keep a
large portion of it as green space. She also expressed concern that their
property could be devalued if Chateau Court was permanently closed off
preventing access to future development on McCullum Road.
Don Nienaber, 66 McCullum Road – stated he had attended all the committee
meetings on this project and voiced his opposition to it.
Mayor Moriconi advised further discussion on this proposal would resume at the
next meeting.
Resolution No. 2012-R-03 – Supporting NKAPC Staff’s Draft Subdivisions
Regulations with Modifications
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-03, a resolution
supporting the NKAPC staff’s draft subdivisions regulations with modifications
presented by the committee of the Kenton County Mayor’s Group. Mayor Moriconi
advised the Council that the proposed updates have stronger construction
standards for streets. He stated that if the proposed regulations are adopted
by the Kenton County Planning Commission they will automatically go into effect
and will not come back to the City for further review or approval. He stated
that under current standards for street construction, the concrete streets have
been failing earlier than the expected lifetime. Mayor Moriconi advised the
Mayor’s Group has been very involved in this effort to get the subdivision
regulations modified.
Council Member Yeager moved to adopt Resolution No. 2012-R-03, seconded by
Council Member Bushong. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2012-R-04 – Supporting Land & Water Conservation Fund Grant to

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
March 5, 2012
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 5,
2012 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and asked for a moment of
silence in remembrance for the victims of the tornado disaster that struck the
region on Friday, March 2, 2012. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris
Reinersman and Donna Yeager. Council Member Jim Bushong was absent. Also
present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Mayor Moriconi welcomed Boy Scout Troop Number 8 from St. Cecilia School who
were attending the meeting to earn their merit badges for communication and
citizenship in the community.
Approval of the February 6, 2012 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, February 6, 2012. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Yeager. Council Member Reinersman requested amendments
on page three; with no objections from Council, roll was called and answered
unanimously to adopt the minutes with corrections. Motion carried 5-0.
Presentation of Award for Outstanding Investigation – Rob Sanders, Commonwealth
Attorney
Kenton County Commonwealth Attorney Rob Sanders was present to present the
Award for Outstanding Investigation to Detective Jim Moore. But, he first
congratulated and thanked the City for the leadership role they assumed in
spearheading the relief efforts for the victims of the tornado/bad weather that
hit the Piner area on Friday evening.
Mr. Sanders went on to present an award for outstanding investigative work to
Independence Detective Jim Moore. Mr. Sanders stated that Detective Moore’s
work on the State versus Richard Noah case went above and beyond the call of
duty. He stated this was a high profile case where Richard Noah, who was a
firefighter for the Independence Fire District, had plotted to murder his wife.
He stated that Detective Moore’s outstanding skills, work ethic and
communication provided invaluable assistance to his office in prosecuting Mr.
Noah.
Tornado Relief
Mayor Moriconi thanked everyone who participated in the tornado relief effort
this past weekend. He stated that good comes out of tragedy and how amazing it
was to see various members of the community come together to help the
neighboring community of Piner. He acknowledged the members of the Independence
Business Association who started the effort shortly after hearing of the
tornado damage on Friday night. Mayor Moriconi stated there were so many people
to thank, but particularly wanted to acknowledge Wiseway for donating the use
of a truck to transport the donations to Piner Baptist Church on Saturday,
Snappy Tomato and LaRosa’s for donating pizza to feed the volunteers, Mark
Kiser of Quik Copy, St. Cecilia and Independence Christian churches and City
employees. He advised offers of assistance are still come in. Council Member
Franzen advised that due to the overwhelming response the Independence
Christian Church is taking the overflow of donated items as Piner Baptist
Church has run out of storage space. Council Member Reinersman stated that cash
donations are needed and that the Bank of Kentucky has a number of accounts
that have been opened for donations.
Proclamation – Brain Injury Awareness Month
Mayor Moriconi presented a Proclamation declaring March 14, 2012 as Brain
Injury Awareness Day.
Presentation of the Downtown Area Form Based Codes, Part II – Steering
Committee and NKAPC Staff
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that this would be the final phase of the three
presentations by the Steering Committee on the downtown area form based codes
proposal. He stated that the specific presentation tonight will be on the
Gateway mixed zone area along McCullum Pike and SR17.
Andy Videkovich, senior planner with the NKAPC, addressed Council with a recap
of the Conservation subdivision zone that was discussed at the February
meeting. He addressed some concerns that Council expressed at the last meeting.
He stated that the purpose of this proposal was born out of the Small Area
Study conducted by the City in 2007 and then adopted into the City’s
Comprehensive Plan. He advised that this document is referred to when
development plans are submitted and are reviewed for consistency with the Plan.
He stated that developers have a difficult time if no tools are in place that
is consistent with the Study. Mr. Videkovich also stated that the proposed
codes will provide options to developers and that offering options should not
be considered a deterrent to a developer. He stated that developers would not
have to consider the form based codes. In closing, he commented that Chateau
Court in the Hartland Subdivision is a separate issue from these form based
code updates and zoning in general.
John Richardson, Chairman of the Steering Committee, presented the
recommendations on the area known as the Gateway Mixed Use zone. He advised
that this is the first development that would be seen on the new section of
SR17 as you enter the City. He stated the committee reviewed the Downtown Study
recommendations that were followed to create the guidelines for this
development area. He stated this is the gateway to the historic downtown area.
He said the committee is recommending the zoning code be modified in this area.
Mr. Richardson also shared some positive comments the committee received at the
two public forum meetings that were held as part of this process.
Mr. Videkovich stated that the purpose of the Gateway area is to promote
development aimed on a pedestrian scale which provides for a mixture of land
uses. He stated the zone permits high density residential or multi-family
apartments. Also allowed would be office, retail service, public and civic
uses. He stated that drive through lanes would be permitted but limited to
three lanes.
Mr. Videkovich the Gateway zone would provide development standards that would
include five acre minimums, fifty foot setbacks, maximum of two-story height
and a 15,000 square foot maximum footprint. Also, in order to decrease the
amount of constructed impervious areas, it is being recommended that off street
parking must be shared or cooperative. Mr. Videkovich stated that every
development within the Gateway zone should provide at least two major public
amenities such as a playground, pocket park, plaza, water feature, etc. He
stated the Design Review Board should allow for flexibility for individuality
and creativity.
At this time, Mayor Moriconi opened the discussion to Council for any questions
they have on the proposal. He also asked Mr. Groth if all the map and zone
change recommendations would be sent to the Planning Commission as a whole. Mr.
Groth advised that after a decision is made by Council regarding the Gateway
Mixed Use zone then all phases of the proposal approved by Council would be
presented as a whole to the Planning Commission who would make a recommendation
for approval or disapproval to the Council.
Mayor Moriconi asked Council if they had any questions/concerns on the map
amendment proposal to change an approximate 60-acre area along Madison Pike in
the Downtown Independence zone. Council Member Reinersman distributed a list of
current and proposed permitted uses in the Downtown Zone. He stated the
proposed zone would allow for twenty more uses. A brief discussion ensued about
the permitted uses and possibly allowing service stations as a permitted use.
Council Members Franzen and Yeager agreed that service stations should remain
as a conditional use.
Resolution No. 2012-R-06 – Approving Application for a Zoning Map Amendment to
Change an Approximate 60-Acre Area on the East and West Sides of Madison Pike
from R-1C, R-1D and NC to the DI (Downtown Independence) Zone
Council Member Reinersman moved to approve Resolution No. 2012-R-06, seconded
by Council Member Franzen.
A discussion ensued. Council Member Little stated he was concerned that the
Small Area Study is being interpreted very different; he doesn’t feel the
intent is what has been proposed by the Steering Committee. He stated the
intent of the Small Area Study is to provide some direction and doesn’t feel it
is appropriate to put the cart before the horse. He stated that in general he
doesn’t feel this is needed at this time and only imposes more control and
bureaucracy and will ultimately hinder development. He stated he feels that the
kind of development proposal being presented will never happen, especially in
this current economy, and also feels a development plan should be presented by
a developer before considering a zone change. He commented that it is obvious
to him that adhering to the text and map changes will cost developers more to
develop in this area. Council Member Little went on to say that the citizens
feel that the zoning is being changed against their wishes. He stated property
owners have the right to say what they want on their property.
Council Member Brinker commented that the developers will not be forced to
comply since the proposed changes will be voluntary.
Council Member Reinersman responded to Council Member Little’s concerns. He
stated that he disagreed that development would be hindered especially in the
Downtown Independence zone. He stated the purpose of the proposed guidelines
would be to preserve the downtown area so as not to adversely impact the goal
of revitalization. He went on to say that he believes it will happen – if
everyone feels the area is dead then let it die – but he was of the
understanding that Council had a vision for this area. He stated that current
zoning leaves it open for a hodge-podge of development. He stated he
appreciates Council Member Little’s concerns but feels the City needs to lay
some groundwork for future development of the downtown area.
Council Member Franzen commented that a valid point to make is that the
proposal does allow for more uses than in the current NC (neighborhood
commercial) zone. She stated that while she has some concerns with other parts
of the overall proposal, she does not have any concerns with this part. She
stated she agrees that the City needs to decide whether to move forward with
future planning or just let the planning be willy-nilly.
Council Member Little responded that he feels zoning is currently in place and
the bottom line should be that property owners need to have some say on a zone
change for their property.
Council Member Reinersman replied that current zoning in the downtown area does
not permit residential apartments above the businesses, but this would be
allowed in the proposed Downtown Independence zone. He expressed concern that
the downtown area is not thriving as there is not enough people in the area on
a regular basis. He went on to say that he agrees that the Downtown Study is
subject to interpretation but the City needs to decide how they want to proceed
with guiding future development. Council Member Yeager advised that the Council
members did not agree with all aspects of the Study. Council Member Reinersman
commented that Council needs to find a way to do something with the Study.
Council Member Brinker wondered what could be done without stepping on the
rights of the property owners in the area. He stated he would prefer to offer
incentives to developers rather than mandates – a different approach that could
provide the same end result.
Council Member Reinersman advised the proposal has broad parameters on design
guidelines and provides more uses and leaves more options than the NC zone. He
feels the City needs to do something to guide future development.
In closing, Council Member Franzen stated that this is just a first step and
nothing is being changed by approving the Resolution to make an application
with the Planning Commission.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered with three ayes
and two no votes cast by Council Members Little and Yeager.
Resolution No. 2012-R-07 – Approving an Application for a Zoning Text Amendment
to Add the DI (Downtown Independence) Zone
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-07, a resolution
supporting the application of a text amendment to the official zoning ordinance
of the City to add the DI (Downtown Independence) zone, specific sign

Council Member Franzen moved to approve Resolution No. 2012-O-07, seconded by

Resolution No. 2012-R-08 – Approving an Application for a Zoning Text Amendment
to Add a Design Review Board (DRB) Regulations & Procedures
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-08, a resolution
supporting the application of a text amendment to the official zoning ordinance
of the City to add Design Review Board (DRB) regulations and procedures to
Article XVI and the necessary cross references.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to approve Resolution No. 2012-R-08. A brief discussion ensued. Council
Member stated she is not really in favor of establishing a Design Review Board
as she feels this Board will incur expenses similar to the Board of Adjustment.
She stated she would prefer that any requested changes be presented to the
Council for review instead of a Board.
Council Member Reinersman commented that while he is not opposed to having this
Board he does have some mixed feelings. He suggested that if this Board was not
established perhaps there could be some form of a trigger chart that would
determine who would review the request for a change, i.e. zoning or building
inspector or Council. There was a brief discussion on making a modification to
the establishment of a Board.
When the discussion ended, the roll was called on the motion and was answered
with one aye and four no votes cast by Council Members Brinker, Franzen, Little
and Yeager. Motion was defeated and Resolution No. 2012-R-07 was not approved.
Resolution No. 2012-R-09 & Resolution No. 2012-R-10 – Approving Applications

0.

Resolution No. 2012-R-09 – Approving Application for a Zoning Text Amendment to
Add the CD-SF (Conservation Development – Single Family) Overlay Zone and Cross
References as Needed
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-09, a resolution
supporting the application of a text amendment to the official zoning ordinance
of the City to add the CD-SF (Conservation Development – Single Family) overlay
zone and the necessary cross-references as needed.
Council Member Reinersman made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2012-R-09,
seconded by Council Member Bushong. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member
Reinersman explained that the overlay zone would be optional to developers. He
stated this was an idea that came out of the Downtown Small Area Study in 2007.
He stated this is actually less restrictive than the zoning that is currently
in place and it will protect the rural feel of the community. He went on to say
that public input was obtained, considered and effected into the final draft of
this proposed text amendment. He stated that developers will be given bonuses
for higher density development plans that would result in more unaffected green
space. Council Member Reinersman commented that he feels these are positive
changes that will provide more land uses and fewer streets that will be an
environmental advantage with less stormwater runoff from those streets. Council
Member Franzen commented that the conservation overlay will require every stage
of development to be approved by the Council and gives the current property
owners more land uses for potential sale of the land to developers.
Andy Videkovich, senior planner with the NKAPC, advised that the proposed text
and map amendments would go before the Kenton County Planning Commission in
July or August for the public hearing and then a recommendation for approval or
disapproval to the City. Council Member Franzen commented that final action for
these text and map amendments would be adopted by Council in the form of an
ordinance.
There being no further discussion, roll was called and answered with all ayes.
Motion carried 5-0.
Resolution No. 2012-R-10 – Approving Application for a Zoning Map Amendment to

McCullum Pike from R-1C, R-1D and NC to R-1C (CD-SF), R-1D (CD-SF) and NC (CD-
SF)

Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the results of the bids received on March
16, 2012 for the curbside collection of trash and recycling. Bids were received
from Bestway Disposal, Rumpke, Republic Services, Bavarian and Forest Green.
Mayor Moriconi advised that Dan Groth, who has years of experience as a solid
waste coordinator has analyzed the bids. Mr. Groth stated he is recommending
that Council accept the bid from Rumpke for once per week trash collection and
once per week recycling collection which would be billed directly to the
homeowner. He stated the cost for the first two years will be $11.47 per month
with no gas fuel surcharge which is less than the current monthly charge the
residents are paying. Mayor Moriconi directed everyone’s attention to the
sample trash and recycling cans that the residents will be provided free of
charge from Rumpke. Rumpke representative Brett Gaspard advised that the larger
recycling bin on display will require a $1 per month additional charge and the
smaller red recycling bins will be provided free of charge. Mayor Moriconi
advised that the proposed bid from Rumpke indicates that it will be 2016 before
arriving at the contracted monthly charge currently being paid by the
residents. Mr. Groth stated that the large brown trash cans come in two sizes –
65 and 95 gallon. He advised Council that under the current contract with
Rumpke the residents opt for curbside recycling on a subscription basis and pay
$4.25 per month for this service. He also stated that under the new contract
the residents would not pay a fuel surcharge.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to a representative from Bestway Disposal who
stated they were a full service company headquartered in Indianapolis and
looking to expand their services to the Northern Kentucky/Cincinnati areas. She
stated they recently purchased fourteen acres in Burlington for a future
facility. In the meantime they have contracted with Bavarian to dump in their
landfill until they get their facility up and running. She said they also offer
recycling.
Council Member Bushong commented that providing the residents with a recycling
bin will encourage more people to participate in recycling.
Mr. Gaspard advised that under the bid proposal submitted by Rumpke all
residents will be provided new trash bins. He stated approximately 800
residents already lease a bin, but everyone will have to have a Rumpke bin so
the truck can pick it up. In response to the Mayor’s question about recycling
the residents old garbage cans, Mr. Gaspard advised that the cans are not
recyclable and suggest the residents may have other uses for them around their
house.
There was a brief discussion regarding items not placed in the trash bins. Mr.
Gaspard stated that Rumpke would request that residents call them in advance
for large item pickup. He stated there would be a $10 charge for large items,
but there would not be a limit as long as it fit into the truck.
Mr. Gaspard stated he would work with Mr. Groth to draft a mailer to the
residents to explain the specifics of a new contract. He said this could also
be put in the City’s newsletter. He said that all items will need to be placed
in the cans/bins for pick up and he acknowledged that there will be a learning
curve for the residents. Mr. Gaspard stated that the recycling trucks will not
use an automated arm. Mayor Moriconi advised the new contract would be
effective July 1.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Bushong moved to accept the
bid from Rumpke for one time per week trash pickup and one time per week
recycling billed directly to the property owner for $11.47/month for the term
of July 1, 2012 through June 30, 2014 and to authorize the Mayor to sign the
contract. Council Member Franzen seconded the motion. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting an Amended 2011/12 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend the 2011-2012 budget. He commented that the major amendment in this
budget was for the expenses related to the Cody Road improvements. There being
no questions by Council, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2012/2013 Fiscal Year Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance
that would adopt a budget for the 2012/2013 fiscal year. In his budget address
Mayor Moriconi stated he is presenting a balanced budget without transferring
money from the reserve fund. He stated the City would not realize an increase
in the Municipal Road Aid for 2012/2013, but it would definitely increase next
year which is a direct result in the City’s population increase over the past
decade. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting an Employee Pay and Classification Plan – 1st
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that will
adopt an employee Pay and Classification Plan for the 2012/2013 fiscal year.
Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Award Bid for Ashgrove & Alpine Roadway Improvements
Mr. Groth reported that the City opened bids on May 3, 2012 for the road
improvements for Ashgrove and Alpine streets. He stated that bids were received
from the following: Len Riegler Blacktop, Easton Asphalt, TMS Construction, and
Paul Michels Sons. He stated he is recommending that Council award the bid to
the lowest bidder, Len Riegler Blacktop, in the amount of $221,585.00. He
stated that this company has done work previously for the City and is in good
standing.
Council Member Franzen moved to award the bid for roadway improvements to
Ashgrove and Alpine streets to Len Riegler Blacktop in the amount of
$221,585.00, seconded by Council Member Reinersman. Roll was called and
answered unanimously; motion carried 6-0.
Mr. Groth stated the work should be started on this project around mid-July.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the public works employees are currently tearing
out 900 feet of asphalt on Wedgewood Drive. He also reported that a section of
Cody Road has been repaved and looks great.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth reported the Recreation Department’s new fitness programs are
increasingly popular with the addition of new classes being offered and a new
summer schedule set to begin soon.
Mr. Groth also announced the annual Memorial Day parade will be held on Monday,
May 28th and begin at 10:30 a.m.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi reported that donations for the annual fireworks display during
the July 4th Celebration have been coming in thanks to Council Member Yeager,
Recreation and Police Departments. He stated their goal this year is $25,000 in
donations and that the City appreciates the support of the local business
community in this endeavor. Mayor Moriconi stated that July 4th is on a
Wednesday this year and the event will take place on Friday and Saturday, July
6th & 7th.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:31 p.m.

June 4, 2012
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 4,
2012 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the May 7, 2012 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, May 7, 2012. Council Member Little so moved, with
second by Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-03 – Adopting an Amended 2011/12 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2012-O-03, an
ordinance that would amend the 2011-2012 budget. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No.
2012-O-03. Mayor Moriconi advised the major amendment in the budget was for the
reconstruction of Cody Road.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to adopt Ordinance No. 2012-O-03, seconded
by Council Member Yeager. There being no discussion, roll was called and

Ordinance No. 2012-O-04– Adopting the 2012/2013 Fiscal Year Budget – 2nd
Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would adopt the budget for the 2012/2013 fiscal year. City Attorney, Mr.
Deters gave Ordinance No. 2012-O-04 a second reading.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Bushong to adopt Ordinance No. 2012-O-04. Mayor Moriconi commented that this
budget has no frills and was balanced without tapping into the reserve account.
He stated that the allocation from the State for the Municipal Road Aid was not
what he had hoped it would be, but feels confident that this revenue source,
which is based on census figures, will increase next year since the City’s
population has increased significantly since the 2000 census. He thanked the
staff for keeping the expenses down and the work they put into preparing this
budget.
There being no discussion, roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0 to adopt the 2012/2013 budget as presented.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-05 – Adopting an Employee Pay and Classification Plan –
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2012-O-05- that
will adopt an employee Pay and Classification Plan for the 2012/2013 fiscal
year. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.
A motion was made by Council Member Yeager and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to adopt Ordinance No. 2012-O-05 enacting a personnel and pay
classification plan for City employees. There being no discussion, roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Declare Surplus Property – Police Cruisers
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a list of seven City vehicles that need to
be declared as surplus property for purposes of disposal by way of the annual
auction held by Kenton County. He stated there are six Ford Crown Vic and one
2003 Chevrolet Impala – all between 7-12 years of age.
Council Member Bushong moved to declare the vehicles presented as surplus
property and authorize the sale of the vehicles at the Kenton County auction.
Council Member Reinersman seconded the motion. There being no discussion, roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2012-R-13 – Approving Application to KCPC for a Text Amendment
Relating to Parking and Storing of Trailers, Mobile Homes, Campers, Etc.
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a resolution that would seek a zoning text
amendment to add additional language to Section 9.23 which regulates the
parking or storing of trailers, mobile homes, campers, inoperable vehicles and
other such equipment. He advised that under Section 9.23, C(1) would add the
words “or owner” of the residence to store the equipment on the property. Mr.
Deters advised that approving this resolution would authorize the application
to the Planning Commission to get their recommendation on whether to approve or
disapprove this text change.
A motion was made by Council Member Yeager and seconded by Council Member
Little to approve Resolution No. 2012-R-13. A discussion ensued.
Council Member Little advised that when this Section was last amended the words
“or owner” was omitted as there was some concern that an owner would store
multiple recreational type vehicles, so it was limited to only allow one
vehicle. He stated that inserting “or owner” will make this section more clear.
Council Member Franzen expressed concerns that if this is allowed on properties
that are not owner-occupied that the City will start seeing an influx of rental
properties storing recreational vehicles of friends and relatives that live in
other cities. She stated this is worrisome, especially in these economic times
with so many properties being rented. Mr. Deters commented that this concern is
addressed in paragraph C(2) of Section 9.23 as this section limits only one
vehicle to be stored outside of an enclosed building on any lot. Council Member
Reinersman agreed this could be an issue.
Mayor Moriconi yielded the floor to Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence –
who asked which Council Member was proposing the text amendment. Council Member
Yeager stated she suggested this amendment be presented to the Council for
consideration. Mrs. Cook stated that in 2009-2010 these regulations were mulled
over by a group that included elected officials. She stated that she sees the
main issue to be lack of enforcement by the City and doesn’t understand why the
City would spend additional funds to make more changes that would not be
enforced. She went on to point out a particular resident that has not been
cited for a recreational vehicle violation for the past eight years and
suggested they should be cited to court if they refuse to come into compliance.
Council Member Franzen stated that 99% of the violators come into compliance
when given notice by the City.
Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview Court, Independence – complained about the campers,
boats, etc. stored on so many properties that are covered, without valid
licenses and are in deteriorating conditions. She stated she has reported many
of these to the City and nothing has been done.
Council Member Brinker expressed concern that the City did not have a “next
step” to get violation compliance. Mrs. Wuestefeld, Zoning Administrator,
advised that the City is on a complaint basis with regard to issuing violation
notices and that there is a process in place for non-compliant property owners.
The City can issue citations and take them to court.
There being no further discussion, roll was called on the motion to approve
Resolution No. 2012-R-13, and answered with four ayes and two no votes cast by
Council Members Reinersman and Franzen. Motion carried 4-2
Resolution No. 2012-R-14 – Approving the MRA Co-Op Agreement for Fiscal Year
Beginning July 1, 2012
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-14 that would approve
and authorize him to enter into the Municipal Aid Co-Op Program contract with
the State Transportation Cabinet for the 2012-2013 fiscal year. Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2012-R-14. Mr. Groth advised that by entering into the
cooperative agreement the City contributes 3% of the municipal aid funding to
the State’s emergency fund. He stated that in the past few years the City has
received $375,000 from the emergency fund while only contributing about $5,500
per year. The three major projects that benefited from the emergency fund were
the Crowe Road Bridge, Marshall Road and Cody Road. Mr. Groth thanked the
Public Works Director Gary Cooper for initiating the City’s involvement in this
program. Mayor Moriconi commented that this program has been a life saver for
the City on some of the road reconstruction projects.
Council Member Reinersman moved to adopt Resolution No. 2012-R-14, seconded by
Council Member Brinker. There being no discussion roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Award Bid for the Reconstruction of Wayman Drive – Mr. Groth reported that on
May 31st at 11:00 a.m. bids were opened for the Wayman Drive Resurfacing
project. He stated that the City received five (5) bids which ranged from a low
bid of $41,641.50 to a high bid of $67,601.25. He stated that after reviewing
the bids, he is recommending that the bid be awarded to Len Riegler Blacktop in
the amount of $41,641.50.
A motion was made by Council Member Little and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to award the bid to Len Riegler Blacktop in the amount of $41,641.50.
Mr. Groth advised that the City Engineer’s cost estimate was $59,672.50 and
since the low bid was so low, the bid figures were double checked. Roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Amphitheater Events – Mr. Groth announced the various amphitheater events
taking place over the next couple months.
Resolution No. 2012-R-15 – Authorizing the Financing of Police Vehicles with
Huntington Bank
Mr. Groth presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-15 that would authorize
the financing of the new police vehicles with Huntington Bank. He stated the
principal amount would be $120,000 with an interest rate of 2.75%.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Yeager to approve Resolution No. 2012-R-15. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi recognized the Police Department for the recent audit conducted
by the Department of Criminal Justice which found the department to be in
compliance.
Leasing of the Lower Level of the Municipal Center – Mayor Moriconi advised
Council that the City has been approached by the Kentucky State Police with a
proposal to lease space in the lower level of the Administration side of the
Municipal Center. He stated the State Police would use the space to conduct
driver testing and take driver i.d. photos. He stated the space would be leased
for roughly $2000 per month. He stated that over the last several months that
he and Mr. Groth have been meeting with the State representatives to discuss
the possibility, but he cannot sign the lease without Council approval.
Council Member Bushong asserted that he was against leasing any part of the
building to anyone. He stated a lot of time was spent on the design of the
building, with the objective being for the City to be able to grow in the
space. He stated he feels if we lease the space then in the future we may find
that we have to lease space for our own employees. Mayor Moriconi advised it
would not be forever and that the lease would be in one year increments. He
stated he would not want to lock the City into a long term lease. Mr. Groth
commented that any future growth the City may have would be in Public Works or
the Police Department, not Administration.
Council Member Reinersman asked John Middleton if they would want to lease for
ten years or more. John Middleton, Circuit Court Clerk, addressed Council by
stating that he has some office space in the Independence Courthouse and that
the State Police currently rent space on Stephenson Road. He stated the growth
in Kenton County is in Independence and he would like to have office space here
for the long term, whether it is here or elsewhere. Council Member Franzen
asked if he would move his offices out of the Courthouse and into here. He
responded that the primary purpose of his office is the court services. But his
office also issues the drivers licenses and he would like to keep his staff
members at the same location as the State drivers testing so that it is more
convenient for the people. Mr. Groth commented that there would be a total of
seven people in the leased space – five State employees and two employees from
the County Circuit Court Clerk’s office.
Council Member Brinker asked how much increased traffic would be coming through
the Municipal Center if the space was leased. Mr. Groth stated that
approximately 250 cars per week.
Council Member Yeager stated that she was against leasing the lower level and
wanted all the City employees in one building. Mr. Brinker asked when the lease
term would begin. Mayor Moriconi stated it would begin in September/October of
this year. Mr. Middleton advised the current lease on Stephenson Road is
through June or July.
Council Member Little stated he shares Council Member Bushong’s sentiments. He
stated the Municipal Center was built larger enough to allow future expansion
of the City offices. He stated that by leasing the space it would displace City
employees currently working in the lower level, alterations to the building
would be needed to accommodate the lessee, the building would incur more wear
and tear with the additional traffic and he feels it would be difficult to
regain the space in the future. He stated the additional revenue would be nice,
but feels it is not worth the trade off. He stated that moving City employees
to another building defeats the purpose of why this building was built in the
first place.
Council Member Reinersman commented that he is in favor of leasing the space
and the lease amount is a fair rental rate and from an investment point of view
it is a good deal. He stated that at the end of the lease period the landlord
(City) would have the option to not renew. He stated he feels the City should
look at this as a temporary means to make up for the shortfall. Council Member
Reinersman also commented that moving three employees is not ideal, but feels
it would put the Building Inspector closer to the other employees. He also
commented that two employees were terminated in recent years because of the
downturn in the economy and less revenue. Council Member Yeager responded that
the revenue is not that far down.
Council Member Brinker asked about leasing the storage space under the Council
Chambers. Mr. Groth stated they would need five offices for a total of 1700-
1800 square feet. He stated the building alterations would be funded by the
State Police. Council Member Franzen stated she would like to speak to the
State Police. She stated she does not want to turn down this proposal now and
would like to table it.
Mayor Moriconi stated he did not expect the Council to vote on this without
first seeing a copy of the proposed lease agreement. He stated if there was any
interest in moving forward he would get a lease for the next meeting. Council
Member Franzen reiterated she would be interested in speaking with the State
Police, getting more information and reviewing a proposed lease. Council Member
Reinersman stated he would like to see more County services in Independence. He
stated he feels like this would be a starting point to establish a foothold in
the City and then as the City grows the County would find other space to lease.
Council Member Franzen stated she feels their presence here could bring more
business into the City. Council Member Yeager expressed concerns that there
will be more disadvantages to the City.
Council Member Bushong asked if there was an alternative location. Mr.
Middleton stated they could stay in their current location on Stephenson Road
or merge with his Covington office. He stated he would prefer a location in the
center of the County. He stated he does not have a “Plan B.” He stated they
have limited funds for rent and that it is unusual for the State to pay rent as
most of the driver testing offices is housed in a County courthouse and that
fact that the State is willing to pay considerably more rent than they are
currently says something. Council Member Little stated, that if that was the
case, why were they leaving their current location. He stated he thinks there
are other alternatives and it is not fair to the City employees to displace
them from their current offices. Council Member Brinker suggested looking at
other available options within the City. Mr. Groth stated he is looking around
for other rental space as well. Mr. Middleton advised that leasing from a
municipality wouldn’t require them to bid out.
In closing, Council Member Franzen stated she wanted to inspect the space in
the lower level and discuss this with the State Police. Mayor Moriconi directed
Mr. Groth to obtain a proposed lease agreement for Council’s review.
Rumpke Curbside Trash Update – Mayor Moriconi advised that the residents will
be getting a letter from Rumpke about the new trash cans that will be
delivered. He suggested residents could use their old cans elsewhere around
their house or set it out for trash pickup. Mr. Groth advised labeling the old
trash can as “trash” so the hauler will know to take it. He stated the City may
also set up a drop off site for those wanting to dispose of their old
containers. Mayor Moriconi advised that additional information will be posted
on the City’s website.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:00 p.m.

July 2, 2012
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 2,
2012 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Dedication – Donna Yeager Amphitheater
Mayor Moriconi announced that in recognition of all her efforts and active
participation in the development of the City parks, that the amphitheater in
Memorial Park would be named the Donna Yeager Amphitheater. He unveiled a
bronze plaque that would be installed at the amphitheater. Mayor Moriconi
stated that Ms. Yeager has also served this community for many years as a
Council Member and is an asset to the City. Council Member Yeager expressed her
surprise for this recognition and thanked Mayor Moriconi and everyone for this
honor.
Mayor Moriconi also announced that the July 4th Celebration events would take
place this weekend at the Memorial Park and Amphitheater with the fireworks
display on Saturday at 10:00 p.m.
Approval of the June 4, 2012, Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, June 4, 2012. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Reinersman. No amendments were noted; roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proclamation – July as Parks and Recreation Month
Mayor Moriconi presented a Proclamation declaring July as Parks and Recreation
Month in Independence.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2005-O-13 Restricting the Issuance
of Building and Zoning Permits to Include Unpaid Assessments or Taxes on the
Property – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2005-O-13 which restricts the issuance of a building permit
when there are outstanding or unremedied violations pending against the owner
of the property. This amendment would further restrict any building or zoning
permits being issued if there are any unpaid taxes or assessments against the
applicant or any entity in which the applicant has an ownership interest. Mr.
Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Discussion Relating to a Possible Amendment to the Nuisance Ordinance
Specifically Regarding All Terrain Vehicles
Mayor Moriconi stated that in speaking with the City staff, it seems that the
City does not currently have legislation that regulates the use of all terrain
vehicles. He stated that he would like to propose that the City adopt some
regulations similar to other communities in the area. City Administrator Dan
Groth stated that he would research other city ordinances and would work with
Mr. Deters to come up with some language to add to the nuisance ordinance. Mr.
Deters commented that it would be a simple modification.
Council Member Little stated that Independence is different than some
communities in that we have rural areas. He stated that all terrain vehicles
are used by hunters. He suggested that a noise decibel reading may solve the
nuisance complaint issues if the noise registered above a specific level that
would be loud enough to be deemed a nuisance. Mr. Deters said the decibel level
could be modified for hunting season. Council Member Reinersman agreed that
addressing the decibel level could be a solution. Mr. Deters commented that it
may be hard to enforce as a nuisance unless someone is there to take a decibel
reading. Chief Shawn Butler stated that according to Kentucky state law in
order to cite the violator the police officer has to witness the violation. He
stated that this is a problem throughout the City and he doesn’t know the
answer to resolving this. Mayor Moriconi stated the challenge in establishing
regulations for all terrain use is that many subdivisions abut farms or
acreage. Council Member Bushong commented that the mufflers on the all terrains
can be adjusted to purposely make it louder. Mr. Groth stated he would work
with Mr. Deters on drafting a proposed ordinance and would send it to them to
review before the next meeting. Mayor Moriconi stated that complaints about the
noise these vehicles make has come up multiple times in the last few years.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Discussion of Proposed Refinancing of the Municipal Center – Mr. Groth advised
Council the City currently has a thirty year bond on the Municipal Center. He
stated the ten-year prepayment penalty will expire in January 2013 and with
record low interest rates it would be a good time to refinance the debt. He
reported that he sought refinancing rates from several banks and received five
proposals. An analysis of the refinancing proposals was presented in the
Council packets. Mr. Groth stated the proposals have been reviewed and he is
recommending that the City refinance the Municipal Center with Ross, Sinclair
and Associates for a fifteen year fixed rate of 2.603%. He stated this would
save the City $1,233,509 in interest over the life of the loan and the building
would be paid off five years sooner.
A motion was made by Council Member Yeager and seconded by Council Member
Reinersman to accept the rate proposal of Ross, Sinclair and Associates and
proceed with the refinancing of the Municipal Center for a fifteen year term
with a fixed rate of 2.603%. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Other Reports: Mr. Groth reported the City has saved $25,000 in insurance
premium costs, due to lower renewal rates for property, liability and workers’
compensation policies.
Announcement: Mr. Groth announced that the Northern Kentucky Area Planning
Commission would be holding an Elected Officials Forum on July 1 from 6:00 – 8:
00 p.m. at the Edgewood Senior Center. He stated that local elected officials
are being invited to provide input for the Direction 2030 Comprehensive Plan.
He stated they are asking that each city have three council members present at
this meeting. He stated he will be attending along with Maura Snyder who is the
City’s representative on the Kenton County Planning Commission.
Leasing of the Lower Level of the Municipal Center
Mr. Groth presented to Council a sample lease agreement which the State has
submitted to the City for a proposal to lease the lower level of the
Administration side of the Municipal Center. He reminded Council that the State
Police is proposing to lease this space for their drivers testing division. He
advised the State drivers testing division is currently located on Stephenson
Road in Erlanger where they have been for more than thirty (30) years. He
stated they would like to move here as their current space is in disrepair. Mr.
Groth stated he would suggest a one-year property lease at $2,100 per month;
this rent would include the cost of the electrical work that the City will have
to do to accommodate their needs. He stated that he feels this is a good move
that will bring more people to the City and support the existing business and
restaurants. He stated in his opinion he feels this is a good deal and may
encourage other government offices to locate in the City. Mayor Moriconi
pointed out that it is a simple, one-page lease agreement.
A lengthy discussion ensued regarding the proposed Agreement. Council Members
shared their concerns with some of the language in the Agreement. Mr. Groth
suggested that Mr. Deters could insert any conditions or stipulations the City
would want and then it could be presented to the State to see if they would
agree. Council Member Franzen stated that this is a divisive issue and wondered
if the State would accept conditions imposed by the City. Council Member Yeager
stated she had a lot of concerns with the Agreement as presented by the State.
Council Member Little suggested the Mayor take a straw poll to see if the
majority of Council was even interested in pursuing a lease agreement. He
stated he had never heard of the Lessee writing their own lease agreement. Mr.
Groth advised that it was a State law and they have the power to do this.
Council Member Little stated there was a host of things that are not even
addressed in the Agreement. He stated he did some research and found that the
monthly lease rate being proposed is below average for this area and does not
take into consideration CAM (Common Area Maintenance) costs. He stated that at
$2,100 per month this will not cover the costs of normal wear and tear on the
building, use of restrooms, hallways, parking lot, increased costs of the
City’s utility bills, etc. He stated that their Agreement requires the City to
provide all the maintenance and insurance costs. Council Member Little stated
this one page agreement doesn’t even begin to cover basic guidelines and
management terms such as leave/enter times, furnishings supplied, key system to
be used, storage, utilities, default, destruction/condemnation, remodel rights,
inspection checklist, default and other services.
Mr. Deters commented that those items would be in a commercial retail lease
agreement and not things that the City should need to worry about with an
agreement with the State.
Council Member Little stated that leasing space to this State agency would
increase the foot traffic in the City building ten-fold.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that he had Mr. Deters prepare a mock lease
agreement and when it was presented to the State representatives the City was
told they would be presenting a State agreement. Council Member Little
commented that the lease agreement the State has presented clearly favors the
tenant. Mr. Deters stated that the agreement form presented is the State
approved form.
Council Member Reinersman stated that he agreed that all the things expressed
by Council Member Little are all parts of the average commercial lease. He
stated that the State of Kentucky has a lot of leased space throughout the
Commonwealth, so it is not uncommon for the Lessee to draft the lease
agreement. He stated that he has not seen the commercial lease rates that
Council Member Little quoted. Mr. Deters commented that CAM is based on square
footage and in this instance it would be a small amount. Council Member Little
stated that most leases require the normal wear to be paid by the tenants.
Council Member Yeager commented that the Municipal Center building was built
large enough so that the City would have space for future growth and was not
intended to house other agencies.
Mayor Moriconi wondered what effect a leased space would have on the City
insurance policies/premiums. Mr. Groth advised he would look into that. Council
Member Yeager asked who would be responsible if one of the State’s clients was
hurt while in the building. Council Member Bushong suggested that probably
everyone would be named in a lawsuit. He stated that some of the State
employees are armed which would change the picture and the City’s exposure.
Council Member Franzen commented that item six on the agreement allows the
State to sublet the space. She stated she does not find that an acceptable
term. Council Member Bushong commented that the lease was a take it or leave
it. Mayor Moriconi agreed that the State agreement terms trump the City and he
doesn’t know if they will accept any revisions to their lease agreement.
Council Member Little stated that he doesn’t think they will delete or add any
terms to what they have presented. Council Member Yeager commented she doesn’t
want to be involved with a tenant dictating the terms of the agreement to the
City. Council Member Reinersman commented that this is the State’s standard
lease.
Council Member Little stated he did a lot of research on this issue. He stated
he feels there is a big difference here in leasing to another government agency
where the City can’t even control the lease agreement. He stated the City is
not supposed to be in the business of leasing things and becoming a landlord.
Council Member Franzen commented that she is not entirely opposed to leasing
the space, but would want some flexibility in drafting the language of the
lease agreement. She stated that this is not an ordinary store front lease
space and is different from their current leased space on Stephenson Road.
Council Member Little commented that if the Council does not support the
principle of leasing a portion of the building then this is a moot point.
Council Member Franzen stated she objects to some parts of the agreement
presented; she stated she would be concerned if they would sub-lease to another
agency. Council Member Bushong commented that he doesn’t object to getting more
information. Council Member Little stated he is against the principle of
leasing space in this building, but if the majority of the Council is open to
the idea and thinks the agreement can be drafted more in the City’s favor then
so be it.
Council Member Reinersman commented that he feels this should be viewed as
providing more convenience to the citizens and good for the economic
development of the City. Council Member Little added that he also doesn’t like
displacing the City employees that currently occupy the space being considered
for leasing.
Mayor Moriconi asked for a show of hands for those who would like more
information. Council Members Brinker, Franzen and Reinersman raised their
hands.
Mayor Moriconi suggested, that taking the CAM into consideration, that perhaps
the State would consider paying more than the proposed $2,100/month in rent. He
stated that he does not think the State is going to make any revisions to the
proposed lease agreement. He stated he also would like item number six deleted.
Council Member Yeager commented that she does not feel this lease proposal has
been thought through. Council Member Bushong wondered if the City would need to
re-do the parking lot for more handicap spaces, etc. Council Member Franzen
stated she would want the City to have an out clause, just as the State does in
item number five. Council Member Little agreed, and the way he reads it the
State can cancel the agreement but the City cannot.
Mayor Moriconi closed the discussion by advising Council they would resume
discussions with the State to get more information and ask for agreement
revisions and a year to year lease term.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor Moriconi recognized and welcomed Mary Kreft, who was sitting in the
audience. He stated Ms. Kreft is the Congressional liaison for U. S.
Congressman Geoff Davis.
Rumpke – Mayor Moriconi advised that the new Rumpke trash and recycling
containers are being delivered to the homeowners. Mr. Groth stated they would
be delivered during August and September. He stated if the 96 gallon is too
large they can downsize to the 65 gallon. He stated that Kenton County will
pick up large white goods/appliances or the residents can take the other larger
items to the County facility on Independence Station Road. If residents decide
to leave their large items at the curb then Rumpke will charge $10 per item. He
stated everyone would receive a small, red recycling bin which is included with
the trash rate. He stated that residents should begin using the new containers
as soon as they get them.
HomeFest – Mayor Moriconi announced that the 2012 HomeFest will in the Manor
Hill Subdivision this year and be held over a three weekend period. He stated
the City is very proud to have this event in the City this year.
Parade – Mayor Moriconi announced that Buddy LaRosa of LaRosa’s Pizzerias will
be the Grand Marshall in this year’s July 4th Celebration Parade to be held on
Saturday, July 7, 2012.
Independence Magazine – Council Member Bushong expressed kudos for the new
version of the Independence newsletter recently published. Mayor Moriconi
stated this magazine will replace the old newsletter format. He advised there
was no additional cost to the City as the business ads supported the
publication. He stated there are many coupons in the magazine and encouraged
everyone to support the local businesses. He stated the next publication will
be in November. Council Member Reinersman stated the magazine was a
collaboration with the local paper – Journal News. The Mayor said the
sponsorship by the local businesses made the magazine a reality.
Privileges of the Floor
Rita Hauke – asked the status of a request she made for a picnic table to be
installed at the Independence Park in the Hartland Subdivision. Recreation
Director, Nita Brake advised that in keeping with ADA compliance, that a
handicap table had to be ordered. She stated the concrete pad for the table was
poured last week. Mayor Moriconi commented that this seemingly small request
was more involved than one would think, but it should be fulfilled soon.
Ms. Hauke also presented some zoning complaints which she feels has been in
violation for years and needs to be addressed. Mayor Moriconi stated that with
24,000 residents and only one employee to handle this workload that it is
impossible to get everything, but he appreciates her going around town to bring
these to the City’s attention.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:24 p.m.
