                     Christian J. Moriconi, Mayor
ATTEST:
_____________________________________
Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
August 6, 2012
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 6,
2012 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Chris Reinersman and Donna Yeager. Council
Member Mike Little was absent. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the July 2, 2012, Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, July 2, 2012. Council Member Reinersman so moved, with
second by Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted; roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Municipal Order No. 2012-O-01 – Approving the Advertisement of Bids for the Re-
bonding of the Municipal Center Debt
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration a municipal order
that would approve the advertisement for the bid and distribution of a
preliminary official statement for the purchase of City general obligation
refunding bonds for an approximate aggregate amount of $4,170,000. Mayor
Moriconi advised Council that the refinancing of the Municipal Center debt
would cut the interest rate by approximately one-half. He introduced bond
counsel Dirk Bedarff from Peck, Shaffer & Williams who was present to give a
brief explanation of the bonding process and answer any questions the Council
Members might have. Mr. Deters read Municipal Order No. 2012-O-01.
Council Member Franzen moved to adopt Municipal Order No. 2012-O-01, seconded
by Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered with all ayes. Motion
carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Authorizing the Issuance of General Obligation Bonds for
the Refinancing of the Municipal Center Building – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
authorize the issuance of general obligation refunding bonds (Series 2012) in
the aggregate principal amount of $4,175,000 to refund the outstanding
principal amount (Series 2003) the proceeds of which were used to finance and
refinance the City’s Municipal Building. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance
a first reading.
Mayor Moriconi asked bond counsel Mr. Bedarff if the proposed interest rate for
the re-bonding could actually be lower by the date of the closing. Mr. Bedarff
advised that in accordance with Kentucky law the bonds will be sold by way of
the bidding process, therefore the rate that will be locked in will be that
which is awarded the bid, so it will depend on the market at the time the bids
are submitted. He stated the rate could be less, but ultimately the City will
accept the lowest bid as submitted. Mr. Bedarff commented that municipal bonds
are currently at a historic low. Mr. Groth, City Administrator advised Council
that the bonds will be sold on Wednesday, September 12, 2012 so the interest
rate will be determined on that date.
There being no further questions, Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Bedarff.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Adding the Downtown
Independence [DI] Zone to the Zoning Ordinance along with the Necessary Cross
References and Sign Regulations – KCPC Case No. 2072R – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that the four proposed ordinances that would
address the zoning text and map amendments for the Downtown Independence area
would have first readings tonight. He stated he would schedule a special
meeting for later this month to have the second readings and possible adoption.
Mayor Moriconi stated he would allow public comments from the citizens
interested in addressing the Council regarding these zone changes.
Mayor Moriconi presented the first proposed zone change that would amend the
zoning text to add the Downtown Independence [DI] zone, provide for cross
references and sign regulations in the DI zone.
Council Member Reinersman asked the Council Members to consider the Downtown
Small Area Study that was adopted in 2007 as he believes the proposed text
amendment to add the DI zone addresses the intent of the Study. Mayor Moriconi
expressed some concern regarding drive-through facilities and how that might
affect U.S. Bank (at the corner of McCullum and Madison) if a disaster occurred
and they would not be permitted to rebuild as they are today. Council Member
Reinersman responded that the bank is basically grandfathered in, but if the
building was destroyed and they wanted to rebuild it would take the City and/or
a private resident to request a Board of Adjustment ruling to allow a non-
conforming use. Council Member Franzen asked if the bank would be allowed to
change the location of their ATM machine. Andy Videkovich, Senior Planner with
NKAPC commented that in his opinion they could not change the location as it
would not be a matter of right. Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld advised
that the ATM location pre-exists the zone so it would take the City or a
citizen to request a Board of Adjustment determination to terminate the bank’s
land use. Council Member Franzen suggested changing the proposed text to allow
drive through lanes for banks and pharmacies. She stated that she did not feel
it would detract from the area. Council Member Reinersman agreed that it would
not hurt the zone and was open to making the change. Council Members Yeager and
Brinker agreed that needed to be allowed for the banks and pharmacies. Council
Member Brinker thought it could delay the rebuild if the drive though lanes
became an issue that had to be taken before the Board of Adjustment. Council
Member Reinersman advised that the committee had considered the drive through
lanes to generate more traffic in the area which is the reason they were
excluded.
Mr. Deters advised this is a minor change to the proposed text, so the
consensus of Council was to allow drive through lanes for banks and pharmacies.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave a first reading to the
proposed ordinance adding the Downtown Independence Zone to the zoning text and
amending page twenty-one to allow drive through lanes for banks and pharmacies
for sub-district one and two.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Chapter 93 of the Code of Ordinances to Add a
Definition for All Terrain Vehicles (ATV’s) and Regulate the Operation Thereof
– 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend the nuisance ordinance by providing a definition of an all-terrain
vehicle (ATV) and regulating the operation of the vehicles. Mayor Moriconi read
the entire text that would be added. Mr. Deters advised that, in summary, the
use of ATV’s would be illegal before 8:00 a.m. or after 10:00 p.m. unless being
used by hunters during hunting season and that any ATV without the muffler
system provided by the manufacturer would be prohibited.
Mayor Moriconi stated that in recent years the City has increasingly received
complaints from residents that abut farm land or acreage where the ATV’s are
causing a nuisance to the citizens. He stated the City is trying to find a
balance without restricting anyone’s freedoms. Council Member Brinker commented
that since this ordinance also prohibits the operation of an ATV within 150
feet of any dwelling on a lot or parcel he feels this should clear up any issue
and continue to allow those with acreage to operate them within the permitted
time frame.
Joe Massey, 9665 Cloverridge Drive, Independence – addressed Council in favor
of adopting regulations for the use of ATV’s. He stated his property and that
of his neighbor’s border property along Senour Road. He stated the noise from
the ATV’s is so loud that they cannot sit on their decks. He said it is even
audible when in the house with the doors and windows closed. He stated the ATV
use occurs several times a night. He expressed concern that the proposed
ordinance will even solve the problem. Council Member Yeager suggested calling
the police. A brief discussion ensued. Ms. Wuestefeld advised that in order for
a police officer to issue a citation they would have to witness the offense.
She stated the resident could file a civil suit with audio/visual proof of the
violation. Mr. Deters commented that the current nuisance ordinance only has
general parameters which do not pertain to ATV’s.
Jamie Ellison, Independence – spoke against regulating the use of ATV’s. He
stated he uses his ATV on a small 3-acre flag lot on Sylvan Drive and he is
respectful of the neighboring properties. He stated the proposed ordinance’s
condition of 150 feet of any dwelling would prevent him from using his ATV on
his property. He went on to say that the decibel rating of an ATV is equivalent
to that of the average lawn mower, or weedeater. Mr. Ellison said he is
respectful of his neighbors and should be free to enjoy his ATV.
Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Ellison that he does not recall any complaints from
the Sylvan Drive area. He stated that the City would issue citations only on a
complaint basis.
Richard Wolfe, 10280 Manassas Drive, Independence – addressed Council in favor
of the proposed ordinance. He stated the noise from the ATV’s has gotten
progressively worse in his neighborhood over the last few years. He said he
doesn’t oppose the use of ATV’s but it should be done in a respectful way.
Mayor Moriconi stated that he thinks the proposed ordinance will help with some
enforcement.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Adding the Conservation
Development/Single-Family Overlay Zone to the Zoning Ordinance along with the
Necessary Cross References – KCPC Case No. 2073R - 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance for a text
amendment to the zoning ordinance that would add the conservation development/
single-family (CD-SF) overlay zone. He explained that the conversation overlay
would be another development option available to a potential developer. Council
Member Franzen commented that the overlay option will not take away any
property rights, but in fact will add another development option to the seller
and buyer. There was a brief discussion and the Mr. Deters gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.
Recess
Council Member Franzen moved to take a brief recess, seconded by Council Member
Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman to reconvene the meeting,
seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment Changing an Approximately 116-
Acre Area Locating along the North and South Sides of McCullum Pike From R-1C,
R-1D and NC to R-1C (CD-SF), R-1D (CD-SF) and NC (CD-SF) Zones– KCPC Case No.
2074R – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve a zoning map amendment changing an approximate 116-acre area located
along the north and south sides of McCullum Pike between Madison Pike and KY17,
approximately 600 feet east of Madison Pike and 1300 feet west of KY17 from R-
1C, R-1D and NC to R-1C (CD-SF), R-1D (CD-SF) and NC (CD-SF) zones.
Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Map Amendment Changing an Approximately 60-
Acre Area Located along the East/West Sides on Madison Pike Between
Independence Station Road and Locust Road from R-1C, R-1D and NC to DI
(Downtown Independence) Zone – KCPC Case No. 2075R - 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
approve a map amendment changing an approximate 60-acre area located along the
east and west sides on Madison Pike between Independence Station Road and
Locust Road from R-1C, R-1D and NC to DI (Downtown Independence) zone.
Council Member Reinersman commented that a request was made by St. Cecilia
Church to be removed from the map amendment area. He stated St. Cecilia’s
request was based on their future development plans which they feel may not
conform to the Downtown Independence (DI) zone. He stated their request was
considered and it was decided to delete the church properties from the zone

Resolution Numbers 2012-R-16 & 2012-R-17 – Authorizing a Text Amendment
Application to Add the Gateway Mixed Use (GMU) Zone to the Zoning Ordinance & a
Map Amendment Application to Change the Zoning of an Approximate 42-Acre Area
Located on the North and South Sides of McCullum Pike and West of New KY17 from
R-1C and R-1D to Gateway Mixed Use Zone
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution Numbers 2012-R-16 & 2012-R-17
which would authorize submitting a text amendment application, as well as a map
amendment application to the NKAPC to add the Gateway Mixed Use (GMU) zone to
the official zoning ordinance and change the zone of approximately 42 acres
located on the north and south sides of McCullum Pike and west of New KY17 from
R-1C and R-1D to Gateway Mixed Use (GMU) zone. He stated that the Gateway Mixed
Use zone is the last of the recommended text and map zone changes as submitted
by the Steering Committee.
Council Member Reinersman advised there were some changes made to the original
text draft submitted by the Steering Committee. He stated some property owners
in the Gateway area had voiced some concerns which were discussed and addressed

A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member

Resolution No. 2012-R-18 – Adopting the NKADD Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-18 which would adopt
the NKADD regional Hazard Mitigation Plan which is a requirement of FEMA in
order to receive future funding in the case of natural hazard damages to people
and properties in the area.
Mr. Groth advised that the Northern Kentucky Area Development District is
asking that all communities in this region execute this resolution.
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Resolution No. 2012-R-18, seconded by

Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Text Amendment Amending the Regulations
Pertaining to Parking and/or Storing of Recreational Vehicles, Inoperable

Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration a proposed
ordinance that would approve a zoning text amendment amending the regulations
pertaining to parking or storing of trailers, mobile homes, campers, inoperable
vehicles and other such type of equipment. He stated the proposed amendment
added two words “or owner” in Section 9.23 (c) (1). He stated this would permit
the storage of a recreational vehicle by the occupier “or owner” of the

Ordinance No. 2012-O-06 – Amending Ordinance No. 2005-O-13 Restricting the

06 which would approve the amendment of Ordinance No. 2005-O-13 which restricts

City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Award Bid for Sylvan Drive Storm Sewer Improvements
Mr. Groth presented to Council the results of the bids received for the project
known as the Sylvan Drive Storm Sewer Improvements. He stated that the City
received nine bids ranging from a low of $105,987 to a high bid of $163,253. He
stated the city engineer is recommending the City award the contract to Lonkard
Construction as the low bidder in the amount of $105,987. Mr. Groth advised
Council that this is a collaborative project with the Sanitation District and
the City will split the cost of the improvements with the District. Mayor
Moriconi advised that the engineer’s cost estimate for this project was
$143,190 and the City was fortunate to receive very aggressive bids for this
project resulting in a $37,000 savings on this project.
Council Member Franzen moved to award the bid to Lonkard Construction as the
best and lowest bid in the amount of $105,987. The motion was seconded by
Council Member Reinersman. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0.
Declare Surplus Property and Authorize Auction of 2000 Ford Crown Vic Police

W7YX206615 as surplus property to be disposed of via auction. Council Member

At 8:44 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to enter into an executive session in

August 20, 2012
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in special session
on Monday, August 20, 2012 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with
Mayor Christian J. Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to
order and opened with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol
Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna Yeager. Also present was City
Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Moriconi welcomed everyone and announced this Special meeting of Council
was being held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
·   Ordinance No. 2012-O-07 – Authorizing the Issuance of General Obligation
Refunding Bonds for the Refinancing of the Municipal Center Building – 2nd
Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2012-O-08 – Approving a Text Amendment Adding the Downtown
Independence (DI) Zone to the Zoning Ordinance along with Necessary Cross
References and Sign Regulations – 2nd Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2012-O-09 – Approving a Text Amendment Adding the
Conservation Development/Single-Family Overlay Zone to the Zoning Ordinance
along with Necessary Cross References – 2nd Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2012-O-10 – Approving a Map Amendment Changing an Approximate
116-Acre Area Located along the North and South Sides of McCullum Pike – 2nd
Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2012-O-11 – Approving a Map Amendment Changing an Approximate
60-Acre Area Located along the East and West Sides on Madison Pike Between
Independence Station Road & Locust Road from R-1C, R-1D and NC to DI (Downtown
Independence) Zone – 2nd Reading
·   Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2012 Tax Rates for Real Estate and
Tangible Property – 1st Reading
·   Ordinance No. 2012-O-12 – Approving a Text Amendment Relating to the
Regulations of Parking and/or Storing of Recreational Vehicles, Inoperable
Vehicles, etc. – 2nd Reading
Ordinance No. 2012-O-07 – Authorizing the Issuance of General Obligation Bonds
for the Refinancing of the Municipal Center Building – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2012-O-07 – an
ordinance that would authorize the issuance of general obligation refunding
bonds (Series 2012) in the aggregate principal amount of $4,175,000 to refund
the outstanding principal amount (Series 2003) the proceeds of which were used
to finance and refinance the City’s Municipal Building. Mr. Deters gave
Ordinance No. 2012-O-07 a second reading.
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2012-O-07, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-08 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Adding the Downtown
Independence [DI] Zone to the Zoning Ordinance along with the Necessary Cross
References and Sign Regulations – KCPC Case No. 2072R – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2012-O-
08. This ordinance would approve a zoning text amendment to add a new zone
called the Downtown
Independence [DI] zone, provide for cross references as well as sign
regulations in the DI zone. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2012-O-08 a second
reading.
Council Member Little commented that this text amendment would just create the
DI zone in the zoning ordinance. Don Nienaber, 57 McCullum Road, Independence,
questioned the exempting of the bank and St. Cecilia Church from the possible
DI zone area. Council Member Reinersman explained that U.S. Bank was not
exempted but that St. Cecilia Church had requested exemption and it was granted
as the church property was on the outer edge. He advised that St. Cecilia would
like to expand in the future and possibly build a bell tower which would exceed
the parameter of this amendment. He stated the deletion of St. Cecilia Church
property was made before the application was submitted to the NKAPC. Mr.
Nienaber also expressed some concern about gas stations in the area and felt
they should be exempt as well. Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld advised
that the B & B auto repair shop is currently a non-conforming use which could
be transferred to a new owner.
Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview Court, Independence – expressed concern that apartment
buildings would be permitted in the Downtown Independence zone and stated that
she did not feel this should be allowed. Council Member Reinersman stated this
is the first objection he has heard about the apartments, besides the June 7th
Kenton County Planning Commission hearing,.Council Member Brinker wondered if a
small parcel would be large enough to even accommodate an apartment building.
Ms. Hauke stated that two parcels could be merged to accommodate an apartment
building. She also stated that she is concerned that this new zone would not
permit some types of businesses. Council Member Reinersman advised that twenty-
three new uses would be added to the uses currently allowed. He agreed that
some uses would not be allowed, such as warehouses, factories and mini storage
units, but he said those uses are not allowed now and the City would not want
those types of businesses in the downtown area in the future.
Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, Independence – stated his wife spoke out
against permitting apartments in the downtown area at the KCPC public hearing
meeting.
Mary Baum, 83 McCullum Road, Independence – presented Mayor Moriconi with two
petitions opposing the proposed map and text amendments establishing the
Downtown Independence [DI] zone. She stated this petition was also presented at
the KCPC public hearing on this issue. Additionally she stated she would like
to go on record as objecting to the apartment units being a permitted land use.
Chuck Baum commented that the DI zone would also permit parking garages.
Council Member Franzen stated she is hearing the concerns being expressed about
restricting businesses in the downtown area and the opposition to creating the
Downtown Independence zone yet the new zone will permit twenty three additional
types of businesses that are not currently allowed. Mayor Moriconi expressed
his concerns to permitting apartments in this zone, which he stated he wouldn’t
want next to him either. James Williamson, 144-B McCullum Road, Independence -
commented that there is adequate property outside the area for the development
of apartment buildings. Mayor Moriconi stated the PUD mixed use development on
Centennial Boulevard has worked well.
Council Member Reinersman stated he has no objection to removing the free-
standing apartment buildings in the Downtown Independence zone, but feels the
store fronts should be allowed to rent the second floor as apartments.
Council Member Reinersman stated that multiple public meetings were held with
the property owners during the process of drafting these text and map
amendments and as a result many changes were made. He stated the committee
worked hard to address the property owners and residents concerns, but the fact
is that some people just don’t want to see any changes. He stated the city has
grown at a rapid pace and these changes will achieve some of the goals outlined
in the Downtown Small Area Study adopted in 2007. Council Member Little stated
he did not agree with the Study in its entirety, but that the document was
adopted as a whole. He stated he is not so much concerned with meeting the
recommendations of the Small Area Study as he is in addressing the resident’s
needs and concerns. Council Member Reinersman stated that the residents pointed
out the flaws in the original draft, which were addressed and he feels that
they have produced a good document. He stated that email notices were sent to
many of the interested residents to remind them of tonight’s meeting and very
few are in attendance.
Mayor Moriconi stated that he feels there is a consensus to delete the eight
apartment unit buildings in the proposed plan. There was a brief discussion;
the eight unit apartment notations were located in the proposed text and
deleted in accordance with the Council.
Mayor Moriconi commented that the bottom line is that this text amendment opens
the possibility for twenty-three more types of businesses currently not
permitted in the downtown area.
There being no further discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Reinersman to approve Ordinance No. 2012-O-08
with a minor modification deleting the text for multi-family uses. Roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-09 – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Adding the
Conservation Development/Single-Family Overlay Zone to the Zoning Ordinance
along with the Necessary Cross References – KCPC Case No. 2073R – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
for a text amendment to the zoning ordinance that would add the conservation
development/single-family (CD-SF) overlay zone.
Council Member Reinersman stated this proposal was also presented at the public
meetings. He stated that the conservation development/single-family overlay
zone would not be mandatory, but an optional plan available to a developer.
Council Member Franzen stated that the overlay development plan would go
through a Stage I approval and the City’s Zoning Administrator would determine,
if needed, to come back to Council for approval.
Council Member Little expressed some concern with regard to the maintenance and
ownership of open space and the language that if a Homeowners Association would
become defunct then the City would take over ownership of the green space. He
stated he did not feel the City should be in the business of taking over the
operation of a Homeowners Association. Mr. Deters advised that the clause in
the document would basically allow the City to step in and take over the
maintenance of the common open space and determine how to dispose of the land.
Council Member Little wondered if there was a better way to handle this. Mayor
Moriconi commented that this would allow the City to sell the common land to
adjoining property owners and get out of the maintenance of the land as quickly
as possible. Mr. Deters stated the fee simple title to the land would let the
City subdivide the land or dispose of the land any way the City saw fit to do
so. Council Member Little thought that it might be difficult to dispose of such
a large area [a 30% common space]. Mr. Deters stated it would be at the City’s
discretion whether or not to assume the common land of a defunct Homeowners’
Association, but that the City has had some success in the past in disposing
City property. Council Member Franzen advised that a developer would have to
show the City a viable plan for a conservation area and the City would then
impose conditions on the development.
Further discussion focused on the misunderstanding and misinformation that has
circulated about the proposed text and map amendments for the downtown area.
Residents in attendance expressed their concerns for how their property values
would be affected and how the changes would affect the local businesses in the
area as well as the White’s farm. They also questioned the need for an overlay
zone that would be optional and did not see the purpose it would serve. Council
Member Franzen explained that only the City can apply for and adopt a text
amendment to the zoning laws and by adding these new zones this would be
available for future development. Council Member Reinersman advised that if a
developer wanted to build patio homes they couldn’t do it because the City’s
doesn’t currently have the zone that would permit that type of development. He
stated without the zone existing the developer might look elsewhere so they
wouldn’t have to go through a lengthy process it would take to request and wait
for the city to adopt the zone needed.
Mary Baum stated she was concerned about the number of homes that could be
allowed with the conservation district zone. She did not feel there was a good
transition of mixed use between the conservation district and McCullum Road and
that the residents of McCullum Road were not being represented. Council Member
Reinersman explained the overlay zone development would provide 30% green space
and build on the remaining area by parceling smaller lots. He stated that the
City does not have many housing options for empty nesters and seniors and as
the economy continues to rebound the City will remain one of the fastest
growing communities in this region. He reiterated that the committee reached
out to the residents on numerous occasions during this process to obtain their
input.
Council Member Bushong addressed the concerns raised about Homeowners’
Associations. He stated that while some people don’t think they are a good
thing, he has seen in his neighborhood that having a strong management company
for the Associations can make them very successful. He stated his neighborhood
of 440 property owners has a very expansive green space which is well
maintained by the management company. He said the City had one Homeowners
Association – Hunters Green subdivision – that went defunct many years ago, but
he feels it unlikely that would ever happen again. Council Member Little stated
his subdivision also has a Homeowner’s Association, but they do not have any
common areas to be maintained by the Association. Council Member Reinersman
agreed that it is unlikely that future Homeowner’s Associations would fail, and
generally it is a failed developer that can cause the problem.
Council Member Little asked why the properties on the north side of McCullum
were left out of the zone change. Council Member Reinersman responded that the
north side has many smaller, occupied parcels while the south side has the
larger parcels which would be open for development. He stated he is open to
including the north side if this is something Council would like.
Council Member Brinker commented that he feels that very little implementation
has resulted from the 2007 Downtown Small Area Study and now that the City is
taking steps to put some of the recommendations in place that there seems to be
a lot of resistance to move forward. Council Member Reinersman stated that the
committee started working on this proposal in April 2010. Council Member
Franzen stated that she and Council Member Reinersman scheduled a meeting for
the residents in the Hartland subdivision to address their concerns and
approximately twenty people showed up. She stated the City has not taken this
proposal lightly, has done due diligence, and while everyone may not agree she
feels this is a good plan for the City. Council Member Little commented that
this doesn’t benefit a developer when they have to deal with multiple owners to
acquire land. He stated that he feels if one property owner feels their rights
are being violated then he is against this proposal. Council Member Franzen
disagreed that one property owner’s opposition should outweigh several that may
be in favor of it. Council Member Reinersman stated that the City has to look
at the proposal as a whole, find a middle ground and do what is in the best
interest of the entire City. He stated he is yet to hear what is harming the
property owners by approving this proposal.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence – commented that when she was on the
City Council in 2004-2005 when the Downtown Small Area Study was presented, she
recalls asking how long the Study would be relevant and one of the Senior
Planners with the Northern Kentucky Planning Commission responded that it was
already obsolete.
Mr. Williamson, 144-B McCullum Road, Independence - commented that he doesn’t
know anyone that is in favor of these text and map amendments. He stated he
does not feel the City is listening to the property owners. Council Member
Reinersman responded that very few opposers have attended this meeting. Council
Member Franzen commented that when the City gives property owners more options
for future development of their land that this should be considered a benefit.
She stated she does not know how this is being interpreted as taking away the
owners rights. She stated that if a developer wants to change the zone they can
come to the City and make the request, but by adding this option for an overlay
zone this now gives them two options for development.
Mayor Moriconi closed the discussion. A motion was made by Council Member
Reinersman to adopt Ordinance No. 2012-O-09, seconded by Council Member
Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-10 – Approving a Map Amendment Changing an Approximate
116-Acre Area Locating along the North and South Sides of McCullum Pike From R-
1C, R-1D and NC to R-1C (CD-SF), R-1D (CD-SF) and NC (CD-SF) Zones– KCPC Case
No. 2074R – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading a proposed ordinance
that would approve a zoning map amendment changing an approximate 116-acre area
located along the north and south sides of McCullum Pike between Madison Pike
and KY17, approximately 600 feet east of Madison Pike and 1300 feet west of
KY17 from R-1C, R-1D and NC to R-1C (CD-SF), R-1D (CD-SF) and NC (CD-SF) zones.
Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2012-O-10.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that on a proposed map amendment if the vote
results in a tie, then the recommendation given by the Kenton County Planning
Commission to approve this map amendment would go into effect within ninety
days of the date of the Commission’s public hearing which was June 7, 2012. Mr.
Deters added that it takes the majority of the Council to turn down this
proposed map amendment and that if no action is taken by the Council then it
becomes law as recommended by the Planning Commission.
There being no discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and
seconded by Council Member Franzen to approve Ordinance No. 2012-O-10. Roll was
called and answered with four ayes and two no votes cast by Council Members
Little and Bushong. Motion carried 4-2.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-11 – Approving a Map Amendment Changing an Approximate 60-
Acre Area Located along the East/West Sides on Madison Pike Between
Independence Station Road and Locust Road from R-1C, R-1D and NC to DI
(Downtown Independence) Zone – KCPC Case No. 2075R – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2012-O-
11, an ordinance that would approve a map amendment changing an approximate 60-
acre area located along the east and west sides on Madison Pike between
Independence Station Road and Locust Road from R-1C, R-1D and NC to DI
(Downtown Independence) zone. Mr. Deters read Ordinance No. 2012-O-11.
There was brief discussion regarding the parcels that were removed from the
original proposal – those parcels being, 5301-5303 Madison Pike, 5305 Madison
Pike (St. Cecilia Church and school) and 5323 Madison Pike.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and second by Council Member
Franzen to approve Ordinance No. 2012-O-11. Roll was called and answered with
four ayes and two no votes cast by Council Members Bushong and Little. Motion
carried 4-2.
Recess
Council Member Little moved to take a brief recess, seconded by Council Member
Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen to reconvene the meeting, seconded
by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Property Tax Rates for 2012 – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
adopt the 2012 real estate tax rate at $0.237 dollars for each one hundred
dollars of the assessed value and a personal property tax rate of $0.656
dollars for each one hundred dollars of the assessed value. Mr. Deters gave the
ordinance a first reading.
Ordinance No. 2012-O-12 – Approving a Text Amendment Amending the Regulations
Pertaining to Parking and/or Storing of Recreational Vehicles, Inoperable
Vehicles, etc.- KCPC Case No. 2083R – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2012-O-
12 approving a zoning text amendment amending the regulations pertaining to
parking or storing of trailers, mobile homes, campers, inoperable vehicles and
other such type of equipment. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2012-O-12 a second
reading.
Council Member Franzen stated she is not in favor of this proposed amendment
that would allow the property owner to store their recreational type vehicles
without actually living at that residence and possibly living in another city.
Mr. Groth commented that the current ordinance requires the owner to also be
the occupant of the property where the recreational vehicle is stored. Council
Member Yeager stated she sponsored this amendment after she was approached by a
property owner that requested this change.
After a brief discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Yeager and
seconded by Council Member Little to adopt Ordinance No. 2012-O-12. Roll was
called and resulted in a tie vote. Council Members voting yes were Yeager,
Little and Brinker with no votes cast by Council Members Reinersman, Bushong
and Franzen. Mr. Deters advised Council that a tie vote defeats Ordinance No.
2012-O-12 because a text amendment requires a majority vote by the Council to
become law and does not defer to the Kenton County Planning Commission’s
recommendation for approval.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Franzen moved to adjourn the
meeting, seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:25 p.m.

Ordinance No. 2012-O-13 – Adopting Real and Personal Property Tax Rates for
2012 – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for their consideration the second reading

of $0.237 Dollars for each One Hundred Dollars ($100.00) of the value thereof,
and an ad valorem tax on all personal property, other than motor vehicles, at

Ordinance No. 2012-O-14 – Amending Section 93 of the Code of Ordinances to Add
a Definition for All Terrain Vehicles and Providing Regulations for Their Use –
2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for the second reading of the above ordinance which
would add the following language to Chapter 93 of the City Code of Ordinances,
Section .03, adding Subsection (Q), which states it shall be declared a
nuisance to operate any ATV within the City, on any day, before 8:00 a.m. or
after 10:00 p.m., except for legal hunting purposes or when being used in an
emergency. It will also be illegal to operate at any speed in excess of the
minimum speed required to maintain the forward motion of the ATV while it is
within 150 feet of any dwelling on a lot or parcel of real estate other than
that upon which the ATV is being operated, and if the sound unreasonably
interferes with the residential use and enjoyment of any other lot or parcel of
real estate. Motion was made by Council Member Chris Reinersman to approve the
above ordinance and seconded by Council Member Mike Little. All members voted
“aye” – motion carried.
Resolution No. 2012-R-19 – Adopting the Northern Kentucky Solid Waste
Management Plan 2013 – 2017 Update
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council the above Resolution that would sign off on
the five-year plan of the Northern Kentucky Solid Waste Management Plan for the
Northern Kentucky Solid Waste Management Area, which comprises the Counties of
Kenton, Boone, and Campbell. City Administrator Dan Groth explained the history
of the NKSWMA and how, in addition to the County Governments approving the
plan, Kentucky State EPA also wants the larger cities in the counties to also
show approval for the plan. Motion was made by Council Member Carol Franzen to
adopt the above resolution, seconded by Council Member Donna Yeager. All
members voted “aye – motion carried.
Adjournment
There being no further business, Council Member Tom Brinker moved to adjourn
the meeting, seconded by Council Member Donna Yeager – all “ayes” – motion
carried and the meeting adjourned at 7:29 p.m.

ATTEST:
____________________________________
Dan Groth, City Administrator
October 1, 2012
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
1, 2012 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the September 10, 2012, Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, September 10, 2012. Council Member Franzen so moved,
with second by Council Member Bushong. Amendments were noted; roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Recognition of P.O. Jeff Young by American Legion Riders
American Legion Riders, Post 4, Director Dave Brotherton, a resident of
Independence, recognized Independence Police Officer Jeff Young for his
participation on Saturday, August 28th for assisting with traffic control
during the motorcycle escort of 225 soldiers from the Kentucky National Guard
1204th Aviation Support Battalion. He stated the Riders met the soldiers at the
Indiana/Kentucky state line, after a tour of duty in Kuwait and were escorted
to a welcome home event at the Florence Freedom Center.
Presentation of the “Spirit of 76” Print by Independence Resident, Gerald
Czulewicz
Mayor Moriconi introduced Independence resident, Gerald Czulewicz, who
presented the City with a print known as the “Spirit of 76” by Archibald
Willard.
Mr. Czulewicz addressed Council by saying it was an honor and a privilege to
present this print to the City. He stated he owned the original painting for
twenty-five years before gifting it to the national collection. He stated the
original painting is currently on display in the Benjamin Franklin State Dining
Room of the White House. Mr. Czulewicz stated he spent many years collecting
Uncle Sam memorabilia; a collection that toured the nation for about fourteen
years. He stated he still has a major part of this collection in his possession
and would like to put it on exhibit sometime in the future as part of a City
event.
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a copy of a book authored by Mr. Czulewicz
which shows his Uncle Sam collection. He advised the Mr. Czulewicz has
personally autographed the book and donated it to the City as well. Mayor
Moriconi thanked him for these gifts and stated he would find a prominent place
to display the print.
Mayor Moriconi also thanked Council Member Yeager for a historical print she
found and has donated to the City.
Presentation by Rhonda Whitaker, Duke Energy Area Representative Regarding the
Proposed 911 Parcel Service Fee
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed Resolution that would express
opposition to the imposition of a 911 parcel service fee for the purpose of
funding a consolidated dispatching center. He went on to say that for 2012 the
Kenton County Fiscal Court has imposed an $85 fee which has been placed on the
2012 property tax bills. He stated this resolution calls upon the members of
the Fiscal Court to re-evaluate their support of the parcel service fee and
support this fee being placed on utility bills. He introduced Rhonda Whitaker,
the Area Representative for Duke Energy who would like to address Council on
this matter and share Duke Energy’s stance on this proposal and why they do not
feel placing this fee on the energy bills is the best option.
Ms. Whitaker stated she realizes that some cities are considering the option to
fund the 911 dispatch center by way of a fee placed on electric bills. She
stated she wanted to educate Council on some issues to consider that they may
not be aware of. She stated that Duke Energy opposes this proposal and that
Owen Electric shares their view as this will set a dangerous precedent on other
private businesses. Ms. Whitaker stated they believe the County does not have
the legal authority to force a private entity to act as a fee and tax collector
and while there are differing legal opinions they don’t believe it can be
legally imposed. She stated that Duke Energy services 7,100,000 customers in
six states and if this was imposed in Kenton County they feel that other
counties in those six states would follow suit. She stated they understand that
the declining number of telephone land lines and had an impact on the declining
revenues to support the dispatching center, but Duke would encourage the County
to look at ways to become more efficient by merging services.
Ms. Whitaker distributed a hand-out that listed the various economic
development and community relation efforts by Duke Energy in this region.
She advised Council that Kenton County did not explore the option of placing
this fee on the electric bills with Duke Energy. She stated they had to be
proactive in opening the lines of discussion. Ms. Whitaker stated that Duke
Energy is also aware there are a lot of challenges with placing the fee on the
real estate property taxes (since everyone does not own property), so there is
a need to explore other options. She encouraged the Fiscal Court to form a
committee to look at other options.
Ms. Whitaker stated that Duke does collect school gross receipts tax for the
state, but this is because the company’s been regulated to do so and becomes
the taxpayer, not the tax collector. She went on to quote K.R.S. mandates on
collecting service fees and surcharges.
She stated that she knows that placing the fee on the utility bills seems like
an expedient method of collection, but they do not feel it is the best option.
There was a brief question and answer session with Ms. Whitaker regarding what
determines the types of tax/fees that can be placed on a public utility bill.
She responded that any fee would have to be regulated under tariff law and be
approved by the Public Services Commission (PSC).
Council Member Franzen stated that she opposes the County’s position to place
the 911 dispatch fee on the utility bills and feels they need to explore
alternate ways to fund the dispatch center. She asked Ms. Whitaker if Duke
Energy would share their customer address file with the County for purposes of
sending a separate bill for the fee. Ms. Whitaker stated that she does not feel
they could legally provide this data which is considered proprietary
information.
Council Member Reinersman asked if this is the first time Duke has been asked
to collect this type of fee. Ms. Whitaker responded yes, this is the first time
this has been requested. She stated they have made inquiries to other utility
companies to see if they have been asked to collect this type fee and found
that those companies had never been asked.
Mayor Moriconi commented there has been some talk about placing the fee on cell
phone bills, but that it was dismissed because there are too many cell phone
providers to make this a viable option.
Mayor Moriconi thanked Ms. Whitaker for discussing this issue with the Council.
She encouraged everyone to contact her if they had any further questions or
needed more information.
Council Member Franzen encouraged the Council Members to call the members of
the Fiscal Court if they had any suggestions for alternate solutions for
funding the dispatch center. She also stated that she works for the Kenton
County Sheriff’s office and advised that a resident can pay their county taxes
and refuse to pay the 911 fee which is on the tax bill. She said they have the
ability to split the bill if the taxpayer does not want to pay the fee. She
stated a list of names that did not pay the fee will be forwarded to the County
Attorney and he will decide how to handle those that did not pay the fee. Mayor
Moriconi advised there will be legal consequences for those not paying the fee.
Further discussion centered on when the 911 fee would be eliminated from the
land line phone bills. Mr. Groth stated he was not sure when that would happen.
Council Member Franzen stated she was told it would be removed before the tax
bills were mailed. She stated that the Erlanger residents are paying the fee
twice. She stated that exemptions can also be filed by taxpayers that own
vacant property, etc. Mayor Moriconi stated there is an appeal application that
can be submitted to the Appeal Board that has been established by the Fiscal
Court. Council Member Franzen advised that all complaints regarding this fee
should be directed to the Kenton County Fiscal Court, not the Sheriff’s Office
that collects the taxes.
Municipal Order No. 2012-MO-03 – Appointing Park National Bank as the Successor
Paying Agent and Registrar for the $4,150,000 General Obligation Refunding
Bonds, Series 2012, Effective on January 7, 2013.
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for consideration a Municipal Order that
would appoint Park National Bank as the successor paying agent and registrar
for the $4,150,000 refunding bonds for the Municipal Center debt. He reminded
Council that this debt was refinanced last month at a 15-year fixed rate of
1.8% which saved the taxpayers $1,400,000 in interest over the life of the
loan. He advised this Municipal Order would transition the original paying
agent/registrar Bank of New York to Park National Bank. Mr. Groth stated the
City would like Park National to handle this account after the first payment in
January 2013 because the City currently holds an account with Park National and
has a business relationship with this bank.
Mr. Deters read Municipal Order No. 2012-O-03. A motion was made by Council
Member Yeager and seconded by Council Member Bushong to adopt Municipal Order
No. 2012-MO-03. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth

Resolution No. 2012-R-21 – Authorizing Participation in the Northern Kentucky
Governmental Purchasing Agreement with Kenton County
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council Resolution No. 2012-R-21 that would
authorize the City’s participation in the Northern Kentucky Governmental
Purchasing Agreement. Mayor Moriconi explained that by participating in this
purchasing agreement it would allow the City to piggyback off of the County’s
bid pricing thereby eliminating the City’s need to go through the same legal
bid process for identical materials that need to be purchased by the City. He
stated he spoke with the City’s auditor and the auditor advises this is the
best way to achieve this and cover all the bases going forward. There was a
brief discussion. Council Member Little commented that this process could drive
prices down for servicing a larger market. Mayor Moriconi concurred that this
collective process garners better pricing for the county and the cities that
participate in the agreement. Council Member Bushong asked if the City would
still have the option to conduct our own bid process for products or services.
Mr. Groth advised the City could, at any time, put out for bids. Mayor Moriconi
advised that the City would continue to bid out major street projects, but
would use the County bid prices for in-house projects. Mr. Deters advised that
this purchasing agreement also allows the City to take advantage of the salt
(for snow and ice) prices the County gets when they bid out for this material.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2012-R-21.
A motion was made by Council Member Little and seconded by Council Member
Bushong to adopt Resolution No. 2012-R-21. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Executive Order No. 2012-EO-03 – Appointing David Cain to the Code Enforcement/
Board of Ethics

Proposed Ordinance – Refunding of the Fowler Creek Sewer Debt with a Four-Year
Note – 1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council for consideration a proposed ordinance that
would authorize the refinancing of the principal balance of Series 1998 general
obligation improvement bonds. He advised Council that the City approached
several local banks to solicit proposals for a four year fixed interest rate to
refinance the remaining principal balance of the Fowler Creek Sewer debt which
is approximately $2,400,000. He stated that seven banks submitted quotes with
US Bank proposing a four year note with a fixed interest rate of 0.94%. He
stated this is much lower than the current interest which is over 4%, which
will save the City around $240,000 in interest and knock four years off the
life of the loan. He stated the new note would pay off this debt by May 1,
2016. A brief discussion ensued. Mr. Groth advised that the City will have to
provide the Bank of New York, who holds the current note, thirty days notice
advising that we will be paying off the loan. He stated if Council decides to
move forward in authorizing the refinancing of this debt he would recommend a
second reading of the ordinance this month. Mayor Moriconi advised that time is
of the essence in locking in the interest rate proposed by US Bank. There was a
brief discussion regarding a special council meeting next week with Council
Members stating they would be available to attend on Monday, December 10th at
6:00 p.m.
There being no further discussion Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance.

Mr. Groth stated he did not have anything to report.

Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report on this evening.

the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Chris Reinersman and Donna Yeager.
Council Member Mike Little was absent. Also present was City Attorney Jed K.
Deters.

Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular

Approval of the December 10, 2012 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the Special
meeting held on Monday, December 10, 2012. Council Member Bushong so moved,
with second by Council Member Franzen. There being no amendments, roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Presentation of the Updated Comprehensive Plan “Direction 2030” by Andy
Videkovich, Senior Planner with NKAPC
Andy Videkovich presented to Council and Mayor Moriconi a draft copy of the
statement of goals and objectives which will serve as a foundation for the all-
new Comprehensive Plan for Kenton County. He advised that per K.R.S. the Plan
is to be updated every five years and since the original Plan foundation was
drafted forty years ago the Planning Commission determined that the Plan needed
a complete re-write. He stated a project team was formed that included a
planning task force and a technical task force. Mr. Videkovich stated that the
Comprehensive Plan provides policy guidelines for all of Kenton County to meet
the diverse needs of the entire county. Therefore, the Plan should be viewed
from a big-picture perspective and the guiding principles and goals that have
been drafted would be appropriate on an area-wide basis.
Mr. Videkovich stated the Plan draft is being submitted to get the City’s
input, such as how the goals can be strengthened, before being presented for a
final review and adoption. He advised that the Kenton County Planning
Commission will review the proposed Plan in April and forward their
recommendation to the cities in the county for final action which much occur
within ninety days of the Planning Commission’s recommendation. He stated if
the City takes no action within the ninety days the recommendation by the
Planning Commission become final.
Mr. Videkovich advised the goals and objectives of the proposed Plan were
drafted using three guiding principles: 1) public input, 2) economic
considerations (which would be relevant regardless of the economic climate) and
3) goal relationships – realizing that all goal categories are intricately
connected and impact one another. He stated the Plan identifies seven goals
with broad-based objectives for each goal. The seven goal categories are:
mobility, healthy communities, natural systems, health, economy, community
identity and governance. Mr. Videkovich stated that it will be easier to
address the goals and objectives now, in draft form, before it is presented in
final form by the Planning Commission in a few months.
A lengthy discussion ensued. Mayor Moriconi questioned the verbiage and
suggested it could be difficult to interpret in its current format. He
suggested it be written in a manner that is easy to understand by people
without planning degrees. Mr. Videkovich addressed the Mayor and Council Member
concerns and questions. Regarding the goal of expanding/enhancing the
effectiveness of the transportation system, he advised that members of the task
force included transportation employees, and while the State has their own
public process for road improvements, transportation issues are inter-related
with land-use and could affect land-use discussions. He stated that NKAPC is
not involved in the road improvements planned for SR536. Mayor Moriconi stated
he wanted to be sure that the Plan would be business friendly. Mr. Videkovich
advised that the HBA (Homebuilders Association) has been very involved in the
process, has closely reviewed the draft and provided feedback. He stated that
it has been the desire of every community that the Plan be business friendly
and since the goals and objectives are broad-based this should not impede
business development in any community. Mr. Videkovich advised that Kenton
County is lacking industrial land uses for warehouses, manufacturing and
distribution and while it may not be relative to Independence it is to other
areas in the county. New areas for this type of land use would have to be
identified for possible rezoning. Council Member Reinersman commented that this
is something that is definitely on the OKI Board’s radar, areas such as Taylor
Mill along Locust Pike along the rail yards.
Regarding the goal of encouraging cooperative governance, Mayor Moriconi
commented that it makes sense to work toward removing barriers, sharing
services and removing duplication of services. Mr. Videkovich stated this is
already occurring as some cities have shared policing.
In closing, Mr. Videkovich advised Council that their feedback is desired, and
that all comments/suggestions will be accepted until February 28, 2013. Mayor
Moriconi thanked Mr. Videkovich for the presentation.
General Discussion Regarding Imposing a Toll to Help Fund the New Brent Spence
Bridge
Mayor Moriconi introduced Alan Daly who requested time to address Council
regarding a proposal by Kentucky and Ohio governments to impose a toll to help
fund the construction of a new Brent Spence bridge (over the Ohio river
connecting Covington and Cincinnati).
Alan Daly, 10330 Limerick Circle, Independence – addressed Council regarding
his opposition to impose a toll for the Brent Spence bridge project. He stated
he feels they already pay a lot of state and federal taxes and a toll would
just be another tax, the majority of which would be collected by the State of
Ohio. He stated many citizens in Northern Kentucky cross the bridge each day
for work and a toll would be an added burden and have an adverse affect on the
vitality of a growing community. Mr. Daly submitted a Resolution that would
support the opposition of this proposed toll and requested that the City
Council adopt this Resolution. Mayor Moriconi read the Resolution summary to
the Council and commented that he tends to agree that imposing a toll is not
the answer for funding the new bridge.
Council Member Bushong asked if the Mayor’s Group has discussed this issue.
Mayor Moriconi advised the Group has discussed it in the past but it is now
coming to the forefront on their agenda.
Mr. Daly reported there is a group that wants the bridge project to be a
public/private partnership. He questioned the legality of such a partnership
being permitted to impose a toll charge. He stated the federal government
collects $67,000,000 per day from the gasoline tax. Council Member Franzen
commented that in her opinion an interstate highway should be financed with
federal funds. She stated she is not sure why Ohio and Kentucky are taking on
the challenge of financing this project. She commented that toll areas are
always congested and this is already a highly congested area. In response to
Mr. Daly’s point that the majority of the bridge cost was being spent in Ohio,
Councilmember Reinersman commented this was likely due to much higher land
acquisition costs on the Ohio side. Mr. Daly commented that the current bridge
is not unsafe, just obsolete.
Carol Halpin, 10326 Limerick Circle, Independence – commented that if a car
goes through without paying the toll an electronic camera will take a photo of
the license plate and the offender will be billed for the toll charge. Mayor
Moriconi stated there is also a cost associated with that. Council Member
Yeager stated she remembers seeing a design that had a toll-free exit for work
commuters to and from Cincinnati.
In closing, Mayor Moriconi advised Mr. Daly he would distribute the Resolution
he submitted to Council for their consideration and possible action at the
February meeting.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth reported that the closing of the refinancing of the Fowler Creek
Sewer debt is scheduled for January 22, 2013. He reminded them the City is
refinancing with US Bank with a 4-year fixed interest rate of 0.94% with no
penalty for an early payoff.
Mr. Groth advised Council that when the City switched to the new curbside trash
containers program in July 2012 it created some displeasure with the residents
regarding large items that do not fit in the container, fall leaf pickup, etc.
The Rumpke driver will not take anything that is not placed in the containers
provided by Rumpke, which has caused some inconvenience to the residents. He
stated that Rumpke is willing to address the complaints that have surfaced over
the last several months and would like to meet with staff, along with a few
involved Council Members, to discuss some possible resolutions to large item
pickup, annual leaf pickup, etc. Council Members Bushong and Franzen
volunteered to meet with Rumpke in an effort to find some resolutions to the
complaints.
City Attorney – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he had nothing to report.
MAYOR’S REPORT – Christian J. Moriconi
Presentation of the Audit ending June 30, 2012 – Mayor Moriconi presented to

State Route 536
Mayor Moriconi advised Council that an important topic of discussion in the
coming years will be the road improvements to State Route 536. He advised that
he has invited representatives of the State Transportation Department, District
6 Director Rob Hans and Bob Yeager, to next month’s meeting to discuss this
road project, specifically to address concerns with the nine turnabouts planned
along a four mile section, all located in Independence. He commented that it
seems like quite a few roundabouts in a short span of roadway and that he is
not opposed to roundabouts, as they are beneficial in certain areas, but nine
within four miles seems excessive. He stated this road and the planned
improvements is a big deal as it is a highly traveled, major east/west corridor
for the City.
