Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
February 4, 2013
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
4, 2013 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J.
Moriconi presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with
the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and
Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the January 7, 2013 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, January 7, 2013. Council Member Bushong so moved, with
second by Council Member Franzen. Council Member Reinersman requested an
amendment to the third paragraph on page three. There being no objection to the
change; the minutes were corrected as requested and roll was called and
answered with five ayes and one abstention cast by Council Member Little.
Motion carried.
Discussion Regarding Road Improvement Plans for State Route 536
Mayor Moriconi introduced Rob Hans, Transportation Cabinet, District 6 Chief
Engineer and Bob Yeager, District 6 Project Development Manager whom he invited
to talk about the planned road improvements for SR 536.
Mr. Yeager distributed to Council new maps of the proposed improvements to the
536 corridor. The improvement area runs from SR25 in Boone County to the new
SR17. He advised that the 536 corridor is a part of the 2000 study. He advised
that traffic on this roadway is expected to double in future years which will
allow travelers to get to the interstate as quickly as possible. He stated they
are currently in the process of acquiring right of way in this four mile
stretch of road, as well as another mile along Turkeyfoot Road. He stated the
two biggest changes will be access management to control through traffic and
separate the east and west lanes. Mr. Yeager advised that roundabouts will be
positioned every 1500 feet or so to prohibit left turns which will
significantly reduce the number of fatal collisions as most accidents occur at
intersections with left turns. He stated they can be confusing for a driver
that has never driven them before but the drivers will quickly learn how to
maneuver through them efficiently. Mr. Yeager went on to say that roundabouts
are better than typical intersections and no worse where you have to wait to
pull out into traffic. He stated the advantage of this type of traffic flow is
important in addressing safety concerns. He said that for the City there is an
advantage of being able to landscape the roundabout area. He stated that a
roundabout is planned for every existing intersection for this area of roadway.
Mr. Yeager advised that roundabouts could be eliminated but the idea is to
increase the flow of traffic which is accomplished with the use of roundabouts.
He advised that roads are designed to move forward twenty years into the future
and controlling access management is a big part of managing the flow of traffic
and it is always safer making a right hand turn.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the Turkeyfoot Road interchange would have a
roundabout. Mr. Yeager responded that the Turkeyfoot interchange would be a
conventional intersection not a roundabout. Council Member Bushong asked how
the proposed roundabouts would compare to the one near the Northern Kentucky
University in Campbell County. Mr. Yeager advised the roundabout near the
University is smaller, only one lane wide, and that the proposed roundabouts on
536 are two lanes wide providing a better angle moving to the right.
Council Member Bushong asked if the I-75 interchange with Mt. Zion Road and
through to Dixie Highway would be part of this road improvement. Mr. Yeager
advised this design phase for 536 would encompass just this side of Dixie
Highway (SR25) and that they are currently in the next design phase for the I-
75 interchange through to U.S.42 in Union.
Mayor Moriconi asked the cost of this project. Mr. Yeager advised that the cost
is $20,000,000 for the right of way acquisitions and $20,000,000 for the
construction phase of the project. Mayor Moriconi asked if the roundabout
mediums would be raised to allow for landscaping in the center. Mr. Yeager
responded yes, with curb and gutter sections 14 feet which will accommodate
small trees or bushes.
Mayor Moriconi pointed out there are nine proposed roundabouts along this four
mile stretch of roadway and asked if this number could be reduced. Mr. Yeager
advised that anything is possible but this would require modification to the
right of way plans and would be taking steps backward to modify the plan.
Council Member Little asked the speed limit on the roadway and how much of an
increase in traffic has been projected. Mr. Yeager advised the speed limit
would be 45 mph with a decreased speed in the roundabouts which would be 20-25
mph. He also advised that the current 6,000 to 10,000 cars per day would
increase to 12,000 to 25,000 over the next 15-20 years. He stated that this
roadway would probably see additional development of homes and businesses along
with the increased through traffic. Council Member Little also expressed some
concern about a two-lane roundabout. Mr. Yeager advised that the traffic would
stay to the right to exit, just like you would exit an interstate. Council
Member Little commented that he liked the entry angle which is an improvement
from what he has seen elsewhere. Mr. Yeager commented that design plan
eliminates all points of contact, straightens sections of the road and provides
better sight distance. Council Member Reinersman remarked that the slower
speeds at the roundabouts could actually take longer to get across the new
roadway.
Mayor Moriconi asked if the section of SR536 going through Boone County has any
roundabouts. Mr. Yeager advised that two roundabouts are planned for that
section of SR536.
Council Member Yeager asked why more roundabouts aren’t planned for the
sections of SR536 running through Boone and Campbell counties. Mr. Yeager
advised this is partially due to the growth in the Independence area and
knowing that this section of the 536 corridor will be heavily traveled. He
stated this is an area which provided more potential to take a more pro-active
approach in their design in implementing more safety features.
Mayor Moriconi asked how long it would be before the construction phase of the
project would begin. Mr. Yeager advised that acquiring property for the right
of ways is a two year process. He stated they have 20+ relocations and a total
of 180 parcels to be accommodated. He said that optimistically there is a three
to four year minimum before they begin the actual construction.
Mr. Yeager reviewed the map with the Council pointing out the locations of the
nine planned roundabouts. The following are the roundabout locations planned
along SR 536 where they intersect with:
   ·   Sigmon Lane
   ·   Bristow Villages Development
   ·   KY 1303
   ·   Falcon Ridge/Hogrefe Road
   ·   Ky 2043/Banklick Road
   ·   Williamswoods Rd/Calvary Road
   ·   Ky 2045 (Independence Road)
   ·   Old KY 536 Access
   ·   Delaware Crossing
Senator Damon Thayer, who serves on the Interim Joint Committee on Local
Government, addressed Council regarding the SR536 road improvements. He
commented that he appreciates the efforts of District 6, and he is not a road
engineer, but a vessel for citizen concerns. He stated that the reconstruction
of 536 has conceptually been on the books for a number of years and while there
are topographical challenges, that span three counties, it will provide access
to the interstate. He stated he is familiar with the need to reconstruct this
corridor, and the State has been able to allocate funds in the budget to begin
the project. He stated he has been approached by some of his constituents who
have brought concerns regarding the nine roundabouts to his attention. He
stated if the concerns persist he will bring this to the attention of Mike
Hancock (Secretary of the Transportation Cabinet) or other appropriate people
who oversee the State road projects. Senator Thayer went on to say that this
area is still fairly rural and the reconstruction of 536 will open up this
area. He stated he has worked with District 6 for ten years and they do a great
job. He stated the roundabouts are fairly new in Kentucky and there has been a
little pushback because the concept is so new. He stated District 6 proposes
the project be completed in two year cycles and it will not be ready for
construction for a few years. He stated he would make every attempt to get the
construction funds in the Governor’s 2014 budget, about a year from now.
In closing, Senator Thayer commented that before moving forward, it should be
certain that the roundabouts planned for the Independence stretch of 536 is not
an experiment. He stated that access to I-75 is critical for travelers and with
the increased population of this area he will continue to fight for the gas
taxes to be returned via road project funding for the area.
Mayor Moriconi also expressed his appreciation for the great relationship with
the District 6 representatives. He stated his satisfaction with the design of
other State road projects in the City. He stated he hopes to partner with
District 6 on a bridge over Shaw Road to Simon Kenton High School. Council
Member Franzen stated the school’s parking lot is at capacity and the students
overflow parking is at the Kroger Town Center lot. Mr. Rob Hans stated they
would look at a design for a bridge during the next phase.
Council Member Brinker asked if the roundabouts would be lighted. Mr. Yeager
commented that roundabouts would have adequate lighting.
Mayor Moriconi asked how citizens could contact the Highway Department
regarding this project. Mr. Yeager advised anyone could call their offices at
859-341-2700
Mayor Moriconi thanked Senator Thayer for attending the meeting and assistance
with the citizens concerns regarding the reconstruction of 536. Senator Thayer
advised he could be reached at damon.thayer@lrc.ky.gov or by calling 502-564-
2450.
Discussion Regarding the Reconstruction Plans for the Brent Spence Bridge (I-
75)
Rob Hans, Chief Engineer for Kentucky Highway Department District 6, provided
Council with an update on the plans for the reconstruction of the Brent Spence
Bridge (I-75) which spans the Ohio River between Covington and Cincinnati. He
reported the District has been working on the engineering feasibility study for
the I-71/I-75 corridor for two years. He stated the preliminary engineering
stage was completed the summer of 2012 with the purpose of the study to address
issues such as improved safety, improved traffic flow, correct geometric
deficiencies and maintain connections to key regional and national
transportation corridors.
Mr. Hans stated they are trying to improve the congestion aspect for commuters,
as they incur costs while sitting in traffic, and also improve connection
points.
Mr. Hans advised the study area is 3.21 square miles, a length of 7.8 miles
with Kentucky section being 5.1 miles (or 53% of the project area) and Ohio
section being 2.7 miles (of 47% of the project area). He stated the bridge
length is 1,736.5 feet (4% of the project area).
Mr. Hans advised this section of the I-75 corridor, a federal highway, is
traveled by 172,000 cars per day with $417,000,000,000 in freight connecting
ten states. He stated a preferred alternative would be a configuration of the
bridge with six lanes in each direction, including the cut-in-the-hill on I-75
south.
Mr. Hans advised the estimated construction costs of the bridge in today’s
economy would be $2,700,000,000, but with inflationary costs that would
increase if the project was delayed for years. He advised that currently they
are projecting a planned project start date of 2015. He stated they began last
year to evaluate the financing options to move the project forward as delaying
the project will only increase the construction costs. Mr. Hans advised they
hope to have final results in April of this year. Mr. Hans advised that the
traditional way to finance a federal highway project would be an 80%
contribution from the federal funds and 20% State funds. He stated that the
alternative funding options would come from public and private sectors. He
stated the public sector would assume operations and maintenance costs and
finance and capital costs. He stated the private entity would take care of
maintenance costs. He stated all options are being evaluated to determine the
best option to move the project forward. He stated Ohio and Kentucky
partnership will review the options. He said that at this time they don’t know
the amount of a potential toll cost. Mr. Hans stated that the initial findings
will be revealed in mid-February as well as their ongoing outreach and
education efforts. He stated that ultimately they have two options: 1) proceed
with the construction project in a timely manner or 2) not move forward with
the project.
After Mr. Hans presentation, there was a question and answer session. Regarding
his opinion on the use of tolls, Mr. Hans stated there was no other way to move
the project forward without funding from tolls. He stated that he hears
comments that this is a federal highway project that should be funded by the
federal government, but the federal funds are distributed to each State every
year and then the States determine the use of the funds. He advised that it
would take over two years of the entire State budget for this project alone
leaving no funds for other projects in the State. He went on to say that Ohio
does not have available funds to move forward on this project.
When asked if the Fifth Street exit in Covington would be eliminated, he
responded the reconstruction plan would revise the movement on I-71/I-75
corridor. He stated the new design would provide a new collective-distributor
access for the 12th Street, Pike Street and 9th Street exits. Once entering the
collective-distributor the driver would make the appropriate exit decision from
that distributor lane. He said the same collective-distributor concept would be
utilized in the southbound lanes.
When Council Member Bushong asked what would be done with the old bridge, Mr.
Hans advised the current bridge would stay in service as the structure is
sufficient for rehabilitation. He stated the newly reconstructed bridge will
allow traffic to flow using three separate corridors.
Mayor Moriconi asked how the national legislators and legislators from Ohio and
Kentucky stand on the issue of tolls. Senator Thayer commented that both
governors from Ohio and Kentucky have voiced their position. He asked Mr. Hans
how much Kentucky has spent on this project thus far. Mr. Hans advised that
Kentucky has allocated $36,000,000 on the project design of which $20,000,000
has been spent on the preliminary phases.
When asked if the State would need to get permission from the federal
government to work on this bridge, Mr. Hans advised that the federal government
has oversight of design and they have to give their approval. Senator Thayer
advised that the State of Kentucky receives a half billion dollars each year
from the federal gas taxes collected by the federal government. Mr. Hans
advised that the federal government does not provide the State extra funds when
there is a special project such as this and added that no major projects are
solely funded with federal dollars. Mr. Yeager commented that Kentucky gets
about 97% of the amount of gas taxes paid each year. Unless there is a large
gas tax increase the State knows the amount of funding that the federal
government will send each year.
Council Member Reinersman commented that the federal legislators no longer
earmark funds for special projects. He stated there is a set formula for how
the funds from the gas taxes are disbursed each year.
Mr. Hans advised that the project study results will be presented in April of
this year. He stated they will make a presentation to OKI Board of Directors
Executive Committee on February 14th and the Kenton County Fiscal Court on
February 19th.
Mr. Hans stated that typically tolls fund about fifty percent of the project
costs, but right now all options are on the table as they begin looking at
alternative financing. He stated that if tolls are used, they could stay in
place forever, but there is nothing to say it couldn’t be a shorter period of
time.
In response to the Mayor’s question about the current reconstruction being cost
prohibitive and scaling the project down to make it more affordable, Mr. Hans
stated he is aware of a bridge in Louisville that was scaled back and lanes
added. He stated they looked at that for this project but the river crossing is
a problem. He stated that in scaling down they would have to look at cost
versus benefit and if those dollars would be spent wisely by scaling down.
Regarding the tolls, Mr. Hans advised that the State entity would be
responsible for setting parameters for tolls and who would collect the tolls.
The State would use the tolls fees to pay back the private investors, or the
private builders of the bridge could collect their own toll fees.
When asked if legislation would be required from Kentucky to move forward with
this project, Senator Thayer replied yes.
Mr. Hans responded to the question about other bridge options for commuters to
downtown Cincinnati. He advised that if tolls are implemented traffic could
divert to other road systems. He said the I-471 bridge is currently over
capacity and he advised there are alternatives but they could potentially cause
user delays costing time and money to the user. He stated they will begin
marketing this project to educate the citizens about some misconceptions he is
hearing. He stated he has heard toll booths cause congestion, but it will not
be necessary to stop at a booth as commuters will have the option to purchase a
transponder devise that will deduct the toll fee out of your bank account, or a
bill can be mailed to you for the use of the corridor.
There being no further questions, Mayor Moriconi thanked Mr. Hans for attending
the meeting to provide information about this Brent Spence Bridge project.
Mayor Moriconi advised Council there is a proposed resolution in their packet
that opposes the use of tolls to fund the reconstruction of the Brent Spence
Bridge. Council Member Reinersman commented that he has come to the conclusion
that it is a bit premature to act on this resolution at this time. He stated it
is a big issue that needs further consideration so that an informed stand can
be taken.
Council Member Reinersman made a motion to table taking action on the proposed
resolution opposing the use of tolls to fund the reconstruction of the Brent
Spence Bridge until the value for money study is presented. Council Member
Little seconded the motion. Council Member Bushong commented that he did not
feel this had a major bearing from Independence on this bridge project. Council
Member Franzen stated she did not favor the use of tolls as she feels this is
just one more thing the middle class has to pay for. She stated she also felt
that, as Council Members, we represent the citizens in Independence that use
the bridge to commute to work each day and we needed to be their voice on this
issue. Council Member Little stated he also did not like the use of tolls to
fund the project. Council Member Brinker commented that he feels this project
is the responsibility of the federal government and they should step forward,
which they won’t do if private, State and toll fees are being put forth to fund
the project. Council Member Little asked Mr. Hans when the financing proposal
would be released. Mr. Hans advised that it would be released at the end of
April and will include recommendations on the most likely way to fund the
project, cost estimate, etc.
There being no further discussion on the motion to table adoption of the
resolution opposing the use of tolls to fund the bridge project, roll was
called and answered with three ayes cast by Council Members Reinersman, Little
and Bushong and three nays cast by Council Members Franzen, Yeager and Brinker.
Mayor Moriconi broke the tie by casting a no vote. Motion to table the
resolution was defeated 4-3.
Resolution Number 2013-R-01 – Opposing the Use of Tolls to Fund the
Reconstruction of the Brent Spence Bridge
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen to adopt Resolution No. 2013-R-01
that would support the opposition of the use of imposing tolls to fund the
reconstruction of the Brent Spence Bridge. The motion was seconded by Council
Member Yeager. Mr. Deters read Resolution Number 2013-R-01. Roll was called and
answered with four ayes by Council Members Franzen, Yeager, Little and Brinker,
one no vote cast by Council Member Bushong and Council Member Reinersman
abstained from voting. Motion carried.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth reported that a meeting has been scheduled with Rumpke
representatives to discuss some complaint issues and the collection of large
items. He stated that Council Members Franzen and Bushong have volunteered to
attend this meeting with him and City staff members.
City Attorney – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he needed to request an executive session to discuss pending
litigation.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor stated he did not have anything to report.
Executive Session
At 9:07 p.m. Council Member Little moved to enter into an executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss possible/pending litigation. The
motion was seconded by Council Member Bushong. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 10:00 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Reinersman. Motion carried with all ayes.
Directive to City Attorney Regarding the Collection of Delinquent Fowler Creek
Assessments
Council Member Franzen made a motion to direct the City Attorney to proceed
with the collection of the delinquent Fowler Creek Sewer Assessment using other

A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Yeager to authorize the Mayor to proceed with the demolition of 60 McMillan
Drive. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Bushong
and seconded by Council Member Brinker to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 10:02 p.m.

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
March 4, 2013
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 4,
2013 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the February 4, 2013 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, February 4, 2013. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Reinersman. No amendments were noted, roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried.
Request by Kary Shankar to Amend Zoning Ordinance to Add Indoor Storage
Facilities to the List of Permitted Uses in the NSC Zone
Mr. Kary Shankar presented to Council his plans to repurpose the building he
owns in the Cherokee Plaza at 6463 Taylor Mill Road. He advised the building
currently houses his medical billing business along with Great Clips, The
Learning Center daycare and Pizza Hut. He stated the medical billing business
will be downsizing and the other three tenants will remain in their locations.
He stated he would like to repurpose the majority of the building space to
house interior rental storage units. He distributed a handout that showed
photos of the building site as well as photos of the type of storage units he
would like to construct. Mr. Shankar also showed Council slides of the internal
structure of the individual units. He stated he is proposing a design that
would place 102 units on the ground floor and 170 smaller units on the second
floor. He stated a freight elevator would also be installed in the building. He
advised there would be two entrances into the building with the access for
trucks being from Cox Road.
Mayor Moriconi asked if there would be changes to the exterior of the building.
Mr. Shankar stated that all the changes would be to the interior – no exterior
alterations.
A discussion ensued. Mr. Deters advised that if Council decided to support this
zoning text amendment, an application would be made to the Kenton County
Planning Commission and their recommendation would be sent to the City for
final action. He advised that any text amendment would not just apply to this
building but would apply to all NSC zones in the city. Zoning Administrator
Annie Wuestefeld advised that the City has three NSC zones, those being the
Cherokee Shopping Center, Beechgrove Shopping Center and the Towne Center.
Council Member Reinersman expressed concern in supporting a text amendment that
would allow this type of business as a permitted use which would apply city-
wide. He suggested the text amendment should be to add it as a conditional use
that would be reviewed by the Board of Adjustment and decided on a case by case
basis. He commented that if the Council preferred to make this a permitted use
in the NSC zone he would want to also add text putting conditions on the
permitted use – conditions such as hours of operation, etc. Mr. Deters advised
the Board of Adjustment has the leeway to explore and impose conditional uses
when it is only allowed as a conditional use.
Resolution No. 2013-R-02 – Supporting a Zoning Text Amendment Application that
would Add Interior Storage Facilities as a Conditional Use in the NSC Zones
Council Member Reinersman made a motion to support a zoning text amendment
application that would add “interior storage facilities” as a conditional use
in the NSC zones, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2011-O-18 Flood Plain Regulations –
1st Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would amend the
current flood plain regulations that were adopted in 2011 by Ordinance No.
2011-O-18. He advised the purpose of this amendment is to adopt the updated
flood map that identifies the areas of special flood hazard by the Federal
Emergency Management Agency (FEMA) in the Flood Insurance Study (FIS) for
Kenton County. Mr. Deters advised this amendment to the current ordinance would
bring the City into compliance. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth announced the annual Easter Egg Hunt would take place on Saturday,
March 23rd at Noon at Memorial Park.
City Attorney – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he needed to request an executive session to discuss pending
litigation.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor stated he, along with the Public Works Director and Mr. Charlie Deters,
met with the State Highway representatives to inspect Declaration Drive,
specifically the section which is the current Kroger egress. He stated they
discussed widening the one lane to three to improve the flow of traffic. He
stated he has received some complaints about this section of roadway and would
like to be proactive in resolving the traffic issues in this area before the
opening of the new Kroger Marketplace this summer. Council Member Little and
Yeager commented they have also heard complaints about the traffic flow in this
busy area. Council Member Yeager commented that the area should have a 4-way
stop. Mayor Moriconi advised this was too close to the lighted traffic signal
on Madison Pike and would therefore not be conducive to good traffic flow.
Executive Session
At 7:23 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to enter into an executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss possible/pending litigation. The
motion was seconded by Council Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 7:43 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Reinersman. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Little and
seconded by Council Member Yeager to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:44 p.m.

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
April 1, 2013
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 1,
2013 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christian J. Moriconi
presiding. Mayor Moriconi called the meeting to order and opened with the
Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman and Donna
Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Presentation of Award to City Administrator Dan Groth
David Plummer, Campbell County Solid Waste Coordinator addressed Council by
saying that Independence City Administrator Dan Groth recently resigned from
the Northern Kentucky Technical Advisory Committee after twenty years of
service to the organization. He stated this is a committee of the Northern
Kentucky Solid Waste Management District that was formed in 1993 to advise the
Governing Body of the Northern Kentucky Solid Waste Management Area during the
preparation and implementation of their Solid Waste Management Plan. He stated
that Mr. Groth was a founding member of the Committee. He presented Mr. Groth
with a plaque in recognition of his efforts, dedication and outstanding
service.
Proclamation – Simon Kenton High School Bowling Team Champs
Mayor Moriconi presented a Proclamation to the students of the Simon Kenton
High School Bowling Team for their efforts in winning the 2012-2013 KHSAA High
School Boys State championship.
Approval of the March 4, 2013 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Moriconi called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, March 4, 2013. Council Member Bushong so moved, with
second by Council Member Reinersman. No amendments were noted, roll was called
and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2013-O-01 – Amending Flood Plain Regulations – 2nd Reading
Mayor Moriconi presented for a second reading Ordinance No. 2013-O-01 amending
the flood plain regulations for the City. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a
second reading.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Bushong to adopt Ordinance No. 2013-O-01. There was no discussion on the
motion. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Award Bid for Ready Mixed Concrete for Various Public Works Projects for the
Fiscal Year July 1, 2013 through June 30, 2014
Mayor Moriconi advised Council the Public Works Department does many in-house
concrete projects during the course of the year and it was suggested the City
solicit bids for the supply of ready mixed concrete for the various street
repair projects. He presented to Council the two bids the City received - one
from Ernst Concrete and the other from All-Rite Ready Mix. Mr. Groth commented
the City was able to get a better price by putting it out to bid. Mayor
Moriconi stated this would fulfill the bidding requirements if a small project
would unexpectedly near the bidding requirement threshold and the City would
then be able to proceed with the additional work without interruption. Public
Works Crew leader Dan Koch concurred that awarding this bid for prices that
would be contracted for the entire year would cover the City with regard to the
State law that requires any project $20,000 or more to be put out for bid. Mr.
Koch recommended the City award the bid to Ernst Concrete. Mr. Groth advised
that Ernst Concrete provided the best price per cubic yard of concrete. He
stated that All-Rite Ready Mix only submitted pricing for a six month term and
the bid specifications were for a twelve month term beginning July 1, 2013
through June 30, 2014.
A motion was made by Council Member Yeager and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to award the ready-mix concrete contract to Ernest Concrete as the best
bid. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex Approximately 58.990 Acres on the Easterly
Side of the Relocated State Route 17, South of Maple Tree Lane and North of
Taylor Mill Road at its Intersection with State Route 17
Mayor Moriconi presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would state the
City’s intention to annex the east side of the new, relocated SR17, south of
Maple Tree Lane to the intersection of Taylor Mill Road. He stated that the
proposal to annex this area along SR17 is an attempt to get ahead of any future
development along that stretch of roadway that would impact the City. He stated
this area has some large tracts of land that could be commercially developed
which would increase traffic coming through the City. Mr. Groth commented that
only the east side of SR17 would be annexed as it posed the least opposition
from the property owners. Council Member Bushong asked if the houses on Maple
Tree were part of this proposal. Mayor Moriconi stated no houses on Maple Tree
were in the annexation area, but there is a church and a nursing home. Mayor
Moriconi advised there is a portion of the street right-of-way that would also
be annexed. Council Member Reinersman commented that the parcels in the
annexation area are prime development land. Mayor Moriconi stated any future
development of these parcels would be advantageous for the City in terms of
future occupational licenses and associated taxes. He also commented that since
SR17 is maintained by the State, the City would not be taking on any road
maintenance with this annexation.
Council Member Brinker asked if the residents of the nursing home would have a
vote in the annexation. Mr. Deters stated he did not think as he believes the
tenants of a nursing home would be similar to that of a hotel, wherein the
occupants are considered transients.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave the proposed intent to annex
ordinance a first reading
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth reported Mayor and City staff were working on the budget for the
2013-2014 fiscal year and would meet again next Thursday.
City Attorney – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report but needed to request an
executive session to discuss pending litigation.
Mayor’s Report – Christian J. Moriconi
Mayor stated he did not have anything to report.
Executive Session
At 7:18 p.m. Council Member Yeager moved to enter into an executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss possible/pending litigation. The
motion was seconded by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 8:10 p.m. Council Member Franzen moved to reconvene the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Motion carried with all ayes.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Little and
seconded by Council Member Reinersman to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:12 p.m.

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
April 18, 2013
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in special session
on Thursday, April 18, 2013 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with
Vice-Mayor Donna Yeager presiding. Vice-Mayor Yeager called the meeting to
order and opened with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Jim Bushong gave
the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little, Chris Reinersman
and Donna Yeager. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
City Administrator Dan Groth announced that Mayor Chris Moriconi has resigned
his position with the City to accept a position with the City of Fort Mitchell
as their City Administrator. He stated that in accordance with City ordinance
the Council Member with the highest number of votes in the last election shall
serve as Mayor Pro Tem and preside at the meetings in the Mayor’s absence.
Mayor Pro Tem Donna Yeager advised this Special meeting of Council was being
held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
   ·   Accept the Resignation of Mayor Chris Moriconi
   ·   Discussion and Possible Action to Fill the Vacancy Created by the
Resignation of Mayor Moriconi
   ·   Swearing-In of a New Mayor (only in the event that a Council Member is
appointed to fill the unexpired mayoral term)
   ·   Possible Discussion and Action on Process to Fill a Vacant Council Seat
(only in the event that a Council Member is appointed to fill the unexpired
mayoral term)
   ·   Executive Session in accordance with KRS 61.810 (only if necessary)
Accept the Resignation of Mayor Chris Moriconi
Presiding Officer Yeager asked Council for a motion to regretfully accept the
resignation of Mayor Moriconi. Council Member Reinersman so moved, seconded by
Council Member Bushong.
Presiding Officer Yeager asked if there was any discussion. Each Council Member
took the opportunity to express to Mayor Moriconi (who was in the audience)
their heartfelt gratitude for his service to the City. Council Member Franzen
stated that it has been a pleasure serving the City along with him over the
last several years and thanked him for his service. Council Member Little
stated he has served five terms all under the administration of Mayor Moriconi
and that it has been a pleasure. He stated that he has appreciated him as an
individual as well as in his capacity of Mayor and that it has been a pleasure
working with him. Council Member Little went on to say that he found Mayor
Moriconi to be a person of good moral character which is hard to find in
today’s world and he has appreciated the opportunity to work with him. In
closing he stated that he felt the Mayor is leaving the City in good shape as
he did an awesome job with the City’s budget, which is a big part of running
the City. He stated he always appreciated the detailed budget information he
provided the Council.
Council Member Bushong recalled the year 2000 when they first served on Council
together. He stated he always appreciated Mayor Moriconi’s guidance and
companionship and everything he accomplished with Council over the last several
years. He wished him all the best in the future.
Council Member Reinersman commented that even though he is the new guy on the
Council he has known Mayor Moriconi for many years, but has gotten to know him
better in the last few years. He stated he has learned a great deal from him
under his administration and appreciated his guidance in learning the ropes. He
said when they disagreed on an issue he appreciated his willingness to work
through it and that they were able to respect one another’s opinion. He stated
it has been a privilege to work with Mayor Moriconi and as the Council
continues to work together for the good of the residents, he feels Mayor
Moriconi has set a standard for the Council in showing the value of working
together instead of working against one another and he is very appreciative of
that guidance and he will be missed a great deal.
Council Member Brinker stated he can’t imagine the City without Mayor
Moriconi’s leadership. He has done a great job and it shows in every modern
part of the City which occurred under his tenure which has made Independence a
great place to live. He thanked Mayor Moriconi for endurance and helping guide
the City and Council through this period of growth.
Presiding Officer Yeager commented that it is a great day for the City of Ft.
Mitchell, but a sad day for Independence. She expressed her appreciation for
all the help he gave her over the years and stated she will miss him a lot, but
teasingly added that she will be calling him.
Mayor Moriconi thanked everyone for their kind words. He stated the City is
bigger than any one person - as mayors come and go. He commented that the last
thirteen years have been some of the most challenging, productive, fun,
enjoyable and rewarding years for him, but when you like what you’re doing it
doesn’t feel like work. He stated that being a part of a team with the current
and previous members of Council it has been very rewarding, and overall,
together they have the City in good shape. He stated that Council is part of
the team and everyone deserves a lot of credit as well. He said that even
disagreements were handled with respect and politeness and they moved on and
remained friends which is part of how the elected officials of this City
gelled. He stated that at all times everyone was looking out for the City’s
best interest, with no personal agendas involved. He stated that he feels every
decision was taken very seriously, always asking ourselves how this decision
would impact the taxpayers of this City. He stated we haven’t been perfect over
the last thirteen years, but all in all, he thinks people are generally happy
with the services provided. He said that sometimes government can’t get
anything done, but as he drives through the City he feels we have accomplished
some great thing together. In closing, he commented that Council deserves
credit for the things accomplished over the last several years as well. He
stated that people think it is easy to sit up there, but when they get up
there, it is then that they realize there are limitations to what you can do.
He stated it is more work than people think, but it is rewarding and he enjoyed
his time as Mayor. He stated that when he thinks back, thirteen years ago when
he began his first term on Council, the City administration was operating out
of an old bank building, with the police department renting space on the second
floor of the Courthouse and the Council meetings held in Courthouse – it’s been
great - and you know what they say “don’t be sorry it’s over, be thankful it
happened.”
At this time, everyone rose to applaud Mayor Moriconi in appreciation for his
service to the City.
Presiding Officer Yeager called for a vote on the motion made by Council Member
Reinersman to accept the resignation of Mayor Moriconi. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Presiding Officer Yeager asked Mayor Moriconi to step forward and the Council
Members presented him with a plaque in recognition of his unselfish devotion,
outstanding leadership and distinguished service to the City of Independence.
Discussion and Possible Action to Fill the Vacancy Created by the Resignation
of Mayor Moriconi
Pro Tem Mayor Yeager advised the next agenda item was to discuss and possibly
take action to fill the vacancy created by the resignation of Mayor Moriconi.
Council Member Little commented there is a lot of experience on Council,
hopefully all will be in agreement that filling this seat should come from
within the Council and I want to make a motion and part of a nomination to
nominate Donna Yeager. He stated he can’t think of anyone else with more
experience on Council or served the City, not to mention taking into account
the electorate, which she is the highest vote getter every election, he would
like to make the nomination and hopefully she will accept to fill the Mayor’s
vacancy until the end of the term. Council Member Franzen seconded the motion.
Council Member Yeager accepted the nomination. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Oath of Office - Swearing-In of a New Mayor
City Attorney Jed Deters administered the Oath of Office to Donna Yeager as the
City’s new Mayor, effective immediately.
Possible Discussion and Action on Process to Fill a Vacant Council Seat
Dan Groth stated the next point of business would be to discuss how to proceed
in filling Council Member Yeager’s seat on the Council.
Council Member Reinersman suggested putting the word out that anyone interested
in the position to submit a resume for consideration. He stated that since the
City is under a thirty day timeline to fill the position, he suggested the
resumes should be submitted in one week. Council Member Franzen commented that
during her tenure on Council she has been through this two times before and she
recalls that Council narrowed the candidates down to a few who would then be
interviewed in an executive session by the Council. She agreed that they do
need to move quickly and thought the open seat should be advertized in the
newspaper. Mr. Deters advised the City can advertise using any method they
desire. Council Member Reinersman expressed concern about the limited time
frame to fill the seat. Council Member Franzen agreed that resumes should be
submitted in the coming week and suggested an announcement be posted on the
City’s website and Facebook page. Council Member Reinersman concurred the City
should use all our available resources and then give a deadline of next week.
He suggested the resumes be submitted to them via email so they can immediately
begin the review process. Council discussed narrowing the number of candidates
that would be interviewed. Council Member Bushong stated he felt three would be
sufficient as did some of the other Members. Council Member Franzen suggested
narrowing down and the number to be granted an interview, and thought it may be
necessary to schedule a Special Meeting. Mr. Deters suggested it could be done
at the next regular meeting on May 6th. Council Member Little agreed that they
could conduct the interviews in executive session at that meeting. Mr. Groth
stated the deadline to appoint someone to the seat would be May 18th. Council
Member Reinersman agreed that a Special Meeting could be scheduled, if
necessary, after the May 6th meeting but sometime before May 18th. Council
agreed that Friday, April 26th at close of the business (4:30 p.m.) would be
the deadline to email or bring /mail resumes to City Clerk and she will forward
them to the Council Members. Council Member Reinersman commented that it
shouldn’t be decided on the number of applicants to interview at this time
until we see how many are submitted. Council Member Little suggested everyone
have several names to discuss at the meeting then decide on the three best
candidates to interview. Everyone concurred.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Bushong to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 6:23 p.m.

Ordinance No. 2013-O-02 – Intent to Annex Approximately 58.990 Acres on the
Easterly Side of the Relocated SR17 South of Mapletree Lane and North of Taylor
Mill Road at the Intersection with the Relocated SR17 – 2nd Reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council for a second reading, Ordinance No. 2013-O-02
which would approve the City’s intent to annex approximately 58.990 acres on
the east side of the relocated SR17 just south of Mapletree Lane and north of
Taylor Mill Road (SR16) at the intersection with the relocated SR17. Mayor
Yeager opened the floor to audience members who wished to comment on this
proposal by the City.
Mr. Gailen Bridges addressed Council by advising he was legal counsel for the
owners of Regency Manor LLC. He stated his clients opposed the annexation as
there would be no advantage for them to be part of the City since they are
already receiving public services from the State highway for road maintenance,
police protection from the Kenton County police and fire protection from the
Independence Fire District. Mr. Bridges stated his clients operate a personal
care home with fifty-eight residents, half of which are registered voters. He
stated he believes they have enough residents to vote down the annexation. He
stated the Goodrich family is also in attendance at this meeting and they also
oppose the annexation.
There was a brief discussion about the residents of the Regency Manor and their
being able to vote on the annexation issue. Mr. Deters stated he is unable to
answer that definitively at this time. He advised that the residents and
property owners will have sixty days to file a petition with the Mayor
declaring their opposition to the annexation. Mr. Groth stated that if more
than fifty percent of the residents and property owners signed the petition
then the issue would be placed on the ballot in the next general election for a
formal vote on the annexation issue, which would require more than 55% opposing
the annexation in order to defeat it.
Council Member Reinersman stated he doesn’t see how the annexation would
adversely impact the property owners. He stated the City has some concerns that
any future development of the vacant parcels in that area would have a great
impact on the City and would therefore like to be proactive and involved in the
plans for any commercial development in order to protect the citizens in the
area.
Council Member Brinker commented there may be a savings to the residents in the
unincorporated area as the City does not collect an insurance premium tax. The
owner of the Regency Manor commented they have looked at the financial end and
have concluded City taxes would be more than the insurance premium taxes they
pay now and also their employees would end up paying City payroll taxes.
Council Member Franzen suggested that the Regency Manor be eliminated from the
proposed annexation.
Council Member Reinersman stated that while he appreciated their concerns, he
felt the Council needed to look at the impact a major development would have on
the City and the only way the City would be able to be involved in the future
planning is if it is situated within the City boundaries.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2013-O-02 a
second reading. A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by
Council Member Reinersman to adopt Ordinance No. 2013-O-02. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Zoning Text Amendment Adding Completely
Enclosed Self-Storage Units and Warehousing Businesses as a Conditional Use
within the NSC Zone (KCPC2105R) – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would approve a
zone text amendment adding completely enclosed self-storage units and
warehousing business as a conditional use within the NSC zone (KCPC2105R) for a
first reading. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Mr. John Huffman, 4290 Richardson Road, Independence – addressed Council
regarding this text amendment. He asked why the City would consider permitting
storage units in the NSC zone. Mr. Deters advised Mr. Huffman that the Council
agreed to sponsor the text amendment application at the request of a property
owner. Mr. Huffman distributed a copy of a letter dated March 5, 1997 and
signed by the City’s Zoning/Building Administrator Allan Bowling. He stated the
letter advises it is the opinion of the NKAPC staff that self-storage units are
appropriate as permitted uses with the IP (Industrial Park) zones. He stated he
recently brought this letter to the attention of the NKAPC staff who stated
they would not have rendered a favorable recommendation on this text amendment
had they had prior knowledge of this letter. Mr. Deters advised that NKAPC
should have had knowledge of this before providing their recommendation.
Council Member Little stated that the proposed text would allow completely
enclosed storage units which is an entirely different concept that Mr.
Huffman’s storage units on Richardson Road. Mr. Kary Shankar, who requested
this text amendment, advised Council that this subject was discussed by the
NKAPC staff and they clarified there was a difference between outdoor storage
units and a completely enclosed and climate controlled facility.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting an Amended 2012-2013 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend the 2012-2013 budget. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2013-2014 Budget – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance that
would adopt a budget for the 2013/2014 fiscal year. In her budget address Mayor
Yeager stated that next year’s street repair program will surpass a half
million dollars. She also stated the budget she is presenting will include
funding for an additional school resource officer, a part time employee for the
parks, a part time employee for zoning code enforcement and a new employee for
the public works department. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Council Member Franzen expressed concern that the part time parks position
would actually be a utility person that would assist three department heads.
She questioned who this employee would answer to and how tasks would be
prioritized. Mr. Groth advised the original intent for this position was to
assist the Recreation Director and it would be up to her and the other
department heads to work harmoniously. Council Member Reinersman stated that he
doesn’t doubt the need for an additional staff person, but he understands
Council Member Franzen’s concern and would also like a better understanding on
how this utility person would function under multiple department heads. A brief
discussion ensued relating to the part time positions for parks and code
enforcement. Council Member Little suggested job descriptions for the new
positions.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Pay and Classification Plan – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that will adopt
an employee Pay and Classification Plan for the 2013/2014 fiscal year. Mr.
Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Resolution No. 2013-R-04 – Adopting and Approving the Execution of the

Cabinet for the 2013-2014 Fiscal Year.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in special session

   ·   Proposed Ordinance – Rescinding Ordinance No. 2013-O-02 (Intent to Annex

Proposed Ordinance – Rescinding Ordinance No. 2013-O-02 (Intent to Annex
Approximately 58.990 Acres on the Easterly Side of the Relocated SR17 South of
Mapletree Lane and North of Taylor Mill Road) – 1st Reading
Mr. Deters presented to Council a proposed ordinance that will rescind
Ordinance No. 2013-O-02 that was adopted at the May 6, 2013 meeting. He stated
this ordinance is being rescinded as the proposed annexation boundary map has
been amended and will cover less acreage. Mr. Deters gave the proposed

Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex approximately 46.225 acres situated in
unincorporated Kenton County and located on the east side of relocated KY17,
north of Taylor Mill Road (KY16) – 1st Reading
Mr. Deters presented to Council a proposed ordinance that will declare the
City’s intent to annex approximately 46.225 acres on the easterly side of the
relocated KY17, south of Maple Tree Lane and north of Taylor Mill Road at its
intersection. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading.
Council Member Franzen commented that this new intent to annex ordinance
addresses the concerns presented by the attorney (Gailen Bridges) representing
the owners of the Regency Manor at the May 6th council meeting. She stated
Council was in agreement to remove this parcel from the annexation. Mr. Deters
concurred that the majority of the parcel was eliminated except for a thirty
foot street that was necessary to keep the annexed areas contiguous.
Resolution No. 2013-R-05 – Opposing rezoning of approximate 28 acre area on the
east side of KY17 north of KY16 and south of Maple Tree Lane
Mr. Deters presented to Council Resolution No. 2013-R-05 that opposes the
rezoning of an approximately 28-acre area located on the east side of KY17 and
on the north side of KY16 approximately 1000 feet north and 1200 feet east of
the KY17/KY16 intersection in the unincorporated Kenton County from R-1B to NSC
(Neighborhood Shopping Center). He stated that this proposed rezoning by the
County’ encompasses parcels the City has declared its intent to annex. Mr.
Deters read Resolution No. 2013-R-05.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Reinersman to adopt Resolution No. 2013-R-05. Roll was called and answered with
all ayes. Motion carried 4-0.
Council Member Franzen asked if it would be appropriate for Council to attend
the Kenton County Planning Commission meeting on June 6, 2013 to oppose the
County’s rezoning request. Mr. Deters advised it would be ok to speak on behalf
of the City and to present their personal opinion as well.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Brinker to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:07 p.m.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 3,

5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Donna G. Yeager presiding.

Presentation of Special Merit Award for Outstanding Project – Andy Videkovich,
NKAPC Senior Planner
Mayor Yeager introduced Andy Videkovich, Senior Planner with NKAPC, who was
present to present the City with a plaque. Mr. Videkovich stated he was the
Project Manager on the recent zoning update for the downtown area and was happy
to be here to present this award. He stated the award was presented by the
Kentucky Chapter American Planning Association, who each year presents six
awards in six different categories. He advised this year there were four state-
wide nominations for the Special Merit Award and the Outstanding Project
recipient for the Independence Zoning Update has been awarded to the City of
Independence and Northern Kentucky Area Planning Commission (NKAPC).
Mr. Videkovich expressed his appreciation to the many volunteers who served on
the Zoning Update Committee and specifically recognized John Richardson who
served as Chair and through his leadership guided the Committee through the
project. He also thanked the Independence residents for their willingness to
work with the Committee and finally thanked the City leaders for their
assistance and support.
Council Member Reinersman thanked Mr. Videkovich and the NKAPC staff for their
guidance during this project. He also acknowledged John Richardson for his
invaluable leadership who went above and beyond to complete the zoning update
project. He commented that the Committee accomplished more than he could have
hoped for. Mayor Yeager thanked Mayor Chris Moriconi who served as mayor during
the zoning update process and supported it’s adoption.

June 10, 2013
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in special session
on Monday, June 10, 2013 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with
Mayor Donna Yeager presiding. Mayor Yeager called the meeting to order and
opened with the Pledge of Allegiance. An invocation was given by Council Member
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Chris
Reinersman. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters announced this Special meeting of Council was
being held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
   ·   Ordinance No. 2013-O-08 Approving an Intent to Annex approximately
46.225 acres situated in unincorporated Kenton County, Kentucky and located on
the east side of relocated KY17 just north of KY16 – 2nd reading
   ·   Resolution No. 2013-R-06 – Authorizing the financing of police and
public services department vehicles
Ordinance No. 2013-O-08 Approving an Intent to Annex approximately 46.225 acres
situated in unincorporated Kenton County, Kentucky and located on the east side
of relocated KY17 just north of KY16 – 2nd reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council for a second reading, Ordinance No. 2013-O-08
which would approve the City’s intention to annex approximately 46.225 acres
situated in unincorporated Kenton County and located on the east side of the
relocated KY17 just north of KY16. Mr. Deters gave Ordinance No. 2013-O-08 a
second reading.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to adopt Ordinance No. 2013-O-08. A brief discussion ensued. Council
Member Reinersman stated that this annexation proposal is not a land grab by
the City, but a plan that will place the City leaders at the negotiation table
in the event that the vacant parcels would be developed in the future. This
would put the City in a position to be part of the negotiations for the
development and address citizen concerns. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
A member of the audience expressed concern that only the residents living in
the affected annexation area would be able to vote on the annexation proposal.
Mr. Groth advised the parcels being annexed are all vacant land. Mr. Deters
stated that the revised intent to annex ordinance has eliminated all but a
thirty foot strip of the Regency Manor and First Baptist Church properties and
totally eliminated the Meenach property. He advised the City needed the thirty
foot strips from the Regency Manor and Church properties in order to have
connection to the other annexation parcels along Madison Pike.
Council Member Reinersman explained the City’s annexation proposal and the
County’s recent filing for a zone change for some of the parcels in the
annexation area. The audience member advised that his mother (Nellie Goodridge)
owns one of the parcels the City is proposing to annex and they are concerned
as they do not see any advantage they will have by being incorporated into the
City. Council Member Reinersman explained the City is concerned about future
development plans along that stretch of Madison Pike because it abuts the City
boundaries. He stated the City is not opposed to future development but doesn’t
want to be a victim to any growth in that area that will have a direct impact
on the City because of its close proximity.
Resolution No. 2013-R-06 – Authorizing the Financing of Police and Public
Services Department Vehicles
City Administrator Dan Groth advised Council that the City solicited proposals
from three banks (Huntington, Park National and US Bank) for the financing of
the new vehicles. He stated the interest rate proposals were very close with
only $272 difference between them. Mr. Groth recommended the City obtain
financing for $266,000 with Huntington Bank, which would include the cost of
the five police cruisers with a three year term fixed rate of 2.054% and the 2
public works vehicles with a four year term fixed rate of $2.223%.
Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2013-R-06. A motion was made by Council Member
Aseere and seconded by Council Member Brinker to adopt Resolution 2013-R-06
authorizing a lease-purchase agreement with Huntington Bank for the financing
of five police cruisers and two public works trucks. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Bushong
and seconded by Council Member Reinersman to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 7:12 p.m.

July 1, 2013
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 1,
2013 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Donna G. Yeager presiding.
Mayor Yeager called the meeting to order and opened with the Pledge of
Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Jim Bushong. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen and Chris Reinersman. Council Member Mike
Little was absent. Also present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters.
Approval of the June 3, 2013 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting
held on Monday, June 3, 2013. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. No amendments were noted and the motion carried
unanimously.
Approval of the June 10, 2013 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the special meeting
held on Monday, June 10, 2013. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second by
Council Member Bushong. No amendments were noted and the motion carried
unanimously.
Approval of Stage II Development Plan for an 8.20 Acre Area Located at McCullum
Pike and KY17 in the Gateway Mixed Use Zone (GMU) by Paul Hemmer Company (KCPC
2114R)
Jack Levermann, Vice President of Real Estate and Development for the Paul
Hemmer Company and Bob Schroeder, Vice President of Arlinghaus Builders LLC
presented to Council a Stage II Development Plan for an 8+ tract of land
located at McCullum Pike and the new KY17. Mr. Levermann advised that has
purchased lot number 2 of the Courthouse Crossing development from Arlinghaus
Builders. He stated the Plan for lot two is to construct a St. Elizabeth
Primary Care Physicians facility including an Express Care clinic which is an
urgent care type of service. Mr. Levermann stated the facility will be 12,400
square feet and St. Elizabeth will employ 20-24 employees. He stated this new
construction will be in the City’s new GMU (Gateway Mixed Use) zone and he went
on to say that they had some preliminary meetings with Mayor Moriconi and City
staff to review and discuss the concept and make revisions as needed. Mr.
Levermann stated that the NKAPC staff has recommended that some of the parking
spaces be relocated at the rear of the building. He stated they feel they have
addressed all concerns for this development, with the exception of adding
parking spaces in the rear. He stated they took the parking space concerns
under consideration and did attempt to accommodate the Planning Commission’s
request but in order to add the parking spaces, another traffic aisle would
have to be added and the sloped topography of the site just made it unworkable.
Mr. Levermann showed Council illustrations of each elevation of the building.
Bob Schroeder, Vice President of Arlinghaus Builders LLC advised Council that
the Stage II Plan includes a total of five lots on 8.20 acres. He stated there
will be access to the site off McCullum Road with a boulevard entrance, with
landscaped island, walkway and retaining wall on one side of the boulevard. Mr.
Schroeder advised interconnectivity between the lots will be provided for
vehicular and pedestrian mobility within the development. He stated the streets
within the development will be wide enough to accommodate on-street parking.
Mr. Schroeder stated the proposed signage are larger than currently permitted
and they will be asking for a variance. He also advised Council that two minor
public amenities will be provided as required of the GMU zone. Mr. Schroeder
advised that since there is limited access on KY17, egress to the development
will be from McCullum Road, but they have moved the entrance further from the
intersection to prevent traffic congestion at the intersection.
Council Member Brinker asked if the other building sites will be graded until
developed. Mr. Schroeder replied they would be graded and seeded.
Council Member Franzen expressed her concern that the proposed monument sign
was too large and that she would like to see it scaled down. A brief discussion
ensued. Council Member Reinersman advised that, as a way finding tool, they
have added the ‘City of Independence’ to this Courthouse Crossing monument
sign. Mr. Levermann advised they were open to discuss revisions to the monument
sign, but they did want a substantial sign for this Gateway zone. Mr. Deters
asked the distance of the sign from the right of way, as the size of the sign
makes a difference when it sets back quite a distance. Mr. Schroeder advised
the State has a large right of way, so it is set back approximately sixty-five
feet. Council Member Franzen stated that if the rest of the Council was okay
with the size of the sign then she will accept that. Mr. Schroeder stated this
monument sign was modeled after the “Shops of Fort Wright” sign and said they
could attempt to reduce the size of the wing walls.
Other items of discussion for this Stage II Development Plan included the
landscaping. Mr. Levermann advised he has discussed the landscaping regulations
with the City’s Zoning Administrator. He stated no landscaping around the trash
dumpsters will be necessary as they will construct a brick enclosure in place
of hedges, etc. Council Member Reinersman asked about the loading and/or
unloading spaces which are required. Mr. Schroeder advised he met with the
City’s Zoning Administrator who stated there wouldn’t be an issue with their
proposal on this regulation. In closing, Mr. Schroeder commented that many of
the issues the Planning Commission staff cited to determine a recommendation
for disapproval for the proposed development plan have been considered and/or
changed.
Council Member Reinersman advised Council that he has been very involved with
the developers from the beginning of this concept plan. He stated he feels they
have met most of the requirements for the intent of the Gateway Mixed Use zone.
He stated the topography of the site limits the parking spaces that could be
constructed as the hillside drops off leaving no solution to provide the number
of spaces that are normally required in this zone. He stated he would love to
see a development plan that met the full intent of the zone but feels the plan
being proposed is a great use of the site. He stated that while he did not want
to yield too much on the requirements of this zone he feels this developer has
made every effort to comply with the concept of the Gateway zone. Council
Member Franzen commented that the City was not giving in much on the parking
requirement. Mr. Groth commented that this is a good business use for the City
and is setting the tone for the type of building development the City would
like to recruit. Council Member Franzen agreed and felt the residents prefer
this type of business of a big-box development. Council Member Reinersman
agreed by stating this is an exceptionally good use on many levels even though
the City will concede some requirements of the zone for this development. Mayor
Yeager commented that she was overall pleased with the development plan.
There being no further discussion, Council Member Reinersman made a motion to
approve the Stage II Development Plan (KCPC 2114R), as submitted by the Paul
Hemmer Company and all items discussed. The motion was seconded by Council
Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Sidewalks Maintenance – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council for a first reading a proposed ordinance that
would amend Chapter 95 of the code of ordinances by adding a new section
providing for permanent waivers for sidewalks and to add a waiver form. Mr.
Deters read the proposed ordinance.
Council Member Franzen commented that the City’s Building Inspector, Kevin
Barbian worked hard on this amendment and she appreciates his thoroughness. She
stated she is comfortable that the waiver will only be allowed when all waiver
criteria is met and agreed upon by three City officials.
Award Bid – Mid-size Dump Truck
Dan Groth advised Council the City is in receipt of two bids for the purchase
of a mid-size dump truck for the Public Works Department. He stated that Fuller
Ford in Cincinnati is $663 higher that the low bid from Kaffenbarger, but
Fuller Ford promises a quicker delivery time and because this dealer is closer
the City would receive better service. He stated that Fuller Ford will also
provide free oil changes which, over a four year period, would make up the
difference between the bids.
Council Member Reinersman move to award the bid for the purchase of a 550
Series, 4-wheel drive dump truck to Fuller Ford in the amount of $62,790.50.
The motion was seconded by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Resolution No. 2013-R-07 – Creating a Park and Recreation Board and Designating
Members of the Board
Mayor Yeager presented to Council Resolution No. 2013-R-07 that would create a
Park and Recreation Board. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2013-R-07.
Council Member Bushong made a motion to adopt Resolution No. 2013-R-07,
seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 5-0.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth stated he did not have anything to report.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters advised he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Donna G. Yeager
Executive Order No. 2013-EO-06 - Mayor Yeager presented to Council an Executive
Order appointing Sara Gadzala to the Senior Board of Directors. Mr. Deters read
the Executive Order No. 2013-EO-06.
Mayor Yeager announced the July 4th Celebration is scheduled for this weekend,
July 5th and 6th. She stated the fireworks will be held on Saturday and this
year a new feature of the Celebration will be the hot air balloon glow on
Friday evening. She also announced the seniors will be holding their annual
Silent Auction fundraiser on Friday evening in the Senior Center. Mayor Yeager
encouraged everyone to participate in the festival events this weekend.

There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Reinersman
and seconded by Council Member Aseere to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:50 p.m.

Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the Real & Personal Property Tax Rates for 2013-
1st Reading
Mayor Yeager submitted for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
adopt the real estate and personal property tax rates for 2013. Mr. Deters read
the proposed ordinance that would adopt the compensating tax rates that have
been calculated at $0.255/$100 assessed value for real estate property and
$0.684/$100 assessed value for personal property. Council Member Reinersman
asked Mrs. Hudson about her summary report which indicates there is a revenue
budget short fall of $271,000, but a significant savings in the health
insurance expense of $295,000. Mrs. Hudson commented that we projected a fifty
percent premium increase in the health insurance line item, but the renewal
came in about the same as last year, which was a good surprise and has put us
ahead by $295,000. There was a brief discussion among Council and it was
suggested and agreed upon to keep the same tax rates as last year since the
employee health insurance would come in well under budget. A motion was made by
Council Member Little and seconded by Council Member Aseere to adopt the real
estate tax rate of $0.237/$100 and the personal property tax rate of $0.656/
$100. Roll was called and answered with all ayes; motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Resolution – Adding a Job Description of Utility Worker for the 2009
Edition of the Employee Personnel Policy Manual
Mayor Yeager presented to Council a proposed resolution to create and adopt as
part of the employee personnel policy manual a job description for a Utility
Worker. Mr. Deters read the resolution.
Council Member Reinersman recommended against taking action on adding this
position at this time. He stated he previously asked for an evaluation of the
positions being added. Mayor Yeager stated the affected employees do not have
the time it will take to make a needs assessment for the new positions. Council
Member Brinker commented that they needed to have faith in the administration
to put this part-time position to good use. He reminded Council that the salary
for the position has already been approved in the 2013/2014 budget. Council
Member Reinersman stated he agreed on this when presented in the budget with
the understanding that more clarification for the needed positions would be
forthcoming. He stated he felt the City should take a private sector approach
to creating and hiring a new position. Council Member Aseere commented that he
thought the Parks & Recreation Board was created to help the Parks & Recreation
Director. He stated that the job description duties for the Utility Worker was
vague. Mayor Yeager stated the City can’t expect the board members to do manual
labor. Council Member Franzen agreed that a needs assessment should be
submitted to the Council. City Administrator, Dan Groth advised Council that he
has been assisting with code violations, but help is really needed in this
area. Council Member Bushong asked who the Utility Worker would report to and
how it would be determined which department they would work in. He expressed
concern that the departments that needed the help would not get the benefit of
this part-time worker. Mr. Groth advised he would manage the work schedule of
the Utility Worker based on the most pressing needs of the departments each
week. Council Member Franzen commented that the Zoning Administrator needs
assistance from someone that has expertise in this area. Council Member Little
stated that he felt the City is bound to the citizens to get comparison
information from other cities such as the number of employees in each
department, the size of the city, the number of zoning violations, etc. Mr.
Groth commented that the City operates on a shoestring budget spending less per
capita than any other local city. Council Member Bushong reiterated that he is
not in favor of tabling the hiring of a Utility Worker. Council Member Franzen
stated that the Council requested this data months ago. Council Member
Reinersman commented that this needed data could assist them in realizing new
efficiencies that could be gained by hiring additional staff.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to table action of creating and adopting a job description for a
Utility Worker. Roll was called and answered with five ayes and one no vote
cast by Council Member Brinker. Motion carried 5-1.
Executive Session (only if necessary)
Mr. Deters advised there was no need for an executive session.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Bushong
and seconded by Council Member Little to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:21 p.m.

Mayor Yeager introduced Kenton County Deputy Judge Executive Mark Kreimborg.

effectively improve public services that would benefit the entire community. He

issue, is just 300 feet outside of Kenton County and the closing has become an
inconvenience to the Independence residents. Council Member Bushong asked that
Kenton County officials collaborate with the Boone County officials to ensure

inconvenience the citizens longer than necessary. Mr. Kreimborg advised he
