Proposed Ordinance – Regulating Underground Utilities – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager submitted for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Chapter 153 of the code of ordinances relating to underground utilities
and the City’s intent to eliminate the extension or addition of above ground
utilities whenever reasonably possible. The ordinance would prohibit the
extension of utilities within any current or new development, be it
residential, commercial, industrial or otherwise, that are above the surface of
the ground but would grant exceptions due to extraordinary natural conditions
which are stated in the ordinance. Mr. Deters gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.

City staff and the City attorney to discuss the deteriorating condition of the
Heritage Park Apartment complex on Richardson Road. She stated this property
went into default after the owner died and that it is now bank owned. Mr.
Deters advised the blighted condition of the property is decreasing the values
of the surrounding properties. He stated he is reviewing the Code Board
ordinances and the recently revised blighted ordinance which will allow the
City to take more action. A brief discussion ensued and it was decided that the
City Attorney would send a notice to the current owner of record which is the
bank and advise them to board up the buildings and clean up the grounds or the
City would consider further legal remedies to clean up the area.

February 3, 2014
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
3, 2014 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Donna G. Yeager

of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Bushong. Roll was

Attorney Jed K. Deters, City Administrator Dan Groth and City Clerk Patricia
Taney.
Approval of the December 2, 2013 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting
held on Monday, December 2, 2013. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second

Proclamation Presented to Simon Kenton High School Football Team
Mayor Yeager along with Council Member Carol Franzen presented the Simon Kenton
High School football team with a Proclamation to commend them for completing
the 2013 regular season undefeated with a record of ten wins and no losses.
Council Member Franzen read the Proclamation.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2007-O-22 and Adopting the 2013
Kentucky Building Code as Promulgated in KAR – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2007-O-22 and adopt the 2013 Kentucky Building Code as
promulgated in 815 KAR 7:105 by the Board of Housing, Buildings and
Construction. Mr. Deters gave the ordinance a first reading. He explained this
is a housekeeping measure to reference the most current building codes, which
is 2013.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2007-O-23 and Adopting the 2013
Kentucky Residential Code – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
amend Ordinance No. 2007-O-23 and adopt the 2013 Kentucky Residential Code that
would apply to all one and two family dwellings and townhouses located within
the City limits and which are fabricated, erected, constructed, enlarged,
altered and or repaired together with such appurtenances and accessory
structures. This code also provides for the issuance of permits and provides
for penalties for the violation of any provision of the code. Mr. Deters gave
the ordinance a first reading and again explained this is a housekeeping
measure to reference the most current building codes, which is 2013.
Resolution No. 2014-R-01 – Authorizing a Grant Application for Assistance under
the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965
Mayor Yeager presented to Council Resolution No. 2014-R-01 which would
authorize the City to apply for a grant for financial assistance under the Land
and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965. Mr. Deters read Resolution No. 2014-R-
01.
Mayor Yeager acknowledged three Park Board members in attendance who have been
researching possible grants to help fund desirable park improvements. Mr. Groth
advised the City would like to use the grant funds to terrace the hillside
between the Senior Center and the Amphitheater. He stated the City applied for
this same grant two years ago but was not awarded the grant. He stated this is
the first of two grants the Park Board would like to apply for. He stated the
second grant application would be with the CDBG (Community Development Block
Grant) for a project that would include basketball courts, walking paths and
restrooms in Memorial Park. He stated the CDBG grant would not require any
matching funds from the City. Mr. Groth added that passing this Resolution is
the first step in the grant application process along with a public hearing
that will be scheduled in March to gather public input on the proposed project.
He advised the hillside terracing project for the Amphitheater would cost the
City around $120,000 which will have to be budgeted but that part of the City’s
expense can be contributed as in-kind services. Council Member Reinersman
commented that the Independence Business Association will write a letter of
support for this project which can be submitted along with the grant
application. Mayor Yeager advised other letters of support will be solicited as
well. Council Member Brinker reported that as Chairman of the Park Committee
the monthly meetings are going well and the members are discussing long and
short term goals for the City’s park system. Council Member Little thanked the
Park Board members stating he feels these volunteers, as well as other members
of City boards/committees, are crucial to the City and he appreciates the time
and effort they give.
There being no further discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Brinker
and seconded by Council Member Franzen to adopt Resolution No. 2014-R-01
authorizing the grant application under the Land and Water Conservation Fund
Act of 1965 for financial assistance for the hillside terracing project in
Memorial Park. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2014-R-02 – Accepting Ownership and Maintenance of Bypassed
Segments of Old KY 536
Mayor Yeager presented to Council Resolution No. 2014-R-02 that addresses the
reconstruction of KY 536 from the Boone County line to KY 17, specifically
resolving that the City shall:
   ·   allow KYTC to perform work on City Right of Way
   ·   allow KYTC to purchase Right of Way in the City’s name for referenced
City Streets
   ·   upon completion of construction accept title to ownership and
maintenance responsibility for:
      *   segments of bypassed KY 536
      *   reconstructed City Streets
      *   sidewalks and multi-use paths within City Limits
      *   street signs or street lights constructed at the City’s request
      *   decorative features added to this project (signs, landscaping, light
poles)
   ·   pay for all City street signs
   ·   pay for the future electric bills for all street lights not located
within the roundabouts and traffic signals within the City Limits
   ·   pay for all decorative features installed with this construction project
that is above the standard installation cost
   ·   pay for all maintenance of decorative street lights even those that
would be included in the roundabouts
   ·   post-construction, provide maintenance for all landscaped medians,
islands, and mowable areas behind the curb and within the median
City streets that will be reconstructed with this project include:
   ·   Hogrefe Road
   ·   Falcon Ridge Drive
   ·   Old Bristow Road
   ·   Bristow Lakes Drive
   ·   Calvary Road
   ·   Williamswood Road
   ·   Delaware Crossing
   ·   Old Madison Pike
Mr. Groth explained the State has also agreed to take over maintenance of short
Richardson Road in exchange for the City taking ownership and maintenance of
the bypassed areas of KY 536 which include:
   ·   Old KY 536 (Bristow Road) from Williamswood Drive to the intersection
with the proposed KY 536 Connector Road, approximately 0.10 miles west of the
junction with KY 2045 (Independence Rd). A total distance of approximately 0.66
miles.
   ·   Old KY 536 (Independence Rd & Shaw Rd) from the junction with KY 2045
and Bristow Road to the intersection with the New KY 536 near station 321+00. A
total distance of approximately 0.57 miles.
Mr. Groth also advised he asked the State the resurface and stripe these
bypassed segments of roadway prior to the City taking over the future
maintenance. He stated the City is taking more roadway sections but will have
less future maintenance. He also reported the State has agreed to install
street lights and pay for the electricity in the roundabouts that will be
constructed in this project. He stated that any grass or landscaping installed
in the roundabouts would be the maintenance responsibility of the City. Mr.
Groth commented that the start of this road project is probably five years down
the road and that the sitting Mayor and Council at that time will make the
final decision on any landscaping/grass that will be installed. He advised that
it is still uncertain if the State has decreased the number of roundabouts as
requested by Council last year from the proposed nine that was originally
presented in the State’s design. He stated there are four phases of
construction and the State is currently in the environmental phase of this
project.
There being no further discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Bushong
and seconded by Council Member Franzen to adopt Resolution No. 2014-R-02. Roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth stated he did not have anything to report.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters advised he did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Donna G. Yeager
Executive Orders - Mayor Yeager presented Executive Order No. 2014-EO-01
appointing Council Members Jim Bushong and Bill Aseere as the City’s primary
and alternate representatives to the Northern Kentucky Area Planning Council
and Executive Order No. 2014-EO-02 re-appointing Council Member Chris
Reinersman to represent the City on the OKI Board of Directors.
Audit ending June 30, 2013 - Mayor Yeager presented to Council the City’s Audit
Report for the fiscal year ending June 30, 2013. She advised Council to direct
any questions or concerns about the audit to Mr. Groth or Finance Director
Teresa Hudson.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Reinersman
and seconded by Council Member Bushong to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:28 p.m.

May 5, 2014
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 5,
2014 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Donna G. Yeager presiding.
Mayor Yeager called the meeting to order and opened with the Pledge of
Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Bushong. Roll was called
and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker,
Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Chris Reinersman. Also present was
City Attorney Jed K. Deters, City Administrator Dan Groth and City Clerk
Patricia Taney.
Presentation of FEMA Funds by Kenton County Judge Executive Steve Arlinghaus
Judge Executive Arlinghaus presented Mayor Yeager with a check for $4,670 which
is the City’s portion of FEMA funds obtained by the County for expenses arising
from the tornado that hit the County in March 2012. He reminded everyone of the
tornado damage that hit the southern portion of the County and these funds will
help reimburse the City for some of the expenses incurred by the police and
public works departments for their assistance with the cleanup. Judge
Arlinghaus also presented a check in the amount of $5,035 to Chief
Messingschlager of the Independence Fire District. He stated the County was
very appreciative of the City and Fire District’s efforts in assisting the
County with the aftermath of the tornado.
Presentation – Daughters of the American Revolution Stephens Project – Pam
Marcum
Pam Marcum advised Council that the Daughters of the American Revolution (DAR)
has initiated the Stephens Project to honor Lt. William Stephens who owned a
farm on Stephens Road where the graves of his son John R. Stephens and John’s
wife Elizabeth Beale Stephens are located. It is also believed that Lt.
Stephens is also buried on this farm at 751 Stephens Road. Ms. Marcum advised
the purpose of the Stephens Project is to honor Lt. William Stephens with a
Revolutionary War grave marker. She stated they plan to have a special ceremony
in the fall to honor Lt. Stephens for his military service at which time they
will place a marker at the grave site. Ms. Marcum advised Lt. Stephens has a
large number of direct descendants and they plan on locating and contacting
them with an invitation to participate in the Grave Marking Ceremony.
Mayor Yeager offered the City’s assistance if Ms. Marcum needed it. Council
Member Reinersman commented that he currently owns the Metcalf-Stephens house
on Madison Pike which is listed on the National Registry of Historic Places and
keeps in contact with the Stephens family.
Approval of the April 7, 2014 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting
held on Monday, April 7, 2014. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. No amendments to the minutes were noted and the motion
carried with all ayes.
Proclamation – Building Safety Month
Mr. Groth presented City Building Inspector Kevin Barbian with a Proclamation
declaring May as Building Safety Month to create awareness to the importance of
construction and building codes and spotlight the role of the code officials in
administering those codes. Mr. Barbian thanked Council for the recognition. He
advised Council that during the month building officials throughout the State
visit schools to promote building safety as well summer safety. He also took
the opportunity to encourage citizens to obtain building permits to ensure
safety in all construction projects on their property.
Announcement – Armed Forces Day – Bill Schneider
Council Member Bill Aseere introduced Bill Schneider, a local military veteran.
Mr. Schneider advised Council that Armed Forces Day is Saturday, May 17th. He
stated it is a challenge to get people to recognize this special day set aside
each year to honor all branches of our military personnel. Mr. Schneider
announced the American Legion Moon Brothers 275 would be holding an
appreciation event at the Independence Senior Center on Saturday from 11:00
a.m. to 4:00 p.m. He stated there will be food and drink concessions available,
live music and vintage military vehicles displayed. He encouraged everyone to
stop by to meet and thank our military members for their patriotic service. Mr.
Schneider thanked the City for assistance in publicizing Armed Forces Day on
the City’s marquee, website and Facebook page.
Mr. Schneider also mentioned that National Peace Officer’s Day is Thursday, May
15th and on Memorial Day there will be a ceremony at the Memorial Oaks of South
Kenton in front of Simon Kenton High School.
Announcement – Kenton County YMCA Outdoor Pool (Marshall Road) Reopening
Mr. Groth introduced Jason Roberts, representing the Kenton County YMCA who
wished to address Council about the reopening of the Marshall Road location of
the YMCA. Council Member Aseere commented that he recently met with Mr. Roberts
and has joined the effort to get this pool reopened, which was closed in 2008.
Mr. Roberts stated he is a long-time resident of Independence and in his youth
spent time at the local YMCA pool which included coaching a swim team. He
spearheaded the effort to get the pool reopened. He stated the residential
growth in Independence could support this reopening and would be a great place
for family gatherings and family fitness. He stated his goal would be to see
this become a vibrant family center for the community.
Mr. Roberts advised they need a minimum of 100 memberships to get the pool
reopened by June 2nd. He stated memberships in year past reached 370. He stated
the pool would be open daily from noon until 6 p.m. for the summer season. He
stated there is a possibility to be open longer hours but that would be
contingent on strong community support. Mr. Roberts advised the need for
volunteer plumbing work to get the baby pool operational and encouraged anyone
with plumbing skills to contact him.
Council Member Franzen stated she would pass the information along to the swim
team coach at Simon Kenton High School. Council Member Reinersman commented
that this could be a great opportunity for the local businesses to sponsor the
pool reopening.
City Administrator Report – Dan Groth
Mr. Groth announced that the City’s current contract with Rumpke for curbside
trash and recycling pickup will expire on June 30, 2014. He stated the current
contract allows for a two year extension. He advised that he along with other
City representatives recently met with Rumpke to discuss the two-year extension
along with adding some services like twice a year curbside large item pickups.
He stated that Rumpke was receptive to adding some services for a nominal
increase in the monthly rate for the next two-year cycle. Mr. Groth advised
that there will be a spring and fall large item pickup and no charge for the
large recycling container. Currently the small red recycling bin is provided
free of charge, but if a resident would request the large recycling container
they would not have to pay the $1.00/month fee. He sated the new monthly rate
that would include the additional services, would be $12.08 effective July 1,
2014.
Mayor’s Report – Donna G. Yeager
Executive Order No. 2014-EO-04 - Mayor Yeager presented Executive Order No.
2014-EO-04 appointing Rita King and Jenny Paul to the Board of Directors of the
Independence Senior Citizens Center, Inc.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters advised he did not have anything to report and there was no need for
an executive session.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Little and
seconded by Council Member Reinersman to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:27 p.m.

Rumpke Contract Amendment
Mr. Groth presented to Council a proposed contract modification from Rumpke for
the collection of solid waste and recyclable material from residential dwelling
units. He stated this would be a two-year renewal at a lower rate that the
original bids received by competing companies. Mr. Groth advised the additional
services in the contract amendment are the result of resident feedback. He
stated for the period July 1, 2014 through June 30, 2016 for an amended rate of
$12.44 per month the additional services will include:
   ·   one time per month single large item pickup when given a minimum 48 hour
advance notice
   ·   will allow reasonable volume of additional waste to be placed alongside
the trash container during the week of Christmas, limited to the equivalent of
up to (6) 30-gallon cans or bags
   ·   will provide yard waste and leaf collection pickup up to four times each
year
   ·   will provide the City up to (4) 30-yard containers each year for special
events not to exceed a period of two weeks
   ·   shall provide the City up to (20) portable toilets each year in lieu of
a cash donation and in exchange for annual event sponsorship
Mr. Groth explained that the leaf pickup will be schedule in advance for the
residents and the will be notified of the dates in advance as well.
Council Member Brinker stated this was a game changer for him and he would not
have voted to renew the contract with Rumpke based on the service the last two
years. Mr. Groth commented that a meeting was held with the Rumpke
representative to discuss and address the complaints received from the
residents over the last couple of years, and he feels this contract amendment
will resolve some of those issues. Council Member Reinersman commented that
Rumpke has provided more in this amendment that we had asked for. Council
Member Little stated he feels this is an excellent rate for the additional
services.
There being no further discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Little
and seconded by Council Member Reinersman to extend the Rumpke contract for the
collection of solid waste and recyclable materials for an additional two year
term beginning July 1, 2014 through June 30, 2016 and authorize the Mayor to
enter into the contract. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.

Discussion Relating to Sewer and Water Line Marketing License Agreement with
Service Line Warranties of America
Mr. Groth presented to Council for their consideration, a marketing license
agreement proposal by Service Line Warranties of America that would grant this
company the right to offer a warranty to property owners within the City
limits. In the agreement the City would grant Service Line Warranties of
America a non-exclusive license to use the City’s name and logo on letterhead,
bills and marketing materials to be sent to City property owners. Mr. Groth
explained that SD1 does not service lateral sewer lines as the lines are on
private properties, so any necessary repairs would fall on the property owners
which can be costly. He stated that Mr. Deters would take some time to read the
entire warranty program before the Council decides if they want to endorse this
program for its residents, then Council could take this under further
consideration next month. Mr. Deters expressed some concern regarding this
program and advised he would look into it further.
Resolution No. 2014-R-04
Mayor Yeager presented to Council Resolution No. 2014-R-04 concerning
Sanitation District #1 proposed increase of wastewater and storm water service
fees. SD1 notified the City they would be accepting comments regarding the
proposed fees to be charged to its customers which would be reflected on the
bills beginning in August.
Mr. Groth commented that Resolution No. 2014-R-04 opposes the rate increases.
He read Resolution No. 2014-R-04.

Patricia H. Taney, City Clerk
July 24, 2014
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in special session
on Thursday, July 24, 2014 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with
Mayor Donna Yeager presiding. Mayor Yeager called the meeting to order and
opened with the Pledge of Allegiance. An invocation was given by Council Member
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Mike Little and Chris Reinersman.
Council Member Carol Franzen was absent. Also present was City Attorney Jed K.
Deters, City Clerk Patricia Taney, Zoning Administrator Annie Wuestefeld and
Public Services Director Dan Koch.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
City Attorney, Jed K. Deters announced this Special meeting of Council was
being held to discuss and take action on the following business items:
   ·   Proposed Ordinance – Amending Chapter 91 of the Code of Ordinances
Relating to Animals – 1st Reading
   ·   Proposed Ordinance – ABC License Amendment – 1st Reading
   ·   Proposed Ordinance – Re-Naming of Street – 1st Reading
   ·   Award Bid for Concrete
   ·   Award Bid for Purchase of Public Works Dump Truck
   ·   Resolution No. 2014-R-05 – MRA Co-Op Agreement for 2014-2015
   ·   Authorize Financing of 4 Police Cruisers and Related Equipment
   ·   Executive Session in accordance with KRS 61.810 (c) to discuss pending
litigation and KRS 61.810 (f) a personnel appointment
Mr. Deters advised that only the items listed on this agenda would be discussed
at this meeting which included discussion in an executive session to appoint a
new City Administrator.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Chapter 91 of the Code of Ordinances Relating to
Animals – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would modify the
Code of Ordinances, specifically Chapter 91, Animals, to define “fowl” and
“livestock” and prohibit the keeping or harboring of them within residential
zones on a lot of land that is less than ten acres. Mayor Yeager opened the
discussion with Council.
Council Members Little and Reinersman expressed some reservations with
requiring ten acres. They felt that it was too large of an area and suggested
five acres or less. Council Member Little stated he favors protecting property
owners’ rights as long as their rights don’t infringe on other owners’ rights.
Council Members Brinker, Bushong and Aseere also agreed that ten acres was too
large of an area and felt it should be less – one to five acres. Council Member
Aseere stated he would like more time to review this issue.
Dan Evans, Kenton County Animal Control, was present to address any questions
from Council. He stated that agricultural land is defined as any tract of ten
acres or more of land and that ten acres is feasible for a couple of horses,
etc. He stated the City could lower the acreage requirement to whatever they
feel is appropriate for the keeping of chickens.
Other concerns expressed by Council regarding the keeping of chickens was the
crowing and odor of these animals. Mr. Deters advised the crowing could be
addressed under the noise nuisance ordinance. Council Member Reinersman stated
he was aware of a particular situation in the Liberty Orchard subdivision where
the chickens, while contained within a fence, were flying over the fence and
becoming a nuisance in the neighborhood. Mr. Evans commented that roaming
chickens is not allowed and is a citable offense, if the City regulates this
type of animal.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Aseere to table action of this proposed ordinance until these concerns could be
addressed in more detail. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proposed Ordinance – ABC License Amendment – 1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would amend
Ordinance No. 2013-O-15 regulating the Alcohol Beverage Control. Mr. Deters
advised Council that this amendment was a housekeeping issue to update the
schedule of license types and associated fees. Mr. Deters read the proposed
ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Re-Naming of Rice Road (off Mills Road) to Coppage Court –
1st Reading
Mayor Yeager presented to Council a proposed ordinance that would re-name a
portion of Rice Road that runs off of Mills Road. This segment of Rice Road is
disconnected from the Rice Road that runs off of Klette Road. Mr. Deters read
the proposed ordinance that would change this segment of Rice Road to Coppage
Court. Council Member Reinersman asked if property owners had any objections to
the new name. Mrs. Wuestefeld, Zoning Administrator, responded there is only
one other property owner on this section of Rice Road and the property is not
occupied.
Award Bid for Concrete
Mayor Yeager presented to Council one bid that was received from Ernst Concrete
for the purchase of concrete needed for the City’s various small concrete
projects during the year.
Dan Koch, Public Services Director advised Council that the new subdivision
regulations now have updated specifications for the concrete mix used in street
construction. He advised this had been bid out last year, but because of the
new mixture requirements and the increased cost associated with the new mixture
it was decided to put this out for bids. Mr. Koch stated only one bid was
received from Ernst Concrete in the amount of $87/yard. He stated the price
quoted in the last contract for the old mixture was $67/yard. He also advised
Council that this concrete mixture will only be used for small projects that
his department does in house.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Little to accept the concrete mix bid from Ernst Concrete at a price of $87/
yard. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Award Bid for Purchase of Public Works Dump Truck
Mayor Yeager presented to Council a bid from Fuller Ford for the purchase of a
Ford 550 dump truck for the Public Works Department.
Dan Koch, Public Services Director, advised he received phone inquiries from
four dealerships but only received one bid, which was from Fuller Ford. He
stated he has learned that most dealerships feel they can’t compete with
Fuller’s low price which may explain the reason he did not received any other
bids.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Reinersman to accept the bid from Fuller Ford in the amount of $65,970 for the
purchase of a Ford 550 Series, 4-wheel drive, dump truck for the Public Works
Department. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Resolution No. 2014-R-05 – Adopting and Approving the Execution of the
Municipal Aid Cooperative Program Contract with the Kentucky Transportation
Cabinet for the 2014-2015 Fiscal Year
Resolution No. 2014-R-05 was presented to Council which would adopt and approve
the execution of the Municipal Aid Cooperative Program contract with the
Kentucky Transportation Cabinet for the 2014-2015 fiscal year. Mr. Deters read
Resolution No. 2014-R-05.
A motion was made by Council Member Little and seconded by Council Member
Reinersman to adopt Resolution No. 2014-R-05. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Authorize Financing of 4 Police Cruisers and Related Equipment
Mayor Yeager presented to Council two financing proposals received by the
police department for the financing of four new cruisers.
Council Member Bushong expressed concern that the police department was only
getting four new cars this year instead of the five cars they typically
procure. He requested that next year during the budget meetings that the needs
of the police department be considered so that they keep their annual five car
rotation schedule.
Assistant Police Chief Dave Nichols advised Council that two bank financing
quotes were obtained – one from Park National Bank and the other from US Bank.
He reported that both interest rates (2.48% from Park and 2.25% from US Bank)
were close, but that the deciding factor for him was the financing fees which
US Bank will waive and Park National will not. Park National Bank indicated
their fees could vary between $500-$1000.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Aseere to authorize the financing of four police cruisers and related equipment
with US Bank for an interest rate of 2.25% for a period of three years. Roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Executive Session
At 6:23 p.m. Council Member Bushong moved to enter into an executive session in
accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss pending litigation and K.R.S.
61.810 (f) to discuss a personnel issue. The motion was seconded by Council
Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.
At 7:03 p.m. Council Member Bushong moved to reconvene the regular meeting,
seconded by Council Member Aseere. Motion carried with all ayes.
Municipal Order No. 2014-MO-01 – Appointment to the Position of City
Administrator
Mr. Deters announced that Council discussed in executive session filling the
City Administrator position that was recently vacated by Dan Groth on July 15,
2014 and would like to put forth Municipal Order 2014-MO-01 authorizing the
appointment of Christian J. Moriconi to the position.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Little to approve the appointment of Christian J. Moriconi to the position of
City Administrator. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-
0.
Mr. Deters advised this Municipal Order would be presented again at the regular
meeting of Council on August 4, 2014 for further confirmation since the only
mention of this personnel action on the agenda was under the Executive Session
item.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Little and
seconded by Council Member Reinersman to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:04 p.m.

Award Bid – Reliance Court Street Repairs
Mayor Yeager presented to Council the bids analysis from the City Engineer for
the Reliance Court and Cobblestone Boulevard Roadway Improvements project.
Public Services Director Dan Koch reported that four bids were received with
the highest bid from M & W Excavation in the amount of $214,337.50 and the
lowest bid from Straight Edge Construction in the amount of $158,960. He stated
the City Engineer’s pre-bid estimate for this project was $168,330. Mr. Koch
stated that Straight Edge is a company from Bracken County who is currently
doing their first residential project for the City of Edgewood. He stated he
has spoken to a representative of the City of Edgewood who reports they have
not had a problem so far with this contractor, but they have three weeks
remaining before completion of that project. There was a brief discussion about
taking the low bid from a contractor that was a relative newcomer to
residential construction. Mr. Koch advised the next lowest bidder was from JPS
Construction in the amount of $168,695 – a difference of $9,735. He stated he
would like to recommend taking the bid from JPS Construction since this is a
contractor that has a good reputation and one the City is familiar with having
a satisfactory work history on past road projects.
A motion was made by Council Member Brinker and seconded by Council Member
Bushong to award the bid for the Reliance Court and Cobblestone Boulevard
Roadway Improvements to JPS Construction as the best bid submitted in the
amount of $168,695.00. Roll was called and answered with four ayes and one no
vote cast by Council Member Aseere. Motion carried 4-1.
Approval of Stage II Development Plan Review for Taco Bell Restaurant Located
at 2019 Centennial Blvd.
City Attorney Jed Deters presented to Council a staff recommendation from the
Planning Commission regarding a Stage II Development Plan for a Taco Bell
Restaurant on an approximate .29 acre site located at 2019 Centennial
Boulevard.
Greg Wolf with GSC Foods, Inc. spoke on behalf of Taco Bell. He stated they are
excited to be building a Taco Bell in Independence which will be located behind
the Walgreen’s. Mr. Wolf advised his company has recently built one store on
Mount Zion Road and another one on 3-L Highway is set to open on Wednesday. He
stated the design of the Centennial Boulevard restaurant will be identical to
the one on Mount Zion Road. Council Member Bushong asked when the new store
would open. Mr. Wolf stated it would open ninety days after construction starts
and they hoped to begin construction by the end of this month.
Council Member Reinersman commented that the new Taco Bell meets the building
requirements of the Planning Commission. Mr. Deters stated that the Planning
Commission is recommending approval subject to two conditions; that the
proposed signage on the site be in compliance with the approved Stage I
Development Plan and that the drainage calculations and design of the regional
retention basin to be used by the site shall be provided which show that on-
site storm water management will not be required and that these conditions
shall be met prior to the issuance of any permits.
There being no concerns by Council or further discussion, a motion was made by
Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member Aseere to accept the
recommendation of the Planning Commission staff and approve the Stage II
development plan review for the Taco Bell Restaurant to be located at 2019
Centennial Boulevard. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried
5-0.
Resolution No. 2014-R-06 – Authorizing the Filing of an Application to the
PDSKC for a Text Amendment to the Official Zoning Ordinance of the City to Add
Development Controls in the NC, NSC and PO Zones
Mr. Deters presented to Council and read Resolution No. 2014-R-06 that would
authorize the filing of an application to the Planning and Development Services
of Kenton County (PDSKD) for a proposed zoning text amendment to the official
zoning ordinance of the city to add development controls in the NC, NSC and PO
zones.
Council Member Reinersman advised that there have been recent concerns relating
to building materials used for exterior surfaces in some commercial zones in

to set building standards with some restrictions on the types of building

equipment. He stated the Family Dollar store on Richardson Road sparked the

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September

Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Donna G. Yeager
presiding. Mayor Yeager called the meeting to order and opened with the Pledge
of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Bushong. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Chris Reinersman. Also
present was City Attorney Jed K. Deters, City Administrator Chris Moriconi and

Approval of the August 4, 2014 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting
held on Monday, August 4, 2014. Council Member Bushong so moved, with second by
Council Member Franzen. No amendments to the minutes were noted and the motion
carried with five ayes and one abstention from Council Member Little.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2014 Real and Personal Property Tax Rates – 1st
Reading
The proposed ordinance to adopt the 2014 property tax rates was presented by
City Administrator Chris Moriconi. He noted that the rates being proposed were
the same rates as 2013. Mr. Deters read the proposed ordinance that would adopt
a real estate rate of $0.237/$100 of assessed value and a personal property
rate of $0.656/$100 of assessed value. Council Member Bushong requested an
updated list of tax rates adopted by other local cities to see how Independence
compares.
Proposed Ordinance – Relating to Fowler Creek Sewer Fund by Setting Parameters
for Delinquencies and Authorizing Administration Fees for Transfer to General
Fund – 1st Reading
Chris Moriconi, City Administrator submitted to Council a proposed ordinance
relating to the Fowler Creek Sewer Fund which would provide for the allocation
of certain expenses against the Fowler Creek Sewer Fund, setting parameters for
delinquencies and authorizing the transfer of administration costs and expenses
from the Fowler Creek Sewer funds to the General Fund. Mr. Deters read the
proposed ordinance. A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Reinersman
expressed concern that the language of the ordinance may be confusing and sound
as if the current properties being assessed would actually be paying on this
assessment longer since the fund would remain on the books after the retirement
of the debt. Mr. Deters explained the intent is that the books of this fund
would remain open solely for the collection of the delinquent accounts and the
language will be changed to clarify that before the second reading of the
ordinance.
Resolution No. 2014-R-08 – Approving the Transfer of Comcast Cable to Charter
Mayor Yeager presented to Council Resolution No. 2014-R-08 that would approve
the transfer of control of Comcast Corporation of Insight Kentucky Partners to
Charter Communications. Mr. Moriconi advised this is the second step in the
merger of Time Warner Cable to Comcast. Council Member Reinersman commented
that he spoke with Tim Broering of the Telecommunications Board who explained
that Comcast has agreed to transfer a portion of its post-merger (Time Warner
Cable to Comcast) subscribers to Charter Communications thereby trading
subscribers in different markets which will let them operate more efficiently
and keep within the regulations of the FCC (Federal Communications Commission).
Council Member Bushong made a motion, seconded by Council Member Reinersman, to
approve Resolution No. 2014-R-08. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Declaring Surplus Property – City Owned Vehicles and Computer Equipment
Mayor Yeager presented to Council a list of city owned property to be declared
as surplus items to be either auctioned or recycled. The list included six
police cruisers, four police bikes, cruiser equipment, refrigerator, microwave
oven, modems, cameras, monitors, portable radios, computer docking stations,
marine band radios, laptop computers, printer, keyboards, computer towers and
miscellaneous computer accessories. The items that could be auctioned would be
placed in the Kenton County auction that will be held on Saturday, September
27, 2014.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Aseere to declare the list of presented items as surplus property for disposal
by auction or recycling. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jed K. Deters
Mr. Deters stated he did not have anything to report, but requested an
Executive Session to discuss pending litigation.

He also reported that a survey conducted by Motovo real estate blog has ranked

adopt the real estate and personal property tax rates for 2014. Mr. Deters gave
the ordinance a second reading that will adopt a real estate tax rate of
$0.237/$100 of assessed value and a personal property tax rate of $0.656/$100
of assessed value. These are the same rates that were adopted for 2013.
Council Member Bushong moved to adopt Ordinance No. 2014-O-08 with a second by
Council Member Franzen. There being no discussion, roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2014-O-09 – Relating to Fowler Creek Sewer Fund by Setting
Parameters for Delinquencies and Authorizing Administration Fees to be
Transferred to the General Fund – 2nd Reading
Mayor Yeager submitted for a second reading Ordinance No. 2014-O-09 relating to
the Fowler Creek Sewer Fund which would provide for the allocation of certain
expenses against the Fowler Creek Sewer Fund, setting parameters for
delinquencies and authorizing the transfer of administration costs and expenses
from the Fowler Creek Sewer funds to the General Fund. Mr. Deters read the
proposed ordinance.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Bushong to adopt Ordinance No. 2014-O-09. There being no discussion, roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Approving a Text Amendment Adding Construction Standards
for Exterior Wall Materials, Roofs and Mechanicals to the NC, NSC and PO Zones
– 1st Reading
Mr. Deters presented to Council for consideration a proposed ordinance that
would approve a text amendment to the official zoning ordinance that would add
regulations to building design criteria specifically exterior wall materials,
roofs and mechanicals in the Neighborhood Commercial (NC), Neighborhood
Shopping Center (NSC) and the Professional Office (PO) zones. Mr. Deters gave

accordance with K.R.S. 61.810 (c) to discuss pending litigation and K.R.S.

Member Little. Motion carried with all ayes.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
6, 2014 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Donna G. Yeager
presiding. Mayor Yeager called the meeting to order and opened with the Pledge
of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member Bushong. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom
Brinker, Jim Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Chris Reinersman. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi and City Clerk Patricia Taney.
Executive Order No. 2014-EO-05 – Appointing John J. Osterhage as Interim City
Attorney
City Administrator Chris Moriconi read Mayor Yeager’s Executive Order No. 2014-
EO-05 appointing John J. (Jack) Osterhage as City Attorney during Jed K.
Deter’s absence.
Approval of the September 8, 2014 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting
held on Monday, September 8, 2014. Council Member Franzen so moved, with second
by Council Member Aseere. No amendments to the minutes were noted and the

Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the special meeting
held on Friday, September 12, 2014. Council Member Reinersman so moved, with

Ordinance No. 2014-O-10 – Approving a Text Amendment Adding Construction
Standards for Exterior Materials, Roofs and Mechanicals to the NC, NSC & PO
Zones – 2nd Reading
Mayor Yeager presented Ordinance No. 2014-O-10 for a second reading. This
ordinance would approve a text amendment to the official zoning ordinance that
would add regulations to building design criteria specifically exterior wall
materials, roofs and mechanicals in the Neighborhood Commercial (NC),
Neighborhood Shopping Center (NSC) and the Professional Office (PO) zones.
Council Member Reinersman commented that the reference to architectural grade
building materials in each zone should be eliminated as this was discussed and
agreed upon at the public hearing held by the Planning Commission. No
objections were noted to his suggestion and the language will be stricken from
the final text amendment.
A motion was made by Council Member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Reinersman to adopt Ordinance No. 2014-O-10. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2014-R-10 – Approving an Interlocal Agreement with PDS for Code
Enforcement Administration and an Agreement for PDS Levels of Service (One Stop
Shop)
City Administrator Chris Moriconi presented Resolution No. 2014-R-10 that would
authorize an Interlocal agreement with the Planning Commission for
administration of the city’s zoning ordinance, property maintenance codes and
other related local ordinances along with a cost sharing agreement to provide
the service.
Mr. Moriconi explained to Council that the ensuing four items on tonight’s
agenda were dependent on the adoption of Resolution No. 2014-R-10 which would
solidify the decision to go with the Planning Commission for zoning related
services and the other business items are relative to entering into this
agreement. Mr. Moriconi introduced Dennis Gordon, Executive Director of the
Planning Commission (PDS) and Martin Scribner, Director of Planning and Zoning
Administration, also with PDS.
Council Member Reinersman stated there are concerns regarding the fee schedule
and asked Mr. Gordon to explain the reason behind the fee structure. Mr. Gordon
explained at the time the One-Stop-Shop was established a committee was formed
to look at the costs associated with the administration of the service and the
fees were structured based on the actual costs in an effort to recover most of
the those expenses. He stated the fees increase every other year using the
Consumer Price Index. Mr. Gordon also commented that the Home Builders
Association actually prefers small incremental adjustments to the fee schedule
so they can calculate this annually along with their other building costs.
Council Member Reinersman commented that the City’s fee schedule has not been
increased in some time.
Council Member Little asked how many cities are currently using the One-Stop-
Shop. Mr. Gordon advised they currently work with fifteen cities as well as the
Kenton County Fiscal Court. Mr. Gordon was asked if the City decided to
contract for the zoning services would a full time staff member from the PDS be
assigned to Independence and work from the City building. Mr. Gordon advised he
would assign a person to handle Independence full-time and would have a
satellite office in the City building.
Council Member Little commented that after the transition period there would be
a cost savings for the City by going with the PDS for the zoning and code
enforcement services. Mr. Moriconi confirmed, that based on the numbers
provided by Mr. Gordon, the City should realize an annual savings of around
$40,000.
Council Member Franzen commented that in years past the City had contracted
with PDS but eventually left and hired a full time employee. She asked Mr.
Gordon how contracting with the PDS will be different this time. Mr. Gordon
invited Council Member Franzen to get references from the mayors of the cities
they contract with as well as the County Judge Executive who can advise her how
the services have worked for them.
Council Member Reinersman asked Mr. Gordon to explain their permit and
complaint tracking software program to the Council. Mr. Gordon advised the PDS
software program is accessible 24/7 making it very efficient and convenient for
the citizens and staff. He stated complaints are received immediately into the
system, and with a user name and password that can be provided to the Council
Members and City staff, it can be accessed any time, day or night. The program
also keeps a history of permits issued.
Council Member Little confirmed that the contract can be terminated with a
sixty day notice if the City decides they want to discontinue the service. Mr.
Gordon stated that outstanding business could be wrapped up sooner than sixty
days if possible.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way – Commented that PDS receives approximately $450,000
in taxes from the Independence citizens and questioned the cost savings for the
citizens. She asked how the zoning violation complaints would be handled. Mr.
Moriconi stated they would be handled on a complaint basis only. Mr. Gordon
responded that PDS receives tax dollars from all the cities they serve. He also
commented that PDS would handle the complaints proactively or complaint basis
only – based on the directive from the City. He stated they would only be
proactive if requested by the City.
Mr. Moriconi advised that part of entering into this agreement with PDS would
include the need to disband the City’s Board of Adjustment and the Code
Enforcement Board. Mr. Gordon said that disbanding these City boards and
becoming a member of the countywide Board the City would get a broader
perspective regarding decisions rendered by the Board. Council Member Little
asked if the City could opt to keep these Boards in-house. Mr. Gordon said that
not all the cities are part of the joint Board so Independence would have the
option to keep their own Boards. He stated the City would have an appointee on
both countywide boards.
There being no further discussion, Mr. Moriconi read Resolution No. 2014-R-10.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Little to approve Resolution No. 2014-R-10 to enter into an Interlocal
agreement with PDS for code enforcement administration as well as an agreement
for their levels of service. Roll was called and answered with three ayes from
Council Members Reinersman, Little and Brinker and three no votes cast by
Council Members Franzen, Aseere and Bushong. Mayor Yeager broke the tie vote
with an aye. Motion carried 4-3.

City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Award Bid for Banking Services - Mr. Moriconi reported bids for the City’s
banking services was advertised and five proposals were received. The five
banks submitting bids included Heritage Bank, Bank of Kentucky, US Bank, Fifth
Third Bank and Republic Bank. He stated that the City’s Finance Director, Terri
Hudson has analyzed the fee schedule and services being proposed by each bank
and submitted in the Council packet for consideration. Mr. Moriconi state that
while all the banks are reputable local banks, Heritage Bank is being
recommended to service the City’s banking needs because of the net earnings,
account services needed by the City, fees, etc. He stated that Mrs. Hudson did
a good job reviewing the bids and feels comfortable that Heritage Bank will be
able to provide all the services the City needs while providing a net earnings
better than the rest of the proposals. Mr. Moriconi stated the effective date
to change from Park National Bank to Heritage Bank would be January 1, 2015.
A motion was made by Council Member Aseere and seconded by Council Member
Bushong to award the City’s banking services to Heritage Bank effective January
1, 2015. Roll was called and answered with five ayes with Council Member
Reinersman abstaining from casting a vote, citing a possible conflict since he
has a professional relationship with the bank. Motion carried.
Auction Proceeds – Mr. Moriconi reported the City’s surplus property items
placed in the Kenton County auction in September netted approximately $23,000
in revenue which is more than was budgeted for auction revenue for this fiscal
year.
Parks – Mr. Moriconi reported that new rubber mulch has been installed in the
playground area of Memorial Park. He said it looks great and the City received
a partial grant of $3,000 to offset the cost.
Mayor’s Report – Donna G. Yeager
Mayor Yeager announced that Halloween trick-or-treating hours would be from 6-
8 p.m. on Friday, October 31, 2014.
Privileges of the Floor
Jay Huber – State President of the Kentucky Motorcycle Association – addressed
Council about promoting a drive-in bike night at the new Throttle Stop Bar and
Grill on Taylor Mill Road similar to the bike night at the Quaker Steak and
Lube in Florence. He said these weekly bike events draw a lot of business to
the restaurants. He stated they want to have outdoor music at the Throttle Stop
but has been informed of the City’s Zoning Administrator that zoning
regulations prohibit sound amplifying equipment. He stated this was news to him
as he knows of other businesses and events in the City that have had outdoor
music. Mr. Huber said he would like to work with the City to get these
regulations changed.
Council Members Aseere and Franzen expressed concerns that the Throttle Stop
(which was originally built as a public library) was too close to residential
properties to permit outdoor music. Council Member Franzen stated the outdoor
music that is permitted in the Towne Center is only one weekend per year and is
in conjunction with the City’s annual July 4th Celebration. She stated the
Throttle Stop location is surrounded by homes. Mr. Huber reiterated that they
would only have outdoor music once a week during the summer months and would
work with the City to keep the sound decibels within reason, etc.
Mr. Moriconi looked to the City Attorney for counsel on the procedure to change
the current regulations. Mr. Osterhage believed the correct procedure would be
a zoning text amendment and suggested the City might want to get citizen input.
Mr. Moriconi stated the Council could request a text amendment to change the
regulations regarding outdoor music which would be submitted to PDS for review
and then a public hearing and a recommendation would be made by the Kenton
County Planning Commission for final review and consideration by the Council.
Mr. Huber stated he would like to start the process now so this could be
resolved by Spring 2015. Mr. Moriconi advised any change to the NSC zone would
affect all NSC zones in the city. Mr. Osterhage advised he could draft a
Resolution for Council to consider at the next meeting and decide if they want
to proceed with a text amendment application. There was a brief discussion on
the public hearing procedure and if the Planning Commission recommended
approval for the text amendment but the City disapproved the recommendation and
whether or not the City would then be required to hold its own public hearing.
Rita Hauke – 5346 Oakview Court – questioned the difference between the loud
noise of outdoor music and noise from fireworks that are set off at all hours
of the night, not to mention the debris from those fireworks that land in her
yard. Mr. Osterhage commented that many laws are difficult to enforce and not
all laws get enforced as aggressively as we would like.
Sandra Brewster – 6674 Frontier Drive – stated she didn’t see a problem with
permitting outdoor music and thinks allowing businesses to hold special events
is a good way for those businesses to prosper. She commented that the outdoor
concerts at the St. Cecilia Festival each year is very loud and she can still
hear the music even with her windows closed.
Cancellation of November 3, 2014 Regular Meeting
Mayor Yeager announced she would like to cancel the regular meeting of November
3rd as it is the night before the general election and thought the candidates
for office may want to do some last minute campaigning that night. Mr. Moriconi
suggested holding a special meeting the following Monday on November 10, 2014.
No objections were voice from the Council Members, so the November 3, 2014
meeting will be cancelled.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Bushong
and seconded by Council Member Aseere to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:58 p.m.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in a special session
on Monday, November 10, 2014 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with
Mayor Donna G. Yeager presiding. Mayor Yeager called the meeting to order and
introduced members of the American Legion Moon Brothers Post 275 who led with

Independence Ball at the Senior Center on Saturday, November 15, 2014 at 6:00
p.m. Tickets for his event are $25 per person and will include dinner, dancing
and an award ceremony that will honor some local citizens who have provided
significant support to local veterans during the past year. Roll was called and
the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Jim
Bushong, Carol Franzen, Mike Little and Chris Reinersman. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi and City Clerk Patricia Taney.
Purpose of the Special Meeting

Approval of the October 6, 2014 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Yeager called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular meeting
held on Monday, October 6, 2014. Council Member Reinersman so moved, with
second by Council Member Bushong. No amendments to the minutes were noted and
roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Presentation by Ken Holiday, Huff Realty – Discussion Regarding Development on
Turkeyfoot Road
Mr. Holiday advised Council he is a commercial realtor with the Huff Group and
is working with the current owner - Lakeside Christian Church - to market
approximately 35 acres of land on Turkeyfoot Road near the Industrial Road
intersection which the Church purchased seven years ago. He stated the church
purchased the land with the intent to build a new church as they are landlocked
at their current location on Buttermilk Pike in Lakeside Park. He stated that
several years ago the land was owned by a development company that came before
Council with a request for a rezoning of the land along with a development plan
that included Remke’s grocery moving across the street into a new building
along with other out lots. In 2008 Remke’s backed out of the new development
and the church purchased the land in 2009 with the intent to build a mega
church. Since that time they have decided to build smaller satellite churches
and are now in the process of selling this land.
Mr. Holiday stated there is interest from Thomas More College to build student
housing on a section of this development tract and the church is asking the
City to consider a rezoning that would permit this type of land use. Mr.
Holiday went on to discuss the condemned Heritage Park Apartment complex that
sits adjacent to the church land and which has recently been purchased by DMG
Properties who renovated and renamed the complex Country Club Estates. He
stated he would like to expand on the R-3 zone of the Country Club Estates as
the current zone of the church property is NC (Neighborhood Commercial) and
Thomas More College student housing development would require the R-3 zone. Mr.
Holiday distributed an “Independence Gateway” booklet that provided various
renderings and maps of the development area.
There was a brief discussion with Council regarding the Thomas More student
housing as well as plans for the remaining out lots. Mr. Holiday advised the
student housing would be three-floor apartment buildings totaling 108 units as
well as a student housing center building which would encompass approximately
eleven (11) acres of the development site. When asked about security for the
student campus, he stated the college would be providing campus security at the
student housing site. He also stated that Thomas More College would manage the
student housing but not own the land as it would fall under a master lease.
Mr. Holiday advised the remaining out lots (approximately 24 acres) would
remain a NC zone as a strip center is planned for the parcels along Turkeyfoot
Road. He stated he is currently marketing the out lots but does not have firm
commitments yet.
Mr. Moriconi advised Mr. Holiday that his next step would be to apply for a map
amendment with the Planning and Development Services of Kenton County.
Planning & Development Services – Dennis Gordon & Martin Scribner
Mr. Moriconi introduced Dennis Gordon and Martin Scribner from the Planning &
Development Services of Kenton County (PDS). He stated they would discuss and
answer any questions regarding the next few items on the agenda which include
the dissolution of the City’s Board of Adjustment and Code Enforcement Board
and then participating in the joint city/county code enforcement board.
Mr. Gordon first introduced Dennis Uchtman, Zoning Official who will be
assigned to Independence as its Code Enforcement official.
Council Member Reinersman asked about the continuing education requirements for
planning and zoning officials. Mr. Gordon stated that the required continuing
education for planning and zoning officials, which would include Board of
Adjustment members is 8 hours every two years. He stated the City would get an
appointee to the regional Board if the City Board of Adjustment is disbanded.
Council Member Reinersman expressed concerns that our current Board members are
not current with their continuing education hours as required by State law.
Council Member Brinker commented that members of a regional board may be more
objective in their rulings. Council Member Franzen stated that she agreed to a
point, but was more concerned that the members of a regional board would not be
familiar with our City. Mr. Gordon stated that each city feels they are unique
and Independence is obviously geographically larger than other cities in Kenton
County but a regional board will provide a more objective view.
Council Member Little asked if the City could withdraw from the joint board and
still remain with the One Stop Shop. Mr. Gordon replied yes. He explained the
differences in the Board of Adjustment and the Code Enforcement Board and
advised that if they were not happy with the regional board, the City could
drop out and recreate its own boards.
Council Member Franzen asked who would attend the Board of Adjustment meetings
for the City. Mr. Gordon advised a PDS staff member would be appointed to
handle a City hearing. Mr. Gordon stated the City would have a financial impact
if it was decided to keep its own boards, possibly doubling the cost. He went
on to give further explanation on the process, and staff involvement, for a
Board of Adjustment hearing.
Council Member Reinersman agreed that by disbanding the boards the City would
be giving up a certain amount of control but expressed concern regarding the
needed continuing education of the board members. Mr. Gordon stated that twice
a year PDS sends notice to the City that provides the hours of continuing
education that each board member has logged, as well as notice of training
opportunities. He stated they cannot compel training, but do offer it and that
the appointing authority (City) can enforce training requirements for their
board members. Council Member Aseere asked, of the sixteen entities that
participate in the One Stop Shop, how many have their own boards. Mr. Gordon
replied that about half of the cities have their own boards. Further discussion
centered on the costs to keep the city boards versus joining the regional board
and the impact it would have on the City. Council Member Franzen inquired about
the cost involved with keeping the current boards. Mr. Gordon advised he would
compile the cost information and Council could delay action on the Boards issue
until the next meeting. Council Member Reinersman stated he would like to have
the continuing education report on the City’s current Board of Adjustment
members also. Mr. Gordon stated he would get all the information to Council
before the December meeting. He advised Council to take final action (second
reading of the ordinance) now on adopting the zoning fee schedule as Mr.
Uchtman has already assumed the position as zoning official for the City and
the new fees need to be in effect as soon as possible.
Ordinance No. 2014-O-11 – Adopting PDS Zoning Permit Fee Schedule – 2nd Reading
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Little to adopt Ordinance 2014-O-11. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.

Proposed Ordinance – Approving an Annexation of Approximately 46.225 Acres

North of Taylor Mill Road (SR16) at its Intersection with Said Relocated Hwy
SR17 – 1st Reading
City Attorney Jack Osterhage provided a first reading of a proposed ordinance
that would annex approximately 46.225 acres lying on the easterly side of
relocated KY SR17, just south of Maple Tree lane and north of Taylor Mill Road
at the intersection with the said KY SR17. He reminded the Council they

December meeting.
Proposed Ordinance – Regulating the Containment of Fowl and Other Similar
Animals within the City Limits
Mayor Yeager presented for a first reading a proposed ordinance that would
modify Chapter 91 of the code of ordinances to address the harboring,
maintaining and regulating the containment of fowl and other similar animals
within the City limits. Mr. Osterhage gave the ordinance a first reading.
A lengthy discussion ensued with concerns from Council and residents regarding
acreage restrictions, limiting the number of chickens per single family
dwelling, deed restrictions, the placement of coops within the property lines,
buffer requirements, concerns that coops draw predators, and requiring a permit
first be obtained in order to keep these types of animals.
Mr. Moriconi stated he researched this subject with other cities and found that
most cities do not have an outright ban on harboring chickens or require a
certain amount of land, but do limit the number of chickens one is permitted to
have. Council Member Reinersman suggested that if a subdivision has deed
restrictions that prohibits chickens that it could be dealt with by the
Homeowners’ Association (if there is one) or with filing civil action. He
stated the city’s nuisance ordinance was not sufficient to handle issues with
keeping chickens.
Council Member Little stated he felt Section II of the proposed ordinance was
complicated and difficult to enforce ducks and geese from running at large. He
stated this ordinance to impose regulations may help somewhat, but doesn’t want
to leave loop holes.
Mr. Osterhage advised that the ordinance cannot be constructed in such a way
that no property owner could qualify. Council Member Reinersman stated he felt
this proposed ordinance was a conservative approach to deal with the issue. He
suggested the Council hold a public hearing on the issue to get more input from
the residents. Council Member Franzen commented that she was in favor of some
kind of regulations to deal with the complaints the City has been receiving
about chickens running at large in subdivisions.
Council Member Reinersman suggested that Council consider this first reading as
valid and then submit the permit application regulations to be attached to this
ordinance at the second reading. He also suggested advertising a public hearing
to obtain citizen comments. Mr. Osterhage suggested providing residents a
discretionary period of time to obtain a permit for those who already own
chickens.
A motion was made by Council Member Reinersman and seconded by Council Member
Little to revise the ordinance to include permit application requirements. Roll
was called and answered with five ayes and one abstain vote cast by Council
Member Aseere. Motion carried 5-1.
Resolution No. 2014-R-12 – Opposing the Kentucky State Auditor Recommendation
of Revising the Governance Structure of the Kenton County Airport Board
Mayor Yeager presented to Council for consideration Resolution No. 2014-R-12
which would assert opposition of the State Auditor’s recommendation of revising
the governance structure of the Kenton County Airport Board. Mr. Osterhage read
Resolution No. 2014-R-12.
A motion was made by Council Member Little and seconded by Council Member
Franzen to adopt Resolution No. 2014-R-12.
A brief discussion ensued. Council Member Aseere stated he felt this Resolution
was political mud throwing from the current Kenton County Judge Executive to
the future Judge Executive. He stated Kenton County has created a task force to
develop a new structure for the Airport Board. Council Member Reinersman
suggested deleting the fourth and seventh paragraphs that makes reference to
political desires. Mayor Yeager commented that the citizens of Kenton County
paid for the airport land and she doesn’t want to see it controlled by Ohio.
Council Member Little moved to revise his motion to adopt Resolution No. 2014-
R-12 as amended by striking paragraphs four and seven. A second was made by
Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Bushong
and seconded by Council Member Little to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:58 p.m.

January 5, 2015
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January

Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and opened
with the Pledge of Allegiance. The invocation was given by Council Member
Bushong. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present:
Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Jim Bushong, Lucas Deaton and Carol Franzen. Council
Member Donna Yeager was absent. Also present was City Administrator Chris
Moriconi, City Attorney John Osterhage and City Clerk Patricia Taney.
Approval of the December 1, 2014 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the minutes of the regular
meeting held on Monday, December 1, 2014. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
second by Council Member Aseere. No amendments to the minutes were noted, roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Ordinance No. 2015-O-01 – Approving Various Text Amendments to Update all
Sections of the Zoning Ordinance as Needed to Conform with the Newly Adopted
Kenton County Comprehensive Plan – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2015-
O-01 that would approve various zoning text amendments to update all sections
as needed to conform with the newly adopted Kenton County Comprehensive Plan.
City Attorney Jack Osterhage read Ordinance No. 2015-O-01.
A motion was made by Council member Bushong and seconded by Council Member
Deaton to adopt Ordinance No. 2015-O-01. There being no discussion, roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Ordinance No. 2015-O-02 – Amending Ordinance No. 2005-O-01 – Setting the Time
and Place of City Council Meetings during Week of November General Election –
2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2015-
O-02 that would amend Ordinance No. 2005-O-01 to establish the alternate
meeting date for the November Council meeting as the Monday following a Tuesday
general election duly authorized by the State. City Attorney Jack Osterhage
read Ordinance No. 2015-O-02.
A motion was made by Council Member Franzen and seconded by Council Member
Brinker to adopt Ordinance No. 2015-O-02. There being no discussion, roll was
called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Ordinance No. 2015-O-03 – Amending Nuisance Ordinance Relating to Fowl – 2nd
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council for a second reading Ordinance No. 2015-
O-03 that would amend the City’s general nuisance regulations in Chapter 93 of
the Code of Ordinances to provide for the inclusion of fowl within the
definition and to further address the keeping of fowl, prohibiting the keeping
of roosters and limiting the number of fowl permitted. Mr. Osterhage read
Ordinance No. 2015-O-03.
Council Member Franzen asked for clarification of the wording in Section 3(b)
of the ordinance which requires the fowl to be kept in a secured enclosure from
“sun down to sun up.” Mayor Reinersman explained that there was concern with
nocturnal predators and there would be less risk to those type of predators if
the fowl are fully secured at night. He added the fowl can never be permitted
to roam free and at all times must be secured in the ground area during the
day.
Council Member Aseere asked how the permit process would work. Mayor Reinersman
explained that anyone that keeps fowl on their property would have to register
with the City Clerk at which time they would be provided with a copy of the
ordinance along with the permit. He stated there would be no fee charged to
obtain the permit as the goal of the permit process would be to have a record
on file of fowl owners and ensure the owners have been made aware of the
ordinance regulations.
Council Member Brinker asked who would enforce the ordinance. Mayor Reinersman
advised the enforcement officials would be Kenton County Animal Control or the
City Police Department. Mr. Moriconi stated that he and the Zoning
Administrator Dennis Uchtman would also handle complaints. Council Member
Franzen stated that Animal Control would be available to respond to complaint
calls after normal business hours and that the city’s Zoning Administrator
would handle the fowl enclosure violations.
Liz Stambaugh, 5135 Noble Court – asked if there was a grandfather clause in
the proposed ordinance, asked for clarification on some of the regulations and
commented that she felt the coop requirements were overly restrictive. Mr.
Osterhage advised there is no grandfather clause and that everyone would have
to come into compliance once the ordinance is in effect. Ms. Stambaugh pointed
out the proposed ordinance does not specify front or back yard regarding the 25
feet distance that the enclosures must be situated from the neighbor’s property
line. She also questioned the need for a building permit for the chicken coop.
Mr. Osterhage advised that this ordinance does not address building permits as
that would fall under other city ordinances such as the zoning ordinance and
would be a separate zoning issue.
Lou Dimmerman, 5139 Noble Court – expressed his displeasure with the proposed
ordinance and asked if a chicken coop would be allowed in a front yard. Council
member Franzen advised Mr. Dimmerman that the zoning ordinance would regulate
the placement of such structures. Mr. Dimmerman also was concerned that noise
from the fowl would not be witnessed by police when they arrived and therefore
the owner could not be cited if the police were not a witness to it. Mr.
Osterhage advised the complaining party would have the option to take this
complaint to circuit court.
There being no further discussion, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Bushong to adopt Ordinance No. 2015-O-03. Roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Providing a Credit of the Occupational License Fee for new
Employees as Part of an Economic Development Project by Balluff Inc. under the
Kentucky Business Investment Program – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance to Council that would authorize
a credit of occupational license fees for a 10-year period equal to 0.625% on
the wages of new Balluff Inc. Kentucky resident employees that would be created
as part of an Economic Development Project. Mr. Osterhage read the proposed
ordinance. Council Member Bushong voiced his objection to granting this type of
tax credit, stated he felt the City should never grant abeyance and reminded
the Council Members that tax credits have been requested in the past and has
always been denied. He suggested they give strong consideration to this request
before the second reading of this proposed ordinance. Mayor Reinersman
commented that he feels economic development is critical to the City and
pointed out that other cities offer these tax credit packages. He stated he
strongly supports this tax credit to Balluff Inc., that it will be good for the
city, will help shift the tax burden from the residents and urged the Council
to strongly consider approving this proposal.
Council Member Deaton agreed that the Council should consider all proposals and
review each proposal case by case. He stated this economic development project
by Balluff is in compliance with Kentucky’s business investment program and
strictly regulated by State statute. He stated this has become a common
practice, so much so that the State has mandated procedures to do it correctly.
He stated there will be immediate net gain with the $5,000,000 improvement
project by way of commercial property taxes.
Mayor Reinersman stated this proposed ordinance would be presented for a vote
at the next meeting.
Attorney’s Report – John J. Osterhage
Mr. Osterhage did not have anything to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi did not have anything to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher Reinersman
