Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2004-O-07 - Relating to Residential
Speed Humps – 1st Reading (TABLED)
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance to amend Ordinance
No. 2004-O-07 which relates to residential speed humps. He stated a couple of
loopholes have been discovered with Ordinance No. 2004-O-07 and it doesn’t
cover all scenarios. Mayor Reinersman stated that himself, Mr. Moriconi, Public
Works Director Dan Koch, Attorney Jack Gatlin and several residents met to
discuss the current speed hump process and came up with the proposed amendment
to address the loopholes. He stated there were several residents that signed in
to address Council in regards to this amendment.
Jonicka Baker, 10291 Meadow Glen Drive, Independence – voiced her concerns
regarding cars speeding up and down Meadow Glen Drive. She stated a speed
survey conducted last summer on Meadow Glen Drive tracked the fastest speed of
49 mph within the 20 mph zone. She stated the vote failed last year to add
speed humps on Meadow Glen Drive and is concerned because new homes are still
being built and traffic will continue to increase. Mrs. Baker stated the police
reports she requested from the May patrol observations report only 3 citations
for speeding were issued to residents.
Chief Lucas advised Council that target enforcement was performed on Meadow
Glen after the meeting with the concerned residents regarding the speeding
issue. He stated 8 or 9 citations were written during the four day period as
well as several warnings. Chief Lucas stated the officers were told to use
their discretion on issuing citations.
Mayor Reinersman stated he stands behind Chief Lucas’ approach of community
policing and giving warnings to residents prior to issuing tickets.
Terry Hall Jr., 10311 Meadow Glen Drive, Independence – expressed his concern
for the speeding cars and reckless driving on Meadow Glen Drive and is fearful
for safety of the children. He stated his concern regarding the minimum
requirement of 75% mailed ballots have to be returned and feels the ballot
cards can be easily thrown away.
Council Member Deaton stated there are other streets in the city that have the
same issue and amending this ordinance can help improve the process of having
speed bumps approved by the residents. He suggested the concerned residents go
door to door to discuss the issue with neighbors and remind them to watch for
the ballot cards coming in the mail and to mail in their card to vote.
Council Member Brinker asked for clarification on the proposed speed hump
ordinance that failed in 2015.
Mayor Reinersman stated making changes to the speed hump program was discussed
in 2015 but residents did not mail in the required amount to have the speed
bump issue added to the ballot to vote on it.
Council Member Aseere questioned if the Police Department could decide if a
speed hump was necessary based on the results of a speed survey. Mayor
Reinersman stated the ordinance regulates the process for speed hump approval
and installation. He stated this proposed ordinance will amend the current
process.
Council Member Franzen stated she has issues on her street also. She suggested
the possibility of adding a crosswalk and a stop sign to help slow down traffic
on Meadow Glen Drive. Chief Lucas stated the addition of a crosswalk in the
middle of the street would give a false sense of security to both children and
adults. He stated the City met with some residents on Meadow Glen Drive and
their suggested ideas are included in this proposed ordinance.
Craig Reinhart, 103018 Meadow Glen Drive, Independence – stated he agreed with
the proposed ordinance. He stated he didn’t see the verbiage in the proposed
ordinance regarding who gets to vote. Mr. Reinhart suggested to not require a
minimum number of ballots be returned and remove the proposed threshold of 75%
that must be returned.
Mr. Gatlin stated the proposed ordinance permits one vote per parcel, per
property owner. He stated the ballot card is mailed to each property owner on
record with the Kenton County PVA office. Mr. Gatlin stated the current
ordinance includes a minimum of 75% of the ballots mailed shall be returned;
and if 75% are not returned, no further consideration for speed humps will be
given. He stated the proposed ordinance reduces that amount to 66% of ballot
cards must be returned for consideration.
Council Member Franzen stated she can relate to residents not receiving their
postcards and questioned if online voting was an option. Mr. Gatlin stated
online voting programs are expensive and paid postage postcards are the
cheapest option. He stated it’s important to maintain a threshold on how many
ballots are received and suggests the City include a threshold in regards to
adding speed humps to residential streets.
Julie Reinhart, 103018 Meadow Glen Drive, Independence – expressed her
agreement with Craig Reinhart in regards to not believing there should be a
threshold for how many ballots are returned. She stated she feels it’s also
important to maintain a minimum number of houses included in ballot card voting
process for speed humps. Mrs. Reinhart questioned the cost of a speed hump.
Mr. Moriconi stated the approximate cost is $5500 per speed hump which includes
signage. He stated when this ordinance was written back in 2004, it was
designed to be tough for a reason and if a situation met the criteria it proved
there really was a problem and speed humps were needed.
Council Member Aseere questioned if it would it be possible for the Police
Department to make the determination that a serious problem exists and
recommend speed hump(s) installation. Mayor Reinersman stated the Police
Department assists with the speed survey and they identify if there is a
problem but the ordinance is in place for the speed hump approval process. He
stated that Council can meet further to discuss the issue and come up with
something else regarding amending the speed hump Ordinance No. 2004-O-07.
A motion was made by Council Member Deaton to table this proposed ordinance
regarding changes to the speed hump program and seconded by Council Member
Brinker. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Setting penalties for trucks on city streets where truck
traffic is prohibited – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance to Council which sets penalties
for trucks on city streets where truck traffic is prohibited and was prompted
by the Pelly Road Bridge incident. He stated Pelly Road Bridge was torn up last
year by a semi-truck trying to cross the bridge and resulted in costing the
city hundreds of thousands of dollars. Mayor Reinersman stated the construction
at Pelly Road Bridge is currently underway and will include a culvert pipe and
reinforced concrete walls on the sides.
Mayor Reinersman stated this proposed ordinance prohibits commercial vehicles
weighing in excess of 26,000 pounds to operate on all city streets that have a
NO TRUCKS traffic sign posted, including Pelly Road Bridge. He stated the first
violation of this ordinance includes a $250 fine as well as any remediation
costs for damages to the roadway (if any) and the second violation includes a
$500 fine and/or up to thirty days imprisonment as well as any remediation
costs for damages to the roadway (if any). Mayor Reinersman stated the posted
signs will state fine amounts as well as possible imprisonment to help deter
trucks from driving illegally over Pelly Road Bridge. Mr. Gatlin gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2016-R-08 – MRA Cooperative Agreement
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Resolution No. 2016-R-08 which adopts and
approves the execution of a Municipal Aid Coop Program Contract between the
Commonwealth of Kentucky, Transportation Cabinet and the Department of
Intergovernmental Programs, for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2016, as
provided in the Kentucky Revised Statutes and accepting all streets referred as
part of the Incorporated City. He stated with this agreement, the city agrees
to pay 3% into an insurance fund for Emergency Road Aid in case we need
emergency funds in the future. Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2016-R-08.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2016-R-08,
seconded by Council Member Deaton. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 6-0.
Interlocal Agreement Joining the Regional Ethics Authority
Mayor Reinersman stated he is proposing the city join the Northern Kentucky
Regional Ethics Authority. He stated the City has had issues seeking City
Ethics Board members as well as to trying to get the Board together to meet two
to three times a year to review the Financial Disclosures for City Officials
and various committee members. He stated Northern Kentucky Area Development
District (NKADD) administers the Regional Ethics Board and the cost is $600 a
year. Mayor Reinersman stated the regional board and is more objective than
having an Ethics Board within the city.
Council Member Deaton stated there were missed pages of the agreement. City
Clerk Patricia Taney addressed Council and stated the missing pages were
signature pages for other City’s Mayors and only our City’s signature page was
included to save paper.
Mr. Moriconi stated the regional board joins multiple counties together and the
Board of Directors includes several City Mayors and Judge Executives. He stated
the Directors can appoint Ethics Board Members and the each City’s Council
votes for approval. Patricia Taney stated the nominees for the Regional Ethics
Board can’t be elected or appointed officials.
Mayor Reinersman asked for a motion to approve the city to enter into the
Northern Kentucky Regional Ethics Authority. Council Member Franzen so moved,
seconded by Council Member Bushong. Roll was called and votes were unanimous.
Motion carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he recently left the law firm of Freund, Freeze & Arnold law
firm. He stated himself and Brandon Voekler have started their own law firm. He
stated it will not change anything for the city due to himself and Mr. Voekler
performing 99.9% of the work for the city.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the city is gearing up for the Independence Day celebration
and preparing for fireworks.
Executive Order No. 2016-EO-04 – Assumption of Contract with Gatlin & Voelker
PLLC as City Attorney
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Executive Order No. 2016-EO-04 which
approves the assumption of contract of Jack Gatlin and Gatlin Voelker, PLCC as
City Attorney.
Council Member Aseere made a motion to approve Executive Order No. 2016-EO-04,
seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll was called and answered with 5 ayes and
Council Member Franzen recused herself from voting. Motion carried.
Mayor’s Report – Chris Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated his appreciation to the Deters Company for being
invaluable partners for the Circus events in May and the upcoming Independence
Day celebrations.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Yeager to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:57 p.m.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 11,
2016 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, opened with a moment
of silence and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the following
Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Lucas Deaton,
Carol Franzen and Donna Yeager. Council Member Bushong was absent. Also present
was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Patricia Taney, Assistant
City Clerk Gina Gabbard, City Attorney Jack Gatlin and Public Works Director
Dan Koch.
Approval of the June 6, 2016 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Meeting Minutes for the regular meeting on June
6, 2016. Council Member Franzen stated a change request in the paragraph
discussing Executive Order No. 2106-EO-04. She stated she recused herself from
the vote, not abstained as noted in the minutes. Changes were noted and the

Police Business – Swearing-in of new Police Officer
Mayor Reinersman swore in Police Officer Billy Roberts. The Mayor stated
Officer Roberts transferred from the Burnside Police Department.
Ordinance No. 2016-O-07 – Setting penalties for trucks on city streets where
truck traffic is prohibited – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2016-O-07 which sets penalties for
trucks on city streets where truck traffic is prohibited. Mr. Gatlin gave the
Ordinance a second reading and stated the ordinance has a small change from the
first reading which will allow public school buses for transporting children,
fire, police, other public protection vehicles as well as waste management
vehicles. Mr. Gatlin stated there had been some discussion regarding the
additional restrictions and if they violate the Commerce Clause of the United
States Constitution. He added the Commerce Clause does allow municipalities to
interfere with commerce as long as it’s not excessively burdensome and there is
rational basis.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2016-O-07,
seconded by Council Member Brinker. Roll was called and answered unanimously.
Motion carried 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Ordinance No. 2004-O-07 - Relating to Residential
Speed Humps – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance that relates to
residential speed humps and stated the proposed ordinance was tabled during the
previous month’s meeting. He stated this proposed ordinance amends Ordinance
No. 2004-O-07 which relates to residential speed humps.
Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading. He stated he provided
to Council Ordinance 2004-O-07 indicating the proposed amendments. Mr. Gatlin
stated the following amendments:
∙   Property owners within 1,000 feet of the proposed speed hump location shall
receive a ballot, a minimum of 50% of ballots mailed shall be returned.
∙   A speed survey shall be used as the primary determination for the
percentage of property owners required to install a speed hump.
∙   If the speed survey indicates the 85th percentile speed is at 8 or more
miles per hour over the speed limit, than 51% of property owners need to vote
in favor of speed hump installation.
∙   If the speed survey indicates the 85th percentile speed is between 5 and 7
miles per hour over the speed limit, than 75% of property owners need to vote
in favor of speed hump installation.
∙   Changing from one vote per household to one vote per parcel per property
owner.
∙   Upon approval of Council, a community may request a second speed survey,
one year after the initial vote, and if the second speed survey indicates at
the 85th percentile, the speed is at eight or more miles per hour over the
speed limit, then a street may engage in a second petition and vote.
Council Member Franzen stated she would also like to add to the last amendment
noted that if the community goes through second petition and the vote fails,
they will have to wait 5 years until they can request an additional speed
survey through Council.
Jonicka Baker, 10291 Meadow Glen Drive, Independence – expressed her
appreciation to Council Member Franzen for her help with changing the ordinance
regarding the speed hump process.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Zoning Text Amendment Adding Restrictions on
Outdoor Storage and Business Activities with the DI and GMU Zones - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which adopts a
zoning text amendment adding restrictions on outdoor storage and business
activities within the DI (Downtown Independence) and GMU (Gateway Mixed Use)
zones. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading. He stated KCPC
(Kenton County Planning Commission) has made a favorable recommendation to
adding the restrictions on outdoor storage and business activities. He stated
their reasons for supporting the proposed text amendment are: the added
restrictions are allowable as authorized by KRS (Kentucky Revised Statute)
100.203 (1), are appropriate given the purposes of the DI and GMU zones, the DI
and GMU zones are intended to allow development at a pedestrian scale and
enhance the community, they help maintain or enhance the community character in
these areas and consistent with similar restrictions in other commercial zones
within Independence.
Award Bid – Frontier Drive Street Repairs
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council the four bids that were received for the
Frontier Drive reconstruction project. He stated the Engineer’s estimate was
$143.100 and the lowest bid was from JPS Construction in the amount of
$119,316.
Council Member Yeager made a motion to award the bid to JPS Construction for
the Frontier Drive reconstruction project in the amount of $119,316. Council
Member Aseere seconded. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 5-0.
Award Bid – 2016 General Street Repair Program
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council the five bids that were received for the

subdivisions. He stated the Engineer’s estimate was $600,600 and the lowest bid

Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence – addressed council to discuss the
noise ordinance. She stated there are autistic children in her neighborhood who

Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview Court, Independence – addressed council to complain

Pelly Road Bridge Update
Public Works Director Dan Koch updated Council on the Pelly Road Bridge
project. He stated the culvert pipe was installed the previous weekend. Mr.
Koch stated the wing walls will be poured very soon and then the block walls
will start to be set and it will start to look like a bridge.
Mayor Reinersman thanked Mr. Koch as well as the City and Kenton County’s

Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he wanted to update Council on the SD1 (Sanitation District
No. 1) Interlocal Agreement situation. He stated several months ago Council
authorized to participate in potential litigation with 10-12 other cities
against SD1. Mr. Gatlin stated that SD1 has agreed to the proposed language and
they will be sending out a new Interlocal Agreement for all cities to sign as
well as a new lateral lines maintenance program. He stated the changes that are
included in the new agreement are: 1) that SD1 will continue to fund an amount
around $350,000 per year, and 2) SD1 will be solely responsible for costs
incurred with fixing necessary lateral lines as well as any remediation costs
for sidewalks, roads, etc. Mr. Gatlin stated with this new Interlocal
Agreement, the indemnification became null and void and the city will receive a
refund.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated his appreciation to everyone who attended the Independence
Celebration during the July 4th event and thanked volunteers and city staff for
their help.
Mayor’s Report – Chris Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated his appreciation to everyone that was a part of the

August 1, 2016
The regularly scheduled Independence City Council Meeting was CANCELLED
August 15, 2016
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August
15, 2016 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and opened
with the Pledge of Allegiance and Council Member Bushong led the invocation.

Sanitation District No. 1 Agreements – For Participation in Private Sewer
Lateral Repair Program and Interlocal Cooperation for Infrastructure Projects,
Programs or Policies   
Mayor Reinersman stated several months ago the city along with several other
cities, threatened a lawsuit against SD1 (Sanitation District No. 1) regarding
the private sewer lateral repair agreement. He stated the most recent agreement
stated the property owner was responsible for repairs under the right of way
and that changes with the new agreement.
Mr. Gatlin stated the new SD1 Board and several Northern Kentucky Mayors
amicably worked out a resolution regarding the lateral lines repair agreement.
He stated the first agreement includes participation in the private sewer
lateral repair program which SD1 will budget $350,000 each year for repairs,
unless a 60 day notice is given prior to the budget cycle. Mr. Gatlin stated
there is no indemnification due to the new agreement and SD1 will be solely
responsible for all lateral line repairs in the right of way. He stated the
second agreement is the Master Interlocal Cooperation Agreement which grants
cooperation between the city and SD1 for infrastructure projects so SD1 can
make repairs needs as needed within the right of way.
There was some discussion with Council regarding the SD1 letter regarding the
$350,000 SD1 has budgeted for repairs as well as the length of the agreement.
Mayor Reinersman stated this agreement removes the responsibility from the
property owners for the right of way repairs and puts it back on SD1. He stated
the budgeted amount of $350,000 is expected to be more than enough to cover any
repairs incurred and is approximately 15% higher than the amount budgeted 2
years ago. Mr. Gatlin stated this agreement isn’t perfect but the three Judge
Executives are approvers of SD1’s budget and won’t back down on this issue in
the future.
Council Member Bushong made a motion to approve the Mayor to sign the SD1
Agreement for Participation in Private Sewer Lateral Repair Program as well as
the SD1 Interlocal Cooperation Agreement for Infrastructure Projects, Programs
or Policies, seconded by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and there were
4 votes in favor of and 2 opposing votes from Council Member Yeager and Council
Member Aseere. Motion carried 4-2.
Ordinance No. 2016-O-08 – Amending Ordinance No. 2004-O-07 - Relating to
Residential Speed Humps – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Ordinance No. 2016-O-08 which is an
ordinance relating to residential speed humps.
Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2016-O-08 a second reading and stated this
ordinance amends Ordinance No. 2004-O-07 which relates to residential speed
humps.
Mr. Gatlin stated the following amendments to Ordinance No. 2004-O-07:
∙   Property owners within 1,000 feet of the proposed speed hump location shall
receive a ballot, a minimum of 50% of ballots mailed shall be returned.
∙   A speed survey shall be used as the primary determination for the
percentage of property owners required to install a speed hump.
∙   If the speed survey indicates the 85th percentile speed is at 8 or more
miles per hour over the speed limit, than 51% of property owners need to vote
in favor of speed hump installation.
∙   If the speed survey indicates the 85th percentile speed is between 5 and 7
miles per hour over the speed limit, than 75% of property owners need to vote
in favor of speed hump installation.
∙   Changing from one vote per household to one vote per parcel per property
owner.
∙   Upon approval of Council, a community may request a second speed survey,
one year after the initial vote, and if the second speed survey indicates at
the 85th percentile, the speed is at eight or more miles per hour over the
speed limit, then a street may engage in a second petition and vote. However if
the community goes through second petition and the vote fails, they will have
to wait 5 years until they can request an additional speed survey through
Council.
Mayor Reinersman asked Council for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2016-O-08
which amends Ordinance No. 2004-O-07 relating to residential speed humps.
Council Member Franzen made a motion, seconded by Council Member Yeager. Roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2016-O-09 – Adopting Zoning Text Amendment Adding Restrictions on
Outdoor Storage and Business Activities with the DI and GMU Zones – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Ordinance No. 2016-O-09 which is an
ordinance that adopts a zoning text amendment adding restrictions on outdoor
storage and business activities within the DI (Downtown Independence) and GMU
(Gateway Mixed Use) zones.
Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2016-O-09 a second reading. He stated KCPC
(Kenton County Planning Commission) has made a favorable recommendation to
adding the restrictions on outdoor storage and business activities. He stated
their reasons for supporting the proposed text amendment are: the added
restrictions are allowable as authorized by KRS (Kentucky Revised Statute)
100.203 (1), are appropriate given the purposes of the DI and GMU zones, the DI
and GMU zones are intended to allow development at a pedestrian scale and
enhance the community, they help maintain or enhance the community character in
these areas and consistent with similar restrictions in other commercial zones
within Independence.
Mayor Reinersman asked Council for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2016-O-09
which adopts a zoning text amendment to add restrictions on outdoor storage
within the DI and GMU Zones. Council Member Yeager made a motion, seconded by
Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion
carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2016 Property Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council the proposed ordinance which adopts the
property tax rates for 2016. He stated the compensating rate is 0.275 on real
property and 0.776 on personal property. Mayor Reinersman stated to balance the
2016/2017 budget, the real property tax rate needs to be 0.271. He stated for
the average home price of $161,000, it would be an increase of about $27 for
the year. He added the personal property rate will stay at 0.642.
Council Member Aseere asked the Mayor to list the highlights of the 2016/2017
budget changes. Mayor Reinersman stated significant items included setting
aside $100,000 for the new digital radio system in 2018, the Pelly Road Bridge
project, Holton Drive replacement, increasing the roads budget from $750,000 to
$1,000,000, which puts us closer to the engineers estimate of $1,200,000 per
year needed to stay on track, as well as adding a much needed public works
employee.
Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading. He stated the proposed
tax rate for real property is $0.271 for each one hundred dollars of the
assessed value and the personal property tax rate will remain at $0.642 for
each one hundred dollars of the assessed value.

Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2016-O-10 which adopts the property

Proposed Ordinance – Code Enforcement Amendment – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council proposed ordinance which amends
procedures of the code enforcement board and supplements Ordinance 2015-O-20
and section 93 of the Independence Code of Ordinances.
Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading. He stated House Bill
422 passed earlier this year and the proposed ordinance deals with housekeeping
items regarding nuisance issues and foreclosed properties. Mr. Gatlin states
with the passing of House Bill 422, this proposed ordinance includes several
items: extending lien statue limitations to 10 years, a creation of a new
lienholder electronic notification system, an interlocal agreement between PDS
and the city which states that PDS will handle the updates to the new
lienholder notification system, citations become final if not appealed or paid
within 7 days, and the approval of the Mayor to appoint members to the Joint
Code Enforcement Board. He stated since the city is part of the Kenton County
Joint Code Enforcement Board, most of these changes will be the responsibility
of PDS and the Joint Code Enforcement Board.
Council Member Deaton asked where the reimbursement monies come from to Joint
Code Enforcement Board Members for participating on the board. Mayor Reinersman
stated Board Members receive a stipend and it comes from PDS’ budget, not from
the city.
Council Member Franzen stated the city’s previous Code Enforcement Board had
issues with attendance and were unable to form a quorum for meetings. Mr.
Gatlin stated the training is critical for Code Enforcement Board Members
because there are statutory requirements for training.
Chris Moriconi stated a model nuisance ordinance will be presented in the
coming months which relates to this issue.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated on his website for his own law firm, a picture of the
Independence courthouse is featured on the main banner page.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the Public Works Department currently has two separate
crews working on two different projects in the city with a new employee
recently added to the department.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman

there will be a biscuits and gravy eating contest at 9:00 a.m. Mayor Reinersman
stated the Parks and Recreation Department has several events going on such as

that you can bring your own wine held on Friday September 23rd and True Crimes
in Independence sponsored by the William Durr Library are held on October 3, 10
and 17 and need to register on library’s website.

OpenGov Demo – Website displaying transparency to city financials
Mayor Reinersman stated OpenGov is a transparency website that is up and ready
for Council and the public to access the city’s financial information. Mr.
Moriconi stated Mayor Reinersman has been supportive on transparency to the
public by adding Council Meeting Agendas on Facebook, communication to the
public via newsletters and social media. Mr. Moriconi stated OpenGov is a very
user friendly site that can be accessed from the city’s website by clicking on
the OpenGov link on the home page. He added his appreciation to the Finance
Director Terri Hudson and City Clerk Gina Gabbard for their help with
implementing this new site.
Finance Director Terri Hudson demonstrated how to get to the OpenGov site from
the home page on the city’s website. She stated the current reports available
for public viewing are 1) Revenues and Expenses, 2) Assets and Liabilities and
3) Budget versus Actual and each report contains three years’ worth of data.
Mrs. Hudson stated on the left column, are example questions the public can
click on to see financial information displayed with graphs as well as the
dollar breakdown. She stated the graphs and data can be downloaded and
displayed in various graph types and will be updated each month.
Council Member Brinker asked if other cities were using this site or something
similar. Mayor Reinersman stated Edgewood, Covington, and Ft Wright are
currently utilizing OpenGov. He stated OpenGov is a great tool for transparency
for both Council Members as well as citizens to view where the tax dollars are
being spent.
Council Member Deaton questioned the cost of the program. Mrs. Hudson responded
the cost was approximately $6,000 which included training and initial set up
fees and years two and three will be around $3,000.
Mr. Moriconi stated a lot of research was done prior to signing up for OpenGov
including conference calls, visiting other cities and talking with other
Mayors.
Donald Barnett, 788 Jimae Ave, Independence, KY. Mr. Barnett stated his
appreciation to Council for this program and believes it will be a useful tool.
He stated he likes the quick access this gives to residents that are interested
in the city’s financials and eliminates the waiting period for copies.

Proposed Ordinance – Adopting New Personnel Policies and Procedures Handbook -
1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which repeals all prior
personnel policies and procedures and adopts a new personnel policies and
procedures handbook for City employees. He stated the KLC Model Handbook and
Northern Kentucky Area Development District Handbook were used as reference and
it was a two year process to complete. He thanked Mr. Moriconi, Chief Lucas,
former City Clerk Patricia Taney, current City Clerk Gina Gabbard and Jack
Gatlin.
Mayor Reinersman stated the first item changing is comp time. He stated it will
be eliminated and hourly employees will be paid time and a half for hours
worked over 40 hours. Mayor Reinersman stated salaried employees will now be
eligible for flex time which needs to be used within 30 days with supervisor
approval. He stated paid time off will go from 3 buckets: annual paid leave
(APL), sick time and personal time into one bucket of APL. Mayor Reinersman
stated employees with at least one year of service will gain a half a day of
paid time off per year with the new policy.
Mayor Reinersman stated the workers compensation policy will change from six
months of full pay to 30 days. He stated the City has one of the worst
multipliers in the state and the premium has increased $100,000 in the past few
years. Mayor Reinersman stated employees may use APL concurrently with short
term disability to help supplement their pay. He stated employees are able to
donate APL to co-workers if something unforeseen happened and they exhaust all
of their APL. Mayor Reinersman stated modified duty is an option to employees
if work is available and fits within their restrictions. He stated the last
change was the addition of a social media policy.
Council Member Deaton asked if employees are able to share APL time and when
the new policy goes into effect. Mayor Reinersman responded that employees may
donate APL time to each other and if passed in December with the second
reading, the new handbook would be effective January 1, 2017. Council Member
Deaton asked what happens to the accumulated comp time. Mayor Reinersman stated
employees won’t lose the accumulated comp time and it will be available for
them to use.
Council Member Yeager stated she would like the City to look into KLC’s
definition of hourly and salary employees for the Park and Recreation Director.
Mayor Reinersman stated he will look into it. Council Member Deaton asked if
other cities have different workers comp policies for Police verses
Administration employees. Mr. Gatlin stated legally, employers cannot
discriminate on workers comp regarding class. Council Member Aseere asked if
there were any retirement changes in the new handbook. Mayor Reinersman stated
there are no changes regarding retirement but there have been discussions of
adding a 401k matching plan for employees. He stated it’s a budget concern and
will be discussed after the first of the year.
Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2016-R-09 – Vet Clinic Text Amendment
Mayor Reinersman stated Resolution No. 2016-R-09 provides a proposal for a text
amendment which allows Veterinary offices for small animals and small animal
clinics as permitted use in the NC Zone.
Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2016-R-09. He stated if the resolution is passed
by Council, it will go to Planning and Development Services (PDS) for review.
Mr. Gatlin added the Kenton County Planning Commission will conduct a public
hearing and make a recommendation concerning the application. Mr. Gatlin stated
if approved, it will come back to Council for a first and second reading and
would be adopted by ordinance.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2016-R-09 which
provides a proposal to add veterinary offices for small animals and small
animal clinics as a permitted use in the NC Zone. Council Member Yeager so
moved, seconded by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 4-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated Ordinances will now be codified and published on a monthly
basis so information will be more up to date and available to residents
regarding local legislation. He stated he will be working remotely from the
Municipal Center on Thursdays and will only need to utilize wifi, there will be
no cost to the city.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the new apartments behind Kroger is having their Grand
Opening Open House on November 15 from noon until 8:00 p.m. He also stated the
20th Annual Christmas Walk will be on December 3, 2016.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman congratulated the newly elected Council Members and expressed
his appreciation to the Council Members whose term ends at the end of this
year.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Deaton to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:41 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
9, 2017 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and opened
with the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll
was called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere,
John Deaton, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney and Greg Waite. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, City
Attorney Jack Gatlin, and Police Chief Tony Lucas.
Approval of the December 5, 2016 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting on December 5,
2016.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on December 5, 2016. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
a second by Council Member Aseere. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Police Recognitions - Promotions of Runge, Paul, Ferayorni, Fuson and Kenner
Mayor Reinersman stated his appreciation and presented plaques for recent
Police promotions. Explorer Tyler Runge was promoted to Captain, Scott Paul to
Captain, Brian Ferayorni to Lieutenant, Nathan Fuson to Sergeant and Andrew
Kenner to Sergeant.
Resolution No. 2017-R-01 – Sponsoring a Proposed Text Amendment for Design
Standards
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Resolution No. 2017-R-01 which sponsors
proposed text amendment for design standards in residential housing. He stated
if this resolution is approved, it is sent to Planning and Development Services
for a public hearing and recommendation from the Kenton County Planning
Commission, then would come back to Council for final approval. Mayor
Reinersman stated the proposed residential design standards are for new
developments only and would limit vinyl, metal, stucco, concrete and aluminum
siding to 25% but there are architectural features that can be added to
increase the allowable amount of up to 50% siding on the home. Mr. Gatlin read
Resolution No. 2017-R-01.
Council Member Taney asked if any other Northern Kentucky communities have
adopted residential design standards. Mayor Reinersman stated Villa Hills and
Union have implemented design standards and PDS helped draft the language in
the resolution. He stated the proposed design standards will not affect
existing developments.
Council Member Aseere asked how larger lots could be associated with this
change. Mayor stated the options are to adopt change by text amendment or the
property could be re-zoned. Mr. Gatlin stated text amendments are the easier
way to update the lot sizes but wouldn’t effect lots that were previously
platted.
Council Member Taney made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2017-R-01 which
sponsors a proposed text amendment for residential design standards in new
developments. Council Member Waite seconded. Roll was called and answered with
5 yes votes and 1 no vote from Council Member Deaton. Motion carried 5-1.
Resolution No. 2017-R-02 – Hogreffe Property Extension to Kenton County School
Board
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Resolution No. 2017-R-02 which allows the
Kenton County School Board an additional 10 years to build a school named after
G. Wayne Bridges at 314 Hogreffe Road. He stated the land was deeded by the
Bridges family to the Kenton County School Board in 2006 with the stipulation
of building a new school within 12 years. Mayor Reinersman added due to
economic downturn around 2008, plans haven’t been made and is still currently
on hold.
Council Member Aseere asked who would make the determination on the traffic
flow if a school was built on Hogreffe. Mr. Moriconi stated a school plan would
be submitted for review and a traffic study would be conducted at that time.
Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2017-R-02 and stated this extension would
provide the Kenton County School Board until 2028 to build a school on the
property.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2017-R-02.
Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second by Council Member Taney. Roll
was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Declare Surplus Property – Dodge Chargers and telephones
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a 2009 Dodge Charger, three 2007 Dodge
Chargers and 50 Avaya telephones that have been declared surplus property. The
Mayor stated the vehicles will be auctioned on govdeals.com. He added the phone
system is original from when the city building was built in 2004 and have been
recently replaced with a new IP phone system. Mr. Moriconi stated the phones
will be turned over to Cincinnati Bell and we’ll receive a rebate for close to
$1,000.
Council Member Aseere made a motion to declare the 2009 Dodge Charger, three
2007 Dodge Chargers, 50 Avaya phones as surplus property, seconded by Council
Member Waite. Roll was called and answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin welcomed the new Council Members and encouraged them to attend the
Kentucky League of Cities’ City Officials Academy. He stated PDS along with
several Northern Kentucky cities have worked together over the past year and
together created a joint agreement regarding mini cell phone towers. Mr. Gatlin
stated PDS has approved new regulations and any cell phone provider that
approaches the city will have to go to PDS first. He stated when that happens,
Council will then pass an ordinance and resolution specific to that cell phone
provider.
Council Member Taney asked if the mini cell towers would be installed on phone
poles and if these would generate any income for the city. Mr. Moriconi stated
they can be attached to existing poles or may need to install a new pole if one
isn’t in the correct spot per the cell phone company. Mr. Gatlin stated the
city is able to charge the provider the cost of the installation but aren’t
able to generate any income.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi welcomed the new members of Council and told them to reach out to
him with any questions.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Executive Order No. 2017-EO-01 – Appointment to the Telecommunications Board of
Northern Kentucky
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2017-EO-01 which appoints
Patricia H. Taney to the Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky for the
term of January 2017 through December 2018.

the Planning and Development Services Council
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2017-EO-02 which re-appoints
Christopher J. Reinersman to the Planning and Development Services Council for
2017.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Engelman
and seconded by Council Member Deaton to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:53 p.m.

Mayor Reinersman stated there were a couple changes made to the minutes prior
to the meeting. He stated the changes included updating the number of surplus
Chargers from four to three and the vote to approve the January meeting minutes
answered all ayes. He asked Council if there were any additional changes or
corrections they would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting
on January 9, 2017.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on January 9, 2017. Council Member Taney so moved, with a

Proposed Ordinance – Text Amendment for Small Veterinary Clinic in NC Zone –
1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which is a text
amendment adding Veterinary offices for small animals and small animal clinics
as a permitted use to the NC Zone. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading and stated the recommendations from the Kenton County Planning
Commission are to pass the text amendment because it’s reasonable, appropriate
and consistent with the purpose of the NC Zone.
Resolution No. 2017-R-03– Transfer Control of Fowler Creek Sewer to Sanitation
District No. 1
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Resolution No. 2017-R-03 which transfers
the control of Fowler Creek Sanitary Sewer System to Sanitation District No. 1
(SD1). Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2017-R-03 and stated the Memorandum of
Understanding between Sanitation District No. 1 and the city is attached. He
stated the Memorandum states that once the transfer is complete, SD1 will be
solely responsible for the maintenance, repair and upkeep of the Fowler Creek
Sewer System and releases the city of any obligation. Mr. Gatlin added the
agreement from 1999 states once the debt is paid off and all litigation has
been resolved, the legal title shall pass to the district.
Council Member Taney stated her concern regarding the language in the
memorandum to include all sewer systems in Independence, not just Fowler Creek.
Council Member Aseere asked if there is a possibility that SD1 would raise the
rates for residents with the addition of Fowler Creek. The Mayor stated rates
are district wide, not particular to each city. Mr. Gatlin added that rate
changes of 3-4% have to be passed with the majority vote from the fiscal
courts.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2017-R-03 which
transfers all sewer systems in the city, including Fowler Creek, to Sanitation
District No. 1. Council Member Taney seconded. Roll was called and answered
unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated there is only about 1.5% remaining to collect on the Fowler
Creek Sewer debt and the majority of the balance is from developers whom have
an agreement with the city to pay as the lots sell.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the city finally received the land and water conservation
grant approval for the basketball courts behind the municipal center. He stated
the $75,000 grant will provide two full-sized basketball courts, a paved road
from Peach Drive and a parking lot, all of which should be completed sometime
in 2017. Mr. Moriconi thanked Senator Thayer for his support with the city’s
request.
Mr. Moriconi stated the county wide sign ordinance is under review and PDS is
currently updating it. He stated it should be coming to Council in May or June
in the form of a text amendment. Mr. Moriconi stated PDS is also working on
county wide zoning update and Council can expect to review later this year.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman presented the Annual Audit results for the fiscal year ending
June 30, 2016. He stated it was a clean audit and the year ended with a reserve
large enough to cover over five months’ worth of expenses.
Mayor Reinersman stated six officers attended the inauguration in Washington
D.C. and thanked both the officers that attended as well as the officers that
were here and helped cover extra shifts.
Mayor Reinersman stated there was a meeting with the Home Builders Association,
Arlinghaus, Fischer and Drees regarding residential home design standards. He
stated it was a good meeting and the builders are working on a list of
suggestions on building standards. Council Member Franzen asked if we can re-
zone lots to make them larger. Mayor Reinersman stated it’s possible but is
tough to change residential zones. He stated the property taxes generated on
some starter homes do not cover the long term cost of services. Mr. Moriconi
stated there are other materials that can be used besides brick such as
concrete siding.
Mayor Reinersman stated the public access show City Talk is being produced
again by TBNK. He stated himself along with Mr. Moriconi and other local mayors
will be doing about eight 30 minute shows per year with the first episode
airing in March.

March 6, 2017
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of March 6, 2017
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 6,
2017 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, City Attorney Jack
Gatlin and Police Chief Tony Lucas.
Approval of the February 6, 2017 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting on February 6,
2017.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on February 6, 2017. Council Member Waite so moved, with a
second by Council Member Deaton. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Police Recognitions - Promotions of Perkins, Young, Boyle and Wood
Mayor Reinersman stated his appreciation and presented plaques for recent
Police promotions. Robert Perkins has been promoted to Detective, Jeffery Young
to Sergeant, Jacob Boyle to Lieutenant and Russell Wood to Captain. He also
thanked retired Captain Mike Thatcher for his years of service with the city.
Ordinance No. 2017-O-01 - Text Amendment for Small Veterinary Clinic in NC Zone
– 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Ordinance No. 2017-O-01 which is a text
amendment adding Veterinary offices for small animals and small animal clinics
as a permitted use in the NC Zone. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2017-O-01 a
second reading and stated the recommendations from the Kenton County Planning
Commission are to pass the text amendment because it’s reasonable, appropriate
and consistent with the purpose of the NC Zone.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2017-O-01 which
is a text amendment adding Veterinary office for small animals and small animal
clinics within the NC Zone. Council Member Aseere seconded. Roll was called and
answered unanimously. Motion carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated it’s been a busy Legislative session so changes can be
expected in the near future. He stated he’s noticed an increase of foreclosures
within the city in recent months but the silver lining is delinquent taxes
should be paid soon. Mr. Gatlin stated northern cities within Kenton County are
noticing abandoned houses which are being turned into flop houses and are
rented by the room. He added Kenton County is working with PDS to come up with
a model ordinance to help regulate these situations.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated with recent storms and high winds, he encourages residents
to secure trampolines and portable basketball goals. He stated the Mayor and
himself are involved in new TBNK show called City Talk and it will air at 6:00
p.m. on Thursdays. He stated City Talk will include local Mayors discussing
issues such as zoning, finance and budget.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the updated residential design standards had been
updated with suggestions from the Home Builders Association, Arlinghaus
Builders, Fischer Homes and Drees.
Council Member Franzen suggested changing the verbiage in section C that refers
to the same floor plan to same house front or façade. Council Member Taney
stated she agreed and suggested the verbiage to say front elevation in place of
floor plan. Council Member Franzen stated she would like to see ‘the Zoning
Administrator with the approval of’ the City’s chief administrative official,
added to section E to the waivers section.
Council Member Deaton stated he doesn’t like the residential building standards
or the government telling him how to build his house. He questioned where the
families are going to come from that can afford these expensive homes and where
are the jobs in Northern Kentucky that have an income of $35,000 to $75,000 in
Northern Kentucky. Mayor Reinersman stated current zoning laws already regulate
certain things that can and cannot be done when building a home. He added the
city already has a large inventory of starter homes and he estimates the taxes
collected for a neighborhood with $125,000 houses is not enough to cover the
cost of services for street maintenance and emergency services.
Council Member Franzen questioned how much the increase would be for the
additional brick on homes and Mayor Reinersman stated the building inspector
estimated $5,000 to $8,000. Council Member Aseere stated he feels like we are
pulling the rug out underneath the builders that have intentions of building in
the city and would like to discuss improving the school district or bringing
more businesses rather than dictating how homes are built. Mayor Reinersman
stated the obligation to tax payers to make sure we can sustain and maintain
our city.
There was some discussion about the possibility of increasing the lot sizes up
to half acre. Mayor Reinersman stated it would cause new construction to slow
down and would require a map amendment. Mr. Gatlin stated with removing high
density zones, there could be legal challenges for the city. Council Member
Waite stated most subdivisions have covenants that already dictate construction
requirements. Mayor Reinersman stated these standards will help uniform
building standards to include the subdivisions that do not have covenants.
Council Member Aseere thanked the Mayor for bringing the vinyl restriction down
to 50% from 75%. Mayor Reinersman stated it was an agreed amount after meeting
and receiving input from the builders.
Mr. Gatlin stated Resolution No. 207-R-01 authorized Mr. Moriconi to submit
application for the hearing with the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC)
and if KCPC recommends the text amendment, it will come back to Council for
final approval.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way – Mrs. Cook stated we might be losing young families
that can’t afford these new homes. She stated building standards were already
addressed with the subdivisions off Fowler Creek. Mayor Reinersman stated he
believes it was a zone change and a stone or brick requirement was added with
the approval of the zone change.
Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike – Mr. Cobble stated if the sirens don’t start
going off when we have storms, no one will live in the city. Mayor Reinersman
stated the National Weather Service coded the alert wrong. He stated it was a
critical mistake and they are working to ensure it doesn’t happen again.
Mayor Reinersman stated the Easter Egg Hunt is on Saturday, April 8th at
Memorial Park. He stated Hickory Grove has partnered with the city and taking
this year’s event to a new level with great prizes.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 1,
2017 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, City Attorney Jack
Gatlin, Police Chief Tony Lucas and Public Services Director Dan Koch.
Approval of the April 3, 2017 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting on April 3,
2017.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on April 3, 2017. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Aseere. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.

community put forth in extracurricular activities in addition to their
academics.

Mayor Reinersman presented a Proclamation to recognize the month of June 2017
as Independence Hates Heroin Month.
Ordinance No. 2017-O-02 - Closing proposed street for Elmer Subdivision/
Marshall Road– 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Ordinance No. 2017-O-02 which closes a
platted proposed street filed of record for the Elmer Davis Subdivision which
abuts to Marshall Road. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2017-O-02 a second
reading and stated the current property owners have requested that the City

Proposed Ordinance – Amending Zoning Ordinance to add Residential Design
Standards – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which amends the
zoning ordinance to add residential design standards for new detached single
family homes. He stated the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) recently
had a public hearing and they did not recommend approval based on their
attorney’s opinion. Mayor Reinersman stated the link to the video of the KCPC
hearing was sent to Council for review.
Brian Miller, 2751 Circleport Drive, Erlanger, KY – Executive Vice President of
the Home Builders Association of Northern Kentucky Brian Miller, stated there
is a price down effect which suggests for every $1,000 you raise the cost of a
home, you price out 1,530 households which can no longer afford the home. Mr.
Miller stated upcoming economic development will bring thousands of jobs paying
$13.00 to $16.00 an hour to Northern Kentucky. He stated growth is currently
stagnant in Kenton County with both single family residences and new commercial
structures. Mr. Miller stated new housing pays for itself with real estate
taxes, occupational taxes and support services. He stated there is a ripple
effect with jobs and occupational taxes, and every home built supports 3.3
jobs.
Mayor Reinersman asked Mr. Miller if he felt like the recommendations and
suggestions of the HBA and local builders were heard and considered during the
meetings with City Officials. Mr. Miller stated the original draft ordinance
was managed down some per their recommendations.
Council Member Deaton stated his concern for the job market and asked Mr.
Miller where the new jobs are coming from and how are people going to afford
building a new home. Mr. Miller stated the HBA is involved in every
comprehensive plan in Northern Kentucky. He stated Amazon Prime will have 2,600
jobs to fill in the upcoming year and 5,000 jobs by 2121. Mr. Miller stated
workforce development works with area high schools and provides adult education
which helps prepare for middle class jobs. He stated over 46,500 jobs will be
needed in the construction industry in the next 10 years.
Council Member Franzen stated she disagrees with Mr. Miller’s statement that
new homes pay for themselves. She stated the city’s budget doesn’t validate his
point and the services of snow removal, police protection, street lights and
the million dollar budget for street repairs isn’t enough to keep up. Council
Member Franzen stated Council tries to do their best not to raise the tax rate
each year and believes there’s a possibility of street assessments in the
future. She stated ten to twenty years ago, Council let every developer come in
and build whatever they wanted and now the city can’t afford to keep up with
the streets. She stated she is representing the current taxpayers of
Independence and Council has a responsibility to say when enough is enough and
stated implementing these design standards may help decrease the need to raise
taxes.
Mr. Miller stated when residents support Independence businesses, it generates
occupational taxes for the city. He stated HBA advocates for the overall
economic health of the community. Mayor Reinersman stated Mr. Miller stated in
the KCPC Meeting that most builders are already building to these proposed
standards. Mr. Miller stated some are building with the proposed design
standards and some are not.
Pam Burton, 6415 Lakearbor Drive, Independence – Mrs. Burton, a homeowner in
the Lakefield subdivision, stated she started the neighborhood Facebook page.
She stated some neighbors are worried about their property values with the
recent addition of starter homes on the same street as their two story, four
bedroom homes. Mrs. Burton stated her favor of the residential design standards
and asked Council to approve the proposed design standards to help provide
better quality homes in the city.
Council Member Aseere stated selfishly he likes the idea of adding building
standards but doesn’t believe the government should tell a private property
owner what they can do with their property. Council Member Deaton stated he
doesn’t agree with having the government telling him that he can’t build a
vinyl home. Mayor Reinersman stated zoning now regulates several items such as
lot and home size, how tall your grass can be, etc. He stated the standards are
simply no more than 50 % vinyl siding and there are other aesthetic features
that can be added to use more vinyl. Mayor Reinersman stated the new
construction permits go through the building inspector for approval, if there’s
an issue, it goes to the Zoning Administrator and City Administrator for
review. Mr. Gatlin stated, if the Zoning Administrator and City Administrator
deny the plan, the next option is going to the Board of Adjustments and the
final appeal step would be circuit court.
Council Member Taney stated we aren’t trying to dictate taste but implement
design standards to help keep current property values up. She stated the extra
$5,000 to $8,000 won’t prohibit someone from getting the loan and would only be
about $25 more a month.
Bob Schroeder – 142 Barnwood Drive, Edgewood, KY – Mr. Schroeder asked if the
discussion was had regarding the possible cost increase of building permits.
Mayor Reinersman stated the cost will remain the same. Mr. Schroeder stated
KCPC’s Attorney Matt Smith‘s stance at the KCPC hearing was that they had no
authority to approve this ordinance based on statute. Mr. Schroeder suggested
to consult with the Attorney General’s office to see what their opinion was
regarding residential design standards. He stated he agrees that these proposed
designs standards is the government regulating aesthetics, not structure.
Council Member Deaton questioned if there was any litigation or cases against
setting residential design standards. Attorney Gatlin stated there haven’t been
any lawsuits where a court said it was illegal for a city to regulate building
standards. Mr. Gatlin stated seven communities in Kenton County currently have
aesthetic design standards and no one has challenged those communities.
Council Member Franzen asked Attorney Gatlin why KCPC’s attorney Matt Smith
believed the building standards were illegal. Mr. Gatlin stated there was no
specific allowance within KRS 100 that discusses aesthetics and Mr. Smith took
the position that you cannot regulate aesthetics from a zoning perspective and
the fact that there is no case in Kentucky that supports zoning aesthetics.
Mr. Gatlin stated looking at KRS 82.082, there is no law against zoning
aesthetics and there hasn’t been one case in Kentucky in regards to design
standards. He stated there are 7 communities in Kenton County that currently
have aesthetic design standards in place and no one has challenged them. Mr.
Gatlin stated zoning aesthetics is not new and it goes back to the 1960s. He
stated the Villa Hills zoning ordinance from 1980 is very similar to what
Independence is proposing and has never been challenged. Mr. Gatlin stated
several other cities such as Fort Mitchell, Covington, Fort Wright and Erlanger
have similar standards, all which have received favorable recommendations from
KCPC.
Mr. Gatlin stated Planning and Development Services (PDS) engaged with American
Planning Association (APA) and did some in-depth research on aesthetics and
discovered there is no case law that affirms zoning aesthetics. He stated KRS
100.203(e) allows planned neighborhood and group housing districts and it does
not place geographic limitations on residential districts. Mr. Gatlin stated
the home rule referenced in KRS 82.082 states a city may exercise any power and
perform any function within its boundaries and is in furtherance of a public
purpose of the city and not in conflict with a constitutional provision or
statute. He stated not one single piece of legal evidence has been received
from the attorneys of the opposing groups of the proposed ordinance to dictate
that the design standards cannot be implemented and he is comfortable moving
forward with the ordinance.
Mayor Reinersman proposed a less restrictive amendment to Section B, by adding
“nor any subdivisions with five or fewer lots”. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading. He stated the draft of KCPC’s minutes is attached to
proposed ordinance and per KRS 100.211, the legislative body shall take final
action upon a proposed map amendment within 90 days of when the KCPC’s final
action upon such proposal.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting an Amended Budget for 2016-2017 – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which adopts the
amended budget for the fiscal year 2016-2017. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2017-2018 Budget - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which adopts the
budget for the fiscal year 2017-2018. In his budget address, Mayor Reinersman
stated for the second year in a row, the city will invest one million dollars
into city roads. He stated a 401(a) retirement saving program will be
instituted and the city will match employee retirement contributions up to 3%.
Mayor Reinersman stated the remaining funds necessary to meet the estimated
cost to replace our radios when Kenton County Emergency Dispatch makes the
switch to digital in 2018 have also been budgeted for the upcoming year. He
stated additional items in this budget are capital funds to replace the roof at
the Senior Center, self-funding for the city’s vehicle fleet and building a
reserve for our self-insured health insurance program.
Mayor Reinersman stated he may come back to Council and request reallocating
part of the radio fund to the roads fund if it can be worked out to get Pearl
and Dorothy completed this year and not wait until next year as originally
planned. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the Employee Pay and Classification Plan for
2017-2018 – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which adopts the
employee pay and classification plan for the fiscal year 2017-2018.
Council Member Taney stated she reviewed the proposed pay plans and has
concerns regarding several positions’ maximums that were decreased. Mayor
Reinersman stated in previous years, the minimum and maximum ranges were raised
3% each year across the board and comparing our ranges to the Northern Kentucky
Area Development District Salary Survey and several other cities, several
positions’ ranges were lowered. Council Member Taney stated the Chief and
Secretaries were the only ones who decreased within the Police Department. She
stated her concern for the Public Service laborer position with the max
decreased by almost $7,000. There was some discussion from Council and several
members requested copies of the data that was used to compare and helped decide
on the proposed pay scales. Mayor Reinersman stated he will get the data
together and send to Council to review.
Mr. Gatlin stated that after Council receives the data from the Mayor and
Council recommends to raise several maximum pay ranges, it would be ok to
update for a second reading but if ranges were cut, another first would be
required with the proposed changes. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Resolution No. 2017-R-04 – Re-appointment of Northern Kentucky Regional Ethics
Authority Members
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Resolution No. 2017-R-04 which re-
appoints Marcus Carey, Robert F. Greene, Darryl Cummins, Carolyn Lainhart,
Robert Sanders, and Tom Quirk and the appointment of Wesley Williams as members
of the Northern Kentucky Regional Ethics Authority Enforcement Committee for a
two year term serving from February 1, 2017 through January 31, 2019.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2017-R-04 to
approve the re-appointments and appointment to the Northern Kentucky Regional
Ethics Authority Enforcement Committee for a two year term. A motion was made
by Council Member Taney, seconded by Council Member Waite. Roll was called and
vote was 4-2 with Council Member Aseere and Council Member Franzen voting no.
Motion carried. 4-2.
Award Bid for Wedgewood and Clubhouse Reconstruction Project
Mayor Reinersman stated bid proposals were opened on April 27, 2017 for the
Wedgewood and Clubhouse Drive reconstruction project. He stated the Engineer’s
estimate for concrete was $944,005 and JPS Construction came in with the lowest

Proposed Ordinance – Amending and replacing Solicitation Ordinances – 1st
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which amends and
replaces existing solicitation ordinances 01-10-84, 2-10-77 and 2010-O-05. He
stated the city was approached by an attorney representing a company wanting to
solicit in the city and they stated our current solicitation ordinance was not
legal as well as too restrictive. Mayor Reinersman stated the proposed
ordinance removes the large bond requirement and implements a no knock registry
for residents.
Council Member Taney stated the proposed ordinance requires residents to submit
a complaint of a solicitor knocking on their door in writing and feels like the
resident should be able to call instead. Council Member Franzen asked if a
salesman violates the no knock list, if their license would be denied in the
future. Mr. Voelker responded that the resident can notify the police and an
officer can site the solicitor for violating the ordinance.
Council Member Taney stated she believes the proposed ordinance protects the
peddlers and solicitors and 9:00 p.m. is too late for someone to be knocking on
doors.
Mr. Voelker stated in the federal court system, speech is speech, and
businesses have a right to sell door to door while it’s light outside. Council
Member Taney stated the no knock list should be communicated on the city’s
website, Facebook page, newsletter etc. to make sure to get the word out to
residents. She stated there is vague language that states “the city may
require” and asked if it’s required or not. Council Member Aseere stated he
would like to see the solicitation application, believes the requirement of a
driver’s license could be possible discrimination and questioned the required
letter from a physician for solicitors selling food. Mr. Voelker stated
companies selling food have to be approved by the U.S.D.A.
Council Member Aseere stated the packet was a lot for him to read in two days
before the meeting. Mayor Reinersman stated going forward, he would like to
send a preliminary agenda two Fridays before each Council Meeting so council
has adequate time to review the information and request any additional
documentation. Council Member Franzen stated the proposed ordinance indicates
if a solicitor is convicted of a felony, their license can be revoked and
questioned if the city would be doing continuous criminal checks on solicitors.
Council Member Taney suggested the ordinance require a photo ID while
soliciting. Mr. Voelker stated it may not work to ask companies to provide an
ID badge. Council Member Taney stated the requirement of having an occupational
license from Kenton County is not mentioned in the proposed ordinance. Mr.
Voelker stated the county requires the occupational license in their ordinance
but it could be added as a required document to be submitted with application.
Mr. Voelker gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Map Amendment for Ashford Village – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which amends the
zoning map for approximately 2 acres located at the end of Ashford Road from an
R-RE (a low density residential zone) to a R-1C (suburban residential zone). He
stated the request was submitted by Chad and Elise Seibt and recommended by the
Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC). Mr. Moriconi stated the street ends
and the Seibts own the property and would like to build a home. He stated the
rest of Ashford Village is R-1C so this 2 acre property would be in line with
the adjoining property. Mr. Voelker gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Dan Koch stated he’s worked with Chad and Elise Seibt and they have been given
approval from KCPC to change the zone to R-1C. Mr. Koch stated if the city
vacates the 25 foot by 50 foot parcel to the Seibts, they can build their home
and the city will no longer need to maintain the property.
Proposed Ordinance – Vacate portion of Ashford Village Subdivision – 1st
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council a proposed ordinance which closes a
platted “proposed street” at the end of the paved portion of Ashford Road. He
stated upon closure of the road, it would authorize him to execute a deed to
transfer the property to adjoining property owners. Mr. Voelker gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2017-R-05 – Adopting the 401(a) Match Retirement Plan
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Resolution No. 2017-R-05 which adopts the
401(a) Match Retirement Plan for city employees effective July 1, 2017. He
stated this match was included in the upcoming budget assuming all employees
participate up to the 3% match. Mr. Voelker read Resolution No. 2017-R-05.
Mr. Aseere stated Exhibit A mentioned in the resolution was not attached. Mayor
Reinersman stated the resolution will be pushed to the July 3, 2017 meeting so
it can include the Exhibit A so Council can review prior to approving the
resolution.
Bill Cobble, 5257 Madison Pike, Independence, KY – Mr. Cobble asked how much of
the taxpayer dollars it would be for the employer match. Mr. Moriconi stated if
all eligible employees participated, it would be around $80,000.
Agreement with Planning and Development Services (PDS) – One Stop Shop
Mr. Moriconi stated nothing is changing for Independence with this new
agreement. He stated according to the previous agreement, some smaller cities
such as Fort Wright and Park Hills were receiving services from PDS for free.
Mr. Moriconi stated the new agreement may save the city $1,000 but doesn’t
change anything else.
Al Daly, 10330 Limerick Circle, Independence, KY – Mr. Daly stated he was
appointed to the zoning appeals board and he learned that HB 422 caused a great
change to the process. He stated previously, fees for violations were rarely
collected and now a resident has to file a strong appeal to have their case
reviewed by the board to have fees waived. Mr. Daly stated they are now
enforcing maximum fines and so far this year, over $67,000 worth of liens have
been put on homes with violations.
Council Member Taney made a motion to allow Mayor Reinersman to sign the
updated One Stop Shop Agreement with PDS, Council Member Engelman made a
second. Roll was called and vote was 4-2 with Council Member Franzen and
Council Member Aseere voting no. Motion carried 4-2.
Concrete Contract Extension – Ernst Concrete
Mayor Reinersman stated the contract with Ernst Concrete has expired and needs
to be renewed. He stated the current contract with Ernst is for concrete usage
for city projects. Dan Koch stated this is the last year we can extend with our
current concrete contract with Ernst. He stated he shopped around to other
competitors and the closest bid was $6 more a yard than what Ernst can provide.
Mr. Koch suggested we stay with Ernst.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the concrete contract extension
with Ernst Concrete for the 2017 to 2018 fiscal year. Council Member Franzen so
moved, seconded by Council Member Deaton. Roll was called and the vote was
unanimous. Motion carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Brandon Voelker
Mr. Voelker had nothing to report other than Mr. Gatlin is on vacation and will
return in a couple of days.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the city will be changing workers compensation carriers
which provides a $50,000 savings.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated his appreciation to everyone who participated the
previous weekend in the neighborhood blitz distributing drug addiction
information door to door throughout the city. He stated Independence’s 175th
birthday party will be on Friday, June 30 and Saturday, July 1 at Memorial Park
for the 4th of July Celebration which will include fireworks, lantern launch
and live music.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 9:22 p.m.
