August 7, 2017
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of August 7, 2017                  City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 7,
2017 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, led the Pledge of
Allegiance as well as a moment of silence. Roll was called and the following
Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Patricia Taney
and Greg Waite. Council Members Amy Engelman and Carol Franzen were absent.
Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and
City Attorney Jack Gatlin.
Approval of the July 3, 2017 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting on July 3, 2017.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on July 3, 2017. Council Member Waite so moved, with a
second by Council Member Aseere. Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0.
Smart Meters – Duke Energy – Rhonda Whitaker and Bob Reis
Rhonda Whitaker introduced Bob Reis, the Manager of Field Meter Deployment to
discuss the upcoming smart meter project. Bob Reis stated smart meters have two
way communication capability over the cellular network and will be read and
updated every 15 minutes. He stated Duke customers can receive usage alerts,
pick their own due date and the new meters lower the risk of human error from
manual meter reads, provide faster service for remote connection and
disconnection and reduce environmental impact and safety risk exposure. Mr.
Reis stated 120 communication devices will be installed on existing Duke Energy
poles and will begin at the end of August and should be complete by the end of
September 2018. He stated residents will receive a postcard letting them know a
contractor will be out to change out the meter and the contractors are required
to knock on the door prior to installation to let the resident know they are
changing out the meter. Mr. Reis stated along with the meter change out, there
will be a brief delay of service – no longer than a minute.
Zoning/Code Enforcement Process Overview – Megan Bessey, Code Enforcement
Officer
Megan Bessey stated her inspections are prompted by anonymous complaints she
receives from residents. She stated if a violation exists, she will take a
photo and open a case. Ms. Bessey stated the most common violations are outdoor
storage, tall grass/weeds, inoperable vehicles, boats, campers, trailers and
other recreational vehicles improperly parked or stored. She stated opening a
case generates a notice of violation which is mailed first class to the
property owner, the resident has 2 weeks to abate the issue and she will re-
inspect after 2 weeks. Ms. Bessey stated if the issue is abated, the case is
closed; if the violation still exists, a second notice of violation with
additional time is given or the first citation could be issued to the property
owner. She stated the first violation fine is $100, second is $200 and third
and subsequent offenses are $400 and if the final order is not paid, a lien
will be filed against the property. Ms. Bessey stated cases can be followed and
filed on the website: www.etrackit.psdkc.org . She stated 128 cases have been
opened since January and 63 are currently open.
Ordinance No. 2017-O-10 – Richardson Road Map Amendment – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented to Council Ordinance No. 2017-O-10 which amends the
zoning map for an area of 6.78 acres located between Briarwood Drive to the
east and Dixie Highway to the west from an IP (Industrial Park) and R-2 (PUD, A
multi-family planned unit development zone) to a R-1D (a suburban single-family
residential zone). He presented a power point presentation to Council to
highlight the area and topography of the property being discussed. Mr. Waite
stated he walked the property himself and the storage facility was interested
until they found out it would cost over $500,000 just to bring in dirt.
Ben Hueser, 4272 Richardson Road, Independence, KY - Mr. Hueser stated
Beechgrove Storage was interested in purchasing the property to expand the
storage business but didn’t want to spend $500,000 to move dirt to get the
topography where it needed to be to expand the business. He stated the bridge
wasn’t conducive for high traffic due to commercial use.
Council Member Taney asked Mr. Hueser why he didn’t first go to the Board of
Adjustments to seek approval for non-conforming use for what he wanted to do to
his property. Mr. Hueser stated there were necessary repairs to the front of
the house and he also wanted to add onto the house and add a bathroom. Rob
Himes with PDS stated the zone change made it non-conforming and the zoning
ordinance states non-conforming use may not be expanded or enlarged and the
Board of Adjustment would not be able to offer any relief. Mr. Himes stated the
Board of Adjustments couldn’t have granted because it was already non-
conforming because it’s being used as residential in an industrial zone. Jack
Gatlin stated a resident has the right to appeal with the Board of Adjustments
but the appeal would be based on interpretation of an ordinance and stated this
one is crystal clear and the attorney would likely not allow the appeal in this
situation.
Council Member Taney made a motion to postpone the vote until the special
meeting on August 28, 2017 as two council members were absent. Council Member
Aseere made a second. Roll was called and the vote was 2-2 with no votes from
Council Members Deaton and Waite. Mayor Reinersman voted no to break the tie
and voted against tabling the vote until the special meeting on August 28,
2017. Motion did not carry 2-3.
Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2017-O-10 a second reading. Mayor Reinersman
asked for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2017-O-10 which amends the zoning
map for an area of 6.78 acres located between Briarwood Drive to the east and
Dixie Highway to the west from an IP (Industrial Park) and R-2 (PUD, a multi-
family planned unit development zone) to a R-1D (a suburban single-family
residential zone). Council Member Deaton made a motion to approve Ordinance No.
2017-O-10, seconded by Council Member Waite. Roll was called and the vote was
2-2 with no votes from Council Members Aseere and Taney. Motion did not carry
with a tie vote of 2-2. With the ordinance not passing, the city did not take
action against the Kenton County Planning Commission's recommendation to
approve the zone change.
Resolution No. 2017-R-06 – Hazard Mitigation Plan
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2017-R-06 which adopts the Northern
Kentucky Regional Hazard Mitigation Plan. Mr. Moriconi stated this allows the
city to be able to receive FEMA if we ever need emergency funds and is all
handled through Kenton County and doesn’t cost the city anything. Mr. Gatlin
read Resolution No. 2017-R-06.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2017-R-06 which

Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2017-R-07 which adopts and approves

Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated the Kenton County Planning Commission is working on an

Mr. Moriconi stated the downtown sidewalks have been delayed due to required

Mayor Reinersman stated a zero-knock list has been incorporated with the

Mayor Reinersman stated the top 25 taxpayers in the city cover about a third of
the city’s revenue with payroll and occupational taxes. He shared the top 10

payer in the city.

August 28, 2017
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of August 28, 2017                  City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August
28, 2017 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, led the
Pledge of Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John
Deaton, Carol Franzen, and Patricia Taney. Council Members Amy Engelman and
Greg Waite were absent. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi,
City Clerk Gina Gabbard and City Attorney Jack Gatlin.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Reinersman announced this Special meeting of Council was being held to
discuss and take action on the following business items:
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2017 Property Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Resolution No. 2017-R-08 – Supporting the Separation of the County Retirement
System from the Kentucky Retirement System
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2017 Property Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which adopts the 2017 property
tax rates. He stated the county re-assessed property values this year and he
proposed the tax rate stay at $.271 for each one hundred dollars of the value
and the personal property rates at $.642 for each one hundred dollars of the
value. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading and stated the
discounts still apply if paid early as well as a penalty plus interest.
Council Member Taney asked what the additional revenue would be for the same
rate as well as the comp rate compared to last year. Mayor Reinersman stated
with keeping the rate the same as last year, it will bring in an additional
$30,000. Council Member Aseere asked how often the Kenton County PVA (Property
Valuation Association) re-assess properties in Independence. Mr. Moriconi
stated they assess every four years but may re-assess with building permits are
issued for additions, decks, etc. Mayor Reinersman stated when a house sells,
it can also be re-assessed based on the sales price of the home.
Resolution No. 2017-R-08 – Supporting the Separation of the County Retirement
System from the Kentucky Retirement System
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2017-R-08 which supports the
separation of the County Retirement System (CERS) from the Kentucky Retirement
System (KRS). He stated last month, the KRS Board of Trustees recommended
cities increase their contributions to 20-44% for employees participating in
the system. Mayor Reinersman stated he asked our Finance Director to run the
numbers and the cost would be over $300,000. He stated the separation of CERS
from KRS would mean local control of local pensions and would ensure the needs
of the CERS are met so it can continue its current path of growth for years to
come.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2017-R-08 which
supports the separation of CERS from the KRS. Council Member Franzen so moved,
with a second by Council Member Taney. Roll was called and the vote was
unanimous. Motion carried, 4-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Deaton to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:27 p.m.

January 8, 2018
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of January 8, 2018               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
8, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, led the
Pledge of Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John
Deaton, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney and Greg Waite. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, City
Attorney Jack Gatlin and Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.
Approval of the December 4, 2017 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting held on December
4, 2017.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on December 4, 2017. Council Member Engelman so moved,
with a second by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Introduction of the 2018 Miss Independence – McKenzie Hill
Mayor Reinersman introduced the new Miss Independence, McKenzie Hill. He stated
she won the pageant held on Friday, December 1, 2017 and will be representing
the city during the 2018 calendar year.
WODA Development – Bryce Ridge Apartments
Andy Videkovich, the Current Planning Manager with Planning and Development
Services, stated the plan being presented for Bryce Ridge Apartments is a stage
2 plan review within the Gateway Mixed Use Zone (GMU). He stated there are
several standards that have to be met within the GMU zone such as parking,
streets, adjoining tracks and sidewalks, pedestrian network, building location,
building architecture, signage and lighting. Mr. Videkovich stated there will
be no direct access from McCullum it will come off of the access point of
Courthouse Crossing. He stated there are 6 buildings in the plan will be two
stories and will have 1-3 bedroom units. Mr. Videkovich stated there would also
be a community building and a playground. He stated that PDS staff has given a
favorable recommendation with the condition that the street connection to the
adjacent property to the west would be aligned with Courthouse Crossing and
will provide a safer option for pedestrian and better traffic flow. Mr.
Videkovich stated there is supporting information that would also be required
for the zoning approval such as internal streets, landscaping, architecture
details, signage and off-street parking.
Cliff Ashburner, Attorney with Dinsmore & Shohl LLP, stated he is representing
the Woda Group with the Bryce Ridge Apartment project for McCullum Drive. Mr.
Ashburner stated they agree with the staff’s recommendation other than the
changing of the access point because it would cause a reduction of 3 units. He
stated this property would be a transition from existing commercial properties
to future properties.
Council Member Franzen stated apartments were not the intention of the zone,
the intent was to have apartments over commercial space or some other mixed use
of the space. Council Member Aseere stated the way the entrance is proposed,
future property owners behind this development would have to drive through the
apartment complex to get to their property and could deter future development
and suggests a straight contiguous road. Mayor Reinersman stated there are
limited opportunities for commercial use within the city and having these
apartments would take away commercial opportunities. Council Member Waite
stated his safety concerns for the residents within the proposed apartments.
Tammy Stansbury, VP with the Woda Group – Ms. Stansbury stated the adjacent
property owner was not interested in selling the property and if Council would
approve with moving the roadway to make it contiguous, then they would adjust
their plans accordingly. Mr. Ashburner stated multi-family units are a
permitted use within the GMU zone and the Woda Group has offered to comply with
PDS and Council’s recommendations.
Mr. Gatlin stated council can decide on the intent of the zone and has the
authority to approve the development plans. Council Member Taney stated the
application submitted wasn’t complete and doesn’t include the landscaping plan
or materials used and she doesn’t feel like council can vote and approve the
plan if the application isn’t complete.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-01 to
approve the stage 2 plans for the Woda Group’s Bryce Ridge Apartments
development. Council Member Aseere made a motion to table the issue and give
the Woda Group another opportunity to return with a complete set of plans
addressing the roadway concern. Council Member Taney seconded. Roll was called
and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-01 – Amending Sign Regulations – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-01 which amends current sign
regulations. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2018-O-01 a second reading and
stated the changes made to the regulations have already been approved by the
Kenton County Planning Commission.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-01 which
amends the current sign regulations. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Reveres Crossing Map Amendment – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented proposed ordinance which amends the zoning map of
four partial lots at the end of Boston Lane from an R-1A zone to R-1C zone. Mr.
Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2018-R-01 – Stage II for Bryce Ridge Apartments
Mayor Reinersman stated the issue was tabled and council will give the Woda
Group an opportunity to return to provide complete plans for the development.
Executive Order No. 2018-EO-01 – Reappointment to the Planning and Development
Services Council
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2018-EO-01 which reappoints
Mayor Reinersman to the as the primary representative and Council Member
Franzen as the alternate representative to the Planning and Development
Services Council.for the 2018 calendar year.
Declare Surplus Property – City Vehicles
Mayor Reinersman presented council with a list of 5 vehicles which include 3
2009 Dodge Chargers, a 2010 Dodge Charger and a 2006 Ford F650 truck. He stated
the vehicles will be placed for auction on Govdeals.com.
Council Member Waite made a motion to declare the 5 city vehicles as surplus
property. Council Member Deaton made a second. Roll was called and votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated there are still significant concerns regarding
retirement including the city’s employer contributions increasing $363,000 in
the upcoming year. He stated the Mayors group recently met with several state
representatives and main points of discussion were for the representative to
suggest a phase-in approach over the next 3-4 years with 10% maximum and keep
the possibility of the County Employees Retirement System (CERS) separating
from Kentucky Retirement System (KRS).
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:30 p.m.

Minutes of March 5, 2018               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 5,
2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, and led the Pledge of
Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and
the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney and Greg Waite. Also present was City

Gatlin and Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.

Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting held on February
5, 2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on February 5, 2018. Council Member Waite so moved, with a

Motion carried, 6-0.
Z21 Update
Andy Videkovich from Planning and Development Services (PDS) presented an
update on the Z21 project. Mr. Videkovich stated the Z21 project will reduce
the number of nonconformities and simplify and consolidate zoning districts. He
stated phase one has been completed and the additional phases should be
completed by 2020.
Proposed Ordinance – Indian Ridge Apartments – Vacating Apartment Road – 1st
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which allows the city to
vacate Apartment Road. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Scott Huber - Engineer with Abercrombie and Associates, 377 Compton Rd Suite
120, Cincinnati, OH 45201 stated he represented the Indian Ridge Apartments
property owner and answered council’s questions. Mr. Huber stated the .2 acre
property would be used as a front yard set-back and the city would no longer
have to be maintain the road.
Resolution No. 2018-R-04 - Residential Design Standards
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2018-R-04 which defines ‘brick wrap’
by adopting the residential design standards. He stated with the approval of
this resolution, the R1-C PUD zone would be subject to the residential design
standards that were adopted by Ordinance No. 2017-O-03 in regards to the
question of what is brick wrap.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-04 to
define brick wrap by referencing residential design standards. Council Member
Franzen so moved, with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and
the votes were split. Council Members Franzen, Engelman and Waite voted in
favor and Council Members Deaton, Taney and Aseere voted against the
resolution. Motion failed, 3-3.
Resolution No. 2018-R-05 – Apple Valley Stage II
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2018-R-05 which would conditionally
approve the Stage II Development Plan for Apple Valley Apartments. Mr. Gatlin
discussed the legalities on State II plans and stated Council will only be
voting on whether the Stage II Plans are in compliance with the previous
ordinance and requirements.
Andy Videkovich, with PDS, stated the submitted Stage II Development Plan has
been favorably recommended with several conditions including submission of a
landscape plan with planting detail, a photometric plan, building height
information, pedestrian connection, details on any fences and/or walls and a
provision for a secondary street stub be made at the southern end of the
parcel. Council Members Taney and Aseere shared concerns of the roadways within
the Apple Valley complex. David Knoll, co-owner of Apple Valley Apartment
Complex, stated minor repairs have been made and the roads will resurfaced
after construction of the new units. Mr. Knoll stated they are willing to meet
all of recommended conditions set by PDS.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-05 for
approval of the Stage II Development Plan for Apple Valley Apartments. Council
Member Deaton so moved, with a second by Council Member Waite. Roll was called
and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2018-R-06 – Meadow Glen Stage II
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2018-R-06 which would conditionally
approve the Stage II Development Plan for Meadow Glen subdivision.
Andy Videkovich with PDS, stated there have been several changes to the
original Stage I Plans which Council approved with 16 conditions back in 2004.
He stated PDS gave an unfavorable recommendation for the Stage II Development
Plan for the addition of 99 single family lots in the R-1C PUD zone in the
Meadow Glen subdivision. Mr. Videkovich stated there are several deficiencies
such as side yard setbacks, pedestrian access to Wolsing Woods, minimum off
street parking and lack of Homeowners Association but the two major concerns
are the rear yard setbacks and greenbelt restriction along Webster Road. He
stated if they aren’t addressed, it could have a significant impact to the
design of the development. Mr. Videkovich stated the rear yard setbacks are
showing 25 feet when it should be 50 feet and that is the main reason for the
unfavorable recommendation.
David Stroup from Grand Communities Limited 3940 Olympic Blvd Suite 100,
Erlanger, KY  stated they have agreed to every suggested condition by PDS. He
stated 99 new homes will be built, then an additional 51 homes and at that
point, they are required to widen Webster Road and create a secondary access
point.
Mr. Gatlin stated two resolutions have been drafted, one is a conditional
approval of the plans with acceptance of the recommended conditions from PDS
and one is to deny per PDS’ unfavorable recommendation. Andy Videkovich stated
for the developer to meet the rear yard setback condition they would not be
able to build on the 10-12 lots that back up to Webster Road as there is not
enough room to satisfy the 50 foot requirement.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-06 which
conditionally authorizes and approves the Stage II Development Plan for Meadow
Glen subdivision. Council Member Deaton so moved with the 6 conditions stated
in the resolution, with a second by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and
the votes were tallied. All voted yes with the exception of Council Member
Taney. Motion carried, 5-1.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin introduced Jeremy Pruitt, stating Mr. Pruitt is a third year law
student and will be an attorney with Gatlin Voelker LLC once he graduates.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated door to door solicitors should be registered and have a
city issued permit lanyard. He stated if they knock on your door and do not
have a permit, call Kenton County Dispatch.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman updated council on pensions and the 536 Kentucky Road project.
Council Member Waite stated he received a question regarding the flooding on
Bristow Road. Mayor Reinersman stated the city’s Public Services will be
checking the culvert on a weekly basis to help try and keep it clear until the
536 Project is completed.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 9:00 p.m.

Gina Gabbard, City Clerk
April 2, 2018
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of April 2, 2018               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 2,
2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, and led the Pledge of
Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and
the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, and Greg Waite. Council Member Patricia Taney was not
present. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina
Gabbard, City Attorney Jack Gatlin and Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.
Mayor Reinersman recognized previous Mayor Marion Schadler with a moment of
silence due to his recent passing and provided some highlights of his life.
Approval of the March 5, 2018 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting held on March 5,
2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on March 5, 2018. Council Member Engelman so moved, with a
second by Council Member Waite. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous.
Motion carried, 5-0.
Operation Honor
Mayor Reinersman presented an overview of Operation Honor. Joe Montgomery with
Operation Honor stated the organization is a Northern Kentucky based non-profit
which helps enhance the lives of veterans and their families. He presented a
sample banner which would hang along Madison Pike. Mr. Montgomery challenged
Council Members to sponsor a banner for a friend or family member.
State Pension Update
Mayor Reinersman presented an update on the State Pension. He stated the Senate
had approved a bill for a 10 year phase-in approach which includes a 12% cap
increase. Mayor Reinersman explained the State Pension funding will affect all
residents in Independence in some manner. He stated the city is in the County
Employees Retirement System (CERS) which is 60-65% funded, compared to the
state’s retirement system which is only 29% funded. Covington Commissioner Bill
Wells explained that Covington will have a $3.2 Million increase.
Chief Scott Breeze with the Independence Fire District discussed the
Independence Fire District Budget and effects of the increase state pension
contributions. He stated the fire district is already running lean so budget
cuts would mean fire district layoffs. Chief Breeze stated the most recent
retirees are not being replaced and that will help save money for the district.
He stated if the phase-in plan goes through, it will be an additional $95,000
in contributions the first year.
Council Member Franzen stated she accompanied the Mayor to Frankfort recently
and spoke to several legislatures which said some state taxes are being raised
and others are being added. Council Member Waite stated Frankfort isn’t
accepting responsibility and putting the bill on the cities and counties.
Al Daly, 10330 Limerick Circle, Independence, KY 41018 stated the investors of
the retirement system are not properly doing their jobs and something needs to
change.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-03 – Vacating Apartment House Drive
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-03 which authorizes the Mayor
to execute a deed to transfer Apartment House Drive to Blair Properties, LLC.
Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2018-O-03 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-03.
Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second from Council Member Waite. Roll
was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried 5-0.
Executive Order No. 2018-EO-03 – Appointing Lisa Davis to the Independence
Senior Board
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2018-EO-03 which appoints Lisa
Davis to the Independence Senior Board.
Award Bid for Basketball Court
Mayor Reinersman presented the Memorial Park basketball court bids to Council.
Chris Moriconi stated the city received a $75,000 matching grant for this
project. He stated Riegler Blacktop submitted the lowest bid with $145,261
which includes completion of the parking lot, installation of the basketball
court surface, basketball goals, fencing and a water line for drinking
fountain.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to award the bid to Riegler Blacktop.
Council Member Engelman so moved, with a second from Council Member Aseere.
Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried 5-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Jack Gatlin stated 4060 Richardson Road was referred to the Master Commissioner
and should be set for sale in the upcoming 30 to 90 days.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
The City Administrator thanked several local companies including American Sound
which helped with the Helping a Hero event.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman had nothing further to report.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Council Member
Franzen and seconded by Council Member Deaton. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:30 p.m.
                     _____________________________________
                     Christopher J. Reinersman, Mayor

May 7, 2018
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of May 7, 2018                     City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 7,
2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, and led the Pledge of
Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and
the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, City Attorney Jack
Gatlin and Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.
Approval of the April 2, 2018 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting held on April 2,
2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Regular Meeting held on April 2, 2018. Council Member Waite so moved, with a
second by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous.
Motion carried, 6-0.
Proclamation: Parker Willman
Mayor Reinersman presented Parker Willman with a proclamation. He stated Parker
has collected millions of toys and treats for pets through ‘Parker’s Pet
Project.’ Mayor Reinersman proclaimed May 8th will be Parker Willman Day.
Police Recognition: Joe Moffett
Mayor Reinersman and Chief Lucas recognized Detective Joseph Moffett. Mayor
Reinersman stated Detective Moffett was promoted from Officer to Detective on
April 1, 2018.
Proposed Ordinance - Adopting an Amended Budget for 2017-2018 - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which adopts the amended
budget for the 2017-2018 fiscal year. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Proposed Ordinance - Adopting 2018-2019 Budget - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which adopts the 2018-2019
budget. He read his budget message and stated the 2018-2019 budget includes
keeping the tax rates the same, contributing an additional $80,000 to the
pension system, increasing the gas and electric franchise fee by .4%,
increasing the number of school resource officers in our community and hiring
an additional public works employee. He stated the city will continue to set
aside $1,000,000 for the road funds. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Proposed Ordinance - Adopting the Employee Pay and Classification Plan - 1st
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which adopts the Employee Pay
and Classification Plan for the 2018-2019 fiscal year. He stated the salary
study is reviewed every 5-10 years and this year’s increases will be 2.1% which
is the standard cost of living. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Resolution No. 2018-R-07 – Rumpke Contract Extension
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2018-R-07 which extends the current
contract with Rumpke for trash collection services through June 30, 2020. Mr.
Moriconi stated the Rumpke contract extension would lock the rate of $13.48 per
month for two years and is the lowest rate compared to other Northern Kentucky
cities.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-07 for
the Rumpke Contract Extension. Council Member Waite so moved with a second by
Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion
carried, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2018-R-08 – Interlocal Purchasing Agreement Extension
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2018-R-08 which authorizes the Mayor
to execute a third amendment to renew the Northern Kentucky Government
Purchasing Agreement that extends through 2028. Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No.
2018-R-08.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-08 for
the Interlocal Purchasing Agreement Extension. Council Member Franzen so moved
with a second by Council Member Waite. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Municipal Order No. 2018-MO-02 – Franchise Fee Notice to Duke Energy and Owen
Electric
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2018-MO-02 which increases the
electric and gas franchise fees by .4%. He stated the current rate is 3% and
the increase to 3.4% will be a minimal impact to residents. Mayor Reinersman
stated the passing of this municipal order will provide the required 90 days
written notice to both Duke Energy and Owen Electric. Mr. Gatlin read Municipal
Order No. 2018-MO-02.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Municipal Order No. 2018-MO-02
to increase the franchise fee to Duke Energy and Owen Electric by .4%. Council
Member Franzen so moved with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was
called. Council Members Franzen, Engelman, Taney, Waite and Deaton voted in
favor and Council Member Aseere abstained. Motion carried, 5-1.
Council Member Aseere stated he wasn’t prepared to vote on the subject and
wants to make sure our rate was similar to other Northern Kentucky cities.
Council Member Aseere stated that he agrees with the budget but would like more
information regarding the franchise fee.
Award Bid for the 2018 Independence Street Program
Mr. Moriconi stated there are three roadway projects this year. He stated the
first project is the Independence Street Program and the lowest bid received
was from Bluegrass Paving at $218,007. Mr. Moriconi stated the project would
provide a blacktop overlay for several streets in Independence.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the bid award for the 2018
Independence Street Program to Bluegrass Paving. Council Member Waite so moved
with a second by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion Carried, 6-0.
Award Bid for the Shadybrook Trails Roadway
Mr. Moriconi stated the Shadybrook Trails Roadway is the second of the roadway
projects this year. He stated the lowest bid received for the project was from
Bluegrass Paving at $322,067 and would include a blacktop overlay for several
streets within the Shadybrook Trails subdivision.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the bid award for Shadybrook
Trails Roadway to Bluegrass Paving. Council Member Franzen so moved with a
second by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous.
Motion Carried, 6-0
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated every three years the city adopts a supplement to the code of
ordinances. He stated American Legal creates the supplements and council can
expect to see an ordinance to adopt the supplement at the next council meeting.
City Administrators Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated there’s been a request for the city to vacate a piece of
property off Independence Road near Courthouse Estates. He stated an agreement
would need to be set in place by property owners prior to the city vacating.
Mr. Moriconi stated it could be another 5 to 6 months before the developer
could do anything to the property. He stated that the state is applying for a
grant for the flood zone on Bristow Road which would raise the elevation one
foot as well as address the issues with the trenches and pipes.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the Kenton County School District has requested for a
police officer in each of the four city schools. He stated he would like the
schools to cover the cost next year and in the future, contract officers will
be used.
Mayor Reinersman stated the Independence Volunteer Corps database has been
created, an online form is available to sign up and there are currently have 75
volunteers. He stated the first Party at the Park will be on Thursday, June
14th and there will be food trucks, drinks, games and a live band. Mayor
Reinersman stated the events will be family friendly and will be the second
Thursday of each month during the summer.
Mayor Reinersman stated the regular council meeting scheduled for June 4, 2018
will be cancelled and a special meeting will be held on June 18, 2018.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion to adjourn was made by Council Member
Engelman and with a second by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 8:15 p.m.
                     _____________________________________
                     Christopher J. Reinersman, Mayor

May 24, 2018
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of May 24, 2018                  City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in a special session
on Monday, May 24, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with
Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to
order and opened with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: John Deaton, Amy Engelman, Carol
Franzen, Patricia Taney and Greg Waite. Also present was City Administrator
Chris Moriconi, City Attorney Jack Gatlin and City Clerk Gina Gabbard. Council
Member Aseere was absent.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Reinersman announced this Special meeting of Council was being held to
discuss and take action on the following business items:
Resolution No. 2018-R-09 – Agreement with Kentucky Transportation Cabinet –
Downtown Sidewalks
Executive Session (if necessary)
Mayor Reinersman advised that only the items listed on this agenda would be
discussed at this meeting.
Resolution No. 2018-R-09 – Agreement with Kentucky Transportation Cabinet –
Downtown Sidewalk Project
Mayor Reinersman stated Resolution No. 2018-R-09 would authorize him to execute
an agreement between the Commonwealth of Kentucky Transportation Cabinet and
the Federal Highway Administration. He stated the temporary easements have been
obtained and he wants to get the Madison Pike sidewalks project moving as soon
as possible to limit the disruption of traffic for the upcoming school year in
the fall. Mayor Reinersman stated the bid process still has to happen which
includes advertising, accepting and awarding the bid. He stated 5306 Madison
Pike has 19 heirs fighting for ownership of the property and it has held up the
process and the project will move forward not including 5306 Madison Pike until
a temporary easement can be obtained. Mr. Gatlin stated the case should be
going to court within the next 60 days.
Mayor Reinersman stated a $250,000 grant was received by the state for the
downtown sidewalk project and the city’s match is 20% plus $30,000 to hire
engineers to oversee the project. He stated he hopes to start project in July
and complete as much as possible by the time school starts back up in August.
Chris Moriconi stated the grant for the downtown sidewalk project was approved
in 2015.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-09 which
authorizes the Mayor to execute an agreement between the Commonwealth of
Kentucky Transportation Cabinet and the Federal Highway Administration. Council
Member Taney so moved, with a second from Council Member Franzen. Roll was
called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried 5-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 6:14 p.m.

and the rate was good through April 1, 2019.

July 2, 2018
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of July 2, 2018                  City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 2,
2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, led the Pledge of
Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and
the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, and Patricia Taney. Greg Waite arrived at 7:10pm. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, City
Attorney Jack Gatlin and Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.
Approval of the June 18, 2018 Special Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the special meeting held on June 18,
2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
Special Meeting held on June 18, 2018. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 5-0.
Al Daly of 10330 Limerick Circle, Independence, KY 41051 spoke regarding the
key lock boxes for commercial buildings. He stated it was useful to keep
unauthorized persons from going into certain areas of buildings and suggested
council pass the proposed ordinance regarding key lock boxes.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-07 – Adopting a Supplement to the Code of Ordinances – 2nd
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-07 which adopts a supplement to
the code of ordinances. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2018-O-07 a second
reading and explained the last three year of ordinances passed would be
officially adopted as a supplement to the code.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-07 which
adopts a supplement to the code of ordinances. Council Member Franzen so moved,
with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 5-0.
Mayor Reinersman stated the tax calculations were not yet ready from the PVA
and Northern Kentucky Ad District so the first reading of the proposed
ordinance for the 2018 tax rates will be pushed back to the August meeting. He
stated they likely won’t be ready by the scheduled regular meeting of August
6th so that meeting will be cancelled and a special meeting will be scheduled
later in the month and will communicate once it’s scheduled.
Proposed Ordinance – A.O. Smith Occupational License – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance for A.O. Smith Occupational
License. Mr. Gatlin gave the ordinance a first reading stating it’s pursuant
with the Kentucky Business Investment Program and will give A.O. Smith a .5%
discount on their occupational license fee. Council Member Franzen stated A.O.
Smith will increase the number employees and generate additional payroll tax.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Park Shelter Rental Fees – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance for amending park shelter
rental fees. He stated raising the shelter rental fees was prompted by the
state’s new sales tax law which requires the city to collect sales tax on
shelter rentals. Council Member Taney asked for the current shelter rental
rates and about possibly raising the rates on Senior Center rentals. Mr.
Moriconi stated the Senior Center room rentals are exempt from tax because it’s
only part of the building and the shelter rental rates have not been raised
since 2004. Mayor Reinersman stated a study can be done to compare our rates to
other cities and possibly increase the park shelter and Senior Center fees at a
later date. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading and stated
strikethroughs and additions will be added to the document for the second
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Key Lock Box Systems – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance for adding key lock box
systems for future constructed buildings within the city. Independence Fire
Chief Breeze discussed the details of the Key Lock Box System. He stated there
are various types of key lock boxes all of which are accessible by the fire
department. Chief Breeze stated he’s requesting the lock box system be mandated
for future new construction. He stated the types of buildings include
industrial buildings, multi-family residential buildings and healthcare
facilities. Chief Breeze stated each individual business in a strip mall does
not need a lock box and one lock box for the entire strip mall is sufficient.
He stated the fire department will have a master key to all key lock boxes and
these keys are only placed in vehicles, not with a person. Chief Breeze stated
the key lock box systems can range from $800-$1000 and are also available for
residential buildings. Mr. Gatlin stated the City of Erlanger adopted the NFPA
(National Fire Protection Association) which falls under the building code and
it was discussed that “all commercial structures” should be added to the
proposed ordinance. Police Chief Lucas stated the ordinance would help with
door replacement costs and aid in emergencies. Council discussed and decided to
postpone the first reading to better clarify the document.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he would make a few changes on the lock box document and will
be available for next month’s council meeting.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated there may be a future zone change at Turkeyfoot Road and
Independence Station Road. He stated the Fifth Third property is currently used
under a conditional use and the owner will be applying for a zone change from
R1D to NC so the owner can try to sell property. Mr. Moriconi stated the owner
wants to replace the existing building with a larger gas station and a strip
center containing offices on lower level and street level would have
miscellaneous businesses.
Mr. Moriconi stated a request for a tattoo parlor or body art services has been
submitted. He stated there currently isn’t a zone that allows a tattoo parlor
or body art services as a permitted use. Mr. Gatlin stated the city will need
to place body art services in a specific zone to avoid litigation. Mr. Moriconi
stated he would gather a more information regarding tattoo parlors and report
back to Council when he had more information.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the regular August 6, 2018 council meeting is
cancelled. He stated the Independence Day Festival is coming up with a lantern
launch, car show, rides, teen zone, parade, concerts and the spectacular
fireworks show. Mayor Reinersman stated after several meetings with Dr. Webb
regarding Kenton County School District, the district has decided to postpone
the redistricting for at least 12 months.
Jim Woeste, 172 Pelly Road, Independence, KY asked on an update on the
additional speed hump request on Pelly Road. Chief Lucas explained there are
two existing speed humps on Pelly Road and the engineer is doing a study on the
driveway placements and proximity to intersections.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Deaton and
seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:22 p.m.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in a special session
on Monday, July 11, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with

Moriconi, City Attorney Jack Gatlin and City Clerk Gina Gabbard. Council
Members Deaton and Engelman were absent.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Reinersman announced this Special meeting of Council was being held to
discuss and take action on the following business items:
RESOLUTION 2018-R-11: To provide financial support regarding Kenton County’s
grant application pertaining to State Route 536
ORDINANCE No. 2018-O-08 – A.O. Smith Occupational License – 2nd Reading
ORDINANCE No. 2018-O-09 – Amending Park Shelter Rental Fees – 2nd Reading
ATTORNEY’S REPORT – Jack Gatlin

EXECUTIVE SESSION in accordance with K.R.S. 61.810(c)
ADJOURNMENT

discussed at this meeting.
Resolution 2018-R-11 – To provide financial support regarding Kenton County’s
grant application pertaining to State Route 536
Mayor Reinersman stated by supporting and providing financial support to the
Kenton County Fiscal Court, it would aid the county’s application to repair
State Route 536. Kenton County Administrator, Joe Shriver, stated the federal
grant is limited to $25 million. He stated Kenton County passed a resolution to
contribute up to one million dollars towards the 536 Project and are looking
for city and private contributions. Mr. Shriver stated the plan will work on
State Route 536 from US25 to KY17. Mayor Reinersman explained adding funding
could expedite the process.
Kenton County Engineer Nick Hendrix, stated if the grant is approved,
construction must be started by 2020 by the transportation cabinet. He stated
the state office has asked the county to apply for this federal grant and will
make up the difference of the remaining balance of the $100,000,000 (one
hundred million dollar) project. Mayor Reinersman stated the resolution
approves our financial support of $250,000 or up to 1% and funding has been
verified. He stated there will also be a cost benefit analysis done for the
project to look at costs, contributions and potential revenue. Council Members
Taney and Franzen expressed concerns on where the money is coming from to put
towards this match. Mayor Reinersman stated with the 536 corridor complete, it
offers more opportunity for commercial within the city. Mr. Moriconi explained
Bristow Road is a separate project and would not conflict with this 536
project. Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2018-R-11.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-11 to
provide financial support regarding Kenton County’s grant application
pertaining to State Route 536. Council Member Taney so moved, with a second by
Council Member Waite. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion
carried, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-08 – A.O. Smith Occupational License – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-08 which provides a .5% credit
to A.O. Smith on their occupational license fee. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No.
2018-O-08 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-08 for
A.O. Smith Occupational License. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second
by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion
carried, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-09 – Amending Park Shelter Rental Fees – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-09 which amends the fees for
park shelter rentals. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2018-O-09 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-09 to
amend park shelter rental fees. Council Member Aseere so moved, with a second
by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion
carried, 4-0.

Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met in a special session
on Monday, August 27, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the
Independence Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with
Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to
order and opened with the Pledge of Allegiance. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Carol Franzen,
Patricia Taney, Amy Engelman, and John Deaton. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Attorney Jack Gatlin and City Clerk Gina
Gabbard. Council Member Greg Waite entered at 8:53pm.
Purpose of the Special Meeting
Mayor Reinersman announced this Special Council Meeting was being held to
discuss and take action on the following business items:
APPROVAL OF COUNCIL MINUTES: Regular Meeting of July 2, 2018
APPROVAL OF COUNCIL MINUTES: Special Meeting of July 11, 2018
ITRODUCTION OF INTERN
RESOLUTION NO. 2018-R-12: Text Amendment for church to be conditional use in
NSC Zone
RESOLUTION NO. 2018-R-13: Stage 1 Amendment for Quast Property
PROPOSED ORDINANCE: Map Amendment – Zone Change for Quast Property – 1st
Reading
PROPOSED ORDINANCE: Key Lock Box System – 1st Reading
PROPOSED ORDINANCE: Highway 16 Clarification – Harris Pike – 1st Reading
PROPOSED ORDINANCE: Adopting 2018 Tax Rates – 1st Reading
PROPOSED ORDINANCE: Cluster Mailbox – 1st Reading
PROPOSED ORDINANCE: Amending Pay Plan with Addition of PT Office Asst Position
– 1st Reading
NOISE ORDINANCE DISCUSSION
ADJOURNMENT
Mayor Reinersman advised that only the items listed on this agenda would be
discussed at this meeting.
Approval of the July 2, 2018 Regular Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the regular meeting held on July 2,
2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
regular meeting held on July 2, 2018. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Deaton. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous.
Motion carried, 5-0.
Approval of the July 11, 2018 Special Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the special meeting held on July 11,
2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
special meeting held on July 11, 2018. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous.
Motion carried, 5-0.
Introduction of Intern
Mr. Moriconi introduced Intern Christina Pletowski. He stated she is from
Munich, Germany and is currently a Political Science Major at Northern Kentucky
University. He stated Christina has been assisting him with several projects,
shadowing the Zoning Administrator and Building Inspector and will be attending
a ride-along with the police.
Resolution No. 2018-R-12 – Text Amendment for church to be conditional use in
NSC Zone
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2018-R-12 which is a text amendment
to add churches as a conditional use in NSC Zone. He stated Grace Fellowship
Church is requesting to occupy the open space in the Independence Town Center
next to Kroger. Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2018-R-12.
Kent Ousley, 2760 Sycamore Creek, Independence, KY 41051, from Grace Fellowship
Church, stated the church would pay for the application fees for the text
amendment.

text amendment to add churches as conditional use in the NSC Zone. Council
Member Aseere so moved, with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was
called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 5-0.
Resolution No. 2018-R-13 – Stage I Amendment for Quast Properties
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2018-R-13 for a Stage I Amendment for
3.08 acres located on the southwest side of the intersection of Richardson Road
and Old Richardson Road. Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2018-R-13.
The property owner Dr. David Quast and his engineer Brock Mackay, stated the
enclosed map labeled “old” was the original plan, the map labeled “new” was
what Quast Properties recently submitted. Mr. Mackay stated most of the primary
changes were made for acquiring the right of ways. Council Member Taney asked
if it was a concept or a final plan. Mr. Mackay stated it was a complete Stage
I Plan and additional information would be provided once the Stage I Amendment
was approved.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2018-R-13 for
the Stage I amendment for Quast Properties. Council Member Aseere so moved,
with a second by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Map Amendment – Zone Change for Quast Property – 1st
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented proposed ordinance which is a map amendment to
change the .82 acres located on the north side of Old Richardson Road from a R-
3 Zone (Multi-Family Residential Zone) to a NC Zone (Neighborhood Commercial).
He stated the request comes from Dr. David Quast who currently owns the
property as well as other surrounding properties. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.
The property owner Dr. David Quast and his engineer Brock Mackay explained they
plan to keep the current structure and turn the building into office space. Mr.
Mackay stated they also plan to construct a parking lot on the property for the
potential business as well as aid the future parking issue for the adjacent
property.
Linda Morehead, 4070 Richardson Rd, Independence, KY stated her home is
directly across the street from the referenced property. She explained the
street is currently a dead end street with 10 homes and an apartment building
and she doesn’t want a commercial building and/or parking lot across from her
home. Mrs. Morehead stated her concerns with regulating of current ordinances
and said the existing UDF was supposed to have an evergreen buffer which was
never completed. Mayor Reinersman explained that Planning and Development
Services (PDS) should enforce the agreed upon plans.
Council Member Franzen stated she didn’t understand the need to change the zone
while other properties are left untouched. She stated if the zone change isn’t
approved, Quast Properties could tear down the existing home and build an
apartment complex. Council Member Aseere stated he does not believe the zone
change makes sense for the area. Council Member Deaton suggested to postpone
the proposed ordinance. Mr. Gatlin stated PDS already recommended the zone
change and there would need to be a majority vote to overrule the decision.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to postpone the proposed ordinance for a
map amendment and zone change for the property. Council Member Franzen so
moved, with a second by Council Member Deaton. Roll was called and votes were
all ayes other than Council Member Waite who abstained since he entered mid
conversation. Motion carried, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Key Lock Box Systems – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented proposed ordinance which requires commercial
structures to have a key lock box system. He stated this ordinance has been
revised since the last council meeting. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance
a first reading.
Council Member Franzen proposed to change the language to only include new
constructed buildings. She stated she thinks there should also be an opt-out
option for businesses which includes signing a waiver to not participate in the
lock box system and the business owner would then be liable for any damages
incurred by the emergency responders. Council Member Taney stated this
shouldn’t be enforced by the city because the fire department is a separate
entity and questioned if any other cities have a similar ordinance.
Lucas Deaton, 10327 Charleston Ln, Independence, KY stated he searched for
similar local ordinances and was unable to find any that included the city and
the fire department as two separate entities. He stated he did not agree with
the language of the document which states the keys would be under control of
the City Administrator and his delegates and believes this would be a violation
of the fourth amendment.
Council Member Deaton stated the city doesn’t need to the liability of getting
involved in the key lock box issue. Council Member Aseere stated he was not in
favor of the proposed ordinance because it should not be governed by the city.
Al Daly, 10330 Limerick Circle, Independence, KY stated the boxes were a huge
help when he was previously a fire chief and explained the difficulties the
fire department has enforcing the key lock box system without the support of
the legislative government. He explained having uniformity in key lock box
systems was also helpful and saved time.
Council Member Taney stated the city does not hold the authority over the fire
department and the fire department should look for aid elsewhere such as the
fire marshals or state department.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion for a short recess at 8:34pm. Council
Member Franzen so moved with a second by Council Member Aseere. Motion carried
with all ayes.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to resume the council meeting at 8:53pm.
Council Member Franzen so moved with a second by Council Member Waite. Motion
carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Assistant Fire Chief Greg Nordmeyer, of the City of Independence Fire District,
stated the fire district is unable to pass and enforce an ordinance themselves.
He stated the program has been around for 20 years and they have not had any
issues with missing keys or breech of privacy. He stated business owners must
be notified prior to entrance and it’s usually due to an alarm system
notification. Mr. Nordmeyer stated the key lock box system is for the larger
business not the small ‘mom and pop’ business. He added there are currently 6
keys which are locked in service vehicles which only the fire department has
access to and around 60 businesses within the city are currently part of the
key lock box system. Mr. Nordmeyer stated not having to check if a business is
in the system helps save the fire district time during an emergency.
Council Members Deaton, Aseere, and Taney expressed they were opposed to the
proposed ordinance of requiring commercial business owners to participate in
the key lock box system. Mr. Gatlin stated he understood council’s desire of
postponing the proposed ordinance until the next meeting and suggested council
make recommendations to update the language in the proposed ordinance to what
they felt more comfortable with.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to postpone the proposed ordinance for Key
Lock Box Systems until the next meeting. Council Member Deaton so moved, with a
second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Highway 16 Clarification – Harris Pike – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which clarifies the road that
runs west to east from Madison Pike to Kentucky Highway 536 as Harris Pike. He
stated the road is called several names including Highway 16, State Route 536,
Harris Road and Harris Pike. He stated this ordinance would clarify the road
consistently named Harris Pike. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2018 Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which adopts the 2018 tax
rates. He stated the tax rates would not be increasing and will remain at $.271
for every one hundred dollars for real property and $.642 for every one hundred
dollars for personal property. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Cluster Mailbox – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which amends section 150.03
of the Independence Code of Ordinances which relates to neighborhood mail
delivery and cluster mail boxes. He stated some neighborhoods have complained
about not receiving mail because of parked cars blocking their mailbox. Mr.
Moriconi stated this has been an ongoing issue with neighborhoods which have
limited on street parking. He stated residents aren’t receiving their mail and
they must regularly pick up mail from the post office. Mr. Moriconi stated a
cluster mailbox would only be installed if the conditions are deemed necessary
and a safe location is accessible. He also explained the city would share the
cost by having the public services department pour a concrete pad among other
tasks. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amending Pay Plan with Addition of Part Time Office
Assistant Position – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance to amend the current pay plan
to include a part time Office Assistant position. He stated the position has
come to light due to the Assistant City Clerk requiring maternity leave in
December. Council Member Taney questioned the difference between this position
and the secretarial/clerical position and why it was being labeled as part
time. Mr. Moriconi stated the part time status would assist with hiring and
budget decisions to express it is solely a part time position. Mr. Gatlin gave
the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Noise Ordinance Discussion
Mayor Reinersman stated there have been requests made for an official noise
ordinance by residents and council. Council Member Franzen stated she’s had
several requests by residents for a noise ordinance due to late night
fireworks, music, etc. Mr. Moriconi stated there is an existing ordinance that
states noise cannot be over a certain decibel however, it is unrealistic to
provide decibel guns to every officer and/or zoning official. Council Member
Franzen stated the noise issue needs to be a new ordinance and not an
adjustment to the nuisance ordinance.
Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview Ct, Independence, KY stated her neighborhood has
several issues with noise including loud music, fireworks, late night pool
parties, loud cars and more.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence, KY stated she has also had issues with
noise including festivals, motorcycles, cars with improper equipment and noisy
neighbors. She expressed that she was in favor of a noise ordinance but it must
be enforceable.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Deaton to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 9:38p.m.
