COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of September 10, 2018               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
10, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, students
from Dixie Heights led the Pledge of Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led
the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney, Amy Engelman
and Greg Waite. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk
Gina Gabbard, City Attorney Jack Gatlin and Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.
Approval of the August 27, 2018 Special Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the special meeting held on August
27, 2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
special meeting held on August 27, 2018. Council Member Aseere so moved, with a
second by Council Member Deaton. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous.
Motion carried, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Map Amendment – Zone Change for Quast Property – 1st
Reading 
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which includes a map amendment
for the .82 acres located on the north side of Old Richardson from R-3 (Multi-
Family Residential Zone) to a NC (Neighborhood Commercial Zone). Mr. Gatlin
stated the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) has made the recommendation
to approve the zone change. He stated there are a few options Council has which
are: council can take no action which will result in an automatic approval,
council could vote on and approve the zone change and an ordinance would be
adopted with two reading or council could deny the zone change, which would
require four votes from council to overturn. Mr. Gatlin stated Council has
until October 31st, 2018 to take action and if no action is taken, the
recommendation of KCPC will be upheld. He stated this is not an evidentiary
hearing and no new evidence would be submitted at the council meeting. Mr.
Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Mr. Robert Morehead, 4070 Richardson Rd, Independence, KY 41051. Mr. Morehead
stated he attended the Kenton County Planning Commission Meeting and expressed
his disapproval for a commercial property on Old Richardson Road which is a
residential street. Mr. Morehead stated the extra traffic will create problems
for neighbors and school buses. He stated in the Planning Meeting Minutes from
the original change states that on Lily Drive no ingress egress allowed 9 years
ago. Mr. Gatlin stated the referenced KCPC minutes were not brought up in the
KCPC’s public hearing on August 2, 2018. Mayor Reinersman reiterated we can
only discuss what was brought up at the previous KCPC public hearing. Mr.
Gatlin explained he is unfamiliar with the minutes from the meeting 9 years
ago.
Justin Verst with Viox and Viox, Inc, 466 Erlanger Rd, Erlanger, KY 41018. Mr.
Verst distributed print outs to council what was presented at the KCPS public
hearing on August 2, 2018. He stated with the current zone, Mr. Quast could
tear down the existing house and construct a multi-family apartment building.
Mr. Verst stated the packets given to Council shows the future land use and the
entire side of Richardson Road would eventually become commercial property
according to the comprehensive plan. He stated Dr. Quast wants to use this
property as a small office space which would not create a large volume of
traffic.
There was some discussion from council regarding the location of the ingress
and egress and if they could put a conditional approval with a specified access
point. Mr. Verst explained the traffic would likely come from behind the
building, however, they need to also have access to Richardson Road since
that’s where the formal address of the property is located. He stated the
parking lot would be to the side and in the back of the building, it would sit
lower than the street and Dr. Quast intends to put foliage in front of the
parking lot. Council Member Aseere asked if they could completely remove the
ingress egress. Mr. Gatlin also explained the property would have to have
access to Richardson Road.
Council Member Deaton asked if Dr. Quast and the Moreheads could come to an
agreement to bring to council. Council Member Franzen asked Mr. Verst and Dr.
Quast if the zone change is not approved, what are his plans and if it’s an
apartment building, how many cars would be going in and out of there. Mr. Verst
stated a 12 unit apartment complex could be constructed and parking would be in
the front of the building. Council Member Franzen asked if additional
landscaping could be put in to block the view of the parking lot. Council
Member Deaton requested a short recess. Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to
recess. Council Member Deaton so moved with a second by Council Member Franzen.
Motion carried with all ayes. Council meeting entered a recess at 7:59 p.m.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to resume the council meeting. Council
Member Franzen so moved with a second by Council Member Waite. Motion carried
with all ayes. Council meeting resumed at 8:05 p.m.
Mayor Reinersman suggested we continue with the first reading and Dr. Quast and
the Moreheads come to an agreement and minor changes can be made with the
second reading on October 1, 2018.
Proposed Ordinance – Key Lock Box Systems – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which requires commercial
structures to have a key lock box system. He stated some of the changes made
from the previous council meeting include: commercial structures would require
a lock box if alterations were made, added the waiver to opt out and keys
should be under control of the fire district chief. Mayor Reinersman stated we
received a copy of Silver Grove’s ordinance regarding lock boxes and they
passed an ordinance requested from their local fire district. He read part of
the ordinance from Silver Grove and Council Member Engelman stated she liked
the verbiage of the Silver Grove ordinance. Mayor Reinersman explained Council
has time to pass this ordinance and if they would like changed made to please
reach out to himself or the City Administrator and a first reading would be
done at the October meeting.
Council Member Taney stated a key lock box ordinance was also being proposed
for the Kenton County Fiscal Court. Council members discussed whether a lock
box was part of the building code. Council Member Aseere asked who would write
the waiver to opt out. Mr. Gatlin expressed his hesitation to write the waiver
and would refer it to the fire district. He also expressed his uncertainty on
how enforceable the waiver would be and he would present council with a waiver
next month. Mr. Gatlin stated he would like to take time to review the Silver
Grove ordinance and incorporate some of their practices for a first reading. .
Council Member Franzen made a motion to table the proposed lock box ordinance
with a second by Council Member Aseere. Roll was called and votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Council Member Taney made a motion to re-numbers as Ordinance No. 2018-O-10 and
2018-O-11 were skipped as they were changed from 2nd readings to 1st readings
per items being tabled at previous council meeting.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-10 – Highway 536 Clarification – Harris Pike – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-12 which clarifies 536 to be
called Harris Pike.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-10.
Council Member Waite so moved with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll
was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-11 – Adopting 2018 Tax Rates – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-11 which adopts the tax rates
for the 2018 fiscal year.
He stated this is the third year the tax rate has not changed with .271 for
real property per $100 and .642 for personal property per $100. Mr. Gatlin gave
Ordinance No. 2018-O-11 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-11.
Council Member Franzen so moved with a second by Council Member Deaton. Roll
was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-12 – Cluster Mailbox – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-12 which amends section 150.03
of the Code of Ordinance as it relates to gang mail boxes. He stated this
ordinance changes the regulations for gang mail boxes in neighborhoods which
have problems with on street parking and blocking of resident’s mailboxes. Mr.
Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2018-O-12 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-12.
Council Member Engelman so moved with a second by Council Member Franzen. Roll
was called. Council Members Franzen, Engelman, Waite, Aseere and Deaton voted
in favor and Council Member Taney opposed. Motion carried, 5-1.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-13 – Amending Pay Plan with Addition of Part Time Office
Assistant Position – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-13 which amends the pay plan
with the addition of a part time office assistant position. Mayor Reinersman
stated by specifying the position as part time, it helps with budgeting
purposes. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2018-O-13 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-13.
Council Member Franzen so moved with a second by Council Member Deaton. Roll
was called. Council Members Franzen, Engelman, Waite, Aseere and Deaton voted
in favor and Council Member Taney opposed. Motion carried, 5-1.
Proposed Ordinance – Noise Ordinance
Mayor Reinersman stated the proposed noise ordinance is a work in progress.
Council Member Deaton asked Assistant Police Chief Lonaker what the Police
Department would like to see in the noise ordinance. He answered they would
like something that is enforceable and a more detailed ordinance would help the
police department determine what is considered too loud or a nuisance. Mr.
Gatlin explained he drafted this ordinance mirroring the Hillview ordinance
with some changes. Mayor Reinersman stated the purpose of the noise ordinance
is to clarify rules and regulations and make it more effective.
Council Member Franzen suggested the end time for the noise ordinance be
changed to 11:00 p.m. rather than 11:59 p.m. There was some discussion and
council agreed to remove the exemption on lawn mowers and to leave the work
week starting time at 7:00 a.m. Mayor Reinersman confirmed with council that
everyone was agreeable to Sunday through Thursday from 10:00 p.m. until 7:00
a.m. and Friday and Saturday to 11:00 p.m. until 7:00 a.m. would be the quiet
hours for the city.
Assistant Chief Lonaker stated it would be easier for the Police if the
firework hours were the same as the regular quiet time house. Council Member
Franzen stated she would like a later time in the morning for fireworks and
there was discussion about fireworks on holidays. Council Member Taney stated
it doesn’t get dark enough for fireworks until 10pm in the summer. Mayor
Reinersman confirmed with council that everyone was agreeable for fireworks
quiet times for on Sunday through Thursday from 10:00 p.m. until 8 a.m. and
Friday and Saturday from 11:00 a.m. until 8:00 a.m., 11:59pm until 8:00 a.m. on
Independence Day, 11:00 p.m. until 12:30 a.m. on New Year’s Eve and Day.
Council discussed exemptions and agreed the construction, lawn mower, and
aircraft exemptions would be removed. Council was unsure on the exemption for
churches and schools. Council Member Franzen expressed her concern with loud
cars and motorcycles. She asked Assistant Chief Lonaker how realistic it is to
enforce a noise ordinance for this. Lonaker expressed what he might consider
loud may not be loud for another individual and the more detailed the ordinance
was, the easier it is to enforce. Mr. Gatlin stated the noise ordinance would
work in conjunction with the current nuisance ordinance.
Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview Ct, Independence, KY 41051, would like the city to
follow the consistency of the state law in regards noise. Mayor Reinersman
explained the Police can enforce the state law. Mr. Gatlin expressed council
can make the parameters more restrictive.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi thanked Christina Pletowski for her time spent with the city and
has been accepted into law school in Munich, Germany.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the last Party at the Park is this Thursday and hopes
for a good turnout. He also explained the School Resource Officer positions
have all been filled and the officers will be starting within the next week.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 9:21 p.m.

October 1, 2018
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of October 1, 2018               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, October
1, 2018 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order, a local Boy
Scout Troop led the Pledge of Allegiance and Council Member Franzen led the
invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Bill Aseere, John Deaton, Carol Franzen, Patricia Taney, Amy Engelman
and Greg Waite. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk
Gina Gabbard, City Attorney Jack Gatlin and Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.
Approval of the September 10, 2018 Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the council meeting held on
September 10, 2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
council meeting held on September 10, 2018. Council Member Deaton so moved,
with a second by Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and the votes were
unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-14– Map Amendment – Zone Change for Quast Property – 2nd
Reading 
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-014 which amends approximately
.82 acres located on the north side of Old Richardson Road from a R-3 zone to a
NC zone.
Robert Morehead, 4070 Richardson Road, Independence, KY expressed his
disapproval of the zone change and stated he met with the Quast developers the
week prior and no agreement was made to change the current plans. He stated his
desire for Quast to move the driveway so it wasn’t facing his property and
believes it would help traffic.
Brock Mackay, Engineer with Viox and Viox Inc., provided drawings to council
and explained how moving the driveway a significant amount would result in
grading which would be too steep. Mr. Mackay stated they were able to move the
driveway slightly but would require a retaining wall which would increase costs
for Dr. Quast. He stated moving the driveway to the location Mr. Morehead
suggests would also be at the top end of the ADA steepness requirements.
Council Member Deaton questioned how many residents the location of the
driveway would affect and stated the comprehensive plan passed by the Kenton
County Planning Commission (KCPC) is to eventually have the entire area zoned
commercial. He stated this issue currently only affects a few residents while
the comprehensive plan would impact thousands of residents in the future.
Council Member Franzen asked the Moreheads if they approved moving the driveway
slightly. Mr. Morehead stated he would like the driveway completely removed.
Mr. Gatlin advised council that KCPC already unanimously approved the plans
with a previously held public hearing. He stated if council would like to
overturn KCPC’s decision or modify the plans, it would require a majority vote
and they would have provide reasons for their modifications.
Council Member Deaton made a motion for a recess so council to gather their
thoughts. Council Member Engelman seconded. A five minute recess passed with
all ayes at 7:40pm.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to resume the meeting at 7:45pm. Council
Member Franzen so moved with a second by Council Member Deaton. Council voted
unanimously in favor to resume meeting.
Mr. Gatlin read Ordinance No. 2018-O-14. Mayor Reinersman asked council if
there were any motions. Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve the
ordinance with an amendment to move the driveway. Council Member Engelman
seconded. Roll was called. Council Members Franzen and Engelman voted in favor.
Council Members Taney, Aseere, Waite, and Deaton voted against. Motion failed
2-4.
Council Member Aseere made a motion to reject the ordinance and overturn KCPC’s
recommendation to approve. Council Member Taney seconded. Roll was called.
Council Member Aseere and Taney voted in favor. Council Members Franzen, Waite,
Engelman, and Deaton voted against. Motion failed 2-4.
No other motions were made by council. Mr. Gatlin stated with no action taken
by council regarding the matter, KCPC’s decision will automatically pass by
default on October 30, 2018.
Proposed Ordinance – Key Lock Box Systems – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which requires commercial
structures to have a key lock box system. Council Member Waite stated the
waiver for the key lock box system goes against council’s authority to override
the fire code. Mr. Gatlin explained the waiver would be for someone who chose
not to install the lockbox and they would be waiving liability for damage done
to the property but not a waiver for federal or state requirements for fire
safety. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Council Member Deaton suggested the city create a proclamation rather than an
ordinance. Council Member Taney asked what the proclamation would do. Mayor
Reinersman stated it would be an encouragement to businesses to install a lock
box with no legal affect. The majority of council acknowledged they would be in
favor of a proclamation rather than an ordinance.
Proposed Ordinance – Noise Ordinance
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which specifies times which
noise levels are monitored and the police can enforce the law when it becomes a
nuisance. Council Member Deaton asked to consider removing exemptions C and E
in section 4 which included public recreation facilities, schools, and
churches. Council Member Franzen asked if the exemptions were removed, how
realistic would it be to send police officers to the schools to shut down a
delayed or late football game. Council Member Deaton stated it should be exempt
and school functions shouldn’t continue later than the times listed on the
drafted ordinance.
Council Member Aseere stated his concerns with exempting all churches. He
stated on Labor Day this year, a local church let off fireworks on a school
night and there were several complaints from residents. Mayor Reinersman stated
he had a conversation with St. Cecilia and they expressed they would not set
off fireworks on a Monday night again. Mr. Gatlin asked if council would like
to change the time to 11:00 pm on weekends. Council Members Franzen, Aseere and
Deaton agreed. Council Member Waite expressed concern on changing times for
school functions in the event a game is delayed.
Council Member Franzen would like to specify the exemption status would be for
schools and school events only. Mayor Reinersman cautioned this would not
exempt St. Barbara Church, St. Cecilia Church or the city fireworks. Police
Chief Lucas stated it is beneficial to continue the band and rides after
fireworks to minimize traffic. He believes that just having a conversation with
St. Cecilia about noise and fireworks would be alleviate the issues. His goal
for the noise ordinance is so the police department can site repeat offenders.
Mr. Gatlin explained exemption C is now noises emanating or originating from
public recreational facilities for city events, exemption E is bonafied school
sponsored events on school grounds, exemption F has become noises emanating or
originating from bonafied civic, charitable, or religious organizations until
11:30pm on Friday, Saturday or Sundays prior to a national holiday.
Mayor Reinersman asked for a motion to amend the first reading to include the
changes made to exemptions as discussed. Council Member Franzen so moved with a
second by Council Member Waite. Roll was called and all votes were unanimous.
Motion carried, 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated there have been recent road slides on Marshall Road and
Crowe Road. He explained the city would be looking into options for repair
including new technology that has been previously used by the state. Mr.
Moriconi stated the city office have processed over 800 passport application in
the past year, bringing in over $20,000 in processing fees. He stated he is
working on a wire franchise agreement with phone companies which would use our
right-of-ways for fiber optics and is working with other cities to create a
master agreement. Mr. Moriconi explained he needs to submit final paperwork for
the basketball court grant and the city will be receiving a $75,000 check.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated he received some valuable information at the recent
Kentucky League of Cities conference including the continued discussions of
CERS separation and encouraged council to support the CERS separation from the
state retirement system. He stated the road funding rule was also discussed in
which cities receive one fifth of the road funding and also mentioned the
monies received from the municipal road aid only cover about half of our annual
road costs.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:47 p.m.

                     Christopher J. Reinersman, Mayor

Proclamation- Key Lock Box
Mayor Reinersman stated rather than doing an ordinance for fire lock boxes,
council agreed to a proclamation to show their support for businesses to
install key lock boxes. Mayor Reinersman read the proclamation.
Ordinance No. 2018-O-15 – Noise Ordinance – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2018-O-15 which specifies times when
noise levels are monitored and the police can enforce the law when it becomes a
nuisance. Mr. Gatlin explained there was an error with the printed ordinance
and section 4, which lists exemptions, wasn’t correct per council’s
recommendations at the previous council meeting. Mr. Gatlin reviewed the
changes to the exemptions and stated the official ordinance will have the
changes as discussed. Mr. Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2018-O-15 a second reading
and noted the changes to section 4.
Council Member Deaton asked if there was a warning period for the noise
ordinance. Mayor Reinersman stated it would be at the officer’s discretion to
issue a warning or citation. Police Chief Lucas stated the police department
attempts to warn citizens with the first offense. Council Member Aseere stated
his concern with the penalty section of the ordinance. Mr. Gatlin explained the
penalty section is written in virtually every city ordinance.
Council Member Deaton made a motion to table Ordinance No. 2018-O-15. Council
Member Taney seconded. Roll was called and Council Members Deaton and Taney
were in favor. Council Members Waite, Franzen, Aseere, and Engelman were not in
favor. Motion failed, 2-4.
Council Member Aseere suggested changing the verbiage of the penalty section to
be more defined. Chief Lucas stated he would be able to track repeat offenders
in the system and they have 30 days from a citation to pay it or go to court.
Mr. Gatlin stated the district judge will assign a dollar amount per citation,
not the officer.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2018-O-15 with a
second by Council Member Waite. Roll was called. Council Members Franzen,
Waite, Engelman, and Aseere were in favor. Council Members Taney and Deaton
were not in favor. Motion carried, 4-2.
Terry Donoghue, 10633 Brent Ridge Circle, Independence, KY . Mr. Donoghue asked
the Mayor if the amphitheater in Memorial Park was available to rent. Mayor
Reinersman stated that it is not available because it causes amplified sound
which could have a large impact on the park as a whole.
Proposed Ordinance – Text Amendment to add churches as a conditional use to the
NSC Zone – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which is a text amendment to
add churches to the NSC (Neighborhood Shopping Center) zone. He stated Grace
Fellowship Church is looking at moving into the Independence Town Center where
the old Kroger was located. He stated churches aren’t currently allowed within
the NSC zone so a text amendment is necessary to add them as a conditional use.
Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Municipal Order No. 2018-MO-03 - Investment Policy
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2018-MO-03 which defines the
investment policy for the city. Chris Moriconi stated having an investment
policy is a best practice and the city is currently following the policy.
Finance Director, Terri Hudson, stated she drafted the policy and referenced
the state statute as well as other cities’ policies to create the policy for
the city. Mr. Gatlin read Municipal Order No. 2018-MO-03.
Council Member Aseere made a motion to approve Municipal Order No. 2018-MO-03
with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and the votes were

trees to plant around the basketball courts at Memorial Park. He also thanked
Barry Mallot who donated the mulch for the landscaping. Mr. Moriconi recognized
Parks and Recreation Facilitator Nita Brake for receiving an award for the
outstanding contribution to the leisure profession from the Kentucky

Mayor Reinersman stated the city was under budget over one million dollars from

Heating and Air. He explained the city Christmas Walk will be Saturday,

and seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes

2019 Minutes
January 7, 2019
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of January 7, 2019               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
7, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom
Brinker, Lucas Deaton, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen and Greg Waite. Also present
was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and Attorney
Brandon Voelker.
Approval of the December 3, 2018 Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the council meeting held on December
3, 2018.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
council meeting held on December 3, 2018. Council Member Engelman so moved,
with a second by Council Member Waite. Motion carried with all ayes.
Resolution No. 2019-R-01 – State grant for Madison Pike Sidewalks
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2019-R-01 which authorizes the Mayor
to sign the agreement for the Madison Pike Sidewalk project. Brandon Voelker
read Resolution No. 2019-R-01. Mr. Moriconi stated with the help of Mr. Gatlin,
all of the temporary easements have been obtained and the Madison Pike sidewalk
project can continue. He stated the resolution will authorize the Mayor to move
forward using the grant to complete the new sidewalks on Madison Pike. Mr.
Voelker read Resolution No. 2019-R-01.
Council Member Brinker questioned the timeline of the project. Mr. Moriconi
stated the project will include new sidewalks from St. Cecilia to Big Bone and
on the other side of the street from Rapunzel’s Hair Salon to Hartland
subdivision and estimates three months to complete and hoping to not impact
school traffic and July fourth festivities.
Council Member Aseere asked where the location of the new sidewalks will be.
Mayor reiterated Mr. Moriconi’s previous response to Council Member Brinker.
Council Member Aseere also questioned if this was all one phase or if was
multiple phases. Mayor Reinersman stated its all one project and it is funded
by a 20/80 grant which the city is contributing twenty percent and the state’s
grant of eighty percent is $250,000.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2019-R-01 which
authorizes the Mayor to sign the Madison Pike Sidewalk Agreement. Council
Member Franzen so moved, with a second by Council Member Brinker. Roll was
called and votes were unanimous. Motion carried 6-0.
Executive Order No. 2019-EO-01- Appointment to the TBNK Board
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2019-EO-01 which appoints
Council Member Brinker to the TBNK (Telecommunications Board of Northern
Kentucky) for the 2019-2020 term.
Executive Order No. 2019-EO-02- Appointment to the PDS Council
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2019-EO-02 which re-appoints
Mayor Reinersman as the primary representative and Council Member Franzen as
the alternate representative to the PDS (Planning and Development Services)
Council for 2019.
Award Bid – Police Radios
Mayor Reinersman stated Kenton County and several cities have been working on a
new radio system for over two years. He stated the two bids submitted for the
Independence Police Department were AMK Services with a bid for $185,964 and
Mobilecomm with a bid for $222,807.
Chief Lucas stated AMK Services offered a higher trade in value and matched the
seven year warranty. He stated the technology is top of the line and won’t
change much. Chief Lucas stated if Council approves, the order will be placed
the next day and testing will be going on in the fall.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to award the bid AMK Services at a price
of $185,964. Council Member Waite made a motion to approve awarding the bid to
AMK Services, Council Member Aseere made a second. Roll was called and the
votes were unanimous. Motion carried 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Brandon Voelker
Mr. Voelker stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated Walgreens is partnering with Kroger to offer grocery pickup
at Walgreens. He stated the store will requires a stage 2 plan for new signage
and will pass along more information as he has it. Mr. Moriconi stated the new
dump truck came in today for Public Services.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman

COUNCIL MEETING

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
4, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom
Brinker, Lucas Deaton, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen and Greg Waite. Also present
was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, Attorney Jack
Gatlin and Finance Director Terri Hudson.

would like made to the Council Minutes for the council meeting held on January
7, 2019.

council meeting held on January 7, 2019. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
a second by Council Member Engelman. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proclamation: Congenital Heart Defect Awareness Week in Independence
Mayor Reinersman proclaimed the week of February 7th – 14th, 2019 will be
hereby be known as Congenital Heart Defect Awareness Week.
Municipal Order No. 2019-MO-01 – Modifying Brick Wrap Requirement
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2019-MO-01 which modifies the
brick wrap requirement for Grand Communities LTD. Mr. Moriconi stated in 2001,

can be used that are just as nice as or even nicer than brick. Mr. Gatlin read
Municipal Order No. 2019-MO-01.

$300,000s based on the elevations in the packets council was given.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Municipal Order No 2019-MO-01.

Brewer to the Kenton County Joint Board of Adjustments.

Mr. Gatlin stated 4060 Richardson Road had several liens and delinquent taxes
and the foreclosure process began about a year ago. He stated the courthouse
auction will now be held on February 12, 2019. Mr. Gatlin stated someone will
need to purchase for at least $3,350. Mr. Gatlin stated the city would like to
purchase the property if there are no other offers for 2/3 of fair market value

March 4, 2019
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of March 4, 2019               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 4,
2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and a couple of local
boy scouts in the audience led the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen
led the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members
registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Lucas Deaton, Amy Engelman, and
Carol Franzen. Council Member Greg Waite was absent. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, Attorney Jack Gatlin and
Assistant City Clerk Karen Kearney.
Approval of the February 4, 2019 Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the Council Minutes for the council meeting held on February
4, 2019.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
council meeting held on February 4, 2019. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
a second by Council Member Engelman. Motion carried with all ayes.
Proclamation: Liam Blanchet
Mayor Reinersman presented a proclamation to Liam Blanchet for achieving Eagle
Scout status by creating a memorial at Summit View Academy.
Z21 Presentation: Megan Bessey with Planning and Development Services
Dennis Gordon, Executive Director at Planning and Development Services (PDS)
gave a brief overview of the Z21 project, stating it is the first major update
for Kenton County. He stated 13 out of the 20 Kenton County cities are
currently participating in the project.
Megan Bessey, Principal Zoning Official at PDS presented the Z21 update
highlighting the three phases. She stated the first phase was a professional
audit, second was creating a blue print code and the third phase is
implementation. Ms. Bessey stated PDS is moving into phase three which includes
the condensing and streamlining of zone codes across the participating cities.
She added the new code will be electronic and user friendly which allows for
easier navigation and understanding. Ms. Bessey stated the plan is to present
the final documents and new ordinances to each city in April.
Award Bid: Madison Pike Sidewalk Project
Mayor Reinersman presented the bids received for the Madison Pike Sidewalk
Project. He stated the engineer’s estimate for the project was $379,200. Mayor
Reinersman stated two bids were received; JPS Construction for $385,600 and TMS
Construction for $409,860. He stated the project will begin in May and
recommended to award the bid to JPS Construction.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to award the bid for the Madison Pike
Sidewalk Project to JPS Construction for $385,600. Council Member Franzen so
moved with a second by Council Member Engelman. Motion carried with all ayes.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he and his office sent delinquent tax letters to around 80
properties which were two or more years’ delinquent.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman congratulated Council Member Franzen on her award for coach of
the year for the boys swim team at Simon Kenton High School.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 7:45 p.m.

Lieutenant Boyle recognized Police Explorer Matalyn Colson for her 4 years with
the Police Explorer Program and congratulated on her recent promotion to

Residents from Glaser Drive
Several residents addressed the Mayor and council with concerns of recent
neighbor activity on Glaser Drive. They stated a new family recently moved in
and speculate there are multiple families living on the single family
residence, it’s creating excessive on-street parking and traffic as well as the
possibility of a business being ran out of the residential property. Chief

there are over 56 acres of high quality forest and wetland expanding the Brushy

forward with the Brushy Fork project.

Resolution No. 2019-R-07 – Wired Telecommunication Franchise Agreement
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2019-R-07 which creates and
establishes a bid for a Wired Telecommunication Franchise Agreement. He stated
the agreement has a 1.3% franchise fee, which mirrors the state’s rate. Council
Member Deaton questioned if the rate was high enough. Mr. Gatlin explained most
cities are following the state and the fee must be rationally related to the
cost for the city. There was some discussion by council and it was agreed upon
to change the initial period to five (5) years and auto renew for three (3)
terms of five (5) years.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2019-R-07 for
the Wired Telecommunication Franchise Agreement with an initial five (5) year
term and auto renew for three (3) terms of five (5) years. Council Member
Aseere so moved, with a second by Council Member Engleman. Motion carried, 5-0.

Council Member Franzen recused herself from the rest of the meeting due to a
conflict of interest with the map amendment issue of in the next agenda item
regarding the Taylor Mill Road Map Amendment.
Resolution No. 2019-R09 - Taylor Mill Road Map Amendment Denial
Mayor Reinersman stated the 6420 Taylor Mill Road map amendment was previously
been discussed at the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) public hearing
on August 6, 2019. He read through a list of items that were discussed at the
public hearing: road access to Sycamore Drive, current professional office zone
was a good buffer between retail and residential, additional lighting, access
to route 16 is dangerous, the City does not need another dollar store, retail
would only bring in low paying wages, increased traffic noise, the owner knew
the zone classification when it was purchased, etc.
Attorney Gatlin stated for council to overturn the KCPC decision, there will
need to be four votes to modify or overturn the KCPC decision. He added that
without four votes either way, the conditional recommendation by KCPC would
will pass by default in 90 days.
Rich Monson of 666 Sycamore Drive, Independence, expressed the state did not
give the variance to build the Dollar General. Attorney Gatlin stated this was
not part of the KCPC hearing record so it is not appropriate for council to
consider the states preliminary indication. Attorney Tom Theissen, who is
representing Mr. Bridges, made an objection to the record. He stated what Mr.
Monson said was not completely accurate and that council must rely what is on
the record from the KCPC hearing which did not include the state variance.
Laura Cochran, 689 Sycamore Drive, Independence, addressed council with her
concerns about the property being in a mixed zone and traffic issues. Attorney
Gatlin explained the property is currently zoned as professional office and the
owners are seeking to make a zone change to neighborhood commercial. He stated
the mixed use zone is what is referenced in the comprehensive plan. Ms. Cochran
stated her concern about the possible increase in traffic.
Daniel Wright, 688 Sycamore Drive, Independence, stated he lives two houses
behind the property. He stated he heard at the KCPC hearing that Dollar General
would not be interested in building on the property if access was not granted
off of KY16. Attorney Theissen stated he would address these concerns when he
has the opportunity to speak. Mr. Wright stated he is concerned with traffic,
speeding, and multiple entrances currently on Taylor Mill Road and there is no
need to add more issues to the problem.
Zachary Zurich, 6433 Taylor Mill Road, Independence, stated he is one of the
owners of the Cherokee Shopping Center and they are planning to make a
substantial investment renovating the existing building in hopes to rent out
the vacant space. Mr. Zurich stated there is already available retail space in
that center and does not see a need to build a new building.
Rich Monson, 666 Sycamore Drive, Independence, stated the creek behind his home
has had serious erosion over the years with the growing population and
businesses and is concerned that his backyard will eventually be taken over by
the creek.
Don Gubser, 6439 Taylor Mill Road, Independence, is the owner of the Cherokee
Drug Shoppe for 33 years, if the dollar store goes in it will not affect his
business. He is worried about the traffic and recent accidents.
Attorney Tom Theissen with Strauss Troy, is representing Dollar General as well
as Mr. Gailen Bridges. He stated the site has been vacant for years. Attorney
Theissen provided council with a packet of information that was presented at
the public hearing. He stated the applicant is limited to what is on the
approved development plan. Attorney Theissen stated the applicant understands
he has to comply with the conditions on the staff report such as lighting,
landscaping, roof, parking, encroachment permit on KY16, etc. He stated he
understands if the state says no to the encroachment permit to KY16 that the
development cannot move forward. Attorney Theissen stated at the afternoon peak
of business, Dollar General‘s traffic generates less than one car per minute.
Council Member Waite stated his concern about the anticipated 522 vehicles
coming in and out of the Dollar General per day per the engineer’s letter. He
stated there are already too many curb cuts and the street is already
dangerous. Mr. Theissen stated he agreed pulling out to the left has poor sight
distance but a Dollar General is not a heavy traffic influence as compared to
other types of businesses.
Gailen Bridges, property owner of 6420 Taylor Mill Road, stated he’s trying to
add a new development in a dying area. He stated if the Dollar General doesn’t
happen, he could split the parcel into two sites and two doctor offices could
go in which could possibly create more traffic. Mr. Bridges stated the question
for council is, does it fit into the plan and does it fit into mixed use. He
stated he’s not sure what will happen if the state says they can’t use KY16 as
an access point and the city says they can’t use Sycamore. He stated he’s
entitled to use one of those roads and if necessary, he’ll file a lawsuit to
help determine that.
Council Member Brinker made a motion for a short recess, Council Member Deaton
seconded. Motion carried with all ayes and recess began at 8:28 p.m. Council
Member Aseere made a motion to go back into session, Council Member Waite
seconded. Motion carried with all ayes and the meeting resumed at 8:33 p.m.
Council Member Aseere made a motion approve Resolution No. 2019-R-09 which
denies the zone change and overturns the KCPC recommendation on the bases that
it is not consistent with the suburban element of the comprehensive plan and
that the professional office is zone appropriate for the area. Council Member
Deaton seconded. Motion carried, 5-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated St. Francis, Belle and McMillan are being blacktopped this
week and the concrete tear out on Pritchard Road is also going on. He stated
the playground equipment will be torn out and replaced in Memorial Park
beginning the week of October 7th.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the Independence Volunteer Corps is growing with about
160 signed up so far and they have several events coming up. He stated each
month they receive donations for a various charities, they are also planning a
community garden and trail system in Memorial Park.
Council Member Aseere questioned how to change the speed limit on Taylor Mill
Road. Mayor Reinersman stated it’s a state road so we would need to ask the
state to consider the change. Mr. Moriconi stated he will reach out to the
state to do a speed study.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Engelman
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:57 p.m.

Proposed Ordinance – Map Amendment for Turkeyfoot Road/Independence Station
Road – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which approves a map amendment
for the 6.2 acres located on the corner of Independence Station Road and
Turkeyfoot Road. He stated Mr. Moriconi met with Dr. Quast regarding the map
amendment. Mayor Reinersman stated no new evidence can be presented that wasn’t
discussed at the Kenton County Planning Commission hearing. Attorney Gatlin
stated Planning and Development Services did not recommend the zone change. He
stated if council does nothing within 90 days, the non-favorable recommendation
of approval decision stands and the zone change will not be approved. Mr.
Gatlin stated the ordinance reads that the property has to be at least 5 acres
for a zone change so Dr. Quast had to include adjacent property to meet the
minimum of 5 acres for the zone change application, so it includes other
parcels besides the Fifth Third Bank property.
Tom Neinaber, 7699 Ewing Blvd, Florence, KY – Mr. Neinaber stated he is
representing Dr. Quast. He stated the bank is a conditional use on the
residential zoned property. Mr. Neinaber stated Fifth Third Bank has put a 10
year restriction on the property to prohibit another bank from coming in. He
stated Dr. Quast has a pending offer on the property contingent on the zone
change to Neighborhood Commercial. Mr. Neinaber stated there were concerns from
the residents of curb cuts and storm water runoff at the public hearing. He
stated if the zone change is approved, Dr. Quast can start working on a Stage I
plan for the property and will go back through the process with the Kenton
County Planning Commission.
John Scheben, 895 Independence Station Rd, Independence, KY – Mr. Scheben
stated he is opposed to the zone change. He believes Independence Station Road
should be a residential road and stated there are other commercial property
options other than re-zoning the bank as Neighborhood Commercial (NC).
David Shafer, 887 Independence Station R, Independence, KY – Mr. Shafer stated
he’s concerned what the property could be used for if re-zoned to NC. Mayor
Reinersman stated some of the possible conditional uses within the current
residential zone are funeral homes, nursing homes, libraries, playground, etc.
John Powers, 890 Independence Station Road, Independence, KY – Mr. Powers
stated he’s the adjoining property owner to the bank property. He stated the
traffic is a big concern with getting in and out of his driveway and constantly
witnesses wrecks and vehicle backups. Mr. Powers stated he feels the traffic
study should be done prior to approving any zone change to see how much traffic
the area could handle.
There was some discussion about carving out 5 acres of the 6.2 acres to have
re-zoned to keep some of the Quast property residential. Council Member Franzen
stated she feels like council would be jumping through a bunch of hoops to help
to re-zone this property without knowing the developer’s plans. She added that
the developer already has commercial property available and ready to develop
down the road from the area in discussion. Mr. Gatlin stated if council doesn’t
take any legislative action, the staff recommendation of not approving will
stand and this plan dissolves.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to table the first reading of the proposed
ordinance for a map amendment for a zone change for 30 days so Dr. Quast and
the neighboring residents can discuss and try to come to an agreement. Council
Member Deaton made a second. Roll was called and vote was unanimous. Motion
carried 6-0.

KLC Investment Pool

choose from and they are Money Market, Government Bond, Corporate Bond, S&P 500
Equity Index and Dividend Focus Equity. He stated the board decided to go with

to update the investment policy and would need to authorize the Mayor to enter
into an Interlocal Agreement. Mr. Moriconi stated there is a 20% investment
cap.

Jack Gatlin stated council would need to make a motion to overturn the decision
of the public hearing and the majority of the legislative body would have to
vote in favor to proceed with the zone change. He stated first reading of the
proposed ordinance would also include a few changes such as the acreage
changing would be adjusted as well as item 3 and would be adding items 3
through 8 which includes adoption of plan 3, update of residential buffer lot,
applicant shall meet buffer requirements, lighting standards and a list of
eliminated permitted uses for the property.
Council Member Aseere made a motion to overturn the recommendations of the
Kenton County Planning Commission with changes to acreage, applicant
requirements eliminated permitted uses and move forward with the zone change,
with a second from Council Member Franzen. Roll was called and pass
unanimously, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2019-O-07 – Annexation of Properties on Madison Pike/Patriot Way
– 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2019-O-07 which annexes properties
located at 5052 Madison Pike, 5056 Madison Pike and 5038-42 Madison Pike.
Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2019-O-07 a second reading. He stated this
annexation ordinance was passed back in 2015 but the process of filing wasn’t
completed.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2019-O-07 which
annexes properties at the corner of Madison Pike and Patriot Way. Council
Member Waite so moved, with a second by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried
with all ayes, 4-0.

Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated there is a need for executive session in regards to KRS
61.810(c) for pending litigation.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated Hartland subdivision will be having trip hazards on the

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, December
16, 2019 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance and stated the purpose of the special meeting. Council
Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the following Council
Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen, and Greg
Waite. Council Members Brinker and Deaton were absent. Also present was City

Ordinance No. 2019-O-08 – Map Amendment for Turkeyfoot Road/Independence
Station Road – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2019-O-08 which approves a map
amendment for 5 acres located on the corner of Independence Station Road and
Turkeyfoot Road. Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2019-O-08 a second reading.
He stated the map amendment re-zones the 5 acre property from a R1D
(Residential) to a NC (Neighborhood Commercial) zone. Attorney Gatlin stated
the proposed zone change does include restrictions such as indoor batting
cages, laundromats, car washes, parking garages/lots, liquor stores, post
office, auto parts store, drive thru restaurants, sports bars, service stations
and pool halls. He stated this ordinance overturns the Kenton County Planning
Commission’s recommendations from their public hearing held on October 3, 2019
and would require all four yes votes from the attending council members to
pass.
Tom Neinaber, 7699 Ewing Blvd, Florence, KY – Mr. Neinaber stated he
appreciates all of the cooperation from the city, council and residents to help
come to an agreement on the zone change.
Council Member Aseere stated he understands the residents are concerned with a
sports bar going in and questioned if a percentage could also be added in
regards to alcohol sales. After some discussion, it was agreed that 60/40 would
be a suitable percentage for alcohol sales if a restaurant was planned for this
property.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2019-O-08 which
approves a map amendment for the corner of Turkeyfoot Road and Independence
Station Road. Council Member Engelman so moved, with a second by Council Member
Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman wished everyone a Merry Christmas.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Aseere to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:18 p.m.

was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and Attorney
Jack Gatlin.

Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
December 2, 2019.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the

Approval of the December 16, 2019 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the special council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
December 16, 2019.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
special meeting held on December 16, 2019. Council Member Engelman so moved,
with a second by Council Member Waite. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Police Promotions
Police Chief Tony Lucas stated there has been several recent retirements which
has created promotion opportunities within the department. The Mayor and Chief
Lucas presented promotional plaques to the new Captains Jake Boyle and Brian
Ferayorni, new Sergeants Joe Moffett, Daniel Potts, Mike Brock and Travis Hager
and new Detectives Billy Roberts, Josh Salyers and Matt Fehler.
Executive Order No. 2020-EO-02 – Appointment to Senior Board
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2020-EO-02 which appoints Tom
Reckers to the Independence Senior Board.
Proposed Ordinance – Amendment to Webster Road Width – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the required width
of Webster Road from twenty two (22) feet to seventeen (17) feet from
Independence Station Road back to the intersection of the access street for the
Meadow Glen development, per Fischer Homes’ request. Mr. Moriconi stated the
current width is twelve (12) feet and with the topography, it’s not feasible to
widen Webster Road to twenty two feet as previously set.
Todd Huss, Fischer Homes, 3940 Olympic Blvd, Erlanger, KY – Mr. Huss stated the
reason Fischer is asking for the change to seventeen feet is due to the
problematic topography and it’s financially unreasonable.
There was some discussion with council and it was stated by Mr. Huss that it’s
not physically possible to widen Webster Road to twenty two feet wide. He
stated there was also easements and right of ways that would have to be
obtained to move forward with the width expansion. Council Member Franzen
stated speeding has been an issue in Meadow Glen for years and they need to
have another entrance for the subdivision.
Mayor Reinersman stated the big issue is the grade on Webster Road and the
steep hill makes it hard to see. He stated the requirement of stubbing in
Webster Road doesn’t have to happen until Fischer has fifty lots left to build.
Mr. Moriconi stated the width of the road is determined on the number of lots
in subdivision. He stated the right turn onto Independence Station Road is
currently tight and something needs to be done.
Mayor Reinersman stated he suggests the builder and the city’s public services
department take a look at the road together to come up with a solution that
will work for everyone. Mr. Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2020-R-01 – Text Amendment for Indoor/Outdoor Storage
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2020-R-01 which proposes a text
amendment for indoor/outdoor storage to include language to specify indoor
storage. Mr. Gatlin read Resolution No. 2020-R-01.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2020-R-01 which
proposes a text amendment for the definitions of indoor/outdoor storage.
Council Member Waite so moved, with a second by Council Member Franzen. Motion
carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Executive Order No. 2020-EO-01 – Appointment to PDS Board
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2020-EO-01 which re-appoints
Mayor Reinersman as the primary representative and Council Member Franzen as
the alternate representative to the Planning and Development Services Council
for the year 2020.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he has nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the National League of Cities (NLC) is wanting to partner
with the city to provide water and sewer line insurance for residents to cover
line breaks and leaks on their property. He stated several other local cities
are utilizing the program and are happy with it.    
Council Member Franzen made a motion to move forward with the NLC Warranty
Program, with a second by Council Member Waite. Motion carried, 4-2. Council
Members Deaton and Aseere voted no.
Mr. Moriconi stated the Investment Policy will be updated and would allow the
city to join the KLC Investment Pool if council votes in favor to participate.
Council Member Franzen so moved to approve the updated Investment Policy, with
a second from Council Member Brinker. Motion carried 6-0.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated Police Explorer Caleb passed away in December and the
Police Department swore him in as a Special Officer during his final days at
Cincinnati Children’s Hospital. He state TBNK has a new streaming site to watch
city council meetings on demand at TBNK.org/ondemand.
Mayor Reinersman stated there is some reorganization going on for Planning and
Development Services Council. He stated it will keep the twenty (20)
representatives for each jurisdiction and will meet six (6) times a year. He
stated the Management Board will have seven (7) seats and cities with a 15,000+
population will each hold permanent seats.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Deaton to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:36 p.m.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, June 22,
2020 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Amy
Engelman and Carol Franzen. Council Members Deaton and Waite were absent. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and
Attorney Brandon Voelker.
Approval of the May 4, 2020 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
May 4, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
regular meeting held on May 4, 2020. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Brinker. Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2020-O-03 – Amended 2019-2020 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented proposed ordinance which amends the 2019-2020
Budget. Attorney Voelker gave Ordinance No. 2020-O-03 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2020-O-03 which
amends 2019-2020 Budget. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second by
Council Member Brinker. Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2020-O-04 – Adopting the 2020-2021 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2020-O-04 which adopts 2020-2021
budget which proposes keeping the tax rate the same for the 2020-2021 fiscal
year. He stated there were two budgets (A and B) presented at the June meeting
anticipating the best and worst case scenario with the COVID-19 pandemic. Mayor
Reinersman stated the numbers came out better than expected and budget C
proposes keeping the tax rate the same at .271 per $100 for real estate.
Attorney Voelker gave Ordinance No. 2020-O-04 a second reading.
Council Member Franzen questioned the changes made to the proposed budget C.
Finance Director Terri Hudson stated budget C includes the following changes
from budget A presented at June meeting: reduced revenue from property taxes
(with keeping tax rate the same), monies restored for police community outreach
supplies, public works tools, capital fund deposit for future restrooms by
Memorial Park basketball courts, park improvements and recreational programs.
Council Member Aseere stated he was confused why the first reading of the
budget was being skipped and he had reached out to the city attorney’s office
about it. Attorney Voelker stated the subject matter hasn’t changed and the
numbers were updated to reflect the current state and modified projections.
Mayor Reinersman stated budget C didn’t include a subsequent change as the
budgets presented at the first reading covered the best and worst case
scenario. Council Member Aseere stated he noticed the retirement contributions
were showing a decrease of over $100,000 on the new budget. Mrs. Hudson stated
the Kentucky Retirement Systems initially planned to raise the employer
contributions 12% each year but earlier this year they voted to freeze the
contributions for the 2020-2021 fiscal year which saves the city over $130,000.
Rita Hauke, 5346 Oakview Court, Independence, KY. Mrs. Hauke stated she knows
people that are struggling and asked Council not to raise taxes. Council Member
Franzen stated the city hasn’t raised property taxes in five years. She stated
the county tax bill may be higher but it includes school taxes, fire district
taxes, etc. and the city has no control over those.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2020-O-04 which
adopts the 2020-2021 Budget. Council Member Aseere so moved, with a second by
Council Member Engelman. Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0
Ordinance No. 2020-O-05 – Employee Pay Classification for 2020-2021 – 2nd
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2020-O-05 which adopts the employee
classification pay scale for the 2020-2021 fiscal year. Attorney Voelker gave
Ordinance No. 2020-O-05 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2020-O-05 which
adopts the employee pay classification scale. Council Member Franzen so moved,
with a second by Council Member Engelman. Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0
Ordinance No. 2020-O-06 – Animal Control Ordinance Update – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman Ordinance No. 2020-O-06 which adopts the updates made to the
Kenton County Animal Control Ordinance. He stated the main change is updating
the name from animal control to animal services. Attorney Voelker gave
Ordinance No. 2020-O-06 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2020-O-06 which
adopts the updates made to the Kenton County Animal Control Ordinance. Council
Member Engelman so moved, with a second by Council Member Brinker. Motion
carried with all ayes, 4-0
Resolution No. 2020-R-08 – Municipal Road Aid
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2020-R-08 which adopts and approves
the execution of a Municipal Aid Coop Program Contract between the city, the
Commonwealth of Kentucky, Transportation Cabinet, Department of Rural and
Municipal Road Aid (MRA). He stated we previously passed the MRA Resolution
back in February but the state has recently made cuts and the city’s
apportionment of the Municipal Road Aid Funds for the fiscal year beginning
July 1, 2020 and is now $450,015.06. Attorney Voelker read Resolution No. 2020-
R-08.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2020-R-08 which
adopts and approves the execution of a Municipal Aid Coop Program Contract.
Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll
was called and motion passed, 4-0.
Resolution No. 2020-R-09 –Grant Application to Widen 536
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2020-R-09 which authorizes the Mayor
to apply for a grant to widen KY536 and the city would contribute up to $50,000
if approved. Attorney Voelker read Resolution No. 2020-R-09.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2020-R-09 which
authorizes the Mayor to apply for a grant to widen KY536. Council Member Aseere
so moved, with a second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and motion
passed, 4-0.
Attorney’s Report – Brandon Voelker
Mr. Voelker stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the Independence Day parade will start at 11:00 a.m.
from Summit View Academy through Simon Kenton but the festival has been
cancelled. He stated the fireworks show will go off at 10:00 p.m. Mayor
Reinersman stated the police currently has 37 officers, expanded equipment with
the help of drug seizure money including a crime scene investigation van,
pickup truck, golf carts, tasers and body cameras.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 8:03 p.m.

July 13, 2020
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of July 13, 2020             City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, July 13,
2020 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Bill Aseere, Tom Brinker, Lucas
Deaton, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and City Attorney Jack
Gatlin.
Approval of the June 22, 2020 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the special council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
June 22, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
special meeting held on June 22, 2020. Council Member Engelman so moved, with a
second by Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Police Promotion – Alesa Collinsworth
Mayor Reinersman presented a plaque to newly promoted Sergeant Alesa
Collinsworth.
Resolution No. 2020-R-10 –Stage II Development – Residences at Courtyard
Crossing
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2020-R-10 which authorizes the Stage
II Development for 3.36 acres located on the corner of McCullum Pike and KY17.
Scott Herald with Spire Development addressed council regarding the development
plan for the Residences at Courtyard Crossing. He stated the residents will be
ages 55 and up with 37 living spaces, three stories, library, community room,
lounge, laundry room and outdoor space. Mr. Herald stated a third party did a
market study and uncovered there is a huge need for senior living in this area.
Mr. Herald stated Planning and Development Services (PDS) did not provide a
favorable recommendation but believes they would have if it weren’t for the
wording in Section J of the zoning code regarding connectivity access. He
stated the items PDS mentioned in their report have been addressed in their
plans.
Andy Videkovich, Planning and Development Services (PDS) stated requirement for
the reasonable drive to the adjoining track is subjective and Mr. Herald has
done a good job of addressing the minor issues on the development plan.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2020-R-10.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2020-R-10 which
approves the stage II development plan for the Residences at Courtyard Crossing
with the conditions of PDS recommendations number 1, 2, 4, 5 and 6 on their
staff report. Council Member Deaton so moved, with a second by Council Member
Franzen. Roll was called and motion passed, 6-0.
esolution No. 2020-R-11 –Authorization to Apply for Coronavirus Relief Funds
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2020-R-11 which approves the filing
of a Coronavirus Relief Fund (CRF) application for reimbursement for
Coronavirus (COVID) related expenses. He stated the police salaries from March
on could qualify for reimbursement as well as other expenses. Mayor Reinersman
stated the money would be apportioned for the city for qualifying expenses.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2020-R-11.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2020-R-11 which
approves the application for CRF for COVID related expenses. Council Member
Franzen so moved, with a second by Council Member Waite. Roll was called and
motion passed, 6-0.
Concrete Bid Award
Mayor Reinersman presented concrete bids for city street projects. He stated
SRM and Ernst are both $1150 a truck and Hometown is $1170 a truck. Public
Services Director Ken Hicks stated Ernst offers better drivers and customer
service and prefers to work with Ernst Concrete for the 2020 fiscal year.
Mayor called for a motion to award the concrete bid to Ernst Concrete SRM.
Council Member Deaton so moved, with a second by Council Member Waite. Motion
carries, 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated the foreclosure process is starting back up in the courts and
there will likely be an increase in master commissioner sales in the next 30 to
60 days.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the old firehouse by the Independence Kenton County
Courthouse is being torn down and the Farmer’s Market will be temporarily moved
to Memorial Park. Mr. Moriconi stated the Kenton Conservancy will be having an
open house and public hearing this week to discuss the passive park area at the
back of Canberra Ridge. He stated there are four acres at the end of Berlander
that may be annexed so the new houses in the development aren’t half in the
city and half in the county and will likely be discussed in next few months.
There was some discussion regarding the Independence Courthouse being closed
and that Kenton County residents have to go to the Covington location to
register vehicles and renew tags and the lines are long.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the coronavirus is still here and asks everyone to mask
up.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Deaton to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:21 p.m.

September 14, 2020
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of September 14, 2020          City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, September
14, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated foreclosures are catching up after a six month backlog due to
COVID.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the Northern Kentucky Water District is replacing water
lines on the east side of town so Persimmon, Walnut, etc. will be repaved in
the spring of 2021 after the water lines are replaced. He stated construction
of new apartments will be beginning soon on the back part of Apartment House
Drive which the city vacated back a few years ago.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated in person early voting will be available between
October 13th through November 2nd at the Senior Center as well as the County
Government Center in Covington. He stated Halloween will be up to residents to
participate and urged everyone to respect each other’s choices. Mayor
Reinersman added if there is a COVID spike or neighboring cities start
cancelling, it will be reconsidered to continue with trick or treating in the
city. He stated the traditional Christmas Walk will likely not happen this year
and are looking for creative ideas to celebrate the holidays in addition to the
parade.  
Mayor Reinersman stated the police department will have two new officers this
month. He stated Rob Auton will be a School Resource Office at Simon Kenton
High School and AJ Kenner will be an officer and comes from the Kenton County
Sheriff’s department.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill
Aseere, Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Lucas Deaton (arrived at 7:17 p.m.) and
Greg Waite (arrived at 7:09 p.m.). Council Member Amy Engelman was absent. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and
Attorney Jack Gatlin.
Approval of the July 13, 2020 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the special council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
July 13, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
special meeting held on July 13, 2020. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Aseere. Motion carried with all ayes, 5-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2020 Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which adopts the 2020 tax
rates of $.271 per $100 for real property and $.642 per $100 for personal
property. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – IT Supply Solutions LLC Occupational Tax Credit – 1st
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which provides a .5% credit
of its occupational license fee for IT Supply Solutions LLC for the 15 newly
created full time jobs. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Senior Center Roof Bid Award
Mayor Reinersman stated the roof replacement was advertised for bid and two
bids were received for removal of shingle roof and replace with a red metal
roof. Kerkan Roofing’s bid is $91,725 and Shield Roofing’s bid is $92,847.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to accept the bid from Kerkan Roofing for
$91,725. Council Member Brinker made a second. Roll was called and motion
carried, 5-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Aseere and
seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:46 p.m.
