COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of October 5, 2020          City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met virtually on Monday,
October 5, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. with Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding. Mayor
Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Council Member Franzen led the invocation.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill
Aseere, Tom Brinker, Amy Engelman Carol Franzen, Lucas Deaton and Greg Waite
(arrived at 7:14 p.m.). Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi,
City Clerk Gina Gabbard and Attorney Jack Gatlin.
Approval of the September 14, 2020 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
September 14, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
regular meeting held on September 14, 2020. Council Member Franzen so moved,
with a second by Council Member Deaton. Motion carried with all ayes, 5-0.
(Council Member Waite arrived). 
Ordinance No. 2020-O-07 – Adopting 2020 Tax Rates – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2020-O-07 which adopts the 2020 tax
rates of $.271 per $100 for real property and $.634 per $100 for personal
property. He stated the personal property rate of $.642 was higher than the
comp rate so the adopted rate will need to be lowered to $.634 which will
generate approximately $10,000 less in taxes collected for personal property.
Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2020-O-07 a second reading.
Council Member Aseere made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2020-O-07. Council
Member Engelman made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2020-O-08 – IT Supply Solutions LLC Occupational Tax Credit – 2nd
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2020-O-08 which provides a .5% credit
of its occupational license fee for IT Supply Solutions LLC for the 15 newly
created full time jobs. Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2020-O-08 a second
reading.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2020-O-08.
Council Member Aseere made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Webster Road Lane Width Change – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which would amend Ordinance
No. 2004-O-15 and 2011-O-15 which changes the width requirement of Webster Road
to be seventeen (17) feet instead of twenty-two (22) feet. He stated before the
last fifty (50) lots can be permitted to build, the Northern Kentucky Water
District (NKWD) will need to install an additional water line and should be
completed before December 31, 2021. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance
a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Berling/Glenhurst Annexation – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the proposed ordinance which annexes 4.191 acres
which is a continuation of the Glenhurst subdivision. Attorney Gatlin gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the Sound the Alarm 5K went well on October 3rd and Hickory
Grove plans to make it an annual event each October.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated there were over 50 attendees for the memorial at the
Senior Center for the late Director Lisa Rymarquis. He stated Halloween is
coming up and residents can participate if they should choose but requested to
do it safely with masks, social distancing, etc. Mayor Reinersman stated the
Christmas Parade will go on but the traditional Christmas Walk will
unfortunately not happen in 2020.
There was some discussion about voting locations, mail in ballot boxes as well
as the Senior Center being used for early voting beginning on October 13th.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Engelman
and seconded by Council Member Deaton to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:04 p.m.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met virtually on Monday,
November 9, 2020 at 7:00 p.m. with Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding.
Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Council Member Franzen led the invocation.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill
Aseere, Tom Brinker, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen, Lucas Deaton and Greg Waite.
Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and
Attorney Jack Gatlin.
Approval of the October 5, 2020 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
October 5, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
regular meeting held on October 5, 2020. Council Member Franzen so moved, with
a second by Council Member Waite. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2020-O-09 – Webster Road Lane Width Change – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2020-O-09 which amends Ordinance No.
2004-O-15 and 2011-O-15 including changes to the width requirement of Webster
Road from twenty-two (22) feet to seventeen (17) feet. He stated before the

Council Member Waite made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2020-R-12. Council

Resolution No. 2020-R-13 – Spegal Development
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2020-R-13 which is an agreement for

buildings. Mayor Reinersman stated this new development will be huge for the
city bringing in new businesses, creating new jobs and collecting additional
real and tangible taxes.

Executive Order No. 2020-EO-08 – Re-appointment for TBNK

Brinker to the Telecommunications Board of Northern Kentucky for the term of

City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the Spegal project has been a great opportunity for the
city and commends Mayor Reinersman for his countless hours he’s spent already
getting the project started.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated there has been some data collection with the help of
Council Member Engelman regarding other local cities’ small business grant
programs. He stated with council and staff’s help, he would like to see a list
of criteria, application and program outline by the December meeting to keep
things moving with the possibility of implementing this grant.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Aseere to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:15 p.m.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met virtually on Monday,

Aseere, Tom Brinker, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen, Lucas Deaton and Greg Waite.
Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard,

Approval of the November 9, 2020 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections, they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
November 9, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
regular meeting held on November 9, 2020. Council Member Deaton so moved, with

Proposed Ordinance – Parking Regulations – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented proposed ordinance which amends Section 72 of the
Independence Code of Ordinances related to motor vehicle parking regulations.
Chief Lucas stated there was a complete review of the parking regulations and
it will make it easier for local law enforcement to police. Attorney Gatlin
gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2020-R-14 – TBNK Transfer
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2020-R-14 which approves the transfer
of control of Cincinnati Bell Inc. and Cincinnati Bell Extended Territories LLC
to Red Fiber Parent LLC and RF Merger Sub Inc.
Council Member Engelman made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2020-R-14.
Council Member Waite made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.

Municipal Order No. 2020-MO-01 – Small Business Grant Program
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No 2020-MO-01 which approves the
appropriation of $400,000 of its (CARES) Act allocation to help businesses
affected by the Governor’s Executive Orders. He stated there will be two tiers
and there is a maximum of $5,000 for each business for each tier. Mayor
Reinersman stated tier one is for PPE (personal protective equipment) expenses
and tier two is for rent, mortgage and utilities. He stated letters will be
mailed to businesses with guidelines and information about how to apply.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve Municipal Order No 2020-MO-01.
Council Member Engelman made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 5-0.
Council Member Aseere abstained.
Municipal Order No. 2020-MO-02 – Fire District Grant

Council Member Aseere made a motion to approve Municipal Order No 2020-MO-02.
Council Member Franzen made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Surplus Property
Mayor Reinersman stated there were several items the city declares surplus
property which includes several vehicles which will be sold on www.govdeals.com
and radio equipment which will be donated to the Kenton County Detention
Center, in accordance with KRS 45A.365.
Council Member Engelman made a motion to approve the lists of surplus property.
Council Member Franzen made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the Senior Center roof project is underway and there have
been several delays due to weather.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the Christmas Parade went well and the Santa Fun Run
set a record with over 200 participants. He thanked the Independence Police
Department for help with directing traffic around the events as well as the IBC
with their assistance with the weekend events. Mayor Reinersman also thanked
Council Member Aseere for his 8 years of service on Council.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Aseere and
seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:32 p.m.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met virtually on Monday,
January 4, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. with Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding. Mayor
Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Council Member Franzen led the invocation.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen, Lucas Deaton, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg
Waite. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina
Gabbard and Attorney Jack Gatlin.
Approval of the December 7, 2020 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections, they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
December 7, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
regular meeting held on December 7, 2020. Council Member Engelman so moved,
with a second by Council Member Waite. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Approval of the December 21, 2020 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections, they
would like made to the special council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
December 21, 2020.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
special meeting held on December 21, 2020. Council Member Franzen so moved,
with a second by Council Member Engelman. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Glenhurst Annexation – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which is a map amendment to
4.12 acres in the Glenhurst subdivision. He stated the amendment changes the
area from A-1 (agricultural zone) to R-1D (residential zone) and the developer
can continue to complete the subdivision. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading and stated it is a consensual annexation and has been
recommended by the Kenton County Planning and Zoning Commission (KCPC).
Ordinance No. 2021-O-01 – Parking Regulations – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2021-O-01 which amends Section 72 of
the Independence Code of Ordinances related to motor vehicle parking
regulations. Chief Lucas stated there was a complete review of the parking
regulations and it will make it easier for local law enforcement to police.
Attorney Gatlin read Ordinance No. 2021-O-01.
Council Member Deaton made a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2021-O-01. Council
Member Franzen made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-01 – Appointment to the Northern Kentucky Regional Ethics
Authority
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-01 which accepts the re-
appoints of Marcus Carey, Robert F. Greene, Darryl Cummin, Robert Sanders, Tom
Quirk and Bryce C. Rhoades and appoints Jack Westwood as members of the
Northern Kentucky Regional Ethics Authority Enforcement Committee (NKREA). He
stated the appointments are for a two-year term from February 1, 2021 through
January 31, 2023. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-01.
Council Member Engelman made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-01.
Council Member Waite made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-02 – Text Amendment for IP Zone
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-02 which proposes a text
amendment to the IP (industrial park) zone. He stated the amendment increases
the maximum height of the buildings in the IP zone to 50 feet and allows
permitted uses including banks, offices, post offices, coffee shops, etc.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-02 and stated with passing this
resolution, it will go to the Kenton County Planning Commission for approval.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-02. Council
Member Brinker made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-03 – Infrastructure
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-03 which urges the Kentucky
General Assembly to enact legislation to increase transportation funding and
modernize the Kentucky’s road funding formula to provide a more equitable
allocation of revenue to cities to ensure the safety, maintenance and
construction of vital city streets and bridges. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution
No. 2021-R-03.
Council Member Engelman made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-03.
Council Member Franzen made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he is available for council members whenever they have
questions and urged them to reach out to him. He also welcomed new Council
Member Vogelpohl.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the audio/visual equipment will be updated in the Council
Chambers in the near future and will help with sharing documents during
meetings. He stated resident Brad Jones had recently reached out to him
regarding a large box truck parked in his neighbor’s driveway and would like
council to review.
Brad Jones, 1244 Cynthiana Ct, Independence, KY – Mr. Jones stated he has a
neighbor that is parking a work box truck in his driveway. He stated these
trucks are not addressed specifically in the zoning ordinance. Mr. Jones
suggested that box trucks should be treated as RVs, trailers, etc. Attorney
Gatlin read the existing zoning ordinances that discuss trucks parked in
residential areas including weight and length limits. Mr. Jones said the owner
of the box truck works each day from approximately 7:00 a.m. and returns around
12:00 p.m. Council discussed the issue and there was concern some were leary to
interfere with someone’s livelihood.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated there has been a lot of comments recently on the city’s
Facebook page when the city shares COVID facts and information from creditable
sources.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Deaton and
seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:05 p.m.

January 11, 2021
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of January 11, 2021          City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met virtually on Monday,
January 11, 2021 at 7:00 p.m. with Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding.
Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Council Member Franzen led the invocation.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Bill
Aseere, Tom Brinker, Lucas Deaton, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen and Greg Waite.
Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard,
Attorney Jack Gatlin and Independence Police Chief Tony Lucas.
Resolution No. 2021-R-04 – Spegal Development Agreement
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-04 which authorizes the
execution of a development agreement between the City of Independence and Lloyd
and Judith Spegal. The Mayor stated VTRE Development (Van Trust) has a purchase
contract to acquire 100-acre property and develop an industrial and business
park on the property located at 861 East Mt Zion Rd. Mayor Reinersman stated
the property is currently in unincorporated Kenton County and will soon be
annexed into the city. He stated the developer Van Trust is proposing to put in
1.2 million square feet of industrial space and the city will be using
industrial revenue bonds.
Mayor Reinersman stated a new road will be installed and will serve as a
dedicated street and will include a round-about to help eliminate truck
stacking. Ryan Lidke and Phil Rasey with Van Trust stated they were involved
with the new Kroger warehouse off 536 and several projects by CVG airport.
Council Member Vogelpohl stated his concern for neighboring subdivisions if a
tenant of this new development wanted to store chemicals. Mr. Parsons stated
the development agreement lays out that it will be re-zoned to an IP
(Industrial Park) Zone so it will be regulated for use within that zone and
will be light industrial.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-04 which authorizes the execution of
a development agreement between the city and VTRE Development. He stated this
also approves and authorizes the application for the map amendment and to
execute the annexation agreement between the city and the property owners.
Attorney Gatlin stated Council will also need to bless the zone change, text
amendment and final approval for the annexation.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-04. Council
Member Brinker seconded. Roll was called and motion carried 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-05 – Inducement – Industrial Revenue Bonds
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-05 which authorizes the
execution of a memorandum of agreement between the city and VTRE Development
relating to the acquisition, construction, equipping and installation of an
industrial and busines park development located in the city and agreeing to
undertake the issuance of industrial building revenue bonds at the appropriate
time.
Jim Parsons, Attorney with Keating Muething & Klekamp PLL, stated the
industrial revenue bond resolution that is being discussed and passed at this
meeting is just stating the intent to undertake the issuance of industrial
building revenue bonds at the appropriate time. He stated several cities in
Northern Kentucky have utilized industrial revenue bonds to secure projects and
the bonds do not become the debt to the city. Mr. Parsons stated they are
issued by a public entity but are the responsibility of the developer. He
stated when these bonds are used, the property becomes tax exempt but the
developer agrees to a settlement amount in lieu of property taxes. Mr. Parsons
stated the benefits to the developer are the city takes care of the map
amendment to annex property into the city, there is also a pilot tax will be
split between the county and city.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-05 and reiterated that none of the
bonds will be general obligations of the city.
Council Member Franzen e made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-04.
Council Member Brinker seconded. Roll was called and motion carried 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Intent to Annex – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented proposed ordinance which authorizes application of
annexation of the 100 acres located at 861 E Mt Zion Road, Independence, KY.
Attorney Gatlin stated per KRS 100.209, the application and annexation and map
amendment can be filed together. He stated the current property owner have
already consented to the annexation. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the city is now the second highest city in Northern
Kentucky with COVID cases. He encouraged everyone to stay safe by wearing masks
and washing hands often. Mayor Reinersman stated his appreciation to council
for their support and help with this development project.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Engelman
and seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:00 p.m.

                     Christopher J. Reinersman, Mayor

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 1,
2021 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Amy Engelman, Carol
Franzen, Lucas Deaton, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard and Attorney Jack Gatlin.

Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they

February 1, 2021.

Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which is a text amendment that
increases the maximum height of buildings in the Industrial Park (IP) zone from
40 feet to 50 feet, adds additional office and accessory uses and development
controls for office uses.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading and stated it was
approved by the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) and was recommended by
Planning and Development Services (PDS) staff.
Resolution No. 2021-R-07 – Community Development Block Grant
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-07 which is authorizes the
Mayor to sign and file an application for the Community Development Block – CV
Grant for up to $200,000. Mr. Moriconi stated the grant program will be
administered by the Northern Kentucky Area Development District (NKADD) and
will provide relief for residents whom are unable to pay for utilities due to
circumstances surrounding COVID. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-07.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-07. Council
Member Deaton made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-08 – Amendment to Spegal Development Agreement
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-08 which authorizes the Mayor
to sign the amendment to the agreement in regards to the acquisition,
construction, and installation of an industrial and business park development
on the property located on East Mt Zion Road. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution
No. 2021-R-08.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-08.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-
0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-09 – Text Amendment for Holland Development
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-09 which is a text amendment
for the PUD (Planned Unit Development) zone to add breweries, distilleries and
wineries as an allowable use. He stated the proposed development in the PUD
zone will be called the Downs of Nicholson and will be on the corner of
Kentucky Highway 17 and Taylor Mill Road. Mayor Reinersman stated it will have
85 residential patio homes which will have 2-3 bedrooms, a clubhouse and pool.
He stated the development will also have a fast-food restaurant, a sit down
restaurant similar to Greyhound Tavern, a fuel center with a mini grocery store
as well as a micro-brewery and outdoor music venue. Mayor Reinersman stated the
Downs of Nicholson will be a cool entertainment place to visit and hang out.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-09 and stated the sponsored text
amendment will go onto the Kenton County Planning Commission for public
hearing.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-09.
Council Member Engelman made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R10 – Map Amendment for Holland Development
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-10 which is a map amendment
for the 29.41 acres at the northwest intersection of Kentucky Highway 17 and
Taylor Mill Road. He stated the amendment would change the property from a R-1B
(single family residential zone at a maximum density of two dwelling units per
net acre) to R-2 (PUD) (a two and multi-family residential zone at a maximum
density of ten dwelling units per net acre, with a planned unit development
overlay zone).
Mr. Moriconi stated he will complete the applications for the text and map
amendments and they should be heard at the public hearing in the coming months.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-10 and stated these should come back
to council for a first reading in the next few months.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-10.
Council Member Waite made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Award Bid – 2021 Resurfacing Program
Mayor Reinersman presented the bid for the 2021 Resurfacing Program for
Plantation Heights. He stated the engineer’s estimate was $715,950 and Riegler
Blacktop came in at $554,675, Paul Michels & Sons’ bid was $609,025 and Eaton
Asphalt’s bid was $652,885. Public Services Director, Ken Hicks, stated the
project should be able to start in the next couple of months and is within the
2020-2021 budget.
Council Member Waite made a motion to accept the bid from Riegler Blacktop for
$554,675. Council Member Engelman made a second. Roll was called and motion
carried, 6-0.
Surplus Property - Backhoe
Mayor Reinersman presented a backhoe that public services no longer use and
would like to surplus. He stated the piece of equipment will be traded locally
or sold on govdeals.com.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to declare the backhoe surplus property.
Council Member Waite made a second. Roll was called and motion carried, 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated he was on the committee to help decide what can be done
with the old Fox Run golf course in addition to the walking trails. He stated
there are currently 7 miles of paved trails and they will eventually connect
with Lincoln Ridge Park.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman presented the annual audit to council for the fiscal year
ending June 30, 2020. He stated it was an unqualified, clean audit with no
areas of concern.
Mayor Reinersman stated the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) will have
a public hearing on March 4, 2021 in regards to the Spegal Development. He
urged residents to attend and stated it was their opportunity to be heard
regarding the project. Mayor Reinersman stated council will not be able to
discuss new evidence that was not discussed at the KCPC hearing. He stated the
city has been interested in the development for years and new businesses will
help alleviate some pressure to tax payers. Mayor Reinersman stated there is a
white paper posted on the city’s website which provides lots of information on
the project.
Mayor Reinersman stated the Police Department will be adding a K-9 officer to
the force. Chief Lucas stated the PD will be fundraising for the $75,000 which
covers the start-up costs for the K-9 including the special vehicle which will
have a special heating and cooling system to keep the dog comfortable while on
duty. He stated there are 5 officers interested in being the K-9 handler and
they are going through a process to determine the best fit.
Mayor Reinersman stated he hopes to present an amended budget at the next
meeting. He stated the payroll taxes were right on target and with the
significant stimulus funding, several projects that were previously cut, will
be added back into the budget.
There was some discussion about the fourth of July events for 2021 and Mayor
Reinersman stated the parade and fireworks will likely happen along with a
musical festival with food and drinks. Mayor Reinersman stated the Independence
Easter Bunny Trail event will be on March 27 in Summit View’s parking lot and
registration is available on the city’s Facebook page.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:41 p.m.

Mayor Reinersman stated the Facebook post about the city being closed on spring

May 3, 2021
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of May 3, 2021               City of Independence, Ky.Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 3,
2021 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Amy Engelman, Carol
Franzen, Dave Shafer, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, Attorney Jack Gatlin and
Police Chief Anthony Lucas.
Approval of the April 5, 2021 Regular Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
April 5, 2021.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the
regular meeting held on April 5, 2021. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a
second by Council Member Engelman. Motion carried with a 5-0 vote; Council
Member Shafer abstained.
Craig Reinhart, Simon Kenton Principal – Mr. Reinhart addressed council in
regards to students at Simon Kenton and recent concerns about overcrowding with
the proposed development at the Downs of Nicholson. He stated with the programs
at Northern Kentucky University, Thomas More College, Ignite Institute, Gateway
College, ROTC, etc., there will be an average of 1,571 students in the Simon
Kenton school building. He stated the capacity of the school is approximately
1,800 students and there are currently about 100 students that open enroll to
attend Simon Kenton.
Mayor Reinersman’s Budget Message
Mayor Reinersman stated the 100+ acre industrial development at the Spegal Farm
property will bring nearly 1.2 million square feet of space, hundreds of jobs
and projected revenue increases approaching 10% of the current city budget. He
stated the proposed development, the Downs of Nicholson, would also add jobs
and non- residential tax revenue. Mayor Reinersman stated the budget being
presented represents a nearly 4% reduction from the current property tax rate
and there is also a proposed 10% COVID discount. He stated the salaries of
public services and the police department are being reviewed and may be
adjusted so they are more in line with competitive standards Mayor Reinersman
stated a merit-based pay increase plan will also be implemented this year.
Mayor Reinersman stated the funding for the street program will again be above
one million dollars for road replacement and resurfacing. He stated the new
budget proposes new playground equipment in Shadler Park, a second restroom and
shelter between the amphitheater and basketball courts at Memorial Park as well
as the addition of pickleball courts.
Tates Creek Development Project
Johan Graham, Workforce Housing Multi-Family Developer with Tates Creek
Development, LLC – Mr. Graham presented a proposed development for an
affordable housing project on the 16 acres at 2172 Harris Pike which is
currently zoned R-1C. He stated the development would offer 72 affordable
housing options including 1–3- bedroom apartments for those making between
$25,000 and $60,000 per year. Mr. Graham stated the project would include 3
apartment buildings, a clubhouse and a pool. He stated the entrance and buffer
zone would be off Centennial and is hoping to present the project at the June
public hearing before the Kenton County Planning Commission.
Proposed Ordinance - Text Amendment for Holland Development - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which is a text amendment by
adding a definition for brewery, distillery, winery as well as adding brewery,
distillery and winery as permitted uses within a PUD (Planned Unit Development)
zone. He stated the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) had a public
hearing on April 1, 2021 and a favorable recommendation was given by PDS staff.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance - Map Amendment for Holland Development - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which is a map amendment for
the 29.41 acres located at the northeast corner of the intersection of Taylor
Mill Rd (KY 16) and Madison Pike (KY 17) to change the zone from a R-1B (single
family residential zone) to a R-2 (PUD) (a multi-family residential zone with a
planned unit development overlay). He stated the Kenton County Planning
Commission (KCPC) had a public hearing on April 1, 2021 in which it was given a
favorable recommendation for approval by PDS staff. Attorney Gatlin gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Annexation for Holland Development - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which annexes the one acre
parcel on the east side of KY 17 and north side of KY 16 along with the 29.41
acres which was previously annexed for the Holland Development. He stated the
Holland Group approached the current property owners and they agreed to sell
the parcel. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting the 2021-2022 Budget - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which adopts the annual budget
for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2021 and ending June 30, 2022. Attorney
Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Employee Pay Classifications - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which adopts the personnel and
pay classification plan for the 2021-2022 fiscal year. Mr. Moriconi stated
salary surveys are reviewed each year to make sure the city is staying
competitive with the private and public sectors and minimums and maximums are
adjusted accordingly. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Interlocal Agreement for One Stop Shop- 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which adopts an amended
interlocal agreement between the Kenton County Fiscal Court and several
Northern Kentucky cities, including Independence, for code enforcement. He
stated the amendment will allocate each city to pay 100% of the costs for
services performed by Planning and Development Services (PDS). Mayor Reinersman
stated this amendment will add a $50,000 increase to Independence directly.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2021-R-13 – MRA Cooperative Agreement
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-13 which adopts and approves
the execution of a Municipal Aid Coop Program Contract between the city, the
Commonwealth of Kentucky, Transportation Cabinet and the Department of Rural
and Municipal Road Aid (MRA). He stated the city’s apportionment of the
Municipal Road Aid Funds for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2021 is
$502,824.23. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2021-R-13.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-13.
Council Member Waite so moved, with a second by Council Member Brinker. Motion
carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-14 – Body Armor GOLD Grant
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-14 which authorizes the Mayor
to enter into an agreement with the Governor’s office for Local Development
(GOLD) for the Kentucky Body Armor Program. Chief Lucas stated this resolution
allows the Mayor to approve the application for new equipment from Homeland
Security for the police department such as aging rifles. Attorney Gatlin read
Resolution No. 2021-R-14.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-14.
Council Member Engelman so moved, with a second by Council Member Franzen.
Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Attorney’s Report – Jack Gatlin
Mr. Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator Report – Chris Moriconi
Mr. Moriconi stated the five-year street survey is complete and distributed to
council. He stated it will be added to the city’s website for the public as
well. Mr. Moriconi stated the report grades each of the city’s streets and
helps dictate which streets will be repaired and/or replaced. Chief Lucas
stated the green street signs are city streets and blue street signs should be
Kenton county streets.
Mayor’s Report – Christopher J. Reinersman
Mayor Reinersman stated the American Legion will move forward with the Memorial
Day parade on the morning of Memorial Day parade on Madison Pike. The
Independence Day festival will be scaled down and will start the day with the
cars and pipes show in the Kroger parking lot at 10:00 a.m., the parade starts
at 3:00 p.m., the festival kicks off at 4:00 p.m. at Memorial Park with two
bands – 24/7 and GenX and circus performances throughout the evening. Mayor
Reinersman stated Hand and Hand Realty will be sponsoring the Parties in the
Park again this summer and they will be the second Thursday of the month in
June, July and August. He added there will be a ribbon cutting on May 8, 2021
at Memorial Park for new exercise equipment at Memorial Park.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 8:32 p.m.

                     Christopher J. Reinersman, Mayor

SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of July 06, 2021               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Tuesday, July 6,
2021 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Amy Engelman, Carol
Franzen, Dave Shafer, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, Deputy Clerk Chelsea Cox
and Attorney David Steele.
Approval of the June 14, 2021 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the special council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
June 14, 2021.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for special
meeting held on June 14, 2021. Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second
by Council Member Shafer. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2021-R-16 – Z21 Zoning Update
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-16 which proposed a text
amendment which updates the Independence Zoning Code. He stated Planning and
Development Services (PDS) conducted an audit of each of the zoning codes in
Kenton County and developed a new zoning blueprint which is referred to as Z21:
Zoning for the 21st Century.
Kristen Martin and Patrick Denbow with Planning and Development Services (PDS)
presented the changes to the Kenton County zoning code. Mrs. Martin and Mr.
Denbow stated there have been several meetings to update the zoning code and
the Z21 plan included three phases: Audit, Blueprint and Implementation. She
stated the new articles are 2) Nonconformities, 3) Zoning Districts-will be
reduced from 23 zones to 16 zones, 4) Use Regulations and Standards, 5)
Dimensional Requirements, 7) Development Standards: lighting standards and
landscaping regulations, 8) Natural Resources and Environment: Stream and Water
Buffers, Green Development, Infill and Grayfield Development, 10) Parking and
Loading Standards, Access Management and Circulation, 13) Process and
Procedure: Combined Map/Variance/Conditional Use, Concept Development Plan and
Final Development Plan.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-16.
Council Member Waite so moved, with a second by Council Member Engelman. Motion
carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Council Meeting Schedule for Holidays – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which addresses when regular
scheduled council meetings fall on a holiday. He stated the ordinance clarifies
previous ordinances that discuss council meetings falling on holidays and they
will now be moved to the following Monday. Attorney Steele gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.

Mayor Reinersman stated the Independence Day festival was a successful event

K-9 to the Independence Police Department. Mayor Reinersman stated there was a

August 30, 2021
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of August 30, 2021               City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August
30, 2021 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol
Franzen, Dave Shafer, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Council Member Engelman
was absent. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, Deputy Clerk
Chelsea Cox and Attorney David Steele.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2021-2022 Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed resolution which adopts the tax rates for
the fiscal year of July 1,2021 through June 30, 2022. He stated $.271 per $100
for the real estate tax and $.634 per $100 for personal property taxes are the
current tax rates. Mayor Reinersman stated the assessed property values were up
15% for the year and he proposed a 10% rate decrease to $.244 for real estate
and $.595 for personal property. Attorney Steele gave the proposed ordinance a
first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting Tax Rebate for 2021-2022 – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which adopts a tax rebate. He
stated the rebate will provide a one-time reduction 10% discount off the entire
real estate property tax bill if paid by December 31, 2021. Attorney Steele
gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2021-R-18 – CARES Grant
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2021-R-18 which authorizes and
approves the Mayor to sign the Memorandum of Agreement related to CARES grant
of $209,367. Attorney Steele read Resolution No. 2021-R-18.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2021-R-18.
Council Member Waite made a second. Roll was called and votes were unanimous.
Motion passed, 5-0.
Attorney Report – David Steele
Attorney Steele stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated the preliminary bids will be coming in shortly to terrace
the amphitheater hill.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the 2020 Census Data came back and we are still the
fasted growing city in Kenton County with a population of 28,676.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 6:33 p.m.

Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they

Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for regular

Member Brinker. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Downs of Nicholson Updated
Mayor Reinersman stated the One Holland Group recently made some plan changes
to the Downs of Nicholson development. Petey Cunningham from the One Holland
Group stated the residential section will now be a total of 90 patio homes as
well as a public gym. Mayor Reinersman stated the development will include a
Roy Rogers restaurant and a microbrewery and the project will likely start by
the end of 2022 with completion of the project hopefully in the fall of 2023 or
early 2024.
Proposed Ordinance – Updated Franchise Agreement w/TBNK/Cincinnati Bell – 1st
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which updates the franchise
agreement with Cincinnati Bell Extended Territories LLC.
Tim Broering, Executive Director with Telecommunications Board of Northern
Kentucky (TBNK)  stated he has been working on this agreement for a couple of
years. He stated Charter is the main company and the updated agreement is valid
for 10 years with an initial period of 5 years with an automatic renewal period
of an additional 5 years. The agreement is for CB to offer cable tv services
(not broadband internet services) with the same 5% franchise fee. Mayor
Reinersman stated the franchise agreement is giving permission to the provider
to install services in the city’s right of way. Attorney Gatlin gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Compensation Update – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which updates the annual salary
for the mayor from $15,000 to $25,000, effective January 1, 2023. He stated by
statute the salary of elected officials cannot be changed during a term and the
salary of the mayor hasn’t been updated since 2007. Council Member Franzen
stated she was the one who brought up the idea after how much work and time the
Mayor does in our city. Council had some discussion about adding health
insurance as an added benefit for the mayor as well in the possible future.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated there was a huge foreclosure ramp up within the last 6
months and it’s now leveled off. He stated we currently have 12 active
foreclosures in the city, which is back to normal.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated Cody Road has finally been repaved and hopefully the bridge
will be replaced next. He stated he was told Oliver and Cox Road will be
repaved in the next month or so.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated he is working with legislators to keep pushing our
street repair projects which include Oliver, Cox, Bristow and Hwy 17. He stated
the first phase of the 536 project has been completed. Mayor Reinersman stated
the Van Trust project on 536, which has been named Park 536, is moving along
and they will be leaving a lot of trees on the hillside. Mayor Reinersman
stated the Christmas Walk will be on December 4th with many holiday festivities
throughout the city including a craft show and a 5K. He stated the Independence
Ball will be on November 20th at Saint Barbara Church which honors veterans and
first responders as well as creates fellowship in the community.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:54 p.m.

Community Commercial (CC) zone. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2022-R-01.
Mayor Reinersman stated there are two interested parties in expanding self-
storage in the Cherokee Shopping Center.
Hark Investments is the current owner of the separate building to the left.
Edward Turner, who is the property manager, said they are wanting to open back
up the laundromat add additional self-enclosed storage. Chris Moriconi stated
the separate building will be going before the board of adjustments in a couple
of weeks because of the variance.
David Cooper, resident, stated he likes the idea and think it would be a good
business with the apartments.
John Huffman, owner of Beechgrove Self Storage – Mr. Huffman stated he has
interest in purchasing the storage facility and adjacent building in the
Cherokee Plaza and updating the storage facility. He presented to council his
ideas are for the Cherokee Plaza with self-storage and other mixed uses in the
spaces. Mr. Huffman stated it would create new synergy in a dying area and the
outside access creates a safer space. Mayor Reinersman stated there are design
standards that include minimal metal or concrete on buildings. He stated self-
storage is mainly seen in industrial areas and it might deter other retail
business from wanting to open in the plaza. Council had some discussion and
agreed to trust him at this point.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2022-R-01 and a
second by Council Member Engelman. Roll was called and motion carried with all
ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2022-R-02 – Build Grant MOA Authorization
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2022-R-02 which authorizes the Mayor
to sign the Memorandum of Agreement related to the USDOT Build Grant for the KY
536 Project. He stated the city has pledged $50,000 in local funding towards
the project. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2022-R-02.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2022-R-02.
Council Member Waite so moved, with a second by Council Member Vogelpohl.
Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Executive Order No. 2022-EO-02 – Appointment to PDS Council
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2021-EO-02 which re-appoints
Mayor Reinersman as the primary representative to the Planning and Development
Services Council and Carol Franzen as the alternative representative for 2022.
Surplus Property – Firearms
Mayor Reinersman presented a list of firearms which includes 36 Glock 22s, 4
Glock 23s, 37 Glock 27s and 10 rifles that the police department wishes to
surplus the weapons to Trigger Firearms of Florence.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the surplus property. Council
Member Franzen made a motion, Council Member Engelman made a second. Motion
carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated nothing to report.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi shared some plan images of the amphitheater terracing. He stated
there will be three sets of stairs coming up the hill with several flat areas
and a large cross walk as well as two viewing areas at the top of the hill. Mr.
Moriconi stated construction is expected to start mid-July and wrapped up by
end of November. He added the party in the park concerts will be held in May,
June and July for 2022. Mr. Moriconi stated the pickleball courts and restrooms
should also be under construction this summer.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated there have been some redistricting throughout the city
and the county clerk is working on putting a new map together.
Council Member Franzen stated after looking into it further, in order for the
city to allow the mayor to be eligible for the city’s medical plan, the council
needs to bless the current mayor to be added as an eligible participant to the
health insurance plan. There was some discussion amongst council about the
issue and it was agreed that it should be offered to the mayor as long as the
appropriate time is put in by the mayor.
Council Member Franzen made a motion for the current mayor to be eligible for
the city’s medical insurance plan as a fringe benefit because he puts in the
time and dedication. Council Member Waite made a second. Roll was called and
votes were unanimous. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Engelman to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 9:23 p.m.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, April 4,
2022 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and Scout Jake from
Troop 31 led the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the
invocation. Roll was called and the following Council Members registered
present: Tom Brinker, Amy Engelman, Carol Franzen and Dave Shafer. Council
Members Vogelpohl and Waite were absent. Also present was City Administrator
Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Gabbard, Attorney Jack Gatlin, Captain Russ
Wood and Police Chief Tony Lucas.
Approval of the March 7, 2022 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
March 7, 2022.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the meeting minutes for regular
meeting held on March 7, 2022. Council Member Shafer so moved with a second by
Council Member Franzen. Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2022-O-02 -Text Amendment for Storage - 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2022-O-02 which amends the text of the
Independence Zoning Code to remove mini-warehouses and personal storage as
conditional uses in the CC (Community Commercial) Zone. He stated there was a
public hearing at the Kenton County Planning Commission (KCPC) on February 3,
2022 where the text amendment was unanimously approved. Attorney Gatlin gave
Ordinance No. 2022-O-02 a second reading.
Todd McMurtry (attorney representing John Huffman) - Mr. McMurtry stated KCPC’s
agreement is strictly zone recommendations, not what is best for the community
and area. He stated Mr. Huffman will be presenting an updated plan with
alternatives.
John Huffman, owner of Beechgrove and Crescent Springs Self Storage Centers.
Mr. Huffman stated he understands that retail generates more payroll taxes and
storage is part of people’s lives when things change. He stated he is planning
to demolish the small side building as the walls are leaning as it’s unsafe.
Mr. Huffman shared his plans of what the storage center would look like during
the day as well as at night. He stated each unit would be separate and would
have sprinklers so in case of a fire, it would be contained and not spread. Mr.
Huffman stated he could sell the parking lot to a developer and put in a gas
station instead of storage. He stated he understands and would conform to
landscape buffers and other requirements set forth for the project.
Laura Mitchell, 6430 Adahi Drive – Ms. Mitchell stated Mr. Huffman stopped by
her house to discuss the storage plan. She stated she wants to keep the trees
and deer in her backyard. Ms. Mitchell stated she doesn’t want to look out her
backyard and see a building and is not in favor of additional storage building
in the lot behind her house.
Karyl Shouse, 737 Cox Road – she stated she’s lived in the city for 25 years.
She doesn’t have a problem with storage but doesn’t want to lose the wooded
area behind her house. She was also concerned the additional storage building
in her backyard would lower her property value.
Katherine Huffman, 2256 Devlin Place, daughter of John Huffman – she stated the
dead trees in the lot would be removed and there would be a landscape buffer
zone so there will still be trees in the neighbors’ back yards. Ms. Huffman
stated they offer free police training on the premise.
Mr. John Huffman stated there are requirements for approval for such as
buffers, setbacks, etc.
Council Member Franzen stated her concern regarding Mr. Huffman telling her his
plan to remove the landscape buffer by the storm pond. Mr. Huffman stated they
no longer are interested in the 4th parcel.
Jack Gatlin stated this is not a proposal for a map amendment. He stated
council is voting on a text amendment which removes self-storage as a
conditional use in a Community Commercials (CC) zone, not voting specifically
on Mr. Huffman’s project.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2022-O-02.
Council Member Brinker so moved with a second by Council Member Shafer. Motion
carried with all ayes, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2022-O-03 - Amended Employee Pay & Classification - 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2022-O-03 which amends the employee
pay and classification plan for the position of Senior Center Director as well
as adding Program Coordinator. He stated with the upcoming retirement of
current Parks and Recreation Facilitator, it’s created an opportunity to look
at several positions. Mayor Reinersman stated that Julie Callahan, the Senior
Center Director, will be moving to full time and a new part time position of
Program Coordinator will be added. Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2022-O-03
a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2022-O-03.
Council Member Engelman so moved with a second by Council Member Franzen.
Motion carried with all ayes, 4-0.
Ordinance No. 2022-O-04 -Text Amendment for Family Child Care - 2nd Reading 
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2022-O-04 which amends the

Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2022-O-04 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2022-O-04.

Michels’ bid was $857,058.75. Mr. Moriconi stated the project is for concrete
tear-outs and he asked council to approve the Part A which is for Constitution

for the 2022 Street Project for the Part A. Council Member Engelman made a

Attorney Gatlin stated they have added a new attorney, Alex Kerns, to their

services. Mr. Moriconi stated more information will be presented at the next
meeting when reviewing the 2022-2023 budget.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the Independence Egg Hunt is scheduled for Saturday,
April 9th at Memorial Day with a rain date of April 16th. He stated the
decision will be made on Wednesday, April 6th on whether to have it or push
back to the 16th. Mayor Reinersman stated there will be thousands of eggs,
jugglers and prizes and thanked Hickory Grove Baptist for partnering again this

Cincinnati, Covington and Newport. He stated the Greater Cincinnati Chamber is

profit event. He is proposing $29,000 which is $1 per resident for our city,

Reinersman stated the fencing is being replaced at Sterling Staggs at the

Mayor Reinersman stated some new things coming to Independence are some
restaurants, a car wash and the Downs of Nicholson which will offer an upscale

Julie Kirkpatrick with meetNKY and Brent Cooper with NKY Chamber of Commerce

stated the ARPA funds were dispersed to help areas that lacked tourism over the
past couple of years.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2022-R-06.
Council Member Brinker made a motion to approve Resolution No. 2022- R-06.
Council Member Shafer made a second. Motion carried with a vote of 4-2. Council
Members Vogelpohl and Waite were opposed.
Ordinance No. 2022-O-05 – Amended 2021-2022 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2022-O-05 which amends the 2021-2022
budget.
Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2022-O-05 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2022-O- 05 which
amends the 2021-2022 budget. Council Member Franzen made a motion and Council
Member Engelman made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
 Ordinance No. 2022-O-06 – Adopting the 2022-2023 Budget – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2022-O-06 which adopts the 2022-2023
budget. Mayor Reinersman stated the new budget includes a lower tax rate, which
makes two years in a row.
Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2022-O-06 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman stated the entire Police Department was looked at piece by
piece and that we do offer a great benefits package, including lots of accrued
paid leave (APL). He stated it can be reviewed and revised later in the year if
we find ourselves out of line with our competition.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2022-O- 06 which
adopts the 2022-2023 budget. Council Member Franzen made a motion and Council
Member Shafer made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2022-O-07 – Employee Pay Classification for 2022-2023– 2nd
Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2022-O-07 which adopts the employee
pay and classification for the 2022-2023 year. Attorney Gatlin gave Ordinance
No. 2022-O-07 a second reading.
Council Members Waite and Vogelpohl stated a suggestion of creating grades for
all positions. Mayor Reinersman stated his concern with changing to grade and
tying that compensation to years of service. He stated to institute the change
would essentially create another layer of numbers to calculate and amend each
year based on what raises would be and we can’t guarantee a certain raise each
year. Mayor Reinersman stated a deep dive is done on salaries every couple of
years and we adjust accordingly. He stated the minimum and maximum are required
to be laid out each year by statute.
Council Member Vogelpohl stated he would like to sit down and discuss the
possibility of adding grades to the payscale going forward.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2022-O- 07 which
adopts the employee pay and classification for 2022-2023. Council Member
Engelman made a motion and Council Member Brinker made a second. Motion carried
with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2022-R-07 – 2028 Centennial – Stage II Development Plan
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2022-R-07 which conditionally
approves the 5,500 square foot Stage II Development Plan at 2028 Centennial
Boulevard.
Patrick Denbow, Senior Planner with Planning and Development Services (PDS),
stated they have conditionally approved the development plan with revisions to
the lighting level and landscape type 2 buffer in the final plan. Mr. Denbow
stated there is some flexibility regarding to the type 2 buffer with options of
a 15-foot strip with fencing and vegetation or a 30 foot strip with just
vegetation
Bill Aseere, co-owner of Space Cowboys, stated his appreciation of lowering the
property tax rates again this year. He stated he is seeking clarification on
what type 2 landscape buffer means. Mr. Aseere stated they are wanting to house
their offices at this location as well as at least one restaurant, one with a
drive thru.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2022-R-07.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2022- R-07 which
approves the Sate II Development Plan for 2028 Centennial Blvd. Council Member
Waite made a motion and Council Member Franzen made a second. Motion carried
with all ayes, 6-0.
Executive Order No. 2022-EO-04 – Appointment to the Northern Kentucky
Independent District Board of Health
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2022-EO-04 which appoints Carol
Franzen as Mayor Reinersman’s designee to the Northern Kentucky Independent
District Board of Health. He stated this appointment takes effect immediately.
Award Bid – Concrete
Mayor Reinersman presented the concrete bids received from Ernst Concrete and
Hometown Concrete. Mr. Moriconi stated concrete work is bid out each year for
projects throughout the city. He stated Ernst’s bid came in at $1,294 for 10
cubic yards and Hometown’s bid came in at $1,354 per 10 cubic yards. Mr.

Attorney Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.

budget. He introduced Sharon Price, who is the city’s new Program Coordinator
that will be handling events throughout the city, upon Nita Brake’s recent
retirement.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated his recommendation of bringing the Board of Adjustments
back to the city, and get out of Kenton County joint board. He stated we will
put the word out to residents to see about finding board members. Attorney
Gatlin stated there will need to be 5-7 board members and they will need
training on the role of the board of adjustments.
Mayor Reinersman stated he will soon be joining Chief Lucas to see Brian

back in full force this year with 2 days of rides, fireworks and fun.

Minutes of August 22, 2022
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August
22, 2022 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol
Franzen, Dave Shafer and Chris Vogelpohl. Council Members Engelman and Waite
were absent. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk
Gina Rawe, Attorney Jack Gatlin, Chief Anthony Lucas and Captain Russ Wood.
Police Recognition – Detective Strine
Mayor Reinersman and Chief Lucas presented a plaque of recognition to Detective
Adam Strine.
Swearing In of Officer O’Brien
Mayor Reinersman swore in Officer Cole O’Brien as a new officer with the City
of Independence.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting 2022-2023 Tax Rates – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed resolution which adopts the tax rates for
the fiscal year of July 1,2022 through June 30, 2023. He stated the current
rates are $.244 per $100 for the real estate tax and $.595 per $100 for
personal property taxes. Mayor Reinersman stated he’s proposing a rate decrease
to $.22 per $100 for real estate and $.534 per $100 for personal property.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Municipal Order No. 2022-MO-01 – ARPA Premium Pay
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2022-MO-01 which will provide
premium pay of $2.00 per hour for full-time employees that worked for the city
between April 1, 2020 through December 30, 2021. He stated the pay will come
out of the Local Fiscal Recovery Funds (ARPA) funds the city received, which
was in excess of the $7,300,000. Mayor Reinersman stated the premium pay is for
any full- time employees that worked in the office and/or the field. He stated
in order for employees to receive the premium pay, they must be employed full
time with the City of Independence on December 1, 2022.
Attorney Gatlin read Municipal Order No. 2022-MO-01.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Municipal Order No. 2022-MO-01
which provides premium pay to city employees. Council Member Franzen made a
motion to approve. Council Member Vogelpohl made a second. Roll was called and
motion carried with a vote of 4- 0.
Ordinance No. 2022-O-08 – Amended Employee Pay Classification for 2022-2023 –
2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2022-O-08 which amends Ordinance No.
2022-O-07 by updating the pay classification plan for city employees. Attorney
Gatlin gave Ordinance No. 2022-O-08 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2022-O- 08 which
amends the previously adopted pay classification plan. Council Member Vogelpohl
made a motion to approve. Council Member Brinker made a second. Roll was called
and motion carried with a vote of 4-0.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated he wanted to provide the updated 5-year street plan. He
stated the plan is to bump up the streets of Centennial, Declaration and
Delaware Crossing and lumping some projects together to get better pricing on
bigger jobs.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated he wanted to express his thanks for our Public Services
crew for helping out in the floods in Eastern Kentucky. He stated the PDS
Director has reached out to him and asked the city to consider staying with the
Joint Kenton County Board of Adjustments, rather than putting together our own
Board of Adjustments and states they are working on some changes to the current
board.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Shafer to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:33 p.m.

Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2022-R-13 which approves the final
development plan for Beechgrove. Mr. Moriconi stated this development goes back
to 1971 and the plan has less density than what is required of the zone. He
stated it should have site elevation and layout for the plan for 35 town homes
which will be on the corner of Wildwood and Beechgrove. Mr. Moriconi stated
Planning and Development Services (PDS) gave a favorable recommendation on the

homes including a new street, sidewalk and parking on 3.5 acres. Attorney
Gatlin read Resolution No. 2022-R-13.

Bid Award – Cody Road Culvert
Mayor Reinersman stated the culvert pipe under the Cody Road bridge and
municipal road aid will help fund. Mr. Moriconi stated a new culvert should
reduce flooding by 50%. He stated the engineer’s estimate was $246,040 and
three bids were received. Mr. Moriconi stated engineer recommends the Ford
Development Corporation with the lowest bid with $324,195 and added that the
pipe will be custom ordered for the project and it will likely be completed
sometime in 2023. He stated Municipal Road Aid, Cody Road Funds and capital
monies will cover the cost of the project.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to award the bid for the Cody Road Culvert
project to Ford Development Corporation. Council Member Franzen made a motion
to award the bid to Ford Development Corporation with a second by Council
Member Brinker. Roll was called and motion carried with a vote of 5-0.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated there are currently 24 homes in foreclosure and 1 of
those was initiated by the city due to code enforcement and should be going up
for sale in early 2023.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated Memorial Park is getting a lot of use with the
expansion of basketball courts, addition of pickleball courts and new shelter
and restrooms are underway. He stated the terracing of the hillside at the
amphitheater is delayed but hoping to obtain bids in November and hope to
complete project by next summer but it’s not looking good.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:44 p.m.

Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, Dave Shafer, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney
Jack Gatlin, Chief Lucas and Captain Russ Wood.
Approval of the September 12, 2022 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
September 12, 2022. Council Member Shafer stated he mentioned a correction to
the minutes to the clerk in regards to meeting attendance.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the council meeting minutes
from the regular meeting held on September 12, 2022, with the mentioned
correction per Council Member Shafer. Council Member Waite made a motion to
approve and Council Member Shafer made a second. Motion carried with all ayes,
6-0.
Approval of the October 24, 2022 Special Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the council meeting minutes for the special meeting held on
October 24, 2022.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the council meeting minutes
from the special meeting held on October 24, 2022. Council Member Franzen made
a motion to approve the meeting minutes for the special meeting held on October
24, 2022. Council Member Engelman made a second. Motion carried with all ayes,
6-0.
Proposed Ordinance –– Golf Carts - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which regulates the use of golf
carts on certain roads within the city. He stated there are subdivisions in the
city where unlicensed teenagers are driving golf carts and the Police
Department is receiving complaints. Chief Lucas stated the Police Department is
looking for something to help officers’ ability to enforce penalties for repeat
offenders and help keep city streets safe. Council Member Brinker stated golf
cart insurance is less than $100 a year and questioned the $75 fee associated
with the permit. Chief Lucas explained the fee would cover the administrative
costs as well as the inspection, certificate, sticker and permit.
Council Member Vogelpohl questioned the inspection part of the process.
Attorney Gatlin referenced the KRS, which was implemented in 2020, in regards
to the requirements for a vehicle to be street legal. After some discussion,
Council agreed they like the idea of the ordinance but not in favor of the $75
fee and suggested $15 instead.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Resolution No. 2022-R-14 – Text Amendment for Commercial Zone(s)
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2022-R-14 which is for a text
amendment to allow permitted coin-operated laundries and drycleaners in the
commercial zones of RC (Rural Commercial), NC (Neighborhood Commercial) and CC
(Community Commercial) zones. There was some discussion amongst Council and
they agreed they would just like to apply the text amendment to the CC zone.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2022-R-14.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2022-R-14 which
allows adding coin- permitted laundry as a permitted use only to the CC zone.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve. Council Member Waite made a
second. Roll was called and motion carried with a vote of 6-0.
Executive Order No. 2022-EO-05 – Re-appointment to TBNK Board
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2022-EO-05 which re-appoints Tom
Brinker to the TBNK Board for the term of January 1, 2023 through December 31,
2024.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated that Josh with PDS is doing a great job with collection
on repeat offenders with code enforcement issues and will have more to report
next month.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated the budget will be amended in December due to ARPA fund
allocation. He stated Hunters Green and Flintlock Court streets need redone.
Mr. Moriconi stated the project will be split into two projects; both projects
would be $720,000 each, totaling $1,400,000. He stated this project would be
completed using ARPA funds and will go to bid. Mr. Moriconi stated the new
pickleball courts have lighting and the park hours will need to be adjusted so
the park doesn’t close at dusk in areas that are lit. He stated if any council
members want to be on the city float at the Christmas Walk parade, to let him
know.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the annual Christmas Walk will be on December 3rd
kicking off at 1:00 with the Santa 5k and craft show on courthouse lawn. He
stated the lighted parade starts at 5:00 and Santa at the city building
beginning at 6:00. He congratulated council members before being re-elected and
expressed his sadness for the departure of Council Member Engelman. Mayor
Reinersman stated another engineering firm is going to take a look at the bid
packet for terracing of the Amphitheater project and see what they think could
be tweaked to help bring cost down.
Council Member Vogelpohl stated the city has started seeing panhandlers in the
city in various grocery store parking lots. Attorney Gatlin stated the city
would need to be careful and he would email council a couple sample ordinances
that other cities have adopted. Council Member Vogelpohl also stated he would
like to review and update the parking time limits for trailers and campers.
Mayor Reinersman stated the code enforcement complaints for the past year will
be ran and shared with council so they can review and see if there is a pattern
in the complaints.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Vogelpohl to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 8:11 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, December
5, 2022 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Amy
Engelman, Carol Franzen, Dave Shafer, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney
Jack Gatlin and Chief Lucas.
Swearing in of Council Members and Mayor
Judge Susanne Cetrulo swore in the Council Members elect Tom Brinker, Dave
Shafer, Carol Franzen, Chris Vogelpohl, Greg Waite and Greg Steffen as well as
Mayor Christopher Reinersman.
Recognitions
Mayor Reinersman recognized Independence resident Maddie Strong, who is the
2022 KHSAA Class AA girls cross country state champion. He presented Ms. Strong
with a sign which will be placed near her home.
Officer Kruetzjans presented a certificate of appreciation to Molly Hancock for
her efforts in assisting with catching a thief in her neighborhood.
Mayor Reinersman presented a plaque to A.J. Kenner for his promotion to
Detective.
Approval of the November 14, 2022 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
