Proposed Ordinance –– Golf Carts -1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented the updated proposed ordinance which regulates the
use of golf carts on certain roads within the city. Attorney Gatlin gave the
proposed ordinance a first reading.
Attorney Gatlin stated there has been some discussion on the inspection process
and new verbiage will have the Kenton County Sheriff’s office do the
inspections.
Proposed Ordinance –– Amended 2022-2023 Budget -1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the 2022-2023
Budget. He stated the lines highlighted in yellow are items that are changing.
Mayor Reinersman mentioned some items that changed: increase in revenue for
property taxes, July 4th festival, increase in costs for adding a second SRO
(School Resource Officer) at Summit View Academy, new IT provider, removed
contractor fees for Finance Director due to retirement and hiring a replacement
as an employee, salary adjustments for police and public services, completion
of new pickleball courts, shelter and restrooms in Memorial Park, new vehicles
for the Building Inspector and Public Services Director and updating streets in
the Hunters Green subdivision.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Trailer, Boat/RV Storage Discussion
Council Member Vogelpohl stated he has been approached by several residents in
regards to reviewing the current ordinance in regards to boat, RV and trailer
storage. He stated he would like to allow empty trailer parking in resident’s
driveways as well as camper parking extended from 3 to 5 business days. There
was some discussion about different scenarios and what was covered regarding
the zoning in Z21.
Police Chief Lucas stated any trailers parked on the street are addressed by
the police, if they are parked in the driveway, that is a code enforcement
issue. There was some discussion from council regarding low profile trailers
and the importance of defining exactly what that is.
Al Daly, 10330 Limerick Circle, Independence, KY, stated he’s on the NKY Code
Enforcement Board and several cities have received several appeals in regards
to complaints about trailer regulations and violations.
John Huffman, owner of Beechgrove Self Storage, asked what zone a trailer could
be parked in and/or stored. Attorney Gatlin stated the information would need
to be checked against the new Z21 Plan as the discussion was just in regards to
residential zones.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way – she questioned enforcement and stated the city’s
code enforcement officer wasn’t able to go on someone’s property to address the
trailer parked in the driveway.
Attorney Gatlin stated he would check what’s included in Z21 in regards to
these parking restrictions in regards to zoning for future discussions.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated this year’s Christmas Walk was a big success and thanks to
all the volunteers and staff that helped make it happen.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated it was another amazing Christmas Walk and expressed his
appreciation to Greg Waite, city staff, volunteers, Independence Business
Association and local businesses and that everyone’s efforts helped make this
event happen and successful. He stated the city is at 74 new homes for the year
in the city and continuing to grow. Mayor Reinersman stated the Police
Department is at full staff and there will be another graduation for new
officers later this week.
Council Member Franzen thanked Council Member Engelman for her service on
council for the past six years and wished her well. Mayor Reinersman agreed and
thanked her for her service.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Engelman
and seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes

2023 Minutes
January 9, 2023
SPECIAL COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of January 9, 2023
City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, January
9, 2023at 7:00 p.m. in at the Kenton County Courthouse, 5272 Madison Pike,
Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding. Mayor
Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the following
Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Dave Shafer,
Greg Steffen, Greg Waite and Chris Vogelpohl. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney Jack Gatlin, Chief
Anthony Lucas and Captain Russ Wood.
Key to the City – Jim Brewer
Mayor Reinersman presented a Key to the City plaque to resident Jim Brewer for
his many years of service on the Kenton County Joint Board of Adjustments as a
representative for Independence.
Children’s Home of Northern Kentucky
Rick Wurth, CEO of the Children’s Home of Northern Kentucky, addressed council
to request financial assistance from the city. Mr. Wurth stated several other
cities have donated up to $100,000 from their ARPA funds to invest in the
growth of the Children’s Home of Northern Kentucky. He stated they are working
on a 4.5 million dollar expansion project and could use council’s help to help
bridge the gap between children and mental health issues.
Council Member Franzen stated her recommendation for a $150,000 donation to the
Children’s Home of Northern Kentucky. Mr. Gatlin stated with this being a
special meeting, council is not able to create new business and can prepare a
resolution authorizing the donation at the February meeting.
Approval of the December 5, 2022 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the regular council meeting minutes for the meeting held on
December 5, 2022.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the council meeting minutes
from the regular meeting held on December 5, 2022. Council Member Vogelpohl
made a motion to approve and Council Member Shafer made a second. Motion
carried with 5-0 vote; Council Member Steffen abstained.
Ordinance No. 2023-O-01 – Golf Carts – 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2023-O-01 which regulates the use of
golf carts on certain roads within the city. Chief Lucas stated the golf cart
regulations require a licensed driver, owner to carry insurance and the
Sheriff’s office will inspect, prior to issuing a permit. Attorney Gatlin gave
Ordinance No. 2023-O-01 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2023-O-01.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a motion to approve and a second by Council
Member Franzen. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried,
6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Amended 2022-2023 Budget -1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends Ordinance No.
2022-O-06 for the annual budget for the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2022 and
ends June 30, 2023. He stated some of the changes that were made were reporting
25% of ARPA as revenue each year, implementation of the new pay program for the
police, changing Finance Director position from a contractor to an employee,
new IT security provider, new vehicles, park improvements, etc. Attorney Gatlin
gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Pay Classification – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the pay plan for
employees. He stated we will be moving the Finance Director position from a
contractor to an employee. Mayor Reinersman stated the Evidence Technician/
Custodian will now be full-time position, which was previously a part time
position. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Park Closing -1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which allows certain city parks
with lighting to be partially open after dark. He stated the amendment updates
the parks closing at dark except areas lit specifically for basketball,
pickleball and city sponsored events. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed
ordinance a first reading.
Municipal Order No. 2023-MO-01 – Board of Adjustments Appointment
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2023-MO-01 which appoints Steven
Sorg to the Kenton County Joint Board of Adjustments for a three-year term.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Municipal Order No. 2023-MO-01.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve and a second by Council Member
Waite. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Executive Order No. 2023-EO-02 – OKI Board Re-Appointment
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2023-EO-02 which re-appoints
himself to the OKI Board of Directors for 2023.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he’s been meeting with Josh at PDS (Planning and
Development Services) regarding various code and lien issues and will have a
full report at the next meeting.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated City Clerk Gina Rawe was awarded as the Outstanding
Municipal Clerk of the Year of Northern Kentucky for 2022. He stated his
appreciation to staff for working together to keep the city running while
dealing with the water damage the administrative offices experienced over the
holidays. He stated Cody Bridge replacement should happen in March and the
sliding glass doors at the Senior Center are being replaced soon. Mr. Moriconi
stated the premiums for the self-insured medical plan is receiving a decrease
for the upcoming plan year and he added that the boy scouts brought a flag
disposal box to the parking lot at the city building.
Trailer, Boat/RV Storage Discussion
Mayor Reinersman stated he’s checked around with other local cities to see what
they have in regards to storage for trailers, boats, RVs, etc. He stated this
is a zoning issue and if council wishes to make changes, they would need to
pass a resolution for a text amendment. Council Member Vogelpohl stated by
giving residents up to 5 days for their campers, exclude empty flatbed trailers
and closed pop-up campers and feels it would cut down on code enforcement
complaints. Mr. Gatlin stated measurements would need to be specified as well
to make changes.
Al Daly, 10330 Limerick Circle – serves on Code Enforcement Board. Mr. Daly
stated if council is wanting to change the allowable timing for recreational
vehicles to be parked at a residence, they would have to apply for a text
amendment.
Mayor Reinersman stated we might need to have a preliminary public hearing to
let the public speak their opinion before it would go to Kenton County Planning
Commission for a public hearing. He stated Attorney Gatlin can draft something
for council to review before moving forward.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the Christmas Walk went off seamlessly this year. He
stated the Kenton County payroll taxes went up substantially and could
potentially hinder local economic growth efforts.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Vogelpohl to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 8:39 p.m.

City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
6, 2023 at 7:00 p.m. at the Kenton County Courthouse, 5272 Madison Pike,
Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman presiding. Mayor
Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of Allegiance.
Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the following
Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Dave Shafer,
Greg Steffen, Greg Waite and Chris Vogelpohl. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney Jack Gatlin, Chief
Anthony Lucas and Captain Russ Wood.
Approval of the January 9, 2023 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the special council meeting minutes for the meeting held on

Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the council meeting minutes

Presentation of Audit – VonLehman
Kristin Leadingham, Senior Manager with VonLehman, presented the audit for the
fiscal year ending on June 30, 2022. She stated they did not have to make any
modifications to the audit report and the extra cash in the budget is from the
ARPA monies received and not yet allocated. Mrs. Leadingham stated the decrease

there were no deficiencies with internal controls.

Resolution No. 2023-R-02 – Text Amendment for Parking and Utility Trailers
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2023-R-02 which sponsors a text
amendment to article 10.13 parking and loading standards. Council Member
Franzen stated the history of the implementation of these regulations which
were decided by committees that included residents both in favor of as well as
opposed of campers and boats being parked in driveways.
Council Member Vogelpohl stated he was contacted by a resident regarding
parking limitations regarding trailers and campers. He stated code enforcement
is taken up by quite a bit of complaints regarding utility trailers and campers
parked beyond the 72-hour period. Council Member Vogelpohl stated his proposal
would be to eliminate violations of empty utility trailers from being parked in
driveways. He stated wants to hear from residents on what they want and hopes
we can find a compromise for everyone. Council Member Brinker questioned the
code in regards to lots that are larger than an acre.
Mayor Reinersman stated code enforcement violations are generated by anonymous
complaints. Council Member Shafer questioned what the complaints were for and
Council Member Vogelpohl stated mainly for items parked in driveways longer
than the 72-hour time limit.
Scott Paul, 4987 Pritchard Lane, Independence, KY- Mr. Paul mentioned the
rising cost of storage and would like to focus on the definition of blight.
Amanda Kremer, 2158 Stoneharbor Lane, Independence, KY – Ms. Kremer stated she
didn’t see anything about travel trailers that were 17-30 feet long or anything
about boats in the proposed changes. She also suggested extending the 72-hour
(3 days) time limit to 5 days or longer.
Al Daly, 10330 Limerick Circle, Independence, KY- Mr. Daly stated he does not
like the proposed changes as a resident. He stated as a code enforcement board
member, pavement is defined as asphalt or blacktop.
Dan Burgey, 3164 Tennyson Place, Independence, KY – Mr. Burgey stated if the
original ordinance that was passed in 2001 is loosened up, there will likely be
some confusion. He asked who to reach out to in regards to parking issues on
the street. Mayor Reinersman instructed him to contact Kenton County Dispatch.
Mike Leming, 11579 Tremont Court, Independence, KY – Mr. Leming stated he would
like to see the policy go away entirely as long as the item is operable. He
stated it costs $1800-$2500 a year to store a boat.
Brian Girvin, 11582 Tremont Court, Independence, KY - Mr. Girvin stated it is
expensive to get a pad poured on the side or behind his house.
Annette Rader, 10468 Canberra Drive, Independence, KY – Mrs. Rader stated they
moved here from Erlanger 6 months ago and wanted clarification on the
restrictions of having campers. She stated she believes that 72 hours is not
enough time to prep and unload when using a travel trailer.
Marge Cook, 96 Carrie Way, Independence, KY – Ms. Cook questioned how someone
can tell if something is operable or not if you aren’t allowed on the person’s
property.
John Huffman, 4290 Richardson Road, Independence, KY – Mr. Huffman questioned
if any final decisions were being made at the meeting. Mayor Reinersman stated
a resolution has been proposed and if council decides to pass, it would go to
the Kenton County Planning Commission for recommendations to council.
Fred Rombold, 11547 Jamestown Lane, Independence, KY – Mr. Rombold stated he
has a pop-up camper and is able to park it behind his house. He doesn’t think
72 hours is enough time for having a camper in your driveway for those that
aren’t able to park it behind their house.
John Rellahan, 1789 Freedom Trail, Independence, KY– Mr. Rellahan stated that
72 hours is not enough time to keep in his driveway.
Chris Baldwin, 22 Peach Drive, Independence, KY – Mr. Baldwin stated by taking
complaints anonymously, they can be made by someone that doesn’t even live in
the city.
Scott Sizemore, 5113 Madison Pike, Independence, KY – Mr. Sizemore stated the
definition of sizes of trailer listed is vague. He stated the cost of storage
is pricey.
Mayor Reinersman stated if council wants to update the zoning code, he would
like to put together specific changes they are proposing.
Council Member Franzen stated residents should be able to park their stuff on
their property but if there aren’t any rules, people abuse it and store their
unsightly stuff on their property. Council discussed and agreed that a
committee would be beneficial to move forward with the issue to propose
updates.
Council Member Waite made a motion for a brief recess at 8:40 p.m. Council
Member Franzen made a second. Motion passed with all ayes, 6-0.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to go back into session at 8:48 p.m.
Council Member Waite made a second. Motion passed with all ayes, 6-0.

Proposed Ordinance – Coin Laundry Text Amendment – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the Independence
zoning ordinance by adding a definition for coin-operated laundries and dry
cleaners as a permitted use within the community commercial (CC) zone. He
stated the Kenton County Planning Commission held a public hearing on January
5, 2023 and gave a favorable recommendation for the text amendment.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Downs of Nicholson – Updated Concept Plan – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends Ordinance No.
2021-O-09, amending the concept development plan for the Downs of Nicholson
development on the northeast corner of Taylor Mill Road (KY 16) and Madison
Pike (KY 17). He stated the changes in the updated plan include combining the
microbrewery and restaurant into one building as well as there being more grass
and a few less patio homes.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading. He stated the
Kenton County Planning Commission had a public hearing and gave a favorable
recommendation of the proposed plan on December 1, 2022. Mr. Gatlin stated the
90 days from action would be March 1, 2023 and council would not have enough
time to do a first and second reading prior to the 90 days. He stated if they
were not in favor, council would need to have a special meeting prior to March
1, 2023 to oppose the proposed changes.
Council Member Steffen stated he thinks the area should be more of a commercial
development instead of more apartments.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a motion to accept the recommendation of the
Kenton County Planning Commission to approve the updated concept plan. Council
Member Waite made a second. Roll was called and votes were 5-1. Council Member
Steffen opposed.
Attorney Gatlin stated the second reading of the ordinance to approve the plan
will still occur at the next meeting on March 6, 2023.
Executive Order No. 2023-EO-03 – PDS Appointment
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2023-EO-03 which re-appoints
himself as the primary representative and Chris Vogelpohl as the alternate
representative to the Planning and Development Services Council for the 2023
year.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated there are 30 active foreclosures in the city and four of
those have been initiated by the city due to code enforcement issues.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated the city building repairs are beginning this week with
drywall. He stated the bid received to terrace the amphitheater last year came
back at $1.2 million, which was over the budgeted amount. Mr. Moriconi stated
he had another engineering firm is take a look at the plan and scaled it back
and the engineer’s estimate for the updated plan is $600,000. He stated this
will go out to bid in the next couple of months and bids should be presented to
council by May or June.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the Board of Adjustments has voted to change
alternating locations between the Independence courthouse as well as meeting in
Covington. He stated he is hosting the mayor’s group meeting later in the month
and voting challenges will be discussed with other mayors and the county. Mayor
Reinersman stated Kenton County occupational and payroll taxes have recently
increased.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 9:31 p.m.

COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, May 1,
2023 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Steffen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Dave
Shafer, Greg Steffen, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney Brandon Voelker,
Captain Russ Wood, Captain Brian Ferayorni, Finance Director Rachyl Gibson and
Building Inspector Mike Carpenter.
Approval of the April 3, 2023 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the council meeting minutes for the regular meeting held on
April 3, 2023.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the council meeting minutes
from the regular meeting held on April 3, 2023. Council Member Franzen made a
motion to approve and Council Member Shafer made a second. Motion carried with
all ayes, 6-0.
Proclamation
Mayor Reinersman presented a Proclamation to recognize May 12, 2023 as child
care provider appreciation day in Independence.
Holly Hill Presentation
James Sherry, CEO of Holly Hill, presented Holly Hill’s strategic plan of
Healthy Minds, Healthy Communities. He stated the vision is a future where all
mental and behavioral health needs are met in the communities they serve. Mr.
Sherry stated they are building a coalition of support in hopes of growing
their residential program 200-300%. He stated they are requesting support from
Independence which would help add staffing and support more local kids. Mr.
Sherry stated Holly Hill offers residential care focused on girls ages 11-17
years old that are in the state’s custody and treat the most traumatized kids
which have include victims of abuse, pregnant and parenting teens. He stated
they also offer targeted case management as well as outpatient behavioral and
mental health care.
Council Member Waite made a motion to donate $100,000 to Holly Hill. Council
Member Brinker with a second. Roll was called and votes were unanimous. Motion
carried 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2023-O-07 - Amending Building Permit Fees - 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2023-O-07 which amends the fee
schedule for city building permits.
Brian Miller, Vice President, Building Industry Association of Northern
Kentucky addressed council in regards to the proposed increase in building
permit fees. He stated the increases amount to an escalation of at least 20%
above the current fee structure. Mr. Miller stated he is asking for a pass to
not increase fees at this time. Council had questions for Building Inspector
Mike Carpenter, regarding the increased fee amounts. Mr. Carpenter stated the
city hasn’t raised fees since 2015 although the costs to the city have
increased. He stated the city has to pay a backup inspector when he takes
vacation time and is currently in the process of training an in-house backup
within the public works department. Mr. Carpenter stated with the proposed
increase in fees, the city will still be 22% lower than neighboring cities and
counties.
There was some discussion regarding some of the fee change amounts such as
commercial building fees for new/addition to structure and tenant finish/
alteration as well as the HVAC permit fee chart. Noted changes under commercial
building permit fees new addition to structure should be $.06/sf to $.072/sf
for 5-30k square feet and $.04/sf to $.048/sf for 30k+ square feet. He stated
the last line of the commercial HVAC permit fees is incorrect as well, should
be $1,600,001 instead of 1,6001. Mayor Reinersman stated the building inspector
is a necessity and we run very lean and we haven’t raised fees in over eight
years.
Attorney Voelker gave Ordinance No. 2023-O-07 a second reading including noted
typos to be corrected in executed ordinance.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2023-O-07 to
update the building permit fees with the mentioned corrections. Council Member
Franzen made a motion to approve and Council Member Steffen made a second.
Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Adopting NKREA Board – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the code of
ordinances related to chapter 38 code of ethics and adopting the Northern
Kentucky Regional Ethics Authority Interlocal Agreement. Attorney Voelker gave
the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Proposed Ordinance – Amended Budget for 2022-2023 – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the 2022-2023
budget.
Attorney Voelker gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Council Member Franzen made a motion for a short recess. Council Member Waite
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes and meeting went into a recess at
8:10 p.m.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to return to active session. Council

into active session at 8:13 p.m.
Mayor’s Budget Message regarding the 2023-2024 Proposed Budget
Mayor Reinersman stated the proposed 2023-2024 budget is not based on an
increase in property taxes. He stated the changes that impact budget are police
education incentives, development of Park 536, Downs of Nicholson development,
amphitheater terracing, ARPA funds and new employees. Mayor Reinersman stated
School Resource Officers, five new police cruisers, new public works pickup,
$2,000,000 investment in street repairs, amphitheater terracing and pass
through costs for building insurance claim from water damage are some of the
expenses in this new budget. He stated several recent retirements have created
new opportunities adding a new full time Program Coordinator as well as a new
Finance Director to city staff.

Municipal Order No. 2023-MO-02 – Home Consortium Interlocal
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2023-MO-02 which authorizes the
Mayor to enter into an interlocal consortium agreement with Bellevue, Bromley,
Covington, Dayton Erlanger, Florence and Newport.
Covington Mayor Joe Meyer presented the program to council and stated to
qualify for the program, the minimum annual income is $53,500 for an
individual, $76,400 for a family of four and maximum home price of $195,000 and
is adjusted each year by the federal government. He stated the City of
Covington will manage the compliance of the HOME Program and its annual share
of funding will be no less than it received prior to the formation of the
Consortium. Mayor Meyer stated the applicants are screened to make sure
applicants are able to afford the home and taxes and can pay all associated
costs of being a homeowner. He stated it’s a great service to provide to the
community, especially young, first-time homebuyers and doesn’t cost the city
anything.

Mayor Reinersman presented the bids for terracing of the amphitheater. He
stated the engineer’s estimate was $575,900 and the two bids received were Ford
Development for $572,180 and Beaumont Building Group. Mayor Reinersman
recommends awarding the bid to Ford Development.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to award the bid to Ford Development.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to award the bid to award to Ford
Development and a second was made by Council Member Waite. Roll was called and
votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Award Bid – Concrete
Mayor Reinersman presented the bids for concrete jobs with two bidders with
Ernst Concrete and Hometown Concrete. Mr. Moriconi stated the Public Works
Director would like to be able to use both if time gets tight and one company
is busy. Attorney Gatlin stated the city can accept both bids and Ernst would
need to be made aware with a condition in their contract that the city could
use Hometown if Ernst isn’t available in a reasonable amount of time.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a motion to accept both concrete bids from Ernst
Concrete and Hometown Concrete. Council Member Shafer made a second. Roll was
called and votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 6-0.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Voelker stated the city currently has 34 active foreclosures and only
5 are city initiated due to code enforcement issues.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the 25th Annual Independence Celebration will include
$15 ride bracelets, Circus Mojo and roman candle show on Friday evening, June

August 7, 2023
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 7,
2023 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Carol Franzen, Dave
Shafer, Greg Steffen, Chris Vogelpohl and Greg Waite. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney Jack Gatlin and
Captain Russ Wood.
Approval of the June 5, 2023 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the council meeting minutes for the regular meeting held on
June 5, 2023.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve the council meeting minutes
from the regular meeting held on June 5, 2023. Council Member Shafer made a
motion to approve and Council Member Vogelpohl made a second. Motion carried
with all ayes, 6-0.
Swearing in of New Officer - Nathan Kling
Mayor Reinersman swore in of Officer Nathan Kling, whom comes with years of
experience with the Taylor Mill Police Department.
Williamswoods Sober Living House Discussion
Mayor Reinersman stated a letter was received from Pinnacle and the home
located at 10609 Williamswoods Drive will be utilized as a sober living house.
He stated they are protected by the ADA, and KRS 100.982-984. Mayor Reinersman
stated it is not a treatment center, it is a home for recovering addicts. He
stated there are several located throughout Northern Kentucky and the only
complaints from neighbors have been regarding multiple cars parked on the
street. Mayor Reinersman stated sober living houses are protected by the
federal government and they are not required to apply for a conditional use
permit or even notify the city. He stated the code enforcement officer believed
it was a rehab facility and that the company would have to go to the Board of
Adjustments to get a conditional use permit. Mayor Reinersman stated it later
turned out to be incorrect, it was in fact a sober living house, not a rehab
facility.
Dan Courtney, 10614 Williamswoods Drive, Independence, KY 41051 - Mr. Courtney
stated his frustration regarding the miscommunication regarding the possibility
of being able to go before the Board of Adjustments in opposition of this rehab
facility opening on his street.
Attorney Gatlin stated the federal government has determined recovering addicts
as disabled and hundreds of cities have been sued trying to fight against sober
living houses.
Doug Gunning, 10593 Williamswoods Drive, Independence, KY 41051 - Mr. Gunning
questioned why a for-profit business is allowed to run in a residential area
without any special permit.
Mike Schroer, 10637 Williamswoods Drive, Independence, KY 41051 - Mr. Schroer
stated he works for Kenton County and he has guys work with him and some of
them go to sober living houses.
Logan Wendling, 10605 Williamswoods Drive, Independence, KY 41051 - Ms.
Wendling stated she lives next door to the sober living house and has a 16-
year-old son and a 9-year-old daughter. She said her son was introduced to
drugs and alcohol at a young age and has spent thousands of dollars on
treatment and is concerned with addicts living next door to her. Ms. Wendling
stated she believes that addicts are self-induced and should not be considered
disabled.
Council Member Franzen stated her concerns as a mother with children living
next door to people to have done drugs but explained that council's hands are
tied as long as the residents of the sober living house follow the rules as
they are covered as a protected class under ADA. She stated having a sober
living house isn't a benefit to the city in any way.
Randel Hamilton, 10613 Williamswoods Drive, Independence, KY 41051 - Mr.
Hamilton stated the city stopped the jail from being built inside the city and
questioned why this can't be stopped as well. Council Member Franzen stated she
helped work on the committee and they worked with the commissioners to get the
jail moved to a better location, it wasn't up to the city to decide where it
was being built.
Connie Ehlen, 10629 Williamswoods Drive, Independence, KY 41051 - Ms. Ehlen
stated drug addicts robbed her 16 years ago. She asked how she is supposed to
feel safe and wants to know what the city is going to do about it. Mayor
Reinersman stated the police are available in case something happens.
Steve Fowler, 10601 Williamswoods Drive, Independence, KY 41051 - Mr. Fowler
stated his concern for the extra cars that will be present on the street.
Franklin Cain, 1159 Gatewood Lane, Independence, KY 41051 - Mr. Cain asked
council if the city had any say in the sober living house because it's located
close to schools.
Ordinance No. 2023-O-12-Timber View Sidewalk Waiver-2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2023-0-12 which waives the sidewalk
requirement by the Independence Zoning Code for Phase 40 of Timber View. He
stated the terrain has unusual topographical or exceptional physical
conditions, regulation compliance could cause an unsafe situation and the
proposed modification would create a materially safer situation than complying
with the regulations. Attorney Gatlin Ordinance No. 2023-0-12 a second reading.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2023-0-12.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve and Council Member Vogelpohl
made a second. Roll was called and motion carried with a vote of 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance - Employee Pay Classification - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the personnel and
pay classification plan. Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first
reading.
Proposed Ordinance - Renewed Cable TV Franchise Agreement - 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which grants and issues a
competitive, non exclusive franchise for a combined term of 10 years with
Spectrum, Mid-America, LLC and authorizes the mayor to sign this agreement.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Council Member Brinker made a motion for a short recess, Council Member Franzen
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0. Council went into recess at
7:57 p.m.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to return to regular session, Council
Member Shafer made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0. Council
returned to regular session at 8:01 p.m.
Resolution No. 2023-R-09 - Richardson Road Map Amendment

Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2023-R-11 which approves a $100,000
donation to Holly Hill Child and Family Solutions for the purpose of supporting
mental health initiatives. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2023-R-11.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2023-R-11.

Mayor Reinersman stated two bids were received for the new maintenance building

Attorney Report - Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated all but 1 foreclosure in the city should be dismissed by

job keeping up with violations as they review them every couple of weeks.
City Administrator's Report
Mr. Moriconi shared his appreciation to Attorney Gatlin and keeping up with
code enforcement issues. He stated the amphitheater terracing will start later
this month and a sidewalk is being added from the parking lots on either side
of the senior center. Mr. Moriconi stated the new restrooms at Sterling Staggs
Park are nearly completed.
Mayor's Report
Mayor Reinersman stated we are hoping to have a special meeting on September
18th as well as one on August 28th to have the first reading of the 2023-2024
tax rates. He stated Police Chief Anthony Lucas retired at the end of June and
Captains Jake Boyle, Brian Ferayorni and Russ Wood are in the running for the
next Independence Police Chief. Mayor Reinersman explained the selection
process which includes surveying officers regarding the qualities and
challenges for each candidate, leadership testing, a panel interview as well as
final interviews with the mayor and city administrator. He stated the

Council Member Franzen left the meeting at 8:30pm.

Moriconi stated the next phase of 536 should start in November.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Shafer to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:38 p.m.

Proposed Ordinance – Map Amendment for 17/Harris Pike – 1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the zoning map for
19.93 acres at the intersection of KY 17 and Harris Pike (KY 536) from
Neighborhood Commercial (NC) and Residential Rural Estate (R-RE) to Community
Commercial (CC) and approving the submitted development plan with conditions.
He stated the development will include a grocery store and restaurant, will not
be a White Castle as they are selling the property to the developer.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading and stated there
was a public hearing with the Kenton County Planning Commission on September 7,
2023. He stated PDS Planning Staff gave a favorable recommendation with
conditions including the installing sidewalks and compliance of drainage
systems by the Northern Kentucky Regional Storm Water Management Program Rules
and Regulations.
Resolution No. 2023-R-12 – Trailer Regulation Update
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2023-R-12 which sponsors a proposed a
text amendment regarding parking and loading standards for trailers within the
city. He stated the proposed text amendment would allow empty flatbed trailer’s
to be stored in property owner’s driveway year- round if in good working order.
Mayor Reinersman stated the amendment would also allow campers, boats and RVs
to be stored in property owner’s driveway for up to 96 consecutive hours within
a seven (7) day period.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2023-R-12 and stated the proposal is for
flatbed trailers limited to thirty (30) feet in length (tongue to bumper),
eight (8) feet in width and five (5) feet tall.
Al Daly, Limerick Circle, Independence, KY – Mr. Daly stated he would like the
text to specify when the time starts and stops on the allowed timeframe.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2023-R-12.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a motion with a second by Council Member Waite.
Roll was called and votes were 6-0. Motion carried.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated the ash trees in median of the Hartland subdivision will
need to be removed. He stated work on the amphitheater should be starting on
October 16th and will be adding block to the restroom at Memorial Park.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman congratulated Council Member Waite for earning a Level 2 in
Excellence in City Government with Kentucky League of Cities.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Waite to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:40 p.m.

Neighborhood Commercial (NC) and Residential Rural Estate (R-RE) to Community

Steffen made a motion to approve the amended minutes and Council Member Shafer

Proclamations
Mayor Reinersman presented a Proclamation to Kenton County Dispatch Supervisors
Missy Eddy and Julie White for their skilled communication techniques which
assisted officers with a domestic dispute that occurred on January 7, 2024.
 
Mayor Reinersman presented a Proclamation to Officers Adam McGuire, Walter
Cooley, Nathan Kling, Nathan Strunk, Samuel Collins and Travis Lovell for their
swift action to detain the suspect safely during a domestic dispute that

Mayor Reinersman and Chief Ferayorni presented the Silver Star for Bravery

for their actions during a domestic dispute call that occurred on January 7,

Madison Pike Condo Development Discussion
Mayor Reinersman stated the developers have withdrawn their initial proposal to
build 120 condos on the property across from St. Cecilia Church. He shared a
presentation to discuss common concerns and misconceptions. Mayor Reinersman
stated the site is currently 3 different zones: PUD, R-M and R-CVS. Mayor
Reinersman stated the 2020 traffic study showed 6,255 cars per day on average
in that same area. He stated the proposed two-bedroom condo complex is
estimated to generate an additional 57 cars during AM peak (6:00 – 10:00am) and
68 additional cars during PM peak (2:00 – 7:00pm) per day. He stated one of the
rumors is the city is going to get a bunch of money from this development and
the truth is it would only be about $65,000 a year in property taxes.  
 
Mayor Reinersman stated some benefits of working with the developer is their
willingness to install a 12’ retaining wall that screens the first 1.5 floors
for the largest buildings, additional tree screening, the building quality
exceeds the minimum design standards and the complex would have a HOA. He
stated the Kenton County Planning Commission recommended disapproval for the
initial plan submitted. Mayor Reinersman stated the developer asked to meet
with the city and it has been discussed of having the developer reduce the
density, add more screening, conduct a traffic study and resubmit a new plan to
the Kenton County Planning Commission. Mayor Reinersman shared some images and
3-D renderings of the proposed buildings which illustrates the view for the
Millcreek neighbors.
 
Council Member Franzen made a motion for a brief recess. Council Member Waite
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0. Council took a recess at 8:00
pm.
 
Council Member Franzen made a motion to go back in session. Council Member
Waite made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0. Council entered back in
session at 8:09 pm.

Medical Cannabis Legislation – Presentation by Sharmili Reddy, Executive
Director of Planning and Development Services
Mrs. Reddy
Kentucky passed KRS 218B in 2023 and HB 829 – Modifications in 2024. Admin
regulations 915 KAR 1.001-110 & 2:00. A cannabis business is licensed by the
cabinet and shall be subject to and required to comply with – any
subsequential…
Cannot be less restrictive than state statute or admin regulations, regulate
time, place and manner and cannot impose undue burden or make the operations
unreasonable or impractical.
Are required to be in enclosed building and local jurisdictions will not be
able to…..
Local gov’t options: 1) adopt regulations (no ballot option), 2) no – enact
ordinance – public petition to allow cannabis operations or 3) on ballot –
enact resolution with question on ballot. If the county votes no, the city can
still vote yes through ordinance. May assess an additional reasonable fee to
compensate for additional corrections.
Cultivation – Processing – Production – Dispensary – Safety Compliance Facility
KRS 218B – 1,000 foot buffer from schools and day cares.
July 1 – August 31: Applications, business licensing lottery, license issued.
Dispensaries cannot open to the public prior to January 1, 2025.
Sharmili stated the city will need be a resolution authorizing the city to
allow medical cannabis and there are limited conditions that would qualify for
the medical cannabis.

Medical Cannabis Program Discussion
Mayor Reinersman stated Kenton County will make a decision next week and has
heard they will be banning the cannabis businesses within the county. Mr.
Moriconi stated someone reached out to the city a few days prior asking if the
city will be allowing dispensaries. There was some discussion regarding the
options for council which include decide to ban it which would require an
ordinance
with 2 readings which includes a 30-day petition period, place on the ballot
and let the voters decide as well as submitting a text amendment to Planning
and Development Services (PDS) to research and make recommendations and have a
public hearing. Council Member Franzen made a motion to put the cannabis it on
the ballot and let the residents vote on the issue.
Resolution No. 2024-R-10-Add Cannabis Business Regulations to be decided by
voters Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2024-R-10 which directs the
question of regulating cannabis businesses to operate within the limits to the
city's voters at the next regular election.
Attorney Gatlin read and clarified that Resolution No. 2024-R-10 would direct
the question "Are you in favor of the sale of medicinal cannabis at a licensed
dispensary and the operation of other cannabis businesses in the City of
Independence which is per KRS 218B.130 (2) (c).
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution 2024-R-10 to add
Cannabis Business Regulations to the ballot during next election. Council
Member Franzen made a motion to approve and Council Member Vogelpohl made a
second. Motion carried with a 4-2 vote with Council Members Shafer and Steffen
voted in opposition.
There was some discussion about also passing a resolution about a sponsored
text amendment for industrial zones. Attorney Gatlin stated since council
passed passing the question to the voters, it could be a conflict if the
businesses are limited to industrial zones. Mayor Reinersman stated PDS can do
a deeper dive and look into the city's zones and identify if there are any
allowable areas that could accommodate the cannabis businesses that are
appropriate distance from schools and daycares.
Council Member Shafer made a motion to rescind Resolution No. 2024-R-10.
Council Member Steffen seconded to rescind the resolution. Roll was called and
the votes were 2-4, motion failed.

Splash Pad Presentation – Carol Franzen
Council Members Franzen presented to council some information regarding splash
pads including: the plans must be submitted by our engineer with their
individual seal, the Health Department will look at the plan first and it will
then be passed onto the state. Operating requirements including recirculating
water must be tested three times a day and have a UV light disinfection system.
Council Member Franzen showed various examples of splash parks with different
equipment packages. Council Member Steffen stated the city has done a great job
of incorporating parks for the families that live here and the splash pad would
be a great investment. He stated the annual expenses are not much but it’s
mainly the upfront costs and if we get the grant, it should cover a big part of
the initial cost. There was some discussion about options on who would be
responsible for testing the water, turning water off and on each day as well as
parking challenges.

Resolution No. 2024-R-12 – Regulation of Medical Cannabis
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2024-R-12 which proposes a text
amendment. He stated this would have Planning and Development Services (PDS)
staff research and issue recommendations as well as moving forward with a
hearing in front of the Kenton County Planning Commission for the regulation of
medical cannabis through zoning.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2024-R-12.

The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, August 5,

5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman

Council Member Waite made a motion to approve the council meeting minutes for
the July 1, 2024 meeting and Council Member Shafer made a second. Motion
carried, 6-0.
AED Importance - Proiect Heart Restart
Mayor Reinersman stated Project Heart Restart is helping with funding AED
machines in cruisers. Josh Vogel with Project Heart Restart stated there are
over 350,000 cardiac arrests annually. He stated the discounted cost is $2,000
per AED machine. Partners include Christ Hospital, create a division just for
police and first responders. Hamilton County police association needed 100
units for all patrol cars. By September or October, every county will have an
AED in every patrol car. Contributor group includes Rotary International, major
national. Phase 3 is to put an AED in every patrol car in Boone, Campbell and
Kenton counties. Assistant Chjef Boyle stated our max patrol officers at one
time is currently 8 to 9. Mayor Reinersman stated we have budgeted for 4 AEDs
for the current year and Project Heart Restart could help us get the additional
AEDs needed by the end of the year.
Resolution No. 2024-R-13 -Text Amendment for Fences in Front Yards
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2024-R-13 which is a text amendment
to allow fences in front yards. He stated the text amendment proposal is to
allow fences with normal setback requirements, with a maximum height of 3 feet
in the front yards of parcels that are over 3 acres in size in the R-CVS, R-RE
and R-LLS zones.
Mayor Reinersman stated PDS did an initial review of the city to find 3+ acre
lots in the city and that is how the listed zones were determined. There was
some discussion and council would like to raise the minimum fence height from
three feet to five feet and add the verbiage to allow fences 'on arterial and
connector roads' to the requirements. Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2024-
R-13.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2024-R-13.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve and Council Waite made a
second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Award - Concrete Bids
Mayor Reinersman presented the bids for concrete jobs with two bidders with
Ernst Concrete and Hometown Concrete. Mr. Moriconi stated the preference is to
use Ernst Concrete, which is a dollar cheaper per yard. He stated the city can
accept both bids and Ernst would need to be made aware with a condition in
their contract that the city could use Hometown if Ernst isn't available in a
reasonable amount of time.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to award of Ernst Concrete and use
Hometown if Ernst isn't available in a reasonable amount of time, Council
Steffen made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Attorney Report - Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he didn't have any business to report.
City Administrator's Report
Mr. Moriconi stated he didn't have any business to report.
Mayor's Report
Mayor Reinersman stated we had a record crowd for our Independence Day festival
this year. He stated we have our last Party in the Park this Thursday as well
as our police and fire department participating in the National Night Out at
Memorial Park on Tuesday, August 6th. Mayor Reinersman stated we'll have a
special meeting on August 26th at 7:00 for first reading of the tax rate and
then another special meeting on September 18th for the second reading.

and seconded by Council Member Shafer to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes
and the meeting ended at 7:48 p.m.

Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Wednesday,
September 18, 2024 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence
Municipal Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor
Christopher Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order
and led the Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation.
Roll was called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom
Brinker, Carol Franzen, Dave Shafer, Greg Waite and Chris Vogelpohl. Council
Member Steffen was absent. Also present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi,
City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney Jack Gatlin and Police Assistant Chief Jake
Boyle.
Ordinance No. 2024-O-10– Tax Rates for 2024-2025 – 2 nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2024-O-10 which adopts real property
tax rate at $.22 or each hundred dollars and the tax rate of $.534 for each one
hundred dollars or personal property.
Mayor Reinersman stated the tax rate has not been raised since 2016 and the
rate will be staying the same as the previous year. He stated Kenton County
Property Value Administrator (PVA) is the entity that re-assesses property
values every four years, per statute. Mayor Reinersman stated the city has
experienced increases as well such as an increase in police salaries as well as
additional services and the tax revenue with keeping the tax rate the same with
just an excess of $20,000 for the year.
Attorney Gatlin read Ordinance No. 2024-O-10 a second reading.
Dan Lambert, 5220 Millcreek Circle, Independence, KY – Mr. Lambert opposed to
keeping tax rate the same and thinks the tax rate should be decreased by 1% to
avoid overinflation. Mayor Reinersman questioned how the city would absorb the
increased costs that would come with decreasing the tax rate. Mr. Lambert
stated he thinks the city needs to just figure it out.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2024-O-10.
Council Member Franzen so moved, with a second by Council Member Waite. Roll
was called and votes were unanimous. Motion carried, 5-0.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated he had nothing to report.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman congratulated Chief Brian Ferayorni as he recently completing
his first year as our Police Chief and to Assistant Chief Jake Boyle who
recently celebrated his 15-year anniversary with the city. He stated
Independence has a new K9 team, Canine Cairo and his handler Officer Ben
Bridges. Mayor Reinersman stated his appreciation to our local donors to help
sponsor our K9 team.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Franzen
and seconded by Council Member Vogelpohl to adjourn. Motion carried with all
ayes and the meeting ended at 7:21 p.m.

weaknesses or significant deficiencies in internal controls as well as no
instances of non-compliance with laws and grant or bond agreements. Mr.
Chamberlin stated there has been a significant drop in liabilities due to
allocating ARPA funds and pension funds.
Approval of the November 11, 2024 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the council meeting minutes for the regular meeting held on
November 11, 2024.
Council Member Shafer made a motion to approve the council meeting minutes for
the November 11, 2024, meeting and Council Member Steffen made a second. Motion
carried, 4-0.
Proposed ordinance – Stephenson Road Truck Restrictions – 1 st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which restricts certain traffic
in excess of 11,000 pounds on Stephens Road at a point from Fowler Creek (State
Route1486) to Oliver Road. There was some discussion regarding the
implementation of a permit and violators would be subject to a city citation.
Mayor Reinersman stated there would be exceptions for public safety, garbage
trucks and school buses. Council agreed to add signs for violators of the
weight limit to receive a city citation for infractions with $500 for first
offense and $750 for each incident thereafter.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Executive Order No. 2024-EO-03 – Appointment for the Kenton County Joint Code
Enforcement Board
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2024-EO-03 which appoints Chris
Barbour to the Kenton County Joint Code Enforcement Board from January 1, 2025
through December 31, 2027.
Executive Order No. 2024-EO-04 – Appointment for the PDS Council
Mayor Reinersman presented Executive Order No. 2024-EO-04 which re-appoints
Mayor Reinersman as the primary representative and Council Member Carol Franzen
as the alternate on the Planning and Development Services Council for the city
for 2025.
Award Bid – Concrete Finishing Contract for 2025
Chris Moriconi stated we received five bids for the concrete finishing contract
for 2025. He suggested Boles Concrete be awarded the bid as they not only have
the lowest price in each category, but they also have a good history with the
city.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to award the 2025 concrete finishing
contract to Boles Concrete. Council Member Wait made a second. Motion carried,
4-0.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated SD1 is working on some re-engineering on the sewer project
for Peach Drive, Allen Drive, Walnut Hall and part of Madison Pike. He stated
there is a grant to cover the lateral pipe as well as the connection to each of
the homes. Mr. Moriconi stated the pickleball court lighting issues should be
fixed soon at Memorial Park.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated the Christmas Walk is happening this upcoming weekend
with the added ice-skating rink which will be open on Friday, Saturday and
Sunday. He stated the Santa 5K kicks off Saturday, crafts at the Christmas
Market at the Courthouse, tree lighting, parade and main festivities from 6:00
to 9:00 p.m. as well as a new event Selfies with Santa on Sunday afternoon.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Shafer and
seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 8:23 p.m.

2025 Minutes
February 3, 2025
COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of February 3, 2025                  City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, February
3, 2025 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal
Center, 5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher
Reinersman presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the
Pledge of Allegiance. Council Member Steffen led the invocation. Roll was
called and the following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker,
Matthew Fehler, Carol Franzen, Greg Steffen, Greg Waite, Chris Vogelpohl. Also
present was City Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney
Jack Gatlin and Chief Brian Ferayorni.
Approval of the December 2, 2024 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the council meeting minutes for the regular meeting held on
December 2, 2024.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a motion to approve the council meeting minutes
for the December 2, 2024, meeting and Council Member Brinker made a second.
Motion carried, 5-0. Council Member Fehler abstained.
Swearing in of Officer Cody Monson
Mayor Reinersman swore in new Police Officer Cody Monson, who was previously
with the Covington Police Department.
Introduction of Police Social Worker
Mayor Reinersman introduced the new Police Social Worker Taylor Graham. He
stated she has been a social worker with the Cabinet for Health and Family
Services for the past six years.
Ordinance No. 2025-O-01 – Stephens Road Truck Restrictions – 2 nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2025-O-01 which restricts vehicles in
excess of 11,000 pounds on Stephens Road at a point from Fowler Creek (State
Route1486) to Oliver Road. He stated motor vehicles or trucks having a width
greater than seen feet may not travel on Stephens Road and public safety
vehicles, school buses and garbage trucks are exempt from this restriction.
Mayor Reinersman stated for violations, there will be a city citation for $500
for first offense and $750 for second and subsequent offense.
Attorney Gatlin read Ordinance No. 2025-O-01.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2025-O-01.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve, with a second from Council
Member Steffen. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried,
6-0.
Resolution No. 2025-R-01 – Approval for Courthouse Crossing Signage
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-01 which approves the final
development plan for the construction of a six-foot tall, detached sign for the
Courthouse Crossing. He stated PDS Staff gave the plan a favorable
recommendation.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-01.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-01.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve, and Council Member Brinker made
a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2025-R-02 – Interlocal Agreement for Drone Program
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-02 which approves an
interlocal agreement for operation of a drone program with the Kenton County
Sheriff’s Office and Marc Fields, Kenton County Jailer. Chief Ferayorni stated
the cost of the drone is approximately $20,000 and will be split 50/50 with the
Kenton County Sheriff’s Office.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-02.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-02.
Council Member Vogelpohl made a motion to approve, and Council Member Franzen
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2025-R-03 – Approval of Final Development Plan – Bristow Rd
Townhomes
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-03 which authorizes and
approves a final development plan for clearing and grading for future
development of the Bristow Road Townhome Development within the Beechgrove
Planned Unit Development (PUD). Mr. Moriconi stated this development goes back
to 1971 which was known as Villages of Beechgrove and included 1,500 total
units of housing.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-03.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-03.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve, and Council Member Vogelpohl
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2025-R-04 – Opposition of Centralized Collection of Occupational
Licenses
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-04 which opposes any action by
the Kentucky General Assembly that provides the centralized collection of legal
occupational business fees and taxes by the Commonwealth of Kentucky. He stated
if this process went to Frankfort, it’s likely the city wouldn’t get the full
fees and would lose the local control.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-04.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-04.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve, and Council Brinker made a
second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Proposed Ordinance – Renaming of Court Street – 1 st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance renaming Court Street to Ponzer
Court. He stated that Vic Ponzer was a long-time Independence resident,
business owner and Kenton County Deputy Sheriff.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading.
Municipal Order No. 2025-MO-01 – Surplus Property – Treadmills
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2025-MO-01 which declares two
Landice L8 Treadmills. He stated the treadmills are several years old and have
been replaced with new models to better serve the fitness needs of the police
department and city staff. Mayor Reinersman stated the treadmills will be
listed for sale on www.govdeals.com.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Municipal Order No. 2025-MO-01.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve, and Council Member Steffen made
a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Attorney Report – Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated there is an uptick in foreclosures and bankruptcies in
the city.
City Administrator’s Report
Mr. Moriconi stated during this month’s Kenton County Planning Commission
meeting, they will be discussing driveway setbacks and the definition of a
shipping container.
Mayor’s Report
Mayor Reinersman stated our Public Services department did a great job keeping
streets clean with the 10 inches of snow we got in early January. He stated the
South Kenton County project is in unincorporated county and not in the city.
Mayor Reinersman stated the transportation cabinet is considering a possible
future traffic interchange off Maher Road. He stated there are two sites being
considered for the splash park location at Memorial Park.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:56 p.m.

                   Christopher J. Reinersman, Mayor

COUNCIL MEETING
Minutes of March 3, 2025   City of Independence, Ky.
Opening
The City Council of the City of Independence, Kentucky met on Monday, March 3,
2025 at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chambers of the Independence Municipal Center,
5409 Madison Pike, Independence, Kentucky with Mayor Christopher Reinersman
presiding. Mayor Reinersman called the meeting to order and led the Pledge of
Allegiance. Council Member Franzen led the invocation. Roll was called and the
following Council Members registered present: Tom Brinker, Matthew Fehler,
Carol Franzen, Greg Steffen, Greg Waite, Chris Vogelpohl. Also present was City
Administrator Chris Moriconi, City Clerk Gina Rawe, Attorney Jack Gatlin and
Chief Brian Ferayorni.
Approval of the February 3, 2025 Council Meeting Minutes
Mayor Reinersman asked Council if there were any changes or corrections they
would like made to the council meeting minutes for the regular meeting held on
February 3, 2025.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve the council meeting minutes for
the February 3, 2025, meeting and Council Member Franzen made a second. Motion
carried, 6-0.
Ordinance No. 2025-0-02 - Renaming of Court Street - 2nd Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented Ordinance No. 2025-0-02 which renames Court Street
to Ponzer Court. He stated this street name change is to honor resident Vic
Ponzer for his contributions to the city.
Attorney Gatlin read Ordinance No. 2025-0-02.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Ordinance No. 2025-0-02.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve, with a second from Coru1cil
Member Steffen. Roll was called and the votes were unanimous. Motion carried,
6-0.
Mayor's Report
Mayor Reinersman stated he is keeping an eye on several bills that threaten
local control. He stated Representative Dunn has been great to work with as
well as Representative Moser for years. Mayor Reinersman stated there are
various proposed bills that are threatening to take away local control from
cities regarding items such as affordable housing, rental registry, short term
rentals, etc.
Proposed Ordinance - Driveway Requirements and Shipping Container Definition -
1st Reading
Mayor Reinersman presented a proposed ordinance which amends the zoning code
adding setback requirements for driveways as a permitted encroachment, adding
standards for portable storage units and shipping containers and adding the
definition of a shipping container.
Attorney Gatlin gave the proposed ordinance a first reading and stated the PDS
Staff gave a favorable recommendation after the public hearing on February 6,
2025.
Ben Bach, I0112 Meadow Glen Drive, Independence, KY - Mr. Bach asked what
prompted this change and the Mayor stated there have been some citations issued
by code enforcement and it was discovered there wasn't a definition of a
shipping container so it needed to be defined so the zoning code was clear.
Resolution No. 2025-R-05-Authorization for Contract Extension for Trash and
Recycling 
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-05 which approves and
authorizes the Mayor to execute an extension of the previously bid fees for
trash and recycling services for residential units in the city from July I,
2025 through June 30, 2027.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-05.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-05.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve, and Council Member Brinker
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2025-R-06- Opposition of HB85 Relating to Sanitation Districts
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-06 which opposes House Bill
85, relating to sanitation districts. He stated this bill would remove the fee
to have SDI manage storm water within the city.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-06.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-06.
Council Member Steffen made a motion to approve, and Council Waite made a
second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2025-R-07-Opposition of House and Senate Bills That Would Remove
Local Control
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-07 which opposes Senate Bills
18 and 110 as well as House Bills 134,173,253,490 and 806. He stated these
proposed bills would all remove local control for cities on local issues.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-07.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-07.
Council Member Franzen made a motion to approve, and Council Member Brinker
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Resolution No. 2025-R-08- Waters of the Commonwealth
Mayor Reinersman presented Resolution No. 2025-R-08 which opposes SB89 which
would remove protection for groundwater drinking sources and wells and
eliminate prohibition on dumping, filing or releasing pollutants in streams.
Attorney Gatlin read Resolution No. 2025-R-08.
Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Resolution No. 2025-R-08.
Council Member Fehler made a motion to approve, and Council Member Steffen made
a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Municipal Order No. 2025-MO-02- Surplus Property- Police Vehicles
Mayor Reinersman presented Municipal Order No. 2025-MO-02 which declares a 2010
Dodge Charger, two 2013 Dodge Chargers, a 2014 Dodge Charger and a 2014 Ford

Mayor Reinersman called for a motion to approve Municipal Order No. 2025-MO-02.
Council Member Waite made a motion to approve, and Council Member Vogelpohl
made a second. Motion carried with all ayes, 6-0.
Attorney Report - Jack Gatlin
Attorney Gatlin stated he had nothing to report.
City Administrator's Report
Mr. Moriconi stated there is a SDI project on Peach, Alvin and Walnut Hall,
construction should start this summer.
Adjournment
There being no further business, a motion was made by Council Member Waite and
seconded by Council Member Franzen to adjourn. Motion carried with all ayes and
the meeting ended at 7:51 p.m.
